value_domain: AEDC preschool program setting type
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by
variable_description: What kind of service delivered the preschool or kindergarten program the child attended in the year before school, separating a standalone preschool or kindergarten from a long day care centre. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "the organisational basis for the child's preschool / kindergarten", which is the distinction most Australian early childhood policy work needs, because the same entitlement is delivered through both service types. It is answered only where E2Y records attendance, and E2AY gives the hours.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for preschool or kindergarten, 2 for long day care centre, 3 for other, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.
limitation: It identifies a setting type, not a provider, a funding source or a governance arrangement, so it cannot separate a government preschool from an independent or community one. Code 3 is an undifferentiated catch-all, so mobile, occasional care and school-attached services cannot be told apart from one another.
rationale: The dictionary gives E2by's exact instrument text, its purpose and its four-code value list, and the registry shows it sitting beside E2Y and E2AY in the same table.
evidence_quote: In what kind of setting was the preschool / kindergarten program?
supersedes_rationale: The entry held only the question stem with no answer categories and the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that long day care is one of the coded settings.

value_domain: AEDC preschool attendance indicator (yes/no/don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y
variable_description: Whether the child attended a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. It is the gate for the rest of the preschool block: E2AY records the weekly hours and E2BY the setting, and both are answered only where this column records attendance. The dictionary describes it as the variable that identifies "if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school", and it was introduced in 2018 in place of the earlier E2 series of childcare and preschool items.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y
value_definition: A two-digit integer with three codes: 1 for yes, 2 for no, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in 2018.
limitation: The coding is 1 for yes and 2 for no, unlike most AEDC yes/no items which use 0 and 1, so treating this as a 0/1 dummy turns every non-attender into an attender. It also does not carry back to earlier cycles: before 2018 the same information came from a different set of items, so an unadjusted trend from 2009 is not comparable.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording, the 2018 introduction, the 1/2/88 code list, and the conditional instructions on the dependent E2ay and E2by items.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question stem alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it missed the unusual 1-for-yes, 2-for-no coding and the 2018 break in the series.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (long day care)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay
variable_description: Whether the child was in long day care on a regular basis in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the first of six parallel columns, E3AY to E3FY, that cover long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative, a nanny and any other person, each coded the same way. Version 8.0 of the dictionary corrected the instruction on all six, recording that they are "asked to All" rather than only to children whose E2Y records a preschool program.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: No is coded 4, not 0, so a naive greater-than-zero test counts every non-attender as attending. Long day care here also overlaps with E2Y, because a long day care centre can deliver the preschool program reported there, so adding the E3 columns and E2Y together double counts the same child.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the five-code list and the version 8.0 correction to the filter, and the registry shows the six E3 columns sitting together in the same core table.
evidence_quote: E3ay – E3fy –correction to instruction, removed "only answer if E2y=yes" as these items are asked to All.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long question stem ending in 'long day care' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not show that 4 means no or that the filter was corrected in 2025.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (family day care)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by
variable_description: Whether the child was regularly in family day care in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. Family day care is the regulated home-based service, so this column separates it from the centre-based care in E3AY and from the informal relative care in E3CY and E3DY. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school", and the 2018 cycle rebuilt it from the earlier E2e and E2etime pair.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: The full-time and part-time split is the only intensity information available, so it cannot yield hours, days per week or weeks of the year. Code 3 is a real answer rather than a missing value, and dropping it as missing biases any full-time share upwards.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the derivation from E2e and E2etime in 2018, and the five-code value list for this specific care type.
evidence_quote: To identify how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry held the shared question stem ending in 'family day care' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the five sibling columns or explained the intensity codes.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (grandparent)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy
variable_description: Whether a grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. This is the largest of the informal care categories in Australia and the reason the E3 block distinguishes grandparents from other relatives, who are captured separately in E3DY. Because the columns are a multiple response set, a child can be recorded here and in the formal care columns E3AY and E3BY at the same time.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It does not say whether the grandparent lived with the child, was paid, or was the child's primary carer, so it cannot identify kinship care arrangements or grandparent-headed households. The teacher is answering about a household arrangement they did not observe, so the don't-know rate is a property of teacher knowledge rather than of the family.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code list for the grandparent element of the non-parental care question, and the registry shows the six-column multiple response block in one table.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with a Grandparent in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'grandparent' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record the intensity codes or that the six columns are a multiple response set.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (other relative)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy
variable_description: Whether a relative other than a parent or grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the residual family category in the E3 block: grandparents are taken out into E3CY, and unrelated carers fall to E3EY for a nanny or E3FY for a friend or neighbour. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school".
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: The relationship itself is not recorded, so an aunt, an adult sibling and a cousin all collapse into one code and no family structure can be reconstructed from it. It also cannot be read as a measure of family support, since a family with no relative nearby and a family that declined help both record 4.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code value list for the other relative element of the non-parental care question, and names the 2018 derivation from E2g and E2gtime.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry held the shared question stem ending in 'other relative' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving the codes and the boundary against E3CY undocumented.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (nanny)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey
variable_description: Whether a nanny regularly cared for the child in the home in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the paid, unregulated, in-home category of the E3 block, distinct from the regulated home-based service captured in E3BY as family day care. Version 7.0 of the dictionary lists a correction to the field format and field values across E3ay to E3fy, so the published code list for this column is not identical in earlier dictionary releases.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It does not distinguish a live-in nanny from one who visits, or paid work from a reciprocal arrangement, so it cannot support any inference about household income. It is also a narrow category, so any subgroup estimate built on it should be checked against the AEDC suppression rules before it is reported.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the corrected five-code value list for the nanny element of the non-parental care question, and the version table records the field value correction covering E3ay to E3fy.
evidence_quote: Correction to field format/field values (PlaceOfBirth, B2-B7, C3-C51, E3ay-fy)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'nanny' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the published code list for this item had been corrected.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (other person)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy
variable_description: Whether someone outside the family, such as a friend or a neighbour, regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It closes the E3 block as the catch-all: anything that was not long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative or a nanny lands here. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying care "with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school".
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: Being the residual category, it holds arrangements with nothing in common beyond not fitting the five named ones, so a positive value supports no statement about the type or quality of care. It is also the category a teacher is least likely to know about, so a low count here reflects reporting as much as behaviour.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code list for the other person element of the non-parental care question, and the registry shows it as the last of the six parallel columns.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'other (includes friend or neighbour)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so its role as the residual category and its code list were both missing.

value_domain: AEDC playgroup attendance indicator (yes/no/don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4
variable_description: Whether the child attended a playgroup at any point in the years before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. Its reference window is deliberately wider than the rest of the E block: E2Y and the E3 columns ask about the single year before school, while this one asks about "the years before entering full time school". The dictionary records that it was introduced in the 2012 cycle and renamed from E3b in 2015, so its name in older AEDC extracts is not E4.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4
value_definition: A two-digit integer with three codes: 0 for no, 1 for yes, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It records attendance ever, not how often or for how long, so a single visit and three years of weekly sessions are the same value. It also does not identify the type of playgroup, so supported and intensive playgroups aimed at families with additional needs cannot be separated from ordinary community ones.
rationale: The dictionary publishes E4 with the playgroup instrument text, the 0/1/88 code list, the 2012 introduction and the 2015 rename from E3b, matching the registry's own description of the column.
evidence_quote: To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended playgroup in the years before entering full time school
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question wording alone with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no warning that the same concept appears as E3b in pre-2015 documentation.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5
variable_description: The teacher's rating of how well the child is settling into school, asked as whether the child "is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school". It is one of three closing instrument questions, with E6 on parental engagement and E7 on reading at home, all sharing the same three-point scale. None of the three feed the five AEDC domain scores, so this column is an independent read on school transition rather than a component of the developmental measures.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is one teacher's global impression at a single point in the child's first school year, not a validated scale, so it cannot be treated as an outcome measure comparable to a domain score. The three points are ordinal and unequally spaced, so averaging them across a school or community produces a number with no defined unit.
rationale: The dictionary gives E5's instrument text, its purpose and its four-code value list, and section 3.1 sets out separately which items build the domain scores.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Child is adapting to school' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the three-point rating scale and the 88 don't-know code were undocumented.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6
variable_description: The teacher's rating of whether the child's parents or caregivers are actively engaged with the school in supporting the child's learning. It is the school-side view of family involvement, and it pairs with E7, which asks about reading at home, to give two crude proxies for the home learning environment. The dictionary records that it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, a filter that was only lifted in 2015.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: New South Wales children are missing for the first two cycles, so a national trend that ignores this treats a coverage change as a real change in parental engagement. The rating also measures engagement visible to the school, so families who support learning at home without contacting the school score low on something they are doing.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the four-code list, and an explicit note that the item was not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 with the filter revised in 2015.
evidence_quote: Not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1/2
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Parents actively engaged with the school' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and omitted the New South Wales coverage gap that makes early-cycle national estimates wrong.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7
variable_description: The teacher's rating of whether the child is regularly read to, or encouraged in reading, at home. The question wording ends "as far as you can tell", which flags on the instrument itself that the teacher is inferring a home behaviour rather than observing it. Like E6, it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, and the same three-point scale is used for both.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is a teacher's inference about the household, so it will partly track how much contact the family has with the school rather than what happens at home. Reading in a language other than English is not asked about separately, so a home rich in reading in another language can be rated as not true.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the instrument text including the 'as far as you can tell' qualifier, the four-code value list, and the New South Wales coverage note for Cycles 1 and 2.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is regularly read to/encouraged in his/her reading at home as far as you can tell
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Child is regularly read to at home' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the second-hand nature of the report nor the coverage gap was recorded.

value_domain: AEDC domain score, zero to ten
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: The child's score on emotional maturity, one of the five AEDC developmental domains, built from the teacher's answers to the emotional maturity items on the instrument. The dictionary states that for each domain "children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development", and that a score is only produced where at least 75 per cent of the domain's items were completed. EMOT_1 to EMOT_4 on the same row break it into prosocial and helping behaviour, anxious and fearful behaviour, aggressive behaviour, and hyperactive and inattentive behaviour, while EMOTCATEGORY converts the score into the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A continuous numeric value from 0 to 10, stored with four decimal places. Higher is better, so the anxious, aggressive and hyperactive sub-domains are reverse scored before the domain score is formed.
limitation: The score cannot be reproduced from the item responses: the dictionary states the calculation methodologies are licensed from the Offord Centre for Child Studies and "are not available to the public". It is also a population measure, and the dictionary warns that AEDC indicators "have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children", so a single child's score is not a clinical result.
rationale: The dictionary defines EMOT as the derived emotional maturity domain score with a 7.4 numeric format, and section 3.1 gives the zero to ten range, the 75 per cent completion rule, the licensing of the calculation and the population-level caveat.
evidence_quote: For each of the five AEDC domains, children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Emotional maturity' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both value definition and limitation, so it did not even give the range of the score.

value_domain: aedc_edi_score_0_10 (numeric, 0 to 10 inclusive, 4 decimal places; higher = higher development)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education (sections 3.1, 15, 16) and AEDC Data Guidelines 2025, Australian Government Department of Education
variable_description: The child's sub-domain score for prosocial and helping behaviour, one of four sub-domains under the emotional maturity domain. The 2025 AEDC Data Dictionary records the element as "Prosocial and helping behaviour" and marks its source as derived, so it is computed from the teacher's instrument answers rather than asked as a single question. EMOT_1_VULN on the same record is the vulnerability cut-off applied to this score.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), section 16 AEDC Sub-Domain Variables
value_definition: A number in a 7.4 numeric field, so up to four decimal places, on the same zero to ten scale the AEDC uses for its five domain scores, where higher means more developed.
limitation: The scoring formula is licensed from the Offord Centre at McMaster University and, in the AEDC's words, is "not available to the public", so the score cannot be rebuilt or checked from the instrument items on the same record. Its four decimal places therefore give precision, not transparency.
rationale: The Prosocial and helping behaviour sub-domain score is stored in the same numeric 7.4 field as the five AEDC domain scores, and the AEDC publishes the domain-score scale as zero to ten; the sub-domain scale is inferred to be the same, but the AEDC never states it for sub-domains.
evidence_quote: children receive a score between zero and ten
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review needed the licensed McMaster scoring formula. The formula stays proprietary, but the scale the score sits on is documented and is enough to give the column a defensible domain.

values: ["0: Not Developmentally Vulnerable","1: Developmentally Vulnerable"]

variable_description: Whether the child fell below the vulnerability cut-off on the prosocial and helping behaviour sub-domain. The 2025 AEDC Data Dictionary gives the purpose as "Indicates the child's developmentally vulnerable status in regards to pro-social and helping behaviour", derived by applying a cut-off to EMOT_1. AEDC cut-offs are set from the 2009 baseline collection and held fixed since, so the flag compares the child against 2009 rather than against their own cohort.

value_definition: A one-digit integer with two published values, 0 for Not Developmentally Vulnerable and 1 for Developmentally Vulnerable.
limitation: It is a threshold, not a measurement: two children a fraction apart on EMOT_1 can land on opposite sides of it. The AEDC also does not calculate developmental categories for children diagnosed with special needs or aged under four, so the flag is not populated for every child and an empty value is a different thing from a 0.
rationale: The 2025 Data Dictionary gives every sub-domain _Vuln variable a 1-digit integer field with exactly two published values; this field is the pro-social and helping behaviour sub-domain flag.

limitation: Vulnerability on this sub-domain does not put the child in the published vulnerable count, which is built from the five domain scores. Summing sub-domain flags will therefore not reproduce DV1 or DV2, and the AEDC does not treat sub-domain flags as reportable indicators at all.

value_domain: AEDC domain percentile category (four bands)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Which of four percentile bands the child's emotional maturity score falls into, where band 1 is the AEDC definition of developmentally vulnerable on this domain. The bands are 0 to 10th, 11th to 25th, 26th to 50th and 51st to 100th percentile, so band 1 is vulnerable, band 2 is at risk and bands 3 and 4 are on track. The cut-offs are fixed against the 2009 national collection: the dictionary states they "have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared".
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th. The percentile positions are those of the 2009 baseline distribution, adjusted for age variation across children in their first year of school.
limitation: The bands do not describe the current cohort, so a 12 per cent vulnerable rate in 2021 means 12 per cent scored below the 2009 tenth percentile, not that 12 per cent were in the bottom decile of 2021. The dictionary also states that domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs or aged under four, so their category is absent rather than high.
rationale: The dictionary gives EMOTCategory's four-band value list and section 3.1 explains that the cut-offs are anchored to the 2009 baseline and are not calculated for special needs children or children under four.
evidence_quote: The cut-off scores used in 2009 have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Vulnerable - emotional maturity' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which implied a yes/no flag when the column is in fact a four-band percentile grouping anchored to 2009.

value_domain: AEDC domain validity flag (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child's emotional maturity result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. The dictionary defines a 1 as "Child does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain", so a single flag folds three separate exclusions together. There is one of these per domain, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of the five a child is valid on.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for this domain; 1 otherwise.
limitation: A 0 does not tell you which of the three reasons applied, so it cannot be used to identify children with special needs or to measure teacher non-response. It is also domain specific, so a child can be valid on physical health and invalid on emotional maturity, and dropping every row with any invalid flag discards usable results on the other domains.
rationale: The dictionary gives the exact two-value list for EMOTValid, naming the three exclusion reasons that collapse into the 0 code, and documents the parallel per-domain flags and the VALIDDOMAINS counter.
evidence_quote: Child has special needs status, is 3 years old or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Valid - emotional maturity' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that special needs status and age three are folded into the same 0 as item non-response.

value_domain: AEDC English as a second language indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the teacher considers the child to have English as a second language, asked on the instrument as "Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)". It is one of three overlapping language columns and the most subjective: LANG asks whether a language other than English is spoken at home, and LBOTE is derived rather than asked. B1, the rating of the child's ability to use English effectively, sits alongside it and is the closer measure of proficiency.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes.
limitation: It is a teacher's classification, not a test, and it carries no threshold, so it varies with how each jurisdiction and school uses the label. A child can be ESL with fluent conversational English, and an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander child speaking Aboriginal English or Kriol may or may not be flagged depending on local practice, so an ESL rate cannot be read as an English proficiency rate.
rationale: The dictionary publishes ESL as an instrument item with its exact question wording and a 0/1 value list, and documents Lang, LBOTE and B1 as the separate language variables it is often confused with.
evidence_quote: Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'ESL (english as a second language)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it restated the acronym and never distinguished the column from LANG or LBOTE.

value_domain: AEDC child sex or gender code
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: The child's sex or gender as recorded through the school enrolment process and carried onto the AEDC instrument. The dictionary describes the data element as "The sex of the child" while giving its purpose as identifying the child's gender, which reflects a change made in 2024 when the instrument item was relabelled from sex to gender and expanded beyond a binary. The absence of a non-binary value in the 2009 to 2021 cycles is a property of the collection instrument of the day, not evidence about the children.

variable_description: Whether the teacher relied on their own observation of the child, or on knowing the child, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the only option in the LANGSOURCE set that involves no third party, so it marks answers based purely on classroom judgement. In practice a teacher who does not speak the home language is judging communication in a language they cannot assess.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. Only 2 means the source was used.
limitation: It carries no measure of how well the teacher knows the child or the language, so it cannot be used to grade the reliability of the CANCOM answer, only to note that no external source was consulted. It also does not indicate that the teacher observed the child speaking the language, merely that the teacher's own knowledge was the basis for the answer.
rationale: The dictionary gives LangSource2's instrument text and its purpose of identifying the sources used for CanCom, together with the shared Lang filter and 0/1/2 value list.
evidence_quote: Indicate the sources of information used to provide your answer to CanCom (select all that apply)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the option label 'Own observation or knowing child' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not connect it to the CANCOM question it qualifies.

LANGSOURCE5, held in the Indigenous table, is the parallel option for an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. Only 2 means the source was used.
limitation: The staff member's role is not recorded, so a bilingual education assistant and an office administrator both produce the same value and no inference about language expertise is available. It also overlaps in practice with LANGSOURCE5, so counting the two together will double count consultations with a staff member who is also the cultural consultant.
rationale: The dictionary lists LangSource3 as the other staff member option in the CanCom source set, with the same filter and the same 0/1/2 value list, and lists LangSource5 as the separate cultural consultant option.
evidence_quote: Other staff member
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Other staff member' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it gave no context at all about which answer the source supports.

evidence_quote: Other sources

value_domain: aedc_language_codeframe_ascl_non_indigenous
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables (accompanying workbook), Australian Government Department of Education, Table 1.1 AEDC Language Codeframe (based on the ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages), non-Indigenous branch; sentinel from AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education
variable_description: The one language other than English the child most often speaks at home, in the AEDC language table. The AEDC Data Dictionary gives the instrument wording as "If the child speaks a language other than English at home, please indicate the language spoken most often" and instructs that the field is answered only where LANG = Yes. CANCOM beside it records whether the child can adequately communicate in that language, and the LANGSOURCE flags record who told the teacher.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025) and AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables
value_definition: A four-digit integer from the AEDC Language Codeframe published as Table 1.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, which is based on the ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages and holds 445 codes, 223 of them outside the Australian Indigenous Languages branch. The sentinel -1 records that the Indigenous language field was used instead.
limitation: An empty cell is not a monolingual English speaker: the whole language block is gated on LANG, so a child who was never asked looks the same as a child with no other language. The teacher, not the family, identifies the language, and only the most-used language is recorded here, with any others going to OTHERLANGUAGEID1 to OTHERLANGUAGEID4.
rationale: The main language other than english spoken at home is coded to the AEDC Language Codeframe, a 4-digit ASCL-based list of 442 languages published in the AEDC reference tables; the non-Indigenous branch holds 223 codes, and the dictionary adds -1 when the traditional-language field was used instead. The fplida bundle already carries an ASCL list at inst/extdata/codeframes/ascl_language.tsv. Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review said no AEDC language reference table was linked. The AEDC publishes the full language codeframe with the data dictionary.

value_domain: AEDC language background other than English indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the child has a language background other than English, derived by the AEDC rather than asked of the teacher. It is the third and broadest of the AEDC language flags, and the dictionary prints the rule that builds it: "Children are considered 'LBOTE' if they speak a language other than English at home, or if they speak English at home but are still considered to have ESL (English as a second language) status." It is therefore the union of LANG and ESL, which is why it is always at least as large as either one on its own. The dictionary lists it among the variables whose names, descriptions or notes were corrected in the 2024 revision, so its published definition is not identical across dictionary versions.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes, with the source given as derived rather than instrument. It equals 1 where LANG is 1 or ESL is 1.
limitation: Because it is the union of two flags it cannot be read as either one: an LBOTE rate counts children who speak only English at home but are classed ESL by the teacher, so it inherits the subjectivity of the ESL judgement. Language background is also not proficiency, so an LBOTE rate is not a measure of how many children need English language support.
rationale: The dictionary gives LBOTE as a derived 0/1 indicator distinct from the instrument-collected Lang and ESL items, and names it in the version 7.0 list of variables whose descriptions were corrected.
evidence_quote: To indicate if the child has a Language Background Other Than English (LBOTE).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the acronym as 'LBOTE indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither expanded the abbreviation nor recorded that the column is derived rather than reported.

value_domain: count_integer (integer count, 0 to 99999 (ABS Estimated Resident Population of the AEDC Local Community))
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The estimated resident population of the AEDC local community the child lives in, repeated on every child in that community. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the field as the "ABS Estimated Residential Population of the AEDC Local Community", while its variable list labels the same field the local community ERP of 5 year olds. It is the denominator behind the LCPUBLIC rule that compares the count of children with instruments against the community's ERP.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025)
value_definition: A five-digit integer count of people, right justified, with no code list and no reference date stored beside it.
limitation: Summing it across children multiplies one community's population by the number of children living there, so it is a contextual attribute rather than a countable quantity. The dictionary's two entries also disagree on whose population it is, the whole local community or five year olds, so check the observed magnitudes before using it as a denominator.
rationale: The dictionary defines LCABSERP as a 5-digit integer holding the ABS Estimated Resident Population of the local community, so it is a population count rather than a code.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review wanted the linked ABS aggregate. The exact numbers are not public, but the field's numeric domain (a 5-digit population count) is, which is enough to type the column.

value_domain: percentage_0_100 (numeric percentage, 0 to 100, 2 decimal places)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: How much of the child's AEDC local community had moved house in the previous year, as an ABS-derived community characteristic. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines it as the "Proportion of persons in the local community who lived at a different address one year ago (%)", and it is one of five community context measures that also cover year 12 completion, unemployment, young single parents and SEIFA.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025)
value_definition: A percentage from 0 to 100 held in a 6.2 numeric field, so two decimal places, with no code list.
limitation: It measures churn around the child, not the child's own moving. A child who has lived at one address since birth carries a high value if the surrounding suburb turns over, and a settled child in a settled community cannot be told apart from a recent arrival there. The figure comes from an ABS collection for the community rather than from the AEDC instrument, and the row does not record which collection year it was drawn from.
rationale: The dictionary defines the field as the proportion (%) of persons in the local community who lived at a different address one year ago and gives it a 6.2 numeric format, so it is a percentage on 0 to 100, not a code.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review typed the column as missing because the underlying Census aggregate is not bundled. The field is a percentage, and its numeric domain is published.

variable_description: The socio-economic quintile of the child's AEDC local community, with quintile 1 the most disadvantaged. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the field as "An ordinal grouping variable for the SEIFA score of the AEDC Local Community", which is the continuous LCABSSEIFASCORE column collapsed into fifths. It answers a question about the community, where SEIFACATEGORY, SEIFADECILE and SEIFAScore answer the same question for the SA1 the child lives in.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025)

value_domain: ABS SEIFA Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage score
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 4.2 SEIFA and section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The ABS socio-economic index score for the AEDC Local Community the child lives in, used as the standard area measure of disadvantage in AEDC analysis. The dictionary is explicit about which index: "In AEDC, we use the Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (IRSD)". The Census vintage behind the score changes by cycle, being 2006 for the 2009 collection, 2011 for 2012 and 2015, 2016 for 2018 and 2021 for the 2021 and 2024 collections. LCABSSEIFACATEGORY beside it groups the same score into ordinal bands.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 4.2 SEIFA and section 12 Local Community Based Geography
value_definition: A numeric value stored with four decimal places, on the ABS IRSD scale that is standardised to a national mean near 1000. Where a local community spans more than one SEIFA area, the score is a population-weighted average of the component scores.
limitation: It describes an area, not a family, so using it as a child-level measure of household disadvantage is an ecological inference and will understate the spread within a community. The IRSD also measures disadvantage only, and the ABS warns it is not a measure of advantage, so a high score means an absence of disadvantage rather than affluence; and because the Census vintage changes between cycles, part of any movement in the score is a change of index rather than a change of the place.
rationale: The dictionary names the specific SEIFA index the AEDC uses, prints the cycle-by-cycle table of SEIFA vintages for local community scores, and explains the population-weighted recalculation used where boundaries split.
evidence_quote: In AEDC, we use the Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (IRSD).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local community seifa score' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say which of the four SEIFA indexes was used, nor that the vintage differs by collection cycle.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The unemployment rate of the child's AEDC local community, attached to the child's record as area context. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the field as the "Proportion of the labour force unemployed in the local community (%)", so the denominator is the labour force rather than the whole adult population. It travels with LCABSSEIFACATEGORY, which grades the same community on socio-economic disadvantage.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025)
value_definition: A percentage from 0 to 100 in a 6.2 numeric field. The base is the community's labour force, which excludes people who are neither working nor looking for work.
limitation: It is not a statement about the child's household: neither parent's employment can be inferred from it, and PARENT1OCCUP and PARENT2OCCUP record what the parents do rather than whether they have work. Because the base is the labour force, a community where few people seek work can show low unemployment and low employment at the same time.
rationale: The dictionary defines the field as the proportion (%) of the labour force unemployed in the local community and gives it a 6.2 numeric format, so it is a percentage on 0 to 100, not a code.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review typed the column as missing because the underlying Census aggregate is not bundled. The field is a percentage, and its numeric domain is published.

value_domain: remoteness_category_code
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education (LCARIACode field format)
variable_description: The remoteness of the child's AEDC local community, held as a short accessibility code. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines it as "The Accessibility and Remoteness Index of Australia (ARIA) code of the AEDC Local Community", stored as four characters of left-justified text, and pairs it with LCARIANAME, which spells the same category out.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025)
value_definition: A short text code, up to four characters, standing one-to-one for an ARIA remoteness category of the local community. The AEDC publishes no value list for this field, so the codes on it are inferred from the categories LCARIANAME enumerates rather than lifted from a table.
limitation: ARIA is not the ASGS Remoteness Structure that REMOTENESSCODE and REMOTENESS carry, and the two can disagree for the same child because one indexes the local community and the other the child's own statistical area. Because the codes are unpublished, treat an unfamiliar value as a category you have not identified rather than as an error.
rationale: No AEDC document publishes the LCARIACode value list; the dictionary gives only a 4-character left-justified text field, so the guess is a short code paired one-to-one with the five ARIA remoteness categories in LCARIAName.

value_domain: remoteness_category_name
values: ["Major Cities of Australia","Inner Regional Australia","Outer Regional Australia","Remote Australia","Very Remote Australia"]
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables (accompanying workbook), Australian Government Department of Education, Table 3.3 ASGS - Remoteness Structure
variable_description: The remoteness category of the child's AEDC local community, written out rather than coded. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines it as "The Accessibility and Remoteness Index of Australia (ARIA) category of the AEDC Local Community" and gives it a 25-character text field, which is exactly the width of Major Cities of Australia.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Education, AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025)
value_definition: A text label naming one remoteness category, up to 25 characters. The AEDC publishes no value list, so the five names carried here follow the remoteness categories in Table 3.3 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables; the ARIA+ accessibility labels are the other candidate wording.
limitation: Grouping on the string is fragile: the AEDC has never published the exact labels, so the wording can differ between cycles and an abbreviation would be indistinguishable from a new category. Because it describes the local community rather than the child's address, it should not be used to place an individual child in a remote area.
rationale: The dictionary gives LCARIAName no value list, only a 25-character text field; the AEDC's own remoteness category names (Table 3.3) are the natural fit and 'Major Cities of Australia' is exactly 25 characters, but the AEDC may instead use the ARIA+ accessibility labels (Highly Accessible, Accessible, Moderately Accessible, Remote, Very Remote). The source's 'Not available' category is dropped so this column enumerates exactly the categories LCARIACODE codes; absence is carried as typed missing instead.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review found no exact codeframe, which is right; a five-category remoteness domain is nonetheless defensible from the field length and the AEDC's published remoteness naming.

value_domain: ABS local government area code (local community based)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The local government area associated with the AEDC Local Community the child lives in, as distinct from the LGA the child's own address falls in. The dictionary keeps two parallel geography blocks for exactly this reason: the child based block holds LGACODE, and the local community based block holds this column. It was introduced in the 2012 cycle, and LCLGANAME beside it carries the readable label.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
value_definition: A five-digit integer on the ABS local government area classification for the edition in force in the cycle, attached to the local community rather than to the child.
limitation: AEDC Local Community boundaries are built on ABS statistical areas, not on council boundaries, so a local community can straddle two councils and this column then names only the one it is associated with. Using it in place of LGACODE therefore assigns some children to a council area they do not live in.
rationale: The dictionary defines LCLGACode as the local government area code associated with the Local Community, in a section separate from the child based LGACode, and section 4.1 explains that local community boundaries are aligned to SA1 building blocks.
evidence_quote: Local Government Area code associated with the Local Community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Local community lga code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the column from the child based LGACODE, which is the confusion that matters.

value_domain: ABS local government area name (local community based)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The written name of the local government area associated with the child's AEDC Local Community, the label for LCLGACODE. It is held in a longer field than the child based LGANAME, at forty characters against thirty, so the two columns can render the same council differently. It was introduced with LCLGACODE in the 2012 cycle.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography

Council names are also not unique across states, so a national join on name alone merges unrelated areas.
rationale: The dictionary gives LCLGAName as a 40-character text field paired with LCLGACode in the local community geography section, and gives LGAName a 30-character field in the child based section, which establishes the differing field widths.
evidence_quote: Local Government Area name associated with the Local Community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local community lga name' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, offering no field length and no reason to prefer the code as a join key.
