value_domain: PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation
variable_description: The person key that ties a child's AEDC record to the rest of PLIDA, and the reason the collection is in this asset at all. Within AEDC it joins the five tables of a cycle, so a child's core record, domain scores, instrument background, language detail and special needs detail assemble on this column; across the asset it is the same key the Census, births, MBS, PBS, DOMINO and the tax products carry, so an AvEDI result can be read against a child's birth record, health history or family's payment history. ABS lists the AEDC among PLIDA's linked sources, naming the 2009, 2012, 2015 and 2018 collections on its data page while this asset carries six cycles, and the linkage is performed centrally against the person linkage spine rather than by matching names in this file.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned for linkage with no meaning in its digits. It is not a student number, an enrolment identifier or an AEDC instrument identifier, so it can be matched but not decoded.
limitation: A child appears here only where their AvEDI record linked to the spine, and children who did not link are missing rather than untested, so AEDC coverage in PLIDA is lower than AEDC coverage in the national collection and the shortfall should not be assumed random. The key is also for the child, not the class or the family: TEACHERID and SCHOOLID group the record, and no parent or sibling identifier is carried, so a family cannot be assembled from this column alone.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA data page lists the Australian Early Development Census among the datasets brought into the asset and describes the central linkage of person records, which is what this column carries; the custodian description in the PLIDA data item list names it as the synthetic person identifier used across products.
evidence_quote: Australian Early Development Census, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018 - Measures how well children in their first year of full time school are developing across 5 important domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 30 occurrences it never said that this is the column joining the five AEDC tables to each other and the AEDC to the rest of PLIDA, nor that linkage failure, not absence of assessment, explains a missing child.

value_domain: Teacher Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status (three values)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI
variable_description: Whether the teacher who completed the instrument identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, asked directly as "Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent". It sits in the instrument background table with the CONSULTTYPE items about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural consultants, and the point of the block is to describe who did the assessing rather than who was assessed. It is the column to use when testing whether teacher background is associated with reported outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, whose own status is on ATSI in the core table.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three values: 0 the teacher was not Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, 1 the teacher was, and 2 the teacher responded inconsistently to their own Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status.
limitation: It describes the teacher, not the child, so it cannot stand in for the child's Indigenous status anywhere. Code 2 is also a data quality state rather than a third identity: it marks contradictory answers within the teacher's own record, so quietly dropping it or folding it into 0 shifts the measured share of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander teachers in an unknown direction.
rationale: The dictionary's TeacherATSI entry gives the origin definition, the instrument wording and all three labelled values, including the inconsistent-response code.
evidence_quote: Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Indigenous teacher' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it read as a yes-or-no flag and hid the third code for inconsistent responses.

value_domain: AEDC teacher identifier (de-identified)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID
variable_description: Which teacher filled in the instrument for this child, as a de-identified number. The dictionary describes it as a "unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information", and its analytic value is as the clustering unit: every AvEDI score is one teacher's judgement of one child, so children sharing a value here share a rater and their scores are not independent observations. SCHOOLID nests these teachers within schools, and CLASSTYPEA_1, CLASSTYPEB and CLASSTYPEC describe the class the teacher was reporting on.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID
value_definition: A right-justified integer, allocated for the collection and carrying no information about the teacher. The dictionary's variable page gives it a length of 11, while its appendix metadata shows the narrower format F6.0.
limitation: It is not a person key on the PLIDA spine, so a teacher cannot be joined to their own tax, payment or health records the way a child can through SYNTHETIC_AEUID; nothing about the teacher beyond TEACHERATSI is available. The dictionary also does not state that the code is stable between collections, so it should not be used to follow one teacher from 2009 to a later cycle.
rationale: The dictionary's TeacherID entry defines the code as unique and non-identifying and gives its integer format; the registry shows the field beside SCHOOLID and the class-type items that make it a clustering variable.
evidence_quote: The Teacher ID uses a unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Teacher identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never told a reader that this is the rater key their standard errors should account for, or that it does not reach the PLIDA spine.

value_domain: Time in class under one month, with completion intent (three values)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch
variable_description: Whether the child had been in class for less than one month when the instrument was started, and if so whether the teacher went on to fill it in anyway. The dictionary's reason for asking is that "If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC", and the teacher may then stop. This is why a row can exist with almost nothing on it: a value of 1 here is the explanation for empty domain scores and empty instrument items, and CANASSESS, asked only when this is a yes, records whether the teacher felt able to assess the child at all.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three values: 0 no, 1 yes and skip the rest of the instrument, and 2 yes but the rest of the instrument will be completed.
limitation: The instrument asks about time in this class while the dictionary's description speaks of time at school, so a child who transferred in October after a full year elsewhere may be coded the same as a child who started school that month. It is also not a data quality flag on the responses that follow: a 1 means there are no responses to judge, while a 2 means the teacher went ahead on under a month's acquaintance and the scores stand in the file unmarked.
rationale: The dictionary's Tmsch entry gives the rationale, the instrument wording and all three values, including the distinction between skipping and completing the rest of the instrument, and records CanAssess as the follow-up item.
evidence_quote: If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'In school for less than one month' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it read as a yes-or-no flag and never explained that one of its two yes values means the rest of the row was deliberately left blank.

value_domain: Count of missing domain scales (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss
variable_description: How many of the five AEDC scales could not be calculated for this child, defined by the dictionary as the "Total number of missing scales (0-5)". It is the sum of the five per-scale missing flags PHMiss, SCMiss, EMMiss, LCMiss and CGMiss, which the dictionary restricts to the master unit record file and which are not carried in the AEDC tables in this asset, so this count is the only summary of scale-level missingness available here. A scale goes missing when fewer than 75 per cent of that domain's instrument items were answered.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5, one unit for each of physical health and wellbeing, social competence, emotional maturity, language and cognitive skills, and communication and general knowledge.
limitation: It does not say which scales are missing, so a value of 2 needs the five domain score columns checked one by one before an analysis can decide whether the loss matters. It is also not the complement of VALIDDOMAINS: a scale can be computed and still be ruled invalid because the child has special needs status or is three years old, so the two columns need not add to five.
rationale: The dictionary's TotalMiss entry gives the definition, the purpose and the 0 to 5 integer format, and the five per-scale flags immediately before it in the same section show what is being counted and that they are master-file-only fields.
evidence_quote: Total number of missing scales (0-5).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Total number of missing scales (0-5)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no hint that the per-scale flags behind the count are absent from this asset.

value_domain: Count of valid domain scores (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains
variable_description: How many of the five AEDC domains yielded a usable score for this child, which the dictionary gives as being "To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid". It is the total of the five per-domain flags PHYSVALID, SOCVALID, EMOTVALID, LANGCOGVALID and COMGENVALID, and it is the input to the reporting rule: children with fewer than four valid domains are the ones VALIDINSTRUMENT marks as not counting. Use it as the first filter on any analysis of domain scores, ahead of the individual flags.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5. The dictionary publishes no value labels because the number is simply the count of domains for which the validity conditions were met.
limitation: A 0 does not mean an empty instrument. Children with special needs status have no valid domain scores by rule, so they sit at 0 while their teacher may have answered every question, and reading this column as a response-quality measure conflates an administrative exclusion with missing data. It also does not say which domains survived, so a study of one domain still has to read that domain's own validity flag.
rationale: The dictionary's ValidDomains entry gives the purpose and the one-digit integer format, and the domain validity entries beside it define the conditions being counted, including the special needs and age exclusions.
evidence_quote: To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Valid domains' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not give the range, did not say what makes a domain valid, and did not connect the column to the coverage rule it feeds.

value_domain: AEDC valid instrument flag (0 or 1)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidInstrument
variable_description: Whether this child's completed instrument counts as valid for AEDC reporting, set from the number of domains that produced a score. The dictionary states the purpose as "To identify children with less than 4 valid domain scores for the purpose of calculating the 80 per cent Coverage Rule", the rule requiring that 80 per cent of the children in an area hold valid instruments before results for that area may be published. The AEDC Data Guidelines set out the arithmetic: divide the count of records with VALIDINSTRUMENT = 1 by the count with SPECIALNEEDS = 0. The dictionary records that the field was called ValidChecklist before the 2015 collection.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidInstrument
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 0 for no and 1 for yes, derived from VALIDDOMAINS with the threshold at four of the five domains.
limitation: A 0 is not a verdict on the teacher's answers. A child with special needs status has no valid domain scores by rule and therefore fails the four-domain test while holding a fully answered instrument, which is exactly why the coverage rule counts only children with SPECIALNEEDS = 0 in its denominator. The flag also governs whether an area may be reported, not whether an individual record may be used, so filtering child-level analysis on it discards children for a reason that belongs to their area's publication test.
rationale: The dictionary's ValidInstrument entry gives the purpose, the two-value code frame and the 2015 rename, and the AEDC Data Guidelines give the 80 per cent coverage rule and the exact numerator and denominator this flag is used in.
evidence_quote: To identify children with less than 4 valid domain scores for the purpose of calculating the 80 per cent Coverage Rule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Valid instrument indicator' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it named neither the four-domain threshold, nor the coverage rule the flag exists to serve, nor the earlier name of the field.

value_domain: AEDC collection year (four-digit)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Year
variable_description: The collection year of the AEDC cycle the row belongs to, defined by the dictionary as "The year in which the AvEDI was completed". Because the instrument is completed in the child's first year of full-time school, it is also, near enough, the year the child started school, which is what makes it the anchor for any before-and-after design built on an AEDC record. The AEDC products are split by cycle, so the column is near-constant within each table, and CYCLE carries the same collection numbered 1 to 6; the two differ only for Cycle 1, which the dictionary records as covering both 2009 and 2010.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Year
value_definition: A four-digit integer. The collection years are 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024, matching the six cycle tables in this asset, and the dictionary notes that Cycle 1 also takes in a 2010 follow-up collection, so a value of 2010 can occur in the first cycle.
limitation: It is not the date the instrument was filled in; MOC holds the month, which runs April to August, so events within a school year cannot be ordered against an AEDC record from this column alone. Nor is it a birth cohort: children in one collection year run across the AEDC age categories from under five years to over six years, and AGEINMONTHS or AGECAT is needed before an age comparison means anything.
rationale: The dictionary's Year entry gives the definition and the four-digit integer format, the Cycle entry beside it confirms the six numbered collections, and the MOC entry gives the April to August completion window that this column does not carry.
evidence_quote: The year in which the AvEDI was completed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Year that the information relates to' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 30 occurrences it never said that only six values occur or that the column is fixed within each cycle table.

value_domain: Age group at AMEP registration
value_source: ACIL Allen Consulting, AMEP Evaluation, final report to the Department of Education and Training, 22 May 2015
variable_description: The client's age band on the day they registered with an AMEP provider, not their age at arrival, at visa grant or at any class. The gap matters because registration and tuition are separate steps: the AMEP evaluation records that "For clients 18 years and older, registration with the AMEP must occur within six months of arrival in Australia and classes must commence within 12 months." So a client can be a year older than this band by the time the first tuition hours appear in the AMEP quarterly columns. The band sits on the treated client profile row beside REGISTRATION_DATE, YEAR_OF_BIRTH and MONTH_OF_BIRTH, which together give exact age at any later event.
description_source: ACIL Allen Consulting, AMEP Evaluation, final report to the Department of Education and Training, 22 May 2015
value_definition: A grouped age label rather than completed years, fixed once at the registration date. The band boundaries are the department's own reporting groups and the PLIDA item list does not publish them, so the width of the youngest and oldest groups is unknown.
limitation: It does not age with the file. A client placed in a young band when they registered in 2004 was well into middle age by the 2019 quarterly hours columns, so using this field as an age control across the tuition panel can misdate a person by more than a decade. It also cannot stand in for age at eligibility, since the program admits people aged 18 and over with a separate pathway for 15 to 17 year olds, and a band cannot separate those two groups.
rationale: The evaluation commissioned by the AMEP's own department sets out the registration step, its timing relative to arrival and the start of classes, and the adult eligibility rule, which is what distinguishes this field from an age at arrival or an age at first class.
evidence_quote: For clients 18 years and older, registration with the AMEP must occur within six months of arrival in Australia and classes must commence within 12 months.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Client age group at time of registration with AMEP', with the domain guessed from the variable name as 'Age in completed years (inferred)', which is the wrong shape for a banded field, and with the inference warning printed as the limitation.

value_domain: ARMS client identifier
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
variable_description: The client number the program's own case system gave this person, and the key that joins the six AMEP tables to each other. ARMS is the AMEP Reporting and Management System, described in the accreditation manual for the program as the source the department monitors outcomes from: "NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS)." It therefore travels with registration, hours, English proficiency, CSWE awards and address for the same client, while SYNTHETIC_AEUID is the separate column that reaches the PLIDA spine.
description_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
value_definition: An opaque identifier minted in ARMS, one value per program client, with no published format and no meaning carried in its characters. It repeats for the same client across the hours, client profile, CSWE award, English proficiency and address tables, and appears in no other PLIDA dataset.
limitation: It reaches nothing outside the program. A client's Centrelink, tax, Census or health records are found through SYNTHETIC_AEUID, not through this number, so it cannot be used as a person key for the asset. It is also not the only ARMS client number on the AMEP tables: amep_englishproficiency carries a second one, CLNT_ID, which the custodian describes as the identifier used to report competency achievements, so the two columns should not be joined as though they were interchangeable without first checking that they agree.
rationale: The accreditation manual names ARMS in full and establishes it as the departmental system that holds client and outcome data for the program, which is what identifies the numbering behind this column.
evidence_quote: NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's phrase about an ID generated in the ARMS database and the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, so it never said what ARMS is, which tables the key joins, or that a second ARMS client number exists on the same asset.

value_domain: Date the case system flagged the client as exited from the program
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
variable_description: The day the program's case system, ARMS, recorded this client as having left the Adult Migrant English Program. The word flagged is doing work: the exit is a status a provider or the system set in the AMEP Reporting and Management System, not an event the client reported. It sits beside ENTITLEMENT_END_DATE on the same client profile row, and the two answer different questions, one being when the department closed the client and the other being when the tuition entitlement lapses whether or not the client ever attended.
description_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
value_definition: A calendar date with an open domain, bounded below by the earliest program registration in the collection and above by the extract day carried in DATE_EXTRACTED. One value per client, held on the client profile table rather than on an episode row.
limitation: It does not date the end of study. A client who simply stops coming is flagged when the provider or the system gets to it, so the gap between the last quarter with hours in amep_clientshours_2011_19 and this date can run to several quarters. A client still on the books at extraction carries no date rather than a future one, so treating a missing value as censoring and a present value as an event will mix administrative tidying in with genuine exits.
rationale: The accreditation manual establishes ARMS as the departmental reporting and management system whose records the department, not the provider's teaching staff, uses to monitor the program, which is what makes this an administrative flag rather than a reported event.
evidence_quote: NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that this is the date a client exited from AMEP and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never distinguished the flag from the entitlement end date or warned about the lag behind the last hours.

The categories come from the AMEP Reporting and Management System that the department uses to monitor the program, so they are administrative reasons chosen by a provider, and the registry publishes no code list for them.
description_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
value_definition: A short categorical code drawn from the exit reasons the case system offers a provider. The classification is the department's own operational one; it is not the Australian Core Skills Framework and not any national training classification.
limitation: It is not an outcome. Using up the tuition entitlement, reaching the assessed level, moving interstate and never coming back are all exits, and this field will not separate a client who finished from one who gave up. rationale: The accreditation manual names ARMS as the departmental system behind program reporting and treats exit assessment results as a separate provider record, which is the distinction this column is most often read across.
evidence_quote: NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS).

value_domain: ARMS code for a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations

description_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
value_definition: A short code from a closed departmental list, resolvable only by joining amep_csweawardsrefcodes on the same column. rationale: The accreditation manual documents the certificates as the licensed curriculum whose assessment providers must moderate, which establishes what an award code stands for and how it is earned.
evidence_quote: annual assessment moderation as required under CSWE licensing
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording about an ARMS code following assessment with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never named the reference table that resolves the code or warned that an absent row is not a failed client.

value_domain: Date a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award was granted
value_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
variable_description: The date a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award was granted to this client, which the custodian records as the date of the assessment. There is one row per award in amep_csweawards, so a client with three certificates has three rows and a client with none has no row at all, and this is the only dated attainment anywhere on the AMEP tables. Assessment was a scheduled, moderated activity rather than a continuous one, the accreditation manual requiring that "External (cross-provider) CSWE moderation should be undertaken at least annually, and teachers kept informed of the results of assessment moderation."
description_source: National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations
value_definition: A calendar date with an open domain, bounded in practice by the program collection window that runs from 2003 to 2019. It dates the assessment that granted the award, not the enrolment, the course start or the course end.
limitation: It cannot date the learning. A certificate assessed in one quarter can rest on hours attended across several, and because moderation is annual and cross-provider the dates cluster into assessment rounds, so the interval between this date and a rise in the hours columns is scheduling as much as progress. Award rows also thin out after 1 July 2017, when new clients moved to Australian Core Skills Framework assessment, so a falling count of awards after that date understates attainment rather than measuring a decline in it.
rationale: The accreditation manual sets out the moderation regime governing when certificate assessments are held, which is what this date records and what makes it a scheduled rather than a continuous measure.
evidence_quote: External (cross-provider) CSWE moderation should be undertaken at least annually, and teachers kept informed of the results of assessment moderation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase about the date an award was granted with the generic no-value-list sentence in both the definition and the limitation slots, so it never said that the date is an assessment date pulled into moderation rounds.

value_domain: Summary text for a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course
value_source: Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019
variable_description: The longer summary of a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award, held once per AWARD_CODE in the reference table amep_csweawardsrefcodes. description_source: Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019

evidence_quote: re-accreditation to meet ASQA requirements in 2018 has seriously impoverished and distorted it
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording about a description of a CSWE award and used the generic no-value-list sentence for both fields, so it never said the row describes a course rather than a client or that the stored text can post-date the award.

value_domain: Count of children needing AMEP childcare
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program
variable_description: The number of the client's children who need an AMEP childcare place, recorded once on the client profile rather than per quarter. Home Affairs states that "People attending face to face classes can access free childcare for children under school age", so the count is of pre-school children whose care would let the parent attend class. It is a stated requirement captured at the client record, which is why it sits beside CHILD_CHILDCARE_CENTRE, the field that names each child and the centre they attended.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program
value_definition: A small non-negative integer counting children. There is no classification behind it: the value is a headcount taken from the client's own record in the AMEP Reporting and Management System, not a code list.
limitation: It is a requirement, not a placement. A client can record two children needing care and receive none, so this column cannot be used to count children actually in AMEP childcare; the quarterly CHILDCARE_YYYY_Qn hours are the only evidence care was taken up.
rationale: The Home Affairs program page states the childcare offer and its age limit, which is what the count is a count of.
evidence_quote: People attending face to face classes can access free childcare for children under school age.

value_domain: ARMS client identifier used for competency reporting
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The AMEP client number used to attach competency and assessment records to a person, carried on the English proficiency table beside AMET_CLNT_ID. The system that issues it is the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS), the provider-facing database in which service providers record attendance, progress and assessment. It is an administrative key of the program, not a PLIDA key: SYNTHETIC_AEUID is the column that links a client to the rest of the asset.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
value_definition: An opaque provider-system identifier issued by ARMS. It has no classification behind it and carries no information about the person; its only job is to tie the ACSF and ASLPR assessment columns on this table back to one client.
limitation: Do not assume it equals AMET_CLNT_ID, which sits on the same row. The item list distinguishes them precisely because the competency reporting stream used its own client number, so joining assessment records on the wrong one silently drops clients.
rationale: The evaluation names ARMS and describes it as the system in which providers record student progress and assessment against the ACSF, which is the reporting stream this identifier serves.
evidence_quote: Currently, providers continue to use ARMS, but must enter extra program data, including student attendance, student progress, child care attendance, and tuition streams into spreadsheets that must be submitted to the department.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and gave the generic 'no finite value list' sentence twice, so it never explained what ARMS is, why a second client number exists on this table, or that it is not the linking key.

value_domain: Country of birth of the AMEP client
value_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
variable_description: The country the AMEP client was born in, as held on their client profile in the program's own records. The evaluation reports that AMEP students come from 197 countries and speak 267 languages, so the field is spread thinly across a very large number of categories. Country of birth in PLIDA is normally carried on the ABS Standard Australian Classification of Countries, which has 255 country categories grouped into 27 minor groups and nine major groups.
description_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
value_definition: A country code or country name. Where the ABS classification applies, the base level is a four-digit country code such as 5101 Myanmar, aggregating to a two-digit minor group and a one-digit major group by geographic proximity.
limitation: Whether the codes on this column are ABS four-digit country codes or the department's own country list is not stated in the item list, so the codes should be checked in the environment before they are mapped; a mismatch shows up as a large residual rather than as an error.
rationale: The ABS publishes the classification that country of birth is normally coded to in PLIDA and gives its structure and code form, which is what a reader needs before using the column; the classification actually applied to this Home Affairs column is not published.
evidence_quote: The country level is the base level of the classification. There are 255 country categories including four residual ('not elsewhere classified') categories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry inferred a SACC domain from the variable name and printed the generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it asserted a classification without saying that the assertion was an inference to be checked.

value_domain: Year the CSWE course was accredited as a VET accredited course
value_source: Australian Skills Quality Authority, Course accreditation
variable_description: The year a Certificates in Spoken and Written English course was accredited as a national VET course, held on the award reference table, not against a client. The Australian Skills Quality Authority is the national VET regulator and says it "accredits courses where a clearly demonstrated training need cannot be met through a nationally endorsed training package qualification". The year therefore dates the version of the course, which is how two CSWE award codes with the same certificate name are told apart.
description_source: Australian Skills Quality Authority, Course accreditation
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year. It is an attribute of the course carried in the reference table, one row per AWARD_CODE, and is set by the accreditation decision rather than by anything the client did.
limitation: It is not the year the client earned anything. AWARD_DATE on amep_csweawards is the date of the client's assessment, and the two can be many years apart because an accredited course stays current for its whole accreditation period.
rationale: ASQA is the body named in the custodian's own wording, and its course accreditation page states what accreditation is and that ASQA grants it.
evidence_quote: ASQA accredits courses where a clearly demonstrated training need cannot be met through a nationally endorsed training package qualification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic sentence twice over, so it never said that the year belongs to the course rather than the client, nor what an accredited course is.

value_domain: CSWE certificate level assigned at entry assessment
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The Certificates in Spoken and Written English level a client was placed at when they were first assessed, held once on the client profile. CSWE runs Preliminary, Certificate I, Certificate II and Certificate III, and the evaluation notes that Certificate III is "the highest level obtainable in the AMEP". The value is a placement judgement made at the start of tuition, so it is the closest thing the file has to a baseline English level under the pre-2017 curriculum.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
value_definition: A CSWE certificate level. The four levels carry very different expected workloads: 210 to 660 supervised hours for Preliminary and 370 to 630 for Certificate III, with 1,415 to 2,430 supervised hours to move from beginner to Certificate III.
limitation: An entry level is not an award. The client has been placed at that level, not certified at it, and amep_csweawards is the only place a granted certificate appears. Entry assessment also moved to the Australian Core Skills Framework for new clients from 1 July 2017, so this column thins out for later cohorts rather than recording a genuine absence of assessment.
rationale: The evaluation sets out the CSWE level structure, the hours each level is expected to take, and the shift of initial assessment to the ACSF under the new business model, which is exactly what an entry level means and when it stops being recorded.
evidence_quote: Progress from total beginner to completion of Certificate III (the highest level obtainable in the AMEP) is expected to take between 1415 and 2430 supervised hours.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'CSWE level attained in entry assessment' with no value domain and the same generic sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it neither listed the levels nor warned that a placement is not an attainment.

value_domain: Certificate level of the CSWE course
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)

value_domain: AMEP tuition stream at the reporting date
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The tuition stream the client was in at the reporting date used for this extract, which for this file is a date before 1 July 2019. Streaming began with the new business model on 1 July 2017 and has two values. The evaluation says "Pre-Employment English is for those students who wish to participate in the workplace or further training and is mandatory for those referred to the AMEP by an employment services provider", while Social English is for clients improving conversational English to live independently in their community. INITIAL_STREAM holds the stream first assigned, so the pair shows whether a client moved.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
value_definition: A two-category stream classification introduced under the 2017 AMEP contract. Pre-Employment English must use a nationally accredited curriculum; Social English may use non-accredited material and has larger classes and lighter teacher qualification requirements.
limitation: A blank is not a data fault for anyone whose AMEP participation ended before 1 July 2017, because streams did not exist then. The split is also far from even: the evaluation reports 77 per cent of classes as Pre-Employment English, 5 per cent as Social English and 18 per cent blended. Centrelink mutual obligation requirements do force some clients into Pre-Employment English, but the evaluation finds only five per cent of students are in that position, so the imbalance is not explained by that referral pathway.
rationale: The evaluation has a section on Targeted Tuition Streams that names the two streams, dates their introduction to July 2017 and explains their curriculum and enrolment differences.
evidence_quote: The two streams, Pre-Employment English and Social English, reflect the government's recognition that many students are seeking sustainable employment and would benefit from a stronger employment focus in their AMEP classes, while others are prioritising settlement in Australia and social participation within their community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Stream type at time of this reporting - prior to 01/07/19' with no value domain and one generic sentence used twice, so it never named the streams or said when streaming started.

description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)

limitation: It cannot be used as an end date for a client's participation. A client still enrolled on the extract date has an open, not a completed, history, and treating the extract date as an exit produces spuriously short spells.
rationale: The ABS page describes PLIDA as an asset built from agency extracts, which is the process this column dates; no published document gives the extract dates of the individual AMEP tables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Date data was extracted' and printed the generic sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish file vintage from client history.

value_domain: Date of referral to a Distance Learning provider
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
variable_description: The date the client was referred to an AMEP Distance Learning provider, held once on the client profile. Distance Learning gives clients one-on-one classes with an AMEP teacher by phone or online rather than in a classroom, and every AMEP client is eligible for it even while attending face-to-face classes. In five remote contract regions there is no local provider at all, so a referral there reflects geography rather than a client's choice of mode.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)
value_definition: A calendar date. It is open ended and takes any date within the client's AMEP participation; there is no code list and no companion end date on the same row.

rationale: The evaluation describes Distance Learning as one of the three AMEP delivery modes, its eligibility, and the remote regions that depend on it entirely.

variable_description: The employment status the client stated about themselves when they registered with an AMEP provider, captured once and never updated. Registration is an early event: an eligible migrant must register within six months of arrival, so the answer describes someone who has usually been in Australia only weeks or months. It sits alongside the other self-reported registration fields, OCCUPATION_AT_REGISTRATION, HIGHEST_QUAL_AT_REGISTRATION and YEARS_OF_SCHOOLING.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)

evidence_quote: They must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia (or within 12 months if they are under 18 years old), commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with no value domain and one generic sentence used twice, so it did not flag that the value is self-reported, unclassified and fixed at a point very early in settlement.

value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program

value_domain: ASLPR rating, listening
value_source: D. E. Ingram, 'The ASLPR: Its Origins and Current Developments', ERIC record ED402735
variable_description: The client's listening rating at their first ASLPR assessment, which for most clients is their entry assessment into the AMEP. The ASLPR, in its co-author's words, is "a scale that describes how second language proficiency develops on a scale from zero to native-like proficiency, providing performance descriptions in terms of practical tasks", and it rates each macroskill separately, this column being the receptive spoken macroskill. INITIAL_ASLPR_DATE dates it and LATEST_ASLPR_LISTEN holds the same rating at the client's most recent assessment.
description_source: D. E. Ingram, 'The ASLPR: Its Origins and Current Developments', ERIC record ED402735
value_definition: A point on the ASLPR scale, which runs from 0 (zero proficiency) to 5 (native-like) across twelve rated points including the minus and plus steps such as 1- and 1+. Each macroskill is stated separately, in the form S:1+, L:2, R:1, W:1+.
limitation: A listening rating is not a comprehension test score and does not convert to IELTS or the CEFR. Listening and speaking are usually judged in the same interview, so the two columns are not independent observations and should not be averaged as though they were.
rationale: The ERIC record for the scale's co-author gives the ASLPR's own definition and its zero to native-like range, and the scale's publisher sets out the twelve rated points and the per-macroskill reporting the four columns follow.
evidence_quote: The Australian Second Language Proficiency Ratings (ASLPR) is a scale that describes how second language proficiency develops on a scale from zero to native-like proficiency, providing performance descriptions in terms of practical tasks.

variable_description: Special Preparatory Program hours the AMEP client attended by distance learning in the July to September quarter of 2015. It isolates the distance-learning share of a client's Special Preparatory Program tuition, the additional hours available to humanitarian entrants; the classroom share of the same quarter sits in SPP_2015_Q3. The quarter falls in 2015-16, when the cap was lifted to $27.34 million to carry the extra 12,000 Syrian and Iraqi humanitarian entrants the government accepted from December 2015. description_source: Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019
value_definition: A count of tuition hours attended, carried as a number rather than a code, for one delivery mode of one AMEP subprogram in one quarter. The classification behind the column family is the AMEP's own program structure: general AMEP tuition, AMEPDL, SPP, SPPDL, SLPT, HTS and CHILDCARE each carry a 32-column quarterly series in amep_clientshours_2011_19 running from 2011 Q3 to 2019 Q2, and EXTEND carries eight columns from 2017 Q3. Hours are entered by the AMEP service provider in the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS) and summed to the quarter. For 2015 Q3 seven of those eight families carry a column, EXTEND excepted.
limitation: A zero or an empty cell does not mean the client did no remote SPP study that quarter. Far more often they were not enrolled at all, had not yet registered, had already used their SPP hours, or took that quarter's SPP tuition in a classroom, which lands in SPP_2015_Q3 instead. What is counted is also session time as the provider recorded it: the evaluation notes that ARMS "only records full session attendance and approved absences", with late arrivals, early departures and unapproved absences handled on spreadsheets outside the system, and the department measured an average 2.8 per cent gap between scheduled and actual attendance. value_domain: Synthetic person-level identifier
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person key that holds an AMEP client's records together and joins them to the rest of the asset. It carries the same value on all six AMEP tables, so hours in 2003-11, hours in 2011-19, addresses, the client profile, CSWE awards and English proficiency assemble into one learner history, while AMET_CLNT_ID is the department's own client number inside its reporting system. In the live asset the equivalent key comes from the ABS Person Linkage Spine, which "allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data"; in fplida the value is generated and means nothing outside this package.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: An opaque person-level identifier, one value per person, repeated on every row that belongs to that person. It encodes nothing: it is not ordered by age, arrival, registration or provider, and no part of it can be decoded.
limitation: It does not make a row a person. A client with two registrations, a break in tuition, a change of provider or several award records keeps one identifier, so counting rows counts episodes; deduplicate before treating a count as a headcount. It also cannot be joined to anything outside the asset, and a client who did not link to the spine is missing from the AMEP tables altogether rather than sitting in them with a blank key, which biases coverage rather than adding noise.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page describes the Person Linkage Spine that supplies the person key in the live asset, which is what this column stands in for, and the AMEP tables all carry it as their only cross-table join.
evidence_quote: allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset', and printed the same generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said which tables the key joins or that the row is an episode rather than a person.

value_domain: Migration stream of the client's AMEP-eligible visa
value_source: ABS, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2023
variable_description: The migration stream of the visa that made this client eligible for the AMEP, set once at registration. It is the level above the subclass: the ABS groups the same Home Affairs codes the same way, noting that "visa subclass (3-digit) information is then aggregated into visa streams (highest-level grouping) to produce the Skilled, Family, Humanitarian, Other and undetermined, and Total permanent groupings". The category is also what opens or closes the Special Preparatory Program, whose hours sit in the SPP and SPPDL columns of the hours tables, because the SPP is for refugee and humanitarian entrants.
description_source: ABS, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2023
value_definition: A stream-level category rather than a list of visas, sitting above the subclass number in VISA_SUBCLASS and the subclass name in VISA_SUBCLASS_DESC on the same row. The streams that carry AMEP eligibility are the humanitarian, family and skilled streams.
limitation: It is a stream at one moment, not a migration history. A person who arrived on a temporary visa and later became a permanent resident carries a single category here, and someone who held a humanitarian visa earlier but registered on a family visa will not read as humanitarian at all. Nor does the category by itself decide AMEP access: eligibility also turns on having less than functional English and on the registration, commencement and completion deadlines that attach to the visa start date.
rationale: The ABS methodology sets out exactly how Home Affairs visa subclasses are collapsed into the Skilled, Family, Humanitarian and Other groupings used across the migrant products in this asset, which is the classification this column carries, and the AMEP evaluation confirms the same three streams govern AMEP eligibility.
evidence_quote: visa subclass (3-digit) information is then aggregated into visa streams (highest-level grouping) to produce the Skilled, Family, Humanitarian, Other and undetermined, and Total permanent groupings
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's wording, 'Visa information - Client's visa migration category', with one generic sentence doing duty as both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader could not tell whether the column held a subclass, a stream or a visa name.

value_domain: Home Affairs visa subclass code
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, visa list
variable_description: The visa subclass held by the client of the Adult Migrant English Program. A subclass is Home Affairs' three-digit identifier for a specific visa product, and here it is also an eligibility statement: entitlement to the program depends on visa type, so the subclass explains why a client is in the file at all. Humanitarian subclasses and family stream subclasses carry different entitlements to tuition hours.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, visa list
limitation: Home Affairs publishes the subclasses but not the code list used here, so the mapping is not confirmed. The subclass is the one recorded at registration, so a client who changed status during their tuition still shows the visa they enrolled on.
rationale: The DIL gives the field as the client's visa subclass code. Home Affairs publishes the visa subclasses; no published crosswalk to the values used here was found.
evidence_quote: Visa information - Client's visa subclass code
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Home Affairs visa subclass name
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, Visa listing
variable_description: The name of the visa subclass the client held when they registered for the AMEP, spelled out in words beside the number in VISA_SUBCLASS. Home Affairs identifies every visa by a subclass number and a name, and its visa listing is the register of those pairs; this column carries the name half. It describes the visa that opened the client's tuition entitlement, not the visa or citizenship they hold now, and not the visa they were on during any particular quarter of tuition.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, Visa listing
value_definition: Free text naming one visa subclass, one value per client. The numbering behind the names is the Home Affairs subclass system, three digits for most subclasses, which VISA_SUBCLASS carries on the same row.
limitation: The text is a label, not a key. Subclasses are renamed, closed and replaced, so one numeric subclass can appear under different words in different extracts and grouping clients on this column will split a single visa across several spellings; group on VISA_SUBCLASS and treat this as display text. It also cannot tell you whether the visa was still in force, since AMEP tuition can run for years after the grant and no end date accompanies the name.
rationale: The Home Affairs visa listing is the department's own register of visas by subclass number and name, which is the vocabulary this column draws on; it resolves and can be checked against any value in the field.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Visa information - Client's visa subclass description', with the value definition and the limitation carrying the same generic sentence, so it did not say that the column is the text twin of VISA_SUBCLASS or warn against grouping on it.

value_domain: Year of birth (four digits)
value_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The AMEP client's year of birth, held beside MONTH_OF_BIRTH and with no day of month anywhere in the table. The ABS describes the AMEP collection as "Information on participants in the English language tuition program, including their visa type, course attendance and educational outcomes", and this is the age anchor for that participant record. AGE_GROUP_AT_REGISTRATION on the same row is the department's own banding of the same fact, so the two will not always agree at the edges of a band.
description_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year, one value per client on the client profile table. Month of birth is held separately, so the pair gives a month and year rather than a date.
limitation: It will not give you an exact age at any event. Age at registration, at first enrolment or at a given quarterly hours column can only be bracketed to a year, and where age decides an entitlement this matters: the Special Preparatory Program splits at 25 years, so two clients born in the same year can fall on opposite sides of that line. The column also carries no sign of whether the year came from the client, from a visa record, or was estimated where no document gave one.
rationale: The ABS page for PLIDA data describes the AMEP collection this table comes from and its reference period from 2003, which fixes what kind of record the year of birth belongs to; the surrounding columns in the client profile table fix its role.
evidence_quote: Information on participants in the English language tuition program, including their visa type, course attendance and educational outcomes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Year of birth', the custodian's wording, and printed one generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing warned that the day of birth is absent and that age at an event is therefore approximate.

value_domain: Years of schooling, self reported
value_source: Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019
variable_description: The number of years of school the client says they completed, given by the client at registration. It is an entitlement variable and not only a background one: the department's evaluation records that "Eligible students are able to access either 100 or 400 SPP hours according to their age and number of years of prior schooling", with the larger 400-hour Special Preparatory Program entitlement going to humanitarian entrants under 25 who had seven years of schooling or less. Read beside the SPP and SPPDL hour columns, it is how you see which clients had the larger entitlement to draw on.
description_source: Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019
value_definition: A count of years, self reported, one value per client. There is no schooling-level classification behind it: the number is taken as given, and it counts schooling anywhere in the world rather than schooling in Australia.
limitation: It is neither a qualification nor a verified record. A client's own count can cover interrupted, informal or overseas schooling that no Australian credential recognises, and tertiary years are counted in a separate column rather than added to this one. A value of seven or less also does not prove the client received 400 SPP hours: that entitlement additionally required a humanitarian visa, an age under 25 and, until 1 July 2017, evidence of difficult pre-migration experiences.
rationale: The evaluation sets out the Special Preparatory Program entitlement table that uses years of prior schooling as one of its two tests, which is what makes this self-reported number consequential in the AMEP record rather than incidental.
evidence_quote: Eligible students are able to access either 100 or 400 SPP hours according to their age and number of years of prior schooling.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Number of years of schooling (self reporting)', and repeated one generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never connected the number to the entitlement rule that makes it worth reading.

value_domain: Years of tertiary study, self reported
value_source: Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019
variable_description: The number of years of post-school study the client says they completed, reported at registration alongside YEARS_OF_SCHOOLING. Unlike school years it plays no part in the Special Preparatory Program entitlement, which the evaluation ties to "age and number of years of prior schooling" and to nothing else, so it is background rather than a rule input. It sits with HIGHEST_QUAL_AT_REGISTRATION and OCCUPATION_PRE_MIGRATION as the pre-migration human capital block of the client profile.
description_source: Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019
value_definition: A count of years, self reported, one value per client, covering study after school at any institution in any country.
limitation: Years of study are not a qualification and not English. The number does not say whether a course was finished, whether the award is recognised in Australia, or whether the teaching was in English, so a client with several tertiary years can still enter at the lowest level recorded in CSWE_ENTRY_LEVEL. A zero is also ambiguous between no tertiary study and nothing reported at registration.
rationale: The evaluation states which client characteristics drive the AMEP subprogram entitlements, which is what establishes that tertiary years are descriptive here while school years are operative.
evidence_quote: Eligible students are able to access either 100 or 400 SPP hours according to their age and number of years of prior schooling.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Number of years of tertiary study (self reporting)', with the value definition and the limitation reduced to the same generic sentence, so it did not distinguish this column from the schooling column beside it.

value_domain: Self-reported disability indicator
value_source: Australian Public Service Commission, APS Employment Database
variable_description: Whether the Australian Public Service employee has told their agency they have a disability. It is a self-disclosure to an employer rather than an assessment, so it measures willingness to disclose as much as it measures disability, and it is not comparable with the HE dataset's field of the same name, which is an eight-character code covering three separate questions.
description_source: Australian Public Service Commission, APS Employment Database
limitation: Disclosure to an employer is voluntary and known to undercount: an employee who has not told their agency is indistinguishable from one who has no disability. The field describes the record at a point in time, so an employee who discloses later appears to acquire a disability on the day they told someone. The exact codes are not published.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as identifying whether the employee has reported having a disability, which is a disclosure to the employing agency. The APSC publishes the database but not this field's code list.
evidence_quote: Identifies if the employee has reported having a disability.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that the field measures disclosure rather than disability.

value_domain: Address reliability status (reliable or unreliable)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: Whether the ATO still trusts the address on this row, which turns unreliable once post sent to it comes back undelivered. The register itself is the ATO's roll of people with a tax file number, which ABS describes as "demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions". Read it with ADDR_STS_CD, which says whether the address is the current one, and with the SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns, which are this address geocoded.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
value_definition: A two-state indicator. The data item list names reliable and unreliable as the outcomes but publishes no codes, so the stored characters are not confirmed.
limitation: It grades the ATO's postal experience, not the person's whereabouts. An address can be perfectly current and still be flagged unreliable because a letterbox or a business tenancy failed, and nothing here dates the returned item, so an unreliable flag cannot be placed in time against the address episode it sits on.
rationale: No ATO or ABS page publishes the codes for this field. The custodian's own wording states the rule that sets it, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes what the client register is and who is on it, which is what the description asserts.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's parenthetical wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the flag is about returned post rather than about whether the person has moved.

value_domain: Address status code (active or inactive)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: Whether the ATO still holds this address as one it would use for the client, or has superseded it. It is the column that separates a client's current address from the trail of earlier ones, so a person-year address panel built without filtering on it will hold several addresses for the same day. START_DATE and END_DATE date the episode; this column reports the state of the record as at the extract.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
value_definition: A short status code. The data item list names active and inactive as the outcomes and publishes no code characters, so the stored values are not confirmed.
limitation: Inactive is not the same as wrong. A correct historical address is inactive the moment the client notifies a new one, and because the status is assessed at extraction, a row that was the client's live address in 2012 reads inactive in a 2022 extract. It also says nothing about whether post to the address arrives, which is ADDR_RELIABLE_STS.
rationale: No published ATO page enumerates the codes. The custodian's wording gives the two outcomes, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes the register as the ATO's demographic roll of tax file number holders, which is what makes the active or inactive distinction an administrative currency flag.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry reused the custodian's bracketed wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing warned that an address panel needs this column to avoid stacking superseded addresses on the same day.

value_domain: Address type (residential or postal)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The 2025 vintage spelling of the column saying whether this address is where the client lives or where the ATO posts their mail. The 1999 to 2022, 2023 and 2024 address tables carry the same field as ADR_TYP, so code that stacks the vintages has to accept both names or it silently drops the type on the newest table. POSTALTYPE beside it sub-classifies a postal address into a box, bag or roadside service.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
value_definition: A short type code. The data item list gives postal and residential as its examples and publishes no code characters, so the stored values are not confirmed.
limitation: The rename is the trap rather than the concept: a series joined on variable name alone loses the 2025 table, and there is no published statement that ADDR_TYP and ADR_TYP use the same codes, so the two cannot be assumed to be interchangeable without checking. A client with only a postal address on file has no residential row at all.
rationale: The registry shows this name only on ato_cr_addr_1999_25 while ADR_TYP appears on the four earlier address tables, which identifies it as the renamed field; the ABS PLIDA page establishes the register the field sits in.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, and said nothing about the rename that makes the 2025 table look as though it lost the field.

value_domain: Address type (residential or postal)
value_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: Whether the address on this row is where the client lives or where the ATO sends their mail. It is the column that decides whether an address episode can be read as a residence at all: a postal address is often an agent's office or a post office box, and treating one as a home puts the taxpayer in their accountant's suburb. Beside it, ADDR_STS_CD says whether the ATO still treats the address as active and ADDR_RELIABLE_STS turns unreliable when mail is returned.
description_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation
limitation: The domain is inferred from the DIL's own example, which names residential and postal without listing the codes, so the exact values are not confirmed. A client with only a postal address on file has no residential row at all, which is a gap rather than a person who lives nowhere.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL describes the field as the type of address and gives residential and postal as its examples. No published list of the codes was found, so the shape is taken from the description and the mapping is not asserted.
evidence_quote: Type of address (e.g. residential postal etc.)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why the distinction matters.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address on the ATO's client register, for one period of the client's address history. START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period, ADDR_TYP separates a residential address from a postal one, and ADDR_STS_CD and ADDR_RELIABLE_STS say whether the ATO still treats it as active and reliable, the latter turning unreliable when mail is returned. This table is one of the sources Core Locations draws on to build a single address history per person.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. A postal address is not a residence, and ADDR_TYP is what tells them apart. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed, truncated ARID on the ATO client register address table, whose other columns (address type, status, reliability, start and end dates) describe the episode the identifier belongs to.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'not specified' as its domain and the same generic sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: ATO client status code
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The standing the ATO gives this person as a client of the tax system, on the demographic side of the client register. It sits with START_DATE and END_DATE, so the register carries a history of statuses rather than one current value, and a person can appear several times with different codes. ABS describes the register as "demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number", which is the population the status applies to.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
value_definition: A short administrative code with no published list. The register's own metadata does not name the outcomes, so both the code characters and the number of distinct statuses are unconfirmed.
limitation: A client status is a state of the ATO's record, not a statement about the person's tax affairs. It cannot be read as employed, resident, lodging or earning, and an inactive client can still have income reported about them by a third party through payment summaries or Single Touch Payroll.
rationale: No ATO or ABS publication enumerates client register status codes. The ABS PLIDA page defines the register and its population, which supports the description of what the status attaches to, but not the values.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's typo, 'Client staus code', with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so a reader learnt neither what the status attaches to nor that it is dated rather than current.

value_domain: Immigration data presence indicator
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Department of Home Affairs Client information
variable_description: A flag saying the person on this ATO client record also appears in the immigration department's client data. The prefix is the Department of Immigration and Citizenship, the name Home Affairs used before 2013, and the PLIDA source it points at holds "Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants", from 1984. It is a coverage flag on the ATO record, not an attribute of the person, so it changes as the immigration extract is refreshed.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Department of Home Affairs Client information
value_definition: A binary indicator on the demographics record. The register's metadata does not publish the characters used for present and absent.
limitation: It is not a migrant marker. The immigration client file covers Australian-born citizens as well as visa holders, so a positive flag does not mean overseas born, and a negative flag mixes people genuinely absent from immigration data with people whose records did not match. Nothing here gives a visa, a country or an arrival date.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page names the Home Affairs Client information dataset that this flag points at and states its population, which is the fact that decides whether the flag can be read as a migrant indicator.
evidence_quote: Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence about presence in immigration data and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have used it as a migrant flag.

value_domain: Month and year of birth (MonYYYY)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The client's birth month and year as the ATO holds them, with the day removed before the file reached the asset. It is the only age information on the ATO client register, so an age at any dated event has to be built from it rather than read off a column. The register is the ATO's roll of tax file number holders, so the date is what was given at registration, not a date verified against a birth record.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
value_definition: A character string pairing a three-letter month with a four-digit year, in the form Mar1978. It is not a date type, so it needs parsing before any arithmetic.
limitation: Dropping the day makes every age uncertain by up to a month, which matters at policy boundaries such as turning 18, 60 or the age pension age within a quarter. The value is also self-reported at registration and can be a default rather than a true birth date, so it should not be treated as vital-registration quality.
rationale: The custodian states the format, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes that the register is the ATO's tax file number client roll, which is what makes the date a registration-time value rather than a verified one.
