ABS defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" and publishes 368,286 of them, so this is the finest geography on a member contributions statement and the block the LGA, SA1 and SA2 codes on the row are built from. It appears on the fifteen tables from 2003-04, not on the four earliest.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Mesh Blocks
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS Edition 3 mesh block code, including 114 non-spatial special purpose codes for people in transit or with no fixed address.
limitation: The address behind it is the one the fund holds for posting member statements, which members update far less often than they update it with the ATO, so the geography lags a person's actual home by more than the ATO client register does. Members with an overseas address are excluded from Australian geography entirely, and a mesh block is a land-use unit rather than a household.
rationale: The custodian labels the column only as an address variable; the ABS ASGS page defines mesh blocks, gives the count and design and identifies the special purpose codes that appear as valid values.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address variable' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it named neither the classification nor whose address is being coded.

value_domain: Month of birth (01 to 12)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.71
variable_description: The month the member was born, as the super fund holds it, with the day dropped before the file reached the asset. The ATO defines the field as "the member's month of birth (in MM format)" and instructs providers to zero fill it when the month is unknown. Age at a contribution therefore has to be built from this and MBR_IDV_CNCTNTD_BRTH_YEAR, which matters for the contribution rules that turn on age 18, 65 and 75.
description_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.71
value_definition: A two-character month from 01 to 12. Zero is a valid stored value meaning the fund did not know the month, not a January default.
limitation: A zero month is easily read as missing data of no consequence, but it removes the member from any age-at-event calculation that needs sub-annual precision. The value is also whatever the fund recorded, which need not agree with the birth month the ATO holds on the client register for the same person.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives its format and range and states the zero-fill rule for an unknown month, which is the fact that decides whether a zero should be treated as missing.
evidence_quote: Month of birth - the member's month of birth (in MM format) If the month of birth is unknown, this field should be zero filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Month of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that zero is a permitted unknown code.

value_domain: Year of birth (CCYY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.72
variable_description: The year the member was born, as recorded by the super fund. The ATO defines it as "the member's year of birth (in CCYY format)" and validates it as "a valid value greater than 1890", with zero filling where the year is unknown. It is the workhorse age variable in the MCS, since it is present on all nineteen tables while the fund-reported death and phase fields are not.
description_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.72
value_definition: A four-digit year above 1890. Zero is a valid stored value meaning the fund did not know the year.
limitation: Year alone puts a member's age within a twelve-month band, which is too coarse for the contribution rules that switch on an exact birthday, such as the work test that once applied from 65. Because the year comes from the fund's own records rather than a verified source, the same person can carry different birth years across accounts with different providers.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives its format, states the validation rule and states the zero-fill rule for an unknown year.
evidence_quote: Year of birth - the member's year of birth (in CCYY format) If the year of birth is unknown, this field should be zero filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Year of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it gave neither the validation floor nor the meaning of a zero.

value_domain: Member deceased indicator (N or Y)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.78
variable_description: Whether the super fund has been told the member has died, which is a statement about the fund's knowledge rather than about the member. The ATO is precise about this: N means the "provider has not received notification of the member's death" and Y that it has. It governs the death date columns on the same row, since the ATO requires Y wherever a date of death is present.
description_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.78
value_definition: A single character, N or Y, present on all nineteen MCS tables.
limitation: It is a notification flag, so an N covers both living members and members whose death the fund has not heard about, and a fund can go on reporting a dead member as N for years. The MCS also records death primarily for co-contribution purposes, so it is not a substitute for the death registrations in the deaths collection, which are the authority.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field in terms of notification received, gives its two values, requires Y where a date of death is present and states that the date is reported primarily for co-contribution purposes.
evidence_quote: Member deceased indicator - indicates if the provider has received notification that the member is deceased.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Member deceased' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it read as a fact about the person rather than as a record of what the fund had been told.

value_domain: Month of death (01 to 12)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.87
variable_description: The month of the member's death as reported by the super fund, taken from the date of death field with the day removed. The ATO requires the date only where MBR_IDV_DCSD_IND is Y and requires it to be zero filled otherwise, so a zero here is the normal state for a living member rather than a gap. With MBR_IDV_DTH_YEAR it fixes the death to a month, which is what the co-contribution rules need.
description_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.87
value_definition: A two-character month from 01 to 12, or zero where the member is not reported as deceased. It is the month part of the single date of death field in the ATO specification, split for the asset.
limitation: A month on its own cannot separate a death near a 30 June boundary, which is exactly the case the ATO says matters: it requires an amended statement whenever the true date falls in a different financial year from the one reported. The value is also the fund's record, so it can be corrected, withdrawn or simply wrong, and the ATO provides for a member reported as dead who is not.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the single date of death field, its dependence on the deceased indicator, the zero-fill rule and the circumstances requiring an amendment, which is what this month column inherits.
evidence_quote: If the Member deceased indicator field is Y then this field should contain a valid date. If the Member deceased indicator field is N then this field should be zero filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Month member deceased' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that zero is the ordinary value for a living member.

value_domain: Year of death (CCYY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.87
variable_description: The year the super fund records the member as having died, split out of the fund's date of death field. It is the column that puts a death in a financial year, and the ATO treats getting that year right as the one case where an amendment is always required: "If the actual DOD is in a different financial year from the originally reported DOD, an amendment is always required once this is known to the fund." The ATO also requires the date to be later than the member's birth date.
description_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.87
value_definition: A four-digit year, or zero where the member is not reported as deceased. It is the year part of the single date of death field in the ATO specification.
limitation: It dates the death, not the reporting, so a death in one year can first appear on a statement lodged several years later and the account will look active in between. Because the MCS records death mainly for co-contribution purposes, funds have limited incentive to correct a year that does not change that outcome, and the deaths collection remains the authority.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the date of death field, states the amendment rule that turns on the financial year, and gives the validation against the member's birth date.
evidence_quote: If the actual DOD is in a different financial year from the originally reported DOD, an amendment is always required once this is known to the fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Year member deceased' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that the year can be reported late or that it is not the authoritative record of a death.

value_domain: Co-contribution acceptance indicator (A or R)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.88
variable_description: Whether the fund would take a government co-contribution or low income super contribution into this account. The ATO defines the field as indicating "whether the provider will accept a super co-contribution and LISC for this member", with A for accept and R for refuse, and sets three conditions: current membership, an account that is not a pension or income stream, and a tax file number held for the member. An A therefore doubles as evidence the fund holds the member's tax file number.
description_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.88
value_definition: A single character, A or R, on the fifteen tables from 2003-04 onwards. Where the value is A, the ATO requires an account balance to be reported, so an A row always carries a balance even if nil.
limitation: It says nothing about whether a co-contribution was paid or whether the member was eligible for one, only about whether this account could receive it. An R has three quite different causes pooled into one character, from a missing tax file number to a trust deed that declines the payments, and only the missing tax file number case tells you anything about the member.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives both codes, lists the three conditions for acceptance, notes that a provider may decline for its own reasons and ties an A value to the requirement to report an account balance.
evidence_quote: Provider can accept super co-contributions and low income super contributions for member account - indicates whether the provider will accept a super co-contribution and LISC for this member.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's two alternative labels with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that the value is about the account's eligibility to receive a payment rather than about a payment made.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS non-assessable foreign fund amount question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 52
variable_description: Money moved into the member's Australian super account from an overseas fund that the Australian fund does not have to pay tax on. The ATO asks the provider to report "any part of the amount transferred to the provider from a foreign super fund or scheme that the provider is not required to include in their assessable income", so the taxed slice of the very same transfer sits in the assessable foreign fund column beside it. The field also carries money brought across from a New Zealand KiwiSaver scheme under the Trans-Tasman portability arrangements. It is reported by the fund, not claimed by the member.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 52
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year. It is the untaxed portion of a foreign super transfer plus any KiwiSaver amount, and it counts towards the member's non-concessional contributions cap.
limitation: It is not a measure of retirement wealth brought into Australia. Only money routed into a complying Australian super fund appears, so savings a migrant leaves offshore or takes as cash are invisible, and a zero can equally mean the fund treated the whole transfer as assessable.
rationale: The abbreviated name expands to the non-assessable foreign fund amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement the fund lodges, and the ATO publishes instructions for that question in both the 2007-08 to 2011-12 and the 2013-and-later editions. The ATO site refuses some automated fetchers but serves the page to an ordinary browser request, which is how it was read.
evidence_quote: Provide any part of the amount transferred to the provider from a foreign super fund or scheme that the provider is not required to include in their assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Non-assessable foreign fund amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the column is one half of a split foreign transfer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS notional taxed contributions question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 44
variable_description: An actuary's estimate of what a year in a defined benefit scheme was worth to the member, standing in for an employer contribution never actually paid. The ATO requires the figure to be determined under the Income Tax Assessment Regulations and says it "will generally be equal to the notional taxed contributions as determined by the provider with advice from an actuary". A grandfathering rule caps it: for a member who held the defined benefit account on 5 September 2006, an actuarial figure above the concessional contributions cap must be reported as the cap. Funds have reported it from the 2012-13 year, which is why the column only appears on the later statements.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 44
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one defined benefit account in one financial year. It measures benefit value accrued rather than cash received, and it is reported separately from the employer contributed amount.
limitation: Grandfathering censors the top of the distribution, writing any figure above the concessional cap down to the cap, so the column understates accrual for exactly the high-value defined benefit members it matters most for. It also overlaps the defined benefit contributions field and must not be added to it.
rationale: The name expands to notional taxed contributions, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction for that question sets out how the amount is determined and how grandfathering caps it. The page is served to an ordinary browser request although the ATO blocks some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: It will generally be equal to the notional taxed contributions as determined by the provider with advice from an actuary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Notional taxed contributions' as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that the amount is an actuarial construct or that it is capped by the grandfathering rule.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the pre-2007 MCS other contributed amount question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 56
variable_description: Contributions into the member's account that fit none of the named categories on the statement used before July 2007. The ATO defines it purely by exclusion: an accumulation provider reports "all other amounts (apart from amounts regarded as reasonably attributable to interest) that are paid for, or by the member to the provider" that were not already reported at the employer, termination payment, allocated surplus and personal questions. Government super co-contributions were deliberately directed here rather than to the personal contribution question, because entitlement to the co-contribution was calculated from that question.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 56
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, being whatever is left after the named contribution questions on the pre-2007 statement have been filled in.
limitation: Because it is a residual, its content is not stable between funds: two funds with identical member experience can split the same dollars differently according to how they classified an amount. It also merges co-contributions paid by government with genuinely miscellaneous credits, so it cannot be read as private saving.
rationale: The pre-2007 tables carry the question set of the Superannuation member contributions statement in force before 1 July 2007, and the ATO publishes the completion instructions for that form as a downloadable guide, which defines question 56 by exclusion and states where co-contributions were to be reported.
evidence_quote: Superannuation (accumulated benefits) providers must report in this field all other amounts (apart from amounts regarded as reasonably attributable to interest) that are paid for, or by the member to the provider
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Other contributed amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that the column is a residual whose meaning depends on how the other questions were filled.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS other family and friend contributions question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 50
variable_description: Super paid in for the member by somebody who is not the member, their employer, their spouse or the parent of a child under 18. The ATO calls it other third-party contributions and asks the fund to "provide the amount of contributions made for the member by relatives, friends and third parties", listing a permanently separated or former spouse, a parent of an adult child, another relative, a friend, an insurer paying contributions under a sickness policy and a government agency compensating an injured worker. A contribution from any of those people made in their capacity as the member's employer belongs in the employer column instead.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 50
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, covering third-party contributors and counting towards the member's non-concessional contributions cap.
limitation: It cannot identify who paid. A workers compensation insurer, an estranged spouse and a friend all land in one figure, so the column is not a measure of family transfers. When a couple separates permanently the same contributor moves out of the spouse and child column into this one, so a relationship breakdown looks like a change in contributor type.
rationale: The name expands to the other family and friend contributions amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction for it enumerates the contributors included and the routing rules against the neighbouring employer and spouse questions.
evidence_quote: Provide the amount of contributions made for the member by relatives, friends and third parties.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other family and friend contributions amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the spouse and child column beside it.

value_domain: Date the account left the accumulation-only phase (DDMMYYYY)
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section D, question 38
variable_description: The day the member's account first stopped being purely an accumulation account and began paying a pension or a lump sum benefit. The ATO ties it to the account phase code on the same row: "provide the date on which the account phase first changed from code A to either code P or code B", and the field is left blank while the phase is still A. Providers may report "a reasonable estimate of the date" when the real date is not held, and the instructions give the example of a fund reporting an arbitrary 1 July 2003 for everyone whose pension predates a system migration.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section D, question 38
value_definition: A calendar date written DDMMYYYY, present only on accounts that have left the accumulation-only phase. It marks the first change of phase ever recorded, not a change within the reported year.
limitation: It is not a retirement date. A transition-to-retirement pension started while the member keeps working sets it, and for a defined benefit member a single rollover or lump sum sets it as well. Because estimates are permitted, clusters of identical dates across many members are administrative artefacts rather than real events.
rationale: The name expands to the date the pension phase or benefit payment phase commenced, a numbered question in the member account details section of the statement, and the ATO instruction defines it against the account phase codes and permits estimation.
evidence_quote: A reasonable estimate of the date may be provided when accurate data is not held by the provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with its date format and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the date is tied to the account phase code or that estimated dates are allowed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS personal contributed amount question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 55
variable_description: Money the member put into their own super out of their own pocket, as reported by the fund rather than claimed by the member. The ATO asks providers to report "any personal contributed amount made by a person to an account in their name" and adds that these "may include deducted and undeducted member contributions", so the column mixes contributions later claimed as a tax deduction with straightforward after-tax saving. Entitlement to the government super co-contribution was worked out from this question, which is why the co-contribution itself had to be reported at the other contributed amount question instead.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 55
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, gross of contributions tax and of any later refund.
limitation: It does not separate deductible from after-tax personal contributions, so it cannot be used to identify who claimed a deduction. It is also per account, so a member with three funds has three rows and none of them is that person's total personal saving.
rationale: The name expands to the total personal contributed amount, a numbered question on the pre-2007 member contributions statement, and the ATO completion guide defines what the question covers and explains its role in the co-contribution calculation.
evidence_quote: Both superannuation (accumulated benefits) providers and superannuation (defined benefits) providers must report any personal contributed amount made by a person to an account in their name.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Personal contributed amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it never said the figure mixes deductible and after-tax contributions or that it is one account among several.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS personal injury election question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 37
variable_description: Compensation money a member put into super after telling the fund to keep it outside the non-concessional contributions cap. The ATO asks the fund to "provide the amount of personal injury payments that a member contributed while notifying the provider that they were to be excluded from the non-concessional contribution cap", and confines the eligible sources to a structured settlement, a court order for a personal injury payment or a lump sum workers compensation payment. The member must have lodged the Contributions for personal injury form on or before the day of the contribution; where that fails, the same money is reported as an ordinary personal contribution.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 37
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, excluded from the non-concessional cap and populated only where the fund held a valid election form.
limitation: It is not a measure of injury or of compensation received. Most personal injury settlements never reach a super fund, and one that does without the election paperwork is invisible here because it is reported in the personal contribution column instead.
rationale: The name expands to the personal injury election amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction states what the amount is, which payment types qualify and what happens when the election requirements are not met.
evidence_quote: Provide the amount of personal injury payments that a member contributed while notifying the provider that they were to be excluded from the non-concessional contribution cap.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Personal injury election amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that the column records an election with strict paperwork rather than the fact of a payout.

value_domain: Date the provider stopped holding the member's contributions
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 74
variable_description: The day the fund stopped holding the member's contributions, reported only on rows where money left the account. The ATO's instruction is short: "Show the date the provider ceased to be the holder of the contributions". It belongs to the transfer-out block of the pre-2007 statement, which had to be completed for any contributions leaving through a lump sum, a pension, an annuity, a departing Australia superannuation payment or a death benefit. The block exists because the superannuation surcharge assessment had to follow the money to whoever was holding it, so the date is an administrative handover point rather than a member decision.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 74
value_definition: A calendar date on the pre-2007 statement, populated only where the member row carries transfer-out information. Rows with no transfer out leave it empty.
limitation: It does not say where the money went or why, which the destination fields on the same row carry. Nor does it mark the end of a member's super: from 1998-99 a rollover to another fund was reported by the destination fund rather than through this block, so ordinary fund switching is largely absent.
rationale: The name expands to the date the provider ceased to be the holder of the contributions, a numbered question in the contributed amounts transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO completion guide states both the instruction and the circumstances that trigger the section.
evidence_quote: Show the date the provider ceased to be the holder of the contributions (if you require any further assistance, see Superannuation Contributions Determination SCD 98/1).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field belongs to a transfer-out block that is empty for most members.

value_domain: De-identified superannuation provider identifier
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B: Provider details
variable_description: The super fund, approved deposit fund or retirement savings account that the member's account sits in, as a de-identified key. The ATO is careful about which entity is meant: the reporting obligation falls on the trustee, but the statement reports "the particular super fund, ADF or RSA that details are being reported for, rather than to the trustee or RSA provider with the obligation to report them". Grouping rows by this key therefore gives fund membership, and counting distinct keys for one member in one year gives the number of accounts that person holds. The provider type column classifies the same entity.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B: Provider details
value_definition: An opaque scrambled identifier with no internal structure, one value per reporting provider. There is no finite list to publish: the domain is as large as the set of funds, approved deposit funds and retirement savings account providers that lodged a statement.
limitation: It is not a trustee and not a corporate group, so two products under one trustee count as two providers and a merged fund appears as a new key rather than as a continuation of the old one. On the later statement self-managed funds are absent, because they report member contributions on the SMSF annual return instead; the pre-2007 instructions still set a lodgment date for them, so the early years are not on the same footing.
rationale: The ATO defines precisely which entity a provider is on this form, which is what the identifier stands for, and lists the provider types that lodge it. The scrambling itself is a PLIDA treatment that ABS does not document, so the key cannot be resolved back to a named fund or an ABN and that part of the reading is inference rather than a published fact.
evidence_quote: the term 'provider' is used in this document to refer to the particular super fund, ADF or RSA that details are being reported for, rather than to the trustee or RSA provider with the obligation to report them
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Provider scrambled identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what kind of entity the key stands for or what grouping by it buys a reader.

value_domain: MCS provider type code
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B, question 14
variable_description: What kind of super provider lodged the statement: public offer fund, non-public offer fund, public sector scheme, retirement savings account and so on. The ATO publishes nine one-letter codes and instructs the provider to "use the appropriate code to classify the provider" and, "if more than one type applies, use the most specific type". P is a public offer fund, N a non-public offer fund limited to the staff of one employer or group, S a public sector scheme, X an exempt public sector scheme, D an approved deposit fund, E an eligible rollover fund, A a small APRA fund, C a constitutionally protected fund and R a retirement savings account. Self-managed funds are absent because they report on their own annual return.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B, question 14
value_definition: A single alphabetic code from the ATO provider type list, constant across every member row a given provider lodges for a year.
limitation: The most-specific rule means the codes are not the sectors an industry reader has in mind: a retail fund and an industry fund both report P, so this column cannot separate retail from industry from corporate funds. Its absence from the earlier tables is a change in the form, not a change in the fund population.
rationale: The name expands to provider type, a numbered question in the provider details section of the statement, and the ATO publishes the full code list with a short definition of each classification and the rule for choosing between them.
evidence_quote: If more than one type applies, use the most specific type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Provider type' with no code list and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the page named a classification without saying what the classes are.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the pre-2007 MCS post-20 August 1996 ETP component question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 53
variable_description: The part of an employer termination payment rolled into super that counted towards the superannuation surcharge. It is the output of a formula, not a payment: the ATO sets it as the post-20 August 1996 period of the employment divided by the total period of that employment, multiplied by the eligible termination payment. The question "only applies to rollovers made on or after 1 July 1997", and the surcharge it fed was abolished for contributions from 1 July 2005, so the column empties out in the later years even where redundancies continued.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar apportioned amount for one member account in one financial year, forming one of the components of the total contributed amount rather than sitting outside it.
limitation: It is not the size of the termination payment. A long-serving worker whose employment was mostly before August 1996 shows a small figure on a large payout, so the column measures a taxable slice under a repealed regime rather than the generosity of a redundancy.
rationale: The name expands to the post-20 August 1996 component of an employer eligible termination payment, a numbered question on the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO completion guide gives the apportionment formula and the rollover date restriction.
evidence_quote: This question only applies to rollovers made on or after 1 July 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label, complete with its typo, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is an apportionment formula tied to a surcharge that no longer exists.

value_domain: ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 1 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1
variable_description: The small area the member's residential address falls in, at the finest level ABS routinely publishes. ABS designs an SA1 around a few hundred people: "SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people", and there are 61,845 of them covering Australia without gaps. The address behind it is the one the super fund held for the member, which the fund is required to report where it has one. The SA2, LGA and state columns on the same row are the same address at coarser resolution.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1
value_definition: An eleven-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 code made up of the one-digit state or territory identifier and the Statistical Area Level 1 to 4 identifiers. Thirty-four non-spatial special purpose codes cover populations such as no usual address and migratory.
limitation: A fund's address is a mailing address kept current only as well as the member keeps the fund informed, so a member who moved and did not tell the fund stays in the wrong SA1 for years. Every year of the statement is coded to the 2021 boundaries, so an early record is placed in an area that did not exist in that form at the time.
rationale: The custodian's description says only 'Address variable', and the column name gives the classification and its edition. ABS publishes what an SA1 is, how many there are, the design population and the structure of the code, which is what a reader needs to know whether the column can carry a small-area analysis.
evidence_quote: SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address variable' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so the page did not even name the geography, let alone its resolution.

value_domain: ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: The suburb-scale area for the member's address, and the level at which fund membership can be compared with a published population. ABS says "SA2s are generally the smallest areas used for the release of ABS non-Census of Population and Housing statistics, including Estimated Resident Population", so this is the finest column on the row with a ready denominator. In large urban areas an SA2 is named for the gazetted suburbs it contains, and in rural areas for the locality or town it is associated with. The SA1 column beside it is a finer cut of the same address.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2
value_definition: A nine-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 code made up of the one-digit state or territory identifier and the Statistical Area Level 2 to 4 identifiers, where the SA2 part is a four-digit code assigned alphabetically within an SA3.
limitation: An SA2 built for a few thousand people is a poor unit in remote Australia, where ABS itself notes that an area of that population may be too large and diverse to be meaningful. The column also cannot be joined to the older five-digit short codes, which Edition 3 withdrew.
rationale: The custodian's description is only 'Address variable', and the column name gives the classification and edition. ABS publishes what an SA2 is for, how it is coded and where it works badly, which decides whether this is the right column for area analysis.
evidence_quote: SA2s are generally the smallest areas used for the release of ABS non-Census of Population and Housing statistics, including Estimated Resident Population and Health and Vitals data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address variable' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the geography nor said what makes SA2 the useful level.

value_domain: Member account balance as a withdrawal benefit (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 58
variable_description: How much the member could have taken out of the account, rather than what the account was worth on 30 June. The ATO asks the fund to "show the member's withdrawal benefit as at the last member reporting date", which for most funds is the 30 June annual statement, and the later editions of the form accept the most recent figure the fund holds when it lodges. The field had to be supplied where the fund could accept government co-contributions for the member, so how completely it is filled follows co-contribution eligibility rather than account size.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 58
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance for one member account, measured as the amount payable on withdrawal at the fund's own reporting date rather than at a date common to all funds.
limitation: Balances are not comparable across funds on a single date, and for a defined benefit interest a withdrawal benefit can differ sharply from the value of the pension actually promised. Summing a person's rows gives a total only where every fund they belong to reported.
rationale: The name expands to the super fund membership account balance amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and both the pre-2007 guide and the 2007-08 to 2011-12 instructions define it as the withdrawal benefit at the fund's own reporting date.
evidence_quote: Show the member's withdrawal benefit as at the last member reporting date - for example, the 30 June annual statement to the member.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Account balance' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that the figure is a withdrawal benefit at a fund-chosen date rather than a 30 June balance.

value_domain: Date contributions first went into the account (DDMMYYYY)
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 32
variable_description: The day contributions first started going into this account with this fund, which is not the day the member joined. The ATO defines it as "the date that contributions began to be paid into, or otherwise attributed or credited to, the member's account with the provider". Two dump codes are written into the rules: an unknown opening before 7 May 1997 is reported as 1 January 1900, and one between 7 May 1997 and 1 July 2007 as 30 June 2007. Those two dates therefore carry a large share of the mass and mean not known rather than opened then.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 32
value_definition: A calendar date written DDMMYYYY for one member account, marking the start of contributions to that account with that provider.
limitation: It cannot date the start of a working life or of super membership. A member who consolidates decades of savings into a new fund gets a fresh opening date, so account tenure built from this column understates how long the person has been in the system.
rationale: The name expands to the date the super fund membership account was opened, a numbered question in the member account details section, and the ATO instruction gives both the definition and the two substitute dates to be used when the real date is unknown.
evidence_quote: Provide the date that contributions began to be paid into, or otherwise attributed or credited to, the member's account with the provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Date account opened' with its format and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned about the two substitute dates that dominate the early distribution.

value_domain: MCS account status code
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section D, question 36
variable_description: Whether the account could still take contributions, in the fund's own judgement. The pre-2007 form offered two states, active or closed; from 2013 the ATO replaced them with three codes, O for open and not lost, L for open where the member is a lost member, and C for closed, which "includes those in pension phase". An account paying a pension is therefore reported as closed even though it holds money, which is the trap in reading the column as whether an account exists. An insurance-only account, by contrast, is reported as open.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section D, question 36
value_definition: A short code for one member account in one financial year: active or closed on the earlier statement, and O, L or C from the 2013 form onwards.
limitation: Closed does not mean empty and open does not mean contributed to. The code tracks whether ATO payments can be accepted, so a large pension account reads as closed while a dormant insurance-only account reads as open, and the two vocabularies either side of 2013 are not the same variable.
rationale: The name expands to the super fund membership account status code, a numbered question in the member account details section, and the ATO publishes the code table with worked examples of which accounts are open and which are closed. The custodian's own label already shows the two vocabularies mixed together.
evidence_quote: The member's account is closed (this includes those in pension phase) and will not accept payments from us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's mixed label, 'Account status: Active/Open and not lost/closed', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither listed the codes nor flagged that the vocabulary changed in 2013.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS spouse and child contributions question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 38
variable_description: Super paid in for the member by their spouse, or paid in for a member who is a child under 18, reported as a single figure. The ATO asks the fund to "provide the contributions made for a member by their spouse or made for a member who is a child under 18 years old" and excludes a spouse who is also the member's employer, whose contributions belong in the employer column. From the 2010 statement the definition of spouse widened to include registered relationships and de facto partners of the same or a different sex, so the series is not continuous across 1 July 2009.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 38
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, combining spouse contributions and contributions for a child under 18 without distinguishing them.
limitation: The two components cannot be separated, so a rise could be either spouse contributions or contributions for children. The widened definition of spouse from 2010 adds contributors without any change in behaviour, which makes a break in the series look like a trend.
rationale: The name expands to spouse and child contributions amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction gives the inclusions, the exclusions that route contributions to neighbouring columns, and the date the definition of spouse changed.
evidence_quote: Only apply the changed definition of spouse to MCSs lodged for the 2010 and later financial years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Spouse and child contributions amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the two components are merged or that the definition of spouse changed mid-series.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory identifier
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, Australia (AUS) and State/Territory (S/T)
variable_description: The state or territory of the member's address, at the top of the ABS geographic hierarchy. ABS recognises the eight states and territories plus a ninth category, since "Jervis Bay Territory, and the Territories of Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are included as one spatial unit at the S/T level under the category of Other Territories". The identifier is the leading digit of the SA1 and SA2 codes on the same row, so the three geography columns cannot disagree with one another.
description_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, Australia (AUS) and State/Territory (S/T)
value_definition: A one-digit ASGS state and territory identifier, the highest level of the hierarchy that also produces the SA1 and SA2 codes on the row.
limitation: It is the state the fund had an address in, not the state the member worked or paid tax in, and cross-border commuting is common enough for the two to differ. An overseas or missing address has no identifier at all rather than a code meaning overseas.
rationale: The custodian's description says only 'Address variable', and the column name gives the classification and its vintage. The ABS geography glossary states which units the state and territory level recognises, including the pooling of the external territories, which is the fact a user coding to eight states would otherwise miss.
evidence_quote: Jervis Bay Territory, and the Territories of Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are included as one spatial unit at the S/T level under the category of Other Territories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address variable' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the classification nor mentioned the Other Territories category.

value_domain: MCS supplier-to-provider relationship code
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B, question 11
variable_description: Who prepared and lodged the statement on the fund's behalf, as a one-letter relationship code. The ATO separates self-administration from the kinds of firm that run other people's funds: A means "there is no supplier and the provider is acting on its own behalf in the lodgment of this MCS", while C is an accountancy practice, F a financial planning practice, I an industry administrator, R a retail administrator, S a specialist firm, consultancy or life insurance office, T a tax agent, U an actuarial administrator, L a liquidator, W a controller or administrator and X the trustee of a bankrupt estate. Where the supplier is neither the provider nor its administrator, the field is left blank.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B, question 11
value_definition: A single alphabetic code describing the lodging party's relationship to the reporting provider, constant across every member row in one lodgment.
limitation: It describes the administrator, not the fund, so an industry fund that outsources administration to a retail administrator reports R. The blank is not a residual category: the ATO's rule makes the code inapplicable in a defined case, so blanks cannot be pooled with any code as an other group.
rationale: The name expands to the supplier's relationship with the provider, a numbered question in the provider details section of the statement, and the ATO publishes the full code list along with the rule for leaving it blank. The same list appears in the pre-2007 and the 2007-08 to 2011-12 editions of the form.
evidence_quote: If the supplier is neither the provider's administrator nor the provider itself, leave this code blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and was tagged as a family and household topic, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so the page suggested a personal relationship rather than a lodgment arrangement.

value_domain: De-identified MCS supplier identifier
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), Section A: Supplier information
variable_description: The organisation that lodged the statement, which is very often an administrator rather than the fund itself, as a de-identified key. The ATO describes the supplier as the party supplying the information, "for example, a tax agent, accountant, superannuation administrator or the provider itself". Grouping rows by this key shows how concentrated super administration is in a handful of firms, and comparing it with the provider key shows which funds run their own back office. The relationship code on the same row says which kind of firm it is.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), Section A: Supplier information
value_definition: An opaque scrambled identifier, one value per lodging supplier. Where a fund lodges for itself the supplier and the provider are the same organisation and the relationship code is A.
limitation: It says nothing about the member. A change of key between years usually means the fund changed administrator, a back-office event no member ever sees, so it must not be read as the member changing fund. ABS does not document the scrambling, so the key cannot be matched to a named firm.
rationale: The ATO defines what a supplier is on this form and how it differs from the provider, which is what the identifier stands for. The scrambling is a PLIDA treatment that is not published, so the de-identification part of the reading is inference.
evidence_quote: The supplier is a person or organisation supplying the information on the statement (for example, a tax agent, accountant, superannuation administrator or the provider itself).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Supplier scrambled identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the supplier from the provider on the same row.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage spine identifier (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The fund member the account belongs to, as the key that carries them across the whole asset. One person has one row per account per year, so the rows under a single key are that person's super history across every fund that lodged for them, which is what makes account counts, contribution totals and balance growth possible. ABS builds the Person Linkage Spine from the Medicare Consumer Directory, DOMINO Centrelink records and Personal Income Tax records and links each dataset to the Spine once, so a contribution can be read against the same person's wages, benefits and Census answers. In this package the values are synthetic: consistent across tables but standing for nobody.
description_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure, one value per person, stable across the yearly member contributions tables and across every other dataset linked through the Spine.
limitation: The member is not the contributor. A spouse contribution, an employer contribution and a third-party contribution all sit under the member's key, so this identifier cannot be used to study who is paying. Coverage is also conditional on linkage: an account for a member whose fund did not hold a tax file number may never have reached the Spine and is then unreachable through this key.
rationale: The data item list gives the field as the synthetic member identifier on every member contributions table, and ABS publishes what the Spine is, which datasets build it, what period it covers and why every dataset is linked to it once, which is what determines where this key can and cannot reach.
evidence_quote: The Spine aims to cover all people who were resident in Australia at any point during a given reference period. The current Spine covers January 2006 to June 2025.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Member scrambled identifier' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the key is the PLIDA spine identifier or that a member row does not identify the contributor.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS transferred from reserves, assessable question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 53
variable_description: Money moved out of a fund reserve into the member's account that the law counts as a concessional contribution. The ATO asks for "the amount that the ITAA 1997 includes as a concessional contribution because an amount was allocated to the member's account from a reserve" and warns that "the amount included by the legislation, and so reported here, may be greater than the amount actually allocated to the member's account". The figure therefore counts against the member's concessional cap even though nobody contributed it and the member may never have asked for it.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, being the legislated concessional contribution arising from a reserve allocation rather than the cash actually allocated.
limitation: It is not saving in any ordinary sense, so counting it as a contribution overstates member behaviour. It also cannot be netted against the non-assessable reserve column on the same row, which arises under a different rule and counts against a different cap.
rationale: The name expands to the assessable half of the transferred from reserves amounts question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction states both the legal basis and the gap between the amount reported and the amount allocated.
evidence_quote: The amount included by the legislation, and so reported here, may be greater than the amount actually allocated to the member's account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred from reserve amounts: assessable' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the reported figure can exceed the money that moved.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS transferred from reserves, non-assessable question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 53
variable_description: Money moved out of a fund reserve into the member's account that the law counts as a non-concessional contribution instead. The ATO defines it as "the amount that the ITAA 1997 treats as a non-concessional contribution because an amount was allocated to the member's account from a reserve and not included as assessable income of the fund". The split from the assessable reserve column beside it is a tax classification, turning on whether the fund had to bring the amount into its own income, not on where the money came from or who benefits.
description_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, counting against the member's non-concessional contributions cap rather than the concessional cap.
limitation: A figure here signals a fund with reserves to distribute rather than a member doing anything, so it cannot be read as member behaviour. Reserve allocations are concentrated in small funds and defined benefit schemes, which makes the column heavily skewed across providers.
rationale: The name expands to the non-assessable half of the transferred from reserves amounts question, and the ATO instruction gives the legal test that separates it from the assessable half reported in the neighbouring column.
evidence_quote: Provide the amount that the ITAA 1997 treats as a non-concessional contribution because an amount was allocated to the member's account from a reserve and not included as assessable income of the fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred from reserve amounts: non-assessable' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what divides it from the assessable column on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the pre-2007 MCS total contributed amount question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 50
variable_description: Everything that went into the member's account for the year on the pre-2007 statement, the control total the component columns build up to. For an ordinary member the ATO defines it as employer contributions plus the post-20 August 1996 termination payment component, allocated surplus, personal contributions and other contributions; for a defined benefit member it is the surchargeable contributions plus personal and other contributions. It is reported by the provider that was holding the contributions for the year, so a fund that transferred the money away before 30 June may not be the one reporting it.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 50
value_definition: A whole-dollar total contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, built from the component amount columns on the same row.
limitation: It does not reconcile in every year. The ATO warned that for the year ended 30 June 2006 the total "may not be the sum of the employer and personal contributed amounts reported" because several component questions became optional, so a gap between the total and its parts is a reporting change rather than an error to fix.
rationale: The name expands to the total contributed amount, the first question in the contributed amounts section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO completion guide lists its components separately for accumulation and defined benefit members and flags the year in which the identity breaks.
evidence_quote: For the year ended 30 June 2006, the total contributed amount may not be the sum of the employer and personal contributed amounts reported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Total contributed amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which columns it totals or that the identity fails in 2005-06.

value_domain: Transferred component of the allocated surplus amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 79
variable_description: The slice of an allocated surplus that left the account when the member's money was transferred out. The ATO asks the fund to "show the amount or part thereof of the allocated surplus amount ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred", so it decomposes the transferred total rather than adding a new contribution. Allocated surplus itself is a fund crediting a member with more than an eligible actuary considers reasonable, which is unusual, so a non-zero value here is rare.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 79
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount on the same row, populated only where the member has a transfer-out record for the year.
limitation: It cannot be added to the allocated surplus amount for the year without double counting, because it is carved out of that figure. A zero means either that no surplus was allocated or that the transfer carried none of it, and the row does not say which.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred allocated surplus amount, a numbered question in the contributed amounts transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide defines it as a part of the transferred total and defines its parent question separately.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the allocated surplus amount (as reported at question 54 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred allocated surplus amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a decomposition of another column rather than a contribution in its own right.

value_domain: Transferred component of the employer contributed amount, accumulation (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 76
variable_description: The employer contributions to an accumulation account that went with the money when the member's balance left the fund. Its parent question covers what an accumulation provider reports as taxable contributions made by an employer or another person, together with superannuation guarantee shortfall amounts and Superannuation Holding Accounts amounts the Commissioner paid across. A defined benefit provider leaves the parent question blank, so this transfer column is blank for them too and the defined benefit transfer column beside it carries their figure instead.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 76
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the accumulation employer contribution reported at question 51 for the same member and year.
limitation: It is not employer generosity at the point of exit but the year's employer contributions apportioned to a transfer, so a member who left in July shows almost nothing regardless of salary. The destination fund reports the same money for the receiving account, so adding this across funds double counts.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred employer contribution amount for accumulation, a numbered question in the transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide defines both the transfer question and the parent employer contribution question it draws from.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the employer contributed amount (accumulation) (as reported at question 51 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred employer contribution amount (accumulation)' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a subset of another column or why it is blank for defined benefit funds.

value_domain: Transferred component of the employer contributed amount, defined benefits (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 77
variable_description: The defined benefit employer amount carried out of the fund when the member's benefit was transferred. The parent figure is not cash: a defined benefit provider reports the surchargeable contributions "that constitute the actuarial value of the benefits that accrued to, and the value of the administration expenses and risk benefits provided in respect of, the member". This column apportions that actuarial value to the transfer out, which is why it can be substantial for a member whose employer never paid a visible contribution.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 77
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the defined benefit employer contribution reported at question 52 for the same member and year.
limitation: It is an actuarial construct rather than money that moved, so it cannot be compared with the accumulation transfer column beside it as though the two were the same currency. For the year ended 30 June 2006 the ATO dropped the requirement to calculate notional amounts, so the column can be blank while accrual continued.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred employer contribution amount for defined benefits, a numbered question in the transfer-out section, and the ATO guide defines the parent question as an actuarial value and records the year in which its calculation stopped being required.
evidence_quote: Superannuation (defined benefits) providers must report that part of the total contributed amount that are surchargeable contributions for the financial year that constitute the actuarial value of the benefits that accrued to, and the value of the administration expenses and risk benefits provided in respect of, the member for the financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred employer contribution amount (defined benefits)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is actuarial rather than paid.

value_domain: Transferred component of the other contributed amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 81
variable_description: The residual other contributions that went with the money when the member's balance left the fund. The ATO asks for "the amount or part thereof of the other contributed amount ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred". Because the parent question is defined by exclusion, this column inherits the same fuzziness: government super co-contributions credited during the year travel here rather than in the personal transfer column beside it.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 81
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the other contributed amount reported at question 56 for the same member and year.
limitation: What sits inside it varies by fund, so comparing this column between two providers compares classification practice as much as member experience. It is a subset of the transferred total on the same row and cannot be added to it.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred other contributed amount, a numbered question in the transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide defines both it and the residual parent question it draws from.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the other contributed amount (as reported at question 56 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred other contributed amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it inherits a residual definition from another column.

value_domain: Transferred component of the personal contributed amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 80
variable_description: The member's own contributions that travelled with the balance when it left the fund. The ATO asks for "the amount or part thereof of the personal contributed amount ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred". Because government super co-contribution entitlements were worked out from the personal contribution question, this column decides in practice whether the co-contribution followed the member to the destination fund or was paid to the fund they left.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 80
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the personal contributed amount reported at question 55 for the same member and year.
limitation: It does not distinguish deductible from after-tax personal contributions, so it says nothing about the tax position of the money that moved. It also measures only the current year's contributions inside the transfer, not the balance transferred.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred personal contributed amount, a numbered question in the transfer-out section, and the ATO guide defines it against its parent question, which the same guide ties to the co-contribution calculation.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the personal contributed amount (as reported at question 55 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred personal contributed amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a slice of the transferred total rather than a contribution.

value_domain: Transferred component of the post-20 August 1996 ETP amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 78
variable_description: The surchargeable slice of a rolled-in termination payment that went out again when the balance was transferred. The ATO asks for "the amount or part thereof of the post-20 August 1996 component of an employer ETP ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred". Its parent applies only to rollovers made on or after 1 July 1997 and fed a surcharge abolished for contributions from 1 July 2005, so a non-zero value places the row inside a narrow window of years.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 78
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the post-20 August 1996 termination payment component reported for the same member and year.
limitation: It is not a redundancy payment. The apportionment formula scales the payment by the share of employment falling after August 1996, so a long-tenured worker with a large payout can show almost nothing here while a recent hire shows the lot.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred post-20 August 1996 employer eligible termination payment component, a numbered question in the transfer-out section, and the ATO guide defines both it and the apportionment formula behind its parent question.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the post-20 August 1996 component of an employer ETP (as reported at question 53 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label, typo included, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is an apportioned slice of a payment under a repealed surcharge.

value_domain: Transferred total contributed amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 75
variable_description: How much of the year's total contributions left the fund with the member, and the control total for the transfer-out block. The ATO states that it "cannot be greater than total contributed amount shown at question 50", and its components sit in the columns beside it: employer accumulation, employer defined benefit, termination payment component, allocated surplus, personal and other. The block is completed when contributions leave through a lump sum, a pension, an annuity, a departing Australia superannuation payment or a death benefit.
description_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 75
value_definition: A whole-dollar total for one transfer-out record, bounded above by the total contributed amount reported for the same member account and year.
limitation: It measures contributions that moved, not the balance that moved, so a member rolling decades of savings into a new fund can show a small figure. Its presence also does not mean the member left the system: a death benefit, a departing Australia payment and an ordinary rollover all populate it, and this column alone cannot tell them apart.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred total contributed amount, the first question in the contributed amounts transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide gives the ceiling rule, the component questions and the events that trigger the section.
evidence_quote: Please note that the 'Transferred total contributed amount' cannot be greater than total contributed amount shown at question 50 in Section E: Contributed amounts information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred total contributed amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the transfer block is for or what bounds the figure.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address held against a person on the birth registration file. PERSON_FLAG says whether the row is the child's address, the first parent's or the second parent's, so the identifier is what shows whether the parents were recorded at one address at registration. CNTRY_CDE carries the country where the address is overseas.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so parents sharing a value were registered at one address rather than shown to be a couple. The address is the one recorded at registration and does not follow a later move. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as Address Register ID on the births address table, whose PERSON_FLAG identifies whether the address relates to the child, parent 1 or parent 2. ABS publishes what the Address Register identifier is.
evidence_quote: Identifies if address relates to Child, Parent 1, or Parent 2
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Address Register ID' with no explanation and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Crop area in hectares, ABS agricultural collection
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia, 2021-22, agricultural commodity data item list
variable_description: Hectares of barley grown for grain, the second cereal in most winter rotations and the one that moves when malting premiums or feed demand shift. The ABS item is "Cereal crops - Barley for grain - Area (ha)", which does not separate malting from feed barley. Read it beside the wheat and canola areas on the same row to see the rotation.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia, 2021-22, agricultural commodity data item list
value_definition: A non-negative number of hectares, reported for the financial year against one line of the ABS agricultural collection form.
