There is no code list; the classification is the ABS agricultural commodity item list, and the reporting unit is the ABN-based business on the ABS Business Register.
limitation: The column will not tell you which end use the grain was destined for, and it is not a substitute for revenue: barley area rises in dry starts because it is sown later and cheaper than wheat, so a larger area can accompany a worse season.
rationale: The ABS data item list gives the exact item and unit for barley area in the collection that FLAD is built from.
evidence_quote: Cereal crops - Barley for grain - Area (ha)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the FLAD label 'Area, Barley' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Crop area in hectares, ABS agricultural collection
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22
variable_description: Hectares of beans grown as a field crop, the nitrogen-fixing break crop in the pulse group. FLAD names beans separately from a_other_legumes, which carries lupins, chickpeas, peas and lentils. Because pulses are sown for rotation as much as for the grain price, the area moves with soil nitrogen and disease pressure.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22
value_definition: A non-negative number of hectares, reported for the financial year against one line of the ABS agricultural collection form. There is no code list; the classification is the ABS agricultural commodity item list, and the reporting unit is the ABN-based business on the ABS Business Register.
limitation: It does not distinguish field or faba beans from the vegetable beans reported in the vegetable items, so a horticultural business and a broadacre grower can both appear in the column meaning different things.
rationale: The ABS methodology page defines the collection, its ABN-based reporting unit and its financial-year reference, which govern this item.
evidence_quote: Estimates from the 2021-22 Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodity Survey are based on a response rate of 68% from a sample of 24,871 agricultural businesses selected.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Area, Beans' with the generic sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Planted area of bearing age in hectares, ABS agricultural collection
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia, 2021-22, agricultural commodity data item list
variable_description: Hectares of bananas old enough to fruit, which is the part of a plantation that can earn revenue this year. There is no code list; the classification is the ABS agricultural commodity item list, and the reporting unit is the ABN-based business on the ABS Business Register.
limitation: It cannot tell you what the crop yielded or whether it was harvested at all; production in tonnes is a separate item and a failed crop still shows its sown area. Nor is a zero evidence that no wheat was grown: in a non-census year the business may simply not have been sampled.
rationale: The ABS agricultural commodity data item list names the exact collection item behind this column and gives its unit.
evidence_quote: Cereal crops - Wheat for grain - Area (ha)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the FLAD label 'Area, Wheat' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the area is the grain crop only, nor that a non-census year has no observation.

value_domain: Programme participation flag (0 or 1)
value_source: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, Agri-Business Expansion Initiative
variable_description: Flags that the business started receiving support under the Agri-Business Expansion Initiative in that financial year, on Austrade's exporter microdata. The department describes it as an investment "to help Australian agribusinesses expand and diversify their export markets", delivered jointly with Austrade after trade disruption in 2020. It marks a commencement, so a firm supported over several years carries the 1 only once.
description_source: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, Agri-Business Expansion Initiative
value_definition: A binary numeric flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, carried once per business and financial year in the Microdata on Australian Exporters panel, which BLADE holds for 2010-11 onwards.
limitation: A zero before 2020-21 means the programme did not exist yet, not that the firm declined support, so the column cannot be used as an untreated comparison over the whole panel. Participation is also self-selected among firms already engaged with Austrade, which is not a random assignment.
rationale: The department's programme page establishes what ABEI is, when it was announced and who delivers it; the ABS BLADE data page establishes that the MAX panel runs from 2010-11.
evidence_quote: Announced on 23 December 2020, ABEI is part of a long-term strategy and commitment by the government to help achieve sustainable growth and resilience in our agribusiness exports.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about commencing the ABEI programme with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what the programme is or that it did not exist before 2020-21.

value_domain: Jurisdiction coverage flag for an enterprise agreement (0 or 1)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Flags that this federal enterprise agreement operates in the Australian Capital Territory. DEWR records "State or Territories covered" as one of about 200 items held for each agreement, so a national agreement sets this and the other jurisdiction flags together rather than choosing one. It describes the agreement's reach, not the employer's head office.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A binary numeric flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, on the agreement record rather than on the business. The jurisdiction flags are not mutually exclusive and several can be set on one agreement.
limitation: It gives no headcount: an agreement covering 5,000 staff nationally with two in Canberra looks the same as one covering an ACT-only workplace. Only federal enterprise agreements are in the database, so ACT public sector and other non-federal instruments are absent regardless of this flag.
rationale: The DEWR page for the Workplace Agreements Database lists the jurisdictions covered as a recorded item and states which agreements are in scope.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indicates whether an agreement operates in the ACT' with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the flags are non-exclusive or that only federal agreements are covered.

value_domain: Declaration on the R&D Tax Incentive registration application (yes, no or not applicable)
value_source: business.gov.au, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The company's own declaration, made on its R&D Tax Incentive registration, that it is claiming work the law bars from being core R&D. The form asks "Will the company be including activities that are excluded from being a core activity in this application?", and a yes means the registration includes activities that section 355-25(2) of the ITAA 1997 excludes - market research, prospecting, management studies, social science research, patent administration, standards compliance, reverse engineering and internal-use software - claimed instead as supporting activities. It is a claim made at registration, not a finding about the work.
description_source: business.gov.au, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A three-state categorical: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and N/A. On the application form the yes option reads "Yes, as supporting activities", so the affirmative response is itself a claim about how the activity is being registered.
limitation: Registration is self-assessed and does not establish eligibility, so a yes is not evidence that the excluded activities qualified as supporting R&D; the department and the ATO can review and disallow them afterwards. The N/A also has two causes that cannot be told apart here: the question not displaying on a dynamic form, and a registration year in which it was not asked.
rationale: The business.gov.au application questions document reproduces this exact registration question, its response options and the statutory list of excluded activities behind it.
evidence_quote: The law, at s 355-25(2) of the ITAA 1997, lists those activities that cannot be core R&D activities for the R&D Tax Incentive
supersedes_rationale: The entry paraphrased the form question and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never named the statutory exclusions or flagged that registration is self-assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
variable_description: Capital gains on forestry managed investment scheme interests that were active assets, worked out under the discount method. That method needs at least twelve months of ownership, and the ATO states that "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies", so an incorporated grower shows nothing here however long it held the interest. The OF prefix on the BLADE label is the old form's wording for this box.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: Because companies cannot use the discount method, this column is a proxy for entity type as much as for holding period, and comparing it across a company and a trust compares two different rule sets rather than two behaviours.
rationale: The ATO CGT schedule instructions state which entities can use the discount method and define the Active assets block that gates this cell.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the old-form schedule label and the generic no-value-list sentence, with nothing on the company exclusion or the active asset test.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on forestry managed investment scheme interests that were active assets, worked out under the indexation method. The ATO allows that method only "if you acquired a CGT asset before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999", so for a forestry scheme interest this cell is rarely used. Gains reach the active assets block only if they qualify for the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption or the small business roll-over.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: A nil here is close to uninformative, because the acquisition date test rules the indexation method out for almost every modern forestry interest, so the absence of a figure says nothing about whether the firm held forestry assets. The forestry row was also dropped when the schedule was redesigned, which breaks any long series.
rationale: The ATO CGT schedule instructions define the Active assets block and its concession test, and the CGT guide definitions fix when the indexation method is available.
evidence_quote: The indexation method is one of the ways to calculate your capital gain if you acquired a CGT asset before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw 'OF:' schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Capital gains on forestry managed investment scheme interests that were active assets and fell to the 'other' method. That is the residual calculation, used when neither indexation nor the discount applies, so for a company it is where essentially all forestry interest gains land. Harvest proceeds and sales of the interest are the events that produce them.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: It misses most of the cash a forestry investor sees: the ATO treats thinning receipts as assessable income rather than capital, so those amounts never reach this column. A nil therefore does not mean the scheme produced nothing.
rationale: The ATO CGT guide sets out the CGT treatment of forestry managed investment scheme interests, including which receipts are capital and which are ordinary income.
evidence_quote: Amounts you receive for thinning are excluded from the CGT treatment of your forestry interest. These amounts are included in your assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with the generic sentence in both slots, so it never separated capital proceeds from thinning income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
variable_description: Capital gains under the discount method on active assets other than shares, units and real estate, together with any other CGT event. In practice this is the goodwill cell for a trust or partnership selling a business it has run for more than a year. Companies cannot use the discount method, so an incorporated seller reports the same sale in the 'other' method column.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: It is a gross gain before the 50% discount and before any small business concession, so it is several steps away from what the vendor keeps, and it should not be compared with a net proceeds figure.
rationale: The ATO CGT schedule instructions define the Active assets block, the residual asset row and the entities that may use the discount method.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the old-form label and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital gains under the indexation method on active assets that are neither shares, units nor real estate, plus any other CGT event. This is where goodwill sits, which for a small business sale is often the largest single gain. Indexation restricts it to assets acquired before 21 September 1999, so it captures long-established businesses.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: The row is a catch-all that mixes goodwill, plant, contractual rights and CGT events that involve no asset at all, so a figure here cannot be attributed to any particular kind of transaction.
rationale: The ATO CGT guide definitions fix the indexation method's acquisition test, and the schedule instructions define the residual asset row and the active asset restriction.
evidence_quote: The indexation method is one of the ways to calculate your capital gain if you acquired a CGT asset before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said what the residual row contains.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
variable_description: Capital gains under the 'other' method on active assets that are neither shares, units nor real estate, and on any other CGT event. The 'other' method is the residual calculation, used when neither indexation nor the discount is available, so for a company selling business goodwill this is the cell that fills. Read with the indexation and discount cells on the same row it separates entity type and holding period.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: The largest small business gains are missing from the whole active assets block: the ATO directs gains covered by the 15-year exemption to item 8 alone, so a firm that sold up after fifteen years shows nothing here.
rationale: The ATO CGT schedule instructions define the three calculation methods, the Active assets restriction and the separate treatment of the 15-year exemption.
evidence_quote: Capital gains to which the small business 15-year exemption applies aren't included on the CGT summary worksheet.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, with nothing on the 15-year exemption gap.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate that was an active asset of the business, worked out under the discount method. That method needs twelve months of ownership and is closed to companies, so the usual filer here is a family trust or partnership selling the premises it trades from. It is a gross gain: the discount itself is applied later in the schedule.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule instructions, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: A nil does not mean the business sold no property. A sale that failed the active asset test, or that qualified for none of the three concessions, is reported in the non-active assets columns instead, and one that qualified for the 15-year exemption is reported only at item 8.
rationale: The ATO CGT schedule instructions state which gains belong in the Active assets columns and where the excluded ones go instead.
evidence_quote: At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the old-form label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained where a non-qualifying property sale goes.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate that was an active asset of the business, worked out under the indexation method. The ATO limits that method to assets "acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999", so a figure here marks a long-held business property. Active asset means property used in running the business, not property held to rent out.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount from one cell of the capital gains item on the CGT schedule, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The row fixes the asset class and the column fixes the calculation method; the trailing letter in the column name follows the label letter printed beside the box on the schedule.
limitation: Where both methods are open the taxpayer chooses between them, so the split between this column and the discount-method column is partly an election and cannot be read as a fact about the asset.
rationale: The ATO CGT guide definitions fix the acquisition-date test for the indexation method, and the schedule instructions define the Active assets restriction.
evidence_quote: The indexation method is one of the ways to calculate your capital gain if you acquired a CGT asset before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the 'OF:' real estate label with the generic no-value-list sentence duplicated, and never said what makes real estate an active asset.

value_domain: Dollar amount of active-asset real estate capital gains, other method, on the CGT schedule
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains the business made in the year on real estate that is an active asset, worked out under the 'other' method. The ATO restricts this block to concession claimants: "At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions", namely the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over. The trailing letter of the BLADE name is the schedule label, and the OF prefix on the label is the old form's wording for an item whose schedule was later redesigned.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount for one cell of the CGT schedule grid: the real estate row, the active assets block, the 'other' method column. It is gross of current year capital losses, of the small business concessions themselves and of any CGT discount.
limitation: A zero here is not evidence that the firm sold no property. Real estate gains only reach this column when the entity is claiming one of the three concessions, gains covered by the 15-year exemption never appear on the worksheet, and a series that spans the old-form to new-form change is not continuous.
rationale: The label names a defined cell of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO instructions define which gains belong in the active assets block and what the 'other' method is.
evidence_quote: At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF label text as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what an active asset is or why the concessions gate the column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of active-asset share and unit capital gains, discount method, on the CGT schedule
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts that are active assets, worked out under the discount method, so the holdings were owned at least twelve months. Shares qualify only conditionally: the ATO says "A share and an interest in a trust can also be active assets if certain conditions are met." Read beside the indexation and other-method columns on the same row, this column separates long-held equity disposals from short-held ones.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount for the shares and units row of the active assets block, discount method column. The discount percentage has not been applied at this point, so the figure is the gross gain rather than the discounted one.
limitation: The column does not show the firm's equity portfolio turnover. It is confined to disposals the entity is treating as active assets for a small business concession, so an operating company that also holds a passive share parcel reports that parcel in the non-active block instead, where BLADE holds it under a different variable.
rationale: The label names the shares and units row of the active assets block under the discount method, and the ATO instructions define both the active asset test for shares and the twelve-month condition on the discount method.
evidence_quote: A share and an interest in a trust can also be active assets if certain conditions are met.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the schedule label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that shares are active assets only conditionally or that the discount is not yet applied.

value_domain: Dollar amount of active-asset share and unit capital gains, indexation method, on the CGT schedule
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains on active-asset shares and units worked out by indexing the cost base rather than by discounting the gain. The indexation column exists inside the active assets block: the ATO directs that a trust gain reduced by the small business 50% active asset reduction be grossed up and included "in row 7 at Active assets under the Capital gains - indexation method or Capital gains - 'other' method." Indexation applies only to assets acquired before the 1999 change to the capital gains rules, so this column thins out as those holdings are sold down.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount for the shares and units row of the active assets block, indexation method column. It is gross of losses and the small business concessions, and unlike the discount column it carries no later halving.
limitation: A rising or falling value here is mostly about vintage, not about business behaviour: only assets held from before the 1999 rule change can use indexation, so the column measures the run-off of a legacy stock rather than current investment activity. It cannot be added to the discount column without double counting the same disposal choice.
rationale: The label names the indexation method column of the shares and units row in the active assets block, and the ATO instructions confirm that the active assets block carries an indexation column and how amounts enter it.
evidence_quote: Include the result in row 7 at Active assets under the Capital gains - indexation method or Capital gains - 'other' method.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label wording and the duplicated generic sentence, so it did not explain that indexation is closed to assets acquired after 1999.

value_domain: Dollar amount of active-asset share and unit capital gains, other method, on the CGT schedule
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains on active-asset shares and units that used neither the discount nor the indexation method, which in practice means holdings sold inside twelve months. The ATO defines an active asset broadly: "Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business)." Against the discount column on the same row, this column is the closest the schedule comes to marking short-held equity disposals.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount for the shares and units row of the active assets block, 'other' method column. No CGT discount attaches to these gains, so the figure needs no later halving, but the small business concessions have not yet been applied.
limitation: Short holding is an inference, not a recorded fact: the column does not carry a holding period, and an entity may also land here after choosing not to use an available method. It also says nothing about losses, which are applied later in the schedule and can extinguish the gain entirely.
rationale: The label names the other-method column of the shares and units row in the active assets block, and the ATO instructions define the active asset test and the method ordering.
evidence_quote: Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the schedule label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish this column from the discount and indexation columns beside it.

value_domain: Imputed business address role (operating, postal, accountant)
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2019 - June 2023
variable_description: Says what a location row on a business actually is: an operating site, a postal box, an accountant's office, or both of the last two. The classification exists because a firm can hold several addresses at once - the ABS notes that "Businesses can operate in more than one geographical location and be represented by a single ABN/TAU" and that "some locations data at the SA1 level are available via the ABS BLADE product". The empty category is a residual for locations research has not yet resolved, and the ABS treats it as most likely the main operating location.
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2019 - June 2023
value_definition: A short categorical code, imputed by the ABS rather than reported by the business. The domain has four states: unclassified (blank), POSTAL, ACCOUNTANT, and the combined POSTAL, ACCOUNTANT.
limitation: The classification is an imputation, so a site flagged as an accountant's office may still be a genuine workplace and an unclassified site may be a mail drop that research has not yet caught. Counting employment or output to the geography of unclassified rows will therefore attribute activity to head offices and agents' premises.
rationale: The ABS business counts methodology documents multi-location businesses on the ABS Business Register and points to BLADE as the product carrying the underlying location detail, which is the population this column classifies.
evidence_quote: Businesses can operate in more than one geographical location and be represented by a single ABN/TAU. These are referred to as multi-location businesses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'Imputed business address type' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it never warned that the categories are inferred.

value_domain: ABS integration run reference for the Agricultural Indicative module
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Records which ABS integration run produced the agricultural indicative row, not anything about the farm business. The ABS lists this module as covering 2010-11 to 2020-21, so the version stamp distinguishes reruns within a fixed and now closed window. Treat it as provenance metadata alongside the substantive agricultural items on the same row.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: An eight character alphanumeric string of the form inNNN_vN, for example in129_v1, where the first part identifies the integration project and the suffix the version within it.
limitation: It is not a reference period and not a quality flag. Two rows carrying different versions can describe the same financial year, and the version string cannot be mapped to any published ABS release, so it will not tell you what changed between runs.
rationale: The ABS page confirms the Agricultural Indicative module and its year coverage in BLADE; the version item itself is an internal ABS reference with no published documentation, so the reading of the string is inferred from its format.
evidence_quote: Agricultural Indicative data items: 2010-11 to 2020-21
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which module the stamp belongs to or that it carries no analytical content.

value_domain: Average annualised percentage wage increase in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes
variable_description: The average yearly percentage rise in base pay promised by this enterprise agreement, spread over the agreement's effective life. It is deliberately narrow: "AAWI data examine only increases to the base rate of pay, and do not take into account allowances and bonus payments that are paid separate to the base wage", and DEWR uses the effective rather than the formal duration as the denominator. It is a term of the agreement covering the firm's employees, not the wages the firm actually paid.
description_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes
value_definition: A percentage per year, unweighted at the agreement level. Flat dollar increases are converted using average weekly ordinary time earnings for the relevant ANZSIC division and quarter before entering the average.
limitation: A zero does not mean the agreement had no pay rises. Agreements whose increases cannot be quantified, such as those tied to future Fair Work Commission minimum wage decisions or to the CPI, are excluded from the estimate, so the population with a usable AAWI is a selected subset of agreements.
rationale: The DEWR technical notes define AAWI, its formula, its denominator and its exclusions for the Workplace Agreements Database, which is the source of this BLADE module.
evidence_quote: Estimates of AAWI generally exclude increases paid in the form of conditional performance pay, one-off bonuses, profit sharing or share acquisition, as these data cannot readily be either quantified or annualised.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording alone with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that the denominator is effective duration or that non-quantifiable agreements drop out.

value_domain: Yes flag for CPI-indexed allowances in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Marks agreements that index employee allowances to the Consumer Price Index rather than fixing them in dollars. Indexation shifts inflation risk from the worker to the employer. Coverage starts with agreements made on or after 1 January 2011 because DEWR revises the condition set over time: "The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database." Allowances sit outside the base rate, so this flag is independent of the agreement's wage increase.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y for yes. There is no explicit N: an agreement without CPI-linked allowances is simply not coded.
limitation: Absence is ambiguous. A blank can mean the agreement has no CPI-linked allowances, or that it predates 1 January 2011 and the field was not being collected at all, so a time series of the flag traces the collection rule as much as bargaining practice.
rationale: DEWR maintains the Workplace Agreements Database, states that its condition fields are reviewed annually and do not span the full series, and supplies the historical subset that BLADE holds.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence and repeated the generic no-value-list line, so it did not explain that a blank conflates 'no' with 'not collected'.

value_domain: Yes flag for annualised salary arrangements in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
variable_description: Marks agreements that roll penalty rates, overtime and similar entitlements into a single salary for some or all employees. The DEWR framework describes the arrangement as one where "The agreement partially or completely absorbs overtime payments and incorporates them into a loaded salary (sometimes called an annualised salary)." For a firm this changes the shape of the wage bill rather than only its level, since hours worked no longer map to separate loadings.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y for yes, coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2014.
limitation: The flag does not say who is on the arrangement or how much is absorbed: 'some or all employees' covers both a single executive class and a whole workforce. Because coding stopped for agreements made from 2014, a later agreement with an identical clause carries no flag.

value_domain: Yes flag for single-day annual leave access in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)

This is usually found in the family/carer's leave section of an agreement", and dates it: "First coded in 2014 (though was also coded up to the end of 2011)." That gap explains the odd coverage note attached to the column.

value_domain: Yes flag for flexible or facilitative annual leave provisions in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
variable_description: Marks agreements that place no clause-level restriction on when annual leave can be taken, leaving access to be settled between the employer and the individual. DEWR's definition is that "The use of and access to annual leave for employees is not limited by any provision in the agreement. Facilitative means that access to the condition or any change over access to the condition is negotiated between the employer and employee." It is a flag about the absence of a rule, which is why it can coexist with the more specific leave flags on the same agreement.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y for yes, sitting under the annual leave header group of the Workplace Agreements Database condition fields.
limitation: Flexibility on paper is not access in practice: a facilitative clause devolves the decision to a bargain between one employee and the employer, so the flag cannot tell you whether leave was actually taken more freely at that firm.
rationale: The DEWR framework carries this field with the definition the custodian's metadata reproduces, and places it in the annual leave group.
evidence_quote: The use of and access to annual leave for employees is not limited by any provision in the agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the custodian's definition with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never noted that the flag records the absence of a restriction rather than a positive entitlement.

value_domain: Weeks of annual leave for non-shift workers under an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)

The reference point is the statutory minimum, which DEWR states as "4 weeks for non-shift workers, and 5 weeks for shift workers", so a value above four marks an above-minimum entitlement for ordinary day workers. Read it against the shift worker column on the same agreement, which is usually a week higher.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
value_definition: A count of weeks, with 111111111 reserved to mean the quantity varies or is unknown rather than a number of weeks. Coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2011.
limitation: The sentinel will destroy any average that treats the column as numeric, since 111111111 weeks is not a quantity. The value is also an entitlement written into an agreement, not leave taken or accrued, and it stops at agreements made from 2011.
rationale: The DEWR framework documents the annual leave quantum fields and states the National Employment Standards baseline that gives the column its meaning.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual leave per year exceeds the entitlements provided in the NES (4 weeks for non-shift workers, and 5 weeks for shift workers).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's sentence and the generic line twice, so it did not warn that 111111111 is a sentinel or name the four week baseline.

value_domain: Weeks of annual leave for shift workers under an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
variable_description: The number of weeks of annual leave the agreement grants shift workers, whose statutory floor is a week higher than for day workers. DEWR sets that floor at "4 weeks for non-shift workers, and 5 weeks for shift workers", so five is the baseline against which this column should be read. A firm with no shift work will have nothing coded here even where its non-shift column is populated.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset (2021 data collection framework)
value_definition: A count of weeks, with 111111111 reserved for a varying or unknown quantity. Coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2011.
limitation: A blank is not zero leave. It usually means the agreement covers no shift workers, so comparing populated shift and non-shift columns across firms compares a subset of shift-employing workplaces against all workplaces.
rationale: The DEWR framework documents the annual leave quantum fields and gives the five week shift worker baseline in the National Employment Standards.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual leave per year exceeds the entitlements provided in the NES (4 weeks for non-shift workers, and 5 weeks for shift workers).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence with the duplicated generic line, so it did not explain the five week baseline or what a blank means.

value_domain: Yes flag for annual leave loading in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Marks agreements that pay a loading on top of ordinary wages while an employee is on annual leave, commonly 17.5 per cent. It is a cost item for the firm that sits outside the base rate and therefore outside the agreement's average annualised wage increase. Coding stopped for agreements made from 1 January 2012, consistent with DEWR's practice that "The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database."

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 class code of the exported commodity
value_source: ABS, Characteristics of Australian Exporters methodology, 2019-20 financial year
variable_description: The industry that most likely produced the exported good, not the industry of the firm that exported it. The ABS derives it by concordance: "Industry of the commodity is derived from Merchandise trade data on an Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC) basis, which is concorded to Australia and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC), 2006." A wholesaler shipping processed food therefore carries a food manufacturing code on the export row and a wholesale trade code on its own business record.

value_definition: A four digit ANZSIC 2006 class code, the most detailed level of the classification, attached to the commodity rather than to the business.

The ABS is explicit that "the exporting business represents the owner of the goods at the time of export and not necessarily the producer", so this column must not be used as the exporter's own industry.
rationale: The ABS exporters methodology documents the AHECC to ANZSIC 2006 concordance that produces a commodity-level industry code in the merchandise trade data BLADE holds.
evidence_quote: Industry of the commodity is derived from Merchandise trade data on an Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC) basis, which is concorded to Australia and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC), 2006.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about product level ANZSIC with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish industry of the commodity from industry of the exporter.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 class code inferred from company web text
value_source: Glass.AI, The Australian Government (DISR) uses Glass.AI to research emerging industries

On a business that also carries an ABS-assigned ANZSIC code, the two can disagree, and the disagreement is the point of the module.

value_definition: A four character industry code following ANZSIC 2006 at the class level, stored as character rather than numeric so that leading zeros survive.
limitation: It is a machine reading of what a company says about itself online, so it inherits the site's marketing language and its currency. A firm with no website, a stale website or a parent-company site will be coded poorly or not at all, which biases the module towards visible, self-promoting businesses.
rationale: The vendor that produced the underlying classification describes the method and its use with Australian government microdata, which is the Emerging Industries module the ABS lists in BLADE.
evidence_quote: In a first for Australia, DISR combined Glass.AI's web-scale research algorithms with econometric methods and government microdata.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'ANZSIC code derived by glass.ai' with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not say that the code comes from web text and may contradict the register code.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 class code of the R&D tax incentive registrant

Since the incentive is claimed by the head company of a consolidated group, the code describes the registrant, which may be a holding company rather than the operating unit doing the research.

value_definition: A four digit ANZSIC 2006 class code. The classification is hierarchical, with an alphabetic division, a two digit subdivision, a three digit group and this four digit class.

supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's sentence and the generic no-value-list line in both fields, so it did not flag that the code is self-nominated by the registrant and describes the firm rather than the research.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 division name of the workplace covered by an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes

limitation: Division is a very coarse cut: a single agreement can cover workplaces spanning several detailed industries, and the database records industry only to division and subdivision, so it will not support a class-level industry analysis of bargaining.
rationale: The DEWR technical notes state which edition of ANZSIC the Workplace Agreements Database uses, from when, and why the division matters to the wage calculations.
evidence_quote: From the June quarter 2009, Trends uses ANZSIC 2006 divisions for data presented by industry, while previous releases used ANZSIC 1993 divisions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not record the 2009 change of classification edition or the coarseness of division.

value_domain: Date a patent application was received by IP Australia
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD) 2019, table IPGOD 103 Patents Application Information
variable_description: The day the patent application entered IP Australia's system, which anchors every later deadline on the file. IPGOD, the public release of the same registry, holds this in its patents application table and describes the collection as "over 100 years of registry data on all intellectual property (IP) rights administered by IP Australia". For a firm it dates the moment the invention was formally lodged, not the moment the research was done.

value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, where the year is a calendar year rather than a financial year.
limitation: It is not the priority date. An application claiming an earlier foreign priority, or entering the national phase from a PCT filing, carries an Australian arrival date well after the date that determines novelty, so using this column as the invention date will systematically place inventions too late.
rationale: IPGOD is IP Australia's public release of the registry data behind IPRAPID and documents the patents application information table this date belongs to.
evidence_quote: The Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD) includes over 100 years of registry data on all intellectual property (IP) rights administered by IP Australia.

value_domain: R&D registration scope: head company, subsidiary members, or both
value_source: ATO, Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive
variable_description: Says which part of a corporate group the registration covers, which decides how the R&D on the row maps onto operating businesses. Tax law collapses the group for this purpose: "If you are the head company of a consolidated group or MEC group, your subsidiary members are treated as part of you (the head company) for as long as they remain part of the consolidated or MEC group for income tax purposes." A registration recorded against the head company alone can therefore describe research physically done inside subsidiaries.
description_source: ATO, Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive
value_definition: A three state categorical field: the head company, subsidiary members, or the head company and subsidiary members.
limitation: It does not identify where the research happened. Attributing group-level R&D to the head company's industry or location will misplace activity carried out by subsidiaries, and the subsidiary link has to be picked up from the separate subsidiary key table.
rationale: The ATO sets out how the R&D tax incentive applies to consolidated and MEC groups, which is the distinction this field records on the registration.
evidence_quote: If you are the head company of a consolidated group or MEC group, your subsidiary members are treated as part of you (the head company) for as long as they remain part of the consolidated or MEC group for income tax purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the three response options as its description with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not explain why the group structure matters to what the row measures.

value_domain: ASIC external administration or controller appointment type
value_source: ASIC, How to interpret ASIC's corporate insolvency statistics
variable_description: Names the kind of formal insolvency appointment made over the company, which is the difference between a wind-up, a rescue attempt and a secured creditor taking control. A company can hold more than one at a time and can move between them: ASIC notes that "a company can be under more than one form of external administration or controller appointment at any one time and can progress from one type to another". The type is taken from the notification lodged with ASIC, chiefly the Form 505.
description_source: ASIC, How to interpret ASIC's corporate insolvency statistics
value_definition: Free text drawn from ASIC's appointment categories, covering liquidation (court, creditors' voluntary, provisional, simplified), voluntary administration and deeds of company arrangement, restructuring and restructuring plans, receivers, controllers and managing controllers, and scheme administrators.
limitation: The same appointment appears under several spellings, so 'Creditors' voluntary liquidation' and 'creditors voluntary winding up' are one category written two ways and must be collapsed before counting. An appointment is also not the same as failure: members' voluntary liquidations wind up solvent companies, and a restructuring can end with the company still trading.
rationale: ASIC publishes the appointment type field, its source form and the way appointments accumulate over one company, which is what the BLADE insolvency module carries.
evidence_quote: As a company can be under more than one form of external administration or controller appointment at any one time and can progress from one type to another, these statistics can include a company more than once.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Type of insolvency appointment' and a long unstructured value list with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not warn that the list contains duplicate spellings of the same category.

value_domain: ABS integration run reference for the ASIC insolvency module
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Records which ABS integration run produced the insolvency row, not anything about the company's administration. The ABS lists ASIC insolvency data in BLADE from 2000-01 to present, so unlike the closed modules this stamp continues to advance with each refresh. It is the field to check when insolvency counts move between two extracts of the same year.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: An eight character alphanumeric string of the form inNNN_vN, for example in162_v1, identifying the integration project and the version within it.
limitation: It cannot tell you what changed. ASIC itself revises appointment records after lodgment, so a shift between versions may be a correction at ASIC, a change in ABS linkage, or both, and the version string does not distinguish them.
rationale: The ABS page confirms the ASIC insolvency module and its coverage in BLADE; the version item is an internal ABS reference with no published documentation, so its reading is inferred from the format.
evidence_quote: ASIC Insolvency data: 2000-01 to present
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which module the stamp covers or why it matters for revisions.

value_domain: Yes flag for conditional wage increases in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes
variable_description: Marks agreements in which at least one pay rise is contingent, typically on productivity changes or on meeting targets. The increase is promised rather than guaranteed. This matters for the wage measure on the same agreement, because DEWR excludes such amounts: "Estimates of AAWI generally exclude increases paid in the form of conditional performance pay, one-off bonuses, profit sharing or share acquisition, as these data cannot readily be either quantified or annualised." A firm can therefore show a low average annualised wage increase and still have substantial conditional pay on the table.
description_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y for yes, set when any one of the agreement's increases carries a condition.
limitation: The flag is binary and says nothing about size or likelihood: one small conditional component sets it just as a wholly conditional wage structure does. It also does not record whether the condition was met, so it cannot be used to measure pay actually received.
rationale: The DEWR technical notes explain how conditional increases are treated in the Workplace Agreements Database wage estimates, which is the reason this flag exists.
evidence_quote: Estimates of AAWI generally exclude increases paid in the form of conditional performance pay, one-off bonuses, profit sharing or share acquisition, as these data cannot readily be either quantified or annualised.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's explanatory sentence with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not connect the flag to the exclusion from the wage increase measure.

value_domain: Yes flag for flat dollar wage increases in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes
variable_description: Marks agreements that express at least one pay rise as a dollar amount rather than as a percentage. Flat amounts compress relativities, being worth proportionally more to lower paid staff. DEWR has to convert these before they can be averaged: flat dollar increases "are converted to a percentage using average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE), drawn from ABS, 6302.0 - Average Weekly Earnings, Australia) for the relevant ANZSIC industry division and quarter". The agreement's own average annualised wage increase therefore depends on an external earnings benchmark for the industry, not on the firm's own wages.
description_source: DEWR, Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining - Technical Notes
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y for yes, set when any increase in the agreement is stated as a dollar figure.
limitation: Where this flag is set, the percentage wage increase on the same agreement is partly an ABS industry average rather than a firm-level fact, so treating that percentage as observed firm behaviour overstates its precision. The flag itself carries no dollar amount.
rationale: The DEWR technical notes document the AWOTE conversion applied to flat dollar increases, which is precisely the case this flag identifies.
evidence_quote: Flat dollar increases are converted to a percentage using average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE), drawn from ABS, 6302.0 - Average Weekly Earnings, Australia) for the relevant ANZSIC industry division and quarter
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not spell out that the conversion imports an industry average into a firm-level number.

value_domain: Count of claims in an Australian patent application
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD) 2019
variable_description: How many separate claims the patent document makes, counted from the claim text rather than reported by the applicant. Claim count is the usual rough measure of how much ground a patent tries to hold, and it also drives cost, since IP Australia charges excess claim fees above a threshold. It sits beside the examination fields on the same row, so it can be read against whether and when the applicant pushed the case to examination.

Count is also a weak proxy for scope: one broad independent claim can cover more than twenty narrow dependent ones.
rationale: IPGOD is IP Australia's public release of the registry and text data behind IPRAPID, and documents the patents tables from which claim text measures are derived.
evidence_quote: The Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD) includes over 100 years of registry data on all intellectual property (IP) rights administered by IP Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Number of claims in Australian patent' with the generic no-value-list line in both fields, so it did not note that claims change during examination or that count is a poor scope measure.

evidence_quote: It also has derived information about the applicants who filed these IP rights, to allow for research and analysis at the regional, business and individual level.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the same template sentence as its nine siblings with the generic no-value-list line, so it did not say which rank it holds or that filing is not research.

value_domain: Deidentified ABN of the applicant on the ninth nearest patent application by text similarity
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD) 2019
variable_description: Identifies the firm behind the ninth most similar patent application to the one on this row, the second-last of the neighbour columns. It is chiefly a sensitivity column: including or excluding it should not change a well-founded result about technological proximity. Where it names a business that appears nowhere else in the set, the neighbourhood is already breaking down.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD) 2019
value_definition: A ten character alphanumeric deidentified ABN, the ninth-ranked entry in an ordered family of ten neighbour columns on the same row.

rationale: IPGOD documents the IP Australia patent text and applicant tables behind these derived similarity columns; the ranking is inferred from the ordered family of ten variables.
evidence_quote: It also has derived information about the applicants who filed these IP rights, to allow for research and analysis at the regional, business and individual level.

value_domain: Deidentified ABN of a research service provider or cooperative research centre
value_source: ATO, Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive
variable_description: Names the external research organisation a claimant paid, either a registered research service provider or a cooperative research centre. These two routes are the exception that lets small claims through: below the ordinary spending floor an offset is still available for "contracted expenditure incurred to a Research Service Provider (RSP) for services within a research field for which the RSP is registered under the IR&D Act" and for "expenditure incurred as a monetary contribution under the Co-operative Research Centre (CRC) program". A populated value therefore marks research the firm bought in rather than performed itself.
description_source: ATO, Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive
value_definition: A ten character alphanumeric deidentified ABN, on the same key as the business spine, so the provider can be traced as a business in its own right.
limitation: It does not carry the amount contracted or the research field, and it does not distinguish a provider engaged for a small piece of testing from one conducting the whole project. A blank does not mean the firm did all its own research, since only RSP and CRC arrangements are captured here.
rationale: The ATO defines the registered research service provider and cooperative research centre routes under the R&D tax incentive, which is the relationship this key records.
evidence_quote: contracted expenditure incurred to a Research Service Provider (RSP) for services within a research field for which the RSP is registered under the IR&D Act. The RSP can't be an associate of the R&D entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Identifier - deidentified RSP or CRC ABN' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain what a research service provider is or why the link exists.

value_domain: Deidentified ABN of a subsidiary member covered by an R&D registration
value_source: ATO, Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive
variable_description: Names a subsidiary whose research is covered by the head company's registration, which is how group R&D is pushed back down to the entities that performed it. Tax law treats the group as one taxpayer here: "the R&D tax incentive applies to your consolidated group or MEC group as if it is a single entity conducting all R&D activities within the group. This means only the head company of the group should register for, and claim, the tax incentive for these R&D activities." This key is therefore the only route from a claim to the operating businesses behind it.
description_source: ATO, Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive
value_definition: A ten character alphanumeric deidentified ABN, on the same key as the business spine, listed one row per subsidiary member so a single registration can have many.
limitation: The link says that a subsidiary was covered, not how much of the expenditure was its own, so R&D cannot be apportioned across group members from this table. Group membership also changes with acquisitions and disposals, so a subsidiary listed one year may be outside the group the next.
rationale: The ATO sets out the consolidated group rule under which only the head company registers, which makes the subsidiary key the mechanism for identifying the entities involved.
evidence_quote: Therefore, the R&D tax incentive applies to your consolidated group or MEC group as if it is a single entity conducting all R&D activities within the group.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Identifier - deidentified Subsidiary member ABN' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain why subsidiaries appear under a head company's claim.

value_domain: Deidentified ABN of the tax agent that lodged the R&D claim
value_source: Tax Practitioners Board, Public Register
variable_description: Names the tax practitioner acting for the company on its R&D tax incentive claim, which makes the adviser visible as a business in its own right. Tax agents must be registered with the Tax Practitioners Board to charge for this work, so the field points at a regulated intermediary rather than an informal helper. Because agents specialise, the same agent ABN recurring across many claimants is a marker of an advisory practice built around the incentive.
description_source: Tax Practitioners Board, Public Register
value_definition: A ten character alphanumeric deidentified ABN, on the same key as the business spine, so the agent can be joined to its own turnover, employment and industry records.
limitation: It identifies who lodged, not who advised: a company can take R&D advice from a specialist consultant and lodge through its ordinary accountant, and only the second appears here. A blank means no agent was recorded on the claim, which usually means the company self-lodged rather than that no adviser was used.
rationale: The Tax Practitioners Board maintains the public register of tax agents entitled to lodge on a client's behalf, which is the population this identifier draws on.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Identifier - deidentified tax agent ABN' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the lodging agent from the R&D adviser.

value_domain: Deidentified ABN of the ultimate holding company
value_source: ASIC, Company officeholder duties
variable_description: Names the company at the top of the ownership chain above the R&D claimant, which is the level at which control over research decisions and profits usually sits. It is a corporate law concept rather than a tax one: ASIC requires a company to maintain records of "any ultimate holding company", separately from any consolidated group it belongs to for tax. Where it differs from the head company on the same registration, the tax group and the ownership group are not the same thing.
description_source: ASIC, Company officeholder duties
value_definition: A ten character alphanumeric deidentified ABN. A foreign parent has no Australian business number, so the field can be empty for a company that certainly has an ultimate owner.
limitation: A blank is ambiguous between no parent and a foreign parent, so the column cannot be used to measure foreign ownership of R&D performers. It also carries no shareholding percentage, so it will not distinguish full ownership from bare control.
rationale: ASIC records the ultimate holding company as a company attribute, which is the concept the abbreviation refers to; no published R&D tax incentive documentation defines this field, so the reading is inferred.
evidence_quote: any ultimate holding company
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Identifier - deidentified UHC ABN' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving the abbreviation unexpanded and the foreign-parent gap unmentioned.

value_domain: ATO branch number under an ABN
value_source: ATO, GST branches
variable_description: Distinguishes one reporting arm of an employer from another under the same ABN, so payroll reported by a division can be told apart from payroll reported by the parent. The ATO explains the structure: "A GST branch is formed when a business entity separately registers its branch to suit the structural, management and accounting arrangements of the organisation", and "The branch effectively operates as a distinct entity for reporting purposes." In payroll reporting the ABN and branch together, not the ABN alone, identify the reporting unit.
description_source: ATO, GST branches
value_definition: A numeric branch suffix that qualifies the ABN on the same row; the unbranched parent reports under the ABN with no separate branch.
limitation: Branches are an accounting convenience, not workplaces, so the number will not locate employees or map to a business site. Adding wages across branches without deduplicating the parent's own statement double counts, and a branch restructure will look like an employment shift when nothing on the ground changed.
rationale: The ATO defines the branch registration this number comes from and states that a branch reports as if it were a distinct entity, which is what makes the branch part of the reporting key.
evidence_quote: A GST branch is formed when a business entity separately registers its branch to suit the structural, management and accounting arrangements of the organisation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about sub-dividing tax obligations with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not warn that ABN alone is not the reporting key.

value_domain: ABS integration run reference for the Business Locations module
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Records which ABS integration run produced the business location row. It matters for geography work because the locations module is rebuilt as addresses are re-geocoded and address types re-imputed, so a firm's recorded sites can move between builds without the firm moving. The ABS lists Business Locations in BLADE from 2001-02 to the latest available year.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: An eight character alphanumeric string of the form inNNN_vN, for example in271_v1, naming the integration project and its version.

rationale: The ABS page confirms the Business Locations module and its coverage in BLADE; the version item is an internal ABS reference with no published documentation, so its reading is inferred from the format.
evidence_quote: Business Locations: 2001-02 to latest available
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not connect the stamp to re-geocoding of business addresses.

value_domain: Dollar amount of R&D clawback added to a company's assessable income
value_source: ATO, Clawback of R&D tax incentive offset and catch-up deductions
variable_description: The extra assessable income a company had to declare because an earlier R&D tax offset was clawed back, reported on its company return. The mechanism is additive rather than subtractive: "Clawback doesn't decrease the grant or offset you receive. Instead, it increases your assessable income. This is called a 'clawback adjustment'." A positive value flags a firm that both claimed the R&D incentive and later received a government recoupment, sold feedstock output, or disposed of an R&D asset.
description_source: ATO, Clawback of R&D tax incentive offset and catch-up deductions
value_definition: A dollar amount reported at the clawback label of the company income tax return, grossed up to an income equivalent by dividing the incentive component by the company's tax rate for the year.
limitation: It is not a penalty and not a measure of an incorrect claim: clawback follows lawfully received grants and ordinary asset disposals. The amount also relates to notional deductions from earlier years, so it cannot be matched against the same year's R&D spending.
rationale: The ATO defines the clawback adjustment, the three events that trigger it and the gross-up that produces the reported figure, which is exactly what this company return item carries.
evidence_quote: Clawback doesn't decrease the grant or offset you receive. Instead, it increases your assessable income. This is called a 'clawback adjustment'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Clawback amounts - additional assessable income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what triggers a clawback or that it relates to earlier years.

value_domain: Dollar amount of aggregated turnover reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, CGT small business entity eligibility
variable_description: A group-wide turnover figure the company self-assesses to test its eligibility for small business tax concessions, not its own sales. The ATO defines it as follows: "Aggregated turnover is your annual turnover plus the annual turnovers of any business entities that are your affiliates or connected with you", where "Annual turnover is your gross income or proceeds, not your net profit." For a standalone company it equals its own turnover, but for a company inside a group it exceeds anything reported elsewhere on its own return.
description_source: ATO, CGT small business entity eligibility
value_definition: A dollar amount of gross ordinary income for the income year, summed over the entity and its affiliates and connected entities, and excluding dealings between them.
limitation: It is a self-assessed eligibility test rather than an audited measure of size, and it is reported chiefly by firms near a threshold, so a blank usually means the company had no reason to work it out rather than that it had no turnover. Comparing it with BAS sales on the same business will therefore mix a group figure with an entity figure.
rationale: The ATO defines aggregated turnover, its grouping rule and its exclusion of intra-group dealings, which is the quantity this company return item reports.
evidence_quote: Aggregated turnover is your annual turnover plus the annual turnovers of any business entities that are your affiliates or connected with you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the label 'Aggregated Turnover' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the figure spans affiliates and connected entities.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover range category code (A to P)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The turnover band the company put itself in, from under $7.5 million up to $1 billion or over. The ATO instruction for the label is "Select a category below based on your aggregated turnover range and write the category code at X", and aggregated turnover is the company's own turnover plus that of its connected entities and affiliates. The company may quote either the current year's or the prior year's range, and the label is only required from firms claiming temporary full expensing, loss carry back or a small business concession.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A single letter A to P in the source form, carried in BLADE as the ordinal codes 5 to 80 in steps of 5. The bands are the sixteen aggregated annual turnover ranges published in the item 8 label X table, narrow below $50 million and $100 million wide above it.

A blank is common and does not mean a small firm: most companies never have to complete the label at all, and a firm that does may report last year's band rather than this year's, so a band change can happen in a year when turnover did not move.
