evidence_quote: Select a category below based on your aggregated turnover range and write the category code at X
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Aggregated Turnover Range" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator for the temporary full expensing alternative income test
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Says whether the company reached temporary full expensing through the alternative income test rather than through the aggregated turnover threshold. The ATO explains that "Corporate tax entities unable to meet the aggregated turnover test may still be eligible for temporary full expensing if they satisfy the alternative income test", which turns on having under $5 billion of ordinary and statutory income and more than $100 million of depreciating asset cost across 2016-17 to 2018-19. A Yes therefore marks a very large firm that still claimed full expensing.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A one-character flag, Y or N, from a Yes or No box on the return. Anything else is an invalid or absent response.

A No cannot be read as ineligibility either, because most companies qualify on turnover and never consider the alternative test.

evidence_quote: Corporate tax entities unable to meet the aggregated turnover test may still be eligible for temporary full expensing if they satisfy the alternative income test.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Are you using the alternative income test?" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: ATO business industry code, five digits, derived from ANZSIC 2006
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 2 Description of main business activity
variable_description: The industry the company nominated for the activity that earned it the most gross income. The ATO says "Our industry codes are a modified version of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC), produced jointly by the Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand", so the code is a tax-return business industry code rather than an ANZSIC class. For a consolidated or MEC group it is the group's largest activity, not the lodging entity's.

A diversified company gets one code for its largest income source only, and because the code is chosen by the lodger it can persist unchanged long after the business has moved on.
rationale: The item 2 instructions define what the company writes in the industry code box, its five-digit shape and its relationship to ANZSIC; the ATO business industry code tool publishes the code set itself.
evidence_quote: Our industry codes are a modified version of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC), produced jointly by the Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "ANZSIC code" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Attributed foreign investment fund income (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Fund income tax return 2010 instructions, label D Attributed foreign income - FIF and FLP income
variable_description: Income attributed to the company from a foreign investment fund, taxed on accrual before any distribution reached the company. The ATO defines the label as "the amount of attributed foreign income from FIFs and FLPs", with FIF taking the meaning in section 481 of the ITAA 1936. It is a legacy column: the accruals regime behind it no longer runs.

value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, calculated under Part XI of the ITAA 1936 rather than taken from the accounts.

A run of zeros from that year is a law change, not a firm that stopped investing offshore, and unapplied FIF losses could not be carried into later years either.
rationale: The DIL label names attributed FIF income, which is the ATO's own label wording on the pre-2011 returns; the ATO publishes both the label definition and the date the measures were repealed.
evidence_quote: The FIF measures have been repealed and do not apply to taxpayers from 2010-11.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "AFI - FIF income" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Attributed foreign income from unlisted countries (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Profits of the company's controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries, taxed to the company here whether or not they were paid out. The ATO instruction is "Write at U the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries", where unlisted means not named in Regulation 19 of the Income Tax Assessment (1936 Act) Regulation 2015. Amounts attributed from transferor trusts go to a separate column instead.

The listed country list has also been rewritten over the life of the series, moving amounts between this column and its listed country neighbours without any change in the firm.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the unlisted country attributed foreign income label and the regulation that fixes which countries are listed.
evidence_quote: Write at U the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "AFI - unlisted country" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Attributed foreign life policy income (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Fund income tax return 2010 instructions, label D Attributed foreign income - FIF and FLP income
variable_description: Income attributed to the company from a foreign life assurance policy with an investment component, such as a life bond. The ATO ties the term to statute: "The terms FIF and FLP have the same meaning as set out in sections 481 and 482 respectively of Part XI of the ITAA 1936". It sits beside the attributed foreign investment fund column and was reported with it on the same pre-2011 label.

Because FIF and FLP amounts shared one return label in the final years, a firm's split between this column and the FIF column may reflect how the lodger apportioned a single figure rather than two separate holdings.
rationale: The ATO's own label definition names foreign life policies and cites the defining section, and the repeal date is published in the foreign income return form guide.
evidence_quote: The terms FIF and FLP have the same meaning as set out in sections 481 and 482 respectively of Part XI of the ITAA 1936.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "AFI - foreign life policy" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Attributed foreign income from transferor trusts (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Income of a non-resident trust attributed to the company because the company once transferred property or services to that trust. The ATO instruction is "Write at V the amount of attributed foreign income from transferor trusts", and it explains that "A company has an interest in a transferor trust if the company has ever made, or caused to be made, a transfer of property or services to a non-resident trust". The listed and unlisted country columns explicitly exclude these amounts.

value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported at item 8 label V of the company return, separate from the controlled foreign company attribution at labels B and U.
limitation: The trigger is a transfer made at any time in the past, so a figure here can arise from an arrangement entered decades before the reporting year and tells you nothing about current offshore activity. It also does not identify the trust or its jurisdiction.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the transferor trust attribution label and the test for having an interest in such a trust.
evidence_quote: Write at V the amount of attributed foreign income from transferor trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "AFI - transferor trust" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Australian franking credits received from a New Zealand franking company (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Australian franking credits the company picked up on a distribution from a New Zealand company that had elected into the Australian imputation system. The ATO instruction is "Write at C amounts of Australian franking credits from a New Zealand franking company that are included in assessable income because of a franked distribution paid to the company by a New Zealand franking company", including credits received indirectly through a partnership or trust. New Zealand imputation credits on the same dividend are not here and cannot be claimed at all, so the column understates the tax already paid on that distribution and is not a measure of trans-Tasman investment.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the label, name the trans-Tasman imputation measure behind it and separate it from the ordinary franking credit label.
evidence_quote: A dividend from a New Zealand franking company may also carry New Zealand imputation credits. An Australian resident cannot claim any New Zealand imputation credits.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Australian franking credits from a New Zealand company" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Bad debts expense from the accounts (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: The bad debts the company wrote off in the year, taken from its accounts as one of the item 6 expense lines. The ATO instruction is "Write at E the bad debts expense incurred for the income year", and it is an accounting figure that still has to survive the reconciliation at item 7 before any of it is deductible. Recoveries of earlier bad debts do not net off here; they are reported as other gross income.

value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, on the same accounting basis as the other item 6 expense labels, and including bad debts arising from financial arrangements under the TOFA rules.
limitation: It is a write-off, not an allowed deduction. A company can report bad debts here and be denied the deduction because it fails the continuity of ownership or business continuity test, and provisions for doubtful debts are excluded entirely, so the column understates how much credit a firm considers at risk.
rationale: The item 6 expenses instructions define the bad debts label, what must not be included in it and the tests that decide deductibility.
evidence_quote: Write at E the bad debts expense incurred for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Bad debts" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Base rate entity indicator
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: Marks the company as a base rate entity, which is what decides whether it pays the lower company tax rate. The ATO sets the test as "its aggregated turnover for 2021-22 is less than $50 million, and no more than 80% of its income is base rate entity passive income", and notes that "the lower company tax rate of 25% applies to a company that is a base rate entity". A company can be both a base rate entity and a small business entity, and the two flags are separate columns.

value_definition: A single indicator carried in BLADE as code 5 where the box was ticked; every other value means the box was blank or the response was invalid.
limitation: A blank is not evidence of a large company. The label is a tick box, so a small firm that leaves it unticked looks the same as a firm that fails the passive income limb, and the turnover threshold behind the test rose from $25 million to $50 million during the series, which moves firms across the flag without any change in their business.
rationale: Item 3 of the company return carries the base rate entity indicator and the instructions state both limbs of the test and the tax rate that follows from it.
evidence_quote: For 2021-22, the lower company tax rate of 25% applies to a company that is a base rate entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Base rate entity" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Count of assets opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: How many depreciating assets the company chose to keep out of the backing business investment accelerated depreciation concession. The ATO instruction is "Show at W the number of assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation", and the choice is made asset by asset and cannot be reversed. It is a count of a deliberate refusal, not of assets the company bought.

value_definition: A whole number of assets, up to five digits, reported at item 9 label W of the 2020-21 company return.

The ATO also says a lodger "will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect amount", so the number is a best attempt.
rationale: The 2021 company return instructions define the backing business investment opt-out labels V, W and X, which are the only place this count is reported.
evidence_quote: Show at W the number of assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Backing business investment - Number of assets you are opting out for" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Cost of assets opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The total cost of the assets the company kept out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation. The ATO instruction is "Show at X the total cost of the assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation", which is a different basis from the temporary full expensing opt-out value on the next label, where the amount is the deduction the company gave up rather than the asset cost. The two opt-out value columns are therefore not comparable.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 9 label X of the 2020-21 company return, measured as asset cost, and pairing with the asset count at label W.
limitation: It cannot be added to the temporary full expensing opt-out value, because that column measures a forgone deduction and this one measures cost. It also says nothing about what deduction the company claimed instead under the ordinary capital allowance rules, so it is not a measure of investment withheld from tax relief.
rationale: The 2021 company return instructions state the measurement basis for this label and, one label earlier, the different basis used for the temporary full expensing opt-out value.
evidence_quote: Show at X the total cost of the assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Backing business investment - Value of assets you are opting out for" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: R&D balancing adjustment catch-up deduction (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Balancing adjustments for R&D assets
variable_description: An extra deduction the company got when it disposed of an asset it had been claiming R&D decline in value on, and the disposal produced a loss. The ATO says "A catch-up deduction is included as a deduction from assessable income if the balancing adjustment event gives rise to a loss (the catch-up amount)", and it is the mirror image of the clawback that applies when the disposal produces a gain. It is calculated in Part B of the R&D tax incentive schedule and carried to item 21 of the company return.
description_source: ATO, Balancing adjustments for R&D assets
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, worked out on the incentive component of the offset rather than on the whole balancing adjustment, and reduced to the R&D share where an asset was only partly used in R&D activities.
limitation: It is a disposal event, not R&D spending, so it can be large in a year when the company did no research at all. The amount also has to be reported again inside item 7 other deductible expenses, so adding it to the item 7 total double-counts it.
rationale: The ATO's R&D balancing adjustment guidance defines the catch-up amount and how it is worked out, and the item 21 instructions state that the amount reported on the return is carried from Part B of the R&D schedule.
evidence_quote: A catch-up deduction is included as a deduction from assessable income if the balancing adjustment event gives rise to a loss (the catch-up amount).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Balancing adjustments - catch up deduction" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Small business entity indicator
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: Marks the company as a small business entity, which is the gateway to the small business tax concessions. The ATO test is that "The company will be a small business entity if it is carrying on a business and has an aggregated turnover of less than $10 million", and the instruction is "Print X at F1 if the company is a small business entity for 2021-22". Despite the DIL name, it is a tax status flag rather than a market segment.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
value_definition: A single indicator carried in BLADE as code 5 where the box was ticked; every other value means the box was blank or the response was invalid.
limitation: It is not a size class. The threshold behind it rose from $2 million to $10 million for 2016-17, so the flag turns on for a large group of unchanged firms at that point, and a company that carries on no business fails the test however small it is. Different concessions run off different thresholds, so the flag alone does not say what the firm could actually claim.
rationale: Item 3 label F1 of the company return is the small business entity indicator, and the instructions give the test, the threshold and the reason the label matters.
evidence_quote: The company will be a small business entity if it is carrying on a business and has an aggregated turnover of less than $10 million.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Small business" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Attributed foreign income from listed countries (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Profits of the company's controlled foreign entities in listed countries, attributed to the company here. The ATO instruction is "Write at B the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in listed countries", where listed countries are those "included in Regulation 19 of the Income Tax Assessment (1936 Act) Regulation 2015". The variable name records the older three-way split, in which this column held broad-exemption listed countries and the sibling column c_ltdexemp held limited-exemption listed countries.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 8 label B of the company return, excluding anything attributed from transferor trusts.
limitation: A comparison over time is unsafe in both directions: the listed and limited-exemption categories were consolidated into a single listed country label, and the regulation naming listed countries has itself been remade, so amounts move between this column, c_ltdexemp and the unlisted country column without any change in the firm's structure.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the listed country attribution label and the regulation that fixes the country list; the sibling BLADE column for limited-exemption listed countries identifies which half of the old split this one is.
evidence_quote: Listed countries are included in Regulation 19 of the Income Tax Assessment (1936 Act) Regulation 2015.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Attributed foreign income - Listed country" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: ATO client market segment code
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The administrative segment the ATO assigned to the client account behind the return, such as micro business, small to medium, or large market. It comes from the ATO's own client management systems rather than from any label on the return, so no lodger chose it. It is useful as a rough size and type split of the tax population, and as a way of separating government and not-for-profit lodgers from trading companies.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A three-character code: GOV government, LGE large market, SME small to medium, INB individual and non-business, MIC micro business, NFP not for profit. Anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The thresholds behind the segments are not published with the data and have been redrawn over the life of the ATO's client segmentation, so the boundary between micro, small to medium and large market is not stable and should not be used as a size cut in a longitudinal analysis. It also does not correspond to the ABS employment size classes used elsewhere in BLADE.
rationale: No ATO page defining these segment codes could be retrieved, so the reading of the code letters is inferred from the code labels in the BLADE data item list and from the ATO's general use of market segments; the BLADE overview is cited as the fetchable source for the asset the column belongs to.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Business market segment" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Middle-year tax loss carried back to the earliest year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: How much of the middle year's unused tax loss the company chose to carry back against the earliest year's tax liability. The loss carry back window covered three loss years and three income years: "Eligible corporate tax entities with less than $5 billion aggregated turnover in a relevant loss year can carry back losses made in the 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22 income years to a prior year's income tax liability in the 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2020-21 income years". This column holds the middle loss year going to the earliest target year, which the current year column beside it does not.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount at the item 13 loss carry back labels. The BLADE label abstracts the year-specific return labels into earliest, middle and current, so which financial years those words point to depends on the return year.
limitation: The amount is a choice, not an entitlement, and the offset it produces is capped by the earlier year's unused income tax liability and by the closing franking account balance, so a large figure here does not become a large refund. Only losses not already utilised can appear, so the column understates the loss the company actually made.
rationale: Item 13 of the company return carries the loss carry back choices and the instructions set out the eligible loss years, the target years and the caps that apply.
evidence_quote: Eligible corporate tax entities with less than $5 billion aggregated turnover in a relevant loss year can carry back losses made in the 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22 income years to a prior year's income tax liability in the 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2020-21 income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Tax loss for middle year (not already utilised) chosen to be carried back to earliest year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Current-year tax loss carried back to the earliest year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: How much of the return year's own tax loss the company chose to carry back against the earliest year's tax liability. It differs from the middle-year column beside it only in which loss year the amount came from, and on the 2022 return it is the 2021-22 loss taken back to 2018-19. A loss carried back this way cannot also be deducted forward: the ATO says a loss carried back "cannot be included at R", the tax losses deducted label.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount at the item 13 loss carry back labels, holding the current loss year against the earliest available target year.
limitation: Reading it as a measure of the year's trading loss is wrong twice over: it is only the part the company chose to carry back, and the choice is bounded by how much unused tax liability the earliest year still has. A zero can mean a profitable year, a loss with nothing to carry back to, or a company that preferred to carry the loss forward.
rationale: Item 13 of the company return holds the year-by-year loss carry back choices, and item 7 states that a carried-back loss is excluded from the tax losses deducted label.
evidence_quote: If a tax loss for the 2019-20 or 2020-21 income year is carried back under the Division 160 of the ITAA 1997, that amount cannot be included at R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Tax loss for current year chosen to be carried back to earliest year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Significant global entity indicator
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: Marks the company as part of a multinational group large enough to attract the significant global entity obligations. The ATO test is a group with "an annual global income of A$1 billion or more", reached either through the company being the global parent or through membership of an accounting consolidated group or notional listed company group containing such a parent. The flag drives country-by-country reporting, general purpose financial statement lodgment and higher penalties.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
value_definition: A single indicator carried in BLADE as code 5 where the box was ticked; every other value means the box was blank or the response was invalid.
limitation: It describes the worldwide group, not the Australian company, so a small Australian subsidiary of a large foreign parent carries the flag while a large standalone Australian company does not. The label was only added for income years from 2015-16, and its sibling country-by-country reporting flag is a different and narrower test.
rationale: Item 3 label G1 of the company return is the significant global entity indicator and the instructions give the A$1 billion global income test and the group definitions behind it.
evidence_quote: Print X at G1 if the entity was a significant global entity (SGE) for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Significant global entity" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Closing trading stock at tax values (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The value of trading stock the company held at the end of the year, measured for tax rather than for the accounts. The ATO instruction is "Write at B the total value of all trading stock on hand at the end of the income year or accounting period for which the company tax return is being prepared", and "The amount at B is the value calculated for income tax purposes under section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997". It is a stock at a date, and the CODE box beside it says which valuation method produced it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label B, excluding input tax credits the company has claimed or can claim, and including floor plan stock and work in progress on manufactured goods.
limitation: A flat series does not mean flat inventories. A small business entity whose stock moved by $5,000 or less may write last year's opening value straight into this label without a stocktake, so the column can repeat a number for years while real stock drifts. The value also depends on the method chosen, which may change between years.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the closing stock label, the statutory basis for the value and the small business rule that allows the opening value to be repeated.
evidence_quote: The amount at B is the value calculated for income tax purposes under section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Closing stock" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Net commercial debt forgiven (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The net amount of the company's own commercial debts that creditors released or waived during the year. The ATO instruction is "Write at K the net amount of commercial debts owed by the company that were forgiven during the income year", where "a debt is a commercial debt if any part of the interest payable on the debt is, or would be, an allowable deduction". A figure here is a distress marker that also has tax consequences in later years.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label K, reported net, and applied in a fixed order to reduce revenue losses, net capital losses, undeducted expenditure and then CGT cost bases.
limitation: It is not a measure of the company's total bad debt relief, because only debts with deductible interest count: an interest-free related party loan written off does not appear. The consequences also show up elsewhere and later, so the year with the amount is not the year the tax attributes fall.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the commercial debt forgiveness label, the commercial debt test and the order in which the forgiven amount reduces the company's tax attributes.
evidence_quote: Write at K the net amount of commercial debts owed by the company that were forgiven during the income year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Commercial debt forgiveness" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Cost of sales from the accounts (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: What the company spent acquiring or producing what it sold, taken from the accounts. The ATO instruction is "Write at A the cost of anything produced, manufactured, acquired or purchased for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business", including freight inwards and sometimes external labour where the accounts put it there. Input tax credit entitlements are excluded.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 6 label A of the expenses side, on the company's own accounting basis and matching its financial statements for the year.
limitation: The sign lives in a separate box. When the cost of sales account is in credit the amount is entered without brackets and an L is printed beside it, so a positive value in this column can in fact be a negative expense. What counts as cost of sales rather than other expenses also follows the company's own accounting practice, which limits comparability across firms.
rationale: The item 6 expenses instructions define the cost of sales label, what belongs in it and how a credit balance is signalled on the form.
evidence_quote: Write at A the cost of anything produced, manufactured, acquired or purchased for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Cost of sales" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Country of the company's business address
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The country of the address the ATO holds as the company's business address on the client register. For almost every lodger it is Australia, so the column mainly picks out companies whose registered or postal contact point sits offshore. It is register data attached to the account, not a label on the return.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A character country code or name carried on the ATO client register. The domain is open and no code list is published with the data item.
limitation: It is not a residence or operations variable. A foreign address can belong to an Australian-operating company whose agent or parent is offshore, and an Australian address says nothing about where the company is tax resident or where its activity happens. Because it is a current register attribute, it can also be overwritten rather than versioned.
rationale: No ATO or ABS page defining this register field could be retrieved, so the reading is inferred from the DIL label and from how the ATO client register carries address data; the BLADE overview is cited as the fetchable source for the asset the column belongs to.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Business Address Country" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Trade creditors at year end (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What the company owed its suppliers at year end for goods and services already received. The ATO instruction is "Write at F the total amounts owed by the company at year end for goods and services received during the income year, that is, current trade creditors", and the same amount is also counted inside all current liabilities on the next label. It is a balance sheet stock taken from the accounts, not a tax figure.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label F, an accounting value from the company's financial statements at the last day of the income year.
limitation: It is a snapshot at one date and can be managed around that date, so it is a poor proxy for how much supplier credit the firm uses through the year. It is also nested inside the current liabilities column, so adding the two together double-counts.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the trade creditors label and state that the amount is also included in all current liabilities.
evidence_quote: Write at F the total amounts owed by the company at year end for goods and services received during the income year, that is, current trade creditors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Trade creditors" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation method code
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Which method the company used to value the closing stock reported beside it: cost, market selling value or replacement value. The ATO instruction is "Print in the CODE box the code from table 5 indicating the method used to value closing stock for income tax purposes", and "If more than one method is used, use the code applicable to the method representing the highest value". The choice is real: a company may value the same item differently in different years.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A single letter from table 5 of the item 8 instructions, C for cost, M for market selling value and R for replacement value, carried in BLADE as the ordinal codes 5, 10 and 15.
limitation: It describes one method for the whole stock even where several were used, so it cannot support a claim about how a particular line of stock was valued. A first-year company with no stock prints C by instruction, so C on a zero stock figure carries no information about method at all.
rationale: The item 8 instructions publish the valuation method code table, the rule for choosing a code when several methods are used and the default for a first-year company.
evidence_quote: If more than one method is used, use the code applicable to the method representing the highest value.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Closing stock action code" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Total current assets from the accounts (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Everything on the company's balance sheet expected to be realised within the year. The ATO instruction is "Write at D all current assets of the company, including cash on hand, short-term bills receivable, inventories and trade debtors", and it sits inside total assets on the next label. It is an accounting value, one of the few balance sheet items the company return collects.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label D, taken from the company's financial statements at the end of the income year, and including the trade debtors reported separately at label C.
limitation: It cannot be netted against current liabilities to build a reliable liquidity ratio across firms, because the split between current and non-current follows each company's own accounting policy and neither label is audited by the ATO. For a group it is the consolidated figure, so a subsidiary's own position is not recoverable.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the all current assets label, list what belongs in it and say the amounts at labels C to H are accounting values.
evidence_quote: Write at D all current assets of the company, including cash on hand, short-term bills receivable, inventories and trade debtors
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Current assets" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Total current liabilities from the accounts (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Everything the company expected to have to pay within the coming year. The ATO instruction is "Write at G the total obligations payable by the company within the coming year", and the trade creditors figure at label F is included inside it. Total liabilities on the next label includes this amount in turn.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label G, an accounting value from the company's financial statements at the end of the income year.
limitation: It is not a debt measure. Trade payables, provisions and the current portion of borrowings all sit here together, and the return's separate total debt label is calculated on a different basis again, as an average of opening and closing balances. Comparing the two as though both were year-end debt is wrong.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the all current liabilities label, its relationship to trade creditors and total liabilities, and the different averaging basis used for total debt.
evidence_quote: Write at G the total obligations payable by the company within the coming year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Current liabilities" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Capital works deduction (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The deduction the company claimed for the cost of buildings and structural improvements, written off over decades rather than depreciated. The ATO instruction is "Write at I the deduction claimed for capital expenditure on buildings, which includes eligible capital expenditure on extensions, alterations or improvements, and shop fitouts", and mining infrastructure and timber milling buildings are excluded. It is a reconciliation item, added in at item 7 rather than appearing in the accounts.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label I of the company return, a Division 43 capital works deduction at the statutory rate of 2.5% or 4% a year on construction cost.
limitation: It is not a measure of building investment in the year. The deduction runs for 25 or 40 years after construction, so an amount here can reflect work done decades ago, and a purchaser of an existing building continues the original owner's write-off. Commercial debt forgiveness can also reduce the deductible amount without any change in the asset.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the capital works deduction label, what it covers and what is excluded from it.
evidence_quote: Write at I the deduction claimed for capital expenditure on buildings, which includes eligible capital expenditure on extensions, alterations or improvements, and shop fitouts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Capital works deductions" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Prior year tax losses deducted this year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: How much of the company's carried-forward tax losses it actually used against this year's income. The ATO instruction is "Include at R those tax losses of prior income years that are deducted for 2021-22 under section 36-17 of the ITAA 1997", and prior year losses must be used in the order they were incurred. Losses carried back under the loss carry back rules are excluded and reported at item 13 instead.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label R, deducted in the reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable income, and distinct from the losses carried forward balance reported at item 13.
limitation: A zero does not mean the company has no losses. Deduction is blocked unless the company passes the continuity of ownership test or the business continuity test, capital losses can never appear here, and a company with excess franking offsets may choose to deduct less than it could. Film losses and some life insurance losses are reported elsewhere entirely.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the tax losses deducted label, the provision it is claimed under, the ordering rule and the categories that must not be included.
evidence_quote: Include at R those tax losses of prior income years that are deducted for 2021-22 under section 36-17 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Tax losses deducted" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Landcare and water facility deduction (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The company's deduction for landcare operations and for the decline in value of water facilities and, in later years, fencing and fodder storage assets. The ATO instruction is "Write at N the company's total deductions for landcare operations expenses and for water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets", and these amounts are deliberately kept out of the ordinary decline in value label. It is a primary production concession, so a non-zero value almost always marks a farming business.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label N of the company return, covering Division 40 subdivision 40-F and 40-G deductions rather than ordinary capital allowances.
limitation: The label changed shape mid-series. Fencing assets and fodder storage assets were added to it for 2015-16, when both became immediately deductible, so a jump at that point is a policy change rather than new investment, and the DIL wording carries only the older water facility form of the label.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the label, its current coverage and its separation from the decline in value label; the DIL wording matches the pre-2016 form of the same label.
evidence_quote: Do not include the deduction for the decline in value of water facilities at F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets item 7
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Landcare operations and deduction for decline in value of water facility" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Environmental protection expenditure deduction (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: What the company deducted for cleaning up or preventing pollution and waste from its own earning activity. The ATO instruction is "Write at O the amount of allowable expenditure on environmental protection activities", and the same expenditure must also be added back at non-deductible expenses to the extent it was already booked as an item 6 expense. It is an immediate deduction for expenditure that would otherwise be capital.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label O of the company return, claimed under the environmental protection provisions in Division 40 subdivision 40-H.
limitation: It is not a measure of environmental spending. Only expenditure on the company's own site and its own earning activity qualifies, prevention that forms part of a building or plant is deducted elsewhere as capital works or decline in value, and voluntary environmental programmes with no earning connection do not appear at all.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the environmental protection expenses label and the add-back that goes with it.
evidence_quote: Write at O the amount of allowable expenditure on environmental protection activities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Deduction for environmental protection expenses" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Small business skills and training boost bonus deduction (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The 20% bonus deduction the company claimed on external training bought for its employees. The ATO instruction is "Write at item 7 - label J the total bonus deduction amount of the company for the small business skills and training boost", and it says "Do not include the total skills and training expenditure amount at this label for which you claim an ordinary deduction". Dividing the amount by 0.2 recovers the eligible training spend behind it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label J of the 2023 and later company return, equal to 20% of eligible external training expenditure incurred between 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2024.
limitation: The year on the return is not the year of the spending. Under the delayed claim rule the bonus for expenditure incurred from 29 March 2022 to the end of 2022-23 is all claimed in the 2023 return, so the 2023 figure stacks two income years of training and 2022 shows nothing. Only training from registered external providers counts, so in-house and unregistered training is invisible.
rationale: The 2023 item 7 instructions define the label and what must be excluded from it; the ATO boost page gives the rate, the eligibility conditions and the expenditure window.
evidence_quote: Write at item 7 - label J the total bonus deduction amount of the company for the small business skills and training boost.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Small business skills and training boost" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Small business technology investment boost bonus deduction (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The 20% bonus deduction the company claimed on spending that digitised its operations. The ATO describes it as "an additional tax deduction of 20%, on top of the ordinary deduction, for the eligible expenditure incurred from 7:30pm (AEDT) on 29 March 2022 to 30 June 2023", capped at $100,000 of expenditure and a $20,000 bonus per income year. Unlike the skills and training boost beside it, this one covers depreciating assets as well as expenses.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label L of the 2023 and later company return, equal to 20% of eligible technology expenditure up to the annual cap.
limitation: The cap censors the series: any firm spending more than $100,000 on eligible technology reports the same $20,000, so the column cannot rank digital investment among larger spenders. The window also closed on 30 June 2023, two years earlier than the skills boost, so a zero in a later year is the end of the measure rather than a change in behaviour.
rationale: The 2023 item 7 instructions define the label, its rate and its caps, and the ATO boost page gives the eligibility conditions and the expenditure window.
evidence_quote: Write at item 7 - label L the total bonus deduction amount of the company for the small business technology investment boost.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Small business technology investment boost" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Consolidation interim rules deduction for rights to future income (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2019 instructions, item 11 Consolidation deductions
variable_description: What the head company of a consolidated group deducted for the tax cost of rights to future income assets acquired in the interim window. The ATO instruction is "Write at E the total amount the company has claimed in this income year under the interim rules at another label in item 6 Calculation of total profit or loss or item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss for the tax cost setting amount of rights to future income assets, consumable stores or assets where section 701-55(6) of the ITAA 1997 applies". The interim window covers acquisitions between the pre rules and the prospective rules.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2019 instructions, item 11 Consolidation deductions
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 11 label E of the company return, reported by the head company of a consolidated or MEC group only.
limitation: It is a disclosure of an amount already claimed somewhere else on the return, so adding it to total deductions counts it twice. Which of the three consolidation windows a deduction falls in depends on when the joining arrangement commenced, not on the year of the return, so this column and its pre-rules and prospective-rules neighbours can all be populated in the same year for the same group.
rationale: Item 11 of the company return splits consolidation rights to future income deductions across the pre, interim and prospective rules, and the 2019 instructions give the label wording for all three.
evidence_quote: The rules applying to an entity will depend on the time when the corporate acquisition took place.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Interim rules deductions" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Consolidation pre rules deduction for unbilled income assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2019 instructions, item 11 Consolidation deductions
variable_description: What the head company of a consolidated group deducted for the tax cost of unbilled income assets acquired before the consolidation integrity changes. The ATO instruction is "Write at D the total amount the company has claimed in this income year under the pre rules at another label in item 6 Calculation of total profit or loss or item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss for the tax cost setting amount of unbilled income assets, consumable stores or assets where subsection 701-55(6) of the ITAA 1997 applies". The pre rules are the most generous of the three windows and cover acquisitions before 12 May 2010.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2019 instructions, item 11 Consolidation deductions
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 11 label D of the company return, reported by the head company of a consolidated or MEC group only, and describing unbilled income assets rather than the rights to future income wording used for the interim window.
limitation: The window is defined by when the acquisition happened, so this column can carry amounts many years after 2010 and says nothing about acquisitions made in the return year. Like its two neighbours it restates a deduction claimed elsewhere on the return, so it is a memorandum figure and not an addition to deductions.
rationale: Item 11 of the company return splits consolidation rights to future income deductions across three windows, and the 2019 instructions give the pre rules label wording and the acquisition dates that define the window.
evidence_quote: Write at D the total amount the company has claimed in this income year under the pre rules at another label in item 6 Calculation of total profit or loss or item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss for the tax cost setting amount of unbilled income assets, consumable stores or assets where subsection 701-55(6) of the ITAA 1997 applies.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Pre rules deductions" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Consolidation prospective rules deduction for work in progress (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2019 instructions, item 11 Consolidation deductions
variable_description: What the head company of a consolidated group deducted for the tax cost of work in progress amount assets acquired under the current consolidation rules. The ATO sets the boundary as "Different rules apply to acquisitions that took place before 12 May 2010 (the pre-rules), after 30 March 2011 (the prospective rules) and the intervening period (the interim rules)". The prospective window is the narrowest in what it allows: work in progress amount assets and consumable stores, not the broader rights to future income of the earlier windows.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2019 instructions, item 11 Consolidation deductions
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 11 label F of the company return, covering the tax cost setting amount of work in progress amount assets under subsection 701-55(5C) and consumable stores under 701-55(5D) of the ITAA 1997.
limitation: It is the only one of the three consolidation windows still open to new acquisitions, so the pre rules and interim rules columns beside it become empty over time while this one does not. It also duplicates an amount claimed at item 6 or item 7, so it cannot be added to the deduction total.
rationale: Item 11 of the company return defines the prospective rules deduction and the 2019 and 2022 instructions both give the acquisition dates that separate the three windows.
evidence_quote: Different rules apply to acquisitions that took place before 12 May 2010 (the pre-rules), after 30 March 2011 (the prospective rules) and the intervening period (the interim rules).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Prospective rules deductions" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Trade debtors at year end (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What customers owed the company at year end for goods and services already supplied. The ATO instruction is "Write at C the total amounts owing to the company at year end for goods and services provided during the income year, that is, the gross amount of current trade debtors from the company's accounts", and the same amount is counted again inside all current assets. It is a gross figure, before any allowance for doubtful debts.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label C, an accounting value from the company's financial statements at the end of the income year.
limitation: Because it is gross, it does not net off the provision for doubtful debts, so it overstates what the company expects to collect. It also cannot be combined with the bad debts expense to estimate a write-off rate, since one is a year-end stock of the current year's sales and the other is a flow that mostly relates to earlier years' sales.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the trade debtors label, state that it is a gross accounting amount and that it is also included in all current assets.
evidence_quote: Write at C the total amounts owing to the company at year end for goods and services provided during the income year, that is, the gross amount of current trade debtors from the company's accounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Trade debtors" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The capital allowance the company actually deducted for the year, worked out under the tax rules rather than its accounting policy. The ATO instruction is "If the company is not a small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules, write the deduction for decline in value of most depreciating assets for taxation purposes at F", and it warns that "This amount is often different from the amount of depreciation calculated for accounting purposes" reported at item 6. The two columns are the tax and accounting views of the same assets and should not be added.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label F of the company return, a Division 40 decline in value deduction added into the reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable income.
limitation: It is empty for exactly the firms most likely to be depreciating small assets. A small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules reports its whole deduction at item 6 instead, so a population-wide sum of this column understates capital allowances, and understates them most among small firms.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the decline in value label, state where small business entities report instead and contrast the tax deduction with the accounting expense at item 6.
evidence_quote: This amount is often different from the amount of depreciation calculated for accounting purposes written at X Depreciation expenses item 6
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Depreciation deducted" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Depreciation expense from the accounts (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: The depreciation the company booked as an expense in its accounts for the year, which is then reversed out in the reconciliation to taxable income. The ATO carves out one group: "Show the depreciation expenses of small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules as tax values, at X Depreciation expenses item 6". The column therefore mixes an accounting figure for most companies with a tax figure for simplified depreciation users.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 6 label X of the expenses side, on the company's accounting basis except for small business entities using simplified depreciation, whose amounts are tax values.
limitation: It is not comparable across firms without knowing which basis produced it, and the return does not flag which basis was used on this label. Profits and losses on the sale of depreciating assets are excluded and reported as other income or other expenses, so the column is not a complete picture of asset consumption either.
rationale: The item 6 expenses instructions define the depreciation expenses label, the small business entity exception that puts tax values on it, and what must be excluded.
evidence_quote: Show the depreciation expenses of small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules as tax values, at X Depreciation expenses item 6
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Depreciation expenses" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Closing franking account balance (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The company's franking account balance at the end of the year, which is the stock of tax paid that it can still attach to dividends. The ATO instruction is "Show at M Closing franking account balance the balance of the franking account at the end of 2021-22", and for a loss carry back claimant "the Closing franking account balance must be greater than zero, otherwise the offset cannot be claimed". It pairs with the opening balance on the previous label.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label M, a stock at the last day of the income year rather than a flow, and reported by the company itself rather than reconstructed by the ATO.
limitation: A zero is ambiguous. A deficit balance is not reported as a negative here, and a company in deficit must lodge a separate franking account tax return and pay franking deficit tax, so the column cannot be used to identify over-franking. Differencing it against the opening balance also will not recover franking credits and debits, because the account moves on payment dates that need not fall inside the income year.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the closing franking account balance label, its role in the loss carry back conditions and how a deficit balance is dealt with.
evidence_quote: If the company is a resident and claiming the loss carry back tax offset, the Closing franking account balance must be greater than zero, otherwise the offset cannot be claimed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Closing Franking Account Balance" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Opening franking account balance (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The company's franking account balance at the start of the year. The ATO instruction is "Write at P Opening franking account balance the balance of the franking account at the beginning of 2021-22", and it is only compulsory for a company claiming the loss carry back tax offset. In principle it should equal last year's closing balance on the neighbouring column.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label P, a stock at the first day of the income year.
limitation: A zero here can be a genuine nil balance or an instruction-driven substitute for a deficit: the ATO says "If your franking account shows a deficit balance at the beginning of 2021-22, you will need to write 0 at P to allow you to complete the loss carry back labels". Companies not claiming loss carry back may leave it blank altogether, so coverage is far from universal.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the opening franking account balance label, who must complete it and the zero substitution rule for a deficit balance.
evidence_quote: If your franking account shows a deficit balance at the beginning of 2021-22, you will need to write 0 at P to allow you to complete the loss carry back labels.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Opening Franking Account Balance" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Franked dividends paid (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What the company paid out to its shareholders with franking credits attached during the year. The ATO instruction is "Write at J the amount of fully franked dividends paid or credited during the income year, including non-share dividends or deemed dividends that are fully franked", and where a dividend was only partly franked the franked part sits here and the rest at the unfranked dividends label. Dividends between members of a consolidated group are excluded.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label J, calculated for tax purposes rather than taken from the accounts, and covering amounts paid or credited during the income year.
limitation: It is not total distributions. Reading it alone understates payout for any company that franked partially, because the balance sits in a different column, and it misses distributions inside a consolidated group entirely, so a group's internal cash movement is invisible.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the franked dividends paid label, the partial franking split and the consolidated group exclusion.
evidence_quote: If a partly franked dividend has been paid during the income year, include the franked portion at J and the unfranked portion at K Unfranked dividends paid item 8 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Dividends paid franked" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Franking credits received on assessable distributions (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The franking credits attached to distributions the company received directly from other Australian companies, grossed up into its assessable income. The ATO instruction is "Write at J the amount of franking credits attached to assessable distributions received from Australian corporate tax entities", and the credits then come back as a tax offset in the calculation statement. It is the receiving side of imputation, not the paying side.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label J of the company return, added to accounting profit in the reconciliation to taxable income.
limitation: It is not the company's whole imputation entitlement. Credits received indirectly through a partnership or trust are counted inside the item 6 distribution labels, credits from a New Zealand franking company have their own label, and credits on shares not held at risk are excluded altogether, so this column alone understates the credits behind the company's offsets.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the franking credits label and list the four categories of credit that must not be included in it.
evidence_quote: Write at J the amount of franking credits attached to assessable distributions received from Australian corporate tax entities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Franking credits" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Excess franking offsets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The part of the company's franking tax offsets that exceeded the tax it would otherwise have paid. The ATO calculates it in three steps, comparing franking offsets against a hypothetical tax figure worked out ignoring franking and carry-forward offsets. The excess is not refundable to an ordinary company: "If the company has excess franking offsets, it may convert the excess franking offsets into an amount of tax loss to carry forward to later income years".
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label H of the company return, produced by the step calculation in the item 8 instructions rather than reported straight from the accounts.
limitation: A figure here is not a refund and not a benefit received in the year: it converts into a tax loss whose value depends on the company making future profits. It also excludes franking offsets subject to the refundable offset rules, so a life insurance company with the same economics reports nothing here.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the excess franking offsets label, publish the three-step calculation and state what happens to the excess.
evidence_quote: If the company has excess franking offsets, it may convert the excess franking offsets into an amount of tax loss to carry forward to later income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Excess franking offsets" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Unfranked dividends paid (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What the company distributed without franking credits attached, including amounts the law deems to be dividends. The ATO instruction is "Write at K the amount of unfranked dividends paid or credited during the income year, including amounts deemed to be dividends by various sections of the ITAA 1936 and the ITAA 1997", and it names Division 7A deemed dividends and off-market share buy-backs among them. It carries the unfranked share of a partly franked dividend as well.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label K, calculated for tax purposes, and including non-share dividends and deemed dividends as well as ordinary cash distributions.
limitation: An amount here need not correspond to any payment. Division 7A treats loans, payments and forgiven debts to shareholders and their associates as assessable dividends, so a private company can report a large figure in a year it paid no dividend at all, and the column cannot be read as cash returned to shareholders.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the unfranked dividends paid label and set out the deemed dividend rules that feed into it.
evidence_quote: Write at K the amount of unfranked dividends paid or credited during the income year, including amounts deemed to be dividends by various sections of the ITAA 1936 and the ITAA 1997.
