supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Unfranked dividends paid" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Trust type code for the gross distribution from trusts
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: What kind of trust the company's trust distribution came from, coded beside the distribution amount at item 6. The ATO instruction is to print the code "that best describes the type of trust for the amount of income written at E", and "If this amount is from more than one type of trust, print the code that represents the trust for the greatest amount of income". The code separates discretionary trusts by the activity behind the income, which is the distinction the ATO cares about.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A single letter from table 2 of the item 6 instructions, carried in BLADE as ordinal codes 5 to 60, covering deceased estates, fixed and fixed unit trusts, hybrid trusts, three kinds of discretionary trust, cash management and public unit trusts, special disability trusts and testamentary trusts.
limitation: It describes one trust when there may have been several, and by design it names only the largest source, so a company with a spread of trust interests looks like a company with one. The code set also grew over time, with special disability and testamentary trusts added later, so an earlier year's code cannot be assumed to be the same choice set.
rationale: The item 6 instructions define the CODE box beside the gross distribution from trusts label, publish the trust type table and give the rule for choosing between several trusts.
evidence_quote: If this amount is from more than one type of trust, print the code that represents the trust for the greatest amount of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Gross distribution from trusts code" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Decline in value deduction, intangible exploration assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The company's deduction for the decline in value of intangible assets used in exploration, such as mining and petroleum rights and information. The ATO instruction is "Write at K the total of your deductions for decline in value of intangible depreciating assets used in exploration or prospecting", and the tangible side of the same activity is reported on the next label. The pair exists so that mining capital allowances can be separated from ordinary ones.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 9 label K of the company return, a Division 40 decline in value deduction restricted to intangible assets used in exploration or prospecting.
limitation: It is a disclosure of part of the decline in value already claimed at item 7, so it cannot be added to that column. A blank is not evidence of no exploration either: the ATO says a company that claimed no such deductions does not complete the question at all, and immediate deductions for exploration expenditure that is not a depreciating asset never reach this label.
rationale: Item 9 of the company return carries the two exploration decline in value labels and the instructions define both and say who has to complete them.
evidence_quote: Write at K the total of your deductions for decline in value of intangible depreciating assets used in exploration or prospecting.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Total deduction - decline in value of intangible depreciating assets used in exploration/prospecting" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Decline in value deduction, other exploration assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The company's deduction for the decline in value of non-intangible exploration assets, which in practice means rigs, vehicles and field equipment. The ATO instruction is "Write at L the total of your deductions for decline in value of other depreciating assets used in exploration or prospecting". Read against the intangible label beside it, the split shows how much of an explorer's capital allowance came from rights and information rather than physical plant.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 9 label L of the company return, a Division 40 decline in value deduction for tangible and other non-intangible assets used in exploration or prospecting.
limitation: The line between this label and the intangible one follows the tax character of the asset, not its physical form, so the split is a legal classification rather than a plant-versus-rights distinction a reader can verify. Like its neighbour it restates part of the item 7 decline in value deduction and must not be added to it.
rationale: Item 9 of the company return carries the two exploration decline in value labels and the instructions define each separately.
evidence_quote: Write at L the total of your deductions for decline in value of other depreciating assets used in exploration or prospecting.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Total deduction for decline in value of other depreciating assets used in exploration or prospecting" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Backing business investment opt-out choice code
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Says whether the company opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation for some of its eligible assets, all of them, or none. The ATO instruction is "Show A at V if you are opting out for some of your eligible assets and show B if you are opting out for all of your eligible assets", and the choice is made asset by asset and "Once a choice is made it cannot be revoked". It is the flag that qualifies the asset count and value columns beside it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A single code at item 9 label V of the 2020-21 company return: A for some eligible assets, B for all, and a No response otherwise, carried in BLADE as ordinal codes 5, 10 and 15.
limitation: A No does not mean the company used the concession. Backing business investment only applied where temporary full expensing and the instant asset write-off did not, and only to assets first used between 12 March 2020 and 30 June 2021, so almost every company that answers No never had an eligible asset in the first place.
rationale: The 2021 company return instructions define the backing business investment opt-out choice label, its code values and the eligibility conditions that surround it.
evidence_quote: Show A at V if you are opting out for some of your eligible assets and show B if you are opting out for all of your eligible assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Are you opting out of Backing business investment for some or all of your eligible assets?" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Count of assets claimed under temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: How many depreciating assets the company wrote off in full under temporary full expensing. The ATO instruction is "Write at T the number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing", and the dollar value of those claims is on the label immediately before it. Together the two give an average cost per asset written off, which is the only asset-level detail the return collects.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A whole number of assets, up to five digits, reported at item 9 label T of the company return for income years from 2020-21 to 2022-23.
limitation: It is a count of claims, not of assets acquired, and the ATO says a lodger "will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect amount at S and T where you have made your best attempt", so it is an estimate. A small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules pools its assets and may report the pool rather than the assets, which makes the count incomparable between firms of different sizes.
rationale: The item 9 instructions define the temporary full expensing asset count label and the accuracy standard the ATO applies to it.
evidence_quote: You will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect amount at S and T where you have made your best attempt to determine the amounts you are claiming for.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Temporary full expensing - Number of assets you are claiming for" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Temporary full expensing opt-out choice code
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Says whether the company chose to keep some, all or none of its eligible assets out of temporary full expensing. The ATO explains that "You can choose to opt out of temporary full expensing on an asset-by-asset basis in the income year it was acquired and apply the other depreciation rules to that asset", and that once made the choice cannot be revoked. Opting out is usually a loss company preserving deductions for later years rather than a firm that could not claim.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A single code at item 9 label P of the company return: A for some eligible assets, B for all, and a No response otherwise, carried in BLADE as ordinal codes 5, 10 and 15.
limitation: It does not say why the company opted out, and the asset count and value columns beside it are the only quantification of the choice. Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules could not opt out at all during the measure, so a No from such a firm is compulsory rather than chosen.
rationale: The item 9 instructions define the temporary full expensing opt-out label, its code values and the asset-by-asset nature of the choice.
evidence_quote: You can choose to opt out of temporary full expensing on an asset-by-asset basis in the income year it was acquired and apply the other depreciation rules to that asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Are you making a choice to opt out of temporary full expensing for some or all of your eligible assets" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Total adjustable value of depreciating assets at year end (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The written-down tax value of everything the company was still depreciating at the end of the year. The ATO instruction is "Write at E the total of the adjustable values of your depreciating assets as at the end of the income year", which it explains as "the value of all assets costs (first and second elements) less any decline in value up to that time". It is the closest thing the company return has to a capital stock measure.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 9 label E of the company return, a stock at the last day of the income year measured on tax written-down values rather than book or market values.
limitation: It is not the company's asset base. Assets costing under $1,000 that were allocated to a low-value pool are excluded by instruction, land and trading stock are not depreciating assets at all, and an asset written off in full under temporary full expensing drops to zero here while still being used, so the column falls sharply in the full expensing years without any disposal.
rationale: The item 9 instructions define the total adjustable values label, the meaning of adjustable value and the low-value pool exclusion.
evidence_quote: Write at E the total of the adjustable values of your depreciating assets as at the end of the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Total adjustable values at end of income year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Income tax liability of the earliest loss carry back year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The tax the company owed in the earliest of the years it could carry a loss back to, which is what caps the refund. The ATO says "The amount you can claim is capped at your unused income tax liability for that earlier income year", and that the liability is reduced by anything already claimed against it in a previous year's return. On the 2022 return this is the 2018-19 liability.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount at the item 13 loss carry back liability labels, reported for a prior income year rather than the return year, and net of any amount already used in an earlier loss carry back claim.
limitation: It is a restatement of a past year's tax by the company, not the ATO's assessed figure for that year, so it will not always agree with the earlier return in the same data. It also only appears when the company is making a loss carry back claim, so it is missing for the great majority of companies that had exactly the same liability.
rationale: Item 13 of the company return collects the prior year income tax liabilities that bound a loss carry back claim, and the instructions state the cap and the reduction for prior claims.
evidence_quote: The amount you can claim is capped at your unused income tax liability for that earlier income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Income tax liability for earliest year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Net exempt income of the earliest loss carry back year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: Unused net exempt income in the earliest year a loss could be carried back to, which reduces how much loss can be carried back there. The ATO defines it as "subtracting expenditure incurred in deriving exempt income from the amount of all income that is exempt from Australian tax", calculated under section 36-20 of the ITAA 1997. Only the unutilised part is reported, so it is a residual rather than the year's whole exempt income.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount at the item 13 net exempt income labels, reported for a prior income year and excluding any net exempt income already used.
limitation: It will not match the exempt income the company reported in that earlier year's return: the ATO says the figure "may differ from the amount of exempt income that was shown in that year's income tax return", because it is net of the expenditure that produced it and net of amounts already utilised.
rationale: Item 13 of the company return collects prior year net exempt income for the loss carry back calculation and the instructions define the term and warn that it differs from the earlier return.
evidence_quote: Net exempt income for an income year is calculated under section 36-20 of the ITAA 1997 and may differ from the amount of exempt income that was shown in that year's income tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Net exempt income for earliest year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Early stage investor tax offset, current year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 23 Early stage investor tax offset
variable_description: The tax offset the company earned this year by buying shares in early stage innovation companies. The ATO instruction is "Write at M the amount of early stage investor tax offset referrable to the current income year", and the offset is 20% of what was paid for eligible shares. It marks the company as an investor in start-ups, not as a start-up itself.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 23 Early stage investor tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 23 label M of the company return, a non-refundable carry forward tax offset equal to 20% of qualifying share subscriptions.
limitation: The $200,000 annual cap is shared with the carried-forward amount and with the company's affiliates, so the column is censored and cannot be scaled up by five to recover investment for larger investors. An investor that fails the sophisticated investor test is also capped at $50,000 of qualifying investment, which truncates the small end as well.
rationale: Item 23 of the company return defines the current year early stage investor offset label and the caps and steps that produce the amount.
evidence_quote: Write at M the amount of early stage investor tax offset referrable to the current income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Early stage investor tax offset C - current year tax offset" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Early stage investor tax offset carried forward from a previous year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 23 Early stage investor tax offset
variable_description: Unused early stage investor tax offset brought forward from earlier years, as distinct from the offset earned this year on the neighbouring label. The ATO instruction is "Write at R the amount of unused early stage investor tax offset carried forward from a previous year", and it may only be brought forward from income years commencing on or after 1 July 2016. A figure here means past investment that the company's tax position was too small to absorb.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 23 Early stage investor tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 23 label R of the company return, a carry-forward balance rather than a flow, subject to the tax offset carry forward rules in Division 65 of the ITAA 1997.
limitation: It is not a complete stock of unused entitlement. Division 65 requires the offset to be applied against net exempt income before it can reduce tax, and any amount that Division 65 blocks must be left out of this label, so the balance can fall for reasons that have nothing to do with the company using it.
rationale: Item 23 of the company return defines the carried forward early stage investor offset label and the Division 65 rules that govern what may be reported in it.
evidence_quote: Write at R the amount of unused early stage investor tax offset carried forward from a previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Early stage investor tax offset - tax offset carried forward from a previous year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset, current year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 22 Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset
variable_description: The tax offset the company earned this year from contributing to an early stage venture capital limited partnership. The ATO instruction is "Write at L the amount of ESVCLP tax offset referrable to the current income year", and for a limited partner it is capped at 10% of the lesser of contributions made and the partner's share of the fund's eligible investments. It records fund investment, where the early stage investor offset beside it records direct share purchases.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 22 Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 22 label L of the company return, a non-refundable carry forward tax offset at a rate of 10% of qualifying contributions.
limitation: It cannot be turned back into a contribution figure. The 10% applies to the lesser of the contribution and the partner's share of investments the fund actually made in a window ending two months after year end, so a company that contributed heavily to a slow-deploying fund reports a small offset. The partnership must also have registered unconditionally on or after 7 December 2015.
rationale: Item 22 of the company return defines the current year ESVCLP offset label and the formula and conditions behind the amount.
evidence_quote: Write at L the amount of ESVCLP tax offset referrable to the current income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset C - current year tax offset" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: ESVCLP tax offset carried forward from a previous year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 22 Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset
variable_description: Unused early stage venture capital limited partnership offset brought forward from earlier years, rather than earned this year. The ATO instruction is "Write at P the amount of ESVCLP tax offset carried forward from a previous year", and only offsets from income years commencing on or after 1 July 2016 may be brought forward. It is the venture capital twin of the carried-forward early stage investor offset.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 22 Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 22 label P of the company return, a carry-forward balance subject to the tax offset carry forward rules in Division 65 of the ITAA 1997.
limitation: A fall in the balance is not evidence that the company used the offset against tax. Division 65 makes the offset reduce net exempt income first, at $1 of net exempt income for each 25 or 30 cents of offset depending on the company's tax rate, and blocked amounts must be left off the label entirely.
rationale: Item 22 of the company return defines the carried forward ESVCLP offset label and the Division 65 rules that decide what may be reported in it.
evidence_quote: Write at P the amount of ESVCLP tax offset carried forward from a previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset - tax offset carried forward from a previous year" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Exempt income (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Income the company earned that Australian tax law exempts, subtracted from accounting profit in the reconciliation to taxable income. The ATO instruction is "Write at V all income that is exempt from Australian tax". Exempt income is not the same as income that simply is not assessable, and the return keeps the two apart deliberately.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label V of the company return, a subtraction in the reconciliation from total profit or loss to taxable income.
limitation: It is not all untaxed income. Non-assessable non-exempt amounts, including foreign branch profits and non-portfolio dividends exempted under sections 23AH and 23AJ, are reported at other income not included in assessable income instead, so a multinational with large untaxed foreign income can show nothing here. Exempt income also reduces carried-forward tax losses, which the column itself does not reveal.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define the exempt income label and list the non-assessable non-exempt categories that must be reported elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Write at V all income that is exempt from Australian tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Exempt income" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Losses and deductions from financial arrangements under TOFA (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The company's total allowable losses on financial arrangements taxed under the taxation of financial arrangements rules. The ATO instruction is "Write at U the total of all allowable TOFA losses from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7", and it lists the seven labels those losses are drawn from, including bad debts and interest expenses. It is a memorandum total that runs across the return rather than a separate expense.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label U of the company return, aggregating TOFA losses already reported inside the item 6 expense labels and the item 7 TOFA deduction label.
limitation: Adding it to total expenses double-counts, because every dollar in it is already inside another expense label. The DIL wording also does not identify which of the company return's two TOFA deduction labels the column carries, so a reader cannot tell from the name alone whether it is the item 8 total or the narrower item 7 deduction for arrangements not already at item 6.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the total TOFA losses label and enumerate the labels it aggregates, which is the only company return field matching an expenses-from-financial-arrangements description; the DIL label does not name a return label, so the mapping is inferred.
evidence_quote: Write at U the total of all allowable TOFA losses from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the DIL label "Expenses from financial arrangements (TOFA)" and the generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which company return label the number comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: What the company spent buying labour and services under contract rather than paying them as salary or wages. The ATO instruction for item 6 label C is to "Write at C the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages", and lists consultants and contractors, labour-hire and voluntary agreement workers, commissions to people not on a retainer, agency fees, service fees, management fees and consultants' fees. The DIL's second wording, External labour costs, is the earlier name for the same line, so the series is continuous across the rename.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, taken from the company's own profit and loss statement, and one of the expense labels A to S that sum to total expenses at item 6.
limitation: It is not the firm's total spending on labour bought in from outside. External labour absorbed into cost of sales sits at label A, and accounting and legal services sit at label S, so a manufacturer and a professional firm with identical outsourcing can report very different amounts here.
rationale: The DIL label is the exact wording of company tax return item 6 label C, including the parenthetical noting the earlier label, and the ATO instruction page defines what belongs at that label and what must go elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Write at C the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which contract labour lands here and which is diverted to cost of sales.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income, and the Company tax return 2005 form
variable_description: A single net line for gains and losses from events outside the company's ordinary trading, reported only on returns up to 2004-05. The ATO describes the amounts as "revenue or gains from events outside the ordinary operations of the company and not of a recurring nature, including work-in-progress amounts assessable under section 15-50 of the ITAA 1997". The company return carried a separate label N for extraordinary revenue or expenses to the 2005 form and dropped it from 2006, after which extraordinary revenue is folded into R Other gross income and extraordinary expenses into S All other expenses.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income, and the Company tax return 2005 form
value_definition: A dollar amount, net of revenue against expenses, sitting between operating profit or loss and total profit or loss in the item 6 arithmetic.
limitation: Nothing is recorded after the 2005 return, so a blank in later years means the label was abolished rather than that the firm had no unusual gains. Because revenue and expenses are netted into one figure, a large one-off gain offset by a large one-off write-down reads as close to zero.
rationale: The DIL label matches the label N wording on the company tax return form to 2005, and the current instructions define extraordinary revenue in the ATO's own words while showing where it now goes instead.
evidence_quote: any extraordinary revenue (that is, revenue or gains from events outside the ordinary operations of the company and not of a recurring nature, including work-in-progress amounts assessable under section 15-50 of the ITAA 1997)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the column exists only for the earliest BLADE years.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Overseas transactions, interests or thin capitalisation, items 26 to 30
variable_description: Whether the company answered yes to having had any dealings at all with international related parties during the year. The return asks "Did you have any transactions or dealings with international related parties (irrespective of whether they were on revenue or capital account)?", and the ATO explains that this covers services, money or property moving in or out of Australia, transfers of tangible or intangible property, and loans or financial services. Read it with the two neighbouring flags: the international dealings indicator records whether the aggregate crossed the reporting threshold, and the overseas interest indicator records branches and interests in foreign entities.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Overseas transactions, interests or thin capitalisation, items 26 to 30
value_definition: Y for yes and N for no, with anything else treated as an invalid or absent response. It is a single answer for the whole income year, not a count of transactions.
limitation: It carries no size and no direction. One small intra-group service charge and a multi-billion dollar related party loan book both produce Y, and a large exporter selling only to unrelated customers produces N, so it cannot stand in for a measure of a firm's international exposure.
rationale: The ATO page sets out the three yes or no questions in this block, and the BIT data item list carries a separate variable for each of them, so the overseas transaction indicator maps to the first question. The DIL does not print the label letter, so the mapping is read off the family rather than stated.
evidence_quote: Did you have any transactions or dealings with international related parties (irrespective of whether they were on revenue or capital account)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the Y and N code text with the generic sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say which of the return's several overseas questions this is.

value_domain: Functional currency code on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The foreign currency a company chose to keep its accounts in and to work out its taxable income, held as a currency code. The ATO instruction at item 8 label O is to "Print at O the functional currency code that corresponds to the functional currency chosen by the company", and the label is completed only where the translation rate at label N is also completed. Because the choice is available only to a company that keeps its accounts "solely or predominantly in a foreign currency", the column is blank for almost every filer and non-blank marks a distinctive class of internationally oriented firm.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A short code standing for a currency rather than a currency name; the BLADE data item list points to its own Appendix 3 for the category codes, and the ATO publishes the matching list as Currency codes for label 8O.
limitation: A code here does not mean the company transacts wholly in that currency. A company that uses a non-Australian functional currency only for an overseas permanent establishment, a controlled foreign company, an offshore banking unit or a transferor trust must leave the label blank, so those firms are indistinguishable from ordinary Australian dollar filers.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of company tax return item 8 label O, and the ATO instruction page states what the code is, when it must be completed and which companies are excluded from completing it.
evidence_quote: Print at O the functional currency code that corresponds to the functional currency chosen by the company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pointed at an appendix of codes and repeated the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained what a functional currency choice is or which firms make one.

value_domain: Currency translation rate on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The exchange rate the company used to convert its taxable income from its functional currency back into Australian dollars. The ATO defines it at item 8 label N as "the amount by which the functional currency amount must be divided in order to reflect an equivalent amount of A$, that is, the number of non-A$ currency units that equal one A$". It is completed only by a company that keeps its accounts solely or predominantly in a foreign currency and has chosen that currency for tax purposes, and it pairs with the currency code on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A positive rate carried to five decimal places in BLADE, expressed as units of the foreign currency per one Australian dollar. The ATO asks for it rounded to four significant figures on the form.
limitation: The direction of the rate is easy to invert, and doing so scales every derived Australian dollar figure the wrong way. It also applies to the single net taxable income figure, so it cannot be used to convert individual transactions or balance sheet items on other labels.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of company tax return item 8 label N, and the ATO instruction states the definition of the rate, its direction and its rounding.
evidence_quote: The translation rate is the amount by which the functional currency amount must be divided in order to reflect an equivalent amount of A$, that is, the number of non-A$ currency units that equal one A$, rounded to four significant figures.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the value has five decimal places and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing told a reader which way round the rate runs.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive schedule 2021 instructions, Part B Feedstock
variable_description: Extra assessable income the company had to bring to account because its subsidised R&D activities also produced saleable output. The ATO says "A feedstock adjustment is an amount you include in your assessable income", triggered when an R&D tax incentive offset was obtained for feedstock expenditure and the activities produced tangible products supplied to someone else or applied to the entity's own use. The amount is reported at item 21 label W of the company return and is also carried into other assessable income at item 7.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive schedule 2021 instructions, Part B Feedstock
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, worked out per R&D activity as one third of the lesser of feedstock revenue and the notional R&D deductions claimed for feedstock inputs, energy and the decline in value of related assets, then summed.
limitation: It is a clawback trigger, not a measure of R&D scale or of product sales. A large R&D claimant whose activities produced nothing marketable reports nothing here, so a blank cannot be read as an absence of R&D, and the year of the adjustment is the year the output was supplied rather than the year the expenditure arose.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of the feedstock adjustment item, and the ATO schedule instructions define the adjustment, its trigger and the arithmetic that produces the amount.
evidence_quote: A feedstock adjustment is an amount you include in your assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both slots, so nothing explained that this is a clawback of an R&D concession rather than ordinary income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 16 Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
variable_description: Fee income a life insurance company or friendly society brought to account, reported only by those entities. The ATO instruction at item 16 label F is to "Write at F the amount of all fees and charges included in assessable income", and it lists premium-based fees, establishment fees, time-based account fees, asset fees, switching fees, surrender penalties, buy-sell margins, exit fees and interest on overdue premiums. A friendly society that carries on no life insurance business writes zero across the whole of item 16.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 16 Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
value_definition: A dollar amount of assessable fee income for the income year, one of the labels B to F that make up item 16.
limitation: This is not a general business services line. Every company outside the life insurance and friendly society population leaves it blank, so it cannot be added across BLADE as an economy-wide measure of fee revenue, and it captures only the part of fees that is assessable income.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 16 label F exactly, and the ATO instruction page enumerates what belongs in the amount and which entities complete the item.
evidence_quote: Write at F the amount of all fees and charges included in assessable income. This includes premium-based fees, establishment fees, time-based account fees, asset fees, switching fees, surrender penalties, buy-sell margins, exit fees and interest on overdue premiums.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the two-word label and the generic sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that only life insurers and friendly societies ever populate it.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2011 form (NAT 0656), item 26 Foreign source income
variable_description: Whether the company crossed either of two foreign income thresholds set on the return, not whether it had any foreign income at all. The return asks "Was the amount of foreign income tax paid greater than $100,000 OR was the amount of assessable foreign income greater than $500,000?", and the earlier form worded the first limb as foreign tax credits paid or carried forward. The question sits in the overseas transactions block and appears on the company return from 2003 to 2012 only.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2011 form (NAT 0656), item 26 Foreign source income
value_definition: Y for yes and N for no, with anything else an invalid or absent response. It is a single answer covering the whole income year.
limitation: It is a threshold test, so a company with $400,000 of assessable foreign income answers no and looks identical to a purely domestic company. The label was removed after the 2012 return, so an empty cell in later years reflects the form, not the firm.
rationale: The DIL label matches the Foreign source income question on the company return form, and the form text gives the exact threshold wording and shows the years in which the question appears.
evidence_quote: Was the amount of foreign income tax paid greater than $100,000 OR was the amount of assessable foreign income greater than $500,000?
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the Y and N code text with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said that this is a threshold question rather than a plain has-foreign-income flag.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Tax losses moved into this company from a wholly owned group member, in the narrow case involving a foreign bank branch or foreign financial entity. The ATO instruction at item 7 label S is to "Write at S the amount of tax losses transferred to the company from group companies under Subdivision 170-A of the ITAA 1997", and the transfer is limited to loss the transferring company cannot use itself and cannot create a loss in the receiving company. The amount is a subtraction item, so it reduces taxable income in the year of transfer.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount of transferred loss deducted in the year of transfer, forming part of the item 7 subtraction items subtotal.
limitation: It is not group loss sharing in general. Losses transferred from subsidiaries to a consolidated or MEC head company under Subdivision 707-A are reported on the losses schedule instead, so the column badly understates how much loss moves between related companies.
rationale: The DIL label is the short form of company tax return item 7 label S, and the ATO instruction states the provision, the eligible parties and the exclusion for consolidated group transfers.
evidence_quote: Write at S the amount of tax losses transferred to the company from group companies under Subdivision 170-A of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read as a generic transferred-losses line with the no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing conveyed how narrow the eligible population is.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Assessable income the company earned from foreign sources, counted before expenses and grossed up for foreign tax. The ATO instruction at item 8 label G is to "Write at G assessable income derived by the company from foreign sources, grossed up by the amount of the foreign tax withheld or paid at source on that income". The net foreign income column on the same row is the same income after expenses, and the difference between the two is the closest thing on the return to a cost of earning offshore revenue.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of expenses and inclusive of foreign tax withheld or paid at source.
limitation: Being gross, it says nothing about whether offshore activity was profitable. It also excludes attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities and transferor trusts, which is reported separately at the listed country, unlisted country and transferor trust labels, so it is not the whole of a firm's foreign exposure.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 8 label G exactly, and the instruction page defines the gross-up and distinguishes it from net foreign income and attributed foreign income on the same item.
evidence_quote: Write at G assessable income derived by the company from foreign sources, grossed up by the amount of the foreign tax withheld or paid at source on that income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence in both slots, so nothing distinguished it from the net foreign income column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The balance of the company's franking account, the running record of tax paid that is available to attach to dividends. The current instruction at item 8 label M is to "Show at M Closing franking account balance the balance of the franking account at the end of 2021-22". The label was a single Franking account balance to the 2020 return and was split into an opening balance at label P and a closing balance at label M from the 2021 return, when the loss carry back offset made both years' positions relevant.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount that is a stock at a point in time rather than a flow for the year, reported at the end of the income year on returns from 2021 and at a single balance date before that.
limitation: A franking account in deficit is not shown at all: the company leaves the label blank, lodges a franking account tax return and pays franking deficit tax, so blank and zero are different states and the column can never go negative.
rationale: The DIL label matches the single Franking account balance label M carried on the company return form to 2020, and the current instruction page defines the label and records the split into opening and closing balances.
evidence_quote: Show at M Closing franking account balance the balance of the franking account at the end of 2021-22.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label and the generic sentence twice, so nothing told a reader that the label changed meaning from 2021 or that deficits are missing rather than negative.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: Money employees paid the company towards fringe benefits they received, which the tax law treats as the company's income. The ATO instruction at item 6 label I is to "Write at I all payments that the company has received from recipients of fringe benefits", because employee contributions form part of the employer's assessable income. A head company of a consolidated or MEC group includes contributions received by any entity that was a subsidiary member at the time.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A dollar amount of receipts for the income year, forming part of total income at item 6 alongside sales, interest, rent and dividends.
limitation: It measures what employees paid, not what the benefits cost or what fringe benefits tax the company bore. A firm providing large fringe benefits with no employee contribution reports nothing here, so the column cannot be used to rank employers by the generosity of non-wage benefits.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of company tax return item 6 label I, and the instruction page states what the payments are and why they are assessable.
evidence_quote: Write at I all payments that the company has received from recipients of fringe benefits.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic sentence in both fields, so nothing explained that the amount flows from employees to the employer rather than the other way.

value_domain: Percentage reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 2 Description of main business activity
variable_description: How much of the company is held offshore, measured as the combined stake of the foreign holders among its ten largest shareholders. The ATO instruction at item 2 label A is to "Examine the top 10 shareholders of the company at the end of the income year. From these top 10 shareholders, identify the foreign shareholders and aggregate their percentage of shareholding held in the company. Write this percentage in whole numbers at A. If this aggregate percentage is less than 10%, disregard A." A foreign shareholder includes one with an overseas address on the register, one directing dividends offshore, and a company not incorporated in Australia or without an ACN.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 2 Description of main business activity
value_definition: A whole number percentage from 10 to 100, measured at the end of the income year. The label first appears on the 2010 company return, so earlier BLADE years have no value.
limitation: It is truncated at both ends. Foreign holders outside the top ten are never counted, and an aggregate below 10 per cent is left blank, so a blank means small or none rather than zero. It is also a single register position at year end, not average foreign ownership over the year, and beneficial owners behind nominee holdings are not seen.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 2 label A, and the ATO instruction gives the counting rule, the reporting floor and the definition of a foreign shareholder.
evidence_quote: Examine the top 10 shareholders of the company at the end of the income year. From these top 10 shareholders, identify the foreign shareholders and aggregate their percentage of shareholding held in the company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the response is a numeric percentage and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the measure covers only the top ten holders and only above 10 per cent.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels E, T4 and F
variable_description: The credit the company claimed for franking deficit tax it had already paid, applied against this year's income tax. The ATO says the amounts at calculation statement label F "are not refundable. They are only offset against gross tax, if there is any gross tax to be paid after C, D and E have been applied to gross tax", and any excess carries forward. The figure combines the current year offset with any offset brought forward from earlier years, so it is the last step in the calculation statement before tax payable.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels E, T4 and F
value_definition: A dollar amount of offset applied, taken after non-refundable, carry forward and refundable offsets have already reduced gross tax.
limitation: It is the offset used, not the franking deficit tax incurred. The offset reduction rule cuts the claimable amount by 30 per cent of the deficit in defined circumstances, so the column understates over-franking, and an excess that could not be used this year sits invisibly in a carry-forward balance.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of the franking deficit tax offset label in the company return calculation statement, and the ATO page sets out its priority, its non-refundable character and the reduction rule.
evidence_quote: The tax offsets shown at F are not refundable. They are only offset against gross tax, if there is any gross tax to be paid after C, D and E have been applied to gross tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence in both slots, so nothing said this is a claim against tax rather than a liability, or where it sits in the offset ordering.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 20 Foreign income tax offset
variable_description: Credit the company claimed for foreign tax it had paid, under the foreign tax credit system that ran on the company return to the 2008 form. From the 2008-09 income year the credit was replaced by the foreign income tax offset, which the ATO caps so that it "cannot exceed the lesser of: the foreign income tax paid, or its foreign income tax offset limit (the greater of $1,000 and the amount calculated under paragraph 770-75(2)(b) of the ITAA 1997)". The old label sat in the calculation statement beside gross tax, so it is a reduction in tax payable rather than an income item.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 20 Foreign income tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount of credit claimed against Australian tax payable for the income year, appearing on company return forms to 2008 only.
limitation: The series stops after the 2008 return and is not continuous with the foreign income tax offset that replaced it: the old system quarantined credits by class of income and allowed unused credits to be carried forward for five years, while Division 770 does neither.
rationale: The DIL label matches the Foreign tax credits label in the company return calculation statement, which the forms show running to 2008, and the current ATO page defines the replacement offset and its limit.
evidence_quote: The company's foreign income tax offset cannot exceed the lesser of: the foreign income tax paid, or its foreign income tax offset limit (the greater of $1,000 and the amount calculated under paragraph 770-75(2)(b) of the ITAA 1997).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the three-word label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the column belongs to a superseded regime and stops in 2008.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Costs the company incurred directly in earning income that was subject to foreign resident withholding. The ATO instruction at item 6 label B is to "Write at B all expenses directly relating to gaining income subject to foreign resident withholding", and those amounts must not be repeated at any other expense label. Only a foreign resident completes the label, and it is the matched expense side of the withholding income reported at the income label B on the same item.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported separately from the other item 6 expense labels and excluded from them.
limitation: It is not a general measure of a firm's internationally related costs. An Australian resident is told not to put the expenses of earning foreign source income here, so a resident exporter shows nothing at all, and the column identifies foreign residents rather than international activity.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of company tax return item 6 expenses label B, and the ATO page states which entities complete it and that the amounts must not be duplicated elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Write at B all expenses directly relating to gaining income subject to foreign resident withholding
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said that only foreign residents populate it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: Payments made to the company that were subject to foreign resident withholding, counted before any tax was taken out. The ATO instruction at item 6 income label B is to "Write at B the gross payments made to the company that were subject to foreign resident withholding. Gross payments include amounts of tax withheld, or that should have been withheld." The expense label B at the same item carries the costs of earning this income, and the two together isolate the withholding-taxed part of a foreign resident's Australian business.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of tax withheld, and gross even of tax that should have been withheld but was not, forming part of total income at item 6.
limitation: It covers only payments inside the foreign resident withholding regime, so it is not the whole of what a foreign resident earned in Australia; income taxed by ordinary assessment or by other withholding rules appears at other labels.
rationale: The DIL label is the short form of company tax return item 6 income label B, and the instruction page states the gross basis and the treatment of tax that should have been withheld.
evidence_quote: Write at B the gross payments made to the company that were subject to foreign resident withholding. Gross payments include amounts of tax withheld, or that should have been withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing spelled out what foreign resident withholding is or that the figure is before tax.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Accelerated depreciation claimed for the first time on assets brought in under the Backing business investment measure. The ATO instruction at item 9 label M is to "Show at M the total amount claimed using Backing business investment for assets first used or installed ready for use in 2020-21", made up of "50% of the cost (or adjustable value where applicable) of the depreciating asset in the income year the asset is first used or installed ready for use, plus the amount of the usual depreciation deduction that would otherwise apply, but calculated as if the cost or adjustable value of the asset were reduced by 50%". A separate label carries later-year claims on the same assets, so this column isolates new entrants to the measure.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount of deduction for the income year, restricted to assets for which the measure is being used for the first time.
limitation: The measure was temporary and was largely overtaken by temporary full expensing, so the column is confined to the 2019-20 and 2020-21 returns; a blank elsewhere reflects the label not existing rather than an absence of capital spending, and it counts deduction claimed rather than the asset's cost.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of company tax return item 9 label M on the 2020 and 2021 forms, and the ATO instruction gives the arithmetic of the first-year claim and distinguishes it from the subsequent-year label.
evidence_quote: Show at M the total amount claimed using Backing business investment for assets first used or installed ready for use in 2020-21.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the measure was, when it ran, or how the first-year amount differs from later years.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: Income the company received from a forestry managed investment scheme in which it holds a forestry interest. The ATO instruction at item 6 label X is to "Write at X the total income from the following activities for each FMIS in which the company holds a forestry interest", covering thinning proceeds and the amounts triggered when a CGT event happens to the interest through a sale or a harvest. What goes in depends on whether the company is an initial participant, who obtained the interest from the forestry manager, or a subsequent participant, who bought it on the secondary market.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, part of total income at item 6, combining actual thinning receipts with formula amounts based on the market value of the forestry interest.
limitation: It is not the cash the scheme paid the company. On a sale or harvest the entry is a market value or the output of a prescribed formula, and any capital gain from the scheme is excluded and shown instead as net capital gain at item 7, so the column cannot be read as scheme proceeds.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 6 label X, and the ATO instruction defines the scheme, the two classes of participant and each amount that goes into the total.
evidence_quote: Write at X the total income from the following activities for each FMIS in which the company holds a forestry interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained that the figure mixes cash receipts with market value amounts.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Payments to a forestry managed investment scheme manager that the company deducted this year. The ATO instruction at item 7 label U is to "Write at U Forestry managed investment scheme deduction the total amount of deductible payments made to an FMIS", and the deduction is available only where the manager has advised that the scheme meets the 70 per cent direct forestry expenditure rule, the company has no day to day control, and the trees are established within 18 months of the end of the year of first payment. The deduction is claimed in the year the payment is made, not when the trees grow.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount of deductible payments for the income year, forming part of the item 7 subtraction items.
limitation: A subsequent participant cannot deduct what it paid to acquire the interest, only ongoing payments, so the column understates what a secondary-market investor put in. Borrowing costs, interest-like payments, stamp duty, GST, post-felling transport, processing and stockpiling payments are all excluded even though the scheme received them.
rationale: The DIL label is the short form of company tax return item 7 label U, and the ATO instruction states the deduction test, the timing rule and the list of excluded payments.
evidence_quote: Write at U Forestry managed investment scheme deduction the total amount of deductible payments made to an FMIS.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing separated deductible scheme payments from the many payments that are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 20 Foreign income tax offset
variable_description: Foreign tax the company was treated as having paid but did not, because a foreign government waived it and an Australian tax treaty preserves the credit. The ATO states that "Foreign income tax includes foreign tax forgone on income by foreign countries under tax sparing arrangements where the tax sparing amounts are subject to Australia's tax treaty with the relevant country". The company return label reads Tax spared foreign tax credits to the 2008 form and Tax spared foreign income tax offset from 2009, and it disappears after the 2012 form.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 20 Foreign income tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount of notional foreign tax reported at item 8 of the company return, alongside net foreign income and the attributed foreign income labels.
limitation: The money was never paid to any revenue authority, so adding it to foreign tax paid double counts the firm's tax burden and overstates the cost of operating offshore. The column also ends after the 2012 return, so later years are silent rather than zero.
rationale: The DIL label matches the tax spared label carried on the company return form from 2003 to 2012, and the current ATO page states in its own words that tax sparing amounts count as foreign income tax under Australia's treaties.
evidence_quote: Foreign income tax includes foreign tax forgone on income by foreign countries under tax sparing arrangements where the tax sparing amounts are subject to Australia's tax treaty with the relevant country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained that tax sparing is a notional credit for tax a country chose not to collect.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The income tax the company was assessed for 2018-19, restated on a later return so a loss carried back to that year can be refunded. The ATO instruction is to "write at label L the amount of income tax assessed to the entity for the 2018-19 income year. This is the amount assessed in the Calculation statement at label T5 Tax payable of the Company tax return 2019 or the tax liability after any amendments to the 2018-19 income year." 2018-19 is the earliest year a loss can be carried back to, so this is the deepest reach of the measure.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount copied forward from an earlier year's assessment, or from the amended figure if that assessment has since changed.
limitation: It is only present where the company chose to carry a loss back to 2018-19, so it is not a population measure of 2018-19 company tax. Being a restatement made years later, it can also differ from what the 2018-19 return itself recorded.
rationale: The DIL label matches the loss carry back income tax liability label for 2018-19, and the ATO instruction names the exact source figure the company must copy.
evidence_quote: write at label L the amount of income tax assessed to the entity for the 2018-19 income year. This is the amount assessed in the Calculation statement at label T5 Tax payable of the Company tax return 2019 or the tax liability after any amendments to the 2018-19 income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is a restatement of an earlier assessment rather than this year's tax.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: Exempt income left unused in 2018-19, which has to be absorbed before a loss can be carried back to that year. The ATO explains that "Net exempt income can be derived by subtracting expenditure incurred in deriving exempt income from the amount of all income that is exempt from Australian tax", calculated under section 36-20 of the ITAA 1997, and instructs the company to leave out any amount already used. Of the four net exempt income labels this is the one attached to the earliest carry back year.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount for 2018-19 on a section 36-20 basis, which the ATO warns "may differ from the amount of exempt income that was shown in that year's income tax return".
limitation: Only the unutilised remainder is reported, so it understates the exempt income the company actually had in 2018-19, and it appears only where a loss is being carried back to that year. Most companies have no exempt income at all, so a blank carries almost no information.
rationale: The DIL label matches the net exempt income label for 2018-19 in the loss carry back block, and the ATO instruction defines net exempt income and states the unutilised restriction.
evidence_quote: Net exempt income can be derived by subtracting expenditure incurred in deriving exempt income from the amount of all income that is exempt from Australian tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing conveyed that only the unused remainder is reported.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The company's actual aggregated turnover for 2019-20, which only the very largest loss carry back claimants have to state. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label P your actual aggregated turnover rounded to the nearest $100 million if you selected category P (that is, aggregated turnover $1 billion or over) at label O or are a significant global entity and completed label O." The figure may be either the 2019-20 turnover or the prior year's 2018-19 turnover, at the company's choice.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount rounded to the nearest $100 million, so the smallest reportable step is larger than the turnover of most companies in the register.
limitation: It is blank for nearly every filer, since only billion-dollar entities and significant global entities complete it, and the ATO adds that a company "will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect amount" where it made its best attempt, so it is a self-assessed estimate rather than an accounting figure.
rationale: The DIL label matches the aggregated turnover amount label for 2019-20 in the loss carry back block, and the ATO instruction states the completion condition, the rounding and the choice of year.
evidence_quote: Write at label P your actual aggregated turnover rounded to the nearest $100 million if you selected category P (that is, aggregated turnover $1 billion or over) at label O or are a significant global entity and completed label O.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the parenthetical label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is reported only above $1 billion and only to the nearest $100 million.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover range category on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: Which turnover band the company put itself in for 2019-20 when it claimed the loss carry back offset. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label O the category for your aggregated turnover range for 2019-20", choosing from sixteen categories A to P that run from $0 to under $7.5 million up to $1 billion or over, and "Your aggregated turnover range selected can be either your 2019-20 aggregated turnover or your 2018-19 aggregated turnover." The choice of band also decides whether the exact turnover amount on the same row has to be given.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A banded code running 5 to 80 in steps of 5, mapping onto the sixteen lettered categories A to P; the bands are narrow at the bottom and very wide at the top.
limitation: The band can come from either of two income years, so a company whose turnover moved sharply can sit in a band that describes neither year well. The ATO also says a company "will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect category" where it made its best attempt, so the code is self-assessed.
rationale: The DIL label and its sixteen coded categories reproduce the aggregated turnover range table in the ATO loss carry back instructions for 2019-20.
evidence_quote: Write at label O the category for your aggregated turnover range for 2019-20. Select a category from the table above based on your aggregated turnover range and write the category code at label O.
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the code labels but repeated the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the band may be taken from either of two years or that it is self-assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: Income tax assessed for 2019-20, restated when a later loss is carried back against that year. The ATO instruction is to "write at label M the amount of income tax assessed to the entity for the 2019-20 income year. This is the amount assessed in the Calculation statement at T5 Tax payable of the Company tax return 2020 or the tax liability after any amendments to the 2019-20 income year." 2019-20 sits in the middle of the measure: it can be a loss year whose loss is carried back, and a liability year that a later loss is carried back to.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount from the 2020 assessment or its amended figure, restated on a 2021, 2022 or 2023 return.
limitation: The offset for this year is capped at this liability, so the column bounds the refund rather than describing the company's 2019-20 tax position generally. It is present only where a carry back to 2019-20 was chosen, which excludes almost all companies.
rationale: The DIL label matches the loss carry back income tax liability label for 2019-20, and the ATO instruction names the assessment figure to be copied.
evidence_quote: write at label M the amount of income tax assessed to the entity for the 2019-20 income year. This is the amount assessed in the Calculation statement at T5 Tax payable of the Company tax return 2020 or the tax liability after any amendments to the 2019-20 income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a cap on the refundable offset.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: Unused net exempt income for 2019-20, subtracted from a loss before that loss is carried back to 2019-20. The ATO instruction is that "If the entity is choosing to carry back a tax loss to the 2019-20 income year, write at label J the amount of any unutilised net exempt income that the entity had in the 2019-20 income year." It is the second of the four year-specific net exempt income labels, and the year it names is the year the loss lands in, not the year the loss arose.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount calculated under section 36-20 of the ITAA 1997, excluding any amount already utilised in an earlier calculation.
limitation: A zero does not mean the company had no exempt income in 2019-20; it means none was left over after the 2019-20 return used it. The label is also completed only when a carry back to that year is being claimed.
rationale: The DIL label matches the net exempt income label for 2019-20 in the loss carry back block, and the ATO instruction ties the label to the year the loss is carried back to.
evidence_quote: If the entity is choosing to carry back a tax loss to the 2019-20 income year, write at label J the amount of any unutilised net exempt income that the entity had in the 2019-20 income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the other three net exempt income columns.

value_domain: Company tax rate for the income year
value_source: ATO, Company tax rates, tax rates 2011-12 to 2020-21
variable_description: The company tax rate that applied to this particular company in 2019-20, used to convert a 2019-20 loss carried back into a dollar offset. The ATO published two rates for that year: base rate entities paid 27.5 per cent and all other companies 30 per cent. Because the rate is the firm's own rather than a single statutory number, the column doubles as a marker of whether the company was a base rate entity in 2019-20.
description_source: ATO, Company tax rates, tax rates 2011-12 to 2020-21
value_definition: A proportion carried to four decimal places, so 0.2750 or 0.3000 for an ordinary company; special rates apply to life insurers, pooled development funds and credit unions.
