limitation: It is completed only where a 2019-20 loss is being carried back, so it cannot be used as a general indicator of base rate entity status across the register. It is also the rate for the loss year, not the rate of the year the loss is carried back to.
rationale: The DIL label matches the loss carry back tax rate label for 2019-20, and the ATO rates page publishes the two company rates that applied in that income year.
evidence_quote: Base rate entities 27.5 Otherwise 30
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the value has four decimal places and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which rates are possible or why they differ between companies.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: How much of the company's 2019-20 tax loss it chose to send back against its 2018-19 income tax liability. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label A the amount of tax losses incurred in 2019-20 that the entity is choosing to carry back to 2018-19", and this is the first and oldest of the ten carry back pairings the measure allows. The dollars here are loss, not refund: the offset itself is worked out from the loss, the tax rate for the loss year and the liability of the earlier year.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount of tax loss allocated to one earlier year, one of several such labels a company may complete in the same return.
limitation: It records a choice, not the size of the loss: a company may carry back part of a loss and keep the rest. The ATO adds that "If you choose to carry back some or all of your tax loss, this amount cannot be utilised again", so these dollars will not reappear in carried forward losses and a naive series of loss stocks will double count without this column.
rationale: The DIL label matches the 2019-20 to 2018-19 carry back label, and the ATO instruction states the pairing and the once-only use rule.
evidence_quote: Write at label A the amount of tax losses incurred in 2019-20 that the entity is choosing to carry back to 2018-19.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is elective or that it removes the loss from carry forward.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The company's actual aggregated turnover for 2020-21, stated only where the turnover band already reported was the top one. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label R your actual aggregated turnover rounded to the nearest $100 million if you selected category P (that is, aggregated turnover $1 billion or over) at label Q or are a significant global entity and completed label Q", and the figure may be either the 2020-21 or the 2019-20 turnover. It is the 2020-21 counterpart of the same disclosure made for the other loss years.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar amount rounded to the nearest $100 million, tied to the 2020-21 income year or, at the company's election, to 2019-20.
limitation: The $5 billion aggregated turnover eligibility test for loss carry back sits well above the $1 billion reporting trigger, so many eligible large companies never state a turnover figure at all and the column cannot rank them by size.
rationale: The DIL label matches the aggregated turnover amount label for 2020-21 in the loss carry back block, and the ATO instruction states its completion condition and rounding.
evidence_quote: Write at label R your actual aggregated turnover rounded to the nearest $100 million if you selected category P (that is, aggregated turnover $1 billion or over) at label Q or are a significant global entity and completed label Q.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the parenthetical label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which companies must complete it.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover range category on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The turnover band the company selected for 2020-21 in support of its loss carry back claim. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label Q the category for your aggregated turnover range for 2020-21" from the same sixteen-category table used for the other loss years, and "Your aggregated turnover range selected can be either your 2020-21 aggregated turnover or your 2019-20 aggregated turnover." Aggregated turnover means the group's turnover, not the single entity's, so a small company inside a large group falls in a high band.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A banded code from 5 to 80, mapping to categories A to P; the first band alone spans $0 to under $7.5 million, so most companies are indistinguishable within it.
limitation: Because the concept is aggregated turnover, this band cannot be read as the reporting entity's own sales, and it is completed only where a 2020-21 loss is being carried back rather than for every company with a 2020-21 turnover.

The amount at F cannot be a loss." Where the taxation of financial arrangements rules apply, all interest received or credited under those arrangements is included as well.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that cannot be negative, sitting on the income side of item 6 opposite the two interest expense labels.
limitation: It cannot be netted against the company's borrowing costs: interest expenses within Australia and overseas are separate expense labels, so a treasury operation running both sides shows a large gross figure here that says nothing about net interest position.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 6 income label F, and the instruction states the all-sources basis, the related party inclusion and the no-loss rule.
evidence_quote: Write at F the total interest from all sources, including interest received from or credited by an associate, a shareholder or an associate of a shareholder. The amount at F cannot be a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is gross and includes related party interest.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: What the company earned by letting out property or equipment, before any of the costs of doing so. The ATO instruction at item 6 label G, headed Gross rent and other leasing and hiring income, is to "Write at G the company's total income from leasing and hiring activities. The amount at G cannot be a loss." It puts real property rent and plant or vehicle hire in the same figure, so a landlord and an equipment hire business are not separable on this column alone.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that cannot be negative, and that is gross of rates, interest, repairs, depreciation and every other cost of holding the asset.
limitation: It is not net rental profit, and the offsetting costs are scattered across other labels: rent expenses, lease expenses within Australia and overseas, interest expenses and depreciation each sit on their own line, so a negatively geared property company still reports a positive figure here.
rationale: The DIL label is the short form of company tax return item 6 income label G, and the instruction defines the label as total leasing and hiring income.
evidence_quote: Write at G the company's total income from leasing and hiring activities. The amount at G cannot be a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is gross or that rent and equipment hire are combined.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 16 Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
variable_description: Superannuation contributions that moved from a complying fund into a life insurance company and became that company's assessable income. The ATO instruction at item 16 label E is to "Write at E assessable contributions of complying superannuation funds that were transferred to the life insurance company under section 295-260 of the ITAA 1997 and are included in its assessable income under paragraph 320-15(1)(i) of the ITAA 1997." Because life insurers split taxable income into an ordinary class and a complying superannuation class, these contributions fall in the second class and are taxed at the superannuation rate.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 16 Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, one of the labels B to F that make up item 16 of the company return.
limitation: It is not a measure of superannuation contributions made by or for the company's own employees. Only life insurance companies and friendly societies carrying on life insurance business complete it, and the amount arises from a transfer between institutions rather than from employer or member payments.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 16 label E, and the ATO instruction cites the provisions that make the transferred contributions assessable to the life company.
evidence_quote: Write at E assessable contributions of complying superannuation funds that were transferred to the life insurance company under section 295-260 of the ITAA 1997 and are included in its assessable income under paragraph 320-15(1)(i) of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label with the generic sentence twice, so a reader would take it for ordinary superannuation contributions rather than a transfer between a fund and a life insurer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
variable_description: The company's tax before any offset or credit is applied, the starting point of the calculation statement. The ATO instruction is that "If you are not an RSA provider, write at B the total of amounts at T1 and M", where T1 is tax on taxable income and M is R&D recoupment tax; a retirement savings account provider adds its further tax on no-TFN contributions income as well. Every offset in the statement is then applied against this figure in a fixed order, so gross tax is the ceiling on what any offset can be worth.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, equal to tax on taxable or net income plus R&D recoupment tax, and mandatory on the return even where it is zero.
limitation: It is not the tax the company actually paid. Non-refundable, carry forward, refundable and franking deficit tax offsets are all deducted after this point, so a company with substantial gross tax can end the statement with nothing payable or with a refund.
rationale: The DIL label matches the gross tax label of the company return calculation statement, and the ATO page gives its composition and its role at the head of the offset ordering.
evidence_quote: If you are not an RSA provider, write at B the total of amounts at T1 and M.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing distinguished gross tax from tax payable.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels T5 and G
variable_description: An interest charge the company owed on money it received from a non-resident trust. The ATO instruction at calculation statement label G is to "Write at G any section 102AAM interest relating to a distribution received from a non-resident trust. Section 102AAM of the ITAA 1936 imposes an interest charge on certain distributions from non-resident trusts." The charge compensates for the deferral of Australian tax while income accumulated offshore, so a figure here marks a company on the receiving end of an offshore trust structure.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels T5 and G
value_definition: A dollar amount added in the calculation statement after tax payable, so it increases the amount due rather than reducing an offset.
limitation: It is an interest charge, not tax on the distribution itself; the distribution is assessed separately, so the column cannot be used to size offshore trust income. It is also rare, and a blank tells a reader nothing about whether the company has non-resident trust connections.
rationale: The DIL label matches the section 102AAM interest charge label in the company return calculation statement, and the ATO page defines the charge and its trigger.
evidence_quote: Write at G any section 102AAM interest relating to a distribution received from a non-resident trust. Section 102AAM of the ITAA 1936 imposes an interest charge on certain distributions from non-resident trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the section reference as its description with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the charge is for.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Income the company had to bring to account because it disposed of an intangible depreciating asset for more than its written down value. The ATO instruction at item 9 label F is to "Write at F the total assessable income you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred this income year (this type of assessable income may arise if, for example, you disposed of an intangible depreciating asset for more than its adjustable value)." Intangible depreciating assets here means patents, registered designs, copyrights and licences of them, in-house software, and mining, quarrying or prospecting rights and information.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, left blank rather than zeroed where there is nothing to report, and excluding assets costing under $1,000 that were allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: It records the recovered depreciation, not the sale price or the gain: the termination value of the same assets is reported on a separate label, and the deductible side of balancing adjustments sits on another again, so no single column shows what a company realised on selling its intellectual property.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 9 label F, and the ATO instruction defines the balancing adjustment, gives the example that produces assessable income, and excludes low-value pool assets.
evidence_quote: Write at F the total assessable income you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred this income year (this type of assessable income may arise if, for example, you disposed of an intangible depreciating asset for more than its adjustable value).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what an intangible depreciating asset is or why a disposal creates income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The deduction the company got because it disposed of an intangible depreciating asset for less than its written down value. The ATO instruction at item 9 label G is to "Write at G the total deductible amount you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred this income year (this type of deduction may arise if, for example, you disposed of an intangible depreciating asset for less than its adjustable value)." It is the mirror image of the assessable balancing adjustment on the row above, and a company can report both in the same year on different assets.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, left blank where there is nothing to report, and excluding assets allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: A large amount here does not mean the assets failed commercially; it can equally mean the depreciation rate used was too slow for how the asset actually lost value, which the balancing adjustment then corrects in one step.
rationale: The DIL label matches company tax return item 9 label G, and the ATO instruction defines the deductible side of the balancing adjustment with its own example.
evidence_quote: Write at G the total deductible amount you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred this income year (this type of deduction may arise if, for example, you disposed of an intangible depreciating asset for less than its adjustable value).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing separated it from the assessable balancing adjustment on the neighbouring label.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Capital spending a resources company wrote off immediately rather than depreciating, chiefly on exploration and site rehabilitation. The ATO instruction at item 7 label E is that "Companies in the mining, petroleum and quarrying industries should write at E the total amount of capital expenditure (other than on depreciating assets) claimed as an immediate deduction for: exploration and prospecting, rehabilitation of mining or quarrying sites, payment of petroleum resource rent tax." It is a subtraction item in the reconciliation, so it reduces taxable income below accounting profit.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year covering capital expenditure other than on depreciating assets, deducted in full in the year it is incurred.
limitation: The label is written for the mining, petroleum and quarrying industries, so it is not a general immediate write-off measure and should not be confused with the instant asset write-off or temporary full expensing, which are reported at their own labels.
rationale: The DIL label is the short form of company tax return item 7 label E, and the ATO instruction names the industries and the three categories of expenditure that belong in it.
evidence_quote: Companies in the mining, petroleum and quarrying industries should write at E the total amount of capital expenditure (other than on depreciating assets) claimed as an immediate deduction for: exploration and prospecting, rehabilitation of mining or quarrying sites, payment of petroleum resource rent tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the label is confined to resources industries.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label D
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Income
variable_description: What the company received as a partner in one or more partnerships, before any tax adjustment. The ATO instruction is to "Write at D the gross distribution from all partnerships, including any share of franking credits attributable to dividends paid by an Australian company." It is an accounting-statement figure taken from the firm's own books, and it can be negative: the form marks a loss with an indicator letter rather than a minus sign.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Income
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, on the accounting basis used at item 6, gross of the expenses the company itself incurred as a partner. Those expenses sit at item 6 label S.
limitation: It names no partnership and gives no count, so the firm cannot be joined to the partnerships behind the number. It is also not assessable income: distributions from a corporate limited partnership are reported as dividends instead, and the tax adjustments to this figure are made at item 7 labels B and X.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 income label D, and the ATO instruction page for item 6 income defines what goes in it and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: Write at D the gross distribution from all partnerships, including any share of franking credits attributable to dividends paid by an Australian company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare form label 'Gross distribution from partnerships' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said this was an accounting figure that can be a loss.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label E
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Income
variable_description: What the company received as a beneficiary of one or more trusts, as advised by the trustees. The ATO instruction is to "Write at E the total amount of gross distributions received from trusts, including any share of franking credits attributable to dividends paid by an Australian company as advised by the trustee." Unlike the partnership column beside it, the ATO states that "The amount at E cannot be a loss", and a code box on the same form records which type of trust supplied the largest share.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Income
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, floored at zero, on the accounting basis used at item 6.
limitation: Because the label cannot be negative, a firm carrying trust losses looks the same as a firm with no trust interest at all. It also excludes capital gains distributed by the trust, which are reported at item 7 label A, and distributions from public trading trusts and corporate unit trusts, which are reported as dividends, so it understates what the firm draws from trust structures.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 income label E, and the ATO instruction page defines the amount, the floor at zero and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: Write at E the total amount of gross distributions received from trusts, including any share of franking credits attributable to dividends paid by an Australian company as advised by the trustee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave a reader no way to tell it from the partnership distribution column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessable gains from financial arrangements under Division 230 (TOFA)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information, taxation of financial arrangements section
variable_description: Income the firm reported from financial arrangements taxed under the taxation of financial arrangements rules in Division 230. The company return asks for the total of these gains separately from the income labels they are spread across: "Write at T the total of all assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7." A non-zero value is close to a size marker, because the rules only bind large entities and financial-sector entities unless a firm elects in.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information, taxation of financial arrangements section
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, covering gains brought to account under the accruals, realisation, fair value, foreign exchange retranslation, hedging and financial reports methods in Division 230.
limitation: The rules apply only above thresholds, an aggregated turnover of $100 million, assets of $300 million or financial assets of $100 million for a general entity and $20 million turnover for a financial-sector entity, so an empty column is not evidence that the firm holds no financial arrangements. The gains are also already inside the interest, dividend and other income labels, so adding this column to those double counts. Which of the two TOFA income labels this column carries, the item 8 total or the item 7 not-in-item-6 residual, is inferred from the label wording.
rationale: The label names TOFA income on a company return, and the ATO's item 8 instructions define the TOFA gains labels, the entities the rules apply to and the income labels the gains are drawn from.
evidence_quote: Write at T the total of all assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the label 'Income from financial arrangements (TOFA)' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that the column is empty for all but the largest firms.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the company return, internet trading question
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2017 instructions, 24. Internet trading
variable_description: Whether the firm used the internet to transact, not merely to have a presence online. The ATO sets a high bar: answer yes if the company used the internet to "receive orders for goods or services", "receive payment for goods or services" or "deliver goods or services", and no if it used the internet only to "advertise the company's goods or services", "give support to the company's customers", "buy the company's stock" or "do the company's banking online". The answer is the company's own, made without any dollar figure behind it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2017 instructions, 24. Internet trading
value_definition: A single character, Y for yes and N for no, with any other value meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It cannot measure how much a firm sells online, because no value is attached and the question is a threshold rather than a share. A firm with a full brochure website that takes no orders records a no, so the column understates digital adoption. The question is also absent from the 2022 company return, so a series across the change ends rather than falling to zero.
rationale: The ATO's internet trading item on the company return sets out exactly which uses of the internet count as yes and which count as no, which is the fact a reader needs before treating the flag as e-commerce.
evidence_quote: Print X in the No box at Q if the company used the internet only to: advertise the company's goods or services, give support to the company's customers, buy the company's stock, do the company's banking online.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Internet Trading Indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would have taken it for a measure of online selling.

value_domain: Dollar cost of assets, company return item 9 label A
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 9. Capital allowances
variable_description: The cost of the intangible assets the firm began depreciating for the first time this year. The ATO instruction is to "Write at A the cost of all intangible depreciating assets for which the company is claiming a deduction for decline in value for the first time", and the assets it counts are named: patents, registered designs, copyrights and licences of these, in-house software, mining, quarrying or prospecting rights and information, spectrum and datacasting licences, and certain telecommunications rights. It is a flow of new intangible capital, not the stock, which is at item 9 label E.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 9. Capital allowances
value_definition: A whole-dollar cost, not reduced for expected non-taxable use, and including intangibles under $1,000 that were put into a low-value pool.
limitation: Cost at first deduction is not spending in the year: an intangible bought earlier but first used for a taxable purpose this year appears now. In-house software allocated to a software development pool is left out entirely, and internally generated brands, goodwill and know-how never appear, so the column cannot stand in for a firm's intangible capital.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 9 label A, and the ATO capital allowances page defines the amount and lists the intangibles that qualify as depreciating assets.
evidence_quote: Write at A the cost of all intangible depreciating assets for which the company is claiming a deduction for decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which intangibles count or that the figure is a first-deduction cost rather than the year's spend.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the company return, international related party dealings question
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, overseas transactions, interests or thin capitalisation (items 26 to 30)
variable_description: Whether the firm dealt with international related parties during the year, on revenue or capital account. The ATO defines those parties as "persons who are not dealing wholly independently with one another in their international commercial or financial relations", and counts the provision of services, transfers of money or property, transfers of tangible or intangible property and the provision or receipt of loans. A yes generally requires an International dealings schedule to be lodged as well.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, overseas transactions, interests or thin capitalisation (items 26 to 30)
value_definition: A single character, Y for yes and N for no, with any other value meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It records existence, not size: the $2 million aggregate test sits at a separate question, so a firm with one small intra-group service charge and one with billions in related-party financing both answer yes. Agents for non-residents lodging on the listed activities are directed to answer no regardless of the underlying flows. Whether this column carries the existence question or the $2 million question is inferred from the label wording.
rationale: The overseas transactions items on the company return are the only international dealings yes-or-no questions on the form, and the ATO page defines who counts as an international related party and what counts as a dealing.
evidence_quote: International related parties are persons who are not dealing wholly independently with one another in their international commercial or financial relations
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only 'International dealings indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a dealing is or that the flag carries no magnitude.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label V
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: What the firm paid to service debt raised in Australia, as an accounting expense. The ATO instruction is to "Write at V the interest expenses incurred on money borrowed from Australian sources." Read against the overseas interest column beside it, the pair splits a firm's borrowing cost by where the lender sits, and read against item 8 label J it gives an implied cost of debt.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6, including interest on financial arrangements where the TOFA rules apply to the company.
limitation: It is the expense in the accounts, not the deduction allowed. Where thin capitalisation disallows part of the interest, the disallowed part is added back at item 7 label W and stays in this column, so the figure overstates deductible interest for geared multinationals. Distributions on non-share equity interests are not deductible either and are handled the same way.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 expense label V, and the ATO expenses page defines it and states where non-deductible interest is added back.
evidence_quote: Write at V the interest expenses incurred on money borrowed from Australian sources.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount is an accounting expense rather than an allowed deduction.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label J
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: What the firm paid to service debt raised offshore. The ATO instruction is to "Write at J the interest expenses incurred on money borrowed from overseas sources", and a non-zero amount pulls a second form with it: "If an amount is reported at J, complete and attach an International dealings schedule 2022." Interest paid to non-residents also generally attracts withholding tax, which the company remits separately.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6, including interest on financial arrangements where the TOFA rules apply to the company.
limitation: It says nothing about the lender, so offshore bank debt and related-party debt from a parent look identical, and the transfer pricing question they raise cannot be answered from this column alone. Like the domestic interest column, it is an accounting expense that thin capitalisation may partly disallow at item 7 label W.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 expense label J, and the ATO expenses page defines it and states the schedule and withholding obligations it triggers.
evidence_quote: Write at J the interest expenses incurred on money borrowed from overseas sources.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the domestic interest column.

value_domain: Currency flag on an IP classification record (IP RAPID application-classification table)
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-classification table
variable_description: Whether the classification on this row still applies to the intellectual property right, or has since been withdrawn. IP Australia defines it as "A flag which indicates whether the classification remains current (TRUE) or has been removed (FALSE)", and because the table holds the whole classification history of a right, the dictionary says it "strongly recommend[s] you use the is_current flag to filter records down to the current records only if you are uninterested in the history of the records". A single patent or trade mark therefore contributes several rows, only some of them current.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-classification table
value_definition: A Boolean in the published IP RAPID extract, carried into BLADE as a numeric flag, 0 for no and 1 for yes.
limitation: It is a state at the extract date, not a date, so a classification dropped a decade ago and one dropped last month are indistinguishable without the effective-date columns. Counting rows without filtering on it counts an application's classification history rather than its current classifications, which inflates any technology-field tally.
rationale: The BLADE description is the IP RAPID dictionary's own wording for the is_current field on the application-classification table, and the dictionary explains why the flag exists and how to use it.
evidence_quote: A flag which indicates whether the classification remains current (TRUE) or has been removed (FALSE)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the dictionary sentence as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing warned that unfiltered rows are a history rather than a current state.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax payable, company return item 19 label X
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 19. Retirement savings accounts (RSAs) providers only
variable_description: Extra income tax a retirement savings account provider owes because super contributions arrived without a tax file number. The ATO instruction is to "Write at X the amount of further income tax payable on no-TFN contributions income written at U above", and that amount is then folded into gross tax on the calculation statement. Only a bank, building society, credit union or life insurer that offers retirement savings accounts completes it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 19. Retirement savings accounts (RSAs) providers only
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax amount for the income year, mandatory for RSA providers and written as zero where there is none.
limitation: It is the tax, not the contributions: the contributions themselves are the separate no-TFN contributions income column. A zero almost always means the firm is not an RSA provider rather than that no contributions lacked a tax file number, so the column cannot be used to measure tax file number compliance across the economy. A later tax file number quote can produce a refundable offset that this column does not net off.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 19 label X, and the ATO page defines it, ties it to the contributions label and states where it flows on the calculation statement.
evidence_quote: Write at X the amount of further income tax payable on no-TFN contributions income written at U above.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that only RSA providers complete it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 14 label A
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 14. Personal services income
variable_description: How much of the company's reported income is really the personal services income of one or more individuals. The ATO instruction is to "Write at A the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 6 income (including income earned in the course of conducting a personal services business)." It is the clearest signal in the return that a company is a vehicle for a person's own labour rather than a business structure.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 14. Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar subset of the item 6 income total, excluding exempt and non-assessable non-exempt components such as GST.
limitation: It does not say how many individuals are behind the amount, and it does not tell you whether the personal services income rules actually bite. Income earned while conducting a personal services business is included here too, so a large value can belong to a firm that passes the results test and is taxed normally. The companion yes-or-no labels for the results test, the determination and the 80 per cent test decide that.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 14 label A, and the ATO page defines personal services income, lists what is and is not personal services income, and defines the label.
evidence_quote: Write at A the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 6 income (including income earned in the course of conducting a personal services business).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what personal services income is or that its presence does not mean the attribution rules apply.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 14 label B
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 14. Personal services income
variable_description: The expenses the company booked at item 6 against the personal services income it reported on the same page. The ATO instruction is short: "Write at B the total amount of deductions against PSI included at item 6 expense." Paired with the personal services income column beside it, the two give the gross margin a firm reports on one person's work.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 14. Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar subset of the item 6 expense total, on the same accounting basis as the expense labels it is drawn from.
limitation: These are deductions claimed in the accounts, not deductions allowed. Where the personal services income rules apply and the income is not promptly paid out as salary, certain related expenses are not deductible and are added back at item 7 label W, so the difference between the income and expense columns here is not a taxable margin.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 14 label B, and the ATO page defines it and states the deduction restriction that applies when the personal services income rules bite.
evidence_quote: Write at B the total amount of deductions against PSI included at item 6 expense.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish claimed deductions from allowed ones.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 7 label D
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The book cost of research and development that the firm added back because it is claiming that spending as a notional R&D deduction instead. The ATO instruction is to "Write at D, the expense amounts included at the expenditure labels at item 6 Calculation of total profit or loss, which relate to amounts that you are claiming as a notional R&D deduction under the R&D tax incentive provisions." It also collects book depreciation and disposal losses on assets used in R&D activities.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A whole-dollar add-back at item 7, and by construction equal to the add-back of R&D accounting expenditure on the Research and development tax incentive schedule for the same year.
limitation: It measures accounting R&D expenditure removed from the profit and loss, not the notional R&D deduction claimed or the offset received, which the R&D schedule and item 21 carry. The ATO directs a company that capitalised its R&D to "write zero (0) at D", so a firm with a substantial R&D claim can show nothing here.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label D, and the ATO reconciliation page defines what goes in it and the zero rule for capitalised expenditure.
evidence_quote: If no expense amounts relating to notional R&D deduction have been included at item 6 (for example, amounts are capitalised) write zero (0) at D.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it read like a measure of R&D spending rather than a reconciliation add-back.

value_domain: Dollar deduction under the former R&D tax concession, company return item 7 label L
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Parts D and E
variable_description: The base deduction a company claimed for Australian-owned research and development under the R&D tax concession that operated before the R&D tax incentive. It is the concessional deduction on the year's eligible expenditure, deliberately excluding the extra incremental 50 per cent premium reported at the neighbouring label M, so the two must be added to get the firm's whole Australian-owned claim. The concession worked as a deduction against taxable income, not as an offset against tax.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Parts D and E
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, calculated on the R&D tax concession schedule and transferred to item 7 of the company return.
limitation: The concession was replaced by the R&D tax incentive from 2011-12, so a series through that change breaks: the successor columns at item 21 are tax offsets rather than deductions and cannot be compared with this one dollar for dollar. Because the label carves out the premium at M, reading it alone understates the claim.
rationale: The BLADE label matches the item 7 R&D concession labels on the pre-2011 company return, and the ATO schedule instructions set out how the Australian-owned concession and its separate incremental premium were calculated and transferred to item 7.
evidence_quote: The schedule will then automatically calculate in Part D (at M item 3) the extra 50% deduction which the company is entitled to (if eligible) under the Australian owned R&D incremental tax concession.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label 'Australian owned R&D tax concession - not including label M' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what label M was or that the whole regime was repealed.

value_domain: Dollar deduction under the former R&D tax concession, company return item 7 label M
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Parts D and E
variable_description: The premium deduction a company earned for increasing its Australian-owned research and development, on top of the base concession at label L. The ATO's schedule instructions describe the transfer plainly: "The schedule will then automatically calculate in Part D (at M item 3) the extra 50% deduction which the company is entitled to (if eligible) under the Australian owned R&D incremental tax concession. Transfer this amount to M - Australian owned R&D - extra incremental 50% deduction item 7 on the Company tax return 2008." A non-zero value therefore marks growth in R&D spending, not its level.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Parts D and E
value_definition: A whole-dollar extra deduction for the income year, calculated in Part D of the R&D tax concession schedule and transferred to item 7 of the company return.
limitation: Eligibility for the premium had its own tests, so a firm with rising R&D can still show zero here while showing a large base concession at label L. The mirror-image label for foreign-owned R&D carried a 75 per cent premium and is a different column, so this one covers only the Australian-owned side of a firm's R&D.
rationale: The ATO schedule instructions name this exact label on the company return and state how the amount reaches it, which fixes the identity of the BLADE column.
evidence_quote: Transfer this amount to M - Australian owned R&D - extra incremental 50% deduction item 7 on the Company tax return 2008.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the premium rewards an increase in spending rather than spending itself.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset under the former R&D tax concession, company return calculation statement label U
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Part F
variable_description: The cash-value R&D tax offset a small company received in place of deducting its Australian-owned R&D. The ATO instruction fixes the arithmetic: "Transfer the amount calculated at Label U (30% of Label Y) to U - R&D tax offset in the Calculation Statement on the Company tax return 2008." It sits in the calculation statement, so it reduces tax payable directly rather than reducing taxable income.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Part F
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax offset for the income year, equal to 30 per cent of the R&D amount reported at the item 7 offset label, calculated in Part F of the R&D tax concession schedule.
limitation: The offset was only open to small claimants. The ATO test was that "the total of the aggregate R&D amount column is $1,000,000 or less and the total of the R&D Group Turnover column is less than $5,000,000", so the column truncates hard at the top of the size distribution. It also adds no information beyond the item 7 offset column, being a fixed 30 per cent of it.
rationale: The ATO Part F instructions name the calculation statement label, give the 30 per cent relationship to the item 7 label and state the grouping thresholds that gate eligibility.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount calculated at Label U (30% of Label Y) to U - R&D tax offset in the Calculation Statement on the Company tax return 2008.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only 'R&D tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell it apart from the later R&D tax incentive offsets or know it was capped to small firms.

value_domain: Dollar R&D amount underlying the former R&D tax offset, company return item 7 label Y
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Part F
variable_description: The R&D amount a small company reported at item 7 when it chose the offset instead of the deduction. The ATO instruction is that "The amount at Y is the company's entitlement to the R&D tax offset. Transfer this amount to Y- R&D tax offset, if chosen at Item 7, on the Company tax return 2008", and the calculation statement then carries 30 per cent of it as the offset itself. The phrase "if chosen" is the point: taking the offset meant giving up the concessional deduction for the same year.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax concession schedule instructions, Part F
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the income year, calculated in Part F of the R&D tax concession schedule and reported at item 7 of the company return.
limitation: The choice is elective and must be made before lodgment, so a zero here means either no R&D at all or a company that took the deduction route instead, in which case the Australian-owned concession labels carry the claim. The two paths are mutually exclusive within a year, so summing this column with the deduction columns overstates R&D activity.
rationale: The ATO Part F instructions name this exact item 7 label, describe it as the company's entitlement and set out the choice that gates it.
evidence_quote: The amount at Y is the company's entitlement to the R&D tax offset. Transfer this amount to Y- R&D tax offset, if chosen at Item 7, on the Company tax return 2008.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'R&D tax offset, if chosen' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the election or the relationship to the calculation statement offset.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label F
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: What the firm paid to lease equipment and vehicles in Australia. The ATO instruction is to "Write at F the expenditure incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing assets, including motor vehicles and depreciating assets such as plant", and it excludes anything acquired under a hire-purchase agreement. Property rent is a separate label, so this is the cost of using someone else's plant and vehicles.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6, covering finance and operating leases together.
limitation: It mixes finance leases, which are financing in substance, with operating leases, which are rental, so it cannot be treated as either. Real estate leasing costs and hire purchase are outside it, so it is not the firm's total cost of assets it does not own, and capital expenditure to terminate a lease is deducted elsewhere at item 7.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 expense label F, and the ATO expenses page defines it and lists the exclusions.
evidence_quote: Write at F the expenditure incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing assets, including motor vehicles and depreciating assets such as plant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which lease types are in and which are out.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label I
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: What the firm paid to lease equipment from overseas. The ATO instruction is to "Write at I the lease expenses incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing depreciating assets, including motor vehicles", and it is narrower than the domestic lease column: it "Exclude[s] the cost of leasing real estate, capital expenditure incurred to terminate a lease or licence, and expenditure on items other than depreciating assets leased from non-residents." Payments under equipment leases to non-residents generally attract withholding tax.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6, restricted to depreciating assets leased from offshore.
limitation: A small value can be a single cross-border equipment lease rather than any sustained offshore relationship, so the column is a poor proxy for international engagement. It also carries no country, counterparty or withholding tax amount, so the cross-border tax treatment behind it cannot be reconstructed.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 expense label I, and the ATO expenses page defines it, states the exclusions and notes the withholding obligation.
evidence_quote: Write at I the lease expenses incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing depreciating assets, including motor vehicles.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the domestic lease column.

value_domain: Dollar loan balance at year end, company return item 8 label N
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
variable_description: What a private company had lent to its shareholders or their associates and was still owed at year end. The ATO instruction is to "Write at N the sum of all such loans that have a debit balance at the end of the income year", and the label is only completed by a private company or closely held corporate limited partnership where the borrower was a natural person, partnership or trust. It is the return's main window on Division 7A, under which such loans can be treated as unfranked dividends to the borrower.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
value_definition: A whole-dollar stock at the end of the income year, taken from the accounts, accompanied by a code recording whether the loans predate 4 December 1997.
limitation: It is a year-end snapshot, so a loan taken and repaid, or put on a complying loan agreement, before the lodgment day can leave the column at zero while money moved all year. It also does not say whether any of the balance was in fact treated as a deemed dividend, and public companies never complete it, so an empty value is uninformative for them.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 8 label N, and the ATO page defines the amount, the eligibility conditions and the Division 7A consequence.
evidence_quote: Write at N the sum of all such loans that have a debit balance at the end of the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a year-end balance for private companies only.

value_domain: Dollar refundable tax offset, company return item 13 loss carry back label
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 13. Losses information
variable_description: Whether and by how much a company converted a recent tax loss into a refund of tax it had already paid. The ATO sets out the eligibility: "Eligible corporate tax entities with an aggregated turnover of less than $5 billion can choose to carry back some or all of tax losses for 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22 to earlier income years in which it had income tax liabilities." The offset is refundable, so it is cash to a loss-making firm, and it is claimed in the calculation statement alongside the other refundable offsets.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 13. Losses information
value_definition: A whole-dollar refundable tax offset for the income year, reported at item 13 of the company return and carried into the refundable tax offsets total.
limitation: Claiming it is a choice, and the amount is capped by the earlier year's unused income tax liability and by the franking account surplus at the end of the claim year, so a zero often means a firm declined or was capped rather than that it had no loss. The measure covers only the 2019-20 to 2021-22 loss years, so it appears and disappears rather than trending. This register also holds a second, near-identically named column for the same form label, and both should be checked.
rationale: The BLADE label names the loss carry back tax offset, and the ATO item 13 page states the eligibility conditions, the loss years covered and the refundable character of the offset.
evidence_quote: Eligible corporate tax entities with an aggregated turnover of less than $5 billion can choose to carry back some or all of tax losses for 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22 to earlier income years in which it had income tax liabilities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label 'Loss carry-back tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the measure was temporary, elective and capped.

value_domain: Dollar refundable tax offset, company return item 13 loss carry back label
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 13. Losses information
variable_description: The dollar value of the loss carry back tax offset, worked out from the loss carried back rather than reported directly. The ATO's method is to take the loss being carried back, subtract the unused net exempt income of the earlier year, multiply by the tax rate of the loss year, then cap the result at the earlier year's unused income tax liability and again at the franking account surplus. Because it depends on both the loss and the earlier year's tax, the amount is not proportional to the size of the loss.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 13. Losses information
value_definition: A whole-dollar refundable tax offset for the income year, the product of the carried-back loss and the loss year's company tax rate, twice capped.
limitation: The double cap means the column cannot be read backwards to recover the size of the loss: two firms with the same loss get different offsets depending on the tax they paid in earlier years and their franking balances. The register carries this column and a second one under a slightly different name for the same form label, so a count of claimants that uses only one of them will be wrong.
rationale: The BLADE label names the loss carry back tax offset amount, and the ATO item 13 page gives the calculation method, the caps and the transfer to the calculation statement.
evidence_quote: The amount you can claim is capped at your unused income tax liability for that earlier income year less any amount that was claimed against that liability for a loss carry back claim in the Company tax return 2021.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the mis-spaced label 'Loss Carry Back Tax Off set' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say how the amount relates to the loss.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income from a limited-exemption listed country
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, taxation of branch profits
variable_description: Income attributed to the company from controlled foreign entities in a limited-exemption listed country. The category belongs to the controlled foreign company rules as they stood before 2010: listed countries were split in two, and the split mattered because the exemption was narrower for the limited-exemption group: the ATO wrote that exemption there was available only where the income "is not adjusted tainted income or is adjusted tainted income and the branch satisfies an active income test". Attributed income is taxed to the Australian parent as it accrues offshore, whether or not any money is remitted.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, taxation of branch profits
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of attributed foreign income for the income year, reported in the attributed foreign income block of the company return.
limitation: The broad and limited exemption split no longer exists on the modern form, which carries only listed country, unlisted country and transferor trust labels, so a series that spans the change ends rather than falling to zero. The amount is also accrued, not received, so adding it to the net foreign income column double counts a firm's foreign result. The reading of the DIL prefix AFI as attributed foreign income is inferred from the label rather than published.
rationale: The label names a limited-exemption listed country, a defined category of the pre-2010 controlled foreign company rules, and the ATO's foreign income return form guide defines that category and the narrower exemption attached to it.
evidence_quote: Non-assessable non-exempt income treatment is generally available for income derived by a resident company through a branch in a limited-exemption listed country if the income: is from carrying on a business in the country, is subject to tax in the country on a current basis, is not adjusted tainted income or is adjusted tainted income and the branch satisfies an active income test.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the cryptic label 'AFI - limited-exemption listed country' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing decoded the abbreviation or said the category has been retired.

value_domain: Dollar capital expenditure allocated to a project pool, mining and minerals transport
value_source: ATO, Guide to depreciating assets, capital expenditure deductible under the uniform capital allowance rules
variable_description: Capital spending on a mine and on the links that move its output, pooled and written off over the life of the project. The ATO sets the test: "To be a project amount, mining capital expenditure or transport capital expenditure must be directly connected with carrying on the mining operations or business, respectively." Mining capital expenditure covers site preparation, necessary buildings, and providing water, light, power, access or communications to the site; transport capital expenditure covers a railway, road, pipeline, port or other facility used principally to move minerals.
description_source: ATO, Guide to depreciating assets, capital expenditure deductible under the uniform capital allowance rules
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the income year, limited to expenditure that does not form part of the cost of a depreciating asset and is not otherwise deductible.
limitation: The label does not make clear whether the figure is expenditure allocated to the pool during the year or the part of the pool that is deductible in the year; treat it as the latter only after checking it against the project pool deduction column, which carries all project pool deductions together. Because the pool excludes anything that is part of the cost of a depreciating asset, most mine plant and equipment is outside it, so the column is not a measure of mining investment.
rationale: The label names mining and transport capital expenditure allocated to a project pool, which is a defined concept of the uniform capital allowance rules, and the ATO guide defines both expenditure types and the project pool write-off.
evidence_quote: To be a project amount, mining capital expenditure or transport capital expenditure must be directly connected with carrying on the mining operations or business, respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the truncated form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing defined mining or transport capital expenditure or said the write-off is spread over the project life.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label Y
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: What it cost the firm to run its vehicles, and nothing more. The ATO instruction is explicit: "Write at Y motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums." The instruction then rules out the other four ways a vehicle costs money, which sit at the lease, interest and depreciation labels of the same item.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar running-cost expense for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6.
limitation: It is not the cost of a fleet: the lease payments, the interest on vehicle finance and the depreciation on owned vehicles all sit at other item 6 labels, so this column understates vehicle costs by however the firm finances them. It also carries no vehicle count or distance, so it cannot be turned into a per-vehicle or per-kilometre measure.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 expense label Y, and the ATO expenses page defines the label as running expenses only and names the labels that carry the rest.
evidence_quote: Write at Y motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Motor vehicle expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited a reader to treat it as the whole cost of a firm's vehicles.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 7 label A
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The capital gain the firm brought into taxable income after losses and concessions. The ATO defines it as "the total of the capital gains it made (gains that are not disregarded other than by one of the small business concessions listed below) reduced by current year capital losses (that are not disregarded), prior year unapplied net capital losses" and any 50 per cent active asset reduction, retirement exemption or rollover. The instructions add a point that changes every comparison with individual taxpayers: "A company is not eligible for the CGT discount."
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount for the income year, taken from part 6 of the capital gains tax schedule or summary worksheet where one is prepared.
limitation: A zero is not evidence that the firm disposed of nothing: current and carried-forward capital losses can absorb the whole gain, and any excess loss goes to the carried-forward capital losses column instead. Because no discount applies, this figure is not comparable with an individual's net capital gain on the same disposal.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label A, and the ATO reconciliation page defines the net capital gain, its inputs and the absence of the discount for companies.
evidence_quote: A company is not eligible for the CGT discount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net capital gain' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that losses can drive the figure to zero or that no discount applies.

value_domain: Dollar amount of taxable income, company return item 19 label V
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 19. Retirement savings accounts (RSAs) providers only
variable_description: The part of a provider's taxable income that comes from the retirement savings accounts it offers, taxed at the superannuation rate. The ATO instruction covers both kinds of provider: "Write at V the RSA component of the taxable income of the RSA provider that is not a life insurance company, or the amount to be included in the complying superannuation class of the taxable income of a life insurance company that is referable to RSAs provided by the company." Only banks, building societies, credit unions and life insurers that offer these accounts complete it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 19. Retirement savings accounts (RSAs) providers only
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of taxable income for the income year, reported separately because it attracts its own rate.
limitation: The column is near-empty by design, so a zero is almost always 'not an RSA provider'. For a life insurance company the same amount is already inside the complying superannuation class figure at item 16, so adding the two double counts. It is also taxable income, not funds under management, and says nothing about how many accounts sit behind it.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 19 label V, and the ATO page defines it separately for life insurers and for other providers.
evidence_quote: Write at V the RSA component of the taxable income of the RSA provider that is not a life insurance company, or the amount to be included in the complying superannuation class of the taxable income of a life insurance company that is referable to RSAs provided by the company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the amount overlaps the life insurance class figures.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 16 label C
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 16. Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
variable_description: The capital gain a life insurer made on the assets it holds to back complying superannuation business. The ATO instruction is to "Write at C the amount of the net capital gain that accrued from the investment of complying superannuation assets." Life insurers split their taxable income into two classes and tax each at its own rate, so which class a gain falls into decides the tax on it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 16. Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
value_definition: A whole-dollar net capital gain for the income year, attributed to the complying superannuation class of a life insurance company or a friendly society carrying on life insurance business.
limitation: Only life insurance companies and friendly societies carrying on life insurance business complete item 16, so this is a sector column, not a general one, and the ATO directs a friendly society with no life insurance business to write zero. The gain accrues to policy holders' superannuation assets rather than to shareholders, so it is not a measure of the insurer's own investment performance.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 16 label C, and the ATO page defines it and explains the two-class structure that gives the split its meaning.
evidence_quote: Write at C the amount of the net capital gain that accrued from the investment of complying superannuation assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the complying superannuation class or who completes the item.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 16 label D
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 16. Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
variable_description: The capital gain a life insurer made outside its complying superannuation business, taxed at the company rate. The ATO instruction is to "Write at D the amount of the net capital gain that is included in the ordinary class of taxable income", and for the head company of a consolidated group it covers the whole group other than gains on complying superannuation assets. The ordinary class is the residual: everything that is not complying superannuation.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 16. Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
value_definition: A whole-dollar net capital gain for the income year, attributed to the ordinary class of taxable income of a life insurance company or friendly society.
limitation: The variable name is misleading. It carries the string for complying, but the label is the ordinary class, which is the other side of the split, so pairing columns by name rather than by label puts the two classes on the wrong footing. Losses of one class can only be applied against future income of the same class, so a zero here cannot be netted against the complying superannuation column.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 16 label D, and the ATO page defines it, contrasts it with the complying superannuation class and states the loss quarantining between classes.
evidence_quote: Write at D the amount of the net capital gain that is included in the ordinary class of taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and nothing flagged that the variable name contradicts the label.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 8 label R
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
variable_description: What the firm earned from foreign sources after the expenses of earning it, with foreign tax added back. The ATO instruction is to "Write at R assessable income derived by the company from foreign sources grossed up by the amount of the foreign tax, but net of expenses", and it includes foreign source capital gains after unapplied capital losses and dividends from New Zealand companies. The gross-up matters: the figure is measured before foreign tax, so it is not what the firm kept.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount for the income year, which can be negative, with a loss marked by an indicator letter rather than a minus sign.
limitation: It excludes attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities and transferor trusts, which have their own labels, so it is not the firm's whole foreign result. Australian franking credits received indirectly through a New Zealand franking company are excluded as well. Any foreign source capital gain in it is also inside the net capital gain column, so the two cannot be added.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 8 label R, and the ATO page defines the amount, the gross-up and the exclusions that separate it from attributed income.
evidence_quote: Write at R assessable income derived by the company from foreign sources grossed up by the amount of the foreign tax, but net of expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net foreign income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is grossed up for foreign tax or that attributed income is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar stock of unapplied capital losses, company return item 13 label V
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 13. Losses information
variable_description: The stockpile of capital losses the firm has not yet been able to use, carried into later years. The ATO instruction is to "Write at V the total of any unapplied net capital losses from collectables and unapplied net capital losses from all other CGT assets and events", and where a capital gains tax schedule is required the figure must match the schedule. Capital losses can only ever be applied against capital gains, so this balance waits for a future gain.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 13. Losses information
value_definition: A whole-dollar cumulative balance at the end of the income year, split in the source schedule between collectables and all other assets but reported here as one total.
limitation: It is a stock, not a flow, so a year-to-year difference mixes new losses made with old losses used and cannot be read as the year's capital loss. A subsidiary member of a consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group leaves the label blank, so members of groups look loss-free when the losses have simply moved to the head company.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 13 label V, and the ATO losses page defines the amount, its components and the consolidation rule that empties it.
evidence_quote: Write at V the total of any unapplied net capital losses from collectables and unapplied net capital losses from all other CGT assets and events.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and its topic tag suggested income when the column is a capital loss balance.

value_domain: Dollar amount of no-TFN contributions income, company return item 19 label U
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 19. Retirement savings accounts (RSAs) providers only
variable_description: Superannuation contributions a retirement savings account provider received for members whose tax file number it did not hold. The ATO instruction is to "Write at U the no-TFN contributions income of the RSA provider. If zero, write zero (0)", and completing the label is mandatory for those providers. Contributions in this category attract extra tax, which is reported separately at the tax label on the same item.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 19. Retirement savings accounts (RSAs) providers only
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of contributions income for the income year, mandatory for RSA providers and written as zero where there is none.
limitation: It records an administrative failure by the member or employer to supply a tax file number, not anything about the provider's business, so it should not be read as a measure of the provider's superannuation activity. Only RSA providers complete it, so it says nothing about no-TFN contributions in the much larger superannuation fund sector, which reports them on a different return.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 19 label U, and the ATO page defines it and ties it to the further tax reported at the neighbouring label.
evidence_quote: Write at U the no-TFN contributions income of the RSA provider. If zero, write zero (0).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said who reports it or what the number is evidence of.
