value_definition: A coded status at item 3 label Z: 5 consolidated head company, 10 consolidated subsidiary member, with anything else an invalid or absent response. Only one of the two can be selected.
limitation: It cannot be used to count group members or measure group size. A subsidiary inside a consolidated group does not lodge a return at all, so it is absent from the data rather than coded, and a subsidiary that does appear is there because of a non-membership period, meaning its figures cover part of a year.
rationale: The two BLADE categories are the company return's Z1 and Z2 boxes at item 3, and the ATO page defines each and the exclusivity between them.
evidence_quote: Select Z1 Consolidated head company if the company was a head company of a consolidated or MEC group at any time during the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label text with the generic sentence twice, and never said that consolidated subsidiaries are missing from the file rather than coded, which is the trap this column sets.

value_domain: Company residency status for tax
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: The company's residency for tax, split into resident, non-resident without an Australian permanent establishment and non-resident with one. The ATO's rule for the third box is "Complete C3 if the company is a non-resident company carrying on a business in Australia through a permanent establishment (PE)". The distinction drives the income base itself: a resident is taxed on income from all sources while a non-resident is taxed on Australian-sourced income, so the same taxable income label means different things across the three categories.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
value_definition: A coded status at item 3 label C: 15 resident, 20 non-resident with no permanent establishment, 25 non-resident with a permanent establishment, and 5 for a blank answer.
limitation: Tax residency is not ownership or incorporation. An Australian-incorporated subsidiary of a foreign group is a resident here, so this column cannot be used to identify foreign-owned firms - the ultimate holding company country code is the label for that.
rationale: The BLADE categories map one to one onto the company return's C1, C2 and C3 residency boxes at item 3, and the ATO page defines the permanent establishment condition that separates the two non-resident states.
evidence_quote: Complete C3 if the company is a non-resident company carrying on a business in Australia through a permanent establishment (PE).
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the codes with the generic sentence twice, and left a reader likely to treat residency as a proxy for foreign ownership.

value_domain: Dollar amount of immediate write-off deductions for cheap depreciating assets
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
variable_description: The deduction a small business claimed by writing off cheap depreciating assets immediately instead of pooling and depreciating them. It is the first label of the simplified depreciation item, whose current wording is a deduction for assets "costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold"; the sts in the variable name points to the Simplified Tax System, the pre-2007 name for these small business concessions, when the same line was described as low cost assets. The threshold that defines cheap has moved repeatedly, so the label's meaning is anchored to the year.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 10 label A of the company return, available only to a small business entity that has chosen the simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: The series is not comparable across years, because the amount depends as much on where the write-off threshold sat as on the firm's spending, and for 2021-22 the ATO directed small businesses to write zero here and use temporary full expensing instead. A zero therefore does not mean the firm bought no cheap assets.
rationale: The label is the immediate write-off line of the company return's simplified depreciation item, and the ATO page states its current scope and the instruction to report zero while temporary full expensing applied. The reading of sts as the Simplified Tax System is inferred from the variable name.
evidence_quote: A small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules must insert 0 at A because, in 2021–22, you do not hold an asset meeting the criteria to claim instant asset write-off.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Deduction for low cost assets' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing recorded that the threshold moves or that the label was forced to zero in the temporary full expensing years.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the general small business pool deduction
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
variable_description: The depreciation a small business claimed on its general pool, the single pool holding the assets that were too dear for the immediate write-off. The ATO instruction is "Write at B the total amount the company claimed at item 6 relating to the general small business pool", and it adds that a company which has already written the pool balance off in a previous year inserts zero. The custodian's description is truncated to 'Deduction for general'; the full label is deduction for general small business pool, and the sts in the variable name is the Simplified Tax System, the older name for the same concessions.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 10 label B of the company return, calculated from the pool balance at a fixed statutory rate rather than asset by asset.
limitation: It lags investment rather than measuring it: a pool deduction is driven by the accumulated balance, so it keeps running for years after the last purchase and falls to zero the moment the pool is written off, even though the firm still holds and uses the assets.
rationale: The truncated DIL label matches item 10 label B of the company return, and the ATO page gives the instruction and the write-off condition that produces zeros.
evidence_quote: Write at B the total amount the company claimed at item 6 relating to the general small business pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the truncated wording 'Deduction for general' as its whole description with the generic sentence twice, so the column did not even name the pool it belongs to.

value_domain: Dollar amount at a calculation statement subtotal
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels C, T2, D and T3
variable_description: The first of the three running subtotals in the calculation statement: tax left after the non-refundable, non-carry-forward offsets are applied to gross tax. The ATO instruction is "Write at T2 the amount of tax payable after C has been offset against B Gross tax" and "T2 cannot be less than zero". It is the step where offsets such as the foreign income tax offset are used or lost.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels C, T2, D and T3
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T2, floored at zero, being gross tax less the label C offsets.
limitation: Because the subtotal floors at zero, it cannot show the value of the offsets that were wasted: offsets at label C that exceed gross tax are neither refunded nor carried forward, and nothing on the statement records the excess.
rationale: The DIL label 'Subtotal 1' is calculation statement label T2, and the ATO label page defines the arithmetic and the zero floor.
evidence_quote: Write at T2 the amount of tax payable after C has been offset against B Gross tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Subtotal 1' and printed the generic sentence twice, which told a reader nothing about which offsets had been applied by that point.

value_domain: Dollar amount at a calculation statement subtotal
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels C, T2, D and T3
variable_description: The second running subtotal: tax left after the non-refundable carry forward offsets are applied to subtotal 1. The ATO instruction is "Write at T3 the amount of tax payable after D has been offset against T2", and it cannot be less than zero. The offsets applied at this step are the ones that survive an unprofitable year, since "Any excess offsets can be carried forward to a later income year".
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels C, T2, D and T3
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T3, floored at zero, being subtotal 1 less the label D offsets.
limitation: It hides the carry-forward that gives these offsets their value: where label D exceeds subtotal 1, the unused part moves to a later year and no column on this row records how much left. Comparing T2 and T3 gives offsets used, not offsets held.
rationale: The DIL label 'Subtotal 2' is calculation statement label T3, and the ATO label page defines the step and the carry-forward treatment that distinguishes it from subtotal 1.
evidence_quote: Write at T3 the amount of tax payable after D has been offset against T2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Subtotal 2' with the generic sentence twice, so it was indistinguishable from the other two subtotal columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount at a calculation statement subtotal
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels E, T4 and F
variable_description: The third running subtotal: tax left after the refundable tax offsets are applied to subtotal 2. The ATO instruction is "Write at T4 the amount of tax payable after E has been offset against T3", and it cannot be less than zero. This is the step at which a company with a large refundable research and development offset drops to nil tax and starts generating a refund at the remainder label.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels E, T4 and F
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T4, floored at zero, being subtotal 2 less the label E refundable offsets.
limitation: A zero here is ambiguous on its own: it covers both a company with no tax to pay before offsets and a company whose refundable offsets more than covered its tax. Only the remainder of refundable tax offsets column separates the two.
rationale: The DIL label 'Subtotal 3' is calculation statement label T4, and the ATO label page defines the step and its relationship to the refundable offsets and the remainder label.
evidence_quote: Write at T4 the amount of tax payable after E has been offset against T3.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Subtotal 3' with the generic sentence twice, and the three subtotal columns were interchangeable on the page.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax payable on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels T5 and G
variable_description: The company's tax payable for the year, the end of the offset sequence: "Write at T5 the amount of tax payable after F has been offset against T4". The ATO makes the label mandatory and requires a zero rather than a blank when no tax is payable, so it is the closest thing on the return to a headline company tax liability. Despite the BLADE description calling it 'Tax payable', the variable name still marks it as the fourth subtotal in the same chain as the three above it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels T5 and G
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T5, floored at zero, being subtotal 3 less the franking deficit tax offset.
limitation: Tax payable is not tax paid and not the final balance. PAYG instalments already made, withholding credits and the section 102AAM interest charge are applied afterwards at the amount due or refundable label, so a large taxpayer with accurate instalments finishes at close to zero there while showing a substantial figure here.
rationale: The DIL description 'Tax payable' with a subtotal-shaped variable name matches calculation statement label T5, and the ATO label page defines the step and the mandatory zero.
evidence_quote: Write at T5 the amount of tax payable after F has been offset against T4.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax payable' with the generic sentence twice, and did not warn that instalments and credits are applied after this label.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Employer superannuation expensed by the company for the year, from its accounts. The ATO instruction is "Write at D the superannuation expenses incurred for the income year", and for a consolidated group "The head company includes at D the employee superannuation expenses of all the members of the group". Any part that is not deductible, including contributions to a non-complying fund, is added back at the non-deductible expenses label at item 7 rather than removed from here.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 6 label D of the company return, on an incurred basis from the financial statements.
limitation: It is not the superannuation guarantee and not contributions paid. Expensing follows the accounts, the superannuation guarantee charge is neither a contribution nor deductible, and it excludes superannuation paid to associated persons only in the sense that those amounts are also reported separately, so it cannot be used to test superannuation guarantee compliance.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 superannuation expense label, and the ATO instruction page gives the wording, the consolidation rule and the non-deductible add-back.
evidence_quote: Write at D the superannuation expenses incurred for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Superannuation expenses' with the generic sentence twice, and left the column open to being read as superannuation guarantee contributions.

value_domain: Dollar balance of tax payable or refundable
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels I, K and S
variable_description: The bottom line of the return: what the company still owes, or is owed back, once everything has been applied. The ATO instruction is "Write at S the balance of tax payable (+) or refundable (-)", worked out by adding tax payable and the section 102AAM interest charge and then subtracting eligible credits, the refundable offset remainder and PAYG instalments. A positive figure is payable by the company and a negative one is refundable to it.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels I, K and S
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label S, signed, being tax payable plus label G less labels H, I and K.
limitation: It is a settlement balance, not a tax burden. A company that paid its whole liability through PAYG instalments lands near zero here while having paid a great deal of tax, so this column cannot be used to rank firms by tax paid; tax payable is the label for that.
rationale: The DIL label 'Amount due or refundable' is calculation statement label S, and the ATO page gives the formula and the sign convention.
evidence_quote: Write at S the balance of tax payable (+) or refundable (−).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, and gave no warning that instalments already paid are netted out, which is the mistake this column invites.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax assessed for the income year
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement
variable_description: The tax assessed for the company for the year, which is an assessment outcome rather than a box the company filled in on its return. Its natural counterpart on the return is the tax payable label at the end of the calculation statement, which the ATO builds by applying gross tax and then each class of offset in a fixed order. Read it alongside tax on taxable income and tax payable, because the three answer different questions: the rate applied to income, the amount after offsets, and the amount finally assessed.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, produced by ATO assessment processing rather than transcribed from a return label.
limitation: It need not equal tax payable as lodged. An amendment, an objection or an ATO adjustment changes what was assessed while the lodged labels on the same row stay as they were filed, so a difference between the two columns is an assessment history, not a data error. No published ATO definition for this column was found, so this reading is inferred.
rationale: The company return's calculation statement is the only published account of how a company's tax is worked out, and it names the labels this column sits between. Nothing fetchable defines a 'tax assessed' data item, so the entry is guessed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax assessed' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell it apart from tax payable on the return.

value_domain: Dollar amount of taxable income at the calculation statement
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
variable_description: Taxable income as it is carried into the calculation statement, which is the base the company tax rate is applied to. The ATO instruction is "Write at A the amount of taxable income of $1 or more" and to "Write zero (0) at A if the company has no taxable income or has a loss", which makes this a floored version of the item 7 figure. For a resident company "taxable income equals assessable income derived from all sources less allowable deductions incurred in gaining that income".
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
value_definition: Whole dollars at calculation statement label A, never negative, mandatory even when zero.
limitation: It is not interchangeable with taxable income or loss at item 7. Every loss-making company reports zero here, so using this column alone treats a firm that broke even and a firm that lost a hundred million as the same, and averages of taxable income built from it are biased upwards.
rationale: The DIL label names the calculation statement version of taxable income, which is label A, and the ATO page defines it, floors it at zero and states the resident and non-resident income bases.
evidence_quote: Write at A the amount of taxable income of $1 or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Taxable income (calculation statement)' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing flagged the zero floor that separates it from the item 7 figure.

value_domain: Dollar amount of taxable income or loss on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The company's taxable income or loss for the year, the end point of reconciling accounting profit to tax. The ATO instruction is "Write at T all assessable income less deductions that equals the amount at T Total profit or loss item 6 plus or minus the reconciliation adjustments at item 7", and a loss is marked by printing L in a separate box beside the amount. Unlike the calculation statement version, this label carries losses as well as income.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 7 label T of the company return, signed in principle but with the sign carried by a separate loss indicator on the form rather than by the number.
limitation: Whether a value is income or a loss depends on that separate indicator, so a magnitude taken without it can turn a large loss into a large profit. Excess franking offsets converted into a loss are excluded from this label, which is why a company can show taxable income here and a tax loss carried forward at item 13 in the same year.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 7 taxable or net income or loss label; the ATO page gives the definition, the loss indicator and the franking offset conversion that breaks the link with item 13.
evidence_quote: Write at T all assessable income less deductions that equals the amount at T Total profit or loss item 6 plus or minus the reconciliation adjustments at item 7.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Taxable income/loss' with the generic sentence twice, and did not mention that the sign lives in a separate indicator.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross tax on taxable income
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
variable_description: Tax on the company's taxable income before any relief is applied. The ATO instruction is "Write at T1 the amount of tax payable before the allowance of any rebates, tax offsets, credits or FDT offsets", and the label is mandatory even when the answer is zero. It is the first line of the calculation statement and the denominator most readers actually want when they ask what rate a company paid.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T1, being taxable income multiplied by the rate or rates applying to the company for that year.
limitation: Dividing it by taxable income does not always recover a statutory rate: base rate entities pay a lower rate than other companies, and life insurers, retirement savings account providers and pooled development funds have income taxed in classes at more than one rate. Research and development recoupment tax is added afterwards at gross tax, not here.
rationale: The DIL label is calculation statement label T1, and the ATO page defines it as tax before any offsets and points to the rate schedule in the appendix.
evidence_quote: Write at T1 the amount of tax payable before the allowance of any rebates, tax offsets, credits or FDT offsets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Tax on taxable income' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that more than one rate can sit behind the figure.

value_domain: Dollar termination value of intangible depreciating assets
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: What the company received for intangible depreciating assets it stopped holding during the year, such as patents, licences and in-house software. The ATO instruction is "Write at H the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for intangible depreciating assets", a balancing adjustment event occurring "if the company stops holding or using a depreciating asset or decides not to use it in the future, for example, assets were sold, lost or destroyed". The termination value is generally what was received, including the market value of non-cash benefits.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 9 label H of the company return, covering assets under the uniform capital allowance rules including those in a low-value pool.
limitation: Proceeds are not profit: the assessable or deductible balancing adjustment - the difference between the termination value and the asset's adjustable value - sits at its own labels. Software for which expenditure went to a software development pool is excluded, so this understates disposals of self-developed software.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 9 label H, and the ATO page defines termination value, the events that trigger it and the software exclusion.
evidence_quote: Write at H the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for intangible depreciating assets to which the UCA rules in Division 40 of the ITAA 1997 apply, including assets allocated to a low-value pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice, and never said the figure is proceeds rather than gain or that pooled software is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar termination value of tangible depreciating assets
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: What the company received for tangible depreciating assets that left the business - plant, vehicles and equipment sold, scrapped, lost or destroyed. The ATO instruction is "Write at I the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for depreciating assets, including assets allocated to a low-value pool". Its pair on the same item is the intangible termination value column, and the split is the only asset-type breakdown the return gives for disposals.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 9 label I of the company return, being amounts received or deemed received plus the market value of non-cash benefits.
limitation: It is not a measure of all asset disposals. Assets in a small business pool, buildings deductible under the capital works rules, assets used in research and development activities, and film investments are all excluded, so a small business or a property-heavy firm shows little here regardless of what it sold.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 9 label I, and the ATO page gives the instruction together with the list of exclusions that bounds the column.
evidence_quote: Write at I the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for depreciating assets, including assets allocated to a low-value pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice and did not carry the exclusions, which are what makes this column narrower than asset sales.

value_domain: Dollar amount of temporary full expensing deductions
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The deduction claimed under temporary full expensing, the pandemic measure letting most businesses write off eligible assets in full. The ATO instruction is "Write at S the total value of the deductions that you are claiming under temporary full expensing", the measure covering assets first held and used or installed "between 7:30 pm AEDT on 6 October 2020 and 30 June 2023" for businesses with aggregated turnover under $5 billion. The count of assets behind the claim sits in the neighbouring label.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 9 label S of the company return, being the business portion of the cost of eligible assets and of improvements to them.
limitation: It is a timing measure, not a permanent tax reduction, and it exists only inside a fixed window, so it cannot be extended into a series. A high figure also does not mean high new investment for a large firm, because second-hand assets qualify only under $50 million of turnover.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 9 label S, and the ATO pages for item 9 and item 7 give the instruction, the eligibility window and the turnover tests.
evidence_quote: Write at S the total value of the deductions that you are claiming under temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice, and did not record the date window that makes the column a one-off rather than a series.

value_domain: Count of assets opted out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: How many eligible assets the company chose to keep out of temporary full expensing and depreciate the ordinary way instead. The ATO instruction is "Write at Q the number of assets for which you have made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing", the choice being made asset by asset and, once made, unable to be revoked. Opting out is usually a loss-year decision, since a full write-off is worth nothing to a company with no income to shelter.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A count, not an amount, at item 9 label Q of the company return, stored as a six digit character field in BLADE.
limitation: A count says nothing about size, and one opted-out asset can outweigh a hundred others, which is why the value column sits beside it. The ATO also accepts an approximation - "You will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect amount at Q and R where you have made your best attempt" - so the number is not audited.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 9 label Q, and the ATO page gives the instruction, the irrevocability of the choice and the best-attempt standard.
evidence_quote: Write at Q the number of assets for which you have made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, and did not say the count is unaudited or that its value pair is a forgone deduction.

value_domain: Dollar value of deductions forgone by opting out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: What the company gave up by opting out of temporary full expensing, measured as the deduction it would otherwise have claimed. The ATO is specific that this is not asset cost: "The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out". Together with the count of opted-out assets it identifies firms that deliberately deferred deductions, typically because they had no taxable income to absorb them.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 9 label R of the company return, being a counterfactual deduction rather than an outlay or a book value.
limitation: Because it is a forgone deduction rather than an asset cost, it cannot be added to the temporary full expensing deduction to get eligible investment; the assets are still depreciated under the ordinary rules and their cost appears nowhere on this item. The choice is also irrevocable, so no later label corrects it.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 9 label R, and the ATO page defines the value explicitly as the deduction that would otherwise have been claimed.
evidence_quote: The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice, and a reader would naturally have read the value as the cost of the assets.

value_domain: Dollar taxable income of the complying superannuation class
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 16 Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
variable_description: The taxable income a life insurance company attributed to its complying superannuation business, as opposed to its ordinary business. The ATO explains that "Life insurance companies separate their taxable income into two classes (the ordinary class and the complying superannuation class) and multiply the taxable income of each class by the appropriate tax rate", the instruction for the label being "Write at B the amount of taxable income of the complying superannuation class". Only life insurers and friendly societies carrying on life insurance business complete item 16.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 16 Life insurance companies and friendly societies only
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 16 label B of the company return, a flow over the income year, worked out separately from the ordinary class and taxed at its own rate.
limitation: It is not additive with ordinary class income for a tax rate calculation, because the two classes carry different rates and "Tax losses of one class can only be applied to reduce future income of the same class". Outside a handful of life insurers and friendly societies the column is empty, so it cannot be used as a superannuation measure.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 16 label B, and the ATO page defines the two-class structure, the separate rates and the quarantining of losses.
evidence_quote: Write at B the amount of taxable income of the complying superannuation class.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Complying superannuation class' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which firms report it or why it cannot be added to ordinary taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar stock of tax losses carried forward
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The stock of unused tax losses the company is carrying into later income years. The ATO instruction is "Write at U the unapplied (undeducted or not transferred) amount of tax losses incurred by the company and carried forward to a later income year under section 36-17 of the ITAA 1997", excluding any losses carried back to earlier years. Net capital losses are carried separately at the next label, so this column is revenue losses only.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 13 label U of the company return, a stock at the end of the income year rather than the loss made in it.
limitation: Differencing it between years does not give the year's loss, because losses deducted, transferred out, carried back or extinguished by commercial debt forgiveness all move the balance. Carrying a loss forward is also not the same as being able to use it, since the continuity of ownership and business continuity tests still have to be met.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 13 label U, and the ATO page defines the balance, excludes carried-back losses and separates net capital losses.
evidence_quote: Write at U the unapplied (undeducted or not transferred) amount of tax losses incurred by the company and carried forward to a later income year under section 36-17 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice, and did not warn against differencing a stock to recover a flow.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the TOFA transitional balancing adjustment
value_source: ATO, Guide to the taxation of financial arrangements (TOFA), When the rules apply
variable_description: The one-off adjustment a company recognised when its pre-existing financial arrangements were brought under the TOFA rules. The ATO describes the calculation as comparing "actual amounts that have been included in assessable income or allowed as a deduction" with "amounts that would have been included in assessable income and allowable as deductions if TOFA had applied to those existing financial arrangements", and "The difference is an assessable or deductible amount that is spread equally over the first income year in which TOFA applies, and the 3 subsequent income years". It only arises for companies that made the existing financial arrangements election, and the return label was dropped after the transition ran out.
description_source: ATO, Guide to the taxation of financial arrangements (TOFA), When the rules apply
value_definition: Whole dollars, one quarter of the transitional difference in each of four income years, reported at item 8 of the company return in the years the label existed.
limitation: It is a transition artefact rather than a measure of financial activity, and it stops for a reason outside the firm: once the four-year spread ended the label left the return, so zeros in later years say nothing about the company's financial arrangements.
rationale: The DIL label names the TOFA transitional balancing adjustment, which the ATO TOFA guide defines and which appears as item 8 label R on company tax returns of that era, for example the 2013 form.
evidence_quote: The difference is an assessable or deductible amount that is spread equally over the first income year in which TOFA applies, and the 3 subsequent income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the acronym-laden label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained that the amount is one quarter of a transition difference or why the column disappears.

value_domain: Dollar amount of unrealised TOFA gains
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The share of the company's TOFA gains that came from financial arrangements moving in value without being closed out. The ATO instruction is "Write at S the total of all TOFA gains recognised at item 6 as a result of unrealised movements in the value of financial arrangements", and it adds that such gains arise "as a result of making certain TOFA rules tax-timing method elections". So the column is as much a signal of an accounting election, such as fair value or reliance on financial reports, as of market movement.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label S of the company return, a subset of the gains already recognised in the income labels at item 6.
limitation: There is no matching unrealised losses column, so the return cannot be used to net unrealised movements, and because these gains are assessable without any cash being received, a large figure can sit beside a company with no capacity to pay.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label S, and the ATO page defines it and attributes it to tax-timing method elections.
evidence_quote: Write at S the total of all TOFA gains recognised at item 6 as a result of unrealised movements in the value of financial arrangements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the compressed label text with the generic sentence twice, and gave no hint that the number follows an election rather than a transaction.

value_domain: Dollar amount of TOFA deductions taken at the reconciliation
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: TOFA losses the company deducted that were not already sitting in its accounting expenses. The ATO instruction is "If the company has financial arrangements to which the TOFA rules apply, include at item W losses allowable under the TOFA rules from financial arrangements which have not been shown at item 6". It is a reconciliation label, so it exists precisely because tax recognition of a financial arrangement can run ahead of, or behind, the accounts.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 7 label W of the company return, a subtraction in the reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable income.
limitation: On its own it is a residual and says nothing about the scale of the company's financial arrangements; total TOFA losses at item 8, which counts losses recognised at both item 6 and item 7, is the column for that. It also has no counterpart for firms below the TOFA thresholds, which never report it at all.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 7 label W, and the ATO page defines it as the TOFA losses not shown at item 6.
evidence_quote: If the company has financial arrangements to which the TOFA rules apply, include at item W losses allowable under the TOFA rules from financial arrangements which have not been shown at item 6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the compressed label with the generic sentence twice, and did not point to the total TOFA losses column that gives it context.

value_domain: Dollar amount of TOFA income taken at the reconciliation
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Assessable TOFA gains that never appeared as income in the company's accounts and so had to be added back in the reconciliation. The ATO instruction is "If the company has financial arrangements to which the TOFA rules apply, include at E assessable gains under the TOFA rules from financial arrangements which have not been shown at item 6". It is the income-side mirror of the TOFA deductions reconciliation label, and both feed the total TOFA gains and losses memoranda at item 8.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 7 label E of the company return, an addition in the reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable income.
limitation: It measures the gap between tax and accounting recognition, not the size or profitability of the company's financial arrangements. Only entities over the TOFA thresholds, or those that elected in, ever report it, so a zero is usually a statement about the firm's size rather than about its treasury activity.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 7 label E, and the ATO page defines it as the assessable TOFA gains not shown at item 6.
evidence_quote: If the company has financial arrangements to which the TOFA rules apply, include at E assessable gains under the TOFA rules from financial arrangements which have not been shown at item 6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the compressed label with the generic sentence twice, and never distinguished it from the TOFA deduction label with an almost identical name.

value_domain: Dollar accounting profit or loss on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: The company's accounting profit or loss for the year, before anything is adjusted for tax. The ATO defines it arithmetically: "Total profit or loss is the amount written at Income, S Total income, less the amount written at Expenses, Q Total expenses. If this amount is a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at T". It is the starting point of the item 7 reconciliation, so it is the return's closest equivalent to a bottom line from the financial statements.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 6 label T of the company return, a flow over the income year, being total income less total expenses on an accounting basis.
limitation: It is not taxable income and not profit for company law purposes. Exempt and foreign income, non-deductible expenses and book depreciation are all inside it, and a loss carries its sign in a separate indicator on the form rather than in the number.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 label T, and the ATO page gives the formula, the loss indicator and the link to the item 7 reconciliation.
evidence_quote: Total profit or loss is the amount written at Income, S Total income, less the amount written at Expenses, Q Total expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total profit or loss' with the generic sentence twice, and left it easy to confuse with taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar average total debt for thin capitalisation
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The company's average total debt for the year, the figure the thin capitalisation rules work from. The ATO instruction is "Write at J the average total debt of the company for the income year. Calculate the average total debt by adding the opening and closing balances of the total debt of the company for the income year, and dividing this sum by two". Debt here is defined by what generates deductible finance expenses, and the ATO is explicit that "there is no requirement that amounts included at J satisfy the definition of 'debt interest'".
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label J of the company return, an average of two point-in-time balances rather than a year-end stock, and computed for tax rather than lifted from the accounts.
limitation: A two-point average conceals the path: a company that borrowed heavily in July and repaid in June and one that borrowed in June look the same. It is also a wider concept than the balance sheet's interest-bearing debt, since anything giving rise to deductible finance expenses counts, so it does not reconcile to total liabilities on the same row.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label J, and the ATO page gives the averaging formula and the deliberately wide definition of debt.
evidence_quote: Calculate the average total debt by adding the opening and closing balances of the total debt of the company for the income year, and dividing this sum by two.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total debt' with the generic sentence twice, so a reader would have taken it for a year-end balance sheet figure.

value_domain: Dollar total of assessable TOFA gains
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: All of the company's assessable gains from financial arrangements under the TOFA rules, gathered from wherever they were reported. The ATO instruction is "Write at T the total of all assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7", and it lists the labels to draw from: partnership and trust distributions, gross interest, dividends, unrealised revaluation gains, other income and the item 7 TOFA income label. It is a memorandum total, so it re-states amounts that are already counted elsewhere on the return.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label T of the company return, a flow over the income year that overlaps the income labels at item 6 rather than adding to them.
limitation: Adding it to total income double counts, because these gains are already inside interest, dividends and other income. It also cannot be compared with total TOFA losses to get a cash result, since both sides mix realised and unrealised amounts.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label T, and the ATO page gives the instruction and the list of source labels that establishes the overlap.
evidence_quote: Write at T the total of all assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total TOFA gains' with the generic sentence twice, and did not flag that the total overlaps the income labels.

value_domain: Dollar total of allowable TOFA losses
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: All of the company's allowable losses from financial arrangements under the TOFA rules, gathered from wherever they were claimed. The ATO instruction is "Write at U the total of all allowable TOFA losses from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7", drawing on bad debts, interest expenses within Australia and overseas, unrealised revaluation losses, all other expenses and the item 7 TOFA deductions label. Like its gains counterpart it is a memorandum column rather than an extra deduction.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label U of the company return, a flow over the income year that restates amounts already inside the expense labels at item 6.
limitation: It cannot be added to total expenses without double counting, and netting it against total TOFA gains gives a tax outcome rather than a cash flow, since unrealised movements sit on both sides.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label U, and the ATO page gives the instruction and the list of expense labels the total is drawn from.
evidence_quote: Write at U the total of all allowable TOFA losses from financial arrangements recognised at item 6 and item 7.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total TOFA losses' with the generic sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the item 7 TOFA deduction label.

value_domain: Dollar total assets from the company's balance sheet
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Everything the company's balance sheet counts as an asset at the end of the income year. The ATO instruction is "Write at E all assets of the company, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets and all current assets", and for a consolidated group the head company reports "all the assets of the group as disclosed in the financial accounts and not the amounts that are calculated by way of the allocable cost amount". It is an accounting value, not a tax value.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label E of the company return, a stock at the end of the income year drawn from the financial statements.
limitation: The reporting unit is not always the trading entity: a head company's figure covers subsidiaries that never lodge their own return, so joining this column to employment or industry for a single ABN can attribute a group's assets to one entity. Where the company was a group subsidiary for part of the year, the balance is measured at the end of the latest non-membership period rather than at year end.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label E, and the ATO page gives the instruction, the accounting basis and the consolidation and non-membership rules.
evidence_quote: Write at E all assets of the company, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets and all current assets as written at D All current assets item 8.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total assets' with the generic sentence twice, and did not say whose assets are counted when a group lodges.

value_domain: Dollar total expenses on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: The company's total accounting expenses for the year, the sum of every expense label at item 6. The ATO instruction is "Write at Q the total of all expense items written at B to S item 6", and where cost of sales is negative and larger than the rest, the total itself is marked as a loss. Total income less this figure is the total profit or loss on the next label.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 6 label Q of the company return, a flow over the income year on an accounting basis, with depreciation at book values for all but small business entities using the simplified rules.
limitation: It is not deductions. Non-deductible expenses inside this total are added back at item 7, tax depreciation is calculated separately, and exempt-income expenditure is removed there too, so subtracting this from total income gives accounting profit and never the tax base.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 label Q, and the ATO page gives the summation rule and the accounting basis of item 6.
evidence_quote: Write at Q the total of all expense items written at B to S item 6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total expenses' with the generic sentence twice, and invited the mistake of reading it as total deductions.

value_domain: Dollar total income on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: The company's total accounting income for the year, the sum of every income label at item 6. The ATO instruction is "Write at S the total of all income items written at B to R item 6". It is the broadest income measure on the return, covering sales, dividends, interest, rent, distributions, government payments and unrealised revaluation gains, and it is one of the labels the ATO uses to decide which entities appear in the Report of entity tax information.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 6 label S of the company return, a flow over the income year on an accounting basis, which can itself be a loss and is then marked with a loss indicator.
limitation: It is not assessable income and not turnover for any tax threshold. Exempt income, non-assessable non-exempt income and foreign source income can all be inside it, while aggregated turnover, which decides small business and temporary full expensing eligibility, is a different concept reported elsewhere.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 label S, and the ATO income and status pages give the summation rule and the use of the income labels for the entity tax transparency report.
evidence_quote: Write at S the total of all income items written at B to R item 6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total income' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing separated it from assessable income or aggregated turnover.

value_domain: Dollar total liabilities from the company's balance sheet
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Everything the company owed at the end of the income year, current and long term. The ATO instruction is "Write at H all liabilities of the company, including other creditors and deferred liabilities such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans", and the figure includes the current liabilities reported on the label above it. Like total assets it is an accounting value taken from the financial statements.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label H of the company return, a stock at the end of the income year, inclusive of the all current liabilities label.
limitation: A year-end stock misses everything that happened in between, which is why the return carries a separate average total debt label for thin capitalisation, and the two do not reconcile because that one is built from deductible finance expenses rather than from the balance sheet. Trade creditors and provisions are inside this figure, so it is not borrowings.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label H, and the ATO page gives the instruction, the accounting basis and the separate treatment of average total debt.
evidence_quote: Write at H all liabilities of the company, including other creditors and deferred liabilities such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total liabilities' with the generic sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the average total debt column on the same item.

value_domain: Dollar total salary and wage expenses
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The company's whole labour cost for the year as it appears in the income statement, including directors' remuneration. The ATO instruction is "Write at D the total salary, wage and other labour costs incurred, including directors' remuneration, as per income statements", and it explicitly pulls in the salary and wage component sitting inside cost of sales, along with allowances, bonuses, casual labour, overtime, leave and workers compensation paid through the payroll. Contractors, agency fees, superannuation, consultant fees and government-reimbursed wages are excluded.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label D of the company return, a flow over the income year, incurred rather than paid, and spanning all the item 6 expense lines that contain labour.
limitation: It is not payroll as reported through single touch payroll and not a headcount proxy: superannuation and contractor payments are outside it, salaries paid to associated persons are inside it and also reported separately, and a labour hire arrangement moves cost out of this column without changing the work done.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 8 label D, and the ATO page enumerates both what belongs in the total and what is excluded from it.
evidence_quote: Write at D the total salary, wage and other labour costs incurred, including directors’ remuneration, as per income statements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total salaries and wage expenses' with the generic sentence twice, and did not list the exclusions that stop it being a payroll measure.

value_domain: Salary and wage expense location code
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: Where in the company's item 6 expenses its salaries and wages were reported: cost of sales, all other expenses, both, or somewhere else. The ATO instruction is "Print in the CODE box at D the code from table 7 that matches the description of the expense component where salary and wage expenses have been wholly or predominantly reported at item 6". It exists because total salary and wage expenses is a memorandum figure assembled from lines that appear elsewhere, and this code says which lines those were.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A four-way code accompanying item 8 label D, mapped in BLADE to 5 for A all other expenses, 10 for B both cost of sales and all other expenses, 15 for C cost of sales, and 20 for O other than those two.
limitation: It is a location, not a split: the code says where wages were predominantly booked and never how much sat in each line, so it cannot be used to apportion labour between cost of sales and overheads. A change of code between years can also be a bookkeeping change rather than a change in how the firm produces.
rationale: The BLADE code list reproduces the ATO's table 7 letters and descriptions, and the item 8 page gives the instruction for the code box and the table itself.
evidence_quote: Print in the CODE box at D the code from table 7 that matches the description of the expense component where salary and wage expenses have been wholly or predominantly reported at item 6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the four codes with the generic sentence twice, and never explained why a wages figure needs a location code at all.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator for dealings with specified countries
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Overseas transactions items 26 to 30
variable_description: Whether the company moved funds or property to or from one of the countries the ATO names in the instructions, or could control assets located in or managed from one. The question is "Did you directly or indirectly send to, or receive from, one of the countries specified in the instructions, any funds or property?", with a second limb about the "ability or expectation to control, whether directly or indirectly, the disposition of any funds, property, assets or investments" connected with those countries. The listed countries are low-tax and secrecy jurisdictions such as the Cayman Islands, Bermuda, Jersey, Luxembourg and Hong Kong.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Overseas transactions items 26 to 30
value_definition: A yes or no flag at item 30 of the company return, coded Y or N with anything else an invalid or absent response, and carrying no amount.
limitation: The list of specified countries is set by the instructions and is revised, so a yes in one year and a no in the next can reflect the list rather than any change in the company's dealings. A yes is also not evidence of avoidance: Ireland, Luxembourg and Hong Kong are ordinary places to trade.
rationale: The DIL label is item 30 of the company return, and the ATO overseas transactions page gives the question in full and publishes the country list behind it.
evidence_quote: Did you directly or indirectly send to, or receive from, one of the countries specified in the instructions, any funds or property?
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Transactions with specified countries' with the generic sentence twice, and never said which countries or that the list changes.

value_domain: Dollar amount of unrealised revaluation gains
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: Gains the company booked as income by revaluing assets and liabilities to fair value, without selling anything. The ATO instruction is "Write at J the amount (if any) of any unrealised gains made on the revaluation of assets and liabilities to fair value that may arise as a result of the adoption of Australian equivalents to the international financial reporting standards", including unrealised gains on financial arrangements assessable under TOFA. Anything not assessable is taken back out at item 7.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 6 label J of the company return, an accounting flow arising from remeasurement rather than from a transaction.
limitation: Nothing was sold, so this is not a realised gain and it is not a capital gain: net capital gains go to their own item 7 label. Its presence depends on the company's accounting policy, so two firms holding identical assets can differ entirely on this column.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 income label J, and the ATO page defines the revaluation, the TOFA inclusion and the item 7 reversal.
evidence_quote: Write at J the amount (if any) of any unrealised gains made on the revaluation of assets and liabilities to fair value that may arise as a result of the adoption of Australian equivalents to the international financial reporting standards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long label with the generic sentence twice, and did not distinguish an unrealised revaluation from a capital gain.

value_domain: ATO country code for the ultimate holding company
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 1 Ultimate and immediate holding company name and ABN or country code
variable_description: Where the top of the company's ownership group sits, filled in only when that parent is not on the Australian Business Register. The ATO defines the ultimate holding company as "the company that has ownership and controlling interest over the whole group of companies of which the company lodging the Company tax return 2022 and the immediate holding company form part", and the rule for this field is "If the ultimate holding company is registered on the ABR, write the ABN of the ultimate holding company. If it is resident in another country, give the code for that country". It is the return's most direct marker of foreign ownership, and it is a different question from the company's own tax residency.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 1 Ultimate and immediate holding company name and ABN or country code
value_definition: A country code drawn from Appendix 3 of the data item list and Appendix 8 of the company tax return instructions, populated at item 1 only where the ultimate parent is foreign.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as Australian ownership: it also covers a company with no holding company at all, and one whose parent is on the Australian Business Register but is itself foreign-owned, so the column identifies immediate foreign parents rather than ultimate beneficial ownership. It is also self-reported and unverified against any register.
rationale: The DIL label names the ultimate holding company country code, which is item 1 of the company return, and the ATO page defines the ultimate holding company and states when the country code rather than an ABN is written.
evidence_quote: If the ultimate holding company is registered on the ABR, write the ABN of the ultimate holding company. If it is resident in another country, give the code for that country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pointed at an appendix for category codes and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the field is only completed for foreign parents.

value_domain: Dollar amount of unrealised revaluation losses
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Losses the company booked as an expense by revaluing assets and liabilities to fair value, with no disposal behind them. The ATO instruction is "Write at G the amount of any unrealised loss made on the revaluation of assets and liabilities to fair value that may arise as a result of the adoption of Australian equivalents to the international financial reporting standards", including deductible unrealised losses under the TOFA rules. It is the expense-side mirror of the unrealised gains label at item 6 income.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 6 label G of the company return, an accounting flow from remeasurement rather than from a transaction.
limitation: It is not a deduction: an unrealised loss that is not deductible is added back at the non-deductible expenses label at item 7, and net capital losses are carried forward at item 13 instead. Because it follows fair value accounting, its size reports an accounting policy as much as a decline in asset values.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 expense label G, and the ATO page defines the revaluation, the TOFA inclusion and the add-back for non-deductible amounts.
evidence_quote: Write at G the amount of any unrealised loss made on the revaluation of assets and liabilities to fair value that may arise as a result of the adoption of Australian equivalents to the international financial reporting standards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long label with the generic sentence twice, and did not say the amount is often added back and therefore not a deduction.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the unregulated investment component of a pooled development fund
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 18 Pooled development funds
variable_description: The unregulated investment component of a pooled development fund, which is whatever is left of its taxable income after the SME component is taken out. The ATO defines it as worked out "by deducting the company's SME income component from its taxable income for the year. The amount (if any) remaining is the company's unregulated investment component", with an adjusted taxable income used instead for a fund that was only a PDF for part of the year. The two components carry different tax rates, which is the reason the return splits them at all.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 18 Pooled development funds
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 18 label H of the company return, a residual of taxable income rather than an independently measured income stream.
limitation: Being a residual, it moves whenever deductions shift between classes, so a fall here can mean higher deductions rather than lower investment income. Only registered pooled development funds complete item 18, so this cannot be used as a measure of non-SME investment income for companies generally.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 18 label H, and the ATO page defines it as the residual after the SME income component and gives the part-year rule.
evidence_quote: The unregulated investment component of a company that is a PDF for the full income year is worked out by deducting the company’s SME income component from its taxable income for the year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Unregulated investment income' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said it is a residual or that it only applies to pooled development funds.

value_domain: Dollar amount of instant asset write-off claimed by non-small business entities
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Instant asset write-off claimed by a company too large to use the small business simplified depreciation rules. The ATO instruction is "Show at O the total amount you claimed at item 7F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets about assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold for which an immediate deduction is available", and it warns that where temporary full expensing applies you use that label instead. It is a disclosure carved out of the main depreciation deduction, added when the write-off was extended to medium and larger businesses.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 9 label O of the company return, a flow over the income year and a subset of the decline in value deduction reported at item 7.
limitation: It is not an additional deduction: the amount is already inside the item 7 decline in value figure, so adding the two double counts a firm's depreciation. Because temporary full expensing takes precedence, the column collapses to near nothing for the years that measure ran, which is a rule change rather than a fall in investment.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 9 label O introduced on the 2021 company return, and the 2021 instruction page defines the label and its overlap with the item 7 deduction.
evidence_quote: Show at O the total amount you claimed at item 7F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets about assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold for which an immediate deduction is available.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic sentence twice, and did not warn that the amount is already counted inside the decline in value deduction.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag for call-back payments
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the federal enterprise agreement covering the business promises extra pay when an employee is recalled to work after leaving for the day. It is one of the condition items that DEWR codes by reading the agreement text: the database "contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997", with around 200 items recorded per agreement. The row is an agreement, not a business, so in BLADE it describes the instrument a firm's employees are covered by.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A single flag with one active value, Y for yes; the absence of Y is not a coded no. The data item list notes it should only be coded for agreements made before 1 January 2010.
limitation: It stops rather than falls to zero: coding ceased for agreements made from 2010, so a run of blanks after that date records a change in DEWR's collection and not the disappearance of call-back clauses. An agreement is also a promise about entitlements, so the flag says nothing about whether anyone was ever called back or paid.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the Workplace Agreements Database, its coverage of conditions coded from agreement text, and its scale; the ABS lists WAD as the DEWR source inside BLADE. No fetchable DEWR document defines this particular condition item, which is why the finding is guessed.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never explained that the flag has no coded no or that coding ceased in 2010.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital purchases reported at G10 on the activity statement
value_source: ATO, Completing your BAS for GST, Step 3 Purchases
variable_description: What the business reported as capital purchases at label G10 of its business activity statement. The ATO defines them as "'capital' items you purchase, including: business assets you purchase such as machinery, cash registers, computers and cars ... land and buildings", new or second-hand and possibly imported, while "Things that aren't capital items include: trading stock, normal running expenses such as stationery and repairs, equipment rentals or leases". It is a GST reporting figure, so it arrives quarterly or monthly rather than once a year and covers acquisitions rather than accounting capital expenditure.
description_source: ATO, Completing your BAS for GST, Step 3 Purchases
value_definition: A dollar amount per activity statement period at label G10, GST-inclusive unless the business uses the accounts method and reports GST-exclusive amounts.
limitation: It is a GST label, not a capital formation measure. A business under $1 million of GST turnover that does not keep the split may report capital items of $1,000 or less at the non-capital label instead, the part of a car's price above the car limit is excluded, and there is no distinction between buying land and buying a laptop.
rationale: The BLADE table is the Business Activity Statement and the label wording matches G10; the ATO BAS page defines capital purchases, the exclusions and the $1,000 reporting shortcut.
evidence_quote: Capital purchases are 'capital' items you purchase, including: business assets you purchase such as machinery, cash registers, computers and cars (these items are also referred to as plant and equipment), land and buildings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Capital purchases*' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is GST-inclusive, sub-annual, or subject to the small business reporting shortcut.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 industry class code, cast across the longitudinal frame
value_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Division, subdivision, group and class codes and titles
variable_description: The business's industry under ANZSIC 2006, cast across time so that a unit keeps a consistent industry through the longitudinal frame. The ABS describes the coding system as "alphanumeric and has a hierarchical structure ... where the leading alpha character denotes the industry division" and "The ANZSIC subdivision, group and class levels are denoted by numeric codes", the class being the four-digit level held here. The cast prefix matters: the same table carries d_anzsic06 as the derived code, latest_anzsic06 as the most recent one, and an impute flag that "denotes where units have been 'cast' back or forward in time to maintain longitudinal nature of the dataset".
description_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Division, subdivision, group and class codes and titles
value_definition: A four-digit numeric ANZSIC 2006 class code, with 0 or 9999 meaning unknown or missing. A nine in the fourth digit marks a residual 'other' class within its group rather than a distinct activity.
limitation: Because the code is cast onto years the ABS did not observe, industry change over a unit's life is understated and a firm can appear in an industry before it entered it; the impute flag on the same row is the only way to see which unit-years were filled in that way. The code also describes the whole statistical unit, so a diversified business is reduced to its main activity.
rationale: The ABS classification page defines the ANZSIC numbering system and the four-digit class, and the neighbouring columns in the BLADE longitudinal indicative table define what casting means and how it differs from the derived and latest codes.
evidence_quote: The numbering system adopted in the ANZSIC is alphanumeric and has a hierarchical structure (see example below), where the leading alpha character denotes the industry division.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the classification's title with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and said nothing about what casting does or how the column differs from the derived and latest ANZSIC columns beside it.

value_domain: ANZSIC 1993 industry class code, cast across the longitudinal frame
value_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Appendix 3 Changes from ANZSIC 1993
variable_description: The business's industry under the 1993 edition of ANZSIC, the classification in force before 2006 and the one that covers the early years of the BLADE frame. The ABS says the 2006 edition "replaces the 1993 edition, which was the first version produced" and that it "reflects the outcomes of a substantial review of the classification", with the changes set out in Appendix 3. Like its 2006 counterpart the code is cast forward or back so a unit keeps a consistent industry through the longitudinal frame.
description_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Appendix 3 Changes from ANZSIC 1993
value_definition: A four-digit numeric ANZSIC 1993 class code, with 0 or 9999 meaning unknown or missing, held on the same row as the ANZSIC 2006 code rather than replacing it.
limitation: It is not comparable with the 2006 code beside it. The 2006 review moved activities between divisions, so a series that switches editions part way through breaks at the switch, and using the ABS correspondences is the only sound way to bridge it. A unit carrying both codes has been dual coded, which is not a change of activity.
rationale: The ABS release page states that ANZSIC 2006 replaced the 1993 edition after a substantial review, and Appendix 3 documents the changes that break comparability between the two editions.
evidence_quote: This 2006 edition of the ANZSIC replaces the 1993 edition, which was the first version produced.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the classification's title with the generic sentence twice, and gave no warning that the 1993 and 2006 codes on the same row are not a continuous series.

value_domain: Non-profit institution flag
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
