variable_description: Whether the business was treated as a non-profit institution in that year on BLADE's longitudinal indicative file. The ABS defines non-profit institutions as "legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit or other financial gain for the units that establish, control or finance them". The cast_ prefix marks a characteristic carried back or forward across years so the unit has a value in every year of the series; the impute column on the same table flags where that happened.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
value_definition: A one-digit flag: 1 non-profit institution, 2 other institution, 9 not determined. It applies the non-profit concept used in the ABS Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia rather than any registration status held by another regulator.
limitation: It does not identify a registered charity, a deductible gift recipient or a tax-exempt body, because the ABS test is about who may take the surplus rather than about tax treatment. A run of code 9 usually means the unit had no live Business Register record for those years and was cast in to keep the series unbroken, so it is a property of the file rather than a change in the business.
rationale: SESCA is the ABS classification that carries the non-profit institution concept used across ABS business collections, and BLADE's business classifications are drawn from the ABS Business Register which applies SESCA.
evidence_quote: Non-Profit Institutions (NPIs) are defined as 'legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit or other financial gain for the units that establish, control or finance them'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label 'Non Profit Institution flag' and the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said whose definition of non-profit applies or what the cast_ prefix does.

value_domain: Australian postcode of the business address
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The postcode recorded against the business on the ABS Business Register for that year, carried across years on the longitudinal indicative file. It locates the registered or main business address, which for a multi-site firm is usually a head office or an accountant's address rather than where the work is done. Read it with cast_state and cast_st_op, which give the main state of operation and the wider set of states the business operates in.
description_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A four-digit numeric Australia Post postcode. Postcodes are a mail delivery geography, not an ABS statistical geography, so they do not nest inside statistical areas.
limitation: It cannot be used to place economic activity. A national retailer, a labour hire firm and a mining company all sit at whatever address the ABN carries, so postcode-level counts built from this column measure where businesses are registered rather than where they employ or produce. Postcode boundaries also change over time and the column carries no edition, so a stable code does not prove a stable location.
rationale: The ABS microdata page confirms BLADE's indicative items come from the ABS Business Register and include business demographics, but no published page defines this specific postcode field, so the address interpretation is inferred from the surrounding columns.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Postcode' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that this is a registration address rather than a place of activity.

value_domain: Public or private sector indicator
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
variable_description: Whether the business was a private or a government-controlled unit in that year, on the ABS public and private split. The ABS draws the line by control: "The Public/Private classification divides the economy into two sectors: Public (government units and units controlled by government); and Private (all other units)." It is the coarsest of the sector columns on this table; cast_sisca93, cast_sisca06 and cast_sisca08 give the full institutional sector underneath it.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
value_definition: A one-digit code: 1 private, 2 public, 9 not determined. It is the public and private dimension of the ABS Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia, which is derived from control rather than from ownership share or legal form.
limitation: Control, not ownership, decides the code, so a government business enterprise that trades commercially is public here while a heavily subsidised private contractor is private. The column also cannot separate Commonwealth from state and local government units; that distinction lives in the SISCA columns, not this one.
rationale: SESCA is the ABS classification that defines the public and private sector split applied on the ABS Business Register, from which BLADE's indicative items are drawn.
evidence_quote: The Public/Private classification divides the economy into two sectors: Public (government units and units controlled by government); and Private (all other units).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Private/Public indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the split is made on control.

value_domain: SISCA 2006 institutional sector code
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
variable_description: The business's institutional sector on the 2006 SISCA coding, the middle of the three sector vintages on this table. Sectors are groupings of like units rather than of like products: "These sectors group institutional units which have similar economic functions and structural characteristics." Where a firm has a 2006 code but no 2008 code it usually left the register before the later coding was applied.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
value_definition: A four-digit numeric code on the 2006 edition of the Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia, with 0 or 9999 for unknown or missing. The top level splits the economy into non-financial corporations, financial corporations, general government, households, non-profit institutions serving households, and the rest of the world.
limitation: Sector is not industry. A finance company and a manufacturer that both borrow and lend inside a group can share a sector code while doing nothing alike, so this column cannot substitute for the ANZSIC columns when the question is about what the business makes.
rationale: SESCA defines SISCA, its purpose and its four-level code structure; the edition in the BLADE label names which vintage of that classification was applied to the unit.
evidence_quote: These sectors group institutional units which have similar economic functions and structural characteristics.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the classification's title as its description and carried the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: SISCA 2008 institutional sector code
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
variable_description: The business's institutional sector on the 2008 SISCA coding, the vintage that covers most of BLADE's span. The ABS describes the classification as follows: "The Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia (SISCA) provides a framework for dividing the Australian economy into institutional sectors." Compare it with d_sisca08 and latest_sisca08 on the same table, which respectively fill gaps and hold the most recent code for the unit.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
value_definition: A four-digit numeric code on the 2008 edition of the Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia, with 0 or 9999 for unknown or missing. SISCA 2008 is aligned with the institutional sector classification of the System of National Accounts 2008.
limitation: The code is assigned to the unit on the ABS Business Register, not to the enterprise group above it, so a subsidiary and its parent can carry different sectors and neither one describes the group. It also says nothing about size or activity, which the employment and turnover columns carry.
rationale: SESCA is the ABS publication that defines SISCA and the 2008 edition named in the BLADE label, and the ABS business counts methodology confirms SISCA is applied on the Business Register.
evidence_quote: The Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia (SISCA) provides a framework for dividing the Australian economy into institutional sectors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the classification's name and the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish this column from the derived and latest sector columns beside it.

value_domain: SISCA 1993 institutional sector code
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
variable_description: The business's institutional sector on the oldest SISCA edition carried in BLADE, kept so the early years can be read on their own coding. The ABS says "SISCA is the classification used to distinguish between market and non-market producers", which is the split this column exists to make. It sits beside cast_sisca06 and cast_sisca08, which code the same business on later editions.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
value_definition: A four-digit numeric code on the 1993 edition of the Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia, with 0 or 9999 for unknown or missing. The digits nest: one digit is the sector, two the subsector, three the group and four the class.
limitation: It is not comparable with the later SISCA columns on the same row. A business can appear to change sector between the 1993, 2006 and 2008 codes purely because the classification was revised, so a transition matrix built by comparing two of these columns measures reclassification as much as it measures real change.
rationale: SESCA is the ABS publication that defines SISCA and its structure; the edition named in the BLADE label is the vintage of the coding applied, and the classification concept is the same across editions.
evidence_quote: SISCA is the classification used to distinguish between market and non-market producers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the classification's name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what SISCA separates or why three editions sit side by side.

value_domain: States and territories of operation indicator
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Which states and territories the business operated in during the year, rather than the single main state that cast_state carries. BLADE's indicative items include "Demographics such as main State or Territory of operation, Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) and other structural business characteristics", and this column is the multi-jurisdiction version of that. A firm operating in three states can be told apart from a single-state firm here but not from cast_state.
description_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A nine-digit numeric category, read as one position per state and territory plus a residual position, so more than one jurisdiction can be flagged at once. The reading of the nine positions is inferred from the valid-response text rather than published.
limitation: It records presence, not scale, so a business with one van crossing a border looks the same as one with a warehouse in every capital. It also cannot be split into employment or turnover by state, and because it is cast across years it may carry a footprint from a year in which the business was not observed.
rationale: The ABS microdata page confirms BLADE's indicative items carry state of operation among the business demographics drawn from the Business Register; the nine-position structure comes from the custodian's valid-response text.
evidence_quote: Demographics such as main State or Territory of operation, Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) and other structural business characteristics.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'States of operation' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that the field flags several jurisdictions at once or how it differs from cast_state.

value_domain: Main state or territory of the business
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The one state or territory the business is assigned to for the year, carried across years on the longitudinal indicative file. The ABS lists among BLADE's business demographics the "main State or Territory of operation", which is what this single-valued column holds; the multi-jurisdiction picture is in cast_st_op. It is the geography most BLADE state tabulations are built on.
description_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A numeric state and territory code with 0 for unknown or missing. It is a single main jurisdiction per business per year, not an apportionment.
limitation: Assigning a whole business to one jurisdiction moves all of its employment and turnover there, so state aggregates built from this column overstate the states that host head offices and understate the states that host branches. It cannot be reconciled with cast_st_op except to say the main state should be one of the operating states.
rationale: The ABS microdata page names main state or territory of operation as one of BLADE's demographic items, and the table's own structure separates this single-valued column from the multi-state one beside it.
evidence_quote: Demographics such as main State or Territory of operation, Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) and other structural business characteristics.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'State' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so a reader could not tell that a whole business is placed in one jurisdiction.

value_domain: Type of Legal Organisation code
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology
variable_description: The legal form of the business - company, trust, partnership, sole trader or public sector entity - and it is populated only for the profiled population. The ABS says "TOLO indicates whether a business is part of the private or public sector, and the type of ownership structure it has", and SESCA classifies units into incorporated private, unincorporated private and public sector entities. The profiled population is the small set of complex businesses the ABS maintains itself: "For a small number of businesses, the ABN unit is not suitable for ABS economic statistics purposes and the ABS maintains its own economic units structure through direct contact with businesses."
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology
value_definition: A code on the ABS Type of Legal Organisation classification, published within the Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia, with a one-digit group level and a two-digit class level. The custodian's valid-response text records the domain as the profiled population.
limitation: Because it is filled only for profiled units, a missing TOLO is the normal case and does not mean the legal form is unknown - it means the business is in the ATO-maintained population, which is most of BLADE. Any share of companies against trusts computed from this column therefore describes large complex enterprises, not Australian business as a whole.
rationale: The ABS business counts methodology defines TOLO and sets out the profiled and non-profiled split of the Business Register, which is what the custodian's 'Profiled Population' valid-response text points at; SESCA publishes the classification itself.
evidence_quote: For a small number of businesses, the ABN unit is not suitable for ABS economic statistics purposes and the ABS maintains its own economic units structure through direct contact with businesses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Type of Legal Organisation (TOLO)' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, and gave no warning that the column is populated only for profiled businesses.

value_domain: Casual loading percentage recorded in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The size of the casual loading the enterprise agreement promises casual employees, as coded by departmental staff reading the agreement. DEWR holds "conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997" and codes around 200 items from each one, of which this is a single provision. It is an agreement term, not payroll: it says what was promised, not what any worker was paid.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A numeric quantum of loading, with 111111111 reserved for a loading that varies or whose size is unknown. The custodian records that it should only be coded in agreements made before 1 January 2011.
limitation: The pre-2011 coding rule truncates the series, so an empty cell on a 2015 agreement means the item was retired rather than that the agreement gave no casual loading. The sentinel 111111111 also has to be removed before averaging, or a single varied-loading agreement will swamp any mean.
rationale: DEWR publishes and maintains the Workplace Agreements Database and describes its coverage, its coding of conditions and its supply of a historical subset to BLADE, which is the source of this column.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about recording the quantum and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not flag that the field was retired for agreements made after 2010.

value_domain: Minimum casual engagement, in hours
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The shortest continuous shift the agreement guarantees a casual employee when called in for one engagement. It is one of the conditions of employment coded from the agreement text by DEWR, whose database records "around 200 data items" for each federal enterprise agreement. A high value protects casuals against very short call-outs; a blank means the coders found no such clause, not that a minimum of zero applies.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A number of hours, with 111111111 reserved for a minimum that varies across classifications or is unknown. It is a floor per engagement, not a weekly or fortnightly guarantee.
limitation: It cannot tell you how casuals were actually rostered. Agreements often set a minimum that is never binding in practice, and where different minimums apply to different classifications the whole agreement collapses to the varies-or-unknown sentinel, so the coded value understates variation within the firm.
rationale: DEWR describes the Workplace Agreements Database as holding coded conditions of employment for federal enterprise agreements, which is the class this provision belongs to, and confirms a historical subset is supplied to BLADE.
evidence_quote: There are over 180,000 agreements in the database. An average of 6,000 agreements are added each year, and around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's descriptive sentence with the generic no-value-list line as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said the value is a coded agreement clause rather than observed rostering.

value_domain: Yes-only flag for casuals working full-time hours
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets casual employees work up to the same hours as the firm's full-time permanent staff. Only a Yes is ever recorded, so the field is a presence flag for the clause rather than a two-way answer, and the custodian notes it should only apply to agreements made from 1 January 2008. DEWR warns that the coded conditions change over time: "The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database."
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A single-valued flag: Y where the clause was found, and otherwise empty. There is no explicit No code.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as No. It mixes agreements that positively exclude the practice, agreements that are silent on it, and agreements made before the item was collected in 2008, so any rate computed as the share of Y over all agreements is a coverage artefact rather than a prevalence estimate.
rationale: DEWR maintains the database and states that the conditions collected are reviewed annually and do not all span the full series, which is exactly the trap this yes-only field sets.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence about the clause and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without warning that no No code exists.

value_domain: Date an enterprise agreement was approved or certified
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The day the workplace tribunal approved or certified the enterprise agreement, which is the event that puts the agreement on DEWR's database. It is the natural time index for the agreement record and the date behind the pre-2008 and pre-2011 coding rules on other WAD columns. Approval is a regulator's act, so it can fall months after the workforce voted for the agreement and after the nominal start of the wage increases it contains.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: An alphanumeric date written dd/mm/yyyy, where yyyy is the calendar year. It is a point in time, not a period.
limitation: It is not the date the agreement began to operate or expired, so it cannot be used on its own to say which agreement covered a workplace in a given year. Approval dates also bunch after legislative changes, so a spike in agreements certified in one quarter usually reflects tribunal processing rather than a burst of bargaining.
rationale: DEWR's Workplace Agreements Database is the source of this column and defines its scope by approval, holding conditions information for federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
evidence_quote: A subset of historical data from the Workplace Agreements Database is available as a module in the BLADE integrated data asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase 'The date the agreement is approved or certified' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without separating approval from commencement.

value_domain: Capital gains from collectables reported on the CGT schedule (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4: Definitions
variable_description: Capital gains the entity made in the year from collectables, reported as its own line because losses on collectables are quarantined. The ATO defines the class narrowly: "A collectable is an artwork, an item of jewellery, an antique, a coin, a medallion, a rare folio, a rare manuscript, a rare book, a postage stamp or a first day cover that is used or kept mainly for personal use or enjoyment." The label carries an old-form and a new-form wording because the schedule changed: the old form split collectables gains by calculation method under non-active assets, while the new form reports one collectables total, so a series spanning the change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4: Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount at the collectables label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: For a business this is rarely core trading activity, so a non-zero value usually signals an entity holding art, coins or wine rather than a change in the operating business. It also cannot be netted against the other gain columns freely, since collectables losses may only be applied to collectables gains.
rationale: The ATO defines collectables and quarantines their losses, and the CGT schedule instructions place collectables at its own label within current year capital gains, which is what this BLADE column carries.
evidence_quote: A collectable is an artwork, an item of jewellery, an antique, a coin, a medallion, a rare folio, a rare manuscript, a rare book, a postage stamp or a first day cover that is used or kept mainly for personal use or enjoyment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the raw OF and NF label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither defined a collectable nor explained the form change.

value_domain: Total current year capital gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: The entity's gross capital gains for the income year, before any loss, discount or concession is applied. It is the sum of the asset-class lines above it: "Add up the amounts at item 1 - labels A - I of the CGT schedule and write the total at label J Total current year capital gains." The old-form label called the same quantity total current year capital gains (CYCG) and split it by calculation method, so a series that crosses the form change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 1 label J of the capital gains tax schedule, being the sum of the nine current year capital gain categories on the same item.
limitation: It is not taxable income and is several steps from it: losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions all come off afterwards, so a firm with a large figure here can still return a nil net capital gain. Gains disregarded under the small business 15-year exemption are excluded from this total by design and appear only at item 8.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define label J as the sum of the current year capital gain categories, which is the quantity this BLADE column carries under both label wordings.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at item 1 - labels A - I of the CGT schedule and write the total at label J Total current year capital gains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what is and is not inside the total.

value_domain: Capital gains disregarded under the demerger exemption (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains the entity dropped out of its assessable income because it was the demerging entity in a demerger. A non-zero value is a strong marker of a corporate restructure in that year, not of trading. The ATO keeps this separate from the demerger rollover: "Write the total amount of any capital gains disregarded by the application of the demerger exemption at item 8 - label E in the CGT schedule. Don't include any amounts disregarded by the application of a demerger rollover."
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label E of the capital gains tax schedule, reported outside the current year gains total at item 1 and not reduced by the CGT discount.
limitation: It marks the demerging entity, not the owners, so the shareholders' side of the same demerger does not appear here. Because the amount is excluded from the item 1 total, adding it to total current year capital gains double counts nothing but also means a demerger year's true gross gains are split across two items.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 8 label E and expressly separate the demerger exemption from the demerger rollover, which is the distinction this column depends on.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of any capital gains disregarded by the application of the demerger exemption at item 8 - label E in the CGT schedule. Don't include any amounts disregarded by the application of a demerger rollover.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the new-form label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not distinguish the exemption from the rollover.

value_domain: Capital gains disregarded under the foreign resident exemption (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains a foreign resident entity kept out of Australian tax by claiming an exemption on an asset that would otherwise be taxable Australian property. It is one of the few columns on the schedule that identifies the lodger as a foreign resident. The ATO explains the boundary: "If you're a foreign resident, you're subject to CGT if a CGT event happens to a CGT asset that is 'taxable Australian property'."
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label B of the capital gains tax schedule, reported before the CGT discount is applied and outside the item 1 gains total.
limitation: A nil value does not mean the lodger is a resident: the ATO tells foreign residents whose asset is not taxable Australian property to skip the question altogether, so non-residents with untaxed gains can leave this blank. The column is a claim made on a self-assessed return rather than an ATO finding on residency.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 8 label B, set out when a foreign resident is within the CGT net, and say when the question does not have to be answered.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of any capital gains disregarded by the application of the foreign resident exemption at item 8 - label B in the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that a blank is uninformative about residency.

value_domain: Year reached within an earnout arrangement
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: How far into a business sale earnout the entity had progressed at the end of the income year - the second year of a four-year deal reads as 2. The ATO instruction is direct: "Write at label C the year of the earnout arrangement you're in." Read with cgerntarngmntsyrsrunfrnum, which gives the total length, it says how much of the deferred consideration is still to come.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A two-digit count of years elapsed within the arrangement, reported at item 7 label C of the capital gains tax schedule. It is an ordinal position within one arrangement, not a calendar year.
limitation: Where an entity is party to more than one earnout, the ATO requires the extra arrangements on an attached sheet, so this single field describes only one of them. It also says nothing about whether the earnout targets are being met, which is what actually drives the payments.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 7 label C and give a worked example of how the year within the arrangement is written.
evidence_quote: Write at label C the year of the earnout arrangement you're in.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question text 'What year of that arrangement are you in?' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say which arrangement or that only one is captured.

value_domain: Party to an earnout arrangement (buyer, seller or none)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Which side of a business sale earnout the entity sat on, or that it was not party to one at all. An earnout defers part of the price until the sold business hits agreed performance targets, so this column separates acquirers from vendors in deals of that shape. It is the gate for the rest of item 7: the ATO asks "Are you a party to an earnout arrangement?" and only a Yes leads to the years, proceeds and gain labels.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A numeric code: 5 buyer, 10 seller, 15 no; anything else is an invalid or absent response. It corresponds to the tick boxes at item 7 label A of the capital gains tax schedule.
limitation: Buyer and seller here are roles in a single reported arrangement, not a link to the counterparty, so this column cannot be used to match the two sides of a transaction inside BLADE. Only entities lodging a CGT schedule answer it, so most business sales never reach the column.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions set out item 7 label A as the gateway question about earnout arrangements and describe the buyer and seller positions in the worked example.
evidence_quote: Are you a party to an earnout arrangement?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare question and its code list with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never explained what an earnout is or why the role matters.

value_domain: Capital gains exempted under the small business 15-year exemption (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: The gain a small business owner wiped out entirely by selling an asset held for at least fifteen years, typically on retirement. The ATO describes it as a total exemption: "The small business 15-year exemption, subject to certain conditions being satisfied, means a capital gain is totally disregarded if you or your small business entity has continuously owned the CGT asset for at least 15 years". The label carries an old-form and a new-form wording - the old form said only exempt capital gains - so a series spanning the change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label A of the capital gains tax schedule, reported gross with no CGT discount applied and shown nowhere else on the schedule.
limitation: Because the ATO tells lodgers not to put the amount anywhere else, this gain is missing from total current year capital gains and from the net capital gain, so summing the item 1 columns understates what small business owners actually realised. The column is a self-assessed claim of eligibility, not an ATO ruling that the fifteen-year and other conditions were met.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define the exemption, state the fifteen-year ownership condition, and direct the amount to item 8 label A and nowhere else.
evidence_quote: Capital gains to which the small business 15-year exemption applies aren't included on the CGT summary worksheet.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the OF and NF label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the amount is excluded from the schedule's own gains total.

value_domain: Asset type code for the small business 15-year exemption
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: What kind of asset produced the gain the small business 15-year exemption was claimed on - goodwill, real estate, shares, units or something else. Goodwill against real estate is the useful split here: it separates an owner selling the business itself from one selling the premises it stood on. The ATO asks for one code only: "If your entity made capital gains from more than one CGT asset or CGT event, select the code which best describes the type of CGT asset or CGT event that produced the largest amount of capital gain."
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A numeric code: 5 goodwill on the sale of a business, 10 other assets or events not involving a CGT asset, 15 real estate, 20 shares, 25 units in unit trusts. It renumbers the ATO's letter codes G, O, R, S and U at the code box beside item 8 label A.
limitation: Only the largest gain is described, so an owner who sold the goodwill and the premises in the same year is recorded once and the smaller disposal disappears. The code also does not carry the exempted amount, which is in cg_exmptn_15_yr_fr_sb_amt on the same row.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions publish the asset and event code list for the code box at item 8 label A and the rule for choosing among them, which the BLADE code list reproduces with numeric values.
evidence_quote: Print in the code box at label A the code from the list below that best describes the CGT asset or CGT event from which your entity made the capital gain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the OF and NF label wording and the code list without saying that only the largest gain is described or that the letters are the ATO's own.

value_domain: Capital gains received from a trust (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains the entity received as a beneficiary of a trust or a unit holder in a managed fund, rather than from selling anything itself. It marks passive investment income flowing up a group or fund structure, so a company with a large figure here may have disposed of no asset at all. The ATO restricts what belongs on the line: "Include in row 7 of table 1 amounts of capital gains your entity received from a trust (including a managed fund) other than a capital gain involving a collectable."
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at the trust capital gains label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, reported gross and using the same calculation method the trustee used.
limitation: It does not identify the trust, so an entity's exposure cannot be traced to a particular fund or related party from this column. Gains from a trust that involve a collectable are excluded and sit in the collectables line instead, so this figure is not the entity's whole trust distribution.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define the trust capital gains row of item 1, its exclusion for collectables, and the requirement to mirror the trustee's calculation method.
evidence_quote: Include in row 7 of table 1 amounts of capital gains your entity received from a trust (including a managed fund) other than a capital gain involving a collectable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the definition and the limitation, so it did not say the gain is received rather than realised.

value_domain: Net capital gain (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4: Definitions
variable_description: The one capital gains figure that reaches the entity's assessable income, after every loss, discount and concession has been taken off. The ATO defines it as "the difference between your total capital gains for the year and the total of your capital losses for the year and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years, less any CGT discount and small business CGT concessions to which you're entitled". It is the bottom line of the schedule and is transferred to label A of the entity's tax return.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4: Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 6 label A of the capital gains tax schedule, being total current year gains less applied losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: It cannot go below zero, so a bad year shows as nil here and the loss appears instead in the carried-forward columns. Because concessions and the 15-year exemption have already been removed, this figure understates realised gains and should not be used as a measure of asset turnover.
rationale: The ATO guide defines net capital gain, and the CGT schedule instructions place it at item 6 label A and route it to the entity's tax return.
evidence_quote: A net capital gain is the difference between your total capital gains for the year and the total of your capital losses for the year and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years, less any CGT discount and small business CGT concessions to which you're entitled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Net capital gain' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say which deductions had already been made.

value_domain: Amended net capital gain or carried-forward loss from an earnout (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: A revised figure for an earlier year's capital gains position, lodged now because an earnout payment changed what the original sale was worth. The ATO uses the label as an amendment request: "write at label G the amended net capital gain or capital losses carried forward amount resulting from the financial benefits received or provided". The year being amended is at the neighbouring label F, so this amount does not belong to the year of the row it sits on.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label G of the capital gains tax schedule. Where the revised position is a loss the lodger prints L beside it, so the sign is carried outside the number.
limitation: Treating it as a current year gain is wrong: it restates an earlier income year, and a zero can mean either a genuine nil position or a capital loss the lodger must temporarily disregard under the look-through earnout rules. It also cannot be joined to the original year's row without label F.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 7 label G, the amendment mechanism, the L indicator and the rule requiring a zero where a look-through earnout loss must be disregarded.
evidence_quote: write at label G the amended net capital gain or capital losses carried forward amount resulting from the financial benefits received or provided.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could easily have read it as a current year amount.

value_domain: Capital gains from real estate outside Australia (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains from property that is not real estate situated in Australia - in practice offshore land and buildings. It is the residual half of the property split on the schedule, paired with cg_rl_este_std_in_aus_amt, and a non-zero value flags an entity holding foreign property. The two lines are separate labels within item 1, which the ATO fills from the entity's CGT summary worksheet.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at the other real estate label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, reported gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: It does not name the country, so it cannot support any analysis of where an Australian business holds property. Nor does it distinguish an operating site from a passive investment, since both are simply real estate to the schedule.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions list the current year capital gain categories of item 1 and include other real estate as a label distinct from real estate situated in Australia.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amounts at 1A - 1I and 1S for capital gains and from 1K - 1R for capital losses in table 1 on your CGT summary worksheet to the corresponding labels at item 1 of the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text and the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say what 'other' excludes.

value_domain: Capital gains from unlisted shares (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains from shares that are not quoted on an Australian securities exchange, which for a business usually means selling a stake in a private company. It is the counterpart to cgshrsincmpnsasxamt, and the listed-unlisted split is the schedule's rough proxy for portfolio investment against ownership of an operating business. Both are labels within item 1 of the CGT schedule.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at the other shares label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, reported before losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: It cannot tell a controlling sale from a minority parcel, so a founder exiting a company and an investor trimming a small holding look identical. Foreign listed shares also fall into this residual line, so it is not purely a private company measure.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions list the item 1 categories and place other shares immediately after shares in companies listed on an Australian securities exchange.
evidence_quote: For example, transfer the figure at 1A in table 1 of the CGT summary worksheet to item 1 - label A Shares in companies listed on an Australian securities exchange of the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the new-form label wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say what falls into the residual category.

value_domain: Capital gains from unlisted unit trust units (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains from disposing of units in unit trusts that are not quoted on an Australian securities exchange, such as a private property trust. It pairs with cgutlistdinasxamt, which covers listed units, and is distinct from cg_frm_trst_incl_mngd_trst_amt, which is a gain received from a trust rather than a gain on selling units in one. Both unit lines are labels within item 1 of the CGT schedule.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at the other units label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, reported gross of losses and concessions.
limitation: It does not identify the trust or its assets, so an unlisted property trust and an unlisted infrastructure fund are indistinguishable. Nor does it separate a redemption by the trustee from a sale to a third party, which have different commercial meanings for the business.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions list other units among the item 1 current year capital gain categories, distinct from listed units and from gains received from a trust.
evidence_quote: other units
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not separate selling units from receiving a distribution.

value_domain: Previously deferred capital gain recognised in the year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: A gain that a superannuation fund parked under the 2016-17 transitional CGT relief and is now bringing to account because the asset was finally sold. The ATO explains the label's job: "Label S on the CGT schedule recognises the previously deferred capital gain in an income year in which a realisation event occurs." It is therefore a legacy of the 2017 super reforms rather than a measure of this year's investment decisions.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 1 label S of the capital gains tax schedule, entered by complying superannuation funds and pooled superannuation trusts only.
limitation: The gain accrued years before the row it appears on, so treating the amount as a current year asset revaluation misdates it by up to a decade. The column is also confined to super funds and pooled super trusts, so it is empty for ordinary trading companies by construction rather than by behaviour.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions describe label S, its origin in the 2016-17 transitional CGT relief, and the entity types that must use it.
evidence_quote: Label S on the CGT schedule recognises the previously deferred capital gain in an income year in which a realisation event occurs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the gain belongs to an earlier year or that the column is super-fund only.

value_domain: Capital gains from Australian real estate (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Capital gains the entity made on land and buildings situated in Australia during the income year. For a business this is usually the sale of premises, an investment property or development stock held on capital account, and it is the single largest CGT line for many small companies and trusts. It is reported separately from cg_othr_rl_este_amt because the location of the property, not its use, decides the label.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at the real estate situated in Australia label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: It gives no address, area or property type, so nothing here supports a geography of business property disposals. Property held as trading stock by a developer is taxed as ordinary income and never reaches this column, so it understates the sector's real estate turnover.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions list real estate situated in Australia among the item 1 current year capital gain categories, distinct from other real estate.
evidence_quote: real estate situated in Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the new-form label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that developer trading stock is outside the column.

value_domain: Capital gains disregarded under scrip for scrip rollover (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Gains the entity deferred by taking shares or units in the acquirer instead of cash, so a takeover produced no immediate tax. A non-zero value marks a paper-for-paper merger or acquisition in that year. The ATO defines the exchange: "Original interests are shares, units or other interests (or an option, right or similar interest in a company or trust), while replacement interests are the same type of interests in another company or trust."
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label C of the capital gains tax schedule, sitting outside the item 1 gains total.
limitation: The gain is deferred rather than forgiven - it comes back when the replacement interests are eventually sold - so reading this as tax-free profit is wrong. The column also does not name the acquirer, so the two sides of the takeover cannot be linked from it.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define scrip for scrip rollover, the original and replacement interests, and direct the disregarded amount to item 8 label C.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of any capital gains disregarded by the application of the scrip for scrip rollover at item 8 - label C in the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the gain is deferred rather than exempt.

value_domain: Capital gains disregarded under the inter-company asset rollover (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Gains removed because an asset simply moved between two companies in the same wholly-owned group, one of which is a foreign resident. It flags an internal restructure rather than a sale to the market. The ATO sets the conditions: "A same asset rollover may be available where: a company transfers or creates a CGT asset in another company that is a member of the same wholly-owned group" and "at least one of the companies is a foreign resident".
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 8 label D of the capital gains tax schedule, reported apart from the current year gains at item 1.
limitation: Because it is confined to same-group transfers involving a foreign resident company, it captures only a slice of internal restructuring; wholly domestic group transfers inside a tax consolidated group never generate a CGT event and appear nowhere. It also does not identify the receiving company, so the asset cannot be followed within BLADE.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define the inter-company asset rollover, its wholly-owned group and foreign resident conditions, and its reporting label.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of any capital gains disregarded by the application of the inter-company asset rollover at item 8 - label D in the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not state the wholly-owned group and foreign resident conditions.

value_domain: Capital gain or loss under an earnout in the income year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: The gain or loss the entity made this year from an earnout attached to a business sale, as distinct from the amended earlier-year figure at label G. The ATO instruction is explicit about the period: "Write at label E the amount of any capital gain or loss you made under your earnout arrangement in the income year for which this schedule is being completed." A loss is indicated by an L printed beside the amount rather than by a negative sign.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label E of the capital gains tax schedule, unsigned, with the loss case carried by a separate indicator on the form.
limitation: Losses on assets subject to a look-through earnout right must sometimes be temporarily disregarded until the arrangement ends, so a small or nil figure can hide an economic loss that the rules do not yet let the entity recognise. Without the loss indicator, a raw amount here cannot be signed.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 7 label E, its income year scope, the L indicator and the temporary disregard rule for look-through earnout losses.
evidence_quote: Write at label E the amount of any capital gain or loss you made under your earnout arrangement in the income year for which this schedule is being completed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain the sign convention or the temporarily disregarded losses.

value_domain: Total length of an earnout arrangement, in years
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: How many years the earnout attached to a business sale runs for in total, which sets how long the sale price stays uncertain. The ATO asks for the whole term: "Write at label B the number of years the earnout arrangement runs for in total." Divided into cg_ernt_arngmnts_yr_in_num it gives the share of the arrangement already elapsed.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A two-digit count of years at item 7 label B of the capital gains tax schedule, describing the arrangement as agreed rather than as it turned out.
limitation: It records the planned term, so an earnout terminated early by a settlement between the parties still shows its original length. Where an entity has several earnouts, only one is described in these fields and the rest go on an attached sheet that does not reach the data.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 7 label B as the total number of years of the arrangement and give a worked example against label C.
evidence_quote: Write at label B the number of years the earnout arrangement runs for in total.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question 'How many years does the earnout arrangement run for?' and the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice.
