evidence_quote: IP Refreshed Automated Product for Information and Data (IP RAPID) provides access to over 100 years of information on IP rights applications.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about a sequence number of a matched US equivalent with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say what the ordering is for.

value_domain: Total capital losses applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: All the losses the entity actually used against this year's gains, current year and carried forward together. It is a subtotal of the three loss columns beside it: "Add up the amounts at item 2 - labels B, C and D and write the total at label E Total capital losses applied." The old-form label reported the same figure by calculation method, so a series spanning the form change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 2 label E of the capital gains tax schedule, being the sum of current year losses applied, prior year net losses applied and the third loss component at label D.
limitation: It counts losses used, not losses held, so a firm sitting on large unused losses shows nothing here in a year with no gains to absorb them; the unused stock is in the carried-forward columns. Because losses are applied before the CGT discount, this figure cannot be compared directly with the discounted net gain.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 2 label E as the sum of the applied loss labels, which is the quantity this BLADE column carries under both label wordings.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at item 2 - labels B, C and D and write the total at label E Total capital losses applied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not separate losses used from losses held.

value_domain: Net capital losses carried forward, other than collectables (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4: Definitions
variable_description: The stock of unused capital losses the entity takes into future years, excluding the collectables losses that are carried forward separately. The ATO says of a net capital loss that "This loss can be carried forward and deducted from capital gains you make in later years. There is no time limit on how long you can carry forward a net capital loss." The old-form label called it unapplied net capital losses from all other CGT assets and CGT events, so a series spanning the form change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4: Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount at the other losses label of item 3 on the capital gains tax schedule, being a closing balance rather than a flow for the year.
limitation: It is a stock, so differencing it between two years does not give the loss made in the second year - losses applied against gains reduce it as well. Companies must also pass a continuity of ownership or business continuity test before using these losses, so a carried-forward balance is not a guarantee of a future deduction.
rationale: The ATO guide defines net capital losses and their indefinite carry forward, and the schedule instructions place the non-collectables balance at item 3 alongside the collectables balance.
evidence_quote: This loss can be carried forward and deducted from capital gains you make in later years. There is no time limit on how long you can carry forward a net capital loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say the column is a stock or that collectables sit outside it.

value_domain: Capital losses from collectables (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Losses the entity made on art, jewellery, coins and similar items in the year, kept in their own line because they are quarantined. The ATO states the rule plainly: "If you have capital losses from collectables, you can only apply those to your capital gains from collectables." Any part that cannot be used is carried forward in its own collectables balance at item 3, not in the general loss balance.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at the collectables loss label of item 1 on the capital gains tax schedule, reported as a positive figure in a loss column.
limitation: It cannot be netted against the entity's ordinary capital gains, so including it in a total loss figure overstates what was usable that year. Losses on personal use assets, which look similar, are disregarded entirely and never appear anywhere on the schedule.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define the collectables loss label, the quarantining rule and the separate carry-forward balance for unapplied collectables losses.
evidence_quote: If you have capital losses from collectables, you can only apply those to your capital gains from collectables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the new-form label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not state the quarantining rule.

value_domain: Current year capital losses applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: How much of this year's own capital losses the entity was able to use against this year's gains. It is the first deduction in the sequence, taken before carried-forward losses and before the CGT discount: the ATO describes prior year losses as applying to "current year capital gains remaining after you applied current year capital losses". The old-form label called it total current year capital losses applied, so a series spanning the form change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 2 label B of the capital gains tax schedule, being the used part of the current year loss total at label A.
limitation: The gap between this and total current year capital losses is the part that could not be used, so reading the applied figure alone overstates how well the year's losses were absorbed. The ordering also matters: because losses come off before the discount, a dollar of loss applied removes a full dollar of gain rather than a discounted one.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions set out the order in which current year and prior year losses are applied and place the applied current year figure at item 2 label B.
evidence_quote: In this part, you're calculating the amount of prior year net capital losses you can apply to reduce your entity's current year capital gains remaining after you applied current year capital losses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label text and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not place the column in the loss ordering.

value_domain: Total current year capital losses (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: All capital losses the entity made in the income year, before any of them are applied against gains. It is a sum of the loss categories on the item above: "Add up the amounts at item 1 - labels K to R and write the total at item 2 - label A Total current year capital losses." The old-form label abbreviated it as total current year capital losses (CYCL), so a series spanning the form change is not continuous.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 2 label A of the capital gains tax schedule, being the sum of the current year capital loss categories at item 1.
limitation: It measures losses made, not losses used, so a year of heavy disposals at a loss can leave the net capital gain unchanged if there were no gains to absorb them. Losses on personal use assets are excluded and disregarded entirely, so the total is not all the value the business lost on assets.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define item 2 label A as the sum of the item 1 loss labels, which is what this BLADE column carries under both label wordings.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at item 1 - labels K to R and write the total at item 2 - label A Total current year capital losses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: How much of the entity's accumulated losses from earlier years it used up against this year's gains. The ATO defines the stock being drawn down: "Prior year net capital losses are the unapplied net capital losses carried forward from earlier income years." Using them is not optional - "You can't choose to defer to a later income year any amount that can be applied" - so a nil value with gains present means there were no usable prior losses.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 2 label C of the capital gains tax schedule, reduced beforehand by any adjustment for commercial debts forgiven.
limitation: It shows the drawdown, not the balance, so it says nothing about how much loss remains; that is in the carried-forward columns at item 3. Companies can only deduct these losses if they pass a continuity of ownership or business continuity test, so a nil figure may reflect a failed test rather than an absence of losses.
rationale: The 2025 CGT schedule instructions define prior year net capital losses, the compulsory application rule, the commercial debt forgiveness adjustment and the company continuity tests.
evidence_quote: Prior year net capital losses are the unapplied net capital losses carried forward from earlier income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label text and the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that applying available prior losses is compulsory.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, other CGT assets and events (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital losses the business made during the year on CGT assets and events that fit none of the schedule's named asset categories. The ATO defines the category as a residual: "Other CGT assets refers to the capital gain or capital loss that you have made and that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule - such as the disposal of your forestry interests in a forestry managed investment scheme or hedging financial arrangements." What lands here therefore depends on what the shares, units, real estate and collectables labels beside it take out. The DIL label carries two wordings because the CGT schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, and the reading of those prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, one of the eight capital loss labels at item 1 of the CGT schedule that add to the total current year capital losses at item 2 label A. It is a gross loss, before any loss is applied against a gain.
limitation: A residual bucket cannot be read as a line of business, and it moves when the schedule redraws the named categories rather than when the firm changes what it holds. It also excludes losses on personal use assets, which the ATO tells lodgers to leave out of this label and disregard entirely, so a zero is not proof the firm sold nothing at a loss. A series spanning the form change is not continuous.
rationale: The DIL label names the current year capital loss for other CGT assets and any other CGT events, a defined label of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO definitions appendix gives the category its own wording and examples.
evidence_quote: Other CGT assets refers to the capital gain or capital loss that you have made and that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said the category is a residual or what falls out of it.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, real estate outside Australia (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital losses the business made during the year on land and buildings held outside Australia. The ATO is explicit about the boundary: "Other real estate on the CGT schedule refers to any real estate including land and buildings that are situated outside of Australia, for example, a rental property situated in the United States." The old form had a single Real estate label, which the new form split into this column and cl_rl_este_std_in_aus_amt, so before the change offshore and onshore property losses sit together and cannot be told apart. The DIL label carries two wordings because the CGT schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, and the reading of those prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, reported at the other real estate capital loss label of item 1 of the CGT schedule. Gross of any loss actually applied against a gain.
limitation: It cannot support a foreign property series across the form change, because the old form's single real estate label mixes Australian and overseas holdings. It is also a realised loss on a CGT event rather than a revaluation, so a firm whose overseas property fell in value shows nothing here until it disposes of it.
rationale: The DIL label names the current year capital loss for other real estate, a label of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO definitions appendix says what other real estate means on that schedule.
evidence_quote: Other real estate on the CGT schedule refers to any real estate including land and buildings that are situated outside of Australia, for example, a rental property situated in the United States.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that other real estate means offshore property or that the old label covered both.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, unlisted and foreign-listed shares (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital losses the business made during the year on shares that were not listed on an Australian securities exchange. The ATO defines the label as "shares that aren't listed on an Australian securities exchange, such as privately held shares or shares listed on a foreign securities exchange, but not also on an Australian securities exchange, for example, shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE)". The old form had one combined Shares and units (in unit trusts) label, which the new form split three ways across this column, cl_othr_unts_amt and cllistduntsinutasxamt. The DIL label carries two wordings because the CGT schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, and the reading of those prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, reported at the other shares capital loss label of item 1 of the CGT schedule, gross of any loss applied.
limitation: It is not a measure of private company investment: an unlisted domestic shareholding and a New York listing land in the same number. Before the schedule split, the same reported figure also covered units in unit trusts, so a shares-only series cannot be built across the form change.
rationale: The DIL label names the current year capital loss for other shares, a label of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO definitions appendix defines what other shares means for that schedule.
evidence_quote: Other shares on the CGT schedule are shares that aren't listed on an Australian securities exchange, such as privately held shares or shares listed on a foreign securities exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that the old label bundled shares with units.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, unlisted and foreign-listed trust units (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital losses the business made during the year on units in unit trusts that were not listed on an Australian securities exchange. The ATO defines these as "units in a unit trust that aren't listed on an Australian securities exchange, such as privately held units or units listed on a foreign securities exchange", and directs lodgers to put units in a private trust here rather than at the listed-units label. Family trusts and private equity trusts fall in this column, so a non-zero value often signals a related party structure rather than a traded investment. The DIL label carries two wordings because the CGT schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, and the reading of those prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, reported at the other units capital loss label of item 1 of the CGT schedule, gross of any loss applied against a gain.
limitation: Because unlisted units include family and private trusts, the figure often reflects an internal restructure priced between related parties rather than a market outcome, and nothing on the row flags which. The old form's combined shares-and-units label also means there is no comparable pre-split figure for units alone.
rationale: The DIL label names the current year capital loss for other units, a label of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO definitions appendix defines that label and says which trusts belong in it.
evidence_quote: Other units on the CGT schedule are units in a unit trust that aren't listed on an Australian securities exchange, such as privately held units or units listed on a foreign securities exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished unlisted units from the listed-units column beside it.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, Australian real estate (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: Capital losses the business made during the year on Australian land and buildings. The ATO defines the label plainly: "Real estate situated in Australia is any real property, including land and buildings, that is in Australia." It is the onshore half of the split the new form introduced, the offshore half being cl_othr_rl_este_amt, and under the old single Real estate label the two cannot be separated. The DIL label carries two wordings because the CGT schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, and the reading of those prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, reported at the real estate situated in Australia capital loss label of item 1 of the CGT schedule, before any loss is applied.
limitation: It records a loss only when a CGT event happens, so it is silent on a portfolio held through a downturn and never sold. It also misses property losses that run through the capital allowance balancing adjustment rules for depreciating assets, which are handled outside the CGT provisions.
rationale: The DIL label names the current year capital loss for real estate situated in Australia, a label of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO definitions appendix defines that phrase.
evidence_quote: Real estate situated in Australia is any real property, including land and buildings, that is in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing marked the onshore and offshore split or the break at the form change.

value_domain: Transferred-in net capital losses applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
variable_description: Net capital losses another company in the same wholly owned group handed to this entity and that it used against its own capital gains this year. Transfers run under Subdivision 170-B of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, and the ATO limits how much can be used: "You need to apply the net capital losses transferred into your entity in the order they were received. Your entity must have enough capital gains to absorb the net capital losses transferred in." A non-zero value therefore marks the entity as part of a corporate group and marks the loss as someone else's. The DIL label carries two wordings because the CGT schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, and the reading of those prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025
value_definition: A dollar amount reported at item 2 of the CGT schedule, alongside the current year and prior year losses applied, the three of which add to total capital losses applied.
limitation: It counts losses used, not losses transferred, so a group that shifted more losses than the receiving entity had gains to absorb shows only the absorbed part. It also cannot identify the transferring company, so it supports no measure of group loss flows. Only companies can transfer losses this way, so trusts and funds are structurally zero here rather than merely empty.
rationale: The DIL label names capital losses transferred in applied, a defined step of the ATO CGT schedule, and the schedule instructions set out the wholly owned group conditions and the ordering and absorption rule for applying transferred losses.
evidence_quote: You need to apply the net capital losses transferred into your entity in the order they were received. Your entity must have enough capital gains to absorb the net capital losses transferred in.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the losses came from a related company or that only absorbed amounts appear.

value_domain: IP classification symbol; the system depends on classification_system and ip_right_type - IPC or CPC symbol (patents), Nice class number (trade marks), Australian Locarno-based design class (designs), UPOV code or genus / genus-species name (plant breeder's rights)

Which scheme the symbol belongs to is set by classification_system and ip_right_type on the same row: an IPC or CPC symbol for a patent, a Nice class number for a trade mark, an Australian Locarno-based class for a design, and a UPOV code or genus name for a plant breeder's right. classification_date and classification_removal_date bound the period the symbol applied, and c_is_current marks the symbols in force at the extract. classification_area holds the simplified reading of the same value.

value_definition: A string whose shape follows the scheme it comes from, with no single fixed width: an IPC or CPC symbol such as A61K 31/00 for patents, a one- or two-digit Nice class number for trade marks, a Locarno-based class number for designs, and a UPOV code or a genus or genus-species name for plant breeder's rights. The full symbol list is published by WIPO and IP Australia and is not listed here.

Reclassification rewrites the value as schemes are revised, so the symbol on the row is the one that applies now rather than the one assigned at filing. A patent carried in both IPC and CPC also appears twice with different symbols, so counting distinct values here counts schemes as well as subjects.
rationale: The column holds the classification symbol itself, drawn from whichever system the sibling classification_type names (IPC and CPC for patents, Nice for trade marks, Locarno for designs, UPOV and botanical names for plant breeder's rights). The sample keeps the bare symbols: a 'system: symbol' rendering would be read as code-and-label and emit the system name into the column.

evidence_quote: The headcount amount is worked out on a daily basis for the JobMaker period and has been designed to ensure that the scheme recognises periods of partial employment during the period
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Low rate days claimed in period 8' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said a day is an employment day rather than a full-time equivalent.

value_domain: Count of eligible additional employees at the lower JobMaker rate
value_source: Treasury, JobMaker Hiring Credit rules, exposure draft explanatory material
variable_description: Lower-rate eligible additional employees counted in the eighth JobMaker period, 7 July 2022 to 6 October 2022. The relatives rule keeps family hires out of it: an entity "cannot claim an amount of the JobMaker Hiring Credit payment in relation to a person who is related to the entity even if the employee would otherwise meet all other eligibility requirements". It is the final count in the series, at the $100 a week rate.
description_source: Treasury, JobMaker Hiring Credit rules, exposure draft explanatory material
value_definition: A whole count of people claimed for at the lower rate in period 8, the band set by age at the start of employment.
limitation: For a family business the count can be zero while the firm did hire in the 30 to 35 band, because related employees are excluded on a look-through basis regardless of how the ownership is structured.
rationale: The explanatory material sets out the relatives exclusion and its look-through operation, which is the specific reason this count can understate hiring in owner-managed firms.
evidence_quote: This provides that a qualifying entity cannot claim an amount of the JobMaker Hiring Credit payment in relation to a person who is related to the entity even if the employee would otherwise meet all other eligibility requirements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Low rate employees period 8' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said family hires are excluded by design.

value_domain: Total payroll for a JobMaker period (dollars)
value_source: Treasury, JobMaker Hiring Credit rules, exposure draft explanatory material
variable_description: Payroll reported for the eighth JobMaker period, 7 July 2022 to 6 October 2022, the last quarter of the scheme. Treasury expected the ATO to derive most of these figures automatically, noting that the calculations "only rely on inputs relating to start and cessation times, the age of eligible employees at the time they commenced employment, the entity's baseline headcount and payroll on 30 September 2020 and the entity's headcount and payroll at the end of the period", which in practice means Single Touch Payroll reporting. Its excess over the baseline caps the final entitlement.
description_source: Treasury, JobMaker Hiring Credit rules, exposure draft explanatory material
value_definition: A dollar amount for the final claim period, summed over pay cycles ending in it, on the JobKeeper wage-condition definition of payroll.
limitation: It is a claim-time figure for one quarter and does not chain with the earlier periods into an annual wage bill, because consecutive periods can contain different numbers of pay cycles and the scheme's coverage of a firm can start or stop mid-year.
rationale: The Treasury explanatory material identifies the inputs behind the payroll calculation and the automated derivation the ATO was expected to use.
evidence_quote: This is possible because the calculations only rely on inputs relating to start and cessation times, the age of eligible employees at the time they commenced employment, the entity's baseline headcount and payroll on 30 September 2020 and the entity's headcount and payroll at the end of the period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Payroll amount for period - period 8' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said where the number comes from or why quarters do not chain.

value_domain: Current year capital loss on shares, CGT schedule (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The capital loss the business made during the year on share disposals, taken from the first asset line of its capital gains tax schedule. The DIL carries two wordings because the schedule changed: OF is the old form's 'Current year capital losses - Shares and units (in unit trusts)', which the ATO guide describes as losses from "shares and units (in unit trusts) at A", and NF is the new form's narrower 'Capital loss - Shares in companies listed on an Australian securities exchange'. The old label bundled trust units in with shares; the new one keeps listed shares on their own.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount of current year capital losses for one asset class, entered gross before losses are applied against any gain and before earlier-year losses are brought in.
limitation: A series that crosses the form change is not continuous, because the old column includes unit trust holdings and unlisted shares that the new column sends to other labels. The figure is also a loss made, not a loss used: whether it reduced tax depends on the gains and concessions recorded elsewhere on the schedule.
rationale: The ATO capital gains tax guide sets out the current year capital losses part of the CGT schedule and names the shares and units asset line that the old-form label reproduces, which is what identifies the quantity and its place in the calculation.
evidence_quote: shares and units (in unit trusts) at A
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the two labels cover different asset sets.

value_domain: Australian Company Number, deidentified
value_source: ASIC, Australian Company Numbers
variable_description: The company the row is about, held as a deidentified version of its ASIC company number. It is the key that lets company-level sources be joined to the ABN-based BLADE spine. ASIC states that "An ACN is a unique 9-digit number that identifies a company" and issues one to every company at registration. The CN to BN key table pairs it with the business number, so the variable is a bridge rather than a business characteristic.
description_source: ASIC, Australian Company Numbers
value_definition: A deidentified identifier standing for one ACN, released in BLADE as a ten-character alphanumeric string rather than as the nine-digit number ASIC issues. It carries no information about the company beyond identity.
limitation: Only incorporated entities have one, so sole traders, partnerships and most trusts appear in BLADE with no value here and cannot be reached through any ASIC-sourced module. A company that is deregistered and later re-registered receives a new ACN, which breaks the link across that gap even though the business may be continuous.
rationale: ASIC is the issuer of the ACN and its page defines the identifier, its length and when it is allocated, which is what the deidentified key stands for.
evidence_quote: An ACN is a unique 9-digit number that identifies a company. ASIC issues every company with an ACN when it is registered.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Identifier - deidentified ACN (Australian Company Number)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which entities have one or why the key table exists.

value_domain: ABS data integration version reference
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Which run of the ABS integration produced this company-to-business link, written as a short internal reference such as in164_v1. It describes the vintage of the key, not the company: two rows with different versions were built by different integration passes and may resolve the same company differently. Use it to check that a join is drawn from one consistent build.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric ABS reference of the form in{number}_v{number}, an administrative label with no business meaning and no published register of values.
limitation: It says nothing about the quality of the link it stamps, so a change of version is not evidence that a match improved. Mixing versions in one analysis can double count a company or drop it, and the column cannot tell you which version is current in your extract.
rationale: No published document defines this column; the reading rests on the DIL wording naming it an internal ABS integration reference and on the ABS BLADE page describing BLADE as an integrated asset built from linked administrative sources.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the column is vintage metadata rather than data about a business.

value_domain: WIPO technology sector or Nice goods and services grouping
value_source: WIPO, Mapping Innovations: Patents and the Sustainable Development Goals
variable_description: The broad subject area of the intellectual property right, one level up from the detailed classification codes. For patents the values follow the WIPO technology sectors: WIPO's concordance "comprises 35 technology fields, grouped into five higher level technology sectors, namely, Electrical engineering, Instruments, Chemistry, Mechanical engineering, and Other fields". For trade marks the values instead say whether the mark covers goods, services or both, which is the top-level split of the Nice classification used for registering marks.
description_source: WIPO, Mapping Innovations: Patents and the Sustainable Development Goals
value_definition: A short lower-case text code from a fixed list covering the five WIPO technology sectors, the goods and services groupings for trade marks, and 'unknown' as a residual where no area could be assigned.
limitation: The two halves of the list are not comparable: a patent sector describes the technology of an invention, while goods or services describes the market a mark is registered in, so counting across the whole column mixes two different classifications. A patent spanning several IPC codes is assigned one sector, which hides multi-technology inventions.
rationale: The five patent values in the domain match the WIPO technology sectors exactly, and the WIPO publication defines those sectors and their basis in the International Patent Classification; the goods and services values match the Nice classification split for trade marks.
evidence_quote: The WIPO PCT system comprises 35 technology fields, grouped into five higher level technology sectors, namely, Electrical engineering, Instruments, Chemistry, Mechanical engineering, and Other fields.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording about a higher level of classification with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the codes come from two different classifications, one for patents and one for trade marks.

value_domain: Date an enterprise agreement starts operating (dd/mm/yyyy)
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Terms and dates to put in an agreement
variable_description: The day the enterprise agreement began to operate over the employer's workforce, a date set by law rather than chosen freely. The Fair Work Commission states the rule: "An agreement starts 7 days after the Commission approves it. You may choose a later start date and ask us to approve it." For a business in BLADE it marks when the agreement's wages and conditions took effect, so it is the date from which the other Workplace Agreements Database flags on the row describe the workplace. It is not the date bargaining began or the date employees voted.
description_source: Fair Work Commission, Terms and dates to put in an agreement
value_definition: A calendar date written dd/mm/yyyy, on or after the Fair Work Commission's approval date and typically seven days later.
limitation: Commencement does not bound the agreement's life at the other end: the nominal expiry date can be up to four years later and, in the Commission's words, "The agreement does not end on that date. It continues to operate after the nominal expiry date." So a firm can still be covered by an agreement that commenced many years earlier and never appears in later bargaining rounds.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission states the statutory rule for when an approved agreement starts operating and the separate treatment of nominal expiry, which is exactly what this date does and does not mark.
evidence_quote: An agreement starts 7 days after the Commission approves it. You may choose a later start date and ask us to approve it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'The date the agreement commences operating' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the date is fixed by the approval rule or how it relates to expiry.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y where present)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement covering this employer commits the parties to discuss major workplace change before it is put in place. It is one of the conditions items DEWR codes from the text of each federal agreement, a database that holds "conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997". The DIL notes it is only coded for agreements made before 1 January 2010, when a consultation term became mandatory under the Fair Work Act and the item stopped distinguishing agreements.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-character flag taking Y where the provision was found in the agreement text. There is no explicit N: an agreement without the provision, or from a year in which the item was not coded, is simply blank.
limitation: After 2009 a blank is uninformative, because the item was retired rather than answered in the negative, so a fall in coverage across 2010 is an artefact of coding practice. The flag also records what the agreement says, not whether consultation ever happened at the workplace.
rationale: DEWR describes the database as conditions information coded for federal enterprise agreements approved since 1997, and warns that conditions items are reviewed annually so they do not all span the full series, which is the pattern the pre-2010 coding note reflects.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about a provision committing parties to discussing major change with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never explained what a blank means after 2009.

value_domain: Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC), 8-digit statistical code
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018 (cat. 5489.0), Data downloads workbook 5489_2026.xlsx, Appendix 6.1 AHECC historical correspondence
variable_description: The AHECC code for the goods on this export line, which is the column that says what was actually shipped. ABS describes the AHECC as "the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia", built as an Australian extension of the World Customs Organization's Harmonized System. The first six digits are the HS subheading and are internationally comparable; the last two are an ABS statistical code and are not. sitc_item_code_ex and anzsic_06_class_code on the same row are both derived from this value, so they add a different arrangement of the same fact rather than new information about the good.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC), 2022
value_definition: An 8-digit AHECC code: HS chapter, heading and subheading in the first six digits, and an ABS statistical code in the last two. The edition in force moves with the Harmonized System revision cycle, most recently AHECC 2022. The full code list is published in the AHECC itself and is not listed here.
limitation: It is not the import classification, and ABS warns that the Working Tariff and the AHECC are not interchangeable, so an export code cannot be matched to commodity_code_im below the shared six-digit HS subheading. It is also unstable as a time series: each Harmonized System revision creates, merges and deletes codes, so a code counted either side of the 2012, 2017 or 2022 changeover need not cover the same goods, and a long run has to be built through the correspondence tables rather than on the code itself.
rationale: The BLADE Data Item List points at 'CSM - Data Downloads (Appendices, Appendix 6.1 column AHECC)'; that appendix is a sheet of this ABS workbook and holds every AHECC code ever operative with its free-standing descriptor. Sample of 26 drawn at random from the 6134 currently operative codes (12055 ever operative).
evidence_quote: AHECC: The 8 digit code
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review could not follow the Data Item List's pointer to an external appendix. The appendix is a downloadable ABS workbook, not a paywalled or unpublished document.

value_domain: Combined Australian Customs Tariff Nomenclature and Statistical Classification (Working Tariff), 10-digit Harmonized Tariff Item Statistical Code (HTISC)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018 (cat. 5489.0), Data downloads workbook 5489_2026.xlsx, Appendix 6.2 Customs tariff historical correspondence
variable_description: The Customs Tariff code for the goods on this import line, the classification that decides what rate of duty was payable. ABS records that "since 1 January 1988, all goods requiring a full customs declaration for import into Australia are classified according to the ten-digit Harmonized Tariff Item Statistical Code (HTISC) of the Customs Tariff". The first six digits are the HS subheading, the next two complete the Australian tariff item that carries the rate, and the last two are an ABS statistical code. sitc_item_code_im, bec_group_code_im and anzsic_06_class_code are all assigned from this value.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Classifications
value_definition: A 10-digit HTISC from the Combined Australian Customs Tariff Nomenclature and Statistical Classification, the Working Tariff. The edition follows the Harmonized System revision cycle, so which code was valid depends on the reference period of the row. The full item list is published in the Working Tariff and is not listed here.
limitation: The tariff item is a legal classification chosen by the declarant and contestable with Home Affairs, so two importers can enter the same product under different items where the boundary is arguable, and later amendment does not always flow back into the statistics. It also cannot be joined to the export commodity code below the six-digit HS subheading, because the Working Tariff and the AHECC extend the Harmonized System in different directions, and it says nothing about the rate actually paid, which depends on preference_code_im and treatment_code_im.
rationale: The Data Item List points at 'Appendix 6.2 column HTISC'; that sheet lists every 10-digit HTISC ever operative with its free-standing descriptor. The first 8 digits are the Home Affairs tariff item, the last 2 are ABS statistical digits. Sample of 26 drawn at random from the 8327 currently operative codes (22273 ever operative).
evidence_quote: HTISC: The 10 digit code
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review treated the appendix reference as unresolvable. It resolves to a public ABS workbook sheet holding the full code list.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement sector flag (Y where a Commonwealth Public Service agreement)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement is a Commonwealth Public Service agreement, which marks the employer as a Commonwealth government agency. Such an employer bargains under central government policy rather than as a private firm. It sits alongside the database's other general details, which DEWR lists as including "Workplace Sector (public or private)", industry division, duration, employees covered and unions covered. For an analyst it is the cleanest way to hold Commonwealth employers apart from the market sector when using WAD variables in BLADE.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-character flag taking Y for Commonwealth Public Service agreements, with no explicit code for everything else.
limitation: It is not a general public sector marker: state and local government employers, universities and Commonwealth bodies outside the Australian Public Service are not flagged here even though they are public employers. Reading a blank as private sector will therefore misclassify a large part of public employment.
rationale: DEWR describes the WAD's general agreement details, including a public or private workplace sector item, which situates this narrower Commonwealth Public Service flag among them.
evidence_quote: This includes general details, such as: Workplace Sector (public or private)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about indicating a Commonwealth Public Service agreement with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that it is narrower than a public sector flag.

value_domain: Business operating status, Dealroom categories
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: What became of the business according to Dealroom's company records: operational, low-activity, acquired or closed. The DIL states the value is time-invariant and copied across every observation of the ABN, so it is an outcome label attached to the firm's whole history rather than a status observed in each year. Treat it as an end-state marker for survival and exit work, not as a yearly status variable.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A short categorical label from Dealroom's own status list, constant within an ABN across all years in which the business appears.
limitation: Because the label is carried backwards over the whole panel, it cannot date an acquisition or a closure, and using it as a right-hand-side variable in a yearly model leaks the future into the past. Dealroom's coverage is also selective, tilted towards start-ups and investor-tracked firms, so most Australian businesses have no status at all.
rationale: No public Dealroom data dictionary for the BLADE module was reachable; the reading rests on the DIL's own statement that the variable is time-invariant and filled over all observations of an ABN, and on the ABS listing Dealroom as a BLADE module.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence describing a categorical status with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing flagged that a time-invariant label copied over all years cannot date an exit.

value_domain: R&D Tax Incentive application answer (Yes, No, N/A)
value_source: business.gov.au, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: Whether the company registering R&D activities sits under a parent that controls it, answered by the company on its own registration form. The guidance defines the term: "A company is an Ultimate Holding company if it has majority ownership of or controlling interests in the R&D company or other companies in the consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group which are connected or affiliated with the R&D company", and it may be incorporated outside Australia. A Yes marks the R&D claimant as part of a wider group rather than a standalone business.
description_source: business.gov.au, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A categorical answer of Yes, No or N/A, taken from a radio button on the registration form for one income year's R&D activities.
limitation: It identifies the existence of a parent, not the parent itself: the ABN or the name of the holding company is asked in separate questions and a foreign parent has no Australian identifier, so this column cannot on its own build a corporate group structure. It is also the applicant's own answer at registration and is not reconciled against ASIC records.
rationale: The published question set for the R&D Tax Incentive registration form contains this exact question and its guidance, which is the form the BLADE RDTI module is built from.
evidence_quote: A company is an Ultimate Holding company if it has majority ownership of or controlling interests in the R&D company or other companies in the consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group which are connected or affiliated with the R&D company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording 'If the company have an Ultimate Holding Company' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing defined the term or said the answer is self-reported on the registration form.

value_domain: R&D Tax Incentive application answer (Yes, No, N/A)
value_source: business.gov.au, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: Whether tax exempt entities control the company registering R&D activities, which decides which offset it can claim. The guidance is direct about the consequence: "If the company is controlled by one or more exempt entities, it cannot claim the refundable offset, but it can claim the non-refundable tax offset instead." Control is tested at 50 per cent, through shares giving at least half the voting power or the right to at least half of distributed income or capital.
description_source: business.gov.au, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A categorical answer of Yes, No or N/A from a radio button on the registration form. A companion question on the form records the percentage of control held by exempt entities where the answer is Yes.
limitation: A Yes does not mean the company received no benefit, only that the benefit could not be a cash refund, so this column marks the form of the offset rather than its size or its success. It also cannot identify which exempt entity is involved, and it is self-assessed by the applicant rather than verified.
rationale: The published R&D Tax Incentive registration question set contains this question, the 50 per cent control test behind it and the offset consequence, which is what the column records.
evidence_quote: If the company is controlled by one or more exempt entities, it cannot claim the refundable offset, but it can claim the non-refundable tax offset instead.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording about control by tax exempt entities with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said why the question is asked or what turns on the answer.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y where present)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement ties pay progression to attaining a competency level in a training structure, usually an industry certificate, rather than to time served. It is one of the training-related conditions DEWR codes from agreement text, sitting in the group of items the department lists as covering training, penalty rates, redundancy, superannuation and leave. For a business in BLADE it is a marker of a formal skills-linked wage structure, useful beside the firm's own training and R&D activity.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-character flag taking Y where the agreement contains such a provision, blank otherwise. The unit is the agreement, not the employee or the workplace.
limitation: A clause is not an outcome: nothing here says any employee attained a competency, moved up a level, or was paid more as a result. Where a business is covered by several agreements the flags describe each agreement separately, so a firm can appear both with and without the provision.
rationale: DEWR describes the conditions items recorded for each agreement, including training provisions, and states that around 200 data items are coded per agreement, which is the collection this flag belongs to.
evidence_quote: The database also records details about conditions of employment contained within enterprise agreements, such as: Individual flexibility arrangements Redundancy provisions Superannuation Leave entitlements Training
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's long description of the provision with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the flag is about agreement text rather than about what employees were paid.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y where present)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement provides a bonus that depends on something happening, such as employees moving to a new classification structure or accepting new technology. It is coded from the agreement text by DEWR, whose database holds "wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991". The dollar value, where the agreement states one, is carried by conditionalbonusamount on the same row.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-character flag taking Y where a conditional bonus provision was found, blank otherwise, recorded once for the agreement.
limitation: The flag cannot tell you whether the condition was met or the bonus paid, and it does not separate a one-off transition payment from a recurring performance bonus. A firm with a productivity bonus outside the agreement, or paid at management discretion, shows nothing here.
rationale: DEWR's description of the WAD establishes that wage provisions in federal enterprise agreements are coded item by item from the agreement text, which is what this flag is.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's example-laden description with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the flag records a clause rather than a payment.

value_domain: Conditional bonus amount stated in an enterprise agreement (dollars)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The flat dollar figure a conditional bonus is worth under the agreement, where the agreement names one. It qualifies the conditionalbonus flag on the same row: the flag says a conditional bonus exists, this column says how much per employee. DEWR's coding uses 111111111 to mean the amount varies or is not known, which is a sentinel rather than a payment.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A dollar amount per covered employee as written in the agreement, with the single reserved code 111111111 standing for a varying or unknown quantity.
limitation: Leaving the sentinel in an average will inflate it by orders of magnitude, and dropping it silently discards the agreements with the most complex bonus arrangements. The amount is also as written when the agreement was made, never indexed, so figures from agreements a decade apart are not comparable in real terms.
rationale: The DIL gives the reserved code and its meaning, and DEWR's description of the database establishes that wage provisions are coded from the text of each federal agreement.
evidence_quote: There are over 180,000 agreements in the database. An average of 6,000 agreements are added each year, and around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording about a flat dollar amount with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that 111111111 is a sentinel and not a value.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y where present)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement limits the employer's use of contractors. The restriction can cap contractor numbers against permanent staff, or limit how long or how many hours a contractor may be engaged. It is a bargaining outcome that bears directly on how a business can organise labour, and pairs naturally with the firm's contractor payments and payroll columns elsewhere in BLADE. The DIL warns that the item was not coded in 2007 or 2008.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-character flag taking Y where such a restriction was found in the agreement, blank where it was not found or not coded that year.
limitation: The two uncoded years create a hole rather than a run of negatives, so a time series built from this column will show a false trough in 2007 and 2008. The flag also mixes weak and strong restrictions: a clause requiring consultation before engaging contractors is coded the same as a hard cap.
rationale: DEWR states that the conditions collected are reviewed annually so not all fields span the full series, which is what the DIL's note about 2007 and 2008 reflects for this item.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL description of contractor restrictions with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the gap in the two uncoded years.

value_domain: Metal content of an exported ore shipment (per cent)
value_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
variable_description: The copper grade of an exported ore or concentrate shipment, that is the share of the gross tonnage that is copper metal. It qualifies the quantity and value on the same export line, because a tonne of high-grade concentrate and a tonne of low-grade ore are very different products under the same AHECC heading. For a mining business it separates volume shipped from metal actually sold.
description_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
value_definition: A percentage between zero and one hundred attached to an export line classified under the AHECC, which the ABS describes as "the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia".
limitation: It applies only to copper-bearing ore and concentrate lines, so it is blank for every other export the business makes and cannot be averaged over a firm's shipments as a whole. Nothing here is the payable metal content used in the sale contract, which is settled after assay and after smelter deductions.
rationale: The ABS AHECC page establishes the export classification the column sits beside, but no reachable publication documents this content percentage field, so the business meaning is inferred from the export declaration context.
evidence_quote: The Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC) is the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Percentage of copper in shipment of ore' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which export lines carry it or how it relates to the tonnage on the same row.

value_domain: Two-letter country code for intellectual property filing activity
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The country associated with the business's intellectual property filing activity, held as the two-letter code used across IP office records. Because a firm's filings can be recorded from different locations over time, the DIL states that IPLORD assigns the modal country code for each deidentified ABN where the source records conflict. The value is therefore one country per business, not one per filing.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A two-character alphabetic code of the kind used by intellectual property offices for states and organisations, essentially the ISO two-letter country codes, with no numeric or long-form variant in this column.
limitation: Taking the mode hides the movement it was meant to smooth, so a firm that shifted its filing activity offshore looks as though it never moved. The code describes where filing activity was recorded, not where the business trades, is owned or does its research.
rationale: No fetchable IPLORD data dictionary was available; the reading rests on the DIL's own statement about modal assignment per deidentified ABN and on the ABS listing IPLORD as an intellectual property module of BLADE.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's long note about modal assignment with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a reader loses by having one country for a firm's whole history.

value_domain: ABS merchandise trade country classification, export destination
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018
variable_description: Where the business said its exported goods were going, coded to the ABS merchandise trade country classification. The ABS defines the concept as "the last country, as far as it is known at the time of exportation, to which goods are to be delivered", reported by the exporter on the declaration to the Department of Home Affairs. It is a shipment attribute, so a single exporter's rows will carry many different values across the year.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018
value_definition: A numeric country code from the classification listed in the BLADE data item appendix, derived from the UN location code the exporter reports and published alongside the country titles of the Standard Australian Classification of Countries.
limitation: Final destination is not the country of consumption. Goods routed through a trading or transhipment hub are recorded against the last country known at export, so Australian sales into a market can be attributed to Singapore, Hong Kong or the Netherlands instead of the buyer's country.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods publication defines country of final destination for exports, states how it is reported and explains the classification used, which is the column's content and its main pitfall.
evidence_quote: the last country, as far as it is known at the time of exportation, to which goods are to be delivered
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Country of final destination' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never warned that the destination is the last known one rather than the market of consumption.

value_domain: ABS merchandise trade country classification, import origin
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018
variable_description: Where the goods the business imported were made, coded to the ABS merchandise trade country classification. The ABS applies customs rules of origin, under which goods originate in a country if they were "wholly manufactured in the country or if partly manufactured, the last process in the manufacture of the goods was performed in the country". It is a production concept, not the country the business bought from or shipped through.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018
value_definition: A numeric country code from the classification listed in the BLADE data item appendix, converted from the UN location code the importer reports to the Department of Home Affairs.
limitation: It cannot identify the firm's supplier or the country money was paid to: an import assembled in one country from components made elsewhere carries only the last-process country, which is why import origin and export destination do not net out into bilateral trade relationships at the firm level.
rationale: The ABS methodology publication states that imports are classified by country of origin under Australian customs rules of origin and describes how the code is reported and converted.
evidence_quote: wholly manufactured in the country or if partly manufactured, the last process in the manufacture of the goods was performed in the country
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Country of origin' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the country of manufacture from the country the business bought from.

value_domain: GST on purchases reported on the business activity statement (dollars)
value_source: business.gov.au, Register for goods and services tax (GST)
variable_description: The GST included in the price of what the business bought during the period, claimed back on its activity statement at the GST on purchases label. As business.gov.au puts it, "If you're registered for GST, you can generally claim back any GST included in the price of things you've bought for your business." Read against GST on sales on the same statement it gives the firm's net GST position, and "If, for any tax period, your GST credits are higher than the amount of GST your business has to pay the ATO, you could get a refund."
description_source: business.gov.au, Register for goods and services tax (GST)
value_definition: A dollar amount for one activity statement period, monthly, quarterly or annual depending on the business, covering GST credits claimed on creditable purchases and importations.
limitation: It is roughly one eleventh of taxable purchases, not purchases themselves, and it silently excludes everything bought GST-free or input taxed, so scaling it up to estimate business expenses understates firms buying fresh food, medical supplies or financial services. Businesses below the $75,000 registration turnover threshold need not be registered at all and can be absent from the series entirely.
rationale: The government's own business guidance defines GST credits for purchases, the refund position and the registration threshold, which fixes what this activity statement label holds and who reports it.
evidence_quote: If you're registered for GST, you can generally claim back any GST included in the price of things you've bought for your business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL label 'Goods and services tax (GST) on purchases' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is a tax credit rather than a purchase total.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade provided this business with a business matching service, that is help pairing it with a potential overseas partner or buyer. It is one of several client service counts on the MAX panel row, each covering a different service type, so the row describes the intensity and mix of the assistance a firm received. Austrade describes the underlying work as helping businesses "assess market potential, develop export strategies, find valuable contacts overseas".
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of service events in one financial year, recorded by Austrade's client management system rather than reported by the business.
limitation: It counts contacts, not results: a match that led to nothing counts the same as one that opened a market. Because it is a count of one agency's activity, a zero can mean the firm exported successfully without ever being an Austrade client, so it must not be read as a measure of export support received.
rationale: Austrade's own description of its services to exporters supports the general nature of the count, but no published document defines this service type or how instances are counted, so the reading is inferred from the DIL wording.
evidence_quote: assess market potential, develop export strategies, find valuable contacts overseas
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about the number of times the entity received a business matching service with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said a zero mostly means not a client.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
variable_description: How many times in the financial year the business received export guidance from Austrade. That is the advisory service which helps a firm work out how to sell into a foreign market. Austrade publishes the same material openly as "export guides for Australian businesses" alongside information on "laws and regulations in your target markets", so the counted service is the tailored version of that advice. Beside the other client service counts on the row it shows how far the firm's engagement went past general advice.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of guidance events in one financial year, held at the business level and drawn from Austrade's client records.
limitation: Guidance is the lightest touch Austrade offers, so a high count here with nothing in the other service columns marks a firm that asked questions rather than one that was actively taken to market. State government and TradeStart assistance is outside the count altogether.
rationale: Austrade's page for Australian exporters describes the export guidance it provides, which is the service type this column counts, though the counting rule itself is not published.
evidence_quote: export guides for Australian businesses
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about the number of times the entity received export guidance with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing placed the service among Austrade's offerings.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade introduced the business to a specific overseas contact. Austrade names this among its core services for exporters, helping eligible businesses "find valuable contacts overseas" through advisers in Australia and in its international posts. It is the most concrete of the client service counts, since an introduction names a counterparty rather than offering advice.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of introduction events in one financial year, recorded against the business in Austrade's client records.
limitation: An introduction is an input, not a contract: nothing in the column says whether the contact responded, whether a sale followed, or which market the contact was in. Repeated introductions to the same partner count separately.
rationale: Austrade's exporter services page names finding overseas contacts as one of its services, which is the activity this column counts, although the internal service taxonomy is not published.
evidence_quote: find valuable contacts overseas
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about the number of times the entity received introductions with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said an introduction is an input rather than an outcome.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
variable_description: How many times in the financial year the business took part in an Austrade in-market experience. These are the hands-on services: a market visit, a trade mission or an in-country programme. It sits with the other client service counts on the MAX panel row and is the type that usually implies the firm spent money and travelled, not just took advice. Austrade frames all of these as help to "expand in overseas markets".
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of in-market service events in one financial year, from Austrade's client records rather than a business return.
limitation: The service label is Austrade's own and its scope has changed with programme design, so counts are not necessarily comparable across years even for the same firm. Nothing in the column identifies the market visited or what the firm spent to attend.
rationale: Austrade's exporter services page supports the general shape of client services, but the market experience service type is not defined in any reachable publication, so the reading is inferred from the DIL wording and the sibling columns.
evidence_quote: help Australian businesses expand in overseas markets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about the number of times the entity received a market experiences service with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what kind of activity that covers.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade supplied the business with market research, the service that helps a firm judge whether a foreign market is worth entering. Austrade lists exactly this work among its services, helping eligible businesses "assess market potential", and publishes "trusted market intelligence, freight, and logistics updates" more broadly. A count here with none in the introductions column suggests a firm still deciding rather than one already selling.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of research service events in one financial year, held at the business level in Austrade's client records.
limitation: The count treats a short data request and a commissioned market study alike, so it measures frequency of contact rather than the depth or cost of the research. Research a firm bought privately or obtained from an industry body is invisible.
rationale: Austrade's exporter services page names market potential assessment and market intelligence among the services it provides, which is the service type this column counts.
evidence_quote: assess market potential
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence about the number of times the entity received market research with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a light data request from a full study.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in the financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade recorded a market-selection service for this business, meaning help deciding which overseas markets to pursue. Austrade describes this work as helping businesses "assess market potential" and "develop export strategies". It is a count of recorded service events rather than hours or dollars, and it sits beside three sibling counts for practical assistance, profile support and troubleshooting.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
value_definition: A non-negative integer tally over one financial year, with no upper bound and no code list. The four client-service counts on the row are separate tallies and can all be non-zero in the same year.
limitation: It cannot measure how much help the business received: a year-long market entry programme and a single advisory call each add one. The MAX panel covers businesses Austrade dealt with, so a zero or an absent row confounds "received no service of this type" with "was never an Austrade client".
rationale: The Austrade services page confirms the agency runs market assessment and export strategy services for Australian businesses, which is the activity the DIL label names; Austrade's internal service taxonomy is not published, so the mapping of the label to a specific service line is inferred.
evidence_quote: Austrade's trade services help Australian businesses expand in overseas markets. We help eligible businesses: assess market potential develop export strategies find valuable contacts overseas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what an Austrade client service event is or why a zero is ambiguous.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in the financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade gave this business hands-on assistance with an export transaction, as distinct from advice about which market to enter. Austrade delivers this through in-market advisers who "find valuable contacts overseas" and through its Go Global Toolkit and Trade Resilience Service. The count rises with the number of separate engagements, so a firm running several deals in one year scores higher than a firm with one large deal.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
