value_definition: A non-negative integer tally over one financial year. There is no published code list and no ceiling; the value is a service-event count, not a dollar value of assistance.
limitation: It does not say what was done or whether it worked. Practical assistance and market selection are recorded separately even when they happen in the same conversation, so the four counts should not be added together as a measure of total engagement without knowing Austrade's recording rules.
rationale: The Austrade services page confirms the agency provides direct in-market help to exporters beyond market research, which is the activity this label names; the internal service-type taxonomy behind the column is not published.
evidence_quote: We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who deliver our services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished this count from the three other client service counts on the same row.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in the financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade raised this business's profile overseas, through promotion, missions, events or awards. Austrade's promotional vehicles include the Australian Export Awards and the Australia Southeast Asia Business Exchange programme of missions. A high count marks a firm Austrade put in front of buyers, which is a different thing from a firm Austrade advised.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
value_definition: A non-negative integer tally over one financial year, with no published code list. It counts occasions of profile support, not the audience reached or the money spent.
limitation: Profile support is largely supply driven: Austrade decides who goes on a mission or into a showcase, so a high count reflects selection by the agency as much as demand from the firm. Treating it as a measure of the firm's own marketing effort would reverse the causality.
rationale: The Austrade services page names the promotional programmes (Export Awards, business exchange missions) that this service type would record, but Austrade does not publish the client-service classification that produced the column.
evidence_quote: Austrade's Australian Export Awards celebrate outstanding Australian exporters with entries from all over Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said how profile support differs from the other service counts.

value_domain: Count of Austrade client service events in the financial year
value_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
variable_description: How many times in the financial year Austrade stepped in to fix a problem the business hit in an overseas market. Austrade runs a Trade Resilience Service that provides "market intelligence, freight, and logistics updates to help keep your exports moving", which is the kind of work this count records. Unlike the other three service counts, a rise here is a sign of trouble rather than of progress.
description_source: Austrade, Australian exporters (services for exporters)
value_definition: A non-negative integer tally over one financial year, with no published code list. It counts interventions, not their cost or the value of trade preserved.
limitation: A zero is not evidence that the business had no problems, only that it did not take them to Austrade. Reading this count as an exposure measure would understate disruption for firms that use a customs broker, a lawyer or their own in-market staff instead.
rationale: The Austrade services page confirms a standing service for keeping exports moving through disruption, which matches the troubleshooting label; the underlying service-type classification is internal to Austrade and not published.
evidence_quote: Austrade's Trade Resilience Service provides trusted market intelligence, freight, and logistics updates to help keep your exports moving.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never explained that this count moves in the opposite direction to the other three.

value_domain: Dollar amount of levy paid to a levy collecting research service provider
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive: Expenditure you can claim
variable_description: The dollars the company paid in the income period as a levy to a registered levy collecting research service provider. Because the levy body performs the research, the ATO warns that "R&D activities funded from voluntary contributions or levy payments are always contracted to another party" and the payer must show it bears the risk and owns the results. The figure is a payment out of the firm, not a measure of research done inside it.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive: Expenditure you can claim
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income period, recorded on the company's R&D Tax Incentive registration with the Department of Industry, Science and Resources. It is the whole levy paid, before the R&D share is applied.
limitation: The whole levy is rarely deductible R&D expenditure, so this number overstates the claimable amount by whatever share went elsewhere; the companion percentage column carries that share. A levy is also usually a statutory obligation on production, so a large figure signals a large farm or producer rather than a research-intensive one.
rationale: The ATO page sets out how levy payments to a levy collecting research service provider qualify under the R&D tax incentive, which is the transaction this column records, and states the conditions the payer must satisfy.
evidence_quote: As R&D activities funded from voluntary contributions or levy payments are always contracted to another party, you must show that you: bear the financial risk associated with the R&D have control over the R&D projects and activities effectively own the project results.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the registration form's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never explained that the levy funds research conducted by someone else.

value_domain: Percentage of a levy attributed to R&D services (0 to 100)
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive: Expenditure you can claim
variable_description: The share of the levy that the registrant says was spent on R&D services, which converts the levy payment into the amount eligible for a notional deduction. The ATO requires the split because "levies frequently support other activities, such as marketing, best practice projects and quality assurance. Eligible expenditure must be allocated where this occurs." Multiply this percentage by the levy amount on the same row to get the R&D component.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive: Expenditure you can claim
value_definition: A number between 0 and 100 with no code list, applying to the levy on the same row for the same income period. It is a proportion of one payment, not a proportion of the company's total R&D.
limitation: It is a claim rather than an audited fact, set for the levy body's overall spending mix rather than for this payer, so identical percentages recur across every member of a levy scheme and carry no firm-specific information. A high percentage says the levy body is research focused, not that the company is.
rationale: The ATO page states that levies commonly fund non-research activities and that eligible expenditure must be allocated, which is precisely the allocation this percentage records.
evidence_quote: However, levies frequently support other activities, such as marketing, best practice projects and quality assurance. Eligible expenditure must be allocated where this occurs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the percentage is a scheme-level allocation rather than a firm-level measure.

value_domain: Customs value of an import consignment (Australian dollars)
value_source: Australian Border Force, Valuation of imported goods
variable_description: What the business paid, or owes, its overseas supplier for the imported goods, as declared to the Australian Border Force. The ABF states that "The information used to determine the customs value of imported goods must correctly reflect the price paid or payable for the goods" and that "The customs value provisions are contained in sections 154 to 161L of the Act", so the figure is a legal valuation subject to prescribed adjustments rather than a raw invoice total. Production assist costs, such as moulds and tooling the importer supplied to the manufacturer, must be added in.
description_source: Australian Border Force, Valuation of imported goods
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for one import declaration line, determined under the Customs Act 1901, with the transaction value method applying to most consignments.
limitation: It is not the landed cost. International freight and insurance sit outside the customs value, so this column is below the cost, insurance and freight figures the ABS also publishes, and consignments under $1,000 are generally outside merchandise trade collection, which understates a small importer's annual total. A related-party price can also fail the arm's length condition and still appear here.
rationale: The ABF page is the administering authority for the valuation this column records and names the statutory provisions, the transaction value basis and the mandatory additions.
evidence_quote: The information used to determine the customs value of imported goods must correctly reflect the price paid or payable for the goods to ensure the customs value declared is correct.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's short label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said which valuation basis applies or what the figure leaves out.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, forestry managed investment scheme interest (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax: Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: The capital loss the entity made during the year on forestry managed investment scheme interests, which had their own row on the old capital gains tax schedule. Only interests held on capital account reach this column: the ATO says "If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest." The OF prefix on the label marks the old form wording, and the current schedule no longer carries a forestry row.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax: Forestry managed investment scheme interests
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital loss for the income year, gross and before any loss is applied against a gain. It records the loss on the interest itself, not the ongoing management fees, which are deductible.
limitation: The row disappeared when the schedule was redesigned, so a series built on this column stops rather than going to zero, and the losses did not stop with it: after the change they fall into the general other-assets category and can no longer be identified as forestry. Thinning receipts are also outside CGT altogether, so this column is not a full account of forestry cash flows.
rationale: The ATO guide sets out when a forestry managed investment scheme interest is a CGT asset at all and what is excluded from the CGT treatment, which is what determines whether a business has a figure in this column.
evidence_quote: If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the row was retired or that revenue-account holders are absent.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, hedging financial arrangements (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax: Hedging financial arrangements
variable_description: The capital loss on hedging financial arrangements, which reaches the CGT schedule only where the entity made a hedging election. The ATO explains that under a valid election, "gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged". Without the election the same hedge would produce an ordinary revenue loss and never appear here.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax: Hedging financial arrangements
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital loss for the income year on financial arrangements designated as hedges, gross and before any loss is applied against a gain.
limitation: Presence depends on a tax election, not on hedging activity, so a zero mixes "no hedging losses" with "hedges but no election" and with "outside the taxation of financial arrangements regime altogether". The regime applies mainly to larger entities, so this column is close to empty across the small business end of BLADE.
rationale: The ATO page explains the character-matching effect of the hedging election and directs taxpayers to report the resulting gains and losses on the capital gains tax schedule, which is the column being documented.
evidence_quote: If this applies to you, specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2016.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that the column exists only where a hedging election is in force.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, real estate (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: The capital loss the entity made during the year on real estate, reported before any loss is applied against a gain. The label carries both wordings because the schedule changed: the old form had one undifferentiated real estate row, while the current schedule separates "real estate situated in Australia" from "other real estate". A loss here means a disposal at less than the reduced cost base, which for property held on capital account is uncommon and worth checking against the gains columns on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital loss for the income year on real property, gross of any application against gains. The reduced cost base cannot be indexed, so this figure carries no inflation adjustment.
limitation: The old and new labels are not the same quantity: an old-form figure covers all real estate, while a new-form figure covers Australian real estate only, so a series spanning the change drops the overseas component without any visible break. Trading stock and revenue-account property never appear here at all.
rationale: The ATO instructions list the asset categories used at item 1 of the current schedule and show that real estate is now split by location, which is what the new-form label wording records.
evidence_quote: real estate situated in Australia other real estate
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the concatenated OF and NF label text as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the two wordings measure different things.

value_domain: Capital loss amount, shares and units (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: The capital loss the entity made during the year on shares and on units in unit trusts, before any loss is applied against a gain. The old form combined the two in one row; the current schedule splits them four ways, with label A now narrowed to "item 1 - label A Shares in companies listed on an Australian securities exchange" and separate categories for other shares, listed units and other units. For a company this is usually the largest of the asset-category loss rows, because listed portfolios turn over faster than property.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital loss for the income year on equity interests, gross of any application against gains and before the collectables ring-fence is applied.
limitation: A series across the form change is not continuous in either direction: the old figure is too broad for the new label and the new figure is too narrow for the old one, so a fall at the changeover is an artefact. Shares held as trading stock also fall outside CGT and are absent, so this is not a measure of a firm's total losses on equities.
rationale: The ATO instructions name the current label A category explicitly and list the four separate share and unit categories that replaced the old combined row.
evidence_quote: For example, transfer the figure at 1A in table 1 of the CGT summary worksheet to item 1 - label A Shares in companies listed on an Australian securities exchange of the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the OF and NF label text and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the category was narrowed at the form change.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 industry class, four digits (agricultural derivation)
value_source: ABS, Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodities Survey (Directory of Statistical Sources)
variable_description: The four-digit ANZSIC 2006 class the ABS derived for an agricultural business from what it grows and runs, not from what the business told the tax office. The ABS says "The ANZSIC codes of agricultural units are determined annually by valuing physical crop and livestock information collected", so the class follows the largest activity by value and can move as production patterns change. The custodian warns that the resulting class may or may not be an agriculture industry class.
description_source: ABS, Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodities Survey (Directory of Statistical Sources)
value_definition: A four-digit numeric ANZSIC 2006 class code. Values 0 and 9999 mean unknown or missing.
limitation: A change of code is not necessarily a change of business. The ABS applies a deliberate damping rule so that drought, flood or a price spike does not reclassify a farm, which means the code lags real switches and understates year-to-year industry mobility in agriculture.
rationale: The ABS statistical source page for the agricultural collection explains how agricultural ANZSIC codes are derived, revalued each year and damped, which is exactly the derivation the DIL label names.
evidence_quote: The ANZSIC codes of agricultural units are determined annually by valuing physical crop and livestock information collected.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long note as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the class is derived from physical production or that the derivation is damped.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 industry group, three digits
value_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Numbering system and titles
variable_description: The three-digit ANZSIC 2006 group for an agricultural business, one level above the four-digit class on the same row. ABS numbering runs from a division letter down through subdivision, group and class, where "the leading alpha character denotes the industry division. The ANZSIC subdivision, group and class levels are denoted by numeric codes." For some sensitive four-digit classes in some states the ABS releases only this three-digit code, so the group exists where the class does not.
description_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Numbering system and titles
value_definition: A three-digit numeric ANZSIC 2006 group code. Values 0 and 999 mean unknown or missing.
limitation: It is not simply the class truncated. Confidentiality suppression means rows exist where the group is populated and the class is 0 or 9999, so the two columns have different non-missing counts, and a study that filters on a valid class silently drops the very farms in small, concentrated industries the suppression was protecting.
rationale: The ABS ANZSIC numbering page defines the group level and its three-digit code, and the DIL states that sensitive classes in certain states are released only at group level.
evidence_quote: the leading alpha character denotes the industry division. The ANZSIC subdivision, group and class levels are denoted by numeric codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's note and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never drew out that suppression makes the group column more complete than the class column.

value_domain: Australian state and territory code (single digit)
value_source: ABS, Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodities Survey (Directory of Statistical Sources)
variable_description: The state or territory where the agricultural holding sits, derived by the ABS from geographic area codes rather than from a business address. The ABS releases agricultural data "at national, state and regional levels (including NRM, SA4, and Murray-Darling Basin)", and this column is the coarsest of those geographies. It describes land, so it can differ from the state on the business register, which follows the ABN.
description_source: ABS, Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodities Survey (Directory of Statistical Sources)
value_definition: A single digit following the ABS state and territory ordering: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory, with 0 for unknown or missing.
limitation: One code is assigned per business, so a pastoral or cropping enterprise operating across a state border is recorded in a single state and its activity in the other is invisible. Analyses that treat this as the firm's location will also disagree with the register-based state on other BLADE modules for any farm whose head office is elsewhere.
rationale: The ABS statistical source page confirms the agricultural collection is geocoded and released by state, which is the geography this derived code carries; the numeric code order follows the standard ABS state sequence given in the DIL.
evidence_quote: REACS data is expected to be available at national, state and regional levels (including NRM, SA4, and Murray-Darling Basin).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line derivation note and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the code describes land rather than the business.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 industry class, four digits
value_source: ABS, Characteristics of Australian Importers methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: The four-digit ANZSIC 2006 class the ABS Business Register holds for the business, describing its predominant productive activity. It is the standard industry variable across BLADE, and the ABS confirms that industry on this asset is "based on the ANZSIC 2006 industry of the business importer as defined on BLADE". Unlike the agricultural class on the same asset, it is a register attribute rather than a derivation from physical production.
description_source: ABS, Characteristics of Australian Importers methodology, 2020-21
value_definition: A four-digit numeric ANZSIC 2006 class code, assigned to the type of activity unit. Values 0 and 9999 mean unknown or missing.
limitation: It is not a time-varying variable. The ABS states that register attributes are taken from the most recent update and "cast back through the BLADE time series", so a firm that changed industry in 2010 carries its latest code across every earlier year, and any estimate of industry switching built from this column will be close to zero by construction.
rationale: The ABS methodology for a published BLADE-based release states where BLADE industry comes from and how the register attributes are applied across the time series.
evidence_quote: ABSBR data loaded to BLADE, such as industry, are updated from the most recent update (June 2021) and then cast back through the BLADE time series
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the classification's name as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the code is backcast and therefore cannot be used to study industry change.

value_domain: Area of agricultural holding (hectares)
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Census: ABS Views on Content and Procedures, core land use data items
variable_description: How much land the agricultural business operated, in hectares, as reported to the ABS agricultural collection and supplemented from frame variables. The ABS carries it as the core land use item "Total area of holding (ha)", covering the whole holding including any part not under crop or pasture. It is one of the two standard size measures the ABS maintains for agriculture, the other being the expected value of agricultural operations on the same row.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Census: ABS Views on Content and Procedures, core land use data items
value_definition: A continuous measure in hectares for one financial year, covering the total area operated rather than the area owned or the area cropped.
limitation: Area is not productive capacity. A half-million hectare pastoral lease and a fifty hectare irrigated horticulture block can produce similar output, so ranking farms by hectares ranks them by rainfall zone; use the EVAO column for economic size. It also counts leased and agisted land as operated, so two businesses can each report the same paddocks in different years.
rationale: The ABS agricultural census content paper lists total area of holding in hectares as a core land use data item of the collection, which is the item this derived column carries.
evidence_quote: Total area of holding (ha)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's derivation note and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what area of holding covers or why it is a poor size measure on its own.

value_domain: Current year capital losses applied against discount-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: How much of this year's capital losses the entity used against discount-method gains, the place where a loss is worth least. The ATO warns that the discount is applied last: "If you use the discount method, do not apply the discount percentage until you have applied current year capital losses and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years." A dollar of loss spent here removes a gain that would have been halved anyway, so a well-advised entity leaves this column small.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, one of the three method components of current year capital losses applied at item 2 label B.
limitation: Most BLADE entities are companies, and the ATO states that "Companies are not eligible for the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business", so this column is structurally blank for the bulk of the asset. Treating a zero as a behavioural choice would be wrong; for a company it is a legal impossibility.
rationale: The ATO instructions describe the loss application step and the ordering of the CGT discount, and state which entities can use the discount at all.
evidence_quote: Companies are not eligible for the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the OF label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that companies cannot use the discount method and that the column is therefore mostly empty in BLADE.

value_domain: Current year capital losses applied against other-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025: Appendix 4 Definitions
variable_description: How much of this year's capital losses the entity used against gains that were neither indexed nor discounted, which the ATO calls the other method. It is the residual calculation: "To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds. You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months". For a company this column normally carries almost all of the losses applied, because the other two methods are shut off.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025: Appendix 4 Definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the third method component of current year capital losses applied at item 2 label B.
limitation: Because it is the residual method, a large figure here does not mean the entity trades quickly: it mixes genuine short-held disposals with every asset for which the indexation and discount methods were unavailable. The method split is therefore a poor proxy for holding period at the company end of BLADE.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method and states when it must be used, which is what determines which gains this loss column can be applied against.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds. You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months (that is, when the indexation and discount methods don't apply).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the other method is a residual rather than a holding-period marker.

value_domain: Current year capital losses applied against indexation-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: How much of this year's capital losses the entity used against gains it had worked out under the indexation method. The ATO describes this step as "calculating the amount of current year capital losses you can apply to reduce your entity's current year capital gains", and it happens before prior year losses and before transferred losses. The indexation, discount and other-method columns together make up total current year losses applied.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, a component of item 2 label B on the schedule. It is a use of losses, not a stock of them.
limitation: The indexation method is available only for assets acquired before 11:45 am on 21 September 1999, so this column thins out year by year as those assets are sold and is close to empty in recent BLADE years. A zero therefore usually means the entity had no pre-1999 assets left, not that it had no losses.
rationale: The ATO instructions define the step this column records and the ordering of the loss application, and the guide's definitions fix the acquisition date that limits the indexation method.
evidence_quote: In this part, you are calculating the amount of current year capital losses you can apply to reduce your entity's current year capital gains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said where the step sits in the sequence or why the indexation column is disappearing.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 industry division (single letter)
value_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Numbering system and titles
variable_description: The single-letter top level of the business's ANZSIC 2006 code, running A for Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing through to S for Other Services. The ABS numbering rule is that "the leading alpha character denotes the industry division", so this column is the letter that sits above the four-digit class on the same row rather than an independent classification. It is the level most BLADE analyses report at, because cell sizes at class level are often too small to clear.
description_source: ABS, ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), Numbering system and titles
value_definition: A single alphabetic character, one of the nineteen ANZSIC 2006 divisions, stored with or without its division title depending on the extract.
limitation: It is derived from the class, so it is missing exactly where the class is missing and the two columns cannot be used to cross-check one another. Divisions are also very uneven: Manufacturing and Construction cover far more businesses and far more heterogeneous activity than Mining or Electricity, so a division fixed effect absorbs much less variation in some parts of the economy than in others.
rationale: The ABS numbering page defines the division level and its alphabetic code, which is what this column holds and how it relates to the class column beside it.
evidence_quote: the leading alpha character denotes the industry division. The ANZSIC subdivision, group and class levels are denoted by numeric codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the classification name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the division is derived from the class and inherits its gaps.

value_domain: Estimated value of agricultural operations (dollars)
value_source: ABS, Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodities Survey (Directory of Statistical Sources)
variable_description: A standardised dollar valuation of the farm's crops and livestock, used by the ABS to size agricultural businesses and to assign their industry code. The ABS is explicit about what it is not: "It should be noted that EVAO is applicable only for industry coding and size valuation purposes. It is not an indicator of receipts obtained by units or of the value of agricultural commodities produced by these units." It is built by applying standard prices to areas sown and stock numbers, so two farms with the same physical output have the same EVAO regardless of what they were paid.
description_source: ABS, Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodities Survey (Directory of Statistical Sources)
value_definition: A dollar amount for one financial year, derived from reported and frame variables by valuing physical crop and livestock quantities at standard prices rather than at transaction prices.
limitation: It doubles as the scope rule for the collection, which truncates the data from below: since 2015-16 only businesses with an EVAO above $40,000 are in scope, against $5,000 before that. A distribution of EVAO across BLADE years therefore shows a cliff at the cut-off and a change of shape at 2015-16 that has nothing to do with farming.
rationale: The ABS statistical source page defines how EVAO is constructed, states what it may and may not be used for, and records the change in the scope cut-off that governs which businesses appear at all.
evidence_quote: The resulting aggregation of commodity values is termed the EVAO. It should be noted that EVAO is applicable only for industry coding and size valuation purposes. It is not an indicator of receipts obtained by units or of the value of agricultural commodities produced by these units.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's derivation note with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never warned that EVAO is not revenue and that it sets the collection's scope.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas among design filings
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different product areas the business filed designs in during the financial year, counted as distinct Locarno classification areas. IP Australia intends scope as a breadth measure: it describes "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year", and reads a wider scope as "economic activity associated with a broader range of products". For designs the ceiling is 32, because "The Locarno system for designs has 32 high-level categories (classification areas)."
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: An integer from 0 to 32 for one financial year, counting distinct Locarno high-level categories rather than distinct Locarno symbols.
limitation: Scope is bounded by the filing count on the same row, so a firm filing one design can never score above one and scope will track volume mechanically; comparing scope across firms of different sizes measures size. The 32 areas are also a coarsening of the full Locarno symbol, so two visibly different products often share an area.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables, states the interpretation IP Australia intends and fixes the number of design classification areas.
evidence_quote: Scope variables are intended to indicate the breadth of an applicant's activity across multiple event streams in a given financial year and are used as a term to describe the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never gave the upper bound or warned that scope is mechanically tied to volume.

value_domain: Count of design applications filed in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many design applications the business lodged with IP Australia during the financial year. IP Australia defines the family plainly: "Count variables are counts of the number of events of a certain kind or the number of rights in the stockpile of an applicant for an IP right." Filing is the entry point of the design lifecycle, so this column says the firm sought protection, not that it got it; the granted and enforceable counts on the same row cover what happened afterwards.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of filing events in one financial year, following the IPLoRD naming rule of right type, event stream and activity metric, where d denotes designs.
limitation: A jointly filed application counts once in full for each applicant, so summing this column across businesses overstates national design filings; the weighted count column on the same row is the one that adds up correctly. It also counts applications, not distinct products, and a single product can attract several design filings.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines count variables, the filed event stream and the naming convention that produces this column name, and IPLoRD is the IP Australia product BLADE integrates.
evidence_quote: Count variables are counts of the number of events of a certain kind or the number of rights in the stockpile of an applicant for an IP right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said a joint filing is counted in full for every applicant.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value among design filings
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The product area the business filed most of its designs in during the financial year, given as a Locarno classification area. IP Australia says these fields "record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year" and are meant for reading a firm's main focus at a glance. The area is a coarsening of the full symbol: "The first two digits of the Locarno symbol determine which high-level group the right belongs to."
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A character code identifying one of the 32 Locarno high-level categories, with 99 meaning unknown. The full Locarno symbol is not carried.
limitation: A mode throws away the rest of the distribution and, for the many firms that file one or two designs a year, is simply the class of that single filing rather than evidence of a focus. Ties have to be broken somehow, and the dictionary does not say how, so a firm split evenly across two areas gets an arbitrary answer.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables and the design classification area they are drawn from, which is what this column holds for the filed event stream.
evidence_quote: Modal value variables record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the code is a 32-way coarsening or that the mode is uninformative at low volumes.

value_domain: Fractional count of design applications filed in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design applications filed in the financial year, split evenly where an application had more than one applicant. IP Australia sets the rule out arithmetically: "when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score." This is the column to sum when the question is how many design applications Australia received, because it preserves the national total.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative rational number for one financial year, equal to the plain filed count for sole applicants and fractional wherever an application was joint.
limitation: Equal shares are an accounting convention, not a measure of contribution: the firm that designed the product and a co-applicant financier each receive 0.5 on a two-party filing. A fractional value below 1 is therefore evidence of collaboration, not of a small design effort.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary states the weighting rule for joint applicants and the reason it exists, which is exactly what this column implements for the design filing stream.
evidence_quote: when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score. The inclusion of weighted count variables allows for accurate numbers of applications to be preserved in aggregate for each IP right type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about a fraction filed and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said how the fraction is calculated or when to prefer it.

value_domain: Financial year of first design application (four-digit year)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The financial year in which the applicant first ever lodged a design application with IP Australia, a lifetime marker rather than an event in the year on the row. IPLoRD carries a matching first-application year for each of the four right types, so the design one can be compared with the applicant's first patent, trade mark or plant breeder's right. Coverage runs a very long way back: IP Australia's public release covers filing activity "from 1904 to the end of 2020".
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A four-digit year identifying a financial year. It is constant for an applicant across every row of the panel rather than varying by year.
limitation: It is a fixed applicant attribute, so it must not be used as a time-varying regressor and any within-firm estimator will drop it. It can also precede the business's ABN and its arrival on the BLADE frame by decades, which makes it useless as a proxy for firm age.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary lists the design first-application financial year among the identity-adjacent applicant variables, and the IP Australia release page states the historical span of the filing data.
evidence_quote: d_first_application_financial_year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the field is constant within an applicant or how far back it can reach.

value_domain: Financial year first design right became legally enforceable (four-digit year)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The financial year the applicant first held an enforceable design right, when design protection first became usable. IP Australia keeps the wording from its parent dataset: "Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia. The terminology is reproduced here for simpler interoperability with the parent dataset." Like the first-application year beside it, it is a lifetime attribute repeated on every row.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A four-digit year identifying a financial year. It is constant within an applicant, and it is missing for applicants that filed designs but never obtained an enforceable one.
limitation: The gap between this year and the first-application year is not a processing time. The first application and the first enforceable right are often different designs, because a design can lapse or go uncertified, so differencing the two columns measures neither examination speed nor persistence cleanly.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary lists this design variable and defines the gained enforceable status concept it rests on, including that the term is inherited from IPGOD.
evidence_quote: Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia. The terminology is reproduced here for simpler interoperability with the parent dataset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never warned that the gap from first application is not a lag for a single design.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas among granted designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different Locarno product areas the business obtained design rights in during the financial year. It is the granted counterpart of the filing scope column, and IP Australia gives the trade marks analogue to show the reading: "an applicant with a trademark granting scope of 20 in 2019/20 would have had trademark applications granted with classifications in 20 different trademark areas". For designs the corresponding ceiling is 32 areas.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: An integer from 0 to 32 for one financial year, counting distinct Locarno high-level categories among the rights granted that year.
limitation: The rights counted here were filed in earlier years, so a change in granted scope is evidence about past strategy, not this year's; using it as a contemporaneous diversification measure will date the firm's decisions wrongly by the length of the examination lag.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables with a worked granting example and fixes the number of design classification areas that bound this column.
evidence_quote: For example, an applicant with a trademark granting scope of 20 in 2019/20 would have had trademark applications granted with classifications in 20 different trademark areas (of the possible 45 in the Nice system).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the granted scope reflects earlier filing decisions.

value_domain: Count of design applications granted in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many of the business's design applications became enforceable rights during the financial year. IP Australia uses grant to mean the moment protection becomes real: "Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia." Grants and filings are separate event streams on the same row, and a grant in one year belongs to an application made in an earlier one.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of grant events in one financial year, counting rights rather than applicants' shares.
limitation: Filed and granted counts in the same year do not form a success rate, because the grants relate to earlier cohorts of applications; a firm can show zero filings and several grants, or the reverse, without any change in behaviour. The lag varies with examination and with whether the applicant requested certification, so it is not a fixed offset either.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the granted event stream and the enforceable-status terminology inherited from IPGOD, which is what a grant means in this column.
evidence_quote: Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned against reading filings and grants in one year as a conversion rate.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value among granted designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The Locarno product area that most of the business's design grants fell into during the financial year. Assigning one area per right is possible because multiple classification is rare in designs: IP Australia notes that "While in designs, multiple classification types for a single Right are possible, they are rare." That makes the design mode cleaner than the equivalent for patents or trade marks, where a single right routinely carries several classifications.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A character code identifying one of the 32 Locarno high-level categories among the year's grants, with 99 meaning unknown.
limitation: It can differ from the filed modal class in the same year without meaning anything, because the two streams describe different cohorts of designs. Reading a divergence between them as a pivot in product focus would confuse the examination queue with a business decision.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables, the granted event stream and the rarity of multiple classification in designs, which is what makes a single modal area meaningful here.
evidence_quote: While in designs, multiple classification types for a single Right are possible, they are rare.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished the granted mode from the filed mode.

value_domain: Fractional count of design applications granted in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design rights granted in the financial year, split evenly among co-applicants. It applies the same weighting rule as the filing column, which IP Australia introduced so that "accurate numbers of applications" are "preserved in aggregate for each IP right type". Use it rather than the plain granted count when adding grants across firms or industries.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative rational number for one financial year, equal to the plain granted count for sole owners and fractional where a right is jointly held.
limitation: Ownership can change between filing and grant, through assignment or a change in the applicant list, so a firm's weighted grant share need not match its weighted filing share for the same design. Differencing the two columns as a measure of attrition will therefore pick up ownership transfers as well as failed applications.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary states the joint-applicant weighting rule and its purpose, and defines the granted event stream to which it is applied here.
evidence_quote: The inclusion of weighted count variables allows for accurate numbers of applications to be preserved in aggregate for each IP right type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase about a fraction granted and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said ownership can shift between the filing and grant streams.

value_domain: Deferred GST on imported goods, activity statement label 7A (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Deferred GST scheme
variable_description: The GST on the business's imports that it deferred to its activity statement instead of paying at the border, reported at label 7A. The ATO explains the mechanism: "The DGST scheme allows the GST payable on taxable imports to be paid via your monthly business activity statement (BAS) rather than to the Australian Border Force (ABF) at the time of importation." It is a tax amount, roughly one eleventh of the taxable value of the imports, not the value of the goods themselves.
description_source: ATO, Deferred GST scheme
value_definition: A dollar amount of GST for the activity statement period, pre-filled by the ATO from Australian Border Force records rather than keyed by the business.
limitation: A zero mostly means the business is not in the scheme, not that it did not import: participation requires ATO approval and monthly reporting, so occasional and small importers never appear. The amount is also usually claimed straight back at label 1B, so it is cash-neutral and must not be read as a cost or a tax burden.
rationale: The ATO page defines the deferred GST scheme, the eligibility conditions, the label the amount appears at and the offsetting credit, which is everything a reader needs to interpret the column.
evidence_quote: If you identify an error in the pre-filled DGST amount at label 7A on your BAS and need to request an adjustment, you will first need to contact either: your customs broker the ABF.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the activity statement label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is a tax amount, is pre-filled, or is usually offset.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas in the enforceable design portfolio
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Across how many Locarno product areas the business's live design portfolio was spread at the end of the financial year. It is the stock counterpart of the filed and granted scope columns, so it accumulates the breadth of past grants net of retirements rather than describing this year's activity. IP Australia builds all scope variables on the same idea of "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity".
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: An integer from 0 to 32 measured at the last day of the financial year, counting distinct Locarno high-level categories represented in the enforceable stockpile.
limitation: It moves slowly and lags: a firm that abandons a product area keeps the area in its scope until the last right there is retired, which for a design can be years. Treating a fall in this column as the moment the firm exited a market will therefore date the exit far too late.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the scope metric and the enforceable event stream that this column combines, and states that the stockpile changes only through grants and retirements.
evidence_quote: The enforceable stockpile is affected by flows from the granted and retired applications.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that portfolio scope lags behind business decisions.

value_domain: Stock of legally enforceable design rights at end of financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many design rights the business could actually enforce at the end of the financial year, which is a stock rather than a flow. IP Australia defines the stream as "Enforceable - Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year" and states that "Filings do not affect the stockpile", so only grants and retirements move it. The BLADE column name uses le for legally enforceable where the public IPLoRD release calls the same stream enforceable.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative integer standing at the last day of the financial year, counting rights held rather than events during the year.
limitation: Because it is a stock, it must not be summed across years the way the filed, granted and retired counts can be; adding twenty years of stockpiles counts the same right twenty times. It also counts rights, not their commercial value or whether the design is still in production.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the enforceable stockpile, states what moves it and what does not, and the naming convention that maps the BLADE le prefix onto that stream.
evidence_quote: Enforceable - Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said this is a stock that cannot be summed over time.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value in the enforceable design portfolio
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The Locarno product area that dominates the business's live design portfolio at the end of the financial year. Unlike the filed and granted modes on the same row, this one describes accumulated holdings rather than a year's events, so it is the closest thing IPLoRD offers to a design-based industry marker for a firm. IP Australia's simplified classification is deliberately coarse, being intended "as a table for high-level economic analysis of an organisation's IP right filing activity across time".
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A character code identifying one of the 32 Locarno high-level categories, measured over the enforceable stockpile at year end, with 99 meaning unknown.
limitation: The portfolio mode is set by whichever product line the firm registered most heavily in the past, so it can keep pointing at a discontinued product long after the firm has moved on. It is a poor instrument for current activity and should be read against the filed modal class, which responds immediately.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables, the enforceable stockpile and the intended level of analysis, which together determine what this column can support.
evidence_quote: As IPLoRD is intended as a table for high-level economic analysis of an organisation's IP right filing activity across time, a simpler classification system is required for some rights.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the portfolio mode lags the firm's current product focus.

value_domain: Fractional stock of legally enforceable design rights at end of financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design rights it could enforce at the end of the financial year, with jointly held rights split evenly among owners. It applies the same one-over-n rule as the flow columns, so it is the column to use when aggregating portfolios across firms without double counting shared rights. IP Australia describes the underlying quantity as the applicant's stockpile of "applications fractions owned and legally enforceable" at year end.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative rational number standing at the last day of the financial year, equal to the plain enforceable count for sole owners and fractional where rights are jointly held.
limitation: Enforcement is not divisible the way the count is. A joint owner with a 0.5 share can generally still act on the whole right, so this column understates what the firm can do while the plain stock column overstates the national total; neither is the right answer to a question about litigation capacity.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines both the weighted count rule and the enforceable stockpile, whose combination is what this column holds; the enforcement consequence is an inference from how joint ownership works rather than a published statement.
evidence_quote: when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about fractions owned and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the fraction does not correspond to a fraction of enforcement rights.

value_domain: Net capital losses transferred in and applied against discount-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: Losses received from another company in the same wholly owned group and applied here against discount-method gains. The order of use is fixed by receipt rather than by size: "You need to apply the net capital losses transferred into your entity in the order they were received." The receiving entity must also have enough gains to absorb what was transferred, so the figure is capped by this year's gains rather than by the group's loss stock.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, a method component of net capital losses transferred in and applied at item 2 label D.
limitation: The losses are not this business's own. Attributing them to the firm's trading history would double count the group, because the loss already appeared as a capital loss in the transferring company's accounts. Conditions in Subdivision 170-B of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 must also be met, so an intragroup transfer that failed those tests never appears.
rationale: The ATO instructions state the ordering rule, the absorption requirement and the statutory conditions for a transfer, which is what a figure in this column implies about the entity.
evidence_quote: You need to apply the net capital losses transferred into your entity in the order they were received. Your entity must have enough capital gains to absorb the net capital losses transferred in.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never warned that the losses were made by a different company.

value_domain: Net capital losses transferred in and applied against indexation-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: Losses another company in the same wholly owned group transferred to this entity and that it applied against its indexation-method gains. The ATO restricts the step sharply: "Transfer of net capital losses is only applicable to group companies. All other entities record zeros in row 2 of table 4." It is the third and last loss step, coming after current year and prior year losses.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, a method component of net capital losses transferred in and applied at item 2 label D.
limitation: A zero is the default for every entity outside a wholly owned group, so this column cannot separate a standalone company from a group company that transferred nothing. Nor can it identify the group: nothing on the row names the transferring company or the year the loss arose.
rationale: The ATO instructions state who may use transferred losses, that all other entities record zero, and where the step sits in the loss application sequence.
evidence_quote: Transfer of net capital losses is only applicable to group companies. All other entities record zeros in row 2 of table 4.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that a zero is structural for most entities.

value_domain: Net capital losses transferred in and applied against other-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: Losses transferred in from a wholly owned group company and applied against other-method gains, where nearly all such losses land. The transfer route is narrow: the ATO allows it where "both companies are members of the same wholly owned group" and one of them is the head company of a consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group, or is not a member of a consolidatable group. This column is therefore a marker of corporate structure as much as of capital gains.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the third method component of net capital losses transferred in and applied at item 2 label D.
limitation: A non-zero value identifies a group without describing it, since neither the transferring entity nor the group's boundary is on the row; joining to the BLADE consolidated groups module is the only way to place the firm. Consolidation itself removes the need for transfers, so the column falls silent for groups that consolidated rather than for groups that stopped transferring.
rationale: The ATO instructions set out the group membership conditions that permit a transfer of net capital losses, which is what a figure in this column implies about the entity's structure.
evidence_quote: A group company may transfer the whole or a part of a net capital loss to another company where: both companies are members of the same wholly owned group
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the OF label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the column is a signal about corporate structure.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied against discount-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: How much of the entity's carried-forward net capital losses it used against this year's discount-method gains. Unlike the choice of which gain to shelter, the choice of which loss to spend is not free: the ATO requires that "you must deduct them in the order in which they were made, for example, you must deduct a 1995-96 capital loss before a 1998-99 capital loss." The amount here therefore reflects the age profile of the loss stock as much as this year's gains.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, a method component of prior year net capital losses applied at item 2 label C.
limitation: It cannot tell you when the losses were made. The oldest losses are always spent first, so a figure here dates from the entity's earliest loss year rather than the most recent one, and a firm that made a large loss last year may still be drawing down losses from a decade earlier.
rationale: The ATO instructions set out the compulsory order for deducting prior year net capital losses, which governs what a figure in this column represents.
evidence_quote: However, you must deduct them in the order in which they were made, for example, you must deduct a 1995-96 capital loss before a 1998-99 capital loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the losses spent are the oldest ones rather than the most recent.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied against other-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: How much of the entity's carried-forward net capital losses it used against other-method gains, where most of a company's loss stock is spent. One class of loss cannot come here at all: the ATO states that "If you have capital losses from collectables, you can only apply those to your capital gains from collectables." Any collectables losses in excess of collectables gains are quarantined and carried forward instead.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the third method component of prior year net capital losses applied at item 2 label C.
limitation: The column mixes two unrelated things, since the other method covers both short-held assets and assets for which no other method was available; and it cannot be used to infer the entity's total unapplied losses, because the collectables quarantine keeps part of the stock permanently out of this column. Deferral is not an option either, as the ATO requires losses that can be applied to be applied.
rationale: The ATO instructions state the collectables quarantine and the compulsory application rule that jointly determine what can reach this column.
evidence_quote: If you have capital losses from collectables, you can only apply those to your capital gains from collectables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the OF label and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never mentioned the collectables quarantine or the compulsory application rule.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied against indexation-method gains (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: How much of the entity's carried-forward net capital losses from earlier years it used against this year's indexation-method gains. The ATO describes this as "calculating the amount of prior year net capital losses you can apply to reduce your entity's current year capital gains remaining after you applied current year capital losses", so the step runs after the current year losses on the neighbouring columns and against whatever gain is left. Prior year losses reduce the carried-forward balance, unlike current year losses which never existed as a stock.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, a component of item 2 label C. It is a draw-down from a stock accumulated over earlier income years.
limitation: The column shows the draw, never the balance: an entity can apply a small amount and still hold a large unapplied stock, which sits in the carried-forward item instead. Prior year losses are also conditional, since a company must satisfy the loss recoupment tests to use them at all, so a zero can mean the losses exist but are locked.
rationale: The ATO instructions define the prior year loss step, its position in the sequence, and the recoupment condition that governs whether a company may use the losses.
evidence_quote: In this part, you are calculating the amount of prior year net capital losses you can apply to reduce your entity's current year capital gains remaining after you applied current year capital losses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the OF label and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never distinguished a draw on the loss stock from the stock itself.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas among retired designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different Locarno product areas the business let design rights lapse in during the financial year. It is the retirement counterpart of the filed and granted scope columns, and reading it against the enforceable scope on the same row shows whether a firm is narrowing its portfolio or merely refreshing it. IP Australia builds every scope variable from the same set of "32 high-level categories (classification areas)" for designs.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: An integer from 0 to 32 for one financial year, counting distinct Locarno high-level categories among the rights retired that year.
limitation: It is bounded by the firm's historical portfolio breadth, so a specialist that abandons designs entirely can show a retirement scope of one while a diversified firm trimming a few rights shows five. Comparing the raw scope across firms therefore ranks past diversity, not the extent of the withdrawal.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables, the retired event stream and the fixed set of design classification areas that bounds this column.
evidence_quote: The Locarno system for designs has 32 high-level categories (classification areas).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the measure is bounded by the firm's own portfolio breadth.

value_domain: Count of design rights retired in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many of the business's design rights ceased during the financial year, which IP Australia calls the retired event stream. The dictionary defines the stream as "Retired - rights retired during the financial year", one of the two flows that move the enforceable stockpile on the same row. A retirement is the end of protection for that design, whatever the reason.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of retirement events in one financial year, counting rights rather than owners' shares.
limitation: It cannot separate a deliberate lapse from an expiry. A firm that stops paying renewal fees because a product line closed and a firm whose right simply reached the end of its maximum term both appear here identically, so a spike in retirements is not by itself evidence of retrenchment.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the retired event stream and its role in moving the enforceable stockpile, which is what this count records.
evidence_quote: Retired - rights retired during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that retirement conflates lapse with expiry.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value among retired designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The Locarno product area that most of the business's retired design rights came from in the financial year. IP Australia names such columns by right type, event stream and metric, giving as its own worked example "the modal classification (activity_metric) of trade marks retired (event stream) is recorded as the variable tm_retired_modal_class"; this is the design equivalent. It answers what the firm is giving up, not what it is pursuing.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A character code identifying one of the 32 Locarno high-level categories among the year's retirements, with 99 meaning unknown.
limitation: The mode of retirements is set by the composition of the portfolio built years earlier, so it says more about what the firm registered heavily in the past than about what it is exiting now. A firm with a single legacy product line will show the same retirement mode for years as that stock winds down.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary gives the naming convention with the retired modal class as its worked example, and defines the modal metric and the design classification areas it draws on.
evidence_quote: Similarly, the modal classification (activity_metric) of trade marks retired (event stream) is recorded as the variable tm_retired_modal_class.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that the retirement mode reflects an old portfolio rather than current choices.

value_domain: Fractional count of design rights retired in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design rights retired during the financial year, split evenly where the right was jointly held. It closes the weighted accounting on the row: weighted filings, grants, retirements and stock all use the same one-over-n rule, so the weighted stock moves by weighted grants less weighted retirements. IP Australia frames the column as the fraction of applications the applicant "has allowed to retire" that year.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative rational number for one financial year, equal to the plain retired count for sole owners and fractional where the retired right was jointly held.
limitation: A joint right retires as a whole, so the co-owners' fractions retire together whether or not each of them wanted it to. The column therefore attributes to a firm a decision it may not have made, which matters for any analysis reading retirement as a signal about that firm's product strategy.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the weighted count rule and the retired event stream that this column combines; the joint-retirement consequence follows from how a single right is held rather than from a published statement.
evidence_quote: Weighted count variables consider the number of applicants associated with an IP Right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about fractions allowed to retire and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said a co-owner cannot retire its share alone.

value_domain: SISCA 2008 institutional sector class, four digits
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
variable_description: Which institutional sector of the economy the business belongs to for national accounting, as a four-digit SISCA 2008 class.
