The ABS explains that "The numbering system adopted in the SISCA has a hierarchical structure, where a 1-digit numeric code denotes the sector, a 2-digit code denotes the subsector, a 3-digit code denotes the group, and a 4-digit code denotes the class", so the leading digit alone separates non-financial corporations, financial corporations, general government, households and non-profits. It answers a different question from ANZSIC on the same row: sector is about economic function and market status, industry is about what the business produces.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA)
value_definition: A four-digit numeric SISCA class code from the 2008 edition, applied to the institutional unit. Values 0 and 9999 mean unknown or missing.
limitation: It classifies the institutional unit, not the operating business, so a subsidiary can carry its parent's sector and a trading arm of government can look like a corporation. The column is also pinned to the 2008 edition while the ABS revised SESCA in 2021, so it will not line up cleanly with current national accounts sector aggregates.
rationale: The ABS classification publication defines SISCA, its purpose in separating market from non-market producers, and the four-digit numbering this column uses.
evidence_quote: The numbering system adopted in the SISCA has a hierarchical structure, where a 1-digit numeric code denotes the sector, a 2-digit code denotes the subsector, a 3-digit code denotes the group, and a 4-digit code denotes the class.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the classification's name and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what an institutional sector is or that the edition is now superseded.

value_domain: Count of distinct employees paid in the calendar month
value_source: ATO, What STP is (Single Touch Payroll)
variable_description: How many distinct people the employer paid during the calendar month, counted from its Single Touch Payroll reports. STP is real-time payroll reporting: "With STP you report employees' payroll information to us each time you pay them through STP-enabled software", so the count is assembled from pay events rather than from an annual return. It is a headcount of payees, which is the only employment measure in BLADE available at monthly frequency.
description_source: ATO, What STP is (Single Touch Payroll)
value_definition: A non-negative integer for one calendar month, counting distinct payees rather than jobs, hours or full-time equivalents.
limitation: It cannot distinguish a casual paid once from a full-time employee, so a month with heavy casual turnover looks larger than a month with the same wage bill on permanent staff, and headcount will move without any change in labour input. Coverage also begins with the STP rollout, which the ATO dates to "1 July 2018 for employers with 20 or more employees and 1 July 2019 for employers with 19 or fewer employees", so earlier months carry no payee count even where the BLADE module is listed as starting in 2001-02.
rationale: The ATO page defines what STP reporting is, when it happens and when each employer size class was brought in, which fixes both the meaning of the count and the period over which it exists.
evidence_quote: STP started on 1 July 2018 for employers with 20 or more employees and 1 July 2019 for employers with 19 or fewer employees and is a mandatory obligation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the count is a headcount of payees or that it starts with the STP phase-in.

value_domain: Capital losses applied, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Capital losses the business entity applied against gains worked out under the discount method. Losses are applied before the discount, and where they are applied is a choice: "When applying your current year capital losses, you can choose the method that gives you the best result to reduce your current year capital gains." OF and NF in the DIL label are the old-form and new-form wordings, and the new form stopped splitting this total by method.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount of losses applied, not the losses available. Current year losses and losses carried forward from earlier years both flow through this step.
limitation: The column shows losses used, so it understates losses held. The old-form and new-form labels are not the same quantity, so a series spanning the form change is not continuous. The OF and NF reading is inferred.
rationale: The BLADE DIL label names total capital losses applied under the discount method, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule.
evidence_quote: When applying your current year capital losses, you can choose the method that gives you the best result to reduce your current year capital gains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Total capital losses applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: Total capital losses the entity applied against gains for the year, but the old and new labels mean different things. The old form's figure is the indexation-method total only, while the new form's is the whole of item 2. On the current schedule the ATO says to "Add up the amounts at item 2 - labels B, C and D and write the total at label E Total capital losses applied", which pools current year, prior year and transferred losses across all three methods. The old-form figure is therefore a small subcomponent of the new-form one.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year. Under the new form it equals the sum of current year losses applied, prior year net losses applied and transferred losses applied.
limitation: A series spanning the form change is not continuous, and the break goes the wrong way for intuition: the total jumps upward at the changeover because the new label pools three components the old label excluded. It also records losses used, not losses made, so unapplied losses go to the carried-forward item and are invisible here.
rationale: The ATO instructions define the current label E total and its components, which is the new-form meaning, and the DIL's OF prefix marks the narrower old-form indexation-method total.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at item 2 - labels B, C and D and write the total at label E Total capital losses applied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the concatenated OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the two wordings differ by an order of magnitude.

value_domain: Capital losses applied, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Capital losses the business entity applied against gains not worked out under the discount method. For a company this is where nearly all applied losses sit, because companies cannot claim the CGT discount. OF and NF in the DIL label are the old-form and new-form wordings.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount of losses applied, not the losses available.
limitation: The column shows losses used, so it understates losses held. Losses from collectables are ring-fenced: "You can only use capital losses from collectables to reduce capital gains from collectables." The OF and NF reading is inferred.
rationale: The BLADE DIL label names total capital losses applied for other capital gains, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule.
evidence_quote: You can only use capital losses from collectables to reduce capital gains from collectables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Date a variation to a federal enterprise agreement takes effect
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The day a variation to a federal enterprise agreement starts to operate, which is not the day it was agreed, lodged or approved. DEWR records the database's span as "wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997", so a variation date sits inside the life of an agreement already on file. One agreement can be varied several times, so a business can carry several of these dates.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A calendar date written dd/mm/yyyy, one row per variation rather than one per agreement.
limitation: The date alone does not say what changed. A pay rise, a change to shift arrangements and a technical correction all stamp this one field, so the variation has to be read against the agreement's own conditions items. WAD also covers federal enterprise agreements only, so award-reliant and individually contracted workplaces never generate a variation date at all.
rationale: The DEWR page is the custodian's description of the database this column comes from, giving its coverage, what it records about each agreement and that variations are tracked alongside agreements.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never distinguished the effect date from the approval date or noted the federal-only coverage.

value_domain: Deidentified Customs Client Identifier
value_source: ABS, Characteristics of Australian Importers methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: A deidentified Customs Client Identifier, which is who the exporter was on the customs declaration when it did not quote an ABN. The ABS defines it as "a unique identifier, administered by ABF, to represent importing persons and organisations that do not report an ABN", and the same registration system covers exporters. It is the fallback identity on a trade record, so its presence marks a party that Australian Border Force could not tie to the business register.
description_source: ABS, Characteristics of Australian Importers methodology, 2020-21
value_definition: A 10-digit alphanumeric identifier, deidentified for BLADE, with 9999999999 meaning unknown.
limitation: A row keyed on this identifier cannot be joined to the BLADE business spine: the ABS states that "CCIDs, which cannot be linked to the ABSBR, are treated as statistical units", so trade attributed to a CCID is missing from any ABN-based firm analysis and will look like a hole in industry or size aggregates. A single entity can also hold both an ABN and a CCID, so counting distinct identifiers overcounts traders.
rationale: The ABS methodology for a BLADE-based trade release defines the Customs Client Identifier, explains why it exists and states that it cannot be linked to the business register, which is the decisive fact about this column.
evidence_quote: CCIDs, which cannot be linked to the ABSBR, are treated as statistical units.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviation as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what a CCID is or that it does not link to the business spine.

value_domain: ABS internal integration version reference
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Which build of the ABS Dealroom integration produced the row, a processing marker rather than a fact about the business. Dealroom is a commercial database of startup and venture activity that the Department of Industry, Science and Resources brings into BLADE, and the ABS lists it as a requestable module for 2025 only. Use this column to tell two extracts apart, not to describe a firm.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric string following an internal ABS naming convention, of the form shown in the data item list as an integration reference. No code list is published.
limitation: It carries no information about the business, so a change in the string between two files is a change in ABS processing, not a change in the firm. Because BLADE holds Dealroom for a single reference year, the version cannot be used as a time dimension either.
rationale: The BLADE data page confirms Dealroom is a requestable BLADE module and gives its single-year coverage, which bounds what a version marker on those rows can mean; the ABS does not publish the internal version convention.
evidence_quote: Dealroom: 2025
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's parenthetical note and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the field is a processing marker with no business content.

value_domain: Date an intellectual property right or application is deemed no longer in force
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The date from which IP Australia treats a right or application as no longer in force, on the IPRAPID applications table. IP Australia uses retirement as the general term for a right leaving the live register, and treats it as one of the two flows that move a holder's enforceable stock: "Retired - rights retired during the financial year". The word deemed matters, because the date is set by rule rather than by an event on the day.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A calendar date written dd/mm/yyyy, applying to one application or right rather than to the applicant.
limitation: It is backdated. When a lapse is recognised later, for example after renewal fees stop, the deemed date is the day protection is treated as having ended, which can be well before the register was updated, so it cannot be used to date the administrative decision. It also does not distinguish a deliberate abandonment from expiry at the end of the maximum term, and it is never a date about the business, only about the right.
rationale: The IP Australia data dictionary for the sister longitudinal product defines retirement of a right and its place in the lifecycle, which is the concept this IPRAPID column dates; IP Australia does not publish a column-level dictionary for IPRAPID.
evidence_quote: Retired - rights retired during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never explained that a deemed date is backdated and set by rule.

value_domain: Capital gains on active assets, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: Capital gains on active business assets under the discount method, the column carrying the double concession on a long-held small business asset. Where the gain came through a trust the amount has been inflated on purpose: the ATO says "If the trust's capital gain was reduced by both the CGT discount and the small business 50% active asset reduction, multiply the distribution amount by 4". It differs from the indexation-method active assets column beside it in the calculation applied, not in the assets covered.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital gain for the income year, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It is the discount-method component of the active assets row.
limitation: Grossing up makes the figure larger than the economic gain the entity actually received, by a factor of two or four for trust distributions, so summing it as income overstates the firm's position. The gross-up is invisible on the row, since nothing marks which amounts have been multiplied.
rationale: The ATO instructions set out the grossing-up rules that determine what amount is entered at the active assets discount-method box for gains flowing through a trust.
evidence_quote: If the trust's capital gain was reduced by both the CGT discount and the small business 50% active asset reduction, multiply the distribution amount by 4 and include the result in row 7 at Active assets under the Capital gains - discount method.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned that trust-sourced amounts in this column are deliberately grossed up.

value_domain: Capital gains on active assets, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: Capital gains on active business assets calculated under the indexation method, shown separately because the small business concessions may reduce them. The ATO limits what belongs here: "At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions". An active asset is one used, or held ready for use, in running the business, which can include goodwill and, in some cases, shares and trust interests.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital gain for the income year, gross of losses, the small business concessions and the CGT discount. It is the indexation-method component of the active assets row.
limitation: It is not all gains on business assets. A gain on an asset the entity uses in its business but which fails the concession tests is reported at non-active assets instead, so this column measures claimed concession eligibility rather than asset use. Indexation also applies only to assets acquired before 21 September 1999, which makes the column progressively rarer.
rationale: The ATO instructions define what may be reported at active assets, the eligibility test that governs it, and the meaning of an active asset.
evidence_quote: At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said that the active assets split is driven by concession eligibility rather than by how the asset is used.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains on the firm's active assets under the other method, after capital losses, and only where a small business concession applies. Active assets are the ones used in running the business: "Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business)". The active columns are narrower than that, though, because the ATO says to include a gain there only if it "qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions" - the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label F, a flow over the income year, struck after losses but before the concessions at Part G that are the reason the gain was put in the active column in the first place.
limitation: It is not a measure of business asset disposals. A firm too large for the concessions reports the sale of its own goodwill in the non-active columns instead, and a gain covered by the 15-year exemption never reaches Part E at all, so the column tracks concession entitlement more than it tracks what was sold.
rationale: The DIL label is the active-asset other-method cell of Part E, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions define an active asset and restrict what may be shown in the active columns.
evidence_quote: At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets worked out under the CGT discount method, after capital losses have been applied. It is the second column of the non-active row in Part E of the old CGT schedule, sitting beside the indexation and other-method columns for the same assets. The discount method covers assets owned at least twelve months, and the ATO notes that it "does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies", so for most BLADE units the column is structurally empty.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label B, gross of the discount itself: the schedule applies the discount percentage later, at Part F, so this figure is the full gain and not the halved one.
limitation: A zero does not mean the firm made no long-held gains. A company reports all of them in the indexation and other columns because it cannot use the discount at all, so the column mainly separates trusts, funds and life companies from ordinary companies rather than measuring holding periods.
rationale: The DIL label is the non-active discount-method cell of Part E, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions state which entities may use the discount method.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains the business made on non-active assets under the indexation method, measured after capital losses have been applied. The old CGT schedule reaches this figure in a part headed "Part E Current year capital gains (CYCG) after applying capital losses", where non-active assets occupy the first row and the indexation method the first column. The ATO restricts that method to "capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999", so the column follows a closing stock of pre-1999 assets. Non-active means the gain does not qualify for the small business concessions, either because the asset is not used in the business or because the entity is not entitled.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label A of the schedule, a flow over the income year. It is struck after current year and prior year capital losses but before the CGT discount at Part F and the small business concessions at Part G.
limitation: The schedule dropped Part E after 2011-12, so the column stops rather than falls to zero and a series that spans the change is not continuous. Nor can the figure be read as a share of gains: an entity that chose the discount method for an eligible pre-1999 asset reports nothing here for that asset even though indexation was available.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the row and column headings of Part E of the pre-2013 CGT schedule, and the variable prefix e_ matches that part. The form itself carries the wording, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions define the indexation method.
evidence_quote: Part E Current year capital gains (CYCG) after applying capital losses
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets that fall under neither the indexation nor the discount method, after capital losses. The ATO defines the residual as the "'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)", which in practice means assets bought after 21 September 1999 and sold within twelve months, plus every gain of a company that cannot use the discount. For an ordinary trading company this is normally the largest of the three non-active columns in Part E.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label C, a flow over the income year, carrying no concession or discount of any kind: the other method is the full gain with no reduction applied at any later part.
limitation: Two different situations collapse into this one figure - a short-held asset and a company that is simply barred from the discount - and nothing on the row separates them, so the column cannot be used as evidence of short holding periods or asset churn.
rationale: The DIL label is the non-active other-method cell of Part E, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions define the other method as the residual of the three.
evidence_quote: 'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: All of the firm's discount-method capital gains surviving capital losses, active and non-active combined. The schedule builds it by addition: "Add amounts at B and E above and write the total at H below." This is the only one of the three totals that then meets the CGT discount, which Part F applies separately to the non-active and active parts of it.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label H, equal to the non-active and active discount cells on the same row, and still gross of the discount percentage itself.
limitation: For a company the total is normally zero because the discount is closed to companies, so a cross-entity comparison of this column measures legal form rather than investment behaviour. It is also not the amount that will be taxed: the discount comes off afterwards.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the discount-method cell of the Part E totals row, and the schedule prints the addition rule that defines it.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at B and E above and write the total at H below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: All of the firm's indexation-method capital gains left standing after capital losses, active and non-active added together. The schedule computes it rather than collecting it: "Add amounts at A and D above and write the total at G below." It is the indexation-method entry point into the final calculation, since Part H subtracts the discount and concession totals from exactly this figure to reach the net capital gain.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label G, equal to the non-active and active indexation cells on the same row. It is a derived total, so it carries the rounding and the reporting errors of both components.
limitation: Adding G, H and I does not give the net capital gain: the CGT discount and the small business concessions are still to come off at Parts F to H, and only after that does an amount reach the return. The total also cannot be split back into active and non-active if the component columns are missing.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the totals row of Part E, and the schedule prints the addition rule that defines the cell.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at A and D above and write the total at G below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: All of the firm's other-method capital gains surviving capital losses, active and non-active combined. The schedule sets it out as an addition: "Add amounts at C and F above and write the total at I below." For a company this is usually the largest of the three totals, because a company cannot use the discount and few of its assets predate September 1999.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label I, equal to the non-active and active other-method cells on the same row, and reduced only by capital losses.
limitation: The column ends with the old form after 2011-12, and the replacement schedule records a single current year capital gain with no method split, so a firm's other-method total cannot be reconstructed for later years and a break in the series is a form change, not a change in behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the other-capital-gains cell of the Part E totals row, and the schedule prints the addition rule that defines it.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at C and F above and write the total at I below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD)
variable_description: The first day this intellectual property right was filed anywhere in the world, which need not be the day IP Australia saw the file. It differs from application_date on the same row whenever the right reached Australia through an international route: a Patent Cooperation Treaty case or a Madrid Protocol trade mark is filed abroad first and arrives in Australia months or years later. For firm-level work it is the better date for asking when a business first sought protection, and the worse date for asking when it engaged with the Australian system.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD)
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, drawn from IP Australia's rights registers, which IPGOD publishes as the open version of the same data. The domain is open and runs back over a century of registry records.
limitation: It is not the priority date and it is not evidence of invention. A filing can claim priority from an earlier application that is itself not in this table, and a firm that files a provisional and then abandons it leaves a filing date attached to a right that never existed.
rationale: IPRAPID is IP Australia's own analytical product built on the rights registers that IPGOD releases publicly, so the IPGOD collection and its data dictionary are the authority for the filing dates the registers hold.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never distinguished this date from the three other dates on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Total allowances the employer paid its workers over the month, on top of ordinary wages. The ATO defines allowances as "payments you made to cover your payee's work-related expenses" and keeps them out of the wages figure: "You must show the total amount of all allowances you paid in the Total allowances field. Do not include these amounts in gross payments." The row is one ABN and branch in one month, so this is the sum across every payee reported in that month.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, aggregated by the ABS from the year-to-date allowance amounts employers report for each payee through STP.
limitation: It does not say which allowances. A tool allowance, a car allowance and a shift allowance land in one figure, and a living-away-from-home allowance is excluded entirely, so the column cannot be read as the cost of any particular working condition.
rationale: The BLADE field is the STP carry-over of the payment summary's total allowances field, and the ATO instruction for that field defines what an allowance is and how it sits against gross payments.
evidence_quote: Allowances are payments you made to cover your payee's work-related expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out as lump sum A, which the ATO limits to older accruals and to leave paid alongside a redundancy. Its instruction covers "unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993", unused holiday pay accrued before 18 August 1993, and post-1993 leave paid in connection with a genuine redundancy, an early retirement scheme or an invalidity segment. In an employer-month total a non-zero value is a marker of separations rather than of ordinary pay, and it is deliberately excluded from the gross payments column.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across payees. Lump sum A carries a type code of R for redundancy or T for any other reason on the payment summary; the code is not in this table, only the amount.
limitation: It cannot separate a redundancy from an ordinary resignation, because the distinguishing type code is absent. Leave accrued after 17 August 1993 and paid on an ordinary resignation goes into gross payments instead, so the column understates leave paid out on separation.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum A box carried into STP from the individual non-business payment summary, and the ATO instruction for that box lists exactly which payments belong in it.
evidence_quote: unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused long service leave from before 16 August 1978, paid out during the month. The ATO reserves the box for "amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978", and it is separated from lump sum A because only a small fraction of it is assessable to the worker. In an employer-month row a non-zero value marks the departure of someone whose service reaches back nearly fifty years.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across the employer's payees, and reported outside gross payments like the other lump sums.
limitation: The column is close to structurally empty and shrinking as pre-1978 service leaves the workforce, so a zero says nothing about how much long service leave the firm paid out; almost all of it will be in the lump sum A column or in gross payments.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum B box of the payment summary carried into STP, and the ATO instruction defines the accrual period that qualifies.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The tax-free part of genuine redundancy and early retirement scheme payments the employer made in the month, despite a field name that suggests leave. The ATO defines lump sum D as "the tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment", so it is the closest thing in this table to a direct redundancy signal: it exists only where the redundancy conditions are met. It is the one lump sum the ATO leaves out of the employer's gross payments total.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across payees. The tax-free component is capped by a base amount plus a per-year-of-service amount that the ATO resets each income year.
limitation: Because of that cap the figure tracks the number of redundancies and the length of service far better than the money the departing workers received; anything above the cap becomes an employment termination payment and is reported outside this column.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum D box carried into STP from the payment summary, and the ATO instruction gives its definition in one sentence.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Back pay for work done in earlier years, paid out during the month and reported as lump sum E. The ATO defines it as "amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments", which is why it is taken out of ordinary wages: the worker is taxed on it with an offset that recognises it belongs to another year. A spike in an employer-month is usually a settlement, a back-dated agreement or a correction of underpaid wages.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across payees, and excluded from the gross payments column on the same row.
limitation: It cannot date the work it pays for. One lump sum E can cover several past years at once, so using the column to reconstruct historical wage bills, or to date when an underpayment happened, will put the money in the wrong year.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum E box of the payment summary carried into STP, and the ATO instruction defines which payments belong there.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: Gross pay the employer reported under the foreign employment income stream, earned by Australian tax residents working overseas. The ATO describes the income type as telling it about "the income an Australian tax resident has earned while working overseas where the qualifying period for foreign employment income is met", and instructs that it be used only where tax was withheld in the foreign country. value_domain: Free on board value of an export consignment line (Australian dollars)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Trade system, valuation and time of recording
variable_description: The value of the goods on this export declaration line at the moment they were loaded for export from Australia, the standard basis for Australian export statistics. The ABS defines it so: "A FOB price at the customs frontier includes the transaction value of the goods, the value of outside packaging (other than international containers used for containerised cargo), and related distributive services used, up to and including loading the goods onto the carrier at the customs frontier of the exporting country." It excludes international freight and insurance, which is why a firm's export revenue on this basis is lower than the price its overseas customer pays on delivery.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Trade system, valuation and time of recording
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for one consignment line, on a free on board basis at the Australian border. Foreign currency values are converted using an indicative Reserve Bank reference rate for the day.
limitation: The declaration threshold truncates the column: export consignments below $2,000 are treated as out of scope, so a small or occasional exporter can have real overseas sales and no row here at all. Exports are also recorded on a date of shipment basis, not when the firm was paid.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines the FOB valuation used for Australian export statistics and the currency conversion applied to reported values.
evidence_quote: A FOB price at the customs frontier includes the transaction value of the goods, the value of outside packaging (other than international containers used for containerised cargo), and related distributive services used, up to and including loading the goods onto the carrier at the customs frontier of the exporting country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the $2,000 threshold that removes small exporters was never stated.

value_domain: Free on board value of an import consignment (Australian dollars)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Trade system, valuation and time of recording
variable_description: The value of an imported consignment at the exporting country's border, before international freight and insurance are added. The ABS uses a free on board type value for imports as well as exports, and notes that "The CIF price is equal to the FOB transaction value, plus the cost of freight and merchandise insurance involved in transporting the goods beyond the place of export to the customs frontier of the importing country." Unlike the export column, this figure sits at the foreign border, so the difference between the two is the whole international leg.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Trade system, valuation and time of recording
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for the whole consignment, converted by the Integrated Cargo System from any reported foreign currency at the rate applying on the date of export from the place of export.
limitation: It is not the landed cost. Freight, insurance, duty and the import processing charge all sit outside this value, so using it as the firm's input cost understates what the goods cost to get onto an Australian loading dock. Imports below the $1,000 threshold are also out of scope.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines the FOB and CIF valuation points for imports and the currency conversion applied.
evidence_quote: The CIF price is equal to the FOB transaction value, plus the cost of freight and merchandise insurance involved in transporting the goods beyond the place of export to the customs frontier of the importing country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long sentence about consignment values and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the contrast with a landed CIF cost was not drawn.

value_domain: Type of import declaration lodged with Customs (Nature 10, 20 or 30)

It comes from the assay details on the export declaration, which the form defines as "A chemical test to determine the content of a particular element" and requires "Only input details if goods are minerals requiring an assay"; gold's prescribed unit on that form is GPT, grams per tonne. It is a property of the shipment, not of the exporting business.
description_source: Australian Border Force, Export declaration supplementary page (form B957a), hosted by the ABS
value_definition: A non-negative number in grams per tonne, declared against the assay element AU on the export declaration supplementary page, and present only on mineral lines that require an assay.
limitation: It cannot be averaged into a firm-level ore grade, because it is populated only on qualifying mineral lines and is weighted by nothing: a large low-grade shipment and a small high-grade one carry equal-looking numbers. Nor is it a reserve or resource grade, since it describes what left the wharf after processing rather than what is in the ground.
rationale: The export declaration supplementary page defines the assay fields, states when they must be completed, and prescribes grams per tonne as the unit for gold, which is exactly what this column carries.
evidence_quote: A chemical test to determine the content of a particular element. Only input details if goods are minerals requiring an assay.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'Grams of gold per tonne of ore' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the field is consignment-level and conditional on the goods requiring an assay.

value_domain: Gross shipping weight of an export consignment, kilograms
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Quantity measurement
variable_description: The shipped weight of the goods the business exported on this line, including the packaging that went with them. The ABS states that "Gross weight is recorded for each commodity on a customs export declaration", which makes the export side of this pair usable at commodity level, unlike its import counterpart. It is a flow for one declaration line, not an annual total for the firm.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Quantity measurement
value_definition: A weight in kilograms in ABS output, covering the goods plus wrapping, crates, boxes and outside packages, but excluding the shipping container itself.
limitation: It is not the traded quantity: the comparable measure is the net quantity in the unit prescribed by the AHECC, and a change in packaging moves this number with no change in what was sold. Weight is also a poor proxy for value, since one tonne of ore and one tonne of medical devices are the same number here.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods publication defines gross weight for exports, states that it is recorded per commodity, and sets the unit used in ABS output.
evidence_quote: Gross weight is recorded for each commodity on a customs export declaration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's definition of gross weight with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never distinguished gross weight from the AHECC net quantity.

value_domain: Gross shipping weight of an import declaration, kilograms
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Quantity measurement
variable_description: The shipped weight of an import declaration, which the ABS reports for the whole declaration rather than for each commodity on it. This is why the custodian warns against commodity or country use: "For imports, gross weight is not recorded at the individual commodity level but total gross weight is reported for all the commodities on a customs import declaration", and the ABS then assigns that whole weight to one line so commodity estimates can be produced. The line carrying the weight is therefore arbitrary within the declaration.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Quantity measurement
value_definition: A weight in kilograms covering the goods plus their immediate packaging on the entire import declaration, attached to a single line of it rather than apportioned.
limitation: Summing this column by commodity or by country produces a nonsense result, because a mixed consignment's entire weight sits on whichever line the ABS attached it to. ABS advises that import gross weight is only reliable when aggregated at the port or state level, so a firm-level weight of imports built from it is not safe either.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods publication states plainly that import gross weight is a declaration-level figure and explains the assignment to one line, which is exactly the caution attached to this column.
evidence_quote: For imports, gross weight is not recorded at the individual commodity level but total gross weight is reported for all the commodities on a customs import declaration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's warning without explaining it, and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Count of Austrade general service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade recorded delivering any kind of general service to the business during the financial year. It is the total that the more specific general service counts on the same row sit under, and it is drawn from Austrade's client records rather than from the business. Austrade describes this work as advisory: "We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who provide information, insights, support and connections".
description_source: Austrade, Programs and services
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of service events in one financial year, covering all general service types including those recorded with an unknown type.
limitation: It counts events, not effort, value or duration, so ten short email introductions outrank one sustained market entry engagement. It also does not add up to Austrade's whole relationship with the firm, since grants and named programmes are recorded in their own columns rather than here.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the trade services and adviser network that generate the service events this column tallies, and the ABS project register confirms Austrade's client records are the source integrated into BLADE.
evidence_quote: We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who provide information, insights, support and connections.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the number counts events rather than effort.

value_domain: Count of Austrade international contact identification services in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade identified relevant overseas contacts for the business during the financial year. This is the introductions component of Austrade's general services, the part that draws on its in-market posts to put a firm in front of possible buyers, distributors or partners. It is a subset of gsallservices on the same row.
description_source: Austrade, Programs and services
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of general service events of the international contacts type in a financial year, one of the components of gsallservices.
limitation: An introduction is not a relationship: the column records that contacts were identified, not that the business pursued them or that anything followed. It also gives no market, so a firm's introductions cannot be traced to the countries in its merchandise trade records.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the in-market adviser network that makes these introductions, which is the activity this service-type count records.
evidence_quote: We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who provide information, insights, support and connections.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Austrade's service-type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing distinguished an introduction from an outcome.

value_domain: Count of Austrade market selection and assessment services in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade helped the business choose and assess overseas markets during the financial year. It is the earliest stage of the export journey among the general service types, coming before market entry work, so a firm showing counts here and nowhere else is still deciding where to go. It is a subset of gsallservices on the same row.
description_source: Austrade, Programs and services
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of general service events of the market selection and assessment type in a financial year, one of the components of gsallservices.
limitation: The column cannot show which markets were assessed or whether any was chosen, so it will not explain a later change in a firm's export destinations. A count here is also compatible with a business that never exported, since assessment often concludes against entry.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the information and insight services its advisers provide, which is the activity behind this market selection count.
evidence_quote: Trade services can help eligible Australian businesses expand in overseas markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's service-type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing placed the service in the sequence of export support.

value_domain: Count of Austrade market entry and expansion services in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade assisted the business with entering or expanding in an overseas market during the financial year. It is the operational end of the general services, and it usually follows market selection work rather than preceding it, so counts here suggest a firm already committed to a market. It is a subset of gsallservices on the same row.
description_source: Austrade, Programs and services
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of general service events of the market entry and expansion type in a financial year, one of the components of gsallservices.
limitation: Entry and expansion are pooled in one count, so a first shipment to a new country cannot be told apart from deepening an existing trade relationship. The column also has no dollar value, so it cannot be used to weight the assistance a firm received.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes trade services aimed at helping businesses expand in overseas markets, which is the activity this service-type count records.
evidence_quote: Trade services can help eligible Australian businesses expand in overseas markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Austrade's service-type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said that entry and expansion are pooled.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at GST on sales on the business activity statement
value_source: business.gov.au, Business activity statement
variable_description: The goods and services tax the business reported as payable on its sales for the period, or its GST instalment amount where it uses that option. The activity statement is the vehicle: "Your BAS helps you to report on taxes like: goods and services tax (GST), pay as you go (PAYG) withholding, PAYG instalments, fringe benefits tax (FBT) instalments, luxury car tax, wine equalisation tax". Because it is roughly one-eleventh of taxable sales, it is often used as a high-frequency proxy for a firm's turnover.
description_source: business.gov.au, Business activity statement
value_definition: A dollar amount reported for a business activity statement period, which may be monthly, quarterly or annual depending on the firm's reporting cycle.
limitation: It is GST on sales, not GST paid: net GST is this amount less the credits claimed on purchases, so reading it as the firm's tax bill overstates it. The column also mixes two different quantities, because an instalment payer reports a pre-set amount rather than a measured one, and businesses under the GST registration turnover threshold report nothing at all.
rationale: business.gov.au sets out what a business activity statement reports and its reporting cycles, which fixes the period, the form and the tax this column comes from; the label itself names GST on sales or the GST instalment.
evidence_quote: Your BAS helps you to report on taxes like: goods and services tax (GST), pay as you go (PAYG) withholding, PAYG instalments, fringe benefits tax (FBT) instalments, luxury car tax, wine equalisation tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing separated GST on sales from net GST or flagged the instalment payers pooled into the same column.

value_domain: Count of Austrade general services of unrecorded type in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many general service events Austrade recorded for the business without capturing what kind of service it was. It is a data quality residual within the general services block, and its size sets how much of gsallservices the named service-type columns actually account for. A firm with a large count here received help that cannot be characterised from this panel.
description_source: Austrade, Programs and services
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of service events in a financial year whose service type was not recorded, forming the unspecified remainder of the general services total.
limitation: It is not a kind of service and must not be modelled as one; doing so treats an administrative recording failure as a business experience. Because recording practice varies with the office and the year, movements in this column can reflect changes in Austrade's own systems rather than in what firms received.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the service delivery whose records generate these counts, which is what makes an unknown-type count a completeness measure for the block rather than a service in its own right.
evidence_quote: Trade services can help eligible Australian businesses expand in overseas markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's unknown service type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned against treating it as a substantive category.

value_domain: Net capital gain, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The part of the business entity's net capital gain that came from assets worked out under the discount method, after losses, the discount and the small business concessions. The ATO restricts the method by holding period, applying it "for assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method", so this column is the long-held end of the entity's disposals. The OF prefix marks it as an old-form label; the new form no longer splits the net gain by method.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount at the net capital gain step of the capital gains tax schedule, after part D losses, the part F discount and the part G concessions have all been applied.
limitation: For most companies this column is empty as a matter of law rather than of business behaviour: the ATO states that "Companies are not eligible for the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business". Reading a zero as an absence of long-held asset sales is therefore wrong for the great majority of company filers.
rationale: The ATO guide defines the discount method and its twelve-month holding requirement, and states which entities are eligible for the discount, which together fix what this method column can and cannot contain.
evidence_quote: the discount method (see note 3 of the worksheet) for assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing explained that companies cannot use the discount at all.

value_domain: Net capital gain, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The part of the entity's net capital gain that came from assets worked out under the indexation method, after all losses and concessions. Indexation is closed to new assets: the ATO allows it only "for capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11.45am (by legal time in the ACT) on 21 September 1999 and owned for at least 12 months", so this column is a window on a firm's oldest holdings. The OF prefix marks the old-form label, which the new form dropped when it stopped splitting the net gain by method.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount at the net capital gain step of the schedule, restricted to gains on assets acquired before 21 September 1999 and worked out with cost base indexation.
limitation: The column thins out mechanically across the panel as pre-1999 assets are sold, so a downward trend measures asset vintage rather than any change in business behaviour. A zero in a later year is close to uninformative, and the column should not be summed with the discount and other-method columns as if the three were comparable measures.
rationale: The ATO guide defines the indexation method and states the acquisition date and holding period that qualify an asset for it, which is what makes this column a declining series by construction.
evidence_quote: the indexation method (see note 2 of the worksheet) for capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11.45am (by legal time in the ACT) on 21 September 1999 and owned for at least 12 months
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the raw OF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the method is closed to assets acquired after 1999.

value_domain: Net capital gain, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The part of the entity's net capital gain that fell outside both the discount and the indexation methods, which the ATO defines residually as "the 'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)". In practice it is dominated by assets held less than twelve months, so for a company it is usually where most of the net gain sits. The OF prefix marks the old-form label, dropped when the new form stopped splitting the net gain by method.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount at the net capital gain step of the schedule, computed as proceeds less cost base with no indexation and no discount applied.
limitation: It is not a clean measure of short-held disposals, because it is defined by exclusion and catches any gain the other two methods cannot take. For a company filer it is close to the whole net capital gain rather than a subset, so comparing its size with the discount column across entity types compares legal eligibility rather than trading behaviour.
rationale: The ATO guide defines the other method residually against the indexation and discount methods, which is what determines the mix of gains this column contains.
evidence_quote: the 'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the category is residual rather than a holding-period measure.

value_domain: Total CGT discount and small business concessions, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Everything the entity took off its discount-method gains: the CGT discount plus the three small business concessions. On a business file this is the single best measure of how much a small business exit was sheltered, but it hides the mix, and only the concession columns beside it separate a deferral from an exemption. OF and NF in the DIL label are the old-form and new-form wordings.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount of reduction, not a gain. Adding it to the individual concession columns double-counts.
limitation: The total treats a roll-over, which defers tax, the same as an exemption, which forgives it. The OF and NF reading is inferred.
rationale: The BLADE DIL label names the total of the CGT discount and small business concessions under the discount method, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule.
evidence_quote: small business 50% active asset reduction, small business retirement exemption, small business rollover.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Total concessions applied against capital gains, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The total taken off the entity's capital gains by the reductions that follow the loss steps, in the indexation-method column of the schedule. The two label wordings are not the same quantity: the old form's total covers the CGT discount together with the small business concessions, while the new form's covers the small business concessions alone. The ATO sequence behind it is fixed, with the discount applied at part F of the worksheet and the concessions at part G.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount summing the reductions applied after capital losses, reported against one calculation method on the old form and as a single figure on the new form.
limitation: A series spanning the form change is not continuous, and the break is not a level shift that can be adjusted away: dropping the discount out of the total changes what is being measured, not just its scale. The total also does not identify which concession did the work, so the active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over columns are needed to tell them apart.
rationale: The ATO guide sets out the order in which the CGT discount and the small business concessions are applied and where each is reported on the schedule, which is what shows the old-form and new-form totals to be different quantities.
evidence_quote: Your entity's net capital gain is the amount remaining after applying any current year capital losses, net capital losses from prior years, capital losses transferred in, the CGT discount and any applicable CGT small business concessions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that the two labels cover different reductions.

value_domain: Total CGT discount and small business concessions, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Everything the entity took off gains not worked out under the discount method: the three small business concessions, with no CGT discount in the total because none applies. For a company this is where nearly all concessional relief sits. OF and NF in the DIL label are the old-form and new-form wordings.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount of reduction, not a gain. Adding it to the individual concession columns double-counts.
limitation: The total treats a roll-over the same as an exemption. The OF and NF reading is inferred.
rationale: The BLADE DIL label names the total of the CGT discount and small business concessions for other capital gains, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule.
evidence_quote: small business 50% active asset reduction, small business retirement exemption, small business rollover.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address of a business location. A business with several sites has one row per location, so this identifier is what makes a site the unit of analysis rather than the business, and what follows a site across years and across changes of owning entity. It is the same address key the person-level products use, which is why a business location and a residence can be recognised as the same address without either holding one.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated, which the BLADE Data Item List gives as 24 alphanumeric characters. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a business or a site, so businesses sharing a building share the value, and a registered office that is an accountant's address is indistinguishable from a place of work. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The BLADE Data Item List names the field as a deidentified ARID on the Business Locations table and gives its valid response as 24 alphanumeric. ABS publishes what the Address Register and its identifier are.
evidence_quote: Identifier - deidentified ARID
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the DIL wording 'Identifier - deidentified ARID' with no explanation of what an ARID is, and gave its domain as 'open numeric domain' when the stored value is alphanumeric.

value_domain: Employee headcount derived from PAYG records
value_source: ABS, Jobs in Australia methodology, 2021-22
variable_description: How many employees the business paid, counted from its PAYG records rather than from a survey answer. The underlying record is annual: the ABS describes it as "The annual summary provided by an employer to the Australian Taxation Office with respect to an employee. This was previously known as the Pay As You Go payment summary", so anyone paid at any point in the year contributes. That makes it a count over the year, not staff on hand at a date.
description_source: ABS, Jobs in Australia methodology, 2021-22
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of payees for the financial year, with "." where the business has no PAYG data.
limitation: It is not the closing stock employment the ABS publishes from BLADE, which is derived from business activity statements, so the two will not agree and should not be spliced into one series. Seasonal and high-turnover businesses are most affected: a cafe that replaces its staff twice can show a headcount several times the number of people it employs at once.
rationale: The ABS Jobs in Australia methodology defines the PAYG payment summary as an annual employer-employee record and separately identifies the published BLADE employment measure as a closing stock from business activity statements, which is the contrast a reader of this column needs.
evidence_quote: The annual summary provided by an employer to the Australian Taxation Office with respect to an employee. This was previously known as the Pay As You Go payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-word label 'Headcount' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the count runs over the year rather than at a point in time.

value_domain: Ordinary weekly hours specified in a federal enterprise agreement
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE), data sources
variable_description: The number of hours the enterprise agreement says are to be regularly worked each week. It is a term of a negotiated instrument coded by the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations into the Workplace Agreements Database, so it records what the agreement promises rather than what anyone worked. The row is an agreement, not a business, so a firm covered by several agreements contributes several values.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE), data sources
value_definition: A number of hours per week, with the sentinel 111111111 standing for an agreement whose hours vary or are unknown rather than for a quantity.
limitation: The sentinel must be removed before any average or regression, because leaving it in moves a mean of about 38 hours into the millions. The column also cannot measure hours actually worked: overtime, averaging arrangements and part-time contracts all sit outside the agreement term, and the agreement covers only the employees within its scope.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page confirms the Workplace Agreements Database as a Department of Employment and Workplace Relations source integrated into BLADE, which fixes the provenance and the agreement-level unit; the coding rule for the sentinel comes from the custodian's own valid response text.
evidence_quote: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations: Workplace Agreements Database (WAD)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about hours regularly worked with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing flagged the 111111111 sentinel or the agreement-level unit.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag (Y = provision present)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset
variable_description: Marks that the federal enterprise agreement covering this business lets employees work longer days and fewer of them. The department's field guide gives the example "an agreement may allow employees to work 4 ten hour days per week", and separates the provision from rostered day off and paid time off arrangements. The row belongs to an agreement rather than to a firm, so a business appears in this module only for the years an agreement covering it was in force.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset
value_definition: A one-sided character flag taking Y where a departmental coder read the provision in the agreement text, and nothing otherwise. It sits in the hours of work block of the Workplace Agreements Database framework, beside averaged weekly hours and the ordinary days fields.
limitation: There is no N. A blank cannot separate an agreement that rules out a compressed week from a year in which the framework did not ask the question, and hours of work fields have been added and revised over the database's life. The flag also says nothing about how many of the firm's employees actually work compressed weeks.
rationale: The BLADE variable carries the Workplace Agreements Database field wording verbatim, and the department's published guide to the dataset defines the field and places it in the hours of work block.
evidence_quote: For example an agreement may allow employees to work 4 ten hour days per week.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the WAD field wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that the unit is an agreement, that the flag has no negative code, or that coverage is limited to federal enterprise agreements.
