value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag (Y = provision present)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset
variable_description: Marks that the covering enterprise agreement lets the workforce set some of its own hours by a majority vote. The department's guide reads: "The agreement allows the employees to decide some aspect of the hours they will work by a majority decision." It sits in the flexible working hours block, so it coexists with a fixed span of ordinary hours and describes start, finish and break times rather than total hours.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset
value_definition: A character flag taking Y alone. Its neighbours in the same block record negotiated hours, hours management may alter after consultation, and make-up time, so the four together describe who controls the roster.
limitation: A majority right written into an agreement is not evidence that employees ever exercised it, and the flag cannot be read as workplace flexibility in practice. Because the field carries no negative code, a business with no flag may simply have had no agreement coded in that year.
rationale: The variable reproduces a numbered field in the Workplace Agreements Database framework, and the department's guide gives the field's definition and the block it belongs to.
evidence_quote: The agreement allows the employees to decide some aspect of the hours they will work by a majority decision.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the WAD field text as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving no sign that this is an agreement-level right in the flexible working hours block rather than a measure of a firm's working arrangements.

value_domain: Compulsory overtime hours per week included in the agreement's averaged weekly hours
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: How many of the weekly hours recorded for the covering enterprise agreement are compulsory overtime rather than ordinary hours. It qualifies the averaged weekly hours field: a 40-hour figure that includes two compulsory overtime hours is a 38-hour ordinary week plus mandated overtime. Reading the hours field without this column overstates the ordinary week for agreements that build overtime in.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A numeric count of hours per week. The value 111111111 is a sentinel meaning the quantity varies or is unknown, and is not a count; zero and a blank both mean something different from it.
limitation: Any mean or sum that does not drop 111111111 first is wrong by orders of magnitude. Compulsory overtime in an agreement is also a maximum the employer may require, not hours actually worked, so the column cannot measure the firm's overtime bill.
rationale: The department publishes the Workplace Agreements Database and states that it records conditions information for federal enterprise agreements, including hours of work provisions, which is the block this field belongs to. The sentinel value is given in the BLADE data item list's own valid-response text.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and in particular never flagged 111111111 as a dump code, which is the single most damaging thing a reader could miss.

value_domain: Country of the company's headquarters (Dealroom company profile)
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: The country Dealroom records as the head office of the company behind this ABN, held constant across every year the ABN appears. It is the one column in the module that marks a foreign-headquartered firm inside an otherwise Australian business register, which matters for reading the venture funding and valuation fields beside it. Dealroom is a commercial startup and venture-funding database that the ABS lists as a requestable BLADE dataset for 2025.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: A country name held as a character string, drawn from Dealroom's company profile rather than from an ABS or ISO classification; the permitted set is the appendix list in the BLADE data item list.
limitation: Being time-invariant by construction, the column cannot date or even detect a head office moving country, and it back-fills the current country onto every earlier year. Dealroom's coverage is also skewed to venture-backed and technology firms, so a missing value across most of BLADE means the firm is not in Dealroom, not that it is headquartered in Australia.
rationale: The ABS page listing what BLADE contains confirms Dealroom as an integrated BLADE dataset and dates it, which establishes the provenance and vintage of the column; the field's own construction is given in the BLADE data item list.
evidence_quote: Additional requestable BLADE data include: ... Dealroom: 2025
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording about a time-invariant categorical variable and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what Dealroom is, why an Australian ABN can carry a foreign country, or that a blank means absence from Dealroom.

value_domain: ATO business industry code (five digits, ANZSIC-derived)
value_source: ATO, Business industry code tool
variable_description: The industry the sole trader nominated on the business schedule for the activity that earned the business most of its income. The ATO defines it as "a five-digit code you include on relevant tax returns and schedules that describes your main business activity", and adds that codes "are derived from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) codes and have been simplified for tax return reporting purposes". It is the taxpayer's own choice of code, so it is a self-classification rather than an ABS industry assignment.
description_source: ATO, Business industry code tool
value_definition: A five-digit character code with leading zeros significant, taken from the Business industry codes booklet for the relevant income year. The codes map onto ANZSIC 2006 but are collapsed for tax reporting, so a code is not itself an ANZSIC class.
limitation: It is not the ABS industry code attached to the business on the BLADE frame, and the two disagree for a large share of businesses, so an analysis that mixes them will double count industries. The code also persists until the taxpayer changes it, which means a genuine change of activity can go unrecorded for years.
rationale: The ATO's own tool page defines the business industry code, gives its length, states the ANZSIC derivation and explains the highest-gross-income rule for choosing between activities, which is exactly what this column holds.
evidence_quote: A business industry code (BIC) is a five-digit code you include on relevant tax returns and schedules that describes your main business activity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'ANZSIC code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which misleads: the value is a simplified tax code, not an ANZSIC class, and it is self-assessed rather than ABS-assigned.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Government grants, rebates, subsidies and fuel tax credits the sole trader counted as assessable income of the primary production side of the business. The ATO's test is broad: "government credits, grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies are assessable income of the recipient if they are received in, or in relation to, the carrying on of a business". It is the farm-facing twin of the non-primary production government payments column.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year at P8 Income label G. Fuel tax credits, the wine equalisation tax producer rebate, the excise refund scheme for alcohol manufacturers and the product stewardship for oil benefit are marked with a D in the adjacent type box.
limitation: Only assessable assistance is here. Tax-free Commonwealth, state and territory grants, including several disaster and pandemic payments, are excluded by instruction, so the column understates public support to the farm. It also names no programme, so a rise cannot be attributed to a policy.
rationale: The ATO instruction for this label defines what counts as assessable government industry assistance, lists the examples, and sets out the primary production column and the D type-box flag that this variable carries.
evidence_quote: Generally, government credits, grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies are assessable income of the recipient if they are received in, or in relation to, the carrying on of a business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label 'Assessable govt industry payments - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that tax-free grants are excluded or what the primary production split means.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Assessable government industry assistance the sole trader allocated to the non-farm side of the business. Employee subsidies, export incentive grants and industry restructuring payments all land here. The boundary with ordinary revenue is drawn by instruction rather than by the payer: "Don't show 'Medicare payments received by medical practices' at this question." Those go to other business income instead, which is why a medical practice can show nothing here while being largely publicly funded.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow at P8 Income label H, the non-primary production counterpart of label G, with the same D type-box marker for fuel tax credits and the listed rebates.
limitation: The primary and non-primary split is the taxpayer's own allocation of the business, not an industry classification, so it will not line up with the reported business industry code. Support delivered as a tax offset or a concessional rate never appears here at all, because it is not income.
rationale: The ATO instruction for this label sets the scope of assessable government industry assistance, gives the non-primary production label and states the Medicare exclusion that separates this column from other business income.
evidence_quote: Don't show ‘Medicare payments received by medical practices’ at this question. Show them at Other business income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Assessable govt industry payments - NPP' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, giving no way to tell it from the primary production column or from other business income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Debts the business wrote off as bad during the year and claimed against business income. The deduction is conditional: "You're not allowed a deduction for bad debts unless you have previously included the amount in your assessable income and it relates to money you lent in the ordinary course of a money-lending business or it represents a business loss or outgoing of a revenue nature." A debt must be bad, not merely doubtful, and accounting provisions for doubtful debts are excluded from this label.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year, split into primary and non-primary production columns. It records the write-off, not the debt outstanding; the trade debtors item holds the balance still owed.
limitation: The column dates a write-off decision, not a default. A business can carry an uncollectable debt for years and then clear the ledger in one year, so the timing tracks the taxpayer's bookkeeping rather than the customer's failure. Recovered bad debts come back as other business income, so the two columns never net.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the bad debts label states the deductibility conditions, the bad-not-doubtful test and the exclusion of doubtful debt provisions, which are the facts that decide what this column can be read as.
evidence_quote: You're not allowed a deduction for bad debts unless you have previously included the amount in your assessable income and it relates to money you lent in the ordinary course of a money-lending business or it represents a business loss or outgoing of a revenue nature.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Bad debts' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing distinguished a write-off from a provision or from the debtors balance.

value_domain: Backing business investment opt-out choice code
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation
variable_description: Whether the business opted out of Backing business investment accelerated depreciation for some, all or none of its eligible assets. The ATO makes the election asset by asset and irreversible: "If you choose not to apply backing business investment to an asset, you apply the general depreciation rules to that asset", and "The choice cannot be changed once made." A code here therefore records a deliberate tax planning decision in 2019-20 or 2020-21, not an eligibility outcome.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation
value_definition: A coded response with three meaningful values: 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets and 15 for none, with everything else an invalid or absent response. The choice was reported through the Backing business investment labels at Capital allowances on the 2021 return.
limitation: The measure ran for two income years only, so a blank in any other year means the label was not on the form rather than a decision to stay in. Small businesses using the simplified depreciation rules could not opt out at all, so their absence from the column is structural. The code also does not say what was deducted instead.
rationale: The ATO page for the measure defines who could opt out, that the choice is per asset and irreversible, and where it was reported on the return, which is what the three response codes distinguish.
evidence_quote: The choice can be made on an asset-by-asset basis. If you choose not to apply backing business investment to an asset, you apply the general depreciation rules to that asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw form question and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the measure covered only two years or that simplified-depreciation small businesses were barred from opting out.

value_domain: Count of depreciating assets opted out of Backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation
variable_description: How many eligible assets the business kept out of Backing business investment accelerated depreciation and depreciated under the general rules instead. Because the ATO placed no cap on how many assets a business could apply the measure to, this count is bounded only by what the firm bought. It is meaningful only beside the opt-out code, which says whether the election covered some assets, all of them or none.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation
value_definition: A count of assets held as a character field of up to five digits, so it is not a dollar amount and should not be summed with the opted-out value column.
limitation: A count of assets is not a measure of investment: one opted-out excavator can be worth more than fifty opted-out laptops, so ranking firms on this column ranks them on asset granularity. It also covers only the assets left out, and nothing on the schedule says how many assets stayed in.
rationale: The ATO page for the measure sets out the opt-out election, its asset-by-asset basis and the absence of any cap on eligible asset numbers, which is what makes this a count rather than a bounded flag.
evidence_quote: There is no limit on the number of eligible assets that you can apply accelerated depreciation to in an income year under backing business investment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the column counts assets rather than dollars or that it is populated only for two income years.

value_domain: Dollar value of depreciating assets opted out of Backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation
variable_description: The dollar value of the assets the business chose to leave out of Backing business investment accelerated depreciation. Read against the count column it gives an average opted-out asset value, which is the only sign on the return of what kind of capital the decision was about. The measure was aimed at larger items: the ATO notes the accelerated deduction "applies to eligible assets with a cost (or adjustable value if applicable) of $150,000 or more" for entities outside the simplified rules.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the cost or adjustable value of the opted-out assets, reported on the 2020 or 2021 return only.
limitation: The amount is the value opted out, not the tax forgone, and the deduction the business took instead under the general rules is nowhere on the schedule. For a passenger vehicle the car limit caps the depreciable cost, so a luxury vehicle's value here does not correspond to any claimable amount.
rationale: The ATO page defines the opt-out election and the cost thresholds and car limit that govern how an asset's value translates into a deduction, which is what a reader needs to interpret this dollar figure.
evidence_quote: Effectively, the backing business investment deduction applies to eligible assets with a cost (or adjustable value if applicable) of $150,000 or more
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the value opted out from the deduction, nor flag the two-year window.

value_domain: Australian postcode of the main business address
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Business information P2 to P6
variable_description: The postcode of the address the sole trader gave for the main business, which is where the taxpayer says the business operates from. The schedule asks for the business name and the business address of the main business as separate items, so this is a trading location rather than a postal address or a tax agent's address. One postcode is recorded for a business that may work from several sites or from none.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Business information P2 to P6
value_definition: A four-digit character postcode with leading zeros retained, so Northern Territory codes beginning 08 must not be read as numbers.
limitation: A sole trader whose work happens at clients' premises usually gives a home postcode, so this is a weak proxy for where economic activity occurs, and a business with several outlets is placed at only one. The value also persists until the taxpayer updates it, so a change of postcode dates the return, not the move.
rationale: The schedule's business information section is where the main business address is reported, and it distinguishes the main business address from the taxpayer's other addresses, which is the fact that gives this column its meaning.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Main business postcode' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the address is self-nominated, singular for multi-site businesses, and often a residence.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: One year's write-off of capital costs the business pooled against an identified business project. The ATO explains the mechanism: "Project amounts are allocated to a 'project pool'. Your deduction for project amounts allocated to a project pool is spread over the 'project life'." Feasibility studies, environmental assessments, site preparation and community infrastructure for a project are the kinds of spending that reach this label, so a non-zero value marks a firm undertaking a discrete, time-limited project rather than ordinary trading.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Reconciliation items label L, being the sum of the primary and non-primary production project pool deductions for the year.
limitation: It is a slice of a write-off, not the project's cost: the same capital spend reappears in this column every year of the project life at a declining amount, so summing across years double counts nothing but summing across firms mixes projects at different stages. A project with no inherent limited life attracts no deduction at all, so significant project spending can be invisible here.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instructions define a project amount, the project pool and the spreading of the deduction over the project life, which is what makes this column a periodic write-off rather than expenditure.
evidence_quote: Project amounts are allocated to a ‘project pool’. Your deduction for project amounts allocated to a project pool is spread over the ‘project life’.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Business deduction for project pool' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could easily have read the column as project expenditure in the year.

value_domain: ATO client market segment code
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: The ATO's own administrative size and sector band for the client behind the return, from micro business up to the large market. The six codes are government, large market, small to medium, micro business, individual and non-business, and not for profit. It is assigned on the ATO client register from turnover and entity type, not reported by the taxpayer, and the ATO uses it to route compliance and service work. For a BLADE user it is a ready-made size and sector band that is independent of the ANZSIC and employment columns.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: A three-letter code with six meaningful values — GOV, LGE, SME, MIC, INB and NFP — and everything else an invalid or absent response. The code is a client attribute for the income year, not a return item.
limitation: The turnover thresholds behind the segments are administrative and have been revised over time, so a firm can change segment without changing size, which breaks a segment-based panel. It is not the small business entity aggregated turnover test used for tax concessions and must not be substituted for it.
rationale: The ABS page confirms Business Income Tax as a BLADE dataset and its coverage, but no fetchable ATO page defines the six-value market segment codeset, so the reading of the codes rests on the BLADE data item list and general knowledge of ATO client segmentation.
evidence_quote: BLADE contains data items from the following datasets: ... Business Income Tax (BIT): 2001-02 to latest available
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Business market segment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say that the segment is assigned by the ATO rather than reported, or warn that the thresholds move.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation method code
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Which of the three permitted methods the business used to value the closing stock reported beside it. The ATO lets the taxpayer choose per item and per year between "C cost", "M market selling value" and "R replacement value", and where several methods were used only one is recorded: "If more than one method was used, select the letter that applies to the largest value." The choice is a lever on taxable income, so the code is a signal of tax position as much as of stock composition.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A coded response with three meaningful values: 5 for C cost, 10 for M market selling value and 15 for R replacement value, with everything else invalid or absent. It is the type box printed beside the closing stock amount.
limitation: One code stands for the whole stock figure, so a business valuing some items at cost and some at market is recorded as using only the method behind the larger value. A small business entity that elected not to account for a stock change under $5,000 simply repeats last year's code, so a stable code can mean no stocktake rather than a stable method.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists the three valuation letters, states that the choice may vary by item and year, and gives the largest-value tie-break, which is exactly what this coded column carries.
evidence_quote: If more than one method was used, select the letter that applies to the largest value
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Closing stock action code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained the largest-value tie-break or the small business election that freezes the code.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: The tax value of trading stock the business held at the end of the income year. The ATO defines it as "the total of the value of all items of trading stock, with the value of each item calculated for tax purposes in accordance with section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997", which means the figure follows the method recorded in the closing stock code column rather than any single accounting convention. It is a stock at 30 June, so it does not belong in a flow aggregate with the expense lines it sits among.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at the end of the income year, reported at P8 label M, and excluding input tax credits for a business registered for GST. It covers all stock on hand whether or not it has been paid for.
limitation: It is a tax value, not a market valuation, and a taxpayer may elect a value below all three methods where stock is obsolete. Small business entities may leave closing stock equal to opening stock when the difference is $5,000 or less, so a flat series can be an election rather than stable inventory.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the closing stock amount by reference to section 70-45, sets out the three valuation methods and the small business $5,000 election, and states that unpaid stock is included.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at Closing stock is the total of the value of all items of trading stock, with the value of each item calculated for tax purposes in accordance with section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Closing stock' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that it is a tax value and that the small business election can hold it flat.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: What the goods the business sold this year cost it: opening stock plus purchases and other direct costs, less closing stock. It is the first line of the P8 expense column and the one that turns the two stock balances into an expense, which is why it moves whenever a stock valuation moves. A services business with no trading stock leaves it blank, so a zero here is normal rather than suspicious.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, built by the schedule's cost of sales worksheet from stock on hand at each end of the year plus purchases. It can be negative, in which case an L is printed beside it.
limitation: It is not cash the business paid: a change of stock valuation method, or a small business election not to account for a stock movement, shifts cost of sales without any change in trading. Contract labour recorded in the cost of sales account also sits inside it and is excluded from the contractor expenses column, so the two cannot be added to get total input costs.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the cost of sales worksheet, its dependence on opening and closing stock, the negative-value convention, and the exclusion of cost-of-sales labour from the contractor label.
evidence_quote: For more information on stock on hand at 1 July 2024, see Opening stock. For more information on stock on hand at 30 June 2025, see Closing stock.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Cost of sales' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never flagged that the figure is derived from two stock valuations and can be negative.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Trade debtors and creditors P13 and P14
variable_description: What the business owed its suppliers at year end for goods and services it had already received. The ATO defines the label as "the total amount owed by the business at the end of the year for goods and services received during 2024-25 (that is, current trade and other creditors)". It is one of only two balance sheet figures on the whole schedule, the other being trade debtors, and together they give a crude working capital position.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Trade debtors and creditors P13 and P14
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at 30 June reported at P14 label F, aggregated over every business the taxpayer runs, covering current trade and other creditors only.
limitation: It is not the firm's debt. Bank loans, hire purchase liabilities, tax debts and provisions sit outside it, so a low figure is compatible with heavy borrowing. A blank is also indistinguishable from a nil balance, because the label is only completed where the taxpayer answers yes to having creditors.
rationale: The ATO instruction for P14 gives the label's definition verbatim and its aggregation across the taxpayer's businesses, which is what fixes it as a current-liability balance rather than total liabilities.
evidence_quote: This is the total amount owed by the business at the end of the year for goods and services received during 2024–25 (that is, current trade and other creditors).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Trade creditors' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that it excludes borrowings or that blank and nil are not separable.

value_domain: Dollar bonus deduction claimed under the small business skills and training boost
value_source: ATO, Small business skills and training boost
variable_description: The extra deduction the business claimed for sending its employees to external training. The ATO describes the measure as "an additional 20% tax deduction for external training courses delivered to employees by registered training providers", available to businesses under $50 million in aggregated annual turnover for spending between 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2024. A value here is therefore evidence of employer-funded formal training, sized at one fifth of the bill.
description_source: ATO, Small business skills and training boost
value_definition: Whole dollars of bonus deduction, calculated as 20 per cent of eligible training expenditure and claimed on top of the ordinary deduction for the same spend.
limitation: Training of the sole trader themselves is excluded, so a business with no employees is structurally zero no matter how much it spends on skills. Only expenditure charged by a registered provider qualifies, which excludes in-house and informal training, and the delayed claim rule can push the bonus into a later year than the spending, breaking the alignment between column and training year.
rationale: The ATO page for the measure gives the rate, the turnover threshold, the eligibility window and the exclusions for non-employee owners and unregistered providers, which are what bound this column.
evidence_quote: Small businesses with an aggregated annual turnover of less than $50 million will be allowed an additional 20% tax deduction for external training courses delivered to employees by registered training providers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Small business skills and training boost' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column is a fifth of the spend, is employee-only, or exists for a short window.

value_domain: Dollar bonus deduction claimed under the small business technology investment boost
value_source: ATO, Small business technology investment boost
variable_description: The extra deduction the business claimed for digitising its operations — hardware, software, cloud subscriptions, e-commerce and cyber security. The ATO sets the window and the cap: "The boost applies to eligible expenditure incurred between 7:30 pm AEDT on 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2023. The boost is for business expenses and depreciating assets and is capped at $100,000 of expenditure per income year." It is the closest thing on the return to a direct measure of small business digital spending.
description_source: ATO, Small business technology investment boost
value_definition: Whole dollars of bonus deduction at 20 per cent of eligible digital expenditure, capped at $20,000 in an income year and $40,000 across the life of the measure.
limitation: The cap censors the measure from above: every business spending more than $100,000 a year on digital items reports the same $20,000, so the column cannot rank heavy investors. The window also closes a full year earlier than the skills and training boost, so the two columns must not be treated as a matched pair across years.
rationale: The ATO page for the measure gives the rate, the expenditure cap, the bonus cap, the eligibility window and the list of qualifying digital expenditure, which together define what this dollar figure can represent.
evidence_quote: An annual cap applies so that expenditure up to $100,000 is eligible for the bonus deduction, with the bonus deduction capped at $20,000 per year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label 'Small business technology investment boost' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention the cap that flattens the top of the distribution.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: What the taxpayer paid an associate for principal work and deducted against personal services income. The instruction is short: "Add up the total amount of payments made to associates for principal work." Principal work is the work that actually generates the income rather than support work, and the personal services income rules deny deductions for paying an associate to do anything else, so this label is the narrow channel through which family payments survive.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label K. It is one of the two deduction labels subtracted from gross personal services income to reach net personal services income, the other being all other deductions at label L.
limitation: It records the payments that met the principal work test, not what the business paid its associates, so it understates family payments by exactly the amount the rules disallowed. A zero is the norm and says nothing about whether associates were engaged.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines this label, the principal work concept and the personal services income limitation on associate deductions, and places the label in the net personal services income calculation.
evidence_quote: Add up the total amount of payments made to associates for principal work.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deductions for payments to associates for principal work' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say that the personal services income rules deny the rest of such payments.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Trade debtors and creditors P13 and P14
variable_description: What customers still owed the business at year end for goods and services already delivered. The ATO defines the label as "the total amount owing to the business at the end of the year for goods and services provided during 2024-25 (that is, current trade and other debtors)". Divided into other business income it gives a rough days-sales-outstanding for a sole trader, which is otherwise unobtainable from a tax return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Trade debtors and creditors P13 and P14
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at 30 June at P13 label E, summed across all of the taxpayer's businesses and limited to current trade and other debtors.
limitation: The balance carries no ageing and no doubtful debt provision, so it cannot separate normal credit terms from collection trouble; the bad debts column is the only companion for that. A business accounting on a cash basis reports little here regardless of turnover.
rationale: The ATO instruction for P13 gives the definition verbatim and states that multiple businesses are added together, which is what makes this an aggregated current-asset balance.
evidence_quote: This is the total amount owing to the business at the end of the year for goods and services provided during 2024–25 (that is, current trade and other debtors).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Trade debtors' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no way to see that the figure is a balance rather than a flow or that cash-basis businesses under-report it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: The depreciation charged in the business's own books for the year, which is not the same as the tax deduction for decline in value. The ATO is explicit: "You show at P8 - label M Depreciation expenses the depreciation you claim in your accounting books other than for those assets you allocate in a prior income year to a general pool." The difference between the book charge and the tax amount is taken out at the expense reconciliation adjustment label.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting charge for the income year, split into primary and non-primary production columns, with pool deductions substituted where assets were allocated to a general pool in an earlier year.
limitation: Treating this column as a capital allowance overstates or understates the deduction by the whole reconciliation adjustment, which is not recoverable from the schedule. It also depends on the taxpayer's own accounting policy, so two identical businesses on different effective lives report different numbers for the same assets.
rationale: The ATO instruction states directly that this label carries book depreciation rather than the tax deduction, and directs the difference to the expense reconciliation adjustment label.
evidence_quote: You show at P8 – label M Depreciation expenses the depreciation you claim in your accounting books other than for those assets you allocate in a prior income year to a general pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Depreciation expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invites the exact mistake of reading a book charge as a capital allowance.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: Losses from an earlier year that the non-commercial loss rules parked, now brought against this year's non-primary-production activity. The ATO defines it as "a loss you incur in a prior year which you were unable to claim against other income", and it can only be applied to an activity that is the same as or similar to the one that produced it. Subtracting it from the current year's non-primary result is what produces the final net figure that reaches the return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label E, the non-primary production counterpart of label D, applied only against a same or similar activity.
limitation: It shows the loss used this year, not the stock of deferred losses the business is carrying, and the unused balance appears nowhere on the schedule. Bankruptcy or release from debt extinguishes deferred losses outright, so a drop to zero can be insolvency rather than absorption.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines the deferred non-commercial business loss, restricts its use to a same or similar activity, and states the bankruptcy consequence, all of which decide how this column can be read.
evidence_quote: A deferred non-commercial business loss is a loss you incur in a prior year which you were unable to claim against other income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish losses applied from losses held.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: Farm losses deferred under the non-commercial loss rules in an earlier year and applied this year against the same or a similar primary production activity. The amount available can shrink for reasons unrelated to trading: "Your prior year deferred non-commercial business loss for a business activity may be reduced if you earned net exempt income in 2024-25." It is the primary production twin of the non-primary deferred loss column and is subtracted from the current year farm result.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label D. The schedule takes it before the final primary production net income figure, and it is excluded from the current-year net income column by instruction.
limitation: Primary producers have their own exceptions to the non-commercial loss rules, so a nil here does not mean the farm made no loss — the loss may have been deductible in the year it arose and never deferred at all. The column also cannot separate a farm that used up its deferred losses from one that had none.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction gives the primary production label, the same or similar activity restriction and the exempt income reduction, which is what distinguishes this column from the non-primary one.
evidence_quote: Your prior year deferred non-commercial business loss for a business activity may be reduced if you earned net exempt income in 2024–25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not note the primary production exceptions that make a nil ambiguous.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Total expenses of the non-farm side of the business for the year, adding every line in that column of P8. The ATO builds it mechanically: "Add up all the expenses you have written in the Non-primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses." Subtracting it from total non-primary business income gives book profit, not taxable income, because the reconciliation items sit outside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 label T, running from cost of sales through to all other expenses. It can be negative, in which case an L is printed beside it.
limitation: The total contains book depreciation and non-deductible items, so it is an accounts figure rather than a deduction total, and the gap is only recoverable through the expense reconciliation adjustment column. Cost of sales inside it moves with stock valuations, so the total shifts with a valuation change alone.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines exactly which lines are added into this total, its label, and the negative-value convention.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Non-primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Total Expenses - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that this is a book total that excludes reconciliation items.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Total expenses of the farming side of the business for the year. The ATO's rule is the mirror of the non-primary total: "Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses." A business with no farming activity leaves it blank, so this column doubles as a marker of which returns carry a primary production activity at all.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 label S, covering the primary production column only; the non-primary total at label T has to be added to it for a whole-of-business expense figure.
limitation: The split between the two columns is the taxpayer's own apportionment of shared costs such as rent, interest and vehicles, and no rule forces the apportionment to stay constant, so a business that changes its allocation moves both totals with no change in trading. The column also cannot be reconciled to any ANZSIC-based idea of agriculture.
rationale: The ATO instruction states the exact set of lines summed into the primary production total and its label, which is what separates it from the non-primary total.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total Expenses - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never explained that the primary and non-primary split is a self-allocation.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The single net adjustment that converts the business's book expenses into deductible expenses. The ATO defines it as "your total expense add-backs less your total expense subtractions", where add-backs are "expenses shown in the accounts which aren't tax deductible" and subtractions are deductible items the accounts never showed. Without this column, total business income less total expenses is book profit, not the figure the tax system acts on.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 Reconciliation items label H, printed with an L beside it when negative, and covering the primary and non-primary production businesses together.
limitation: One net number hides everything inside it. Accounting depreciation added back and tax decline in value subtracted both land here, so a large value cannot be read as aggressive non-deductible spending; it may be nothing more than a capital allowance timing difference. Denied thin capitalisation and debt deduction creation amounts are also buried in the same figure.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction lists what goes into add-backs and subtractions and defines the reported amount as the net of the two, which is what makes this column uninterpretable line by line.
evidence_quote: Your expense reconciliation adjustment is your total expense add-backs less your total expense subtractions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Expense reconciliation adjustment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving a reader no idea that depreciation timing differences dominate the number.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: What the business paid for labour it bought in rather than employed. The ATO defines the label as "expenses for labour and services provided under contract, other than salaries or wages", covering consultants and contractors, labour-hire payments, commissions to people not on a retainer, and agency, service, management and consultant fees. The BLADE label records that the form used to call this external labour costs, so a series across the rename is one item under two names rather than two items.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Expenses label F, split into primary and non-primary production columns and totalled.
limitation: It is not the firm's total spend on outside labour. Contract labour already recorded in the cost of sales account is excluded, accounting and legal fees go to all other expenses, and payments made without meeting withholding obligations are excluded from the deduction altogether, so three different rules push spending out of this column.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, lists what belongs in it and gives the three exclusions that determine what is missing from it; the rename is recorded in the BLADE data item list itself.
evidence_quote: These are expenses for labour and services provided under contract, other than salaries or wages
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label including the rename note with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never named the exclusions that make this an incomplete measure of contracted labour.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Expenses the business incurred directly in earning income that was subject to foreign resident withholding. It is a non-primary-production-only label — the ATO states that "You'll not have any primary production expense amounts at this question" — and it pairs with the foreign resident withholding income column so that the two can be read as a margin on that narrow stream of work.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Expenses label U, entered in the non-primary production column and transferred straight to the totals box.
limitation: Very few taxpayers report anything here, so any ratio built on it rests on a tiny denominator and is not a population statistic. Anything connected with foreign resident capital gains withholding is out of scope by instruction and never reaches the schedule at all.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, restricts it to the non-primary production column and excludes foreign resident capital gains withholding, which sets both what it holds and what it cannot hold.
evidence_quote: You'll not have any primary production expense amounts at this question.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Foreign resident withholding expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the column is almost entirely empty.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Gross payments the business received that were subject to foreign resident withholding, before the tax withheld was taken out. The ATO defines it as "the total income you receive from your payers that is subject to foreign resident withholding", and adds that "It includes any amounts of tax withheld." The figure is reconciled to the taxpayer's PAYG payment summary schedule, so it is administrative rather than self-estimated.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label B, gross of withholding and reported in the non-primary production column only, calculated from payment summaries with an F in the type box.
limitation: Foreign resident withholding covers a narrow set of activities, mainly construction, entertainment and sports, and casino gaming junkets, so a nil here is not evidence that the business has no foreign dealings. Amounts subject to foreign resident capital gains withholding are excluded by instruction and go to the capital gains question instead.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, states that it is gross of tax withheld, ties it to the payment summary schedule and excludes capital gains withholding.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label B is the total income you receive from your payers that is subject to foreign resident withholding. It includes any amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Gross payments subject to FRW - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is gross of withholding or how narrow the underlying regime is.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: The primary production column for gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding, which the current schedule does not provide a label for. The instructions carry only a non-primary production label for this income and send the whole amount straight to the totals box, so this column is a symmetry residual rather than a measured quantity. Read it beside the non-primary column, which holds the reported figure.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars, in the same units as its non-primary production twin. Any populated value would come from an earlier form layout or from an extract that keeps both columns for structural symmetry.
limitation: A zero here means the form has no matching label, not that no farm income was subject to foreign resident withholding. Adding it to the non-primary column produces a total identical to that column alone, so a reader who sums the pair gains nothing and may believe they have measured a split.
rationale: The ATO instruction for this income label provides only a non-primary production entry and transfers it directly to the totals box, which is the evidence that no primary production counterpart is collected on the current schedule.
evidence_quote: Step 2: Transfer the amount at label B to the adjacent Totals box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Gross payments subject to FRW - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know the column has no corresponding form label.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Gross income the business earned under a labour-hire arrangement or as a specified payment, including the tax withheld from it. The ATO defines the label as "the total income you receive from labour hire or specified payments and includes the tax that is withheld", and draws the line firmly at employment: "Don't include income you receive as an employee of a labour-hire business." A value here therefore marks contracted labour hire, not agency employment.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label O, non-primary production, built from payment summaries with an S in the type box.
limitation: Specified payments — Indigenous tutorial services, translating and interpreting work, and promotional appearances by performing artists — are pooled into the same label and cannot be separated from labour hire. Where the personal services income rules apply, the same kind of income is reported at the P1 labour hire label instead, so the two columns must not be added.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines this label, states that it is gross of withholding, lists the specified payments folded into it and excludes labour-hire employees.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at P8 Income – label O is the total income you receive from labour hire or specified payments and includes the tax that is withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Gross payments Labour Hire - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish contractors from labour-hire employees or flag the overlap with the personal services income labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Farm income the business received under a PAYG voluntary agreement to withhold, gross of the tax withheld. A voluntary agreement is an arrangement a payer and a contractor enter into so that tax is withheld from payments that would otherwise carry none, so the column measures a withholding arrangement rather than a kind of work. The ATO says the label holds "the total income you receive that is subject to a voluntary agreement to withhold tax and include the tax withheld".
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label E, in the primary production column, taken from payment summaries with a V in the type box.
limitation: Voluntary agreements are uncommon in agriculture, so this label is thin next to its non-primary production twin and a nil says nothing about how the farm was paid. The column also cannot show the withheld amount, which is reported separately on the supplementary return.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the voluntary agreement labels, states that they are gross of tax withheld and identifies the primary production label and the V type-box source.
evidence_quote: The amounts you show at P8 Income – labels E and F is the total income you receive that is subject to a voluntary agreement to withhold tax and include the tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross payments voluntary agreement - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that a voluntary agreement is an elected withholding arrangement.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Non-farm income received under a PAYG voluntary agreement to withhold, gross of tax withheld. The ATO builds it from payer documents: "Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule derived from non-primary production activities that have a V in the Type box." This is the label most contractors with a voluntary agreement use, and it is far more populated than the primary production one beside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label F. Where the taxpayer's income falls under the personal services income rules, the equivalent voluntary agreement amount goes to the P1 voluntary agreement label instead.
limitation: The same payment can appear here or at the personal services income label depending on whether the taxpayer passes the personal services business tests, so a firm moving across that boundary shifts income between columns with no change in what it does. Adding the two columns therefore risks double counting nothing, but comparing them across years risks reading a legal reclassification as a change in trading.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the non-primary production label, the V type-box construction and the separate personal services income treatment of the same arrangement.
evidence_quote: Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule derived from non-primary production activities that have a V in the Type box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Gross payments voluntary agreement - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not flag the personal services income routing that moves the same income elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: The primary production labour-hire label, which the ATO instructs taxpayers to leave empty. Its wording is unambiguous: "It is expected you'll not have any primary production amounts at this question. Leave P8 Income - label N blank." The column exists to keep the primary and non-primary production columns symmetrical, and the reported figure for labour hire sits in the non-primary column beside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label N, the primary production counterpart of label O, expected to be blank on every return.
limitation: A non-zero value is more likely a lodgment error than farm labour-hire income, so it should be inspected rather than aggregated. The column cannot be used to measure labour hire in agriculture; that would require the non-primary production label, which does not distinguish industry at all.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the labour hire question states directly that the primary production label is expected to be blank, which is the fact that determines what this column can mean.
evidence_quote: It is expected you'll not have any primary production amounts at this question. Leave P8 Income – label N blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross payments Labour Hire - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have treated it as a real farm labour-hire measure.

value_domain: Dollar cost of intangible depreciating assets first deducted
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Depreciating assets P17 to P20
variable_description: The cost of intangible assets the business started depreciating this year. Patents, registered designs, copyright, acquired or commissioned software, mining rights and spectrum licences all qualify. The ATO defines the label as "the cost of all intangible depreciating assets that you're claiming a business deduction for decline in value for the first time". Because it is a cost of new assets rather than a deduction, it is the schedule's closest proxy for intangible investment in the year.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Depreciating assets P17 to P20
value_definition: Whole dollars of cost at P17 label I, not reduced for estimated non-taxable use, and including intangible assets under $1,000 allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules do not complete the label at all, so the column is systematically blank for most small firms, and in-house software allocated to a software development pool is excluded outright. Software investment is therefore undercounted by both rules at once.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists which intangibles are depreciating assets, defines the label as first-year cost, excludes simplified-depreciation taxpayers and excludes software development pool expenditure.
evidence_quote: At P17 Intangible depreciating assets first deducted you need to show the cost of all intangible depreciating assets that you're claiming a business deduction for decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Intangible depreciating assets first deducted' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that small business entities and software pools are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Interest the business paid to lenders in Australia during the year, as its accounts recorded it. The schedule keeps it apart from lease charges and from the interest inside a hire purchase agreement, so the column is narrower than the firm's total financing cost. Any part of it that the thin capitalisation or debt deduction creation rules deny is still shown here and taken out later at the expense reconciliation adjustment label.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense for the year, entered in the primary and non-primary production columns and totalled; it sits immediately before the overseas interest label so that the two can be compared.
limitation: It is a cost, not a debt: nothing on the schedule gives the loan balance, the interest rate or the lender, and the only other liability figure is trade creditors. Interest capitalised into an asset's cost never appears here at all, so a firm financing construction can show low interest and high depreciation.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction gives this label its own question, separates it from lease and hire purchase costs and from overseas interest, and directs denied debt deductions to the reconciliation label.
evidence_quote: Don't include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Interest expenses in Australia' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that denied deductions remain inside the figure or that no balance is available.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Interest the business paid to lenders outside Australia, reported at its own label so it cannot be netted against domestic interest. A non-zero value marks a sole trader borrowing offshore or from a related foreign party, which is the pattern the thin capitalisation and debt deduction creation rules are aimed at. It is one of very few signals of cross-border financing anywhere on an individual's business schedule.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense for the year, the overseas twin of the Australian interest label, split by primary and non-primary production.
limitation: Overseas is defined by where the lender sits, not by the currency of the loan or where the borrowed money was spent, so a foreign-currency facility from an Australian bank is not here. Withholding tax paid on the interest is reported elsewhere, so the column cannot be used to estimate interest withholding.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction gives overseas interest its own question and label, distinct from Australian interest, and routes denied debt deductions to the reconciliation label, which fixes what the column separates.
evidence_quote: Don't include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Interest expenses overseas' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that the split is by lender location rather than by currency.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: What the business paid to lease plant, equipment or vehicles during the year. The boundary with instalment purchase is sharp: "Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses." Those are handled through the reconciliation label instead, so two firms with identical equipment can report very different lease figures depending only on how they financed it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense for the year, split into primary and non-primary production columns. Rent for land and buildings is a separate label, so this figure does not include premises rent.
limitation: The column mixes operating and finance leases as the accounts recorded them, and the non-deductible or capital parts are stripped out later at the reconciliation label, so it is not a deduction. A car leased above the car limit is subject to special rules that this single number cannot show.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction defines the lease expenses label, excludes hire purchase, notes the car limit rules and keeps rent of land and buildings at a separate label.
evidence_quote: Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Lease expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not separate leasing from hire purchase or from premises rent.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: Deductions for landcare work and for the decline in value of water facilities, fencing and fodder storage assets. The ATO allows the landcare part in full in the year it is spent: "You can claim a deduction for capital expenditure you incur on a landcare operation for land in Australia in the year you incur it, if you're carrying on a primary production business." A value here identifies a farm making on-farm capital improvements, which is otherwise invisible in the expense lines.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Reconciliation items label W, the sum of the primary and non-primary production columns. Landcare and water facilities can appear in both columns; fencing and fodder storage assets are primary production only.
limitation: Four separate concessions are added into one number, so a dam, a fence and a silo cannot be told apart. A small business entity that claimed the same asset under the simplified depreciation rules must leave it out of this label, so a farm with real capital spending can still report nothing here.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines the landcare deduction, lists what a water facility covers, restricts fencing and fodder storage to primary production, and excludes assets claimed under simplified depreciation.
evidence_quote: You can claim a deduction for capital expenditure you incur on a landcare operation for land in Australia in the year you incur it, if you're carrying on a primary production business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that simplified depreciation removes assets from the column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: What the business claimed for running motor vehicles, with the capital and financing side stripped out. The ATO is explicit about the exclusions: "Don't include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid", which go to the depreciation, lease and interest labels instead. Ride-sourcing vehicle costs belong here, so the column picks up gig-economy driving as a business expense.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Expenses label N, split into primary and non-primary production columns, with the calculation method recorded in the adjacent type box column.
limitation: The number's meaning depends on the method code beside it. A cents-per-kilometre claim is a statutory rate applied to distance and does not measure what the vehicle cost, while a logbook claim is a business-use share of actual outlays, so pooling the two compares two different constructions rather than two levels of spending.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction defines the label, states the depreciation, lease and interest exclusions, includes ride-sourcing, and sets out the method codes that qualify the amount.
evidence_quote: Don't include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Motor vehicle expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not tie the amount to the method code that determines how it was constructed.

value_domain: Motor vehicle expense calculation method code
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: How the business worked out the motor vehicle amount beside it, or a marker that the vehicle sits outside the car substantiation rules. The current schedule offers two methods — "S if you used the 'cents per kilometre' method" and "B if you used the 'logbook' method" — plus code N for a motorcycle, a taxi taken on hire, or a vehicle carrying a tonne or more or nine or more passengers. Where a taxpayer has more than one code, only the one covering the largest claim is kept.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A coded response with five values in the BLADE frame: 5 for S cents per kilometre, 15 for O one-third of actual expenses, 20 for B logbook, 30 for T 12 per cent of original value and 35 for N vehicles outside the car rules. Anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The one-third of actual expenses and 12 per cent of original value methods were withdrawn after 2014-15, so codes 15 and 30 appear only in earlier years and a method series spanning the change is not continuous. The largest-claim rule also means the code describes part of the amount, not all of it.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction lists the current method letters, the N category and the largest-claim tie-break, and the presence of the O and T codes in the BLADE frame dates the column to the earlier four-method regime.
evidence_quote: S if you used the ‘cents per kilometre’ method
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the five-value code list with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that two of the five methods were abolished, which is what breaks the series.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The farming business's own result for the year, before any losses deferred from earlier years are brought in. The ATO's instruction for this step says plainly: "Don't include any non-commercial business loss deferred from a prior year." That makes it the cleanest available measure of current-year primary production performance, and it is not the figure that reaches the tax return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount for the income year, printed with an L beside it when it is a loss. It is total primary production business income less total primary production expenses, after the income and expense reconciliation adjustments.
limitation: Using this column as farm income overstates it for any business carrying deferred non-commercial losses, because those are subtracted afterwards to produce the figure that is transferred to the return. It also aggregates every primary production activity the person runs, so a profitable enterprise and a loss-making one cancel inside it.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines this step, excludes deferred non-commercial losses from it, and shows the later step that applies them, which is what separates this column from the final net primary production figure.
evidence_quote: Don't include any non-commercial business loss deferred from a prior year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net income or loss from business this year - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it could not be told apart from the post-deferral net primary production column in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
