variable_description: The non-farm business result that actually reaches the tax return, after deferred non-commercial losses have been applied. The ATO flags the difference from the current-year figure directly: "This amount takes into account non-commercial losses deferred from a prior year." It is transferred to the income question in the individual's supplementary return, so it is the number the tax system acts on.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 label Z, with an L printed beside it when it is a loss, carried to label C of question 15 in the supplementary return.
limitation: A loss here triggers a further reporting obligation for business loss activity details, so a loss is a year with consequences rather than simply a bad year, and the reporting itself may shape what is declared. The figure also pools every non-primary business the person runs and cannot be attributed to one activity.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines this label as the post-deferral figure, gives its transfer to the supplementary return and states the loss reporting consequence.
evidence_quote: This amount takes into account non-commercial losses deferred from a prior year.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The farming business result that reaches the tax return, after deferred non-commercial losses have been applied. The ATO closes the step by moving it off the schedule: "Transfer the amounts at Y and Z to B and C (respectively) question 15 in your supplementary tax return." It is the primary production twin of the post-deferral non-primary column, and differs from the current-year primary production figure by exactly the deferred loss applied.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 label Y, flagged with an L when it is a loss, and transferred to label B of question 15 in the supplementary return.
limitation: Primary production income is subject to income averaging and to farm management deposits elsewhere in the individual's return, so this column is not the amount the farmer is finally assessed on. A farm that moved activities between the primary and non-primary columns also breaks its own series here without any change in operations.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines the post-deferral primary production label and its transfer to the supplementary return, which is what separates it from the current-year primary production figure.
evidence_quote: Step 4: Transfer the amounts at Y and Z to B and C (respectively) question 15 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net income/loss - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which is indistinguishable from the current-year primary production column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Non-farm income paid to the business with tax withheld because it did not quote an ABN to the payer. The ATO defines the pair of labels as "the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN". A non-zero value is a compliance signal rather than an income type: it says the business traded without a quoted ABN with at least one payer, which typically happens around registration or lapse.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label D, gross of the tax withheld, taken from payment summaries with an N in the type box for non-primary production activities.
limitation: The column cannot tell you how much tax was withheld — that is a separate label on the supplementary return — and it names no payer, so the exposure cannot be traced. It is also not a measure of cash economy activity: a payer who withholds is reporting the payment to the ATO.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines both no-ABN labels, ties them to the payment summary schedule and distinguishes the primary from the non-primary production column.
evidence_quote: The amounts you show at P8 Income – labels C and D is the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Gross Payment ABN not quoted - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what a value signals about the firm.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Farm income paid to the business with tax withheld because no ABN was quoted. The ATO builds it from the taxpayer's own payer documents: "Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box." It is the primary production twin of the non-primary no-ABN column.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label C, gross of tax withheld, in the primary production column.
limitation: Farm output is usually sold to processors, agents and saleyards that hold an ABN on file, so this label is sparse and a value is more often a new or lapsed registration than a persistent pattern. It also cannot separate one large payment from many small ones, so it is a poor basis for inferring how a farm sells.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the primary production label and its payment summary type-box construction, which is what distinguishes it from the non-primary label.
evidence_quote: Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross Payment ABN not quoted - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and offered no way to distinguish it from its non-primary twin.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The non-farm business result for the year in its own right, before deferred non-commercial losses are applied. It pools every non-primary activity the sole trader runs, and the ATO uses a loss in it as a trigger for further disclosure: a loss in any one activity means "you need to complete P3 Number of business activities and P9 Business loss activity details". The number of activities behind the figure is therefore only recoverable from a separate item.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount for the income year, the non-primary production counterpart of the current-year primary production figure, printed with an L when it is a loss.
limitation: A profitable business and a loss-making one net off inside this single number, so it cannot be used to count failing activities. It is also not the figure carried to the tax return, which is the post-deferral non-primary net income column, so the two must not be used interchangeably.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines the current-year net income step, excludes deferred losses from it and states the multi-activity disclosure trigger that reveals its aggregation.
evidence_quote: If the amount at label B or C includes details from more than one business activity, and any one of these activities resulted in a net loss, you need to complete P3 Number of business activities and P9 Business loss activity details.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Net income or loss from business this year - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, indistinguishable from the post-deferral non-primary column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: The tax value of trading stock the business held at the start of the income year. It is not an independent observation: the ATO ties it to the previous return, since "The value of your stock on hand at the start of the income year is the same value as the closing value shown in your schedule in the previous year." Stock of a business that commenced during the year is excluded, so a first-year business reports nothing here.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at 1 July, equal by rule to the prior year's closing stock for the same items, and split into primary and non-primary production columns before being totalled.
limitation: Because it is defined as last year's closing value, it inherits last year's valuation method and any small business election not to account for a stock movement, so a difference between opening and closing stock measures a reported change rather than a physical one. It also cannot be used to check the previous return, since the two are the same number by construction.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction defines opening stock by reference to the previous year's closing value and excludes stock of a business that commenced during the year.
evidence_quote: The value of your stock on hand at the start of the income year is the same value as the closing value shown in your schedule in the previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Opening stock' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that it is last year's closing value by rule rather than a fresh measurement.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Ordinary trading income of the farming business — despite the name, this is the main revenue line for most farms. The ATO's list starts with "gross sales of trading stock" and "gross sales from produce", and then reaches non-cash items including goods taken from stock for own use, the "value of livestock killed for rations" and livestock exchanged for other goods or services. Everything already reported at the withholding, government payment and labour hire labels is excluded from it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 Income label I; a loss is possible and is flagged with an L. Primary producers build it from the gross income from primary production worksheet before entering it.
limitation: Treating this as miscellaneous income understates farm turnover badly, because it is where sales land. It also mixes cash sales with imputed non-cash amounts such as rations and own use, so it is not a receipts figure and cannot be reconciled to a bank statement.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists what other business income comprises, states the exclusions against the other income labels and gives the primary production worksheet route into this label.
evidence_quote: Other business income includes: gross sales of trading stock, gross sales from produce, goods taken from stock for your own use, value of livestock killed for rations
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Other business income - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, inviting a reader to treat the largest revenue line on a farm return as a residual.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Ordinary trading income of the non-farm business, which for most sole traders is nearly all of their turnover. It reaches beyond invoiced sales to platform work: the ATO includes "income earned through the sharing economy, or other marketplace, where you're carrying on a business", along with rent from a renting business, royalties, insurance recoveries and profit on selling a depreciating asset. It excludes everything shown at the withholding, government payment and labour hire labels.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 Income label J, the non-primary production counterpart of label I, with a loss flagged by an L.
limitation: It absorbs one-off items — insurance payouts, gains on selling equipment, foreign exchange gains — alongside recurring sales, so a single year's figure is a poor measure of trading and a spike may be an asset disposal. Ride-sourcing and taxi income may sit here or at the personal services income item depending on the taxpayer, so the column is not a stable definition of gig work.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists what other business income comprises, including sharing economy earnings and one-off recoveries, and states the exclusions against the other income labels.
evidence_quote: income earned through the sharing economy, or other marketplace, where you're carrying on a business
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other business income - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing signalled that this is the main turnover line and that it carries one-off gains.

value_domain: Dollar cost of tangible depreciating assets first deducted
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Depreciating assets P17 to P20
variable_description: The cost of tangible assets the business began depreciating this year — plant, vehicles, equipment and fit-out. The ATO defines the label as "the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time". Because it is cost rather than deduction, it is the closest the schedule comes to gross fixed capital formation by a sole trader.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Depreciating assets P17 to P20
value_definition: Whole dollars of cost at P18 label J, not reduced for estimated private use, and including assets under $1,000 allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules do not complete the label, so the column is systematically missing for the smallest firms and thins out further in years when the instant asset write-off threshold was high. It also counts assets first deducted, so a second-hand asset already depreciated by its previous owner still appears as new investment here.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label as first-year cost of non-intangible depreciating assets, excludes simplified-depreciation taxpayers and states the low-value pool inclusion and the no-reduction-for-private-use rule.
evidence_quote: At P18 Other depreciating assets first deducted you need to include the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other depreciating assets first deducted' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no warning that small business entities are absent from the column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Everything the business spent that no named expense line covers, which for most sole traders includes the wages bill. The ATO defines it as "the total of all other expenses that you incur in deriving your profit or loss and you haven't already shown elsewhere at P8 Expenses", and lists wages, accounting and professional fees, advertising, office supplies, foreign exchange losses and any book loss on selling a depreciating asset. It is usually the largest single expense line on a services return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense at P8 Expenses label P, split into primary and non-primary production columns; business gifts and donations and fees paid to professionals for the business's tax affairs also belong here rather than in the individual's personal deductions.
limitation: Because wages are buried inside it, the column is not comparable across firms with different mixes of employed and contracted labour; the separate total salary and wage expenses item is the only way to pull wages back out. Capital and other non-deductible items are also reported here and removed later at the reconciliation label, so it is not a deduction total.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label as the residual expense line, lists what belongs in it, and directs non-deductible amounts inside it to the reconciliation label.
evidence_quote: This is the total of all other expenses that you incur in deriving your profit or loss and you haven't already shown elsewhere at P8 Expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'All other expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned a reader that wages sit inside the residual line.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Payments to associated persons P16
variable_description: What the business paid relatives and related partnerships during the year. The ATO defines the item as "amounts, including salary, wages, commissions or allowances, paid to your relatives", and adds that "These also include super contributions paid for the benefit of your relatives." It is a disclosure item that supports the excessive payment test, so a value marks a family-staffed business rather than a separate category of spending.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Payments to associated persons P16
value_definition: Whole dollars at P16 label H, aggregated across the taxpayer's businesses. The salary and wage portion is also inside the total salary and wage expenses item, so the two items overlap by design.
limitation: Adding this column to the expense lines double counts, because the same payments already sit in wages or other expenses. It says nothing about how many relatives were paid or what work they did, and payments the ATO later treats as excessive and disallows still appear here at their full amount.
rationale: The ATO instruction for P16 defines what the item covers, requires the same amounts to be included in total salary and wages, and states the excessive payment rule that gives the disclosure its purpose.
evidence_quote: These are amounts, including salary, wages, commissions or allowances, paid to your relatives. These also include super contributions paid for the benefit of your relatives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Payments to associated persons' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the amounts are also counted inside the expense lines.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Personal services income received with tax withheld because the taxpayer did not quote an ABN to the payer. The ATO defines it as "your total PSI from which an amount is withheld because you didn't quote your ABN, including the amounts of tax withheld". It is one of the four gross labels that feed the net personal services income calculation, and it reports the same withholding event as the business no-ABN labels but for a different population.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label N, gross of tax withheld, taken from payment summaries with an N in the type box.
limitation: Income reaches P1 only where the personal services income rules apply, so a contractor moves between this column and the business no-ABN columns as their personal services business status changes, and the two sets must never be added. It also does not show the tax withheld, which is reported at the supplementary return.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines this label, states that it is gross of tax withheld, ties it to the payment summary type box and places it among the labels summed to reach net personal services income.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label N is your total PSI from which an amount is withheld because you didn't quote your ABN, including the amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'PSI where Australian Business Number not quoted' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never distinguished it from the identically named business income labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Personal services income earned under a labour-hire arrangement or as a specified payment, gross of tax withheld. The ATO defines the label as "the total income you receive from labour hire or other specified payments, including amounts of tax withheld", and specified payments here mean Indigenous tutorial services, translating and interpreting work, and promotional appearances by performing artists. Employment income from a labour-hire business is excluded and goes to the salary question on the individual return instead.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label O, built from payment summaries with an S in the type box, and one of the four gross personal services income labels added before deductions.
limitation: The three specified payment types are pooled with genuine labour hire and cannot be separated, so a rise in the column is not necessarily a rise in labour hire. A taxpayer can report labour hire at this label and other labour hire at the business income labels in the same year, so neither column alone measures the firm's labour-hire exposure.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, states that it is gross of withholding, lists the specified payments and excludes labour-hire employees.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label O is the total income you receive from labour hire or other specified payments, including amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'PSI labour hire or other specified payments' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the specified payments or the employment exclusion.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Net personal services income for the year: the four gross personal services income labels less the two personal services income deduction labels. The ATO's arithmetic is explicit — "Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1" — and the result is carried to the personal services income question on the supplementary return. A populated value means the personal services income rules applied to at least some of the taxpayer's income.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P1 label A, printed with an L beside it when it is a loss, and transferred to label A of question 14 in the supplementary return.
limitation: The column identifies a tax status, not an occupation: the personal services income rules turn on the results, unrelated clients, employment and business premises tests, so two people doing the same work can sit on opposite sides of it. Income earned through a personal services business is reported at the business income item instead, so a nil here does not mean the person sells no personal services.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the net personal services income calculation step by step, its label, the loss convention and the transfer to the supplementary return, and elsewhere sets out the tests that decide whether income reaches P1 at all.
evidence_quote: Step 3: Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1. Write your answer at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net PSI' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing told a reader that presence in the column is a legal test rather than a description of the work.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Personal services income that had no tax withheld at source, which is the residual of the four gross personal services income labels. The instruction is short and self-assessed: "Work out the total amount of other PSI and write this amount at P1 Personal services income (PSI) - label J." For a contractor invoicing clients directly with an ABN quoted and no voluntary agreement, this is where nearly all of their income lands.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label J, excluding GST for a taxpayer registered or required to be registered, and added to the three withholding labels to give gross personal services income.
limitation: It is the only personal services income label with no payment summary behind it, so it rests entirely on the taxpayer's own records and cannot be cross-checked against payer reporting the way the withholding labels can. A large value therefore carries a different evidential weight from the same amount at the withholding labels.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, gives the GST exclusion and places it among the labels summed in step 1 of the net personal services income calculation, which is what makes it the unreconciled residual.
evidence_quote: Work out the total amount of other PSI and write this amount at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label J.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'PSI other' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that this is the one personal services income label with no payer document behind it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: All deductions claimed against personal services income other than payments to associates for principal work. The ATO folds prior-year losses into it: "Add up the total amount of all other expenses (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) that you can deduct from your PSI." With the associates label, it is one of the two amounts subtracted from gross personal services income to reach the net figure.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label L, excluding anything already shown at the associates label and excluding amounts relating to input tax credit entitlements for a GST-registered taxpayer.
limitation: The personal services income rules deny many ordinary business deductions, including home occupancy costs and payments to associates for non-principal work, so this column shows what survived the rules rather than what the person spent. Deferred non-commercial losses from earlier years sit inside it, so it is not a clean current-year expense figure either.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, states that deferred non-commercial losses are included, excludes the associates amounts and the GST component, and places it in the net personal services income calculation.
evidence_quote: Add up the total amount of all other expenses (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) that you can deduct from your PSI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total amount of other deductions against PSI' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not flag that prior-year deferred losses are mixed into the total.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income voluntary agreement label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Personal services income - P1
variable_description: Personal services income the entity reported as paid under a PAYG voluntary agreement, gross of the tax the payer withheld. The ATO defines the label as "the total income you receive that is subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement, including amounts of tax withheld", and defines the income itself as "income that is mainly a reward for an individual's personal efforts or skills". A voluntary agreement is an arrangement where a contractor who has quoted an ABN asks the payer to withhold anyway, so a non-zero figure marks a business whose earnings are one person's labour sold under contract.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Personal services income - P1
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one income year, reported in the personal services income section of the return rather than in business income, and reported gross of the amounts withheld by the payer.
limitation: It does not tell you whether the personal services income rules bit. Deduction restrictions turn on the results test, the other personal services business tests or a Commissioner's determination, none of which this column carries. A zero is also not an absence of personal services income: income earned without a voluntary agreement sits at the labour hire, ABN-not-quoted or other personal services income labels instead.
rationale: The BLADE Business Income Tax module carries income tax return items. The ATO's business and professional items instructions define the voluntary agreement label directly and define personal services income in the same document.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label M is the total income you receive that is subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement, including amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the purchases and other costs expense label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: What the business spent during the year on trading stock and the direct materials that went into what it sold. The ATO defines the label as "the direct cost of materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business", and says it "includes inwards freight and the cost of stock acquired when starting or acquiring a business during the year". It is one component of cost of sales, which also moves with opening and closing stock reported beside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense amount for one income year, entered separately for primary production and non-primary production and totalled, and reported net of any input tax credit entitlement where the entity is registered for GST.
limitation: It is not the cost of the goods actually sold. Cost of sales adds opening stock and subtracts closing stock, so a firm that built up inventory shows purchases well above the cost of what it sold that year. The boundary with contractor expenses also moves with the firm's own bookkeeping: the ATO tells lodgers that contract labour recorded in the cost of sales account belongs here rather than at contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses.
rationale: The purchases and other costs label is defined verbatim in the ATO business and professional items expense instructions, including the treatment of inwards freight, start-up stock and contract labour.
evidence_quote: Purchases and other costs represent the direct cost of materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the income reconciliation adjustments label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Reconciliation items - P8
variable_description: The net adjustment that carries the business from the income in its accounts to the income assessable for tax. The ATO says these adjustments "reconcile your business operating profit or loss with your business taxable income", and that "your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions". Add-backs are assessable amounts not in the accounts, such as balancing adjustments on disposing of depreciating assets; subtractions are accounting income that is not assessable, such as exempt income and book profit on the sale of a depreciating asset.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Reconciliation items - P8
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount for one income year. The return carries a separate loss indicator for a negative value, so the sign is held outside the number itself.
limitation: Read without the sign flag, a large negative adjustment looks like a large positive one. The column is also a residual: exempt income, cash flow boost amounts, balancing adjustments and plain omissions all net off inside one figure, so a movement cannot be attributed to any of them, and the expense-side adjustment is a separate column that must be read with it.
rationale: The reconciliation items instructions define what an income reconciliation adjustment is, how it is built from add-backs and subtractions, and what it is for.
evidence_quote: These adjustments reconcile your business operating profit or loss with your business taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the rent expenses label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: What the business paid as a tenant to rent the land and buildings it used to earn income. The ATO defines the label as "expenditure you incur as a tenant for rental of land and buildings used for producing assessable income" and tells lodgers to "include the cost of leasing real estate". Equipment and vehicle leasing is a different label, so this column is premises cost alone.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense amount for one income year, split between primary production and non-primary production columns and totalled, and net of input tax credits for a GST-registered entity.
limitation: A nil value is a fact about tenure, not about premises cost. A business that owns its site reports nothing here while carrying the same occupancy cost through interest, capital works and rates, so rent cannot be used as a proxy for the cost of space, and comparisons across firms of different tenure are misleading.
rationale: The rent expenses label is defined in one sentence in the ATO business and professional items expense instructions, and the company return carries the same expense line at item 6 label H.
evidence_quote: This is expenditure you incur as a tenant for rental of land and buildings used for producing assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the repairs and maintenance expense label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: What the business spent keeping its premises, plant and equipment in working order, as the figure appears in its accounts. The ATO defines it as "expenditure shown in your accounts for repairs and maintenance of premises, plant, machinery, implements, utensils, rolling stock or articles associated with the production of income". value_definition: A binary flag taking 1, 0 or . for missing, drawn from Dealroom's industry tag list rather than from a statistical classification. Multiple tags can apply to one firm, so this column is independent of the other ind_ columns rather than exclusive of them.
limitation: It cannot be used to build a telecommunications sector aggregate. The definition is about disrupting the industry, so infrastructure owners, tower companies and the large established carriers are outside it, and a firm selling enterprise communication software may be tagged enterprise software instead on a Dealroom editorial call.
rationale: The Dealroom industries page carries the telecom definition verbatim as it appears in the BLADE data item list, which identifies the taxonomy and its scope.
evidence_quote: Startups developing solutions aiming at disrupting the telecommunications industry: startups offering mobile plans, internet subscriptions, better communication services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the custodian's label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving the reader without the tag's publisher, its exclusion of incumbents, or its overlap with the other industry flags.

value_domain: Dealroom transportation industry tag flag
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
variable_description: Whether Dealroom tagged this business to transportation, defined around the movement of people and goods rather than around owning vehicles. Dealroom's definition is "Startups developing solutions, software, tools and machines used to solve problems or improve conditions with respect to the movement of people and goods", which pulls in ride hailing, last-mile delivery, freight software and electric vehicle technology. The flag belongs to the ABN and does not change over the firm's observed years.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
value_definition: A binary flag, 1 or 0, with . where the ABN has no Dealroom industry information. It is a tag in a non-exclusive taxonomy: a delivery platform can be tagged both transportation and food.
limitation: It is not the ANZSIC transport, postal and warehousing division and will not reproduce it. Most of the firms that division counts, such as trucking operators and bus companies, are not in Dealroom's tracked population at all, while a software firm selling to them is flagged 1, so the column measures technology exposure to transport rather than transport activity.
rationale: The Dealroom industries page publishes the transportation definition in the same words the BLADE data item list uses, establishing both the source and the technology-first scope of the tag.
evidence_quote: Startups developing solutions, software, tools and machines used to solve problems or improve conditions with respect to the movement of people and goods.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the data item list wording alone with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never warned that the tag is not an industry classification and does not line up with ANZSIC.

value_domain: Dealroom travel industry tag flag
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
variable_description: Whether Dealroom tagged this business to travel, a tag built around booking and trip platforms rather than around tourism operators. Dealroom writes that "Travel startups develop digital platforms and services that streamline booking, enhance travel experiences, and connect travelers with local offerings." The flag is attached to the ABN once and repeated across its years, so it cannot show a pivot into or out of travel.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
value_definition: A binary flag with values 1, 0 and . for missing. One of the Dealroom industry tags, which overlap by design: an accommodation marketplace can be tagged travel and real estate together.
limitation: It is a poor frame for pandemic travel analysis, because the population is platform businesses rather than the airlines, hotels and tour operators that carried most of the shock, and because the tag is time invariant it stays 1 for a firm that abandoned travel in 2020.
rationale: The Dealroom industries page gives the travel definition verbatim as carried in the BLADE data item list, which fixes the tag's scope to digital travel platforms.
evidence_quote: Travel startups develop digital platforms and services that streamline booking, enhance travel experiences, and connect travelers with local offerings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing flagged that the tag is fixed over time or that it excludes conventional travel operators.

value_domain: Dealroom wellness and beauty industry tag flag
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
variable_description: Whether Dealroom tagged this business to wellness and beauty, a single tag spanning mental wellbeing, fitness, skincare and personal care. Dealroom's definition is "Startups offering products and services to improve mental and physical wellbeing, including tech-driven innovations in beauty, skincare, and personal care." It is one Dealroom tag on the ABN, held constant across the firm's observed years, and it sits close enough to the health tag that many firms carry both.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
value_definition: A binary flag, 1 or 0, with . where Dealroom holds no industry information for the ABN. Tags are additive rather than exclusive, so this flag does not partition the population with the other ind_ columns.
limitation: It merges two quite different businesses - a cosmetics brand and a mental health app - under one flag, so a count of wellness firms cannot be read as either a beauty industry or a digital health measure. Firms with a clinical product are more likely to be tagged health instead, which makes the boundary an editorial one rather than a rule.
rationale: The Dealroom industries page publishes the wellness and beauty definition word for word as the BLADE data item list carries it, which shows the breadth of the single tag.
evidence_quote: Startups offering products and services to improve mental and physical wellbeing, including tech-driven innovations in beauty, skincare, and personal care.
supersedes_rationale: The entry was the data item list wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both definition and limitation, and did not say that beauty and mental wellbeing share one flag.

value_domain: Self-reported Indigenous control of the company, R&D Tax Incentive registration
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive application form questions (business.gov.au)
variable_description: Whether the company said its board or management committee is majority Indigenous, answered when it registered R&D activities for the tax incentive. The application asks "Is the company Indigenous controlled (where at least 51% of the organisation's board or management committee are Indigenous)?" with the options Yes, No and Prefer not to answer, and the department explains the question is asked because "Indigenous ownership and Indigenous controlled details are required as part of policy and program development, review and evaluation". Control is about who governs the company, which is why it sits beside indigenousowned, the question about who holds the shares.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive application form questions (business.gov.au)
value_definition: A categorical response taking Yes, No, N/A or Prefer not to answer. It is a registration-form answer for one income year rather than a verified register entry, and there is no partial or percentage response.
limitation: The population is companies that registered R&D activities, so the field says nothing about Indigenous control of Australian business generally, and it can only be observed in the years a company registered. Prefer not to answer is a real and non-random category, so treating anything other than Yes as No understates Indigenous-controlled firms.
rationale: The published R&D Tax Incentive application form questions carry this exact question, its 51 per cent board threshold and its response options, which is the instrument that generates the BLADE column.
evidence_quote: Is the company Indigenous controlled (where at least 51% of the organisation's board or management committee are Indigenous)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form's wording as the description and used the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the answer is self-reported at registration, that the population is R&D claimants, or how the non-response option behaves.

value_domain: Self-reported Indigenous ownership of the company, R&D Tax Incentive registration
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive application form questions (business.gov.au)
variable_description: Whether the company said its members or proprietors are majority Indigenous, answered on its R&D Tax Incentive registration. The form asks "Is the company Indigenous owned (where at least 51% of the organisation's members or proprietors are Indigenous)?", with Yes, No and Prefer not to answer as the choices. Ownership and control are asked separately and can differ: a company can be majority Indigenous owned while its board is not, which is why the answer here need not match indigenouscontrolled on the same row.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive application form questions (business.gov.au)
value_definition: A categorical response of Yes, No, N/A or Prefer not to answer, recorded once per registration. The 51 per cent test is applied by the company itself when it answers, not by the department.
limitation: It is a claim about equity held at registration and carries no evidence: no supporting documentation, Supply Nation certification or Indigenous Business Register check stands behind the answer. It also cannot be read as a business count, since only companies that register R&D activities are asked at all.
rationale: The published application form questions give this question, its 51 per cent ownership threshold and its options, and set out why the department collects it, which is the origin of the BLADE column.
evidence_quote: Is the company Indigenous owned (where at least 51% of the organisation's members or proprietors are Indigenous)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form wording as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not distinguish ownership from control or warn that the answer is unverified.

value_domain: Derived flag for a patent covering both product and process innovation
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: A derived flag marking a patent application whose subject matter was classified as both a new product and a new way of making or doing something. It is the overlap of the two flags beside it, so a row with innovation_both set to 1 should also be readable as product and process together rather than as a third, separate kind of invention. The classification attaches to the patent application, not to the firm, so a business-level measure has to be built by aggregating its applications.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A numeric flag taking 0 or 1 on the IPRAPID applications table. It is a derived variable rather than an IP Australia register field, and it applies only to patents, so trade mark and design rows carry no meaningful value.
limitation: How the classification was made is not published in the IP RAPID data dictionary, so the reader cannot check whether it came from patent claim text, the IPC marks or a model, and cannot judge its error rate. Nor does it say anything about commercialisation: a patent classified as both is a description of the document, not evidence that the firm brought either innovation to market.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary documents the applications table this column sits in but contains no product or process innovation field, so the derivation is unpublished and the meaning is read from the label, from the pair of flags beside it and from the standard product against process distinction used in innovation statistics.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label 'Whether the patent relates to both a process and product innovation' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record that the flag is derived, undocumented and defined on the application rather than the firm.

value_domain: Derived flag for a patent covering a process innovation
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: A derived flag marking a patent application whose subject matter is a method or process - a new way of making, treating or doing something - rather than an artefact. Process patents are the ones usually read as evidence of production or efficiency improvement, which is why they are separated from product patents in productivity research. The flag sits on the application row in IPRAPID and is not mutually exclusive with innovation_product, since a single specification can claim both.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A numeric 0 or 1 flag on the IPRAPID applications table, defined for patents. It is derived rather than reported by the applicant, and there is no accompanying strength or confidence score.
limitation: A process patent is a claim to a method, not proof that the firm adopted it: patents are frequently filed defensively or licensed out, so the flag cannot stand in for process innovation as the Oslo-style business surveys measure it. Because the derivation is not documented in IP Australia's IP RAPID dictionary, misclassification cannot be bounded.
rationale: No published IP Australia or ABS documentation for this derived column could be fetched, so the description rests on the label, on the neighbouring product and both flags, and on the settled meaning of process innovation in patent research.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Whether the patent relates to a process innovation' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, and gave no warning that the flag is an undocumented derivation.

value_domain: Derived flag for a patent covering a product innovation
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: A derived flag marking a patent application whose subject matter is a thing - an apparatus, device, compound or composition - rather than a method. Product patents are usually treated as the closer proxy for new goods reaching a market, and the split from innovation_process is what allows a firm's patent portfolio to be read as output-facing or production-facing. The flag is defined on the application, so a firm with many applications carries many rows.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A numeric 0 or 1 flag on the IPRAPID applications table, meaningful only for patent rows. It is a derived classification of the specification, not a field an applicant supplies.
limitation: It says nothing about whether the product exists: an application can be abandoned, refused or never worked, and the flag is set from the document regardless of the status column beside it. Filing strategy also differs by technology, so a rise in product-flagged patents can reflect drafting practice rather than a change in what firms are inventing.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary covers the applications table but not this flag, so no fetchable source defines it; the meaning is assembled from the label, the sibling flags and the standard product against process reading of patent claims.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Whether the patent relates to a product innovation' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate the document-level classification from any statement about commercialisation.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement clause flag, non work-related illness or injury insurance
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 Data Collection Framework
variable_description: Whether the federal enterprise agreement on this row contains an insurance scheme covering absence from work for illness or injury that did not happen at work. The DEWR framework defines the field as covering an agreement that "provides for an insurance scheme covering absence from work due to a non work-related illness or injury", notes that employees may have to "cash in" part of their sick leave to pay the premiums, and states that it "also covers 'Income Protection Insurance' that relates to non work-related injury or illness". The framework keeps it strictly apart from the redundancy income protection field, which is a different clause type. The unit is the agreement, coded by departmental analysts from the approved document, not the employer or the employee.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 Data Collection Framework
value_definition: A presence flag written as Y when the clause is found. There is no explicit N: an agreement without the provision is simply left blank, and the field is one of about two hundred conditions items coded per agreement.
limitation: Blank is ambiguous and is the trap here - it can mean no such clause, or a year in which the item was not part of the coding framework, since DEWR reviews the conditions collected each year and codes conditions only for agreements approved from 1 January 1997. A Y also says nothing about the premium, the benefit or how many of the covered employees ever used the scheme.
rationale: The WAD 2021 Data Collection Framework, published by DEWR as the introduction to the dataset, carries this field with the exact description the BLADE data item list reproduces, and the department's WAD page states the 1997 start for conditions coding and the annual review of the fields.
evidence_quote: The agreement provides for an insurance scheme covering absence from work due to a non work-related illness or injury.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework text as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both definition and limitation, so it did not say that the unit is the agreement, that only Y is recorded, or that conditions coding begins in 1997.

value_domain: Count of accelerator investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many of the business's known backers are accelerators, the fixed-term programs that take a small stake in return for seed money, mentoring and a demo day. A non-zero count marks a firm that went through a structured early-stage program rather than one that simply raised money, which is why it is kept apart from investors_inc_n for incubators. Like every Dealroom field in BLADE it is time invariant and written on every year of the ABN, so it dates nothing.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of distinct investors carrying the accelerator type, with . for missing. An investor can hold more than one type, so the type counts overlap and do not add to investors_n.
limitation: It carries no dollars and no date, so two accelerators can mean less capital than none, and a firm accelerated in 2015 looks identical in 2012. It also cannot say whether the program was finished or the equity still held.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the investor concept and the tracked company population behind the count, but publishes no separate accelerator definition, so the type's meaning is read from the data item list wording and general knowledge of accelerator programs.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Dealroom's paragraph as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the count is undated, overlapping and limited to firms Dealroom tracks.

value_domain: Count of advisor investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many of the business's recorded investors are investment banks or financial advisory firms, which Dealroom counts as an investor type in their own right. Advisors usually appear on larger or more complicated rounds, so a non-zero count is a weak signal of deal complexity rather than of a new source of capital. The count is an attribute of the ABN, repeated unchanged across its years in BLADE.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct investors tagged advisor. Investor types are not exclusive, so an entity counted here can also be counted in another investors_ column.
limitation: An advisor is normally paid a fee to run a transaction rather than committing its own money, so adding this column to the others overstates how many parties actually funded the firm. Dealroom also tags advisory businesses as service providers elsewhere in its taxonomy, so the same firm can be recorded twice under two different ideas of what it did.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page establishes what an investor record is and how the tracked population is drawn, but does not publish an advisor definition, so the description is assembled from the data item list text and standard practice in advised rounds.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the Dealroom paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not flag that an advisor is usually a paid intermediary rather than a capital provider.

value_domain: Count of individual angel investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many named individuals are recorded as investing their own money in the business. Dealroom builds this from its people records: "A people entity that makes various investments into companies is considered as an Individual Angel investor." It counts individuals only, so an angel who invests through a syndicate vehicle is counted in investors_angelfund_n instead, and the two columns cannot be added without double counting the same person's money.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of distinct individuals tagged as angels, with . for missing. It counts people rather than legal entities, which is what separates it from every other investors_ column.
limitation: Angel participation is the least completely recorded part of any private-market database, since individuals are often unnamed in round announcements, so a zero is at least as likely to mean undisclosed as to mean none. The count also says nothing about how much each angel put in, and it never falls when an angel sells out.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the individual angel investor as a people entity that invests, which is the record type this count is built from, and sets out the tracked company population that bounds it.
evidence_quote: A people entity that makes various investments into companies is considered as an Individual Angel investor.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's paragraph and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the count is of people, that it overlaps angel funds, or that undisclosed angels read as zero.

value_domain: Count of angel fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many angel funds - vehicles through which individual angels invest collectively - are recorded as backing the business. Dealroom treats the angel fund as a sub-type of investment fund and attributes the investment to the fund rather than to the individuals inside it. That makes this column the pooled counterpart of investors_angel_n, which counts named individuals investing in their own right.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer, . where missing, counting distinct entities tagged angel fund. Because angel funds sit inside the investment fund family, the same entity can also be counted in investors_inv_n.
limitation: One vehicle is one investor no matter how many people stand behind it, so a syndicate of thirty angels adds 1 here while the same thirty investing directly would add 30 to investors_angel_n. Adding the two columns to measure angel involvement therefore mixes two incompatible units.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines investment funds and the investor concept but does not publish a separate angel fund definition, so the meaning comes from the data item list text and the fund-of-individuals structure it describes.
evidence_quote: According to Investopedia : " An investment fund is a supply of capital belonging to numerous investors used to collectively purchase securities while each investor retains ownership and control of his own shares".
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the Dealroom paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the entity and the individual counts are on different units.

value_domain: Count of operating company investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many ordinary companies, as opposed to funds or individuals, are recorded as having invested in this business. It is the broadest of the company-shaped investor tags and sits above the narrower corporate and corporate venture fund tags rather than beside them. In BLADE the count is fixed for the ABN, so it describes the firm's investor register over its whole recorded life, not a particular year.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct investor entities that are companies. Investor types overlap, so a single backer can appear in this count and in investors_corporate_n at the same time.
limitation: It does not separate a strategic backer from a founder's own holding company or a parent funding its subsidiary, so a high count can be a group structure rather than external support. Summing it with investors_corporate_n and investors_cvf_n counts the same corporate group up to three times.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page explains how companies become investor records once they invest, but publishes no standalone company investor-type definition, so the description is built from that page, the data item list wording and the neighbouring corporate columns.
evidence_quote: Companies founded after 1990 are labeled as 'corporate' (without the 'mature' tag, given their founding date) as soon as they make investments in other companies, for example .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line Dealroom text with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it did not explain the overlap with the corporate columns or the group-structure confusion.

value_domain: Count of corporate investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many established companies backed this business directly, as distinct from through a venture arm. Dealroom's tag turns on founding date, not size: "Companies founded after 1990 are labeled as 'corporate' (without the 'mature' tag, given their founding date) as soon as they make investments in other companies", while companies founded before 1990 are labelled mature as well. Read against investors_cvf_n, this column is the parent investing off its own balance sheet rather than through a fund.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer, . where missing, counting distinct investor entities tagged corporate. The tag is applied by Dealroom when a company first invests, so the count reflects the investor's status rather than the recipient's.
limitation: The date-based rule hides the largest backers: a bank or miner founded before 1990 is tagged mature, so corporate venture money from Australia's oldest firms need not raise this count at all. It is also silent on strategy - a supplier taking a small stake and an acquirer building a position look the same.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page states the rule that produces the corporate tag, including the founding-date condition and the mature label that applies instead to older companies, which is what governs when this count moves.
evidence_quote: Companies founded after 1990 are labeled as 'corporate' (without the 'mature' tag, given their founding date) as soon as they make investments in other companies, for example .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's descriptive paragraph and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the founding-date rule that decides which corporates are counted was missing.

value_domain: Count of equity crowdfunding platform investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many equity crowdfunding platforms are recorded as an investor in this business. Dealroom scopes the category tightly to "Platforms for equity crowdfunding", so the entity counted is the platform that ran the raise, not the retail investors who subscribed. A count of 1 can therefore sit behind hundreds of new shareholders, which matters for any reading of ownership dispersion.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct crowdfunding platform entities. Platforms are counted once regardless of how many raises or how many subscribers passed through them.
limitation: Reward and donation platforms are outside the definition, so a firm that raised on a pre-sales platform reads zero here even though it raised money from a crowd. The column also cannot show the amount raised or the number of subscribers, which is the part of crowdfunding a reader usually wants.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines crowdfunding entities as equity crowdfunding platforms, which fixes both what is counted and what is excluded from this column.
evidence_quote: Platforms for equity crowdfunding. Example Seedrs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Dealroom paragraph and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not make clear that the unit is the platform rather than the crowd.

value_domain: Count of corporate venture fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many corporate venture funds - the dedicated investment arms of larger companies - are recorded as backing this business. The fund and its parent are separate investor records in Dealroom, which is why this column exists alongside investors_corporate_n rather than inside it. A non-zero count usually marks strategic money with an industrial parent behind it, as opposed to a purely financial venture fund.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged corporate venture fund. As a fund type it also falls within the broader investment fund family that investors_inv_n counts.
limitation: One corporate group can raise two columns at once, because a filter on the parent company in Dealroom also picks up the investments made by its venture arm, so this count and investors_corporate_n are not additive. It also cannot tell you whether the strategic relationship survived, since the count never falls when a corporate parent winds up its fund.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page documents the investor and fund concepts and the relationship between corporates and their venture arms, but publishes no standalone corporate venture fund definition, so the description leans on the data item list text as well.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, and did not warn that the parent and its fund can both be counted.

value_domain: Count of family office investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many family offices - the wealth vehicles of very wealthy individuals or families - are recorded as investors in this business. Dealroom names family offices as one of the investor entity types, and they matter here because they behave differently from funds: no fixed life, no limited partners to report to, and often a longer horizon. The count is fixed for the ABN and does not identify the family behind the office.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged family office. Some family offices also invest through funds they back, in which case the fund rather than the office is the counted investor.
limitation: Family offices disclose selectively and many prefer not to be named at all, so this count is a floor rather than a measure, and a zero cannot be read as no private wealth backing. It is also silent on size, and a single office writing the largest cheque in a round counts the same as one taking a token stake.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page lists family offices within its definition of an investor but publishes no separate family office definition, so the meaning is taken from the data item list wording and from how family offices operate in private markets.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Dealroom paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record that family office coverage is selective and the count is a lower bound.

value_domain: Count of fund of funds investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many funds of funds are recorded as investors in this business, a vehicle that normally allocates to other funds rather than to companies. Because their usual role is one step removed, a non-zero count here is unusual and generally means either a direct co-investment or an attribution of a backed fund's deal to its own investors. The column is written on every year of the ABN and does not date the commitment.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged fund of funds. It is one of the specialised fund types that also sit within the broader investment fund category.
limitation: A non-zero value should not be read as an extra financing round, since the vehicle's normal exposure to the firm is indirect through the funds it backs. Treating it as a distinct capital source alongside investors_vc_n therefore risks counting the same money twice.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines investment funds and the investor record generally but gives no fund of funds definition, so the description rests on the data item list text and on the standard structure of a fund of funds.
evidence_quote: According to Investopedia : " An investment fund is a supply of capital belonging to numerous investors used to collectively purchase securities while each investor retains ownership and control of his own shares".
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the Dealroom paragraph and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain why a direct fund of funds investment is unusual or how it can double count.

value_domain: Count of government investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many government-backed investors are recorded as having put equity into this business. Dealroom groups the public and philanthropic sector as "Government agencies and non-profit organisations", and this column is the government slice of that group, typically state and commonwealth venture vehicles and development funds. It is the equity channel only, which is what separates it from the grant and tax-offset support recorded elsewhere in BLADE.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct investor entities tagged government. It sits inside the wider government and non-profit grouping that investors_govtnp_n counts.
limitation: It understates public support badly, because the money that reaches most Australian firms arrives as a grant, a loan or an R&D tax offset rather than as equity, and none of those raise this count. The RDTI columns in BLADE catch a different and much larger slice of the same idea.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the government and non-profit entity group that this tag is drawn from, and the entities page also fixes the tracked company population within which the count is observed.
evidence_quote: Government agencies and non-profit organisations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that only equity participation is counted or how the column relates to the combined government and non-profit tag.

value_domain: Count of combined government and non-profit investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many investors sit in Dealroom's combined public and philanthropic category, which it describes as "Government agencies and non-profit organisations". This is the parent tag of the two narrower columns beside it, so it is the one to use when the question is whether any non-commercial money backed the firm at all. Its value is fixed for the ABN and repeated on every year of the record.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities in the combined government and non-profit group. By construction it contains the entities counted in investors_govt_n and investors_np_n.
limitation: Adding this column to the government and non-profit columns counts the same investor twice, since it is their parent rather than a residual. It also merges two quite different motives - a state development mandate and a charitable one - so a non-zero value cannot support a claim about public sector involvement on its own.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the combined government and non-profit entity group in its own words, which is exactly what this tag counts.
evidence_quote: Government agencies and non-profit organisations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the same Dealroom paragraph as the two narrower columns with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the combined tag from its parts.

value_domain: Count of incubator investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many incubators are recorded as supporting this business. Dealroom separates an incubator from an accelerator by the absence of equity, funding and a fixed program end, and incubators work with firms at a very early stage over longer periods. A non-zero count therefore usually marks a young company with institutional hand-holding rather than one that has raised capital. The value belongs to the ABN and is repeated across its years.
description_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged incubator. It is a separate tag from accelerator, so the two counts describe different program types rather than the same one twice.
limitation: Because incubators typically take no equity, a count here records an affiliation rather than a financing, and treating it as investment inflates the number of funders. It also gives no duration, so a two-year incubation and a short co-working placement both add 1.
