variable_description: Capital gains from hedging financial arrangements treated on capital account, at the discount label F of the hedging row on the old CGT schedule. The row exists only because of the taxation of financial arrangements rules: with a valid hedging tax-timing election in place, "gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged". The hedging row has no indexation cell at all, so it is split across two columns rather than three.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, hedging financial arrangements
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and the discount, reported only by entities within the TOFA rules that have made a hedging tax-timing method election.
limitation: It is not a measure of a firm's hedging: an entity that hedges heavily but has made no hedging election, or whose hedges relate to revenue rather than capital items, reports nothing here. The amount also mirrors the tax treatment of the hedged asset rather than the economics of the hedge itself.
rationale: The ATO page explains why hedging gains reach the CGT schedule at all and names the election that gates the row, and the 2012 form shows the hedging row with only discount and other columns.
evidence_quote: gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the row depends on a TOFA hedging election or that it has no indexation cell.

value_domain: Capital gains on hedging financial arrangements, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, hedging financial arrangements, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains from hedging financial arrangements worked out under the other method, at label H of the hedging row on the old CGT schedule. For a company this is normally the only hedging cell with an amount in it, since the discount is closed to companies and the row carries no indexation cell. The ATO directs entities with a hedging tax-timing election to "specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule", which is what this column holds.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, hedging financial arrangements, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to proceeds less cost base on the hedging arrangement, before capital losses are applied.
limitation: Losses on hedging arrangements are reported in a separate part of the schedule, so this column is a gross gain and cannot be read as the net result of a hedging programme. It also shares the label letter H with the other CGT assets discount cell, so the row, not the letter, identifies it.
rationale: The ATO page states that hedging gains and losses go on the CGT schedule under the tax-timing election, and the 2012 form places label H in the hedging row's other-gains column.
evidence_quote: If this applies to you, specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2016 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained why this is the only hedging cell most companies use.

value_domain: Capital gains on other CGT assets, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets that fall outside the named categories, worked out under the discount method, at label H of part A of the old CGT schedule. This is the catch-all row, so it absorbs goodwill, intangibles, plant used privately and any CGT event that is not a disposal of shares, real estate, collectables or a forestry interest. A company will almost always show zero, because the ATO states that "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies".
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering every non-active asset class not itemised elsewhere in part A.
limitation: Being a residual, it cannot be decomposed: a large amount says a gain was made on something outside the named categories but not on what. It is also not evidence of a twelve-month holding period for a company, since the few company amounts that do appear are life insurance cases rather than ordinary trading entities.
rationale: The current schedule instructions define the discount method and its company restriction, and the 2012 form fixes label H as the non-active other-assets discount cell.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form schedule label with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the row is a residual category or that companies rarely use the discount method.

value_domain: Capital gains on other CGT assets, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets outside the named categories, worked out under the indexation method, at label G of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO describes the category as covering "the capital gain or capital loss that you have made and that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule", which for a business usually means goodwill, intangibles or a CGT event that is not an asset disposal. Indexation restricts it further: the method is only available where the asset was acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and concessions, with the cost base increased by an indexation factor based on consumer price index movements up to September 1999.
limitation: The column shrinks mechanically over time as pre-1999 assets are sold out of the population, so a downward trend is an ageing effect and not a change in business behaviour. It also cannot be compared with the discount column on the same row, because an entity that could use either had to choose one and the schedule does not record the choice.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines both the other CGT assets category and the indexation method, including the acquisition cut-off that governs eligibility.
evidence_quote: The indexation method is one of the ways to calculate your capital gain if you acquired a CGT asset before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so nothing said what the residual category holds or why the column empties out over time.

value_domain: Capital gains on other CGT assets, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets outside the named categories, worked out under the other method, at label I of part A of the old CGT schedule. For most companies this is the single most populated cell of the whole part A grid, because the residual asset category and the residual method are the two defaults. The ATO requires the method for short holdings: "You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months".
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: Because both the row and the column are defaults, a large amount here is the least informative number in part A: it identifies neither the asset nor the holding period. Reading it as short-term trading gains would be wrong, since assets held for years also land here whenever indexation and the discount do not apply.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method and the other CGT assets category, which are the two residuals that intersect in this cell.
evidence_quote: You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months (that is, when the indexation and discount methods don't apply).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never warned that this cell is where everything unclassified accumulates.

value_domain: Capital gains on real estate, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate held as a non-active asset, worked out under the discount method, at label E of part A of the old CGT schedule. It is the property equivalent of the shares discount cell, and it is closed to ordinary companies: the ATO says "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies". Non-active is a concession status, not a statement about use, because the ATO directs that "If the asset doesn't qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets".
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
value_definition: A dollar amount before capital losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering land and buildings disposed of in the year.
limitation: A trust or fund with an amount here is not necessarily a property business: an incidental sale of premises produces the same entry as a portfolio disposal, and the schedule holds no count of properties. The non-active label also means a genuine business premises can appear here whenever the small business concessions were not available.
rationale: The current schedule instructions state both the company restriction on the discount method and the rule that pushes non-qualifying assets into the non-active rows.
evidence_quote: If the asset doesn't qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained what non-active means or that companies cannot use the discount method.

value_domain: Capital gains on real estate, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate held as a non-active asset, worked out under the indexation method, at label D of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO defines the category narrowly as location-based: "Real estate situated in Australia is any real property, including land and buildings, that is in Australia", so foreign property falls into the other CGT assets rows instead. Indexation makes this the long-held property cell, since the method needs an acquisition before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and concessions, with the cost base uplifted by an indexation factor frozen at the September 1999 consumer price index.
limitation: Overseas real estate is excluded from the row, so this column understates a firm's property gains whenever it holds assets offshore. Indexation was also frozen rather than abolished, so the uplift shrinks in real terms every year an old property is held and the gain reported here grows for reasons unrelated to the market.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines real estate situated in Australia and the indexation method, and the 2012 form fixes label D as the non-active real estate indexation cell.
evidence_quote: Real estate situated in Australia is any real property, including land and buildings, that is in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the row excludes overseas property or what indexation does to the cost base.

value_domain: Capital gains on real estate, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate held as a non-active asset, worked out under the other method, at label F of part A of the old CGT schedule. This is where a company's property gains normally sit, since indexation is confined to pre-1999 acquisitions and the discount is closed to companies. The gain is simply proceeds less cost base, with no holding-period adjustment of any kind.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base, gross of capital losses and of the small business concessions.
limitation: Sharing the label letter F with the hedging discount cell, it can only be identified by its row, which matters when reading the raw schedule rather than the BLADE column name. The amount is also gross: development costs already deducted elsewhere and any prior-year losses are not netted here, so it is not the profit on the sale.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method, and the 2012 form shows label F appearing twice in part A, in the real estate other-gains cell and in the hedging discount cell.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so nothing said this is the usual cell for company property gains or that the label letter repeats.

value_domain: Capital gains on shares and units, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts held as non-active assets, worked out under the discount method, at label B of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO's rule for the method is that "the CGT event happened after 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999" and "you acquired the asset at least 12 months before the CGT event", so an amount here marks a holding of at least a year. The discount itself is not applied at this point: current year and prior year losses come off first.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering shares and units disposed of in the year.
limitation: The column is not a company portfolio measure, because ordinary companies cannot use the discount method at all and the amounts that do appear come mostly from trusts and funds lodging the same schedule. It also cannot be netted against the losses parts of the schedule to give a net gain, since the sequence of loss application is set out separately.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the discount method, its twelve-month test and the order in which losses and the discount are applied.
evidence_quote: the CGT event happened after 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999 you acquired the asset at least 12 months before the CGT event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the discount is applied after losses or who can use the method.

value_domain: Capital gains on shares and units, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts, non-active, under the indexation method, at label A of part A of the old CGT schedule. It is the first cell of the schedule's method grid and covers the oldest holdings: the ATO explains that the method "allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999)". Amounts here therefore come from parcels acquired before that date and still held when the CGT event happened.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with the cost base uplifted by the frozen indexation factor.
limitation: A zero does not mean no share gains: the same disposals appear in the discount or other cells whenever indexation was unavailable or the entity chose a different method, and the schedule never records which method was rejected. Label A is also reused in the forestry row of the same part, so the column name rather than the letter identifies the cell.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the indexation method and its cut-off date, and the 2012 form fixes label A as the non-active shares and units indexation cell.
evidence_quote: This method allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said what indexation does or that a zero can hide a gain reported by another method.

value_domain: Capital gains on shares and units, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts held as non-active assets, worked out under the other method, at label C of part A of the old CGT schedule. For a company this is the working column for equity disposals, because the discount is closed to it and indexation reaches only pre-1999 parcels. The ATO makes the method compulsory for short holdings: "You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months".
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base on shares and units, gross of capital losses and concessions.
limitation: It cannot be read as short-term trading, because a company holding shares for a decade also reports here once indexation and the discount are out of reach. Gains distributed from a trust are grossed up and reported in a separate row of the modern schedule, so this cell is not a complete picture of a firm's equity gains.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method and states when it is compulsory, and the 2012 form fixes label C as the non-active shares and units other-gains cell.
evidence_quote: You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months (that is, when the indexation and discount methods don't apply).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained that the other method is a residual rather than a marker of short holdings.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at part N of the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part N
variable_description: Whether Division 149 applied to the company, so that assets bought before 20 September 1985 lost their pre-CGT status. It applies when the majority underlying ownership of those assets changed, and the schedule puts it as "Same majority underlying ownership and pre-CGT assets - Division 149 - to be completed by companies only" at label O. It matters because the ATO treats pre-CGT assets as "generally exempt from CGT", so a yes marks the year an old asset base came into the CGT net.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part N
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, from a yes and no tick box; anything else is an invalid or absent response. Companies only, and only those lodging a CGT schedule.
limitation: The flag does not value the assets that lost their pre-CGT status, so it identifies the event without measuring it, and nothing on the schedule links it to the gains reported in part A. Earlier forms worded the same question as a change in majority underlying ownership, so wording rather than meaning shifts across the series.
rationale: The form carries the part title, the division reference, the label letter and the companies-only restriction, and the ATO definitions appendix supplies the pre-CGT asset concept the question turns on.
evidence_quote: Part N Same majority underlying ownership and pre-CGT assets - Division 149 - to be completed by companies only
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with its OF prefix unexplained and the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said what Division 149 does or why a company would answer yes.

value_domain: ABS nature of tariff code (single letter)
values: ["C: Confidential - This is set when ABS confidentialises data.","G: Government - Includes imports for Government.","N: Normal - Items attracting the rate of duty as prescribed in Schedule 3 of the Customs Tariff.","Q: Quota - This covers goods entered under the quota provisions of the Customs Tariff.","R: Concessional - Includes goods where a concessional rate of duty applies."]
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018 (cat. 5489.0), Data downloads workbook 5489_2026.xlsx, Appendix 10 section A 'Nature of tariff'
variable_description: A single letter recording the kind of tariff arrangement the import line was dutied under - duty information rather than information about the goods. It is the third of three duty qualifiers on the row: preference_code_im names the agreement claimed, treatment_code_im names the concession applied, and this records the nature of the tariff in play when the duty was worked out. ABS publishes the code list in the appendices to its merchandise trade concepts, sources and methods, beside the treatment and preference code lists.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018 (cat. 5489.0), appendices
value_definition: A single alphabetic character from an ABS code list published with the merchandise trade appendices. The domain is small and closed, and it is unrelated to the numeric preference and treatment code lists on the same row.
limitation: It is not the nature of the entry. Nature 10, 20 and 30 - direct home consumption, warehousing, and clearance from a bonded warehouse - are the line nature type, and form_id_im carries them, so reading this column as the declaration type puts warehoused goods in the wrong bucket. Nor does it give an amount: no duty rate, duty paid or concession value can be recovered from a letter, and the customs value on the line is unaffected by it.
rationale: Appendix 10 section A gives the complete 5-code list with labels and descriptions. It is an ABS-created data item, not a Home Affairs one, which is why it is documented in the ABS CSM rather than in the Customs Tariff.
evidence_quote: N | Normal | Items attracting the rate of duty as prescribed in Schedule 3
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review recorded no codeframe; the appendix the Data Item List cites contains it in full.

value_domain: ABS integration version identifier
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Which ABS integration run produced this row of the National Family Violence Funded Agencies data. The dataset is not part of standard or requestable BLADE: the ABS notes that as an accredited data service provider it integrates additional sources "for approved projects and subject to agreement from data custodians", which is how a service-delivery collection like this reaches a business asset. The version string is therefore also the marker of which approved project the row belongs to.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric string of the form inNNN_vN, for example in293_v1, identifying the ABS integration project and its version.
limitation: It is not a date and not an attribute of the funded agency, so it cannot order records in time or distinguish one agency from another. Because the underlying collection is project-specific rather than an enduring BLADE module, the version cannot be matched against the version columns on the standard modules.
rationale: The ABS page explains the project-based route by which non-standard collections are integrated into BLADE, which is the status of this dataset; the version string itself is documented only as an internal ABS reference.
evidence_quote: As the ABS is an Accredited Data Service Provider , additional data sources can be integrated to BLADE for approved projects and subject to agreement from data custodians.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the column marks an extract vintage from a project-specific integration.

value_domain: Nickel content of an ore shipment, per cent
value_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
variable_description: The assayed nickel content of an exported ore or concentrate shipment, as a percentage of the shipment. Nickel is usually shipped as a low-grade concentrate or matte and priced on contained metal, so the grade recorded here is what converts a tonnage into the quantity the buyer pays for. It qualifies a single export line of a single consignment, not the exporter's output for the year.
description_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
value_definition: A number expressed as a percentage, held against an export transaction classified by the AHECC, the eight-digit Australian extension of the Harmonized System maintained with the Department of Home Affairs.
limitation: It cannot be compared with the lead percentage on the same shipment as if the two were shares of one whole, since each metal is assayed against the total mass and other elements make up the rest. A missing value is also not a zero grade: it marks a line that is not an ore or concentrate, which for a nickel producer includes refined and intermediate products.
rationale: The AHECC page establishes the classification governing Australian export lines, including the ore and concentrate classes this grade qualifies; no fetchable page defines the metal-percentage field itself.
evidence_quote: The AHECC is used in the preparation of export documentation and in the compilation of Australian export statistics
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Percentage of nickel in shipment of ore' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the figure is a per-consignment grade rather than a firm-level composition.

value_domain: Nominal term of an enterprise agreement, in years
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Nominal expiry date
variable_description: How long the enterprise agreement runs on paper, measured in years from commencement to its nominal expiry date. The nominal term is capped: the Commission notes it "will not be more than 4 years from the date the Commission approves the agreement". A negative value is not an error but a timing artefact, arising when the Commission approved the agreement after the expiry date the parties had written into it.
description_source: Fair Work Commission, Nominal expiry date
value_definition: A numeric duration in years, normally between 0 and 4, and negative where approval postdates the nominal expiry date.
limitation: It is not the period the agreement actually governed the workplace: the Commission states that "Agreements continue to operate after their nominal expiry dates until they are replaced or terminated", so an expired agreement can still set pay years later. Treating this as coverage duration therefore understates how long an employer's terms stayed in force.
rationale: The Commission page defines the nominal expiry date, the statutory four-year cap and the fact that agreements keep operating past it, which is what separates nominal duration from effective duration.
evidence_quote: Agreements continue to operate after their nominal expiry dates until they are replaced or terminated by the Commission.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's note about negative values with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the term is nominal and that agreements outlive it.

value_domain: Binary flag for New South Wales coverage of an agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement operates in New South Wales, one of a set of per-jurisdiction flags DEWR records as "State or Territories covered". The flags are not mutually exclusive, so a national employer's agreement carries a 1 in several of them at once and the set cannot be collapsed into a single state variable. It describes the reach of the agreement, not where the employer's ABN is registered.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 for yes, 0 for no, held alongside equivalent flags for the other states and territories.
limitation: It gives no weight, so an agreement covering a single site in Sydney and one covering thousands of employees across the state look identical, and it cannot be used to apportion employees between jurisdictions. A 1 also does not place the firm in New South Wales, since coverage follows the agreement rather than the business location.
rationale: The DEWR page lists state and territory coverage among the general details recorded for each federal enterprise agreement, which is what this flag set carries.
evidence_quote: State or Territories covered
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Indicates whether an agreement operates in NSW' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the flags overlap or that they carry no employee weight.

value_domain: Binary flag for Northern Territory coverage of an agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement operates in the Northern Territory, part of the same per-jurisdiction flag set DEWR records as "State or Territories covered". Because the Territory has few employers of its own, most agreements flagged here are national or multi-state agreements that reach into it, rather than agreements negotiated locally. The flag therefore reads more as a marker of national coverage than of Territory-specific bargaining.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 for yes, 0 for no, set independently of the flags for the other states and territories.
limitation: Counts of agreements flagged here overstate Territory bargaining activity, since a national agreement counts once in every jurisdiction it touches. The flag also cannot separate the Territory portion of an employer's workforce from the rest, so it supports no per-jurisdiction employee analysis.
rationale: The DEWR page lists state and territory coverage among the general details recorded for each agreement, which is the basis for this flag.
evidence_quote: State or Territories covered
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Indicates whether an agreement operates in the NT' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never warned that national agreements dominate the flag.

value_domain: Head count of Australia-based staff from a company web profile
value_source: Glass.AI, Emerging Industries Database work with the Department of Industry, Science and Resources
variable_description: A count of the business's Australia-based staff taken from its LinkedIn profile, not from payroll or tax records. It comes from the Emerging Industries collection, which the Department of Industry, Science and Resources built by combining "Glass.AI's web-scale research algorithms with econometric methods and government microdata" to identify firms in industries that conventional classifications miss. Read against BLADE's own employment measures, it is a web-derived signal of firm size rather than a measure of jobs.
description_source: Glass.AI, Emerging Industries Database work with the Department of Industry, Science and Resources
value_definition: A numeric head count, scoped to staff the profile places in Australia, at whatever date the web source was captured.
limitation: It is self-reported on a social platform and updated irregularly, so it can lag reality by years and is missing entirely for firms with no LinkedIn presence, which biases coverage towards larger and more digital businesses. It also counts people who list the employer rather than people paid by the ABN, so it will not reconcile with the Single Touch Payroll or PAYG headcounts in BLADE.
rationale: The Glass.AI page establishes the provenance and method of the Emerging Industries collection this column belongs to; the LinkedIn source of the count comes from the BLADE data item list.
evidence_quote: DISR combined Glass.AI's web-scale research algorithms with econometric methods and government microdata .
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Number of Australia-based staff, per LinkedIn' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never warned that the figure cannot be reconciled with payroll-based employment in the same asset.

value_domain: Days of paid personal or sick leave per year under the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: How many days of paid sick leave the agreement provides, as a number rather than a yes flag. DEWR codes it as field 34, "Days ____ sick leave": "The agreement provides for paid leave available for employees when they are sick or injured. The number of days of paid leave is recorded." It is one of the few WAD condition fields carrying a quantity rather than a yes flag, which makes it usable as a measure of entitlement generosity. Two sentinels sit in the same column, so it has to be filtered before it is averaged.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: A whole number of days. The value 111111111 means the quantity varies or is unknown and 222222222 means no limit, matching the separate unlimited sick leave flag DEWR also codes.
limitation: Averaging without excluding 111111111 and 222222222 produces a nonsense figure, since both are codes rather than day counts. The number is also an entitlement written into an agreement, not leave taken, and it excludes the separate carer's leave and casual personal leave provisions coded in neighbouring fields.
rationale: The DEWR framework defines the field, and the neighbouring entries for unlimited sick leave and carer's leave show what this count does and does not include.
evidence_quote: The agreement provides for paid leave available for employees when they are sick or injured. The number of days of paid leave is recorded.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's coding rule and listed both sentinels as valid responses, with the generic sentence twice below, so nothing warned what they do to a mean.

value_domain: Full-time equivalent R&D staff on an R&D tax incentive registration
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: How much employee labour went into the R&D activities in this registration, measured in person years rather than head count. The application defines question 39 as "the full-time equivalent (FTE) number of people engaged by the company to perform research and development (R&D) activities during the income year covered by this application", with part-time staff counted as a fraction, so someone working half a full-time load is 0.5. For a consolidated group the figure is reported across all relevant subsidiaries, which is why the BLADE label says it spans all companies in the application.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A numeric full-time equivalent count, which can be fractional, covering employees including working directors, partners and proprietors.
limitation: Independent contractors are counted in a separate question, so this figure understates the people who worked on the R&D wherever a firm outsourced. Because it is reported across a consolidated group but attaches to the registering ABN, R&D staffing intensity computed against that ABN's own payroll can exceed one, and the application guidance accepts best reasonable estimates rather than payroll extracts.
rationale: The application guidance defines the field, its FTE basis, the consolidated group treatment and the separate contractor question, which together give both the unit and the main confusion.
evidence_quote: This is the full-time equivalent (FTE) number of people engaged by the company to perform research and development (R&D) activities during the income year covered by this application.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about employees across all companies with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the unit is full-time equivalent person years or that contractors are excluded.

value_domain: Count of employers covered by an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: How many employers are party to the agreement, which separates a single-enterprise agreement from a multi-enterprise or greenfields one. Most federal agreements cover one employer, so a value above one marks the minority that bargain collectively across firms, and the same agreement record then attaches to several businesses in BLADE. DEWR records agreement type alongside it, so the two together identify what kind of bargaining produced the terms.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A whole number of employers, counted at the agreement rather than at the workplace, so a single employer with many sites counts once.
limitation: An employer here is a bargaining party, not an ABN, so the count cannot be used to work out how many BLADE businesses a multi-employer agreement reaches. It also carries no employee weight: a two-employer agreement can cover more workers than a fifty-employer one.
rationale: The DEWR page lists the general details recorded for each agreement, including agreement type and the number of employees covered, which places this count at the agreement level; the field's own coding note comes from the data item list.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Indicates the number of employers covered by an agreement' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said an employer is a bargaining party rather than an ABN.

value_domain: Count of wage increases scheduled in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: How many separate wage increases the agreement schedules over its term, which is the count behind the quantum and timing series DEWR maintains. The framework records "Quantum and timing of any wage increases" for each agreement, so this column is the number of those events rather than their size; dividing the total increase by it gives the average step. A count of zero belongs with the agreements DEWR flags as containing no wage rates or no quantifiable increase.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: A whole number of scheduled increases over the life of the agreement, held with separate fields recording the reason where an increase cannot be quantified.
limitation: More increases do not mean higher pay: an agreement with four small annual steps and one with a single large rise can deliver the same wage outcome, so the count has to be read with the quantum fields. It also does not distinguish increases that were expressed as percentages from those linked to Minimum Wage Panel decisions or to the consumer price index, which DEWR records separately.
rationale: The DEWR framework sets out the wage increases group of fields, including the non-quantifiable and no-wage-rates cases that explain zero values here.
evidence_quote: Wage increases Quantum and timing of any wage increases
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'The number of wage increases that apply to the agreement' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the count is silent on size or how zeros arise.

value_domain: Total cost base reduction from debt forgiveness (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2004 (NAT 3423-6.2004), part O
variable_description: The total amount by which the company cut the cost bases of its CGT assets after a commercial debt was forgiven, at label Q of part O. The form heads the part "Cost base adjustments resulting from debt forgiveness - Division 139 - to be completed by companies only" and pairs this amount with the yes or no at label P, "Interest in creditor". A reduced cost base means a larger capital gain whenever the affected assets are later sold, so the figure is a forward-looking tax consequence rather than a gain in the year.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2004 (NAT 3423-6.2004), part O
value_definition: A dollar amount, reported once for the year rather than per asset, on a part of the schedule completed only by companies.
limitation: It does not say which assets were written down or by how much each, so the future gains it creates cannot be traced to anything in the data. Part O left the CGT schedule after 2004, so an empty column in later years reflects the form and not a stop to commercial debt forgiveness, and the ATO's own guidance describes the current rules under Division 245 rather than the division named on the form.
rationale: The 2004 schedule carries the part title, the division reference, both label letters and the companies-only restriction, and the 2005 schedule shows the part gone, which fixes the end of the series.
evidence_quote: Part O Cost base adjustments resulting from debt forgiveness-Division 139-to be completed by companies only
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the part is companies-only, that it was dropped after 2004, or what a cost base reduction does to later gains.

value_domain: Total cost base adjustment from debt forgiveness (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2004 (NAT 3423-6.2004), part O
variable_description: The total cost base adjustment the company made on the debtor side of a commercial debt forgiveness, at label S of part O of the old CGT schedule. It is the companion to the reduction at label Q: the form pairs label S with the yes or no at label R, "Interest in debtor", where label Q is paired with an interest in the creditor. The two amounts therefore describe the same transaction from opposite ends of the relationship and should not be added together as if they were one exposure.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2004 (NAT 3423-6.2004), part O
value_definition: A dollar amount for the year, reported by companies only, on the same part of the schedule as the creditor-side reduction.
limitation: Confusing it with the label Q amount reverses the direction of the transaction, since one side holds an interest in the creditor and the other an interest in the debtor. The ATO also applies a forgiven amount in a fixed order - revenue losses, then capital losses, then deductible expenditure, then cost bases - so this figure is only the residue that reached cost bases and understates the size of the forgiveness.
rationale: The 2004 schedule shows part O's two label pairs and their headings, and the ATO's commercial debt forgiveness appendix gives the order in which a net forgiven amount is applied.
evidence_quote: Interest in debtor R yes no Print X in the appropriate box Total cost base adjustment S
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never distinguished the debtor side from the creditor side or said where cost bases sit in the order of application.

value_domain: Non-capital purchases reported at G11 of the business activity statement (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, step 3 purchases
variable_description: The business's non-capital purchases for the BAS period, label G11, which is the closest thing BLADE has to a high-frequency measure of operating inputs. The ATO tells businesses to report at G11 "all of your business purchases relevant to the reporting period (other than those reported at G10 ), such as most business purchases, including services and stock bought for resale", so it covers trading stock, running expenses and equipment leases. The split from capital purchases at G10 is partly conventional: firms expecting turnover under $1 million may put capital items of $1,000 or less at G11.
description_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, step 3 purchases
value_definition: A dollar amount for one BAS period, reported GST-inclusive unless the business uses the accounts method and has chosen to show amounts as GST-exclusive.
limitation: It is not an expense measure from the accounts: it is purchases in the period on the firm's chosen GST accounting basis, so a cash-basis remitter's G11 moves with payment timing rather than with activity. The $1,000 threshold also lets genuinely capital spending sit in G11, so the G10 and G11 split cannot be used as a clean investment and operating expenditure divide.
rationale: The ATO page defines what belongs at G11, lists the inclusions and states the $1,000 rule that blurs the boundary with capital purchases.
evidence_quote: At G11, you need to report all of your business purchases relevant to the reporting period (other than those reported at G10 ), such as most business purchases, including services and stock bought for resale
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Non-capital purchases' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never named the BAS label, the GST basis or the threshold that lets capital items in.

value_domain: Binary flag on the ABN to business unit mapping
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses methodology, statistical unit and two-population model
variable_description: Whether this ABN is split by the ABS across more than one Type of Activity Unit, which happens when one legal entity runs distinct kinds of production. The ABS builds TAUs so that each "consists of one or more business entities, sub entities or branches of a business that can be grouped according to production activity", and classifies each by the industry of its main activity. When the flag is set, the ABN carries one tax record but several industry classifications, so an industry analysis using ABN-level ANZSIC will attribute all of the firm's activity to whichever unit won the label.
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses methodology, statistical unit and two-population model
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and a full stop for missing. It is the mirror image of many_abn_to_one_tau, and both can be 0 for a simple one-to-one mapping.
limitation: It does not say how the ABN's reported income, purchases or wages divide between the units, and the ABS does not publish that apportionment in BLADE, so a flagged ABN cannot be split for analysis. It also does not mark a change: an ABN can gain or lose units as the ABS re-profiles the business, without anything happening to the business itself.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the TAU as a production-activity grouping classified by main activity, which is what makes a one-to-many mapping possible and what it costs an analyst.
evidence_quote: A Type of Activity Unit (TAU) consists of one or more business entities, sub entities or branches of a business that can be grouped according to production activity, and can report a minimum set of data items.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'One ABN to many Type of Activity Units (TAUs)' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never explained what splitting an ABN does to industry coding.

value_domain: Count of options or rights issued in a scrip-for-scrip rollover
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part L
variable_description: How many options or rights the acquiring entity issued as consideration in a scrip-for-scrip rollover, at label I of part L of the CGT schedule. Part L is headed "Scrip-for-scrip rollover for acquiring entity - to be completed by companies and trusts only", so a value here identifies the firm as the acquirer in a takeover or merger, not the target. The ATO explains that such a rollover "allows you to defer your CGT obligation until a later CGT event happens to your shares or units", which is why the count of paper issued is collected alongside the number of original entities and the cost base of the interests acquired.
description_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part L
value_definition: A count, up to eleven digits, of options, rights and similar instruments issued. It sits beside a separate count of shares and units issued in the same part.
limitation: It is a number of instruments and not a value, so it cannot be compared across deals without a price, and a large count can represent a small consideration. Nor does it identify the target: the schedule collects the original entity's tax file number in a neighbouring label, which is not carried through to a usable business identifier.
rationale: The 2012 schedule shows part L, its companies-and-trusts restriction and the label I count, and the ATO definitions appendix explains what a scrip-for-scrip rollover does.
evidence_quote: Part L Scrip-for-scrip rollover for acquiring entity - to be completed by companies and trusts only
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Number of options/rights etc issued' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the row marks an acquirer in a scrip-for-scrip rollover.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year that the business entity did not work out under the discount method, as reported on its capital gains tax schedule. The ATO requires the other method where the holding period is short: "If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method to calculate your capital gain." OF and NF in the DIL label are the old-form and new-form wordings.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and the small business concessions. No CGT discount applies to these gains.
limitation: The column mixes the other method with the indexation method. Companies cannot claim the CGT discount at all, so for a company entity this column is close to its whole capital gain rather than a subset. The OF and NF reading of the DIL prefixes is inferred.
rationale: The BLADE DIL label names the total current year capital gains for other capital gains, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide defines the methods.
evidence_quote: If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method to calculate your capital gain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Other GST-free sales reported at G3 of the business activity statement (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, step 1 sales
variable_description: GST-free sales other than exports, label G3 on the business activity statement. It is where basic food, most health and education services, childcare, water and sales of going concerns are reported. The ATO instructs that "All amounts reported at G3 should also have been reported at G1", so it is a carve-out of total sales rather than an addition to them. The label is a strong industry signal: a food retailer, a medical practice or a childcare centre will show a large G3 where a manufacturer shows nothing.
description_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, step 1 sales
value_definition: A dollar amount for one BAS period, covering the GST-free categories listed in the ATO instructions, and excluding export sales, which have their own label at G2.
limitation: A large G3 does not mean a firm paid no GST: it still claims credits on its purchases, and it can have taxable sales at the same time. Food retailers may also use simplified accounting methods to estimate the GST-free share, so G3 for those businesses is an approved estimate rather than a transaction total, and a sale of a going concern can put an unusually large one-off amount in an otherwise small firm's G3.
rationale: The ATO page lists what belongs at G3, states its relationship to G1 and notes the simplified accounting methods available to food retailers.
evidence_quote: At G3 report your other GST-free sales as listed below. All amounts reported at G3 should also have been reported at G1 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Other GST-free sales' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the amount is a subset of total sales or that exports go elsewhere.

value_domain: Dealroom binary tag for businesses outside its technology taxonomy
value_source: Dealroom, sector taxonomy guide
variable_description: Whether Dealroom tags the business as sitting outside technology, held constant across every observation of the ABN. Dealroom classifies companies through a structured taxonomy of "industries, sub-industries, tags, and technologies", and this flag marks the firms its own classification treats as not belonging to that technology universe. It is a vendor judgement about the company, so it will not agree with an ANZSIC-based definition of the technology sector.
description_source: Dealroom, sector taxonomy guide

limitation: The flag is defined by exclusion from a commercial taxonomy, so it moves when Dealroom revises its sectors rather than when the business changes what it does. evidence_quote: the combination of industries, sub-industries, tags, and technologies
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence about a binary time-invariant tag with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the classification is a vendor's and cannot be mapped to ANZSIC.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement clause indicator (Y = yes)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Flags a federal enterprise agreement that caps how much overtime an employee can be required or allowed to work. It is a coded reading of the agreement's clauses by DEWR staff, not a measure of overtime actually worked, and the unit is the registered agreement rather than the business. DEWR holds "conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997", but the valid-response note confines this particular flag to agreements coded between 2002 and 2009.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A single character, Y for yes, on the agreement record. No explicit N is published, so a blank is the absence of a coded yes rather than a coded no.
limitation: It will not support a trend. Coding stops after 2009, so a business whose current agreement was approved in 2015 looks identical to one whose agreement says nothing about overtime limits, and DEWR warns that "not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database". A capped-overtime clause also says nothing about how binding the cap is in practice.
rationale: DEWR publishes what the Workplace Agreements Database is, which agreements are in scope, that about 200 items are coded per agreement, and that the set of conditions coded is reviewed annually, which is what explains a flag that exists only for part of the series.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's one-line clause wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said the flag is coded only for 2002 to 2009 agreements or that it describes a clause rather than hours worked.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement clause indicator (Y = yes)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Flags an agreement that folds overtime pay into an annualised or loaded salary instead of paying it as a separate penalty. It marks a pay-structure choice in the agreement text, so a business with this clause can have staff working overtime with no overtime line in the payroll. DEWR codes "around 200 data items" for each agreement, of which this is one, and the record covers the agreement rather than any one employee under it.
description_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A single character, Y for yes, on the agreement record. Partial and complete absorption share the one code, and no salary loading percentage is attached.
limitation: It cannot tell you whether workers are better or worse off, because the size of the loading that replaces the overtime penalty is not recorded. Nor does it say what share of the employees covered by the agreement are on the annualised arrangement, since the flag is set for the agreement as a whole.
rationale: The DEWR page defines the database, its coverage of conditions since 1997 and the volume of coded items per agreement, which places this clause flag in its collection and fixes the unit of record.
evidence_quote: There are over 180,000 agreements in the database. An average of 6,000 agreements are added each year, and around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's clause wording and used the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the flag is an agreement-level clause code with no loading amount behind it.
