variable_description: Whether the partnership chose not to use the accelerated depreciation offered under backing business investment, for some of its eligible assets or for all of them. The ATO instruction reads: "Show A at V if you are opting out for some of your eligible assets and show B if you are opting out for all of your eligible assets." The choice is made asset by asset and cannot be reversed: "Once a choice is made it can't be revoked." Backing business investment applied to new assets first used between 12 March 2020 and 30 June 2021, so the column is alive for two income years only.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2021 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
value_definition: A coded flag with 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets and 15 for no; anything else is an invalid or absent response. The letters A and B on the paper return map to 5 and 10.
limitation: Opting out is not the same as not claiming. A firm that bought no new assets, or that used temporary full expensing or the instant asset write-off instead, never reaches this question, so a code of 15 or a blank covers both a deliberate no and a firm the measure never touched.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the 2021 partnership return question at label V, and the ATO instruction for that label gives the two response letters, the irrevocability of the choice and the years the measure ran.
evidence_quote: Show A at V if you are opting out for some of your eligible assets and show B if you are opting out for all of your eligible assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text and its code list but printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the choice is per asset, irreversible, or confined to 2019-20 and 2020-21.

value_domain: Count of assets claimed under temporary full expensing, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: How many separate assets the partnership wrote off in full under temporary full expensing this year. The ATO label guide says to "Show the total number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing", at label 49T on the partnership return. It is a count that sits beside the dollar deduction, so the two together give an average cost per asset written off, which no other column in the return provides.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A five-digit character count of assets at the partnership return's temporary full expensing label, reported for income years from 2020-21 to 2022-23.
limitation: The number is a best effort rather than a verified count: the ATO states that "You will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect number of assets where you have made your best attempt to determine the number of assets you are claiming for." A firm that groups a fitout as one asset and a firm that lists every component report very different counts for the same spend.
rationale: The ATO label guide maps this exact wording to the partnership return label and states both what the count covers and the tolerance applied to it.
evidence_quote: You will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect number of assets where you have made your best attempt to determine the number of assets you are claiming for.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the count is self-assessed and tolerant of error, or that it pairs with the deduction amount.

value_domain: Coded choice to opt out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: Whether the partnership chose not to write off some or all of its eligible assets immediately under temporary full expensing. The ATO label guide directs the lodger to write "A if you are opting out for some of your assets" or "B if you are opting out for all of your assets", at label 49P on the partnership return. Opting out is a real economic choice, because it moves a deduction from this year into later years and can preserve a loss position or a distribution to partners.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A coded flag with 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets and 15 for no; anything else is an invalid or absent response. It mirrors the letters A and B used on the paper return.
limitation: The question is closed to small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules, who cannot opt out at all and are told to leave the label blank. A blank therefore mixes those firms with firms that had no eligible assets and firms that simply took the full deduction, and this column cannot separate the three.
rationale: The ATO label guide gives the response letters for this question and, in the tables covering small business entities, states that firms using simplified depreciation cannot opt out and must leave it blank.
evidence_quote: You cannot opt out of temporary full expensing for assets that the simplified depreciation rules apply to. Leave this blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text and its codes with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a whole class of small businesses is barred from answering.

value_domain: Personal services business employment test indicator (Y or N)
value_source: ATO, Personal services income, Employment test
variable_description: Whether the firm claims it passed the employment test, one of four tests that let personal services income be treated as a personal services business. The ATO sets the bar as employing or contracting others, plus one of two conditions: "at least 20% of the principal work is performed by others" or "one or more apprentices are employed for at least 6 months of the income year". Passing means the personal services income rules do not apply, so income is not attributed back to the individual who earned it.
description_source: ATO, Personal services income, Employment test
value_definition: A single character flag, Y for yes and N for no, with anything else an invalid or absent response. It sits in the personal services income block alongside the results, unrelated clients and business premises tests.
limitation: This is a self-assessment, not a determination: the ATO allows a taxpayer to self-assess against the employment test without applying for a ruling, so a Y is the firm's own claim and can be overturned on review. Where a partnership or company has more than one individual generating personal services income the test is applied to each of them separately, so one flag cannot describe the whole entity.
rationale: The ATO's personal services income guidance defines the employment test, its two alternative conditions, the 80 per cent rule that must also be met, and its application to partnerships, which is what a Y or N on this column asserts.
evidence_quote: If you operate through a company, partnership or trust and you have more than one individual generating PSI, you will need to work out whether you pass the employment test for each individual.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Employment test' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which test it is, what passing requires, or that the answer is self-assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of expense reconciliation adjustments, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss item 5
variable_description: The single line that bridges the partnership's accounting expenses and its tax deductions. It nets add backs, such as non-deductible entertainment, penalties and fines and prepayments not yet deductible, against subtractions, such as the tax decline in value of depreciating assets, project pool deductions and section 40-880 deductions. The ATO notes the result may be negative: "If the expense subtractions exceed the expense add backs, the total is a negative amount."
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at item 5 label B of the partnership return, with a loss indicator printed beside it on the paper form when the net figure is negative.
limitation: The column is a residual, so a large value can come from timing, from permanent differences, or from a single depreciation regime change, and no part of the return decomposes it. Because the loss position is carried by a code letter rather than by the number, an extract that drops the indicator silently converts negative reconciliations into positive ones.
rationale: The DIL label is item 5 label B of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction lists the add backs and subtractions that make it up and states that the net figure can be negative.
evidence_quote: If the expense subtractions exceed the expense add backs, the total is a negative amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Expense Reconciliation Adjustments' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is signed or that it is the accounting-to-tax bridge.

value_domain: Dollar amount of contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: What the partnership paid for labour it bought in rather than employed. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label C the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages", and the examples run from consultants and sub-contractors to commissions, agency fees and management fees. The DIL label records a form change: the item used to be called External labour costs, so a long series has one wording before the change and another after it.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense at item 5 label C, reported in the primary production, non-primary production or totals column. It sits beside Total salary and wage expenses, which carries employed labour.
limitation: It is not the whole of a firm's outsourced labour: the ATO directs external labour recorded in the cost of sales account to stay there, and sends accounting and legal fees to All other expenses, so labour-heavy firms that book contractors into cost of sales show little here. Renaming the item also means the label change, rather than any change in behaviour, can shift what lodgers put in it.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 5 label C on the partnership return, including the note about the previous label, and the ATO instruction defines the expense and names what is directed elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Show at label C the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the return label, including the parenthetical about the previous name, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that cost-of-sales labour is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of fringe benefit employee contributions, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: What employees paid the partnership towards fringe benefits they received, such as a contribution towards a car. The ATO instruction for item 46 reads: "Show at label T all the payments the partnership has received from recipients of fringe benefits", and adds that "Employee contributions form part of the employer's or associate's assessable income in situations where employees make payments for fringe benefits they have received." A non-zero value therefore marks a firm that both provides fringe benefits and recovers part of their cost.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
value_definition: A whole-dollar income amount at label T of item 46 in the partnership's business and professional items, assessable to the partnership.
limitation: It measures recovery, not provision. A firm that gives generous fringe benefits and charges nothing for them reports zero, exactly like a firm that gives none, so this column cannot be used to identify which businesses provide fringe benefits. The value of the benefits themselves is reported in the separate fringe benefits tax system, not here.
rationale: The DIL label is item 46 of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the receipts and states their assessable character.
evidence_quote: Show at label T all the payments the partnership has received from recipients of fringe benefits.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Fringe benefit employee contributions' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is income to the firm rather than a cost, or that zero does not mean no benefits.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franking credits received indirectly, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Franking credits that reached the partnership through another partnership or trust rather than straight from the paying company. The ATO instruction for item 8 reads: "Show at label D the partnership's share of any franking credits from a franking entity received through another partnership or trust", and directs credits received directly to item 12 instead, which is p_dimpcred. The split matters because it separates a firm that holds shares from a firm that holds an interest in an entity that holds shares.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 8 label D of the partnership return, part of the share of credits block that also carries ABN withholding, TFN withholding and foreign resident withholding credits.
limitation: A credit shown here is not necessarily usable. The ATO excludes credits where the holding period rule or the related payments rule fails, or where dividend washing applies, but only credits the lodger already knew were excluded are kept out, so the column records a claim rather than a settled entitlement. The credit is ultimately used by the partners, not by the partnership.
rationale: The DIL label is item 8 label D of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the credit, contrasts it with the direct credit at item 12 and lists the integrity rules that exclude amounts.
evidence_quote: Show at label D the partnership's share of any franking credits from a franking entity received through another partnership or trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Share of franking credits from franked distributions' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished indirect credits from the direct credits at item 12.

value_domain: De-identified predecessor farm business identifier in the Farm Level Analytical Dataset
value_source: ABARES, Agricultural Data Integration Project
variable_description: The identifier a farm business carried before the one in fd_id on the same row, which is what lets a farm be followed across a change of unit. ABARES describes FLAD as combining "farm-level micro-data from all ABS Agricultural surveys and census' undertaken between 2000-01 and 2017-18", so units are re-formed as collections change and this column is the link back to the earlier record. It sits on the FLAD control table beside fd_id, the de-identified ABN and the time series identifier, the four keys that hold a farm's history together.
description_source: ABARES, Agricultural Data Integration Project
value_definition: A ten-digit alphanumeric identifier of the same shape as fd_id, opaque by construction and pointing to a farm business unit in an earlier FLAD build or collection.
limitation: It records a link, not a reason for the link, so a change of identifier could be a merger, a split, a change in the ABS unit model or a correction, and this column cannot say which. Where a farm has no predecessor, or where the antecedent could not be established, the field is empty, so a blank cannot be read as evidence that the business is new.
rationale: The ABARES page describes the Farm Level Analytical Dataset, its coverage across successive ABS agricultural collections and its integration into BLADE, which is what makes a previous-unit link necessary and interpretable.
evidence_quote: farm-level micro-data from all ABS Agricultural surveys and census' undertaken between 2000-01 and 2017-18
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'De-identified previous Ag unit' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column is an antecedent link to fd_id or why a farm's unit identifier changes.

value_domain: Count of distinct technology areas filed in across all patents (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different technology areas the business filed patents in this year, counted over the whole classification rather than within one coarse group. IP Australia sets the ceiling: "For patents, designs and trade marks there are 35, 32 and 45 possible classification areas respectively." A firm with a scope well above its coarse-area scopes is filing across technological boundaries rather than deepening one field.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: An integer from zero to 35, counting distinct technology areas among the year's filings. It is bounded above by p_filed_count only when patents carry a single classification each.
limitation: The measure is annual, so a firm that files in a different area each year looks narrow every year and broad only when the years are pooled; nothing on the row does that pooling. Because a single application can be classified into several areas, scope can exceed the number of distinct inventions the firm actually worked on.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables and states the number of patent classification areas, which sets what this column counts and its upper bound.
evidence_quote: For patents, designs and trade marks there are 35, 32 and 45 possible classification areas respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing gave the ceiling of 35 or warned that the count is reset each financial year.

value_domain: Count of all patent applications filed in the financial year (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many patent applications the business filed with IP Australia during the financial year, across all technologies. It is the total that the five coarse-area filing counts on the same row sit inside, and because "it is possible for a right to exist in more than one of the coarse classification areas simultaneously", those five will add to more than this number. IPLoRD is applicant-centric, with an ABN attached where one could be found, which is what puts patent filings on a business row in BLADE.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of patent applications filed in the year by the applicant, the unweighted metric, with joint applications counted in full for each applicant.
limitation: A filing is an intention, not an invention: many applications are provisional or lapse without ever being examined, and nothing in the count separates them. IPLoRD covers filings with IP Australia, so a firm that patents mainly overseas can report zero here while holding a substantial international portfolio.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the count metric and the filed event stream, states that patents may sit in several coarse areas at once, and describes IPLoRD as an applicant-centric view of Australian filings linked by ABN.
evidence_quote: For patents, it is possible for a right to exist in more than one of the coarse classification areas simultaneously.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total number of patent filings during the financial year' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the coarse-area counts overstate the total or that coverage is Australian filings only.

value_domain: Most frequent technology area among all patent filings (IPLoRD class code)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The single technology area that best describes what the business filed patents on this year, chosen from the full set rather than within one coarse group. IP Australia notes why a simplification was needed at all: the raw patent classification "comprises tens of thousands of classification symbols" and is "not intended for use by lay audiences to gain a high-level understanding of a company's IP activity". The mode here can fall outside electrical engineering, so it will not always match p_elec_eng_filed_modal_class.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A character code for one of the 35 technology areas in IP Australia's simplified patent classification, derived from the WIPO technology-to-IPC concordance with post-2008 symbols added by IP Australia.
limitation: The classification is a translation of examiner-assigned patent symbols, so it describes the technical content of a document and not the market the firm sells into; a manufacturer and its software supplier can share a modal class. Ties between areas are resolved by the production rules rather than reported, so a firm with an even spread still shows a single decisive-looking code.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the modal metric and explains the construction and purpose of the 35-area simplified patent classification that supplies the codes.
evidence_quote: The IPC classification system comprises tens of thousands of classification symbols which may be applied either singly or multiply to a patent application to describe its subject matter.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Most common technology area class for all patent filed applications during the financial year' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said where the classification comes from or how coarse it is.

value_domain: Applicant-weighted count of all patent applications filed (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of all patent applications filed in the year, with each joint filing divided among its applicants. This is the column to sum when building an industry or economy-wide filing total, because the unweighted count would count a two-party application twice. IP Australia's weighting is mechanical: an application filed by n applicants contributes 1/n to each of them.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative fractional count of applications across all technology areas, formed from 1/n applicant shares, and equal to p_filed_count for any firm that files alone.
limitation: The gap between this column and the unweighted count is a measure of joint filing, not of research collaboration: co-applicants are often related entities within one corporate group, and that shows up as collaboration here. The weighting also ignores how much each party contributed.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the weighted count metric, its 1/n rule and its purpose of preserving aggregate application numbers, which is what this all-technology column carries.
evidence_quote: Weighted count variables consider the number of applicants associated with an IP Right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording about application fractions filed with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said when the weighted total is the correct one to use.

value_domain: Financial year of the applicant's first patent application (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The financial year in which the business first ever applied for an Australian patent, repeated unchanged on every year of its record. It is IPLoRD's p_first_application_financial_year, one of "a range of variables that identifies when an applicant first applied for or was granted a particular type of IP right", and it lets a first-time patentee be separated from an established one without reconstructing the whole history. Because the register goes back a long way, the year can precede BLADE's business data by decades.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A four-digit financial year. IPLoRD's coverage runs from 1904 to the end of 2020, so values can be very early for long-lived firms and the column is time-invariant within an applicant.
limitation: It is the first application by this applicant identity, not by this business: a firm that patented under a predecessor entity, under a founder's name, or before it obtained the ABN that links it to BLADE will show a later year than its real patenting history. Applicants matched by IPGOD party identifier rather than ABN cannot be joined to the business data at all.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary names this field among the new 'first' variables, explains what they identify, and states the dataset's coverage period and its applicant identification scheme.
evidence_quote: In this new release, we also included a range of variables that identifies when an applicant first applied for or was granted a particular type of IP right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'The financial year the applicant had filed its first patent application' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the value is fixed across years or that it belongs to an applicant identity rather than a business.

value_domain: Financial year the applicant first held an enforceable patent (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The financial year the business first had a patent granted enforceable status, held constant on every row for that applicant. IP Australia explains the phrasing: "Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia. The terminology is reproduced here for simpler interoperability with the parent dataset." Set against p_first_application_fy on the same row, the gap between the two years is the applicant's wait from first filing to first enforceable right.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A four-digit financial year, time-invariant within an applicant, and empty for an applicant that has filed but never had a patent granted.
limitation: The gap from first application to first enforceable status is not an examination time: the first filing and the first grant are usually different applications, and an abandoned first attempt inflates the gap. A missing value also mixes a firm still waiting on examination with one whose applications all failed.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary names this field among the 'first' variables and defines the enforceable status terminology it uses, carried over from IPGOD.
evidence_quote: Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'The financial year the applicant was first granted an enforceable patent right' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the enforceable status wording or what an empty value means.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign resident withholding credit, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Tax withheld in Australia under the foreign resident withholding measure and claimed by the partnership as a credit. The regime is narrow: it "applies to foreign residents who engage in certain regulated categories of activities in Australia, such as foreign residents involved in sport, entertainment, and building and construction". The 'share of' wording points to item 8 label U, the partnership's share of credits flowing from other partnerships and trusts, rather than item 6 label U, where withholding from the partnership's own payments is claimed.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit amount on the partnership return, reported in whole dollars alongside the gross payments it relates to. Foreign resident capital gains withholding is excluded by instruction.
limitation: The column identifies a withholding obligation, not the firm's residence or its foreign ownership, and it exists only for the handful of regulated activity classes prescribed in the Taxation Administration Regulations. The numeric infix in the column name is a form-label sequence marker that the data item list does not explain, so it should not be read as pinning the amount to a particular return item.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the partnership return defines foreign resident withholding, sets out both the direct claim at item 6 and the share of credits at item 8, and states what is excluded, which together fix the meaning of a 'share of credit' column.
evidence_quote: Show at label U the partnership's share of any foreign resident withholding credits received from other partnerships and trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which activities the regime covers or that capital gains withholding is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franked distributions from trusts, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Franked dividends that reached the partnership through a trust, reported grossed up by the franking credit attached to them. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label F the partnership's share of the franked distribution (described as franked dividends, franked distributions or attributable franked distributions) plus its share of the franking credit attached to the franked distribution." The deductions against this income sit at p_dtnfdtrst, and the credit itself is also counted at p_fcr_wheld_amt.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 8 label F, inclusive of the franking credit gross-up, and therefore larger than the cash the partnership actually received.
limitation: Because the figure is grossed up, treating it as cash income overstates receipts by the amount of the franking credit, and adding it to p_fcr_wheld_amt counts that credit twice. Distributions traceable to a New Zealand franking company are excluded by instruction and reported as foreign income, so a trans-Tasman group's franked income is split across two parts of the return.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 8 label F on the partnership return, and the ATO instruction states that the amount includes the franking credit gross-up and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: Show at label F the partnership's share of the franked distribution (described as franked dividends, franked distributions or attributable franked distributions) plus its share of the franking credit attached to the franked distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Franked distributions from trusts' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount is grossed up and overlaps the franking credit column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of first year backing business investment accelerated depreciation, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2021 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: The accelerated depreciation the partnership claimed in the first year it held a new asset under backing business investment. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at M the total amount claimed using Backing business investment for assets first used or installed ready for use in 2020-21", and defines the amount as 50 per cent of the asset's cost plus the ordinary decline in value calculated on the remaining half. A separate label carries the subsequent year claims for the same assets, so this column isolates new investment.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2021 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at label M in the capital allowances block of the 2020-21 partnership return, restricted to assets first used or installed ready for use in that year.
limitation: The measure ran only for assets first held from 12 March 2020 and first used by 30 June 2021 by businesses under $500 million turnover, and it cannot be used on an asset that took temporary full expensing or the instant asset write-off. A zero is therefore usually a choice of a competing concession rather than an absence of investment, and a series across 2020-21 to 2021-22 breaks because the label ceases.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the 2020-21 partnership return label M, and the ATO instruction for that label gives the calculation, the eligible assets and the year covered.
evidence_quote: Show at M the total amount claimed using Backing business investment for assets first used or installed ready for use in 2020-21.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is a first-year-only claim or that it is mutually exclusive with temporary full expensing.

value_domain: Dollar amount of forestry managed investment scheme deduction, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
variable_description: What the partnership deducted for payments into a forestry managed investment scheme. The ATO allows the deduction at item 17 where the partnership holds a forestry interest, paid a forestry manager under a formal agreement and was told the scheme met the 70 per cent direct forestry expenditure rule in Division 394 of the ITAA 1997. Timing is cash based: "The deduction is claimed in the income year in which the payment is made." Its income counterpart is p_frstry_mis_incm_amt.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at item 17 of the partnership return, covering both initial and ongoing payments for an initial participant in a scheme.
limitation: The deduction is conditional after the fact: it is denied if the partnership disposes of its forestry interest within four years of the end of the year of first payment, unless the disposal was outside its control, so a claim in the data can later be reversed. A payment here buys an interest in trees managed by someone else and is not evidence that the partnership carries on forestry.
rationale: The DIL label is item 17 of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction gives the eligibility conditions, the timing rule and the four-year clawback.
evidence_quote: The deduction is claimed in the income year in which the payment is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Forestry managed investment scheme deduction' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the deduction can be clawed back or that it is cash-timed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of forestry managed investment scheme income, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
variable_description: What the partnership received back from a forestry managed investment scheme, at item 10 of the return. It gathers thinning proceeds, harvest and sale receipts, and, where a capital gains tax event ended or reduced a forestry interest, the market value of the interest rather than the cash received. The DIL calls it income, but part of it is a deemed amount: a partnership that sold its interest reports the market value at the time of the event.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 10 label Q, combining actual receipts with market-value amounts brought to account on a capital gains tax event affecting a forestry interest.
limitation: It is lumpy and event-driven, so a large value marks a harvest or a sale rather than a year of trading, and it can appear in a year in which no money changed hands. Because initial and subsequent participants are treated differently, two partnerships with the same interest can report very different amounts on the same event.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 10 of the partnership return sets out exactly which receipts and deemed amounts go to label Q and how the treatment differs for initial and subsequent participants.
evidence_quote: Include the market value of the forestry interest at the time of the CGT event at label Q

value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5

description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5

rationale: The DIL label is the primary production side of item 5's gross payments where ABN not quoted, and the ATO instruction defines the three-column structure that gives the PP and NPP suffixes their meaning.
evidence_quote: primary production, showing relevant amounts of income and expenses from primary production

value_domain: Dollar amount of expenses against foreign resident withholding income, partnership return

description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense at item 5 label P of the partnership return, reported only where the partnership had gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding.
limitation: Because the instruction excludes these costs from every other expense label, summing the item 5 expense labels without this one understates the firm's total costs for the year. rationale: The DIL label is item 5 label P of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the expense, ties it to the label B income and states that it must not appear elsewhere.

evidence_quote: Show at label B gross payments to the partnership that were regulated foreign resident income. Gross payments includes amounts withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross payments subject to FRW - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which activities are regulated or that treaty-exempt payments are left out.

value_domain: Count of distinct patent technology area classes, IPLORD
value_source: WIPO, Concept of a Technology Classification for Country Comparisons (WIPO IPC Technology Concordance Table)
variable_description: How many distinct technology areas the year's patent grants spanned, which says how broad the new protection was rather than how much of it there was. Grant is the point at which the right becomes usable: IP Australia says that once granted "you can take legal action for any infringements that occur on and after the publication date". Grant follows filing by several years, so the year a grant lands is not the year the invention was worked on. It reads with the matching modal_class column: scope says how wide, modal class says where.
description_source: WIPO, Concept of a Technology Classification for Country Comparisons (WIPO IPC Technology Concordance Table)
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of distinct technology area classes reached by the applications granted during the financial year, capped by the thirty-five fields the concordance defines. The class list is the full technology area class list at Appendix 10 of the IPLORD documentation, which follows the WIPO IPC Technology Concordance: five sectors and thirty-five fields built from International Patent Classification codes.
limitation: Breadth in the classification is not breadth in the market: the classes are the codes patent examiners assigned to the business's applications, not the products or customers the business serves. A firm selling one invention into several markets therefore looks narrow, and a firm whose single invention carries several codes looks wide. It also moves with how many codes an examiner attached to an application, which is not a decision the business made.
rationale: IPLORD is IP Australia's longitudinal patent product inside BLADE, and the ABS names it as a BLADE source. The column is one cell of a grid of technology area (all technology areas) by event (granted) by measure (class_scope), so the meaning follows from what granted means in the Australian patent system and from the technology classification the class names come from. The WIPO IPC Technology Concordance defines the sectors and fields the IPLORD class names reproduce.
evidence_quote: The classification should be based exclusively on codes of the IPC, for many data sources do not provide useful text elements for more advanced analyses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and the generic 'does not publish a finite value list' sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what the granted stage of a patent is, what the all technology areas classes cover, or why the class_scope measure differs from the three measures in the columns beside it.

value_domain: Count of patent applications, IPLORD
value_source: IP Australia, How to apply for a standard patent

Grant is the point at which the right becomes usable: IP Australia says that once granted "you can take legal action for any infringements that occur on and after the publication date". Grant follows filing by several years, so the year a grant lands is not the year the invention was worked on. Whole counting, so a co-owned right counts once for this business and once for every other owner; the matching w_count column is the fractional version.
description_source: IP Australia, How to apply for a standard patent
value_definition: A non-negative whole count of applications granted during the financial year, one value per business per financial year. The classification behind the column is the full technology area class list at Appendix 10 of the IPLORD documentation, which follows the WIPO IPC Technology Concordance: five sectors and thirty-five fields built from International Patent Classification codes.
limitation: The count says nothing about the size or value of what was granted, so a platform patent and a minor improvement weigh the same. Grant lags filing by years, so a fall here reports a filing decision taken several years earlier rather than a fall in this year's inventive effort.
rationale: IPLORD is IP Australia's longitudinal patent product inside BLADE, and the ABS names it as a BLADE source. The column is one cell of a grid of technology area (all technology areas) by event (granted) by measure (count), so the meaning follows from what granted means in the Australian patent system and from the technology classification the class names come from. IP Australia's own patent pages define that stage of the right.
evidence_quote: If no-one opposes your patent, your patent application will be granted
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and the generic 'does not publish a finite value list' sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what the granted stage of a patent is, what the all technology areas classes cover, or why the count measure differs from the three measures in the columns beside it.

value_domain: Patent technology area class code, IPLORD
value_source: WIPO, Concept of a Technology Classification for Country Comparisons (WIPO IPC Technology Concordance Table)
variable_description: The technology area that most of the business's patents granted this year fall into, its centre of gravity in the year's grants. Grant is the point at which the right becomes usable: IP Australia says that once granted "you can take legal action for any infringements that occur on and after the publication date". Grant follows filing by several years, so the year a grant lands is not the year the invention was worked on. It reads with the matching class_scope column: scope counts the areas, this names the largest of them.
description_source: WIPO, Concept of a Technology Classification for Country Comparisons (WIPO IPC Technology Concordance Table)
value_definition: A character class code from Appendix 10 of the IPLORD documentation, taken over the applications granted during the financial year, so it cannot be summed or averaged. The class list is the full technology area class list at Appendix 10 of the IPLORD documentation, which follows the WIPO IPC Technology Concordance: five sectors and thirty-five fields built from International Patent Classification codes.

A business with two patents in different classes and a business with twenty split eleven and nine both report one class, and the rule for breaking a tie is not published. It also describes the year's grants only, which for a small filer can be a single application chosen by examination timing.
rationale: IPLORD is IP Australia's longitudinal patent product inside BLADE, and the ABS names it as a BLADE source. The column is one cell of a grid of technology area (all technology areas) by event (granted) by measure (modal_class), so the meaning follows from what granted means in the Australian patent system and from the technology classification the class names come from. The WIPO IPC Technology Concordance defines the sectors and fields the IPLORD class names reproduce.
evidence_quote: the classification should allow crude analysis based on about 5 groups, on the other hand, a more detailed analysis with about 20 fields should be feasible
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and the generic 'does not publish a finite value list' sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what the granted stage of a patent is, what the all technology areas classes cover, or why the modal_class measure differs from the three measures in the columns beside it.

value_domain: Fractional count of patent applications, IPLORD
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The business's fractional share of the patent applications granted this financial year, with a jointly owned application split between its applicants. Grant is the point at which the right becomes usable: IP Australia says that once granted "you can take legal action for any infringements that occur on and after the publication date". Grant follows filing by several years, so the year a grant lands is not the year the invention was worked on. Adding this column across businesses recovers the number of applications, which adding the whole count does not.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A non-negative number that need not be whole, covering applications granted during the financial year, because an application shared between applicants contributes a fraction to each. The classification behind the column is the full technology area class list at Appendix 10 of the IPLORD documentation, which follows the WIPO IPC Technology Concordance: five sectors and thirty-five fields built from International Patent Classification codes.
limitation: A fraction of an application is not a fraction of its value, and an even split between applicants is an accounting convention rather than a statement about who controls the right. The splitting rule IPLORD uses is not published with the data, so these totals should not be mixed with counts built on another convention. Two businesses with the same fractional total can also sit very differently, one holding half of two grants and the other a tenth of ten.
rationale: IPLORD is IP Australia's longitudinal patent product inside BLADE, and the ABS names it as a BLADE source. The column is one cell of a grid of technology area (all technology areas) by event (granted) by measure (w_count), so the meaning follows from what granted means in the Australian patent system and from the technology classification the class names come from. No fetchable page documents how IPLORD splits an application between applicants, so this entry rests on the DIL wording and the ABS BLADE overview.
evidence_quote: Intellectual Property Australia: Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD) and Intellectual Property Refreshed Automated Product for Information (IPRAPID)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and the generic 'does not publish a finite value list' sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what the granted stage of a patent is, what the all technology areas classes cover, or why the w_count measure differs from the three measures in the columns beside it.

value_domain: ATO trust type code, partnership return item 8 non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Which kind of trust the partnership's non-primary-production trust distribution mainly came from. The ATO instructs that at the label for the share of net income from trusts "print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made", and "If this amount is from more than one type of trust, print the code that represents the trust with the greatest amount of distribution." It qualifies the dollar amount reported for the non-primary-production share of trust income on the same row, and it is only printed when that amount is not a loss.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A single ATO trust code carried in BLADE as a numeric mapping: 5 D deceased estate, 10 F fixed trust, 15 H hybrid, 20 I discretionary trust with investment income, 25 M cash management unit trust, 30 P listed public unit trust, 35 Q unlisted public unit trust, 40 S discretionary trust with service or management income, 45 T discretionary trust with trading income, 50 U fixed unit trust, 55 C special disability trust and 60 E testamentary trust, with everything else invalid or no response.
limitation: One code stands for a whole year of distributions, so a partnership that received income from a discretionary trust and a public unit trust shows only the larger of the two and the mix is lost. No code is printed at all when the amount is a loss, so a blank is not evidence that no trust distribution was received.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-primary-production distribution from trusts action code, which is the trust code box beside label R of item 8 on the ATO partnership tax return. The ATO instructions publish both the rule for choosing the code and the code table itself.
evidence_quote: If this amount is not a loss, in the box at the right of label R print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the code describes the source trust, that only the largest source is recorded, or that a loss suppresses it.

value_domain: ATO trust type code, partnership return item 8 primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Which kind of trust the partnership's primary-production trust distribution mainly came from. It is the primary-production twin of the non-primary-production trust code on the same return, sitting beside the partnership's share of primary production income included in a trust's net income. The ATO directs the lodger to "print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made", so this column tells a reader whether farm and forestry income reached the partnership through a deceased estate, a discretionary trust or a unit trust.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: The same ATO trust code list as the non-primary-production column, carried in BLADE as a numeric mapping from 5 through 60 onto the letters D, F, H, I, M, P, Q, S, T, U, C and E, with everything else invalid or no response. Primary production here has the ATO's meaning for the return, not an ANZSIC industry test.
limitation: It classifies the trust, not the farming activity, so it cannot be used to identify agricultural businesses; a discretionary trust code says nothing about what the trust does. It is also only present where a primary production trust distribution was reported and was not a loss, which makes it a small and selected subset of partnerships.
rationale: The DIL label names the primary production distribution from trusts action code, the trust code box at label Z of item 8 on the partnership return, for which the ATO publishes the selection rule and the code table.
evidence_quote: If this amount is not a loss, in the box at label Z print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish the primary production code from its non-primary-production twin.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, gross interest
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 11 Gross interest
variable_description: Interest the partnership received or was credited during the year, before any expense is set against it. The ATO defines the label as "the interest from banks and credit unions, building societies, debentures, notes and deposits, income accrued on discounted or deferred interest securities, government securities, and interest paid by us". It is a whole-year flow and it is gross, so the firm's interest expense sits separately at the total interest expenses label.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 11 Gross interest
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, not negative, self-assessed by the lodger. It includes amounts accrued rather than paid on discounted and deferred interest securities.
limitation: It is not the partnership's whole interest income. Interest received through a cash management trust or other trust investment product is reported with trust distributions at item 8 instead, and interest from an account held jointly outside a business partnership belongs on the partners' own returns, so a low figure can mean interest was reported elsewhere.
rationale: The DIL label matches the gross interest item of the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction for that label lists exactly what belongs in it and what is reported elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the interest from banks and credit unions, building societies, debentures, notes and deposits, income accrued on discounted or deferred interest securities, government securities, and interest paid by us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Gross interest' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the figure is gross, whole-year and self-assessed, nor which interest is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, gross rent
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 9 Rent
variable_description: Rental income the partnership earned from property held in the business, before any rental deduction. The ATO says "Show at label F the gross amount of rental income. This item can't be a loss." and counts booking and letting fees, retained bond money, insurance payouts for lost rent and tenant reimbursements of deductible expenses as part of it. Interest deductions, capital works deductions and other rental deductions on neighbouring labels are what turn it into net rent.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 9 Rent
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, never negative, excluding GST where the partnership is registered and GST is payable on the rent.
limitation: It only exists where the rent is business income of the partnership. Where the property is merely a joint investment the partners report their shares on their own returns, so a zero here does not mean the partners hold no property. Rent from foreign sources is reported with other assessable foreign source income instead.
rationale: The DIL label matches the gross rent label of item 9 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction for that label defines its content, its sign and its exclusions.
evidence_quote: Show at label F the gross amount of rental income. This item can't be a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the label 'Gross rent' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both slots, so it did not say the amount is gross, cannot be negative, or only appears for partnership business rent.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, personal services business determination
value_source: ATO, Personal services income: Self-assessing as a PSB
variable_description: Whether the partnership holds a Commissioner's determination that it is conducting a personal services business for at least one individual whose income it receives. A determination is granted by the ATO on application, and the ATO says "If you are unable to self-assess as a PSB for a particular income year, you may be able to apply for a PSB determination (PSBD) in some circumstances." That makes this column administratively different from the four self-assessment tests reported beside it, which the partnership asserts for itself.
description_source: ATO, Personal services income: Self-assessing as a PSB
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and everything else an invalid or absent response. It sits beside the four self-assessment indicators on the same return, for the results test, the unrelated clients test, the employment test and the business premises test.
limitation: A yes does not say how many individuals are covered or that all the partnership's personal services income is protected: the ATO applies the tests to each individual separately, so one determination can cover one worker and not another. It also does not date the determination, so a yes cannot be read as coverage for the whole income year.
rationale: The DIL label is the personal services business determination question on the partnership return, and the ATO's PSI guidance defines what a determination is and how it relates to self-assessment against the four tests.
evidence_quote: If you are unable to self-assess as a PSB for a particular income year, you may be able to apply for a PSB determination (PSBD) in some circumstances.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the question with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish a determination granted by the ATO from the self-assessed tests recorded on the same return.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, personal services income present
value_source: ATO, Personal services income: Income that is PSI
variable_description: Whether any of the partnership's income is really the reward for one individual's personal effort. The ATO defines it as income "that is mainly a reward for your personal effort or skill", and where an individual earns it through a company, partnership or trust that entity is a personal services entity. This is the gate question on the return: a yes opens the personal services income labels and the four personal services business tests, and a no closes them.
description_source: ATO, Personal services income: Income that is PSI
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and everything else an invalid or absent response. It gates the personal services income amount labels on the return, which stay blank unless the answer is yes.
limitation: A yes does not mean the personal services income rules bit. A partnership that answers yes can still be conducting a personal services business, in which case the attribution and deduction rules do not apply. The answer is also a self-assessment of the more-than-half test, so it records the lodger's judgement rather than an audited fact.
rationale: The DIL label is the personal services income gate question on the partnership return, and the ATO's own PSI page gives the definition of personal services income that the question turns on.
evidence_quote: Personal services income (PSI) is income that is received by you, or another entity connected with you, that is mainly a reward for your personal effort or skill
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never explained what personal services income is or that a yes does not imply the rules apply.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, total net income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: The partnership's whole-of-year net income or loss for tax purposes, Australian and foreign together, before it is divided among the partners. It is the total box at the foot of the income side of the return: the ATO says "Show at item 24 the total of the amounts shown at items 20 to 23", which adds net Australian income or loss to attributed foreign income and other assessable foreign source income. The statement of distribution then splits this figure between the partners.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be a loss. The item number moves between form years; it is item 24 on the 2024 partnership return.
