supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and the generic 'does not publish a finite value list' sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what the retired stage of a patent is, what the mechanical engineering classes cover, or why the w_count measure differs from the three measures in the columns beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, motor vehicle expenses
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: What it cost the partnership to run its vehicles over the year. The ATO says "Show at label L motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums." A code beside the amount records how a car claim was worked out, S for cents per kilometre and B for logbook, or N where the claim is for a motorcycle, a taxi, a one-tonne or nine-passenger vehicle, or where no partner is an individual.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year covering running costs only, reported as an expense within item 5 and accompanied by a claim-method code.
limitation: It is not the cost of the fleet. Leasing, interest and depreciation on the same vehicles are reported at three other labels, so a firm that leases its vehicles looks cheap here. Where the cents-per-kilometre method is used the figure is a statutory formula rather than money actually spent, and the method varies between businesses and between vehicles within a business.
rationale: The DIL label matches the motor vehicle expenses label of item 5 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction restricts it to running expenses and publishes the claim-method codes.
evidence_quote: Show at label L motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the amount excludes lease, interest and depreciation or that a cents-per-kilometre claim is a formula.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, income tests net rental property income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The partnership's whole-of-year net result from rental property, reported so that each partner can complete the income tests on their own return. The ATO says "Show at item 53 - label H the amount of the partnership's net income or loss from rental properties" and requires Australian rent, foreign rent and net rental income distributed from other partnerships all to be counted. It exists for eligibility testing, feeding study and training loan repayment income, super co-contributions and the Medicare levy surcharge.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be a loss, reported at the income tests item and split between partners in the statement of distribution.
limitation: It is not the net rent reported at the rent item and the two will not agree, because this figure adds foreign rent and rental income received through other partnerships. It is also not a return on property: capital gains and capital losses on rental property are excluded, so a business that made its money on disposal shows nothing here.
rationale: The DIL label matches the net rental property income or loss label of the income tests item on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO defines its scope and its purpose.
evidence_quote: Capital gains or losses made in regard to a rental property are not included in the partnership’s net rental property income or loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say this is an income-tests figure with a wider scope than the rent item's net rent.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, income tests net financial investment income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The partnership's net result from financial investments over the year, reported for the partners' income tests rather than for the partnership's own assessment. The ATO instructs that "If the partnership received income or claimed deductions during 2023-24, then work out the net income or loss from financial investments and show it at label G", counting shares, interests in managed investment schemes including forestry schemes, rights and options over them, and investment income distributed from other partnerships. Each partner's share is then carried into the statement of distribution.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be a loss, reported at the income tests item alongside the net rental property income or loss figure.
limitation: It is not the partnership's investment return. Interest from everyday transaction accounts is excluded by rule, and so are capital gains and capital losses, which is where most of the return on shares actually lands. Its purpose is to stop a partner reducing income-tested entitlements through an investment loss, so a zero says the tests found nothing to report, not that the firm holds no investments.
rationale: The DIL label matches the net financial investment income or loss label of the income tests item on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO lists what is a financial investment and what is left out.
evidence_quote: Don't include any of the following when calculating the partnership's net financial investment income or loss: interest from everyday transactions accounts, capital gains, capital losses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not name the excluded items that make the figure unusable as a measure of investment return.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The partnership's overall business profit or loss for the year, primary production and non-primary production combined. The ATO defines it as "total business income minus total expenses incurred in producing that income, adjusted by any reconciliation items", and it is reported at item 5 label S of the partnership return. It sits at the end of the trading account, after the accounting figures at labels C to N have been converted to tax figures by the income and expense reconciliation adjustments.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount and a flow over the income year. It can be negative; on the paper form a loss is marked with an L indicator beside the amount rather than a minus sign, so the sign may need reconstructing from a companion loss flag.
limitation: It is not the partnership's taxable income and not what the partners are taxed on. Distributions received from other partnerships and trusts, rent, interest, dividends and foreign income are all reported at separate items and sit outside this figure, so a firm with a small trading business and large investment income looks small here.
rationale: The BIT table carries c_, i_, p_ and t_ variants of the same tax labels for the company, individual, partnership and trust returns; the p_ prefix identifies the partnership return, where net income or loss from business is item 5 label S and the ATO instruction defines it directly.
evidence_quote: The net income or loss from business is total business income minus total expenses incurred in producing that income, adjusted by any reconciliation items.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Net income or loss from business' as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is the post-reconciliation total or that investment income sits outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The non-primary-production half of the partnership's business result, kept apart from its farming, fishing and forestry income. The ATO directs the lodger to "Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production, R for non-primary production", so this column is label R. Read with p_netincpp it decomposes the total at label S, and the split exists because primary production income attracts averaging and farm management deposit treatment in the partners' own returns.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow over the income year, signed, with losses flagged rather than signed on the form. It is one of two columns of the item 5 trading account, not a standalone total.
limitation: The split is made on the activity, not on the entity, so it cannot be read as an industry classification of the firm. A mixed farm with a farm-gate shop divides its own income and expenses between the two columns on its own allocation, and nothing in the data records how that allocation was made.
rationale: The p_ prefix in the BIT table marks the partnership return, where the ATO instruction names labels Q and R as the primary and non-primary production halves of net income or loss from business.
evidence_quote: Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production R for non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net income or loss from business - NPP' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never explained what NPP means or why the return splits the result at all.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The farming, fishing and forestry share of the partnership's business result, reported at item 5 label Q. The ATO instruction is "Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production", and the amount is what flows through to each partner's share of primary production income. A non-zero figure here is the clearest sign in the tax data that the partnership carries on a primary production business.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow over the income year, signed, and one of the two columns whose sum is the item 5 label S total. The form marks a loss with an L indicator rather than a minus sign.
limitation: A positive primary production figure can sit alongside a non-primary-production loss that leaves the partnership in deficit overall, so this column alone does not say whether the business made money. The non-commercial loss rules can also quarantine a partner's share of a loss, so a negative value here is not a deduction anyone necessarily received.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the partnership return names label Q as the primary production net income or loss, which is the item the p_ prefixed BIT label refers to.
evidence_quote: Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production R for non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net income or loss from business - PP' with the generic sentence printed twice, so a reader could not tell PP from NPP or know which partners' concessions it drives.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 9 Rent
variable_description: Rent the partnership earned as part of its business, after the interest, capital works and other deductions claimed against it. The ATO sets the arithmetic out directly: "Calculate net rent by subtracting the deductions at labels G, X and H from label F Gross rent." It is the bottom line of item 9, and p_othrtldt is one of the three deductions taken off it.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 9 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, which can be negative; the form flags a rental loss with an L indicator beside the figure.
limitation: It covers only rent that is partnership business income. Where a property is merely held jointly as an investment, the ATO sends the rent to each owner's individual return instead, so a partnership of passive landlords can show nothing here while collecting rent all year.
rationale: Item 9 of the partnership return is the rent item and the instruction gives both the calculation and the boundary between business rent and jointly held investment property.
evidence_quote: Calculate net rent by subtracting the deductions at labels G, X and H from label F Gross rent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Net rent' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as definition and limitation, so it did not say which deductions were netted off or that passive rental income is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: What the partnership spent to earn its non-primary-production distributions from other partnerships and trusts. The ATO instruction for item 8 label T is to show "the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to non-primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts", and it excludes expenses of earning franked distributions, which go to label G. Its own expenses are the point: costs the upstream trust incurred on its own account are not deductible here.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, sitting beside the two non-primary-production income labels B and R that it is netted against to give the net non-primary production amount.
limitation: It is not the cost of running the business. These are only the holding costs of interests in other entities, typically interest on money borrowed to buy in, and thin capitalisation or prepayment rules may already have cut the figure down before it is written on the form.
rationale: The partnership return's item 8 label T is defined by the ATO as the deductions relating to the non-primary-production distribution labels B and R, which is exactly what the DIL label describes.
evidence_quote: Show at label T the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to non-primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deductions relating to distribution - NPP' and the generic sentence twice, leaving unclear whose expenses these are and which income labels they attach to.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Income this partnership received as a partner in another partnership, on the non-primary-production side. The ATO instruction for item 8 label B is to "Show at label B the amount of non-primary production income or loss distributions from other partnerships", including any share of foreign resident withholding credit attached. A non-zero value is direct evidence that the firm sits inside a tiered partnership structure rather than trading alone.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year that can be a loss, in which case the form marks it with an L indicator. Foreign source amounts are stripped out and reported at item 23 instead.
limitation: It does not identify the upstream partnership, so this column cannot be used to reconstruct a group structure on its own; the counterpart partnership has to be found through other means. It also excludes any capital gain, because a partnership holds no CGT assets and each partner reports their own gain.
rationale: Item 8 of the partnership return covers distributions received from other partnerships and trusts, with label B the non-primary-production partnership distribution named by the DIL label.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the amount of non-primary production income or loss distributions from other partnerships.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Distribution from partnerships - NPP' with the generic sentence printed twice, and never distinguished a distribution received from a distribution made.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partnership's share of a trust's non-primary-production net income, reported at item 8 label R. The ATO defines it as "the partnership's share of non-primary production income that was included in the net income (for tax purposes) of trusts", excluding capital gains, foreign income and franked distributions, which have their own labels. The amount is what the partnership became presently entitled to, whether or not the cash arrived.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar entitlement for the income year, carrying a trust type code on the form alongside the amount. Where the amount is not a loss the lodger also prints a code identifying the kind of trust it came from.
limitation: It is a tax-law share of trust net income, not a cash distribution, so it can be positive in a year the partnership received nothing. It also strips out the franked distribution component, which is reported at label F, so it understates what a partnership with a share portfolio in a family trust actually got.
rationale: Label R of item 8 on the partnership return is the share of trust net income on the non-primary-production side, which the ATO instruction defines and bounds against the neighbouring labels.
evidence_quote: Show at label R the partnership's share of non-primary production income that was included in the net income (for tax purposes) of trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Distribution from trusts - NPP' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that present entitlement rather than cash drives the figure.

value_domain: Refundable tax offset entitlement in dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The refundable tax offset the partnership claims for renting dwellings under the National Rental Affordability Scheme, at item 51 label F. The amount is not self-calculated: the ATO says "The amount of the entity's tax offset is the amount stated in the certificate issued by the Secretary of the Department of Social Services", and the offset is available only where such a certificate exists. A value here identifies the firm as an NRAS investor supplying dwellings below market rent.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset entitlement for one NRAS year, which for the 2023-24 return runs from 1 May 2023 to 30 April 2024 rather than over the income year.
limitation: The scheme has been winding down since allocations ceased, so a fall to zero measures the end of a dwelling's ten-year incentive period rather than a change in the business. The column also does not say how many dwellings the certificate covers, so it cannot be turned into a count of affordable homes.
rationale: Item 51 of the partnership return is the NRAS tax offset, and the instruction states both that a Department of Social Services certificate is required and that the certificate sets the amount.
evidence_quote: The amount of the entity's tax offset is the amount stated in the certificate issued by the Secretary of the Department of Social Services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label 'National rental affordability scheme tax offset entitlement' and the generic sentence twice, without saying that the figure is certified externally or that the NRAS year is offset from the income year.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation in dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The value of the partnership's inventory at the start of the year, at item 39 label C. The ATO defines it as "the total value of all trading stock on hand at the beginning of the income year or accounting period", valued for income tax purposes under section 70-40 of the ITAA 1997. Unlike most of the surrounding tax items it is a stock rather than a flow, and it is chained: "The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous year."
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar valuation at a single point in time, on the tax basis rather than the accounting basis, and including motor vehicle floor plan stock and work in progress of manufactured goods.
limitation: A zero does not mean the business held nothing. A partnership that started operations during the year is told to leave this blank and report the stock through cost of sales instead, and small business entities using the simplified rules may carry opening value forward untouched, so year-on-year movement can be an accounting choice rather than real destocking.
rationale: Item 39 of the partnership return is opening stock, and the ATO instruction gives the definition, the valuation provision and the rule that links it to the previous year's closing value.
evidence_quote: Show at label C the total value of all trading stock on hand at the beginning of the income year or accounting period for which the partnership tax return is being prepared.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Opening stock' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing flagged that this is a point-in-time valuation on a tax rather than accounting basis.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Foreign income - items 22 to 24
variable_description: All the assessable income the partnership earned offshore, before any deduction, at item 23 label B. The ATO asks for "the gross amount of assessable income derived from foreign sources, including amounts distributed from partnerships and other trusts as well as New Zealand franking company dividends and supplementary dividends", with foreign tax withheld at source added back in. It is the broadest single measure in the return of a partnership's exposure to offshore earnings.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Foreign income - items 22 to 24
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross flow for the income year, stated before deductions; the net figure after allowable deductions is the separate label V.
limitation: Gross is the trap: a partnership with large offshore turnover and matching costs looks internationally exposed here while earning almost nothing. Attributed foreign income under item 22, foreign capital gains and income exempt under sections 23AI and 23AK are all excluded, so this is not the whole of the firm's foreign activity either.
rationale: Item 23 label B of the partnership return is gross other assessable foreign source income, and the instruction lists exactly what is in and out of the figure.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the gross amount of assessable income derived from foreign sources, including amounts distributed from partnerships and other trusts as well as New Zealand franking company dividends and supplementary dividends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Other Assessable Foreign source Gross Income' and the generic sentence twice, without distinguishing gross from net or naming what item 22 takes out.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 14 Other Australian income and 15 Total of items 5 to 14
variable_description: Australian income that fitted nowhere else on the partnership return, gathered at item 14 label O. The ATO lists what lands there: gains on the disposal of traditional securities, bonuses from life insurance companies and friendly societies, royalty income, add-backs of listed investment company capital gain deductions, and assessable foreign exchange gains not already shown at item 5. The DIL calls it a type of income but the recorded response is a dollar amount, so this column holds the amount at label O and not a category code.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 14 Other Australian income and 15 Total of items 5 to 14
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual income flow for the income year, which can be a loss; the current partnership return has no type-of-income code box beside it despite the DIL wording.
limitation: It is a mixed bag by construction, so a movement in it cannot be attributed to any one activity without other columns; a forex gain, a life insurance bonus and a royalty stream all read the same here. The DIL's trailing 'type of Income' has no counterpart on the 2024 partnership return, so do not expect a code list behind this column.
rationale: Item 14 of the partnership return is other Australian income and the ATO instruction enumerates its components; the DIL's numeric response type rules out the column being a code, but the source does not explain the label's trailing wording.
evidence_quote: Show at label O the assessable Australian source foreign exchange (forex) gains or deductible losses that you have not already included at any other label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Other Australian income - type of Income' and the generic sentence twice, which left a reader expecting a category code where the data holds dollars.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Ordinary trading revenue from the partnership's primary production business, at item 5 label G. The ATO describes labels G and H as "other business income such as revenue from the sale of goods, services rendered, disposal of depreciating assets, work in progress amounts assessable under section 15-50 of the ITAA 1997, and royalties", with G the primary production column. For most farming partnerships this is the largest single income figure on the return, since the specialised labels above it capture only withholding and government payments.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system amount for the income year, GST exclusive where the partnership is registered, and able to be a loss, in which case the form marks it with an L.
limitation: It is an accounting figure, not a tax figure: adjustments for tax purposes are made further down at the reconciliation labels, so this does not equal assessable primary production income. Assessable government industry payments such as drought and disaster grants are reported separately at label E and are absent from here.
rationale: Item 5 of the partnership return splits business income into primary and non-primary production columns, with other business income at labels G and H respectively.
evidence_quote: Show at labels G and H, as appropriate, other business income such as revenue from the sale of goods, services rendered, disposal of depreciating assets, work in progress amounts assessable under section 15-50 of the ITAA 1997, and royalties.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Other business income - PP' and the generic sentence twice, so it never said that this is the main sales line rather than a residual.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Ordinary trading revenue from everything the partnership does outside primary production, at item 5 label H. It takes the same content as the primary production column beside it, and the ATO singles out one case worth knowing: "Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F Assessable government industry payments." For a professional or retail partnership this is effectively turnover.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system amount for the income year, GST exclusive where the partnership is registered for GST, and signed with an L indicator when it is a loss.
limitation: It is not turnover as the ABS would define it, because the withholding, foreign resident and government payment labels above it hold income that never reaches this line. Nor is it a tax figure, since the income reconciliation adjustment at label A can move large amounts in or out afterwards.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines labels G and H as the other business income columns for primary and non-primary production, and gives the medical practice example that pins label H.
evidence_quote: Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F Assessable government industry payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other business income - NPP' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing indicated that this line is close to turnover for a non-farming partnership.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The cost of tangible assets the partnership began depreciating this year, at item 49 label B. The ATO asks for "the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) for which the partnership is claiming a deduction for the decline in value for the first time", so the column measures new capital going into the business rather than the deduction taken. It is the tangible counterpart of label A, which holds patents, in-house software and other intangibles.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar cost, not reduced for any estimated non-taxable use, and including assets under $1,000 that were allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: It is investment, not expense: the deduction actually claimed is elsewhere, and a large figure here can sit beside a small depreciation charge. Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules skip item 49 entirely, so the column is missing for exactly the firms that write off most assets immediately.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return covers capital allowances, with label B the cost of non-intangible depreciating assets first deducted in the year, and the instruction states the small business entity exclusion at the top of the item.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) for which the partnership is claiming a deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other depreciating assets first deducted' with the generic sentence twice, so a reader could mistake a cost of acquisition for a depreciation deduction.

value_domain: Count of distinct patent technology areas within Other Fields
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How broadly the business filed patents within the Other Fields technology grouping in the financial year. IP Australia describes scope variables as "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year", and Other Fields holds just three of the 35 areas: furniture and games, other consumer goods, and civil engineering. A value of 3 means the firm filed across all of consumer products, furnishings and construction in one year.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
value_definition: A whole number bounded at 3, counting distinct technology areas from the WIPO IPC concordance as adapted for IPLoRD, over the applications the applicant filed during the Australian financial year.
limitation: The ceiling of 3 makes it incomparable with p_filed_class_scope, which runs to 35, so a ratio of the two is not a diversity measure. It is also a count of areas, not of applications: a firm filing one patent that carries two classifications outscores a firm filing fifty in a single area.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables, states that patents have 35 classification areas grouped into five coarse areas, and lists the three areas that make up Other Fields in its Annex A concordance table.
evidence_quote: Scope variables are intended to indicate the breadth of an applicant's activity across multiple event streams in a given financial year and are used as a term to describe the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about other fields technology area classes and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that Other Fields contains only three areas or what they are.

value_domain: Count of patent applications filed in a financial year
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How many patent applications the business filed during the year within the Other Fields technology grouping. That grouping covers three areas: furniture and games, other consumer goods, and civil engineering. IP Australia defines the filed event stream as "rights filed during the financial year", so this is a flow of new applications, not a stock of patents held. It is the whole-number companion of p_other_filed_w_count, which shares jointly filed applications between applicants.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
value_definition: A whole count of applications over the Australian financial year, classified by the WIPO IPC technology concordance as adapted for IPLoRD.
limitation: A patent can carry classifications in more than one coarse area, so the five coarse-area counts sum to more than the total filings and cannot be treated as a partition. A filing is also not an invention that reached the market: many applications lapse before grant, and this column says nothing about what became of them.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines count variables and the four event streams, and states that a patent right can sit in more than one coarse classification area simultaneously.
evidence_quote: Count variables are counts of the number of events of a certain kind or the number of rights in the stockpile of an applicant for an IP right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording about total number of patents in the other fields technology and the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that coarse areas overlap.

value_domain: IPLoRD patent technology area, Other Fields grouping
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: The single technology area the business filed most patents in during the year, restricted to the Other Fields grouping. IP Australia says modal variables "record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year", and within Other Fields the only possible answers are area 33 furniture and games, 34 other consumer goods, and 35 civil engineering. Unlike the counts beside it, this column is a label rather than a quantity.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021

The ATO defines it as "the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts", and adds that "expenses incurred on behalf of the trust are not to be deducted by the partnership". Labels A, Z and S together give the net primary production amount from upstream entities.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, netted against the two primary production income labels rather than against trading income at item 5.
limitation: These are financing and holding costs of an interest, not farming costs, so adding this column to item 5 expenses to build a cost of production double counts the concept and misstates the farm. Prepayment and thin capitalisation rules may already have reduced the amount that reaches the label.
rationale: Label S of item 8 on the partnership return is defined by the ATO as the deductions relating to the primary production distribution labels A and Z.
evidence_quote: Show at label S the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deductions relating to distribution - PP' and the generic sentence twice, without saying whose expenses they are or which income they attach to.

value_domain: Balance sheet amount in dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2010 instructions, 36 Proprietors' funds
variable_description: The partners' equity in the business, taken straight from the partnership's accounts. The ATO asks for "the net proprietors' funds from the accounting records of the partnership" and pins the arithmetic: "The amount shown at item 33 Total assets less the amount shown at item 35 Total liabilities equals the amount shown at K." It is the only net worth measure in the partnership return's key financial information block.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2010 instructions, 36 Proprietors' funds
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at the end of the income year, an accounting rather than tax figure, and able to be negative, in which case the form marks it with an L indicator.
limitation: The item was dropped from the partnership return: it appears in the ATO instructions up to 2012 and is absent from 2013 onwards, where key financial information stops at total liabilities. Any series built on this column ends there, and a run of empty years is a form change rather than firms losing their equity.
rationale: The 2010 partnership return instructions define item 36 label K and give the total assets less total liabilities identity; comparing the 2010, 2012, 2013 and later key financial information pages shows when the label was removed.
evidence_quote: Show at K the net proprietors' funds from the accounting records of the partnership.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Proprietors' funds' with the generic sentence printed twice, and gave no warning that the label ceased to exist on the return after 2012.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
variable_description: The part of a non-primary-production partnership distribution that is carved out of the NCMI rules, at item 32 label J. The ATO defines it as "the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production", meaning income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities. The pair to it is p_pshp_npp_ncmi_amt, and both belong inside the item 8 label B distribution.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of an amount reported elsewhere on the same return, identifying income that keeps concessional managed investment trust withholding treatment.
limitation: It records an exclusion from a penalty rate, not an exemption from tax, and it is already inside item 8, so treating it as additional income overstates the partnership. Only entities within a managed investment trust chain complete item 32 at all, which makes the column empty for almost every business in the register.
rationale: Item 32 of the partnership return separates NCMI by source and production type, with label J the excluded-from-NCMI component of non-primary-production partnership distributions.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Non-PP - Distribution from partnerships - Excluded from NCMI' and the generic sentence twice, so neither the exclusion nor its narrow population was explained.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
variable_description: Non-primary-production income from another partnership that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, at item 32 label I. The ATO defines the non-primary-production NCMI content as "cross staple income, trading trust income and residential housing income", and label I as "the total NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production". It is the clearest signal in the return that the firm sits inside a stapled infrastructure or build-to-rent structure.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the item 8 label B distribution, re-reported at item 32 so the character of the income passes down to the partners.
limitation: It is a tag on income already counted, not new income, and it measures character rather than any tax the partnership paid; the higher withholding falls on foreign investors upstream. The column also cannot separate the four kinds of NCMI from one another.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 32 defines NCMI and assigns label I to the non-primary-production partnership distribution component that the DIL label names.
evidence_quote: Show at label I the total NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Non-PP - Distribution from partnerships - NCMI' with the generic sentence twice and left the acronym and the double-count risk unexplained.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: What the partnership bought in as direct materials during the year, at item 40 label B. The ATO asks for "the cost of direct materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange, in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business". With opening and closing stock either side of it, this is the purchases term of the cost of sales identity rather than a deduction in its own right.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow of purchases over the income year, distinct from the stock valuations at items 39 and 41 that bracket it.
limitation: It is direct materials only, so it is not a measure of what the business spent with suppliers: services, subcontracting and overheads are elsewhere in item 5. A partnership still using the old simplified tax system accounting method shows only purchases it has paid for, which breaks comparability with accrual lodgers.
rationale: Item 40 of the partnership return is purchases and other costs, and the ATO instruction defines label B and notes the cash-basis variant for former STS taxpayers.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the cost of direct materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange, in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Purchases and other costs' and printed the generic sentence twice, without saying that the figure is direct materials feeding a cost of sales calculation.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: What the partnership paid to occupy premises it does not own, at item 5 label H of the expenses column. The ATO defines it as "the expenditure incurred as a tenant for the rental or lease of land and buildings used in the production of income". Read against item 9, which is rent the partnership receives, the two labels tell opposite stories about the same firm's property position.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, GST exclusive where input tax credits are available, and split between the primary and non-primary production columns.
limitation: It covers land and buildings only. Equipment and vehicle leases are reported at the separate lease expenses label, so this cannot be used as a measure of total leasing, and a firm that owns its premises shows zero regardless of how much property it holds.
rationale: Item 5 of the partnership return holds the trading account expenses, and the ATO instruction restricts label H to premises rent paid as a tenant.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the expenditure incurred as a tenant for the rental or lease of land and buildings used in the production of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Rent expenses' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not separate premises rent from equipment leasing or from rent received.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Upkeep of the partnership's plant and premises, at item 5 label M. The ATO defines it as "the expenditure on repairs and maintenance of plant, machinery, implements and premises", and expects capital items to be written back later: "Write back any non-deductible expenditure, such as items of a capital nature or amounts relating to private use of an item at label M, at item 5 Reconciliation items." It is one of the few direct indicators in tax data of whether a firm is maintaining its capital stock.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, before any tax adjustment, GST exclusive where input tax credits are available.
limitation: The figure mixes deductible repairs with capital improvements that are added back afterwards, so a spike can be a renovation rather than maintenance. Remedying defects that existed when an asset was bought is capital in nature, which means a firm's first year of owning second-hand equipment reads high here for reasons that have nothing to do with wear.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines label M and sets out the repair against capital improvement boundary that governs what is reported and what is written back.
evidence_quote: Show at label M the expenditure on repairs and maintenance of plant, machinery, implements and premises.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Repairs and maintenance' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that capital work can sit inside the number.

value_domain: Count of distinct patent technology areas, all 35
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: Across how many technology areas the business let patents lapse in the financial year, counted over the whole classification rather than one grouping. IP Australia uses the WIPO concordance to assign each patent to one or more of 35 technology areas: "This 35 category classification system has been used for IPLoRD." This is the unrestricted version of p_other_retired_class_scope, so it can reach 35 where the Other Fields column stops at 3.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
value_definition: A whole number between 0 and 35, counting distinct technology areas among the rights retired in the Australian financial year, using the WIPO IPC concordance as adapted and extended by IP Australia since 2008.
limitation: The concordance has been amended by hand as new IPC symbols appeared, so an area assignment made for a patent filed in 1995 does not rest on the same mapping as one made in 2019, and long series carry that drift. Breadth of retirement also carries no volume, so it must be read beside p_retired_count.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary states that patents have 35 classification areas from the WIPO technology concordance, defines scope variables, and records that the concordance was extended manually after 2008.
evidence_quote: This 35 category classification system has been used for IPLoRD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Number of different technology area classes represented in the patent applications allowed to retire in the financial year' with the generic sentence twice, and gave no upper bound or classification name.

value_domain: Count of patents retired in a financial year
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How many patents the business let go in the financial year, across all technology areas. It is the whole-of-portfolio total that the five coarse-area retirement counts sit under, and the outflow term in the enforceable stockpile identity. For a firm with a long patenting history a steady figure here is mostly patents reaching the end of their 20-year term.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
value_definition: A whole count of rights retired over the Australian financial year, unrestricted by technology area and not weighted for joint applicants.
limitation: The five coarse-area counts do not add to this total, because a patent can be classified into more than one coarse area and would be counted in each. The column also carries no reason for retirement, so a lapse to save fees and an expiry at end of term are indistinguishable.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines count variables and the retired event stream, and states that a patent right can exist in more than one coarse classification area at once, which is what breaks the sum.
evidence_quote: For patents, it is possible for a right to exist in more than one of the coarse classification areas simultaneously.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total number of patent applications retired during the financial year' with the generic sentence twice, and did not warn that the coarse-area counts overlap it.

value_domain: IPLoRD patent technology area, all 35
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: The technology area the business retired most patents from during the year, chosen from all 35 areas rather than one grouping. The areas run from 1 electrical machinery through 16 pharmaceuticals to 35 civil engineering, and are grouped into five coarse areas: electrical engineering, instruments, chemistry, mechanical engineering and Other Fields. It is the widest-domain mode among the retirement columns, and the one to use when the firm's activity is not confined to consumer goods and construction.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
value_definition: A character value naming one of the 35 technology areas of the WIPO IPC concordance as adapted for IPLoRD, taken over the rights retired in the Australian financial year.
limitation: It is empty in any year the firm retired nothing, which is most years for most businesses, so it cannot be treated as a portfolio descriptor. The mode is also taken over classifications rather than rights, and a patent classified into several areas contributes to each, so a single multi-area patent can decide the value.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables, states that patents have 35 classification areas from the WIPO concordance, and notes that more than one classification can attach to a single right.
evidence_quote: It is possible to have more than one of these classifications associated with a right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Most common technology area class for all patent applications retired in this financial year' with the generic sentence twice, and named no classification and no domain size.

value_domain: Fractional count of patents retired
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: The business's share of all patents that retired in the year, across every technology area, with co-owned rights divided between their applicants. It is the whole-of-portfolio version of p_other_retired_w_count and the retirement counterpart of p_filed_w_count. Because it is additive across firms without double counting, it is the right column for building national or industry retirement totals from BLADE.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
value_definition: A fractional count over the Australian financial year, no greater than p_retired_count, formed from 1/n terms where n is the number of applicants on each retired right.
limitation: The fraction tracks names on the right rather than economic interest, so it should not be read as the value of intellectual property written off. Its gap from the unweighted count measures collaboration in the firm's historic filings, not in its current work, since retiring patents were filed up to twenty years earlier.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines weighted count variables, gives the 1/n rule, and states that the weighting exists so that aggregate application numbers are preserved for each IP right type.
evidence_quote: The inclusion of weighted count variables allows for accurate numbers of applications to be preserved in aggregate for each IP right type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Number of patent applications fraction that the applicant has allowed to retire during the financial year' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said why a fractional count exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation - items 29 to 30
variable_description: Royalties the partnership paid offshore, at item 29 label E. The ATO instruction is to show "the royalty expenses paid to non-residents", and the amount is a subset of the total royalty expenses at item 5 label J rather than an addition to it. Because paying a royalty abroad triggers withholding tax and an International dealings schedule, this column marks a firm that licenses foreign intellectual property.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation - items 29 to 30
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year, reported in the overseas transactions item and repeated inside the item 5 royalty total after any reconciliation adjustment.
limitation: It does not say who was paid or in which country, and it is not deductible unless the withholding tax was remitted, so the reported amount is a claim rather than a settled deduction. Adding it to the total royalty expense figure double counts the same payments.
rationale: Item 29 of the partnership return covers overseas expenses, and the ATO instruction defines label E and states its relationship to item 5 label J.
evidence_quote: Show at label E the royalty expenses paid to non-residents during 2023-24.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Royalty expenses overseas' and printed the generic sentence twice, so the overlap with total royalty expenses was invisible.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Everything the partnership paid to use someone else's intellectual property, at item 5 label J. The ATO defines it as "the royalty expenses for the income year" and adds "Include royalties paid to residents and non-residents", which makes it the superset of the overseas-only figure at item 29 label E. Differencing the two gives a rough split between domestic and imported licensing.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, split between the primary and non-primary production columns of item 5.
limitation: It is a payment for the right to use, not a measure of technology transfer: franchise fees, mineral royalties and software licences all land in the same line. Where withholding tax on a foreign royalty was not remitted the deduction is not allowable, so the label can overstate the deduction actually available.
rationale: Item 5 of the partnership return holds total royalty expenses at label J, and the instruction states that both resident and non-resident royalties belong there.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the royalty expenses for the income year. Include royalties paid to residents and non-residents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total royalty expenses' with the generic sentence twice and did not say that the overseas royalty column is a component of it.

value_domain: Country-by-country reporting entity indicator
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 and 2
variable_description: Whether the partnership declared itself a country-by-country reporting entity, at item 2 label G2. The ATO test is membership of a very large multinational group: "An entity is a CBC reporting entity if it is either a CBC reporting parent, or a member of a CBC reporting group, and one of the other group members is a CBC reporting parent with an annual global income of A$1 billion or more." A tick therefore identifies one of a few hundred entities in the country with global reporting obligations.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 and 2
value_definition: A single flag rather than a graded code: one value marks a country-by-country reporting entity and every other response, including a blank, is treated as no response given.
limitation: Absence of the flag is not evidence of a small business, because it also covers an unticked box or a form version that predates the label; only a positive value carries information. The flag is also self-assessed at lodgment, and it is close to but not the same test as the significant global entity flag at label G1, so the two do not always agree.
rationale: Item 2 of the partnership return records business status and the two multinational flags, and the ATO instruction gives the country-by-country reporting entity definition and the A$1 billion threshold.
evidence_quote: Print X at label G2 if you were a country-by-country (CBC) reporting entity for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Country by country reporting entity' and the generic sentence twice, so it neither gave the threshold nor warned that a non-response looks identical to a no.

value_domain: Salary and wage reporting location code
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Where the partnership's wage bill was booked in its own accounts, not how big that wage bill was. The code box beside item 44 records the section "salary and wages were wholly or predominantly reported in": C for the expense component of cost of sales, A for all other expenses, B for both, and O for neither. It is the key that lets a reader work out whether labour cost is already sitting inside cost of sales at item 5 label E or inside all other expenses at label N.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A single-character code taking the values C, A, B and O, mapped in the BLADE metadata to numeric codes with all other responses treated as invalid or missing.
limitation: It carries no dollars, so it cannot be used to measure labour cost; the amount is the separate item 44 figure. It is also a predominance judgment made by the lodger, so a business splitting wages evenly between cost of sales and other expenses may be coded either B or one of the single categories depending on who prepared the return.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 44 sets out the code table that determines where salary and wages have predominantly been reported, and the codes in the table match the DIL's valid responses one for one.
evidence_quote: Print in the CODE box the code from Table: Determine where salary and wages have predominantly been reported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Total salary and wage expenses action code' and the generic sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have expected dollars rather than a bookkeeping location code.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The slice of the partnership's income that qualifies its individual partners for the small business income tax offset, at item 5 label V. The ATO defines it as "the partnership's assessable income from carrying on a small business, less deductions to the extent that they are attributable to that assessable income", combined across all its businesses. Only a partnership that is a small business entity completes it, so a value here is itself a turnover-threshold marker.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year. Where the partnership has no business income or deductions outside item 5 label S, the ATO says label V simply repeats the label S figure.
limitation: The population is truncated by the small business aggregated turnover threshold, so the column is blank for larger firms rather than zero, and comparisons across the size distribution are censored. Personal services income that is not from a personal services business, tax-related expenses and gifts are excluded, so it does not reconcile to net income from business.
rationale: The ATO instruction attached to item 5 of the partnership return defines net small business income, states who must complete it and describes the shortcut where label V equals label S.
evidence_quote: The net small business income is the partnership's assessable income from carrying on a small business, less deductions to the extent that they are attributable to that assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net small business income' with the generic sentence twice and did not say that the column only exists for small business entities.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Depreciation still being claimed on assets first written down under the COVID-era Backing business investment concession, at item 49 label N. The ATO instruction is conditional on an earlier year: "If you used the Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation in 2019-20 or 2020-21 for one or more assets, show at label N the amount of depreciation you are claiming in 2023-24 for those assets." It is a tail measure, tracing the later-year cost of a stimulus decision taken in 2020 or 2021.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the current income year attributable to a defined cohort of assets, not to assets acquired in the year being reported.
limitation: The column exists only from the year after the concession was used and shrinks as the cohort depreciates away, so a decline measures the ageing of 2020 and 2021 assets rather than any change in investment behaviour. It also cannot be read as the value of the concession, since it is a claim in a later year, not the accelerated amount originally deducted.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return includes the subsequent-year Backing business investment label, and the ATO instruction ties it to assets first treated in 2019-20 or 2020-21.
evidence_quote: If you used the Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation in 2019-20 or 2020-21 for one or more assets, show at label N the amount of depreciation you are claiming in 2023-24 for those assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long DIL label and the generic sentence twice, without saying that the column refers back to a fixed cohort of assets from two specific years.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Business capital expenditure the partnership is writing off over five years under the blackhole expenditure rules, at item 49 label K. The ATO asks for "the total of the partnership's deductions allowable under section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997", which is the provision that lets a business deduct capital costs with no other home in the tax law: setting up or restructuring an entity, raising equity, and the costs of starting or ceasing a business. A value here is a reasonable marker of structural change in the firm.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for one income year, being one instalment of expenditure spread across five years rather than the expenditure itself.
limitation: It is one fifth of an earlier outlay, so it lags the event that caused it by up to five years and cannot date a restructure. The provision is a last resort by design, which means the same underlying cost may appear here for one firm and inside all other expenses for another depending on advice.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return carries the section 40-880 deduction at label K, and the ATO instruction identifies it by provision.
evidence_quote: Show at label K the total of the partnership's deductions allowable under section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Section 40-880 deduction' and printed the generic sentence twice, which left the provision unexplained and the five-year spreading unmentioned.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Whether the partnership set its own depreciation lives rather than accepting the Commissioner's, at item 49 label C. The ATO frames the choice as "work out the effective life yourself (self-assess), or adopt the Commissioner's determination in Taxation Ruling TR 2022/1", and a yes means at least one asset was self-assessed. Because self-assessment usually shortens the life and brings deductions forward, the flag marks a firm taking an active position on its capital allowances.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A two-state flag, Y for yes and N for no, with any other response treated as invalid or not given.
limitation: It is an any-asset flag, so one self-assessed laptop reads the same as a fully self-assessed plant fleet, and it carries no dollars. It is also missing rather than false for small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules, who are told to skip item 49 altogether.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return asks whether the effective life of any depreciating asset was self-assessed, and the ATO instruction states the yes and no conditions for label C.
evidence_quote: Yes - Print X in the Yes box at label C, as you have self-assessed the effective life of one or more of your depreciating assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text 'Have you self-assessed the effective life of any of these assets?' with the generic sentence twice, and did not say that one asset is enough to trigger it.

value_domain: Business status code (ceased, commenced, continuing)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 and 2
variable_description: Whether the partnership says it started, stopped or kept trading during the year, at item 2 labels B1 to B3. The ATO instruction is to "Print X at label B1, B2 or B3 to show the appropriate description for the status of the business", and it is the closest thing in the tax return to a self-reported entry and exit marker. It sits beside the industry code at item 1 and the multinational flags at labels G1 and G2.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 and 2
value_definition: A single code with three substantive states, ceased, commenced and continuing, with any other response treated as invalid or not given.
limitation: It cannot record two events in one year: the ATO tells lodgers that "If more than one selection applies, select the first applicable option", so a business that both started and finished within the year reports only one status. A blank is also permitted when none of the descriptions apply, so absence is not evidence of continuity, and the field is a lodger's assertion rather than a registry event.
rationale: Item 2 of the partnership return records business status, and the ATO instruction gives both the three-way choice and the tie-breaking rule that limits it.
evidence_quote: If more than one selection applies, select the first applicable option.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Status of your business' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that a start and a cessation in the same year collapse to one code.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The depreciation a small business partnership claimed on its general pool, at item 50 label B. Under the simplified depreciation rules assets above the instant write-off threshold go into one pool rather than being tracked individually, and the ATO directs the lodger to "Add up the general small business pool amounts" from the simplified depreciation worksheet and write the total here. It is the slower half of item 50, sitting beside the immediate deduction at label A.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, derived from a pool balance rather than from any single asset, and reported only by small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: Because the pool has no asset identity, nothing here says what was depreciated or when it was bought, and a pool balance below the write-off threshold can be deducted in full, producing a large one-off figure that is not new investment. The item is completed only by small business entities, so it is missing rather than zero for larger firms.
rationale: Item 50 of the partnership return is small business entity simplified depreciation, with label B the general pool deduction, and the ATO instruction states who completes the item and how the amount is derived.
evidence_quote: Complete this item only if the partnership is a small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Small business entity simplified depreciation - Deduction for general small business pool' with the generic sentence twice, without noting that the item is confined to small business entities.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Assets a small business partnership wrote off in full in the year of purchase, at item 50 label A. The ATO names the label "Deduction for certain assets (costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold)", which makes this the instant asset write-off line of the return. Unlike the pool deduction beside it at label B, the whole cost is deducted at once, so the figure is close to a measure of that year's small-asset capital spending.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, equal to the cost of the qualifying assets rather than to a decline in value, and reported only by small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: The threshold moved repeatedly, from $20,000 to $30,000, to unlimited temporary full expensing and back to $20,000, so the same firm buying the same asset falls in or out of this label depending on the year; a break in the series is policy, not behaviour. The item is also blank rather than zero for firms outside the small business rules.
rationale: Item 50 of the partnership return holds the two simplified depreciation deductions, and the ATO instruction names label A as the deduction for assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the superannuation expenses label of the partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5

It is a flow taken from the partnership's own accounts, and it is an employer cost only: a partner cannot be an employee of the partnership, so a partner's own contributions are claimed in that partner's return instead. Contributions to a non-complying fund and super guarantee charge paid on a shortfall are not deductible and so need never be shown here, which means a small or empty value can signal a compliance problem rather than a workforce without super.

value_domain: Closing written-down value of depreciating assets, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The written-down value of everything the partnership was still depreciating at the end of the year, at item 49 label E. The ATO defines it as "the total of the adjustable values of your depreciating assets as at the end of 2023-24. This is the value of all assets' costs (first and second elements) less any decline in value up to that time, or the closing value of all assets." Unlike the depreciation expense on the same return this is a stock at a point in time, so it is the closest thing in the return to a tax book value of the firm's capital.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
value_definition: A dollar amount measured at the last day of the income year, on tax values rather than accounting values. Assets costing under $1,000 that were put into a low-value pool are excluded from the total.

Small business entities using simplified depreciation report their pool separately at item 50, buildings written off under the capital works rules never enter an adjustable value, and assets fully expensed under temporary full expensing fall to zero immediately, so the number can collapse in a year when the firm actually invested heavily.

The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
