value_domain: Yes or no answer to the thin capitalisation question on the partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
variable_description: Whether the partnership says the thin capitalisation rules cut its debt deductions this year, at item 29 label O. The ATO asks "Did the thin capitalisation provisions affect you?" and a yes, like a yes on international related party dealings above $2 million, obliges the firm to lodge an International dealings schedule. The rules only reach entities with foreign control or overseas operations and whose debt deductions, with those of associates, exceed a $2 million de minimis threshold, so a yes marks a large, internationally financed business.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else an invalid or absent response. It is the taxpayer's own answer to a form question, not a determination made by the ATO.
limitation: A no does not mean the firm has no foreign debt. Most borrowers fall under the $2 million debt deduction de minimis or are purely domestic and answer no by default, so the column separates affected multinationals from everyone else rather than measuring gearing, and it says nothing about how much deduction was denied.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 29 sets out the question, the label and the schedule obligation that follows a yes. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the form question and the Y/N code list with the generic sentence repeated as definition and limitation, so it never said who the rules can reach or what a no actually rules out.

value_domain: Termination value of intangible depreciating assets, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: What the partnership received when it stopped holding intangible depreciating assets such as patents, in-house software or spectrum licences, at item 49 label H. The ATO instruction is "Show at label H the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for intangible depreciating assets to which the UCA rules applied, including assets allocated to a low-value pool." It is a gross disposal proceeds figure, including the market value of any non-cash consideration, and it pairs with label I, which does the same job for tangible assets.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53

The profit or loss on disposal only appears once the adjustable value is netted off at labels F and G, and internally generated goodwill, brands and customer lists are not depreciating assets at all, so a firm that sold its most valuable intangible can report nothing here.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label and the balancing adjustment event that triggers it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Termination value of tangible depreciating assets, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: What the partnership received on disposing of its ordinary plant, vehicles and equipment, at item 49 label I. The ATO instruction is "Show at label I the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for depreciating assets, including assets allocated to a low-value pool." Read with label H, which covers intangibles, it gives the year's gross asset sales; a balancing adjustment event happens whenever the partnership stops holding or using an asset, so assets lost or destroyed count as well as assets sold.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
value_definition: A dollar amount aggregated over the income year, including the market value of non-cash consideration received. Assets in a small business general pool, buildings under the capital works rules, research and development assets and Australian film investments are excluded from it.

Small business entities using simplified depreciation put their disposals through the pool instead, so an entire class of firm reports zero here, and a firm that clawed back temporary full expensing on an asset still located overseas records a market value it never actually received.
rationale: The ATO instruction names label I and lists the disposals excluded from it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label wording and the generic sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the intangible column or warned that pooled small business disposals never reach it.

value_domain: Count of assets the entity chose to exclude from temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P11 Temporary full expensing
variable_description: How many eligible assets the business deliberately kept out of temporary full expensing, so that it could depreciate them normally instead. The ATO wording for the label is "Number of assets you are opting out for, write the number of assets for which you made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing", and the choice is made asset by asset in the year of acquisition and cannot be revoked. Because temporary full expensing ran only from the 2020-21 to the 2022-23 income years, the column exists for those years and is empty everywhere else.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P11 Temporary full expensing
value_definition: A count of assets, held as a six character field rather than a dollar amount, paired with the opt-out value column that gives the deduction forgone. The ATO accepts a best estimate: a taxpayer is not penalised for an incorrect count.
limitation: It is not a measure of investment. Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules could not opt out at all and always report nothing, so a zero mixes them with firms that expensed everything, and a firm opting out of one very large asset looks identical to one opting out of a single trivial one.
rationale: The ATO gives this label's instruction in the schedule instructions for the same temporary full expensing item that appears across the individual, partnership, trust and company returns; the wording of the BLADE label matches it exactly. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: At D Number of assets you are opting out for, write the number of assets for which you made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the label text and '6 digit character' with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the measure only exists for three income years or that small business entities are structurally absent from it.

value_domain: Value of the deduction forgone by opting out of temporary full expensing, dollars
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P11 Temporary full expensing
variable_description: The deduction the business gave up by choosing not to apply temporary full expensing to some of its assets. The ATO is explicit that this is a counterfactual: "The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out." It is the dollar companion to the opt-out asset count on the same row, and it only exists for the 2020-21 to 2022-23 income years in which the measure ran.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P11 Temporary full expensing
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, representing forgone rather than claimed deductions. It records a self-assessed choice; the deduction actually taken on those assets shows up instead in the ordinary depreciation labels.
limitation: It is not spending, and it is not the assets' cost. The figure is what full expensing would have allowed, which for an asset held part-year and part privately is less than what was paid for it, and firms that never became eligible or that used simplified depreciation report nothing at all.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the opt-out value as the deduction that would otherwise have been claimed, which is what makes this column different from an asset cost. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label wording with the generic sentence printed twice, so a reader would have taken this for the cost of the assets rather than the deduction given up on them.

value_domain: Tax file number amounts withheld from interest, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 11 Gross interest
variable_description: Tax an investment body held back from the partnership's interest because no tax file number had been given to it, reported at item 11 label I. The ATO instruction is "Show at label I any TFN amounts withheld from gross interest where a TFN has not been provided to the investment body." The gross interest that the withholding was taken from sits beside it at label J, so the pair shows both the income and the penalty rate deduction taken at source.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 11 Gross interest
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, credited against the partners' tax rather than the partnership's, since a partnership is not itself a taxpayer. It is an administrative amount reported by the payer as well, and the ATO data matches it.

Almost every partnership reports nothing here even when it earns substantial interest, so the column cannot be used as a proxy for interest income or for financial assets.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 11 defines the label and the circumstance that produces an amount in it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text and the generic sentence twice, leaving a reader unable to tell this from interest income or to know that the amounts are rare by construction.

value_domain: Total business income, non-primary production column, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The partnership's gross trading income from everything other than farming, in the non-primary production column of item 5. The return splits business income into a primary production and a non-primary production column and the ATO says of the total row "Show the total of all income items at labels C, D, B, E, F, G and H", which for this side means gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, foreign resident withholding payments, assessable government industry payments and other business income at label H. It is turnover before any expense, not profit.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5

limitation: It is not the firm's sales figure and does not match BAS turnover: the return is annual and tax-basis while the activity statement is quarterly and GST-basis, and a partnership carrying on both a farm and another business splits its income across this column and the primary production one on judgement, so the split can move between years without any change in activity.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the total business income row and lists the income labels feeding it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Total Business Income - NPP' with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what NPP means, what is inside the total, or why it will not reconcile with the activity statement.

value_domain: Total business income, primary production column, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The partnership's gross farming income, reported in the primary production column of item 5. It is split out there because primary producers get concessional treatment elsewhere in the tax law. The ATO instruction for the total row is "Show the total of all income items at labels C, D, B, E, F, G and H", and on this side the components include livestock and produce sales worked out on the primary production worksheet and other business income at label G. A partnership with a non-zero value here is farming, fishing or forestry to some degree, whatever its registered industry code says.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, gross of all expenses, taken from the partnership's accounts. Livestock killed for rations, exchanged for goods or taken for private use are brought in here as other business income rather than left out.
limitation: It does not identify a farm business. The column is filled whenever any part of the income is primary production, so a small agistment or forestry sideline puts an amount here, and averaging, farm management deposits and livestock valuation elections mean the figure is not comparable across years for the same operation.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 sets out the total business income row and the primary production column that this variable takes. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Personal services income included in business income, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: How much of the partnership's business income was really a reward for one person's effort or skill, at item 30 label A. The ATO instruction is "Write at A the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 5 income labels", excluding exempt amounts and GST. It is a carve-out of income already counted at item 5, not extra income, and a large value relative to total business income marks a consultancy or professional practice rather than a trading business.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, self-assessed by the partnership as the personal services component of amounts it has already reported as business income. The matching deductions figure sits at label B on the same item.
limitation: It does not say whether the personal services income rules actually bit. That depends on the results test, the 80 per cent rule, a personal services business determination and the three self-assessed tests recorded in the neighbouring columns, so a partnership can report a large amount here and still be taxed normally.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 30 gives the label, its scope and its relationship to item 5. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Write at A the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 5 income labels.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the label wording, which mentions item 5 without saying what item 5 is, and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained personal services income or that this is a subset of income already reported.

value_domain: Assessable gains from financial arrangements under Division 230, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Assessable gains the partnership brought to account under the taxation of financial arrangements rules, at item 31 label M. The ATO instruction is "Show at label M the partnership's total assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements." The amount is a memorandum total: the same gains are already inside the income labels at items 5, 8, 11, 12, 14 and 23, so adding this to reported income double counts it.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, measured under the Division 230 methods, which include accruals and realisation, fair value, foreign exchange retranslation, hedging and reliance on financial reports.
limitation: It exists only for large or financial entities, so a zero usually means the rules do not apply rather than that no financial gains were made: the thresholds are $100 million aggregated turnover, $300 million of assets or $100 million of financial assets, and $20 million turnover for deposit-taking institutions and securitisation vehicles.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label and lists both the entities the rules reach and the other items where the same amounts appear. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total TOFA gains' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what TOFA is, that only large entities report it, or that the amount duplicates income counted elsewhere.

value_domain: Deductible losses from financial arrangements under Division 230, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Deductible losses the partnership brought to account under the taxation of financial arrangements rules, at item 31 label N. The ATO instruction is "Show at label N the partnership's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements." Like the gains figure beside it, it restates amounts already claimed in the ordinary deduction labels, so the pair is best read as a disclosure of exposure to derivatives, debt and hedging rather than as new income or expense.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, worked out under the Division 230 tax-timing methods. Once an entity is inside the rules it stays inside them even if its turnover or assets later fall below the threshold.
limitation: Gains and losses are reported gross and cannot be netted into a meaningful position, because hedging elections mean an offsetting gain may sit in a different year or a different label. Elections under the rules are irrevocable, so two firms with identical arrangements can report very different amounts.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the label wording and the election and threshold rules that govern who reports it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label N the partnership's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label text with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing distinguished it from an ordinary expense or explained why netting it against the gains column is unsafe.

value_domain: Total assets on the partnership balance sheet, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Key financial information items 33 to 36
variable_description: The partnership's whole balance sheet asset side at year end, reported at item 34 label G. The ATO instruction is "Show at label G all of the partnership assets, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets, and all current assets from item 33 All current assets." rationale: The ATO instruction for item 34 defines the label and its relationship to the current assets item beneath it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Total expenses at item 5 of the partnership return, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: Everything the partnership deducted against business income in the year, summed at item 5 label O. The ATO instruction is "Show at label O the total of all expense items shown at labels P to N", which is the block running from foreign resident withholding expenses and cost of sales through superannuation, rent, interest, royalties, depreciation, motor vehicle, repairs and all other expenses. Total business income less this figure is the starting point for net business income, before the reconciliation adjustments that follow.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5

Small business entities using simplified trading stock or depreciation rules substitute tax values in two of the components.

Prepayments, leased car limits, hire purchase, non-compliant payments and thin capitalisation denials are all corrected later at the reconciliation label, so the tax deduction actually allowed differs from this number, and no split between primary and non-primary production is available on the expense side.

The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Total income across the return's income items, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 14 Other Australian income and 15 Total of items 5 to 14
variable_description: The sum of every income item on the return, which on the partnership form is item 15, the total of items 5 to 14. It is broader than total business income because it also picks up trust and partnership distributions, rent, interest, dividends and other Australian income, and narrower than the firm's worldwide receipts because foreign income is reported separately at later items.

value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, signed: it can be negative when a business loss at item 5 exceeds the investment income items. It is a derived total rather than a separately reported quantity.

Deductions at items 16 to 20 have not been taken off, foreign source income is outside it, and because a partnership is not itself taxed the amount is eventually distributed to partners, so it cannot be compared with a company's total income without allowing for that.
rationale: The data item wording describes a total of the items under the return's Income heading, which on the partnership return is item 15; the ATO instruction defines that total and its scope. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Total liabilities on the partnership balance sheet, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Key financial information items 33 to 36

The ATO instruction is "Show at label J all the partnership liabilities, including other creditors and deferred liabilities, such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans", and it includes the current liabilities already shown at item 35. Nothing in the tax calculation depends on the number, so it is less carefully prepared than the income labels.

value_domain: Deductions against personal services income, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income

Like the income figure at label A it is a carve-out of amounts already reported at item 5, and the difference between the two is the net personal services income that may have to be attributed to the individual who earned it.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income

value_domain: Total salary and wage expenses of the partnership, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The partnership's whole wage bill for the year, at item 44 label L. description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53

value_domain: Trust distribution excluded from non-concessional MIT income, non-primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32

description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32

value_domain: Non-concessional MIT income from trusts, non-primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Trust income of a non-primary production kind that carries the non-concessional managed investment trust label, at item 32 label K. description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32

rationale: The ATO instruction defines both the label and the four categories that make an amount non-concessional MIT income. value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32

The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Non-concessional MIT income from trusts, primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Primary production trust income that is caught by the non-concessional managed investment trust rules, at item 32 label G. It is the farming counterpart of label K and is likewise a component of the item 8 label Z distribution rather than an addition to it.

value_domain: Tax withheld from the partnership's income because it did not quote an ABN, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 6 Tax withheld
variable_description: Tax that payers held back from the partnership's own receipts because it failed to quote an Australian business number, at item 6 label T. Withholding is at the top marginal rate, so an amount here is expensive and unusual.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 6 Tax withheld
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, equal to the sum of the tax withheld boxes on the Non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule lodged with the return. It is a credit passed through to the partners, since the partnership itself is not taxed.

Any share of ABN withholding that reached it through another partnership or trust is reported instead at item 8, so the two columns must be read together, and neither says anything about tax the firm withheld from its own suppliers.

value_domain: Share of an ABN withholding credit received through a trust or partnership, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 8 Partnerships and trusts

The failure to quote happened at the distributing entity, not at this business, which is what separates this column from the direct withholding figure at item 6.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, taken from the statement of distribution or trustee advice, which must disclose it separately. It is a credit attached to distributed income rather than to the partnership's own receipts.

value_domain: Yes or no answer to the specified countries question on the partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
variable_description: Whether the partnership moved funds or property to or from, or controlled assets in, any of the countries on the ATO's specified list, at item 29 label C. The question covers indirect movements "through another entity or country" and control that is only expected or indirect, so the threshold for a yes is deliberately low. The list of roughly forty-five jurisdictions includes Bermuda, the Cayman Islands, Hong Kong, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Singapore and Switzerland, so a yes is a flag for the ATO rather than an allegation.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else invalid or missing. The specified country list is published in the return instructions and has changed between editions, so the meaning of a yes is not fixed across years.
limitation: It cannot distinguish tax planning from ordinary trade. Sending funds to a Singapore supplier, banking in Hong Kong and holding a Cayman Islands structure all produce the same Y, and because the list has been revised the same transaction can flip the answer between years without any change in the firm's behaviour.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 29 sets out the two questions behind the label and publishes the country list they refer to. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Transactions with specified countries' and the Y/N codes with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which countries are specified or how broad the question is.

value_domain: Yes indicator for the personal services income unrelated clients test
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the partnership self-assessed that it passes the unrelated clients test, one of three escape routes from the personal services income rules, at item 30 label E1. The ATO defines it: "You will meet the unrelated clients test in the income year if the individual doing the personal services work generates PSI from two or more clients who are not associated with each other, or with the individual, or with you", and the work must come from offers to the public such as advertising. Clients won through a labour hire firm or placement agency do not count.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else invalid or missing. It is one of a set of self-assessed test indicators sitting beside the results test, the business premises test, the employment test and any personal services business determination.
limitation: It is a claim, not an entitlement. The test can only be self-assessed when no single client supplied 80 per cent or more of the individual's personal services income, so a Y from a firm that fails the 80 per cent rule is not effective without a Commissioner's determination, and the column records no such check.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 30 defines the unrelated clients test and the 80 per cent rule that governs when it may be self-assessed. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: You will meet the unrelated clients test in the income year if the individual doing the personal services work generates PSI from two or more clients who are not associated with each other, or with the individual, or with you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the three-word test name and the Y/N codes with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the test requires or that passing it is self-assessed and conditional.

value_domain: PAYG amount withheld from wages, activity statement label W2, dollars
value_source: ATO, Business activity statements: Pay as you go (PAYG) withholding
variable_description: The tax the business took out of its own payroll for the activity statement period, at label W2. The ATO instruction is "Include at W2 the total amount you withheld from salaries, wages and other payments shown at W1", and W1 is the gross payments column beside it, so the two together give payroll and payroll tax withheld at the same frequency. It is the main type of withholding and is reported monthly or quarterly, which makes it the highest-frequency labour indicator in the BLADE tax data.
description_source: ATO, Business activity statements: Pay as you go (PAYG) withholding
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one activity statement period, left blank rather than zero-filled where nothing was withheld. Amounts withheld where no ABN was quoted go to W4 and investment and foreign resident withholding to W3, not here.
limitation: The largest employers are missing by design: a large withholder, meaning one that withheld more than $1 million in a past income year, completes only W1 and leaves W2 blank. It is also tax, not wages, so it moves with the tax scales and with employees' tax-free threshold and offset claims as well as with the payroll itself.
rationale: The ATO page for the activity statement PAYG withholding section defines label W2 and the large withholder exception. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Include at W2 the total amount you withheld from salaries, wages and other payments shown at W1.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Amount withheld from salary, wages and other payments' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing identified the W2 label, distinguished it from W3 and W4, or warned that large withholders never report it.

value_domain: Instant asset write-off deductions claimed by a non-small business entity, dollars
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The deduction a business too large to be a small business entity claimed by writing assets off immediately rather than depreciating them. The ATO instruction for the label is "Show at O the total amount you claimed at item 7F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets about assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold for which an immediate deduction is available." The label belongs to the enhanced instant asset write-off that ran from March 2020 for businesses with aggregated turnover under $500 million and it was removed from the 2022 returns, so the series stops there.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, and a component of the depreciation deduction rather than an addition to it. Assets covered by temporary full expensing are reported at the temporary full expensing label instead of here.
limitation: It is not capital expenditure and not a complete write-off measure. Small business entities using simplified depreciation never report at this label, the threshold moved repeatedly between $1,000 and $150,000 over the life of the measure, and from the 2022 return the label was removed, so a zero after that year means the question stopped being asked.
rationale: The ATO capital allowances instruction defines this label in the same words as the BLADE data item, and the 2022 what's new page records its removal from the return. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at O the total amount you claimed at item 7F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets about assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold for which an immediate deduction is available.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the label text with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which businesses the label was for, that it duplicates part of the depreciation deduction, or that it ceased after the 2021 return.

value_domain: Yes or no answer to the effective life recalculation question
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: Whether the partnership reworked the effective life of any depreciating asset during the year, at item 49 label D. The ATO asks "Have you recalculated the effective life of any of your depreciating assets in 2023-24?" and notes that recalculation is sometimes optional and sometimes compulsory when the life in use is no longer accurate. It is a different question from the self-assessment indicator at label C, which asks whether the firm set the life itself instead of adopting the Commissioner's determination.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else invalid or missing. It applies to all depreciating assets and is asked only of firms outside the small business simplified depreciation rules, who skip item 49 entirely.
limitation: It says nothing about size or direction. One asset revised by a year and a whole fleet written down produce the same Y, the deduction effect is invisible, and small business entities using simplified depreciation never answer, so a blank is as likely to mean the firm is small as that it recalculated nothing.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 49 states the question at label D and distinguishes it from the self-assessment question at label C. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Have you recalculated the effective life of any of your depreciating assets in 2023-24?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form question and the Y/N codes with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing separated it from the self-assessment indicator or noted who never answers it.

value_domain: Days of paid bereavement leave provided by the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The number of days of paid bereavement leave written into an enterprise agreement covering this business, as coded by DEWR from the lodged agreement. It is a promise in a document, not leave anyone took, and it attaches to the agreement rather than to the firm, so a business covered by several agreements has several values. Coding of this item stopped for agreements made from 1 January 2011, when bereavement leave was folded into compassionate leave entitlements.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A count of days, numeric, with 111111111 reserved for a quantity that varies or is unknown, including where leave is granted on a per occasion basis. Coded by DEWR from the agreement text rather than reported by the employer.
limitation: A blank after 2010 means the item was retired, not that the entitlement vanished, so the column cannot be used to track bereavement leave over time. It also says nothing about how many covered employees could realistically use it, since the agreement may set qualifying conditions the coding does not capture.
rationale: DEWR publishes the database description and states that the conditions collected are reviewed annually, which explains the field's start and stop and its agreement-level unit; the valid response text on the data item carries the pre-2011 coding rule.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about days being recorded with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the field was retired in 2011 or that the unit is the agreement rather than the business.

value_domain: Days of paid family carer's leave provided over and above personal leave
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Days of paid leave an agreement gives employees to care for a sick family member on top of their ordinary personal or sick leave. The distinction from personal leave is what the item is for: carer's leave drawn from the personal leave balance is the statutory minimum and is not counted here, so a value marks an above-award condition. DEWR codes it from the agreement text and the number of days is only recorded where the agreement specifies one.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A count of days, numeric, with 111111111 standing for a varying or unknown quantity. It is coded per agreement, and the database holds conditions information for federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
limitation: It cannot be compared with total carer's leave available to employees, because the statutory entitlement inside personal leave is deliberately excluded. An absent value mixes agreements with no separate provision, agreements that provide it without quantifying it, and years in which the item was not coded.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the database, its coverage of conditions since 1997 and the annual review of what is collected, which sets the unit of observation and the coverage limits for this item.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the custodian's long definition and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said why the separation from personal leave matters or what a missing value can mean.

value_domain: Count of part-time employees covered by the agreement at lodgement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: How many part-time employees an enterprise agreement covered on the day it was lodged with the Fair Work Commission. It is a one-off snapshot taken at lodgement, not a payroll series, so it does not move as the workforce changes over the agreement's life, and it is reported by the parties to the agreement rather than measured. Read against the full-time and casual counts on the same record it gives the composition of the covered workforce at that moment.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A numeric headcount, not a full-time equivalent, attached to one agreement. Around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement in the database and this is one of the general details captured at lodgement.
limitation: It is not the firm's part-time workforce. Employees outside the agreement's scope are not counted, a multi-employer agreement spreads its count across businesses, and because the figure is fixed at lodgement it becomes stale immediately: an agreement running four years reports the same number in each of them.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the database and lists the number of employees covered among the general details recorded for each agreement, which establishes the unit and the point of measurement.
evidence_quote: There are over 180,000 agreements in the database. An average of 6,000 agreements are added each year, and around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line description with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the count is frozen at lodgement or that it counts agreement coverage rather than the business's employees.

value_domain: Presence flag for a full-time to part-time switching clause
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets full-time employees move to part-time work, and back, at their own request. It is a flexibility provision recorded because the initiative sits with the employee: clauses that let the employer impose reduced hours are a different thing and are not what this flags. DEWR codes it from the agreement text as a presence indicator only.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-sided flag: Y where the clause is present, and nothing recorded otherwise. There is no N code, so absence and non-coding share the same blank.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as no such clause. Because only Y is coded, agreements with no provision are indistinguishable from agreements coded before the item existed or coded incompletely, which makes any share calculated over blanks a lower bound rather than an estimate.
rationale: The DEWR page names flexibility arrangements among the conditions recorded for each agreement and explains that the conditions collected change over time, which is what makes the one-sided coding hazardous.
evidence_quote: The database also records details about conditions of employment contained within enterprise agreements
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's description and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the field carries only a Y and that blanks are ambiguous.

value_domain: Presence flag for a part-time hours loading clause, 2008-09 agreements only
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement pays part-time employees a loading on every hour worked, rather than only on hours beyond their rostered pattern. The item is unusual in that DEWR coded it only for agreements made in 2008 and 2009, so it is a snapshot of one bargaining round and not a series. A loading of this kind pushes part-time hourly pay above the full-time rate, which is why it was coded separately from ordinary penalty and overtime provisions.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y where the provision is present, with nothing recorded otherwise, and coded only for agreements made in 2008 and 2009. It is one of roughly 200 items held for each agreement.
limitation: The column is empty for almost every agreement in the database, and that emptiness carries no information about the clause. Any comparison of firms on this field is really a comparison of which of them happened to lodge an agreement in a two-year window.
rationale: The valid response text limits coding to 2008-09 agreements, and the DEWR page explains that the conditions collected are reviewed annually so items do not span the full time series.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's description and code note with the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained why coverage is confined to one bargaining round or what a blank means.

value_domain: Minimum continuous hours in a single part-time engagement

supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about fractions owned and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the split is equal by construction or why it exists.

value_domain: Count of distinct plant genus classes among rights retired
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: How many different plant genus classes the applicant's retirements of the year spanned. A value well below the retired count means the exits were concentrated in one crop, which is what withdrawing from a genus looks like in this data; a value close to it means scattered housekeeping across the portfolio. It is the exit-side analogue of the filed and granted scope columns.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
value_definition: An integer count of distinct genus classes among the year's retirements for one applicant, bounded above by the retired count and zero where nothing was retired.
limitation: It cannot show whether a genus was abandoned altogether, because it does not compare the retirements with what the holder still has: exiting one of ten wheat rights and exiting the last one look identical here. The enforceable scope column has to be read with it.
rationale: The data item defines the column as the number of distinct genus classes represented in applications allowed to retire in the year, within the IPLORD applicant-year frame.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what could be inferred from it or that it must be read against the standing portfolio.

value_domain: Count of plant breeder's rights allowed to retire in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, What are plant breeder's rights?
variable_description: How many plant breeder's rights the applicant let go during the financial year. Retirement is usually a decision not to keep paying: IP Australia requires annual renewal fees and warns that otherwise the right "lapses and can't be reactivated", so the column is the clearest signal in the plant breeder's rights data that a business has stopped commercialising a variety. It is a flow that reduces the enforceable stock on the same row.
description_source: IP Australia, What are plant breeder's rights?
value_definition: An integer count of rights or applications ending in the financial year for one applicant, counted whole regardless of co-ownership. Zero in the great majority of applicant-years.
limitation: It cannot separate abandonment from natural expiry, or from a withdrawal during examination: a variety that reached the end of its 20 or 25 year term counts the same as one dropped after two years. A high count therefore does not by itself indicate a business in retreat.
rationale: IP Australia states the annual renewal requirement and the consequence of not meeting it, which is the mechanism behind a retirement; IPLORD supplies the applicant-year frame.
evidence_quote: Note that you need to pay annual renewal fees for your PBR to maintain protection. Otherwise it lapses and can't be reactivated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the word 'retired' with no explanation and the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what retirement is or that it mixes lapse with expiry.

value_domain: Most frequent plant genus class among rights retired
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: The plant genus in which the applicant retired the most rights during the financial year. Where it matches the enforceable modal class the holder is shedding rights in its main crop; where it differs it is more likely pruning a side line. Retirements are few in any year, so the value usually rests on one or two events.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
value_definition: A character genus class code for one applicant in one financial year, empty where nothing was retired. It is the exit-side analogue of the filed, granted and enforceable modal class columns.
limitation: It cannot distinguish a strategic exit from a right reaching the end of its term, since both produce a retirement in the same genus. With so few events the mode is unstable, and a tie is resolved without any record of the alternatives.
rationale: The data item defines the column as the most common genus class among applications retired in the year; IPLORD supplies the applicant-year structure.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the value is a genus code or how thin the evidence behind it usually is.

value_domain: Fractionally attributed count of plant breeder's rights retired
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: The applicant's share of the plant breeder's rights that ended during the financial year, with jointly held rights split among their holders. It is the exit-side counterpart of the weighted filing and grant counts, and it is the column to use when totalling retirements across applicants without counting a shared right more than once.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
value_definition: A fractional count for one applicant in one financial year, non-integer where the retired rights were jointly held. It draws on the same events as the unweighted retired count.
limitation: A fraction here does not mean part of a right ended: rights lapse whole, and the fraction only reflects how many holders shared it. Because it mixes deliberate abandonment with term expiry, it cannot be read as a portfolio decision by this applicant alone, since any co-holder's choice moves the same number.
rationale: The data item defines the column as the fraction of applications the applicant allowed to retire in the year, within the IPLORD applicant-by-year structure.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's phrase about fractions retired with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what the fraction represents or why it may not be this applicant's decision.

value_domain: Percentage of the R&D entity controlled by tax exempt entities
value_source: ATO, R&D tax incentive: refundable and non-refundable offsets
variable_description: How much of the company registering research and development activity is controlled by tax exempt entities, reported on its registration. The number decides which offset it can claim: the ATO says a company with aggregated turnover "less than $20 million and you are not controlled by any exempt entities" can claim the refundable offset, while one that is "controlled by exempt entities" gets the non-refundable offset regardless of size. A high value therefore usually marks a research entity sitting under a university, a hospital or another exempt body.
description_source: ATO, R&D tax incentive: refundable and non-refundable offsets
value_definition: A numeric percentage between 0 and 100, self-reported on the research and development tax incentive registration rather than assessed by the ATO. It measures control by exempt entities, not ownership by government or by non-residents.
limitation: It is not a public ownership share. Exempt entity status is a tax concept covering charities, some non-profits and various government bodies, so a company can be majority government owned and still report zero, and the figure is a claim on a registration form rather than a verified shareholding.
rationale: The ATO sets out the exempt entity control test that this percentage exists to answer, and states the consequence for the offset the firm receives.
evidence_quote: less than $20 million and you are not controlled by any exempt entities, then you can claim the refundable tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Percentage control held by tax exempt entities' with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what an exempt entity is or why the percentage matters.

value_domain: Presence flag for group-based performance pay in the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement offers a recurring performance payment to groups of employees, or to the whole workforce, for meeting targets. The group basis is the point of the item: it separates collective incentives such as site or company bonuses from individual performance pay, which is coded elsewhere in the database. It is a clause in the agreement, so it says a scheme exists, not that any payment was made.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y where a group performance payment provision appears, with nothing recorded otherwise. It is coded per agreement, among roughly 200 items held for each.
limitation: It carries no amount, frequency or target, so a token annual bonus and a substantial gainsharing scheme look identical. Nothing records whether the targets were met, so the column cannot support any claim about performance pay actually received by employees of the business.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the database and the conditions coded for each agreement, including productivity provisions, which places this item and fixes its agreement-level unit.
evidence_quote: around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's description with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the flag is one-sided, carries no dollar value and records a clause rather than a payment.

value_domain: Agreement clause flag, individual performance pay
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: Marks an enterprise agreement that offers extra pay to an individual employee for meeting performance targets, rather than to a work group. It is a property of the agreement document, not of the firm: the row is one registered agreement, and the Fair Work Commission must approve every agreement and check it against the Better Off Overall Test before it operates. A business appears here only for the years an agreement of its own was in force, so award-reliant and individually contracted workplaces are absent by construction.
description_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
value_definition: A single-sided flag coded Y for yes. The Department of Employment and Workplace Relations codes it by reading the agreement text, so the domain is one value plus absence, not a yes and no pair.
limitation: A blank is not a no. It records that the coder did not find an individual performance pay clause, which covers agreements that are silent, agreements coded before the item existed, and agreements where the payment sits in a policy outside the agreement. It also says nothing about how much was paid or whether anyone met a target.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page establishes what the unit on this row is, that agreements are approved and tested by the Commission, and that they set terms and conditions above the National Employment Standards, which is the frame a reader needs before reading any WAD clause flag.
evidence_quote: Employees must be notified of their right to be represented
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's sentence about recurring performance payments with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the row is an agreement rather than a firm, or that a blank is not a denial.

value_domain: Platinum grade of an exported ore or concentrate shipment (per cent)
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The assayed platinum content of one exported shipment of ore or concentrate, as a percentage of shipment weight. It sits with the copper, lead, nickel, tin, tungsten, zinc and tantalum percentage columns and the gold and silver grams-per-tonne columns, which together let contained metal be worked out from gross weight. It is a grade attribute of the consignment, not a quantity, so it is meaningful only on the mineral commodity codes that carry an assay.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A percentage between zero and one hundred, attached to a single export declaration line rather than to the business or the year. It is a ratio of contained metal to shipment mass, and it does not follow the AHECC unit of quantity that governs the quantity column beside it.
limitation: It is empty for almost every export line, because only ore and concentrate consignments are assayed, so treating a missing value as zero platinum turns the whole non-mining economy into a zero-grade producer. The percentage is also the exporter's declared assay for one shipment and cannot be averaged across a year without weighting by shipment mass.
rationale: No fetchable ABS or Home Affairs page documents the metal-grade fields on the export declaration, so the reading rests on the column's neighbours in the BLADE merchandise trade table and on the BLADE overview naming Home Affairs customs declarations as the source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Percentage of platinum in shipment of ore' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the column is a grade rather than a quantity, nor that it is blank on nearly every line.

value_domain: Overseas port of discharge code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The first overseas port at which a firm's exported consignment is unloaded after leaving Australia. The ABS defines it as "the place where goods are unloaded from an aircraft or ship after it leaves Australia". It is the foreign end of the voyage, so it pairs with port_of_loading_ex, the Australian port the goods left from. It is not the same thing as the country of final destination on the same row, because a consignment can be discharged at a transhipment hub in one country and consumed in another.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A six-digit international merchandise trade overseas port code. The ABS derives it from the five-character UN location code declared to Home Affairs and corresponds it to its own six-digit overseas port classification, so the code is a UN/LOCODE in origin but not in form.
limitation: It does not tell you where the goods ended up. Discharge at a hub such as Singapore or Rotterdam is common for onward shipment, so building an export destination series from this column instead of country_of_final_dest_ex overstates trade with entrepot economies.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines the export port of discharge and states how UN location codes are corresponded to the six-digit overseas port classification the BLADE column carries.
evidence_quote: the place where goods are unloaded from an aircraft or ship after it leaves Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and pointed at an appendix the reader cannot open, with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never distinguished discharge from final destination.

value_domain: Australian port of discharge code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian port where a firm's imported consignment came off the ship or aircraft. The ABS treats this as the Australian end of an import voyage - "For exports, the Australian port is the port of loading and for imports the Australian port is the port of discharge" - so it is the import mirror of port_of_loading_ex. It describes the arrival point of the goods, not where the importing business is located or where the goods were eventually used.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A three-digit international merchandise trade Australian port code, corresponded by the ABS from the five-character UN location code on the import declaration. The three-digit form is what makes it shorter than the six-digit overseas port codes on the same table.
limitation: The port of arrival is not the state of the market. Container traffic for the whole eastern seaboard clears through a handful of ports, so counting imports by discharge port attributes goods to the port state rather than to state_of_destination_im, which is the state where the goods are released from customs control.
rationale: The chapter states explicitly that the Australian port for imports is the port of discharge and describes the correspondence to three-digit Australian port codes, which matches the three-digit domain the BLADE data item list gives.
evidence_quote: For exports, the Australian port is the port of loading and for imports the Australian port is the port of discharge
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's sentence and an appendix reference with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, so nothing told a reader the code is an ABS three-digit port code rather than a raw UN/LOCODE.

value_domain: Australian port of loading code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian port from which a firm's exported consignment left the country. It is the port behind state_of_loading_ex, which the ABS defines as "the Australian state in which the goods are loaded onto an international carrier for export", and it is distinct from state_of_origin_ex, the state where production or the final stage of manufacture occurred. For a firm that trucks goods interstate to a deepwater port, the loading port and the production state disagree, and both columns are on the row.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A three-digit international merchandise trade Australian port code, corresponded from the five-character UN location code on the export declaration. Australian ports use the three-digit classification while overseas ports on the same table use six digits.
limitation: It cannot locate the exporting business. A Victorian manufacturer shipping through Port Botany records a New South Wales loading port, so a state export series built from this column measures freight logistics rather than where the goods were made.
rationale: The chapter defines the Australian port for exports as the port of loading, gives the state of loading and state of origin definitions that separate freight routing from production, and states the three-digit coding.
evidence_quote: the Australian state in which the goods are loaded onto an international carrier for export
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording and cited an appendix, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never warned that the loading port is not the production state.

value_domain: Overseas port of loading code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The overseas port where a firm's imported consignment was put on the ship or aircraft bound for Australia. The ABS defines it as "the place where the goods are loaded onto an aircraft or ship for the purpose of being transported to Australia". It is the foreign end of an import voyage and pairs with port_of_discharge_im, the Australian arrival port. It is a shipping fact and is not the same as country_of_origin_im, which follows the rules of origin rather than the route.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A six-digit international merchandise trade overseas port code, corresponded by the ABS from the five-character UN location code declared to Home Affairs. Overseas ports carry six digits, so this column is wider than the three-digit Australian port columns beside it.
limitation: The loading port does not establish where the goods were made. Goods manufactured inland or in a third country are routinely loaded at a regional transhipment port, so using this column as a proxy for country of origin misattributes imports to the shipping hub.
rationale: The chapter gives the import port of loading definition verbatim and describes the six-digit overseas port coding that matches the domain the BLADE data item list states.
evidence_quote: the place where the goods are loaded onto an aircraft or ship for the purpose of being transported to Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's sentence and an appendix reference with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, so it never separated the shipping route from country of origin.

value_domain: Australian postcode of the intellectual property applicant
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Postal Areas
variable_description: The postcode of the address an applicant gave IP Australia when filing, reduced to one value per applicant by taking the most common postcode on their filings. It locates the party named on the application, which for a firm is usually a head office or an attorney's office rather than the site where the invention or the design work happened. Overseas addresses are not given a postcode at all: they are set to 9999, and a full stop marks a missing value.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Postal Areas
value_definition: A four-digit numeric Australia Post postcode, with 9999 reserved for an overseas address and '.' for missing. Postcodes are a delivery construct rather than a statistical geography; the ABS equivalent is the Postal Area, "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes".
limitation: Taking the modal postcode destroys movement. An applicant that relocates, or that files some applications through an attorney and others directly, is collapsed to whichever postcode appears most often, so this column cannot be used to date a change of address or to split filings by site. Joining it to ABS geography also introduces approximation error, because Postal Areas do not match postal boundaries exactly.
rationale: The ABS Postal Areas page establishes what a postcode is in statistical terms and how it relates to the geography a BLADE user would join to, which is the fact the IP Australia data item list omits; the modal rule and the 9999 and '.' codes come from the BLADE data item list itself.
evidence_quote: Postal Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's own sentence with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the modal rule removes any address history or that postcodes are not an ABS geography.
