value_domain: Superseded de-identified business identifier, JobKeeper release
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The holding identifier a JobKeeper business carried in an earlier release, before its ABN could be matched to the BLADE spine. It is a bridging column, not a business attribute: it lets analysis written against a previous JobKeeper extract be re-pointed at the bn that now identifies the same firm. It is populated only for the businesses whose identifier changed, so it is empty for firms that were de-identifiable from the start.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier with a JK prefix, drawn from the JobKeeper scheme's own numbering rather than from the BLADE business number series. It has no meaning outside the linkage; the digits do not encode industry, size or location.
limitation: It is not a business history. A value here records a change in how the ABS de-identified the entity, not a merger, a restructure or a change of ABN, so counting non-missing values measures linkage improvement rather than churn in the business population.
rationale: No published page documents this column; the reading is assembled from the BLADE overview, which names JobKeeper as an ATO source in BLADE and describes the business as the unit, and from the CN to BN and ID to BN key tables that sit beside it in the same asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's sentence about the JK prefix with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, so it never said the column is a bridge between releases rather than something about the firm.

value_domain: Weeks of paid primary care giver leave in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: How many weeks of paid parental leave an enterprise agreement gives the primary care giver of a new child. Unlike most WAD columns this one carries a quantity rather than a yes flag, and the wording it is coded from varies: some agreements say maternity leave and some are gender neutral. Two sentinel values sit outside the count, 111111111 where the agreement leaves the quantity open and 222222222 where it sets no limit.
description_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
value_definition: A number of weeks, with 111111111 meaning varies or unknown and 222222222 meaning no limit. Because an enterprise agreement can only improve on the National Employment Standards, the figure is paid employer leave in addition to the statutory unpaid entitlement.
limitation: It is entitlement on paper, not leave taken. Nothing here says how many employees used the leave, at what rate of pay, or whether the firm's government-funded parental leave pay sits on top. The two sentinel codes must also be filtered out before any average is taken, or a single 'no limit' agreement will dominate the mean.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page establishes that an agreement is negotiated, approved by the Commission and cannot exclude the National Employment Standards, which is what makes a recorded number of weeks an improvement on the statutory floor rather than a substitute for it.
evidence_quote: Terms that exclude the NES
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long clause description with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never flagged that the column is a numeric count with two sentinel values that break an unfiltered average.

value_domain: Priority date of an intellectual property application
value_source: IP Australia, Patent Manual of Practice and Procedure, 5.6.1.1 Priority dates and filing dates
variable_description: The date from which a firm's application outranks any competing application for the same kind of right, which for patents can be earlier than the day it was filed. IP Australia states that "Under s43(1), each claim of a specification must have a priority date" and that the priority date is what novelty and inventive step are judged against, with the filing date as the latest possible priority date. It is the date to use when timing an innovation, because filing and grant both lag the point at which the firm secured its position.
description_source: IP Australia, Patent Manual of Practice and Procedure, 5.6.1.1 Priority dates and filing dates
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, one per application row across the patent, trade mark, design and plant breeder's right series that IPRAPID carries. The table's reference period runs from 1904-05, so dates far predate the tax and survey sources BLADE links to.
limitation: It is one date for a whole application, while the law attaches a priority date to each claim, so an application whose claims have different priority dates is flattened here. It also does not mean the right exists: a priority date is recorded for applications that lapse, are withdrawn or are refused, so counting priority dates counts attempts rather than granted rights.
rationale: The IP Australia patent manual gives the statutory basis and function of the priority date and explains its relationship to the filing date, which is the distinction the BLADE data item list leaves implicit.
evidence_quote: Under s43(1), each claim of a specification must have a priority date. The priority date of a claim is primarily of relevance when assessing the claim against the criteria of novelty and inventive/innovative step.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's one-line description with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the priority date can precede filing or that it is recorded per application rather than per claim.

value_domain: Agreement clause flag, employee profit sharing
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: Marks an enterprise agreement under which employees share in company profits once a profit threshold or set of indicators is reached. It differs from the performance pay flags beside it because the trigger is the firm's result rather than the employee's or the team's output. The row is an agreement approved by the Fair Work Commission, so the flag attaches to a bargaining outcome and appears only while that agreement is on foot.
description_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
value_definition: A single-sided flag coded Y for yes, assigned by the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations from the agreement text. There is no companion no code, and no amount, share or threshold is recorded.
limitation: It does not measure profit sharing in the economy. Employee share and profit schemes are commonly set out in company policy or in a separate plan document rather than in the agreement, and those never reach this flag, so it undercounts the practice rather than measuring it.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page establishes that the row is a negotiated, Commission-approved instrument setting terms and conditions of employment, which is what limits the flag to provisions that were written into the agreement itself.
evidence_quote: Terms & conditions of employment
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's clause description with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the flag captures only agreement text and so undercounts profit sharing.

value_domain: Agreement clause flag, dismissal procedure, pre-2010 agreements
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: Marks an agreement that sets out a process for dismissing an employee, and it is coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2010. The cut-off is a coding rule rather than a change in practice: after the Fair Work system took effect the statutory unfair dismissal regime made a bespoke agreement clause less common and the Department stopped coding it. Any series built on this flag therefore ends at the same date for every firm, whatever the agreement says.

value_domain: Agreement operates in Queensland indicator
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Marks that the workplace agreement on this row covers work performed in Queensland. The table records employees and femaleemployees for the agreement as a whole and gives no state split, so a Queensland flag on an agreement covering 4,000 workers nationally cannot be turned into a Queensland headcount. value_domain: Export quantity, counted in the unit named by unit_of_quantity_ex
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods (5489.0), Units of Quantity
variable_description: How much of the commodity left Australia on this export line, counted in whatever unit unit_of_quantity_ex names on the same row. The ABS fixes that unit by commodity rather than by shipment: "the unit of quantity shown against a particular commodity code is that specified in the AHECC (8 digit level) or Customs Tariff (10 digit level) classification". It sits beside fob_value_ex and gross_weight_ex, which give the value and the shipped weight of the same line, so quantity is the physical measure the trade classification chose for that good.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods (5489.0), Units of Quantity
value_definition: A count with no unit of its own; the unit comes from unit_of_quantity_ex, set at the eight-digit AHECC code for exports. Where a code spans a diverse range of goods the ABS records the unit as NR and supplies no quantity at all.
limitation: Quantity must not be added across commodities. The ABS warns that "aggregating data for commodities with mixed units of quantity...will produce meaningless quantity totals", so a firm-year total quantity is uninterpretable unless it is built within one unit. A zero or empty value can also mean the commodity code has no unit rather than that nothing moved.
rationale: The variable counts the number of units of unit_of_quantity_ex, and the ABS concepts and methods publication defines exactly how that unit is chosen, when it is absent, and why quantities cannot be pooled.
evidence_quote: Because the unit of quantity is recorded against the most detailed classification code, any quantity aggregation must be undertaken with care.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's circular wording, 'counts the number of unit_of_quantity_ex variable', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Import quantity, counted in the unit named by unit_of_quantity_im
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods (5489.0), Units of Quantity
variable_description: How much of the commodity entered Australia on this import line, counted in the unit that unit_of_quantity_im names on the same row. For imports the unit is set at the ten-digit Customs Tariff code rather than the eight-digit AHECC used for exports, so the same physical good can be counted on a finer commodity split coming in than going out. The ABS notes the unit is normally the industry's own: "Where the WCO standard unit is not used for that commodity in the Australian industry, the unit of quantity will generally be the normal unit of quantity used for a particular commodity in the associated industry".
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods (5489.0), Units of Quantity
value_definition: A count with no unit of its own; the unit is taken from unit_of_quantity_im, specified at the ten-digit Customs Tariff level. Codes covering mixed goods carry NR and no quantity.
limitation: It is not comparable with quantity_ex without care, because the two are anchored to different classifications at different levels of detail. Import quantity also belongs to a customs declaration line and not to a purchase, so re-imports, temporary imports and consignments split across lines all inflate a naive count of how much a business bought from abroad.
rationale: The variable counts units of unit_of_quantity_im, and the ABS concepts and methods publication states that the import unit is specified at the ten-digit Customs Tariff level and how the unit is chosen.
evidence_quote: the unit of quantity shown against a particular commodity code is that specified in the AHECC (8 digit level) or Customs Tariff (10 digit level) classification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's circular wording, 'counts the number of unit_of_quantity_im variable', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said imports are classified on a different and finer commodity code than exports.

Twenty BLADE tables carry it, chiefly the quarterly Business Activity Statement records and the merchandise trade lines, which is where a single business contributes up to four rows a year rather than one.

value_domain: ASIC registration basis of the R&D entity
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: How the company claiming the R&D Tax Incentive is incorporated, which is the test of whether it may claim at all. A fourth answer exists on the form and does not appear here, because "If the company is not registered with ASIC, it is not eligible for the R&D Tax Incentive".
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance

limitation: Everything in this column is a claimant, so it says nothing about the incorporation mix of Australian business generally. It is also a self-reported answer at registration and is not refreshed if the company's residence or permanent establishment position changes later in the project.

value_domain: Project covered by an advance or overseas finding (yes/no)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), Apply for an overseas finding from the R&D Tax Incentive
variable_description: Whether the registered R&D project contains activities already covered by a binding eligibility decision from the department. Two different decisions sit behind the one flag: an advance finding, which is optional assurance about Australian activities, and an overseas finding, which is compulsory before overseas work can be claimed. A company that plans to "claim expenditure on R&D activities conducted overseas" is told "You must have a positive overseas finding in place first". A flagged project is therefore either an unusually cautious claimant or one doing R&D offshore, and the column cannot tell you which.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), Apply for an overseas finding from the R&D Tax Incentive
value_definition: Categorical: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and UNKNOWN where the answer was not captured. It is set at the project level, not for the company as a whole.
limitation: It does not identify overseas R&D. Because advance and overseas findings share a single flag, a 1 cannot be read as offshore activity, and a 0 does not rule it out either, since a company may hold a finding for a different project. Nor does the flag say the finding was positive.
rationale: The department's own guidance defines both findings and states which of them is compulsory, which is what distinguishes the two decisions this single flag collapses.
evidence_quote: You must have a positive overseas finding in place first.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's question wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving the two very different findings behind the flag undistinguished.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover of the R&D entity and its connected and affiliated entities (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The turnover figure that decides which R&D tax offset the company gets, reported for the most recently completed income year. It is not the company's own sales: "The company's aggregated turnover is the sum of the annual turnover for all of the following: the company (including all members of the consolidated group), any entity connected with the company..., any entity affiliated with the company...", with dealings between them removed. The test is applied to the grouped figure rather than to the company's own trading, so a small Australian claimant inside a large group is assessed on the group's turnover.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, GST exclusive, covering the claimant plus its connected and affiliated entities worldwide. The form defines annual turnover as "the total ordinary income it derived in the income year in the ordinary course of carrying on its business activities".
limitation: It is not a measure of the claimant's own size, and it is not the BLADE business's turnover. Grouping brings in entities that may sit outside the BLADE unit altogether, so comparing this against the same ABN's business activity statement turnover will disagree by design. The figure is also self-reported on the registration form and not reconciled to a tax return.
rationale: The published R&DTI application questions state the exact aggregation rule for this field and define annual turnover, which is the difference between this column and any turnover measure elsewhere in BLADE.
evidence_quote: An entity's annual turnover is the total ordinary income it derived in the income year in the ordinary course of carrying on its business activities. This amount does not include GST.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line about aggregated turnover for the selected income period and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure includes connected and affiliated entities outside the business.

value_source: ABS, Australian and New Zealand Standard Research Classification (ANZSRC), 2020
variable_description: The field of research that best describes the majority of the R&D activity in this project, coded to the ABS research classification. The ABS defines ANZSRC as "a set of three related classifications developed for use in the measurement and analysis of research and experimental development (R&D) statistics in Australia and New Zealand", of which Fields of Research is the one used here, running from two-digit divisions through four-digit groups to six-digit fields. It answers what kind of research a firm claimed for, which no other BLADE column does.
description_source: ABS, Australian and New Zealand Standard Research Classification (ANZSRC), 2020

Nor is the code a description of the firm - it is the field of one project, chosen by the applicant, and a firm registering several projects has several codes.

evidence_quote: Only the head company of a consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group can apply to register R&D activities.

value_domain: Total estimated expenditure over the life of the R&D project (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance

rationale: The published R&DTI application questions give the exact question and the guidance that the amount is a reasonable estimate for the project as a whole, which distinguishes it from the annual activity amounts.
evidence_quote: Enter a reasonable estimate of the expected expenditure on this project.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line 'How much is expected to be spent over the life of this project' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is an unaudited forecast.

value_domain: Registered expenditure on core R&D activities for the income period (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: What the company reported spending on its core R&D activities in the registration year. Core activities are the experimental ones, whose outcome the department says "cannot be known or determined in advance" and "can only be determined by applying a systematic progression of work". The form asks the applicant to "Enter a reasonable estimate of the expenditure incurred on this core R&D activity for the income year of registration", so it is an estimate lodged with the registration and not a figure from the tax return. The custodian notes the column combines the legacy and current registration systems.

The combination of legacy and current systems in one column also means a change in level across the system changeover can be a reporting artefact rather than a change in R&D spending.
rationale: The published application questions give the exact wording for the core activity expenditure field and the instruction that it is a reasonable estimate for the registration year, and the department defines what makes an activity core.
evidence_quote: Enter a reasonable estimate of the expenditure incurred on this core R&D activity for the income year of registration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's raw label, including the legacy-and-current-system note, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a registered estimate from a claimed deduction.

value_domain: Registered expenditure on supporting R&D activities for the income period (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: What the company reported spending on activities that support its core R&D rather than constituting it, for the registration year. The form's instruction is wider than the core equivalent: the estimate "should include expenditure on the activity conducted by the company, and contracted expenditure to research service providers or Cooperative Research Centres (if any)". Supporting activities must be directly related to a core activity, and some must also be conducted for the dominant purpose of supporting one, so the split against rdti_expenditureoncore is a legal test rather than an accounting one.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, summed over the project's supporting activities, and including money paid out to research service providers and cooperative research centres. Like the core figure it combines the legacy and current registration systems.
limitation: The core and supporting split is a self-assessed classification and is not audited at registration, so the ratio between the two columns measures how a company chose to characterise its work as much as what it did. Activities excluded from being core, such as some production and market research, can appear here, which makes this the softer of the two measures of R&D intensity.
rationale: The published application questions give the exact supporting-activity expenditure question and state that contracted amounts belong in it, and the department's guidance defines the direct-relation and dominant-purpose tests that separate supporting from core.
evidence_quote: This should include expenditure on the activity conducted by the company, and contracted expenditure to research service providers or Cooperative Research Centres (if any).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's misspelt label 'Total Project Expenditure on supportinge Activity' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what makes an activity supporting rather than core.

value_domain: Revenue from export sales reported on the R&D registration (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: Export sales revenue for the income year, reported by the R&D claimant across the whole group. The form ties the figure to a tax lodgment rather than to accounts: it is the company's "total revenue from export sales for the income year covered by this application as reported in the company's business activity statement provided to the Australian Taxation Office", and applicants are told to add up the export amounts from each activity statement for the year. That makes it comparable in concept with the export label on the BAS, though it is entered by hand on a different form.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, covering the claimant and the entities reported with it, built by summing the export sales amounts across the year's business activity statements.
limitation: It is not merchandise trade. The activity statement export label covers services and GST-free export sales as well as goods, so this figure will not reconcile with the fob_value_ex totals in BLADE's merchandise exports tables for the same ABN. It is also only collected from R&D claimants, so it cannot support an exporter population count.
rationale: The published application questions state that the field is taken from the company's business activity statements and how it is to be assembled, which is what fixes its concept and its span.
evidence_quote: To find the total revenue on export sales add up the individual export sale amounts in each business activity statement provided to the Australian Taxation Office for the income year of this application.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line about revenue earned across all companies from export sales and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing linked the figure to the business activity statement or warned that it is not merchandise trade.

value_domain: Start date of the income period the registration covers
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The first day of the income year the R&D registration relates to, which for most claimants is 1 July. The form's first income-period question is "Does the company follow a standard income period (1 July to 30 June)?", and it directs the applicant to "the income period on the company's income tax return submitted to the Australian Taxation Office". A start date other than 1 July therefore signals a substituted or transitional accounting period approved by the ATO, which is exactly the population whose R&D year does not line up with the BLADE financial year.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A ten-character date in dd/mm/yyyy form, where yyyy is the calendar year. Standard-period companies carry 1 July; substituted and transitional accounting periods carry other dates.
limitation: It is the accounting period of the claim, not the period in which the research happened. Project and activity dates can start before it and run past its end, so using this date to time R&D effort will misplace multi-year projects. It also gives no warning where a transitional period is shorter or longer than twelve months.
rationale: The published application questions define the income period the registration is made against and identify the substituted and transitional accounting periods that produce non-standard start dates.
evidence_quote: This should be the income period on the company's income tax return submitted to the Australian Taxation Office.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label 'Income Period Start Date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said why a date other than 1 July appears.

value_domain: End date of the income period the registration covers
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The last day of the income year the R&D registration relates to, and the boundary that dates every financial figure on the row. Registration is lodged after that year has closed, so a row enters the data some months after the work it reports. Where the company has an ATO-approved substituted accounting period, "the income year will end on a date other than 30 June", which is what makes this column worth reading rather than assuming.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A ten-character date in dd/mm/yyyy form. Most rows carry 30 June; substituted accounting periods end on other dates and transitional periods can run more or less than twelve months.
limitation: The date the registration was actually lodged is unobserved, so the column cannot be used to date when the department learned of the R&D. Pairing it with rdti_incomeperiodstarton also does not guarantee a twelve-month window, and treating every row as a full year will overstate a transitional period's R&D intensity.
rationale: The published application questions fix the income period a registration is made against and state that a substituted accounting period ends on a date other than 30 June, which is what a non-standard value in this column means.
evidence_quote: If the company has a substituted accounting period approved by the Australian Taxation Office, the income year will end on a date other than 30 June.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label 'Income Period End Date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing connected the date to the registration deadline.

value_domain: Country the R&D claimant was incorporated in (Australia or foreign)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: Whether the claiming company was incorporated in Australia or overseas, collapsed to two categories. The underlying form question, "What country was the company incorporated in?", is only asked of companies that answered the ASIC registration question with one of the two foreign-law options, so the Australian value here is largely a derived residual rather than a country the applicant typed. It works with rdti_residencecountryname, which is asked only of the double tax agreement group, to place a foreign claimant.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: Categorical with two values, AUSTRALIA and FOREIGN. The actual country is not retained in BLADE even though the form collects it from a drop-down list of countries.
limitation: It cannot identify which foreign country a claimant came from, so it cannot support any analysis of where foreign-owned R&D originates. It also describes incorporation, not ownership: an Australian-incorporated subsidiary of an overseas parent reads as AUSTRALIA here, and only rdti_uhcincorporationcountry hints otherwise.
rationale: The published application questions show the incorporation question, the drop-down of countries behind it and the condition under which it is displayed, which explains why the BLADE column has only two values.
evidence_quote: This question will display if either 'B & C' were selected for Q10.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line 'The country that the company incorporated in' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the country itself has been suppressed to a binary.

value_domain: Levy paid to a levy-collecting research service provider, apportioned to core R&D activities (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The share of an industry levy the company paid that its levy-collecting research service provider says went to core R&D activities. It exists only for companies that ticked "Expenditure paid via a levy to a Research Service Provider" on the registration, which in practice means levy payers in industries such as agriculture whose research is done collectively. The form requires "the apportionment of the levies between core and supporting R&D activities as reported to the company by the levy-collecting research service provider", so the split comes from the provider and not from the firm.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income period, one of a set of levy sub-fields that also record the provider, the total levy paid, the proportion used for R&D services and the supporting-activity share.
limitation: It is empty for almost every claimant, so a zero or blank is overwhelmingly 'this route does not apply' rather than 'no levy R&D'. The amount also measures a contribution to research the firm did not itself conduct, so adding it to the firm's own core expenditure conflates in-house R&D with a levy paid into a collective research body.
rationale: The published application questions set out the levy-collecting research service provider sub-questions in order, including the core and supporting apportionment this column holds and where that apportionment comes from.
evidence_quote: the apportionment of the levies between core and supporting R&D activities as reported to the company by the levy-collecting research service provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total levy allocated to core R&D activities' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what a levy-collecting research service provider is or why the column is almost always empty.

value_domain: Postcode where most of the project's R&D was conducted
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The postcode of the place where the company did most of the R&D in this project, taken from the address it gave at registration. The form asks for one address even when the work was spread: "If the company's R&D activities are conducted at multiple locations (e.g. different states, labs, or field sites), please enter the address where the majority of the R&D activities were performed." Where the R&D address matches the main business address the applicant is not asked again, so this column is a research location rather than a head office location.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A four-digit categorical code, with 9999 reserved for an invalid entry. It is the Australia Post postcode typed into the registration form, not an ABS geography; the ABS itself only approximates postcodes for statistical use through Postal Areas.
limitation: One postcode per project hides everything else. A project run across three states is reduced to the majority site, so mapping R&D by this column understates the geographic spread and overstates concentration in the largest laboratory. Postcodes are also an Australia Post delivery construct rather than a statistical geography, so they do not nest into ABS regions and the ABS only approximates them through Postal Areas.
rationale: The published application questions show the address question, the condition under which it is asked and the majority-of-activities rule, which is what fixes whose location this column records.
evidence_quote: If the company's R&D activities are conducted at multiple locations (e.g. different states, labs, or field sites), please enter the address where the majority of the R&D activities were performed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label about where the company conducts most of its R&D and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what is lost when a multi-site project is reduced to one postcode.

value_domain: Expected end date of the R&D project
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: When the company expects the whole R&D project to finish, given at registration as a month and year. The form collects it as one half of "the expected duration of this project" and instructs the applicant to "Enter the expected start and end dates (month and year) for the project". Individual activities are bounded by it, because their own start and end dates "must fall within the dates specified for the related project", so this date sets the outer edge of everything else the project reports.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A ten-character date in dd/mm/yyyy form in BLADE, although the registration form only collects a month and a year, so the day component carries no information.
limitation: It is an expectation recorded once, not an observed completion. A project abandoned early or extended keeps the date it was registered with unless a later registration revises it, so the column cannot be used to measure project duration or survival. The custodian's own description for this column is also wrong, repeating the start date variable's name.
rationale: The published application questions give the project duration question and the rule that activity dates must sit inside the project dates, which is the only thing that makes this column interpretable.
evidence_quote: The start and end dates (month and year) for the core activity must fall within the dates specified for the related project.
supersedes_rationale: The entry's official description was the string 'rdti_projectstartdate', which is the wrong variable name, and the generic no-value-list sentence was printed as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Expected start date of the R&D project
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: When the R&D project began or is expected to begin, given at registration as a month and year. It is the opening bound of the project, and every core and supporting activity registered under it must start on or after this date. Because a company registers each year and may re-register a continuing project, a start date well before the income period on the same row is the normal signature of a multi-year project rather than an error.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A ten-character date in dd/mm/yyyy form in BLADE, though the registration form collects only a month and a year, so the day component is not meaningful.
limitation: It dates a project as the applicant described it, not the first R&D the firm ever did. Firms differ in whether they carve work into many short projects or one long one, so counting projects by start year measures registration practice, and the earliest start date in a firm's records is not its entry into R&D.
rationale: The published application questions define the project duration fields and require activity dates to fall inside them, which fixes what a project start date bounds.
evidence_quote: Enter the expected start and end dates (month and year) for the project.
supersedes_rationale: The entry's official description repeated the variable name and the generic no-value-list sentence appeared as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the date bounds.

value_domain: Country of tax residence of a foreign-incorporated R&D claimant (Australia or foreign)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: Where the claiming company is resident for tax, collapsed to Australia or foreign. The form only asks this of one narrow group: the question "is only shown for companies registered under foreign law that are residents of a country with which Australia has a double tax agreement and are carrying on business in Australia through a permanent establishment as defined in the double tax agreement". For every other claimant the value is filled by construction rather than answered, so it carries no information about them.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: Categorical with two values, AUSTRALIA and FOREIGN, against a form question that collects an actual country from a drop-down list.
limitation: It is not a general residence field and should not be compared across claimants. The value is only meaningfully collected for the double tax agreement group identified by rdentityasicregistrationtype code 3, and reading FOREIGN as a measure of offshore claimants across the whole file will mix a real answer with a default.
rationale: The published application questions state precisely which claimants see the residence question, which is the fact that decides whether the value on a given row means anything.
evidence_quote: The question is only shown for companies registered under foreign law that are residents of a country with which Australia has a double tax agreement and are carrying on business in Australia through a permanent establishment as defined in the double tax agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'The company's country of residence' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field is asked of a small subgroup and defaulted for everyone else.

value_domain: Taxable income or loss reported on the R&D registration (dollars)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The company's taxable income or loss for the most recently completed income year, self-reported on the R&D registration. The form is explicit about the sign and the reporting unit: "This is the company's taxable income or loss for the selected income year. Losses should be shown as negative figures. A consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group is a single entity for income tax purposes; therefore, the taxable income or loss will be for the group." Loss-making claimants are common here, because the refundable form of the offset lets a company benefit while making a loss.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A signed dollar amount for one income year, negative for a loss, covering the tax consolidated group where one exists.
limitation: It is not the taxable income the ATO assessed. The figure is typed onto a registration form, often before the return is finalised, so it will not always match the company's own business income tax record in BLADE, and it is not an audited series. Where the claimant heads a group, it also does not describe the ABN on the row alone.
rationale: The published application questions give the field's exact wording, its sign convention and the group reporting rule, which are the three things needed before the number can be compared with anything else.
evidence_quote: This is the company's taxable income or loss for the selected income year. Losses should be shown as negative figures.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line about taxable income or loss across all companies and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said losses are negative or that the figure is self-reported.

value_domain: Total employees on the claimant's payroll at the end of the income year (count)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: How many people the R&D claimant employed at the end of the income year, counted as a head count and not as full-time equivalents. The form defines the scope: "This includes working directors, partners, proprietors, and all full-time, part-time, and casual employees" and "It does not include contractors, whether engaged as individuals or through a company structure". It is a separate field from the R&D workforce, which the form collects as a full-time equivalent person-years figure, so this column measures firm size rather than research effort.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: A count of persons at a single point, the end of the most recently completed income year, on a head-count basis. For consolidated groups it covers all relevant subsidiaries in the group.
limitation: A stock at year end is not employment over the year, so it misses seasonal and short-tenure staff entirely and will disagree with the payroll-based employment measures elsewhere in BLADE. Excluding contractors also understates the labour of firms that outsource, which is common in the small, R&D-intensive companies that dominate this population.
rationale: The published application questions state the point in time, the head-count basis, the inclusion of casual and working-director staff, and the exclusion of contractors.
evidence_quote: This question asks for the total number of employees on the company's payroll at the end of the most recently completed income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line about employees across all companies at the end of the income period and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said whether contractors or part-timers are counted.

value_domain: Country the claimant's ultimate holding company was incorporated in (Australia or foreign)
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: Where the company that ultimately controls the R&D claimant was incorporated, collapsed to Australia or foreign. It is the closest thing on the record to a foreign ownership marker. The form defines the parent it means: "A company is an Ultimate Holding company if it has majority ownership of or controlling interests in the R&D company or other companies in the consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group which are connected or affiliated with the R&D company." The field is only asked of claimants that answered yes to having an ultimate holding company at all.
description_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au), R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
value_definition: Categorical with two values, AUSTRALIA and FOREIGN, derived from a country drop-down. It is absent where the company reported no ultimate holding company.
limitation: A blank is not evidence of independence, because the ultimate-holding-company question is itself self-assessed and companies with dispersed ownership answer no. The two-value collapse also destroys the distinction between a parent in a low-tax jurisdiction and one in a major research economy, which is normally the reason to want the field.
rationale: The published application questions define an ultimate holding company, state that the incorporation country question follows a yes answer, and show the country drop-down that BLADE has collapsed.
evidence_quote: A company is an Ultimate Holding company if it has majority ownership of or controlling interests in the R&D company or other companies in the consolidated or multiple entry consolidated group which are connected or affiliated with the R&D company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Country of the incorporated Ultimate Holding Company' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing defined an ultimate holding company or explained the blanks.

value_domain: ABS integration version identifier for the RDTI module
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Which build of the R&D Tax Incentive integration the row came from, an ABS housekeeping stamp rather than anything about the business. It is the RDTI counterpart of the exp_version, frame_version and ag_version columns on other BLADE modules, and it changes when the ABS re-runs the linkage, not when the firm's R&D changes. The RDTI module in BLADE covers 2013-14 to 2020-21.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric categorical code of the form in269_v1, naming an internal ABS integration reference.
limitation: It is not a data quality flag and not a date. A reader cannot infer from the version string when the extract was taken, what changed between versions, or whether two versions are comparable, so it should be used only to check that a single vintage is being analysed.
rationale: The ABS holdings list confirms the RDTI module and its year span within BLADE; the version string itself is described by the custodian as an internal ABS reference and has no published documentation.
evidence_quote: Research & Development Tax Incentive (RDTI) Program: 2013-14 to 2020-21
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column describes the extract rather than the firm.

value_domain: Agreement provides for redundancy or income protection scheme payments (Y flag)
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Marks an agreement that obliges the employer to pay into an external redundancy or income protection fund, such as INCOLINK or ACIRT. Only Y is coded, so the column records the presence of a clause and never its absence. Because the money goes to a portable industry fund rather than to the worker, the field is a payment obligation on the employer and not an entitlement amount for an employee.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: A one-sided character flag: Y where the agreement carries the provision, and blank otherwise. There is no N code and no dollar amount attached.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as 'no scheme'. The conditions recorded about each agreement are reviewed from year to year, so a blank may mean the item was not collected for agreements of that vintage, and the clause itself says nothing about how much was contributed or how many workers were covered.
rationale: The ABS list of BLADE data holdings confirms the Workplace Agreements Database is a Department of Employment and Workplace Relations module in BLADE covering 2001-02 to 2022-23, and the sibling columns in the same table fix the unit of the row. The department's own WAD page was not reachable, so the meaning of the individual field is assembled rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Workplace Agreements Data: 2001-02 to 2022-23
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence about redundancy schemes and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the column has no explicit negative code.

value_domain: Agreement restricts or caps part-time work (Y flag)
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Marks an agreement that limits part-time work, for example by imposing a quota on part-time positions. The valid-response note confines the code to agreements made before 1 January 2009, so this is a closed series rather than a continuing measure. Agreements made from that date carry a blank whether or not they restrict part-time work, which makes the column useful only for the earlier part of the 2001-02 to 2022-23 window.
description_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
value_definition: A one-sided character flag: Y where the restriction is present, blank otherwise, and coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2009.
limitation: It cannot support a trend. Counting Y over time will show restrictions collapsing to zero after 2008, which is a change in what the department coded and not a change in bargaining practice. The flag also does not say how tight the restriction is, so a hard ban and a soft quota look identical.
rationale: The ABS list of BLADE data holdings confirms the Workplace Agreements Database is a Department of Employment and Workplace Relations module in BLADE covering 2001-02 to 2022-23, and the sibling columns in the same table fix the unit of the row. The department's own WAD page was not reachable, so the meaning of the individual field is assembled rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Workplace Agreements Data: 2001-02 to 2022-23
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and buried the 1 January 2009 cut-off in the valid-response text where nothing explained that it breaks the series.

value_domain: Dealroom manufacturing revenue model flag (1/0)
value_source: Dealroom.co, Tech sector taxonomy
variable_description: Marks a business Dealroom classifies as making goods and selling the finished product to a customer. It is one of several non-exclusive revenue model flags on the same row, so a firm that both manufactures and sells software by subscription carries a 1 in more than one column. The flag is time invariant and repeated across every year of the ABN, so it describes the business as Dealroom last profiled it and not as it was in any particular year.
description_source: Dealroom.co, Tech sector taxonomy
value_definition: A binary indicator: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and a full stop for missing. The tag comes from Dealroom's own taxonomy rather than from ANZSIC or any ABS classification.
limitation: It is not an industry code and does not line up with ANZSIC manufacturing. Dealroom's tagging is built from public sources and company self-description, so the flag records how a company presents itself to investors. Dealroom covers startups and high-growth companies rather than all Australian business, so a 0 mostly means the firm was never profiled, and BLADE holds a single 2025 vintage back-filled over every year of the ABN.
rationale: Dealroom publishes the taxonomy that these flags come from, including the separation of business models and revenue models from industries, which is what tells a reader the column is not an industry classification.
evidence_quote: The 18 simplified sectors are algorithmically derived from the combination of industries, sub-industries, tags, and technologies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Dealroom's own definition of the manufacturing revenue model verbatim and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said how the tag is produced or what a 0 means.

value_domain: Dealroom marketplace and ecommerce model flag (1/0)
value_source: Dealroom.co, Tech sector taxonomy
variable_description: Marks a business Dealroom classifies as running a marketplace or ecommerce operation, connecting buyers and sellers rather than selling only its own output. Dealroom lists Marketplace & eCommerce as one of three business models, beside SaaS and Manufacturing, which are the other two flags in this group, so a firm can carry more than one. The flag is time invariant across the ABN's rows.
description_source: Dealroom.co, Tech sector taxonomy
value_definition: A binary indicator: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and a full stop for missing. It reflects Dealroom's business model layer, which sits above the finer income-stream labels such as commission and selling own inventory.
limitation: The label conflates two different economics. A commission-taking platform and a retailer holding its own stock both read as 1, so margin, capital intensity and inventory risk cannot be inferred from the flag. Dealroom covers startups and high-growth companies rather than all Australian business, so a 0 mostly means the firm was never profiled, and BLADE holds a single 2025 vintage back-filled over every year of the ABN.
rationale: Dealroom's published taxonomy names marketplace and ecommerce as one of its business models and lists the separate income streams underneath them, which is the distinction the BLADE column loses.
evidence_quote: Marketplace & eCommerce SaaS Manufacturing
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Dealroom's own wording about a place connecting buyers and sellers and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the flag mixes commission platforms with inventory retailers.

value_domain: Dealroom software-as-a-service model flag (1/0)
value_source: Dealroom.co, Tech sector taxonomy
variable_description: Marks a business Dealroom classifies as delivering software by subscription over the internet rather than selling installed licences. Dealroom lists SaaS as a business model rather than an industry, so the flag can sit on a firm tagged to health, fintech or education, and it sits beside Marketplace & eCommerce and Manufacturing in the same group. It is time invariant and repeated over every year of the ABN.
description_source: Dealroom.co, Tech sector taxonomy
value_definition: A binary indicator: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and a full stop for missing. It is a business model tag, not a revenue model in Dealroom's own sense, where the matching income stream would be subscription.
limitation: It says nothing about scale or recurring revenue. rationale: The taxonomy page lists Travel Analytics as a Travel child and Marketing Analytics under two other parents, which is how the analytics flags are kept apart.
evidence_quote: Sub-industries reuse labels across industries — e.g., “Content Production” appears under Media, Telecom, Music, etc. The sub-industry is contextual to its parent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and no limitation of substance, so it did not warn that the tag is a single 2025 judgement copied across every year of the ABN.

description_source: Dealroom.co, Tech Sector Taxonomy
value_definition: Binary, with . for an ABN Dealroom does not cover. It encodes membership of the Booking & Search sub-industry of Travel in Dealroom's commercial company taxonomy, not in any statistical classification.
limitation: The line between this and the online travel agency column is Dealroom's own and firms carry both, so the two cannot be added or treated as separate markets.
rationale: The taxonomy page lists Booking & Search under Travel and under Event Tech, and lists Online Travel Agency separately, which is the overlap named here.
evidence_quote: Sub-industries reuse labels across industries — e.g., “Content Production” appears under Media, Telecom, Music, etc. The sub-industry is contextual to its parent.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier entry described the sub-industry in Dealroom's own promotional terms and left the value definition and the limitation identical, so neither said what the classification is not.

evidence_quote: Sub-industries reuse labels across industries — e.g., “Content Production” appears under Media, Telecom, Music, etc. The sub-industry is contextual to its parent.

value_source: Dealroom.co, Tech Sector Taxonomy
variable_description: A 1 marks the business as an online travel agency, letting users search, compare and book flights, hotels and packages. Dealroom publishes Online Travel Agency as a Travel child in its own right, distinct from the Booking & Search tools held in s_ind_travel_booking.
description_source: Dealroom.co, Tech Sector Taxonomy
value_definition: One flag in a set of binary sub-industry indicators: 1 tagged, 0 not tagged, . missing. The label is Dealroom's Online Travel Agency child of its Travel industry, taken from the Dealroom extract the ABS carries for 2025.
limitation: It is not an accreditation record, so nothing here says the firm is a bonded or accredited travel seller, and the column carries no bookings or transaction value.

evidence_quote: Sub-industries reuse labels across industries — e.g., “Content Production” appears under Media, Telecom, Music, etc. The sub-industry is contextual to its parent.
