value_domain: De-identified IP right application number (IP Australia IPRAPID)
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The de-identified application number of the intellectual property right on the other side of a link recorded in IP Australia's IPRAPID data. It is de-identified with the same key as s_an, so a value here joins straight back to the application-level IPRAPID tables and lets a filing be walked to its counterpart. IPRAPID is IP Australia's refreshed registry product covering patents, trade marks, designs and plant breeder's rights, which the ABS lists in BLADE from 1904-05 to 2024-25.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: An alphanumeric categorical identifier with no internal meaning, de-identified consistently with s_an so the two can be joined. The right type, filing date, status and owner live in the IPRAPID application tables, not in this column.
limitation: It is a key, not a count. A links table holds one row per link, so a filing with several counterparts appears several times and counting rows counts links rather than IP rights. The column also does not say what kind of relationship the link records, and IPRAPID's own dictionary is not published openly, so the direction of the link has to be established from the table rather than assumed.
rationale: The ABS page listing BLADE's data inclusions names IPRAPID as IP Australia's contribution and gives its reference period, and IP Australia's open data on data.gov.au shows the same registry organised as application-level tables per right type. Neither publishes the IPRAPID links table itself, so the meaning of the linked application number is inferred from the data item wording.
evidence_quote: Intellectual Property Refreshed Automated Product for Information 1904-05 to 2024-25
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the data item's own sentence and printed the generic no-value-list text as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which agency's registry this is, how far back it runs, or that a row is a link rather than a right.

value_domain: De-identified previous ABS agricultural unit identifier
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22
variable_description: The de-identified unit identifier this agricultural business carried before its ABS agricultural unit identifier changed. That is what lets a holding be followed across collections. The population it belongs to is size-tested, not universal: businesses were in scope "if: they undertook agricultural activity, and the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater" (ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22). The ABS carries the Agricultural Indicative data items in BLADE for 2010-11 to 2020-21.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier, de-identified, taking the same form as the current agricultural unit identifier it supersedes. It is present where the ABS recorded a change of unit identifier for the holding and carries no information of its own beyond the link.
limitation: It cannot tell you why the identifier changed. A sale, an amalgamation, a split of the holding and an ABS reclassification of the statistical unit all look identical here. It also gives only one step back, so a holding whose identifier changed twice cannot be traced through both changes from this column alone.
rationale: The ABS methodology for the agricultural collection defines the population these units come from, including the activity and size test that decides whether a farm business is on file at all, and the BLADE data inclusions page gives the Agricultural Indicative data items their reference period.
evidence_quote: Businesses on the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Business Register (ABSBR) were in scope for the 2021-22 Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodity Survey if: they undertook agricultural activity, and the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the data item wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the agricultural population is cut at an EVAO threshold or that the column only ever reaches one identifier back.

value_domain: De-identified R&D Tax Incentive registration application identifier
value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Apply for the R&D Tax Incentive
variable_description: The de-identified identifier of one application to register research and development activities under the R&D Tax Incentive. The company lodges it with the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, and registration is annual and bound to the income year, since "The deadline to apply for the R&DTI is 10 months after the end of your company's income year" (business.gov.au), so a company that registers every year has a different identifier each year. The ABS carries RDTI Program data in BLADE for 2013-14 to 2020-21.
description_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Apply for the R&D Tax Incentive
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier, de-identified, with one value per registration application. It carries no income year, activity or dollar amount of its own; those sit in the other columns of the RDTI table and in the company's tax return.
limitation: A registration is a claim, not an audited fact, and it is not the offset. The company self-assesses that its activities meet the eligibility rules, and the money is claimed separately through the company return, so the presence of an identifier says a company registered activities, not that it received or kept an R&D tax offset. BLADE's RDTI coverage stopping at 2020-21 also means later years show no registrations regardless of what companies did.
rationale: The business.gov.au page for applying to the programme sets out that registering activities is an application to the department, made through its portal within ten months of the end of the income year, which is what the identifier counts; the ABS data inclusions page gives the years BLADE holds.
evidence_quote: The deadline to apply for the R&DTI is 10 months after the end of your company's income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the data item's own six-word label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which agency receives the application, that registration is annual and self-assessed, or that it is not evidence an offset was allowed.

value_domain: De-identified R&D Tax Incentive project identifier
value_source: business.gov.au (AusIndustry), Apply for the R&D Tax Incentive
variable_description: Groups the R&D activities a firm registered for the tax incentive into the project they belong to. AusIndustry registers activities rather than projects, and warns that "Confirmation of registration does not mean your activities are eligible for the R&DTI. The R&DTI is a self-assessment program", so the identifier marks a claim the firm made, not research anyone has verified. Because the code is stable within the RDTI tables, a firm's activity records can be followed across registration years.
description_source: business.gov.au (AusIndustry), Apply for the R&D Tax Incentive
value_definition: A ten-character de-identified alphanumeric code. It identifies a project within the R&D Tax Incentive product only, and is neither an ABN nor an AusIndustry registration number.
limitation: It cannot tell you whether the R&D was eligible or whether an offset was ever paid, because registration is self-assessed and AusIndustry or the ATO may later find activities ineligible. A project also has no standing in the legislation, so how many projects a firm registers reflects how it chose to bundle its activities in the portal rather than any defined unit of research.
rationale: business.gov.au publishes the AusIndustry guidance for the registration that creates this record, and states both the activity-level basis of registration and its self-assessed character.
evidence_quote: Confirmation of registration does not mean your activities are eligible for the R&DTI. The R&DTI is a self-assessment program - you are responsible for determining the eligibility of your activities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Identifier - deidentified RDTI project id', with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the incentive registers activities rather than projects, or that registration is a claim rather than a finding.

value_domain: De-identified ABS related-entity identifier for agricultural units
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2021 - June 2025
variable_description: Ties together the agricultural units and ABNs that report to the ABS as one business, so a farm run through several ABNs is not counted as several farms. The ABS units model allows this because "The relationship between TAUs and their associated legal entities (ABNs) may be one-to-one, many-to-one, or one-to-many", and complex agricultural businesses are usually those with multiple farm locations. Rows sharing a related-entity id belong to one reporting group whatever their individual ABNs suggest.
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2021 - June 2025
value_definition: A ten-character de-identified alphanumeric key. It repeats across every unit in the same reporting group and has no meaning outside the agricultural tables.
limitation: A reporting relationship is not ownership, control or a family. Two ABNs can share this id because the ABS profiles them together for statistical purposes while they are separately owned, and a genuine farming partnership that reports through a single ABN gets no group at all, so the column understates how concentrated farm ownership is.
rationale: The ABS business methodology defines the profiled-population units model that produces many-to-one relationships between reporting units and ABNs, which is the relationship this column carries for agricultural units.
evidence_quote: The relationship between TAUs and their associated legal entities (ABNs) may be one-to-one, many-to-one, or one-to-many.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about a 'related entity' id and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what relationship the ABS is recording or why an agricultural business would have more than one ABN.

value_domain: De-identified Fair Work agreement number of the superseded agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Points from an enterprise agreement to the agreement it supersedes, which is what lets a workplace's bargaining history be chained together. The WAD collection framework records "Replaced agreements | List of agreements which the current agreement replaces", and the underlying agreement number is "As allocated by Fair Work Australia" before de-identification. A blank means the agreement replaces nothing, so it is a first agreement at that workplace or a greenfields agreement made before anyone was employed.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: A ten-character de-identified alphanumeric code matching s_agreementnumber on the row for the earlier agreement. It is not an ABN and does not identify the employer.
limitation: The chain runs between agreements, not between employers, so it breaks whenever coverage is redrawn: a business that splits one agreement into two, or that moves employees onto a different agreement, leaves gaps that look like new bargaining. A blank also cannot prove the workplace never had an agreement, only that no replaced agreement was recorded.
rationale: The DEWR collection framework is the custodian's own field list for the WAD and names both the replaced-agreement field and the source of the agreement number.
evidence_quote: Replaced agreements | List of agreements which the current agreement replaces
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about a blank field and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the column is a link to another row in the same table.

value_domain: Count of replacement interests issued under a scrip-for-scrip roll-over
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: How many shares or units the business issued in exchange for the interests it acquired under a scrip-for-scrip roll-over. The ATO instruction for this label is to "Show at H the number of shares, units or other interests issued in exchange for the shares or units or other interests acquired in the original entity", and only a company or trust that was an acquiring entity completes it. The OF prefix marks an old-form label with no new-form counterpart, so the item stops at the schedule change rather than continuing under a new wording.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A count of securities, up to eleven digits. It is a number of interests rather than a dollar amount, so it cannot be added to or compared with the dollar columns beside it.
limitation: A count of paper says nothing about what the paper was worth, so it is not a measure of deal size: one firm's million ten-cent units and another's thousand hundred-dollar shares look very different here and may be the same acquisition. Nearly every business reports nothing, because the label applies only in the year a firm acquired another entity under a scrip-for-scrip arrangement.
rationale: The DIL label matches the acquiring-entity part of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO guide gives the label-by-label instruction for completing it.
evidence_quote: Show at H the number of shares, units or other interests issued in exchange for the shares or units or other interests acquired in the original entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw 'OF:' schedule label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said this is a scrip-for-scrip item completed only by an acquiring company or trust.

value_domain: Within-ABN business unit label in the Dealroom product
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Splits one ABN into the separate ventures Dealroom tracks under it, so a firm running several startups on a single ABN is not collapsed into one business. The label is time invariant within a business number, but it is only a sequence marker: BU1 under one business number and BU1 under another are unrelated firms. A row is identified by the business number, this unit label and the funding round together, not by the unit label alone.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric label. It is unique only in combination with the business number and the round number, and carries no meaning outside the Dealroom tables.
limitation: It cannot be joined to anything else in BLADE. The ABS units model has no sub-ABN unit of this kind, so a Dealroom business unit does not correspond to a type of activity unit, a location or a tax reporting entity, and financial data drawn from the tax tables for the ABN cannot be apportioned across the units under it.
rationale: No published Dealroom or ABS dictionary defines this column. The reading rests on the custodian's own note that the identifier is meaningful only within a business number, read against the ABS description of what BLADE links and at what unit.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the custodian's long note as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader was left thinking the label was an identifier they could group on across the dataset.

value_domain: Binary indicator, agreement operates in South Australia
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Flags whether the enterprise agreement's coverage extends to South Australia, one of a set of one-per-jurisdiction flags. The WAD collection framework records the field as "State | State/Territories coverage", so it describes where the agreement operates rather than where the employer is registered. A national agreement carries a one here and in every other jurisdiction flag on the row.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Numeric, 1 for yes and 0 for no. There is no separate missing code.
limitation: It cannot be used to count employees in South Australia. The row's employee count is for the whole agreement and is not broken down by jurisdiction, so a national agreement covering 20,000 people looks the same here as a single Adelaide site covering twelve.
rationale: The DEWR collection framework lists state and territory coverage among the fields recorded for each agreement, which is what the per-jurisdiction flags implement.
evidence_quote: State | State/Territories coverage
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Indicates whether an agreement operates in SA' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that coverage is an agreement property rather than an employee location.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The finest ABS geography released for an agricultural business, placing the unit inside a small area rather than at an address. The ABS builds SA1s to hold people, not land: they "generally have a population of 200 to 800 people", so in farming country a single SA1 can run for hundreds of kilometres. The sa2_code_2021 and sa2_name_2021 columns on the same row are this area rolled up one level.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
value_definition: An eleven-digit fully hierarchical numeric code on ASGS Edition 3, which took effect in July 2021. The last two digits identify the SA1 within its SA2, and SA1s are not named.
limitation: It locates the unit's recorded holding, not its paddocks. A farm whose land spans several SA1s still gets one code, and a business run from a town office is coded to the town, so the column cannot be used to map where production physically happens.
rationale: The ABS ASGS Edition 3 page defines the SA1, its population range and its code structure, which is the classification the 2021 suffix names.
evidence_quote: SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Statistical Area 1 Code' with a valid-response of 'Numeric' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave neither the edition, the code length nor the fact that SA1s are sized by population.

value_domain: ABS Statistical Area Level 2 maincode
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The SA2 a farm is assigned to on the FLAD control table, given as the full maincode rather than the old five-digit short code. The ABS says "An SA2 is identifiable by a 9-digit fully hierarchical code comprising the 1-digit State or Territory identifier, and Statistical Areas Level 2-4 identifiers", so state, SA4 and SA3 can all be cut from this one field. Because it sits on the control table it is the frame's view of where the farm is, and it applies to every commodity record for that farm in the year.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
value_definition: A nine-digit fully hierarchical numeric code. SA2s hold between about 3,000 and 25,000 people and are generally the smallest areas the ABS uses to release its non-Census statistics.
limitation: The column does not name its ASGS edition. FLAD is built from ABS agricultural collections that run across more than one ASGS edition, and SA2 boundaries were redrawn at each edition, so a farm can appear to move between SA2s when only the boundaries changed. Do not treat a change in this code across years as relocation without checking the edition.
rationale: The ABS ASGS page defines the SA2 maincode structure that 'Maincode of SA2' refers to, and ABARES documents the years FLAD covers, which is what makes the edition ambiguous.
evidence_quote: An SA2 is identifiable by a 9-digit fully hierarchical code comprising the 1-digit State or Territory identifier, and Statistical Areas Level 2-4 identifiers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Maincode of SA2' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so a reader could not tell the maincode from the retired five-digit short code or know that the edition is unstated.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The community-sized area an agricultural business is located in, one level up from sa1_code_2021 on the same row. The ABS designs SA2s to "represent a community that interacts together socially and economically" and gives them "a population between 3,000 and 25,000 with an average of about 10,000 people", which makes this the level at which most ABS regional statistics can be joined to the farm. Unlike the SA1 code it has a matching name, carried in sa2_name_2021.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
value_definition: A nine-digit fully hierarchical numeric code on ASGS Edition 3, in force from July 2021 to June 2026. The leading digit is the state or territory.
limitation: An SA2 is built for population, so it is a poor unit for agriculture: one SA2 in the rangelands can contain a handful of very large holdings while an SA2 on the urban fringe contains hundreds of small ones. Counts of farms per SA2 therefore say more about how the geography was drawn than about farm structure.
rationale: The ABS ASGS Edition 3 page defines the SA2, its purpose, its population range and its code structure, which the 2021 suffix on the column names directly.
evidence_quote: SA2s generally have a population between 3,000 and 25,000 with an average of about 10,000 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Statistical Area 2 Code' with 'Numeric' as its valid response and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no edition, no code length and no sense of what an SA2 is meant to represent.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: Where one business location sits, on a table that carries a row per location rather than a row per business. A firm operating from six premises has six rows and can have six different SA2s, so this column is the one that lets a multi-site business be spread across a map instead of being pinned to a single registered address. The code is on ASGS Edition 3, which the ABS says gives "a 9-digit fully hierarchical code" carrying state, SA4, SA3 and SA2 together.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
value_definition: A nine-digit fully hierarchical numeric code on ASGS Edition 3. The custodian's own note points to ASGS 2021, so it is Edition 3 rather than the 2016 or 2011 standards.
limitation: A location is not a measure of activity. The table does not weight sites by employment or turnover, so counting locations in an SA2 counts premises, and a large distribution centre and an unstaffed storage yard both count once. Some locations are also the address a business gave rather than a place where work happens.
rationale: The custodian's valid-response text names ASGS 2021, and the ABS page for that edition defines the nine-digit SA2 code the column holds.
evidence_quote: An SA2 is identifiable by a 9-digit fully hierarchical code comprising the 1-digit State or Territory identifier, and Statistical Areas Level 2-4 identifiers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Statistical Area 2 code' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the row is a location rather than a business, which is the whole point of the table.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 name
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The readable name of the area in sa2_code_2021, supplied so a farm's region can be labelled without a lookup table. ABS naming follows the settlement pattern: in town an SA2 "will retain the name of the suburb", and in the country SA2s "are named for the gazetted localities they contain, or the towns, cities, or regions with which they are associated, for example: Benalla Surrounds". Where a name occurs in more than one jurisdiction the ABS appends the state, as in "O'Connor (ACT)".
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
value_definition: A character string, the ASGS Edition 3 SA2 name for the code on the same row. It is a label, not a code, and has no fixed length.
limitation: Do not join on it. Names are reused between editions while the boundaries beneath them change, some names repeat across states unless the abbreviation is attached, and a name can be respelt between releases, so a merge on the name silently drops or duplicates farms that a merge on sa2_code_2021 would keep.
rationale: The ABS ASGS Edition 3 page sets out the SA2 naming rules, including the rural convention and the state suffix used to break ties.
evidence_quote: Where an SA2 name appears in two or more State and Territories, the State or Territory abbreviation is attached to the SA2 name, for example: O'Connor (ACT)
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Full name of SA2' with a valid response of 'Char' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that names are not stable keys.

value_domain: Binary flag, monetary allowances absorbed into base rates
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that folds monetary allowances into the ordinary rate of pay. That lifts the headline hourly rate without lifting the firm's total labour cost. The WAD framework defines the item as "The agreement provides that monetary allowances are to absorbed into the normal rates of pay" and records that it was "First coded in 2014 (though was previously coded up until the end of 2010)". It is one of a small group of loaded-rate items alongside absorbed overtime, absorbed public holidays and absorbed shift loadings.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the provision is present and left blank otherwise. There is no explicit no value, so blank carries both 'not present' and 'not assessed'.
limitation: There is a hole in the middle of the series. The item was not coded for agreements made between 2011 and the end of 2013, so a blank in those years is a gap in collection rather than evidence that allowances stayed separate, and any trend drawn straight through that window is wrong.
rationale: The DEWR framework carries this exact field with the same wording as the DIL, and its coding-window note explains the unusual valid-response text on the variable.
evidence_quote: The agreement provides that monetary allowances are to absorbed into the normal rates of pay. First coded in 2014 (though was previously coded up until the end of 2010).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and the coding window as raw text, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so the reader was not told the window is a break in the series.

value_domain: Binary flag, entitlements rolled into a loaded hourly rate
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that pays one loaded hourly rate in place of separate shift loadings, allowances and overtime penalties. A rate set that way is not comparable with an unloaded one. It is the pre-2014 form of the concept the WAD later split apart: from 2014 the framework carries a header item, "The agreement rolls some entitlements or additional payments into a loaded hourly or annual salary", with separate flags underneath for absorbed overtime, public holidays, shift loadings and allowances.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the provision is present, blank otherwise, and only for agreements made before 1 January 2014.
limitation: It stops rather than continuing. An agreement made from 2014 that rolls entitlements into a loaded rate is recorded in the newer component flags instead, so a count of loaded-rate agreements built from this column alone falls to zero after 2013 and looks like the practice ended when it did not.
rationale: The 2021 DEWR framework carries the loaded wage rates group first coded in 2014, which explains why this earlier single flag is limited to agreements made before that date; the mapping between the old and new items is inferred from the two wordings.
evidence_quote: This is a header field. The agreement rolls some entitlements or additional payments into a loaded hourly or annual salary. First coded in 2014.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence and the cut-off date with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, and never said what replaced the field.

value_domain: Small business active asset reduction claimed (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The amount a small business took off its capital gain under the 50% active asset reduction. The ATO describes the concession plainly: "The small business 50% active asset reduction: this concession provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset." The old form reported the reduction separately for each calculation method and this column is the indexation-method cell, while the new form reports one figure without splitting by method.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount, the reduction claimed rather than the gain itself. It is applied after current year and carried-forward capital losses and after any CGT discount.

evidence_quote: The small business 50% active asset reduction: this concession provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF and NF label text and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the concession does or that the two labels measure different things.

value_domain: Total small business CGT concessions applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The total the business took off its capital gains through the small business concessions. It is the closest single measure of what the concessions were worth to that firm in the year. The ATO limits the underlying amounts to gains on active assets that qualify for one or more of the "small business 50% active asset reduction", the "small business retirement exemption" or the "small business rollover". On the old form this cell also carried the CGT discount and was reported for the indexation method only; on the new form it is a concessions-only total across methods.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount that aggregates the component concession columns beside it. It measures reductions applied, not tax saved, and no rate has been applied to it.
limitation: The old and new labels are different totals, because the old one bundles the CGT discount in with the concessions and the new one does not, so adding a pre-change year to a post-change year overstates the level and invents a fall at the join. The 15-year exemption is also reported separately, so a firm that disregarded its entire gain under that exemption can show nothing here.
rationale: The DIL label names the concessions total on the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the guide lists which concessions the active-asset amounts may relate to and how the old schedule split totals by calculation method.

supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the OF and NF label strings and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not reveal that the old label includes the CGT discount and the new one does not.

value_domain: Small business roll-over amount deferred (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The capital gain a small business pushed into a later year by choosing the roll-over rather than paying tax now. The ATO defines it as follows: "The small business rollover: this enables you to defer a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset and satisfy other conditions." The old form reported the roll-over separately by calculation method and this column is the indexation-method cell; the new form carries a single amount.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax

rationale: The DIL label names the small business roll-over line of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the guide defines the concession and the replacement-asset condition behind it.
evidence_quote: The small business rollover: this enables you to defer a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset and satisfy other conditions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could easily have counted a deferral as a permanent reduction.

value_domain: Small business retirement exemption amount disregarded (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax

rationale: The DIL label names the retirement exemption line of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the guide defines the concession and states the lifetime limit.
evidence_quote: The small business retirement exemption: this allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the conditions are satisfied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the OF and NF label strings with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not mention the lifetime cap that governs how large the amount can be.

value_domain: Semantic cosine similarity of Australian and EPO claim text (0 to 1)
value_source: IP Australia Economic Research Paper 14, Kollmann, Palangkaraya, Sarwar, Webster, Anglim and Falk, Raising the Bar reforms: Measuring the impact on relative patent scope
variable_description: How close the Australian patent's full claim set is in meaning to its EPO twin's, scored by cosine similarity. Here the full claim set is every claim in the patent, mixing the broad independent claims with the dependent claims that narrow them. The measure is the cosine of the angle between spaCy language vectors built from the two claim texts, and here it is run over every claim rather than the first one, so drafting habits in the dependent claims move the score. It is an attribute of one patent application, so a firm's breadth has to be built by averaging over the applications it owns, and only those with a granted EPO equivalent carry a value.
description_source: IP Australia Economic Research Paper 14, Kollmann, Palangkaraya, Sarwar, Webster, Anglim and Falk, Raising the Bar reforms: Measuring the impact on relative patent scope
value_definition: A number between 0 and 1 from the cosine of the angle between spaCy language vectors of the two claim texts. Values near 1 mean the two texts point the same way in semantic space; values near 0 mean they are unrelated.
limitation: Similarity is symmetric, so the score cannot say which of the two patents is broader: two claims can be near-identical in wording while one carries a limitation the other does not. Semantic vectors also flatten the technical vocabulary that carries scope, so a chemistry claim and its equivalent can score high on shared field language alone. Only Australian patents that have a granted EPO equivalent in the triplet are scored, so a firm that files only in Australia is absent rather than average.
rationale: IP Australia commissioned the study that produced these columns, and the paper sets out the patent triplet design, the spaCy semantic cosine similarity measure and the separate treatment of the first claim and the full claim set.
evidence_quote: Semantic similarity using the cosine similarity score of Spacy language vector representation of the claim texts of the two patents
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried one description shared by every scope column, 'Relating to given EP/US and First/All claims', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said which comparator office or which claim set this particular column uses.

value_domain: Jaccard similarity of Australian and EPO claim text, raw (0 to 1)
value_source: IP Australia Economic Research Paper 14, Kollmann, Palangkaraya, Sarwar, Webster, Anglim and Falk, Raising the Bar reforms: Measuring the impact on relative patent scope
variable_description: How much wording the Australian patent's full claim set shares with its EPO twin's, as a Jaccard index on raw text. Here the full claim set is every claim in the patent, mixing the broad independent claims with the dependent claims that narrow them. It divides the words the two texts share by the total distinct words across both, computed on untreated text, so a long Australian claim set can score low against a short overseas one purely on length. It is an attribute of one patent application, so a firm's breadth has to be built by averaging over the applications it owns, and only those with a granted EPO equivalent carry a value.
description_source: IP Australia Economic Research Paper 14, Kollmann, Palangkaraya, Sarwar, Webster, Anglim and Falk, Raising the Bar reforms: Measuring the impact on relative patent scope
value_definition: A number between 0 and 1: the size of the intersection of the two word sets divided by the size of their union, taken over raw claim text with no cleaning applied.
limitation: Raw text keeps claim numbering, reference signs, punctuation and standard drafting boilerplate, so two claims can agree because both were written to convention rather than because they claim the same invention. Read it against scope_jacalp_* and scope_jacmalp_*, which strip and lemmatise the same text and will not agree with it. Only Australian patents that have a granted EPO equivalent in the triplet are scored, so a firm that files only in Australia is absent rather than average.
rationale: IP Australia commissioned the study that produced these columns, and the paper sets out the patent triplet design, the Jaccard similarity on raw claim text measure and the separate treatment of the first claim and the full claim set.
evidence_quote: The Jaccard similarity coefficient or Jaccard index is a measure of similarity in which roughly can be defined as the size of the intersection of sets of information divided by the size of the union of the same sample sets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried one description shared by every scope column, 'Relating to given EP/US and First/All claims', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said which comparator office or which claim set this particular column uses.

description_source: IP Australia Economic Research Paper 14, Kollmann, Palangkaraya, Sarwar, Webster, Anglim and Falk, Raising the Bar reforms: Measuring the impact on relative patent scope

Only Australian patents that have a granted EPO equivalent in the triplet are scored, so a firm that files only in Australia is absent rather than average.

variable_description: How many more words the Australian patent's full claim set uses than its EPO twin's, the oldest proxy for relative scope. Here the full claim set is every claim in the patent, mixing the broad independent claims with the dependent claims that narrow them. Over a whole claim set the proxy weakens: the report finds that for multiple claims "the method appears to require additional help from other methods such as supervised machine learning models". It is an attribute of one patent application, so a firm's breadth has to be built by averaging over the applications it owns, and only those with a granted EPO equivalent carry a value.

value_definition: A signed integer: the number of words in the Australian claim text less the number in the overseas claim text, counted on raw text. Positive means the Australian side is wordier.
limitation: Word count confounds scope with drafting style and with translation. A claim translated into English from another language, or drafted to a different office's formatting conventions, gains or loses words without changing what is claimed, so the difference should not be read as a measured narrowing on any single patent. Only Australian patents that have a granted EPO equivalent in the triplet are scored, so a firm that files only in Australia is absent rather than average.

value_domain: Weeks of paid secondary caregiver leave in the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: How many weeks of paid leave the agreement gives the parent who is not the primary carer, which is the main workplace-level measure of paid partner leave. The WAD framework describes the item as covering "paid paternity leave or paid leave for the 'Secondary Care Giver' of child/children" and records that "The number of weeks of paid leave is recorded". It pairs with the primary caregiver item, which records weeks of paid maternity or primary carer leave on the same agreement.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Weeks, as a number. Two sentinel codes sit in the same field: 111111111 for a varying or unknown quantity and 222222222 for no stated limit.
limitation: The sentinels are not weeks and will wreck any average left unfiltered, since a single 111111111 shifts a mean of a few weeks by millions. The figure is also an entitlement in an agreement, not leave anyone took, and it says nothing about the Commonwealth paid parental leave a parent may draw on top of it.
rationale: The DEWR framework lists the secondary caregiver item with the same wording as the DIL and confirms that the quantity recorded is weeks of paid leave.
evidence_quote: The agreement includes paid paternity leave or paid leave for the 'Secondary Care Giver' of child/children.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the custodian's long definition and the two sentinel codes as raw valid-response text, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so the trap in the sentinels was never spelled out.

value_domain: Public or private sector of the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement covers a public sector or a private sector workplace. It is the first split any bargaining analysis makes, because wage outcomes and bargaining rules differ sharply between the two. The WAD framework records the field simply as "Sector | Public or private". It is a property of the agreement rather than of the employing entity, so a government business enterprise is classified by how the agreement was made.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: A character value, either "public" or "private". There is no third category and no explicit missing code.
limitation: A two-way split hides the level of government. State, local and Commonwealth agreements all read as public here, so the column cannot separate a council from a Commonwealth agency, and outsourced services delivered by a private contractor to government sit on the private side.
rationale: The DEWR collection framework lists sector among the demographic fields held for every agreement and gives its two values.
evidence_quote: Sector | Public or private
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never noted that the split is by agreement rather than by employer.

It is a machine classification of what a firm says it does, not an ANZSIC code and not a classification of what it sells: the Department of Industry, Science and Resources built the Emerging Industries database by combining "Glass.AI's web-scale research algorithms with econometric methods and government microdata". value_domain: Year of the business's seed funding round
value_source: Dealroom.co, Australia deep dive
variable_description: The year Dealroom records the business as having raised seed capital, held constant on every row for that ABN. Dealroom's own funnel places seed after pre-seed and before Series A, so the year marks an early external equity raise rather than when the business was founded or first traded. Because it does not vary within a business, it is a cohort marker rather than an event date.
description_source: Dealroom.co, Australia deep dive
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year, for example 1990. It is a single value per ABN and is not tied to the round on the row.
limitation: It is not the firm's birth. A business that bootstrapped for a decade before raising seed capital carries a late year, one that raised a pre-seed round first carries a year that misses that round, and a firm that never raised seed money has no year at all rather than a zero. Dealroom's coverage is assembled from public announcements, so silence is not evidence that no round happened.
rationale: Dealroom publishes the underlying company and funding database and its Australia guide reports seed-stage rounds as a distinct funding stage, which is the reading behind this column; no Dealroom data dictionary for the BLADE extract is published.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence about a time-invariant seed year and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a seed year from a founding year.

value_domain: Assigned exporter segment on the MAX panel
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)

The five are Born Global, Novice Exporter, Expanding Exporter, Stable Exporter and Global Leader. The segments are cut on export history rather than on size or industry, so they separate a firm that exported from the outset from one that reached the same export value after twenty domestic years. A blank means the firm was not assigned to any segment, which is not the same as not exporting.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)

rationale: The ABS documents BLADE and the export declarations it links, which is what the panel is built from, but no public document defines the five segment labels; the description rests on the custodian's own value list.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the custodian's list of segment names and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the assignment rules are unpublished or that a blank is an unassigned firm.

value_domain: Binary flag, agreement commits to severance pay on redundancy
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that promises severance pay if the employer makes people redundant, which is the crudest of the three redundancy flags on the row. It was coded only for agreements made between 2007 and 2011, and the current WAD framework has replaced this yes-or-no reading with graded measures such as "Severance entitlement at four years' service. The number of weeks' pay employees are entitled to after four years' service." Read it with severancepaynotpaid and severancepayatmanagementdiscreti, which cover the other two positions an agreement can take.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the commitment is present, blank otherwise, and only within the 2007 to 2011 coding window.
limitation: The flag is silent on how much. A firm promising the statutory minimum and a firm promising a year's pay both read Y, and after 2011 the field stops, so a series built on it shows severance provisions disappearing when only the coding practice changed.
rationale: The DEWR framework is the custodian's field list for the WAD; this flag is absent from the 2021 collection and the redundancy items that replaced it record weeks of pay rather than a yes or no.
evidence_quote: Severance entitlement at four years' service. The number of weeks' pay employees are entitled to after four years' service. First coded in 2011.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and the coding window as raw text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say what happened to the field after 2011.

value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework

It is the middle position between severancepaid and severancepaynotpaid, and the narrowest of the three in time, coded only for agreements made between 2007 and 2009, and it disappears from the WAD entirely thereafter: the 2021 framework's redundancy items record entitlements in weeks and have no discretion category at all. A blank in 2010 or later therefore says nothing about whether discretion clauses survived.

rationale: The DEWR framework is the custodian's field list for the WAD; the redundancy group it now carries measures weeks of entitlement and includes no discretionary category, which is consistent with the short coding window on this flag.

value_domain: Binary flag, agreement does not provide severance pay
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that expressly does not pay severance on redundancy. It is the only one of the three redundancy flags that records a negative provision rather than a positive one. It was coded for agreements made between 2007 and 2010, a window opening before the National Employment Standards took effect in 2010 and closing shortly after, so it spans a change in the statutory floor it sits above. Its value is that it distinguishes a genuine exclusion from a silent agreement, which severancepaid cannot do.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the exclusion is present, blank otherwise, and only within the 2007 to 2010 coding window.

The National Employment Standards set a redundancy entitlement that an agreement cannot undercut, so silence or exclusion in the agreement leaves the statutory entitlement standing, and this flag records the drafting rather than the employee's position.

value_domain: Binary flag, employees may acquire shares in the business
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that lets employees take shares in the business, usually as part of a remuneration package or a productivity bonus. The WAD framework files it under employee share ownership, recording "Incidence (profit sharing or share acquisition)", so it is the share-based half of a pair with the profit sharing flag. Because the WAD covers federal collective agreements, this measures share access bargained collectively, which is a different thing from the executive schemes that dominate published share scheme statistics.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the provision is present and blank otherwise, with no explicit no value.
limitation: Presence is not participation. The flag records that the agreement offers the option, not how many employees took shares, what they were worth, or whether the scheme ever opened, so it cannot be used to measure employee ownership in a firm.
rationale: The DEWR collection framework lists employee share ownership among the performance and productivity fields and names share acquisition as one of the two forms recorded.
evidence_quote: Employee share ownership | Incidence (profit sharing or share acquisition)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not place the flag beside the profit sharing item or warn that it measures an offer rather than take-up.

value_domain: Binary flag, sick leave accumulation capped by the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that caps how much sick leave an employee may carry from one year to the next. The cap is a direct constraint on the firm's accrued leave liability. The WAD framework defines the item as "The amount of sick leave that an employee may accumulate from year to year is limited by the agreement." It is the counterpart of sickleaveaccumulationbankunlimit, and the two are not exhaustive because most agreements say nothing either way.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the cap is present and blank otherwise. The size of the cap is not recorded here.
limitation: It does not say how large the cap is, so a ten-day ceiling and a two-hundred-day ceiling are the same value, and the column cannot be turned into a liability estimate. A blank is also ambiguous between an agreement with no cap and an agreement that simply does not address accumulation.
rationale: The DEWR collection framework carries this field under personal and sick leave with the same wording the DIL uses.
evidence_quote: Accumulation bank - limited. The amount of sick leave that an employee may accumulate from year to year is limited by the agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the size of the cap is missing or how a blank should be read.

value_domain: Binary flag, no cap on sick leave accumulation
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Marks an agreement that puts no ceiling on how much sick leave an employee can bank over a career, which for the employer is an open-ended accrual. It was coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2011 and does not appear in the current WAD collection, whose nearest surviving item is about days available in a year rather than the accumulated balance: "The agreement is open-ended on number of days of sick leave available to the employee". Its capped counterpart, sickleaveaccumulationbanklimited, is still collected.
description_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database Dataset, 2021 data collection framework
value_definition: Coded Y where the agreement is silent on any ceiling or states there is none, blank otherwise, and only for agreements made before 2011.
limitation: The pair is asymmetric after 2010. The capped flag continues while this one stops, so a ratio of unlimited to limited accumulation computed across years falls to zero for reasons of collection, not bargaining. Unlimited accumulation also does not mean unlimited payment, since an accrued balance is usually not paid out on resignation.
rationale: The DEWR framework is the custodian's field list for the WAD; it retains the limited accumulation item but not this one, and its unlimited sick leave field refers to days available rather than to the accumulated bank.
evidence_quote: The agreement is open-ended on number of days of sick leave available to the employee, for example, there is no limit on the number of days of leave providing a certificate is produced.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence with the pre-2011 cut-off appended and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the flag's counterpart outlived it.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y = present)
value_source: Fair Work Ombudsman, Paid sick and carer's leave
variable_description: Marks an enterprise agreement that pays out accumulated sick leave, in full or in part, when an employee resigns, retires or is otherwise terminated. This is a term above the minimum standard: the Fair Work Ombudsman says paid sick leave accumulates and "The balance at the end of each year carries over to the next year", and that "A registered agreement, award or contract can set out different entitlements to paid sick and carer's leave, but they can't be less than the minimum in the National Employment Standards". For the employer it converts an accrual that would ordinarily lapse into a payable liability on exit.
description_source: Fair Work Ombudsman, Paid sick and carer's leave
value_definition: A single-character flag on the Workplace Agreements Database agreement record, coded Y where the provision is present and left blank otherwise, so there is no explicit No code.
limitation: It does not say how much is paid, whether the payout is the full value or a capped number of days, or how many employees ever claim it, so it cannot be costed. The unit is the agreement rather than the business, so a firm with several agreements has several rows and one Y does not extend to staff covered by its other agreements.
rationale: The Fair Work Ombudsman page sets out the National Employment Standards baseline for paid sick and carer's leave that this agreement clause sits above, which is what makes the flag informative rather than descriptive.
evidence_quote: A registered agreement, award or contract can set out different entitlements to paid sick and carer's leave, but they can't be less than the minimum in the National Employment Standards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the WAD clause wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the payout is an above-standard term or that the row is an agreement rather than a firm.

value_domain: Declared silver assay concentration, grams per tonne

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y = present)
value_source: Fair Work Ombudsman, Types of parental leave
variable_description: Marks an enterprise agreement that extends concurrent unpaid parental leave beyond the eight weeks the National Employment Standards allowed at the time. The National Employment Standards have since changed and the Fair Work Ombudsman now states the position without a concurrent-leave cap: parents can each take up to "12 months of parental leave" and "They don't have to take the leave at the same time as each other". The clause is a scheduling concession rather than a payment one, since the leave being extended is unpaid.
description_source: Fair Work Ombudsman, Types of parental leave
value_definition: A single-character flag on the Workplace Agreements Database agreement record, coded Y where the provision is present, and coded only for agreements made on or after 1 January 2006.
limitation: The eight-week benchmark the item measures against is no longer the National Employment Standards position, so the flag does not mean the same thing across the series and a fall in the Yes rate in later years is a change in the baseline rather than in employer generosity. It also gives no duration: an agreement offering one extra week and one offering six months both code Y.
rationale: The Fair Work Ombudsman page states the current National Employment Standards position on both parents taking parental leave, which is the baseline the WAD clause was coded against and which changed part way through the series.
evidence_quote: They don't have to take the leave at the same time as each other.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the WAD clause wording as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the eight-week benchmark had since been repealed or that the flag has no duration behind it.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement bargaining structure flag (Y = present)
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Single interest employer authorisations
variable_description: Marks an agreement bargained by two or more employers acting as one bargaining unit, so the row does not describe a single business. The Fair Work Commission explains that where it makes a single interest employer authorisation, "2 or more employers can bargain for a single interest employer agreement together if they are part of a franchise or share a 'common interest'". For BLADE this is the flag that warns against attributing the agreement's employee counts and conditions to one ABN.
description_source: Fair Work Commission, Single interest employer authorisations
value_definition: A single-character flag on the Workplace Agreements Database agreement record, coded Y where the agreement was bargained on a single interest basis and left blank otherwise.
limitation: It does not name the employers covered or say how many there were, so an agreement's employee count cannot be split between the businesses on it. The legal test has also widened over the life of the series, from franchisees and ministerially declared employers to employers with clearly identifiable common interests, so the population behind a Yes is broader in later years than in early ones.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page defines the single interest employer authorisation that makes this bargaining structure possible and names the two grounds, franchise and common interest, on which it rests.
evidence_quote: If we make a single interest employer authorisation, 2 or more employers can bargain for a single interest employer agreement together if they are part of a franchise or share a 'common interest'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the WAD wording 'bargained by multiple enterprises operating as a single interest' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned a BLADE user that the row spans several businesses.

value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database

On such a row the other WAD condition flags understate what the employees actually receive, because the missing terms live in an instrument that is not linked to this record. The item belongs to the pre-Fair Work Act era of federal bargaining, so it is a historical marker rather than a current characteristic.

It also does not say which issue the agreement dealt with, so a wage-only agreement and a dispute-resolution-only agreement look identical.

value_domain: Standard International Trade Classification (SITC) Rev. 4, 5-digit basic heading (ABS rendering)

variable_description: The economic commodity grouping for the exported goods, which ABS derives from the AHECC code on the same row. Revision 4 of the Standard International Trade Classification arranges goods by stage of processing, industrial origin and material, which is why export series are published and compared internationally on this basis rather than on the commodity code. The derivation is mechanical: ABS states that "it is possible to link data (with the exception of refined petroleum products) at the five-digit SITC level to the six-digit level of the HS classification". value_definition: A five-digit SITC Rev. 4 basic heading, which rolls up to the three-digit group, the two-digit division and the one-digit section. Australian trade statistics have been compiled on a Rev. 4 basis since July 2005. The full basic-heading list is published in SITC Rev. 4 and is not listed here.
limitation: The basic heading does not carry back across that changeover. Moving from Rev. 3 to Rev. 4 deleted 247 basic headings and added 84 new ones, so strict period-to-period comparability was lost for a number of series and a five-digit run spanning July 2005 is not continuous; the two- and three-digit levels survive the break better. The classification is also silent on who bought the goods and why, so it cannot be read as a split between inputs and final demand.
rationale: The Data Item List points at 'Appendix 6.1/6.2 column SITC R4'. That column holds the ABS 5-digit rendering of UN SITC Rev. 4: 2973 distinct values across exports and imports, of which 2,652 are UN 5-digit basic headings verbatim and 316 are UN 4-digit basic headings padded with a trailing zero; 5 further codes (28099, 51099, 95100, 98888, 99999) are ABS additions. Labels below are the UN Comtrade SITC Rev. 4 reference table entries. SITC Rev. 4 has 10 sections, 67 divisions, 262 groups and 1,023 subgroups. Sample of 26.
evidence_quote: SITC R4: The 5 digit SITC code to which the code corresponds
