value_domain: Estimated capital proceeds from an earnout arrangement (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
variable_description: The seller's own estimate of the total capital proceeds it expects from an earnout arrangement, over the whole arrangement rather than the current year. The ATO instruction is "Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement", and a seller completes that label only "for arrangements which don't involve look-through earnout rights". For a business that has sold assets, it is a forward-looking figure for a contingent payment stream tied to how the sold business performs after settlement.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 7 label D of the capital gains tax schedule, covering the entire arrangement, and reported beside label B, the number of years the arrangement runs, and label C, the year of the arrangement the entity is in.
limitation: It is an expectation, not a receipt: the earnout pays only if performance thresholds are met, so the estimate can sit well above anything the seller is ever paid, and nothing on the schedule reconciles the two. Coverage is partial by design, because look-through earnout rights are excluded from this label, which leaves a missing value ambiguous between having no earnout and having a look-through one.
rationale: The CGT schedule instructions name label D as the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement and set out exactly which sellers complete it, which is the coverage fact this column needs.
evidence_quote: Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule's own question as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is an estimate over the whole arrangement or that look-through earnouts are excluded from the label.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement provision flag (Y = present)
value_source: Fair Work Ombudsman, Stand downs
variable_description: Marks an agreement that writes down its own procedure for standing employees down when the business has no useful work for them. The Fair Work Ombudsman describes the underlying power as one where "Employers may be able to stand employees down from work due to circumstances that are outside the employer's control", citing Fair Work Act 2009 sections 522 to 527, and notes that "Employees who are stood down without pay under the Fair Work Act can't use paid sick and carer's leave or compassionate leave during the stand down". For a firm it marks how a shutdown, breakdown or industrial action translates into wage cost.
description_source: Fair Work Ombudsman, Stand downs
value_definition: A single-character flag on the Workplace Agreements Database agreement record, coded Y where the clause is present, and coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2010.
limitation: The item was retired at the start of 2010, so a blank after that date means the question stopped being asked rather than that agreements dropped the clause; the WAD item that replaced it records only stand down terms that differ from the Fair Work Act. The flag also does not say whether stood-down employees are paid, which is the term that decides what a shutdown costs.
rationale: The Fair Work Ombudsman page defines the statutory stand down power, the circumstances that trigger it and its interaction with paid leave, which is the entitlement an agreement clause of this kind varies or restates.
evidence_quote: Employees who are stood down without pay under the Fair Work Act can't use paid sick and carer's leave or compassionate leave during the stand down.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the WAD clause wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the item was retired in 2010 or that it is silent on whether stood-down employees are paid.

value_domain: Australian state or territory of the IP applicant
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021 (data.gov.au)
variable_description: The Australian state of the party that filed the intellectual property right, taken as the state that appears most often across that party's filings. IP Australia defines it as the "Australian state code of the applicant" and adds that "modal values are taken if the applicant has multiple associated state codes", so it is a summary of an applicant's filing addresses rather than a business location on any one application. It is one value per IPLoRD party identifier, which is usually an ABN.
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021 (data.gov.au)
value_definition: A two- or three-letter state or territory abbreviation from NSW, VIC, QLD, SA, WA, TAS, NT and ACT, one per lord_party_id, drawn from the IPGOD party address rather than from the ABS Business Register.
limitation: It is the modal address of the filing party, not the location of the research, the inventors or the firm's employment, so a Sydney head office collects the patents of a Perth laboratory. There is also no code for an overseas applicant, whose location sits in country_code instead, so filtering on state quietly drops foreign filers rather than grouping them.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the state_code field and states the modal rule that resolves conflicting addresses, which is the fact that determines how the column can be used.
evidence_quote: As for country_code, modal values are taken if the applicant has multiple associated state codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated IP Australia's field label as the description with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the code is a modal address of the filing party or that overseas applicants have no value here.

value_domain: Australian state of final destination for an import (ABS state classification)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian state where an imported consignment was released from customs control. The ABS defines it as "the Australian state in which the imported goods are released from customs control", so it is the clearance state for the import line, so it follows the importer's broker or bonded warehouse rather than the customer who eventually uses the goods. Compare it with state_of_discharge_im on the same row, which is the state where the goods physically came off the ship or aircraft.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A full state or territory name from the ABS state classification used in international merchandise trade statistics, one value per import line.
limitation: It is not where the goods are consumed or installed. A national distributor clearing everything through one warehouse concentrates its imports into a single state, which makes state-level import series a poor proxy for regional demand. It also describes a consignment, so a business importing through several states produces several rows rather than one location.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines state of final destination for imports in the exact terms this column carries and distinguishes it from the state of discharge on the same declaration.
evidence_quote: the Australian state in which the imported goods are released from customs control
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL phrase 'The state of final destination' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the state is where customs control ended rather than where the goods were used.

value_domain: Australian state of discharge for an import (ABS state classification)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian state where an imported consignment was unloaded from the ship or aircraft that brought it. The ABS defines it as "the Australian State/Territory in which imported goods are unloaded from the international carrier", and it is a port fact, so it describes logistics rather than the importing firm's own location, and it is the only one of the four trade state columns whose BLADE value list carries a confidentialised residual, shown as state details not available. Read it against state_of_destination_im, which records where the goods left customs control.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A full state or territory name from the ABS state classification, plus a residual category for consignments whose state is suppressed for confidentiality, applied since September 2008 for imports.
limitation: Goods trucked interstate after unloading are still counted at the wharf state, so this column overstates the port states and understates landlocked destinations. The suppressed category is not a place and must be kept separate rather than dropped, otherwise state shares are computed on a shrinking and non-random base.
rationale: The ABS chapter defines the state of discharge for imports and documents the confidentiality category that appears in this column's valid response list.
evidence_quote: the Australian State/Territory in which imported goods are unloaded from the international carrier
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL phrase about where goods will be or were unloaded with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing explained the confidentialised residual in its own value list or how it differs from the destination state.

value_domain: Australian state of loading for an export (ABS state classification)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian state where an export consignment was loaded onto the ship or aircraft leaving the country. The ABS defines it as "the Australian state in which the goods are loaded onto an international carrier for export", so it is the departure port's state, so for a producer that trucks goods to a larger port it is not the state where the goods were made. The column to pair it with is state_of_origin_ex, which records where production finished.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A full state or territory name from the ABS state classification, one value per export line, with no re-export or suppressed category in this column's valid response list.
limitation: It measures port throughput rather than production, so it credits the states with deep-water container and bulk terminals and under-counts inland producers. A firm-level export map built on this column will therefore misplace manufacturers that ship through another state's port.
rationale: The ABS chapter defines the state of loading for exports in the terms this column carries and sets it against the state of origin recorded on the same declaration.
evidence_quote: the Australian state in which the goods are loaded onto an international carrier for export
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL phrase about where goods will be loaded with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the value is a port state rather than a production state.

value_domain: Australian state of origin for an export (ABS state classification)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian state where the exported goods were produced, or where the last stage of their manufacture happened. The ABS defines it as "the Australian state in which the whole of production occurs or the final stage of production or manufacture occurs", which makes it the closest of the four trade state columns to an economic statement about the exporting business, because it follows manufacture rather than shipping. Its valid response list also carries a re-exports category for goods that were imported and then sent out again in the same or near-same condition.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
value_definition: A full state or territory name from the ABS state classification, plus a re-exports category that stands in place of a state where the goods were not produced in Australia.
limitation: Re-exports are a category rather than a state, so adding the eight states omits them and a national total built that way does not match published export values. The state is also where production finished, not where the exporting entity is registered, so a firm headquartered in one state exports from another without anything on the row saying so.
rationale: The ABS chapter defines the state of origin for exports and documents the re-export category that appears in this column's valid response list.
evidence_quote: the Australian state in which the whole of production occurs or the final stage of production or manufacture occurs
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL phrase 'The state of origin' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said what production stage fixes the state or why re-exports sit outside the state list.

value_domain: IP right lifecycle status (IP RAPID categorical)
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary (data.gov.au)
variable_description: Where the intellectual property right stands as at the extract, which IP Australia defines as "This is the current status of the IP right or IP application". It is the field that separates a live, enforceable right from an application that lapsed, was withdrawn or was refused, so it is what decides whether a firm's patent or trade mark count is a stockpile or a filing history. The vocabulary is right-type specific: a design can be registered or certified, a trade mark protected or removed, and a patent granted, ceased or expired.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary (data.gov.au)
value_definition: A lower-case categorical string from a fixed list that includes ceased, lapsed, expired, withdrawn, process_error, granted, revoked, converted, refused, filed, accepted, certified, unknown, registered, published, not_filed, cancelled and received, with the meaning of each value set by the right type in Table 2 of the IP RAPID data dictionary.
limitation: It is a snapshot that is overwritten, so it cannot date the change: a patent showing ceased gives no clue when it stopped, which is recorded in the application-events table instead. Reading a value across right types is also unsafe, because certified means a legally protected design but for patents is particular to innovation patents, and unknown is reserved for early patents where the type of termination was never recorded.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary defines the status field, publishes its complete value list, and gives a per-right-type meaning for each value in a dedicated table.
evidence_quote: This is the current status of the IP right or IP application.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's one-line field label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, even though the dictionary publishes a complete code list and a per-right-type reading of each code.

value_domain: ABS internal integration version reference
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: An ABS build stamp saying which integration run produced the Single Touch Payroll rows on this record; it describes the data, not the employer. The ABS lists Single Touch Payroll among the Australian Taxation Office sources brought into BLADE, and each integration of that source is versioned so that a researcher can tell rows from different runs apart. Its only analytical use is to hold an analysis on one vintage.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric internal reference, for example in139_v1, with no published code list and no ordering guaranteed beyond the version suffix.
limitation: It carries no information about the business, the payroll or the pay period, so it must never be used as a covariate or a control. Because it is an internal ABS reference, a change in the string cannot be mapped to any documented change in method, which means it can flag that two extracts differ but not say how.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page confirms Single Touch Payroll is one of the ATO sources integrated into the asset, which is what this stamp versions; the ABS does not publish the internal reference itself, so the reading of the column is inferred from the DIL note.
evidence_quote: Australian Taxation Office: Business Activity Statements (BAS), Business Income Tax (BIT) filings, Pay as You Go (PAYG) summaries, Single Touch Payroll (STP), JobKeeper Payment Scheme, JobMaker Hiring Credit Scheme, Capital Gains Tax (CGT) and Consolidated Groups
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL phrase 'Integration version of dataset (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the column is a vintage stamp with no business content and no safe analytical use.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover reported on the trust return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: The trust's aggregated turnover in dollars, reported only by the very largest entities and rounded heavily. The ATO asks the question of a trust with turnover of $1 billion or more or one that is a significant global entity, and instructs it to "Print at label Q Aggregated turnover your actual aggregated turnover rounded to the nearest $100 million". Aggregated turnover is not the trust's own sales alone: it adds the annual turnover of connected entities and affiliates, so it is a group-scale measure sitting on a single entity's return.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 49 label Q of the trust tax return, rounded to the nearest $100 million, and able to be drawn from either the current or the immediately preceding income year.
limitation: This is not a turnover series. The label is blank for every trust below the $1 billion threshold, and where it is present the rounding destroys year-to-year variation, so growth cannot be measured from it; the banded range code on the same return is the column that reaches smaller firms. Because either of two years' turnover may be used, the figure need not belong to the year on the row.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions state who must complete the aggregated turnover amount, the rounding required, and the choice of reference year, which together define the coverage and precision of this column.
evidence_quote: Print at label Q Aggregated turnover your actual aggregated turnover rounded to the nearest $100 million.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label 'Aggregated Turnover' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the amount exists only above $1 billion or that it is rounded to the nearest $100 million.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover range category code (trust return)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: A banded reading of the trust's aggregated turnover, completed only where the trust is relying on turnover to claim a concession. The ATO says the range label must be completed "if you are relying on your aggregated turnover for eligibility" for measures such as the instant asset write-off, the small business CGT concessions, the small business restructure roll-over and the small business energy incentive. The DIL codes 5 to 80 map to the ATO's sixteen categories A to P, from "$0 to less than $7.5 million" up to "$1 billion or over".
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
value_definition: A numeric code in steps of five, 5 for category A through to 80 for category P, mapping to sixteen aggregated turnover bands; any other value is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: A missing code does not mean a small trust, it usually means the trust claimed no turnover-tested concession that year, so presence in this column is driven by concession use rather than by size. The band is self-assessed and may be taken from either of two income years, and the ATO adds that a taxpayer "will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect category" made in good faith.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions state the condition under which the range label is completed and publish the full category table that the DIL codes reproduce.
evidence_quote: You must complete item 49 Select your aggregated turnover range - label P if you are relying on your aggregated turnover for eligibility for any of the following:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Aggregated Turnover Range' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the code is present only for concession claimants or that a blank is not a small firm.

value_domain: Managed investment trust indicator (trust return)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Trust election status, trust type, details and tax payable
variable_description: Whether the trust reported itself as a managed investment trust, which changes how it is taxed and how it withholds. A managed investment trust is treated as a collective investment vehicle rather than as an ordinary trust, and the ATO describes it this way: "A MIT is broadly a publicly-held and commercially-operated collective investment trust that invests in primarily passive income activities". In BLADE it separates funds management structures from operating businesses that happen to be trusts.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Trust election status, trust type, details and tax payable
value_definition: Y or N on the trust tax return front section; anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It is a self-assessment against a six-part test covering residency or central management, no active trading business, being a managed investment scheme, the widely held requirement, the closely held restriction and operation by a regulated entity, so a Yes is a position taken rather than an ATO determination. The question is only put to trusts using five of the trust type codes, so an N can mean the question was never asked.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions define what a managed investment trust is, list the qualifying conditions, and state which trust types must answer the question, which is what fixes the meaning of both answers.
evidence_quote: A MIT is broadly a publicly-held and commercially-operated collective investment trust that invests in primarily passive income activities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own question as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the answer is self-assessed or that it is only asked of certain trust types.

value_domain: Managed investment trust type code (trust return)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Trust election status, trust type, details and tax payable
variable_description: Which kind of managed investment trust the trust says it is, which sets the withholding treatment of its fund payments. The three ATO types are a withholding MIT, coded W, a managed investment trust that is not a withholding MIT, coded N, and a clean building MIT, coded C, which the ATO defines as one that "holds one or more clean buildings, including the land on which the buildings are situated" and derives no assessable income from other taxable Australian property. The type is only asked once the MIT indicator on the same return is Yes.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Trust election status, trust type, details and tax payable
value_definition: A numeric code, 5 for a withholding MIT, 10 for a managed investment trust that is not a withholding MIT and 15 for a clean building MIT, mapping to the ATO codes W, N and C; anything else is invalid or absent.
limitation: Because the type exists only where the MIT indicator is Yes, this column cannot be used on its own to count managed investment trusts, and a blank confounds not a MIT with not answered. Clean building status also depends on a green star or energy rating held throughout the year, which is not carried on the return, so the code cannot be checked from anything in BLADE.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions publish the MIT type table with its three categories, the letter codes and the definition of each type, which is exactly what the DIL numeric codes reproduce.
evidence_quote: A MIT is a clean building MIT if it: holds one or more clean buildings, including the land on which the buildings are situated
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Type of managed investment trust' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the code depends on the MIT indicator or what distinguishes a withholding MIT from a clean building MIT.

value_domain: Personal services income results test indicator (trust return)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Personal services income item 30
variable_description: Whether the trust says it met the personal services income results test for at least one individual whose income it received. Passing lets the trust keep that income instead of attributing it to the person who earned it. The ATO sets the test out as three conditions together: "at least 75% of the PSI of the individual doing the personal services work is paid to achieve a contractually specified result", the trust provides any necessary tools or equipment, and "you are liable for the cost of rectifying defects in the work performed". For BLADE it marks a trust operating as a contracting vehicle rather than as a labour intermediary.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Personal services income item 30
value_definition: Y or N at item 30 label C of the trust tax return; anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It is a per-individual test collapsed into one flag, so a Yes means only that at least one individual passed, and it does not say how many did or what share of the trust's income they earned. It is also self-assessed: a personal services business determination from the Commissioner is a separate label on the same item, so this column records a position taken rather than one accepted.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions state the question in the same words as the DIL label and set out the three conditions that make up the results test, which is what a Yes on this column asserts.
evidence_quote: You will meet the results test in an income year if: at least 75% of the PSI of the individual doing the personal services work is paid to achieve a contractually specified result under your contract or agreement
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own question as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said what the results test requires or that the flag is a claim covering at least one individual.

value_domain: ATO business industry code (five digit, modified ANZSIC)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status items 1 and 2
variable_description: The industry the trust nominated for the business earning most of its gross income, coded to the ATO's five-digit business industry code. The ATO instructs the preparer to "Show at label A Industry code the appropriate industry code for the trust's main business" and states that "The industry coding regime used by us is a modified version of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)". It is a self-selected tax-form code, so it is not the ABS Business Register industry that BLADE also carries for the same business.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status items 1 and 2
value_definition: A five-digit business industry code, for example 01600 for dairy cattle farming, taken from the ATO's business industry code list for the relevant income year, which the ATO describes as a modified version of ANZSIC.
limitation: Because the coding regime is modified, the code does not always join cleanly to ABS industry tables and a BLADE analysis should prefer the register industry where the two disagree. It describes only the largest single activity by gross income, so a diversified trust is coded as one industry, and it tends to be sticky, because a code once chosen is usually carried forward into later returns.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions define the industry code label, its five-digit form and its relationship to ANZSIC, which is the classification question this column raises.
evidence_quote: The industry coding regime used by us is a modified version of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) External Link produced jointly by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) and Statistics New Zealand.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label 'ANZSIC code' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the code is the ATO's modified business industry code rather than ANZSIC itself.

value_domain: Assessable balancing adjustment on intangible asset disposal (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: Income the trust brought to account because it stopped holding an intangible depreciating asset for more than its written-down value. The ATO instruction is to "Show at label F Assessable balancing adjustments on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets the total assessable income you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred this income year". The intangibles in scope are patents, registered designs, copyrights, certain licences, in-house software, mining and prospecting rights and information, spectrum licences and telecommunications rights, so this is the tax trace of a firm selling or retiring its intellectual property.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 50 label F of the trust tax return, gross of the matching deductible balancing adjustments at label G, and excluding assets that were allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: It is not the sale value of the intellectual property: only the excess over adjustable value is shown, so a large sale of a fully written-off patent and a small sale of a nearly new one can produce the same figure. Disposals at a loss go to a different label, so a zero here is entirely consistent with heavy divestment of intangibles during the year.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions define the label in the same words as the DIL description, list the intangible assets it covers, and name the low-value pool exclusion that shapes the coverage.
evidence_quote: Show at label F Assessable balancing adjustments on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets the total assessable income you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred this income year

value_domain: Assessable government industry payments, primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Income excluding foreign income item 5
variable_description: Government assistance the trust took to income against its primary production business, reported in the primary production column at item 5. The ATO instructs the preparer to "Show at label E and F Assessable government industry payments, as appropriate, the total amount of assessable government industry assistance", and its examples run from bounties, employee subsidies and export incentive grants to fuel tax credits and the wine equalisation tax producer rebate. This is the farm-side twin of the non-primary production label, and the two are split by the preparer's own allocation.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Income excluding foreign income item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount at the primary production label of item 5 of the trust tax return, one of three columns on that item covering primary production, non-primary production and the total of the two.
limitation: It records assistance the trust treated as assessable, not the assistance it received: amounts relating to starting or ceasing a business, and support the trust treated as non-assessable, are not here, so it understates public support to the farm. Because the primary production split rests on the preparer's allocation, a mixed farming and trading trust can move the same grant between this label and its non-primary production twin between years.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions define the assessable government industry payments labels, list what belongs in them, and describe the primary production and non-primary production column structure that separates this column from its twin.
evidence_quote: Show at label E and F Assessable government industry payments, as appropriate, the total amount of assessable government industry assistance.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label 'Assessable govt industry payments - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said what kinds of assistance it covers or how the primary production split is decided.

value_domain: Assessable government industry payments, non-primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Income excluding foreign income item 5
variable_description: Government assistance the trust took to income against its non-primary production business. It is the label that carried JobKeeper and the JobMaker Hiring Credit for most trading trusts, and the ATO lists those two beside standing items such as fuel tax credits, export incentive grants and the wine equalisation tax producer rebate, and rules one common case out explicitly: "Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F". It is the non-farm counterpart of the primary production label on the same item.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Income excluding foreign income item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount at the non-primary production label of item 5 of the trust tax return, sitting in the middle of the item's three columns for primary production, non-primary production and the total.
limitation: The label mixes standing programmes with one-off crisis support, so the spike in 2019-20 and 2020-21 is a policy event and not a change in the firm's ordinary subsidy position. It also excludes Medicare payments to medical practices, which the ATO directs to other business income, so a health services trust can look unsubsidised while receiving most of its revenue from government.
rationale: The trust tax return instructions define the non-primary production government industry payments label, enumerate the payments that belong in it including the pandemic-era programmes, and give the Medicare exclusion that shapes how health businesses appear.
evidence_quote: Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label 'Assessable govt industry payments - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the label carried JobKeeper and JobMaker or that Medicare revenue is excluded from it.

value_domain: Assessment calculation code for a trustee assessment under section 99 or 99A
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Trustee choice, beneficiaries and non-resident trust items 58 to 60
variable_description: Which basis the trustee is assessed on for the capital gains it chose to be taxed on itself rather than through beneficiaries. The ATO instruction for item 58 is "You will need to insert an assessment calculation code from Appendix 12 at label X Assessment calculation code as appropriate for your trust." The listed codes separate an inter-vivos trust assessed under section 99A (36) from one assessed under section 99 (37), and a deceased estate with (15) or without (16) the tax-free threshold. It is filled in only where the trustee made the item 58 choice, so it is absent for most trusts.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Trustee choice, beneficiaries and non-resident trust items 58 to 60
value_definition: A short numeric code beside the trustee choice amount on the trust tax return, drawn from the assessment calculation code appendix. The BLADE metadata points to an appendix of category codes rather than reproducing them.
limitation: The code names the assessing provision, not the size or source of the gain, and it does not mean the trust had no beneficiaries - a trustee can make the choice while beneficiaries remain presently entitled to other income. Appendix numbering moves between years, so a code table read from one year's instructions may not line up with another's.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the assessment calculation code that sits beside the trustee's capital gains choice, and the ATO instruction for that item names the code source and lists the codes that apply.
evidence_quote: You will need to insert an assessment calculation code from Appendix 12 at label X Assessment calculation code as appropriate for your trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which provision the code stands for or why only some trusts have one.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign source income retained in the trust
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
variable_description: Net foreign source income that stayed in the trust because no beneficiary was presently entitled to that share of trust income. The ATO defines the label as "each beneficiary's share of other assessable net foreign source income included in the net income of the trust for tax purposes", and this column holds the corresponding share for income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, reported at the end of item 57. The trustee is assessed on it, generally under section 99A at the top rate, though section 99 applies to some trusts.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label H of item 57 on the trust tax return, allocated from the net foreign source income the trust reported at item 23 label V.
limitation: It is a residual rather than a decision. The amount falls out of whatever share of distributable income nobody was entitled to, so it moves with deed mechanics and year-end resolutions rather than with the trust's foreign activity, and it excludes attributed foreign income, which is a separate label.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the other assessable foreign source income entry on the trust's statement of distribution, and the ATO instruction for that label defines both the beneficiary column and the no-beneficiary block.
evidence_quote: Print at label H Other assessable foreign source income each beneficiary's share of other assessable net foreign source income included in the net income of the trust for tax purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is the undistributed slice of item 23, taxed to the trustee.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income from broad-exemption listed countries
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide 2004, Modifications for a broad-exemption listed country
variable_description: Attributed income from controlled foreign entities in countries on the old broad-exemption list, the group given the widest relief from Australian accruals tax. The ATO guide says "Working out attributable income for a CFC in a broad-exemption listed country is similar to working out attributable income for a CFC in a non-broad-exemption listed country. However, more exemptions are provided for CFCs in broad-exemption listed countries." The three-way split into broad-exemption, limited-exemption and unlisted was later collapsed into listed and unlisted, so the column only carries data for the older form years.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide 2004, Modifications for a broad-exemption listed country
value_definition: A dollar amount at the broad-exemption listed country label of the attributed foreign income item on the older trust tax return, self-assessed by the trustee under Part X of the ITAA 1936.
limitation: Attributed income is not money received. It is income of a foreign entity that Australian law treats as the trust's, so the column can be large in a year with no foreign cash at all. A series that crosses the country-list change compares three categories against two and is not continuous.
rationale: The label names the broad-exemption listed country category of the controlled foreign company rules, and the ATO foreign income return form guide sets out how attributable income is worked out for that category.
evidence_quote: Working out attributable income for a CFC in a broad-exemption listed country is similar to working out attributable income for a CFC in a non-broad-exemption listed country. However, more exemptions are provided for CFCs in broad-exemption listed countries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the category belongs to a superseded country-list regime.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator for an overseas branch or a foreign entity interest
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Whether the trust had overseas branch operations or a direct or indirect interest in a foreign trust, foreign company, controlled foreign entity or transferor trust. The ATO instruction is "If the answer to this question is yes, print X in the Yes box at label S . Attach the completed International dealings schedule 2022 to the tax return." A Yes therefore predicts an international dealings schedule, and it is the practical screen for which trusts have offshore structures at all.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: Y or N at label S of the attributed foreign income item; anything else is an invalid or absent response. It is one tick box, self-assessed by the trustee.
limitation: It flags the existence of a foreign interest, not its size, country or purpose. A dormant shareholding and a large controlled foreign company both give Y, and the same box covers overseas branches, so it cannot separate an operating foreign business from a passive holding.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the indicator question that opens the attributed foreign income item, and the ATO instruction for that question states what it covers and what a Yes obliges the trust to lodge.
evidence_quote: If the answer to this question is yes, print X in the Yes box at label S . Attach the completed International dealings schedule 2022 to the tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the tick covers or what follows from a Yes.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign investment fund and foreign life policy income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Income attributed to the trust under the foreign investment fund and foreign life policy rules, a category that no longer exists. The ATO notes that "With the repeal of the foreign investment fund rules, foreign trust in this context refers to a controlled foreign trust", and the FIF rules were repealed from the 2010-11 income year. The column can only carry a figure for earlier years and is structurally empty afterwards.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: A dollar amount at the FIF/FLP label of the attributed foreign income item on trust returns for years before the repeal.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as no offshore investment. Once the label was removed every trust reports nothing regardless of what it holds, and the pre-repeal figures rest on the trustee's own fund calculation rather than on any third-party statement.
rationale: The current ATO foreign income instruction records the repeal of the foreign investment fund rules, which is what determines the years in which this label can hold a value.
evidence_quote: With the repeal of the foreign investment fund rules, foreign trust in this context refers to a controlled foreign trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the underlying rules were repealed and the column is dead after 2009-10.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income from limited-exemption listed countries
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Attributed income from controlled foreign entities in countries on the old limited-exemption list, which sat between the broad-exemption list and unlisted countries. The current form keeps only two categories, defined by regulation: the ATO now says "Unlisted countries are countries that are not listed in Regulation 19 of the ITA (1936)R." Read the column beside the broad-exemption and unlisted columns, which together exhausted attributed foreign income on the older form.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: A dollar amount at the limited-exemption listed country label of the attributed foreign income item on the older trust tax return, self-assessed under Part X of the ITAA 1936.
limitation: The category was abolished when the country lists were collapsed, so a nil in a later year reflects the form rather than the trust, and any long series is discontinuous at that point. The column also cannot be used to identify the countries involved, because membership of each list was set by regulation and changed over time.
rationale: The current ATO foreign income instruction defines the surviving listed and unlisted categories and the regulation that sets them, which is what the older three-way split was reduced to.
evidence_quote: Unlisted countries are countries that are not listed in Regulation 19 of the ITA (1936)R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the limited-exemption category no longer exists on the return.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income from unlisted countries
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Attributed income from controlled foreign entities in countries the listed-country regulation does not name. The ATO instruction is "Print at label X Unlisted country the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries. Unlisted countries are countries that are not listed in Regulation 19 of the ITA (1936)R." Income attributed from a transferor trust also lands here where it was not reported at the listed country label.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: A dollar amount at label X of the attributed foreign income item, worked out under Division 7 of Part X of the ITAA 1936 and grossed up under section 392 to the extent of foreign taxes paid.
limitation: Unlisted is a legal residual, not a measure of tax haven activity: it takes in every country the regulation does not name, from major economies to small jurisdictions. Nor can it be netted against the listed country column to give total foreign exposure, because the two are attributed on different assumptions.
rationale: The ATO foreign income instruction defines label X directly, including the regulation that decides which countries fall into it.
evidence_quote: Print at label X Unlisted country the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries. Unlisted countries are countries that are not listed in Regulation 19 of the ITA (1936)R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what makes a country unlisted or that the figure is attributed rather than received.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator for an interest in a foreign trust or foreign investment fund
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Whether the trust held an interest that brought it within the foreign trust or foreign investment fund attribution rules, recorded as a tick rather than an amount. The ATO explains that "With the repeal of the foreign investment fund rules, foreign trust in this context refers to a controlled foreign trust", so what the question captures narrowed over time even though the wording did not. Use it with the attributed foreign income amounts on the same row, which say how much was attributed.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: Y or N against the foreign trust and FIF/FLP entry of the attributed foreign income item; anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The tick does not distinguish a controlled foreign trust from a foreign investment fund, and after the repeal it can only mean the former, so the meaning of a Yes changes across years without the label changing. It also carries no amount, so it cannot rank trusts by offshore exposure.
rationale: The ATO foreign income instruction states what a foreign trust means for this question and records the repeal that narrowed it, which is what the indicator turns on.
evidence_quote: With the repeal of the foreign investment fund rules, foreign trust in this context refers to a controlled foreign trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the meaning of the indicator narrowed when the FIF rules were repealed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income retained in the trust
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
variable_description: Attributed foreign income that no beneficiary was presently entitled to, so the trustee is assessed on it. The ATO directs: "If there is trust income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, show that share of the trust's attributed foreign income at label G under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 ." It is the retained slice of the total already reported at the attributed foreign income item, not a separate source of income.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label G of item 57, worked out by applying the undistributed percentage of trust income, or the trustee's adjusted Division 6 percentage, to the trust's total attributed foreign income.
limitation: It cannot tell you why the income was retained. Accumulation by choice, a deed that blocks distribution and a failed year-end resolution all produce the same figure, and the allocation is a percentage of the whole rather than a tracing of particular foreign income to the trustee.
rationale: The ATO statement of distribution instruction names label G and states explicitly how the no-beneficiary share of attributed foreign income is reported.
evidence_quote: If there is trust income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, show that share of the trust's attributed foreign income at label G under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is the undistributed share taxed to the trustee rather than a distinct income item.

value_domain: Dollar amount of Australian franking credits on New Zealand dividends retained in the trust
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
variable_description: The trustee's own share of Australian franking credits attached to New Zealand franking company dividends, where no beneficiary was presently entitled. The ATO directs: "If there are relevant distributions to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, include the trustee's share of the Australian franking credits attached to a dividend paid by a New Zealand franking company at label N under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 ." These trans-Tasman credits are kept out of the ordinary franking credit label on the same statement.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label N of item 57, being the trustee's percentage share of the Australian franking credit on a trans-Tasman imputation dividend, including credits received through a partnership or another trust.
limitation: The amount is not necessarily claimable: the ATO says the label N figure "is not necessarily the amount that can be claimed by each beneficiary", and it can be cut by a supplementary dividend paid with the franked dividend. It also says nothing about New Zealand imputation credits in the same dividend, which Australian residents cannot use at all.
rationale: The ATO statement of distribution instruction defines label N and states how the trustee's share is reported where no beneficiary is presently entitled.
evidence_quote: If there are relevant distributions to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, include the trustee's share of the Australian franking credits attached to a dividend paid by a New Zealand franking company at label N under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the credits are trans-Tasman and are deliberately excluded from the franking credit label.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net Australian income or loss on the trust return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
variable_description: The trust's Australian income after Australian deductions, before foreign income, capital gains and prior year losses are brought in. The ATO instruction is "Print at item 20 Net Australian income or loss the net income or loss relating to Australian income, that is, total Australian income, minus total deductions." It is a flow for the income year and can be negative, in which case the form carries an L beside it rather than a minus sign.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 20 of the trust tax return, equal to total Australian income less the total deductions reported at item 19, with a separate loss indicator.
limitation: It is not taxable income and it is not what beneficiaries are assessed on. Capital gains, attributed foreign income and other foreign source income are added after it, and prior year tax losses are deducted after that, so the trust can show a loss here and still distribute net income.
rationale: The ATO deductions instruction defines item 20 and its arithmetic, which is exactly the DIL label's parenthetical.
evidence_quote: Print at item 20 Net Australian income or loss the net income or loss relating to Australian income, that is, total Australian income, minus total deductions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said where item 20 sits in the return's sequence or that it excludes foreign income and capital gains.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deductions against Australian investment income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
variable_description: What the trust spent to earn its Australian interest, unfranked dividend and other investment income. The ATO puts franked and unfranked costs in different boxes: "Expenses related to unfranked distributions are shown at label P ." Deductions relating to franked distributions sit at label R in the neighbouring column, and the thin capitalisation rules can cut either.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
value_definition: A dollar amount at label P of item 16 on the trust tax return, covering deductions directly related to Australian investment income other than franked distributions.
limitation: It is not the whole cost of the trust's investing. Interest and borrowing costs disallowed by thin capitalisation drop out, low-value pool deductions are reported at other deductions instead, and the label carries no split between interest, dividend and other investment expenses.
rationale: The ATO deductions instruction defines label P by contrast with label R, which is what separates this column from the franked distributions deduction beside it.
evidence_quote: Expenses related to unfranked distributions are shown at label P .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that franked distribution costs are excluded and sit in a separate column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Bad debts on the trust return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15
variable_description: Debts the trust wrote off as unrecoverable during the year and claimed as a business expense. The ATO instruction is "Print at label F Bad debts the bad debts expenses incurred for the income year." A deduction is only allowed where the amount was previously returned as assessable income or was money lent in a money-lending business, so the label tracks realised trading losses rather than a provision for doubtful debts.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15
value_definition: A dollar amount at label F under Expenses at item 5 of the trust tax return, reported in the primary production and non-primary production columns and totalled.
limitation: A bad debt expense is not a measure of customer default. The ATO requires a debt to be bad rather than merely doubtful, so write-offs lag the failure that caused them, and a trust that never returned the income as assessable cannot claim here at all.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines label F and sets out the precondition that the debt must previously have been included in assessable income.
evidence_quote: Print at label F Bad debts the bad debts expenses incurred for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that a bad debt claim requires the income to have been returned first.

value_domain: Count of assets opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
variable_description: How many depreciating assets the trust chose to keep out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation. The ATO says "You can make a choice to opt out of backing business investment for an asset if you are not using the simplified depreciation rules for small business ." The choice is made asset by asset and cannot be reversed, so a count here marks deliberate tax planning in 2019-20 or 2020-21 rather than an absence of eligible assets.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
value_definition: A count held as up to five characters. On the 2021 return the opt-out is reported at the backing business investment labels V, W and X in the capital allowances section.
limitation: A zero or a blank is not evidence that the trust used accelerated depreciation. A small business on the simplified depreciation rules cannot opt out at all and so never reports a count, and the measure itself ran for only two income years.
rationale: The ATO measure page defines who may opt out, how the choice is made and where it is reported on the return, which is what this count records.
evidence_quote: You can make a choice to opt out of backing business investment for an asset if you are not using the simplified depreciation rules for small business .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the count exists only for two stimulus years and only for firms outside the simplified rules.

value_domain: Dollar value of assets opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
variable_description: The dollar value of the depreciating assets the trust kept out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation. It pairs with the count on the same row: the count says how many assets, this says what they were worth. The ATO records that the choice "cannot be changed once made", so the value is fixed at lodgment and never revised in a later year.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
value_definition: A dollar amount reported with the backing business investment opt-out labels, covering only the 2019-20 and 2020-21 income years.
limitation: It is the value of assets excluded, not deductions forgone. Those assets still attract ordinary depreciation, so the figure overstates any tax effect, and it says nothing about the assets the trust did claim the accelerated rate on.
rationale: The ATO measure page sets the rules for the opt-out choice, its irrevocability and the years it covers, which determine what this amount can mean.
evidence_quote: The choice cannot be changed once made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the amount is a value of excluded assets rather than a deduction.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator that a beneficiary under a legal disability had income from another trust
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Trustee choice, beneficiaries and non-resident trust items 58 to 60
variable_description: Whether a beneficiary of this trust who was under a legal disability was also presently entitled to income from another trust. The ATO asks it as "Was any beneficiary in this trust, who was under a legal disability on 30 June 2022, also presently entitled to a share of the income of another trust?", re-dated each year; the BLADE label carries the 2019 wording. A Yes matters because the beneficiary's shares from every trust are combined to set the rate at which the trustee is assessed on their behalf.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Trustee choice, beneficiaries and non-resident trust items 58 to 60
value_definition: Y or N at the item on the trust tax return that follows the trustee's capital gains choice; anything else is an invalid or absent response. The date inside the question moves with the income year.
limitation: It does not identify the beneficiary or the other trust, and it is not a minor-beneficiary flag: legal disability covers minors, bankrupts and people unable to manage their own affairs. The supporting detail the ATO asks for is attached to the return rather than captured in this field.
rationale: The ATO instruction reproduces the question word for word and explains why the answer changes the trustee's assessment rate for that beneficiary.
evidence_quote: Was any beneficiary in this trust, who was under a legal disability on 30 June 2022, also presently entitled to a share of the income of another trust?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said why the question is asked or that the date in the label moves with the form year.

value_domain: Dollar amount of credit for foreign resident withholding tax
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
variable_description: Tax already withheld from payments to the trust under the foreign resident withholding rules, claimed back as a credit. The ATO instruction is "Print at label U Credit for tax withheld - foreign resident withholding (excluding capital gains) the total amount of tax withheld from payments subject to foreign resident withholding." It only makes sense beside the gross payments figure, which the ATO requires to be shown at item 5 whenever this credit is claimed.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
value_definition: A dollar amount at label U of item 6 on the trust tax return, excluding foreign resident capital gains withholding and excluding any share of credits distributed to the trust by partnerships or other trusts.
limitation: It is tax paid, not income earned, and it is not the trust's whole foreign resident exposure: capital gains withholding is reported separately, and shares of credit received through partnerships and other trusts belong to a different label.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines label U and states the exclusions that separate it from the other withholding credit labels on the return.
evidence_quote: Print at label U Credit for tax withheld - foreign resident withholding (excluding capital gains) the total amount of tax withheld from payments subject to foreign resident withholding.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that capital gains withholding and distributed shares are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of non-primary production business income excluded from NCMI
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
variable_description: Non-primary production business income the trust carved out of the non-concessional MIT rules because it came from transitional or approved infrastructure arrangements. The ATO instruction is "Print at label D the total excluded from NCMI amount in relation to non-primary production income, that is, income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities." Excluded income keeps the concessional managed investment trust withholding treatment, which is the point of the split.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
value_definition: A dollar amount at label D of the non-concessional MIT income item, and part of the figure already reported at item 5 label H Non-primary production: Other business income.
limitation: Do not add it to business income: the ATO says amounts at labels C and D "must be shown at item 5 Business income and expenses - label H Non-primary production: Other business income", so it is a subset. It also appears only for managed investment trusts, which leaves every other trust at zero.
rationale: The ATO non-concessional MIT income instruction defines label D and states where the same amount is already reported.
evidence_quote: Print at label D the total excluded from NCMI amount in relation to non-primary production income, that is, income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what excluded from NCMI means or that the amount is already inside business income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of non-primary production business income reported as NCMI
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
variable_description: Non-primary production business income the trust reported as non-concessional MIT income, which loses the concessional managed investment trust rate. The ATO names what falls in: "Print at label C , the total NCMI amount in relation to non-primary production income, that is, cross staple income, trading trust income and residential housing income." It is the anti-stapling measure made visible in the return.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
value_definition: A dollar amount at label C of the non-concessional MIT income item, and part of the other business income figure already reported at item 5.
limitation: A zero does not mean the trust has no cross staple arrangement. The item applies only where the trust is a managed investment trust making fund payments, and the classification is the trustee's own, tested by the ATO afterwards rather than at lodgment.
