evidence_quote: Print at label C , the total NCMI amount in relation to non-primary production income, that is, cross staple income, trading trust income and residential housing income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which income types the NCMI classification covers.

value_domain: Dollar amount of primary production business income excluded from NCMI
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
variable_description: Primary production business income the trust excluded from the non-concessional MIT rules, typically under transitional or approved infrastructure arrangements. The ATO instruction is "Print at label B the total excluded from NCMI amount in relation to primary production income, that is, income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities." The primary production split exists because rent from agricultural land was the case the rules were aimed at.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
value_definition: A dollar amount at label B of the non-concessional MIT income item, and part of the figure already reported at item 5 label G Primary production: Other business income.
limitation: It cannot be read as a farm income measure. The trust here is a landlord rather than a farmer, and the exclusion is a grandfathering status, so the amount tracks when the arrangement was entered into rather than any agricultural activity.
rationale: The ATO non-concessional MIT income instruction defines label B and names the arrangements that make income excluded.
evidence_quote: Print at label B the total excluded from NCMI amount in relation to primary production income, that is, income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the exclusion is a grandfathering status rather than a description of the activity.

value_domain: Dollar amount of primary production business income reported as NCMI
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
variable_description: Primary production business income the trust reported as non-concessional MIT income, which loses the concessional managed investment trust withholding treatment. The ATO's own illustration of what falls in is "income attributable to agricultural land held for rent". The figure caps what can be distributed to beneficiaries as primary production NCMI on the statement of distribution.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
value_definition: A dollar amount at label A of the non-concessional MIT income item, and part of the primary production other business income figure already reported at item 5.
limitation: The column caps a distribution rather than describing one: the ATO says the total distributed to beneficiaries at the PP NCMI label cannot exceed the total of this label and the partnership and trust NCMI labels beside it. And because NCMI is self-classified, an amount here is the trustee's view of the arrangement rather than a determination.
rationale: The ATO non-concessional MIT income instruction defines label A and gives the agricultural rent example that distinguishes the primary production column.
evidence_quote: Print at label A the total NCMI amount in relation to primary production income, for example, income attributable to agricultural land held for rent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said why a primary production NCMI category exists or what it caps.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator that the personal services business premises test was met
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Personal services income item 30
variable_description: Whether the trust says it met the business premises test for an individual whose personal services income it received. The ATO sets the test out as "You will meet the business premises test if, at all times during the income year, you maintain and use business premises" that are mainly used for that work, exclusively held, and physically separate from private premises and from clients' premises. Passing one of the personal services business tests keeps the personal services income rules from attributing the income back to the individual.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Personal services income item 30
value_definition: Y or N at label E3 of the personal services income item on the trust tax return; anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It is a self-assessment, not a ruling. The ATO bars self-assessment where 80 per cent or more of an individual's personal services income came from one client, and a trust in that position leaves the label blank, so a missing value can mean concentrated income rather than a failed test.
rationale: The ATO personal services income instruction defines label E3 and states when a trust is not permitted to self-assess against it.
evidence_quote: You will meet the business premises test if, at all times during the income year, you maintain and use business premises:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the tick is a self-assessment and is unavailable to trusts with concentrated PSI.

value_domain: ATO client market segment code
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Which of the ATO's own client segments the trust sat in when the return was processed, from government and large market down to micro business and not-for-profit. It is an administrative classification the ATO applies to the client rather than a figure the trustee reports, and it is used to route compliance work and to group entities in published tax statistics. Read it as the ATO's view of size and type at a point in time, not as a turnover measure.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A three-letter code: GOV government, LGE large market, SME small to medium, INB individual and non-business, MIC micro business, NFP not for profit. Anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The segment is not a size band you can convert to dollars, and the thresholds behind it have moved over time, so a trust that changes segment between years may have been reclassified rather than grown. It attaches to the ATO client registration, not to the ABS Business Register unit that BLADE counts.
rationale: No fetchable ATO page defines this segmentation as a return data item; the code list comes from the BLADE data item list itself, so the entry is recorded as an inference against the ABS BLADE overview.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the code is an ATO administrative segment rather than anything the trustee reports.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net capital gain on the trust return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Capital gains item 21
variable_description: The trust's net capital gain for the year, after losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions are applied. The ATO defines it: "The trust's net capital gain is the total capital gains it made for the income year, less its current year capital losses, unapplied prior year net capital losses, CGT discount and any other relevant concessions." It heads the capital gains and foreign income block, and a CGT schedule is attached once current year gains or losses exceed $10,000.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Capital gains item 21
value_definition: A dollar amount at label A of the capital gains item, taken from part 6 of the CGT summary worksheet or from label A of the CGT schedule.
limitation: It never goes negative. A year of net capital losses shows zero here and the loss appears instead as net capital losses carried forward, so the column cannot be used to build a gains-and-losses series or to measure realised losses.
rationale: The ATO capital gains instruction defines the net capital gain and names the worksheet and schedule the figure is transferred from.
evidence_quote: The trust's net capital gain is the total capital gains it made for the income year, less its current year capital losses, unapplied prior year net capital losses, CGT discount and any other relevant concessions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the figure is net of discounts and concessions and cannot be negative.

value_domain: Dollar amount of Australian franking credits from a New Zealand franking company
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Australian franking credits attached to dividends the trust received from a New Zealand franking company. The ATO instruction is "Print at label D Australian franking credits from a New Zealand franking company the amount of Australian franking credits that are included in the net income of the trust because of franked dividends received from a New Zealand franking company directly or indirectly through a partnership or other trust." It is the trans-Tasman imputation figure, deliberately kept out of the ordinary franking credit label.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
value_definition: A dollar amount at label D of the other assessable foreign source income item, covering credits received directly and through partnerships and other trusts.
limitation: It is not an amount that can necessarily be claimed. The ATO says the figure "is not necessarily the total amount that the trustee or beneficiaries can claim", and New Zealand imputation credits carried by the same dividend are worthless to Australian residents and must be left out of the return altogether.
rationale: The ATO foreign income instruction defines label D and warns that the amount reported is not the amount claimable.
evidence_quote: Print at label D Australian franking credits from a New Zealand franking company the amount of Australian franking credits that are included in the net income of the trust because of franked dividends received from a New Zealand franking company directly or indirectly through a partnership or other trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the credits are trans-Tasman and are reported in the foreign income block.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital gains the trustee chose to be assessed on
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Trustee choice, beneficiaries and non-resident trust items 58 to 60
variable_description: Capital gains the trustee chose to be taxed on itself instead of passing to beneficiaries. The ATO instruction is "You should include the amount of the capital gain for which the trustee is making this choice at label Y Amount of capital gains on which the trustee has chosen to be assessed on behalf of beneficiaries ." The choice is only open where no beneficiary received an amount referable to the gain during the year or within two months after it, and it must cover the whole gain.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Trustee choice, beneficiaries and non-resident trust items 58 to 60
value_definition: A dollar amount at label Y of the trustee choice item, being the total across every gain for which the choice was made.
limitation: Gains reported here are excluded from beneficiary capital gains on the statement of distribution, so adding beneficiary shares understates the trust's gains unless this column is added back. It also does not say which asset produced the gain or which provision the trustee is assessed under; that is in the assessment calculation code beside it.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the trustee choice defines label Y, the conditions for making the choice and its effect on the beneficiary capital gains label.
evidence_quote: You should include the amount of the capital gain for which the trustee is making this choice at label Y Amount of capital gains on which the trustee has chosen to be assessed on behalf of beneficiaries .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the amount is excluded from beneficiary capital gains and must be added back.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator that the trust is a charitable trust
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Whether the ATO records this trust as a charitable trust. Charitable trusts are taxed differently from ordinary discretionary and unit trusts and many are income tax exempt, so the flag mostly identifies rows that should not be read as commercial business results. It is an administrative marker carried with the return rather than a figure the trustee calculates.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: Y or N; anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It is not a registration status. The flag does not say whether the trust is registered with the charities regulator or endorsed as income tax exempt, and a charitable trust that lodges a return may still be reporting taxable business income.
rationale: No fetchable ATO instruction defines this as a labelled return item, so the entry is recorded as an inference against the ABS BLADE overview rather than sourced to a return instruction.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the flag marks a trust type whose income is often exempt.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net capital losses carried forward
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Losses information item 27
variable_description: Unapplied net capital losses the trust carries into later income years. The ATO instruction is "Print at label V Net capital losses carried forward to later income years the total of any unapplied net capital losses from collectables and all other CGT assets and CGT events." It is a stock at year end, not a flow, so it accumulates until gains are made that it can be used against.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Losses information item 27
value_definition: A dollar amount at label V of the losses information item, reconciling to part A item 2V of the losses schedule where one is required.
limitation: Capital losses cannot be deducted against ordinary income, only against future capital gains, so this figure must not be netted against the tax losses carried forward beside it. It also merges collectables losses, which can only ever be used against collectables gains, with all other losses.
rationale: The ATO losses information instruction defines label V, its components and how it reconciles to the losses schedule.
evidence_quote: Print at label V Net capital losses carried forward to later income years the total of any unapplied net capital losses from collectables and all other CGT assets and CGT events.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the figure is a year-end stock usable only against future capital gains.

value_domain: Significant global entity indicator code
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business description and status items 1 to 2
variable_description: Whether the trust was a significant global entity, the marker for a member of a group with A$1 billion or more of annual global income. The ATO instruction is "Significant global entity Print X at label G1 Significant global entity if the entity was a significant global entity (SGE) for the income year." An SGE faces country-by-country reporting, higher lodgment penalties and the multinational anti-avoidance provisions, so the flag isolates the small set of trusts inside very large groups.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business description and status items 1 to 2
value_definition: Coded 5 for significant global entity; anything else is an invalid or absent response. It corresponds to the tick at label G1 on the front of the trust tax return.
limitation: It says nothing about the trust's own size. A small Australian trust inside a large foreign group is an SGE while a substantial standalone trust is not, so the flag measures group membership rather than the scale of the reporting entity.
rationale: The ATO business description and status instruction defines label G1 and sets out the A$1 billion global income test behind it.
evidence_quote: Significant global entity Print X at label G1 Significant global entity if the entity was a significant global entity (SGE) for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the flag turns on group global income rather than the trust's own size.

value_domain: Dollar value of closing trading stock on the trust return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 51
variable_description: The value of trading stock the trust held on the last day of the income year. The ATO instruction is "Print at label D the total value of all trading stock on hand at the end of the income year or accounting period for which the trust tax return is being prepared." It is a stock read on one day, valued for income tax under section 70-45 rather than on an accounting basis, and the method used is recorded in the code beside it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 51
value_definition: A dollar amount at label D of the closing stock item, excluding input tax credits where the trust is registered for GST and including work in progress on manufactured goods.
limitation: A small business entity that estimates a change of $5,000 or less may simply repeat opening stock here, so a flat figure across years can mean no stocktake rather than no movement in inventory. Stock of a business that ceased during the year is excluded entirely and reported as business income instead.
rationale: The ATO business and professional items instruction defines label D and sets out the small business simplification that decides whether the value was actually measured.
evidence_quote: Print at label D the total value of all trading stock on hand at the end of the income year or accounting period for which the trust tax return is being prepared.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that a small business may carry opening stock forward unchanged.

value_domain: Closing stock valuation method code
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 51
variable_description: Which valuation method the trust used for its closing stock: cost, market selling value or replacement value. The ATO directs the trustee to "Print in the CODE box the code from table 7 indicating the method used to value closing stock for income tax purposes. If you use more than one method, use the code for the method representing the greatest value." That tie-break matters, because the code describes only the dominant method, not the whole inventory.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 51
value_definition: A code beside the closing stock label. BLADE stores it numerically - 5 for C cost, 10 for M market selling value, 15 for R replacement value - against the ATO's letter codes.
limitation: The code is not a signal of stock quality or of a write-down. A trust may elect to value an item below all three methods for obsolescence, and that election is reported elsewhere, so a cost code can still sit above a heavily discounted inventory. A small business entity in its first year has closing stock of zero and is told to print C, so the code there records no valuation at all.
rationale: The ATO business and professional items instruction gives the code table and the rule for choosing between methods.
evidence_quote: Print in the CODE box the code from table 7 indicating the method used to value closing stock for income tax purposes. If you use more than one method, use the code for the method representing the greatest value.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the code names only the dominant method where several were used.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Cost of sales on the trust return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15
variable_description: What the goods the trust sold actually cost it, the direct input line of the business income statement. The ATO instruction is "Print at label E Cost of sales the cost of anything produced, manufactured, acquired or purchased for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business." It includes freight inwards and may include external labour where the trust's accounts record it there, which is why external labour is not a clean separate cost line.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15
value_definition: A dollar amount at label E under Expenses at item 5, reported in the primary production and non-primary production columns. It can be negative, in which case an L is printed beside it.
limitation: It is not a gross margin denominator you can compare across firms. What falls into cost of sales depends on the trust's own accounting, and a small business entity on the simplified trading stock rules computes it from tax values rather than from a stocktake.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines label E and notes that external labour costs may be folded into it.
evidence_quote: Print at label E Cost of sales the cost of anything produced, manufactured, acquired or purchased for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the boundary with external labour depends on the trust's own accounts.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital gains excluded from NCMI
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
variable_description: Capital gains the trust classified as excluded from non-concessional MIT income, keeping the concessional withholding treatment. The ATO instruction is "Print at label Z the aggregate amount of all capital gains categorised as Excluded from NCMI." These gains are already inside the net capital gain reported at the capital gains item, so the column decomposes that figure rather than adding to it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
value_definition: A dollar amount at label Z of the non-concessional MIT income item, aggregated across gains for the income year.
limitation: It cannot be added to the net capital gain: the ATO says amounts at labels X and Z "must be included in the calculation of the amount at item 21 Capital gains - label A Net capital gain". Nor does it identify the assets the gains came from or the arrangement that made them excluded.
rationale: The ATO non-concessional MIT income instruction defines label Z and states its relationship to the net capital gain.
evidence_quote: Print at label Z the aggregate amount of all capital gains categorised as Excluded from NCMI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the amount is already counted inside the net capital gain.

value_domain: Dollar amount of NCMI capital gains on the statement of distribution
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
variable_description: The share of non-concessional MIT capital gains carried by income that no beneficiary was presently entitled to. The ATO defines the label as "the total NCMI capital gains amount for the relevant beneficiary of the trust", and repeats it in the block for income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled. It exists only for managed investment trusts that report NCMI at all.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label F1 of the statement of distribution, capped in aggregate by the NCMI capital gains total reported at the non-concessional MIT income item.
limitation: It is a category tag on part of the capital gains figure beside it, not a separate gain, so adding the two double counts. Zero is the normal value for any trust that is not a managed investment trust, which makes the column useless as a screen for capital-gains activity.
rationale: The ATO statement of distribution instruction defines label F1 and caps it against the NCMI capital gains total.
evidence_quote: Print at label F1 NCMI capital gains the total NCMI capital gains amount for the relevant beneficiary of the trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the amount is a tag on the capital gains label rather than an addition to it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital gains reported as NCMI
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
variable_description: Capital gains the trust reported as non-concessional MIT income, which loses the concessional managed investment trust withholding treatment. The ATO instruction is "Print at label X the aggregate amount of all capital gains which are included in the assessable income of a MIT as NCMI." Read it against the excluded from NCMI gains in the neighbouring column; together they split the gains sitting inside the trust's net capital gain.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Non-concessional MIT income item 32
value_definition: A dollar amount at label X of the non-concessional MIT income item, aggregated across gains for the income year.
limitation: It is not a gross gain. The figure sits inside a net capital gain already reduced by losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions, so it cannot be compared with disposal proceeds or with the method totals on the CGT schedule.
rationale: The ATO non-concessional MIT income instruction defines label X and states that it feeds the net capital gain calculation.
evidence_quote: Print at label X the aggregate amount of all capital gains which are included in the assessable income of a MIT as NCMI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the amount is a component of an already-netted capital gain.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital gains retained in the trust
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
variable_description: Capital gains that stayed with the trustee because no beneficiary was presently entitled to that share of trust income. The ATO directs: "If there is trust income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, show that share of the trust's capital gains at label F under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 ." Gains covered by the trustee's separate capital gains choice are deliberately not shown here, which keeps the two retained-gain routes apart.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label F of the statement of distribution, worked out from the undistributed percentage of trust income or the trustee's adjusted Division 6 percentage.
limitation: Gains taxed to the trustee under section 99A lose the CGT discount and the small business 50 per cent reduction, so the amount is not comparable with a beneficiary's share of the same gain. It also excludes gains reported under the trustee's capital gains choice, which is the other way a trustee ends up assessed.
rationale: The ATO statement of distribution instruction defines label F for the no-beneficiary block and states the interaction with the trustee's capital gains choice.
evidence_quote: If there is trust income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, show that share of the trust's capital gains at label F under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that retained gains lose the CGT discount and exclude the trustee choice amount.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital gains excluded from NCMI on the statement of distribution
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
variable_description: The share of capital gains excluded from non-concessional MIT income that no beneficiary was presently entitled to. The ATO defines the label as "the total capital gains amount excluded from NCMI for the relevant beneficiary of the trust", repeated in the block for income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled. It is the excluded twin of the NCMI capital gains column beside it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Statement of distribution item 57
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label F2 of the statement of distribution, capped in aggregate by the excluded from NCMI capital gains total at the non-concessional MIT income item.
limitation: The exclusion reflects a transitional or approved infrastructure status rather than the nature of the asset sold, so the column cannot separate infrastructure gains from other gains. Like the NCMI column it tags part of the capital gains label and must not be added to it.
rationale: The ATO statement of distribution instruction defines label F2 as the excluded counterpart of the NCMI capital gains label.
evidence_quote: Print at label F2 Excluded from NCMI capital gains the total capital gains amount excluded from NCMI for the relevant beneficiary of the trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the amount tags capital gains already reported and reflects a grandfathering status.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital works deductions on rental property
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
variable_description: Deductions the trust claimed for the construction cost of rental buildings and structural improvements. The ATO instruction is "Print at label X Capital works deductions the total capital works deductions amount for rental buildings and structural improvements, such as fences, retaining walls and sealed driveways." It belongs to the rent item, so it is about property the trust owns and rents out, not premises the trust occupies.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
value_definition: A dollar amount at label X of the rent item on the trust tax return, claimed under the Division 43 capital works rules at a fixed annual rate over a long write-off period.
limitation: Capital works deductions are not a cash cost in the year claimed. They spread a past construction outlay over decades, so they depress net rent with no current outgoing, and they reduce the property's cost base, which surfaces later as a larger capital gain rather than here.

value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
variable_description: The taxed element of a superannuation death benefit lump sum the trustee received where the estate's beneficiary is not a dependant. The ATO instruction is "Print at label V Death benefit superannuation lump sum where the beneficiary is a non-dependant the taxed element and at label W Death benefit superannuation lump sum where the beneficiary is a non-dependant the untaxed element." The trustee, not the beneficiary, pays the tax on it, and the taxed and untaxed elements are split because they are taxed differently.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
value_definition: A dollar amount at the taxed element label of the superannuation lump sums and employment termination payments item, being the total of taxed elements across every payment summary received.
limitation: It is a deceased estate item rather than a business measure, so a value here usually marks a trust that is not trading at all. The tax-free component of the same benefit is excluded, which means the column understates what the estate actually received.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction names both labels and states that the trustee is taxed on the amount according to the beneficiary's dependency status.
evidence_quote: Print at label V Death benefit superannuation lump sum where the beneficiary is a non-dependant the taxed element and at label W Death benefit superannuation lump sum where the beneficiary is a non-dependant the untaxed element.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is a deceased estate item taxed to the trustee.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the untaxed element of a death benefit superannuation lump sum
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
variable_description: The untaxed element of a superannuation death benefit lump sum received by the trustee for a non-dependant beneficiary. It pairs with the taxed element on the same row: the ATO says to "add the taxable component elements together and print the total of the taxed elements at label V and the total of the untaxed elements at label W ." The two are separated because they attract different rates in the trustee's hands.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 5 to 15, Reconciliation items
value_definition: A dollar amount at the untaxed element label of the superannuation lump sums and employment termination payments item, being the total of untaxed elements across every payment summary received.
limitation: A nil here is not evidence that the whole benefit was taxed in the fund, because many funds pay no untaxed element at all, so the column separates fund types more than it separates estates. Death benefit employment termination payments are reported at different labels and are not included.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction states how multiple payment summaries are aggregated into the taxed and untaxed element labels.
evidence_quote: If you have more than one payment summary, add the taxable component elements together and print the total of the taxed elements at label V and the total of the untaxed elements at label W .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO data item label as its whole description, with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the untaxed element is a separate component of the same lump sum.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Superannuation lump sums and employment termination payments
variable_description: The part of a death benefit employment termination payment for a dependant beneficiary that is above the ETP cap and therefore assessable. Everything below the cap is invisible here: the ATO says that "To the extent that the beneficiary of the estate is a dependant, taxable component amounts up to the ETP cap ($225,000 for 2021-22) are not subject to tax and are not shown on the return." A business carrying this amount is almost always a deceased estate administering an employment payout, not a trading enterprise.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Superannuation lump sums and employment termination payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, reported at item 13 label X of the trust tax return. The t_ prefix marks it as a trust return item, so it exists only for entities that lodge a trust return.
limitation: A zero or missing value does not mean the estate received no death benefit ETP for a dependant; it usually means no payment exceeded the ETP cap, which is indexed and changes each year. The column also says nothing about who the dependant is or how the estate was distributed.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the trust return label at item 13 for a death benefit ETP where the beneficiary is a dependant, and the ATO instructions define exactly what part of that payment reaches the label.
evidence_quote: To the extent that the beneficiary of the estate is a dependant, taxable component amounts up to the ETP cap ($225,000 for 2021-22) are not subject to tax and are not shown on the return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said that the column is truncated at the ETP cap.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Superannuation lump sums and employment termination payments
variable_description: The whole taxable component of a death benefit employment termination payment the trustee received for a non-dependant beneficiary. Unlike the dependant column beside it there is no cap: the ATO says "To the extent that a non-dependant is the beneficiary of the estate, the taxable component of the payment is assessable income". The trustee, not the beneficiary, pays the tax on it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 13 Superannuation lump sums and employment termination payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, reported at item 13 label Y of the trust tax return, alongside the separate labels for death benefit superannuation lump sums.
limitation: The amount excludes the tax-free component of the same payment, so it understates what the estate actually received. It also cannot be compared like for like with the dependant column, which only records amounts above the ETP cap.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the trust return label at item 13 for a death benefit ETP where the beneficiary is a non-dependant, and the ATO instructions state which component is assessable.
evidence_quote: To the extent that a non-dependant is the beneficiary of the estate, the taxable component of the payment is assessable income and should be shown at Y Death benefit employment termination payment where the beneficiary is a non-dependant .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the dependant column on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a deduction claimed on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The trust's own expenses of earning the franked distributions it received from other trusts, deducted against the amount at item 8 label F. The ATO restricts it to the trust's own costs: "Print at G Deductions relating to franked distributions from trusts in label F the trust's deductions for its own expenses incurred in deriving its share of the franked distributions from trusts". It is the deduction side of a two-column pair, so reading label F without it overstates the net benefit of the distribution.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year at item 8 label G of the trust tax return, separate from the general non-primary production deductions at label T.
limitation: The figure is the deduction actually claimed, not the expense incurred: prepayment and thin capitalisation rules can cut it, and expenses relating to a distribution excluded from assessable income cannot be claimed at all. It also does not identify which trusts the distributions came from.
rationale: The DIL label is the trust return label at item 8, and the ATO instructions define what may and may not be deducted there.
evidence_quote: Print at G Deductions relating to franked distributions from trusts in label F the trust's deductions for its own expenses incurred in deriving its share of the franked distributions from trusts at label F Franked distributions from trusts .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the return label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell it apart from the other item 8 deduction columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a capital allowance deduction
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
variable_description: The deduction the trust claimed this year for project pools, which write off capital project expenditure over the project's life rather than at once. The ATO gives it its own label: "Print at label J Deduction for project pool the trust's deductions for project pools." A non-zero value marks a business with capital spending tied to a defined project, such as a mine, a plantation or a major site development.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year at item 50 label J of the trust tax return, drawn from the uniform capital allowance rules rather than from accounting depreciation.
limitation: It shows one year's slice of a multi-year write-off, so it cannot be read as the size of the project or as this year's capital outlay. Nothing here identifies the project, and pooled amounts from several projects are added together.
rationale: The DIL label matches the item 50 label wording in the ATO trust return instructions, which put the deduction under the uniform capital allowance rules.
evidence_quote: Print at label J Deduction for project pool the trust's deductions for project pools.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to say a project pool is a spread deduction rather than an expense.

value_domain: Dollar amount of dividend income on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 12 Dividends
variable_description: Unfranked dividends the trust received directly from Australian companies, gross of any tax withheld. The ATO defines the label as "the gross amount of unfranked dividends, and the unfranked amount of partially franked dividends (if the dividend statement shows this amount separately) received before any TFN amounts were withheld." Certain private company payments and forgiven loans caught by Division 7A are also returned here, so a large figure can signal related-party dealings rather than a share portfolio.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 12 Dividends
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year at item 12 label K of the trust tax return, sitting beside the franked amount at label L and the franking credit at label M.
limitation: It covers only dividends received directly from Australian companies; dividends flowing through a partnership or another trust go to item 8, and foreign dividends to item 23, so this column understates the trust's total dividend income.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 12 label wording, and the ATO instructions give a direct definition plus the Division 7A inclusions.
evidence_quote: Print at label K Unfranked amount the gross amount of unfranked dividends, and the unfranked amount of partially franked dividends (if the dividend statement shows this amount separately) received before any TFN amounts were withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing explained the direct-receipt boundary or the Division 7A inclusions.

value_domain: Opt-out choice code for backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
variable_description: Whether the trust chose to forgo the accelerated depreciation rate under backing business investment for some, all or none of its eligible assets. Backing business investment let a business with aggregated turnover under $500 million deduct "50% of the cost (or adjustable value where applicable) of the depreciating asset" plus the usual rate on the remainder, and the choice to opt out was made asset by asset on the return. The code therefore records a deliberate tax election, not an eligibility test.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
value_definition: A small integer code for the backing business investment opt-out choice: 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets, 15 for no, with anything else meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The measure ran only for the 2019-20 and 2020-21 income years, so the column is empty for every other year and cannot be used as a continuous series. A 15 or a blank cannot be read as "claimed the concession", because most trusts had no eligible assets at all.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the return question about opting out of backing business investment, and the ATO page defines the measure, the turnover threshold, the two eligible years and the asset-by-asset opt-out choice.
evidence_quote: Businesses are eligible for the backing business investment deduction if they have an aggregated turnover of less than $500 million in the year they are claiming the deduction. The deduction is available in the 2019-20 and 2020-21 income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question wording with the generic no-value-list sentence duplicated, so it never said what backing business investment was or that the column exists for two years only.

value_domain: Count of assets claimed under temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
variable_description: How many separate depreciating assets the trust wrote off in full under temporary full expensing this year. The ATO asks for "the number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing", and pairs it with the dollar deduction at the neighbouring label so the two together give an average asset size. It is a count of assets, not of purchases or of suppliers.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
value_definition: A non-negative integer stored as up to five characters, reported at item 50 label T of the trust tax return.
limitation: The ATO does not police the figure - it states that you will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect number where a best attempt was made - so the count is a rough self-assessment rather than an asset register. Improvements to existing assets are also deductible under the measure without necessarily adding to the count.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 50 label wording and the ATO instructions define the count and its tolerance for error.
evidence_quote: Number of assets you are claiming for Print at label T Number of assets you are claiming for the number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the field is a five digit character with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what was being counted or how soft the count is.

value_domain: Opt-out choice code for temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Opting out of temporary full expensing
variable_description: Whether the trust chose not to apply temporary full expensing to some, all or none of its eligible assets for the year. The ATO allows the choice only to businesses outside the simplified depreciation rules: "You can make a choice to opt out of temporary full expensing for an income year on an asset-by-asset basis if you are not using the simplified depreciation rules." Opting out usually signals a firm managing its taxable income across years rather than one that cannot use the concession.
description_source: ATO, Opting out of temporary full expensing
value_definition: A small integer code for the temporary full expensing opt-out choice: 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets, 15 for no, with anything else meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: A blank or a 15 does not identify a business that used the concession, since most trusts never had an eligible asset in the first place. Small business entities using simplified depreciation cannot opt out at all, so the column is structurally silent for them.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the return question, and the ATO page states who may opt out, that the choice is asset by asset, and that it must be notified on the return.
evidence_quote: You can make a choice to opt out of temporary full expensing for an income year on an asset-by-asset basis if you are not using the simplified depreciation rules.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying which businesses are even permitted to answer it.

value_domain: Yes/no indicator on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the trust says it passed the employment test, one of the personal services business tests that let a trust keep an individual's personal services income. The ATO sets the bar as engaging others to do the work: you meet it if you "have employees, engage subcontractors or engage entities that perform at least 20% (by market value) of the principal work, or have apprentices for at least half the income year". A yes therefore indicates a business with real outside labour rather than a single-person service vehicle whose income would be attributed to the individual.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, at item 30 label E2 of the trust tax return; any other value means an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The answer is self-assessed and is only completed in a narrow case: a trust that satisfied the results test, held a personal services business determination, or drew 80% or more of an individual's personal services income from one client does not fill it in at all. A blank therefore mixes "not applicable" with "failed the test".
rationale: The DIL label is the item 30 label wording, and the ATO instructions define the employment test and state the circumstances in which the label is left blank.
evidence_quote: Subject to certain exceptions below, you will meet the employment test in the income year if you: have employees, engage subcontractors or engage entities that perform at least 20% (by market value) of the principal work, or have apprentices for at least half the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Employment test" with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the test is or why the column is mostly blank.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a non-refundable tax offset
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Tax offsets items 52 to 54
variable_description: The early stage investor tax offset the trust reported for the year, earned by investing in a qualifying early stage innovation company. The ATO puts the total at item 54 as "Label I Early stage investor tax offset the total amount of the early stage investor tax offsets", and it is capped: the combined current-year and carried-forward offset for the trust and its affiliates cannot exceed $200,000. The offset is allocated out to beneficiaries on the statement of distribution, so the trust rarely uses it itself.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Tax offsets items 52 to 54
value_definition: A dollar amount including cents, reported at item 54 label I of the trust tax return as a non-refundable carry forward tax offset.
limitation: It measures an entitlement, not tax actually saved: the offset is non-refundable, so an amount here can sit unused and be carried forward. It also says nothing about the size of the underlying investment or which company received it.
rationale: The DIL label names the early stage investor tax offset and its carry-forward treatment, and the ATO tax offsets page defines the item 54 label, the $200,000 cap and the interaction with the statement of distribution.
evidence_quote: Label I Early stage investor tax offset the total amount of the early stage investor tax offsets .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label including its stray code letters and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the offset is non-refundable, capped and usually passed to beneficiaries.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a non-refundable tax offset
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Tax offsets items 52 to 54
variable_description: The tax offset the trust reported for contributions to an early stage venture capital limited partnership. The entitlement follows the trust's stake in the partnership: the ATO works it from "the trust's share (based on the trust's interest in the entire capital of the ESVCLP at the end of the current income year) of the sum of eligible venture capital investments made by the ESVCLP". Unlike the early stage investor offset beside it, this one rewards investing through a registered venture capital vehicle rather than directly in a start-up.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Tax offsets items 52 to 54
value_definition: A dollar amount including cents at item 54 label H of the trust tax return, reported as a non-refundable carry forward tax offset.
limitation: The amount reflects the partnership's investing during a window that extends two months past the trust's year end, so it does not line up cleanly with the trust's own cash flows for the year. Being non-refundable, it can also be entirely unused in the year it appears.
rationale: The DIL label names the ESVCLP tax offset, and the ATO tax offsets page defines the item 54 label and the calculation based on the trust's interest in the partnership.
evidence_quote: the trust's share (based on the trust's interest in the entire capital of the ESVCLP at the end of the current income year) of the sum of eligible venture capital investments made by the ESVCLP during the period starting at the start of the current income year and ending two months after the end of the current income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label with its stray code letters and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, giving no basis for telling it apart from the early stage investor offset.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deductions against personal services income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: How much of the trust's business expenses at item 5 were incurred against an individual's personal services income. The ATO defines it as "the total amount of expenses against PSI included at item 5 Expense", so it is a carve-out of an amount already counted in total expenses, not an extra deduction. Read against the matching income column it shows how much of the trust's cost base belongs to work done personally rather than by the business as a whole.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 30 label B of the trust tax return, a subset of the expense labels at item 5.
limitation: Adding it to total expenses double counts. It is also not the deductible amount: where the personal services income rules bite, some of these expenses are not deductible and are added back at the expense reconciliation adjustment label instead.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 30 label wording, and the ATO instructions state that the amount is drawn from the item 5 expense labels and explain the add-back treatment.
evidence_quote: Print at label B Total amount of deductions against PSI included at item 5 expense labels the total amount of expenses against PSI included at item 5 Expense .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the amount is already inside total expenses.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a tax reconciliation adjustment
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The net adjustment that turns the trust's accounting expenses into deductible expenses for tax. The ATO describes the two sides as expense add backs, which are "expenses shown in the accounts, which are either not tax deductible or are only partly tax deductible", and expense subtractions, which are deductions not shown in the accounts. It is the single field that reconciles a firm's profit and loss statement with its tax position, and it carries depreciation, provisions, entertainment, fines and capital items.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 5 label B of the trust tax return, which can be negative when subtractions exceed add backs; the sign is carried on the form by an L indicator rather than by a minus.
limitation: It is a net figure, so a small number can hide large offsetting add backs and subtractions, and it cannot be decomposed into its components from this column. Whether a negative value survives as a negative number in the extract depends on how the loss indicator was handled, so check the sign convention before differencing.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 reconciliation label, and the ATO instructions define both classes of adjustment and list what falls into each.
evidence_quote: Expense add backs are expenses shown in the accounts, which are either not tax deductible or are only partly tax deductible, including timing adjustments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that this is the accounts-to-tax bridge or that it nets two opposing flows.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a business expense on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: What the trust paid for labour and services bought in under contract rather than employed: consultants, contractors, commissions and agency fees. The ATO defines the label as "the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages". Read against total salary and wage expenses it distinguishes a firm that hires from one that contracts out.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense for the income year at item 5 expense label C of the trust tax return, taken from the profit and loss statement before tax adjustments.
limitation: The label was renamed from external labour costs to contractor, subcontractor and commission expenses, so a series spanning the change is not a like-for-like series and needs checking before it is differenced. Contract labour absorbed into cost of sales is also excluded, and accounting and legal fees sit in all other expenses instead, so the column understates outsourced services.
rationale: The DIL label carries both the current and the previous wording of the item 5 expense label, and the ATO instructions define the label and list what must be shown elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Print at label C Contractor, subcontractor and commission expenses the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label including its parenthetical rename and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without warning that the rename breaks comparability or that some contract labour is booked elsewhere.

value_domain: Income year (YYYY) specified in an interposed entity election
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Family trust election status and interposed entity election status
variable_description: The earliest income year specified in an interposed entity election the trust has made, marking it as part of another trust's family group. The ATO instructs that "If the trustee has previously made one or more interposed entity elections specifying a day in an income year before 2021-22, write the earliest income year specified in the box at this item." A value here means distributions outside the specified individual's family group can attract family trust distribution tax at the top marginal rate.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Family trust election status and interposed entity election status
value_definition: A four-character year written YYYY, repeated on every later return once the election is in force; the same box can instead carry R where an election is being revoked.
limitation: It is the year the election specifies, not the year it was lodged and not the year on the return, so it does not date the trust's structure change. A trustee cannot make a new interposed entity election specifying a year earlier than 2004-05 on the 2022 return, but earlier years still appear for elections already in place, so the column is not a consistent measure of how long a group arrangement has existed.
rationale: The DIL label matches the return item, and the ATO instructions state what year is written, that it persists across years, and that a revocation is marked with a letter in the same field.
evidence_quote: If the trustee has previously made one or more interposed entity elections specifying a day in an income year before 2021-22, write the earliest income year specified in the box at this item.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the field is four digits with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what an interposed entity election is or that the year is a specified year rather than a lodgment year.

value_domain: Dollar amount of employee contributions towards fringe benefits
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 46 Fringe benefit employee contributions
variable_description: What the trust's employees paid the business towards the fringe benefits they received, such as a contribution towards a work car. The ATO asks for "all payments the trust has received from recipients of fringe benefits". The amount reduces the taxable value of those benefits for fringe benefits tax, so it is a marker of how a firm structures remuneration rather than a measure of pay.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 46 Fringe benefit employee contributions
value_definition: A whole-dollar receipt for the income year at item 46 label T of the trust tax return, reported in the business and professional items section.
limitation: It records what employees contributed, not the value of the fringe benefits provided, so it cannot be used to size a firm's non-cash remuneration. It is also an income tax return field, not a fringe benefits tax return field, so it will not reconcile with the trust's FBT position.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 46 label and the ATO instructions define the payments to be included.
evidence_quote: Print at label T Fringe benefit employee contributions all payments the trust has received from recipients of fringe benefits.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is a contribution received rather than a benefit provided.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franking credits retained by the trustee
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 57 Statement of distribution
variable_description: The franking credits attached to the trust's income that no beneficiary was presently entitled to, and which therefore stay with the trustee. The ATO works the trustee's share by expressing "that part of the dividend in respect of which no beneficiary has an entitlement as a percentage of the total dividend" and applying it to the franking credit. It sits in the block at the foot of the statement of distribution where the trustee, not a beneficiary, is assessed.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 57 Statement of distribution
value_definition: A dollar amount including cents at label D of the income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled block of item 57, mirroring the label D used for each beneficiary above it.
limitation: It is the trustee's residual share only, so it understates the franking credits flowing through the trust; the beneficiaries' shares sit in separate rows of the same statement. Credits denied under the holding period or related payments rules never reach the label at all.
rationale: The DIL variable name marks the no-beneficiary block and the label is the statement of distribution franking credit label, which the ATO instructions define for the trustee's residual share.
evidence_quote: To work out the trustee's entitlement, express that part of the dividend in respect of which no beneficiary has an entitlement as a percentage of the total dividend.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Franking credit" with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which did not distinguish it from the beneficiary-level franking credit columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount of indirect franking credits
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Franking credits the trust received indirectly, through a partnership or another trust rather than from the paying company. The ATO defines the label as "the trust's share of any franking credits from a franking entity received indirectly through a partnership or other trust", and directs credits received directly to item 12 instead. A trust with a large amount here sits inside a chain of entities rather than holding shares itself.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 8 label D of the trust tax return, part of the share of credits from income block.
limitation: It excludes franking credits received directly from a company, so it is not the trust's total imputation position. Credits attributable to a New Zealand franking company, or denied by the holding period, related payments or dividend washing rules, are excluded even though the underlying distribution is reported.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 8 label wording and the ATO instructions define it and set out the four exclusions.
evidence_quote: Print at label D Share of franking credits from franked distributions the trust's share of any franking credits from a franking entity received indirectly through a partnership or other trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the credits are indirect and that direct credits are recorded elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total net income before losses
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 26 Total net income or loss and item 24
variable_description: The trust's total net income or loss for the year before any prior year tax losses are deducted, the subtotal that closes the income section of the return. The ATO ties it to the next item: item 26 is "the amount shown at item 24 Total of items 20 to 23 , less any amount shown at item 25 - label C Tax losses deducted", so this column is that item 24 figure. It is the cleanest measure of a trust's current-year trading and investment result, unaffected by loss history.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 26 Total net income or loss and item 24
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, positive or negative, summing the trust's business, investment, capital gains and foreign income items for the year.
limitation: The column name points at foreign income while the label describes a whole-of-return total, because the subtotal sits at the end of the foreign income block on the form; treat the label as authoritative and reconcile against the total net income column before using it. It is also a tax figure, not accounting profit, and cannot be compared with a firm's reported earnings.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 26 defines it by subtraction from item 24, which fixes item 24 as total net income or loss before tax losses deducted - the wording the DIL label carries.
evidence_quote: Print at item 26 Total net income or loss the amount equal to the amount shown at item 24 Total of items 20 to 23 , less any amount shown at item 25 - label C Tax losses deducted .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not flag that the column name and the label point at different things.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign tax relief retained by the trustee
value_source: ATO, Guide to foreign income tax offset rules 2024, Eligibility and rules for the FITO
variable_description: Relief for foreign tax paid on the part of the trust's income that no beneficiary was presently entitled to, so the trustee carries it. The label wording is the pre-2008 one: the foreign tax credit system was replaced by the foreign income tax offset, and the ATO says of the offset rules that "These rules apply for income years that start on or after 1 July 2008. Different rules apply for income periods up to 30 June 2008". On current returns the same box is labelled foreign income tax offset in the income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled block.
description_source: ATO, Guide to foreign income tax offset rules 2024, Eligibility and rules for the FITO
value_definition: A dollar amount including cents at label I of the no-beneficiary block of item 57 on the current trust return, carried under the older foreign tax credits wording in the BLADE item list.
limitation: The quantity behind the label changed in 2008-09 when quarantining by class of foreign income was dropped, so a series spanning that year is not continuous. Being the trustee's residual share, it also excludes the foreign tax relief allocated to beneficiaries on the same statement.
rationale: The DIL label uses the superseded foreign tax credits wording for the no-beneficiary block, and the ATO guide dates the change of system and states the current rules.
evidence_quote: These rules apply for income years that start on or after 1 July 2008. Different rules apply for income periods up to 30 June 2008; see How to claim a foreign tax credit 2007-08 (NAT 2338).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Foreign tax credits" with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the term is the pre-2008 one or that the column belongs to the trustee's residual share.

value_domain: Dollar amount of withholding credit on a capital gain
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 21 Capital gains
variable_description: Credit for tax a purchaser withheld from the trust when it sold Australian property as a foreign resident. The ATO keeps it strictly apart from the other withholding credits: amounts of foreign resident capital gains withholding must not be shown at the ordinary foreign resident withholding label and "should be shown at item 21 Capital gains - label B Credit for foreign resident capital gains withholding amounts". A value therefore marks a foreign-resident vendor of taxable Australian property, usually real estate.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 21 Capital gains
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit at item 21 label B of the trust tax return, claimed against the tax on the gain rather than treated as income.
limitation: It is a credit for tax withheld at settlement, not the tax finally payable and not the size of the gain, so it cannot be used to value the disposal. Where a variation reduced the withholding rate the credit is smaller than the standard rate would imply.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 21 label wording, and the ATO instructions repeatedly direct these amounts to it and away from the other withholding labels.
evidence_quote: Do not include amounts of foreign resident capital gains withholding at label U . These should be shown at item 21 Capital gains - label B Credit for foreign resident capital gains withholding amounts .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the other foreign resident withholding credit columns on the same return.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franked distributions received from trusts
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The trust's share of franked distributions received from other trusts, grossed up to include the franking credit attached. The ATO asks for "the trust's share of the franked distribution (described as franked dividends, franked distributions or attributable franked distributions), plus its share of the franking credit attached to the franked distribution". Franked distributions from a partnership go elsewhere, so this column isolates income coming down a chain of trusts.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up amount at item 8 label F of the trust tax return, paired with the deduction label G on the same row.
limitation: Because the figure includes the franking credit, it is larger than the cash the trust received and must not be read as a distribution paid. Unfranked distributions from the same trusts sit at label R, so this column alone understates income from other trusts.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 8 label wording, and the ATO instructions define the gross-up and the split against label R.
evidence_quote: Print at label F Franked distributions from trusts the trust's share of the franked distribution (described as franked dividends, franked distributions or attributable franked distributions), plus its share of the franking credit attached to the franked distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount is grossed up by the franking credit.

value_domain: Dollar amount of accelerated depreciation in the first year
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
variable_description: The first-year depreciation the trust claimed on new assets under backing business investment, the 2020 stimulus measure that front-loaded write-offs. The ATO sets the first-year deduction as "50% of the cost (or adjustable value where applicable) of the depreciating asset" plus the usual rate on the remaining half. A separate column records the second-year deduction on the same assets, so the two together trace a cohort of stimulus-era investment.
description_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, reported in the capital allowances block of the trust tax return in the years the measure operated.
limitation: The measure covered only assets first held on or after 12 March 2020 and used by 30 June 2021, so the column exists for the 2019-20 and 2020-21 returns and is empty either side; it is not a general depreciation series.
