An asset written off under temporary full expensing or the instant asset write-off cannot appear here, so the column understates accelerated write-offs overall.
rationale: The DIL label names the first-year accelerated depreciation deduction for assets using backing business investment, and the ATO page gives the formula, the asset dates and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: 50% of the cost (or adjustable value where applicable) of the depreciating asset plus, the amount of the usual depreciation deduction that would otherwise apply but calculated as if the cost or adjustable value of the asset were reduced by 50%.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice and gave no dates, so a reader could not tell the column covers two income years only.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a forestry scheme deduction
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 17 Forestry managed investment scheme deduction
variable_description: What the trust deducted this year for payments into a forestry managed investment scheme. The ATO defines the label as "the total amount of deductible payments made to an FMIS", which for an initial participant covers the payments that establish and maintain the trees. It is the deduction side of the forestry scheme pair, matching the forestry scheme income column elsewhere on the return.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 17 Forestry managed investment scheme deduction
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year at item 17 label D of the trust tax return, claimed under the specific forestry scheme rules rather than as a general business expense.
limitation: It cannot tell you whether the trust is an initial or a subsequent participant, and the two are taxed differently on exit. Deductions claimed here also feed a later clawback if the interest is sold within four years, so a figure in one year is not settled by that year's return.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 17 label, and the ATO instructions define the deductible payments and the interaction with the forestry scheme income item.
evidence_quote: Print at label D Forestry managed investment scheme deduction the total amount of deductible payments made to an FMIS.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing connected the deduction to the matching income item or to the four-year clawback.

value_domain: Dollar amount of forestry scheme income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Forestry managed investment scheme income
variable_description: Income from the forestry interests the trust holds in a forestry managed investment scheme, including thinning and harvest proceeds. The ATO asks for "the total income from the forestry interests that the trust holds in a forestry managed investment scheme (FMIS)", and where the interest ends through a CGT event the market value of that interest is reported here rather than the sale price. Capital gains from the same interest are excluded and go to the capital gains item.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Forestry managed investment scheme income
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year at item 10 label Q of the trust tax return, distinct from the ordinary business income labels at item 5.
limitation: For an initial participant who ceases to hold the interest, the amount can be a market value rather than cash received, so it is not a receipts measure. It also excludes any capital gain on the interest, which means the column understates what a disposal was worth.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 10 label, and the ATO instructions define the income and the market-value substitution on a CGT event.
evidence_quote: Print at label Q Forestry managed investment scheme income the total income from the forestry interests that the trust holds in a forestry managed investment scheme (FMIS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the figure can be a market value rather than a receipt.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign resident withholding credit retained by the trustee
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 57 Statement of distribution
variable_description: The credit for foreign resident withholding that stays with the trustee because no beneficiary was presently entitled to the income it relates to. The ATO ties the label to the rest of the return: "The total of the amounts at label L must equal the total amount of credit shown on the tax return at item 6 Tax withheld - label U ... and item 8 Partnerships and trusts - label U". Where the trust has no net income, the whole of the withholding lands in this box rather than being split among beneficiaries.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 57 Statement of distribution
value_definition: A dollar amount including cents at label L of the income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled block of item 57, mirroring the beneficiary-level label L above it.
limitation: It excludes foreign resident capital gains withholding, which is reported separately, so it is not the trust's whole foreign-resident withholding position. A large value can mean a loss-making year rather than undistributed income, because a trust with no net income reports the full amount here by default.
rationale: The DIL variable name marks the no-beneficiary block and the label is the statement of distribution withholding credit label, which the ATO instructions define and reconcile to items 6 and 8.
evidence_quote: If the trust has no net income, the beneficiaries are not entitled to a share of the credit for tax withheld. Instead, show the sum of the amounts withheld at label L under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which did not separate it from the beneficiary share column or explain the no-net-income default.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign resident withholding credit received indirectly
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The trust's share of foreign resident withholding credits attached to distributions it received from partnerships and other trusts. The ATO defines the label as "the trust's share of any foreign resident withholding credits received from partnerships or other trusts" and requires the matching gross amount to be included in the distribution income above. The withholding arises on a narrow set of payments to foreign residents: entertainment, sports, construction and casino junket activities.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit at item 8 label U of the trust tax return, part of the share of credits from income block.
limitation: It covers credits arriving through another entity only; withholding on payments made directly to the trust is credited at item 6 instead, so this column is not the trust's total. Amounts subject to foreign resident capital gains withholding are excluded even though they are also foreign resident withholding.
rationale: The DIL label matches the item 8 label wording, and the ATO instructions define the credit, the gross-up requirement and the excluded capital gains withholding.
evidence_quote: Print at label U Share of credit for tax withheld - foreign resident withholding (excluding capital gains) the trust's share of any foreign resident withholding credits received from partnerships or other trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the credit is an indirect share or which activities generate it.

value_domain: Income year (YYYY) specified in a family trust election
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Family trust election status and interposed entity election status
variable_description: The income year specified in the trust's family trust election, which fixes the test individual whose family group the trust may distribute to. A value here marks a trust that has narrowed its distribution field in exchange for easier access to losses and franking credits: the ATO warns that "you may have to pay Family trust distribution tax if you distribute to an entity outside of the family group of the individual specified in the family trust election". The same box carries V where the test individual is being varied and R where the election is being revoked.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Family trust election status and interposed entity election status
value_definition: A four-character year written YYYY, restated on every later return while the election stands; letters V and R occupy a companion box on the form for variation and revocation.
limitation: It is the year the election specifies, not the year it was made. A family trust election lodged with the 2022 return cannot specify a year earlier than 2004-05, but years before that still appear for trusts that specified an earlier year under an existing election, so the column is not a consistent measure of how long the election has stood. It also does not name the test individual or the family group, so it cannot be used to link related entities.
rationale: The DIL label matches the return item, and the ATO instructions state which year is written, how variations and revocations are marked, and what the election commits the trust to.
evidence_quote: If the trustee makes a family trust election or an interposed entity election, you may have to pay Family trust distribution tax if you distribute to an entity outside of the family group of the individual specified in the family trust election.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the field is four digits with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the election or the 2004-05 floor.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign tax credits on the general class of foreign income
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide 2008, Part 3 What credit can you claim for foreign tax
variable_description: Foreign tax credits attributable to the general or other class of the trust's foreign income under the pre-2008 credit system. Credits were then worked out class by class: "You must work out your foreign tax credit entitlement separately for each class of foreign income. This is called quarantining." The general class was the residual one, holding commercial trading income rather than dividends, interest, rent or royalties, which fell in the passive class.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide 2008, Part 3 What credit can you claim for foreign tax
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit amount for one quarantined class of foreign income, paired on the return with the general class net foreign source income it relates to.
limitation: The column belongs to a system abolished for income years starting on or after 1 July 2008, so it stops rather than continuing into the foreign income tax offset era; do not splice it to a later foreign tax series. A credit was also capped at the Australian tax on that class, so the figure is an allowable credit rather than the foreign tax actually paid.
rationale: The DIL label names the general class of net foreign source income and its foreign tax credits, which are terms of the pre-2008 foreign tax credit system that the ATO guide defines, including the four classes and quarantining.
evidence_quote: You must work out your foreign tax credit entitlement separately for each class of foreign income. This is called quarantining. Your foreign tax credit for each class cannot be more than the Australian tax applicable to that class of your taxable foreign income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what a class of foreign income is or that the concept was retired in 2008.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net foreign source income, general class
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide 2008, Part 3 What credit can you claim for foreign tax
variable_description: The trust's net foreign source income falling in the general or other class under the pre-2008 quarantining rules. The ATO described that class as the residual one: "Other income is income that does not belong to any of the other classes of income. For instance, it would include income from commercial activities, salary or wages and most pensions." For a business this is the closest thing on the old return to offshore trading income, as distinct from the passive class that held dividends, interest, rent and royalties.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide 2008, Part 3 What credit can you claim for foreign tax
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, gross foreign income of the class less the deductions attributable to it, grossed up by any creditable foreign tax.
limitation: Classes of foreign income ceased to be used for income years starting on or after 1 July 2008, so the column ends there and cannot be joined to the later single foreign source income measure. Because it is net of deductions and grossed up for credits, it is not comparable with a gross offshore revenue figure.
rationale: The DIL label uses the general class wording of the pre-2008 foreign tax credit system, and the ATO guide defines the classes, what falls in the other class and how the amount is grossed up.
evidence_quote: Other income is income that does not belong to any of the other classes of income. For instance, it would include income from commercial activities, salary or wages and most pensions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what general meant or that the classification was abolished.

value_domain: Dollar amount of business income subject to no-ABN withholding
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: Non-primary production business income the trust received from payers who withheld tax because the trust had not quoted an ABN. The ATO asks for "gross income received by the trust that was subject to withholding where an ABN was not quoted, this includes amounts of tax withheld", so the figure is gross of the 47% withheld. A non-zero value usually marks a business operating outside the ordinary invoicing chain, and it obliges the trust to lodge a payment summary schedule.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount in the non-primary production column at item 5 label D of the trust tax return, with the matching tax withheld reported at item 6.
limitation: It measures only the slice of turnover that triggered no-ABN withholding, not the trust's business income, and cannot be read as informal or cash activity. Shares of no-ABN amounts arriving through a partnership or another trust are reported at item 8 instead, so the column is not the trust's whole exposure.
rationale: The DIL label matches the item 5 income label for the non-primary production column, and the ATO instructions define the amount and the linked schedule and withheld-tax label.
evidence_quote: Print at label C and D Gross payments where ABN not quoted , as appropriate, gross income received by the trust that was subject to withholding where an ABN was not quoted, this includes amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the abbreviated label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is gross of withholding or what NPP means.

value_domain: Dollar amount of primary production income subject to no-ABN withholding
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: Primary production income the trust received from payers who withheld tax because no ABN was quoted. It is the farming column of the same row as the non-primary production figure: the ATO splits item 5 into three columns - "primary production, showing relevant amounts of income and expenses from primary production", non-primary production and totals - and this is the primary production cell of the no-ABN income row. It marks agricultural, forestry or fishing receipts paid without an ABN on the invoice.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount, inclusive of the tax withheld, in the primary production column at item 5 label C of the trust tax return.
limitation: The primary production split reflects how the trust classified the activity for tax, not an industry coding, so it will not agree with the trust's ANZSIC code. Because it is one narrow withholding category, a zero here says nothing about whether the trust farms.
rationale: The DIL label matches the item 5 income label for the primary production column, and the ATO instructions define the three-column structure and the no-ABN amount.
evidence_quote: Income and expenses are divided into three columns: primary production, showing relevant amounts of income and expenses from primary production non-primary production, showing relevant amounts of income and expenses from non-primary production totals, showing the total of the previous two columns.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving PP undefined and the primary production split unexplained.

value_domain: Dollar amount of expenses against foreign resident withholding income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: Expenses the trust incurred in earning the income that was subject to foreign resident withholding, quarantined into their own label. The ATO restricts it to "all expenses directly relating to gaining the income included at Income - label B Gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding" and forbids showing those expenses at any other item 5 expense label. It exists only for non-resident trusts, so the column is a marker of foreign-resident business activity in Australia.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense at item 5 expense label P of the trust tax return, reported in the non-primary production and totals columns only.
limitation: It is not a general expense measure and must not be added to the other expense labels as though it were a category of them, because those labels exclude it by construction. Expenses of earning income not assessable in Australia are also excluded, so it understates the cost of a non-resident trust's overall operations.
rationale: The DIL label matches the item 5 expense label wording, and the ATO instructions define the expenses, the exclusivity rule and the non-resident restriction.
evidence_quote: Print at label P Foreign resident withholding expenses (excluding capital gains) all expenses directly relating to gaining the income included at Income - label B Gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding . Do not include these amounts at any other expense entry in item 5 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the expenses are quarantined or that only non-resident trusts complete the label.

value_domain: Dollar amount of income subject to foreign resident withholding
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: Gross payments to the trust that were regulated foreign resident income, reported in the non-primary production column. The ATO limits the label to non-resident trusts and defines it as gross payments "that were regulated foreign resident income", meaning payments prescribed in the taxation administration regulations as subject to the foreign resident withholding measure - broadly entertainment, sport, construction and casino junket activities. The amount includes the tax withheld.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount at item 5 income label B of the trust tax return, reported in the non-primary production and totals columns.
limitation: It is not a measure of foreign-sourced income: a resident trust must leave it blank even when it earns income overseas, and payments varied to nil under a tax treaty are excluded. Amounts subject to foreign resident capital gains withholding are reported at the capital gains item instead.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 income label wording for the non-primary production column, and the ATO instructions define regulated foreign resident income and the resident exclusion.
evidence_quote: Complete label B only if the trust is a non-resident trust. For a resident trust, do not include an amount, such as foreign sourced income at label B .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could easily have read it as foreign income earned by a resident trust.

value_domain: Dollar amount of income subject to foreign resident withholding, primary production column
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The primary production cell of the foreign resident withholding income row, which the return does not actually collect. The ATO says of that row that "Income subject to foreign resident withholding is shown at label B in the Non-primary production column and the Totals column", and adds plainly: "You will not have any primary production amounts at this item." The column exists to keep the three-column shape of item 5 rather than to hold data.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar field in the primary production column of the item 5 foreign resident withholding income row, with no corresponding box on the paper return.
limitation: Any non-zero value is a reporting or processing artefact rather than farm income subject to foreign resident withholding, so the column should not be added into a primary production total. It is also not evidence that the trust has no foreign resident withholding income, which would appear in the non-primary production column instead.
rationale: The ATO instructions for item 5 restrict the foreign resident withholding income row to the non-primary production and totals columns and state that there will be no primary production amounts, which fixes what this column can contain.
evidence_quote: You will not have any primary production amounts at this item.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the abbreviated label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the return does not collect a primary production figure here.

value_domain: Trust type code for a non-primary production distribution received
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: What kind of trust the reporting trust received its non-primary production distribution from, coded from the ATO trust type list. The code box sits beside the share of net income from trusts at item 8, and where several trusts distributed the ATO says to "print the code that represents the trust with the greatest amount of distribution". It is the clearest signal in the return of the shape of the structure a trust sits inside: a discretionary trading trust, a public unit trust, a deceased estate.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A small integer standing for one letter of the ATO trust type list - D deceased estate, F fixed trust, H hybrid, I, S and T discretionary by activity, M cash management unit trust, P and Q public unit trusts, U fixed unit trust, C special disability trust, E testamentary trust - with anything else meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It describes the source trust, not the trust lodging the return, and only the largest source when there are several, so it cannot be used to enumerate a group. It is also blank whenever the share of net income is a loss, since the code is only printed when the amount is not a loss.
rationale: The DIL value list reproduces the ATO trust type codes, and the item 8 instructions state that the code beside the non-primary production label describes the trust the distribution came from and which code to use when there are several.
evidence_quote: If this amount is not a loss, in the box at the right of label R print the code from table 1 that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made. If this amount is from more than one type of trust, print the code that represents the trust with the greatest amount of distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw code list as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said whose trust type is being described or that only the largest source is coded.

value_domain: Trust type code for a primary production distribution received
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The type of trust that distributed primary production income to the reporting trust, coded from the ATO trust type list. It is the farming twin of the non-primary production code and is printed beside the share of primary production net income from trusts: "in the box at the right of label Z print the code from table 1 that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made". A value here means the trust's farm income arrives through another trust rather than from its own operations.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A small integer standing for one letter of the ATO trust type list, using the same D, F, H, I, S, T, M, P, Q, U, C and E codes as the non-primary production column.
limitation: The presence of a code says the distribution was classified as primary production for tax, which is not the same as the source trust being a farming business. Like its non-primary production counterpart it is left blank when the share is a loss, so blanks are not simply missing data.
rationale: The DIL value list reproduces the ATO trust type codes, and the item 8 instructions state that the code beside the primary production label describes the source trust.
evidence_quote: If this amount is not a loss, in the box at the right of label Z print the code from table 1 that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw code list and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and its label gave no way to tell it apart from the non-primary production code column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of interest income on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 11 Gross interest
variable_description: Interest the trust earned directly, before any tax was withheld. The ATO defines the label as "the interest from banks and credit unions, building societies, debentures, notes and deposits, income accrued on discounted or deferred interest securities, government securities and interest paid by us", and adds that accrued discount on a qualifying security counts even though no cash was received. It is a gross receipts measure and stands beside, not inside, the business income at item 5.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 11 Gross interest
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount at item 11 label J of the trust tax return, with any TFN amounts withheld reported separately at label I.
limitation: Interest arriving through a cash management trust or a similar pooled product is reported at item 8 rather than here, so the column understates a trust's interest income. It is gross income, not a return on assets, and carries no information about the balances that produced it.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 11 label wording and the ATO instructions define the sources included and the accrual treatment.
evidence_quote: Print at label J Gross interest the interest from banks and credit unions, building societies, debentures, notes and deposits, income accrued on discounted or deferred interest securities, government securities and interest paid by us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the two-word label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is gross, accrual-based, or missing pooled trust interest.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross rental income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Rent
variable_description: The gross rental income of the trust's properties, before interest, capital works and other rental deductions. The ATO defines the label as "the gross amount of rental income" and specifies that it "cannot be a loss", and includes booking and letting fees, retained bonds, lost-rent insurance payouts and tenant reimbursements. It measures a trust's landlord activity, which for many trusts is the whole of the business.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount at item 9 label F of the trust tax return, excluding GST where the trust is registered and GST is payable on the rent.
limitation: It excludes rent from foreign sources, which is reported at the foreign income item, so it is not the trust's whole rental turnover. Gross rent also says nothing about occupancy, the number of properties or whether the properties are residential or commercial.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 9 label wording and the ATO instructions define what rental income includes and where foreign rent goes.
evidence_quote: Print at label F Gross rent the gross amount of rental income. This item cannot be a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what is bundled into gross rent or that foreign rent is excluded.

value_domain: Yes/no indicator on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the trust's income includes the personal services income of an individual, the gateway question that opens the rest of item 30. The ATO defines the concept as "income that is mainly a reward for an individual's personal efforts or skills", decided contract by contract on a more-than-50% test. A yes marks a business whose revenue depends on one or more named people rather than on assets, goods or a business structure.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, at item 30 label N of the trust tax return; any other value means an invalid or absent response.
limitation: A yes does not mean the personal services income rules bit: a trust that passes the results test, holds a determination or meets one of the other tests keeps the income and deducts normally. The answer is also self-assessed against a contract-level test the return never shows.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 30 gateway question, and the ATO instructions define personal services income and set out what the answer triggers.
evidence_quote: Personal services income (PSI) is income that is mainly a reward for an individual's personal efforts or skills, or would mainly be such a reward if it was derived by the individual.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what personal services income is or that a yes does not imply attribution.

value_domain: Dollar amount of offshore income retained by a non-resident trust
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 60 Non-resident trust
variable_description: Income a non-resident trust earned outside Australia that no beneficiary was presently entitled to. The ATO asks for it only in one case: "If the trust is a non-resident trust, print in the box marked $ at this item the amount of income derived outside Australia to which no beneficiary is presently entitled." A trust is non-resident where no trustee was an Australian resident at any time in the year and central management and control was not in Australia.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 60 Non-resident trust
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 60 of the trust tax return, reported beside the yes/no non-resident trust question.
limitation: It is confined to non-resident trusts, so a blank is the normal state and cannot be read as an Australian trust having no offshore income. It also captures only the undistributed part, so it says nothing about offshore income that beneficiaries were entitled to.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the item 60 instruction word for word, and the ATO page defines non-residence for a trust and what the dollar box holds.
evidence_quote: If the trust is a non-resident trust, print in the box marked $ at this item the amount of income derived outside Australia to which no beneficiary is presently entitled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field is confined to non-resident trusts.

value_domain: Dollar amount of distributable trust law income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 56 Income of the trust estate
variable_description: The trust's distributable income under trust law, the pool that beneficiaries can be made presently entitled to. The ATO defines it as "the total distributable income of the trust that the trustee determine is legally available for distribution to trust beneficiaries in the income year" and warns that "it may be different to the accounting income of the trust or the net (taxable) income of the trust for tax purposes". It is the denominator behind every beneficiary share on the statement of distribution.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 56 Income of the trust estate
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 56 label A of the trust tax return; where the income of the trust estate is a loss, the instruction is to report zero.
limitation: It is not taxable income and cannot be reconciled to the total net income column: the two are different subject matters, one set by the trust deed and general law, the other by tax law. Because a loss is written as zero, the column cannot distinguish a trust with no distributable income from one that lost money.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 56 label, and the ATO instructions give the trust law definition, the Bamford propositions and the zero-for-a-loss rule.
evidence_quote: This is the total distributable income of the trust that the trustee determine is legally available for distribution to trust beneficiaries in the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that trust law income and taxable income are different quantities.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total net income or loss for tax
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 26 Total net income or loss
variable_description: The trust's net income or loss for tax purposes after prior year tax losses are deducted, the bottom line of the return. The ATO defines it as "the amount equal to the amount shown at item 24 Total of items 20 to 23 , less any amount shown at item 25 - label C Tax losses deducted", and this is the figure the statement of distribution then allocates to beneficiaries and the trustee. Where item 24 is positive, item 26 cannot be a loss.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 26 Total net income or loss
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount for the income year at item 26 of the trust tax return, with a loss carried on the form by an L indicator rather than a minus sign.
limitation: It is a tax figure and not a profit measure, and it differs from the income of the trust estate reported at item 56, which is set by trust law. Because losses are only deducted up to the available net income, a zero at this item can mean either a break-even year or a year where losses exactly absorbed the income.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 26 label, and the ATO instructions give the arithmetic and the constraint on losses.
evidence_quote: Print at item 26 Total net income or loss the amount equal to the amount shown at item 24 Total of items 20 to 23 , less any amount shown at item 25 - label C Tax losses deducted .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said whether losses were already deducted or how it relates to the trust estate income column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of personal services income within business income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: How much of the trust's business income at item 5 was the personal services income of one or more individuals. The ATO asks for "the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 5 Income", excluding exempt and non-assessable components such as GST. Against total business income it measures how far a firm's revenue rests on named people rather than on assets or a business structure.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 30 label A of the trust tax return, a subset of the income already reported at the item 5 income labels.
limitation: Adding it to business income double counts. It also does not say whether the income was attributed to the individual: a trust that passed one of the personal services business tests reports the amount here and still keeps the income.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 30 label wording, and the ATO instructions state that the amount is drawn from the item 5 income labels and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: Print at label A Total amount of PSI included at item 5 income labels the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 5 Income .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the amount is already counted inside business income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a tax reconciliation adjustment
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The net adjustment that turns the trust's accounting income into assessable income. The ATO splits it into income add backs, amounts "not shown in the accounts, but are assessable income", and income subtractions, income in the accounts that is not assessable - exempt income, profit on the sale of a depreciating asset, attributed personal services income and, for 2020-21 and 2021-22, cash flow boost payments. It is the income-side twin of the expense reconciliation adjustment on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 5 label A of the trust tax return, which can be negative when subtractions exceed add backs; the sign is carried on the form by an L indicator.
limitation: Because it nets two opposing flows, a small value can conceal large add backs and subtractions, and the components cannot be recovered from this column. It is also not a measure of tax aggressiveness: most of what passes through it is ordinary timing and statutory treatment.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 reconciliation label, and the ATO instructions define both classes of adjustment and list examples of each.
evidence_quote: Income add backs are amounts not shown in the accounts, but are assessable income, including timing adjustments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said this is the accounts-to-tax bridge on the income side.

value_domain: Dollar cost of intangible depreciating assets first deducted
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
variable_description: The cost of intangible assets the trust started depreciating this year: patents, designs, copyrights, in-house software, mining rights and spectrum licences. The ATO asks for "the cost of all intangible depreciating assets for which the trust is claiming a deduction for decline in value for the first time", undiminished by expected private use. It is one of the few direct measures in the tax return of a firm's investment in knowledge assets.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
value_definition: A whole-dollar cost at item 50 label A of the trust tax return, a cost figure rather than a deduction, covering assets first deducted in the income year.
limitation: It is not intangible investment: internally generated goodwill, brands and most research spending are not depreciating assets and never appear, and in-house software allocated to a software development pool is excluded by instruction. It also counts first-year cost, so an asset already being depreciated drops out even though the firm still holds it.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 50 label, and the ATO instructions define the cost basis, list which intangibles qualify and state the software development pool exclusion.
evidence_quote: Print at label A Intangible depreciating assets first deducted the cost of all intangible depreciating assets for which the trust is claiming a deduction for decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a cost rather than a deduction or which intangibles it misses.

value_domain: Dollar amount of interest paid to non-residents
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 29 Overseas transactions
variable_description: The part of the trust's interest expense that was paid to non-residents. The ATO defines the label simply as "the amount of interest paid to non-residents" and requires it to be reconciled to the item 5 interest expense: it "should have been included at item 5 Business income and expenses - label I Total interest expenses", adjusted for any reconciliation item. Reporting an amount here obliges the trust to lodge an international dealings schedule, so a non-zero value marks a business with cross-border financing.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 29 Overseas transactions
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 29 label D of the trust tax return, a subset of total interest expenses rather than an additional expense.
limitation: Adding it to total interest expenses double counts. It also does not establish related-party lending: interest to an unrelated foreign bank is reported here as well, and only the separate international related party question distinguishes the two.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 29 label, and the ATO instructions define the amount and its relationship to the item 5 interest expense label and the international dealings schedule.
evidence_quote: Print at label D Interest expenses overseas the amount of interest paid to non-residents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount sits inside total interest expenses.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a business expense on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: All the interest the trust incurred on borrowings for its business, in Australia and overseas. The ATO defines the label as "the interest incurred on money borrowed within Australia and overseas to acquire income-producing assets, to finance business operations or to meet current business expenses". It is the standard leverage cost line of the return, and against net income it is the usual basis for an interest cover measure.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense at item 5 expense label I of the trust tax return, taken from the accounts before tax reconciliation.
limitation: Interest incurred to earn rental income is excluded and reported at the rent item instead, so for a property-owning trust this column badly understates borrowing costs. It is also an accounting figure: interest denied by the thin capitalisation rules or incurred for private purposes is still in it, and is removed later at the expense reconciliation label.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 expense label, and the ATO instructions define it and state both the rental exclusion and the reconciliation treatment.
evidence_quote: Print at label I Total interest expenses the interest incurred on money borrowed within Australia and overseas to acquire income-producing assets, to finance business operations or to meet current business expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said rental interest is excluded or that the figure is pre-reconciliation.

value_domain: Yes/no indicator for overseas transactions
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 29 Overseas transactions
variable_description: The yes/no answer at item 29 Overseas transactions, on dealings with international related parties and on the thin capitalisation rules. The related-party question has a $2 million threshold and counts dealings gross: the ATO says "a $600,000 purchase from, and a $700,000 sale to, a related party should be treated as totalling $1,300,000, not $100,000". A yes to either question forces the trust to lodge an international dealings schedule, so the flag identifies the multinational tail of the business population.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 29 Overseas transactions
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, at item 29 of the trust tax return; any other value means an invalid or absent response.
limitation: A no is not evidence of no offshore activity, only that the dealings fell below $2 million and thin capitalisation did not apply, so small exporters and importers answer no. Item 29 carries two separate yes/no boxes and the column does not say which of them it holds, so treat it as the item's overall flag rather than as the related-party question alone.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the item 29 heading and the valid values are the yes/no pair, and the ATO instructions define both questions, the threshold, the gross counting rule and the schedule that a yes triggers.
evidence_quote: Transactions must not be netted off against each other. For example a $600,000 purchase from, and a $700,000 sale to, a related party should be treated as totalling $1,300,000, not $100,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Overseas transactions" with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing gave the threshold or said what a yes obliges the trust to lodge.

value_domain: Dollar amount of interest deducted against rental income
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Rent
variable_description: Interest the trust deducted against its rental income, kept separate from the interest on its trading borrowings. The ATO defines the label as "the total deductible amount of interest expense incurred in earning the rental income" and directs it away from item 5: "Do not include interest expenses incurred in relation to deriving rental income, these interest deductions are included at item 9 Rent - label G Interest deductions." Read against gross rent it shows how heavily a property-holding trust is geared.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at item 9 label G of the trust tax return, reported with capital works deductions and other rental deductions on the same rent block.
limitation: It is the deductible amount, already apportioned for private use and cut by the thin capitalisation rules, so it is smaller than the interest actually paid on the properties. It also cannot be attributed to individual properties, since the rent block is reported in total.
rationale: The DIL label matches the item 9 label, and the ATO instructions define it and separate it explicitly from total interest expenses at item 5.
evidence_quote: Print at label G Interest deductions the total deductible amount of interest expense incurred in earning the rental income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Interest deductions" with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which was indistinguishable from the trust's other interest columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount of PAYG withholding reported on the activity statement
value_source: ATO, Business activity statements, Pay as you go (PAYG) withholding
variable_description: Tax the business withheld from investment distributions it paid out because the investor had not quoted a tax file number. It belongs to the W3 group on the activity statement, which covers "interest, dividends, unit trust or other investment distributions you made, where the person you are paying has not filled in a TFN declaration form or otherwise provided you with a TFN". Unlike the two withholding columns beside it, which cover wages and no-ABN payments, this one identifies a business that pays investors.
description_source: ATO, Business activity statements, Pay as you go (PAYG) withholding
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount withheld for the activity statement period, reported alongside the wages withholding and the no-ABN withholding fields for the same period.
limitation: It is tax withheld, not distributions paid, so it cannot be scaled to the size of the payout without knowing the withholding rate and how many investors failed to quote. The activity statement's W3 box also gathers foreign resident and departing superannuation withholding, so this narrower field will not always tie back to a lodged W3 figure.
rationale: The BAS table gives three withholding fields distinguished by prefix - TFN, ABN and payments - and the ATO page defines which withholding types are reported at each activity statement label, including investment distributions where no TFN is quoted.
evidence_quote: interest, dividends, unit trust or other investment distributions you made, where the person you are paying has not filled in a TFN declaration form or otherwise provided you with a TFN (includes a foreign resident)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the field label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing tied it to the activity statement label or set it against the sibling withholding fields.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a business expense on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: What the trust spent leasing equipment, vehicles and plant under both finance and operating leases. The ATO defines the label as "the expenditure incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing assets, such as motor vehicles, plant or other equipment", and excludes the cost of leasing real estate, which goes to rent expenses. Against depreciation it distinguishes a firm that leases its capital equipment from one that owns it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense at item 5 expense label G of the trust tax return, taken from the accounts before tax reconciliation.
limitation: Hire purchase and instalment sale payments are not lease expenses and do not appear here, so the column misses a common way of financing equipment. Luxury car lease payments and capital lease termination costs are also included in the accounts figure and then added back at the expense reconciliation label, so this is not a deductible amount.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 expense label, and the ATO instructions define the expenditure, the real estate exclusion and the hire purchase carve-out.
evidence_quote: Print at label G Lease expenses the expenditure incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing assets, such as motor vehicles, plant or other equipment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said property leases and hire purchase are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a primary production capital allowance
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
variable_description: The deduction the trust claimed for landcare operations and for the decline in value of water facilities and similar farm assets. The ATO describes the label as covering "the deduction available to the trust for landcare operations and for the decline in value of water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets". These are concessional write-offs available to primary producers, so a value here marks a farming business investing in land and water infrastructure.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 50 Capital allowances
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at item 50 label L of the trust tax return, claimed under the specific uniform capital allowance provisions for primary production assets.
limitation: The label was widened over time to add fencing and fodder storage assets, so the column covers more kinds of spending in later years than in earlier ones and is not a constant definition across a long series. A small business entity that puts these assets in its simplified depreciation pool instead reports nothing here despite making the same investment.
rationale: The DIL label is a shortened form of the item 50 label, and the ATO instructions define the deduction and note that small business entities may use the simplified depreciation rules for the same assets.
evidence_quote: Print at label L Landcare operations and deduction for decline in value of water facility, fencing asset and fodder storage asset the deduction available to the trust for landcare operations and for the decline in value of water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the shortened label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the label widened over time or that pooling hides the same spending.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a carried-forward tax offset
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 28 Landcare and water facility tax offset
variable_description: Unused landcare and water facility tax offset the trust brought forward from earlier years and can still apply. The offset is closed to new spending - the ATO states that "You cannot claim the landcare and water facility tax offsets for expenditure incurred after 2000-01" - so every amount here is a residue of expenditure made two decades ago or more. It is a balance carried into the year, not a deduction for anything the trust did in it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 28 Landcare and water facility tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar carried-forward balance at item 28 label G of the trust tax return, distinct from the landcare capital allowance deduction in the capital allowances block.
limitation: It records an entitlement carried forward, not an offset used, and it says nothing about current investment because the underlying concession has been closed since 2000-01. Do not read it alongside the landcare capital allowance column as though the two measured the same activity.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 28 label, and the ATO instructions define the brought-forward amount and state that the concession is closed to later expenditure.
evidence_quote: You cannot claim the landcare and water facility tax offsets for expenditure incurred after 2000-01.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the concession is closed and the balance is historical.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a business expense on the trust tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: What the trust spent running its vehicles: fuel, repairs, registration and insurance. The ATO restricts the label to "motor vehicle running expenses only", and excludes the lease, interest and depreciation costs of the same vehicles, which are reported at their own labels. It is therefore a usage measure rather than a measure of what a firm's fleet costs.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense at item 5 expense label L of the trust tax return, in the primary production, non-primary production or totals column as appropriate.
limitation: Because the financing and capital costs of the vehicles sit in other labels, this column cannot be used as total fleet cost. It also carries no vehicle count and no business-use percentage, so private-use adjustments made later at the expense reconciliation label are invisible here.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 expense label, and the ATO instructions define it as running expenses only and list the three labels that carry the other vehicle costs.
evidence_quote: Print at label L Motor vehicle expenses motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said lease, interest and depreciation costs are elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net business income for tax
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The trust's net income or loss from business for tax purposes, the totals-column result of item 5. The ATO defines it as "the amount of the trust's net income or loss for tax purposes that is from business ... total business income less total expenses incurred in producing that income according to the accounting systems, adjusted by any tax reconciliation items". It equals the sum of the primary production and non-primary production results reported beside it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 5 label S of the trust tax return, equal to total business income less total expenses plus or minus the two reconciliation adjustments; a loss is flagged on the form by an L indicator.
limitation: It covers business activity only, so a trust's interest, dividends, rent, capital gains and distributions from other entities are all outside it and it is not the trust's bottom line. Because the reconciliation adjustments are already applied, it also will not match the operating profit in the trust's own accounts.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 totals label, and the ATO instructions give both the definition and the arithmetic linking it to the income, expense and reconciliation labels.
evidence_quote: The trust's net income or loss from business is the amount of the trust's net income or loss for tax purposes that is from business. It is the total business income less total expenses incurred in producing that income according to the accounting systems, adjusted by any tax reconciliation items.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is post-reconciliation or that non-business income is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net business income, non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The non-primary production half of the trust's net business result for tax, reported in its own column at item 5. The ATO reconciles the three columns: "The amount at label S equals the sum of the net income or loss from business at: label Q for primary production, and label R for non-primary production." For a mixed trust it separates the shop, workshop or professional practice from the farm.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 5 label R of the trust tax return, one of the two components that add to the totals-column result; a loss is flagged by an L indicator on the form.
limitation: The split follows the trust's own tax classification of each activity, not an industry code, so it will not line up with the entity's ANZSIC coding. A trust with no farming reports its whole business result here, which makes a large value ordinary rather than informative on its own.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 non-primary production label, and the ATO instructions state the identity between the totals label and the two column labels.
evidence_quote: The amount at label S equals the sum of the net income or loss from business at: label Q for primary production, and label R for non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the abbreviated label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving NPP unexplained and the relationship to the totals column unstated.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net business income, primary production
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The primary production half of the trust's net business result for tax, covering farming, forestry, fishing and similar activity. It is the label Q component of the item 5 totals figure, which the ATO defines as the sum of the primary production and non-primary production results. A non-zero value marks a trust carrying on a primary production business in its own right, as distinct from receiving farm income through another trust.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 5 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 5 label Q of the trust tax return, one of the two components that add to the totals-column result; a loss is flagged by an L indicator on the form.
limitation: Primary production classification here is the trust's own tax treatment, which triggers averaging and other concessions, and it is not an industry classification, so it can disagree with the entity's ANZSIC code. Farm income arriving as a distribution from another trust or partnership is reported at item 8 and never reaches this column.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 5 primary production label, and the ATO instructions give the identity linking labels Q and R to the totals label S and set out the three-column structure of the item.
evidence_quote: The amount at label S equals the sum of the net income or loss from business at: label Q for primary production, and label R for non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the abbreviated label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving PP unexplained and giving no way to tell it from the non-primary production column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net rental income or loss
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Rent
variable_description: The trust's rental result after deductions: gross rent less interest, capital works and other rental deductions. The ATO instructs the trustee to "Print at Net rent the net amount of any rent", and unlike gross rent this figure can be negative, in which case the form carries an L indicator. It is the standard measure of whether a trust's property holdings are negatively geared.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at the net rent line of item 9 on the trust tax return, computed from the four labels reported above it.
limitation: It is a total across all the trust's properties, so a positive figure can hide loss-making individual properties and the reverse. Foreign rental income and its deductions are excluded and reported at the foreign income item, so a trust with overseas property shows only part of its landlord result here.
rationale: The DIL label is the item 9 net rent line, and the ATO instructions define it and set out the deduction labels that feed it.
evidence_quote: Print at Net rent the net amount of any rent. If this amount is a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the two-word label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure can be negative or that it aggregates every property.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a tax offset carried forward by the trustee
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Tax offsets items 52 to 54 and item 57 Statement of distribution
variable_description: Unused early stage investor tax offset the trustee carried forward from the previous year against income no beneficiary was presently entitled to. The ATO directs a trustee with a carried-forward amount to report it under the statement of distribution at "Label M Early stage investor tax offset carried forward from previous year". It also eats into the annual cap: the carried-forward amount is subtracted from $200,000 when working out how much current-year offset the trust can claim.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Tax offsets items 52 to 54 and item 57 Statement of distribution
value_definition: A dollar amount including cents at label M of the income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled block of item 57, distinct from the current-year offset reported at item 54.

value_domain: Primary production income retained by the trustee (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, Statement of distribution - item 58
variable_description: The primary production part of the trust's taxable income that no beneficiary was presently entitled to, and on which the trustee is assessed.
