variable_description: The deduction the trust claimed under temporary full expensing, which wrote eligible assets off in full in their first year of use. The measure was a pandemic-era one, and the ATO's label guide puts it at trust tax return item 50 label S and says to "Show the total amount of any deduction under temporary full expensing you claimed at Depreciation expenses". The number of assets claimed for is reported at the next label, so the two together give an average cost per asset.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year at item 50 label S, forming part of the depreciation expense already reported at item 5 rather than adding to it.
limitation: The measure ran only for assets first held and used or installed between 6 October 2020 and 30 June 2023, so the column is empty outside that window for reasons of policy, not of investment. It also cannot be added to the depreciation expense at item 5, of which it is a component.
rationale: The ATO's temporary full expensing label guide maps the measure to a specific label on each return type, including the trust return, and says what the amount holds.
evidence_quote: Show the total amount of any deduction under temporary full expensing you claimed at Depreciation expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which return item the figure comes from or what it says about the firm.

value_domain: Count of depreciating assets excluded from temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: How many depreciating assets the business deliberately kept out of temporary full expensing in the year, so they depreciate under the ordinary rules instead. The ATO instruction is plain: "Write at Q the number of assets for which you have made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing." The choice is made asset by asset and cannot be revoked once made, and it reads alongside the value of the opted-out assets on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A whole number of assets, at label Q of item 9 on the company return and at the matching labels of the trust, partnership and individual returns. It exists only for the income years in which temporary full expensing applied, broadly 2020-21 to 2022-23.
limitation: A count is not a size: one opted-out asset can be worth more than fifty, so the number cannot rank firms by the investment involved. Firms using the simplified depreciation rules cannot opt out at all, so they are absent rather than at zero, and the ATO treats the figure as best-effort rather than exact.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the ATO's own capital allowances label wording, and the company tax return instructions define what the number counts and when the choice can be made.
evidence_quote: Write at Q the number of assets for which you have made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said what opting out means or which years the label exists for.

value_domain: Dollar value of assets excluded from temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The immediate deduction the business gave up by opting out of temporary full expensing, measured as what it would otherwise have written off. The ATO is explicit that this is a counterfactual: "The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out." It pairs with the count of opted-out assets, so the two together give an average value per asset foregone.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount at label R of item 9 on the company return, reported for the income years in which temporary full expensing applied. It is a deduction not taken, not a purchase price and not a written-down value.
limitation: Nothing is lost to the firm here, only deferred: the opted-out assets still depreciate over later years, so reading this as forgone investment or forgone tax relief overstates it. The ATO also accepts a best attempt at the figure, so it is a reasonable estimate rather than a reconciled account balance.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO label for the value of opted-out assets, and the company return instructions define exactly how that value is worked out.
evidence_quote: The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the ATO label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that the amount is a counterfactual deduction rather than a cost.

value_domain: TFN withholding credit retained by the trustee (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2021 instructions, item 57 Statements of distribution
variable_description: Credit for tax withheld from the trust's interest, dividends and unit trust distributions because no tax file number was quoted, held against income no beneficiary is entitled to. The ATO directs that "If there is trust income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, show that share of the credit for the TFN amounts withheld at E under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled". The trustee claims this credit rather than any beneficiary, so a figure here marks income the trust retained and was itself assessed on.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2021 instructions, item 57 Statements of distribution
value_definition: A dollar credit in whole dollars, reported in the no-beneficiary block at the end of item 57 of the trust return. Where the trust has no net income, the whole of the withheld amount is shown here rather than apportioned to beneficiaries.
limitation: It records an identification failure by an investment body, not the size of the trust's investments, and because withholding applies at the top rate a modest amount of income produces a large credit. A zero is the normal case and says nothing about whether the trust held investments at all.
rationale: The BLADE variable name marks the no-beneficiary block, and the ATO's statement of distribution instructions define what the TFN amount withheld at label E is and when it falls to the trustee rather than a beneficiary.
evidence_quote: If there is trust income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled, show that share of the credit for the TFN amounts withheld at E under Income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled at the end of item 57 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'TFN amounts withheld' with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never said whose credit it is or that the row is the trustee-assessed slice of income.

value_domain: TFN withholding credit on interest income (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 11 Gross interest
variable_description: Tax a bank or other investment body held back from the entity's interest income because no tax file number had been given to it. The ATO instruction is to "Show at label I any TFN amounts withheld from gross interest where a TFN has not been provided to the investment body." It is a credit against the entity's own tax, and it sits directly beside gross interest at label J, which is the income the withholding came out of.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 11 Gross interest
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 11 label I of the partnership and trust returns, supported by the investment body's own payment records rather than by any calculation on the return.
limitation: It covers interest only, so TFN withholding on dividends and on unit trust distributions is at other labels and adding this column alone understates the total. A figure here says a registration step was missed with one payer, not that the entity lacks a tax file number, and the credit flows through to partners or beneficiaries rather than being tax the entity finally bears.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's own label for item 11, and the partnership return instructions define the amount and tie it to the gross interest label on the same item.
evidence_quote: Show at label I any TFN amounts withheld from gross interest where a TFN has not been provided to the investment body.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing said why an amount appears or what it can be compared with.

value_domain: Unused tax losses carried into future years (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
variable_description: The stock of unused tax losses the business carries into later years, after losses deducted this year and after any losses carried back. The ATO defines it as "the unapplied (undeducted or not transferred) amount of tax losses incurred by the company and carried forward to a later income year under section 36-17 of the ITAA 1997". It is a balance at year end rather than the loss made this year, and it deliberately excludes net capital losses, which are carried forward at a separate label.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2023 instructions, item 13 Losses information
value_definition: A dollar balance at the end of the income year, at item 13 label U of the company return. It must agree with the total in part A of the losses schedule where one is required.
limitation: A carried-forward loss is not a deduction the firm can rely on: it must still pass the continuity of ownership or business continuity test, so the balance overstates what will ever be used. It also pools losses from many past years, so it cannot date the trading loss that produced it, and a subsidiary member of a consolidated group does not complete the label at all.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's item 13 label wording, and the company return instructions give the statutory definition and the exclusions that determine what the balance contains.
evidence_quote: Write at item 13 – label U the unapplied (undeducted or not transferred) amount of tax losses incurred by the company and carried forward to a later income year under section 36-17 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing distinguished the balance from the current-year loss or flagged the loss recoupment tests.

value_domain: Assessable gains from financial arrangements under Division 230 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 31 Taxation of financial arrangements
variable_description: Gains the business brought to account on financial arrangements under the taxation of financial arrangements rules, disclosed as one total. The ATO asks the lodger to "Print at label M Total TOFA gains the trust's total assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements." The amounts are already inside the income items elsewhere on the return, so this is a disclosure of how much of the return is driven by Division 230 rather than an extra slab of income.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 31 Taxation of financial arrangements
value_definition: A dollar total at the TOFA item of the return, aggregating gains taken up under the accruals, realisation, fair value, foreign exchange retranslation, hedging, financial reports and balancing adjustment methods.
limitation: Coverage is a threshold, not a census: the rules reach entities with roughly $100 million of aggregated turnover, $300 million of assets or $100 million of financial assets, with lower entry points for financial sector entities, so a blank means the business sat outside the regime rather than that it held no financial arrangements. Smaller entities may also elect in, so the covered set is not a clean size cut.
rationale: The DIL label matches the ATO's TOFA label, and the return instructions define the label and set out the entity thresholds that decide who reports it.
evidence_quote: Print at label M Total TOFA gains the trust’s total assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label and used the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amounts double up with income reported elsewhere or that reporting is threshold-bound.

value_domain: Deductible losses from financial arrangements under Division 230 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 31 Taxation of financial arrangements
variable_description: Losses on financial arrangements the business took as deductions under Division 230, the mirror of the TOFA gains total on the same row. The ATO instruction is to "Print at label N Total TOFA losses the trust's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements." Read together with the gains total, it gives the gross scale of a firm's financial arrangement activity, which the netted income items on the rest of the return hide.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 31 Taxation of financial arrangements
value_definition: A dollar total at the TOFA item, covering losses recognised under any of the Division 230 methods and picked up wherever the underlying amounts sit in the income and expense items.
limitation: Gains and losses here are not two sides of one position, so subtracting one from the other does not give trading profit: each method brings amounts to account on its own timing, and hedging and fair value can put a gain and a loss on unrelated instruments in the same year. Nothing identifies which instruments produced the loss.
rationale: The DIL label matches the ATO's TOFA loss label, and the same instructions define the label and list the recognition methods that determine when a loss is taken up.
evidence_quote: Print at label N Total TOFA losses the trust's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing warned against netting the two TOFA totals.

value_domain: Gross business income, non-primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: All income the business earned from activities other than primary production, before any expense is taken off. It is the non-primary production column of the return's business income block, which the ATO builds as "the total of all income items at labels C, D, B, E, F, G and H" - gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, payments subject to foreign resident withholding, assessable government industry payments and other business income. Set against the primary production column on the same row it splits a mixed farming-and-trading business.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount in the non-primary production column of the business income block on the partnership and trust returns, taken from the accounting system before any tax reconciliation adjustment.
limitation: It is not the entity's revenue: interest, dividends, rent, foreign source income and distributions from other partnerships and trusts are reported at their own items and never reach this total. Because the figure is an accounting amount, the deductible and assessable position is settled by the reconciliation items further down the return.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's business income total split by production type, and the partnership return instructions state exactly which income labels the total is built from.
evidence_quote: Show the total of all income items at labels C , D , B , E , F , G and H .
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Total Business Income - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said which income items are inside the total or which are excluded.

value_domain: Gross business income, primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: All income from the business's primary production activities - farming, forestry, fishing and the like - before expenses. Primary production has its own column because it carries concessions the rest of the return does not, including income averaging and farm management deposits. The ATO totals the column across the same income row as the non-primary production column, "the total of all income items at labels C, D, B, E, F, G and H", except that foreign resident withholding has no primary production entry, so assessable government industry payments such as drought and disaster support land here alongside crop and livestock proceeds.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount in the primary production column of the business income block on the partnership and trust returns, drawn from the accounting system for the income year.
limitation: The split follows the activity, not the entity, so a trading company with a small grazing block reports a primary production figure while remaining an ordinary business in every other respect. A zero cannot be read as no farming, because a loss-making season shows in the expense side and in the reconciliation items rather than as negative income here.
rationale: The DIL label is the primary production side of the ATO's business income total, and the partnership return instructions define how the total is assembled from the income labels.
evidence_quote: Show the total of all income items at labels C , D , B , E , F , G and H .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total Business Income - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained why the return splits income by production type or what a zero means.

value_domain: Book value of total assets at year end (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What the business owned at the end of the income year, at the book values in its own financial statements. The ATO asks the lodger to "Write at E all assets of the company, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets and all current assets", and the trust return carries the same figure in its key financial information block. It is a stock at a single date, which is what separates it from the income and expense items on the return, all of which are flows over the year.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar balance at the last day of the income year, at item 8 label E of the company return and item 34 of the trust return. It sits above all current assets, which is a subset of it.
limitation: Book value is not market value and self-generated intangibles are largely absent, so the column systematically understates knowledge-intensive firms against asset-heavy ones. Where the entity was a subsidiary member of a consolidated group the amount covers only the latest non-membership period, so a year-on-year change can be an artefact of group membership.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's own balance sheet label, and the company return instructions state what the amount must include and how consolidated group members report it.
evidence_quote: Write at E all assets of the company, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets and all current assets as written at D All current assets item 8 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total assets' with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said it is an accounting stock or how consolidation affects it.

value_domain: Total expenses reported on the face of the return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Everything the business booked as an expense on the face of the return, from cost of sales through to all other expenses. The ATO defines it as "the total of all expense items written at B to S item 6", and subtracting it from total income gives the total profit or loss reported on the next label. These are accounting amounts, so the deductions actually allowed are settled by the reconciliation items further down the return.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
value_definition: A dollar total at item 6 label Q of the company return, the sum of the individual expense labels for the income year.
limitation: It is not a deduction total: expense reconciliation adjustments add back non-deductible amounts, and capital allowances, tax losses and offsets claimed elsewhere never pass through here. A negative cost of sales can also pull the total below the sum of the individual expenses, which the ATO marks with an L indicator that a numeric extract will not carry.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's expense total, and the company return instructions state which labels it aggregates and how the total relates to reported profit.
evidence_quote: Write at Q the total of all expense items written at B to S item 6 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing warned that accounting expenses are not tax deductions.

value_domain: Total income reported on the face of the return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: Everything the business counted as income on the face of the return, added up before any expense is taken off. The ATO defines it as "the total of all income items written at B to R item 6", which takes in gross sales, gross distributions from partnerships and trusts, gross interest, rent and leasing, dividends, forestry scheme income and unrealised gains. It is an accounting revenue line rather than taxable income, and the ATO allows it to be a loss.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
value_definition: A dollar total at item 6 label S of the company return, the sum of the income labels for the income year, with a loss marked by an indicator rather than a negative sign on the form.
limitation: Taxable income is several steps further on: the reconciliation items add and subtract, and a firm with very large total income can end the return with nil tax. Because the figure comes from the financial statements it also moves with accounting policy and with group structure, so a jump need not mean the business grew.
rationale: The DIL label carries the ATO's own gloss that this is the total of the items under the income heading, and the company return instructions state exactly which labels are summed.
evidence_quote: Write at S the total of all income items written at B to R item 6 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the label text with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing separated accounting income from taxable income.

value_domain: Book value of total liabilities at year end (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What the business owed at the end of the income year, current and long term, at book values from its own accounts. The ATO asks for "all liabilities of the company, including other creditors and deferred liabilities such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans", inclusive of the all-current-liabilities figure recorded just above it. Set against total assets on the same row it gives book net worth, which is the closest thing on the return to a balance sheet.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar balance at the last day of the income year, at item 8 label H of the company return and item 36 of the trust return.
limitation: A year-end snapshot misses debt raised and repaid inside the year, which is why the return asks separately for average total debt at the thin capitalisation label. Related-party and shareholder loans are not separated out, so apparent gearing in a private group can be internal rather than borrowed from a bank.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's balance sheet liability label, and the company return instructions state what the amount must include and how it nests with current liabilities.
evidence_quote: Write at H all liabilities of the company, including other creditors and deferred liabilities such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total liabilities' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a point-in-time book figure or how it differs from average total debt.

value_domain: Salary, wage and other labour costs (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: What the business spent on labour it employed, including directors' remuneration and the wage component buried inside cost of sales. The ATO defines it as "the total salary, wage and other labour costs incurred, including directors' remuneration, as per income statements", covering bonuses, casual labour, holiday and long service leave, overtime and incentive payments. It deliberately excludes contract and sub-contract payments, agency fees, superannuation, consultant fees and government-reimbursed wages, which sit at other expense labels.
description_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 8 label D of the company return, accompanied by a code showing where the salary and wage component was reported when it was folded into the expense items.
limitation: It counts dollars, not people, so it cannot give headcount and it rises with wage rates as readily as with employment. Because labour hire and contractor payments are excluded, a firm that moves work to contractors shows a falling wage bill without shedding labour, and superannuation is missing so it understates total employment cost.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's own label, and the company return instructions list in detail what is inside the total and what is deliberately kept out of it.
evidence_quote: Write at D the total salary, wage and other labour costs incurred, including directors’ remuneration, as per income statements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said that contractors and superannuation are excluded or that the column carries no headcount.

value_domain: ATO trust assessment calculation code
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2021 instructions, item 57 Statements of distribution
variable_description: Which assessing situation the trustee is taxed under for the slice of trust income that no beneficiary is entitled to. The ATO requires a code "for each beneficiary presently entitled to a share of the income of the trust... and also for income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled and in which no beneficiary has an indefeasible vested interest". In the trustee-assessed part of the code table, 36 covers a resident or non-resident trust where no beneficiary is presently entitled, 37 covers a bankrupt estate and the case where subsection 99A(2) of the ITAA 1936 is applied, and deceased estates use 15, 16 or 17 according to how long ago the deceased died and whether the trust is a non-resident.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2021 instructions, item 57 Statements of distribution
value_definition: A two or three digit code from the ATO's Appendix 12 trust assessment code table, where inter vivos trusts and deceased estates use different ranges and a leading 1 marks the non-resident beneficiary variant. The valid response text points to Appendix 3 of the BLADE data item list, which reproduces the same table.
limitation: The code names the assessing situation, not the amount assessed or the tax paid, and one code covers unlike cases: bankrupt estates share code 37 with trusts to which subsection 99A(2) is applied. It also says nothing about income assessed to beneficiaries in their own right, which is the bulk of trust income.
rationale: The variable name marks the no-beneficiary block of the statement of distribution, and the ATO instructions define when the code is required there and which codes cover a trustee assessment.
evidence_quote: Insert an assessment calculation code from Appendix 12 for each beneficiary presently entitled to a share of the income of the trust ... and also for income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled and in which no beneficiary has an indefeasible vested interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Assessment calculation code' and pointed at an appendix, with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the codes distinguish or why it matters for tax.

value_domain: Trust distribution excluded from non-concessional MIT income, non-primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
variable_description: Non-primary production income the business received from another trust that falls outside the non-concessional managed investment trust rules and so keeps concessional treatment. The ATO instruction is to print at label L "the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as non-primary production", and to carry the same amount into the share of net income from trusts at item 8 label R. It is the benign half of a pair: the NCMI column beside it is the income that loses the concession.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 32 label L of the trust return, capped by the paying entity's own reporting and duplicated inside the item 8 trust distribution label.
limitation: The exclusion is a status of the paying trust - transitional arrangements or an approved economic infrastructure facility - not a property of the business on this row, so the column describes where income came from rather than what the recipient does. Because the amount also sits inside the item 8 distribution, adding the two double counts.
rationale: The DIL label maps onto the trust distribution, non-primary production, excluded-from-NCMI cell of ATO item 32, and the instructions define that cell and state where the amount must also appear.
evidence_quote: Excluded from NCMI Print at label L the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Net income from trust - Excluded from NCMI - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what NCMI is or that the amount is duplicated elsewhere on the return.

value_domain: Trust distribution that is non-concessional MIT income, non-primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
variable_description: Non-primary production income from another trust that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, meaning it loses the concessional managed investment trust withholding treatment. The ATO instruction is to "Print at label K the total NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as non-primary production", and to carry the same amount into the item 8 share of net income from trusts. The non-primary production NCMI category is the one the ATO describes on the same item as "cross staple income, trading trust income and residential housing income", reflecting the stapled structures measures that targeted arrangements recasting trading income as passive rent.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 32 label K of the trust return, bounded by the totals the paying trust reported and repeated inside the item 8 trust distribution label.
limitation: It flags a tax character rather than an economic activity: the same rent is NCMI or not depending on how the paying structure is arranged, so the column cannot identify what the underlying business does. Treating it as income additional to the item 8 distribution overstates the recipient's receipts.
rationale: The DIL label maps onto the trust distribution, non-primary production, NCMI cell of ATO item 32, and the instructions define that cell and name the income types in the non-primary production NCMI category.
evidence_quote: Non-concessional MIT income (NCMI) Print at label K the total NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said why the return separates NCMI or what it implies about the paying structure.

value_domain: Non-resident trust indicator (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 60 Non-resident trust
variable_description: Whether the trust was foreign for tax purposes across the whole income year, which decides how much of its income Australia can tax. The ATO's test is strict: a trust is a non-resident "if no trustee of the trust was a resident of Australia, at any time during the income year, or the central management and control of the trust was not in Australia at any time during the income year". A yes also obliges the trust to report the income it derived outside Australia to which no beneficiary is presently entitled.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 60 Non-resident trust
value_definition: A single character flag: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else an invalid or missing response, answered at item 60 of the trust return.
limitation: Residence is all or nothing here, so a trust with an Australian trustee for even part of the year is simply not a non-resident and the flag cannot show a change of residence mid-year. It also says nothing about where the trust's assets, income or beneficiaries are, which are separate disclosures at the overseas transactions item.
rationale: The DIL question is the ATO's item 60 question, and the trust return instructions give the residence test that determines the answer and the extra reporting a yes triggers.
evidence_quote: A trust is a non-resident of Australia if: no trustee of the trust was a resident of Australia, at any time during the income year, or the central management and control of the trust was not in Australia at any time during the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question and its Y/N codes with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing gave the residence test or said what a yes obliges the trust to report.

value_domain: Trust distribution excluded from non-concessional MIT income, primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
variable_description: Primary production income distributed to the business from another trust that sits outside the non-concessional managed investment trust rules. The ATO instruction is to print at label H "the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as primary production income", and to include the same amount at item 8 label Z, share of net income from trusts. It is the concessionally treated counterpart of the primary production NCMI column beside it.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 32 label H of the trust return, bounded by the paying trust's own reporting and repeated inside the item 8 primary production trust distribution.
limitation: The primary production tag follows the character of the income in the paying trust, so a passive investor in an agricultural trust carries a primary production figure without farming anything. The exclusion also rests on transitional arrangements with expiry dates, so the split between the excluded and NCMI columns is not stable from year to year.
rationale: The DIL label maps onto the trust distribution, primary production, excluded-from-NCMI cell of ATO item 32, and the instructions define that cell and where the amount must also be shown.
evidence_quote: Excluded from NCMI Print at label H the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as primary production income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said whose activity the primary production tag describes.

value_domain: Trust distribution that is non-concessional MIT income, primary production (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
variable_description: Primary production income from another trust that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, so it loses the concessional managed investment trust withholding rate. The ATO instruction is to print at label G "the total NCMI amount distributed from a trust categorised as primary production income" and to include the same amount in the item 8 share of net income from trusts. The ATO's example of primary production NCMI on the same item is income attributable to agricultural land held for rent, which is why a figure here often marks a landlord rather than a producer.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 32 Non-concessional MIT income
value_definition: A dollar amount at item 32 label G of the trust return, capped against the paying trust's reported totals and duplicated inside the item 8 primary production trust distribution.
limitation: It does not mean the business farms: NCMI attaches to rent from agricultural land as readily as to production income, so the column identifies a landlord as often as a producer. The amount is a share of a total reported by the paying trust rather than an independently verified receipt.
rationale: The DIL label maps onto the trust distribution, primary production, NCMI cell of ATO item 32, and the instructions define the label and give agricultural land held for rent as the example of primary production NCMI.
evidence_quote: Non-concessional MIT income (NCMI) Print at label G the total NCMI amount distributed from a trust categorised as primary production income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said that a primary production NCMI amount usually signals rent rather than farming.

value_domain: Managed investment trust capital account election indicator (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Type of trust and managed investment trusts
variable_description: Whether a managed investment trust has elected to treat gains and losses on its eligible assets on capital account rather than revenue account. The ATO explains that the rules "allow the trustee of an eligible MIT to irrevocably choose to apply the capital gains tax provisions for the taxation of gains and losses on disposal of eligible assets, rather than on revenue account." The answer decides whether a disposal produces a capital gain, and so whether the CGT discount can reach the trust's investors.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Type of trust and managed investment trusts
value_definition: A single character flag - Y, N, or anything else for an invalid or missing response - answered in the managed investment trust block of the trust return, and only where the trust answered yes to being a managed investment trust.
limitation: Missing is the normal case rather than a defect, because the ATO tells a trust that is not a MIT to leave the question blank, and BLADE folds those blanks into the same residual as invalid responses - so absence cannot be read as an eligible MIT that declined. The election also has to be made in the first year the trust qualifies, so an N is close to permanent and is not a decision revisited each year.
rationale: The DIL question is the ATO's own managed investment trust question, and the trust return instructions explain the election, its irrevocability, the first-year deadline and when the question is left blank.
evidence_quote: The MIT capital treatment rules allow the trustee of an eligible MIT to irrevocably choose to apply the capital gains tax provisions for the taxation of gains and losses on disposal of eligible assets, rather than on revenue account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said what the election does or why an N is uninformative.

value_domain: ATO trust type code
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Type of trust
variable_description: What kind of trust lodged the return - discretionary, fixed, unit, deceased estate, special disability or testamentary. The ATO asks for "the code from table 1 that best describes the type of trust for which the trust tax return is being lodged", and defines a discretionary trust as one "that is not a fixed trust within the meaning of section 272-5 of Schedule 2F to the ITAA 1936". The three discretionary codes split further by main source of income - service and management, trading, or investment - which is the closest thing in the data to what a family trust actually does.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Type of trust
value_definition: A two-digit BLADE code pairing the ATO letter code with its label, running 5 to 65: S, T and I for the three discretionary types, D deceased estate, M cash management unit trust, P and Q listed and unlisted public unit trusts, U fixed unit trust, F fixed trust, H hybrid, C special disability trust, R refund of franking credits claimant and E testamentary trust.
limitation: The code is a best fit chosen at lodgment and not tested, so the split of discretionary trusts by service, trading or investment activity is a self-description rather than an audited classification. It describes legal form, not size or industry, and it can change between years without anything about the trust changing.
rationale: The BLADE value list follows the ATO trust code table, letter for letter apart from the refund of franking credits claimant code R that the 2022 table does not carry, and the ATO page defines each type and states how the code is chosen.
evidence_quote: Print in the first box at this item the code from table 1 that best describes the type of trust for which the trust tax return is being lodged.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed 'Type of trust' with the code list attached and the generic no-value-list sentence used as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the categories mean or how reliable the coding is.

value_domain: Withholding credit where no ABN was quoted (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, items 5 to 15 Income excluding foreign income
variable_description: Tax that payers held back from the business because it did not quote an Australian Business Number on its invoices, claimed back on the return as a credit. The ATO ties the credit to the income it came out of: "If you complete label C or D, print the corresponding amount of tax withheld at item 6 - label T Tax withheld where ABN not quoted." An amount here signals a business trading without quoting an ABN to at least one payer, which is unusual and usually a registration or contracting problem rather than a tax planning choice.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, items 5 to 15 Income excluding foreign income
value_definition: A dollar credit at item 6 label T of the trust and partnership returns, paired with gross payments where an ABN was not quoted in the business income block, and supported by a non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule.
limitation: It measures a compliance gap, not turnover: withholding applies at the top rate to the whole payment, so a small amount of unquoted work produces a disproportionately large credit. The column cannot say whether the business held an ABN at all, only that one was not quoted to the payer who withheld.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's item 6 label, and the trust return income instructions state the link between the gross payment labels and the withheld amount reported at label T.
evidence_quote: If you complete label C or D , print the corresponding amount of tax withheld at item 6 – label T Tax withheld where ABN not quoted .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what causes an amount to appear or that the credit is disproportionate to the work involved.

value_domain: Share of withholding credit where no ABN was quoted (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The business's slice of an ABN-not-quoted withholding credit that arose inside a partnership or trust it invests in, rather than on its own invoices. The ATO instruction is that where the distributed income "includes any share of amounts that have had tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, show any share of credit for the tax withheld at label C", and the paying entity's distribution statement must disclose the share separately. It is the indirect counterpart of the withholding credit a business claims for its own unquoted payments.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, item 8 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A dollar credit in whole dollars at item 8 label C, worked out from the recipient's share of the paying entity's net income, which the paying entity's statement of distribution or advice must disclose separately.
limitation: The compliance failure belongs to the underlying partnership or trust, not to the business on this row, so reading it as this firm's ABN problem is the mistake to avoid. Because the share follows each party's share of the paying entity's income, it moves when entitlements change even if the amount withheld does not.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's item 8 share label, and the partnership return instructions define whose withholding it is and how each recipient's share is calculated.
evidence_quote: If the income shown at label A , Z , B , R or F includes any share of amounts that have had tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, show any share of credit for the tax withheld at label C .
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing distinguished the share credit from the direct withholding credit at item 6.

value_domain: Credit for foreign tax forgone under a tax sparing article (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, credit for notional tax forgone by developing countries
variable_description: Credit claimed for foreign tax the business never actually paid, because a treaty partner waived it under a development incentive and a tax sparing article preserves the Australian credit anyway. The ATO explains that "Certain double taxation agreements with developing countries provide for 'tax sparing'" and that "If tax sparing applies to a tax incentive, you can claim a credit for tax forgone by a treaty partner under the incentive." An amount here marks a business operating in a treaty partner that granted it a tax holiday or concession.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, credit for notional tax forgone by developing countries
value_definition: A dollar amount of notional foreign tax credited, distinct from the ordinary foreign income tax offset for tax actually paid. The taxes eligible for sparing are listed in each double taxation agreement rather than in the return.
limitation: It is not evidence of tax paid anywhere, which is exactly the confusion the label invites, because the point of tax sparing is that the foreign tax was forgone. The label belongs to the foreign tax credit system replaced from 1 July 2008 by the foreign income tax offset, so a series that crosses that change is not measuring one thing.
rationale: The ATO guide defines tax sparing and the credit for notional tax forgone, which is the only mechanism the DIL label can refer to; the mapping to a particular return label is inferred from the label wording rather than published.
evidence_quote: Certain double taxation agreements with developing countries provide for 'tax sparing'. Tax sparing preserves taxation incentives which are provided by a treaty partner to promote economic development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Tax spared foreign tax credits' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing explained that the credit is for tax that was never paid.

value_domain: Dealings with ATO-specified countries indicator (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 29 Overseas transactions
variable_description: Whether the business sent funds or property to, received them from, or could control assets in any of the countries on the ATO's specified list at the overseas transactions item. The question reaches beyond transfers to control: the ATO asks whether the entity has "the ability to control the disposition of any funds, property, investments, or any other assets located in any of the countries listed below", including indirectly through another entity or country. A yes is a risk disclosure that helps target compliance work rather than a measure of anything.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 29 Overseas transactions
value_definition: A single character flag - Y, N, or anything else for an invalid or missing response - at label C of the overseas transactions item. The specified country list is published with the instructions and runs from Andorra and Anguilla through Caribbean, European, Gulf and Pacific jurisdictions to Vanuatu.
limitation: The list is published with each year's instructions rather than fixed in the law, so any comparison across years should check the list for that year rather than assume it is unchanged. No amount accompanies the flag, so it cannot separate a single small payment from a substantial offshore structure.
rationale: The DIL question is the ATO's overseas transactions question, and the return instructions state both limbs of the test and publish the list of specified countries it applies to.
evidence_quote: Did you send any funds or property to, or receive any funds or property from, any of the countries listed below? This includes sending or receiving funds or property indirectly, through another entity or country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question with its Y/N codes and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which countries are specified or that control counts as well as transfers.

value_domain: ATO trust type code, shorter code list
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Type of trust
variable_description: The legal type of a trust estate, coded on the shorter of the two ATO trust code lists. The list stops at special disability trust and carries neither the refund of franking credits claimant code nor the testamentary code. The ATO's list runs from discretionary trusts split by "service and/or management activities", "trading activities" and "investment activities" through fixed trusts, hybrid trusts and listed and unlisted public unit trusts. Nothing published explains why this column carries a shorter list than the type of trust column beside it, so treat the two as related but not interchangeable.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Type of trust
value_definition: A two-digit BLADE code pairing the ATO letter code with its label, running 5 to 55 across the eleven trust types from discretionary service and management through to special disability trust.
limitation: It shares its wording with the type-of-trust column but not its full code list, so the two cannot be pooled across entity types or years. The custodian label restricts it to trust returns, and because the code is a best fit chosen at lodgment rather than a tested classification, the split of discretionary trusts by service, trading or investment activity is a self-description.
rationale: The BLADE value list is the ATO trust code table minus the two codes this shorter table omits, and the ATO page defines every type in that list; nothing published explains why the two BLADE trust type columns differ.
evidence_quote: Print in the first box at this item the code from table 1 that best describes the type of trust for which the trust tax return is being lodged.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Type of trust estate (trust only)' with the code list attached and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said how its code list differs from the type-of-trust column beside it.

value_domain: Division 7A transaction code on an unpaid present entitlement
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, item 47 Unpaid present entitlement to a private company
variable_description: Whether the trustee did anything during the year with an unpaid entitlement owed to a private company that could bring Division 7A into play. The ATO asks for code D where the trustee, in favour of a shareholder or associate of that company, "made a payment that is attributable to an unrealised gain that discharged or reduced a present entitlement", made a loan, or forgave a debt, and code X "if none of the above transactions took place". BLADE stores 5 for X and 10 for D.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, item 47 Unpaid present entitlement to a private company
value_definition: A two-digit BLADE code standing for the ATO letter code: 5 for X, no such transaction, and 10 for D, at least one of the three transactions occurred. It is only completed where the unpaid present entitlement amount on the same row is greater than zero.
limitation: A single code covers three quite different acts, so it cannot say whether the trustee paid out an unrealised gain, lent money or forgave a debt, nor how large any of them was. It is self-assessed at lodgment, so it records what the trustee reported rather than what the Commissioner later determined.
rationale: The BLADE value labels reproduce the ATO's D and X code descriptions word for word, and the trust return instructions define both codes and the condition under which the code box is completed.
evidence_quote: Print X in the CODE box at label Y if none of the above transactions took place.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw code list with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing said what the codes are for or that they only apply when an entitlement is outstanding.

value_domain: Unpaid present entitlement owed to a private company (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, item 47 Unpaid present entitlement to a private company
variable_description: How much trust income a private company beneficiary was entitled to but had still not been paid by the trust's lodgment day. The ATO asks for "any amounts of the income of the trust from this year or a previous year of income to which a private company is entitled, and that remain unpaid by the lodgment day", where the lodgment day is the earlier of the due date and the actual date of lodgment. A balance here is the classic private group arrangement that Division 7A polices, and it pairs with the transaction code on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2024 instructions, item 47 Unpaid present entitlement to a private company
value_definition: A dollar balance at the lodgment day, cumulative across income years rather than a flow for the year, at label Y of the trust return's business and professional items.
limitation: It is a balance owed to private companies in general, so it cannot be attributed to a named company or reconciled against any one loan account. Whether it is actually taxed as a deemed dividend turns on sub-trust and complying loan arrangements the return does not record, so a large figure is not by itself a Division 7A liability.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's item 47 label, and the trust return instructions define what the amount covers and fix the lodgment day it is measured at.
evidence_quote: Show at label Y Unpaid present entitlement to a private company any amounts of the income of the trust from this year or a previous year of income to which a private company is entitled, and that remain unpaid by the lodgment day .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the balance is cumulative or explained why the lodgment day matters.

value_domain: Personal services business unrelated clients test indicator (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the entity self-assessed that an individual's personal services income passed the unrelated clients test, one of the routes out of the personal services income rules. The ATO's condition is that "the individual doing the personal services work generates PSI from two or more clients who are not associated with each other, or with the individual, or with you, and those clients were obtained as a direct result of making offers to the public, for example, by advertising." Clients found through a labour hire firm or placement agency are expressly not counted.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, item 30 Personal services income
value_definition: A single character flag - Y, N, or anything else for an invalid or missing response - at label E1 of the personal services income item on the trust, partnership and company returns.
limitation: The label is only reached where the results test failed, there is no personal services business determination, and no single client supplied 80% or more of the individual's PSI, so a blank usually means the question never arose rather than that the test was failed. The answer is a self-assessment the ATO can reject on review, and it says nothing about the amount of personal services income involved.
rationale: The DIL label is the ATO's label E1, and the return instructions define the test, the gateway conditions for completing the label and the exclusions that apply to it.
evidence_quote: You will meet the unrelated clients test in the income year if: the individual doing the personal services work generates PSI from two or more clients who are not associated with each other, or with the individual, or with you, and those clients were obtained as a direct result of making offers to the public, for example, by advertising.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Unrelated clients test' with its Y/N codes and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the test requires or why most entities leave it blank.

value_domain: Instant asset write-off deductions, non-small business entities (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instant asset write-off for eligible businesses
variable_description: Immediate deductions a medium or large business claimed under the instant asset write-off, in the short window when the concession reached past small business. The ATO describes the deduction as an entitlement to write off "the business portion of the cost of an asset in the year the asset is first used or installed ready for use", subject to a per-asset limit that for these firms was $30,000 for aggregated turnover under $50 million from April 2019 and $150,000 for turnover under $500 million to 30 June 2021. The label sat at item 9 of the company return and was removed from the 2022 return when temporary full expensing replaced it.
description_source: ATO, Instant asset write-off for eligible businesses
value_definition: A dollar amount of deductions claimed in the income year at the former label O of the company return's capital allowances item, present only for the years in which non-small businesses were eligible.
limitation: It is a deduction claimed, not investment made: assets costing at or above the limit are absent entirely and are pooled or depreciated instead, so the column measures the tail of a firm's capital spending. Because the label was removed from the 2022 return, a series that continues past 2020-21 records the end of a policy rather than a change in business behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-small business form of the instant asset write-off, and the ATO page defines the deduction and publishes the separate turnover thresholds and limits that applied to businesses above the small business threshold.
evidence_quote: Eligible businesses can claim an immediate deduction for the business portion of the cost of an asset in the year the asset is first used or installed ready for use.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so nothing gave the thresholds, the per-asset limit or the years the label existed.

value_domain: Tantalum content of an exported ore shipment (per cent)
value_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
variable_description: The assayed tantalum content of an exported ore or concentrate shipment, given as a share of the gross tonnage. Tantalum is almost always recovered alongside something else, from tantalite and from tin slags, so this grade usually sits on a line that carries other metal percentages for the same shipment. Multiplied by the shipment weight it gives contained tantalum, which is how the trade is priced.
description_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
value_definition: A percentage attached to an export transaction classified under the AHECC, which the ABS describes as "the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia" and which currently follows the seventh edition of the Harmonized System, HS2022.
limitation: It cannot be averaged over a firm's exports without weighting by tonnage, and it is blank on every line that is not ore or concentrate, so a miner's overall grade cannot be rebuilt from it. It is also the declared assay rather than the payable content settled after smelter deductions, so it will not reconcile with the firm's revenue.
rationale: The ABS AHECC page establishes the export classification that governs the line this percentage qualifies, but no reachable publication documents the metal content field itself, so the business reading is inferred from the export declaration context.
evidence_quote: The Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC) is the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Percentage of tantalum in shipment of ore' with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never said the column is a grade that has to be combined with weight to mean anything.

value_domain: Binary flag for Tasmanian coverage of an agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement operates in Tasmania, one of the per-jurisdiction flags DEWR records as "State or Territories covered". Tasmania is small enough that a single national agreement can dominate a sector there, so a 1 often reflects a mainland employer's national instrument rather than a Tasmanian business. The flags are not mutually exclusive, so they cannot be collapsed into one state variable.
description_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 for yes, 0 for no, held alongside equivalent flags for the other states and territories on the same agreement record.
limitation: It carries no employee weight, so an agreement covering one shop in Hobart and one covering a statewide workforce read the same, and the flag cannot apportion employees between jurisdictions. Coverage follows the agreement, so a 1 does not place the employer's ABN in Tasmania and a 0 does not rule out the firm employing people there under a different instrument.
rationale: The DEWR page lists state and territory coverage among the general details recorded for each federal enterprise agreement, which is what this flag set carries.
evidence_quote: State or Territories covered
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Indicates whether an agreement operates in TAS' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the flags overlap or that they carry no employee weight.

value_domain: Dealroom technology flag, 3D technology
value_source: Dealroom.co, Tech Sector Taxonomy
variable_description: Marks a business Dealroom judges to work with three-dimensional technology, which in its taxonomy spans virtual 3D reconstruction at one end and 3D printing at the other. Dealroom sets the technology fields out as "Core technologies the company uses or develops", so the flag is about the firm's own capability rather than its customers. Because reconstruction and additive manufacturing are quite different businesses, a 1 here needs the industry fields beside it before it means much.
description_source: Dealroom.co, Tech Sector Taxonomy

It is the broadest of the six overlapping AI-related flags in this family, and it usually co-occurs with the machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision and recognition flags.

The tag is also read from how a company describes itself, so it tracks marketing language as much as capability, and a firm that quietly uses AI internally will not carry it.
rationale: The Dealroom taxonomy page publishes the technology field and lists Artificial Intelligence among its values, which is the field this BLADE column carries.

value_domain: Nice class code, most frequent in the live services-only trade mark portfolio, IPLORD
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary
variable_description: The service class that dominates the business's live services-only portfolio at year end. Because it is taken over accumulated holdings, it moves far more slowly than the filed modal class on the same row and describes what the firm has protected rather than what it is protecting now. IPLoRD offers it for a high-level read of an applicant's economic area, not as an exact description of the business.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary
value_definition: A character Nice class code in the services range Nice 35 to 45, taken as the most frequent class among the services-only marks held at the end of the financial year. It is a nominal code, so it cannot be summed or averaged. WIPO reissues the classification regularly, with a new version each year since 2013, and IP Australia classifies on the edition in force when the application was made.
limitation: For a firm holding two or three service marks the portfolio mode is effectively fixed for the life of those registrations, so a panel of this column has almost no within-firm variation to exploit. It also cannot distinguish a firm whose service marks are all in one class from one whose marks are split evenly and broken by a tie.
rationale: The dictionary defines modal value variables and their intended high-level use, and defines the enforceable stockpile over which this mode is taken.

value_domain: Weighted count of live services-only trade marks, IPLORD
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary
variable_description: The business's share of the live services-only marks at the end of the financial year, with jointly held marks split evenly among owners. It is the services slice of the weighted portfolio and exists so that service-brand holdings can be added across firms without a shared registration being counted more than once. The plain services stock column is the one that answers what this business is on the register for.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary
value_definition: A non-negative rational number covering the marks enforceable at the end of the financial year: a right shared by n applicants adds 1/n to each, so the column equals the plain count where the applicant is the sole party and falls below it wherever a mark is jointly held. A right joins the services group only where every class on it falls in Nice 35 to 45, eleven classes against the thirty-four available to goods, and the three trade mark groups are built as disjoint sets.
limitation: The weighting divides ownership, not the ability to act, so a franchisor holding half of a jointly registered service mark can still enforce all of it. Because joint ownership is uncommon, a fraction here is a rare event worth checking rather than a routine adjustment.
rationale: The dictionary defines the 1/n weighting and applies it to the enforceable stockpile within each coarse area; how often trade marks are jointly held is not stated there and is a general observation.
evidence_quote: Weighted count variables consider the number of applicants associated with an IP Right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's applications-fraction-owned-in-services-classes wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the fraction does and does not divide.

value_domain: Count of distinct Nice classes given up on services-only trade marks, IPLORD
value_source: IP Australia, Trade Marks Manual of Practice and Procedure, Part 40.1 What is renewal?
variable_description: How many different service classes the business let lapse during the year on services-only marks. Because renewal runs "at ten year intervals dating from the original filing date", the classes that appear here are those whose renewal fell due and went unpaid, not those the firm decided to abandon this year. On an eleven class range the column is close to binary for most firms.
description_source: IP Australia, Trade Marks Manual of Practice and Procedure, Part 40.1 What is renewal?
value_definition: An integer for one financial year counting distinct Nice classes, drawn from the forty-five class Nice Classification, which IPLoRD carries across unaltered. The ceiling is eleven, over the services-only marks retired that year. WIPO reissues the classification regularly, with a new version each year since 2013, and IP Australia classifies on the edition in force when the application was made.
limitation: The count is bounded by the classes the firm held, so it can never show that a business abandoned service branding it never had, and it gives no sense of proportion: losing one class out of one and one out of eleven look identical. Pairing it with the live services scope is the only way to see how much was left.
rationale: The IP Australia manual defines the ten-year renewal cycle that fixes when a services registration can lapse, and the dictionary defines scope as a count of distinct classification areas.
evidence_quote: A trade mark registration may be renewed at ten year intervals dating from the original filing date of the application for registration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line about services classes the rights holder allowed to retire, with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the timing is fixed by the renewal cycle.

value_domain: Count of services-only trade marks retired, IPLORD
value_source: IP Australia, Trade Marks Manual of Practice and Procedure, Part 40.4 Failure to renew
variable_description: How many of the business's services-only marks fell away during the year. IP Australia's manual states that an unrenewed registration "ceases to have effect after the date of expiry", and that during the six months in which late renewal is still possible the lapsed mark keeps being cited against new applications. With the services granted count it accounts for the change in the live services portfolio on the same row.
description_source: IP Australia, Trade Marks Manual of Practice and Procedure, Part 40.4 Failure to renew
value_definition: A non-negative whole number of trade mark rights retired by one applicant in one financial year, counted once per right however many Nice classes it claims. A right joins the services group only where every class on it falls in Nice 35 to 45, eleven classes against the thirty-four available to goods, and the three trade mark groups are built as disjoint sets.
limitation: The date recorded is the expiry, but a late renewal within the following six months can revive a registration, so a retirement in one year is not always permanent and the stock can move back. Nor can the column separate a service line being closed from a group restructure in which the mark is re-registered by another entity.
rationale: The IP Australia manual sets out what happens when a registration is not renewed, including the six-month window in which late renewal remains possible, which qualifies the retired stream IPLoRD counts.
evidence_quote: If the registration of a trade mark is not renewed, then it ceases to have effect after the date of expiry.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's total-retired-in-services-classes wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said a lapse can be reversed by a late renewal.

value_domain: Nice class code, most frequent among services-only trade marks retired, IPLORD
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary
variable_description: The service class most common among the business's lapsed services-only marks in the year. It is the narrowest of the retirement modal columns, being taken over eleven possible classes and usually over very few marks. IPLoRD names this family by convention, right type then event stream then activity metric, so tm_services_retired_modal_class is the modal class of retired services trade marks.
description_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary
value_definition: A character Nice class code in the services range Nice 35 to 45, taken as the most frequent class among the services-only marks retired in the financial year. It is a nominal code, so it cannot be summed or averaged. WIPO reissues the classification regularly, with a new version each year since 2013, and IP Australia classifies on the edition in force when the application was made.
limitation: In most years a firm retires a single services mark, so the mode is that one mark's class and describes an administrative event rather than a pattern of withdrawal. Reading a sequence of these codes as a path out of service markets over-interprets what is often one renewal notice going unanswered.
rationale: The dictionary sets out the naming convention of right type, event stream and activity metric, and defines modal value variables and the retired event stream.
evidence_quote: Modal value variables record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's most-common-class-for-services-retired wording with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the mode usually rests on a single lapse.

value_domain: Applicant-weighted count of services-class trade marks retired in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many services-class trade marks the business let go during the financial year, counted as a share where the right was held jointly. IPLoRD names variables as right type, then classification area, then event stream, then metric, so this is trade marks, services, retired, weighted count. Services means "having only Nice classifications 35-45", retired means "rights retired during the financial year", and the weighting is that "when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score".
description_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
value_definition: A non-negative number that need not be a whole number, because a jointly held right contributes only a fraction to each applicant. The classification is the Nice system, and the services subset is classes 35 to 45 of the 45 classes.
limitation: It counts rights leaving the register, not marks deliberately abandoned: non-renewal, surrender and removal for non-use all land here and the file records no reason. A firm shedding old marks while filing new ones looks the same as one winding down, so this column only means something read against the matching filed and enforceable counts.
rationale: IPLoRD publishes its naming convention, its event streams and its weighting rule, and the variable name decomposes exactly into those documented parts.
evidence_quote: when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about a retired applications fraction with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what services means, what retired covers, or why the count is fractional.

value_domain: De-identified export transaction line identifier
value_source: ABS, International Trade in Goods methodology, August 2024
variable_description: A key for one commodity line on one export declaration, not for a business, a shipment or a customer. Merchandise trade statistics come from "customs declarations submitted by exporters and importers or their agents to the Department of Home Affairs", and a single declaration carries a separate line for every AHECC code in the consignment. A firm's exports for a year are therefore many tn values, and the identifier is what holds the commodity, country, quantity and value columns of one line together.
description_source: ABS, International Trade in Goods methodology, August 2024
value_definition: A 14-character alphanumeric string, de-identified for BLADE. The characters carry no meaning and impose no ordering.
limitation: Counting distinct tn values counts declaration lines, not export events or consignments, so it is not a measure of how often a firm exported. The identifier also carries no date and no business key, so the reference period and the exporter have to come from neighbouring columns.
