evidence_quote: customs declarations submitted by exporters and importers or their agents to the Department of Home Affairs
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's phrase about a transaction identifier and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what a line is or warned against counting them as export events.

value_domain: Dollar amount of business purchases reported on the activity statement, GST excluded
value_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, Step 3: Purchases
variable_description: What the business told the ATO it spent on purchases in the activity statement period, capital and non-capital added together with GST stripped out. The two underlying labels split by asset life rather than by function: capital items go to G10, and at G11 "you need to report all of your business purchases relevant to the reporting period (other than those reported at G10), such as most business purchases, including services and stock bought for resale". Read against turnover on the same row, it is a purchases margin rather than a profit margin.
description_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, Step 3: Purchases
value_definition: A dollar amount for one activity statement period, being capital purchases at label G10 plus non-capital purchases at label G11, reported excluding GST. Periods are monthly, quarterly or annual depending on how the business lodges.
limitation: These are purchases, not accounting expenses. Wages, superannuation, interest, depreciation and most other GST-free or out-of-scope costs never reach a BAS purchase label, so the figure sits well below a firm's total cost base and subtracting it from turnover does not give profit.
rationale: The custodian's description defines the item as capital plus other expenditure excluding GST, which is the G10 plus G11 pair, and the ATO instruction sets out exactly what belongs at each label.
evidence_quote: At G11, you need to report all of your business purchases relevant to the reporting period (other than those reported at G10), such as most business purchases, including services and stock bought for resale
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the parenthetical formula capex plus oexp and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving a reader to assume the column was total business costs.

value_domain: Cumulative disclosed funding raised, AUD millions
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: How much money Dealroom has been able to observe the business raising in total, in millions of Australian dollars. Dealroom builds the figure by harvesting public sources rather than by collecting accounts, describing its method as applying AI and algorithms to public sources such as news, company filings, registries, job boards, web analytics and investor portfolios. The value is time-invariant, repeated on every row for an ABN, so it is a standing total at extraction rather than a series.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A dollar amount in millions of AUD. Zero marks a funding event with no monetary value, such as an accelerator or support programme place, while a missing value can mean either that nothing is known or that the round was undisclosed.
limitation: It is disclosed funding, not capital raised: an undisclosed round leaves the total unchanged, so the column systematically understates rather than measures. Because the same total is repeated across an ABN's rows, differencing it between years yields zero and cannot recover funding raised in a given year.
rationale: Dealroom publishes how its company data is assembled, which is what determines whether this number is an administrative fact or an observation, and the custodian's own note explains the zero and missing conventions.
evidence_quote: We apply AI and algorithms to gather data from public sources including news, company filings, registries, job boards, web analytics, and investor portfolios.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the figure is harvested rather than reported, nor that it cannot be differenced across years.

value_domain: Dollar amount of R&D feedstock input expenditure for the income year
value_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive schedule instructions, Part B - Feedstock
variable_description: What the business spent on materials that its R&D activities consumed and turned into something saleable during the income year. The ATO instruction for the matching schedule item says to enter "the total amount of feedstock inputs attributable to feedstock outputs on all R&D activities, if those activities have produced products supplied to someone else, or applied to the R&D entity's own use", and it directs the claimant to add into that total the energy put directly into the transformation and the decline in value of the assets used to acquire or produce the inputs. A non-zero figure therefore marks R&D that reached a marketable product, not merely R&D that was expensive.
description_source: ATO, Research and development tax incentive schedule instructions, Part B - Feedstock
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, covering goods and materials transformed or processed in R&D activities, plus the energy input directly into that transformation and the decline in value of assets used in acquiring or producing those inputs.
limitation: The item exists to trigger a clawback, not to measure research: a value here feeds a feedstock adjustment that adds income back, so it is a signal about the tax outcome rather than about R&D intensity. Firms whose R&D produced no marketable product leave the item blank, so blank means the schedule part was not required rather than that nothing was spent.
rationale: The custodian's description names spending on feedstock inputs for the income period, which is the schedule item the ATO instruction defines word for word, including what else is folded into the same total.
evidence_quote: Enter at item 2 Expenditure on feedstock inputs attributable to feedstock output the total amount of feedstock inputs attributable to feedstock outputs on all R&D activities
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's one-line question about feedstock spending and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a feedstock input is or that the item only exists where a marketable product resulted.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year worked out using the discount method, as reported on the business entity's capital gains tax schedule. The ATO makes the discount method available only where the asset was held at least twelve months: "If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method". The BLADE label carries two wordings because the schedule changed: OF is the old form's label and NF the new form's, which stopped splitting this total by method.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: The amount is a gross gain, not taxable income. The old-form and new-form labels are not the same quantity, so a series spanning the form change is not continuous. The OF and NF reading of the DIL prefixes is inferred from the label pairs rather than published.
rationale: The BLADE DIL label names the total current year capital gains under the discount method, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and gives an old-form and a new-form wording. The ATO guide defines the methods and when each applies.
evidence_quote: If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method to calculate your capital gain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF/NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Indexing the cost base
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year that the business worked out by lifting the asset's cost base for inflation, rather than by the discount or other method. Indexation is only open on very old assets and stops at a fixed date: the costs "must have incurred the costs by 21 September 1999" and a taxpayer "can index for inflation only up to 30 September 1999". For a company the choice is not really a choice, because the ATO notes that "Companies can't use the CGT discount. They should use indexation for assets acquired before 21 September 1999." The label carries OF and NF prefixes marking two wordings of the item, and the NF wording drops the split by method and carries the total of current year capital gains; what the prefixes stand for is not published.
description_source: ATO, Indexing the cost base
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of capital losses and of any small business concessions. Under the OF wording it is the indexation-method share of current year gains; under the NF wording the same column carries the total of current year gains whatever method produced them.
limitation: The two label wordings are not the same quantity, so a series spanning the change is not continuous and any level shift at that point is an artefact rather than firm behaviour. A non-zero value also marks an asset bought before September 1999 rather than a large gain, so the column is closer to a holding-period marker than to a measure of disposal activity. The reading of the OF and NF prefixes is inferred from the label pair rather than published.
rationale: The label names total current year capital gains under the indexation method, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO page sets out the eligibility date, the freeze date and the fact that companies rely on indexation because the discount is closed to them.
evidence_quote: Companies can't use the CGT discount. They should use indexation for assets acquired before 21 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF and NF label text and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what indexation is, that eligibility depends on a 1999 acquisition date, or that the two labels break the series.

value_domain: Count of colour-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
variable_description: Whether the business filed the mark as a colour mark, expressed as a count of colour-type rows on the application. IP Australia says colour trade marks protect "a colour or combination of colours", which is a claim over the colour itself rather than over a coloured logo. The row carries no text, so the count works as a type marker: above zero means the application was lodged as a colour mark.
description_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of rows in IP RAPID's application-description table whose description type is the colour type. In practice zero or one, and the row's description value is empty.
limitation: A count above zero says the mark was filed as a colour mark, not that the colour was accepted or the application succeeded; the status columns carry that. Zero does not mean the mark has no colour in its image, only that no colour-type row exists.
rationale: IP RAPID's dictionary lists the colour type among the trade mark description types and states that such rows are type indicators rather than text, and IP Australia defines what a colour trade mark protects.
evidence_quote: Colour trade marks protect a colour or combination of colours.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the same one-line count-of-descriptions wording used for every trade mark type column and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the ten sibling columns.

value_domain: Count of fancy-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
variable_description: Whether the application was recorded as a fancy mark, meaning a stylised or invented word presentation rather than plain text or a picture. IP Australia's public guide to kinds of trade marks does not use the term, so this is an internal filing convention in the register rather than a legal category of mark. The count behaves like the other type columns: the underlying row is a marker, not a description.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows carrying the fancy type. The rows hold no readable content, so any value above zero is a flag.
limitation: Because the term is not defined in IP Australia's published guidance, the boundary between a fancy mark, a word mark and a figurative mark rests on registry practice and can move over time, so counts are not safely comparable with the word and figurative columns or across long periods.
rationale: The IP RAPID dictionary confirms the fancy type exists among the trade mark description types and that its rows are non-descriptive, but publishes no definition of the category, which is itself the finding.
evidence_quote: (*) indicates that the description_value will not be descriptive. The presence of these rows indicate that the trade mark is of the type indicated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared count-of-descriptions wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that fancy is an undefined registry category.

value_domain: Count of figurative-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
variable_description: Whether the mark was filed as a figurative mark, that is a device or picture rather than plain text. IP Australia's dictionary is explicit that these rows carry no content: "(*) indicates that the description_value will not be descriptive. The presence of these rows indicate that the trade mark is of the type indicated." Read with trade_mark_word, it separates businesses protecting a logo from those protecting a name.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows whose type is figurative. The value is a presence indicator rather than a measure of how elaborate the device is.
limitation: A figurative filing is not evidence of a designed brand: a plain stylised word can be lodged as a figurative mark. The column also says nothing about what the image shows, which sits instead in trade_mark_image_words and in the separate image description rows.
rationale: The IP RAPID dictionary lists the figurative type and states plainly that the presence of such a row is the information, which is what a count of them measures.
evidence_quote: (*) indicates that the description_value will not be descriptive. The presence of these rows indicate that the trade mark is of the type indicated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the shared count-of-descriptions wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no way to tell the column from trade_mark_word or trade_mark_fancy.

value_domain: Count of image-words description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
variable_description: How many records the application carries of the words that appear inside the mark's image. Unlike the type-flag columns beside it, this description type is one of the few that holds real content, since the table "contains information about how the IP right is described. This includes patent titles, design product descriptions, trade mark word phrases and image descriptions". A count above zero therefore means the logo contains readable text that the registry transcribed.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the image-words type. Each row's description value holds transcribed text, so the count can exceed one where a mark carries several word elements.
limitation: It counts records, not words: one row can hold a whole phrase, so the number does not measure how much text the logo contains. The transcription also exists only where an examiner or system captured it, so zero can mean an unindexed image rather than a wordless one.
rationale: The IP RAPID dictionary lists this description type without the marker used for non-descriptive types, and describes the table as holding trade mark word phrases and image descriptions, which is what distinguishes it from the flag columns.
evidence_quote: The application-description table contains information about how the IP right is described. This includes patent titles, design product descriptions, trade mark word phrases and image descriptions and plant breeder's rights common names.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared count-of-descriptions wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that this column holds content while its siblings hold flags.

value_domain: Count of movement-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
variable_description: Whether the business filed a movement mark, which IP Australia describes as protecting "a motion or movement". These are rare and usually belong to broadcasters, software firms and large consumer brands protecting an animated identity. The count is a type marker on the application rather than a description of the motion.
description_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the movement type, normally zero or one, with no text in the row.
limitation: Because movement marks are so uncommon, this column is zero for almost every business in BLADE and cannot support any rate or share calculation at industry level. A value above zero records the filing, not whether the movement was accepted as distinctive.
rationale: IP RAPID lists the movement type among the trade mark description types and marks its rows as non-descriptive, and IP Australia defines what a movement trade mark protects.
evidence_quote: Movement trade marks protect a motion or movement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the shared count-of-descriptions wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a movement mark is or how rare the column is.

value_domain: Count of other-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
variable_description: Whether the mark was filed as a type that does not fit any of the named categories, counted as description rows. It is the residual of the trade mark type family, sitting alongside word, figurative, shape, colour, sound, movement, scent, taste and feel. Like those, the row itself is a marker rather than text, so the count says which box the filing went into and nothing about what the mark looks like.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the other type. It is a residual category, not a description of an unusual mark.
limitation: The composition of a residual changes whenever the registry adds a named type, so a rise in this column across years can be reclassification rather than new filing behaviour. It cannot be used to identify non-traditional marks, since taste and feel have their own types in the dictionary.
rationale: The IP RAPID dictionary enumerates the trade mark description types including the other type and marks all of them as non-descriptive rows, which establishes both the residual role and the flag behaviour.
evidence_quote: (*) indicates that the description_value will not be descriptive. The presence of these rows indicate that the trade mark is of the type indicated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared count-of-descriptions wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that this was a residual box rather than a mark type.

value_domain: Count of scent-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
variable_description: Whether the business filed a scent mark, which IP Australia describes as protecting "a distinct smell associated with a product or service". Scent marks are the rarest category on the Australian register, because the smell has to be shown to be distinctive rather than a natural property of the goods. The count marks the filing type; the row holds no description of the smell.
description_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the scent type, effectively a zero-or-one flag.
limitation: The column is zero for virtually the whole file, so a non-zero value identifies an individual applicant rather than supporting any aggregate measure. It also records an attempt: most scent filings do not survive examination, and nothing here says whether this one did.
rationale: IP RAPID lists the scent type among the non-descriptive trade mark description types, and IP Australia publishes what a scent trade mark protects.
evidence_quote: Scent trade marks protect a distinct smell associated with a product or service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared count-of-descriptions wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the column is near-empty and effectively identifying.

value_domain: Count of shape-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
variable_description: Whether the business filed a shape mark, which IP Australia describes as protecting "three-dimensional shapes". In practice these protect packaging and product form, so the column picks out manufacturers and consumer goods firms defending a physical design through the trade mark system rather than through a design right. The row is a type marker with no text.
description_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the shape type, normally zero or one.

rationale: IP RAPID lists the shape type among the trade mark description types whose rows are flags, and IP Australia publishes what a shape trade mark protects.
evidence_quote: Shape trade marks protect three-dimensional shapes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the shared count-of-descriptions wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish a shape trade mark from a registered design.

value_domain: Count of sound-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
variable_description: Whether the business filed a sound mark, which IP Australia describes as protecting "a sound or combination of sounds". Typical holders are broadcasters, telecommunications firms and consumer brands protecting a jingle or a device tone. The count records the filing type; the audio itself is not in BLADE.
description_source: IP Australia, Kinds of trade marks
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the sound type, normally zero or one, with an empty description value.
limitation: The column cannot be read as evidence of advertising or marketing spend, since a single sound mark can sit behind decades of campaigns and most heavy advertisers file none at all. Nor does it record what the sound is, so identical counts describe entirely different assets.
rationale: IP RAPID lists the sound type among the trade mark description types whose presence is the information, and IP Australia publishes what a sound trade mark protects.
evidence_quote: Sound trade marks protect a sound or combination of sounds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared count-of-descriptions wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a sound mark is or what the column cannot support.

value_domain: Count of word-type description rows on a trade mark application
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
variable_description: Whether the mark was filed as a plain word mark, which is the most common and broadest form of protection because it covers the name however it is styled. The dictionary marks this type as a flag rather than text: "(*) indicates that the description_value will not be descriptive. The presence of these rows indicate that the trade mark is of the type indicated." The words themselves sit in trade_mark_word_mark_phrase, not here.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, application-description table
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of application-description rows of the word type. It is a filing-form indicator, not a count of the words in the mark.
limitation: Reading this as the number of words in the trade mark is the obvious mistake and gives nonsense, since the row holds no text. A zero also does not mean the mark is wordless, because a logo containing text is usually filed as figurative with the text captured separately.
rationale: The IP RAPID dictionary lists the word type among the description types whose rows are non-descriptive markers, which fixes both what the count means and what it cannot mean.
evidence_quote: (*) indicates that the description_value will not be descriptive. The presence of these rows indicate that the trade mark is of the type indicated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared count-of-descriptions wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, inviting a reader to treat the count as the number of words in the mark.

value_domain: Count of word-mark-phrase description rows on a trade mark application

Where trade_mark_word says the mark was filed as words, this column counts the records that hold those words.

value_domain: Count of Austrade-recorded trade outcomes in the financial year
value_source: Austrade, Annual Report 2024-25, performance measure 2
variable_description: How many commercial export results Austrade attributed to this business in the financial year. Austrade defines the measure as counting "the number of commercial export results (trade outcomes) achieved by Austrade clients while working with Austrade across the financial year", recorded from "Client Relationship Management (CRM) system entry from client notification". It is therefore a record of Austrade's client servicing, not an independent measure of a firm's exporting.
description_source: Austrade, Annual Report 2024-25, performance measure 2
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of approved trade outcomes for one financial year, taken from Austrade's client relationship management system. The dollar side sits in tradeoutcomevalue on the same row.
limitation: A business that exported without Austrade's involvement scores zero, so the column separates Austrade clients from everyone else before it says anything about trade. The outcomes are also notified by the client rather than verified against customs or tax records, so this is a claim recorded in a system rather than an audited count.
rationale: Austrade publishes the definition and the data source for its trade outcomes measure in the annual report, which is the same concept the BLADE MAX panel carries at the entity level.
evidence_quote: Austrade measures the number of commercial export results (trade outcomes) achieved by Austrade clients while working with Austrade across the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that an outcome is client-notified and attributed to Austrade.

value_domain: Dollar value of Austrade-recorded trade outcomes in the financial year
value_source: Austrade, Annual Report 2024-25, note on the value of trade outcomes
variable_description: What Austrade valued the business's trade outcomes at for the financial year. Austrade defines it as "the total dollar value of the commercial export results that Austrade's clients have achieved with Austrade's support, as measured through (1) their export sales; (2) contracts or tenders they have won; or (3) the growth in their annual sales during the period Austrade provided them with services". Those three bases are added together, and Austrade notes that the results "are provided by the client and reviewed and relied upon by Austrade".
description_source: Austrade, Annual Report 2024-25, note on the value of trade outcomes
value_definition: A dollar amount for one financial year, summing the values Austrade assigned to that year's approved outcomes for the entity.
limitation: The three measures behind the total are different quantities, so an export sale, a contract won and a year of sales growth are stacked into one number that is not comparable between firms and is not export revenue. The whole value is attributed to Austrade's support, so it cannot be read as the effect of that support, and it will not reconcile with the merchandise trade tables.
rationale: Austrade publishes the exact construction of the value of trade outcomes, including the three alternative bases and the client-provided origin of the figures.
evidence_quote: The 'value of trade outcomes' is the total dollar value of the commercial export results that Austrade's clients have achieved with Austrade's support, as measured through (1) their export sales; (2) contracts or tenders they have won; or (3) the growth in their annual sales during the period Austrade provided them with services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would have taken the figure for export revenue.

value_domain: Presence flag for a training bond clause in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement makes a departing employee repay the cost of training, which is a retention device that ties a worker to the employer. The framework codes it where "the employee will refund to the employer a sum of money representing full or part value of training received by the employee at the employer's expense in the course of that employment". Read with the other general training fields, it separates employers who fund training with strings attached from those who do not.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A one-value flag: Y where the clause is present and blank otherwise. There is no explicit No code, so a genuine absence and a year in which the field was not coded look identical.
limitation: DEWR codes the field only for agreements approved from 1 January 2007, so every earlier agreement is blank whether or not it carried a bond, and a series across that date measures a coding change rather than employer behaviour. The flag also records the clause, not whether a bond was ever enforced or any money recovered.
rationale: The department's own data collection framework defines the training bonds field in the same words the BLADE data item list carries, and the valid-response text records the coding start date.
evidence_quote: The agreement contains a provision where an employee agrees that, in the event of resignation or termination of employment, the employee will refund to the employer a sum of money representing full or part value of training received by the employee at the employer's expense in the course of that employment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework wording as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that blank is not No or that the field starts in 2007.

value_domain: ABS mode of transport code for an export line (A, P, S)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Mode of transport
variable_description: How the goods on this export line left the country. The ABS defines the concept plainly: "The mode of transport describes the manner in which goods enter or leave Australia." For exports the Department of Home Affairs accepts only air and sea on the declaration, so the postal code is close to unused on this side of the trade file even though it is a valid value.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Mode of transport
value_definition: A single character from the ABS mode of transport classification: A for air, P for post, S for sea. It is recorded per export declaration line, so a business with mixed shipping appears under several codes in a year.
limitation: It describes only the leg leaving Australia, so a container railed across the country and then shipped is recorded as sea and the domestic freight task is invisible. Because exporters cannot declare post, the column cannot be used to measure small-parcel or e-commerce exporting.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the mode of transport concept and sets out which modes Home Affairs accepts for exports as against imports, which is what makes the export and import versions of this column different domains.
evidence_quote: The mode of transport describes the manner in which goods enter or leave Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the code list inline in the custodian's description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that post is effectively unavailable to exporters.

value_domain: ABS mode of transport code for an import line (A, P, S, U)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Mode of transport
variable_description: How the goods on this import line arrived in Australia, with a fourth code for arrivals the ABS cannot publish. Imports carry the full classification because Home Affairs accepts air, sea and post on an import declaration, plus a hand-carried category that the ABS reassigns to air or sea. The U code is not a transport method at all: it marks an import for which the mode cannot be released.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Mode of transport
value_definition: A single character: A for air, P for post, S for sea, U for unknown. Recorded per import declaration line, so one business can show all four codes in a year.
limitation: Treating U as a real mode, or dropping it, both distort a modal split, because it marks a confidentiality restriction rather than an unknown journey. Post is also available here but not on exports, so import and export modal shares are not comparable.
rationale: The ABS methodology sets out the four-category classification, that Home Affairs accepts more modes on imports than on exports, and that goods hand-carried by passengers are reclassified by the ABS.
evidence_quote: The mode of transport describes the manner in which goods enter or leave Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the code list inline in the custodian's description with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that U is a publication restriction.

variable_description: Whether the import line was entered under a concession or other special customs treatment, usually one that reduces or removes duty. A value of '000' means no treatment code, which is the ordinary case.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Data sources and compilation methods
value_definition: A three-digit Department of Home Affairs treatment code, with '000' standing for no treatment. The list is open and grows over time as concessional items are added to Schedule 4.
limitation: The code describes the duty treatment, not the goods, so it cannot stand in for what was imported and it cannot be aggregated with the commodity classifications. It also gives no money: the duty forgone under a concession depends on the general rate and the customs value, and neither is recoverable from this column. Because a code exists only from the date its concession was legislated, a series built on one code shows a concession appearing when it was coded rather than when the trade started.
rationale: Appendix 10 section B lists the 91 treatment codes the ABS outputs, with ABS 76-character labels. '000' is added because the BLADE description states that value means no treatment code. The appendix notes that historical inoperative treatment codes are excluded, so a BLADE series back to 2003-04 may carry a few codes not in this list.

value_definition: A non-negative integer count of service events for one financial year, covering all tailored service types together.

value_domain: Assayed tungsten content of an ore or concentrate export, per cent
value_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC), Explanatory Notes
variable_description: How much tungsten the exported ore or concentrate assayed at, as a percentage of the consignment. The AHECC attaches assay requirements to particular mineral codes, and tungsten is one of the metals reported as a percentage rather than as grams per tonne, which is how gold and silver are declared. It is a property of the shipment declared by the exporter, not a characteristic of the business.
description_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC), Explanatory Notes
value_definition: A percentage between 0 and 100 of tungsten content in the consignment, attached only to the AHECC ore and concentrate codes that require an assay.
limitation: It measures grade, not the tungsten exported: only multiplying by the line quantity, and only where that quantity is a mass, gives a metal weight. Every export line for any other commodity is blank, so the column is empty across almost the whole trade file and cannot be averaged over a firm's exports.
rationale: The AHECC explanatory notes set out the assay elements and their reporting units for mineral exports, which is where a tungsten percentage field on an export line comes from.
evidence_quote: The Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC) is designed: for use by exporters and agents to classify goods when providing export declarations to the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field is an AHECC assay requirement or that grade is not tonnage.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total sales reported on the activity statement, GST excluded
value_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, Step 1: Sales
variable_description: The business's total sales for the activity statement period as it reported them at BAS label G1, with GST removed. The label is broader than trading revenue: the ATO requires a business to include "the sale of business assets, such as office equipment or motor vehicles (including trade-ins)", export sales, memberships and earnings from financial supplies, while excluding dividends, grants without a supply, and trust and partnership distributions. It is the most common turnover measure in BLADE and the denominator behind most productivity and growth work built on the asset.
description_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, Step 1: Sales
value_definition: A dollar amount for one activity statement period, summing taxable, GST-free and input-taxed sales. Periods are monthly, quarterly or annual, so annual turnover for a firm has to be built by adding its periods rather than taken from one row.
limitation: Only businesses registered for GST lodge an activity statement, so firms below the registration turnover threshold are absent rather than recorded as small, and entry into the data can be a registration event rather than a new business. Because one-off asset sales sit in the same label, a spike can be a sold vehicle rather than a trading year.
rationale: The custodian's description names total sales excluding GST, which is BAS label G1, and the ATO instruction sets out exactly what belongs in and out of that label.
evidence_quote: the sale of business assets, such as office equipment or motor vehicles (including trade-ins)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the three-word custodian description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that asset sales are included or that non-registered firms are missing.

value_domain: Position of a company within its emerging industry
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Whether the business sits at the core of its emerging industry or only at its edge. The Emerging Industries file comes from the "Department of Industry, Science and Resources", and the columns beside this one are algorithmically derived from company web presences, including an ANZSIC code and a theme drawn from a departmental taxonomy. Read with emerging_industry, which names which of seven industries applies, this column separates firms developing the technology from firms adopting it.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A short text category. The custodian's description names core and peripheral, and the valid-response text adds ADOPTER, so the column is a three-way position within an industry rather than a yes-or-no membership flag.
limitation: The classification is inferred from company web content, so a business with a thin, stale or absent website can be mis-positioned or missed entirely; it is not self-declared and not administrative. It also says nothing about how much of the firm's revenue the emerging industry accounts for, so a peripheral firm can earn more from it than a core one.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page confirms who supplies the Emerging Industries file, and the neighbouring columns in the same table state that the industry classification is algorithmically derived rather than reported, which is what governs how this category should be read.
evidence_quote: Department of Industry, Science and Resources: Research & Development Tax Incentive (RDTI) Program, Emerging Industries and Dealroom
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the category is machine-inferred from web content or that a third value exists.

value_domain: Category of change made by a formal variation to an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: What a formal variation to the enterprise agreement changed: wages, conditions, or both. The framework records variations as a "list of variations to current agreement" where the "agreement record includes details of varied agreement provisions", so each variation is a row of its own rather than an edit to the agreement record. A wages variation is the signal that the pay outcome coded on the agreement no longer describes what the employer pays.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A short text category taking wages, conditions, or wages and conditions together. One row per variation, so an agreement varied twice contributes two rows.
limitation: The category says what was varied, not in which direction or by how much, so a wages variation can be an increase, a deferral or the correction of an error. Because variations live in a separate table, anyone reading only the agreement table sees the original terms and misses every change made to them.
rationale: The department's data collection framework documents the variations record and what it holds, which establishes that a variation is a separate dated record rather than an amendment to the agreement row.
evidence_quote: list of variations to current agreement. Agreement record includes details of varied agreement provisions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the four-word custodian description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that variations sit outside the agreement table.

value_domain: Presence flag for an unconditional bonus in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether the agreement pays a bonus that does not depend on performance, most often a sign-on payment when the agreement is approved. The framework splits bonuses into "Conditional or unconditional", and the unconditional side is the part that behaves like a lump-sum wage rather than an incentive. Its dollar figure, where the agreement states one, sits in unconditionalbonusamount on the same row.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A one-value flag: Y where an unconditional bonus applies and blank otherwise, with no explicit No code.
limitation: A Y does not say the bonus was paid, or to how many employees, so it cannot be turned into a wage cost. Because there is no No code, blank covers both an agreement with no bonus and a period when the field was not coded, and conditional bonuses are recorded elsewhere, so this is not all bonus activity.
rationale: The department's framework lists bonuses as a performance and productivity payments field split into conditional and unconditional, which is the distinction this flag records.
evidence_quote: Bonuses Conditional or unconditional
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework's example about a sign-on bonus and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that blank is not No.

value_domain: Dollar amount of an unconditional bonus in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: The flat dollar amount of the agreement's unconditional bonus, where the agreement states one. It quantifies what unconditionalbonus only flags, and it applies at the commencement of the agreement rather than each year. Because the amount comes from the text of the agreement, it is what was promised at approval, not what any employee received.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A dollar amount per employee under the agreement, with 111111111 used as a sentinel for a bonus whose quantum varies or is unknown.
limitation: Averaging or summing the column without first removing 111111111 destroys the result, because the sentinel is a nine-digit number rather than a missing value. The figure also cannot be multiplied by employee coverage to get a wage bill, since a bonus stated in an agreement need not have been paid to everyone or at all.
rationale: The department's framework records bonuses as conditional or unconditional and records quantums where stated; the sentinel convention comes from the custodian's own valid-response text for this field.
evidence_quote: Bonuses Conditional or unconditional
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that 111111111 is a sentinel that will corrupt any average.

value_domain: Presence flag for a union consultation clause in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether the agreement requires the employer to consult a union before making a workplace change. The framework codes it where "an agreement provides a provision for a company and/or employees to consult with a union on any workplace issue, condition or proposal prior to implementing an agreement". It is one of three trade union fields, alongside right of entry and deduction of dues, that together describe how much institutional standing a union has at the workplace.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A one-value flag: Y where a union consultation clause is present and blank otherwise. There is no No code, so blank covers both an agreement without the clause and an agreement made before the field was coded.
limitation: It is coded only for agreements made from 1 January 2009, so agreements from 1997 to 2008 are blank by rule rather than by content and a trend through that boundary is a coding artefact. Consultation is a procedural right, so its presence says nothing about union membership or bargaining strength at the workplace.
rationale: The department's framework defines the union consultation field in the words the BLADE data item list carries, and the valid-response text records the 2009 coding start.
evidence_quote: An agreement provides a provision for a company and/or employees to consult with a union on any workplace issue, condition or proposal prior to implementing an agreement
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field only exists for agreements made from 2009.

value_domain: Presence flag for a payroll deduction of union dues clause
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets union dues be taken out of pay by the employer, which lowers the effort of staying a member. The framework codes it where "the agreement includes a clause that provides for union dues to be collected at source, i.e. to be deducted by the employer from the employee's salary". Of the three union fields it is the one closest to a membership-retention mechanism rather than a procedural right.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A one-value flag: Y where a dues-at-source clause is present and blank otherwise. With no No code and a coding window broken in the middle, blank means either no clause or an agreement made in 2007 or 2008, when the field was not coded at all.
limitation: The coding window has a hole in the middle: DEWR coded the field for agreements made before 1 January 2007 and again from 1 January 2009, so agreements made in the two years between are blank whatever they contained, and an uninterrupted series through 2007 and 2008 shows a fall that did not happen.
rationale: The department's framework defines the union deduction of dues field in the same words as the BLADE data item list, and the valid-response text records the split coding period.
evidence_quote: The agreement includes a clause that provides for union dues to be collected at source, i.e. to be deducted by the employer from the employee's salary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing flagged the two-year gap in coding.

value_domain: Presence flag for a union right of entry clause beyond the statutory minimum
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether the agreement gives union officials access to the workplace over and above what the law already requires. The exclusion is what makes the field informative: "This field is not coded if the only right of entry provisions for the union are those under the mandatory consultation and dispute settlement terms." A Y therefore marks a negotiated concession, not a restatement of statutory rights.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A one-value flag: Y where an additional right of entry is present and blank otherwise, with no explicit No code.
limitation: A blank does not mean officials cannot enter the workplace, since the statutory right stands regardless; it usually means the agreement adds nothing to the law. The same two-year coding gap applies as for union dues, so agreements made in 2007 and 2008 are blank by rule.
rationale: The department's framework defines the field and states the exclusion that determines when it is coded, which is the fact that changes how a blank should be read.
evidence_quote: This field is not coded if the only right of entry provisions for the union are those under the mandatory consultation and dispute settlement terms.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a blank usually means the agreement matched the statutory position.

value_domain: Binary indicator of union coverage of an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether any union is covered by this enterprise agreement. Union coverage is one of the wages and demographics fields the department records for every agreement since 1991, unlike the conditions fields that only start in 1997, so this column runs across the whole database. It is the cleanest available marker of whether bargaining at a workplace was union-involved.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 where unions are covered by the agreement and 0 where none are. It is one of the few workplace agreement fields with an explicit zero rather than a Y-only code, so a 0 really does mean no.
limitation: Coverage by an agreement is not union membership or density: a union can be party to an agreement at a workplace where very few employees belong to it. The column also does not say how many unions or which ones, so a single-union and a multi-union workplace look identical.
rationale: The department's framework lists union coverage among the fields recorded for all agreements since 1991, which is what makes this column continuous where the conditions flags are not.
evidence_quote: Union coverage Union coverage
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished coverage from membership.

value_domain: ABS unit of quantity code for an export commodity line
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Quantity measurement
variable_description: Which physical unit the quantity on this export line is counted in. The ABS defines the underlying concept as follows: "Quantity is the measure of how many or how much of a commodity is imported or exported." The unit is fixed by the AHECC code rather than chosen by the exporter, so it is a property of the commodity, and some AHECC codes require no quantity at all.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Quantity measurement
value_definition: A short character code from the ABS unit of quantity list, covering weight, volume, area, length, electrical power and count units. It is assigned by the commodity classification, so all exporters of the same commodity share it.
limitation: Adding quantities across commodities with different units gives a meaningless total, so any aggregation has to be filtered to one unit first; the ABS warns that wood chips in tonnes and railway sleepers in cubic metres cannot be summed. A blank quantity is a classification property rather than a nil shipment, so it must not be treated as zero.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines quantity, lists the unit families used and states the aggregation warning, which is precisely the trap a reader of this column falls into.
evidence_quote: Quantity is the measure of how many or how much of a commodity is imported or exported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pointed at an appendix and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that quantities in mixed units cannot be added.

value_domain: ABS unit of quantity code for an import commodity line
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Quantity measurement
variable_description: Which physical unit the quantity on this import line is counted in, set by the Customs Tariff code rather than by the importer. Imports are classified under the Combined Australian Customs Tariff Nomenclature and Statistical Classification, so the unit families are the same as on exports but the code that assigns them is a different classification. Comparing a firm's import and export quantities therefore means checking that the two lines carry the same unit.
description_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Quantity measurement
value_definition: A short character code from the ABS unit of quantity list, attached to the import commodity code. Weight, volume, area, length and count units all appear.
limitation: Because exports and imports are classified under different systems, the same physical good can carry different units on the two sides, so a net trade quantity built without checking units is wrong. A missing unit means the tariff code requires no quantity, not that nothing was imported.
rationale: The ABS methodology sets out how quantity is measured and recorded against the most detailed classification code, and the trade methodology confirms that imports use the Customs Tariff while exports use the AHECC.
evidence_quote: Quantity is the measure of how many or how much of a commodity is imported or exported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pointed at an appendix and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the unit comes from the import classification and need not match the export side.

value_domain: Days per year of unpaid carer's leave provided by an enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: How many days a year of unpaid carer's leave the agreement gives, where it states a number. It sits alongside the paid carer's leave fields, which record extra paid days over and above personal leave, so the two together describe how an employer splits caring entitlements between paid and unpaid. This is a retired field: it does not appear in the department's current collection framework.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A number of days per year, with 111111111 standing for an entitlement that varies, is unknown, or is granted per occasion rather than as an annual quantum.
limitation: DEWR stopped coding the field for agreements made from 1 January 2011, so it is blank across the whole recent period and cannot support a trend to the present. The sentinel 111111111 also has to be removed before any average, and a per-occasion entitlement can be more generous than a numbered one, so a large number is not straightforwardly a better deal.
rationale: The department's framework documents the family and carer's leave fields it currently codes and does not include this one, which supports reading it as a retired field, and the custodian's valid-response text gives the sentinel and the 2011 cut-off.
evidence_quote: Paid leave (separate from ordinary sick/personal leave) is available for employees to care for a sick family member in addition to them being able to access paid days as part of their Personal leave entitlements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field was retired in 2011 or that the sentinel corrupts averages.

value_domain: Count of claims in the corresponding United States patent document
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary
variable_description: How many claims the matching United States patent document sets out, which is a rough measure of how finely the business fenced its invention. Claims are the operative part of a patent: they define what is protected, so a count is closer to a measure of drafting scope than of technical content. Because it refers to a US document, a value exists only where the invention was also filed in the United States.
description_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of claims, independent and dependent together, on the US family member rather than on the Australian application carried on the same row.
limitation: It is not a measure of invention quality or breadth, because dependent claims are added in and drafting convention inflates counts in some technology fields. A blank means no US family member was matched rather than a patent with no claims, so the column silently selects for firms that took their inventions offshore. IP Australia's published IP RAPID dictionary does not document this column, so the reading rests on the name and on the table it sits in.
rationale: The IP RAPID dictionary defines the application tables that BLADE's IPRAPID Applications data draws on, but carries no US claims field, which is why this is recorded as an inference rather than a sourced definition.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's five-word description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the count belongs to a US document or that blank means no US filing.

value_domain: Upper bound of Dealroom's estimated business valuation, AUD millions
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The top of the range Dealroom estimates the business was worth at its most recent valuation event, in millions of Australian dollars. It pairs with valuation_min, and the two are equal where Dealroom produced a point estimate rather than a range. Dealroom assembles these from harvested public sources, describing itself as delivering insights into funding rounds, valuations and business models rather than collecting accounts from firms.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A dollar amount in millions of AUD, an estimate rather than a reported figure. Time-invariant across an ABN's rows, so it describes the business at extraction and not the row's financial year.
limitation: A valuation is a market estimate, not equity or net assets on a balance sheet, so it cannot be reconciled with the tax and activity statement columns beside it in BLADE. Dealroom only estimates valuations for companies in its coverage, which is heavily weighted to venture-backed technology firms, so a blank is the normal state and says nothing about a firm's worth.
rationale: Dealroom publishes what its platform tracks and how the data is assembled, which is what determines that these figures are observations and estimates rather than reported financial positions.
evidence_quote: Our platform leverages advanced data science and real-time tracking to deliver deep insights into funding rounds, valuations, business models, and emerging trends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is an estimate that cannot be matched to tax data.

value_domain: Lower bound of Dealroom's estimated business valuation, AUD millions
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The bottom of the range Dealroom estimates the business was worth at its most recent valuation event, in millions of Australian dollars. Where Dealroom did not produce a range it equals valuation_max, so the gap between the two columns is a measure of Dealroom's own uncertainty and not of any spread in the market. Both are dated by valuation_month and valuation_year rather than by the row's period.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A dollar amount in millions of AUD, an estimate rather than a reported figure, repeated unchanged on every row for the ABN.
limitation: Taking this column as a conservative floor is a mistake, because it collapses onto the maximum whenever no range was estimated, so a narrow range can mean confidence or simply that no range exists. It also cannot be compared across firms as a valuation method, since Dealroom's basis varies with what it could observe.
rationale: Dealroom publishes how it builds company intelligence, and the custodian's note states the equal-values convention, which together determine how the pair of bounds should be read.
evidence_quote: We combine machine learning and data engineering with robust verification processes and a strong network of ecosystems for real-time, predictive intelligence.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the minimum collapses onto the maximum where no range exists.

value_domain: Calendar month of Dealroom's valuation estimate
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The calendar month Dealroom attached to its valuation estimate for the business. It is only interpretable with valuation_year, and together they date the valuation_min and valuation_max pair. Because the valuation fields are time-invariant across an ABN's rows, this month anchors the estimate rather than describing the row it appears on.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A three-character month abbreviation, Jan through Dec, with the year held separately.
limitation: It dates the valuation on a calendar basis, so it does not align with the Australian financial year that governs the BAS and income tax columns elsewhere in BLADE, and pairing them without converting will misdate the estimate. A month on its own carries no year, so it cannot order valuations at all.
rationale: Dealroom publishes the real-time tracking basis of its company data, which is why a valuation carries its own date rather than a reporting period, and the custodian's description gives the format.
evidence_quote: Our platform leverages advanced data science and real-time tracking to deliver deep insights into funding rounds, valuations, business models, and emerging trends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's format note and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the month is calendar-based and must be read with the year.

value_domain: Calendar year of Dealroom's valuation estimate
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The calendar year Dealroom attached to its valuation estimate for the business. Only the latest valuation is carried, so a business revalued several times shows one year rather than a history. Read with valuation_month, it is the only thing that says how current the valuation range on the same row is.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year. Like the valuation amounts, it is time-invariant across all rows for an ABN.
limitation: Because the valuation fields are repeated on every row, this year can sit years away from the financial year of the row it appears on, and using it as the row's event year without checking will misdate the valuation. A stale year is also the normal case for a firm Dealroom stopped tracking, so an old year is not evidence that the business stopped growing.
rationale: Dealroom publishes that its coverage is maintained by continuous tracking of a defined universe of companies, which is what makes a single stale valuation year the expected outcome for a firm outside active coverage.
evidence_quote: Our platform leverages advanced data science and real-time tracking to deliver deep insights into funding rounds, valuations, business models, and emerging trends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's format note and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the year is time-invariant and can be far from the row's period.

value_domain: Sequence number of a variation within one enterprise agreement
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Which formal variation this row is in the agreement's history: 1 for the first, 2 for the second, and so on. The department holds variations as a "list of variations to current agreement", so the highest value for an agreement is the number of times its terms were formally reopened. It orders the rows of the variation table for one agreement; typeofvariation says what each one changed.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A positive integer counting within one agreement, starting at 1. It resets for every agreement, so the value has no meaning across agreements.
limitation: It carries no date, so the interval between variations, and whether they cluster early or late in an agreement's life, has to come from other columns. A high number marks an agreement reopened often, which can mean either an unstable bargaining relationship or simply a long-lived agreement, and the column cannot tell those apart.
rationale: The department's framework documents that variations are held as a list against the agreement record, which establishes that this column is a within-agreement sequence rather than a national identifier.
evidence_quote: list of variations to current agreement. Agreement record includes details of varied agreement provisions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the sequence resets per agreement or that it carries no date.

value_domain: Binary indicator that an enterprise agreement operates in Victoria
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)

Summing the state flags across agreements counts multi-state agreements several times over, which overstates agreement activity in every jurisdiction.

value_domain: Presence flag for a voluntary employee superannuation contribution clause
value_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
variable_description: Whether the agreement records that employees may put extra money of their own into their superannuation fund. The department's current framework instead codes whether voluntary contributions attract a higher employer contribution, which is a different and stronger provision.
description_source: Department of Employment, Workplace Agreements Database 2016 Data Collection Framework (published by the Fair Work Commission)
value_definition: A one-value flag: Y where the agreement records the option and blank otherwise. There is no No code, so blank covers an agreement without the clause and every agreement made from 2011, when coding of the field stopped.

value_domain: Volume of irrigation water applied to cotton, megalitres
value_source: ABS, Water Use on Australian Farms methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: How many megalitres of irrigation water the farm business put on cotton in the reference year. The water items are built from the ABS agricultural collections, whose frame is size-limited: for the 2020-21 Agricultural Census a business was in scope "if: they undertook agricultural activity, and the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater", and earlier collections applied their own cut-off. Cotton is the most water-intensive broadacre crop the ABS collects separately, so this column dominates the water total on farms that grow it, and dividing it by a_irrig_cotton gives a comparable rate in megalitres per hectare.

The ABS uses exactly this test to decide whether a business is trading: "Businesses are defined to be engaging in productive activity where they have a Goods and Services Tax (GST) role and are actively remitting GST through Business Activity Statements (BAS)." The long term non-remitter state is the one that matters most, because such a business is registered but is excluded from ABS business counts.

limitation: Holding an active GST role is not a turnover measure and its absence is not proof of a very small business: registration is compulsory only above the turnover threshold, and the ABS notes that "businesses that have turnover that is under the threshold for registration (currently $75,000) may choose not to apply for an ABN". A business can also flip to non-remitter and back, which shows up as an exit and re-entry in any panel built on this field.

The ATO describes the obligation as regular prepayments "of the expected tax on your business and investment income", so the role marks an entity expected to earn taxable income rather than one that employs people. It is the counterpart of the withholding role in x_itw, which is about tax taken out of other people's pay.

For a consolidated group the head company pays instalments for the whole group, so subsidiaries can show no role while their income is being taxed.
