value_domain: Non-profit institution indicator
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
variable_description: Marks the business as a non-profit institution, barred by its own status from paying profit out to the people behind it. The ABS defines such units as "legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit or other financial gain for the units that establish, control or finance them". In practice these are mostly companies limited by guarantee and incorporated associations, so the flag is a legal restriction on distribution rather than a statement about the size or the commerciality of the operation.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
value_definition: A single digit indicator separating non-profit institutions from other institutions, with a third code for units the register could not determine.
limitation: It does not mean the entity runs at a loss or trades outside the market. The ABS is explicit that the term "reflects the embargo on distribution of financial gains and is not intended to imply that NPIs cannot make a profit", and non-profit institutions can be market producers with substantial revenue. The not-determined code is also not a small residual for this item, so treating it as non-profit or as other will both bias a comparison.
rationale: The ABS sector classification publication defines non-profit institutions, sets out the distribution embargo that identifies them, and states that the label does not preclude making a profit.
evidence_quote: Non-Profit Institutions (NPIs) are defined as 'legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit or other financial gain for the units that establish, control or finance them'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Non Profit Institution flag' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not define a non-profit institution or correct the common reading that such an entity cannot profit.

value_domain: Australian postcode of the business's register address
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2021 - June 2025
variable_description: The postcode the ABS Business Register holds for the business, which for a simple business is the address where its main activity takes place. The ABS explains that "The main business address of a business relates to the physical address where the main business activity takes place", so the postcode is meant to locate the operation rather than the mail. It gives BLADE its cheapest geography, sitting beside the state and states-of-operation items on the same indicative record.
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2021 - June 2025
value_definition: A four digit numeric Australian postcode. It is a postal geography, not a statistical one, so it does not nest inside the Australian Statistical Geography Standard.
limitation: One postcode cannot represent a multi-site business, and for the largest firms it is close to meaningless: the ABS codes fine geography only for the non-profiled population, noting that "SA2 data is only coded for businesses in the non-profiled population", with profiled units grouped into unknown categories. Postcode boundaries are also revised by Australia Post, so a stable postcode is not a guarantee of a stable location.
rationale: The ABS business counts methodology defines the address concept behind register geography and states the limits on how far it is coded for complex businesses; the postcode item itself is not separately documented, so the reading is assembled from that.
evidence_quote: For businesses in the non-profiled population, main state is derived from the main business address. The main business address of a business relates to the physical address where the main business activity takes place.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Postcode' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it said nothing about which address the postcode belongs to or that it is unreliable for large multi-site firms.

value_domain: Public or private sector indicator
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
variable_description: Splits the business into the public or the private sector on the basis of government control. The ABS classification is exactly this binary: "The Public/Private classification divides the Australian economy into the Public Sector (resident units controlled by government) and the Private Sector (all other resident units)." Control is the test, not ownership share or funding, so a heavily subsidised private provider stays private and a government business enterprise trading commercially stays public.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
value_definition: A single digit indicator with a private code, a public code and a not-determined code. It is a cruder cut of the same information carried in more detail by the institutional sector and legal organisation items.
limitation: It does not say which government controls the unit, so Commonwealth, state and local entities are pooled in one public code, and the level of government has to come from elsewhere. Because control can change with a privatisation or a machinery of government change, a business can switch sector without any change in what it does.
rationale: The ABS sector classification publication defines the public/private split and the control test that decides it, which is what this indicator implements on the register.
evidence_quote: The Public/Private classification divides the Australian economy into the Public Sector (resident units controlled by government) and the Private Sector (all other resident units).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Private/Public indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the test is government control or that the level of government is not recorded.

value_domain: SISCA institutional sector code, edition labelled 2006
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
variable_description: An institutional sector code carried under a 2006 edition label, alongside the 1993 and 2008 labelled columns on the same indicative record. SISCA itself groups units by economic function into non-financial corporations, financial corporations, general government, households and non-profit institutions serving households. The 2006 label is the point of difficulty: the ABS publishes SISCA as editions 1998, 2008 and 2021, so this column is best read as the sector held on the register at a mid-2000s vintage rather than as a separately published revision.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
value_definition: A hierarchical numeric SISCA code, one to four digits from sector down to class, with 0 for unknown or missing.
limitation: Do not assume the three SISCA columns are the same classification at three dates. They carry different edition labels, and because no ABS publication corresponds to a 2006 edition, a difference between this column and the 2008 one cannot be attributed confidently either to a reclassification of the business or to a change of edition.
rationale: The ABS sector classification publication defines SISCA and lists its published editions as 1998, 2008 and 2021, which supports what the classification is but not the 2006 edition label used here, so the mapping is inferred rather than sourced.
evidence_quote: The data downloads include a series of correspondences which provide links between SISCA 1998, SISCA 2008 and SISCA 2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia (SISCA) 2006' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither defined the classification nor flagged that the edition label does not match a published ABS release.

value_domain: SISCA institutional sector code, 2008 edition
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
variable_description: The institutional sector the ABS assigns the business under the 2008 edition of SISCA, which is the edition aligned to the 2008 System of National Accounts. The ABS defines it as "a classification of institutional units which provides a framework for dividing the Australian economy into institutional sectors", grouping units by economic function rather than by industry. This is the item that separates non-financial corporations, financial corporations, general government, households and non-profit institutions serving households.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
value_definition: A hierarchical numeric code from SISCA 2008, one digit for the sector, two for the subsector, three for the group and four for the class, with 0 for unknown or missing.
limitation: Sector is not industry and not size: a small consultancy and a large manufacturer both sit in the non-financial corporations sector. Sector codes on the register are also revised in bulk from time to time, and the ABS applies a business's final classification back over the publication period, so a recorded sector change can be a data quality project rather than anything the business did.
rationale: The ABS sector classification publication defines SISCA, its numbering system and its relationship to the 2008 System of National Accounts, which is the edition this column names.
evidence_quote: The Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia (SISCA) is a classification of institutional units which provides a framework for dividing the Australian economy into institutional sectors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia (SISCA) 2008' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what an institutional sector is or why the code can move without the business changing.

value_domain: SISCA institutional sector code, edition labelled 1993
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
variable_description: The oldest of the three institutional sector codes on the indicative record, labelled to the 1993 vintage. The sectors of that generation follow the 1993 System of National Accounts, which the ABS implemented in the SISCA edition it published as 1998, so this column is the pre-2008 sector view of the business rather than a fourth classification. It is the code to use when reconciling early BLADE years with national accounts aggregates of the same period.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
value_definition: A hierarchical numeric SISCA code of one to four digits, with 0 for unknown or missing, drawn from the pre-2008 System of National Accounts generation of the classification.
limitation: It is not comparable with the 2008 labelled column without a correspondence, because the 2008 System of National Accounts changed sector boundaries, and the ABS publishes the mapping as a correspondence table rather than a rename. Pooling the two columns to fill gaps will therefore move units between sectors for classification reasons alone.
rationale: The ABS sector classification publication defines SISCA and documents correspondences between the pre-2008 and later editions, which supports the classification and the comparability warning, but no published edition is labelled 1993, so the alignment is inferred.
evidence_quote: The data downloads include a series of correspondences which provide links between SISCA 1998, SISCA 2008 and SISCA 2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Standard Institutional Sector Classification of Australia (SISCA) 1993' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the code belongs to the pre-2008 national accounts generation or that it needs a correspondence to be compared.

value_domain: Set of states and territories in which the business operates
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2021 - June 2025
variable_description: Lists every state and territory the business operates in, packed into a single nine position string where each position stands for one jurisdiction. It is a multi-state field, unlike the single main state item, so it is the column to use when asking whether a firm crosses borders at all. Where it comes from differs by unit: the ABS maintains structures for complex businesses directly, since "the ABS maintains its own economic units structure through direct contact with businesses", while for everyone else it derives from ABN registration data.
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2021 - June 2025
value_definition: A nine digit numeric string in which each digit position corresponds to a state, territory or an unknown slot, so 100050780 records operations in New South Wales, Western Australia, the Northern Territory and the Australian Capital Territory.
limitation: It carries no weight at all, so a firm with one interstate contractor looks the same as one with half its workforce interstate, and the field cannot apportion turnover or employment between jurisdictions. For most businesses it also reflects what was declared at ABN registration and is not refreshed as the business expands, so it understates interstate operation among growing firms.
rationale: The ABS business counts methodology documents the two population model that the custodian's own note invokes, and how register geography is maintained for profiled and non-profiled units; the nine position encoding itself is described only in the BLADE data item list.
evidence_quote: For a small number of businesses, the ABN unit is not suitable for ABS economic statistics purposes and the ABS maintains its own economic units structure through direct contact with businesses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'States of operation' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain the packed encoding, the difference in provenance between profiled and non-profiled units, or the absence of any weighting.

value_domain: State or territory recorded for the unit on the ABS Business Register
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2020 - June 2024
variable_description: The state or territory the ABS Business Register held for this business in the quarter, with 0 the residual for unknown or missing. For a simple business the value comes from the registered main business address, so it is an administrative address rather than an answer the business gave; for a profiled business the ABS instead takes the state or territory with the highest employment. The item is cross-sectional, restated for each quarter alongside frame_version, so it can move when a business changes its registered address without moving any operations.
description_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits methodology, July 2020 - June 2024
value_definition: A single-digit state and territory code following the ABS state and territory classification, with 0 carried as the residual for unknown or missing. One value per unit per quarter.
limitation: It is not where the business produces. A national operator with a head office in Melbourne sits in Victoria on this column no matter where its sites are, and x_st_op on the same table is the column that lists every state of operation.
rationale: The ABS business counts methodology explains how a state is attached to a unit on the ABS Business Register, and distinguishes the profiled from the non-profiled population, which is what decides the meaning of this column.
evidence_quote: For businesses in the non-profiled population, main state is derived from the main business address
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-word label 'State' and reprinted the single residual code '0 - Unknown or missing' as the whole value definition, so nothing said where the state comes from or that it is a registered address.

value_domain: Type of Legal Organisation (TOLO) code, SESCA 2021
value_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
variable_description: The legal form of the business in that quarter - company, sole proprietor, partnership, trust or public sector entity. The ABS defines the classification as one that "is used to classify institutional units according to the type of legal organisation that best describes their structure", with three groups at the one-digit level: incorporated private sector entities, unincorporated private sector entities and public sector entities. The DIL's valid-response text is only the fragment "Profiled Population", which on the sibling column x_st_op marks how the value is maintained for profiled units rather than naming any code.
description_source: ABS, Standard Economic Sector Classifications of Australia (SESCA), 2021
value_definition: A hierarchical code from the Type of Legal Organisation classification in SESCA 2021: one digit for the group, two digits for the class. The BLADE item list does not carry the code list itself.
limitation: Legal form is not economic size, ownership or control. One enterprise commonly runs a trust and a company side by side, and both appear here as separate legal forms, so this column cannot be used to count businesses as economic entities or to infer who owns whom.
rationale: TOLO is an ABS classification published in SESCA, and the SESCA release gives the definition and the three top-level groups that the BLADE column codes to.
evidence_quote: The Type of Legal Organisation (TOLO) classification is used to classify institutional units according to the type of legal organisation that best describes their structure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry expanded the acronym and nothing more, and printed the stray fragment 'Profiled Population' as its value definition, which reads as a code and is not one.

value_domain: Financial year of the FLAD farm observation
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The financial year that the areas, quantities and livestock numbers on this FLAD row belong to. The ABS lists the source in BLADE as "Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20", so this column is the year index within that twenty-year window and, with fd_id, keys one farm-year. It is the observation table's own year; the Control table carries z_year for the frame attributes that apply to the same farm-year.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A four-digit integer naming an Australian financial year ending 30 June. The item list does not say whether the digits name the opening or the closing year of the pair.
limitation: A row for a year is not evidence the farm was collected that year. The ABS runs a full agricultural census only in some years and samples in others, so a run of years for one fd_id can mix reported with derived values, and FLAD ships an IDW and a SUC version of the same farm-years that must not be pooled.
rationale: The ABS BLADE data page names FLAD as a BLADE data source and gives its exact coverage, which is what bounds the values this column can take.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Financial year' with '4 digit numeric' as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said which years exist or that a year present does not mean a year observed.

value_domain: Share of business income from agricultural production, per cent
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: How much of the farm business's income for the year came from agricultural production, as a percentage. It is one of four income shares on the row, the others being government grants (z_gov_income), off-farm earnings (z_nonfarm_income) and other sources (z_other_income), so together they describe the composition of income rather than its level. A low value marks a landholder for whom farming is a side activity even where the area of holding is large.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A percentage between 0 and 100, one value per farm-year, derived within FLAD rather than reported as a dollar figure.
limitation: The share carries no scale, and no dollar total sits on this table. A farm at 95 per cent agricultural income may be turning over $50,000 or $50 million, and z_evao on the Control table is the only size measure FLAD offers to tell them apart.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page establishes FLAD as an integrated farm-level source in BLADE; the composition reading comes from the four shares sitting together on the same table with no dollar total, which the registry itself shows.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Income sources: share of income from agricultural production' with '%' printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the share is of, or that no denominator ships with it.

value_domain: ANZSIC 2006 industry code
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: The industry the farm business was classified to under ANZSIC 2006, which is also what put it into the agricultural collection. The ABS says "Businesses are identified as undertaking agricultural activity if any of their primary or secondary productive activities fall within the ANZSIC Agriculture Subdivision", so the code is a frame attribute carried from the ABS Business Register rather than something the farm reported. On the FLAD Control table it sits with z_evao and z_state as that year's classification of the unit.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
value_definition: A numeric ANZSIC 2006 code; the item list does not say which level of the classification it is held at. Agricultural units fall within Subdivision 01, Agriculture.
limitation: It is the business's classified main activity, not what the paddocks grew. A mixed cropping and grazing farm gets one code, and the code is maintained on the register rather than at the farm, so a change between years can be an ABS reclassification rather than a change of enterprise.
rationale: The ABS agricultural methodology states that ANZSIC is what identifies a business as agricultural for the collection FLAD is built from, which is exactly the role this column plays on the Control table.
evidence_quote: Businesses are identified as undertaking agricultural activity if any of their primary or secondary productive activities fall within the ANZSIC Agriculture Subdivision.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'ANZSIC industry code 2006' with 'Numeric' as both value definition and limitation, and gave no edition, no level and no hint that the code is a frame attribute used for selection.

value_domain: Area of holding set aside for conservation, hectares
value_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
variable_description: The area of the farm's holding set aside for conservation or protection during the year, in hectares. It is one of six land use columns that divide the same holding by purpose; the ABS calls this class "Land set aside for conservation/protection purposes" and put it at 7.4 million hectares nationally in 2016-17, against 393.8 million hectares of agricultural holdings in total. The use columns are a different cut of the holding from the four tenure columns (owned, leased, crown and other land), so the two sets should not be added together.
description_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date rather than a flow over the year.
limitation: Setting land aside is a management statement by the operator, not a covenant, a reserve listing or a protected-area declaration, so this column cannot be read as land under a formal conservation agreement, and nothing on the row says whether the set-aside persisted into the next year.
rationale: The ABS land management release names conservation and protection as one of the reported land uses on agricultural holdings and gives the national area, which fixes both the meaning and the scale of this column.
evidence_quote: Land set aside for conservation/protection purposes
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Land use: Conservation land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the figure is a self-declared set-aside rather than a protected area.

value_domain: Area of holding under crops, hectares
value_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
variable_description: The area of the farm's holding under crops during the year, in hectares. It is the second largest of the six land use columns nationally, with the ABS reporting 31.1 million hectares of crops against 340.8 million hectares of grazing land in 2016-17. This is the whole-of-holding total; the a_ columns on the same row give area by individual crop, and the a_irrig_ columns give the irrigated part.
description_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date, covering the holding as a whole rather than any one crop.
limitation: This total and the sum of the a_ crop columns need not agree, because a paddock double cropped in one year counts under two crops but is one area of cropping land. It also does not separate irrigated from dryland cropping, which is what the a_irrig_ columns are for.
rationale: The ABS land management release reports cropping as one of the land uses on agricultural holdings with a national area, which fixes the concept and its scale; the relation to the per-crop columns comes from the FLAD item list itself.
evidence_quote: 31 million hectares
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Land use: Cropping land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and gave a reader no way to see why it will not reconcile with the per-crop area columns beside it.

value_domain: Area of holding held as Crown land, hectares
value_source: ABS, 2020-21 Agricultural Census topics and data release plan
variable_description: The part of the farm's holding occupied under a Crown tenure rather than owned outright or privately leased, in hectares. It is one of four tenure columns that between them partition k_land, the total area of holding, alongside owned, leased and other land. Crown tenure is the normal arrangement across the pastoral rangelands, so this column is what separates the pastoral north and west from the largely freehold south and east.
description_source: ABS, 2020-21 Agricultural Census topics and data release plan
value_definition: Hectares of the holding occupied under a Crown tenure, a stock at the collection's reference date and one of the four tenure parts of the area of holding.
limitation: The boundary between this column and z_leased_land is not defined in the item list, and a pastoral lease is itself a Crown lease, so operators in different states can split the same arrangement differently and the two tenure columns are not safely comparable across jurisdictions.
rationale: The ABS confirms the Agricultural Census collects "area of holding and area of land used by purpose", which places this column in the holding rather than in the land use split; the tenure categories themselves come from the BLADE item list.
evidence_quote: area of holding and area of land used by purpose
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Area of holding: Land area crown land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and never flagged the overlap with the leased-land column.

value_domain: Estimated Value of Agricultural Operations, dollars
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: The ABS's own estimate of the scale of a farm's agricultural activity in dollars, which is also what decides whether the farm is in the collection at all. The ABS defines it plainly: "EVAO is an ABS construct used to estimate the extent of agricultural activity undertaken, and relative size of agricultural businesses", and "It is calculated by applying three-year average prices to estimated livestock sales, livestock numbers and crop production of a business." Because the frame is cut on it - a business was in scope for 2020-21 if "the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater" - it works as a selection variable as much as a size variable.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
value_definition: A dollar amount, derived annually by the ABS from volumes and three-year average prices. It is not reported income, turnover or profit, and it is not taken from the tax data elsewhere in BLADE.
limitation: It will not move with a price spike or a drought-year destocking, because the prices in it are three-year averages applied to volumes. The $40,000 cut-off is the figure the ABS states for 2020-21, and the earlier years FLAD spans are not documented on that page, so the scope rule behind any given FLAD year has to be checked before a population is treated as constant.
rationale: The ABS agricultural methodology defines EVAO, gives its calculation and states the dollar cut-off that puts a business in scope, which is exactly what this frame column carries.
evidence_quote: EVAO is an ABS construct used to estimate the extent of agricultural activity undertaken, and relative size of agricultural businesses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Expected Value of Agricultural Operations (EVAO) frame' with 'Numeric ($)' as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the dollars are an ABS construct rather than revenue, or that the cut-off moved.

value_domain: Area of holding under plantation forest, hectares
value_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
variable_description: The area of the farm's holding under plantation forest during the year, in hectares. It is the smallest of the six land use columns for most farms: the ABS reported plantation and native forest on agricultural holdings together at about 774 thousand hectares in 2016-17, against 393.8 million hectares of holdings overall. It is therefore a specialist column, non-zero for a minority of farms, and not a measure of tree cover on the property.
description_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date, restricted to planted production forest.
limitation: Native forest and remnant vegetation on the holding do not count here and generally fall into other non-agricultural land, so this column understates trees on farms. A zero and an unreported value also look identical, which matters because most farms genuinely have none.
rationale: The ABS land management release reports forestry on agricultural holdings, separating plantation from native forest and giving the national area, which fixes what this column does and does not include.
evidence_quote: Total area of Land used for forestry now includes the area of both Plantation and Native forests.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Land use: Plantation forest land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and did not warn that native forest is excluded.

value_domain: Share of business income from government grants, per cent
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The share of the farm business's income for the year that came from government grants, as a percentage. It is the column that makes drought, flood and disaster assistance visible in a farm's income mix, so it rises in bad seasons and in declared regions rather than tracking anything about the farm's production. It is one of four income shares on the row and is read against z_ag_income, the agricultural share it is usually displacing.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A percentage between 0 and 100, one value per farm-year, derived within FLAD as a component of total business income.
limitation: It names neither the programme nor the payer, so exceptional circumstances relief, an exit grant and an industry levy rebate are indistinguishable. Being a share, a rise can equally mean grants went up or that farm income collapsed, and the row carries no dollar total to tell which.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page establishes FLAD as an integrated farm-level source; the reading of this column as one of four mutually exclusive income shares with no dollar denominator comes from the FLAD item list itself.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Income sources: government grants share of income' with '%' as both value definition and limitation, so nothing warned that a share can move because the denominator fell.

value_domain: Area of holding used for grazing, hectares
value_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
variable_description: The area of the farm's holding used for grazing during the year, in hectares, which for most of Australia is nearly the whole holding. The ABS put grazing at 340.8 million of the 393.8 million hectares of agricultural land held in 2016-17, about 87 per cent, spread across 88,073 agricultural businesses. Because rangeland grazing runs at very low stocking rates, this column dominates any land area total and has to be read against k_beef and k_sheep on the same row to get intensity.
description_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date, covering land grazed rather than land sown to pasture.
limitation: Hectares are not carrying capacity. A hectare of Barkly Tableland and a hectare of Gippsland pasture each count once, so grazing area is a poor proxy for herd size, output or land value, and a farm that destocks in drought shows no change in this column.
rationale: The ABS land management release reports grazing as the dominant land use on agricultural holdings with a national area and a business count, which fixes both the concept and how much of the holding it typically is.
evidence_quote: 341 million hectares (or 87%)
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Land use: Grazing land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said that this one column carries most of the continent's agricultural area.

value_domain: Area of holding held under lease, hectares
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Land and Water Ownership, explanatory notes, 2015-16
variable_description: The part of the farm's holding held under lease rather than owned outright, in hectares. It is one of four tenure columns that partition k_land, the total area of holding, alongside owned, Crown and other land. The lease share is what exposes a farm business to rent and to non-renewal, and it tends to move first when a farm expands, since operators commonly lease country before buying it.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Land and Water Ownership, explanatory notes, 2015-16
value_definition: Hectares of the holding held under lease, a stock at the collection's reference date and one of the four tenure parts of the area of holding.
limitation: Tenure is not defined the same way across ABS agriculture products: the Agricultural Land and Water Ownership survey treated "holders of agricultural land leases of five years or longer" as owners of that land, so a farm that is lease-heavy here can appear as an owner-occupier there, and the two cannot be reconciled by arithmetic.
rationale: The ABS ownership survey explanatory notes state the five-year rule that makes ABS lease and ownership measures non-comparable, which is the specific trap a reader of this column falls into.
evidence_quote: holders of agricultural land leases of five years or longer were considered to be owners of the land
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Area of holding: Land area leased' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and gave no warning that other ABS products count long leases as ownership.

value_domain: Count of units sharing one latitude and longitude in the year
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: How many units in that year sit at exactly the same latitude and longitude as this farm. It is a crowding measure on the geocode rather than anything about the farm itself: a value of 1 means the coordinate identifies this farm alone; a high value means the point is shared, typically a locality or postcode centroid standing in for several holdings at once. It is read with z_ll_filter, which records how the coordinate was derived in the first place.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A positive integer, one value per farm-year, counting occurrences of the coordinate pair within that year.
limitation: It says nothing about how far apart the farms actually are, only that a coordinate cannot separate them, so it is a precision and disclosure warning rather than a measure of neighbouring farms or of local farm density.
rationale: The custodian's own item text describes the column as a count of how often a latitude and longitude combination appears in a given year; the ABS BLADE page establishes FLAD as the BLADE source it belongs to. No published FLAD dictionary was reachable.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the custodian's sentence as the description with 'Numeric' as both value definition and limitation, so it never said why a user would care - that a high count marks an imprecise geocode.

value_domain: Code for the spatial method used to geocode the unit
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: Which spatial technique was used to place this farm on the map in that year, which is what tells a reader how far to trust its coordinates. It is the quality flag sitting behind mb_code_2021 and sa2 on the same Control row, so any weather, soil, water or distance measure joined to a farm by location inherits whatever precision this code records. Unlike z_ll_count, which counts collisions after the fact, this column names the method that produced the point.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A numeric code identifying a geocoding technique. The BLADE item list does not publish the techniques or their code values.
limitation: It gives no distance error. A code cannot be converted into metres, so records can be ranked by method but not tested for whether a farm was placed within its paddocks or merely within a postcode, and there is no threshold at which a location join becomes safe.
rationale: The custodian's item text says the column filters the types of spatial analysis technique used to determine a unit's latitude and longitude in a year; the ABS BLADE page confirms FLAD as the BLADE source. No published code list was reachable.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the custodian's sentence with 'Numeric' as both value definition and limitation, and did not say that the geography columns on the same row depend on this flag.

value_domain: Area of holding in non-agricultural use, hectares
value_source: ABS, 2020-21 Agricultural Census topics and data release plan
variable_description: The area of the holding that carried no agricultural use at all during the year, in hectares - buildings, tracks, unused country and remnant vegetation. It is the outer residual of the six land use columns, absorbing whatever the other five do not name, so on a small intensive holding it can be a large fraction while on a rangeland property it is trivial beside grazing land. It is not the same residual as z_other_ag_land, which holds land in an agricultural use the classification does not name.
description_source: ABS, 2020-21 Agricultural Census topics and data release plan
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date, defined by exclusion from the five named uses.
limitation: Its size depends on how completely the other five use columns were filled in, so a farm that did not report its conservation area can show that land here instead. It therefore cannot stand on its own as a measure of unused or natural land on farms.
rationale: The ABS confirms the Agricultural Census collects area of land used by purpose, which is the split this residual closes; the residual reading comes from the FLAD item list, where this is one of six exhaustive land use columns.
evidence_quote: area of holding and area of land used by purpose
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Land use: Other non-agricultural land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and did not distinguish it from the other-agricultural-land residual beside it.

value_domain: Share of business income earned off the farm, per cent
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The share of the business's income for the year earned off the farm, as a percentage. Off-farm earnings are what keep many small Australian holdings solvent, so a high value marks an operation leaning on wages, investments or a second business rather than on production. Read against z_ag_income, it separates commercial farms from part-time and lifestyle holdings far better than area of holding does.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A percentage between 0 and 100, one value per farm-year, as a component of total business income.
limitation: It does not say what the off-farm income is or who earned it, so a partner's salary, a contracting sideline and a share portfolio all read the same. FLAD's unit is the business, so this is not a household income measure and cannot be compared with survey estimates of farm household income.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page establishes FLAD as the integrated farm-level source; that this is one of four income shares with no dollar denominator and a business rather than household unit comes from the FLAD item list.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Income sources: off-farm income share' with '%' as both value definition and limitation, and did not flag that the unit is the business, not the farm household.

value_domain: Area of holding in other agricultural use, hectares
value_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
variable_description: The area of the holding under an agricultural use that is not cropping, grazing, plantation forest or conservation, in hectares. The ABS reported land for other agricultural purposes at about 110 thousand hectares in 2016-17, so it is negligible nationally and matters only for particular industries such as intensive animal production and nurseries. It is the residual inside the agricultural side of the land use split, distinct from z_non_ag_land, which covers land with no agricultural use at all.
description_source: ABS, Land Management and Farming in Australia, 2016-17
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date, defined by exclusion from the four named agricultural uses.
limitation: It pools unlike industries into a single number, so a value here cannot be attributed to any activity, and its national total is small enough that a handful of large holdings can dominate any regional figure built from it.
rationale: The ABS land management release reports other agricultural purposes as a distinct land use on agricultural holdings and gives its national area, which fixes both the concept and how small it is.
evidence_quote: Other agricultural purposes
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Land use: Other agricultural land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and never separated it from the non-agricultural residual.

value_domain: Share of business income from other sources, per cent
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The share of the business's income for the year from sources other than agriculture, government grants and off-farm earnings. It is the residual of the four income shares, so its job is to close the composition to 100 per cent rather than to name any income type. A large value is a warning about the other three shares, since it means most of that farm's income was not classified.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A percentage between 0 and 100, one value per farm-year, defined by exclusion from the three named income sources.
limitation: Because it is defined by what it is not, its content changes with how well the other three shares were measured in that year. It therefore cannot be compared across years or between farms as though it were a stable income category.
rationale: The ABS BLADE page establishes FLAD as the integrated farm-level source; the residual reading comes from the FLAD item list, where these four shares are the only income columns on the table.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Income sources: other funding sources share' with '%' as both value definition and limitation, and did not say the column is a residual whose meaning shifts with the quality of its neighbours.

value_domain: Area of holding under other tenure, hectares
value_source: ABS, 2020-21 Agricultural Census topics and data release plan
variable_description: The part of the farm's holding held under a tenure that is neither owned, leased nor Crown land, in hectares. It covers arrangements such as sharefarming, agistment and occupation under licence, and is the residual of the four tenure columns, which together should reconcile to k_land, the total area of holding on the same row. It answers a different question from z_non_ag_land: that column is about what the land is used for, this one about how it is held.
description_source: ABS, 2020-21 Agricultural Census topics and data release plan
value_definition: Hectares, a stock at the collection's reference date, defined by exclusion from the three named tenures.
limitation: It names no tenure, so it supports no statement about property rights or security of occupation. In practice a large value usually means the operator could not fit an arrangement to the three named categories, not that an exotic tenure exists.
rationale: The ABS confirms the Agricultural Census collects area of holding, which is the total this tenure residual helps close; the four-way tenure split comes from the FLAD item list.
evidence_quote: area of holding and area of land used by purpose
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Area of holding: Other land' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and did not say it is a tenure residual rather than a land use.

value_domain: Area of holding owned by the business, hectares
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Land and Water Ownership, explanatory notes, 2015-16
variable_description: The part of the farm's holding the business owns, in hectares, as against land it leases or occupies under Crown tenure. With z_leased_land, z_crown_land and z_other_land it partitions the area of holding on the same row. Ownership share is the closest thing FLAD carries to a balance sheet: an owner-occupier holds land value and mortgage risk, a lessee holds rent obligations instead.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Land and Water Ownership, explanatory notes, 2015-16
value_definition: Hectares of the holding the business owns outright, a stock at the collection's reference date and one of the four tenure parts of the area of holding.
limitation: This is area owned, not value owned and not equity, so a fully mortgaged property counts as owned in full and a debt-free farm cannot be told from a heavily geared one. The ABS ownership survey also counted long leases as ownership, so the two products disagree by construction rather than by error.
rationale: The ABS ownership survey explanatory notes state the rule that makes ABS ownership measures non-comparable with a lease-based tenure split, which is the confusion a reader of this column meets first.
evidence_quote: holders of agricultural land leases of five years or longer were considered to be owners of the land
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Area of holding: land area owned' with 'Numeric (ha)' as both value definition and limitation, and left a reader free to treat area owned as a wealth or equity measure.

value_domain: ABS-assigned agricultural frame code (PSI)
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: An ABS-assigned code attached to the farm unit on the FLAD control record, sitting with its industry, state, EVAO and geocode. The Control table holds the frame attributes for a farm-year rather than anything the farm reported, so this code belongs to how the ABS organised the collection, not to how the farm operated. The published ABS agricultural methodology does not expand the acronym or list the code values, so its meaning cannot be confirmed from a fetchable source.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
value_definition: A numeric code. The ABS agricultural statistics pages neither expand PSI nor publish the values it can take.
limitation: It should not be used as an explanatory variable before the DataLab documentation is read. An unexplained frame code can encode collection, stratification or estimation treatment, and modelling on it would attribute the collection's mechanics to the farms.
rationale: The ABS agricultural methodology describes how the agricultural frame is built from the ABS Business Register and which attributes classify a unit, which places this column among the frame attributes even though it does not name PSI.
evidence_quote: Businesses on the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Business Register (ABSBR) were in scope for the 2020-21 Agricultural Census if: they undertook agricultural activity, and the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'ABS PSI code' with 'Numeric' as both value definition and limitation, and did not say that the acronym is unexplained, which is itself the finding a reader needs.

value_domain: ABS state and territory code, 1 to 8
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS), Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The state or territory the farm holding was recorded in for that year, coded 1 for New South Wales through to 8 for the Australian Capital Territory. It is a Control table frame attribute, fixed for the farm-year rather than restated on every observation, and it follows the ABS states and territories level, which the ASGS describes as "a cartographic representation of legally designated state and territory boundaries". It is the coarsest of the three geographies on the same row, above sa2 and mb_code_2021.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS), Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
value_definition: A single digit: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory, with missing carried separately. No code for Other Territories appears in the item list.
limitation: A holding can straddle a state border and a business address can sit in a different state from its paddocks, so this column cannot be used to allocate land or production to a state; the mesh block and SA2 columns are the ones that carry the location the geocode actually resolved to.
rationale: The ASGS is the ABS classification that defines the states and territories level this column codes to; the specific numbering is carried in the variable's own valid-response text in the BLADE item list.
evidence_quote: a cartographic representation of legally designated state and territory boundaries
supersedes_rationale: The entry reprinted the eight-code list as both the valid values and the value definition and said nothing about which state is meant when a holding crosses a border.

value_domain: ABS estimation treatment code (USI)
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: An ABS code marking the estimation treatment applied to the farm unit, rather than any quantity the farm reported. That reading follows the label's own wording, and it sits with z_psi as a processing attribute of the collection, which makes it the column a careful analyst would want in order to separate reported farm-years from derived ones. The accessible ABS agricultural documentation does not expand USI or publish the code values, so which treatments the codes distinguish cannot be confirmed here.
description_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2020-21
value_definition: A numeric code. The ABS agricultural statistics pages neither expand USI nor publish the estimation treatments its values stand for.
limitation: Without the code list a reader cannot tell a reported farm-year from an estimated one, which is the check FLAD most needs given it spans census and non-census years. Do not assume the modal value means fully reported, or that a constant value across a farm's history means the farm was collected every year.
rationale: The ABS agricultural methodology describes the collection FLAD is built from, including the census scope rules that create the need for estimation, which is the context this code belongs to even though the page does not name USI.
evidence_quote: It is calculated by applying three-year average prices to estimated livestock sales, livestock numbers and crop production of a business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'ABS USI estimation codes' with 'Numeric' as both value definition and limitation, and never said that this is a processing flag rather than a farm characteristic.

value_domain: Financial year of the FLAD control record
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The financial year whose frame attributes - industry, state, EVAO, geocode and geocoding quality - this control record describes. It is the Control table's own year index and matches the year column on the FLAD IDW and SUC observation tables, which is how a farm's measurements are joined to the classification in force for them. The ABS gives FLAD's span in BLADE as "Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20", which bounds the values.
description_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
value_definition: A numeric financial year within 2000-01 to 2019-20. One control row per farm-year.
limitation: It says which year a classification applies to, not that the farm was collected in that year, and it does not distinguish a census year from a sample year. Joining an observation to the wrong control year silently attaches the wrong industry, state or EVAO, since all three can change between years for an unchanged farm.
rationale: The ABS BLADE data page names FLAD as a requestable BLADE source and states its coverage, which bounds this year index; the control-versus-observation split comes from the BLADE item list.
evidence_quote: Farm Level Analytical Dataset (FLAD): 2000-01 to 2019-20
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Financial year' with 'Numeric' as both value definition and limitation, and did not distinguish it from the year column on the observation tables.

value_domain: Declared zinc content of an exported ore shipment, per cent
value_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
variable_description: The zinc content declared for an exporter's shipment of ore or concentrate, as a percentage of the shipment. The AHECC "is used in the preparation of export documentation and in the compilation of Australian export statistics", and metal content is what turns a declared gross weight into a contained-metal quantity, so this is a property of the goods on the declaration rather than of the business. It is populated only for the small number of firms exporting zinc-bearing ores, and sits with the copper, lead, nickel, platinum, tantalum, tin and tungsten percentage columns, several of which can be non-zero on one polymetallic shipment.
description_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
value_definition: A percentage from 0 to 100 taken from the export declaration, against a commodity classified under the AHECC, chapter 26 for ores, slag and ash. The export data are administrative by-product from customs declarations lodged with the Department of Home Affairs, not an ABS collection.
limitation: It is a declared grade, not an assay the ABS verified, and it belongs to a shipment. Averaging it over a firm's exports without weighting by tonnage produces a grade no shipment had, and a zero or missing value means no zinc-bearing ore was declared on that export rather than that the firm mines no zinc.
rationale: The AHECC is the classification exporters use on the declarations that BLADE's merchandise export data are compiled from, and the AHECC release itself points to the Department of Home Affairs and the Australian Border Force as the agencies those declarations are lodged with, which is what makes this a declared rather than a measured figure.
evidence_quote: The AHECC is used in the preparation of export documentation and in the compilation of Australian export statistics.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Percentage of zinc in shipment of ore' with 'Numeric (%)' as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the figure is declared by the exporter and belongs to a shipment rather than to the firm.

value_domain: Australian Business Number (hashed and truncated)
value_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
variable_description: The partnership, trust or company the individual held an interest in. Business ownership is recorded as a link between a person and an entity, and this is the entity half of that link, so it is what turns the file from a list of people into a list of ownership relationships. The same entity carries the same value in BLADE and in the ATO products, which is how an owner can be followed to the business they own.
description_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
value_definition: A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as "a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register", structured as "a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded and is useful only for matching one record to another.
limitation: The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a business as a going concern. A structure with several entities appears as several identifiers with nothing linking them, and an entity that restructures takes a new ABN, so continuous ownership can look like a disposal and an acquisition. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The DIL gives the field as a hashed ABN on the partnership tables, which record an individual's interest in an entity. The Australian Business Register publishes the ABN's format and issuer.
evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Hashed abn' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: ABS BLADE business identifier
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The business the person had an interest in, keyed the way the business is keyed in BLADE. The later business owner tables replaced the truncated ABN hash, which runs through to 2021-22, with this identifier; the 2023-24 data item list calls it the BLADE number. Because BLADE holds business activity statements, business income tax filings, PAYG and Single Touch Payroll for "all active businesses from 2001-02 to current", the key is what lets a partner or sole trader be joined to their business's turnover, employment and survival. The person on the same row is identified by the synthetic person key instead.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: An opaque business-level identifier, one value per business unit, stable across BLADE tables and across the business owner tables that carry it.
limitation: A business identifier is not a business as an owner would describe it: a restructure or a new ABN can mint a new key for the same underlying operation, so ownership spells break where the entity is reorganised. The key also carries no industry, size or location, all of which have to come from the BLADE frame.
rationale: The 2023-24 business owner tables label the field 'BLADE number' while the earlier tables in the same series use a hashed ABN in the same position, and ABS publishes what BLADE is and which business data it combines. The switch from hashed ABN to BLADE number is read from the data item list rather than from a published note.
evidence_quote: The current BLADE asset contains data on all active businesses from 2001-02 to current
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried no description at all from the custodian and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the page named a column with nothing behind it.

value_domain: ATO extract reference period
value_source: ABS administrative income sources
variable_description: The period the ATO extract this row came from refers to, not anything about the owner or the entity. Partnership and trust returns are lodged later than individual returns and amended more often, so an ownership file is more sensitive to extract timing than an income file: an early extract can miss an ownership interest entirely rather than merely understate it.
description_source: ABS administrative income sources
limitation: The column describes the extract, not the ownership, so it is never an analysis variable. An interest absent from an early extract may exist and be lodged later, which reads as an acquisition that did not happen.
rationale: The field is named as an extract reference period on the ATO partnership tables. ABS documents the administrative income sources as point-in-time extracts but publishes no definition of this column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Extract reference period' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Income year the ownership record belongs to
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return and instructions 2024
variable_description: The income year in which the person is recorded as owning the business, running 1 July to 30 June. Each table covers one year and each row is a person-business pair within it, so a spell of ownership is reconstructed by stacking years rather than by reading a start and end date. The underlying record comes from the annual return the business lodges, and the ATO does not require a partnership return where the only joint income was "rent from a jointly owned investment property", interest from a joint account or dividends from jointly held shares, so passive co-ownership does not generate a row.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return and instructions 2024
value_definition: A financial year label for the table the row sits in, constant within a table and used to order the yearly files into a panel.
limitation: It dates the return, not the ownership. A partnership formed in March and one formed the previous July look identical, and a business that ceased mid-year still appears for the whole year, so entry and exit cannot be dated more finely than annually. Some tables also come in twelve-month and sixteen-month extract versions for the same year, which are different vintages of the same reporting year rather than different periods.
rationale: The business owner tables are built one file per income year from the annual partnership and sole trader returns, and the ATO instructions for that return state who must lodge it, which sets the population the yearly file covers. The mapping from the field to the return's income year is read from the table structure rather than from a published data dictionary.
evidence_quote: You don't need to lodge a partnership tax return if you were not in a partnership carrying on a business or where the only income you derived jointly (or in common) with another person was: rent from a jointly owned investment property
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Financial year' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the year dates the return rather than the ownership, or that the sixteen-month tables are a second vintage of the same year.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage spine identifier (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The individual whose interest in a business the row records, as the key that carries them across the whole asset. Each row pairs one person with one business for one year, so the rows under a key are that person's ownership history: how many businesses, over how many years, and as a partner or a sole trader according to which table the row sits in. Because the key is the PLIDA spine identifier, that history joins to the same person's wage income, Centrelink payments and Census answers, which is what makes questions about who starts a business answerable. In this package the values are synthetic and stand for nobody.
description_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure, one value per person, stable across the yearly partnership and sole trader tables and across every other dataset linked through the Spine.
limitation: It records a link to a business, not control of one: a silent partner and a working partner look identical, and the row carries no ownership share. Company directors and shareholders are outside these tables entirely, so a person running an incorporated business has no row here at all.
rationale: The data item list gives the field as the synthetic person identifier on every business owner table, and ABS publishes what the Spine is, which datasets build it and why each dataset is linked to it once, which is what determines what this key can be joined to.
evidence_quote: Instead of linking datasets one-to-one for individual projects, we can link all datasets to the Spine once and then combine datasets via the Spine as needed for multiple projects.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a row means or that incorporated businesses are out of scope.

value_domain: Census Australian Defence Force service, detailed
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)
variable_description: Whether a person is in the Australian Defence Force now, has served before, or has done both, kept separate for regular and reserve service. The ABS says the ADF "consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), so it distinguishes a current regular who once served in the reserves from one who has only ever been a regular. ADFP on the same person row is the four-category collapse of the same answer, and both columns are new to the 2021 Census person table.
description_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)
value_definition: A single digit 1 to 8: four codes for people still serving (regular only, reserves only, and the two mixed histories), three for people who have left (regular only, reserves only, both), and 8 for never served. Not stated is '&', not applicable '@' and overseas visitor 'V'. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over.
limitation: It carries no rank, service branch, length of service, deployment or discharge date, so it cannot identify veterans by war service or by eligibility for Department of Veterans' Affairs support. It is a self-report at one Census night in August 2021 and there is no equivalent column on the 2011 or 2016 person tables, so a service history cannot be assembled across Censuses.
rationale: The variable is an ABS Census output variable and the ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for it, giving the definition, the eight-way category split and the scope.
evidence_quote: The Australian Defence Force (ADF) consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Australian defence force service detailed', with the value domain given as 'finite source-defined values' and the limitation as 'The source defines the value domain. Frequency information is not included.', so nothing on the page said how it differed from ADFP.

value_domain: ASGS Australian Drainage Division code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
variable_description: The river basin the dwelling sits in, coded from where the dwelling was enumerated. The ABS defines these divisions as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric" (ASGS Edition 3), so this is a hydrological region rather than an administrative one. It sits with the other geography codes on the 2021 dwelling row - SA1UCD to SA4UCD, STEUCD, LGAD, POAD and CEDD - and is the one that places a dwelling in a catchment rather than in an administrative area.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
value_definition: A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: the letter D followed by a two-digit division number, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. There are 17 Australian Drainage Divisions covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps, and that count already includes the three non-spatial special purpose codes D94 No usual address, D97 Migratory - Offshore - Shipping and DZZ Outside Australia. D91 Unclassified (Aust.) carries Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island.
limitation: A drainage division is not nested inside a state - the Murray-Darling Basin crosses four states and territories - so division totals and state totals are different groupings and the two cannot be treated as a hierarchy. Because the boundary is a Mesh Block approximation of the Geofabric rather than a surveyed catchment line, a dwelling close to a divide can be allocated to the neighbouring division.
rationale: The '(en)' suffix in the PLIDA item name and the dwelling table it sits on identify this as the enumeration-based ASGS coding of the dwelling, and the ASGS Edition 3 Non ABS Structures page defines the division, its coding and its count.
evidence_quote: Australian Drainage Divisions are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and the sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page never said what a drainage division is or that the codes come from the ASGS.

value_domain: ASGS Australian Drainage Division code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
variable_description: The river basin containing the person's usual address, coded from place of usual residence rather than from where they were counted on Census night. The ABS defines the divisions as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric" (ASGS Edition 3). Where a person was away from home in August 2021 this can differ from ADDIVD on the dwelling record they were enumerated in, which is the enumeration-based coding of the same classification.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
value_definition: A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: D followed by two digits, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. The 17 divisions cover the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps and that count already includes the three non-spatial special purpose codes D94, D97 and DZZ; D91 Unclassified (Aust.) holds the Other Territories.
limitation: Living in a division does not mean drawing on its water, since most urban supply is piped across catchments, so this is a location code rather than a measure of exposure to a basin's water resources. It is also one snapshot of usual residence, so a move between divisions during the year leaves no trace here.
rationale: The '(ur)' suffix and the person table identify this as the usual-residence coding of the ASGS drainage division, and the ASGS Edition 3 page defines the division and its codes.
evidence_quote: Australian Drainage Divisions are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' was printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page never explained the classification or that this is the usual-residence coding of it.

value_domain: Census Australian Defence Force service
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service (ADFP)
variable_description: Whether a person has ever served in the Australian Defence Force and, if so, whether they are still serving. value_domain: ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
variable_description: The top level of the geographic coding of the person's usual address: whether that address is in geographic Australia at all. The ABS defines place of usual residence as "the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and AUSTP is the Australia (AUS) level of that coding, the coarsest of the geography columns on the 2021 person table alongside STEUCP, SA4UCP down to MBUCP for the same address. Its practical job is to isolate the overseas visitor, no usual address and migratory, off-shore and shipping cases before any finer geography is analysed.
description_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
value_definition: The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS Main Structure, the top of the hierarchy that Mesh Blocks, SA1s to SA4s and states and territories aggregate into, together with the extra categories the usual residence coding carries: no usual address, migratory, off-shore and shipping, and overseas visitor (VVVV). There is no not stated code: an incomplete usual address is imputed, and IFPURP records that it was.
limitation: Being the top of the hierarchy, it separates almost nobody: nearly every person counted has a usual address in Australia, so a cross-tabulation on this column alone will look empty. It also records the address as at Census night 2021, not a residency test, so a person on a short overseas posting who kept an Australian usual address is coded in Australia.

value_domain: Census country of birth of parents summary
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of parents (BPPP)
variable_description: Whether each of a person's parents was born in Australia or overseas, reduced to one code. The ABS says it "indicates if a person's father and/or mother was born in Australia or overseas" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021).
