value_domain: Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains made by a later buyer of a forestry scheme interest held twelve months or more, before the CGT discount. The people who report here are second-hand holders, not the original investors: "In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant", and such buyers "are not able to claim a deduction for the costs of acquiring the forestry interest" and instead carry them in the cost base. The gain arises on sale of the interest or on receipt of harvest proceeds.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It is the discount cell of the forestry row, present on the schedule from the 2008 edition onwards.
limitation: The column describes the secondary market only. An initial participant deducts the cost of the interest and reports scheme income at the forestry income item on the return, so the money that built the plantations is not in this dataset. Thinning receipts are also excluded, being assessable income rather than capital proceeds.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active forestry managed investment scheme row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide defines subsequent participants and their capital account treatment.
evidence_quote: In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said only later buyers report here.

value_domain: Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains on a forestry scheme interest worked out under indexation, a box that in practice is almost never used. The ATO treats a forestry interest as a CGT asset only for a later buyer: "You are a subsequent participant if you are not an initial participant", and "Amounts you receive from a CGT event that happens to your forestry interest, for example the sale of your forestry interest or as harvest proceeds, are capital proceeds for CGT purposes". Indexation needs an acquisition before 21 September 1999, which is years before the forestry scheme rules and this row existed.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It is the indexation cell of the forestry row that the ATO added to part A of the schedule in the 2008 edition.
limitation: Expect this cell to be empty in almost every year, and treat a value in it as a lodgement error rather than a signal. The registry lists the column from 2000-01, but the 2007 edition of the schedule has no forestry row at all and the 2008 edition is the first that does.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active forestry managed investment scheme row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide sets out when a forestry interest is held on capital account and produces a capital gain. That indexation is closed to assets acquired after September 1999 is my inference applied to this row, not a statement the ATO makes about it.
evidence_quote: Amounts you receive from a CGT event that happens to your forestry interest, for example the sale of your forestry interest or as harvest proceeds, are capital proceeds for CGT purposes
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the row postdates the years it is listed for.

value_domain: Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains on a forestry scheme interest that qualify for no method relief, typically an interest bought and resold inside twelve months or held by a company. The ATO treats such an interest as a CGT asset only where it is not trading stock: "If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest." The gain here is simply proceeds less cost base.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no method-based reduction to come. It is the third cell of the forestry row, beside the indexation and discount cells.
limitation: This column cannot distinguish a quick resale from a company disposal, since both land here for different reasons. A dealer in forestry interests holds them on revenue account and reports nothing on this schedule at all, so the most active traders are invisible.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active forestry managed investment scheme row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide distinguishes revenue account from capital account holdings.
evidence_quote: If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said which holders are excluded.

value_domain: Hedging financial arrangement capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements
variable_description: Gains on a hedge that take capital character from the asset being hedged, reported under the discount method. The taxation of financial arrangements rules do this deliberately: they allow "gains and losses from certain hedging financial arrangements to be characterised and taxed in accordance with the tax treatment of the underlying item being hedged". Where the hedged item is a CGT asset, the ATO instructs the entity to "specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule".
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It is the discount cell of the hedging row, which the ATO added to part A of the schedule in the 2010 edition.
limitation: Only an entity with a valid hedging tax-timing election reports here, so the column measures an election as much as a hedging position; the same derivative held without the election produces ordinary income and never reaches this schedule. The registry lists the column back to 2000-01, but the 2009 edition of the schedule has no hedging row.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active hedging financial arrangements row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO page explains how the TOFA hedging method gives a hedge the character of the hedged item and directs the amount to this schedule.
evidence_quote: gains and losses from certain hedging financial arrangements to be characterised and taxed in accordance with the tax treatment of the underlying item being hedged
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing connected the row to the TOFA hedging election.

value_domain: Hedging financial arrangement capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements
variable_description: Capital gains on hedging arrangements where no method relief applies, which is the usual cell for a company running a hedge book. The ATO explains that under a valid election "gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged". The old schedule gives the hedging row only these two boxes, discount and other; there is no indexation box.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no later method-based reduction. It is the second and last cell of the hedging row.
limitation: The figure is one side of a hedge and means little on its own: the loss on the hedged asset it was meant to offset is reported in a different row of the same part, and the two cannot be paired from the schedule. It also gives no information about the notional value or the instrument type.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active hedging financial arrangements row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO page explains the character-matching rule that puts a hedging gain on this schedule.
evidence_quote: gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is one leg of a hedge.

value_domain: Other CGT assets and events, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
variable_description: Gains on assets held twelve months or more that have no row of their own, reported before the CGT discount is applied. The ATO example of what this row absorbs is telling: it names "the disposal of your forestry interests in a forestry managed investment scheme or hedging financial arrangements". This is the largest and least specific of the non-active rows, and the one most likely to move when the form is redesigned.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It stands for a mixed bag of CGT events rather than one asset class.
limitation: The content of this cell is not stable across years. Forestry scheme interests were pulled out into their own row on the 2008 schedule and hedging financial arrangements on the 2010 schedule, so a level shift around those years is a change in the form rather than in behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active other CGT assets row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix names forestry and hedging as examples of what falls in this class.
evidence_quote: the disposal of your forestry interests in a forestry managed investment scheme or hedging financial arrangements
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing warned that the row's coverage changed between editions of the form.

value_domain: Other CGT assets and events, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
variable_description: The residual row of the schedule under indexation: goodwill, contractual rights, payouts on the ending of an asset, anything without a row of its own. The ATO describes the class as covering a gain "that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule". Indexation confines it further to assets acquired before 11:45 am on 21 September 1999.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, measured against an indexed cost base. It is a catch-all row, so a single figure can combine several unrelated CGT events.
limitation: The column names no asset, so it cannot say what was disposed of, and two rows with the same amount can be entirely different transactions. It also absorbs whatever the form has not yet given a row to, which is why forestry and hedging gains sat here before those rows were added in 2008 and 2010.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active other CGT assets row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix defines the residual category.
evidence_quote: Other CGT assets refers to the capital gain or capital loss that you have made and that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this is a residual class.

value_domain: Other CGT assets and events, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
variable_description: Gains on unclassified CGT assets and events where neither indexation nor the discount applies, so the gain is simply proceeds less cost base. The ATO states the arithmetic as "you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds". For a company this is where most non-real-estate, non-share gains end up, because a company cannot use the discount column beside it.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no further method-based reduction. It combines any number of CGT events that share only their lack of a dedicated row.
limitation: This cell cannot be read as short-held activity the way the shares and real estate other-method cells can, because a company puts long-held assets here too. Payments that end a right or extinguish an asset also land here, and those are not disposals in any ordinary sense.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active other CGT assets row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained why a company concentrates in this column.

value_domain: Real estate capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method
variable_description: Capital gains on land and buildings held at least twelve months, stated before the CGT discount, and outside the small business concessions. The ATO allows the discount method for "assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method". This is the cell where an investment property sale by a trust or a superannuation fund normally lands.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses. Cost base adjustments made before this point, such as capital works deductions claimed over the ownership period, are already inside the figure.
limitation: It is a gain, not a sale price, and one row covers every property the entity disposed of in the year, so it cannot count transactions or track a single property. Gains on a property owned by an individual do not appear in this dataset at all unless a CGT schedule was lodged.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active real estate row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the twelve-month test that puts a gain in this column.
evidence_quote: assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is a gain before the discount.

value_domain: Real estate capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Indexation method
variable_description: Capital gains on land and buildings worked out by indexing the cost base for inflation, where no small business concession is claimed. The ATO explains that the method "allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999)", and that "The indexation of the cost base of an asset is frozen on 30 September 1999." Because indexation stops there, a long-held property indexed in 2010 gets no relief for the eleven years since.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Indexation method
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. The gain is measured against an indexed cost base rather than the historical cost, so it is smaller than the same disposal reported under the other method.
limitation: The old schedule has a single real estate row, so this cannot separate Australian property from foreign property; that split arrived only with the redesigned schedule, the 2013 form, which the CGT product picks up in the second part of 2012-13. Choosing indexation over the discount is an election, so a low value can reflect an adviser's arithmetic rather than the type of property sold.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active real estate row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix explains the indexation factor and the September 1999 freeze.
evidence_quote: The indexation of the cost base of an asset is frozen on 30 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what indexation does to the cost base.

value_domain: Real estate capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
variable_description: Capital gains on property that qualified for neither indexation nor the discount, which is mostly land and buildings bought and sold within a year. The ATO puts the calculation plainly: "To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds." Against the discount cell on the same row, a large figure here points to quick turnover or to a company vendor.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, and with no later reduction on the discount side of the form. It is the closest of the three real estate cells to a taxable amount.
limitation: Property developed and sold as a business is taxed as ordinary income, not as a capital gain, so the fastest turnover of all is missing from this column rather than concentrated in it. Nothing here says whether the property was residential or commercial.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active real estate row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix sets out the other method and when it must be used.
evidence_quote: You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing distinguished this column from the discount one.

value_domain: Shares and units capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units held at least twelve months, before the CGT discount is taken off. The ATO reserves the discount method for "assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method", and adds that "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies". The amount is the whole gain, not the halved one, because the discount is applied later at part F.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Together with the indexation and other cells on the same row it makes up the entity's total share and unit gains for the year.
limitation: The figure overstates what is taxed, often by half, because the discount is applied two parts later on the same form. A non-trivial value on a company return is a reporting error rather than a discount claim, since a company is not entitled to the discount unless it is a life insurance company or a friendly society.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active shares and units row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define when the discount method applies and which entities may use it.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that the discount has not yet been applied.

value_domain: Shares and units capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method and Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units that the entity worked out by indexing the cost base, and on which it claimed no small business concession. Indexation is closed to anything bought after the 1999 change, the ATO restricting it to "capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999". Non-active is the residual side of the grid: "If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets".
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method and Step 2 active assets
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It is one cell of the part A grid on the old CGT schedule, whose rows are asset classes and whose three columns are the indexation, discount and other methods.
limitation: A zero here does not mean the entity held no shares. A gain on shares bought after September 1999 has to be reported in the discount or other column instead, so this cell tracks the age of the holding as much as the asset class. The old schedule also runs shares and units together and does not separate listed from unlisted, so it cannot measure exposure to the Australian market.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active shares and units row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the three calculation methods and set the rule for what goes at non-active assets.
evidence_quote: If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what non-active means or which assets are allowed to use indexation.

value_domain: Shares and units capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units that get neither indexation nor the discount, which in practice means parcels bought and sold inside twelve months. The ATO defines the calculation as follows: "To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds." Read against the discount cell on the same row, this column is a rough marker of short-held trading rather than long-term holding.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Nothing further is deducted from these gains at parts F or G on the discount side, so the amount is closer to the taxable figure than its discount-method neighbour.
limitation: It is not a clean count of short-held disposals. A company reports every share gain here whatever the holding period, because it cannot use the discount, so the column measures entity type as much as trading behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active shares and units row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix sets out how the other method is worked out and when it must be used.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what the other method is.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at label O, part N of the CGT schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part N
variable_description: Whether the company still held assets bought before 20 September 1985 that Division 149 had not turned into post-CGT assets. The ATO puts the question as "At the end of the income year, did the company still have any assets that were acquired before 20 September 1985 and that were not treated as post-CGT assets under Division 149?" Division 149 resets the cost base of a pre-1985 asset once the majority underlying ownership of the company changes, so a yes marks a company still carrying genuinely grandfathered assets. Only companies answer it, which is why the custodian's wording is the eligibility line rather than the question.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part N
value_definition: A single yes or no indicator at label O, with no dollar amount attached. Part N is answered by companies only, so trusts and funds leave it empty rather than answering no.
limitation: It cannot tell you how many pre-CGT assets there are or what they are worth, and a no is ambiguous: the company may never have held pre-1985 assets, or Division 149 may already have converted every one of them. The question was also reworded between years - by 2006 the ATO instead asked whether there had been no change in the majority underlying interests - so the same label does not carry the same question across the whole series.
rationale: The table cgt_2000_01 is the 2000-01 capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO's guide for that year gives the exact wording of part N and its single label O.
evidence_quote: At the end of the income year, did the company still have any assets that were acquired before 20 September 1985 and that were not treated as post-CGT assets under Division 149?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the eligibility line 'To be completed by companies only' as its whole description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which question the label answers.

value_domain: Cost base reduction after an intra-group debt forgiveness (dollars), label Q
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part O
variable_description: How much a company wrote off the cost base of its shares in, and loans to, an associated company after a debt inside the group was forgiven. The ATO asks for "the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of all its shares and loans to the associated company", and only after the company answers yes at label P, which asks whether such a forgiveness or a substantial and permanent fall in the value of the debt happened. The amount matters because it lowers the gain the company can defer to a later year: value that left through the forgiven debt is taken out of the investment now.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part O
value_definition: A dollar amount of cost base written off across all affected shares and loans, reported as one total rather than asset by asset. It is a reduction in the base of an unsold asset, so no capital gain or loss is recorded with it.
limitation: It does not record the debt that was forgiven, only the flow-on adjustment to the shareholder's cost bases, so it cannot be read as the size of the write-off inside the group. It is also separate from the Division 245 net forgiven amount that the debtor company applies against its own losses and cost bases, which this schedule never captures.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part O prefix with label Q, and the ATO's 2001 guide sets out part O of the schedule, its trigger question at label P and exactly what amount label Q carries.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label P is Y for yes, show at label Q the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of all its shares and loans to the associated company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base reduction' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell which of the schedule's two cost base reductions this was.

value_domain: Cost base adjustment on a CGT event after an earlier debt forgiveness (dollars), label S
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part O
variable_description: How much a company adjusted the cost base of its shares in an associated company when it later sold them, after a debt inside the group had been forgiven. The ATO asks for "the total amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of all its shares in the associated company to which a CGT event happened", after a yes at label R. It is the later half of the same story as label Q on the same row: Q is the write-down when the debt goes, S is the correction made when the shares are finally disposed of.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part O
value_definition: A dollar amount of adjustment reported as one total across the shares that a CGT event happened to. It covers shares only, not the loans that label Q also covers.
limitation: It records an adjustment made at disposal, so a company that took a forgiveness hit but held on to the shares reports nothing here even though its cost bases changed. A zero therefore cannot be read as no debt forgiveness in the group; label Q is the column that answers that.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part O prefix with label S, and the ATO's 2001 guide gives part O in full, including the label R trigger question and the amount required at label S.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label R is Y for yes, show at label S the total amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of all its shares in the associated company to which a CGT event happened.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base adjustment' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it was indistinguishable from the loss transfer adjustment at label W.

value_domain: Count of options, rights or similar interests issued under a scrip for scrip arrangement, label I
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part L
variable_description: How many options, rights or similar interests the acquiring company or trust handed over in a scrip for scrip takeover. The ATO asks it of the acquirer: "Show at label I the number of options, rights or similar interests issued in exchange for the options, rights or similar interests acquired in the other entity." It sits beside the count of shares and units issued, so together the two columns describe the size of the paper consideration in a takeover where the target's holders took replacement scrip instead of cash.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part L
value_definition: A whole number of instruments issued, not an amount of money. Only the acquiring entity completes it, and only after answering yes at label E to being an acquiring entity in a scrip for scrip arrangement.
limitation: A count of options and rights says nothing about their value, and options with different exercise prices are added together, so it cannot be scaled into consideration paid. Where the acquirer bought interests in several original entities it reports only the one arrangement with the greatest cost base, so the figure understates a multi-target year.
rationale: Part L of the CGT schedule has labels E to M, and the registry holds a variable for every one of them except the target's tax file number at G and the two counts at H and I; this column is the options and rights count that the ATO requires at label I.
evidence_quote: Show at label I the number of options, rights or similar interests issued in exchange for the options, rights or similar interests acquired in the other entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text 'Number of options/rights etc issued' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to say that the count belongs to a scrip for scrip takeover or who reports it.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year that were not worked out under the discount method - the 'other' method and, for older assets, the indexation method. The ATO requires the other method where the holding period is short: "If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method to calculate your capital gain." Read against the discount-method total on the same row, this column is a rough measure of short-held against long-held disposals.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and the small business concessions. No CGT discount applies to these gains, so unlike the discount-method total this figure needs no later halving.
limitation: The column mixes the other method with the indexation method, which are different calculations, so it is not purely short-held gains. The amount is a gross gain rather than taxable income.
rationale: The DIL label names the total current year capital gains for other capital gains, a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide defines the three methods and states when the other method must be used.
evidence_quote: If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method to calculate your capital gain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Cost base adjustment where a group company received a transferred loss (dollars), label W
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part P
variable_description: The cost base adjustment a company made on selling shares in a group company that had earlier been given a tax loss by another member of the group. The ATO asks for "the amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of such assets" once label V is answered yes. Receiving a loss makes the subsidiary worth more, so the adjustment runs the opposite way to the reduction at label U on the same row, where the subsidiary had given a loss away.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part P
value_definition: A dollar amount of adjustment, totalled across the shares and loans that a CGT event happened to in the year. Part P is answered by companies only.
limitation: The direction of the adjustment is not recorded, so the column cannot be added to the reduction at label U to get a net figure without assuming which way each ran. Nothing here identifies the group company that transferred the loss or the size of the loss itself.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part P prefix with label W, and the ATO's 2001 guide gives part P in full, including the label V question about losses transferred into the investee and the amount required at label W.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label V is Y for yes, show at label W the amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of such assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base adjustment', identical to the debt forgiveness label, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Cost base reduction where a group company transferred a loss away (dollars), label U
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part P
variable_description: The cost base write-down a company made on selling shares in a group company that had earlier handed a tax loss to another member of the group. The ATO asks for "the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of such assets" once label T is answered yes. A company that gives away a loss gives away future deductions, so the investment in it is worth less and the holder must take that value out of its cost base rather than bank it as a capital loss on sale.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part P
value_definition: A dollar amount of cost base removed, totalled across the shares and loans that a CGT event happened to in the year. Part P is answered by companies only.
limitation: It measures the adjustment, not the loss transferred, so it cannot be used to size loss trading inside a group. Only assets that a CGT event happened to in the year appear, so a group that transfers losses freely but never sells the underlying shares reports nothing.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part P prefix with label U, and the ATO's 2001 guide gives part P in full, including the label T question about a loss transferred out of the investee and the amount required at label U.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label T is Y for yes, show at label U the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of such assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base reduction', identical to the debt forgiveness label, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Count of shares, units or other interests issued under a scrip for scrip arrangement, label H
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part L
variable_description: How many shares, units or other interests the acquiring company or trust issued to the target's holders in a scrip for scrip takeover. The ATO asks it of the acquirer: "Show at label H the number of shares, units or other interests issued in exchange for the shares or units or other interests acquired in the original entity." Scrip for scrip roll-over lets the target's holders defer their capital gain because they were paid in paper, so this count is the volume of that paper, with the cost base of the interests acquired reported separately at label K.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part L
value_definition: A whole number of shares, units or other interests issued, not an amount of money. Only the acquiring entity completes it, and only after answering yes at label E.
limitation: A share count cannot be turned into value without a price, and shares of different classes are added together, so it is not a measure of the deal size. It is also reported only for the single arrangement with the greatest cost base where several targets were acquired in the year.
rationale: Part L of the CGT schedule has labels E to M, and the registry holds a variable for every one of them except the target's tax file number at G and the two counts at H and I; this column is the shares and units count that the ATO requires at label H.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the number of shares, units or other interests issued in exchange for the shares or units or other interests acquired in the original entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text 'Number of shares/units etc. issued' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing connected the count to a takeover or said who reports it.

value_domain: Small business active asset reduction, all calculation methods (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: The whole-of-year small business 50% active asset reduction, reported as one figure rather than split by calculation method. The ATO describes the concession plainly: "The small business 50% active asset reduction provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset." It is the redesigned schedule's version of the same claim that the older schedule carried in three method columns, and in this registry those method columns stop after the first 2012-13 file while this column runs across all twenty-four year tables.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain removed by the concession, taken after losses and the CGT discount and before the net capital gain. It sits at item 5 label A with the retirement exemption and the roll-over at labels B and C.
limitation: Because the older schedule split the same claim three ways, a series that reads this column alone breaks at the schedule change and has to be rebuilt by adding the indexation, discount and other-method columns for the early years. Eligibility is self-assessed against turnover and net asset value tests, so the column records a claim rather than a verified entitlement.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define the concession and place it at item 5, and the registry's own table lists show the split-by-method labels ending after cgt_2012_13_part1 while this column continues to 2022-23.
evidence_quote: The small business 50% active asset reduction provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Small business active asset reduction' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that an earlier schedule reported the same claim in three separate columns.

value_domain: Total small business concessions applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: Three of the four small business concessions added together at item 5 label D: the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over. The fourth concession is deliberately outside it, because the ATO says this part "doesn't include the small business 15-year exemption which is shown separately at item 8 of the CGT schedule". A gain fully wiped out by the 15-year exemption never enters the schedule's arithmetic at all, so this column understates total small business relief by exactly the largest concession of the four.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount that is the sum of the three concession columns beside it, applied after the CGT discount and before the net capital gain. Adding it to those three columns double-counts.
limitation: It treats a roll-over, which only defers tax, as equivalent to an exemption, which forgives it, so it overstates the revenue given up in the year by whatever share was deferred. It also omits the 15-year exemption entirely, which sits at item 8 and is the concession that disregards a gain in full.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define item 5 as the sum of labels A, B and C at label D, and state that the 15-year exemption is reported separately at item 8.
evidence_quote: This part doesn't include the small business 15-year exemption which is shown separately at item 8 of the CGT schedule (if a schedule is required).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Total small business concessions applied' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the exclusion of the 15-year exemption was nowhere on the page.

value_domain: Small business roll-over, all calculation methods (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: The gain a small business put off rather than gave up, by buying a replacement asset or improving one it already had. The ATO defines the concession as one that "enables you to defer all or part of a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset or make an improvement to an existing asset and satisfy other conditions". On a business file a figure here reads as reinvestment, which is the opposite signal to the retirement exemption in the column beside it, where the owner is taking money out.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain deferred, not forgiven, reported at item 5 label C without a split by calculation method. Nothing in this dataset records the year in which a deferred gain is brought back to account.
limitation: Treating the amount as tax relief overstates the concession, because a roll-over is a timing difference that resurfaces when the replacement asset goes or the conditions fail. The replacement asset test is applied by the taxpayer after the fact, so a claim can be unwound in a later amendment that this column will not show.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define the small business roll-over and place it at item 5 label C alongside the other two concessions.
evidence_quote: The small business roll-over enables you to defer all or part of a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset or make an improvement to an existing asset and satisfy other conditions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Small business roll-over' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a deferral from an exemption.

value_domain: Small business retirement exemption, all calculation methods (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: The gain a small business owner disregarded under the retirement exemption, which is capped over a lifetime rather than a year. The ATO says it "allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the eligibility conditions are satisfied". A claimant under 55 must pay the amount into superannuation, so a figure here should have a matching contribution in the superannuation records elsewhere in the asset. The lifetime cap is what makes a single year's figure hard to read on its own.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain disregarded, at item 5 label B, with no split by calculation method. It counts toward a lifetime limit, and the running total a person has used is held nowhere in this dataset.
limitation: One year's claim cannot be interpreted without the claimant's history, and where a company or trust makes the claim the lifetime limit attaches to the individual behind it rather than the lodging entity, so the file cannot show whether the cap was reached. Eligibility is self-assessed.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define the retirement exemption, state the lifetime limit and the superannuation condition, and place the claim at item 5 label B.
evidence_quote: The small business retirement exemption allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the eligibility conditions are satisfied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Small business retirement exemption' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the lifetime cap was not stated anywhere on the page.

value_domain: Seller's estimated total capital proceeds from an earnout arrangement (dollars), item 7 label D
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 7 Earnout arrangements
variable_description: What a seller expects to end up with in total from a business sale whose price depends on how the business performs after the handover. The ATO's instruction is short - "Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement" - but the surrounding rule is what matters: a seller completes labels D and E only "for arrangements which don't involve look-through earnout rights". Since look-through treatment covers rights created on or after 24 April 2015, this column captures the shrinking remainder of arrangements outside that treatment.
description_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 7 Earnout arrangements
value_definition: A dollar estimate of proceeds across the whole arrangement, not the year, made by the seller at lodgment. Labels B and C beside it give the arrangement's length in years and the year the seller is in.
limitation: It is a forecast, not a settled amount, so it cannot be reconciled with what the seller actually received; the realised gain or loss for the year sits in a separate column. A blank does not mean no earnout, because sellers under a look-through right leave it empty by instruction, and buyers never complete it at all.
rationale: The custodian's description is the schedule's own question wording, and the ATO's current schedule instructions give item 7 label D, who completes it and the look-through exclusion that governs when it is left blank.
evidence_quote: Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule question as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the figure is an estimate or that look-through arrangements are excluded.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person a capital gains tax schedule row is attached to, and the key that carries an asset disposal out to their other records in PLIDA. ABS keeps the joining information away from the data itself: the "Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data". Read this column with ENTITY_TYPE and BN on the same row, because a CGT schedule is lodged by a taxpaying entity, and a person-level count of gains that ignores the entity type will mix individuals with the companies, trusts and funds beside them.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: An opaque synthetic number, one value per person, stable across every column of the row and across the twenty-four year tables. In fplida the values are generated rather than derived from anyone.
limitation: It identifies a person, not a taxpaying entity, a household or a business, so it cannot answer who controls a company that lodged a schedule. Only entities with more than $10,000 of gains or losses must lodge, so a person with no row in a year is not a person with no capital gains.
rationale: ABS describes the PLIDA spine and how linkage keys are held separately from the data, which is what this column is; the surrounding CGT columns show it is carried alongside an entity type and a business number rather than on its own.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the row belongs to a lodging entity as well as a person.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year worked out using the discount method, before any losses or concessions are applied. The ATO says a taxpayer uses one of three methods for each asset - "indexation method", "discount method, or" the "'other' method" - and the discount method is available only where the asset was held at least twelve months: "If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method". The split matters because the discount is not applied yet: "If you use the discount method, do not apply the discount percentage until you have applied current year capital losses and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years."
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It pairs with the other-method total on the same row; adding the two gives total current year capital gains before any reduction.
limitation: The amount is a gross gain, not taxable income, and is several steps away from the net capital gain that reaches the return. A zero here does not mean no gains: it can mean every gain was worked out under the other or indexation method instead.
rationale: The DIL label names the total current year capital gains under the discount method, which is a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide defines the three methods, when each applies and where the discount is applied in the sequence.
evidence_quote: If you use the discount method, do not apply the discount percentage until you have applied current year capital losses and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the discount method is or why the column is split by method.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), the indexation method
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year worked out by inflating the cost base rather than halving the gain, which only assets bought before the 1999 reform can use. The ATO limits it to a CGT event on "an asset you acquired before 11.45am on 21 September 1999" that was held for twelve months or more, and the indexation itself stops early: "As indexation is frozen as at 30 September 1999, you can index your cost base only up to the September 1999 quarter." Read against the discount-method and other-method totals on the same row, this column marks the disposal of assets held since the old regime.
description_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), the indexation method
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of capital losses and of the small business concessions. No further discount is applied to these gains, because the inflation relief has already been taken inside the cost base.
limitation: The column can only shrink over time, since no asset acquired after September 1999 can ever enter it, so a fall across years is a change in the eligible stock rather than in behaviour. In this registry it stops after the first 2012-13 file, when the schedule dropped the method split, so a series that continues past that point is not the same measure.
rationale: The DIL label names the total current year capital gains under the indexation method, a defined column of the 2000-01 capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO's guide for that year sets out when the method is available and how far indexation runs.
evidence_quote: As indexation is frozen as at 30 September 1999, you can index your cost base only up to the September 1999 quarter.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained why a third method column exists or why it empties out over time.

value_domain: ATO processing date
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The day the ATO put this capital gains tax schedule through its systems, which is an administrative date rather than anything about the assets. It is the only date on the row: the income year the figures belong to is carried by INCM_YR, and no column records when a CGT event actually happened. Its practical use is vintage, telling you how long after the end of an income year a record was settled, and how far apart two rows for the same year were processed.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A calendar date. The domain is open, running from the earliest processing in the series to the extract date rather than being confined to the income year on the row.
limitation: It is not the lodgment date and not the date of any disposal, so a gain cannot be timed from it; a schedule processed in one year routinely reports events from an earlier one. An amended schedule is processed again, so where amendments survive as their own rows the column dates the amendment rather than the original claim.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS, Creating a child mobility indicator using the Life Course Dataset
variable_description: The address a person lived at, held as a key rather than as text. In plida_core_loc and the per-source address tables one row is one episode: the person was at this address from START_DATE to END_DATE, and the MB, SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it are that address geocoded. The ar_addr table is the other side of the join, holding one row per address with its use and its dwelling structure, so the identifier is what turns a location episode into a described dwelling. Because the key is the address and not the person, everyone living there carries the same value, and SOURCE_FLAG records which agency's records the episode was drawn from.
description_source: ABS, Creating a child mobility indicator using the Life Course Dataset
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person, a household or a dwelling, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. An administrative address is only as current as the person's last dealing with the agency, so an episode can outlast a move. ABS found that 4.3% to 11.2% of children with an address history between 2006 and 2021 were missing an ARID, and the version of Core Locations used for the child mobility indicator imputes those gaps. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL names the field Address Register ID. ABS documents the Core Locations module as holding a secure hashed ARID standing for each address in the ABS Address Register, and describes the address history structure (ARID with start and end dates of residence) that the registry's own table layout shows: SPINE_ID, ARID, START_DATE, END_DATE and the ASGS codings, with ar_addr holding address use and dwelling structure against the same key.
evidence_quote: a secure hashed Address Register Identifier (ARID) that represents each address in the ABS Address Register

value_domain: Australian Business Number (hashed and truncated)
value_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
variable_description: The organisation delivering the DSS-funded service, not a client. It sits on the organisation table beside ORGANISATIONID, which is the Data Exchange's own internal key, so the ABN is what matches a funded provider to the same entity outside the Data Exchange: to its employees in the ATO products, to its business record in BLADE, and to itself across funding rounds where the internal key changes.
description_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
value_definition: A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as "a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register", structured as "a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded and is useful only for matching one record to another.
limitation: The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a service or an outlet. One entity can run many outlets and one outlet can host services from several entities, so this cannot be read as a service provider on the ground. Not-for-profit structures often place the funding agreement with a parent entity that does not deliver the service. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as the organisation's ABN, hashed, on the Data Exchange organisation table. The Australian Business Register publishes the ABN's format and issuer.
evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: DEX accommodation setting label
value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 10
variable_description: The kind of dwelling a client was living in, as one of twelve settings ranging from a private residence to an institutional or crisis placement. It is a Commonwealth Home Support Programme field, so the protocols list it among items that "are required and will only present if the client is participating in the Commonwealth Home Support Programme activity", and it is empty for clients of every other funded activity. HOMELESSCODE and HOUSEHOLDCOMPOSITIONCODE sit beside it on the client record and answer different questions: whether the housing is secure, and who else lives there.
description_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 10
value_definition: A short label, held in the curated extract as a three-character code, drawn from the twelve settings in Table 10 of the protocols: boarding house; crisis, emergency or transition; independent living unit; Indigenous community or settlement; institutional setting such as residential aged care or hospital; private residence owned or being purchased by the client or family; private rental; public rental; public shelter; supported accommodation; other; and not stated.
limitation: The column cannot date the arrangement. The client table holds a current row plus superseded versions behind RECORDSEQNBR, so a move between settings is visible only where the provider updated the record, and there is no date attached to the setting itself. It is also not a homelessness measure, even though public shelter and crisis accommodation overlap with one: HOMELESSCODE carries that judgement, and 'not stated' is a common answer here.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry names the field 'Client: Accommodation Type, Code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution with format X(3), and the Data Exchange Protocols publish both the setting list and the fact that the field only appears for Commonwealth Home Support Programme clients.
evidence_quote: The following items are required and will only present if the client is participating in the Commonwealth Home Support Programme activity:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line wording and a generic sentence saying no finite value list is published, which is wrong twice over: the protocols publish the list, and nothing told a reader the field is confined to one programme.

value_domain: Aged Care Planning Region, 2015 boundaries
value_source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2015 Aged Care Planning Region maps
variable_description: The aged care planning region the client's residential address fell in, on the boundaries used between February 2015 and April 2018. "The Australian Government uses Aged Care Planning Regions to plan aged care services across Australia", so this is the column that places a Data Exchange client inside an aged care supply unit rather than an ABS statistical one. DSS's own address validation and geocoding service tagged it from the recorded address, in the same pass that produced the SA1 to SA4, LGA and federal electorate codes on the row.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2015 Aged Care Planning Region maps
value_definition: A planning region code from the 2015 determination, which the department signed in February 2015 and published as a set of whole-state region maps with a correspondence to 2011 Statistical Areas Level 2. The regions nest inside states and territories and do not cross them.
limitation: The value is not comparable with the 2018 column beside it. The determinations were remade in April 2018 on a different SA2 base, so a client who never moved can hold two different region codes across the two columns, and a change between them is a boundary change rather than a move. The column also says nothing about aged care use: most Data Exchange clients are in programmes with no aged care component.
rationale: The DIL says the code is the 2015 Aged Care Planning Region boundary tagged by the DSS IQ Office geocoder. The Department of Health publishes what the regions are, when the 2015 determinations were signed, and the correspondence to 2011 SA2s.
evidence_quote: The Government signed the determinations for the 2015 Aged Care Planning Regions in February 2015. These were replaced by the current 2018 Aged Care Planning Regions in April 2018.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, which names the geocoding service but never says what an aged care planning region is or who determines it, and gave the same generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation.

value_domain: Aged Care Planning Region, 2018 boundaries
value_source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2018 Aged Care Planning Region maps
variable_description: The aged care planning region the client's residential address fell in, on the boundaries in force since April 2018. "The Government signed the determinations for the current 2018 Aged Care Planning Regions in April 2018. These replaced the 2015 Aged Care Planning Regions." DSS's address validation and geocoding service tagged it from the recorded address, so it is derived geography rather than anything the client or provider entered, and it is the current-boundary companion to ACPR2015BOUNDARYCODE on the same row.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2018 Aged Care Planning Region maps
value_definition: A planning region code from the 2018 determination, built by aggregating whole 2016 Statistical Areas Level 2; the department publishes both the region shapefile and a correspondence from the regions to 2016 SA2s.
limitation: A region is a planning unit, not a service catchment or a market. Providers deliver across region boundaries and clients travel across them, so counting clients by region measures where people live rather than where they were served. The column also cannot be compared with the 2015 column without the department's correspondence, because the two sets were determined on different SA2 vintages.
rationale: The DIL says the code is the 2018 Aged Care Planning Region boundary tagged by the DSS IQ Office geocoder. The Department of Health publishes the determination date, the region maps and the SA2 correspondence that defines the boundaries.
evidence_quote: The Government signed the determinations for the current 2018 Aged Care Planning Regions in April 2018. These replaced the 2015 Aged Care Planning Regions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about the geocoding service and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, so nothing on the page said what the region is or how it differs from the 2015 column.

value_domain: DEX program activity identifier
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Program activity identifier, ID number'
variable_description: The funded activity a service was delivered under, which the DSS metadata registry defines as "an identifier for a unique program activity record in the Data Exchange". In special_activity this is the key of the reference table itself: one row per activity, with NAME giving its title, PROGRAMID the programme it sits under, and STARTDATE and ENDDATE the window in which providers could select it when creating a case. Joining that table to the attendance, session and assessment tables is what turns a bare number on a service record into the name of the thing DSS funded.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Program activity identifier, ID number'
value_definition: A short whole number, one to three digits in the registry's format N[NN], with no internal structure. The activity's name, its parent programme and its availability dates come from the reference table, not from the digits; SOURCESYSTEMCODE records whether the activity row came from FOFMS or an external system.
limitation: An activity is not an organisation and not an outlet. The same activity is delivered by many providers from many outlets, and one provider commonly delivers several, so an activity count is a count of funding lines rather than of services on the ground. Identifiers are also not stable across programme redesigns: a restructured or renamed activity takes a new number, so a break in a series can be an administrative change rather than a change in service delivery.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry defines the ActivityId data element and gives its numeric format in the same curated DEX tables the PLIDA extract is drawn from, and the registry's own table layout shows the activity reference table holding the name, programme and availability dates against this key.
evidence_quote: An identifier for a unique program activity record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL sentence 'This data item is inclusive of all program activities with sessions recorded in the Data Exchange', which describes the table's coverage rather than the column, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: outlet address validation status (inferred)
variable_description: A code recording how the service outlet's street address fared in the DSS address validation and geocoding check. It qualifies OUTLETLOCALITY, OUTLETPOSTCODE and OUTLETSTATE, and it is what decides whether the boundary columns on the same row — the SA1 to SA4, LGA, federal electorate and aged care planning region codes tagged by the DSS IQ Office service — could be populated at all. Read it before trusting any geography attached to an outlet.
description_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), Department of Social Services, section 3.5, with the PLIDA DEX data item list
value_definition: A short code emitted by the DSS address validation and geocoder service, indicating whether the supplied address matched a reference address and to what level. DSS does not publish the code set for this column, so the domain is open and the codes have to be read against the boundary columns they govern.
limitation: It grades the address string, not the outlet. A clean status means the text matched a reference address, not that the outlet was open, staffed or delivering services, and CURRENTRECORD with the SYSSTARTTIME and SYSENDTIME pair carry the record's currency instead. The protocols also forbid an outlet being created at a client's home or at a sensitive location such as a refuge, and forbid a post office box standing in for a physical location, requiring the outlet to show where staff are based instead. A cleanly validated address is therefore often deliberately not where the service was delivered.
rationale: Sibling columns in special_outlet are described as 'tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)', so the status of an outlet address is most plausibly the outcome of that validation step, taking a handful of short codes. No DEX Protocol, bulk upload spec or web services spec publishes the list, and a second reading (record status: current versus superseded) cannot be ruled out, so this is a coarse shape only and the specific labels are illustrative rather than sourced.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination was correct that no public codeframe exists; a coarse three-state status shape is now an allowed outcome, but treat it as low confidence.

value_domain: reason-for-assistance domain flag
value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2
variable_description: A flag for whether age-appropriate development was one of the reasons a client sought assistance, defined in the protocols as "where the client is seeking to improve age-appropriate development". The row it sits on is one combination of reasons, identified by ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY, and the flags beside it cover the other domains: community, family, money, employment, education, training, material, housing, mental, personal and physical. The attendance table stores only the key, so this reference table is what unpacks that key into the set of needs recorded.
description_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2
value_definition: A two-state flag, set when age-appropriate development is one of the reasons in the combination the key stands for. The domain names come from the eleven SCORE circumstance domains, which the protocols reuse for reasons for seeking assistance so that presenting need and measured outcome share a vocabulary.
limitation: The flag records what a provider entered as a presenting reason near the start of service, not a developmental assessment and not a diagnosis. The protocols warn that the real reason often only becomes apparent after the client engages. Reporting is optional and confined to organisations in the partnership approach, so an unset flag means 'not recorded' at least as often as it means 'not a reason'.
rationale: The protocols define the eleven reason-for-seeking-assistance categories and name age-appropriate development among them, and the reference table's columns are those categories one per column against a key.
evidence_quote: Age-appropriate development: where the client is seeking to improve age-appropriate development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seeking assistance related to Age appropriate development' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that the column is one flag in a keyed set or where the categories come from.

value_domain: age in completed years
value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2
variable_description: The client's age in completed years on the day the session took place. It is derived rather than reported: the protocols say date of birth "provides a direct means of calculating the client's age", and CONDUCTEDDATE on the same row gives the session date. Because it is recalculated for every attendance, one client's value rises across their own rows, which is what lets the attendance table carry an age profile without joining back to the client record.
description_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2
value_definition: A whole number of years, not an age band. Where the client's date of birth was estimated rather than known, flagged by BIRTHDATEESTIMATED and usually set to the first day of a year, the age inherits that approximation.
limitation: This is not the age at which a client entered a service, and it is not a person-level attribute. Because one row exists per attendance, an age distribution built straight off this column counts a person once for every session they attended, so it over-represents frequent attenders unless clients are deduplicated first.
