value_domain: Country of usual residence code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA), column ctry_code
variable_description: The country of an address held for the recipient on the raw location detail table, defined by DSS as "The country of usual residence of a person, as represented by a code". On loc_dtls it qualifies the Australian geography columns beside it — MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE, SA2_MAINCODE, STATE and POSTCODE — which have nothing to hold for an overseas address, while ADDR_TYPE_CODE says whether the address is residential, postal or something else. The same column appears on loc_pos_temp_term_dtls, the temporary and terminated postal address table, where overseas values are more common.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA), column ctry_code
value_definition: A country code with the same definition the derived location table gives to CNTRY_CDE. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code list.
limitation: It describes the address on the row, not the person's residency status, so it cannot be used to identify migrants, temporary residents or recipients being paid overseas under portability rules. Because ADDR_PRTY ranks competing addresses, a person can hold several current rows with different countries, so the priority column has to be applied earlier in this one is read.
rationale: The registry's LOC_DTLS_EXT PLIDA distribution defines ctry_code verbatim, lists the address priority and address type columns that qualify it, and gives the same definition to cntry_cde on the derived table.
evidence_quote: The country of usual residence of a person, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address country' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not connect the column to the address priority ranking that decides which row applies.

value_domain: Hours per week
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 54225 'Recipient: Current capacity hours, Total number'
variable_description: How many hours a week the recipient is currently assessed as able to work, which DSS defines as "The number of current capacity in hours a recipient is able to work in a week". This number is what the partial capacity to work rules and the Disability Support Pension assessment turn on, so it decides mutual obligation requirements as much as it describes health. Three columns qualify it on the same row: WITH_INTRVN_NUM gives capacity if intervention or support were provided, TEMP_REDN_CAP_HRS_NUM a temporary reduction, and INCAP_WK_WRK_HRS the hours the issuing doctor considers the client able to work, with ASSMT_ID keying the assessment they all came from.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 54225 'Recipient: Current capacity hours, Total number'
value_definition: Whole hours per week, format N(2), so values from 0 to 99, with a full stop used as the missing value indicator.
limitation: It is an assessed capacity, not observed work. A recipient assessed at 15 hours may be working none of them or more than them, and inc_emp_cont is where actual earnings and hours sit, so this column measures what an assessment concluded rather than labour supply. The value is also frozen at the assessment and stays put until a reassessment, so it can be years old on any given row.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the two-digit format, the hours-per-week unit and the full stop as the missing value, and the MCD_DTLS_EXT PLIDA distribution shows the related capacity and incapacity columns.
evidence_quote: The number of current capacity in hours a recipient is able to work in a week.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Current work capacity number' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell the units were hours per week or that a full stop means missing.

value_domain: Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 467 'Person: Date of death, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the recipient died, as Centrelink's records hold it, defined by DSS as "The date upon which a person ceases to live, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". It sits on the static demographics table because it is an attribute of the person rather than an event, and it exists for an administrative reason: a death stops payments and starts bereavement provisions. DEATH_IND beside it flags that the person is recorded as deceased, and the two disagree wherever a death is known but not dated.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 467 'Person: Date of death, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form. Other DOMINO releases carry only month of death and year of death as separate columns, so the precision available depends on which version of the static demographics table is in hand.
limitation: This is not a death registration and it is not complete: only deaths that came to Centrelink's attention are here, so a former recipient who died years after leaving the payment system has no date. The PLIDA deaths module, built from state and territory registrations, is the source for mortality; this column is best used to explain why a payment stopped.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition and the date format, and its STATIC_DEMOGS PLIDA distribution carries month and year of death as separate columns, which is why the precision caveat is worth stating.
evidence_quote: The date upon which a person ceases to live, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Recipient date of death' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to warn that the column only sees deaths the payment system learned about.

value_domain: Yes/no indicator
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA), column death_ind
variable_description: Flags that Centrelink's records show the recipient as deceased, defined by DSS in plain terms as "The indicator represents the death of a person". It is a static attribute of the person rather than a dated event, and DATE_OF_DEATH carries the date where one is held, so a flag set without a date is possible. Snap-DOMINO carries the same concept on its snapshot rows under the name DEATH_INDICATOR.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA), column death_ind
value_definition: An indicator flag on the person's demographic record. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code values.
limitation: It shows what the payment system knows, not whether the person is alive. Deaths of people who left income support years earlier often never reach Centrelink, so a false value cannot be read as survival, and this flag should not be used to censor a longitudinal analysis in place of the PLIDA deaths data built from registrations.
rationale: The registry's STATIC_DEMOGS PLIDA distribution defines the column verbatim and shows it sits with the date, month and year of death columns on the person-level demographics table.
evidence_quote: The indicator represents the death of a person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Death indicator', was tagged social security, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the flag reflects administrative knowledge rather than vital status.

value_domain: Death indicator (Y/N)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Death, Indicator X(6)" (item 84486), bound to snap_domino_beta.death_indicator
variable_description: Whether Centrelink had recorded the person as deceased by the time the Snap-DOMINO extract was drawn. Snap-DOMINO holds one row per person per snapshot, so the flag is a property of the extract rather than of SNAP_DATE, and it is the only mortality information on the table. The static demographics table carries the fuller account: DEATH_IND with DATE_OF_DEATH, which is what you need to close off a person's exposure period rather than merely drop them.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Death, Indicator X(6)" (item 84486), bound to snap_domino_beta.death_indicator
value_definition: A single letter held in a six-character field: Y where a death has been recorded. DSS treats N as a supplementary default value rather than a positive statement, so N carries less information than Y does.
limitation: A recorded death is a death Centrelink learned about, usually because a payment stopped or a family member notified the agency, so someone who died years after leaving the payment system can sit at N indefinitely. The flag also carries no date on this table, so it cannot say whether the death fell inside or outside the snapshot period, and a Y on an old snapshot does not tell you when the person died.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds death_indicator to "Person: Death, Indicator X(6)", whose value domain publishes Y as the only permissible value and N as the default.
evidence_quote: The indicator represents the death of a person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's one-line description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so a reader could not tell that N is a default rather than a confirmed survival.

value_domain: Australian dollars per day
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) daily amount, Total Australian currency" (item 570), bound to inc_dfi.dfi_dly_dfisa_amt
variable_description: The daily rate of Defence Force Income Support Allowance the person was paid over the period the row covers, which DSS defines as the "Daily Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) amount paid to a recipient". DFISA topped up a veteran's social security payment to offset the effect of counting adjusted disability pension as income, so it only ever attached to another payment: BEN_TYPE_CODE on the same row names which one. The custodian's own description on this column reads "Department of Veterans Affairs daily income amount", which is the wording that belongs to DVA_DLY_INC in inc_dva; the two are different amounts on different tables.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) daily amount, Total Australian currency" (item 570), bound to inc_dfi.dfi_dly_dfisa_amt
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents at a daily rate, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default. It is a rate, not an instalment, so a period's total is the rate times the days between PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE.
limitation: It is neither the veteran's DVA disability pension nor the income support payment itself, only the allowance that compensated for one being counted against the other, so it understates a veteran's income by a wide margin. DFISA ceased on 1 January 2022, when adjusted disability income became exempt under the social security income test, so an absence of rows after that date is the payment ending rather than the person's circumstances changing.
rationale: INC_DFI_EXT (PLIDA) binds dfi_dly_dfisa_amt to DSS data element 570, which names the payment, gives the currency value domain and the N[9].NN format, and states that the amount is daily.
evidence_quote: Daily Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) amount paid to a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's description, which names the wrong agency's payment, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Count of days
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Event: Event period duration, Number" (item 405), bound to det_ben.durn_days
variable_description: How long the benefit determination on this row ran, which DSS defines as "The duration of a reporting episode expressed as number of days". The det_ben table holds one row per spell of a given payment, so the count spans PERIOD_START_DATE to PERIOD_END_DATE for the payment named in BEN_TYPE_CODE. BEN_STATUS says whether the spell was current or suspended, and END_RSN and END_RSN_CODE say why it closed, so the duration is only interpretable with those three columns beside it.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Event: Event period duration, Number" (item 405), bound to det_ben.durn_days
value_definition: A whole number of days in a five-digit field, format {NNNN}N, with 0 the default value.
limitation: It counts days on a determination, not days paid: a spell that ran at a nil rate or under suspension still contributes its days, so summing the column overstates time actually in receipt of money. Because each row is one payment's spell, a person who moved between payments has several rows whose durations overlap, and adding them gives more days than the person actually spent on income support.
rationale: DET_BEN_EXT (PLIDA) binds durn_days to "Event: Event period duration, Number", whose definition states the unit is days and whose value domain gives the five-digit count format.
evidence_quote: The duration of a reporting episode expressed as number of days.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Duration of episode (days)" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Australian dollars per day
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) daily income, Total Australian currency" (item 568), bound to inc_dva.dva_dly_inc
variable_description: The daily amount of Department of Veterans' Affairs income Centrelink counted for the person over the period on the row, which DSS defines as "The daily income amount received by a client from the Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA)". DVA_TYPE_CODE beside it names which of the seventy-eight DVA payments the amount is, so the column cannot be read on its own: a service pension, a war widow's pension, a disability pension at one of the general rates and a pharmaceutical supplement all appear here as a number. This is DVA income entering Centrelink's means test, which is why it sits in the income module rather than in a payments table.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) daily income, Total Australian currency" (item 568), bound to inc_dva.dva_dly_inc
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents at a daily rate, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default.
limitation: It is what Centrelink recorded as DVA income for its own assessment, not what DVA paid, so it will not reconcile with DVA's payment records for the same person. One person holding several DVA payments has several rows, so a person's total DVA income has to be summed across DVA_TYPE_CODE rather than read off any one row.
rationale: INC_DVA_EXT (PLIDA) binds dva_dly_inc to DSS data element 568, which gives the definition, the Australian currency value domain and the N[9].NN daily format, and binds dva_type_code beside it to the seventy-eight-value DVA income type code list.
evidence_quote: The daily income amount received by a client from the Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a misspelt one-line description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation.

value_domain: domino_dva_income_type_code
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) income type, Code" (item 562), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
variable_description: The kind of Veterans' Affairs payment behind the DVA income Centrelink assessed for this person. DSS defines the element as "The type of income or allowance received by a client from the Department of Veterans Affairs", and DVA_DLY_INC on the same row gives the daily dollar amount the code describes. The row exists because DVA income affected a Centrelink assessment, so inc_dva is a means-testing record rather than a DVA payment file.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) income type, Code" (item 562)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, from the DSS 77-value DVA income type list. It mixes pensions (AGC social security pension paid by DVA, DVA service pension), disability rates (BLI blinded special rate, EDA extreme disablement adjustment), specific disability items such as I07 and I08, and dependant allowance percentages from D10 through to DEP at 100 per cent.
limitation: It is not a veteran status flag: a person with no inc_dva row can still be a veteran, because only DVA income that entered a Centrelink assessment appears here. Codes the registry marks as no longer valid also persist on historical rows rather than being restated under current arrangements, so a code frequency over time mixes schemes.
rationale: INC_DVA_EXT binds dva_type_code to "Recipient: Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) income type, Code", a 77-value list.
evidence_quote: AGC Social Security Pension Paid by DVA | AMS Adequate Means of
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these DVA income codes.

value_domain: Australian dollars per day
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Daily income amount from continuous employment" (item 54285), bound to inc_emp_cont.emp_dly_inc_cont
variable_description: The daily earnings Centrelink derived from a person's continuous employment for the period on the row, defined by DSS as the "Daily earnings amount from continuous employment". Continuous employment means earnings reported at a regular frequency, and FREQ_CODE names that frequency: weekly, fortnightly, monthly, quarterly and so on. This column is the derived daily equivalent of the amount the person actually stated in EMP_INC_CONT, with AVG_IND recording whether an averaging rule was applied, and EMPLYR_ID separating one job from another where a person holds more than one.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Daily income amount from continuous employment" (item 54285), bound to inc_emp_cont.emp_dly_inc_cont
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents at a daily rate, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default.
limitation: It is the daily rate Centrelink used to assess the payment, not money that arrived on that day: a monthly wage becomes a smooth daily figure, so the column cannot show when in the period the person was paid. It also cannot be compared like for like with EMP_DLY_INC_VAR in inc_emp_var, which is derived from irregular reports on a different basis.
rationale: INC_EMP_CONT_EXT (PLIDA) binds emp_dly_inc_cont to DSS data element 54285, which supplies the definition, the currency value domain and the daily rate format, and binds freq_code, avg_ind and emplyr_id on the same row.
evidence_quote: Daily earnings amount from continuous employment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, leaving the difference between the derived daily figure and the stated amount undocumented.

value_domain: Australian dollars per day
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Daily income amount from variable employment" (item 54295), bound to inc_emp_var.emp_dly_inc_var
variable_description: The daily earnings Centrelink derived from a person's variable employment for the period on the row, defined by DSS as the "Daily earnings amount from variable employment". Variable employment is work whose earnings change from one reporting period to the next — casual shifts, irregular hours, commission — as against the regular pay recorded in inc_emp_cont. The row's stated amount is EMP_INC_VAR, the hours are EMP_INC_VAR_HRS, and EMPLYR_ID tells one casual job from another.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Daily income amount from variable employment" (item 54295), bound to inc_emp_var.emp_dly_inc_var
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents at a daily rate, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default.
limitation: A spike in this column can be a back payment, a bunched roster or a lump sum reported late rather than a real change in the person's usual hours, because variable earnings are reported as they occur. A nil day also does not mean the job ended: an unpaid week in a continuing casual job looks the same as unemployment on this column alone.
rationale: INC_EMP_VAR_EXT (PLIDA) binds emp_dly_inc_var to DSS data element 54295, which gives the definition, the Australian currency value domain and the daily N[9].NN format.
evidence_quote: Daily earnings amount from variable employment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, so nothing on the page distinguished variable from continuous employment income.

value_domain: Australian dollars per reporting period
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Income amount from continuous employment as stated, Total Australian currency" (item 533), bound to inc_emp_cont.emp_inc_cont
variable_description: The earnings from continuous employment the person themselves reported to Centrelink, which DSS defines as the "Earnings amount from continuous employment as stated by the recipient". It is the raw declared figure before Centrelink converted it to the daily rate in EMP_DLY_INC_CONT, so the two columns on one row are the same money expressed two ways. The number is meaningless without FREQ_CODE, which says what period the stated amount covers, and EMP_INC_CONT_HRS holds the hours the same report covered.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Income amount from continuous employment as stated, Total Australian currency" (item 533), bound to inc_emp_cont.emp_inc_cont
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default. The amount covers whatever period FREQ_CODE names rather than a fixed period.
limitation: It is a self-report, not a payroll figure, so it can disagree with what Single Touch Payroll shows for the same person and weeks. Because each row's amount covers the period FREQ_CODE names, adding the column across rows adds sums covering different lengths of time, which is what EMP_DLY_INC_CONT exists to avoid.
rationale: INC_EMP_CONT_EXT (PLIDA) binds emp_inc_cont to DSS data element 533, whose definition makes the self-reported character explicit, and binds freq_code beside it to the fifteen-value income frequency code list.
evidence_quote: Earnings amount from continuous employment as stated by the recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying that the amount is undated until FREQ_CODE is read.

value_domain: Hours worked per fortnight
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Hours worked in continuous employment as stated" (item 535), bound to inc_emp_cont.emp_inc_cont_hrs
variable_description: The hours the person reported working in regular employment for the reporting fortnight, which DSS defines as the "Hours worked in continuous employment as stated by the recipient". It pairs with EMP_INC_CONT, the earnings from the same report, so the two together give an implied hourly rate for the job identified by EMPLYR_ID. Centrelink collects hours as well as dollars because several payments carry participation requirements measured in hours, and because a person's part-time status affects which requirements apply.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Hours worked in continuous employment as stated" (item 535), bound to inc_emp_cont.emp_inc_cont_hrs
value_definition: A whole number of hours in a two-digit field, so 0 to 99, with a full stop as the missing-data value.
limitation: The two-digit field cannot hold more than 99 hours in a fortnight, so long-hours workers are truncated rather than recorded. Hours are declared rather than drawn from payroll, and a report of earnings without a matching roster leaves zero hours against a positive amount, so an hourly rate calculated from a single row is unreliable.
rationale: INC_EMP_CONT_EXT (PLIDA) binds emp_inc_cont_hrs to DSS data element 535, whose value domain is "Total number N(2)" with a full stop as the missing marker, and whose definition makes the figure a recipient statement.
evidence_quote: Hours worked in continuous employment as stated by the recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding the two-digit ceiling that truncates long-hours workers.

value_domain: Australian dollars per reporting period
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Income amount from variable employment as stated, Total Australian currency" (item 538), bound to inc_emp_var.emp_inc_var
variable_description: The earnings from irregular or casual work the person declared to Centrelink for the reporting period, which DSS defines as the "Earnings amount from variable employment as stated". It is the declared figure behind the derived daily rate in EMP_DLY_INC_VAR, and FREQ_CODE says what period it covers. Because variable earnings drive fortnightly payment adjustments, this column is the closest thing in DOMINO to a record of when casual work actually happened.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Income amount from variable employment as stated, Total Australian currency" (item 538), bound to inc_emp_var.emp_inc_var
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default. The amount covers the period named by FREQ_CODE.
limitation: The amount is attached to the period the person reported it in, which is not always the period they earned it in, so a late declaration puts a fortnight's wages in the wrong fortnight. Reporting also stops when the payment stops, so the column tracks casual earnings only while the person is claiming, and a rising figure that ends abruptly usually means the claim closed rather than the work ending.
rationale: INC_EMP_VAR_EXT (PLIDA) binds emp_inc_var to DSS data element 538, which supplies the definition, the Australian currency value domain and the N[9].NN format.
evidence_quote: Earnings amount from variable employment as stated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Hours worked per fortnight
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Hours worked in variable employment as stated" (item 539), bound to inc_emp_var.emp_inc_var_hrs
variable_description: The hours of casual or irregular work the person declared for the reporting fortnight, which DSS defines as the "Hours worked in variable employment as stated". Read with EMP_INC_VAR on the same row it gives an implied casual hourly rate, and read across rows for one EMPLYR_ID it shows how much a person's shifts moved from fortnight to fortnight. Hours matter here because several payments assess participation in hours and because fifteen hours a week and thirty hours a fortnight are thresholds in the payment rules.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Hours worked in variable employment as stated" (item 539), bound to inc_emp_var.emp_inc_var_hrs
value_definition: A whole number of hours in a two-digit field, so 0 to 99, with a full stop as the missing-data value.
limitation: A zero in this column means no hours were declared for that report, which happens both when the person did not work and when they declared a lump sum without a roster, so it cannot be used to date a break in casual work. The two-digit field also cannot hold more than 99 hours in a fortnight.
rationale: INC_EMP_VAR_EXT (PLIDA) binds emp_inc_var_hrs to DSS data element 539, whose value domain is "Total number N(2)" with a full stop as the missing marker.
evidence_quote: Hours worked in variable employment as stated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Within-person employer sequence number
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Employer identifier, ID number" (item 528), bound to the DOMINO employment income tables
variable_description: A sequence number telling one of a person's employers from another within their own DOMINO record. DSS defines it as an "Employer identifier. Starts at 1, automatically incremented by 1 for each new employer", so employer 1 for one person has nothing to do with employer 1 for anyone else. It appears on the continuous and variable employment income tables and on the two Community Development Employment Projects income tables, and it is what makes a second job visible: two rows for one person in one fortnight with different values are two employers, not a duplicate.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Employer identifier, ID number" (item 528), bound to the DOMINO employment income tables
value_definition: A small whole number in a two-digit field, so 1 to 99, with a full stop as the missing marker. Numbering restarts at 1 for every person.
limitation: It cannot be joined to an ABN, to BLADE, or to an employer in any other dataset, and it cannot be compared across people, so it will not support a firm-level analysis of who employs income support recipients. It also numbers employers in the order Centrelink recorded them, not the order the person held the jobs, so a higher number is not a later job.
rationale: INC_EMP_CONT_EXT and INC_EMP_VAR_EXT (PLIDA) both bind emplyr_id to DSS data element 528, whose definition states the sequential within-recipient numbering and whose value domain is a two-digit total number with a full stop for missing.
evidence_quote: Employer identifier. Starts at 1, automatically incremented by 1 for each new employer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Synthetic employer id" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited a reader to treat it as a business key when it is a per-person counter.

value_domain: Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Relationship end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 54341), bound to rlt_parent_child_list.end_date
variable_description: The day a recorded relationship ended, on the three family relationship tables, which DSS defines as the "End date for a relationship if reported". It is not the same as PERIOD_END_DATE sitting beside it: that closes the reporting episode the row was extracted in, while this closes the relationship itself, and END_RSN says why. On loc_derived the same column name means something different again — it ends an address episode that START_DATE opened, and the custodian's "Relationship end date" wording there is carried over from the relationship tables in error, as the neighbouring "Effective address start date" shows.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Relationship end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 54341), bound to rlt_parent_child_list.end_date
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters. DSS notes the value is present only where an end was reported, so an open relationship or a current address leaves it empty.
limitation: A missing value means no end was reported, not that the relationship or the address is current: parent and grandparent relationships are rarely closed off, and Centrelink only learns of an address change when the person tells it. Because the column carries two meanings across the tables it appears in, code that pools DOMINO tables on the column name will mix relationship ends with address moves.
rationale: RLT_PARENT_CHILD_LIST (PLIDA) binds end_date to data element 54341 and period_end_date separately to data element 394, which is what shows the two dates are different things. LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA) has no relationship column at all, so the identical custodian wording there cannot be a relationship date.
evidence_quote: End date for a relationship if reported.

description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Carer Allowance child identifier, ID number" (item 452), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_cda_child_id
value_definition: A randomised numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits, drawn from the DSS person identifier domain. The digits are assigned by Centrelink and carry no information about the child.

value_domain: Count of children listed on a concession card
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Concession Card, Number of Listed Children" (item 458), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_child_id_list_count
variable_description: How many children were listed on the person's concession card, defined by DSS as "The maximum number of children listed on a concession card held by the card holder". The column appears on all four concession card tables, so the count always belongs to the card that table covers: Health Care Card in ccd_hcc, Pensioner Concession Card in ccd_pcc, low-income Health Care Card in ccd_hcc_lic and Seniors Health Card in ccd_shc. CONCESSION names the card type and CARD_START_DATE and CARD_END_DATE bound the period, so the count is the high-water mark over that period rather than a figure for any one day.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Concession Card, Number of Listed Children" (item 458), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_child_id_list_count
value_definition: A whole number in a five-digit field, format {NNNN}N, with 0 the default. DSS specifies it as a maximum over the card period, not a point-in-time count.
limitation: Being a maximum, it will exceed the number of children actually listed on any given day wherever children were added and removed, so it cannot be used as a family size on a date. Children listed for concession purposes are also not the same as children in the person's care: a child can be in care without being listed, and a listed child can be the partner's dependant.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_child_id_list_count to DSS data element 458, whose definition specifies the maximum rather than a current count, and whose value domain is a five-digit total number with 0 as default.

supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Number of listed children" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding that the figure is a period maximum rather than a current count.

A dependent customer is someone who is themselves a Centrelink customer but whose concession flows from this card holder, most often a young person past the age at which they would be recorded as a child. DSS defines it as "A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies a dependent customer listed on a concession card". EXT_DOM_PARTNER_ID beside it records the partner, and the three child columns record children on their own basis for listing.

value_domain: DOMINO income unit identifier
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Domino Household ID" (item 108241), bound to snap_domino_beta.dom_household_id
variable_description: The income unit the person belonged to on the snapshot date: either the person alone, or the person and their partner. DSS defines it as "A unique identifier used to identify a financial unit made up of a person and their partner", covering married, de facto and registered relationships, and the PLIDA data item list adds that the value is built by concatenating the person's DOMINO identifier with their partner's. Two partnered people therefore share one value, and PARTNERED_STATUS on the same row is the flag that says which of the two cases applies.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Domino Household ID" (item 108241), bound to snap_domino_beta.dom_household_id
value_definition: A numeric value of up to nineteen characters, formed from one or two DOMINO person identifiers. It carries no information about the unit beyond the identities it joins.
limitation: The unit is a couple for means-testing purposes, not a household or a dwelling, so it cannot be used to count household size or to reconstruct who lives together: children and other adults at the same address are outside it, and two units can share one address. The value also changes whenever a partnership starts or ends, so it is not a stable key for following a person over time.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds dom_household_id to DSS data element 108241, which defines the unit as a person and their partner for payment eligibility and gives the nineteen-character numeric format.
evidence_quote: A unique identifier used to identify a financial unit made up of a person and their partner
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's concatenation note but printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing warned a reader against reading the column as a household.

evidence_quote: A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies an 'other' child listed on a concession card.

REL_CODE names the type — married, de facto, parent, child, sibling, guardian, ward and so on — and REL_QUAL_CODE qualifies it, so this column is the who and those two are the what.

value_domain: DSS benefit type code
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: First Active ISP" (item 108857), bound to snap_domino_beta.first_active_isp
variable_description: Which income support payment the person was on when their current unbroken run of income support began. Snap-DOMINO builds that run by joining spells across short breaks, so this is the payment that opened the period bounded by ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE, not the payment the person is on at the snapshot. Read with LAST_ACTIVE_ISP, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP it shows how someone moved between payments inside a single spell of support, which is the usual pattern for a person who goes from a student payment to unemployment and then to a parenting payment.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: First Active ISP" (item 108857), bound to snap_domino_beta.first_active_isp
value_definition: A three or four letter code, format AAA{A}, from the 95-value DSS benefit type code list: JSP for JobSeeker Payment, AGE for Age Pension, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS and PPP for the two parenting payments, and UNK where the payment is unknown.
limitation: It resets every time a break longer than the tolerance ends a run, so for a person with a long and interrupted history it is a recent fact rather than a first-ever payment. It also gives one payment where a person can hold several at once, so the supplement or family payment they also received at that moment is not visible here.

value_definition: A whole number in a field of up to three digits, awarded in five-point steps. The companion code list runs 0 no functional impact, 5 mild, 10 moderate, 20 severe and 30 extreme, with the intermediate values and everything up to 95 also permitted.
limitation: A rating exists only where an assessment was done, so a blank means no assessment rather than no impairment, and the rated population is skewed towards people claiming Disability Support Pension. The rating measures functional impact on work capacity rather than diagnosis or clinical severity, so two people with the same condition can score very differently and a high score is not a measure of how ill someone is.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds imprmt_rate to DSS data element 616, which gives the definition and the five-point increment rule, and binds imprmt_code beside it to data element 65080, whose value list supplies the functional-impact labels for 0, 5, 10, 20 and 30.
evidence_quote: the impairment rating for a recipient's medical condition(s), expressed as a percentage in 5% increments
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Impairment rating" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know the scale, the increment or that a blank means no assessment.

value_domain: Date (DD-MM-YYYY)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Medical Assessment: Record Start Date, DD-MM-YYYY" (item 59541), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_ver_date
variable_description: The day the version of the impairment assessment on this row became current, which DSS defines as "The particular day on which the record of a medical assessment became current". The mcd_dtls table keeps a history, so a person reassessed after a change in condition has several rows and this date is what orders them: the rating in IMPRMT_RATE belongs to the version starting here. It is a record-keeping date, distinct from PERIOD_START_DATE, which bounds the reporting episode the row was extracted in.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Medical Assessment: Record Start Date, DD-MM-YYYY" (item 59541), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_ver_date
value_definition: A calendar date in a ten-character field. DSS specifies the format as DD-MM-YYYY, which is the reverse of the YYYY-MM-DD used by the period and incapacity dates on the same table.
limitation: It dates the record, not the examination or the onset of the condition, so it sits after the medical evidence it summarises and can move when an assessment is corrected. It cannot be used to date the start of impairment: a condition present for twenty years but first assessed in 2015 carries a 2015 date.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds imprmt_ver_date to DSS data element 59541, whose definition makes it a record currency date and whose value domain is DD-MM-YYYY, while the neighbouring date columns on the same table bind to YYYY-MM-DD elements.
evidence_quote: The particular day on which the record of a medical assessment became current.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Impairment version date" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without noting the different date format or that it is a record date.

value_domain: Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 642), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_end
variable_description: The day a certified period of temporary incapacity ended, which DSS defines as "The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition ends". Incapacity here is the medical-certificate arrangement that suspends a person's mutual obligation requirements while they cannot work or study, so the period matters for whether a payment could be suspended. INCAP_START is the other end of the same period, INCAP_EXEMPT records whether an exemption was actually granted, and INCAP_WK_WRK_HRS how many hours a week the certifying doctor still thought the person able to work.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 642), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_end
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters. DSS's definition writes the same date as YYYYMMDD while the value domain gives the hyphenated form.
limitation: It is the end date the certificate specified, not the day the person recovered or returned to work, and a certificate superseded early still carries its original end date. Successive certificates for one illness appear as separate periods, so the length of an illness is not the length of any one period and has to be built by joining consecutive rows.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_end to DSS data element 642, which supplies the definition and the YYYY-MM-DD value domain, and binds incap_start, incap_exempt and incap_wk_wrk_hrs on the same row.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition ends, expressed as YYYYMMDD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity period end date" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without explaining what incapacity means administratively or that the date is a certificate date.

value_domain: Incapacity exemption indicator (Y/N)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity exemption indicator, Code" (item 654), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_exempt
variable_description: Whether the person was granted an exemption from mutual obligation requirements on the ground of incapacity, which DSS defines as an indicator of "whether an incapacity exemption has been granted or not". A medical certificate covering INCAP_START to INCAP_END does not by itself excuse a person; a delegate has to grant the exemption, and this flag records that decision. It matters because an exemption stops participation requirements and the payment suspensions that follow from missing them.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity exemption indicator, Code" (item 654), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_exempt
value_definition: A single letter: Y where the exemption was granted, N where it was not. DSS publishes the two codes as "Incapacity Exemption Granted" and "Incapacity Exemption Not Granted".
limitation: An N is a decision recorded against this period, not evidence that the person was well, and the flag does not say why an exemption was refused. It covers exemption on incapacity grounds only, so a person exempted for another reason — a major personal crisis, caring responsibilities, a natural disaster — still shows N here.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_exempt to DSS data element 654, whose value domain publishes the two codes with their meanings and whose definition names the granting decision.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether an incapacity exemption has been granted or not.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity exemption indicator" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, although a published two-value code list exists.

value_domain: Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 641), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_start
variable_description: The day a certified period of temporary incapacity began, which DSS defines as "The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition commences". It opens the period that INCAP_END closes, and the pair is what makes this table a history of episodes of ill health among income support recipients rather than a static medical record. INCAP_EXEMPT says whether the period produced an exemption from requirements and INCAP_WK_WRK_HRS what residual work capacity the doctor certified.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 641), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_start
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters. DSS's definition writes the same date as YYYYMMDD while the value domain gives the hyphenated form.
limitation: It dates the certified period, not the onset of the illness: a person who was unwell for months before seeing a doctor about their payment obligations starts here on the day the certificate begins. The column also only exists where incapacity was reported to Centrelink, so it measures illness that interfered with a claim rather than illness in the population.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_start to DSS data element 641, which gives the definition and the YYYY-MM-DD value domain, and pairs it with incap_end on the same row.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition commences, expressed as YYYYMMDD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity period start date" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Certified work capacity, hours per week
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity adjusted weekly work hours, Total number" (item 657), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_wk_wrk_hrs
variable_description: The weekly hours the certifying doctor considered the person still able to work during a period of incapacity, which DSS defines as "The number of hours per week that the issuing doctor considers the client able to work". It is what separates partial from total incapacity: a person certified for some hours can be held to reduced requirements rather than exempted outright, which is why it sits beside INCAP_EXEMPT. The hours apply to the period bounded by INCAP_START and INCAP_END.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity adjusted weekly work hours, Total number" (item 657), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_wk_wrk_hrs
value_definition: A whole number of hours per week in a two-digit field, so 0 to 99, with a full stop as the missing marker.
limitation: It is a clinician's judgement about capacity, not hours the person actually worked; declared hours live on the employment income tables. A zero means certified as able to work no hours, which is a positive finding rather than a gap, and confusing it with the missing marker turns full incapacity into no data.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_wk_wrk_hrs to DSS data element 657, whose definition attributes the figure to the issuing doctor and whose value domain is a two-digit total number with a full stop for missing.
evidence_quote: The number of hours per week that the issuing doctor considers the client able to work.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity adjusted work hours" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying whose judgement the hours are or that zero differs from missing.

value_domain: DSS Indigenous status code
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Indigenous status, Code" (item 461), bound to indg_stat.indig_code
variable_description: Whether the person identified as Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander or South Sea Islander in their dealings with Centrelink, defined by DSS as "Whether a person identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, as represented by a code". The indg_stat table holds nothing but this column and the person key, because DSS treats the item as sensitive and releases it separately from the rest of the demographic data. The code set is wider than the ABS standard question: it separates South Sea Islander origin, records where a person declined to answer, and marks where an ATO customer was never asked.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Indigenous status, Code" (item 461), bound to indg_stat.indig_code
value_definition: A single letter from a thirteen-value list: A Aboriginal, T Torres Strait Islander, B both, S South Sea Islander, with C, E and F combining South Sea Islander with the others, G South Sea Islander only, N none of them, D and H for declining to answer, and X and Z where an ATO customer was not asked. DSS groups A, B, C, E, F and T as Indigenous, and blank, D, G, H, N, S, X and Z as not identified as Indigenous.
limitation: It is administrative self-identification captured at some point of contact with Centrelink, not a Census response, so it is missing for anyone who never had reason to answer and is not refreshed when a person's identification changes. The "not identified" grouping mixes people who said no with people who declined and people who were never asked, so treating it as a non-Indigenous count overstates that group and understates Indigenous status.
rationale: Indigenous Status - sensitive (PLIDA) binds indg_status.indig_code to DSS data element 461, which publishes the full thirteen-code value domain and the two supplementary groupings, and shows the table carries only this column and the person key.
evidence_quote: Whether a person identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Recipient indigenous code" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, although DSS publishes the complete code list and the Indigenous grouping rule.

value_domain: domino_education_institution_type_code
values: ["B: Both Primary and Secondary","H: Higher Education Private Providers","O: Special School","P: Primary School","Q: Higher Education TAFEs","R: Private Provider","S: Secondary School","T: TAFE","U: University"]
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Education institution type, Code" (item 733), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
variable_description: The kind of institution the student attends, from primary school to university. DSS defines the element as one that "Identifies the type of institution at which the student is studying", so it describes the provider while COURSE_LVL describes the level of study. The codeframe keeps TAFEs and private higher education providers separate from universities, a distinction that matters to Family Tax Benefit and student payment rules.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Education institution type, Code" (item 733)
value_definition: A single letter, format A, with nine values: P primary school, S secondary school, B both primary and secondary, O special school, T TAFE, U university, Q higher education TAFEs, H higher education private providers and R private provider.
limitation: It names no institution, sector funding or location, so it cannot be used to study particular providers or to link to higher education collections. Provider type and course level can also disagree, since a TAFE can deliver a degree, so it is no substitute for COURSE_LVL.
rationale: EDU_DTLS_EXT and EDU_FTB_EXT bind inst_type to "Course: Education institution type, Code", nine single-letter institution types.

value_domain: Interpreter required indicator (Y/N/null)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Interpreter Required Indicator, Yes/No Code N" (item 65860), bound to static_demogs.interpreter_ind
variable_description: Whether Centrelink recorded that the person needs an interpreter to deal with the agency, which DSS defines as "The code that indicates whether an interpreter service is required by or for the person". It sits on the static demographics table beside LANG_CODE, the preferred spoken language, and the two answer different questions: the language code says what the person prefers to speak, this says whether that preference amounts to a service need. Together with BIRTH_CTRY_CODE it is the closest DOMINO comes to a signal of English proficiency.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Interpreter Required Indicator, Yes/No Code N" (item 65860), bound to static_demogs.interpreter_ind
value_definition: A single character: Y yes, N no, and an underscore for null.
limitation: It records an operational flag set when someone asked for or was offered an interpreter, not a measured level of English, so it under-counts people who manage in English with difficulty and people who rely on family members to interpret. A blank is not a no: the value domain carries an explicit null for the case where nothing is known.
rationale: STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA) binds interpreter_ind to DSS data element 65860, whose definition names the service requirement and whose value domain publishes Y, N and the underscore null.
evidence_quote: The code that indicates whether an interpreter service is required by or for the person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Interpreter service required indicator" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, although the domain has three published values including an explicit null.

value_domain: Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108889), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_end_date
variable_description: The last day of the person's unbroken run on income support, where Snap-DOMINO's definition of unbroken tolerates short exits. DSS allows gaps of up to six weeks where the whole period including gaps is under a year, and up to thirteen weeks where it is longer, so this date can sit well after several brief departures from payment. LAST_ACTIVE_ISP names the payment the run ended on, and ISP_PANEL_DAYS counts the days actually spent on payment within the panel.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108889), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_end_date
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters.
limitation: Subtracting the start date from this one measures the run including its tolerated gaps, so it overstates time on payment; ISP_PANEL_DAYS is the column that counts days actually received. An end date at or near the snapshot also does not establish that the person left income support, because a run still open when the extract was drawn has to be read against SNAP_DATE and ISP_ON_SNAP.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds isp_active_end_date to DSS data element 108889, whose definition sets out the six-week and thirteen-week gap tolerances and whose value domain is a ten-character YYYY-MM-DD date.
evidence_quote: End of an active Income Support Payment period, allowing for gaps of up to 6 weeks if the total period (including gaps) is under one year, and up to 13 weeks if over one year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing warned against reading the interval as time on payment.

value_domain: Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108888), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_start_date
variable_description: The first day of the person's current unbroken run on income support. Snap-DOMINO builds the run by joining spells across short breaks — up to six weeks where the whole period is under a year, up to thirteen weeks where it is longer — so the date reaches back past exits that a spell-based measure would treat as the end of a claim. FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP names the payment the run opened on, which need not be the payment the person is on at the snapshot.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108888), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_start_date
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters.
limitation: It is the start of the current run, not the person's first contact with income support: a break longer than the tolerance resets it, so a long history can appear as a recent start and duration measures built from this column understate lifetime receipt. It also cannot be used to date a job loss, because a run can open on a student, carer or parenting payment rather than an unemployment one.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds isp_active_start_date to DSS data element 108888, whose definition sets out the gap tolerances and the intended use in identifying people struggling to find work, and whose value domain is a ten-character YYYY-MM-DD date.
evidence_quote: Start of an active period on an Income Support Payment
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying that the date resets after a long break.

value_domain: domino_isp_status_code
values: ["CUR: Current","SUS: Suspicious","N: Not Applicable (supplementary)"]
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Status Code" (item 108850), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
variable_description: The state of the person's income support payment at the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. DSS gives the definition as "Income support payment status" and says the field "displays the customers entitlement to ISP", with the payment itself named in ISP_TYPE_CODE. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE, ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE and ISP_PANEL_DAYS on the same row bound the active spell this status describes.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Status Code" (item 108850)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, with CUR and SUS as permissible values and N as the default. The registry labels SUS "Suspicious", which reads as a typographical error for suspended.
limitation: It is a state on one day, not an outcome: suspensions are frequently restored within days, so counting SUS records as exits from income support overstates them. The status attaches to whichever payment ISP_TYPE_CODE names, so it cannot be used to follow one payment across a transfer to another.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds isp_ben_status to "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Status Code", published as CUR and SUS with NA.
evidence_quote: CUR Current | SUS Suspicious
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these benefit-status codes.

value_domain: Yes/no flag
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108846, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap'
variable_description: Says whether the person was being paid an income support payment on the day the snapshot was taken. It is the flag that turns Snap DOMINO into a point-in-time count of income support recipients: SNAP_DATE gives the day, ISP_TYPE_CODE names which payment, ISP_BEN_STATUS gives its status, and ISP_PANEL_DAYS counts activity over the surrounding window rather than on the day alone. Read it beside the parallel FTBA_ON_SNAP, FTBB_ON_SNAP, RENT_ON_SNAP and SUP_ON_SNAP flags, which cover family payments, rent assistance and supplements on the same date.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108846, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap'
value_definition: One character from the DSS yes/no/missing code domain: Y for received on the snapshot date, N for not. The domain admits a missing value as well, so a person with no income support record at all need not read as N.
limitation: A day is not a year. Someone paid for eleven months who happened to be off payment on the snapshot date reads as N, so the flag understates how many people touch income support over a period. It also carries no amount, and it does not separate a full-rate entitlement from one reduced to nil by the income test.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry binds the snap_domino_beta column isp_on_snap to the data element 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap', which publishes both the definition and the yes/no/missing value domain.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating Income Support Payment received on snap date
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the data item list wording as its whole description and repeated 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing said what a snapshot flag measures or what it misses.

value_domain: Count of days
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108845, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days'
variable_description: Counts the days the person spent active on an income support payment across the panel window the snapshot belongs to, rather than on the snapshot day itself. It is what separates someone continuously on payment from someone who cycled on and off between snapshots, which the ISP_ON_SNAP flag cannot show. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE bound the underlying spell, and DOMINO treats that spell as tolerating breaks of up to six weeks where the whole period runs under a year.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108845, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days'
value_definition: An integer count of days in the registry's Count N(8) domain, with a published default of 0. Days are summed across income support payments of any type, so the total measures time on income support rather than time on one payment.
limitation: The total cannot tell you which payment the days belonged to, so a move from JobSeeker Payment to Disability Support Pension inside the window collapses into a single number and only ISP_TYPE_CODE, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP separate them. Because 0 is the default, a genuine zero and a person with no income support history look identical.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry binds snap_domino_beta.isp_panel_days to 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days' and publishes its Count N(8) domain and its default of 0. The registry does not publish the length of the panel window, so that part of the description is read off the snapshot design rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Number of days active on Income Support Payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so a reader could not tell what period the days were counted over.

value_domain: DSS language code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 65366, 'Person: Preferred Spoken Language, Code XXX'
variable_description: The language the person prefers to speak, as recorded by Centrelink through the interpreter process. The DSS registry defines the field as "The code that represents the preferred spoken language of a customer who has requested the assistance of an interpreter", which is why it sits on static_demogs next to INTERPRETER_IND, the flag saying an interpreter was required. The same code is repeated on snap_domino_beta so that a snapshot of recipients can be cut by language without joining back to the demographics table.

Because it is populated through interpreter requests, a person who never asked for an interpreter can be blank or sit on a default regardless of what they speak, so counts of language groups from this column understate every community that manages without one. It is also not comparable with the Census language variable, which uses the ABS classification.

supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Preferred spoken language code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the field is collected for interpreting rather than as a language statistic.

value_domain: DSS benefit type code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'
variable_description: The income support payment the person was on at the close of the active payment spell that the snapshot falls in. With FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP it brackets the spell, so a row shows where a period on income support started and where it finished without joining to the payment history tables. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE give the dates of that spell, which DOMINO builds by stitching over breaks of up to six weeks.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'

limitation: It names the last payment inside one stitched spell, not the last payment a person ever received, so a person who returns to income support after a longer break starts a new spell with its own closing payment. The column also gives no date for the change and no reason for it.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.last_active_isp to 'Payment: Last Active ISP' and gives its value domain as the DSS benefit type code, the same code set used by ISP_TYPE_CODE, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP.
evidence_quote: Last payment in active Income Support Payment period

It sits on the medical conditions details table beside MED_SCNDRY_GRP, which names the condition group, and MED_SCNDRY_PERM, which records how lasting the condition was judged to be.

The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", so it is the finest location DOMINO records for a person. MESHMATCH beside it says whether the code came from matching the address itself or only its coordinates, SA1_MAINCODE, SA2_MAINCODE, POSTCODE and STATE are the same address at coarser levels, and the column repeats on the temporary and terminated address table and on snap_domino_beta.

The DSS registry defines it as an "Indicator identifying if a meshblock code was matched by address or longitude/latitude coordinates", which makes it the quality flag for every geography column on the location details table. It matters because a coordinate match can put a record on the wrong side of a boundary, so MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE are less reliable at fine resolution where this column reads L.

value_domain: Calendar month of birth
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'
variable_description: The month the person was born, held separately from YEAR_OF_BIRTH because the PLIDA release of DOMINO carries no full date of birth. The department's internal equivalent of this table, stt_pit_ext, holds a single date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD; the PLIDA version splits it into month and year, which is a disclosure control rather than a difference in what was collected. Combined with YEAR_OF_BIRTH it fixes a person's age to within a month, and AGE on the same row gives their age as at the extract date.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'
value_definition: A calendar month. The DSS registry restricts the metadata for this column, so neither the coding, the width nor the treatment of missing values is published, and the value should be inspected in the extract before use.
limitation: There is no day of birth, so an exact age on a given date cannot be calculated and anyone whose birthday falls in the month of an event sits on either side of an age threshold with equal probability. That matters for payments with sharp age tests, such as the move from Youth Allowance to JobSeeker Payment or reaching Age Pension age, where a month of uncertainty is enough to misclassify eligibility.
rationale: The registry's STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA) distribution lists month_of_birth and year_of_birth as columns but marks their data elements permission restricted, while the internal stt_pit_ext distribution for the same table lists a single date_of_birth field. That supports what the column is and why it exists, but publishes nothing about its value domain, so the status stays guessed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Birth month' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that the split from a full date of birth is the reason exact ages cannot be built.

Where the current payment is the last in the spell there is nothing to point to, and LAST_ACTIVE_ISP names the closing payment instead.

value_domain: DSS object type code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'
variable_description: Says what kind of entity the demographic record describes: a person, a child, or an organisation. The DSS registry defines the column as containing "the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer", and it matters because DOMINO's customer records are not all adults with a claim of their own. Children listed on a carer's or a family payment record, and organisations acting as nominees or payees, sit in the same customer table, so this is the column that keeps them out of a count of recipients.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'
value_definition: A three-character code with three permissible values: PER, CHI and ORG. The registry publishes the codes without written meanings, so the expansions to person, child and organisation come from the code letters themselves.
limitation: It classifies the record, not a person's role in a payment: a CHI record does not say which payment the child was listed against or who claimed for them, and the relationship tables carry that link. Filtering to PER is also not the same as filtering to adults, because the object type follows how the record was created rather than the person's age now.
rationale: The registry maps static_demogs.object_type_code to 'Recipient: Object Type, Code' and publishes the three-value domain. The expansion of each code and the caution about age are read from the code letters and the table's contents rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Contains the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Object type code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the domain has exactly three values and decides whether a row is a recipient at all.

variable_description: Says whether Centrelink had the person recorded as a member of a couple on the snapshot date. Partnered status drives rates, income tests and asset tests across almost every payment, so it explains rate differences on the snapshot table that ISP_TYPE_CODE alone cannot. EXT_DOM_HOUSEHOLD_ID pairs the person with their partner by concatenating the two DOMINO person identifiers, so a Y here should sit beside a two-person household identifier.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108240, 'Partnered status'
value_definition: One alphabetic character: Y for partnered and N for not partnered, with U as the registry's supplementary value for unknown. Three states can therefore appear.
limitation: It is a social security assessment of whether a couple relationship exists, not a marital status, so a de facto couple reads as Y and a married couple who have separated under one roof can read as N. It also refers only to the snapshot date and says nothing about how long the relationship had been recorded or how often it changed.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.partnered_status to the 'Partnered status' data element and publishes the Y and N permissible values plus the U supplementary value.

The DSS registry defines it as "The date upon which a recipient's blindness was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". It is the only medical field on the static demographics table, and it belongs there rather than in the dated medical condition records because blind status is assessed once and then attaches to the person.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 615, 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. It is populated only for recipients assessed as permanently blind, so it is empty for almost every person on the table.
limitation: A populated date means blindness was diagnosed, not that the person was paid a blind pension from that date or paid at all; claim, grant and rate information sit in the payment history tables. It is also not an onset date, since it records the ophthalmologist's diagnosis rather than when sight was lost, and those can be years apart.

value_domain: Yes/no flag
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 428, 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code'
variable_description: Says whether the concession card determination on this row was still pending rather than settled. The DSS registry defines it as an indicator of "whether a concession card is pending", so it is what separates a card the person actually held from a determination still in progress. It appears on all four concession card tables, covering the Health Care Card, the Pensioner Concession Card, the low income card and the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, and it should be read with CARD_ISSUE_DATE, CARD_START_DATE and CARD_END_DATE, because a pending row can carry a start date before any card was produced.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 428, 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code'
value_definition: One character, Y or N, with N as the registry's default. The field is boolean, so a row carrying no explicit value is treated as not pending.
limitation: It records the state of the determination when the row was written, not the eventual outcome, so a pending row is not evidence that the card was later granted or refused. Counting card holders without excluding pending rows overstates coverage, and the flag cannot tell you how long the determination stayed pending.
rationale: The CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps pending_flag to 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code', which publishes the definition, the Y and N values and the N default.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether a concession card is pending.
