value_domain: Date
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 394, 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the record on this row stops applying, closing an episode that PERIOD_START_DATE opened. The DSS registry defines it as "The date on which a reporting period relating to an event ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". Nearly every DOMINO table is built this way, with one row per person per period, whether the period covers an address, a concession card, a medical assessment, an income record or a payment component, so this column and its start-date partner are what make DOMINO longitudinal rather than a set of snapshots.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 394, 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. Whether a still-open episode is left blank or carried with a sentinel far-future date varies between DOMINO tables, so check a column's maximum value before filtering on it.
limitation: The date closes an administrative record, not the circumstance behind it: an address period ends when the department was told of a change, not when the person moved, and a card period ends when the determination changed, not when the person stopped using the card. Periods on the same table can also abut or overlap after a retrospective correction, so counting rows is not the same as counting spells.
rationale: The registry maps period_end_date on the DOMINO distributions, including loc_dtls, ccd_hcc, mcd_dtls, inc_shc and the payment history tables, to the single data element 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD', which publishes its definition and date domain.
evidence_quote: The date on which a reporting period relating to an event ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Event end date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which said nothing about DOMINO's episode structure or about how open periods are represented.

value_domain: Date
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 393, 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the record on this row starts applying. The DSS registry defines it as "The date on which a reporting period relating to an event commences, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". Every DOMINO table that holds history is keyed on a person and this date, so to use any of them you filter the pair of period columns against a date of interest; without them a table is a stack of overlapping records with no time dimension. On tables such as loc_dtls and ccd_hcc one person has many rows, and the start dates are what put them in order.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 393, 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain.
limitation: The start date is when the department recorded a circumstance as taking effect, not when it happened. A backdated grant carries an effective date earlier than the decision, and a late-reported address change carries one later than the move, so the column cannot be used to time real-world events precisely. It also marks the start of this record only, not of the person's dealings with the department.
rationale: The registry maps period_start_date across the DOMINO distributions to the single data element 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD', which publishes its definition and its ten-character date domain.
evidence_quote: The date on which a reporting period relating to an event commences, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Event start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing on the gap between an administrative effective date and the event it stands for.

value_domain: DSS benefit type code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108854, 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment'
variable_description: The income support payment the person was on immediately before the current one, within the same active payment spell. It is what lets a single snapshot row show a pathway rather than a state: a DSP row with JSP behind it is a successful disability claim, and a JSP row with PPS behind it is usually a single parent whose youngest child aged out of Parenting Payment Single. NEXT_ISP is the forward-looking partner, and FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP names where the spell began.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108854, 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment'
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which covers about a hundred payments: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS for Parenting Payment Single.
limitation: The previous payment is scoped to the current spell, so a person's earlier history before a long break is not visible here and the field is simply empty at the start of a spell. It also gives no date and no reason for the change, so it cannot distinguish a voluntary transfer from an automatic one such as the transfer of single parents onto JobSeeker Payment when a child reached the age cut-off.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.prev_isp to 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment' with the DSS benefit type code domain. That the field is empty at the start of a spell follows from the definition's scoping to the period of activity rather than being stated.
evidence_quote: Refers to the previous Income Support Payment type benefit (in this period of activity)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the code set or explaining that the lookback stops at the spell boundary.

value_domain: Yes/no flag
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 110042, 'Person: Principal Carer Indicator, Code X'
variable_description: Says whether the person was treated as the principal carer of a dependent child under 16 on the snapshot date. Principal carer status is what triggers the parenting payment rules, the reduced participation requirements and the higher single rate that apply to sole parents, so it explains rate differences that ISP_TYPE_CODE alone cannot. PRI_CARER_TOTAL_CHILDREN counts the qualifying children and PRI_CARER_AGE_YOUNGEST_CHILD gives the age of the youngest, which is the number most of the payment rules actually turn on.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 110042, 'Person: Principal Carer Indicator, Code X'
value_definition: One character, Y or N, with N as the registry's default, so a person with no qualifying children reads as N rather than as missing.
limitation: It is a payment status, not a statement of who lives with a child: care can be shared, and the parent who does not hold the status still cares for the child, so counting Y values undercounts parents. The under-16 test also means a parent supporting a 16-year-old reads as N while still carrying the cost.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.pri_carer to 'Person: Principal Carer Indicator, Code X' and publishes the Y and N permissible values with N as the default.
evidence_quote: The code that indicates whether a person is considered to have primary care of a dependent child under the age of 16 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the two-value domain nor the shared-care ambiguity was recorded.

value_domain: Age in years
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 69050, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Youngest Child Age, Number'
variable_description: The age of the youngest child in the principal carer's care on the snapshot date, which is the number most parenting payment rules turn on. Parenting Payment Single ends when the youngest child reaches a set age, under eight until 20 September 2023 and under 14 from that date, and part-time participation requirements begin earlier, so this column explains transitions between payments that the payment type alone makes look arbitrary. It is only meaningful where PRI_CARER is Y.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 69050, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Youngest Child Age, Number'
value_definition: An integer age in whole years, held in the registry's Count N(8) domain. It refers to the youngest of the children counted by PRI_CARER_TOTAL_CHILDREN, not to all children in the household.
limitation: The value is an age at one date, so it cannot be used to date a birth or to identify the child, and successive snapshots of the same person can skip a year where a child enters or leaves care. Because the count behind it is payment scoped, a younger child who fails a residence or dependency test is ignored and the age recorded can be older than the youngest child actually present.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.pri_carer_age_youngest_child to 'Recipient: Principal Carer Youngest Child Age, Number' and publishes its Count N(8) domain. The Parenting Payment Single age cut-offs come from the 2023 legislative change that lifted the youngest child age from eight to 14.
evidence_quote: The age of the youngest child in the care of the Principal Carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without connecting the age to the payment thresholds that make it worth having.

value_domain: Count of qualifying children
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 66073, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Children in Care Count, Total'
variable_description: Counts the children the person was responsible for on the snapshot date who met the dependency tests for a payment. It is a payment-scoped count and not a count of a person's children: the DSS registry defines it as the total of young people who meet "age, residence, income, study or job seeking or other dependency requirements for a particular payment, benefit or service". Read it with PRI_CARER, which says whether the person held principal carer status at all, and with CARD_ANY_MAX_CHILD_LISTED, which counts children listed on concession cards instead.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 66073, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Children in Care Count, Total'
value_definition: An integer count in the registry's Count N(8) domain. Zero appears for a person with no qualifying children.
limitation: A child who fails a residence, study or income test is invisible here, so the count can be lower than the number of children living in the home and should not be used as a family size measure. It is also not a fertility measure: children who have aged out of dependency drop out of the count, so the number falls over a parent's life while the number of children born to them does not.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.pri_carer_total_children to 'Recipient: Principal Carer Children in Care Count, Total', whose published definition names the dependency tests that scope the count, and gives the Count N(8) domain.
evidence_quote: The total count of young people for whom a customer has responsibility and who meets age, residence, income, study or job seeking or other dependency requirements for a particular payment, benefit or service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the difference between a payment-scoped count and the number of children in a family was never stated.

rationale: The CIR_PRIN_CAR_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps principal_parent_ind to 'Recipient: Principal Carer Indicator, Code', whose value domain publishes Y as the only permissible value with a missing supplementary value.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 84497, 'Payment: History Source, Code XXX'
variable_description: Says how the payment component on this row arose: as a regular recurring payment, as a one-off, or as an amount paid through a third party. It separates the fortnightly benefit stream from lump sums such as economic support payments and from money paid to someone else on the person's behalf, so summing CMPNT_DLY_AMT without filtering on it adds three different kinds of money together. The column appears on all twenty payment history tables, one per payment group, of which pyh_combined_dis is the disability and carers group.

It also does not identify the third party in a THP row, so payments to a nominee, a landlord under rent deduction, or a service provider cannot be told apart here.
rationale: The PYH_COMBINED_DIS (PLIDA) distribution maps pyh_source to 'Payment: History Source, Code XXX', whose value domain publishes exactly three codes with their meanings. supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Payment source' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the domain has three values and mixing them corrupts any total of payment amounts.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108892, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA1 main code, Code'
variable_description: The SA1 the person's address fell in, on the derived location table that holds one row per address episode. The ABS designs SA1s, in the registry's words, "to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data", which makes this the level at which a DOMINO record can be joined to Census small-area counts or to SEIFA. MB_ASGS_2021 on the same row is finer, SA2_ASGS_2021 and SA4_ASGS_2021 coarser, ARID_HASH_TRUNC identifies the address itself, and START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108892, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA1 main code, Code'
value_definition: An eleven-character ASGS 2021 SA1 code. SA1s are built from whole mesh blocks and aggregate to whole SA2s, so the geography columns on the row nest exactly and never contradict each other.
limitation: An SA1 holds roughly 200 to 800 people, so it is a neighbourhood rather than a household and a shared code is not evidence of co-residence. SA1 boundaries are also redrawn between ASGS editions, so codes cannot be compared across editions without a correspondence, and the edition of other SA1 columns in DOMINO should be checked before joining because the PLIDA data item list and the DSS registry disagree on some of them.
rationale: The LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA) distribution maps sa1_asgs_2021 to the ASGS 2021 SA1 main code data element, which publishes the ABS definition and the X(11) value domain.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) are geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks. Whole SA1s aggregate to form Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s). SA1s are designed to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data, represented as a code
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Sa1 location' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no code width, no nesting rule and no population scale to tell a reader how fine the geography is.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108679, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA2 main code, Code'
variable_description: The SA2 of the person's address on the snapshot date. SA2 is the level most published ABS regional output uses, so this is the practical join between Snap DOMINO recipient counts and Census, SEIFA or regional population data, and the level at which a rate of income support receipt per head of population can be built. SA3, SA4, LGA, CED, GCCSA and POSTCODE on the same row are the same address at other levels, and MESHBLOCK is the finest.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108679, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA2 main code, Code'
value_definition: An ASGS 2021 SA2 code. The registry records the value domain with a four-digit format, which is shorter than the ABS nine-digit SA2 main code, so check the width of the column in the extract before joining to a boundary file.
limitation: An SA2 is designed to approximate a community of interest, not an administrative area, so it does not line up with the LGA or the Commonwealth electoral division on the same row and totals will not reconcile across them. It is also the address on file rather than where the person spends their time, so it cannot support claims about where services were used.
rationale: The SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps sa2 to the ASGS 2021 SA2 main code data element, whose published definition is the wording carried in the PLIDA data item list, and which names the 2021 SA2 value domain.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s) are medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s). Their purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically, represented as a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the classification text as its description but repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what edition applied, how wide the code is, or what an SA2 fails to line up with.

value_domain: Annual amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 499, 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency'
variable_description: The deemed income counted against the person for the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card income test in this reporting period. The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual deemed income a recipient receives", and deemed income is not money actually received but the return the deeming rules assume a person's financial assets, including account-based income streams, produce at set rates. It sits with SHC_AN_INC_TXB, SHC_AN_INC_FGN, SHC_AN_PRP_LOS, SHC_AN_EMP_BEN and SHC_AN_SAL_SCF, which together make up the adjusted taxable income the card is tested on, and PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the year it covers.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 499, 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency'
value_definition: An amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN, covering one year. It is a figure calculated from the deeming rates rather than a reported one.
limitation: It is not investment income actually received, so it cannot measure returns: two people with identical balances carry identical deemed income however their investments performed, and a year of losses still produces a positive number. It also reaches only the assets the deeming rules cover, so it is not a measure of a person's wealth.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_dmd_inc to 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency', which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain, and the same distribution shows the other income components tested for the card.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual deemed income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual deemed income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without explaining that deemed income is assumed rather than received.

variable_description: Employer-provided benefits the person received that do not appear in taxable income, added back for the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card income test. The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual employer-provided benefits a recipient receives, not included in taxable income". The column exists because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income rather than taxable income, so the amounts a tax return leaves out are collected separately here alongside SHC_AN_SAL_SCF for salary sacrifice, SHC_AN_INC_FGN for foreign income and SHC_AN_PRP_LOS for net investment and property losses.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 498, 'Recipient: Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits income, Total Australian currency'
value_definition: An annual amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN. It is zero for anyone with no employer, which is most card holders, since the card is aimed at people of Age Pension age.
limitation: It captures reportable fringe benefits for one income test, so it is not a measure of total remuneration and does not include compulsory employer superannuation contributions. A zero cannot be read as no employment either, only as no reportable benefits, so it is not a proxy for retirement.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_emp_ben to the Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits data element, which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual employer-provided benefits a recipient receives, not included in taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual employer provided benefits income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why an income test needs amounts left out of taxable income.

value_domain: Annual amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 501, 'Recipient: Annual foreign income, Total Australian currency'
variable_description: Income from overseas sources counted for the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card income test, expressed in Australian dollars. The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual foreign income a recipient receives". It is collected because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income, so a retiree living on an overseas pension is tested on that income even where it does not appear on an Australian tax return, and SHC_AN_INC_TXB on the same row holds the domestic taxable amount.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 501, 'Recipient: Annual foreign income, Total Australian currency'
value_definition: An annual amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN, converted from the source currency. Unlike the deemed income on the same row it is a reported figure rather than a calculated one.
limitation: It does not say where the income came from or what kind it was, so an overseas age pension, foreign rent and offshore investment income collapse into one number and no country can be identified. Because it is reported only for a card income test, it appears only for people who claimed or held the card and cannot be used to measure foreign income among older Australians generally.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_inc_fgn to 'Recipient: Annual foreign income, Total Australian currency', which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual foreign income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual foreign income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no currency, no units and no note that the figure exists only for card claimants.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: The taxable income Centrelink held for a person when testing them for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which DSS defines as "The amount of annual taxable income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). The inc_shc table carries one row per annual reporting period, bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, for people whose card eligibility was assessed. This column is one of seven income components on the row: deemed income, foreign income, employer provided benefits, net property and investment losses and salary sacrificed income sit beside it and are added to it to reach the adjusted taxable income the card is tested against. It answers what the card decision was based on, not what the person earned in total.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: A dollar amount for a whole year, unlike DOMINO's other income tables which hold a daily rate. The figure is what was reported to or held by Centrelink for the card assessment, and the external release applies variable rounding to the amount so that a person cannot be recognised from an unusual value.
limitation: It is not the person's ATO assessment. Centrelink records the taxable income relevant to the card test at the time of the test, so it can predate, lag or differ from the assessed figure in the ATO products in PLIDA, and it is only present for people whose seniors card eligibility was assessed rather than for all older Australians. Reading it as household income is also wrong: a couple is tested on combined income, but this row belongs to one person.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents inc_shc_ext as the longitudinal history of annually reported Centrelink income tied to seniors health card eligibility, and gives each column of the table its own definition, including this one.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual taxable income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's label 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual taxable income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing said what the figure was for or how it related to the six income columns beside it.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: An estimate of a year's taxable income used for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card assessment where an assessed figure was not available, defined by DSS as "The amount of annual estimated taxable income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). It sits directly beside SHC_AN_INC_TXB on the same annual row, which is the assessed rather than the estimated amount. Estimates arise when someone claims the card before a tax assessment exists for the relevant year, typically at retirement or on a first claim. The pair together shows whether the card decision rested on an estimate or on a settled figure.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: A dollar amount for a whole year, on the same footing as the assessed taxable income column and subject to the same variable rounding in the external release. It records what was estimated at the time of the assessment, not a revised figure.
limitation: The column cannot tell you which figure decided entitlement, nor whether the estimate was later replaced once a tax assessment issued. An estimate present alongside an assessed amount is not evidence of a dispute or of ineligibility, and the difference between the two is not an error measure: they can refer to different income years.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines every column of inc_shc_ext, including the estimated taxable income field, and describes the table as the annual Centrelink income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual estimated taxable income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell an estimate from the assessed amount held in the next column.

value_domain: Annual loss amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: The investment and rental property losses added back when a person's income is tested for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which DSS defines as "The amount of annual property and net investment losses a recipient incurs" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). Losses are added back because they reduce taxable income without reducing a person's capacity to support themselves, so the adjusted taxable income used for the card is higher than the taxable income beside it. A non-zero value here therefore raises the tested income rather than lowering it.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: An annual dollar amount standing for a loss rather than a receipt, reported for the same year as the other income columns on the row and variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: The column does not separate a negatively geared rental property from a geared share portfolio, so it cannot be used to identify property investors. It also says nothing about the asset behind the loss, which is tested separately under the assets test and is not carried in this table, and the sign convention is not published, so check the direction of the values before adding them to taxable income.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry gives this column its own definition inside the inc_shc_ext distribution, which it documents as the annual income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual property and net investment losses a recipient incurs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label 'annual net investment/property loss' and used one generic sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so it never explained that a loss increases the income the card is tested on.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: Income a person gave up under a salary sacrifice arrangement, counted back into the income test for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card and defined by DSS as "The amount of annual salary sacrificed income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). Like the property and investment loss column beside it, it is added back because sacrificing salary lowers taxable income without lowering the resources available to the person. For a card cohort at or near Age Pension age it usually reflects reportable contributions to superannuation made in the last working years.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: An annual dollar amount reported for the same year as the other income components on the row, variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: It is a measure of reportable sacrificed income, not of superannuation saving: compulsory employer contributions are outside it, so the column understates what went into a fund and cannot be used to study contribution behaviour. Nor does it say what the salary was sacrificed for, since sacrificed income can go to a car, an expense package or a fund.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_shc_ext, the distribution it documents as the annual Centrelink income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual salary sacrificed income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label, which even carries a typo ('sacrified'), and gave the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: The day the Snap-DOMINO row describes, defined by DSS as "A primary reference date for derived items in Snap-Domino, recorded as a day of a month of a year, and represented as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). Everything else on the row is measured as at that day: the on-snap flags for income support, family payments, rent assistance and supplementary payments, the concession cards held, the address and its geography, age, partnered status and principal carer status. Snap-DOMINO exists so that a cross-section can be taken without assembling episodes from the underlying event tables, so this column, with the person key, is what makes a row unique.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, taking one of the fixed reference days on which the snapshot is cut rather than any day a person had a dealing with the agency.
limitation: It marks a chosen observation day, so anything that started and ended between two snapshot days is invisible: a short spell on a payment, a card that lapsed and was reissued, or a move and a move back. Rates built from Snap-DOMINO are point-in-time prevalence, not incidence, and comparing two snap dates measures stocks rather than flows.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT as snapshot views of individuals' interactions with the welfare system on specified days of the year, and defines this column as the reference date those derived items hang off.
evidence_quote: A primary reference date for derived items in Snap-Domino, recorded as a day of a month of a year, and represented as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's wording and then said only that no finite value list applies, twice, so nothing explained that every other column on the row is measured as at this date.

value_domain: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
variable_description: The day an address became the recipient's effective address in Centrelink's records, opening the location episode the rest of the row describes. The loc_derived table holds one row per episode: the hashed address register identifier, the address type and priority, and the mesh block, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state codings of that address under ASGS 2021. Read with END_DATE it gives a residential history assembled from welfare administration rather than from a survey, and ADDR_PRTY exists because a person can hold more than one open address at once.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, as every date column in DOMINO's location distributions is.
limitation: It dates a record, not a removal van. The address becomes effective when the person tells the agency or the agency updates its records, so a start date can trail a move by weeks or months and a person who stops dealing with Centrelink keeps an address that is no longer theirs. Episodes across address types can also overlap, so a start date here does not close the previous episode.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents the loc_derived distribution as derived location boundaries and lists its contents: the anonymised address register identifier, the address priority code, the address type and the ASGS 2021 geography, with dates carried in YYYY-MM-DD form. The registry does not publish this column under the PLIDA name START_DATE, so the shape is sourced and the reading of the date as the start of the address episode is written from the table's contents.
evidence_quote: Derived code highlighting address priority for identifying the location of a recipient on a given day.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Effective address start date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say what the episode was, what closed it, or why more than one address can be open at once.

value_domain: Australian state or territory code
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution loc_dtls_ext
variable_description: The state or territory of the address held for the person, defined by DSS as "The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, loc_dtls_ext). Which address that is depends on the table: loc_dtls holds home addresses, loc_pos_temp_term_dtls holds postal, temporary and term addresses, and snap_domino_beta holds the address as at the snapshot day. On the location tables the column sits with POSTCODE, MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE for the same address, so it is the coarsest of several geographies for one place rather than a separate fact.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution loc_dtls_ext
value_definition: A short character code rather than a name: the registry gives the column as a character string of up to three characters, so the values are the usual state and territory abbreviations rather than numbers. Snap-DOMINO's STATE_CODE, by contrast, is a one-digit numeric code, so the two columns cannot be compared without recoding.
limitation: The state belongs to an address on file, not to a person, so a stale record puts someone in the state they left. On the postal and temporary address table the value can be a mailing state or a term address for a student, which is not where the person lives, and MESHMATCH warns that the finer geography beside it may have been matched from coordinates rather than from the address itself.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines loc_dtls_ext as the location of an individual's home addresses in DOMINO and gives this column its own definition; the companion distribution loc_pos_temp_term_dtls_ext, documented as non-home addresses, carries the same column.
evidence_quote: The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address state' and used one generic sentence for both the definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish the home address table from the postal, temporary and term address table where the same column means something different.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 state and territory code
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
variable_description: The state or territory of a location episode as coded to the ABS geography, defined by DSS as "The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, LOC_DERIVED). It is the top of a coding chain on the same row: the mesh block, SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it code the same address to finer ASGS 2021 areas, all derived from the address rather than reported by the person. Unlike STATE in loc_dtls, which travels with the recorded address, this is what the geocoding produced for the address that the episode's ARID stands for.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
value_definition: A single-digit ASGS state and territory code: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 the Northern Territory, 8 the Australian Capital Territory and 9 Other Territories.
limitation: It is the state of an address episode, not of a person on a given day, and a person with overlapping episodes can appear in two states at once, which is what ADDR_PRTY is there to resolve. It also says nothing about where a payment was administered or assessed, so it should not be used as a service-delivery region, and an address that could not be geocoded contributes no code at all rather than an unknown-state code.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents the loc_derived distribution and defines this column as the state or territory of an address represented by a code; the ASGS single-digit state and territory codes are the ABS standard the 2021 suffix names.
evidence_quote: The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'State (number)' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say which classification the number came from or how it related to the mesh block and SA codes beside it.

value_domain: Australian state or territory code
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: The state or territory a person was located in on the snapshot day, which DSS documents with the note that "Australian states and territories are identified by unique one-digit codes" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). It is one of a stack of geography columns on the Snap-DOMINO row: postcode, mesh block, SA2, SA3, SA4, local government area, greater capital city area and Commonwealth electoral division all describe the same address as at SNAP_DATE. Snap-DOMINO also carries STATE and REPORTED_STATE, so the row holds more than one view of the same thing.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A one-digit code for the state or territory, in the ABS ordering that runs from New South Wales through the Australian Capital Territory and then the other territories.
limitation: The registry does not say which of the snapshot's state columns takes precedence, so treat a disagreement between this and REPORTED_STATE as a sign of address quality rather than assuming one is wrong. The code also fixes a person to one day: someone who moved interstate a week after the snapshot is counted in the state they left.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes the Snap-DOMINO distribution and reproduces the definition of this column, which states the one-digit form of the code; the surrounding geography columns are listed on the same page.
evidence_quote: Australian states and territories are identified by unique one-digit codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about one-digit codes and then the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the code describes the snapshot day, or that two other state columns sit on the same row.

value_domain: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution edu_ftb_ext
variable_description: The day a course event stops for the student it belongs to, defined by DSS as "End date for a student of a course event" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, edu_ftb_ext). Whose study it is depends on the table: in edu_ftb the course belongs to a Family Tax Benefit recipient's child, whose study is what keeps an older teenager an FTB child, while in edu_dtls it is the recipient's own course, which is what supports a student payment. COURSE_LVL, COURSE_TYPE and INST_TYPE describe the course, and STDNT_PRTCPN_STS says whether the student was still participating.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution edu_ftb_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, recorded against a course event rather than an academic year.
limitation: An end date is not a completion. CMPLTN_IND and CMPLTN_DATE carry whether the course was finished, so a course event can close because the student left, changed institution or stopped being assessed for the payment. The date can also be the end expected when the course was recorded rather than the day study actually stopped.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside edu_ftb_ext, documented as the longitudinal history of FTB related educational information, and the same column with the same definition sits in edu_dtls_ext, documented as historical details of educational courses undertaken by a recipient.
evidence_quote: End date for a student of a course event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Student end date for course' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not distinguish a course ending from a course being completed, nor the child's study in edu_ftb from the recipient's own study in edu_dtls.

The flag is one of a matched set with ISP_ON_SNAP, FTBA_ON_SNAP, FTBB_ON_SNAP and RENT_ON_SNAP, so a person's whole payment position on the day can be read across five columns.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A boolean flag on the snapshot row, set from whether a supplementary payment was active on SNAP_DATE.
limitation: It does not say which supplementary payment, or how many: a person receiving Carer Allowance and Parental Leave Pay looks the same as a person receiving one of them. SUP_TYPE_CODE names the type and SUP_BEN_STATUS gives its status, so the flag alone cannot support any statement about a particular programme.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes this column's definition on the Snap-DOMINO distribution, and its companion value domain, Payment: Supplementary Type Code, lists the payments the supplementary group covers.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT

It is the duration counterpart to SUP_ON_SNAP: the flag says whether a supplementary payment was current on the snapshot day, and this column says how many days of activity lie behind it. The same pairing exists for income support, both parts of Family Tax Benefit and rent assistance, so intensity and point-in-time receipt can be compared across payment groups on one row.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT

Days active is also not days paid: a payment can be current while the rate is nil, and the count says nothing about which supplementary payment ran or whether the days were continuous.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column on the Snap-DOMINO distribution and, on the underlying data element Payment: Supplementary Panel Days, gives its form as an eight-digit count while documenting no window over which the days are counted.
evidence_quote: Number of days active on supplementary benefit
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's sentence and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the counting window is undocumented, which is the first thing anyone using the number needs.

value_domain: DSS person identifier for linkage (synthetic)

variable_description: The person key every DOMINO table is joined on, described by DSS as "A synthetic numeric sequence of characters used for the purposes of identifying a unique DOMINO entity" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, CCD_HCC_EXT). One value ties a person's payment history, income, concession cards, addresses, relationships, education and medical assessments together across the sixty-odd tables that carry it, which is what makes DOMINO a longitudinal record rather than a set of extracts. Within PLIDA the same key runs across products: MBS, PBS, the tax products, Census and the rest carry SYNTHETIC_AEUID under the same custodian description, Synthetic MADIP Person ID, so a DOMINO row joins to another agency's row on this column directly rather than through a separate mapping file.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA)
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned for linkage, with no meaning in its digits. It is not a Centrelink customer reference number and carries nothing about the person, so it can be matched but not decoded.
limitation: It identifies one person, not a household or an income unit, so it cannot be used to assemble a family: EXT_DOM_PARTNER_ID, CHILD_ID and the other listed-person identifiers on the same rows are a separate numbering space and do not equal another person's value here. A person absent from DOMINO is a person with no dealings with the department rather than a person with no need, and a person who fails to join to another PLIDA product has no record there rather than no history: the key is only as complete as the linkage behind it.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry gives the column its definition on every DOMINO distribution released to PLIDA, including the health care card determination table this occurrence sits in, and the PLIDA data item list names it as the synthetic MADIP person identifier held against the agency spine.
evidence_quote: A synthetic numeric sequence of characters used for the purposes of identifying a unique DOMINO entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' with a value domain of 'Opaque identifier (inferred)' and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 64 occurrences it never said what the key joins, or that a cross-agency join has to go through the spine.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_tac_ext
variable_description: Income attributed to a person from a private trust or private company they are connected to, defined by DSS as the "Amount of income derived by a recipient from a trust or company" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_tac_ext). The column exists because social security law looks through private structures: where a person controls or benefits from a trust or company, its income is attributed to them and tested like their own. The inc_tac table holds nothing else about the entity, so the row is the person, the period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, and this amount.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_tac_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate rather than a period total, held to two decimal places in a format of up to nine digits before the point. A period figure is the rate multiplied by the days in the period, and the external release variably rounds the amount.
limitation: The attributed amount follows social security rules, not tax rules, so it will not reconcile with a trust distribution in the same person's income tax return in the ATO products. It also names neither the trust nor the company and gives no share of control, so two people attributed income from the same entity cannot be identified as connected.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents inc_tac_ext as the longitudinal history of Centrelink reported income from trusts and companies in DOMINO, and gives this column its own definition and its decimal format.
evidence_quote: Amount of income derived by a recipient from a trust or company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Trust and company daily income amount' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say why a welfare dataset holds trust income or that the figure is an attribution under means-test rules.

value_domain: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: The day a period of temporarily limited work capacity closes on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as "The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). The mcd_dtls table is the record of medical conditions and work capacity assessments behind disability and participation decisions, holding the primary and secondary condition codes, an impairment rating, and the assessed hours a person can work. This date and its start-date pair bound the window in which the assessment treats the limitation as temporary rather than continuing.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, set by an assessment rather than by a payment event.
limitation: The close of a temporary limitation is not recovery and not a payment change: the condition codes and the impairment rating on the same row can be unchanged, and whether anything happened to the person's payment is in the payment history tables, not here. A date in the future is the period the assessment set, not an observed end.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents mcd_dtls_ext as the longitudinal history of Centrelink medical conditions and work capacity assessments in DOMINO, and defines each of the capacity date columns individually.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary limited capacity end date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say the date comes from an assessment or how it relates to the assessed hours on the same row.

value_domain: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: The day a period of temporarily limited work capacity opens on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as "The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment starts, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). It marks when an assessor accepted that a condition limits what the person can do for a bounded time, which is the distinction that separates a temporary exemption from participation requirements from a continuing incapacity. INCAP_START and INCAP_END on the same row hold incapacity periods, and IMPRMT_CODE and IMPRMT_RATE hold the impairment that was rated.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, recorded against the assessment that set the period.
limitation: It dates a decision, not the onset of a condition: a person can be unwell long before an assessment records a limited capacity, and someone who never had an assessment has no row at all. It is therefore a poor measure of when ill health began, and comparing it with a medical event date in the health products will overstate any delay attributed to the person.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents mcd_dtls_ext as the longitudinal history of Centrelink medical conditions and work capacity assessments, and gives this date column its own definition.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment starts, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary limited capacity start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the date belongs to an assessment rather than to the illness.

value_domain: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: The day a period of temporarily reduced working hours closes on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as "The date on which a period of temporary reduction in capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). Reduced capacity is the milder of the two temporary findings on this table: limited capacity suspends what a person can be asked to do, while reduced capacity cuts the hours, and TEMP_REDN_CAP_HRS_NUM holds the size of that cut. Reading the two together shows whether an assessment stopped or merely trimmed a person's participation obligations.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, closing a period set by an assessment.
limitation: No matching start-date column is published for the reduced-capacity period, so its beginning has to be inferred from PERIOD_START_DATE or from the preceding assessment; do not borrow TEMP_LMT_CAP_START_DATE, which belongs to the limited-capacity finding rather than this one.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry lists the columns of mcd_dtls_ext and defines this one; the same listing shows a temporary reduction end date and hours column with no corresponding start date.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of temporary reduction in capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary reduced capacity end date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither separated reduced from limited capacity nor warned that no start date exists for this period.

value_domain: Hours per week
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: How many weekly hours an assessment took off a person's work capacity for a temporary period, defined by DSS as "The number of reduction in hours a recipient is able to work in a week" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). It is a change, not a level: CURR_CAPCTY_NUM on the same row holds the current assessed capacity in hours a week and WITH_INTRVN_NUM holds the capacity with intervention, so this column has to be read against them to say what the person was assessed as able to do. Weekly hours are the currency of these decisions because payment and participation rules turn on hour thresholds rather than on a diagnosis.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A whole number of hours in a week, recorded against the assessment that made the finding.
limitation: Assessed hours are not worked hours. Nothing here records whether the person had a job, and actual earnings sit in the employment income tables, so the column cannot be used to measure labour supply. Because the value is a reduction, treating it as remaining capacity inverts its meaning.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside mcd_dtls_ext, alongside the current capacity and with-intervention hour columns that give it its scale.
evidence_quote: The number of reduction in hours a recipient is able to work in a week
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary reduced capacity hours number' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the number is a reduction rather than a capacity, which is the error a reader would otherwise make.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext
variable_description: Whether the person being cared for has a terminal illness, defined by DSS as an "Indicator that a caree has a terminal illness" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_caree_ext). The mcd_caree table is medical information about care receivers, collected because someone claimed Carer Payment or Carer Allowance for them, so every column on the row describes the cared-for person while the person key on the row is the carer. A terminal illness matters administratively because it changes how a carer claim is assessed and how quickly it can be granted.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext
value_definition: A yes or no indicator recorded against a care receiver's medical record for the period the row covers.
limitation: The flag belongs to the care receiver, not to the person whose identifier is on the row, so reading it as the carer's own health inverts the record. It also reflects what was reported to support a claim, so it is not a clinical diagnosis, gives no prognosis or date, and its absence means only that nothing was recorded.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents mcd_caree_ext as the medical conditions of the caree for a recipient of Carer Payment or Carer Allowance, and defines this indicator directly.
evidence_quote: Indicator that a caree has a terminal illness.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Terminal illness indicator' with the value domain left as 'not specified' and the generic sentence in both fields, so it never said whose illness is being flagged.

value_domain: Treating health professional identifier (synthetic)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext
variable_description: The health professional who supplied the medical evidence about a care receiver, which DSS describes as identifying "which Treating Health Professional from which the data was supplied", adding that "It is not a foreign key to an external provider/third party file" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_caree_ext). Carer Payment and Carer Allowance claims turn on a medical report about the person being cared for, and this column is what distinguishes the doctor or specialist who completed one report from another. Rows sharing a value came from the same professional, which is the only clinician-level structure DOMINO carries.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext
value_definition: A synthetic identifier standing for the professional, with no name, provider number or registration detail in it, and no meaning in its digits.
limitation: Because it is not a foreign key, it cannot be joined to any provider file: not to a Medicare provider number in MBS or PBS, and not to a registration record. It also identifies only the professional who completed evidence for this claim, so it is not the care receiver's usual doctor, and it does not tell you the profession, specialty or location of whoever supplied the report.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside mcd_caree_ext and states explicitly that it is not a foreign key to an external provider file, which is the claim a reader most needs.
evidence_quote: Identifies which Treating Health Professional from which the data was supplied. It is not a foreign key to an external provider/third party file.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Treating health professional synthetic id' with an inferred opaque-identifier domain and the generic sentence twice, so it left open the join to MBS provider data that the source explicitly rules out.

The ABS data item list glosses the column as the type of apprenticeship, while the DSS element bound to it is the field of education of the course of study, so the two readings differ and the safer treatment is as the trade or field rather than a contract type. APT_START_DATE, APT_END_DATE and EUEA_ID bound and identify the apprenticeship episode.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Education field of study, Code" (item 725), read against the ABS PLIDA DOMINO data item list

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
variable_description: Compensation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous income from compensation received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). The inc_une_cont table splits recurring unearned income into six named sources, one column each, over a period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, with BEN_TYPE naming the payment the income was assessed against. Compensation here means periodic payments such as workers compensation or an insurance income stream, which reduce a payment dollar for dollar under the compensation rules rather than through the ordinary income test.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate, not a period total. Multiply by the days in the period for an amount, and expect variable rounding: the external release perturbs the figures so that an unusual amount cannot identify a person.
limitation: It carries periodic compensation only. A lump sum settlement produces a preclusion period rather than a daily income rate, so a person with a large payout can show nothing in this column while receiving no payment at all, and the column does not say whether the compensation reduced the payment or by how much.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents inc_une_cont_ext as the longitudinal history of Centrelink reported unearned income from continuous sources, and defines each of the six source columns separately.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of continuous income from compensation received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Continuing unearned daily income - compensation income' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say the amount is a daily rate or that lump sums are handled outside this table.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
variable_description: Overseas income counted against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous income from foreign sources received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). It is most often a foreign age or invalidity pension paid to a migrant with a working life in another country, which Australia's international agreements require to be claimed and then assess as income. The column sits with five other recurring unearned income sources on the same row, so a person's total assessed unearned income is the sum across them for the period.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate in Australian currency, converted from the paying country's currency, and variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: It names neither the country nor the scheme, so an agreement pension cannot be told apart from private overseas income or from a foreign annuity. Because the amount is converted, a change between periods can be an exchange rate movement or a scheduled revaluation rather than any change in the person's circumstances, and no exchange rate or revaluation date is carried to tell the two apart.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_une_cont_ext, which it documents as the longitudinal history of Centrelink reported unearned income from continuous sources.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of continuous income from foreign sources received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Continuing unearned daily income - foreign income' and used the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that movements in the amount can be currency effects.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
variable_description: Income from a person's financial investments, given by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous unearned income from Managed Investments, Securites or Savings received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext), which is what the abbreviation in the column name stands for. It is the column that carries the return on savings and market investments for people on payments, and for most recipients that return is set by the deeming rules rather than by what the investment actually paid. The other five recurring sources on the row are compensation, foreign income, superannuation, other government payments and a residual bucket.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate covering three sources in one figure, variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: The three sources are not separable: a term deposit, a managed fund and a share parcel produce one number, so the column cannot support any statement about what people invest in. It also holds income, not the value of the assets, which are assessed separately and are not in this table, and it does not say whether the figure was deemed or actual.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry expands the column's abbreviation in its definition inside inc_une_cont_ext, the distribution it documents as the longitudinal history of continuous unearned income.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of continuous unearned income from Managed Investments, Securites or Savings received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Continuing unearned daily income - min/siv/sav income', which does not expand the abbreviation, and gave the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, leaving a reader unable to tell what the three letters meant.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
variable_description: Money from another government payment counted as income against this person's Centrelink payment, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous income from other government payments received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). Veterans' payments and some state or foreign government support are assessable this way, so a person can hold a Centrelink payment at a reduced rate because of an entitlement paid by someone else. BEN_TYPE on the same row says which Centrelink payment the income was assessed against.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate over the row's period, variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: It records income counted against this person's payment, not the other payment itself, so it is not a source of truth about what any other agency paid. DOMINO holds Department of Veterans' Affairs amounts in its own income table as well, so adding this column to those figures will double count the same money.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_une_cont_ext, the distribution documented as the longitudinal history of Centrelink reported unearned income from continuous sources.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of continuous income from other government payments received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Continuing unearned daily income - other government payment income' and repeated the generic sentence, so it did not flag the double-counting risk against the DVA income table.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
variable_description: The residual column for recurring unearned income, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous unearned income from other sources received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). It takes whatever regular non-work income did not fit the five named sources on the row, which are compensation, foreign income, managed investments and savings, superannuation and other government payments. A value here is the assessed daily rate for that leftover income over the row's period.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate over the row's period, variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: Being a residual, the column has no subject matter of its own: a large amount says only that it was not one of the five named types, so it cannot be interpreted as rent, royalties, maintenance or anything else. Its composition can also change as coding practice changes, which makes it unsafe to compare across years without checking the named columns beside it.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_une_cont_ext and lists the five named sources it is residual to on the same page.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of continuous unearned income from other sources received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Continuing unearned daily income - other income' and gave the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that a residual category cannot be given a substantive reading.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
variable_description: Superannuation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous income from superannuation received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). It matters most for people of pension age drawing an income stream while holding a part rate of Age Pension, and it is one of six recurring unearned income sources held side by side for the same period. The row says what was assessed, so the column answers how much of a person's superannuation the means test counted, not what their fund holds.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate over the row's period, variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: The assessed amount is not the amount the fund paid. An account-based pension is generally assessed under the deeming rules on the account balance rather than on the drawdown, so a person taking more than the deemed return shows less here than they received, and someone in accumulation phase with a large balance can show nothing at all.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_une_cont_ext, the distribution documented as the longitudinal history of continuous unearned income reported to Centrelink.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of continuous income from superannuation received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Continuing unearned daily income - superannuation income' and gave the generic sentence in both fields, so it did not distinguish assessed income from money actually drawn from a fund.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income, Total Australian currency
variable_description: Unearned income that changes from one reporting period to the next, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of variable unearned income received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income). The inc_une_var table is the counterpart to inc_une_cont: the continuing table splits steady income into six named sources, while this one carries the fluctuating amount as a single figure, with BEN_TYPE naming the payment it was assessed against and TASK_CODE saying what prompted the record. It answers how much irregular non-work income was counted against a payment over a period.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income, Total Australian currency
value_definition: A daily dollar rate in Australian currency, held to two decimal places in a format of up to nine digits before the point, and variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: The amount is not split by source, so unlike the continuing table it cannot tell you where the income came from. Expressing a fluctuating amount as a daily rate also flattens it: a single receipt inside the period and a steady trickle across it produce the same number.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes the data element behind this column with its definition, its Australian currency units and its decimal format, and lists the DOMINO distributions that carry it, including inc_une_var_ext.
evidence_quote: Daily rate of variable unearned income received by a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Variable unearned daily income' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not explain how the variable table differs from the continuing one.

value_domain: Hours per week
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: The weekly hours an assessor judged a person could work if support were provided, defined by DSS as "The number of current capacity in hours with intervention a recipient is able to work in a week" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). Its pair is CURR_CAPCTY_NUM, the hours the person can work as things stand, and the gap between the two is the question disability and participation decisions turn on: whether help would lift someone over the hours threshold that separates a disability payment from an activity-tested one. The medical condition codes and impairment rating on the same row are the clinical basis the assessment worked from.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A whole number of hours in a week, recorded against the assessment that made the judgement.
limitation: It is a projection, not a record: no intervention need have been offered, taken up or delivered, and DOMINO holds no employment services history to check against. Treating the value as hours the person went on to work would be wrong, and comparing assessments over time measures changes in assessment practice as much as changes in people.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside mcd_dtls_ext, which it documents as the longitudinal history of Centrelink medical conditions and work capacity assessments, alongside the current-capacity column it is read against.
evidence_quote: The number of current capacity in hours with intervention a recipient is able to work in a week.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'With intervention number', which does not even say the unit, and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation.

value_domain: Calendar year (YYYY)
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Client: Date of birth, Year
variable_description: The year a person was born, which DSS defines simply as "The client's year of birth" and derives as the year part of the recorded date of birth (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Client: Date of birth, Year). The static_demogs table holds one row per person for characteristics that do not change, and DOMINO splits the date of birth into this column and MONTH_OF_BIRTH rather than releasing a full date, which is a disclosure control. AGE on the same row is the person's age at the extract date, so the birth year is what lets an age be worked out at any other point in a person's payment history.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Client: Date of birth, Year
value_definition: A four-digit year in YYYY form, taken from the year component of the date of birth held by Centrelink.
limitation: Without a day of birth an exact age cannot be computed: an age derived from the year alone is out by up to a year, which matters at every age-based threshold in the payment system, from the youth rate boundaries to Age Pension age. Pairing the column with MONTH_OF_BIRTH narrows the error to a month but never removes it.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes the data element behind this column, with its definition, its YYYY format and the derivation from the date of birth, and lists the static demographics distribution that carries it.
evidence_quote: The client's year of birth.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Birth year' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that no day of birth is released or what that costs anyone computing an age.
