Several distinguish setting rather than substance: CA, HS and HB are the community, private hospital and public hospital forms of highly specialised drugs, and IN and IP the private and public hospital forms of chemotherapy. SY and SZ are retired special authority codes, replaced by TY and TZ, and should appear only in historical data, mostly for periods before the Herceptin programme began on 1 October 2006.
limitation: It does not classify a drug pharmacologically, so two prescriptions for the same molecule take different codes depending on the pathway that supplied them. Counting by this code measures how medicines reached patients, and a shift between HB and HS reflects a change in hospital arrangements rather than in prescribing; use ITM_CD when the product is what matters.
rationale: METeOR's PBS DSS maps this element to "Variable name = DRG_TYP_CD", its short name is "Type of drug prescribed (broad category)" against the PLIDA description "Type of drug supplied - broad category code", and it publishes a closed 21-code XX domain.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: CA Highly Specialised Drugs (community access items) CT Chemotherapy support drugs
supersedes_rationale: The generator currently fills DRG_TYP_CD from the `benefit_type` column of inst/extdata/pbs_item_lookup.csv, which is the PBS Schedule's benefit_type_code (A/R/S/U = authority required / restricted / streamlined / unrestricted). That is the restriction level of a listing, a different concept from the claim's broad drug category. The four generated values are not members of this domain.

value_domain: date
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602774, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—record extract date, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)
variable_description: The day Services Australia cut the claim file this row came out of, which is a fact about the data rather than about the patient. METeOR defines it as "the date for which the Department of Human Services (DHS) creates the file of Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) claim details for provision to the Department of Health", and notes that it "reflects a cut-off date for data records that are to be extracted from a computer system, e.g. all records processed or finalised on or before a particular date". Because PLIDA holds PBS as one table per month, this column is what put a row in its file. Use SPPLY_DT for when the medicine changed hands and PRSCRB_DT for when the script was written.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602774, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—record extract date, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A date, published by METeOR in DDMMYYYY form with a maximum of eight characters. Values bunch on the extract cut-off days rather than spreading through the month, because a single date covers every record in a file.
limitation: The distance between this date and the supply date is a claiming and processing lag, and METeOR warns that the lag varies from prescription to prescription, so it carries no clinical meaning. A row's presence in the table named for a month is therefore not evidence that the medicine was supplied in that month, and counting rows by this date will push late claims into the wrong period.
rationale: METeOR publishes this exact field and the PBS state/territory data extract specification records 'Variable name = EXTRCT_DT' against data element 602774, so the definition and the lag warning are the custodian's own words about this column.
evidence_quote: The date for which the Department of Human Services (DHS) creates the file of Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) claim details for provision to the Department of Health, expressed as DDMMYYYY.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Date of processing' and nothing more, and its limitation described the ddmmmYY output format instead of naming the confusion between a processing date and a date of care.

value_domain: pbs_item_code
value_source: Australian Government Department of Health and Aged Care, Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits
variable_description: The PBS item code for the medicine supplied, which fixes the drug, its form and strength, the maximum quantity and the repeats allowed. AIHW METEOR defines the code set as "The code set representing the medicinal and therapeutic products included in the Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits", and notes that the same structure covers the Repatriation schedule. It is the join key to the published PBS Schedule, which is where ATC classification, brand and price for the item are found.
description_source: AIHW METEOR value domain 600257, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item code NN[NNN]A, and data element 600778, PBS item prescribed
value_definition: Four or five digits followed by an alphabetic check character, format NN[NNN]A. The fifth digit was added in 2013, with new codes issued in that longer form from 1 December 2013, and the codes recorded here are a sample of real listings rather than the whole schedule.
limitation: An item code is a listing, not a medicine. Changing the maximum quantity, the repeats or the restriction on a listed product creates a new item code for the same molecule, and codes are also retired when a listing ends, so a time series on one code tracks an administrative listing. Codes are sometimes padded with leading zeros, so joins to the schedule need the padding handled.
rationale: The bundled inst/extdata/pbs_item_lookup.csv already serves as the domain: 4,274 real General Schedule item codes taken from the PBS public data API, and every code matches METeOR's published format NN[NNN]A with a final alphabetic check digit.
evidence_quote: Classification scheme: Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits ... Format: NN[NNN]A
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass called this inferred. It is not: the generator samples from a real published item list. The one caveat worth recording is vintage - the lookup is a single current-schedule snapshot (program_code GE, non-effective items dropped), so items delisted before 2026 never appear even in 2006-2015 tables, and the five-digit codes introduced from December 2013 appear in earlier years where they did not yet exist.

value_domain: pbs_prescriber_specialty_group
value_source: AIHW METeOR 600681, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—specialty of prescriber, group code NN (Department of Health)
variable_description: The broad specialty group of the health professional who wrote the prescription. AIHW METEOR defines it as "The broad field of specialty of the authorised health professional responsible for the writing and signing of a prescription for a medicinal product included in the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS), as represented by a code", and notes that more detailed major-field and subspecialty versions of the domain also exist. PRSCRBR_TYP_CD beside it records the profession authorised to prescribe rather than the field of practice.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 600681, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—specialty of prescriber, group code NN
value_definition: A two-digit code with four values: 01 general practitioner, 02 specialist, 03 allied health professional and 04 dental practitioner.
limitation: Despite the variable name, the codes stored are at the group level, so every medical specialist collapses into 02 and a cardiologist cannot be told from a psychiatrist. The value also describes the prescriber of record on the form, so a hospital discharge script written by a junior doctor is attributed to whatever group that prescriber falls in, not to the treating team.
rationale: METeOR 600681 is the only PBS specialty element that carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD", and its four groups map cleanly onto the generator's existing GP/SP/OT split; confidence is medium because METeOR also publishes a 66-code four-digit element, 607130 "Major specialty of prescriber" (https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/607130), whose short name is the PLIDA description word for word, so an implementer should decide between NN and NNNN before relabelling.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: 01 General practitioner (GP) 02 Specialist 03 Allied health professional 04 Dental practitioner
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass recorded "public code table not found". Note METeOR states 607130 "is not part of the 2013-14 data extract provided to the states and territories", which is why I take the two-digit group as the field's domain despite the description matching the four-digit element's title.

value_domain: count of packs or units of use
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 601876, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—quantity of PBS item supplied, total number N[NNN]' (Department of Health)
variable_description: How much of the item the pharmacist handed over on this supply, counted in packs or in units of use. METeOR defines the field as "the total amount of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item dispensed by a pharmacist, expressed either as a number of packs or units of use", and the adjustment in the name is the rule that follows it: "Where supply of the original prescription and any repeat(s) is made at the one time, pursuant to Regulation 24 of the National Health (Pharmaceutical Benefits) Regulations 1960 (Cwth), the value reported must be the total quantity supplied." A row with RGLTN24_IND set to Y therefore carries the combined quantity for the original and every repeat. What one unit means is set by the item, so ITM_CD has to be read alongside it.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 601876, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—quantity of PBS item supplied, total number N[NNN]' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A non-negative whole number in METeOR's format N[NNN], four characters at most, with 9999 reserved for not stated or inadequately described. Whether the count is packs or units follows the item: an unbreakable pack is one pack, a breakable pack is counted in the units taken from it, and a cream or a liquid is counted in tubes or bottles rather than by volume.
limitation: It is not a dose, a volume or a days-of-supply figure, so a value of 1 can be a single tube of ointment or a pack of 30 tablets, and two rows with the same quantity can differ many-fold in the amount of drug supplied. Converting it to defined daily doses needs the pack size and strength from the Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits, which this table does not carry.
rationale: The PBS state/territory data extract specification records 'Variable name = PBS_RGLTN24_ADJST_QTY' against METeOR data element 601876, which is the only published source that both defines the quantity and states the Regulation 24 adjustment the variable name refers to.
evidence_quote: Where supply of the original prescription and any repeat(s) is made at the one time, pursuant to Regulation 24 of the National Health (Pharmaceutical Benefits) Regulations 1960 (Cwth), the value reported must be the total quantity supplied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Quantity supplied' and a generic count limitation about the trailing token naming the unit, which is exactly wrong here: the unit is set by the item, and the RGLTN24 token in the name is about bundling, not about units.

value_domain: pbs_pharmacy_approval_type
value_source: AIHW METeOR 601577, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—pharmacy approval type, code X (Department of Health)
variable_description: The kind of approval the dispensing pharmacy holds, separating community pharmacies from hospitals and dispensing doctors. AIHW METEOR defines it as "The approval type of the pharmacy at which the prescription medicinal product is dispensed, as represented by a code", and ties each code to a section of the National Health Act 1953. It is the field that tells you which supply channel a prescription came through, and it qualifies PHRMCY_PSTCD and PHRMCY_ID_SCRAM on the same row.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 601577, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—pharmacy approval type, code X
value_definition: A single character with six values: 0 an approved community pharmacy under section 90, F the same flagged as a friendly society, D a dispensing doctor approved under section 92, Y a public hospital participating in Pharmaceutical Reform Arrangements, B a non-participating public hospital approved only for highly specialised drugs, and H a private hospital approved under section 94.
limitation: It describes an approval, not the setting a patient was in. Public hospital supply is only visible where the state or territory participates in Pharmaceutical Reform Arrangements, so hospital dispensing is unevenly covered across jurisdictions, and a state comparison built on this column measures which reform arrangements are in place rather than how hospitals treat patients.
rationale: The METeOR page carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = PHRMCY_APPRVL_TYP_CD", and its guide for use ties code 0 to section 90, code D to section 92 and code H to section 94 of the National Health Act 1953, which is the statutory structure the assignment expected.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: Y Participating public hospital B Non-participating public hospital 0 Approved community pharmacy
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass recorded "public code table not found". The generator's A/F pair (A for a plain approved pharmacy, F for friendly society) has the friendly-society code right but the ordinary community-pharmacy code wrong: the published code is the digit 0, not A, and there is no A in the domain.

value_domain: open_identifier_domain
value_source: AIHW METeOR 600674, Pharmacy—pharmacy identifier, identifier XXNNNA (Department of Health)
variable_description: A scrambled key for the pharmacy or approved supplier that dispensed the prescription, used to group supply to one site. The field it replaces is defined by AIHW METEOR as "A sequence of alphanumeric, numeric and alphabetic characters which uniquely identify a pharmacy", a six-character identifier whose first character marks hospital pharmacies and dispensing doctors and whose second gives the state for hospitals. Scrambling removes that structure, so PHRMCY_APPRVL_TYP_CD and PHRMCY_PSTCD carry what is left of it.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 600674, Pharmacy—pharmacy identifier, identifier XXNNNA, which is the unscrambled field this column is derived from
value_definition: An opaque key with no readable internal structure, consistent within the collection so that rows sharing a value were dispensed by the same approved supplier.
limitation: The pharmacy type and the state encoded in the real identifier cannot be recovered from it, and it joins to no pharmacy register, so nothing about ownership, banner group, opening hours or accreditation is available. It also identifies an approval attached to premises, so a single business operating several approved outlets appears as several unrelated keys.
rationale: Open identifier domain, no code list. METeOR documents the underlying field as the pharmacy approval number in format XXNNNA, but PLIDA supplies it scrambled, so the published format does not survive and there is nothing to enumerate; leave the generator's PHAR-prefixed opaque strings alone.
evidence_quote: A sequence of alphanumeric, numeric and alphabetic characters which uniquely identify a pharmacy

value_domain: Australian postcode
value_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the pharmacy location and remoteness items
variable_description: The postal area of the approved pharmacy that dispensed this supply and claimed for it. The PBS specification says of the matching pharmacy items that "In the context of PBS data, this data element describes the location (physical address) of the dispensing pharmacy", and that the pharmacy's published remoteness category "is based on the postcode of the pharmacy at which the prescription was dispensed", which is the postcode held here. Read against PTNT_PSTCD it shows whether a person filled the script near home, and against PRSCRBR_MJR_PSTCD whether they filled it near the prescriber. PHRMCY_ID_SCRAM says which pharmacy; this column says where it is.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the pharmacy location and remoteness items
value_definition: A four-digit Australian postcode. METeOR's general Australian postcode domain (data element 611398) takes its values from the Postcode datafile and reserves 0097, 0098 and 0099 for not applicable, unknown and not stated, though the PBS specification does not say which of those the extract uses.
limitation: A postcode is a postal delivery area, so it does not nest inside the ABS statistical areas and any conversion to SA2 or to remoteness runs through a correspondence that carries error. The value also belongs to the claiming approved supplier, which for a hospital pharmacy or a mail-order dispensary can sit a long way from where the patient collected the medicine, so the distance between this postcode and the patient's is a weak proxy for how far anyone travelled.
rationale: The PBS data set specification carries the department's own notes on what the pharmacy location items mean in PBS data and states that the pharmacy remoteness classification is derived from the dispensing pharmacy's postcode, which fixes what this column holds and whose address it is.
evidence_quote: In the context of PBS data, this data element describes the geographic remoteness of the dispensing pharmacy, and is based on the postcode of the pharmacy at which the prescription was dispensed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Pharmacy postcode' twice over and gave a generic postcode limitation about four digits from 0800 to 7999, which describes the format rather than the confusion between a supplier's location and a patient's.

value_domain: date
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602772, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of prescribing, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)
variable_description: The day the prescriber signed the script that this supply was made against. METeOR defines it as "the date on which the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescriber signs the prescription, expressed as DDMMYYYY", and notes it is "Not required for continued dispensing". Subtracting it from SPPLY_DT gives the delay between a medicine being written and being collected, which is the main use of the column. On a repeat supply the date still belongs to the original script, so one prescribing date recurs across all the rows that share a prescription.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602772, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of prescribing, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A date, published by METeOR in DDMMYYYY form with a maximum of eight characters. It falls on or before the supply date, and can fall well before it where a patient collected a repeat months later.
limitation: It is not the date of a consultation and is not evidence the patient saw the prescriber that day, since PBS holds no consultation record and a script can be written without a face-to-face visit; MBS is where an attendance would appear. Because METeOR exempts continued dispensing supplies from reporting it, a missing value can mark a pharmacist supply made without a prescription rather than a data fault.
rationale: METeOR publishes this exact concept for PBS and the PBS state/territory data extract specification implements it as the prescribing date on the same record as the supply date, so the definition and the continued-dispensing exemption apply to this column.
evidence_quote: The date on which the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescriber signs the prescription, expressed as DDMMYYYY.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Date of prescribing' and gave a limitation about the ddmmmYY output form, which told a reader nothing about how the date relates to the supply date or why it can be missing.

value_domain: open_identifier_domain
value_source: AIHW METeOR 600762, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber identifier, identifier N[N(19)] (Department of Health)
variable_description: A scrambled key for the prescriber who wrote the prescription, used to group prescribing to one practitioner. AIHW METEOR defines the field it replaces as "A unique numeric identifier for the prescriber of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item for which the PBS benefit is being claimed", and notes that the real identifier may need suppression because it identifies individual prescribers. MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD and PRSCRBR_TYP_CD are the only attributes of the prescriber that survive alongside it.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 600762, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber identifier, identifier N[N(19)], which is the unscrambled field this column is derived from
value_definition: An opaque key replacing a numeric prescriber number, consistent within the collection so that rows sharing a value were written by the same prescriber.
limitation: It is not the Medicare provider key, so a doctor's prescribing cannot be joined to their MBS billing in SCRAM_SPR, and a practitioner who holds more than one prescriber number appears as more than one key. Hospital prescriptions are frequently written under a departmental or registrar number, so a high-volume key can be a ward rather than a person.
rationale: Open identifier domain, no code list. METeOR documents the underlying prescriber number as numeric of up to 20 digits, but PLIDA supplies it scrambled, so the published format does not apply; leave the generator's PRES-prefixed opaque strings alone.
evidence_quote: A unique numeric identifier for the prescriber of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item

value_domain: Australian postcode
value_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the prescriber location and remoteness items
variable_description: Where the prescriber did most of their Medicare work, not where this prescription was written. The PBS specification is explicit that the prescriber's location "is based on the postcode of the location at which the prescriber performed the majority of Medicare services for the most recent relevant quarter", which is what the MJR token in the name records. It is therefore a property of the doctor over a quarter rather than of the prescribing event on the row. PRSCRBR_ID_SCRAM says which prescriber wrote the script, and PRSCRBR_TYP_CD and MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD say what kind of practitioner they are.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the prescriber location and remoteness items
value_definition: A four-digit Australian postcode from the same domain as the patient and pharmacy postcodes on the row, with values drawn from the Postcode datafile behind METeOR data element 611398.
limitation: It cannot place a prescription geographically. A specialist who consults one day a week in a regional town but bills most of their services in a capital city carries the capital's postcode on every script they write, so counts of prescribing by area understate practice in small centres. The quarterly basis also means the value can shift between one patient's rows without the prescriber having moved.
rationale: The PBS data set specification states the derivation rule for the prescriber location items in PBS data, which is the only published account of what the majority qualifier in this variable name means and the reason the postcode is not the prescribing site.
evidence_quote: In the context of PBS data, this data element describes the location (physical address) of the prescriber, and is based on the postcode of the location at which the prescriber performed the majority of Medicare services for the most recent relevant quarter.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Prescriber postcode', which is actively misleading: it invites a reader to treat the value as the place the script was written, and nothing on the page explained the MJR token or the quarterly majority-of-services rule behind it.

value_domain: pbs_prescriber_type
values: ["M: Medical practitioner","D: Dental practitioner","B: Both","O: Optometrist","N: Nurse practitioner","W: Midwife"]
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603862, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber type, code A (Department of Health)
variable_description: The profession of the person who wrote the prescription: medical practitioner, dentist, optometrist, nurse practitioner or midwife. AIHW METEOR defines it as "The broad field of specialty of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescriber responsible for the writing and signing of the prescription, as represented by a code". The available codes are a history of prescribing rights, since optometrists were authorised from 1 January 2008 and nurse practitioners and midwives from 1 September 2010.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 603862, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber type, code A
value_definition: A single letter with six values: M medical practitioner, D dental practitioner, O optometrist, N nurse practitioner, W midwife, and B for prescribers qualified as both medical and dental practitioners, which appears only in records before 1 January 2008.
limitation: The absence of a code before its start date is a rule about authorisation, not evidence about practice, so no nurse practitioner rows exist before September 2010. Each authorised group is also restricted to a defined subset of PBS items, so the mix of codes reflects what each profession is permitted to prescribe and cannot be read as a measure of workforce substitution.
rationale: The METeOR page carries "DSS specific information: Variable name = PRSCRBR_TYP_CD" and publishes the closed single-character domain, including the historical code B for prescribers qualified as both medical and dental practitioners.
evidence_quote: M Medical practitioner D Dental practitioner B Both O Optometrist N Nurse practitioner W Midwife
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass recorded "public code table not found". The generator's M/N pair is a correct subset of this domain but omits D, B, O and W. Code B should only appear before 2008, O only from 1 January 2008, and N and W only from 1 September 2010, per the METeOR guide for use - useful if the generator is made period-aware.

value_domain: count of supplies
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 605072, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised medication supplies, total number N[N]' (Department of Health)
variable_description: How many separate supplies this one prescription authorised, which is 1 on almost every row. METeOR defines it as "the total number of times that the prescribed medicinal product is supplied to the patient or PBS consumer", and sets the rule that a repeat prescription takes "a value of 1 for those prescriptions where Regulation 24 applicable indicator has a negative response, or a value equivalent to 1 plus the number of repeats specified by the prescriber" where that indicator is positive. It rises above 1 only on the Regulation 24 rows, where the original and all its repeats went out together. Counting rows counts supply events; summing this column counts the supplies bundled inside them.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 605072, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised medication supplies, total number N[N]' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A whole number in METeOR's format N[N], two characters at most, with 99 reserved for not stated or inadequately described. Ordinary rows carry 1, and a Regulation 24 row carries 1 plus the repeats the prescriber allowed, so a script with five repeats supplied at once carries 6.
limitation: It is not a count of prescriptions written and not a count of packs, so summing it over a patient's year gives supply occasions rather than scripts or medicines held. It also says nothing about whether the medicine was taken, and on a Regulation 24 row a whole course is dated to one day, which will distort any adherence measure built from the spacing of supplies.
rationale: The PBS state/territory data extract specification records 'Variable name = PRSCRPTN_CNT' against METeOR data element 605072, whose guide for use gives the exact rule tying the value to the Regulation 24 indicator that sits on the same row.
evidence_quote: For a given Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription, the total number of times that the prescribed medicinal product is supplied to the patient or PBS consumer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Number of authorised medication supplies' and gave a generic count limitation claiming the trailing token names the unit counted, which left a reader free to read the column as a count of prescriptions.

value_domain: count_with_not_stated
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603916, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of times previously supplied, total number N[N] (Department of Health)
variable_description: How many times this medicine had already been supplied against this prescription, counting the original supply. AIHW METEOR defines it as "For a given prescription, the total number of times that the prescribed medicinal product has previously been supplied to the patient or Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) consumer, including the original supply". A single-supply prescription records 1, and a repeat prescription counts up as each repeat is dispensed, so this column tells you where in a prescription's life the row sits, while RPT_ORDR_NMBR says how many repeats were allowed.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 603916, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of times previously supplied, total number N[N]
value_definition: One or two digits, format N[N]: 1 on an original supply, rising with each subsequent supply up to 98, and 99 reserved for not stated or inadequately described.
limitation: The count belongs to one prescription form, not to a course of treatment. A fresh prescription resets it to 1, so it cannot measure how long someone has been taking a medicine or whether they persisted with it. The 99 code is missing data rather than a large count, and averaging the column without excluding it will pull any mean sharply upwards.
rationale: Open count, but METeOR publishes the representation for this exact variable name: format N[N], counted inclusive of the original supply, with 99 reserved for not stated.
evidence_quote: For a 'single supply' prescription, this data item should have a value of 1
supersedes_rationale: The existing "not specified" treatment is defensible, but the generator's floor of 0 conflicts with the published guide for use, which says the count includes the original supply and so should be at least 1. Shifting the generated range from 0-6 to 1-7 would match the source at no cost.

value_domain: month of year, 1 to 12
value_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item
variable_description: The calendar month of the patient's birth, held without a day so no row can be dated to a birthday. The PBS specification says the underlying field is the patient's date of birth and that "'Patient date of birth' is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)", which PLIDA splits into this column and PTNT_BRTH_YR. Taken with the year it fixes age at supply to within a month, which is what age-group analyses of dispensing rest on. It describes the person the medicine was supplied to, not the prescriber and not whoever paid.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item
value_definition: A month number from 1 to 12, carrying the month component of METeOR's date of birth element (287007), whose full domain is DDMMYYYY. The day component is not supplied in this asset.
limitation: On its own it gives no age, cannot order two people's births inside a month, and cannot be joined to a full date of birth held in another dataset. It also inherits whatever the Medicare enrolment holds, so a birth date estimated at enrolment leaves a month that is administrative rather than real, and there is no accuracy flag on the row to show which values those are.
rationale: The PBS data set specification names the source of the patient's birth date and its custodian, which is what determines the quality of the month PLIDA derives from it; METeOR's element 287007 fixes the underlying DDMMYYYY representation that this column is a component of.
evidence_quote: 'Patient date of birth' is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Month of birth' and its limitation only warned that the domain was inferred and that the field holds a month component, which repeated the value definition instead of naming what a month without a day cannot do.

value_domain: calendar year
value_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item
variable_description: The calendar year of the patient's birth, the coarser half of the birth date PLIDA keeps for PBS. The PBS specification says of the underlying field that it "can be used to identify individual patients and may, in some use cases, need to be suppressed or perturbed", which is why only a year and a month survive here, and that it "is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)". Subtracting it from the year of SPPLY_DT gives age at supply to within a year, and PTNT_BRTH_MTH tightens that to a month. It is the patient's year of birth, not the year they came onto Medicare.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year, the year component of METeOR's DDMMYYYY date of birth element (287007). Values run from the birth year of the oldest enrolled Medicare patient up to the year of the extract.
limitation: It cannot settle whether a patient had passed an age threshold on the day of supply, which matters for concession rules and for paediatric dosing, because the day of birth is gone. A year here also cannot be assumed to agree with the year of birth in Census, birth or death records: each comes from a separate enrolment or form, and the spine links people rather than reconciling the dates they reported.
rationale: The PBS data set specification identifies the Medicare record as the source of the patient's date of birth and flags it as an identifying item, which explains both where the year comes from and why PLIDA supplies only a year and a month.
evidence_quote: This data element can be used to identify individual patients and may, in some use cases, need to be suppressed or perturbed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Year of birth' and its limitation restated that the field holds a year component, so the page never said where the birth date came from or what a missing day rules out.

value_domain: Australian currency amount, dollars and cents
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 603362, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—PBS patient contribution, total Australian currency N[NNNNN].NN' (Department of Health)
variable_description: What the patient paid the pharmacy for this supply, on the PBS's narrow definition of a co-payment. METeOR defines it as "the total amount paid by the patient or PBS consumer to the approved pharmacy for a prescription, exclusive of any special patient contributions, e.g. brand price premiums or therapeutic group premiums", and adds that the amount "also excludes any optional fees imposed at the discretion of the pharmacy and payable by the patient". The value moves with the patient's entitlement rather than with the medicine, so it is set by PTNT_CTGRY_DRVD_CD and by whether the Safety Net threshold had been reached that calendar year. With BNFT_AMT it splits the dispensed price between the patient and the Commonwealth.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 603362, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—PBS patient contribution, total Australian currency N[NNNNN].NN' (Department of Health)
value_definition: Australian currency to two decimal places, in METeOR's format N[NNNNN].NN. The value tracks the co-payment published in the Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits, which METeOR says is adjusted each 1 January in line with the CPI, although statute has since frozen the concessional rate at $7.70 for 2025 to 2029: METeOR gives $36.90 for a general patient and $6.00 for a concessional patient in 2014, and the schedule's fee table gave $25.00 and $7.70 as at 1 July 2026.
limitation: It is not the money that left the patient's pocket. Brand price premiums, therapeutic group premiums and any discretionary pharmacy fee are excluded by definition, so a patient who chose a premium brand paid more than this column shows. It is also not a basis for a consistent affordability series over the whole 2006 to 2025 span, because supplies priced below the general co-payment were not collected at all until April 2012.
rationale: The PBS state/territory data extract specification records 'Variable name = PTNT_CNTRBTN_AMT' against METeOR data element 603362, whose definition states precisely which charges the amount includes and excludes and whose guide for use gives the entitlement and Safety Net rules that move it.
evidence_quote: This amount also excludes any optional fees imposed at the discretion of the pharmacy and payable by the patient, e.g. fees associated with the maintenance of Safety Net records on behalf of the patient by the pharmacy.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Patient contribution amount', declared whole dollars when the field carries cents, and gave a generic limitation about losses and offsets being negative, which does not apply and hid the real trap that premiums are excluded.

value_domain: pbs_patient_entitlement_status_derived
value_source: AIHW METeOR 604103, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—patient entitlement status (derived), Commonwealth government assistance scheme code AX (Department of Health)
variable_description: The patient's PBS entitlement at the moment of supply: general or concessional, and whether the Safety Net had been reached. AIHW METEOR defines it as "The derived entitlement status of the patient at the time the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item is supplied, as represented by a code", derived by combining payment category with patient payment category. It determines what appears in PTNT_CNTRBTN_AMT and BNFT_AMT on the same row, so it is the field that explains why two supplies of the same item cost different amounts.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 604103, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—patient entitlement status (derived), Commonwealth government assistance scheme code AX
value_definition: Two characters, format AX. G, C and R give the general, concessional and Department of Veterans' Affairs repatriation schemes, and the digit marks Safety Net status; DB covers prescriber bag orders, OC stoma products and OP paraplegic or quadriplegic products.
limitation: Concessional status here belongs to the supply, not to the person. Someone who gains or loses a concession card changes code part-way through a year, and Safety Net status resets every calendar year and returns as the year's prescriptions accumulate, so the column measures entitlement on the day and cannot stand in for a stable indicator of low income.
rationale: METeOR's PBS state/territory data extract DSS maps this exact element to "Variable name = PTNT_CTGRY_DRVD_CD", its synonymous names include "Patient entitlement status (derived)" which is the PLIDA description verbatim, and it publishes a closed 2-character domain.
evidence_quote: Permissible values: G1 General Safety Net prescription G2 General non-Safety Net prescription
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass searched pbs.gov.au and the PBS API dictionary and concluded no code table existed; it did not check METeOR, where the Department of Health registered this element under the exact PLIDA variable name. The generator's current C/G is the right idea at the wrong granularity - it loses the Safety Net split and the DVA/prescriber-bag/stoma/paraplegic categories.

value_domain: Australian postcode
value_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient state item
variable_description: The postal area of the patient's home as Medicare last recorded it, which is not necessarily where they lived when the medicine was supplied. The PBS specification says the derived patient state "is derived from 'Patient postcode', i.e. it is derived from the Medicare record of the patient and is based on the most recent patient address reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)", and this column is that postcode. It is the geography every patient-side analysis of PBS rests on, including the remoteness categories the department publishes. Set against PHRMCY_PSTCD it shows whether the script was filled near home.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient state item
value_definition: A four-digit Australian postcode. METeOR's general Australian postcode domain (data element 611398) sources values from the Postcode datafile and reserves 0097, 0098 and 0099 for not applicable, unknown and not stated.
limitation: Medicare holds one current address rather than an address history, so an old value can be stamped on a recent supply and a move stays invisible until the person tells Services Australia. The postcode also belongs to an enrolment rather than to a residence: a child on a parent's record carries the parent's postcode, and someone living away for study or care may carry a family address. For an actual residential history the address episodes in Core Locations, keyed by ARID, are the source.
rationale: The PBS data set specification states that the patient geography items are derived from the patient postcode held on the Medicare record and describes it as the most recent address reported to the custodian, which fixes both what the column holds and why it can be stale.
evidence_quote: This data item is referred to within the PBS system as 'Patient state', and is derived from 'Patient postcode', i.e. it is derived from the Medicare record of the patient and is based on the most recent patient address reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Patient postcode' twice and warned only that the domain was inferred and ran from 0800 to 7999, so nothing on the page said the address came from the Medicare enrolment or that it need not be current at the time of supply.

value_domain: sex code
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602450, 'Person—sex, code A' (Department of Health), with the PBS specific note recorded against it
variable_description: The patient's sex as the Medicare entitlement record held it at the moment the claim was archived. METeOR's PBS note is explicit that "this data item is defined as being 'the gender of the consumer as held in the entitlement tables at the time the PBS claim was archived'", and warns that "gender is a social/cultural concept rather than a biological (anatomical or chromosomal) concept, although for most people the two concepts are the same". It belongs to the patient the medicine was supplied to, not to the prescriber or the cardholder. With PTNT_BRTH_YR it gives the two demographic splits available on a PBS row without leaving the table.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602450, 'Person—sex, code A' (Department of Health), with the PBS specific note recorded against it
value_definition: A one-character alphabetic code from METeOR's Sex code A domain, covering male, female, and intersex or indeterminate, with separate supplementary codes for not stated or inadequately described and for unknown, and a blank also read as unknown.
limitation: It is a point-in-time administrative value, so a person whose Medicare record changed will carry different codes on rows before and after the change and a person-level mode will quietly erase that. It is also not comparable with the sex and gender items in Census, surveys or birth records, which are self-reported against different questions, so a disagreement between PBS and Census is not by itself evidence of a bad link.
rationale: METeOR carries both the value domain for the code and the department's own PBS specific note stating what the item means in PBS data and where it is drawn from, and the PBS state/territory data extract specification implements it as the patient sex item on the prescription record.
evidence_quote: In the context of PBS data, this data item is defined as being 'the gender of the consumer as held in the entitlement tables at the time the PBS claim was archived'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Patient sex' with a domain of 'Sex (inferred)' and a limitation that only repeated the inference warning, so the page never said the value is an entitlement-table attribute captured at claim archive.

value_domain: yes/no code
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 601746, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—Regulation 24 applicable indicator, yes/no code A' (Department of Health)
variable_description: Whether the pharmacist was allowed to hand over the original script and all its repeats at once. METeOR defines it as "an indicator of whether supply of the original Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item and all repeats is made at the one time", under a regulation that "allows a pharmacist to supply an original prescription medication and all of its repeats at the one time", and restricts such prescriptions to medical practitioners, midwives and nurse practitioners. Where it is positive, PRSCRPTN_CNT and PBS_RGLTN24_ADJST_QTY on the same row cover the whole bundle instead of a single supply, so this is the switch that decides how those two columns should be read.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 601746, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—Regulation 24 applicable indicator, yes/no code A' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A one-character code with only two permissible values, one for yes and one for no, and no supplementary values published. A positive value means the prescription allowed concurrent supply of the original and every repeat; a negative one means the prescriber did not specify that.
limitation: A positive value does not mean the patient consumed the medicine over the following months, only that the pharmacy released it in one go, so treating the supply date as the start of a single short course will misdate months of treatment. It is also a poor marker of remoteness or chronic illness: those are eligibility conditions the prescriber attests to rather than facts recorded on the row, and optometrist and dental prescriptions are outside the provision altogether.
rationale: The PBS state/territory data extract specification records 'Variable name = RGLTN24_IND' against METeOR data element 601746, which publishes the definition, the two-value domain and the eligibility conditions behind a positive response.
evidence_quote: An indicator of whether supply of the original Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item and all repeats is made at the one time, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Regulation 24 applicable indicator' without saying what Regulation 24 is, and its limitation, that the field records whether a condition holds rather than its value, applied to any indicator and told a reader nothing about this one.

value_domain: count_with_not_stated
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603919, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised prescription repeats, total number N[N] (Department of Health)
variable_description: The number of repeat supplies the prescriber authorised on this prescription. AIHW METEOR warns that "the number of repeats specified in a given prescription is typically one less than the total number of times that the patient can be supplied with the prescribed medication", so five repeats permit six supplies in all. The value can differ from the repeats listed in the PBS Schedule for the item, because the prescriber decides how many to write, and PRVS_SPPLY_NMBR records how far through them a given row is.
description_source: AIHW METEOR data element 603919, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised prescription repeats, total number N[N]
value_definition: One or two digits, format N[N]: 0 for a single-supply prescription, 1 to 98 for the repeats authorised, and 99 for not stated or inadequately described.
limitation: It records what was authorised, not what the patient collected. A repeat that is never dispensed generates no row at all, so multiplying this column by the quantity per supply overstates the medicine that reached people; the dispensed rows themselves, counted through PRVS_SPPLY_NMBR, are the only evidence of uptake.
rationale: Open count, not a code list, but METeOR does publish the representation for this exact variable name: format N[N], 0 for single-supply prescriptions, and the supplementary value 99 for not stated.
evidence_quote: Supplementary values: 99 Not stated/inadequately described
supersedes_rationale: The existing "not specified" treatment is fine and the generator's 0-15 range sits inside the published format; the only additions are the two-digit width cap and the reserved 99.

value_domain: date
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602767, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of supply, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)
variable_description: The day the patient took delivery of the medicine from the pharmacy, and the date a medicine-use history should be built on. METeOR defines it as "the date on which the prescribed medicinal product is supplied by a pharmacist to the patient or PBS consumer", and explains that it "essentially equates to the date of purchase", usually but not always the same as the dispensing date printed on the label. Prefer it to PRSCRB_DT, which belongs to the script, and to EXTRCT_DT, which belongs to the claim file. Each row is one supply, so a patient's repeats appear as separate rows with separate supply dates unless Regulation 24 applied and they all went out together.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 602767, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of supply, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A date, published by METeOR in DDMMYYYY form with a maximum of eight characters. It falls on or after the prescribing date and on or before the extract date of the file the row sits in.
limitation: It marks the transfer of a medicine, not the start or the continuation of treatment, so it cannot show whether or when the patient took anything and a gap between supplies is only a proxy for stopping. METeOR also notes that supply and dispensing can fall on different days where a patient does not collect immediately, so the date will not always match a pharmacy's own dispensing record.
rationale: METeOR publishes this exact concept for PBS, the PBS state/territory data extract specification implements it on the prescription record, and its guide for use gives the distinction between supply, purchase and dispensing that governs how the column should be used.
evidence_quote: The date on which the prescribed medicinal product is supplied by a pharmacist to the patient or PBS consumer, expressed as DDMMYYYY.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Date of supply' and gave a limitation about the ddmmmYY output form, so the page never distinguished this date from the prescribing date or the extract date, which is the whole reason PBS carries three of them.

value_domain: repeat prescription code
value_source: AIHW METeOR data element 604005, 'Prescription—repeat prescription indicator, code X' (Department of Health)
variable_description: Whether this row is the first supply against a prescription or a later one. METeOR defines the element as "an indicator of whether a prescription is a repeat prescription or an original prescription, as represented by a code", and puts the initial supply of a script that allows repeats on the original side, not the repeat side. It is what lets a patient's rows be grouped into prescriptions instead of counted as separate treatment decisions. PRVS_SPPLY_NMBR says how many supplies came earlier in this one and RPT_ORDR_NMBR how many the prescriber authorised.
description_source: AIHW METeOR data element 604005, 'Prescription—repeat prescription indicator, code X' (Department of Health)
value_definition: A one-character code with two published meanings: a blank marks an original prescription, including the first supply of one that allows repeats, and a single letter marks a repeat supply. The blank is a meaningful value in METeOR's domain rather than a missing one.
limitation: It does not say how far through a prescription a supply sits, so a run of repeat rows cannot be ordered without the previous-supply number, and it cannot be used to count prescriptions where Regulation 24 applied, because the original and all its repeats arrive as a single row marked as an original. A blank also does not mean the medicine was new to the patient, only that a new script had started.
rationale: The PBS state/territory data extract specification records 'Variable name = SRT_RPT_IND' against METeOR data element 604005, whose guide for use states which supply counts as original and which as repeat, and that is the fact the column turns on.
evidence_quote: This code is used where the prescription is either for the one-off supply of a medicinal product, i.e. a single bottle, packet, dose etc. of the prescribed item, or for the initial supply of a medicinal product for a prescription that allows for repeat supplies.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Repeat prescription indicator' and gave the generic indicator limitation about recording whether a condition holds, which missed both the blank-as-original convention and the way Regulation 24 rows break a naive count of repeats.

value_domain: pbs_streamlined_authority_code
value_source: PBS Schedule, Streamlined Authority item listing (Department of Health and Aged Care), with the format stated in PBS Explanatory Notes section 1.2
variable_description: The streamlined authority code the prescriber wrote on the form to claim a restricted PBS item without seeking approval first. The PBS Explanatory Notes state that "prior approval is not required from Services Australia or DVA to prescribe an Authority required (STREAMLINED) item" and that "an authority prescription for an Authority required (STREAMLINED) item is not valid unless the code is included on the prescription form". Each code is published against the item's restriction in the Schedule, so it names the indication the prescriber attested to.
description_source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, PBS Explanatory Notes, Section 1.2, Prescribing Medicines — Information for PBS Prescribers
value_definition: A four or five digit number identifying one restriction, that is one indication and its clinical criteria, on one listed item. It is blank on items that carry no streamlined authority requirement, which is most of the schedule. The codes recorded here are a sample of published streamlined codes rather than the whole set.
limitation: The code names a restriction, not a diagnosis. The same clinical indication attracts different codes on different items and one code can cover several criteria, so codes do not aggregate into a disease count. Nothing is verified at the point of prescribing either, since the arrangement replaces prior approval with an attestation, so the code records a claim rather than a confirmed condition.
rationale: The PBS publishes a streamlined authority code against each restriction on each Authority required (STREAMLINED) item; I scraped the A-Z browse listing (23 pages, 4,468 item/brand rows) and found 1,031 distinct codes, all bare 4- or 5-digit numerics, which matches the Explanatory Notes' "four or five digit streamlined authority code".
evidence_quote: the authority prescription form must include a four or five digit streamlined authority code
supersedes_rationale: The generator currently writes S0001-S9999, an invented alphabetic-prefixed form, and only when the item lookup's benefit_type is S. The prefix is wrong: real codes are bare numerics such as 4512, 5942 and 14604. The 1,031 count is the current schedule only, so it is a floor, not the historical universe for 2006-2025; codes are also per-restriction, so one item can carry several (the listing shows cells like "4512-4454").

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage spine identifier (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The patient the medicine was supplied to, as the key that carries them across the whole asset. Every PBS row belongs to one person, and this is what lets a dispensing history be assembled from the monthly tables and then joined to that person's MBS services, Centrelink payments, tax records and Census responses. ABS calls the Person Linkage Spine "central to our data linking methods" and builds it from the combined population of the Medicare Consumer Directory, DOMINO Centrelink Administrative Data and Personal Income Tax records, so PBS is linked to the Spine once rather than to each dataset in turn. In this package the values are synthetic: they are consistent across tables but stand for nobody.
description_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure, one value per person, stable across the monthly PBS tables and across every other dataset linked through the Spine. There is no finite list to publish: the domain is as large as the Spine population, which ABS says aims to cover everyone resident in Australia at any point in the reference period, currently January 2006 to June 2025.
limitation: It identifies a person, not a prescription, a household or a Medicare card, so rows sharing a value are one patient's supplies rather than a family's, and a script filled for a child sits under the child. The bigger trap is absence: no rows in a month is not evidence that no medicine was taken, because private prescriptions, over-the-counter purchases and medicines given to public hospital inpatients never enter PBS, and a PBS record that failed to link to the Spine cannot be reached through this key at all.
rationale: The PLIDA data item list gives the field as the synthetic person identifier on every PBS table, and ABS publishes what the Spine is, which datasets it is built from, what period it covers and why datasets are linked to it once, which is what determines how this key behaves and where it can and cannot reach.
evidence_quote: The Spine aims to cover all people who were resident in Australia at any point during a given reference period. The current Spine covers January 2006 to June 2025.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' as its description and called the domain an inferred opaque identifier, with a limitation that only said there was no finite value list, so the page said nothing about the Spine, about what the key joins to, or about the coverage gaps that make an empty history misleading.

value_domain: Short code distinguishing types of under co-payment prescription; null where the claim is not under co-payment (inferred)
values: ["1: under co-payment prescription, general patient","2: under co-payment prescription, concessional patient"]
value_source: AIHW METeOR 603902, PBS claim type, code A (supports the under co-payment concept and its collection from 1 April 2012, not this field's code list)
variable_description: Which kind of under co-payment prescription this row is, meaning one whose dispensed price fell below the co-payment the patient would otherwise have paid. Under co-payment supplies produce no government benefit, so they are invisible in claims data and were only reported at all after approved suppliers were required to lodge them from 1 April 2012. The companion concept in AIHW METEOR is the PBS claim type, whose code U covers claims where "the dispensed price of the prescribed medicinal product is less than the amount of the applicable co-payment".
description_source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, PBS Under Co-payment Data, and AIHW METEOR data element 603902, PBS claim type, code A
value_definition: A short code separating general from concessional under co-payment supplies, held as 1 and 2, and null on rows that are ordinary co-payment claims. The two code values are inferred from the field's role, since the Department publishes the concept but not this column's internal values.
limitation: It is empty for everything dispensed before 1 April 2012, so a count of all PBS prescriptions that spans that date shows a jump which is a change in reporting rather than in medicine use. Concessional patients also reach the co-payment threshold at a far lower price than general patients, so the two codes are not comparable measures of how cheap a medicine was.
rationale: No published code table found: this variable is absent from METeOR's PBS data set specification, which covers every other coded field in this assignment under its exact PLIDA variable name, and the PBS under co-payment statistics pages publish no type classification. The generator's existing 1/2 split on patient category, null when the claim is above co-payment, is a defensible shape given the field only exists on under co-payment claims, so I recommend leaving it alone and simply labelling it guessed.

value_domain: ATO extract reference date
value_source: ABS administrative income sources
variable_description: When the ATO took the extract this row came from, not anything about the taxpayer. It matters more on the edited income file than elsewhere: these records have already been through the ATO's own editing, so an extract date fixes both how much lodgement had happened and which editing rules were in force when the row was made.
description_source: ABS administrative income sources
limitation: The column describes the extract, not the person, so it is never an analysis variable. An early extract understates a year's income because late lodgers are missing. Mixing lags across years builds a trend out of coverage rather than out of income.
rationale: The field is named as an extract time on the ATO edited income tables. ABS documents the administrative income sources as point-in-time extracts but publishes no definition of this column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Ato data extract time' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Australian financial year (1 July to 30 June)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23
variable_description: The financial year the edited income amounts on the row refer to, running 1 July to 30 June. Every table in this product covers a single year, so the column is constant within a table and only earns its keep once several years are stacked into a panel. It is the anchor for every amount beside it: the income measures are annual totals for this year, not point-in-time figures, and the person's age or address is not necessarily measured on the same basis.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23
value_definition: A financial year label rather than a date, one value per table. The ABS builds the income measures on a financial-year basis because they come from annual tax records.
limitation: It says nothing about when in the year income was received, so it cannot be used to place a job start, a retirement or a business failure inside the year. A person who appears in consecutive years has not necessarily been in scope throughout, since lodgment and employer reporting decide entry to the file each year.
rationale: The ABS methodology for the income series that this product is drawn from describes financial-year releases built from annual tax records, which fixes the reference period the column carries.
evidence_quote: The current release includes data for the five financial years between 2018-19 and 2022-23.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Reference financial year' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the value is constant within a table.

value_domain: ABS income-derivation marker
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23
variable_description: A marker the ABS attaches to the row, recording that the income measures in this table are ABS constructions rather than raw tax return labels. That distinction is the whole point of the product: each amount beside it is built by mapping a set of tax items into an income concept, a step the ABS warns is imperfect because "the Australian tax system is purpose-built and complex, and in some cases it is difficult to determine how a particular income tax item should be used to describe income standards". The column is the flag for that processing, not an amount.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23
value_definition: A short indicator rather than a dollar figure. No published code list gives the meaning of its individual values.
limitation: It cannot tell you which income item was derived, imputed or corrected, nor what the underlying tax return figure was, so it is no substitute for the raw ITR product when a specific label is needed. Because its values are undocumented, it should not be used as a data quality filter.
rationale: No published page defines this column. The reading comes from the custodian's wording, from the table name, and from the ABS methodology describing how the income categories in this family are derived from tax items.
evidence_quote: Conceptual misalignment. The Australian tax system is purpose-built and complex, and in some cases it is difficult to determine how a particular income tax item should be used to describe income standards, and in some cases the item can be a partial conceptual match.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Income derived variable by abs' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said whether the column was an amount or a marker.

value_domain: Annual investment income, ABS derived (dollars, may be negative)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: What a person earned from their savings and assets in the year: interest, dividends with the franking credit attached, trust distributions, and rent. The ABS builds it from the tax return items for gross interest, franked and unfranked dividends, the franking credit, non-primary-production trust shares and distributions, New Zealand franking credits, net rent and net foreign rent. Rent and trust shares enter net of expenses, so a negatively geared landlord can drag the whole figure below zero even in a year of strong interest and dividends.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax but net of rental and trust expenses, and grossed up by franking credits. It can be negative, and the ABS treats a negative value as income from the source rather than as missing.
limitation: It is not a return on wealth, because it mixes a gross flow (interest) with a net one (rent) and because a person's assets are nowhere in this file. Net capital gains are excluded, so a year of large realised gains can leave investment income looking flat.
rationale: The ABS methodology lists the exact tax return items that make up investment income in this family of measures and states that all values are gross pre-tax dollars.
evidence_quote: All monetary values are presented as gross pre-tax dollars, wherever possible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Investment income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which tax items feed it or that it can be negative.

value_domain: Investment income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Counts of individuals
variable_description: Whether the person counts as having investment income in the year, which in ABS usage includes people whose investment income was negative. The rule is explicit: "The number of individuals for each income source includes all persons with either positive or negative net income from that source." So a landlord who lost money on a rental property and a retiree living on term deposit interest are both flagged here, and the flag exists because a simple test of INVINC being above zero would drop the first of them.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Counts of individuals
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, derived from the investment income measure on the same row. It marks presence of the income type rather than its size or sign.
limitation: It cannot separate a large portfolio from a single interest-bearing account, and it does not distinguish gain from loss, so counting flagged people as investors overstates active investing. People below the lodgment threshold with modest interest income are missing from the file entirely, so the flag understates how widespread small investment income is.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines how individuals are counted against each income source, including the treatment of negative net income, which is the rule this flag implements.
evidence_quote: The number of individuals for each income source includes all persons with either positive or negative net income from that source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Invinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the inclusion of negative amounts was not stated.

value_domain: Source of the employee income amount (tax return or payment summary)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Non-lodgers
variable_description: Where the employee income figure beside it came from: the person's own tax return, or their employer's payment summary because they did not lodge one. The ABS defines the group it identifies: "Non-lodgers are individuals who do not lodge a tax return. This can include employees who have employee income reported by their employers, persons who receive an income below certain levels (i.e. the tax-free threshold), or persons who derive their income from some Commonwealth of Australia Government pension, benefit and allowance payments that are exempt from income tax." It is the single most important control column in the table, because a payment-summary row can only ever carry employee income.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Non-lodgers
value_definition: A short code distinguishing the two sources of the employee income amount. It qualifies WANDS specifically rather than the other income measures on the row.
limitation: It flags how the income was reported, not whether the person was obliged to lodge, so it cannot be read as tax compliance. It also cannot identify non-lodgers who had no employer reporting at all, such as a self-funded retiree below the threshold, because those people never enter the file to be flagged.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the two sources, and the ABS methodology defines non-lodgers and explains that employer-reported income is what brings them into this family of measures.
evidence_quote: Non-lodgers are individuals who do not lodge a tax return. This can include employees who have employee income reported by their employers, persons who receive an income below certain levels (i.e. the tax-free threshold), or persons who derive their income from some Commonwealth of Australia Government pension, benefit and allowance payments that are exempt from income tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Source of wands amount (itr or ps)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without explaining what turns on the distinction.

value_domain: Payment-summary-only earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Non-lodgers
variable_description: Whether the person is in the file only because an employer reported paying them, with no tax return of their own behind the record. These people are a genuinely different population: they are typically low earners, since the ABS notes non-lodgers include "persons who receive an income below certain levels (i.e. the tax-free threshold)", and their record can contain nothing but wages. Excluding them makes a low-income sample thinner; including them without care makes total income look artificially concentrated in employment.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Non-lodgers
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, applied to the person for the year. It is the earner counterpart of the source code beside it.
limitation: A flagged person's investment, business and superannuation income is unknown rather than zero, so treating their total income as complete understates them by whatever they did not have to declare. The flag also moves year to year for the same person as their lodgment obligation changes, which can look like an income change in a panel.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the non-lodger population and states that employees with employer-reported income are part of it, which is the group this flag marks.
evidence_quote: Sometimes, Individual Tax Returns are not lodged, or not all items (e.g. occupation) are completed. The ABS advises caution when interpreting data subject to high rates of missing information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Ps-only unit earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the analytical consequence of the group was unstated.

value_domain: Annual other income, ABS derived (dollars)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: The residual income category: everything on the tax return the ABS could not place in employment, business, investment or superannuation. It is defined by exclusion - "Other income comprises income items reported on the individual income tax return that were not allocated to one of the above categories" - and mostly holds foreign pensions and annuities, controlled foreign company income, transfer or trust income and other foreign source income. The ABS does not trust it on its own account: "Other income is not published separately as it does not provide a reliable view of the category."
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax, folded into total income. Its contents depend on the mapping applied for the year rather than on a single return label.
limitation: The ABS itself says the category is not reliable enough to publish on its own, so a series built from it is weaker than one built from the four named categories. It is defined by what the other categories left behind, so a change in the mapping can move income into or out of it without anything changing in a person's affairs.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines other income by exclusion, lists the tax return items it draws on and states the publication caveat.
evidence_quote: Other income is not published separately as it does not provide a reliable view of the category. It is included in total income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Other income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the ABS's own warning about the category was missing.

value_domain: Other income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person had any income in the residual category during the year. It is the flag most likely to be misread, because being flagged says only that some tax item fell outside the four named income concepts, and the underlying category is the one the ABS declines to publish separately. In practice it picks out people with foreign pensions, foreign source income or controlled foreign company income, so it works better as a marker of unusual affairs than as an income indicator.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of income in the residual category for the person and year.
limitation: Because the category is a remainder, the flag is not stable in meaning across years: an item reclassified into employment or investment income stops flagging people without any change in what they received. It should not be used as a proxy for having a foreign income source, since not everything in the category is foreign.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the residual category and its contents, which is what this flag marks; the publication caveat on the category applies equally to the flag.
evidence_quote: Other income comprises income items reported on the individual income tax return that were not allocated to one of the above categories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Othinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing about the residual nature of the category.

value_domain: Annual own unincorporated business income, ABS derived (dollars, may be negative)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: What a sole trader or partner made from their own business in the year, after expenses but before tax.
