The ABS defines it as "the profit or loss that accrues to owners of, or partners in, their own unincorporated businesses", and treats a bad year as negative income: "Losses occur when operating expenses are greater than receipts and are treated as negative income." The custodian's label reads 'incorporated', which inverts the concept - income from an incorporated business the person works in is employee income, not this.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, net of operating expenses, depreciation and reportable superannuation contributions but before income tax. It is built from the net business income, personal services income, partnership distribution and primary-production trust items on the tax return.
limitation: It is not a measure of self-employment in general, because working directors of their own companies are classified as employees and their income sits in the employee measure instead. Non-primary-production trust distributions are deliberately left out, so a person running a business through a discretionary trust can show nothing here.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the concept, lists the tax return items behind it, states the treatment of losses and states explicitly that incorporated business owners are excluded.
evidence_quote: It also excludes the income of working directors/owners of incorporated businesses who are classified as employees; consequently their income is included under Wage and salary income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Own incorporated business income amount', which states the opposite of the concept, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Own unincorporated business income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person had income or a loss from their own unincorporated business in the year. Loss-making owners are flagged as earners, because the ABS treats a loss as negative income rather than as an absence of income, which makes this the closest thing in the table to a count of sole traders and partners. It is also the flag that moves the aggregate figure around most, since a small number of large business losses can pull the mean well below the median.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of unincorporated business income of either sign for the person and year.
limitation: It counts people, not businesses, so a partnership of four is four flagged people and a person running two businesses is one. It also misses anyone operating through a company or a discretionary trust, so it undercounts small business owners rather than measuring them.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the income concept, states that losses are treated as negative income, and sets out how individuals are counted against an income source.
evidence_quote: Losses occur when operating expenses are greater than receipts and are treated as negative income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Ownuninc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that loss-makers are included.

value_domain: Annual superannuation and annuity income, ABS derived (dollars)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Superannuation and annuity income the person declared for tax. The ABS builds it from the annuity and income stream labels, superannuation lump sums, life insurance bonuses and, from 2018-19, released First home super saver amounts. The measure has a hole in the middle of it by design: "From 1 July 2007, people aged 60 years and over who receive superannuation income in the form of a lump sum or income stream (such as a pension) from a taxed source, receive that income tax free", and the ABS concludes that its superannuation statistics "are regarded as partial, subject to under-coverage".
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, drawn only from amounts that reach a tax return. It mixes regular income stream payments with one-off lump sums, so a single year's figure can be dominated by a withdrawal.
limitation: It cannot measure retirement income, because the largest group of retirees - people over 60 drawing on a taxed source - has nothing to declare and often lodges no return at all. The ABS points to survey data for a fuller picture, and the gap grows with age, so comparing superannuation income across age groups in this column compares coverage as much as income.
rationale: The ABS methodology lists the tax return items in the concept and states in the same section why the measure under-covers superannuation income after 2007.
evidence_quote: Due to the above reason, the superannuation statistics (persons, income) included in this release are regarded as partial, subject to under-coverage.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Superannuation and annuity income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the under-coverage that dominates this column was unstated.

value_domain: Superannuation and annuity income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person declared superannuation or annuity income in the year, which marks taxable superannuation rather than superannuation income in general. A 62-year-old on an account-based pension from a taxed fund is not flagged, because the income is tax free and never reaches a return, while a 58-year-old on the same pension is. The flag therefore tracks the tax treatment and the person's age far more than it tracks retirement.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of superannuation or annuity income for the person and year.
limitation: Using it to date retirement will systematically place people too early, because the flag tends to switch off at 60 exactly when the person's superannuation income becomes their main support. It also fires for a one-off lump sum withdrawal by someone still working full time.
rationale: The ABS methodology explains the post-2007 tax treatment that removes most superannuation income from tax records, which determines who this flag can and cannot mark.
evidence_quote: From 1 July 2007, people aged 60 years and over who receive superannuation income in the form of a lump sum or income stream (such as a pension) from a taxed source, receive that income tax free.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Supinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the age discontinuity that drives the flag was not mentioned.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person whose year of income the row summarises, and the key that turns these annual totals into a person's income history when the year tables are stacked. Each table holds one row per person per financial year, so this column is what makes a panel possible and what carries an income measure out to the same person's Census, health and payment records. ABS holds the joining information apart from the data itself, through a "Person Linkage Spine" that links datasets "separate from the main body of data".
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: An opaque synthetic number, one value per person, consistent across the tables of this product. In fplida the values are generated rather than derived from anyone.
limitation: A person missing from a year's table has not necessarily had no income, because entry to the file depends on lodging a return or having an employer report payments. The key is a person, not a household or a family, so partner and household income cannot be assembled from it without a separate relationship source.
rationale: ABS describes the PLIDA spine and its separation from the data, which is what this key is; the structure of the product, one row per person per year, is visible in the registry's own table list.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Individual encrypted scrambled identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column is what makes the annual tables into a panel.

value_domain: Annual total income, ABS derived (dollars, may be negative)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: The person's whole market income for the year, and the one column in this table that is a sum rather than a component. The ABS defines it as "the sum of all reported income derived from Employee income, Own unincorporated business, Superannuation, Investments and Other income", and then names what it leaves out: "Government pensions, benefits or allowances are excluded from the ABS income data and do not appear in Other income or Total income." The ABS puts that missing piece at between 9% and 11% of total income on survey estimates.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax and before the Medicare levy, and equal to the five income components on the same row. It can be negative where business or investment losses exceed other income.
limitation: It is market income, not the money a person had to live on, so a pensioner shows near zero and a benefit recipient shows only their earnings. Adding a pension estimate to it will double-count for people whose payments were taxable and already declared through the components.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines total income as the sum of the five components used in this product and states in the same passage that government payments are excluded, with an order of magnitude for the exclusion.
evidence_quote: Government pensions, benefits or allowances are excluded from the ABS income data and do not appear in Other income or Total income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Total income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the exclusion of government payments, which is the main thing a reader needs, was missing.

value_domain: Any-income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person counts as an earner at all in the year, on the broadest of the definitions in this table. The ABS rule is that "anyone who earns income, whether from employment, superannuation, investment etc. is counted as an earner". It is the union of the five component flags rather than their sum, which is why the ABS warns that adding the component counts overstates the population - a person with wages, dividends and a rental property is flagged three times among the components and once here.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of any income for the person and year. It sits with the five component flags on the same row.
limitation: It cannot be used as a population denominator, because people with no taxable income and no employer reporting never enter the file to be flagged as non-earners. Someone receiving only a government pension is not an earner here, however substantial their income.
rationale: The ABS methodology gives the definition of an earner used in this family of measures and explains why counts across income sources cannot be added.
evidence_quote: In PIA, anyone who earns income, whether from employment, superannuation, investment etc. is counted as an earner.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Totalinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the relationship to the five component flags was not stated.

value_domain: Annual employee income, ABS derived (dollars)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Everything the person earned for their labour in the year. The ABS defines it as "the total (or gross) income received as a return for labour from an employer or from a person's own incorporated business (when they are employed by this business)". It is wider than salary: allowances, tips and director's fees, employer lump sums, termination payments, attributed personal services income, employee share scheme discounts, reportable fringe benefits, reportable employer superannuation contributions and foreign employment income are all in it. Unlike the other income measures it does not need a tax return, because "the data used in deriving employee income comes from both ITRs and Income Statements (where an individual has not lodged an ITR)".
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax and of the Medicare levy. It includes non-cash components such as reportable fringe benefits, so it exceeds cash wages for anyone salary packaging.
limitation: It is not take-home pay and not a wage rate, since it says nothing about hours, weeks worked or the number of jobs behind it, so a low value can be a full year on low pay or a fortnight on high pay. Because it includes termination payments and employer superannuation contributions, a redundancy year can look like a pay rise.
rationale: The ABS methodology gives the definition verbatim, lists every tax return and income statement item that feeds it, and states the dual source.
evidence_quote: Employee income is the total (or gross) income received as a return for labour from an employer or from a person's own incorporated business (when they are employed by this business).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Employee income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the breadth of the concept nor the payment summary source was on the page.

value_domain: Employee income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person had employee income in the year, and the best covered flag here because employers report pay whether or not a return is lodged. That coverage is the reason to prefer it over the others for questions about who was working: a person can be missing from the investment and business measures for want of a tax return, but an employed person with a tax file number generally reaches the file through their employer.
description_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of employee income for the person and year. It pairs with the source code on the same row, which says whether the underlying amount came from a return or a payment summary.
limitation: It is not a measure of employment during the year: an employment termination payment or a lump sum received long after a job ended will flag someone who did no work, and a person paid cash off the books will not be flagged at all. It also says nothing about full time or part time, since hours are not in this file.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines employee income and states that it is derived from income statements where no tax return was lodged, which is what gives this flag its wider coverage.
evidence_quote: The data used in deriving employee income comes from both ITRs and Income Statements (where an individual has not lodged an ITR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Employee income earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why its coverage differs from the other flags.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 7 label J of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: Superannuation pension income on which the fund has already paid tax, taken straight from the payment summary. The ATO's instruction is mechanical: "Add up the taxed element amounts under the heading 'Taxable component' on all your PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream" and write the total at label J. The element is reported by the fund rather than worked out by the taxpayer, and most people over 60 drawing from a taxed source are told not to show it at all, so the column is dominated by recipients under 60 and by defined benefit cases.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A dollar amount for the year, gross of tax withheld, covering regular income stream and annuity payments only. The untaxed element and the two lump sum in arrears elements sit in separate columns on the same row.
limitation: It is not total superannuation income, because the tax-free component never appears on the return and the taxed element of an over-60 pension from a taxed source is excluded by instruction. A zero in a retiree's record is therefore ordinary, and reading it as no pension will misclassify most people over 60.
rationale: The custodian's description is the return label wording for item 7, and the ATO's instructions for that question say exactly which payment summary amounts are added and where they go.
evidence_quote: Add up the taxed element amounts under the heading 'Taxable component' on all your PAYG payment summary – superannuation income stream.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the taxed element or why the column is largely empty for people over 60.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 7 label N of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: Pension income the fund never paid tax on, usually from an unfunded public sector scheme, plus annuities net of their purchase price. The ATO does not take this straight off the payment summary: "Work out the untaxed element amount for label N using the worksheet", which adds the untaxed elements and then the annuity amount after subtracting "the deductible amount of the annuity's UPP". Unlike the taxed element beside it, an untaxed element stays declarable after 60, so this column keeps working at ages where the taxed element column goes quiet.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A dollar amount for the year, gross of tax withheld, combining untaxed elements of super income streams with the assessable part of Australian annuities. The undeducted purchase price is netted off inside the figure and is not reported separately here.
limitation: Because two different things are added into one box, it cannot be split back into public sector pension income and annuity income. It is not comparable with the taxed element column, since the two carry different tax treatments and different age coverage, so summing them gives a total whose meaning changes with the recipient's age.
rationale: The custodian's description is the return label wording, and the ATO's instructions for question 7 set out the worksheet that produces the label N amount and what it combines.
evidence_quote: Work out the untaxed element amount for label N using the worksheet.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a worksheet result that folds in annuity income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 7 label Z of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: Back payments of untaxed superannuation pension income, paid this year but owed for earlier ones. The ATO keeps them apart from ordinary pension income: "Add up the untaxed element amounts under the heading 'Lump sum in arrears - taxable component' on all your PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream" and write the total at label Z. The reason for the separate box is relief - a recipient "may be eligible for lump sum payment in arrears tax offsets" - and to claim it they must attach a schedule splitting the amount by the year it relates to, which the return itself does not capture.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A dollar amount for the year, reported by the fund as arrears of an untaxed element. It is separate from, and not included in, the ordinary untaxed element at label N.
limitation: The income belongs to earlier years, so counting it in the year of payment overstates that year's income and understates the years it accrued in, and nothing on the row says which years those were. A large value usually signals an administrative correction by a fund rather than a change in the person's circumstances.
rationale: The custodian's description is the return label wording, and the ATO's instructions for question 7 give the exact payment summary heading that feeds label Z and the offset it attracts.
evidence_quote: Add up the untaxed element amounts under the heading 'Lump sum in arrears – taxable component' on all your PAYG payment summary – superannuation income stream.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount belongs to earlier income years.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 7 label Y of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: Back payments of taxed superannuation pension income, paid this year for earlier years. The ATO's step is the mirror of the untaxed one: "Add up the taxed element amounts under the heading 'Lump sum in arrears - taxable component' on all your PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream" and write the total at label Y. It carries the same age rule as the ordinary taxed element, so a recipient over 60 drawing from a taxed source generally has nothing to report, and where a capped defined benefit income stream is involved the ATO instructs the taxpayer to leave label Y out and use label M instead.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A dollar amount for the year, reported by the fund as arrears of a taxed element. It is separate from the ordinary taxed element at label J and from the untaxed arrears at label Z.
limitation: The amount relates to earlier income years, so a person's income series built from this table will show a spike in the year of payment that never happened in the year of entitlement. Under a capped defined benefit income stream the figure is redirected to a different label by instruction, so a zero here can coexist with substantial arrears having been received.
rationale: The custodian's description is the return label wording, and the ATO's instructions for question 7 give the payment summary heading feeding label Y and the capped defined benefit exception.
evidence_quote: Add up the taxed element amounts under the heading 'Lump sum in arrears – taxable component' on all your PAYG payment summary – superannuation income stream.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it read identically to the three other annuity and income stream columns.

value_domain: Australian Business Number (hashed and truncated)
value_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
variable_description: The payer on the wages and salaries record: the entity that withheld tax and reported the payment to the ATO. On the income tax return context tables it is what ties a taxpayer's reported income back to who paid it, so an employment history can be reconstructed from tax records alone. The same employer carries the same value here as in the payment summaries and in BUSOWN.
description_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
value_definition: A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as "a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register", structured as "a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded, cannot be checked against the public register, and is useful only for matching one record to another.
limitation: The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a workplace or a job. A large employer commonly holds several ABNs across its subsidiaries, so one job can look like several employers. An entity that restructures takes a new ABN, which breaks a continuous employment relationship in two. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as the payer's hashed ABN on the wages and salaries tables. The Australian Business Register publishes the ABN's format and issuer.
evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Outstanding ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan balance (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
variable_description: What is still owed on an ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan after the year's compulsory repayment has been taken out. The loan itself is narrow: the ATO says the scheme "started on 1 January 2016 and replaced the Student Start-up Scholarship payment" and is available to higher education students receiving Youth Allowance, Austudy or ABSTUDY Living Allowance. Because the balance is indexed each year and does not fall unless a repayment is made, a rising figure across years is ordinary rather than a sign of new borrowing.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
value_definition: A dollar balance at the end of the assessment, sitting with the repayable debt and the compulsory repayment for the same loan on the same row. Balances for HELP, VSL, SFSS, SSL and the apprenticeship loan are separate columns.
limitation: The column cannot exist before 2015-16, so an empty value in an earlier year says nothing about a person's study debts. It is a balance owed to the Commonwealth, not a measure of study costs or of how much a person borrowed, since indexation and earlier repayments have both moved it.
rationale: The ATO defines the loan, its start date and who can get it, and states that outstanding amounts continue to be indexed; the split of this table's three ABSTUDY columns into a repayable balance, a repayment and a residual balance follows the label wording and the identical HELP, SSL and SFSS trios beside them.
evidence_quote: The Student Start-up Loan (SSL) and ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan (ABSTUDY SSL) schemes started on 1 January 2016 and replaced the Student Start-up Scholarship payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'ABSTUDY Student Start-Up Loan Outstanding Repayable Debt' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it could not be told apart from the repayable debt column.

value_domain: Repayable ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan debt at assessment (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
variable_description: The ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan balance the ATO had on hand when it assessed the year, before working out any compulsory repayment. The loan is voluntary and small by design, paid to Indigenous higher education students on ABSTUDY Living Allowance and their Youth Allowance and Austudy counterparts, and administered by Services Australia rather than by an education provider. Read with the compulsory repayment and the outstanding balance on the same row, it gives the opening position for the year.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
value_definition: A dollar balance at the point of assessment, after the year's indexation. It relates to one loan type only, so a person's whole study debt is the sum of this and the HELP, VSL, SFSS, SSL and apprenticeship loan columns.
limitation: A balance is not a borrowing history: it cannot show how many instalments were taken or when, and voluntary repayments made during the year have already reduced it. It is also silent on whether the person is still studying, since repayment obligations run whether or not study has finished.
rationale: The ATO defines the loan and who receives it, which fixes what the balance is a balance of; the distinction between this column and the outstanding balance beside it is read from the label wording and the parallel trios for the other loan types on the same table.
evidence_quote: This is a voluntary loan available to eligible students in higher education who receive: Youth Allowance, Austudy, ABSTUDY Living Allowance.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'ABSTUDY Student Start-Up Loan Repayable Debt' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to say what the loan is or who can hold one.

value_domain: Compulsory ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan repayment raised on the assessment (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, When you must repay your loan
variable_description: How much of an ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan the ATO required the person to repay out of this year's assessment. Nothing is due until a threshold is crossed: "You must start making compulsory repayments against your study or training support loan when your repayment income exceeds the minimum repayment threshold", and repayment income is wider than taxable income, adding back reportable fringe benefits, net investment losses, reportable superannuation contributions and exempt foreign employment income. A zero therefore usually means income below the threshold rather than no debt.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, When you must repay your loan
value_definition: A dollar amount raised on the notice of assessment for the year, distinct from the balances on either side of it. Voluntary repayments made outside the assessment are not part of it.
limitation: The amount is set by income rather than by the size of the debt, so it measures the person's earnings more than their borrowing. It also cannot be read as the person's whole study debt repayment, because a taxpayer with several loan types has the year's compulsory amount distributed between the columns for each type.
rationale: The ATO page states the threshold rule and defines repayment income, which is what determines whether and how much appears in this column; the identification of the column as the amount raised on the assessment follows the label wording and its position beside the two ABSTUDY balances.
evidence_quote: You must start making compulsory repayments against your study or training support loan when your repayment income exceeds the minimum repayment threshold.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'ABSTUDY SSL compulsory repayment due' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a zero is usually a threshold effect.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 1 July
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The taxpayer's age in completed years at the start of the income year, fixed once for the whole year. It sits in the context table with occupation, spouse details and dependant counts, which is the set of characteristics used to interpret the money columns in the other tables, and it is the age most tax thresholds are read against. Anyone with a birthday during the year is a year older by 30 June, so an age-based cut applied to this column and to a mid-year event will not agree.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A whole number of years with no fractional part, one value per person per income year. It is derived from date of birth rather than reported on the return.
limitation: It is not age at any event in the year, so pairing it with a dated transaction such as an employment termination payment or a superannuation lump sum will be wrong by up to a year. Where the ATO holds no reliable date of birth the derived value is only as good as the registration record behind it, and nothing on the row flags that.
rationale: No published page defines this column. The reading comes from the custodian's wording, from the column sitting among the return's context characteristics, and from the parallel start-of-year and end-of-year age pair in the 2009-10 context table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Age at the beginning of the given financial year' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned against using it as age at an event.

TaxPack 2000 explains that "Your rebate code letter tells us the amount of rebate your entitlement will be based on", and the letter encodes both the paying agency, Centrelink or Veterans' Affairs, and the taxpayer's living arrangement. value_domain: Dollar amount of Age Pension declared as assessable income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 6 Australian Government pensions and allowances
variable_description: How much Age Pension the person declared as taxable income in 2000-01, separated from the other government pensions reported at the same question. The ATO lists the payments that belong there, with the Age Pension first, alongside Carer Payment, Disability Support Pension for people of pension age, Parenting Payment (single) and the veterans' service pensions. The figure comes from the paying agency's payment summary or letter rather than from the person's own records, so it is third-party reported income that the taxpayer transcribes.

value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of any tax withheld, which is carried in its own column. It is the assessable pension only.
limitation: It is not pension entitlement and not a measure of pension receipt, because a pensioner whose income falls below the lodgment threshold never files and never appears; Centrelink payment records are the source for that. Exempt government pensions are excluded by instruction, so a zero can mean the person's pension was not taxable rather than absent.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 6 name the Age Pension as the first payment declared at that item and describe the payment summary or agency letter it is taken from; the separation of an Age Pension component in the 2000-01 record is read from the custodian's label rather than from a published return label.
evidence_quote: Declare at this question the following Australian Government payments or allowances: Age Pension
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Age Pension Amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is taxable pension only and third-party reported.

value_domain: ato_age_range
value_source: ATO Taxation statistics 2023-24, Individuals Table 3, column 'Age range' (note 3: age as at 30 June at the end of the income year, from the birth date on the return)
variable_description: The taxpayer's age in bands at 30 June at the end of the income year, worked out from the date of birth held on the return. The banding is the ATO's own reporting classification, the one used in the age range column of the individuals tables in Taxation statistics, rather than a general purpose age classification. AGE_FY_START and TAXPAYER_AGE sit beside it in the same context table and give age in single years at different reference points.
description_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Individuals Table 3, column 'Age range'
value_definition: Thirteen ordered text bands running from 'Under 18' through five-year groups to '75 and over', with an open band at each end.
limitation: The bands hide the ages that matter for tax. The 18 to 24 band straddles the point at which the minor rates stop applying, and the 60 to 64 and 65 to 69 bands each straddle preservation and pension ages, so an age eligibility cut-off cannot be built from this column without the single year age variables.
rationale: This is the ATO's standard age banding for individual income tax return data, so it is the most likely banding for an ITR AGE_RANGE field, but the PLIDA bin boundaries are not confirmed.
evidence_quote: a. Under 18; b. 18 - 24; ...; m. 75 and over

value_domain: Age in completed years at 30 June 2010, best available source
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)

The word 'best' in the custodian's description is the point: more than one source can supply a date of birth for a taxpayer, and this column carries the one the compilers preferred. Paired with the start-of-year age on the same row it also identifies who had a birthday during the year, which is the group any age-based threshold will treat inconsistently.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)

It is a year-end snapshot, so it is the wrong age for anything dated earlier in the year.
rationale: No published page defines this column. The reading comes from the custodian's wording, in particular the quoted word 'best', and from the column's pairing with a start-of-year age in the same context table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording "Derived 'best' age at end of financial year" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what 'best' implies for consistency with other age sources.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 1 July 2009, best available source
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)

Its end-of-year twin on the same row will differ by one for everyone whose birthday fell inside the year, so the two should never be mixed within one series.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording "Derived 'best' age at start of financial year" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from its end-of-year twin.

The custodian's metadata gives it no description at all, so the reading rests on the column name and the table it sits in.

Use it when the age has to be fixed before the year's earnings occurred, which is the usual requirement for age-banded earnings profiles; the end-of-year column beside it is the one that matches an age reached by 30 June. The custodian's metadata carries no description for either, so both readings rest on the column names and the table they sit in.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item P8 label P of the business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: The catch-all line of a sole trader's or partner's business expenses: everything not already itemised in the named expense boxes above it. The ATO describes it as "the total of all other expenses that you incur in deriving your profit or loss and you haven't already shown elsewhere at P8 Expenses", naming wages, accounting and professional fees, advertising, office supplies, foreign exchange losses and any loss on the sale of a depreciating asset. It is the total column, so it adds the primary production and non-primary production amounts written beside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, taken from the taxpayer's own accounts rather than from a tax calculation, and reported without cents. It is the sum of the two production columns on the same line.
limitation: It is not a deduction. Non-deductible and capital items shown here are added back at the expense reconciliation adjustment label, so the amount can exceed what was actually claimed against income. Its size also depends on what the taxpayer chose to itemise in the named boxes, so it is not comparable between businesses or across years without those columns.
rationale: The custodian's description is the schedule's own line label, and the ATO's instructions for item P8 define what the line covers, state that it is written at label P and set out the reconciliation add-back.
evidence_quote: This is the total of all other expenses that you incur in deriving your profit or loss and you haven't already shown elsewhere at P8 Expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'All other expenses - total' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the figure is an accounting total rather than a deduction.

value_domain: Dollar amount of taxable Australian Government allowances and payments
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 5 Australian Government allowances and payments
variable_description: Taxable working-age income support the person declared for 2000-01: the unemployment, student and parenting allowances rather than the pensions. The modern equivalent of the same question tells the taxpayer to "Declare at this question the following Australian Government allowances or payments", and the list runs from JobSeeker Payment, Youth Allowance and Austudy payment through Parenting Payment (partnered), Special Benefit and Farm Household Allowance to the education allowances for people 16 and over. Declaring an amount here can attract the beneficiary tax offset, which the ATO calculates from the answer rather than from a claim, so the figure has a direct consequence for tax payable.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 5 Australian Government allowances and payments
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of tax withheld, taken from the paying agency's payment summary or letter. Pensions belong to the neighbouring government pensions column, not this one.
limitation: It captures only allowances that are taxable and only for people who lodged, so it undercounts income support badly at the bottom of the distribution where exempt payments and non-lodgment are common. The payment types behind one figure are not identified, so it cannot separate unemployment from student or parenting payments; Centrelink payment records are needed for that.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 5 list the allowances declared at that item and describe the payment summary or agency letter behind the figure, which is the same item the 2000-01 label belongs to.
evidence_quote: Declare at this question the following Australian Government allowances or payments: JobSeeker Payment Youth Allowance Austudy payment Parenting Payment (partnered) Special Benefit Farm Household Allowance
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Allowance or Benefit Amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the government pensions column.

value_domain: Tax withheld reported at the left of item 2 label K of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 2 Allowances, earnings, tips, directors fees etc
variable_description: Tax already taken out of the allowances, tips, director's fees and other non-salary work income declared at the same item. The ATO defines it residually: "Add up any tax withheld from these payments. Don't include any amount of tax withheld that you show at other questions, such as question 1." That exclusion is what makes the column useful and dangerous at once - it is the withholding that did not belong to salary or wages, so it cannot be read on its own as the person's total tax paid.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 2 Allowances, earnings, tips, directors fees etc
value_definition: A dollar amount of pay as you go withholding for the income year, sitting to the left of the income figure at item 2. It relates only to the payments declared at that item.
limitation: Withholding is not tax paid on the income: it is a prepayment that is reconciled against the year's assessment, so a person can have a large figure here and still owe money or get most of it back. Much of the income at item 2 is paid without any withholding at all, so a zero is common and does not imply the income was untaxed.
rationale: The custodian's description names tax withheld from allowances, earnings, tips and director's fees, and the ATO's instructions for question 2 give the step that produces the amount and the exclusion of withholding shown elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Add up any tax withheld from these payments. Don't include any amount of tax withheld that you show at other questions, such as question 1.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is residual to salary and wage withholding.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 2 label K of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 2 Allowances, earnings, tips, directors fees etc
variable_description: Work income that did not come through as ordinary salary: allowances, tips, director's fees, consultation fees, honoraria and casual earnings. The ATO's list at this item runs from car, travel, tool, clothing and meal allowances through to "payments from income protection, sickness, and accident insurance policies" and money from part-time and casual jobs. Together with salary or wages at item 1 it makes up the employee income an individual declares, so neither column measures employment earnings on its own.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 2 Allowances, earnings, tips, directors fees etc
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of the tax withheld reported beside it. It is what the taxpayer declares, drawn from income statements and payment summaries plus anything not reported by a payer.
limitation: It systematically understates allowances received, because an overtime meal or travel allowance that was fully spent, not reported by the employer and within the Commissioner's reasonable amount is left off the return by instruction. Because it lumps allowances, tips and director's fees together, it cannot be used to measure any one of them.
rationale: The custodian's description is the return label wording for item 2, and the ATO's instructions for that question list what belongs there, where the total is written and which allowances are deliberately omitted.
evidence_quote: Write the amount under Income at question 2 – label K.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the instructed omission of fully spent allowances was not recorded.

value_domain: ATO amendment code
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: A processing code on a payment summary record showing that the row has been amended rather than lodged as first reported. It matters because the table holds one row per payment summary, so an employer's correction can leave more than one row for the same job and period: the period start and end dates, the payment date and the payer's business number are what identify them as the same record. Treat it as a control column for de-duplication rather than as information about the payee.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A short code rather than an amount. No published code list gives the meaning of its individual values.
limitation: It flags that an amendment happened but not what changed, so a gross amount cannot be compared before and after from this column alone. It also cannot say whether the original row survives in the same extract, so counting payment summaries without checking the period and payer columns risks counting one job twice.
rationale: No published page defines this column. The reading comes from the custodian's wording and from the payment summary columns beside it, which carry the period, payment date, payer business number and payment summary type that an amendment would be matched on.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Amendment code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said why the column matters for counting rows.

value_domain: Industry code from the ANZSIC classification, held against the ABN on the Australian Business Register
value_source: ATO, Business industry code tool
variable_description: The industry recorded against the taxpayer's ABN on the Australian Business Register, attached to the return as context rather than answered afresh each year. The ATO says the codes it uses on returns "are derived from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) codes and have been simplified for tax return reporting purposes", and that a business updates the register separately from the return. BROAD_INDUSTRY_ABR on the same row is a coarse grouping of this code, so the two are not independent measures.
description_source: ATO, Business industry code tool
value_definition: An industry code from the ANZSIC classification, held against the ABN on the register rather than written on the return. The number of digits is not stated in the data item list, and it should not be assumed to match the five-digit business industry code the ATO uses on the schedule itself. It is blank for an individual with no ABN, which is most individual lodgers.
limitation: It records a registration, not this year's trading. A sole trader who changed trade and never updated the register keeps the old code, so an industry series built from it will lag real switching and will disagree with the industry code the same person writes on the business schedule.
rationale: The ATO's business industry code page states the relationship between the codes used for tax reporting and ANZSIC, and says the register-held code is maintained on the Australian Business Register rather than through the return. That is exactly the distinction the ABR suffix on this column marks. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: BICs are derived from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) codes and have been simplified for tax return reporting purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'ANZSIC code from ABR' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said that the code belongs to the registration rather than to the return.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address the ATO held for the individual on the income tax return context and payment summary records. It is the key behind the ASGS geography on the same row, and the key that matches the individual's address here to the same address in Core Locations and in the other ATO products, so a residence can be followed across returns without any address text.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. An administrative address is only as current as the taxpayer's last dealing with the ATO, so it can lag a move by a year or more. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed, truncated ARID, and ABS publishes what the Address Register and its identifier are.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'not specified' as its domain and the same generic sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Dollar amount carried on the notice of assessment
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The amount the ATO assessed when it issued the notice of assessment for this return. It is worked out by the ATO from the lodged return, not written by the taxpayer, and the ATO describes the notice as showing the tax owed, the credit for tax already paid and the tax to pay or refund. Which of those figures this column holds is not stated in the data item list, so treat it as the assessment's headline amount rather than a defined label.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A dollar amount produced by the ATO's assessment calculation and stamped on the notice. It sits in the withholding and debt table beside the compulsory study loan repayment and the assessment balance, which are also ATO-calculated rather than reported.
limitation: It cannot tell you what the taxpayer eventually paid or received. An amendment reissues the assessment with a different figure, and penalties, general interest and offsets against other debts are handled on the statement of account, so this column is not a settlement record.
rationale: The ATO page explains what a notice of assessment contains and confirms that the figures on it are ATO-calculated at processing. It does not name a field called assessment issued amount, so the reading of which figure this column holds stays an inference and the status is guessed. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Your notice of assessment (NOA) is the statement we issue that explains how your tax assessment is calculated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Assessment issued amount (calculated)' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the number comes from the ATO's own calculation rather than from a return label.

value_domain: Dollar amount of employee share scheme discount assessable under the pre-2009 rules
value_source: ATO, ESS interests with a taxing point before 1 July 2009
variable_description: Discount on employee share scheme interests acquired before 1 July 2009 that became assessable this year because a cessation time occurred. These interests fall under the old Division 13A rules rather than the taxed-upfront and deferral labels beside them at item 12, and the ATO says of them that "the latest possible deferred taxing point for these interests was 30 June 2019. This means there will be no income reportable on these interests in the 2019-20 income year and onwards." The column therefore has real content only for the earlier years of the asset.
description_source: ATO, ESS interests with a taxing point before 1 July 2009
value_definition: A dollar amount: the difference between the market value of the shares or rights and what the employee paid for them, brought to account when the cessation time happened. It is gross: the $1,000 concession under these older rules belongs to the upfront exemption branch, not to a discount brought to account at a cessation time.
limitation: A zero is ambiguous. It can mean the person held no pre-2009 interests, or held them with no cessation time in the year, and from 2019-20 onwards it means the rules had run out rather than anything about the taxpayer.
rationale: The ATO page sets out the Division 13A rules that governed interests acquired before 1 July 2009, the cessation time concept that triggers assessment, and the date after which nothing is reportable. That is the whole content of this label. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: The latest possible deferred taxing point for these interests was 30 June 2019. This means there will be no income reportable on these interests in the 2019-20 income year and onwards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label about interests acquired pre 1 July 2009 and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what a cessation time is or that the column empties out after 2018-19.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 20 label E of the supplementary return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, Part F
variable_description: Total assessable foreign source income the taxpayer declared at item 20, label E of the supplement. It is built by adding the assessable rows of the item 20 worksheet, covering foreign employment income not on a payment summary, foreign pensions and annuities, foreign rent and other foreign income. The ATO warns that the amount at label E "does not include any exempt foreign income or income shown on a PAYG payment summary - foreign employment or income statement", both of which are reported at their own labels.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, Part F
value_definition: A dollar amount, self-assessed, gross of the deductible expenses that are netted off at the individual foreign net-income labels on the same row. It excludes exempt foreign employment income at label N.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's total income from abroad. Foreign employment income shown on a payment summary and exempt foreign employment income sit outside it, so using label E alone will understate gross receipts from overseas for anyone posted abroad by an Australian employer.
rationale: Part F of the ATO's question 20 instructions defines label E as the sum of the assessable rows of Worksheet 1 and states what must not be included in it. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Make sure the amount you have shown at label E does not include any exempt foreign income or income shown on a PAYG payment summary - foreign employment or income statement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's run-together phrase 'Foreign source income assessable foreign source income' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which foreign income the label gathers or which it deliberately leaves out.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Income label H of the business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments
variable_description: Government grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies the taxpayer treated as assessable income of their non-primary-production business, reported at P8 label H. The ATO's rule is broad: "Generally, government credits, grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies are assessable income of the recipient if they are received in, or in relation to, the carrying on of a business." Its examples include fuel tax credits, export incentive grants, employee subsidies and apprentice wage subsidies. The primary production half of the same item is ASSBL_GOVT_INDY_PMTS_PP_AMT and the two add to the total column.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, no cents, summed across every non-primary-production business the individual carried on. It is gross assistance received, before any expense the grant paid for.
limitation: It is a self-classified total with no programme attached, so it cannot say which department paid or under what scheme. Grants that are tax free, including several disaster and COVID payments, are excluded by instruction, so the column understates public support to the business.
rationale: The schedule instructions define what counts as assessable government industry assistance, list the examples and direct the non-primary-production total to label H. The instructions PDF and its landing page were confirmed live by direct HTTPS requests; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Generally, government credits, grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies are assessable income of the recipient if they are received in, or in relation to, the carrying on of a business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviation 'Assessable govt industry payments - non-primary production' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said which payments qualify or that tax-free grants are left out.

value_domain: Single-character type flag beside P8 Income label H
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments, Step 3
variable_description: A flag beside the non-primary-production government payments amount, marking that the amount includes one of four specific credits. The ATO's instruction is to "print D in the Type box at the right of the amount at P8 Income - label G (for primary production government industry payments) or label H (non-primary production government industry payments)" where the total includes fuel tax credits, the wine equalisation tax producer rebate, the excise refund scheme for alcohol manufacturers or the product stewardship for oil benefit. This column is the label H side of that pair.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments, Step 3
value_definition: A single character: D where one of the four named credits is inside the amount, otherwise blank. It qualifies the dollar column on the same row and carries no amount of its own.
limitation: A D does not say how much of the amount is the flagged credit, nor which of the four it is, so fuel tax credits cannot be separated out of the total from this column. A blank is equally uninformative, since it may reflect a taxpayer who simply did not mark the box.
rationale: Step 3 of the schedule instructions for assessable government industry payments names the type box, the single letter used and the four credits it marks. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: If your assessable government industry payments include fuel tax credits, producer rebate (wine equalisation tax), excise refund scheme for alcohol manufacturers or product stewardship for oil program benefit, print D in the Type box at the right of the amount at P8 Income - label G (for primary production government industry payments) or label H (non-primary production government industry payments).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Assessable govt industry payments - non-primary production - type' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left a reader unable to guess that the field holds a single letter with one meaning.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Income label G of the business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments
variable_description: Assessable government grants, rebates and subsidies the taxpayer attributed to primary production, reported at P8 label G. For a farmer the amount comes off the primary production worksheet: the ATO says to "include at P8 Income - label G the amount from PP11 in the worksheet". Drought, disaster and industry restructuring assistance land here when they are assessable, while the tax-free equivalents do not, and the non-primary-production half of the item is reported at label H.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, no cents, covering government assistance received in or in relation to carrying on a primary production business, summed across every such business the individual ran.
limitation: The primary and non-primary split is the taxpayer's own attribution, and it is not a labelling nicety: primary production income drives eligibility for tax averaging, so a payment put on the wrong side changes the averaging component rather than just the presentation.
rationale: The schedule instructions direct primary production government industry payments to label G and tie the amount to row PP11 of the primary producers worksheet. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: If you have completed the Gross income from primary production worksheet in Information for primary producers 2025, include at P8 Income - label G the amount from PP11 in the worksheet.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Assessable govt industry payments - primary production' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained where the figure comes from or why the primary production split matters.

value_domain: Single-character type flag beside P8 Income label G
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments, Step 3
variable_description: The type box on the primary production side of assessable government industry payments. It marks that the label G amount includes a fuel tax credit or one of three similar rebates, and fuel tax credits are the common case in farming. The equivalent flag for non-primary-production payments is ASSBL_GOVT_INDY_PMTS_NPP_CD, and the flag qualifies the dollar amount at label G rather than adding to it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments, Step 3
value_definition: A single character: D where the primary production amount includes fuel tax credits, the wine equalisation tax producer rebate, the excise refund scheme for alcohol manufacturers or the product stewardship for oil benefit; otherwise blank.
limitation: It marks presence, not composition, so a flagged row cannot be split into credits and other grants. Because farming rows are the ones most likely to include fuel tax credits, treating the flag as a general indicator of credit receipt will bias any comparison between primary producers and other businesses.
rationale: Step 3 of the assessable government industry payments instructions describes the same type box for label G as for label H, and names the four credits it marks. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
