supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Assessable govt industry payments - primary production - type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, leaving the field looking like an unlisted classification rather than a one-letter flag.

value_domain: Dollar total of P8 Income labels G and H
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments, Step 4
variable_description: All assessable government industry assistance the individual's businesses received in the year, primary and non-primary production added together. The ATO's step is plain: "Add up the amounts you have written at P8 Income - labels G and H and write the total in the adjacent Totals box." It is the figure that flows into total business income rather than a separate receipt.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Assessable government industry payments, Step 4
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount equal to the primary production and non-primary production government payment columns on the same row added together.
limitation: It is a subtotal of the two columns beside it, so adding all three counts the same money twice. It also cannot be compared with published programme spending, because only assessable assistance is in scope and the amount is attributed to the individual rather than to a business entity.
rationale: Step 4 of the assessable government industry payments instructions defines the totals box as the sum of labels G and H. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts you have written at P8 Income - labels G and H and write the total in the adjacent Totals box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Assessable govt industry payments - total' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know the column is the sum of two others on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P16 label H of the business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P16 Payments to associated persons
variable_description: What the business paid relatives, or partnerships in which relatives are partners, as a business expense. The ATO defines the item as "amounts, including salary, wages, commissions or allowances, paid to your relatives", and adds that it "also include super contributions paid for the benefit of your relatives". It is a disclosure item, asked so the ATO can test whether family payments are reasonable.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P16 Payments to associated persons
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, no cents, added up across every business the individual carried on. It covers remuneration and superannuation paid to relatives and related partnerships.
limitation: It is not an extra deduction: the salary and wage part is also inside the total salary and wage expenses column, so adding the two overstates expenses. It also records the claim, not the outcome, since the ATO can deny excessive or unreasonable family payments and the personal services income rules cap deductions for payments to associates.
rationale: The schedule instructions define payments to associated persons, direct the total to P16 label H, and state the overlap with total salary and wage expenses. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: These are amounts, including salary, wages, commissions or allowances, paid to your relatives. These also include super contributions paid for the benefit of your relatives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Payments to associated persons' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the payees are relatives or that the amount overlaps the wages column.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at question D10 label N
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
variable_description: Interest the ATO charged the taxpayer, claimed as a deduction at question D10 label N. The ATO allows the claim for "the late payment of taxes and penalties", for increases in tax from an amended assessment and for increases in other liabilities such as GST or PAYG amounts. D10 is split three ways, so this column sits beside litigation costs at label L and other tax-management expenses at label M.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for interest charges incurred in the income year, whether or not paid by 30 June, provided a bill was received or the charge was made and paid.
limitation: It is the deductible interest claimed, not the taxpayer's debt or their arrears through the year. Penalties for failing to meet obligations are not deductible and are excluded, so the column cannot stand in for ATO compliance action, and D10 carried a single undivided figure before the three-label split, which breaks a long series at the change.
rationale: The ATO's D10 instructions state which interest charges are deductible, which are not, and that the three components are reported at labels N, L and M. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: You can claim a deduction for an interest charge that we imposed on you for: the late payment of taxes and penalties
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Cost of managing tax affairs - interest charged by the ato' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish deductible interest from the penalties that are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of compulsory study and training loan repayment raised on the assessment
value_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments (study and training support loans)
variable_description: The compulsory HELP repayment the ATO raised on this assessment, not an amount the taxpayer wrote on the return. The ATO says "you don't have to provide loan information in your tax return" and that "if you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment". It is based on the person's own repayment income, not household income.
description_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments (study and training support loans)
value_definition: A dollar amount raised as a debt on the notice of assessment. It is nil below the minimum repayment threshold and nil for a person entitled to a Medicare levy reduction or exemption on family income grounds.
limitation: It is neither the loan balance nor the money withheld from pay during the year. Employers withhold an extra amount against an expected repayment, and the ATO applies that money to the loan only after the return is assessed, so pay-cycle withholding and this column do not line up in any year.
rationale: The ATO page describes how the compulsory repayment is calculated by the ATO from repayment income, raised on the notice of assessment, and how it relates to the extra amounts an employer withholds. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Australian HELP assessment debt' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is calculated by the ATO or how it differs from the loan balance.

value_domain: Dollar amount of compulsory VET Student Loan repayment due on the assessment
value_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments (study and training support loans) and Types of loans
variable_description: The compulsory repayment due on a VET Student Loan for the year, worked out by the ATO at assessment rather than reported by the taxpayer. The ATO describes the scheme as one that "offers income contingent loan support to eligible students studying certain diploma level and above vocational education and training qualifications", and it replaced VET FEE-HELP, which the ATO says "operated between 2008 and 2016". The column appears in only a handful of table vintages, so early years carry no VSL repayment at all.
description_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments (study and training support loans) and Types of loans
value_definition: A dollar amount raised as a debt on the notice of assessment, driven by repayment income against the same threshold used for other study and training loans.
limitation: A person can hold several study loans at once, and this column carries only the VET Student Loan share, so it is not the taxpayer's total study loan repayment. Because the scheme is recent, a zero in an early year reflects the absence of the scheme, not the person's circumstances.
rationale: The ATO's types-of-loans page defines the VET Student Loans programme and dates it against the closed VET FEE-HELP scheme, and the compulsory repayments page explains that repayments across all study and training loans are calculated by the ATO and shown on the notice of assessment. Both pages were confirmed live by direct HTTPS requests; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: VSL offers income contingent loan support to eligible students studying certain diploma level and above vocational education and training qualifications.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'VET Support Loan Australian Compulsory Repayment Due' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said which loan scheme this is or that the amount is ATO-calculated.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 20 label F of the supplementary return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, Part G
variable_description: Australian franking credits attached to dividends from a New Zealand franking company, claimed at item 20 label F. They arise under trans-Tasman imputation, where a New Zealand company that has paid Australian tax can attach Australian credits to its dividends. The ATO tells taxpayers not to include "New Zealand imputation credits" or "Australian franking credits you received from an Australian company", which belong at questions 11 and 13.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, Part G
value_definition: A dollar amount of Australian franking credits the taxpayer is entitled to, received directly as franked dividends or indirectly through a trust or partnership. It is reduced where a supplementary dividend was paid and a foreign income tax offset is claimed on the same dividend.
limitation: It says nothing about tax paid in New Zealand: New Zealand imputation credits cannot be claimed on an Australian return and are excluded by instruction. It is also an entitlement claimed, so credits denied under the holding period or related payments rules never appear.
rationale: Part G of the ATO's question 20 instructions defines the amount at label F, lists what must be excluded and explains the supplementary dividend reduction. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Write the amount you worked out in Part G, Step 1 at question 20 - label F.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the run-together 'Foreign source income australian franking credits from a nz company' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish Australian franking credits from New Zealand imputation credits.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed under the Australian film industry incentives
value_source: ATO, Australian film industry incentives, Deductions for expenditure or contributions
variable_description: The amount claimed under the Australian film industry incentives, the concession for investing in a certified Australian film. The ATO explains that "under Division 10BA a deduction is generally allowable for capital moneys spent to produce a film or contributed to the cost of producing it", and that the deduction falls in the year the money is spent. The column belongs to the early schema of this asset, when these incentives were still open to individual investors.
description_source: ATO, Australian film industry incentives, Deductions for expenditure or contributions
value_definition: A dollar amount of capital contribution to film production, limited to the part of the contribution spent directly on production costs. Related expenses such as interest on borrowed contribution money are capped at the film income of the year and are not part of this figure.
limitation: The claim can be unwound years later. The ATO says the deduction "will be later disallowed" if the film misses certification or commercial exhibition, and it can amend at any time, so the column records what an investor claimed rather than a deduction that stood.
rationale: The ATO's own film industry incentives guidance defines what the deduction is for, when it falls, and the conditions that reverse it. It does not tie the amount to a numbered return label for the year this table covers, so the label mapping stays uncited. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Under Division 10BA a deduction is generally allowable for capital moneys spent to produce a film or contributed to the cost of producing it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Australian film industry incentives' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is a film investment deduction or that it can be reversed on later certification failure.

rationale: The ATO's question 5 instructions define the tax withheld field, its source documents and the label it is written against. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label about tax withheld on allowances with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is a sum across payment summaries or how it pairs with the income column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at question 5 label A

value_domain: Dollar benchmark income used in the ATO's income averaging calculation
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: The average income the ATO used to work out this taxpayer's averaging adjustment, the benchmark their basic taxable income is measured against. The ATO sets the test against average income: where it is "less than your basic taxable income - you will receive an averaging tax offset", and where it is more, the taxpayer pays extra income tax on the averaging component. It is a calculated figure that never appears on the return, and it sits beside the four earlier-year basic taxable income columns that feed it.
description_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by the ATO from basic taxable income over a window of up to five years. It is a rate-setting benchmark rather than income the person received in any year.
limitation: It does not tell you the direction or size of the averaging outcome. Whether an offset or extra tax resulted depends on the comparison rate and the averaging component, and the label leaves open whether the value is a primary production average income or the notional income used for special professionals.
rationale: The ATO's income averaging page defines average income, basic taxable income and the comparison that produces an offset or extra tax, which is the calculation this column belongs to. The column name allows a second reading as notional income, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: When your average income is: less than your basic taxable income - you will receive an averaging tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry echoed 'Average Income or Notional Income Amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say the figure is an ATO benchmark used to set a rate rather than income received.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other refundable tax offsets claimed in the supplement
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question T9 Other refundable tax offsets
variable_description: Refundable tax offsets available to the taxpayer from the residual offsets question in the supplement, before they are applied in the assessment. Two claims dominate it: exploration credits, and the special disability trust offset, where the ATO says "if the trustee of the special disability trust has lodged a tax return and paid tax on the net income of the trust, you are entitled to claim the amount of the tax paid by the trustee as a refundable tax offset". Refundable means the offset can produce a refund beyond the tax otherwise payable.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question T9 Other refundable tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, one total covering every claim made at the question, with a separate code box beside it recording which offset or offsets it holds.
limitation: The amount alone does not say which offset it is; that lives in the code box. Available is not applied, so the figure is what the taxpayer claimed at the question rather than what the assessment ultimately allowed.
rationale: The ATO's T9 instructions define the two offsets in scope, the single total that is written for them and the code box that distinguishes them. Which item number and label letter carried the question in the earlier year of this table is not established, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.

value_domain: Dollar total of the primary and non-primary production bad debts columns at P8
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Bad debts
variable_description: Debts the business wrote off as bad during the year and claimed as an expense, primary and non-primary production added together. The ATO sets a threshold on the claim: "before you can claim a bad debt, it must be bad and not merely doubtful", and the debt must previously have been included in assessable income or be a loss from money lending. Accounting provisions for doubtful debts are excluded and are handled through the expense reconciliation instead.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Bad debts
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, no cents, equal to the primary production and non-primary production bad debt columns of P8 added together. Partial write-offs and debt-for-equity swap losses are inside it.
limitation: It is not a measure of credit losses arising in the year. The deduction depends on the amount having been booked as income earlier, so a business on a cash basis records nothing here for the same commercial loss, and recoveries of past bad debts turn up as income at another label rather than reducing this one.
rationale: The schedule instructions define the deduction, its conditions, the exclusion of doubtful debt provisions and the two columns that are added to reach the total. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Before you can claim a bad debt, it must be bad and not merely doubtful.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Bad debts - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the total is the sum of two columns or that provisions are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar balance of the assessment, payable or refundable
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The bottom line of the assessment: tax payable or refundable after levies, offsets and credits for tax already paid. It is calculated by the ATO from the lodged return, not written by the taxpayer.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A dollar amount, the residual after income tax, the Medicare levy and any surcharge are reduced by offsets and by credits such as tax withheld and franking credits.

value_domain: De-identified business identifier shared with BLADE
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The de-identified business identifier for the paying entity on this payment summary row, the same key that identifies a business across BLADE. It stands for the employer or payer, not for the individual, so it is the join that lets a person's pay be attached to firm characteristics. The ABS describes BLADE as "an economic data tool combining tax, trade and intellectual property data with information from ABS surveys", and this column is the key those business tables are built on.
description_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
value_definition: An opaque numeric identifier standing for one registered business, stable within the asset and shared with the business data environment. It carries no name, address or industry of its own.
limitation: A business identifier is not a firm over time and not a workplace. A restructure retires one identifier and starts another with no link between them, and a large employer that pays through several entities will look like several employers, so job spells and employer counts built on this key alone will break.
rationale: The ABS page describes BLADE and the business data it assembles, which supports the reading that this key is the business identifier the two assets share. The ABS page does not itself state that the key is a de-identified Australian Business Number, so the status stays guessed and the reading of the column as the payer rather than the payee comes from the other columns in the same table.
evidence_quote: an economic data tool combining tax, trade and intellectual property data with information from ABS surveys to provide a better understanding of the Australian economy and businesses performance over time
supersedes_rationale: The entry had no description at all beyond the column name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said whether the identifier belongs to the person or to the business paying them.

value_source: ABS, Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)

The custodian's own wording says it is based on the ABR ANZSIC code, so it adds no information beyond that code and is a convenience for grouping. The finer code sits in ANZSIC_CD_ABR beside it.

rationale: The ABS classification page establishes what ANZSIC is and that it is the classification the underlying code belongs to. Neither the ABS nor the ATO publishes the specific broad grouping used for this derived column, so the status is guessed and the confidence is low.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Broad industry base on abr_anzsic_cd' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the column is derived from its neighbour and adds no independent information.

value_domain: Dollar amount of Medicare levy calculated on the assessment
value_source: ATO, What is the Medicare levy?
variable_description: The Medicare levy the ATO calculated on this assessment, before any surcharge. The ATO states that "the Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income" and that "we calculate your Medicare levy when you lodge your tax return", so it is an ATO figure rather than a taxpayer entry. The taxpayer's part is the reduction or exemption claim at question M1, which lowers the amount in this column.
description_source: ATO, What is the Medicare levy?
value_definition: A dollar amount, two per cent of taxable income, reduced where family income puts the taxpayer in the reduction range and nil where a full exemption applies.
limitation: A zero is not a low income signal. A full exemption for a foreign resident, a person with no Medicare entitlement or certain veterans also gives zero, and the Medicare levy surcharge is a separate liability that is not inside this amount.
rationale: The ATO's Medicare levy page gives the rate, the base and states that the ATO calculates the levy at lodgement, and separates the levy from the surcharge. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: The Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Medicare levy' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is calculated by the ATO or that a zero can mean exemption rather than low income.

value_domain: Dollar basic taxable income for the year before the current one
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: The taxpayer's basic taxable income for the year immediately before this one, carried into the income averaging calculation. The ATO says "Your basic taxable income is your taxable income excluding: net capital gains", along with certain superannuation lump sums and death benefit termination payments, above-average income of a special professional, and deductions excluded under the non-commercial loss provisions. This is the year the entry test looks at, because averaging does not start until basic taxable income is at least as high as the year before.
description_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
value_definition: A dollar amount computed by the ATO for the prior income year on the averaging definition, not on the ordinary taxable income definition.
limitation: It will not match the taxable income assessed for that earlier year. Capital gains, certain lump sums and non-commercial loss deductions are stripped out, so joining it to the earlier year's taxable income column will show differences that are definitional rather than errors.
rationale: The ATO's income averaging page defines basic taxable income and the multi-year window the calculation uses, which is what the four averaging-year columns hold. The mapping of the column suffix to a specific offset year is read off the custodian's label and is not published, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Your basic taxable income is your taxable income excluding: net capital gains, certain superannuation lump sums and death benefit termination payments, above-average income of a special professional, deductions that are excluded under the non-commercial loss provisions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Averaging income - 1st year amount (calculated)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which year is meant or that the figure is basic rather than ordinary taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar basic taxable income for two years before the current one
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: Basic taxable income for the second year back, the middle of the five-year window income averaging looks over. The ATO describes the purpose plainly: "Income averaging evens out your income and tax payable over a maximum of 5 years to allow for fluctuations." This figure is restated on the averaging definition rather than lifted from what that year's return reported.
description_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year two before the current one, computed by the ATO on the basic taxable income definition used for averaging.
limitation: It does not carry the primary production and non-primary production split, so the averaging component for that year cannot be rebuilt from this column alone and neither can eligibility be checked from it.
rationale: The ATO's income averaging page sets out the five-year window and the definition of the income used in it, which is what these four earlier-year columns supply. The mapping of the suffix to an offset year is read off the custodian's label rather than published, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: As a primary producer, income averaging allows you to even out your income and tax payable over a maximum of 5 years to take good and bad income years into account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Averaging income - 2nd year amount (calculated)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it read as an unexplained repeat of the column before it.

value_domain: Dollar basic taxable income for three years before the current one
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: Basic taxable income for the third year back in the averaging window. A taxpayer who has been lodging for fewer than five years has nothing to put here, so the window shortens rather than reaching further back. The ATO notes that averaging "calculations won't start until the first year that your basic taxable income is greater than or equal to your basic taxable income from the year before", which is why a long history of columns can still produce no adjustment.
description_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year three before the current one, on the averaging definition of basic taxable income.
limitation: An empty value means no averaging history was available for that year, not that income was zero, so treating blanks as zeros will pull the average down for anyone newly in the system.

value_domain: Derived dollar amount, estimated net tax attributable to business income

variable_description: The share of a person's net tax that the ATO attributes to their business income, worked out by the ATO rather than written on the return. The ATO defines it as "an estimate of the amount of net tax attributable to net business income" and calculates it as net income or loss from business divided by taxable income, capped at one, multiplied by net tax. It sits beside NET_TAX_AMT and GRS_TAX_AMT in the same withholding and debt table, which are the totals it is carved out of.
description_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2014-15, Definitions and calculations
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by pro-rating net tax by the proportion of taxable income that comes from net business income at items 15B and 15C, with the proportion set to one where it would exceed one.
limitation: It is an apportionment, not a tax actually assessed on business income, so it cannot be used to say what a person paid on their business. The ATO notes that net tax itself "does not generally equate to the amount of tax payable or refundable as shown on a notice of assessment", and the field is only calculated for taxable individuals with net business income, so a zero can mean either no business or no tax.
rationale: The ATO's taxation statistics definitions page publishes the exact formula and scope of business net tax, and the column sits with the other calculated assessment amounts in the PLIDA withholding and debt table.

The distinction changes the tax treatment, because a subsequent participant cannot deduct the cost of acquiring the interest and must carry it in the cost base instead.

value_domain: Dollar amount, dependant's separate net income
value_source: ATO Legal database, Explanatory Memorandum, Tax Laws Amendment (2009 Measures No. 1) Act 2009, chapter 16
variable_description: The income of the taxpayer's own child who kept house for them, used to scale the now-abolished child-housekeeper tax offset. A child-housekeeper "is any child of the taxpayer who was wholly engaged in keeping house for the taxpayer during the income year", and separate net income is "broadly defined as gross income that the dependant earned or received while being maintained by the taxpayer less expenses" directly charged against it. The offset fell by "$1 for every $4" once that income passed $282, so the amount here is a means test input, not the taxpayer's own income.
description_source: ATO Legal database, Explanatory Memorandum, Tax Laws Amendment (2009 Measures No. 1) Act 2009, chapter 16
value_definition: A dollar amount of another person's income, reported by the taxpayer. Separate net income is wider than taxable income because it takes in some exempt payments, which the explanatory memorandum illustrates with disability support pensions.
limitation: It is a second-hand figure about a household member, so it cannot be joined to that child's own tax record and is only as accurate as the parent's knowledge. It also only exists for the years the dependency offsets ran on separate net income, before adjusted taxable income replaced that test, so a break in the series is a form change and not a change in behaviour.
rationale: The ATO's copy of the explanatory memorandum defines both the child-housekeeper dependant category and separate net income, including the threshold and taper, which is what this reported amount feeds.
evidence_quote: 'Separate net income' is broadly defined as gross income that the dependant earned or received while being maintained by the taxpayer less expenses that are regarded, according to ordinary accountancy and commercial principles, as a direct charge against that income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Child-housekeeper's separate net income' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing said whose income it is or what it was used for.

Reading it across years gives a running stock of unused losses, since next year's return starts from "the amount at label V at the capital gains question in your last year's tax return".
