It has three states, since the instruction is to "print X in the Yes , Don't know or No box". The ATO lists the situations it is aimed at as future income below the tax-free threshold, only an Australian Government pension, becoming eligible for the seniors and pensioners offset, or moving overseas permanently, and it is also ticked No on a return lodged for someone who has died.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
value_definition: A three-state tick, Yes, Don't know or No, answered by the taxpayer or their agent about their expected future lodgement, not about the year being reported.
limitation: It is an intention, not an outcome. People who tick No often lodge again, and a death is recorded here only indirectly through the No box on a deceased estate return, so it cannot be used as a death or emigration marker.
rationale: The ATO's individual information instructions define the question, its three answer boxes and the circumstances it is aimed at, which is the question this final return indicator records.
evidence_quote: Depending on your situation, print X in the Yes , Don't know or No box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Final tax return' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the answer has three states or that it is a forward-looking intention.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, Australian residency for tax purposes
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
variable_description: Whether the person was an Australian resident for tax purposes, which decides their tax-free threshold and rates. The tick is not a citizenship or visa field: the ATO's tests include having "been in Australia continuously for 6 months or more" in the one job and place, and it treats an overseas student on a course longer than six months as a resident. Part-year residents also tick Yes, and are picked up separately at question A2.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
value_definition: A two-state tick answered by the taxpayer, with Yes covering both full-year and part-year residency for tax purposes.
limitation: It cannot be used to identify migrants or new arrivals, because a Yes covers a person who has always lived here and a student on a temporary visa alike, and it cannot separate full-year from part-year residents without the part-year threshold question beside it.
rationale: The ATO's individual information instructions set out the residency question, the Yes and No conditions and the residency tests behind them.
evidence_quote: If you're an Australian resident for tax purposes for part of 2024–25, print X in the Yes box and complete question A2 Part-year tax-free threshold in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's question 'Are you an australian resident?' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said this is tax residency or that part-year residents answer Yes.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation method code, C, M or R
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Which method the business used to value its closing trading stock, printed in the Type box beside the closing stock amount. The ATO gives three: "C cost", "M market selling value" and "R replacement value", and where more than one was used the taxpayer enters the letter that applies to the largest value. A business in its first year, with no closing stock, prints C.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A single letter, C, M or R, attached to the closing stock total at P8 label M. It qualifies the amount rather than adding to it.
limitation: It does not identify businesses that valued stock below all three methods for obsolescence, which is disclosed separately at P19, and because the letter reflects only the largest valuation it hides mixed methods within the one business.
rationale: The DIL label 'Closing stock - total - type' matches the Type box at P8, and the ATO instructions define the three code letters and the tie-break rule.
evidence_quote: Step 6 From the list below, choose the letter that matches the method you used to value closing stock. If more than one method was used, select the letter that applies to the largest value: C cost M market selling value R replacement value.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Closing stock - total - type' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, even though the ATO publishes a three-letter code list for exactly this box.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label M, closing stock total
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: The value of trading stock the sole trader still held at 30 June, primary production and other stock added together. The ATO defines it as "the total of the value of all items of trading stock, with the value of each item calculated for tax purposes in accordance with section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997", and requires all stock on hand to be counted "regardless of whether you have paid for the stock". It is a balance sheet quantity sitting inside the expenses block, because the change in stock is what turns purchases into cost of sales.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax value of stock on hand at year end, excluding any input tax credit component for businesses registered for GST, and shown as the sum of the primary production and non-primary production columns.
limitation: It is not a business expense despite its position on the schedule, and it is not always a genuine year-end count: a small business entity whose stock moved by $5,000 or less may repeat its opening stock figure instead of valuing stock at all, so small movements in this series can be an accounting choice.
rationale: The DIL label 'Closing stock - total' matches P8 label M, and the ATO instructions define what the amount comprises and the simplified trading stock rule that lets small businesses repeat the opening value.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at Closing stock is the total of the value of all items of trading stock, with the value of each item calculated for tax purposes in accordance with section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Closing stock - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that the $5,000 simplified rule lets the figure be carried over unchanged.

value_domain: Dollar amount, compulsory trade support loan repayment raised on assessment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Compulsory repayments
variable_description: The trade support loan repayment the ATO raised on the person's assessment for the year, worked out from their repayment income rather than claimed by them. The ATO says "You don't have to provide loan information in your tax return" and that "we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment". Trade support loans went to apprentices, and the programme has since been renamed the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Compulsory repayments
value_definition: A dollar amount calculated at assessment, sitting beside the equivalent repayment fields for HELP, SFSS, SSL and ABSTUDY SSL in the same withholding and debt table.
limitation: It is not what the person paid during the year. Employers withhold extra tax against the expected repayment, but the ATO says the balance "doesn’t reduce after each pay cycle; it is only applied as a lump sum after your income tax return is lodged", so this amount times a year count is not a cash flow. A zero can also mean income below the threshold rather than no loan.
rationale: The DIL label names the trade support loan compulsory repayment due, and the ATO explains that compulsory repayments are worked out by the ATO on assessment from the person's repayment income.
evidence_quote: If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Trade support loan (tsl) compulsory repayment due' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is ATO-calculated rather than declared.

value_domain: Dollar amount, excess concessional contributions for the year
value_source: ATO, Concessional contributions cap
variable_description: The amount by which the person's before-tax super contributions passed their cap, which the ATO adds to their assessable income. The ATO says "If you exceed your concessional contributions cap, the excess concessional contributions (ECC) are included in your assessable income" and are "taxed at your marginal tax rate less a 15% tax offset". The ATO works the figure out from fund reporting, not from the return, and will "amend your tax return and send you an amended NOA" when a fund reports late.
description_source: ATO, Concessional contributions cap
value_definition: A dollar amount determined by the ATO from super fund reporting and tax return data, after any unused cap carried forward from the previous five years has been applied.
limitation: It is not a measure of contribution generosity or of a mistake by the taxpayer, since it can be created by an employer's payment timing or a late fund report, and it appears on the record only after the ATO determination, which can arrive after the original assessment. It also does not show whether the person elected to release the amount from their fund.
rationale: The ATO's concessional contributions cap page defines excess concessional contributions, their inclusion in assessable income, the 15 per cent offset and the determination process, which is what this reported amount represents.
evidence_quote: We determine if you exceeded your concessional contributions cap from information reported by your super fund and in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Excess concessional contributions amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the ATO determines it or that it enters assessable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label F, contractor and commission expenses
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: What the sole trader paid for labour and services bought in under contract rather than through wages. The ATO defines these as "expenses for labour and services provided under contract, other than salaries or wages", and lists payments to consultants and contractors, labour-hire arrangements, commissions to people not on a retainer, agency, service, management and consultant fees. It is the contracted-out counterpart to the salary and wage total at P15 on the same schedule.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of primary production and non-primary production contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses, shown in the Totals column at P8 label F.
limitation: It is not a complete count of outsourced labour, because the ATO directs external labour recorded in the cost of sales account to be excluded here, accounting and legal fees to go to all other expenses, and payments made without meeting withholding obligations to be left out altogether. A low value can therefore reflect bookkeeping practice rather than less contracting.
rationale: The DIL label matches P8 contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses, and the ATO instructions define what belongs in the label and what is expressly excluded.
evidence_quote: These are expenses for labour and services provided under contract, other than salaries or wages, for example: payments to self-employed people, such as consultants and contractors, including payments subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement to withhold, and payments made under a labour-hire arrangement
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence as both fields, so nothing named the exclusions that make this an incomplete measure of contracted labour.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 7 label M
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
variable_description: The part of a defined benefit pension that is taxed because the pension exceeds the person's defined benefit income cap. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to work the amount out on its worksheets and "Write the amount from row i at question 7 – label M", and sets the cap for 2024-25 at $118,750. It applies only to capped defined benefit income streams, so it separates old public sector and similar pensions from ordinary account-based pensions reported at labels J and N on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable amount calculated from the tax-free component, taxed element and untaxed element of every capped defined benefit income stream the person received, including lump sums in arrears.
limitation: It is not the pension paid: most of a capped defined benefit pension sits under the cap and never reaches this label, so the column measures the excess above a threshold and cannot be used as a retirement income amount. It also only exists from the year the transfer balance cap rules began, so earlier years are absent by design rather than by non-response.
rationale: The DIL label names the assessable amount from a capped defined benefit income stream, which the ATO instructions place at question 7 label M and define through their worksheets and the defined benefit income cap.
evidence_quote: The amount at row i is your assessable amount from your capped defined benefit income stream. Write the amount from row i at question 7 – label M .
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the amount only arises above the defined benefit income cap.

value_domain: Dollar amount of interest on early payments claimed as a credit
value_source: ATO, Interest on early payments
variable_description: Interest the ATO owes the person for paying a tax debt early, claimed on the return as a credit. The ATO pays it "when you make a payment towards any of the following tax liabilities more than 14 days before the due date", covering income tax, compulsory HELP, VETSL, SFSS, SSL, ABSTUDY SSL and apprenticeship loan repayments. It is small by construction: the ATO "only pay IEP if your interest amount is $0.50 or more".
description_source: ATO, Interest on early payments
value_definition: A dollar amount of interest, claimed at the credit for interest on early payments question, that reduces the balance of the assessment. The same interest is assessable income and belongs at the gross interest question as well.
limitation: It is not a general measure of early payment behaviour, because PAYG instalments and amounts withheld by payers are not eligible, and because the ATO automated the calculation for payments made since 1 July 2021, so later years reflect ATO processing rather than taxpayer claiming.
rationale: The ATO's interest on early payments page defines which payments earn the interest, the 14-day rule and the $0.50 minimum, which is the entitlement this claimed credit records; the return's label letter for the claim is not confirmed on that page.
evidence_quote: Interest on early payments (IEP) is interest we pay when you make a payment towards any of the following tax liabilities more than 14 days before the due date
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Credit for interest on early payments - amount of interest' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said which payments qualify or that the interest is also assessable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 13 label S, cents shown
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Tax a trustee already paid on the person's share of trust income, claimed back as a credit on their own return. The ATO says to "write the total of your share of credits for tax paid by a trustee at question 13 – label S (show cents)". A trustee pays this tax where the beneficiary is under a legal disability or is not an Australian resident, so the credit marks a particular relationship to the trust rather than ordinary trust income.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A dollar and cents amount taken from the statement of distribution or advice issued by the trustee, and claimed as a credit against the person's own tax.
limitation: It is not the trust income itself, which is reported separately at the same question, and it excludes credits for a principal beneficiary of a special disability trust, which the ATO directs to a different question, so the column is not a complete record of trustee-paid tax attributed to a person.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of credit for tax paid by trustee, and the ATO instructions place it at question 13 label S and set out both the entitlement and the special disability trust exception.
evidence_quote: other credits for tax paid by a trustee on trust income, then write the total of your share of credits for tax paid by a trustee at question 13 – label S (show cents).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Share of credit for tax paid by trustee' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said who has trustee-paid tax or that one class of beneficiary is reported elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question IT7, child support paid
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT7 Child support you paid
variable_description: What the person paid or provided during the year for the maintenance of their own child, self-reported for the income tests. The ATO defines it as "amounts you pay or benefits you provide to another person other than your partner for the maintenance of your natural or adopted child", and it is subtractive rather than additive: "we deduct this amount from the total of the other components that make up your adjusted taxable income". A person with nothing to report writes zero rather than leaving it blank.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT7 Child support you paid
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of cash paid and benefits provided over the year, including private arrangements as well as amounts collected through the child support system.
limitation: It is a taxpayer's own figure with a direct incentive attached, since a larger amount lowers adjusted taxable income and can improve entitlements, and it cannot be reconciled with a child support assessment because payments in kind and private arrangements both count. Amounts paid to acquire goods or services are excluded.
rationale: The ATO's IT7 instructions define what counts as child support paid, how it is totalled and how it is used in the income tests, which is exactly what this column holds.
evidence_quote: Child support are amounts you pay or benefits you provide to another person other than your partner for the maintenance of your natural or adopted child.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Child support you paid' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the amount reduces adjusted taxable income or that benefits in kind count.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8, cost of sales total
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: The cost of the goods the sole trader actually sold, worked out from stock and purchases rather than entered directly. The ATO's worksheet adds opening stock, purchases at cost, freight inwards and other costs such as labour and services, then subtracts closing stock. It can be negative, in which case the ATO directs the taxpayer to "print L in the box at the right of this amount", so the sign is carried in a separate code and not in the figure.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the primary production and non-primary production cost of sales columns, derived from the stock movement over the year.
limitation: Because it is a derived figure, it moves with the stock valuation choices recorded beside it rather than only with trading, and it double counts nothing but overlaps with the contractor expenses label, since labour recorded in the cost of sales account is deliberately kept out of that label. Reading it as purchases would overstate goods bought in a year of stock run-down.
rationale: The DIL label 'Cost of sales - total' matches the P8 cost of sales Totals box, and the ATO worksheet and steps define how the figure is built and how a negative result is flagged.
evidence_quote: Step 6 If your total cost of sales is a negative amount, print L in the box at the right of this amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Cost of sales - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the amount is derived from stock movement or that negatives are carried in a separate code box.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 17 label D, deductible farm management deposits
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 17 Net farm management deposits or repayments
variable_description: Money a primary producer put into farm management deposits during the year and can deduct, letting them shift taxable income out of a good year. The ATO makes the deduction conditional: the person's "taxable non-primary production income for 2024–25 is $100,000 or less", individual deposits are at least $1,000 and no more than $800,000 in total, and the money is held for at least twelve months unless a natural disaster or drought exception applies. Repayments come back as income at labels N and R on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 17 Net farm management deposits or repayments
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of deductible deposits made in the year, before the netting against repayments that produces the net amount at label E.
limitation: It is a gross deposit figure, so it cannot be read as savings accumulated: the same person can deposit and withdraw in the one year and the account balance is nowhere on the return. Deposits made in a year the owner became bankrupt, ceased farming for 120 days or died are not deductible and so are absent even though the money moved.
rationale: The DIL label names the deductible deposits box at the farm management deposits question, and the ATO instructions define the eligibility conditions and the step that writes the total at label D.
evidence_quote: Add up deductible deposits you make in 2024–25. Write the total at question 17 – label D in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Net farm management deposits or repayments deductable deposits' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said what makes a deposit deductible or that repayments are reported separately.

value_domain: Dollar amount, deduction for environmental protection activities
value_source: ATO, Other capital asset and expense deductions, Environmental protection activities
variable_description: What the sole trader deducted for cleaning up or preventing pollution caused by their own earning activity. The ATO allows "an immediate deduction for expenditure for the sole or dominant purpose of carrying on environmental protection activities (EPAs)", which it describes as "activities undertaken to prevent, fight and remedy pollution, and to treat, clean up, remove and store waste". The deduction had its own line on the older business and professional items schedule; on the current schedule it reaches the return through the expense reconciliation adjustment instead.
description_source: ATO, Other capital asset and expense deductions, Environmental protection activities
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction claimed in the year the expenditure was incurred, covering a person's own site and a site leased to another party whose pollution the person remedies.
limitation: It is not a measure of environmental spending by a business, since the ATO excludes expenditure that forms part of the cost of a depreciating asset and excludes the cost of an environmental assessment of a project, both of which are the larger items in practice. The label also moved between schedule versions, so a break in the series is a form change.
rationale: The ATO's capital asset and expense deductions page defines environmental protection activities and the immediate deduction, which is the deduction the schedule label totals; the historical label letter on the 2006-07 schedule is not published on a live page.
evidence_quote: You can claim an immediate deduction for expenditure for the sole or dominant purpose of carrying on environmental protection activities (EPAs). These are activities undertaken to prevent, fight and remedy pollution, and to treat, clean up, remove and store waste from your earning activity
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Deduction for environmental protection expenses - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said what counts as an environmental protection activity or what is left out.

value_domain: Dollar amount, small business skills and training bonus deduction
value_source: ATO, Small business skills and training boost
variable_description: The extra 20 per cent deduction a small business claimed for training its employees through an outside registered provider. The ATO allowed "an additional 20% tax deduction for external training courses delivered to employees by registered training providers" for businesses under $50 million turnover, and the measure ran "from 7:30 pm AEDT on 29 March 2022 until 30 June 2024". The amount here is the bonus alone, on top of the ordinary deduction for the same spending.
description_source: ATO, Small business skills and training boost
value_definition: A whole-dollar bonus deduction equal to 20 per cent of eligible external training expenditure, calculated on the GST-exclusive amount for a business registered for GST.
limitation: It is not training spending: multiplying by five recovers only eligible external expenditure, and the ATO excludes training of the business owner, of partners and of contractors, along with any intermediary's commission. Because the measure is time limited, a zero outside its window means the concession did not exist, not that no training happened.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business skills and training boost, and the ATO page defines the 20 per cent bonus, the eligibility test and the exact period the measure ran.
evidence_quote: Small businesses with an aggregated annual turnover of less than $50 million will be allowed an additional 20% tax deduction for external training courses delivered to employees by registered training providers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Small business boost - small business skills and training boost' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the amount is a 20 per cent bonus or that the measure was time limited.

value_domain: Dollar amount, small business technology investment bonus deduction
value_source: ATO, Small business technology investment boost
variable_description: The extra 20 per cent deduction a small business claimed for digital spending such as hardware, software, cloud services, e-commerce and cyber security. The ATO capped it hard: the boost "is capped at $100,000 of expenditure per income year" with "a maximum bonus deduction of $20,000 per income year", and it applied only to spending between 7:30 pm on 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2023. It is the shorter-lived twin of the skills and training boost reported beside it.
description_source: ATO, Small business technology investment boost
value_definition: A whole-dollar bonus deduction of 20 per cent of eligible digital expenditure, restricted to the business share where an item is partly private, and calculated GST exclusive for a business registered for GST.
limitation: The cap makes it a censored measure of digital investment, since every business spending more than $100,000 records the same $20,000 bonus, and depreciating assets only count if they were in use by 30 June 2023. Individuals also claim the bonus inside the expense reconciliation adjustment on the schedule, so it is not separately visible in the ordinary expense labels.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business technology investment boost, and the ATO page defines the 20 per cent bonus, the expenditure and bonus caps, the eligible period and how individuals claim it.
evidence_quote: The boost applies to eligible expenditure incurred between 7:30 pm AEDT on 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2023. The boost is for business expenses and depreciating assets and is capped at $100,000 of expenditure per income year. You can receive a maximum bonus deduction of $20,000 per income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Small business boost - small business technology investment boost' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the amount is capped at $20,000 or that it covers only two income years.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P1 label K, payments to associates for principal work
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: What a person earning personal services income paid a spouse or other associate for work that actually earns that income. It is the only payment to an associate the personal services income rules allow as a deduction. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "Add up the total amount of payments made to associates for principal work. Write the total at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label K", and defines principal work as "the main work that generates the PSI", which "doesn't usually include support work, such as secretarial duties". Payments to an associate for support work are expressly not deductible.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of payments to associates for principal work only, kept separate from all other personal services income deductions, which go to label L on the same block.
limitation: It cannot be read as household income splitting, because it excludes exactly the payments that splitting would use: amounts paid to an associate for non-principal work are outside the label and are not deductible at all. A zero is therefore common in couples where one partner does the administration.
rationale: The DIL label names the personal services income deduction for payments to associates for principal work, and the ATO instructions define both the label and the principal work test that governs it.
evidence_quote: Principal work is the main work that generates the PSI and doesn't usually include support work, such as secretarial duties.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Psi - deductions for payments to associates for principal work' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what principal work means or why the label exists at all.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question A3 label H, other deductions from business income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions
variable_description: Business deductions the person had to report separately so the ATO could test them against the super co-contribution and low income super tax offset rules. The ATO says to write at "question A3 – label H Other deductions from business income" any business deductions "other than those you include in the deduction items at P8", giving as examples a partnership loss share, partnership deductions attributable to business income, personal services income deductions and the cost of managing business tax affairs. A person with none writes zero.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of business deductions not already captured in the schedule's own expense labels, reported only for the government super contribution tests.
limitation: It is a residual by design, so it cannot be added to the schedule's expense labels to get total business costs without double counting the partnership and personal services income deductions it draws on. It is also only completed by people testing for the co-contribution or the low income super tax offset, so a blank does not mean the deductions do not exist.
rationale: The DIL label 'Government super contributions deductions from business income' matches question A3 label H, and the ATO instructions define what the label collects and when it must be completed.
evidence_quote: Yes , write the total of these amounts at question A3 – label H Other deductions from business income .
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the amount is a residual reported only for the super co-contribution tests.

value_domain: Dollar amount, TOTAL DEDUCTIONS on the individual return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total deductions
variable_description: Everything the person claimed as a deduction that year, added up on the face of the return. The ATO builds it from the main return and the supplement together: "Add up the deductions you claimed at questions D1 to D10 and label D in the Deductions section of your tax return", where label D carries the supplementary deductions. It is the figure subtracted from total income on the way to taxable income, and it is the same total that the ATO's own net tax calculation uses.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total deductions
value_definition: A whole-dollar sum of the work-related, investment, gift and tax affairs deductions at D1 to D10 plus the supplementary deductions at D11 to D15.
limitation: It is not the whole of a person's deductible spending, because business expenses are netted off inside the business income items on the schedule and never appear as deductions here, so a sole trader's total looks small next to an employee claiming the same dollars. It is also self-assessed at the point of lodgement rather than verified.
rationale: The ATO's total deductions instruction defines exactly which questions are added to produce the total, which is what this column holds.
evidence_quote: Add up the deductions you claimed at questions D1 to D10 and label D in the Deductions section of your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Total deductions' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said which questions feed it or that business expenses sit outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, VET Student Loan repayable debt at assessment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
variable_description: The VET Student Loan debt the ATO treated as repayable when it assessed the person for the year. The ATO describes VET Student Loans as "income contingent loan support to eligible students studying certain diploma level and above vocational education and training qualifications", collected through the tax system. The table carries the same pair of fields for each loan type, so this unprefixed one is the vocational loan counterpart of the ABSTUDY and student start-up loan columns beside it.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
value_definition: A dollar balance held against the assessment, distinct from the compulsory repayment raised in the year, which sits in its own column in the same table.
limitation: It is not the person's total study debt: HELP, SFSS, student start-up and apprenticeship loans are all held separately, so a vocational figure read alone understates what a former student owes. The reading of this unprefixed field as the VET Student Loan pair is inferred from the naming of the neighbouring loan columns rather than from ATO documentation.
rationale: The ATO defines the VET Student Loans programme and its collection through the tax system, but publishes no data item for the repayable debt field, so the mapping rests on the pattern of loan-specific columns in the same PLIDA table.
evidence_quote: VSL offers income contingent loan support to eligible students studying certain diploma level and above vocational education and training qualifications.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'VET Support Loan Repayable Debt' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished it from the outstanding repayable debt column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, VET Student Loan repayable debt still outstanding
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, How study and training support loans work
variable_description: The part of the person's VET Student Loan debt still owing after the year's repayment was applied. The ATO says of these loans that "The debt will be indexed annually to keep up with changes in the cost of living" and that "Your loan may grow over time if no compulsory or voluntary repayments are made", so this balance can rise between years without any new borrowing. It is the closing counterpart to the repayable debt column on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, How study and training support loans work
value_definition: A dollar balance outstanding at the point of assessment, after compulsory and voluntary repayments and after indexation have been taken into account.
limitation: A year-on-year fall in this balance cannot be read as repayment alone, because indexation pushes it the other way in the same period, and a rise does not mean new study. Like the repayable debt column, the mapping of this unprefixed field to the vocational loan is inferred from the loan-specific columns beside it.
rationale: The ATO explains indexation and the growth of unrepaid income contingent loan balances, which is what an outstanding balance field records, but does not publish a data item for this particular column.
evidence_quote: The debt will be indexed annually to keep up with changes in the cost of living. Your loan may grow over time if no compulsory or voluntary repayments are made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'VET Support Loan Outstanding Repayable Debt' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the balance moves with indexation as well as with repayment.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total work-related deductions claimed
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Deduction questions D1 to D10
variable_description: The employment-related part of a person's deductions, being the work expense questions added together. On the current return these are D1 work-related car expenses, D2 travel, D3 "clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning", D4 self-education and D5 "other work-related expenses", each of which the ATO frames as "a deduction for expenses you incur as an employee". It is narrower than total deductions, which also takes in investment deductions, gifts and the cost of managing tax affairs.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Deduction questions D1 to D10
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the work expense questions on the main return, excluding the low-value pool, interest and dividend deductions that follow them.
limitation: It is a self-assessed claim rather than a verified expense, and it is only meaningful for employees: a sole trader's equivalent costs are deducted inside business income on the schedule and never enter this total, so comparing employees with the self-employed on this column is misleading.
rationale: The ATO's deduction question index defines D1 to D5 as the employee work expense questions, which is what a declared total work-related deduction adds together; the ATO does not publish this total as a return label, so the composition for the earliest form version is inferred.
evidence_quote: D5 Other work-related expenses 2025 Complete question D5 to claim a deduction for other work-related expenses you incur as an employee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Declared Total Work Related Deduction Amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing named the questions it sums or how it differs from total deductions.

value_domain: Dollar amount, deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
variable_description: The part of an Australian pension or annuity payment that is a return of the person's own after-tax capital and so is not taxed again. The ATO tells the taxpayer they will need payment summaries "that show the amount of your annuity and its undeducted purchase price (UPP)", and to "subtract the deductible amount of the annuity’s UPP from the gross amount showing on the payment summary". The figure is worked out by the payer over the expected term of the pension, so it is an actuarial split rather than a taxpayer's estimate.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the year, being the annual slice of the purchase price the person contributed from already-taxed money, spread across the life of the pension or annuity.
limitation: It is not income and not a deduction in the ordinary sense: subtracting it from the gross pension gives the assessable part, and the ATO directs a negative result to be written as zero, so the column cannot be used to reconstruct gross pension payments. It also only exists where an annuity has a purchase price component, which excludes most public pension income.
rationale: The ATO's item 7 instructions define the undeducted purchase price and its deductible amount and set out the subtraction it is used for, though the reported amount had its own label on older return versions that the ATO no longer publishes.
evidence_quote: if you did receive Australian annuities, subtract the deductible amount of the annuity’s UPP from the gross amount showing on the payment summary. Write 0 (zero) if the result is negative.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deductable amount of undeducted purchase price of pension or annuity' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing explained that this is a return of the person's own capital.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 16 label F
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
variable_description: The person's share of losses from business activities run in partnership that the non-commercial loss rules stopped them claiming this year. The ATO says to "Write the total of your net losses to be deferred from business activities you carry on in partnership with others at question 16 – label F", and the partner counterpart for sole trader losses sits at label G. The amount is quarantined rather than lost: "You can't use the amount at question 16 to reduce your 2024–25 taxable income."
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
value_definition: A whole-dollar total across all of the person's partnership business activities in loss, before the primary production and non-primary production split reported at labels I and J.
limitation: It is not a deduction and does not reduce taxable income in the year it appears, so treating it as an expense overstates business costs. It also excludes any loss that passed an exception, met the income requirement with one of the four tests, or was allowed by the Commissioner's discretion, so it counts blocked losses rather than partnership losses.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of deferred losses from partnership activities, which the ATO places at question 16 label F, with an explicit statement that the amount cannot reduce taxable income.
evidence_quote: Write the total of your net losses to be deferred from business activities you carry on in partnership with others at question 16 – label F in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's long wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is quarantined rather than deducted.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label D, primary production deferred losses from a prior year
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
variable_description: Farming losses deferred in an earlier year that the person is now bringing against this year's primary production result. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "write the amount of primary production losses you deferred in a prior year from activities that are the same or similar to your 2024–25 activity" at P8 label D, with the non-primary production equivalent at label E. It is applied before the schedule's net income or loss figure at label Y, so it is inside that result rather than beside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of prior year deferred primary production losses for activities that are the same as, or similar to, a current year activity, shown without cents.
limitation: It cannot be added to the current year business result to get an economic profit, because it is already inside the net income or loss reported at labels Y and Z, and adding it again double counts. The same-or-similar activity test also means a farmer who switched enterprises may hold deferred losses that never appear here.
rationale: The DIL label names deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year for primary production, which the ATO places at P8 label D and folds into the net income or loss calculation at label Y.
evidence_quote: Step 1: At P8 Income – label D in your schedule write the amount of primary production losses you deferred in a prior year from activities that are the same or similar to your 2024–25 activity. Don't show cents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing warned that the amount is already inside the reported net business result.

value_domain: Dollar amount, P8 Reconciliation items, deferred non-commercial losses from a prior year, non-primary production column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
variable_description: A loss from a non-farming business the taxpayer was blocked from claiming in an earlier year and is now deducting against that same activity. The ATO defines it as "A deferred non-commercial business loss is a loss you incur in a prior year which you were unable to claim against other income", and it sits in the non-primary production column at P8 label E. It is self-assessed and activity specific: the loss can only be revived against the same or a similar business activity, and it may be cut down by any net exempt income earned in the current year.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
value_definition: Whole dollars, no cents, summed across all of the taxpayer's non-primary production business activities. The amount is a deduction brought into the current year's business result, not a new loss incurred in the current year.
limitation: It shows losses revived, not losses held in reserve, so a taxpayer sitting on years of quarantined losses with no matching activity this year records nothing. It also collapses every non-farming activity into one figure, so it cannot say which business the loss came from.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-primary production side of the P8 reconciliation row for deferred non-commercial losses from a prior year, and the ATO schedule instructions define the row, the column split and the exempt income reduction.
evidence_quote: A deferred non-commercial business loss is a loss you incur in a prior year which you were unable to claim against other income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is a revived earlier-year loss rather than a current-year one.

value_domain: Dollar amount, P8 Reconciliation items, deferred non-commercial losses from a prior year, Totals column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The whole of the earlier-year business losses a taxpayer is deducting this year, farming and non-farming added together. The ATO builds it as a sum of the two columns beside it: "Step 3: Add up your primary and non-primary production deferred non-commercial business losses. Write the total at Deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year in the Totals column." It is the figure that then feeds the net business result at P8 labels Y and Z, and from there item 15 of the supplementary return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
value_definition: Whole dollars, no cents. It comprises the primary production column at P8 label D plus the non-primary production column at P8 label E, both being deductions carried in from an earlier income year.
limitation: It is a subtotal of the two column figures on the same row, so adding it to them counts the same losses twice. It also cannot be read as the stock of unclaimed losses, because a loss stays quarantined and invisible until the taxpayer carries on the same or a similar activity again.
rationale: The DIL label names the Totals column of the P8 reconciliation row for deferred non-commercial losses from a prior year, and the ATO schedule instructions set out the addition step that defines it.
evidence_quote: Step 3: Add up your primary and non-primary production deferred non-commercial business losses. Write the total at Deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year in the Totals column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year - totals' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell it was the sum of two neighbouring columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 16 label G of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
variable_description: Losses from the taxpayer's own sole trader businesses that the non-commercial loss rules quarantined this year, pushing the deduction into a later year. The ATO instruction is "Write the total of your net losses to be deferred from business activities as a sole trader at question 16 – label G." The neighbouring label F holds the same quantity for activities carried on in partnership, and labels I and J re-split the two into farming and non-farming totals.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
value_definition: Whole dollars, summed across every sole trader activity that failed the tests. It is a loss set aside for the future, and the ATO is explicit that "You can't use the amount at question 16 to reduce your 2024–25 taxable income."
limitation: A deferred loss is not a disallowed loss, so this column measures timing rather than denial, and a reader who treats it as a rejected claim will overstate the tax cost of the rules. It also says nothing about which of the four tests, the exceptions, the safe harbour or the Commissioner's discretion the activity failed.
rationale: The DIL label names the sole trader side of item 16, and the ATO instructions for question 16 give the label letter, the completion step and the rule that the amount does not reduce taxable income.
evidence_quote: Write the total of your net losses to be deferred from business activities as a sole trader at question 16 – label G.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving the timing point unsaid.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at item D8 label H of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D8 Dividend deductions
variable_description: What the taxpayer claimed it cost to earn their Australian dividend income, mostly interest on money borrowed to buy shares plus management fees. The ATO's test is that "To claim a deduction for dividend expenses, you must incur expenses in earning any income from dividends and distributions." One item in here is not an expense at all: a taxpayer holding a listed investment company may claim 50% of the LIC capital gain amount at the same label.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D8 Dividend deductions
value_definition: Whole dollars claimed at item D8 label H, self-assessed by the taxpayer. It comprises interest on investment borrowings, management and specialist advice fees, the deductible share of computer decline in value, and the 50% listed investment company capital gain concession.
limitation: It is a claim, not an audited fact, and it is not the taxpayer's whole investment expense: costs of earning trust and partnership distributions go to item 13 labels X and Y, and costs of foreign dividends go to item 20 or D15. Brokerage and other transaction costs are excluded here because they sit in the CGT cost base instead, so this column understates the cash cost of holding shares.
rationale: The DIL label names item D8, and the ATO instructions for D8 give the deductibility test, the label letter, the LIC concession and the boundary against items 13 and 20.
evidence_quote: To claim a deduction for dividend expenses, you must incur expenses in earning any income from dividends and distributions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label 'Dividend deductions' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what a dividend deduction is or what it leaves out.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total of item 11 dividend labels S, T and U
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends
variable_description: The whole of the taxpayer's directly held Australian dividend income at item 11, grossed up to include the company tax already paid on it. The ATO says to "Declare at this question dividends and distributions that you receive or are credited from Australian companies that you had shares in", and to bring the franking credits into assessable income alongside the cash. The total therefore adds the unfranked amount at label S, the franked amount at label T and the franking credits at label U.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends
value_definition: Whole dollars, the arithmetic total of the three item 11 income labels. It is a grossed-up figure, so it exceeds the cash the shareholder banked by the amount of the attached credits.
limitation: It is not a household's dividend income and not even the taxpayer's whole dividend income: dividends received through a trust, a managed fund or a partnership belong at item 13, and foreign company dividends at item 20. Because it is grossed up, dividing it by a share portfolio value overstates the yield.
rationale: The DIL label names the item 11 total, and the ATO instructions for question 11 define the scope of the question, name the three component labels and state that franking credits form part of assessable income.
evidence_quote: Declare at this question dividends and distributions that you receive or are credited from Australian companies that you had shares in.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total dividends' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is grossed up by franking credits or which dividends are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 11 label U of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label U
variable_description: Company tax already paid on the taxpayer's franked dividends, added to their income and then handed back as a credit against their own tax. The ATO puts it as "Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution." For an individual the credit is refundable, so a retiree on a low rate can end up with cash back rather than merely a smaller bill.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label U
value_definition: Whole dollars written at item 11 label U, taken from the dividend statement but entered by the taxpayer. It covers only credits on directly held Australian shares; credits arriving through a trust are claimed at item 13 label Q.
limitation: The figure is a claim of entitlement, not proof of it. The 45-day holding period rule, the related payments rule and the dividend washing rule can each strip a credit the shareholder has already written in, so a non-zero value does not establish the credit was allowed.
rationale: The DIL label names item 11's franking credit label, and the ATO instructions define a franking credit, give the label letter and list the three rules that can deny it.
evidence_quote: Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dividends franking credit' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never explained that the amount is company tax nor that entitlement is self-assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 11 label T of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label T
variable_description: The cash part of dividends paid out of profits the company had already been taxed on, before the franking credit is added back. The ATO instruction is to "Add up all the franked dividend amounts from your statements and any other franked dividends you receive or are credited to you." This label also acts as the catch-all for statements that do not break the dividend up: "If any of your statements don't show franked and unfranked portions of the dividend, show the total dividend amount at label T."
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label T
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 11 label T, being the franked cash amount only. The company tax attached to these dividends is reported separately at label U, so the taxable value of a franked dividend is the two labels added.
limitation: A large figure here does not prove full franking, because unsplit dividend statements are dumped at this label whatever their franking status. Jointly held shares are reported at the owner's share, so the column reflects a legal interest rather than the dividend the company actually paid out.
rationale: The DIL label names the franked amount at item 11, and the ATO instructions give the completion step, the label letter and the rule that unsplit dividends default to this label.
evidence_quote: If any of your statements don't show franked and unfranked portions of the dividend, show the total dividend amount at label T.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dividends franked' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and in particular did not warn that unsplit statements land here.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at item 11 label V of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label V
variable_description: Tax a share registry took out of the taxpayer's dividends because they had not given the company their tax file number. The ATO explains that "TFN amounts are amounts of tax withheld from dividends and some distributions by investment bodies because you didn't give them your TFN or ABN." The amount is withheld by a third party, shown on the dividend statement, and comes back as a credit at assessment, so the taxpayer loses timing rather than money.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label V
value_definition: Dollars and cents, and it is one of the few item 11 labels where cents are kept. Only amounts not already refunded by the investment body are included.
limitation: It cannot be read as a marker of an untaxed or unregistered person, because a single unquoted holding produces a positive value for someone otherwise fully compliant. The withheld money is also already inside the unfranked figure at label S, so adding this column to the dividend labels double counts it.
rationale: The DIL label names the TFN amounts withheld from dividends, and the ATO instructions for question 11 define the amount, name the label and state that it is included in the unfranked dividend total.
evidence_quote: TFN amounts are amounts of tax withheld from dividends and some distributions by investment bodies because you didn't give them your TFN or ABN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label as 'Tax file number amounts withheld from dividends' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the amount is nested inside label S.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 11 label S of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label S
variable_description: Dividends paid with no franking credit attached, taxed in full at the shareholder's marginal rate. The ATO instruction is to "Add up all the unfranked dividend amounts from your statements, including any TFN amounts withheld", so the figure is gross of any tax the registry took out. It also absorbs deemed dividends under the private company rules, which the ATO describes as payments, loans or debts forgiven by a private company to a shareholder or associate and says "these are generally unfranked dividends".
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends, label S
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 11 label S. It comprises ordinary unfranked dividends, the unfranked share of partly franked dividends, deemed private company dividends, and earnings credited on non-share equity interests.
limitation: It is not a clean measure of listed-company income, because deemed private company distributions with no cash involved are pooled into the same box. A rise in this column can therefore reflect a Division 7A adjustment to a family company loan rather than any change in share investment.
rationale: The DIL label names the unfranked amount at item 11, and the ATO instructions give the completion step, the inclusion of TFN amounts withheld, and the treatment of private company payments and loans as unfranked dividends.
evidence_quote: Add up all the unfranked dividend amounts from your statements, including any TFN amounts withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dividends unfranked' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never flagged that deemed private company dividends sit in the same column.

value_domain: Count of dependent children reported at question IT8 label D
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT8 Number of dependent children
variable_description: How many children the taxpayer says they help support, collected only to widen the private health insurance rebate and Medicare levy surcharge thresholds. A dependent child is a child under 21, or aged 21 to 24 and studying full time, and their own income does not matter; the ATO adds that "The child must be an Australian resident and you must contribute to their maintenance." A taxpayer with no children writes zero rather than leaving the box blank.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT8 Number of dependent children
value_definition: A small non-negative integer at question IT8 label D, self-reported, covering natural, ex-nuptial, adopted and step children. The definition is a maintenance test, not a residence test.
limitation: It is not a count of children living in the dwelling and not a fertility measure. Two separated parents can each count the same child because each contributes to maintenance, and a taxpayer whose thresholds are irrelevant to them has no incentive to fill it accurately, so the count is uneven across the income distribution.
rationale: The DIL label names question IT8, and the ATO instructions give the purpose of the count, the age and study test, the residence and maintenance conditions and the zero-filling rule.
evidence_quote: The child must be an Australian resident and you must contribute to their maintenance.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Number of dependent children' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that the count is a tax threshold device rather than a household roster.

value_domain: Short code recorded alongside the business depreciation expense claim at P8
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses, Depreciation expenses
variable_description: A short code filed with the taxpayer's business depreciation claim in the 2006-07 extract, most likely marking how the deduction was worked out. The published ATO instructions for the depreciation label carry an amount box and no code box, so the code is an ATO processing field rather than something the taxpayer writes on the form. The obvious distinction it could carry is the one the instructions themselves draw, between a small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules and every other business using the uniform capital allowance rules, but that reading is not confirmed by any published document.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses, Depreciation expenses
value_definition: A short code value, not a dollar amount, held on the 2006-07 income tax return extract and appearing on one table only. Its code list is not published.
limitation: Nothing published ties a meaning to any value, so the column cannot be used to classify depreciation method without an internal ATO code list. Treating it as an indicator that depreciation was claimed is also unsafe, since a processing code can be present or absent for administrative reasons unrelated to the claim.
rationale: The ATO instructions establish what the depreciation expense label at P8 holds and that the label has no code box, which is what makes this column an unexplained processing field rather than a form label. No published source names the code values.
evidence_quote: You show at P8 – label M Depreciation expenses the depreciation you claim in your accounting books other than for those assets you allocate in a prior income year to a general pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Depreciation expenses - code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice; this at least records what is and is not known about the field, and marks the reading as unconfirmed rather than silent.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 label M, Depreciation expenses, Totals column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses, Depreciation expenses
variable_description: What a sole trader wrote off against business income for wear and tear on plant, vehicles and equipment, farming and non-farming columns added together. What the figure means depends on the business: for a small business entity using the simplified rules it is the tax deduction itself, while for everyone else the ATO says "You show at P8 – label M Depreciation expenses the depreciation you claim in your accounting books other than for those assets you allocate in a prior income year to a general pool." Profits and losses on selling depreciating assets are kept out of this label and reported as income or as other expenses instead.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses, Depreciation expenses
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 label M, being the primary production and non-primary production depreciation columns added. It covers both immediate write-offs and pool deductions for a small business entity, and book depreciation for other businesses.
limitation: For a business that is not using the simplified rules this is accounting depreciation, not the capital allowance actually deducted, and the gap between them is folded into the expense reconciliation adjustment at label H. A time series of this column therefore tracks book policy as much as tax policy, and it will not reconcile to instant asset write-off statistics.
rationale: The DIL label names the depreciation expenses total at P8, and the ATO schedule instructions explain what the label holds for each type of business, name the totals step, and set out where the reconciliation to the tax deduction happens.
evidence_quote: You carry out the reconciliation between accounting depreciation and the deduction for decline in value at P8 Reconciliation items – label H Expense reconciliation adjustments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Depreciation expenses - total' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the figure is book depreciation for most lodgers.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 12 label F of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes, label F
variable_description: The discount on employee shares or rights that became taxable this year because the deferred taxing point arrived, not because the equity was granted this year. The ATO step is to "Add up all the discount amounts you receive from deferral schemes where a deferred taxing point occurs during 2024–25", the discount being the gap between market value and what the employee paid. Unlike the taxed-upfront labels beside it, nothing here qualifies for the $1,000 reduction.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes, label F
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 12 label F, taken from the employer's employee share scheme statement and including foreign source discounts where a foreign employer gave written details instead. It is assessable income in the year the taxing point falls.
limitation: The year the amount appears is the year the restrictions lifted, which can be several years after the grant, so it cannot be used to date equity awards or to measure the value of pay packages agreed in that year. Ceasing employment is no longer a deferred taxing point, so a departure does not reliably bring the income forward either.
rationale: The DIL label names the deferral scheme discount at item 12, and the ATO instructions define a deferral scheme, name the label, give the completion step and state that the $1,000 reduction applies only to taxed-upfront amounts.
evidence_quote: Add up all the discount amounts you receive from deferral schemes where a deferred taxing point occurs during 2024–25
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about deferral schemes with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that the amount is dated by the taxing point rather than the grant.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 12 label E of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes, label E
variable_description: Discounts on employee shares taxed in the year they were acquired, under a scheme whose own conditions fail the test for the $1,000 concession. The ATO step is to "Add up all the discount amounts you receive from taxed-upfront schemes not eligible for reduction", taking in the employee share scheme statements and any foreign sourced discounts, then "Write the total amount at question 12 – label E." Ineligibility is a feature of the scheme rules, which is what separates this label from label D beside it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes, label E
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 12 label E, taken from the employer's statement. It is fully assessable in the acquisition year with no reduction available against it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 12 label D of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes, label D
variable_description: Discounts on employee shares taxed up front under a scheme that qualifies for the small concession, recorded before the concession is taken off. The ATO says "You may be entitled to reduce the amount of the discounts you receive under taxed-upfront schemes by up to $1,000", and it is this label that triggers the $180,000 adjusted income test deciding whether the reduction is allowed. The reduction, when allowed, is applied later when the total assessable discount is worked out at label B.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes, label D

Because the reduction is capped at $1,000, the column also says nothing about how generous a scheme was, only that it met the qualifying conditions.
rationale: The DIL label names the taxed-upfront eligible discount at item 12, and the ATO instructions give the label letter, the $1,000 reduction, the $180,000 income test and the point in the calculation where the reduction is applied.
