value_domain: Dollar amount, Net non-primary production amount at item 13 of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of everything except farming that came through a partnership, trust or managed fund, after the deductions they claimed against it. The ATO builds it as "Add the income amounts or loss amounts at labels O and U. Then add any amount at label C and subtract the amounts at labels J and Y." It is a share of the entity's taxable net income rather than the cash distributed, and the ATO warns those two can differ.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: Whole dollars, no cents. It comprises the partnership distribution at label O, the trust net income share at label U and franked distributions from trusts at label C, less landcare and electricity connection deductions at label J and other deductions at label Y.
limitation: The amount can be negative, and the sign lives in a separate loss box on the form rather than in the number, so a naive read treats a loss as income. Net capital gains and foreign income are carved out to items 18 and 20, so this column is not the taxpayer's whole return from managed investments.
rationale: The DIL label names the net non-primary production amount at item 13, and the ATO instructions give the exact addition and subtraction of the component labels and the loss box convention.
evidence_quote: Add the income amounts or loss amounts at labels O and U. Then add any amount at label C and subtract the amounts at labels J and Y.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net non primary production amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never listed the labels that make it up or warned that losses carry their sign elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Net primary production amount at item 13 of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of farming income earned through a partnership or trust, after the primary production deductions claimed against it. The ATO builds it as "Add the income amounts or loss amounts at labels N and L, and subtract the amounts at labels I and X." Keeping farm income separate is not cosmetic: the split is what feeds primary production income averaging and the chosen beneficiary rules for discretionary trusts that make a farming loss.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: Whole dollars, no cents. It comprises the primary production partnership distribution at label N and the primary production trust net income share at label L, less landcare and water facility deductions at label I and other primary production deductions at label X.
limitation: It captures farming only where the farm is run through a partnership or trust; a farmer operating in their own name reports at item 15 instead, so this column alone badly undercounts farm households. An eligible beneficiary of a loss-making primary production trust is told to write zero here, so a zero can mean a loss was made rather than no farming interest.
rationale: The DIL label names the net primary production amount at item 13, and the ATO instructions give the component labels, the arithmetic, the averaging purpose of the split and the zero-writing rule for eligible beneficiaries.
evidence_quote: Add the income amounts or loss amounts at labels N and L, and subtract the amounts at labels I and X.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net primary production amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained why the split exists or that sole trader farming is elsewhere.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities, label W; and question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code D
variable_description: A yes or no flag whose registry label and column name point at two different questions on the return, so it has to be checked against the extract before use. The label text is the transferor trust question at item 19 label W, which the ATO asks as "Do you, at any time, directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of money, property or services to a non-resident trust?" The column name expands to a death benefits deceased dependant indicator, and that fact lives at item 4, where the ATO's question 4 instructions define code D as "If you receive a death benefit ETP and you're a death benefits dependant." Both are yes or no facts on the same return, which is how the mismatch survives.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities, label W; and question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code D
value_definition: A two-state indicator. Under the label reading it is the X-in-a-box answer to the item 19 transferor trust question; under the name reading it is a dependency status attached to a death benefit employment termination payment.
limitation: Because the two readings are incompatible, the column cannot support either measure on the strength of the registry alone: counting yes values as transferor trust exposure and counting them as bereaved dependants give completely different populations. Neither reading should be used without checking the delivered extract against the form for the year in question.
rationale: Both ATO pages were read and each supports one of the two readings, which is what establishes that the registry's label and the column name disagree rather than that one of them is simply unclear.
evidence_quote: Do you, at any time, directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of money, property or services to a non-resident trust?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the foreign entities question as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it presented a mismatched label as settled fact and gave no warning to check it.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed as the education tax refund, 2008-09 to 2010-11
value_source: ATO, Education tax refund - what you need to know
variable_description: A refundable amount families claimed on their tax return for school costs such as computers, textbooks and stationery, in the years the scheme ran, the last of them 2010-11. The ATO describes it as "The education tax refund (ETR) helps eligible families and independent students meet the cost of primary and secondary school education", paid as 50% of eligible expenses up to a per-child cap, which for 2010-11 was a refund of $397 per primary child and $794 per secondary child. Entitlement ran through Family Tax Benefit Part A, so it reached families receiving that payment and independent students, not all parents.
description_source: ATO, Education tax refund - what you need to know
value_definition: Whole dollars claimed on the individual return. It is half of the eligible expenses the taxpayer incurred, capped per child by school level, and it is refundable rather than a reduction in tax payable.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as no school spending, because a family outside Family Tax Benefit Part A was ineligible however much they spent. The column also ends rather than falls: the ATO states "You cannot claim the ETR for expenses incurred in 2011-12", the scheme being replaced by a direct payment, so any trend through 2012 is a legislative event and not a change in family behaviour.
rationale: The ATO's own page for the education tax refund gives the purpose, the eligibility gateway through Family Tax Benefit Part A, the 50% rate, the per-child caps and the date the scheme stopped.
evidence_quote: The education tax refund (ETR) helps eligible families and independent students meet the cost of primary and secondary school education.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Education tax refund' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no dates, no eligibility gate and no warning that the column simply ends.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported in Spouse details, reportable fringe benefits from FBT-exempt employers
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto, label R
variable_description: The taxpayer's report of their partner's salary packaged benefits from an employer that pays no fringe benefits tax, such as a public hospital or charity. The ATO instruction is "At label R, write the amount your spouse shows at question IT1 – label N in their tax return", so the number is copied across from the spouse's own return rather than derived independently. It is kept apart from the spouse's non-exempt benefits at label S because several offsets treat the two categories differently.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto, label R
value_definition: Whole dollars at the spouse details label R. It is the grossed-up taxable value of benefits reported by the spouse's employer, and only benefits at or above the reporting threshold are ever included.
limitation: It is one person's account of another person's tax return and can disagree with what the spouse actually lodged, particularly where the spouse lodges late or not at all. It is also not interchangeable with the spouse's non-exempt figure: the ATO does not adjust the exempt amount when calculating the invalid carer, zone, seniors and low income super offsets.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse's section 57A exempt reportable fringe benefits, and the ATO spouse details instructions give the label letter, the copy-across rule and the offsets in which exempt amounts are treated differently.
evidence_quote: At label R, write the amount your spouse shows at question IT1 – label N in their tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's long label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the value is second-hand or why the exempt category is split out.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at question IT1 label N of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts, label N
variable_description: The taxpayer's own salary packaged benefits from an employer exempt from fringe benefits tax under section 57A, mostly hospital and charity employment. The amount comes off the employer's income statement or payment summary rather than being estimated by the taxpayer, and small benefits never appear: "Don't show any benefit less than $3,773." It is not taxable income, but it counts in the income tests that decide the Medicare levy surcharge, family assistance and several offsets.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts, label N
value_definition: Whole dollars at question IT1 label N, being the grossed-up taxable value of the benefits. Zero is written explicitly rather than left blank, and the non-exempt equivalent is reported separately at label W.
limitation: A zero does not mean the person received no fringe benefits, because anything under the reporting threshold is invisible and an employer aggregating below it reports nothing at all. The grossed-up value is also well above the cash cost of the benefit, so it cannot be added to salary to recover the real value of a remuneration package.
rationale: The DIL label names IT1 label N, and the ATO instructions give the reporting threshold, the section 57A test, the source of the figure and the split against label W.
evidence_quote: Don't show any benefit less than $3,773.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never mentioned the reporting threshold or that the amount is grossed up.

value_domain: Dollar adjustment reported at question A3 label G of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions, label G
variable_description: A correction the taxpayer supplies so the super co-contribution test counts the right amount of employment and business income, not their earnings as such. The ATO says "Our systems automatically treat some amounts you earn as employment income or business income. If these amounts aren't the same as your actual employment or business income, you need to make an adjustment at label G." It exists because the co-contribution and the low income super tax offset both require at least 10% of total income to come from employment or business.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions, label G
value_definition: Whole dollars at question A3 label G, and it can be negative, in which case an L is printed in the code box beside it. It is an addition to or subtraction from what the ATO already infers from items 1, 2, 3, 4, 12 label B, IT1, IT2 and the business schedule.
limitation: It is not employment or business income and must never be summed as such: a person earning a full salary normally leaves it blank, while a large value can simply mean a back payment relating to an earlier year had to be taken out. It is also only completed by people testing eligibility for a government super contribution, so it is missing for most lodgers by design.
rationale: The DIL label names the government super contributions employment and business income field, and the ATO instructions for A3 define the 10% test, name label G and explain that the label carries an adjustment rather than a total.
evidence_quote: Our systems automatically treat some amounts you earn as employment income or business income. If these amounts aren't the same as your actual employment or business income, you need to make an adjustment at label G.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, which reads like a measure of earnings, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice; nothing said the figure is an adjustment and usually blank.

value_domain: Dollar amount of associated earnings on excess non-concessional super contributions
value_source: ATO, Non-concessional contributions cap
variable_description: A notional earnings amount the ATO adds to taxable income when someone went over the after-tax super contributions cap and took the excess back out. The ATO calls it a proxy, not a fund return: "Associated earnings are an approximate amount earned from excess contributions while they were in your super fund", worked out at an average of the quarterly general interest charge rates, compounding daily from 1 July of the year of the breach to the date of the original determination letter. Where it is assessed the taxpayer also gets a non-refundable 15% offset against it, and the excess contributions themselves are released rather than taxed at 47%.
description_source: ATO, Non-concessional contributions cap
value_definition: Whole dollars determined by the ATO, not written by the taxpayer, and inserted into the assessment for the financial year in which the excess contributions were made. Only 85% of the amount actually leaves the super fund.
limitation: It is not investment earnings and will not match anything in the fund's records, because the rate is a general interest charge proxy the ATO says it has no discretion to change. A zero is also ambiguous: it can mean no breach, or a person who elected to leave the excess in the fund and pay excess non-concessional contributions tax instead.
rationale: The ATO's non-concessional contributions cap page defines associated earnings, states the rate, the compounding basis and the period, and sets out the two options that decide whether the amount is assessed at all.
evidence_quote: Associated earnings are an approximate amount earned from excess contributions while they were in your super fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the earnings are notional or that the column depends on an election the taxpayer made.

value_domain: Private health insurance benefit code (30, 31, 35, 36, 40 or 41), policy details line 1
value_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
variable_description: The code on the first line of the private health insurance details, which sets the rebate rate by age band and by the part of the year the premium covers. The ATO says "Your level of rebate is calculated on the age of the oldest person covered by the policy. We use the benefit code to apply the right level of rebate", and that "The valid benefit codes are 30, 31, 35, 36, 40 and 41." Codes 30 and 31 are under 65, 35 and 36 are 65 to 69, and 40 and 41 are 70 or over, with the second of each pair covering 1 April to 30 June.
description_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
value_definition: A two-digit code drawn from the insurer's statement, one per line of policy detail, reported by the health fund rather than chosen by the taxpayer. Line 1 normally carries the 1 July to 31 March period.
limitation: The code follows the oldest adult on the policy, so it is not the taxpayer's own age band and cannot be used as an age proxy for the person on the row: a 30 year old on a parent's policy carries a 40. It is also not the tax claim code, which the ATO notes is a separate letter code based on circumstances at 30 June.
rationale: The custodian labels the four columns as benefit codes 1 to 4, which are the per-line benefit codes on the private health insurance policy details of the individual return, and the ATO statement page defines the code, its values and its age and period basis.
evidence_quote: Your level of rebate is calculated on the age of the oldest person covered by the policy. We use the benefit code to apply the right level of rebate.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Benefit code 1' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing identified it as a private health insurance code or gave its six valid values.

value_domain: Private health insurance benefit code (30, 31, 35, 36, 40 or 41), policy details line 2
value_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
variable_description: The code on the second line of the private health insurance details, which almost always covers premiums paid from 1 April after the rebate rate is reset. The ATO explains the routine split: "There are 2 lines of information on your private health insurance statement because, on 1 April each year, generally your rebate percentage is adjusted by a rebate adjustment factor." So a taxpayer with a single policy held all year still has two codes, usually 30 then 31, or 35 then 36, or 40 then 41.
description_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
value_definition: A two-digit code from the insurer's statement for the second period or policy line. Each line carries its own premium and rebate amounts, and the ATO tells taxpayers to enter each line separately without combining them.
limitation: Two populated lines do not mean two policies or two insurers; they are the normal consequence of the 1 April rate change, so counting lines overstates policy holdings. A pairing that is not consecutive, such as 30 followed by 36, signals a birthday rather than data error.
rationale: The ATO statement page explains why a second line exists, which is the fact that distinguishes this column from the first benefit code rather than duplicating it.
evidence_quote: There are 2 lines of information on your private health insurance statement because, on 1 April each year, generally your rebate percentage is adjusted by a rebate adjustment factor.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Benefit code 2' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no reason why a taxpayer would have a second code at all.

value_domain: Private health insurance benefit code (30, 31, 35, 36, 40 or 41), policy details line 3
value_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
variable_description: The code on the third line of the private health insurance details, which is filled only when the ordinary two lines are not enough. The ATO gives the usual reason: "There may also be 2 or more lines because the oldest person covered by the policy turned 65 or 70 years old during the year." A third line also appears where the taxpayer held more than one policy or changed insurer part way through the year.
description_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
value_definition: A two-digit code from the insurer's statement for a third premium period or a third policy line. It sits alongside its own eligible premium and rebate received amounts.
limitation: A populated third line is not evidence of a 65th or 70th birthday on its own, since a mid-year change of fund produces the same pattern, and the code alone cannot separate the two. An empty third line is the ordinary case and should not be treated as missing data.
rationale: The ATO statement page states the specific circumstance that produces more than two lines, which is what gives the third column a meaning distinct from the first two.
evidence_quote: There may also be 2 or more lines because the oldest person covered by the policy turned 65 or 70 years old during the year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Benefit code 3' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain when a third code appears or why it is usually empty.

value_domain: Private health insurance benefit code (30, 31, 35, 36, 40 or 41), policy details line 4
value_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
variable_description: The code on the fourth and last line of the private health insurance details, provided for taxpayers with several policies or several rate periods. The ATO's instruction against tidying the lines up is what makes the fourth slot necessary: "Make sure you enter all lines of information into your income tax return separately, without performing any calculations." Its values are the same six benefit codes, each one setting the rebate percentage for the premiums on that line.
description_source: ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code
value_definition: A two-digit code from the insurer's statement, occupying the last of the four slots the extract provides. It carries the rebate percentage for whichever premium period or policy the insurer reported on that line.
limitation: The four columns are a fixed set of slots, so a taxpayer whose statements run to more lines than the form allows cannot be fully represented here, and the number of populated slots is a form constraint rather than a count of cover. The column also says nothing about how many days of hospital cover the policy provided, which is what the Medicare levy surcharge turns on.
rationale: The ATO statement page defines the benefit code and requires each statement line to be entered separately, which is why the return carries a fixed set of numbered slots and what the fourth one is for.
evidence_quote: Make sure you enter all lines of information into your income tax return separately, without performing any calculations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Benefit code 4' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the four columns are fixed slots rather than a count of policies.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net small business income reported for the entrepreneurs tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label N
variable_description: The small business income the entrepreneurs tax offset was worked out on, deliberately reported before the taxpayer's own income tax deductions. The ATO's instruction for a partner is to "write the amount of your share of the net small business income at N (do not reduce this amount by any deductions that you are entitled to claim for income tax purposes)". For a sole trader it is business turnover less the deductions attributable to that turnover; a share received from a partnership or trust is entered at its face value.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label N
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T13 label N. It comprises the taxpayer's sole trader net small business income, or their share of a partnership's or trust's net small business income, or both added together.
limitation: It is a purpose-built figure for a now-abolished offset and is not the taxpayer's business income for any other purpose, since ordinary deductions are excluded by instruction. Only lodgers with aggregated turnover under $75,000 completed the item, so the column is a truncated, self-selected slice of small business rather than a population measure, and it stops after 2011-12.
rationale: The DIL label names the entrepreneurs tax offset net small business entity income, and the archived ATO instructions for question T13 give the label letter, the no-deductions rule and the turnover gate for completing the item.
evidence_quote: write the amount of your share of the net small business income at N (do not reduce this amount by any deductions that you are entitled to claim for income tax purposes)
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount excludes ordinary deductions or that only low-turnover claimants appear.

value_domain: Dollar amount of aggregated turnover reported for the entrepreneurs tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label K
variable_description: The turnover of the business the entrepreneurs tax offset was claimed on, measured across the whole related group rather than the taxpayer alone. The ATO defines aggregated turnover as "your annual turnover for the income year plus the annual turnover of any entity connected or affiliated with you at any time during the income year less income derived from dealings between you and any entity connected or affiliated with you." A partner or beneficiary writes the partnership's or trust's turnover here, not their own share of it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label K
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T13 label K, excluding GST charged and ordinary income from retail fuel sales, and grossed to a full year estimate where the business operated for only part of the year.
limitation: Because a partner writes the entity's turnover rather than a share, adding this column across individuals counts the same business once per partner. The value is also censored by the rules of the item, which was completed only where aggregated turnover was less than $75,000, so the observed distribution stops dead at that point rather than tailing off.
rationale: The DIL label names the entrepreneurs tax offset aggregated turnover, and the archived ATO instructions define aggregated turnover, name the label and gate the item at aggregated turnover of less than $75,000.
evidence_quote: Were you a sole trader with an aggregated turnover of less than $75,000 or did you receive business income from a partnership or trust with an aggregated turnover of less than $75,000?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is an entity-level, group-wide turnover that is censored at $75,000.

value_domain: Dollar amount of entrepreneurs tax offset allowed at assessment
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
variable_description: The tax break a very small business owner received, worth up to a quarter of the tax on their business income and phased out as the business grew. The ATO defines it as "a tax offset equal to 25% of the income tax liability attributable to the net small business income of a small business entity with an aggregated turnover of $50,000 or less", tapering to nothing at $75,000 of turnover, with a further reduction of 20 cents in the dollar once income passed $70,000 for a single person or $120,000 for someone with a family. The taxpayer did not claim a figure: "We will automatically calculate your ETO from the information you provide at this item and at other items on your tax return."
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
value_definition: Whole dollars calculated by the ATO from the turnover and net small business income reported at question T13 together with the rest of the return. It is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or transferred.
limitation: Because the offset is non-refundable, a zero can mean the person had no tax to reduce rather than no entitlement, so the column measures tax position as well as business size. The offset was abolished from 2012-13, so its disappearance is a change in the law and not a collapse in small business activity.
rationale: The archived ATO instructions for question T13 define the offset rate, both taper rules, the automatic calculation and the non-refundable, non-transferable character of the entitlement.
evidence_quote: The entrepreneurs tax offset (ETO) is a tax offset equal to 25% of the income tax liability attributable to the net small business income of a small business entity with an aggregated turnover of $50,000 or less.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Entrepreneurs tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is ATO-calculated, non-refundable, or that the offset ended.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 17 label N of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 17 Net farm management deposits or repayments, label N
variable_description: Farm management deposits a primary producer withdrew inside the normal twelve-month minimum, under the exception for a declared natural disaster or for drought. The ATO instruction is to "Add up early repayments you withdraw during 2024-25 that qualify for the natural disaster or drought exception. Write the total at label N." Keeping the exception separate matters because a normal early withdrawal would strip the deduction claimed when the deposit was made, whereas these withdrawals keep their concessional treatment.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 17 Net farm management deposits or repayments, label N
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 17 label N, being repayments made in the year. It sits beside label R, repayments of deposits held twelve months or more, and label D, deposits made, which together produce the net figure at label E.
limitation: The label pools the natural disaster exception and the drought exception, so it cannot tell you which event triggered the withdrawal, and it carries no location. It also records a use of the exception, not distress as such, since the disaster declaration and the Category C assistance are the qualifying facts rather than the farm's own circumstances.
rationale: The DIL label names the early repayment natural disaster component of item 17, and the ATO instructions give the label letter, the completion step and both exceptions that feed it.
evidence_quote: Add up early repayments you withdraw during 2024–25 that qualify for the natural disaster or drought exception. Write the total at label N.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no sense that the column marks a concession being used rather than a farm in trouble.

value_domain: Dollar amount of early stage investor tax offset reported at question T8
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor, label L
variable_description: The tax offset a taxpayer earned this year for buying shares in a qualifying early stage innovation company, worth 20% of what they paid. An investor who does not meet the sophisticated investor test is limited to $50,000 of qualifying investment, and the ATO states that "The maximum tax offset (including current year and amounts you carry forward from a prior income year) that you, and your affiliates combined, can claim in 2024-25 is $200,000." Entitlements passed through a partnership or trust are added in at the same label.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor, label L
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T8 label L, being the current year entitlement after the annual cap is applied. The sibling columns hold the amount actually used, the amount carried into future years and the amount brought in from last year.
limitation: Because the $200,000 cap is applied before the figure is written, it cannot be divided by 20% to recover how much was invested, and any entitlement lost to the cap is not carried forward. It also tells you nothing about the investment's success, since eligibility rests on the company's status at the time the shares were issued.
rationale: The DIL label names the early stage investor amount at question T8, and the ATO instructions give the 20% rate, the sophisticated investor limit, the combined cap and the worked example showing the cap binding before the figure is written.
evidence_quote: The maximum tax offset (including current year and amounts you carry forward from a prior income year) that you, and your affiliates combined, can claim in 2024–25 is $200,000.

value_domain: Dollar amount of early stage investor tax offset applied in the current year

variable_description: How much of the early stage investor offset actually came off this year's tax bill, which stops at the tax the taxpayer owed. The offset is non-refundable, so the used amount is capped by gross tax payable rather than by the entitlement: in the ATO's own example an investor entitled to $200,000 with $180,000 of tax payable uses $180,000 and carries the remaining $20,000 forward. The figure is worked out at assessment rather than written on the return.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor

It is also a derived assessment figure rather than a taxpayer claim, so it will not always match the labels on the lodged form.

The published instructions do not name a return label for the used amount, so the reading that it is an assessment output is an inference.

value_domain: Dollar amount of unused early stage investor tax offset carried to later years

It is the amount that will reappear as the brought-forward figure in the following year.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor

evidence_quote: If you're a limited partner of an ESVCLP, your amount of the tax offset for each contribution in the ESVCLP is 10% of the lesser of the following:

No published instruction names a return label for the used amount, so the reading that it is an assessment output is an inference.

value_domain: Date of an employment termination payment, item 4 of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments

A missing date therefore signals multiple payments rather than a gap in the data, and treating it as the date employment ended will misdate a late or disputed payment.

value_domain: Dollar amount of employment termination payment tax offset calculated at assessment
value_source: ATO, How ETP components are taxed
variable_description: The offset that holds the tax on a termination payment down to a concessional rate, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed by the taxpayer. It brings the rate on the taxable component to "17% if you reach your preservation age" or 32% if not, and only up to a cap: the ATO says "Any amount over the relevant cap will be taxed at the top marginal rate of 45% plus Medicare levy of 2%." Which cap applies depends on the ETP code, since codes O and P are tested against the whole-of-income cap as well as the ETP cap.
description_source: ATO, How ETP components are taxed
value_definition: Whole dollars derived at assessment as the difference between tax at the taxpayer's marginal rate and tax at the capped concessional rate on the taxable component. It is not a label the taxpayer completes.
limitation: The offset covers only the part of the payment inside the cap, so a very large redundancy shows an offset that is small relative to the payment and the two cannot be compared directly. It also carries no information about why the payment was made, which lives in the ETP code on the same row.
rationale: The ATO page on ETP taxation gives the concessional rates, the preservation age split, the two caps and the code-based rule that selects between them, which is what determines the offset amount.
evidence_quote: Amounts above the relevant cap are taxed at the top marginal rate of 45% plus Medicare levy of 2%
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Termination payment tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the offset is ATO-calculated or that it is bounded by a cap.

value_domain: ETP code at item 4 of the individual tax return (R, O, S, P, D, B, N, T, M)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code descriptions; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed
variable_description: A single letter saying why the termination payment was made, which then decides how much of it is taxed concessionally. R covers redundancy, early retirement, invalidity and compensation for personal injury, unfair dismissal, harassment or discrimination; O covers everything else, such as a golden handshake or payment in lieu of notice; S and P mark a second payment for the same termination; D, B and N mark death benefit payments by the recipient's dependency status; and T marks a payment to the trustee of a deceased estate. The taxpayer copies the letter rather than choosing it: "You must enter a valid code, find it on your income statement or payment summary." The distinction is not cosmetic, because the ATO's page on how ETP components are taxed says a payment "is subject to the whole-of-income cap, if the code on your end of year statement is O or P".
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code descriptions; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed
value_definition: A one-character code taken from the payer's income statement or payment summary. Code M is used instead where the taxpayer received two or more ETPs and lodged an employment termination payment schedule.
limitation: For exactly the people with several termination payments the reason is lost, because code M replaces the substantive codes and the schedule is not carried here. The code is also chosen by the payer, so a redundancy coded O rather than R reflects the employer's judgement and not the character of the payment.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 4 publish the full code table with the circumstances behind each letter, the M code for multiple payments and the cap consequence attached to codes O and P.

value_domain: Dollar amount, excessive component of an eligible termination payment, to 30 June 2007
value_source: ATO, Other super rates and thresholds, Reasonable benefit limits
variable_description: The part of a 2006-07 termination payment that took the person past their lifetime concessional limit and so lost every concession. Under the pre-2007 regime each person had a reasonable benefit limit, which the ATO describes as being used "to determine the concessional tax rates limits of a reasonable benefit limit (RBL) for a particular financial year", covering both pension and lump sum benefits. Anything above that limit was the excessive component and was taxed at the top rate, which is why the return reported it apart from the rest of the payment.
description_source: ATO, Other super rates and thresholds, Reasonable benefit limits
value_definition: Whole dollars on the 2006-07 individual return, reported separately from the balance of the payment, which the column names on the same row describe as the amount other than the excessive component.
limitation: Reasonable benefit limits were abolished from 1 July 2007, so the column empties out after 2006-07 and that break is a change in the law rather than a change in redundancy behaviour. It is also not comparable with the ETP cap that replaced it, since a reasonable benefit limit was a lifetime measure across a person's whole benefits and the cap applies payment by payment.
rationale: The ATO's superannuation rates page confirms that reasonable benefit limits operated up to 30 June 2007 and published the limits used to work out concessional treatment, which is the framework that produced an excessive component. No live ATO page defines the excessive component itself, so the connection between the label and the limits is drawn rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Up to 30 June 2007, the following table can be used to determine the concessional tax rates limits of a reasonable benefit limit (RBL) for a particular financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with a stray quotation mark and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the abolished regime that gives the column its meaning.

value_domain: Dollar amount, taxable component of employment termination payments, item 4 label I
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, label I; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed
variable_description: The assessable part of a termination payment, being what is left once the tax-free amount is stripped out. The instruction is to "Write the taxable component of your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary at question 4 – label I", and the ATO's page on ETP components explains that "After any tax-free amount is deducted from your payment, the balance is the taxable component". The column name preserves the older framing of an amount other than the excessive component, from the reasonable benefit limit regime that no longer applies, but the quantity reported is the taxable component at item 4 label I.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, label I; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed
value_definition: Whole dollars taken from the payer's income statement or payment summary and written at item 4 label I. Where the taxpayer received two or more payments it is the sum of the taxable components across all of them.

Where several payments are summed the reason for each is lost, so a genuine redundancy and a golden handshake are indistinguishable inside one figure.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 4 name the label, the source document and the summing rule, and the ATO page on ETP components defines the taxable component as the balance after the tax-free amount.
evidence_quote: Write the taxable component of your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary at question 4 – label I.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Employment termination payments taxable component' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained the tax-free amount it excludes or the old wording in the column name.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from employment termination payments, item 4
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments

The ATO instruction is to "Write the total amount of tax withheld from your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary under Tax withheld at the left of question 4 – label I", so the figure is reported by the payer rather than estimated by the taxpayer. It is a credit at assessment, sitting to the left of the taxable component it was withheld from.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments
value_definition: Whole dollars taken from the income statement or payment summary. Where two or more termination payments were received the taxpayer adds the withheld amounts across the schedule and reports one total.

supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax withheld on employment termination payments' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish withholding from the tax finally assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the 15% excess concessional contributions tax offset
value_source: ATO, Concessional contributions cap
variable_description: A credit that gives back the 15% the super fund already paid when before-tax contributions above the cap are added to the person's taxable income. The ATO explains that excess concessional contributions "are taxed at your marginal tax rate less a 15% tax offset to account for the contributions tax already paid by your super fund." The offset is non-refundable, so it reduces tax payable but never produces a refund on its own.
description_source: ATO, Concessional contributions cap
value_definition: Whole dollars equal to 15% of the excess concessional contributions included in assessable income for the year. It is calculated by the ATO from the determination and applied in the assessment or the amended assessment.
limitation: Its presence dates the breach to the year the contributions were made, not the year the assessment was issued, and the two are often different because determinations arrive after lodgment. Being non-refundable, a nil offset does not mean there was no excess, only that there was no tax left for it to reduce.
rationale: The ATO's concessional contributions cap page states that excess contributions enter assessable income, gives the 15% offset rate, names it as non-refundable and describes the assessment process that produces it.
evidence_quote: These are taxed at your marginal tax rate less a 15% tax offset to account for the contributions tax already paid by your super fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Excess concessional contributions offset available' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the 15% represents or that it is non-refundable.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the 15% offset on associated earnings from excess non-concessional contributions
value_source: ATO, Non-concessional contributions cap
variable_description: A credit against the notional earnings added to income when someone released after-tax super contributions that went over their cap. Where the person takes option 1 and releases the excess, the ATO includes "your associated earnings in your taxable income" and gives "a non-refundable tax offset of 15% of the associated earnings." The offset attaches to the earnings only; the excess contributions themselves are released to the person rather than taxed as income.
description_source: ATO, Non-concessional contributions cap
value_definition: Whole dollars equal to 15% of the associated earnings assessed for the year. It is worked out by the ATO from the excess non-concessional contributions determination, not claimed on the return.
limitation: It measures the credit on the earnings and not the cost of the breach, which for someone who leaves the money in the fund is excess contributions tax at the top marginal rate plus Medicare levy. A nil value therefore fits both a person with no excess and a person who chose to be taxed at 47% instead.
rationale: The ATO's non-concessional contributions cap page sets out both options, states that option 1 brings associated earnings into taxable income with a non-refundable 15% offset, and gives the rate that applies under option 2.
evidence_quote: a non-refundable tax offset of 15% of the associated earnings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Excess non-concessional contributions offset available' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the offset attaches to earnings rather than to the contributions.

value_domain: Dollar liability for excess private health insurance rebate claimed as a premium reduction
value_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: Health insurance rebate the taxpayer already took as a premium discount but was not entitled to on their actual income, recovered as a debt at assessment. The ATO says "If you claim too much private health insurance rebate as a premium reduction, we recover the amount as a tax liability. This liability will be listed on your notice of assessment as an Excess private health insurance refund or reduction (rebate reduced)." It is calculated at assessment against the income tiers, not claimed or self-assessed by the taxpayer.
description_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
value_definition: Whole dollars added to the tax assessed. It is the gap between the rebate percentage the insurer applied through the year and the percentage the taxpayer's income for surcharge purposes turned out to support.
limitation: It records a mismatch against income tiers, usually because income rose during the year, and is not evidence of misreporting by the taxpayer or the insurer. It is not necessarily even the taxpayer's own liability: where a spouse does not lodge in time, the ATO shifts that spouse's private health insurance liability onto this person.
rationale: The ATO's page on claiming the rebate uses the same wording as the custodian's label, describes the recovery mechanism, works an example and sets out the spouse transfer rule.
evidence_quote: If you claim too much private health insurance rebate as a premium reduction, we recover the amount as a tax liability.

value_domain: Dollar amount of exempt foreign employment income, item 20 label N
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N
variable_description: Foreign salary an Australian resident earned that Australia does not tax, as carried on the 2023-24 twelve-month extract of the income tax return. It is the item 20 label N figure, reported net of the non-capital costs of earning it and floored at zero: the ATO says to "write the total that is exempt from tax less any expenses that aren't capital in nature that you incur in earning that exempt income at question 20 – label N. If the amount is a loss, write 0 (zero)." No foreign income tax offset can be claimed on it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N
value_definition: Whole dollars converted to Australian currency, reported net of related non-capital expenses. Taxpayers reporting an amount here also attach a schedule of additional information setting the income out.
limitation: Exempt does not mean invisible: the amount lifts the rate applied to the person's other income and counts as the spouse's target foreign income in the family tests, so treating it as income of no consequence understates the tax effect. This column also spells the abbreviation differently from the long-running income tax return column of the same meaning, so stacking years on column name alone will drop one of them.

supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Exempt foreign employment income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that a near-identical column name exists on the other income tax return tables.

value_domain: Dollar amount of exempt foreign employment income, item 20 label N
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N
variable_description: Salary earned working overseas that Australia exempts from tax because the foreign posting ran long enough, reported on the main income and loss table. Length of service is the gate: "If your period of continuous service in a foreign country was 90 days or less, your foreign employment income isn't exempt from tax. If it was 91 days or more, your foreign employment income will generally be exempt from tax." The exemption is narrow, reaching relief work financed from a declared developing country relief fund, employment by a prescribed charitable or religious institution, deployment as a member of an Australian Government disciplined force and Austrade-approved projects, rather than expatriate employment generally.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 20 label N, converted to Australian currency and reduced by the non-capital expenses of earning the income, with a loss written as zero.
limitation: It is not a measure of overseas work: a posting of 90 days or less produces nothing here even though the income was foreign and the person was abroad, and taxable foreign employment income goes to item 20 label U instead. Because it is net of expenses, it also cannot be read as gross foreign salary.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 20 state the 91 day continuous service test, the exemption's narrow scope and the net-of-expenses reporting rule, which together fix what the label counts and what it misses.
evidence_quote: If your period of continuous service in a foreign country was 90 days or less, your foreign employment income isn't exempt from tax. If it was 91 days or more, your foreign employment income will generally be exempt from tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Foreign source income exempt foreign employment income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a short posting produces a zero here.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Reconciliation items label H
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The net add-back that turns the sole trader's booked expenses into the expenses tax law allows. The ATO defines it as a difference: "Your expense reconciliation adjustment is your total expense add-backs less your total expense subtractions." Add-backs are accounting entries that are not deductible, chiefly depreciation, provisions and income tax expense; subtractions are tax deductions that never appear in the accounts, chiefly decline in value. It is the figure that stands between total expenses on the same row and net business income.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering the primary production and non-primary production adjustments together. It can be negative, in which case the return marks it with an L in a separate loss box rather than a minus sign.
limitation: The sign lives in a separate loss indicator, so an unsigned value read on its own can be wrong by twice its size. A zero does not mean the accounts and the tax return agree, because many sole traders keep their books on a tax basis and have nothing to reconcile.
rationale: The DIL label names the total expense reconciliation adjustment, a defined step of the ATO business and professional items schedule. The P8 reconciliation items instructions define the adjustment, list what goes into each side and give the worksheet that produces it.
evidence_quote: Your expense reconciliation adjustment is your total expense add-backs less your total expense subtractions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses, Totals column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Everything the sole trader's business spent in the year as booked in its accounts, before any tax adjustment. The ATO builds it by adding "all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses" and the same run down the non-primary production column. It therefore equals the two expense columns on the same row added together, and it is an accounting figure rather than a deduction total.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount running from cost of sales through to all other expenses, self-assessed from the taxpayer's own books. A negative total is marked with an L in a loss box.
limitation: Subtracting this from total business income does not give taxable business income; the expense reconciliation adjustment on the same row is what makes the two agree. Expenses of personal services income reported at P1 are excluded, so a contractor caught by the personal services income rules shows less here than they actually spent.
rationale: The DIL label names the P8 total expenses figure, and the ATO expenses instructions give the exact addition that produces it and the range of expense lines it spans.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses label T
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Business expenses the sole trader booked against activities other than farming, fishing or forestry. The ATO builds it by adding "all the expenses you have written in the Non-primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses" and putting the result at label T. For most sole traders this column carries the whole expense figure and the primary production column beside it is blank.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount spanning cost of sales, foreign resident withholding expenses, contractor, superannuation, bad debts, lease, rent, interest, depreciation, motor vehicle, repairs and all other expenses for non-primary production activities.
