The column also gives no count of businesses, so one figure can cover several unrelated activities.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-primary production total expenses figure at P8, and the ATO expenses instructions set out the addition that produces label T.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Non-primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses . Write the total at label T .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses label S
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Business expenses the sole trader booked against farming, fishing or forestry activities. The ATO instruction is to "Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses" and write the result at label S, after working through the primary production worksheet. A non-zero value is a reasonable marker that the person carried on a primary production business in the year.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering the same expense lines as the non-primary production column but for primary production activities only, self-assessed and drawn from the primary production worksheet.
limitation: A non-zero value says the person claimed primary production expenses, not that farming was their main activity or their main source of income, so a hobby-scale operation and a large farm look the same here. Farm management deposits, which are the main tax instrument farmers use to smooth income, are handled at item 17 and are not in this figure.
rationale: The DIL label names the primary production total expenses figure at P8, and the ATO expenses instructions give the addition that produces label S and point to the primary production worksheet.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses . Write the total at P8 – label S in your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: ATO extract reference date
value_source: ABS administrative income sources
variable_description: When the ATO took the extract this row came from, not anything about the taxpayer. Income tax returns keep changing after the year closes, as returns are lodged late, amended and audited, so the same income year extracted at two dates is two different datasets. The suffix on the table name is that lag: ato_itr_context_2021_16m is the 2020-21 year as it stood sixteen months after the year ended. Comparing across years means comparing like lags rather than like income years.
description_source: ABS administrative income sources
limitation: The column describes the extract, not the person, so it is never an analysis variable. An early extract understates a year's income because late lodgers are missing, and the shortfall falls hardest on people with complex affairs and on agent-lodged returns. Mixing lags across years builds a trend out of coverage rather than out of income.
rationale: The field is named as an extract time on the ATO tables, and every product carrying it has a table-name suffix giving a lag in months from the end of the income year. ABS documents the administrative income sources as point-in-time extracts but publishes no definition of this column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'ATO data extract time' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item A5 label X
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item A5
variable_description: The value of distributions the person received on which a trust, partnership or company had already paid family trust distribution tax. The ATO says "You don't include in your assessable income any part of a distribution to you on which family trust distribution tax has already been paid", so the money never reaches taxable income. It is collected anyway because the Medicare levy surcharge test adds it back, and a spouse copies it into the spouse income section of their own return.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item A5
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, being the distributions that would have been assessable less any expenses that would have been deductible against them. It covers property and the free use of assets as well as cash, and is left blank when the result is zero or negative.
limitation: The amount is outside taxable income, so a reader who adds it to taxable income has built a different concept from the one the return reports and from the one used in tax statistics. A zero or negative result is left blank rather than written as a number, so blanks mix people with no such distribution and people whose deductible expenses exceeded it.
rationale: The DIL label names the amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid, which is a single labelled question on the ATO supplementary return. The instructions give the calculation, the exclusion from assessable income and the reason the ATO still collects it.
evidence_quote: You don't include in your assessable income any part of a distribution to you on which family trust distribution tax has already been paid, and which would otherwise be assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 13 label Q
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F
variable_description: The person's share of franking credits that reached them through a partnership or trust rather than through shares they held themselves. The ATO instruction is to "Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 – label Q." The claim only stands where the matching franked distribution is at label O, U or C on the same row, and where the holding period and related payments rules are satisfied.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents amount, self-assessed from the distribution statement the partnership or trust issued, covering imputation credits received indirectly only.
limitation: It is the credit claimed rather than the credit the trust or partnership was entitled to pass on, and a trust in overall tax loss passes on none at all. Franking credits on directly held shares sit at item 11 and are absent here, so this column understates a person's total imputation credits.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of franking credit from franked dividends, which is a single labelled question in Part F of item 13. The ATO instructions define what the label carries and the conditions on claiming it.
evidence_quote: Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 – label Q .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign investment fund and foreign life policy income (income years to 2009-10)
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, chapter 4
variable_description: Income attributed to the person from a foreign investment fund or foreign life assurance policy, a measure that stops after 2009-10. The ATO now states flatly that "The FIF measures have been repealed and do not apply to taxpayers from 2010–11." Until then Part XI of the ITAA 1936 taxed Australian residents on income accumulating inside a foreign company or trust they did not control, whether or not any of it was paid out. The column appears only in the 2009-10 extract for that reason.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, chapter 4
value_definition: A whole-dollar accruals amount worked out under Part XI of the ITAA 1936 and reported in the foreign entities item of the supplementary return. It is an attribution, not a cash receipt.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as no offshore fund holdings: a long list of exemptions, including the balanced-portfolio and active-business exemptions, removed a holding from attribution altogether. The column disappearing after 2009-10 records a repeal, not taxpayers giving up offshore investment.
rationale: The DIL label names FIF and FLP income, which was a labelled amount in the foreign entities item until the measures were repealed. The ATO guide chapter states the repeal and the year it took effect, and describes what the measures attributed.
evidence_quote: The FIF measures have been repealed and do not apply to taxpayers from 2010–11.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator for an interest in a foreign investment fund or foreign life assurance policy
value_source: ATO, Foreign investment funds guide 2010, chapter 2
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person held an interest in a foreign investment fund or a foreign life assurance policy. The ATO's definition is very wide: "A FIF is any foreign company or foreign trust." A foreign life assurance policy is one issued by an entity that was not an Australian resident at any time in the income year. The flag sat beside the attributed income amount in the foreign entities item and, like it, stops after 2009-10.
description_source: ATO, Foreign investment funds guide 2010, chapter 2
value_definition: A single self-assessed flag on the supplementary return, answered before the taxpayer works out any attributable amount.
limitation: A yes does not imply an attributed amount, since the exemptions removed the income while leaving the interest in place, so the flag and the income column on the same row need not agree. A no is not proof of no offshore holding either, because an interest in a controlled foreign company was a separate question on the same row.
rationale: The DIL label is the FIF or FLP interest question from the foreign entities item. The ATO guide chapter defines both terms and the exclusions that decide who answers yes.
evidence_quote: A FIF is any foreign company or foreign trust .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Australian income year (year ending 30 June)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The Australian income year the return covers, running 1 July to 30 June and named by its closing year. The ATO's 2025 instructions are the instructions for 2024-25, so a value of 2025 means the year ended 30 June 2025. Every income, deduction, offset and levy amount on the same row belongs to that year.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025
value_definition: A year value naming the income year of the lodgement. It is the reference period for the row, not a point in time.
limitation: It is not the year the return was lodged or processed, and late or amended lodgements can arrive years afterwards; the form received date on the same row is what carries that. It is also not a calendar year, so joining to calendar-year sources without apportionment mixes two different twelve-month windows.
rationale: The ATO publishes one set of individual tax return instructions per income year, and the 2025 edition covers 2024-25, which fixes the naming convention this column follows.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the income year from the lodgement date.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 17 label E
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 17
variable_description: The net movement in the person's farm management deposits: repayments taken out less deductible deposits put in. The ATO's step is to "Add up the amounts you show at labels N and R , and subtract the amount you show at label D", where N and R are early and ordinary repayments and D is deductible deposits. Repayments count as assessable income in the year they are made, so a positive figure adds to taxable income and a negative one reduces it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 17
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed net flow for the year, assembled from the deposit and repayment labels on the same row. A negative result carries an L in a loss box.
limitation: It is a flow, not a balance, so nothing here says how much the person has on deposit or how long it has been sitting there. Non-deductible deposits are excluded from the deposit side, so a farmer can move money into the scheme without this figure moving at all.
rationale: The DIL label names the net farm management deposits or repayments amount, a single labelled question on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions give the arithmetic and the treatment of repayments as assessable income.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts you show at labels N and R , and subtract the amount you show at label D .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Count of dependent children reported at tax return item M1 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item M1
variable_description: The number of dependent children the person counted when claiming a Medicare levy reduction based on family income. The ATO instruction is to "Write the number of your dependent children (from worksheet 2 – row e ) at question M1 – label Y . If you have none, write 0 (zero)." A dependent child must be an Australian resident the person maintained and must fall under the adjusted taxable income limits for the year. Each child raises the family income threshold at which the levy starts to bite.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item M1
value_definition: A small non-negative integer, self-assessed against the ATO's dependency and income tests for that income year.
limitation: The counting rule depends on partnering status, so it is not a household child count: a person single or separated on 30 June counts only children for whom family tax benefit was paid, while a partnered person counts all of them. People who do not claim the reduction leave the label blank, so a missing value is not evidence of childlessness.
rationale: The DIL label names the Medicare levy reduction dependent children and students count, which is a single labelled question at item M1. The ATO instructions define a dependent child, give the counting rules and state the label.
evidence_quote: Write the number of your dependent children (from worksheet 2 – row e ) at question M1 – label Y . If you have none, write 0 (zero).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign investment fund and foreign life policy income under the mid-2000s foreign entities column name
value_source: ATO, Fund income tax return 2010 instructions, item 13 label D
variable_description: Income attributed to the person under the foreign investment fund rules, carried under the earlier foreign entities column name used in the mid-2000s extracts. The ATO describes the matching label as follows: "Attributed income of a FIF or FLP is the income attributed to the taxpayer from FIFs or FLPs, calculated in accordance with Part XI of the ITAA 1936." The 2009-10 extract renames the same quantity, and the rules were repealed from 2010-11.
description_source: ATO, Fund income tax return 2010 instructions, item 13 label D
value_definition: A whole-dollar accruals amount computed under Part XI of the ITAA 1936, covering both foreign investment funds and the investment component of certain foreign life policies.
limitation: Because the column was renamed between extract vintages, stacking years on the variable name alone drops either the earlier or the later half of an already short series. Attributed income is also not a distribution, so it cannot stand in for money the person actually received from offshore.
rationale: The DIL label names FIF and FLP income in the foreign entities item of the 2006-07 extract. The ATO instruction for the corresponding label on the fund return defines the attributed amount and the legislation it is worked out under.
evidence_quote: Attributed income of a FIF or FLP is the income attributed to the taxpayer from FIFs or FLPs, calculated in accordance with Part XI of the ITAA 1936.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item D11 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item D11
variable_description: The tax-free slice of a foreign pension or annuity, deducted because it returns the person's own contributions to them. The ATO explains that "That part of your annual pension or annuity income that represents a return to you of your personal contributions is free from tax", and calls that slice the deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price. It only makes sense alongside the gross foreign pension declared at item 20 on the same return.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item D11
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, normally the undeducted purchase price divided by a life expectancy factor, or a fixed country percentage such as 8% of a United Kingdom State Pension or 25% of a Dutch pension.
limitation: It is a deduction against foreign pension income rather than income itself, so adding it to an income measure inflates the total. Because several country formulas are a fixed percentage of the gross pension, the amount often moves mechanically with the pension and says nothing about what the person actually contributed.
rationale: The DIL label names the deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price of a foreign pension or annuity, which is item D11 on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions define the undeducted purchase price, the calculation and the country-specific rates.
evidence_quote: That part of your annual pension or annuity income that represents a return to you of your personal contributions is free from tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at tax return item 20 label P
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 20 Part I
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person held overseas assets worth A$50,000 or more at any point in the year. The return asks it directly: "At any time during 2024–25, do you own or have an interest in assets outside Australia that have a total value of A$50,000 or more?" It is answered at item 20 label P and carries no dollar value at all.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 20 Part I
value_definition: A single flag against a fixed A$50,000 threshold applied to the combined value of all assets located outside Australia, self-assessed by the taxpayer.
limitation: The threshold is not indexed, so the same flag stands for less real wealth every year and the share flagged drifts upward with asset prices alone. It also cannot separate a person just over A$50,000 from one with millions offshore, and anyone below the line is indistinguishable from a person with no foreign assets.
rationale: The DIL label is the foreign property indicator, which is the item 20 label P question. The ATO instructions give the question wording, the threshold and the fact that only a yes or no is recorded.
evidence_quote: At any time during 2024–25, do you own or have an interest in assets outside Australia that have a total value of A$50,000 or more?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign-sourced employee share scheme discounts reported at tax return item 12
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 12
variable_description: The part of the person's employee share scheme discount that came from a foreign employer or a foreign scheme. The ATO folds these into the scheme totals rather than treating them as extra income, telling taxpayers to add up the discounts "including amounts on your Employee share scheme statements" and "any foreign source discounts you receive" at each of the taxed-upfront and deferral labels. The column is therefore a memorandum subset of the discount figures on the same row, not an addition to them.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 12
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount already counted inside the taxed-upfront and deferral discount labels on the same row, sourced from the foreign employer's written advice where no Australian employee share scheme statement exists.
limitation: Adding it to the item 12 discount totals double counts, because it is a component of them rather than a separate income stream. The number is a discount measured at a taxing point, so it does not record what the shares were eventually worth or whether the person ever sold them.
rationale: The DIL label names employee share schemes foreign source discounts. The ATO item 12 instructions establish that foreign source discounts are added into the taxed-upfront and deferral totals, which fixes this column as a component of those amounts.
evidence_quote: Add up all the discount amounts you receive from taxed-upfront schemes eligible for reduction , including: amounts showing on your Employee share scheme statements any foreign source discounts you receive.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 20 label O
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 20 Part H
variable_description: Credit for foreign tax the person already paid on income that Australia also taxes, claimed as the foreign income tax offset. The ATO caps the simple case: "Write the total amount of foreign tax paid at question 20 – label O . Show cents. This amount can't be greater than $1,000." Above $1,000 the taxpayer works through the offset limit in the Guide to foreign income tax offset rules, so the number becomes a limited entitlement rather than raw foreign tax paid. The ATO notes the offset was "formerly foreign tax credits", which is where the column name comes from.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 20 Part H
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents offset amount, equal to total foreign tax paid where that is $1,000 or less, and equal to a calculated offset limit above that point.
limitation: The column changes meaning at $1,000, so it is a clean measure of foreign tax paid only below the threshold and a capped entitlement above it. Unused foreign income tax offset cannot be carried forward and nothing on the row records how much was forgone.
rationale: The DIL label names the foreign income tax offset at item 20. The ATO instructions give the label, the $1,000 threshold, the two ways the amount is worked out and the former name of the offset.
evidence_quote: No – Write the total amount of foreign tax paid at question 20 – label O . Show cents. This amount can't be greater than $1,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at tax return item 19 label W
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 19 Part B
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person ever transferred money, property or services to a non-resident trust. The ATO explains that the transferor trust measures "may apply if, at any time, you directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of property (including money) or services to a non-resident trust." The question reaches back over the person's whole history rather than the income year, and a yes is followed by an attributed foreign income amount on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 19 Part B
value_definition: A single lifetime flag covering direct and indirect transfers to a trust that has no Australian resident trustee and no Australian central management and control at any time in the year.
limitation: It is not a flag for holding an offshore trust interest: a beneficiary who never transferred anything answers no, and a person who controls a foreign company answers the separate controlled foreign company question instead. Because the question covers any time in the past, a yes need not relate to anything that happened in the reference year.
rationale: The DIL label is the foreign transfer indicator, which is item 19 label W. The ATO instructions give the question, the definition of a non-resident trust and what follows a yes answer.
evidence_quote: The transferor trust measures may apply if, at any time, you directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of property (including money) or services to a non-resident trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Whole hours reported at the BPI schedule label S under 'How long did it take you to complete this schedule?'
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, About these instructions
variable_description: The hours the person says it took to prepare and complete the business and professional items schedule. The ATO explains why it asks: "We are committed to reducing the costs involved in complying with your tax obligations. Your response to this item will help us monitor these costs." The count is meant to cover reading instructions, collecting information, making calculations and putting the business's affairs in order for the agent, plus the agent's own time, rounded up to the nearest hour.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, About these instructions
value_definition: A whole-hour count for one schedule, combining the taxpayer's time and their tax agent's time.
limitation: It is a compliance-cost self-report rather than a measured duration, and where an agent prepares the schedule the client's hours are the agent's estimate of someone else's effort. It covers the business schedule alone, so it is not the time taken over the whole tax return and cannot be compared with return-level compliance-cost figures.
rationale: The DIL label names the hours to complete the business and professional items section. The ATO instructions state the label, the purpose of the question and exactly which activities the taxpayer should count.
evidence_quote: We are committed to reducing the costs involved in complying with your tax obligations. Your response to this item will help us monitor these costs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Lodgement receipt date
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The date the ATO received the lodgement, which is not the date the person sent it. The gap can be large on paper: the ATO aims to process paper lodgements within 50 business days "from the date we receive the lodgment (paper lodgments may take up to 7 weeks to show on our systems)", against 12 business days online. Read against the financial year on the same row, the date separates on-time self-lodgers from agent-lodged and late returns.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A date stamped when the return entered ATO systems, not when the taxpayer signed, posted or transmitted it.
limitation: It measures ATO intake as much as taxpayer behaviour, so the paper-against-online gap makes part of any lag an artefact of lodgement channel rather than a person being late. It also cannot distinguish an original return from one re-received after a correction, so a very late date may reflect an amendment.
rationale: The variable is lodgement metadata rather than a return label. The ATO page on the notice of assessment describes the receipt of a lodgement and the delay between sending and appearing in ATO systems, which is what makes a received date different from a lodgement date.
evidence_quote: by paper, we aim for processing within 50 business days (10 weeks) from the date we receive the lodgment (paper lodgments may take up to 7 weeks to show on our systems)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a received date from the date the taxpayer lodged.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 18 label X
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 18
variable_description: Credit for tax a purchaser withheld from the person when they sold property under the foreign resident capital gains withholding rules. The ATO says the rules apply "to certain transactions entered into on or after 1 July 2016", so the column is empty in earlier years as a matter of law. The buyer withholds and remits the amount, the ATO tells the seller it has been received, and the seller claims it back at item 18 label X.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 18
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit against tax, recorded from ATO advice to the seller rather than worked out by the taxpayer. It is deliberately kept out of the business withholding credits at item 15.
limitation: Its presence means a property transaction was caught by the rules, not that the seller was a foreign resident, because Australian residents who did not give the purchaser a clearance certificate also have amounts withheld. Nothing on the row gives the sale price, the gain or whether the seller ended up with a refund.
rationale: The DIL label names the capital gains credit for foreign resident capital gains withholding amounts, which is item 18 label X. The ATO instructions state the start date of the rules, who withholds and where the credit is claimed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item D14 label F
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item D14
variable_description: A deduction for payments the person made into a forestry managed investment scheme. value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction covering initial and ongoing scheme payments for an initial participant, and ongoing payments only for a subsequent participant.

rationale: The DIL label names the forestry managed investment scheme deduction, which is item D14 on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions give the label, the eligibility test and the excluded payments.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 23 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 23
variable_description: Income the person received from a forestry managed investment scheme, including thinning and harvest proceeds. The ATO directs the taxpayer to show "the total income from forestry interests you hold in an FMIS" at item 23 label A, and to bring in the market value of the interest, rather than any cash, where a capital gains tax event ends or reduces their holding. It is the income leg of the same investment the D14 deduction pays for.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 23
value_definition: A whole-dollar total covering thinning receipts and, where a capital gains tax event happens, the market value of the interest given up or the reduction in its market value.

It only reaches this item where a deduction was claimed or claimable, so scheme investments with no deduction history are invisible here.
rationale: The DIL label names forestry managed investment scheme income, which is item 23 on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions define what the label carries for initial and subsequent participants.
evidence_quote: Show at question 23 – label A the total income from forestry interests you hold in an FMIS from the following activities: Initial participants Subsequent participants .

limitation: Because it is inside total expenses, adding the two together counts the same spending twice. The allocation of costs to one income stream is the taxpayer's own, so a business with mixed income can put very different amounts here without changing anything real.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 13 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F
variable_description: The person's share of tax withheld inside a partnership or trust under the foreign resident withholding rules. The ATO directs it to item 13 label A where the distribution includes income the person derives "as a foreign resident from which an amount of tax is withheld because of the operation of the foreign resident withholding rules". In the current form the same label also absorbs non-resident withholding tax and managed investment trust withholding, so the box is now wider than its original wording.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents credit, being the person's share of amounts withheld before the partnership or trust distributed the income, claimed against their own assessment.
limitation: The label widened over time to take in managed investment trust and non-resident withholding, so a series stacked across years is not one consistent quantity even though the column name never changed. The figure is a credit, not income, and the underlying gross distribution is at labels O, U or C on the same row.

value_domain: abs_address_coding_index_identifier
value_source: ABS Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, 'Geocoding unit record data using address and location'
variable_description: Which address coding index placed the taxpayer's return address into the geography columns on this row. The ABS matches administrative addresses to the Geocoded National Address File, "the authoritative list of Australian addresses and locations coordinates", and this column identifies the release of the index used. ARID_HASH_TRUNC on the same row is the address that was matched, and MB_CODE_2021, SA1_CODE_2021, SA2_CODE_2021 and LGA_CODE_2024 are what came back. Because the index is versioned, this is the column that explains why one address can code differently in two income years.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, SSF Guidance Material - Geocoding Unit Record Data Using Address and Location
value_definition: A short identifier for one release of the coding index. Neither the ATO nor the ABS publishes the identifiers, so the codes have to be read from the data rather than looked up.
limitation: It is neither a geography nor a date. The index release does not tell you which ASGS edition the mesh block and SA1 codes on the row belong to, and the two can disagree, so the geography columns' own names remain the authority on vintage.
rationale: The ABS matches reported addresses to a dated G-NAF based coding index, so this field names which index was used; sibling ATO_CR field IN_MAY_24 ('coded to the May 2024 ASGS index') shows the indexes are identified by vintage, but no list of index identifiers is published, so no values can be given.
evidence_quote: the geocoding system should use a G-NAF based coding index
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination gave no concept; the concept is now identified even though the domain remains unenumerable.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item D9 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item D9
variable_description: The total the person claimed as a deduction for gifts and donations. The claim is tightly bounded: "To claim a deduction for gifts or donations you make, you need a receipt from an organisation that has a deductible gift recipient (DGR) status", and the gift must be $2 or more. Contributions to registered political parties, independent candidates and independent members go here too. Donations made under a salary sacrifice arrangement, and payments where the giver got something in return, cannot be claimed at all.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item D9
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of deductible gifts, taking in workplace giving already shown on the income statement and up to $10 of unreceipted bucket donations.
limitation: It measures deductible giving, not giving: donations to non-deductible causes, crowdfunding appeals and religious tithing sit outside it, so it understates generosity by an unknown and probably uneven amount. It is a self-assessed claim, so it records what was put on the return rather than what was substantiated.
rationale: The DIL label names gifts or donations, which is item D9. The ATO instructions state the receipt and deductible gift recipient requirement, the $2 floor, the political contribution rules and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: To claim a deduction for gifts or donations you make, you need a receipt from an organisation that has a deductible gift recipient (DGR) status.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of beneficiary tax offset applied in the assessment
value_source: ATO, Beneficiary tax offset
variable_description: The part of the beneficiary tax offset that was actually used to reduce the person's tax, not the part they were entitled to. The offset exists so that certain Australian Government allowances attract no tax when they are the person's only income. Nothing here is claimed by the taxpayer: "We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return." Because the offset is not refundable, the used amount is capped by the tax otherwise payable.
description_source: ATO, Beneficiary tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset amount worked out by the ATO from the qualifying Australian Government allowance and payment income declared on the return and the person's other taxable income, then limited to the tax that would otherwise be payable.
limitation: It is the offset used, so it understates entitlement whenever tax payable is the binding constraint, and it is exactly zero for the people whose incomes are lowest. Where a person qualifies for both this and the seniors and pensioners tax offset only the larger one is applied, so a zero can mean the other offset won rather than that no entitlement existed.
rationale: The DIL label names the government allowance beneficiary tax offset used, and the ATO page for that offset states who receives it, that the ATO calculates it, that tax must be payable for it to be used, and how it interacts with the seniors and pensioners offset.
evidence_quote: We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Whole-dollar gross payment amount on the PAYG payment summary - individual non-business
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Gross pay the employer reported for the person on a PAYG payment summary, before any tax was withheld. The ATO tells payers to "Include all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder. Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld." Anything shown separately on the summary as an allowance, a lump sum payment or a reportable fringe benefits amount stays outside this figure, and salary-sacrificed amounts are left out entirely.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payer over one reported period, reported by the employer rather than the employee, alongside a period start and end date on the same row.
limitation: It covers one job over one period, so a person with several employers has several rows and no single row is their annual employment income. Because salary sacrifice is stripped out before reporting, the figure understates what the employer paid for the person and understates their pre-sacrifice earnings by an amount that never appears anywhere on the row.
rationale: The table this variable sits in carries the individual non-business income type, lump sum A to E and total allowances fields of the PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, and the ATO instructions for that form define the gross payments box.
evidence_quote: Include all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder. Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 10 label L
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 10
variable_description: All the interest the person received or was credited from Australian sources during the year. The ATO requires it gross of withholding: where a bank took TFN amounts because no tax file number was given, "You must show these amounts as gross interest in your tax return." Interest distributed through a partnership or trust belongs at item 13 instead, and foreign interest at item 20. Joint account holders show only their own share.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 10
value_definition: A whole-dollar total across all Australian sources, taking in ATO interest on early payments and overpayments and interest on children's accounts the person effectively controls.
limitation: It is not all the interest a household earned: cash management trust and other trust distributions sit elsewhere, and totals under $1 are not written at all. The share of a joint account is self-allocated, so two people can split the same account unevenly and neither return shows the account balance.
rationale: The DIL label names gross interest, which is item 10 label L. The ATO instructions define the scope, the gross basis, the exclusions and the joint account rule.
evidence_quote: TFN amounts are amounts of tax withheld by financial institutions because you didn't give them your TFN or ABN. TFN amounts show on your statement or document as 'Commonwealth tax' or 'TFN withholding tax'. You must show these amounts as gross interest in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income, labour hire and specified payments totals box
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: All payments the sole trader received in the year under labour hire arrangements or as specified payments, with tax withheld included. The ATO defines the underlying label as follows: "The amount you show at P8 Income – label O is the total income you receive from labour hire or specified payments and includes the tax that is withheld." Specified payments are a short statutory list: performing artists in promotional activity, Indigenous Student Success Programme tutoring, and translating and interpreting services.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross total across the primary production and non-primary production labels beside it, built by adding the payment summary schedule rows typed S.
limitation: Because the primary production half is expected to be blank, this total is effectively one of the two columns it sums, so treating all three as independent inputs counts the same dollars repeatedly. It also cannot be split back into labour hire and the three specified payment types.
rationale: The DIL label names the total gross labour hire or other specified payments at P8. The ATO income instructions define the amount, state that it includes withheld tax and list the specified payments.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at P8 Income – label O is the total income you receive from labour hire or specified payments and includes the tax that is withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 1, Income column
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 1
variable_description: The person's total salary and wages for the year, added across every income statement and payment summary. The ATO scopes item 1 as income "from salary or wages where tax was withheld", which takes in commissions, bonuses, part-time and casual work, parental leave pay, and lost-wage payments under income protection, sickness and accident or workers compensation arrangements. Allowances are excluded and belong at item 2. The label is a calculated total, so it aggregates the payer rows rather than naming one employer.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 1
value_definition: A whole-dollar total across payers, self-assessed but assembled from employer-reported income statements that the ATO pre-fills.
limitation: It is not total employment income: allowances, employment termination payments, employer lump sums and any business or personal services income are separate items, and amounts salary sacrificed to superannuation never appear anywhere on the return. Foreign employment income only lands here for a narrow class of Australian Government employees.
rationale: The DIL label is salary or wages, which is item 1 of the individual return. The ATO instructions define the income types included, the exclusions and the way multiple payment summaries are combined into the reported figure.
evidence_quote: Declare at this question income from salary or wages where tax was withheld
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label D
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Non-farm business income the sole trader received from payers who withheld tax because no ABN was quoted. The ATO defines the pair of labels as "the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN", and label D is the non-primary production half. The taxpayer builds it from the payment summary schedule rows typed N. Completing the label obliges the person to claim the matching credit at item 15 label W.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of the tax withheld, built by adding payment summary schedule rows typed N that came from non-primary production activities.
limitation: A non-zero value marks a registration or paperwork failure rather than a level of activity, so it cannot be read as a measure of contracting income. It also cannot say whether the person had no ABN at all or simply failed to quote one on that job.
rationale: The DIL label names gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, non-primary production, which is P8 Income label D. The ATO income instructions define the label, give the type-box coding that produces it and state the credit that must be claimed alongside it.
evidence_quote: The amounts you show at P8 Income – labels C and D is the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label C
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Farming, fishing or forestry income the sole trader received from payers who withheld tax because no ABN was quoted. The taxpayer builds it by adding "all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box." The split from the non-primary production half matters because primary production income runs through separate averaging and farm concession rules later in the assessment.

value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of withheld tax, covering primary production activities only.
limitation: The primary production tag comes from the taxpayer's own classification of the activity when they fill in the payment summary schedule, not from the payer, so the split against the non-primary production column is self-assessed. The column also says nothing about the size of the farm business, only about payments where an ABN went unquoted.
rationale: The DIL label names gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, primary production, which is P8 Income label C. The ATO income instructions give the exact addition and the type-box coding that produces it.
evidence_quote: Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box. Write the total at P8 Income – label C on your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income, ABN not quoted totals box
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: All the sole trader's business income for the year from which tax was withheld for failure to quote an ABN. It is the totals box of the pair: the ATO says to "Add up the amounts you have written at labels C and D and enter the total in the adjacent Totals box." Reaching this label at all means a payer had to withhold at source, and the ATO then requires the person to claim the matching credit at item 15 label W in the supplementary return.

value_definition: A whole-dollar gross total covering both the primary production and non-primary production ABN-not-quoted labels on the same row, inclusive of the tax withheld.
limitation: Because it is the sum of the two columns beside it, using all three together counts the same dollars three times. The total cannot be converted into the tax withheld, which is a separate credit label reported to the cent at item 15.
rationale: The DIL label names the total gross payments where an ABN was not quoted at P8. The ATO income instructions give the addition that produces the totals box and the credit label that must be completed with it.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts you have written at labels C and D and enter the total in the adjacent Totals box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label O
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income

rationale: The DIL label names gross labour hire or other specified payments, non-primary production, which is P8 Income label O. The ATO income instructions give the type-box coding, the exclusion of employees and the expectation that the primary production label stays blank.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label N
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Labour hire and specified payments the sole trader attributed to farming, fishing or forestry work. The ATO expects the box to stay empty: "It is expected you'll not have any primary production amounts at this question. Leave P8 Income – label N blank." The column exists because the schedule prints a primary production and a non-primary production box on every income row, not because the payment types arise in agriculture.

value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount that mirrors the non-primary production labour hire label but is left blank by design on the ATO's own instruction.
limitation: A non-zero value is more likely a form-filling error than a distinct kind of income, so it should not be read as agricultural labour hire. Being near-empty, it is unsafe as a denominator or as the base of a share.
rationale: The DIL label names gross labour hire or other specified payments, primary production, which is P8 Income label N. The ATO income instructions state directly that the label is expected to be left blank.
evidence_quote: It is expected you'll not have any primary production amounts at this question. Leave P8 Income – label N blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income

The ATO defines it as follows: "The amount you show at label B is the total income you receive from your payers that is subject to foreign resident withholding. Completing the label requires the matching credit at item 15 label E.

evidence_quote: The amount you show at label B is the total income you receive from your payers that is subject to foreign resident withholding. It includes any amounts of tax withheld.

value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income

value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of withheld tax, present only in the earliest extract vintage and paired with the non-primary production column on the same row.
limitation: With so few occurrences the column cannot support a rate, a share or a trend, and a single unusual return would dominate any statistic built from it. Its disappearance records a change in the schedule's layout, not a change in who was subject to foreign resident withholding.
rationale: The DIL label names gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding, primary production. The ATO P8 income instructions show that the current schedule carries only a non-primary production label for this row, which is what identifies this column as the older form's counterpart.

value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income

rationale: The DIL label names gross payments under a voluntary agreement, non-primary production, which is P8 Income label F. The ATO income instructions define the amount and the ATO payment summary guidance defines a voluntary agreement.
evidence_quote: The amounts you show at P8 Income – labels E and F is the total income you receive that is subject to a voluntary agreement to withhold tax and include the tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label E
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Farming, fishing or forestry income the sole trader received under a pay as you go voluntary agreement to withhold tax. It is built by adding "all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule derived from primary production activities that have a V in the Type box." The primary production half is kept separate because that income later runs through the income averaging rules.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of the tax withheld, covering primary production activities only and paired with the non-primary production voluntary agreement label.
