value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, termination value of intangible depreciating assets
variable_description: What the business got for intangible assets it stopped holding or using during the year, such as software or a patent sold, lost or scrapped. The ATO defines the amount as follows: "Generally, the termination value is the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using." Non-cash consideration counts at market value, and a non-arm's length sale is brought back to market value. It pairs with the first-deducted cost column as the disposal side of the same asset class.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, termination value of intangible depreciating assets
value_definition: A dollar amount summed over all intangible assets disposed of across the person's businesses, gross of any balancing adjustment. It is proceeds, not profit.
limitation: The gain or loss on disposal is not here: the balancing adjustment worked out against the asset's adjustable value is dealt with in the reconciliation labels. Assets in the general small business pool, low-cost assets written off immediately, and software in a development pool are all excluded, so this understates disposals for a pooling business.
rationale: The schedule instruction defines termination value for this label and lists what is excluded from the total.
evidence_quote: Generally, the termination value is the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that termination value is disposal proceeds, or which pooled assets are left out of the total.

value_domain: Deceased estate flag on the return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, completing individual information
variable_description: Whether this return was lodged on behalf of someone who had died, rather than by the taxpayer. The ATO's instruction is that "If you're completing a tax return for someone who has died: write Deceased estate on the top of page 1 in the tax return", and the executor or administrator signs it. The return still covers the person's own income up to the date of death.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, completing individual information
value_definition: A flag on the return record, set where the return is lodged for a person who has died. Its natural companion is the answer to whether an Australian return will be needed in future, which the same instruction says to mark as no.
limitation: It marks the return, not the death: there is no date of death here, and a final return can be lodged in the financial year after the person died, so the flag can appear in a later year than the death. Income the estate earns after death goes on a separate trust return and never appears on this row.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the individual information section is where the deceased estate marking is defined and says who signs the return.
evidence_quote: If you're completing a tax return for someone who has died: write Deceased estate on the top of page 1 in the tax return
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the flag marks a return lodged by an executor rather than a recorded date of death.

value_domain: ATO salary and wage occupation code (6 digits)
value_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
variable_description: The occupation the taxpayer nominated for their main wage or salary job, as a six-digit code. The ATO requires that you "provide an accurate description of the main salary and wage occupation at question 1 of the individual tax return and insert the appropriate 6-digit code", and where a person has more than one job the code describes the one that pays most. The codes follow the ABS occupation classification, so an ambulance officer is 411111 and an unlisted job is 999000.
description_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
value_definition: A six-digit code from the ATO's published salary and wage occupation list, keyed to the ANZSCO structure. Codes are revised year to year as the published list is reissued.
limitation: It covers wage and salary work only, so a sole trader, a retiree or an investor with no employment income carries no meaningful code, and 999000 is a genuine answer rather than a missing value. Because the taxpayer or their agent picks the code, it records how the job was described at lodgment, not an audited occupation.
rationale: The ATO publishes the code list for this label and states the six-digit format, the main-job rule and the not-listed fallback.
evidence_quote: You must provide an accurate description of the main salary and wage occupation at question 1 of the individual tax return and insert the appropriate 6-digit code from the list at question 1 – label X .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the code is six digits from a published ATO list and describes only the person's main wage job.

value_domain: Sex or gender recorded on the ATO client record
value_source: ATO, Update your gender (tax file number registration details)
variable_description: The sex the ATO holds for the taxpayer, carried onto the return record from their tax file number registration rather than asked as a question on the form. The register is not limited to two states: "You also have the option to record your gender (sex) as indeterminate in your ATO record." Changing it requires documents such as a passport, a birth certificate or a practitioner's statement, so the value is sticky and lags a person's own change.
description_source: ATO, Update your gender (tax file number registration details)
value_definition: A short code for sex or gender as registered with the ATO. Male, female and indeterminate are the states the ATO documents; the stored characters are not published.
limitation: It is a registration attribute, not a statement made in the year of the return, so it can be out of date and it changes only when the person lodges documents. It is also not a sex recorded at birth nor a Census-style gender question, so it should not be treated as either.
rationale: The ATO page on updating gender establishes that the ATO holds sex or gender against the tax file number record, names indeterminate as an available state, and sets out the evidence needed to change it. That the income tax return record inherits the value rather than asking the question is an inference from the return forms, which carry no such question.
evidence_quote: You also have the option to record your gender (sex) as indeterminate in your ATO record.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said where the value comes from, or that the ATO records a third state alongside male and female.

value_domain: Decoded sex or gender label from the ATO client record
value_source: ATO, Update your gender (tax file number registration details)
variable_description: The sex or gender the ATO holds for the taxpayer, stored as a readable label rather than as a code. The underlying record is the ATO's own registration attribute, which the ATO will change only on documentary evidence and which can also be set to indeterminate. It appears in a later year of the return tables than the coded column, and where both appear they are two renderings of one field rather than two variables.
description_source: ATO, Update your gender (tax file number registration details)
value_definition: A decoded text label for sex or gender, such as the words the ATO uses for male, female and indeterminate. The exact strings are not published.
limitation: Decoding hides a distinction the code kept: an unknown, a not-stated and a genuine indeterminate can all resolve to similar text, so the label cannot be used to count non-binary registrations. Comparing it across years to the coded column risks reading a change of storage as a change of population.
rationale: The same ATO page supports what the underlying register holds and how it is changed. That the DCD suffix marks a decoded rendering of the coded column is an inference from the pair of variables sitting in the same table family.
evidence_quote: We can't change your recorded gender (sex) over the phone unless we have recorded it incorrectly from an identity document supplied at registration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the decoded twin of the coded sex column rather than a separate measure.

value_domain: Medicare levy reduction amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: The dollar amount by which this person's Medicare levy was cut because family income was low, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed. The ATO states plainly: "We work out the reduction for you, using your spouse details and number of dependent children." Eligibility rests on the combined taxable income of the person and their spouse and on how many dependent children they have, which is why the label describes an individual share of a family entitlement.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
value_definition: A dollar amount subtracted from the 2% levy on taxable income, tapering to zero as family taxable income rises through the year's threshold band.
limitation: A reduction is not an exemption: a person exempt on medical or foreign residence grounds records that at a different label and can show nothing here. The amount also gives no reading of family income, because two families at different incomes inside the taper can produce the same reduction.
rationale: The M1 instruction sets out the family taxable income test, the dependent children count and the fact that the ATO calculates the reduction from the spouse details on the return.
evidence_quote: We work out the reduction for you, using your spouse details and number of dependent children.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the reduction is calculated by the ATO from family taxable income, or how it differs from an exemption.

value_domain: Spouse's gender as reported in the spouse details section
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The gender the taxpayer reported for their spouse in the spouse details section of their own return. The instruction is explicit about the categories: "Print X in the relevant box for your spouse's gender (male, female or indeterminate). Indeterminate includes non-binary." The ATO asks for it to help match the spouse to their own record, so it sits with the spouse's name, date of birth and taxable income on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A three-state code for male, female or indeterminate, reported by the taxpayer about another person. It exists only on returns where a spouse is declared for part or all of the year.
limitation: It is a report about someone else, so it can disagree with what the spouse records on their own return, and it is not evidence of how the spouse identifies. Its absence means no spouse was declared for the year, which is not the same as being single on 30 June.
rationale: The spouse details instruction names the three categories for this exact box and explains why the ATO collects it.
evidence_quote: Print X in the relevant box for your spouse's gender (male, female or indeterminate ). Indeterminate includes non-binary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that a third category exists or that the answer is given by the taxpayer about their spouse.

value_domain: Franking credit amount at question 11 label U (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends
variable_description: The company tax already paid on the taxpayer's franked dividends, reported at the franking credit label and known in older wording as an imputation credit. The ATO defines it as follows: "Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution." It counts twice on the return, once as assessable income and once as a credit: "You also receive a tax credit on your tax assessment for an amount equal to the franking credits."
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends
value_definition: A dollar amount taken from dividend statements, added to the franked and unfranked dividend labels on the same row and also carried to the credits side of the assessment.
limitation: It is not a payment the person received, so treating it as cash income overstates their means, and treating it as tax paid by them attributes a company's tax to a household. It is also not automatic: the holding period, related payments and dividend washing rules can deny it, and the label does not record whether they applied.
rationale: The question 11 instruction defines franking credits, states that they are both assessable and creditable, and names the rules that can deny them.
evidence_quote: Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is company tax attributed to the shareholder and appears on both sides of the assessment.

value_domain: Individual non-business income type
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business
variable_description: What kind of individual non-business payment this row records. The individual non-business payment summary is the form an employer gives to "workers or payees who are employees, company directors or office holders", and it carries pensions and annuities, Commonwealth benefits and allowances, compensation and sickness payments and working holiday maker earnings alongside ordinary salary. Treating every row on this form as wages counts pensions and benefits as employment income.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business
limitation: The ATO publishes the form but not the codes PLIDA uses for the income type, so the mapping is not confirmed. The distinctions this column carries are precisely the ones that matter for measuring employment, so the gap is a real constraint.
rationale: The field is named as an individual non-business income type on the payment summary tables. The ATO publishes what the form covers but not the type codes.
evidence_quote: if you make payments to workers or payees who are employees, company directors or office holders
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Individual non-business income type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Small business share of taxable income used for the offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: The part of the person's taxable income the ATO attributed to unincorporated small business, used to work out their small business income tax offset. The ATO describes the mechanism as follows: "The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income", built from sole trader net small business income plus any share from a small business partnership or trust. The proportion is capped at one, so this amount never exceeds taxable income on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by the ATO from the return, not a label the taxpayer fills in. It is net of business deductions, excludes salary, wages and net capital gains, and is treated as zero when the business made a loss.
limitation: It is a calculation input, not income the person can spend, and it is not added to taxable income anywhere. It also exists only for years and turnovers in which the offset ran, so a blank can mean an ineligible business rather than none: the turnover threshold was $2 million in 2015-16 before rising to $5 million.
rationale: The ATO offset page defines net small business income, the proportion used and the eligibility thresholds by year, which is what this derived column measures.
evidence_quote: The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is an ATO-derived input to the small business income tax offset rather than reported income.

value_domain: Total income or loss on the return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Subtotal
variable_description: Everything the taxpayer declared as income for the year, added up before any deduction is taken off. The return works down from it: the ATO says to "subtract the amount at Total deductions from the amount at Total income or loss" and write the result at Subtotal, which after earlier-year losses becomes taxable income. It gathers the twelve income questions on the main return and the supplement total on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Subtotal
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum of the income labels across the main return and the supplement, which can be negative and is then flagged as a loss.
limitation: It is a gross figure, so it is not a measure of what the household kept: a sole trader with $400,000 of turnover-driven income and $390,000 of deductions looks wealthy here and poor at taxable income. It also excludes non-assessable amounts such as most redundancy tax-free components and many government payments, so it is not total receipts either.
rationale: The subtotal instruction states the arithmetic relationship between this line, total deductions and the rest of the assessment, which is what fixes its meaning as a pre-deduction total.
evidence_quote: subtract the amount at Total deductions from the amount at Total income or loss
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is measured before deductions and sits above taxable income in the return's arithmetic.

value_domain: Income reconciliation adjustment at P8 label X (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items
variable_description: The bridge between the business's accounting income and its taxable income, added or subtracted at the reconciliation label. The ATO puts the arithmetic simply: "Your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions." Add-backs are assessable amounts missing from the accounts, such as balancing adjustments on asset disposals; subtractions are book income that is exempt or not assessable. The figure is the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns and can be negative.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items
value_definition: A dollar amount, signed, that is the net of add-backs and subtractions across both production columns. Its sibling column at label H does the same job for expenses.
limitation: It measures a difference between two accounting bases, so its size says nothing about the size of the business, and a large adjustment is a sign of accounting treatment rather than of profitability. A zero does not mean the accounts and the tax law agreed, because add-backs and subtractions can cancel out.
rationale: The P8 reconciliation instruction defines the adjustment, lists the add-backs and subtractions that make it up, and names the label it is written at.
evidence_quote: Your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount reconciles accounting profit to taxable income and can be negative.

value_domain: Total supplement income or loss (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss
variable_description: The income total from the supplementary return, covering the parts of a person's affairs the main return does not reach. The ATO builds it by adding "all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24" and subtracting the losses from partnerships and trusts, farm deposits, foreign income and rent. It is then carried to label I on the main return, which is where it joins wages, interest and dividends in total income or loss.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss
value_definition: A dollar amount, signed, that nets the supplement's income and loss questions. It is present only where the person lodged a supplementary return.
limitation: It is a mixed bag rather than a category: business, rent, capital gains, foreign income and one-off other income all land in the one number, so a change in it cannot be read as a change in any of them. A blank means no supplement was lodged, not that the person had no investments.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists exactly which supplement questions are added and subtracted to form this line and where it is transferred.
evidence_quote: Add up all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13 , 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 and 24 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which questions feed the total, or that losses on the supplement are netted off within it.

value_domain: ato_stp_income_type
values: ["SAW: salary and wages","CHP: closely held payees","WHM: working holiday makers","FEI: foreign employment income","IAA: inbound assignees to Australia","SWP: seasonal worker programs","JPD: joint petroleum development area","VOL: voluntary agreement","LAB: labour hire","OSP: other specified payments"]
value_source: ATO Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, 'Income types'
variable_description: The income type the employer assigned to the payments on this row when reporting them through Single Touch Payroll. The code separates ordinary wages from income taxed under different rules, such as working holiday maker earnings or foreign employment income. The ATO makes the residual nature of the main code plain: "If the payments you are making to your employee don't belong in one of the other specific income types, use the SAW income type." The table holds one row per payer per year, with ABN_HASH_TRUNC naming the employer and SW_GRS_PMT_AMT and SW_TW_AMT carrying the amounts.

Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination assumed a private ATO codeframe; the ATO publishes the income type codes in the STP Phase 2 guidelines.

value_domain: Financial year of the return (income year)
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, glossary entry Income year
variable_description: The financial year the return reports on, which for individuals runs from 1 July to 30 June. The ATO's own definition allows for exceptions: an income year "is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act". It is the year the income was earned, not the year the return was lodged or assessed.
description_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, glossary entry Income year
value_definition: A year identifier for a 1 July to 30 June period, usually stored as the ending year or as a paired label such as 2010-11.
limitation: It is not a lodgment date and not a payment date, so a return for an early year can be lodged years late and still carry that year here. Amended assessments also keep the original income year, so a row cannot tell you which version of the assessment it reflects.
rationale: The ATO glossary gives the statutory meaning of an income year, including the substituted accounting period exception, which is what this column identifies.
evidence_quote: An income year - or year of income - is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the year is the year income was earned rather than the year the return was lodged.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on internet selling
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return instructions 2014, question 4 Did you sell any goods or services using the internet?
variable_description: Whether the business used the internet to take orders, take payment or deliver what it sold, answered yes or no on the business and professional items schedule. The ATO drew the line at transacting rather than having a web presence: you tick no if you used the internet only to "advertise your goods or services, give support to your customers, buy your stock, do your banking". The question ran on the individual, partnership and trust returns and was dropped from the schedule in later years.
description_source: ATO, Trust tax return instructions 2014, question 4 Did you sell any goods or services using the internet?
value_definition: A two-state self-assessed indicator. The cited wording is the trust return's version of the identically worded question, because the individual schedule's own page has been retired from the ATO site.
limitation: It is a yes-or-no about method, so it measures neither how much was sold online nor whether the business had a website; a shop taking one order by email answers the same as a full online retailer. Because the question was removed from the schedule, a blank in later years means the question was not asked rather than that the answer was no.
rationale: The ATO page for the identically worded question on the trust return sets out both the yes conditions and the narrower no conditions, which is what fixes the meaning of the individual schedule's label. The individual schedule's own instruction page for this item is no longer served.
evidence_quote: Print X in the No box at Q , if you used the internet only to: advertise your goods or services, give support to your customers, buy your stock, do your banking.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said where the line between selling online and merely advertising online was drawn.

value_domain: Interest deductions claimed at question D7 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D7 Interest income deductions
variable_description: What the taxpayer claimed as the cost of earning interest income, such as account fees and interest on money borrowed to invest. The ATO ties the claim to the income it produced: "To claim a deduction for interest income expenses, you must incur expenses in earning interest from any source in Australia." Deductions against dividends go to the next question instead, and interest costs inside a business, a rental property or a trust distribution are claimed elsewhere again.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D7 Interest income deductions
value_definition: A dollar amount claimed against the gross interest label on the same return. Joint account holders show only their own share.
limitation: It is a self-assessed claim, not an audited expense, and it is not the interest the person paid on their home or their business loans. The narrowness matters: the interest on a margin loan against shares belongs at the dividend question, so a small figure here does not mean small investment borrowing.
rationale: The D7 instruction defines the deductible expenses for this label and states which interest costs belong at other questions.
evidence_quote: To claim a deduction for interest income expenses, you must incur expenses in earning interest from any source in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which costs qualify or that dividend-related interest belongs at a different question.

value_domain: Combined interest and dividend deductions on the earlier return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, questions D7 and D8
variable_description: One combined claim for the costs of earning both interest and dividends, as the earlier editions of the return recorded them in a single item. The current return splits the same ground across two questions, D7 for interest income deductions and D8 for dividend deductions, and the ATO's apportionment rule shows they are treated as one pool of investment cost: a shared computer's decline in value is claimed "once, at either question D7 or D8". A series that spans the split therefore has to add the two later columns to match this one.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, questions D7 and D8
value_definition: A dollar amount covering account fees, investment advice and borrowing costs against both interest and dividend income, before the return separated the two.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed: nothing in the row says how much of the claim belonged to shares as against deposits, which is exactly the split later returns record. Comparing it directly with the later interest-only column understates the earlier years' investment costs.
rationale: The current D7 and D8 instructions define the two deductions and show that the ATO treats them as one apportionment pool, which is what makes a combined earlier column readable. That this column is the combined earlier item is inferred from the custodian's own label wording rather than from a published page.
evidence_quote: you can claim only the proportion of the decline in value relating to managing those investments once, at either question D7 or D8
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the column combines two claims the later return reports separately.

value_domain: Overseas interest expenses at P8, total column (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
variable_description: Interest the business paid to overseas lenders, totalled across its primary production and non-primary production activities. The schedule keeps two columns and one total: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production overseas interest expenses and write the total at label R." It is deliberately separated from interest paid within Australia, which sits in its own label on the same schedule, because overseas interest carries withholding and thin capitalisation consequences.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the sum of the two production columns on the expenses page of the schedule. Label letters have moved between editions of the schedule.
limitation: It is business interest only, so a sole trader's investment or home borrowing never reaches it, and it does not say whether withholding tax was paid or whether a debt deduction was later denied. A denial under the thin capitalisation rules is added back in the reconciliation labels, leaving this figure unchanged.
rationale: The P8 expenses instruction names this label, states that it is the total of the two production columns, and separates it from interest paid within Australia.
evidence_quote: Add up your primary production and non-primary production overseas interest expenses and write the total at label R .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount totals two production columns, or why overseas interest is reported apart from domestic interest.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on interests in foreign entities
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer had a controlling interest in a foreign company or had moved property or services to a non-resident trust. The controlled foreign company test is a control test, not an income test: the ATO asks whether you have "direct or indirect controlling interests totalling 10% or more in a foreign company" or effective control of one. The transferor trust question is answered separately at the same item, and each yes opens an attributed income label beside it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
value_definition: A self-assessed indicator against the foreign entities question. On the current return the two limbs are two boxes; this column carries the answer without separating them.
limitation: A yes says control or a transfer existed, not that any income was attributed, and a taxpayer can answer yes with a nil attributed amount. Simply holding foreign shares, a foreign bank account or an interest below the control threshold produces a no, so it is not a marker of foreign investment.
rationale: The question 19 instruction sets out both limbs of the foreign entities question, the 10% control test and the attributed income labels that follow a yes. Which limb a single combined indicator reflects is not published, and that is stated rather than assumed.
evidence_quote: direct or indirect controlling interests totalling 10% or more in a foreign company
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the question turns on a 10% control test and on transfers to non-resident trusts.

value_domain: Australian interest expenses at P8, total column (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
variable_description: Interest the business paid to Australian lenders, totalled across primary production and non-primary production. The schedule adds the two columns into one figure: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production interest expenses within Australia and show the total at label Q." For most sole traders it is the largest financing cost on the schedule and the counterpart to the overseas interest label beside it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the sum of the two production columns. It is the deduction claimed in the accounts, before any reconciliation adjustment.
limitation: It says nothing about how much was borrowed or at what rate, and it excludes non-business interest, which is claimed at the personal deduction questions instead. Because a sole trader can hold the same loan for mixed purposes, the split between this label and personal interest reflects the taxpayer's own apportionment.
rationale: The P8 expenses instruction names this label and states that it is the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns.
evidence_quote: Add up your primary production and non-primary production interest expenses within Australia and show the total at label Q .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is a business financing cost totalled over two production columns.

value_domain: Income from investment, partnership and other sources at question A3 label F (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions
variable_description: The taxpayer's non-employment income, worked out for the government super co-contribution test rather than for tax. The ATO's step is to "Transfer the amount at row y to question A3 - label F Income from investment, partnership and other sources", gathering interest, dividends, franking credits, trust and partnership distributions, foreign income, rent and life insurance bonuses. It sits opposite the employment and business income label, and the pair decide whether at least 10% of total income came from work.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions
value_definition: A dollar amount assembled from worksheets rather than transcribed from a single label, covering the investment and other income components of total income for co-contribution purposes.
limitation: It is not a component of taxable income and does not appear in the assessment, so adding it to income labels elsewhere on the return double counts. A zero can be a genuine nil or a code the taxpayer prints when the worksheet result is nil, so it cannot be read as an absence of investments.
rationale: The A3 instruction defines this label, lists the income types the worksheet collects for it, and explains the 10% employment income test it serves.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount at row y to question A3 – label F Income from investment, partnership and other sources . If row y is 0 (zero), print C in the CODE box at label F .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is assembled for the super co-contribution income test rather than for the assessment.

value_domain: ato_itr_a3_code_box
values: ["C: the amount at F item A3 (income from investment, partnership and other sources) is zero","(blank): the amount is not zero"]

variable_description: The code box beside the super co-contribution label where the taxpayer reported income from investment, partnership and other sources. It marks a genuine nil rather than classifying the income: TaxPack 2010 says "If (v) is 0, print C in the CODE box at F." The ATO needs the distinction because the co-contribution test weighs income from employment against total income, so a zero and a blank produce different entitlements. The dollar amount itself sits at the matching label on the return, not in this column.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2010 (NAT 0976-6.2010), question A3 Super co-contribution, label F
value_definition: A one letter box that is either C, meaning the amount at label F is zero, or empty, meaning it is not zero.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as a nil return. It is left empty both by a taxpayer with a positive amount and by one who never had to answer the co-contribution question, so the column cannot be used to identify who was tested for the co-contribution.

value_domain: Small business share of income tax liability used for the offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: The part of the person's basic income tax liability the ATO attributed to small business income, which is the base the offset percentage is applied to. The ATO caps what comes out of it: "Your offset will be your rate of offset of the following amount, up to the limit of $1,000." It is the tax counterpart of the small business share of taxable income on the same row, and the offset rate applied to it rose from 5% in 2015-16 to 16% from 2021-22.
description_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount of tax, derived by the ATO from the return by multiplying basic income tax liability by the small business proportion, which is capped at one.
limitation: It is not the tax the person actually paid on their business, because the offset itself, other offsets, the Medicare levy and loan repayments all sit outside it. Nor is it the offset: the offset is a percentage of this amount and stops at $1,000, so two taxpayers with very different figures here can receive the same offset.
rationale: The ATO offset page sets out the calculation, the rate by year and the $1,000 cap, which together define what this derived tax figure is used for.
evidence_quote: Your offset will be your rate of offset of the following amount, up to the limit of $1,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is an intermediate step in the small business income tax offset, not the offset or the tax paid.

value_domain: Total PAYG tax withheld reported on the return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax withheld
variable_description: All the tax that payers took out of the person's income during the year and sent to the ATO, added up on the return. The ATO defines the line as follows: "Total tax withheld is the pay as you go (PAYG) withholding amounts withheld during the year by the payer from the amounts you declare as income at questions 1 to 9." It is a credit against the assessment rather than a tax, so a refund is the gap between it and the tax finally worked out.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax withheld
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum of the withheld column beside the first nine income questions. It covers wages, allowances, lump sums, termination payments, government payments and annuities.
limitation: It is not the person's tax for the year, and it is not the whole of what they remitted: PAYG instalments are credited separately and are explicitly kept off the return, and withholding on interest or dividends for a missing tax file number sits at those questions. Extra amounts withheld for a study loan are inside this figure and cannot be separated from ordinary withholding.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the line, names the questions that feed it and says instalments are not to be shown on the return.
evidence_quote: Total tax withheld is the pay as you go (PAYG) withholding amounts withheld during the year by the payer from the amounts you declare as income at questions 1 to 9.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the line is a credit built from the withheld column of the first nine questions rather than the person's tax.

value_domain: Landcare, water facility, fencing and fodder storage deduction at P8 label W (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items
variable_description: Capital spending on land and water improvements that farmers and some other businesses may write off, reported as one total on the business schedule. The ATO combines four things in the label: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production deductions for landcare operations, water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets and write the total at label W." Landcare covers works such as levees, drainage and fencing to keep stock off degraded land, and it is deductible in the year it is incurred where the business is a primary producer.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items
value_definition: A dollar amount, the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns. Fencing and fodder storage components are available to primary producers only; landcare and water facilities can also reach a rural land irrigation water provider.
limitation: The four components cannot be told apart in the one figure, so it cannot be used to measure water infrastructure spending on its own. It is also a deduction rather than an outlay, and the immediate write-off means a single year's figure can reflect several years of building work finished at once.
rationale: The P8 reconciliation instruction defines each component of the label, states who can claim it, and gives the totalling rule for the two production columns.
evidence_quote: Add up your primary production and non-primary production deductions for landcare operations, water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets and write the total at label W .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that four different concessions are added into one label, or that the deduction is immediate rather than depreciated.

value_domain: Lease expenses at P8, total column (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
variable_description: What the business paid to lease plant, vehicles or premises during the year, totalled across primary production and non-primary production. The ATO draws a boundary that matters for anyone reading the figure as equipment finance: "Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses." Hire purchase is dealt with in the reconciliation labels instead, and a lease can also be caught by the thin capitalisation debt deduction rules.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum of the two production columns for lease payments claimed in the accounts.
limitation: It cannot separate a property lease from a car or equipment lease, so it is not a measure of business premises cost. Because hire purchase and chattel mortgage arrangements are excluded, a business that finances its plant that way can show nothing here while carrying substantial equipment.
rationale: The P8 expenses instruction defines the label, excludes hire purchase and states the totalling rule for the two production columns.
evidence_quote: Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what counts as a lease expense, or that hire purchase is excluded from the label.

value_domain: Life assurance bonus tax offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses
variable_description: The tax offset that comes automatically with a life insurance or friendly society bonus declared on the return. The rule is fixed and the calculation is not the taxpayer's: "You'll get a tax offset equal to 30% of the amount you show at this question. We'll work out this tax offset for you." The 30% matches the tax the life company has already paid on the earnings inside the policy, so the offset is there to stop the same income being taxed twice.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to 30% of the assessable bonus reported at question 22, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed.
limitation: It is a non-refundable offset, so a person with little tax payable does not receive the full 30% as cash, and the recorded amount can therefore overstate the benefit. It also cannot be read as a measure of policy earnings, because only part of a bonus is assessable in the ninth and tenth years of a policy.
rationale: The question 22 instruction states the 30% rate, that the ATO calculates the offset, and how much of a bonus is assessable in each policy year.
evidence_quote: You'll get a tax offset equal to 30% of the amount you show at this question. We'll work out this tax offset for you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the offset is a fixed 30% of the declared bonus and is calculated by the ATO.

value_domain: Life insurance and friendly society bonuses at question 22 label W (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses
variable_description: The assessable part of a bonus received on a life insurance policy or friendly society bond cashed in within ten years of starting it. How much counts depends on when it is taken: the whole bonus in the first eight years, "two-thirds of the bonus amount you receive in 2024-25 if you receive it during the 9th year of the policy", and one-third in the tenth year. Bonuses after the tenth year, and bonuses paid because the insured person died or surrendered the policy through illness or hardship, are not declared at all.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses
value_definition: A dollar amount already reduced to the assessable fraction for the policy year, so it is smaller than the bonus the person received in years nine and ten.
limitation: It is not the investment return on the policy and not the amount received: the two-thirds and one-third steps mean the same cash bonus produces different figures depending on timing. A blank is common even for policyholders, because a policy held past ten years produces no entry.
rationale: The question 22 instruction states the qualifying conditions, the fractions assessable by policy year and the exclusions, which is what the label holds.
evidence_quote: two-thirds of the bonus amount you receive in 2024–25 if you receive it during the 9th year of the policy
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is a tapered fraction of the bonus rather than the bonus itself.

value_domain: Local government area, ASGS non-ABS structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the taxpayer's address falls in, coded to the ABS geography for the year on the table's name. It is a statistical approximation rather than the legal boundary: "Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory." It sits with the other geography columns from the same address, so it is the coarser partner of the statistical area codes on the same row.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Local Government Areas
value_definition: A code and name from the ASGS non-ABS structures, built from whole mesh blocks. LGA boundaries are reissued each year as councils change, and unincorporated areas have no council.
limitation: It is a place, not a jurisdiction the taxpayer dealt with, and the ABS warns that these approximations "should only be used for statistical purposes", so it must not be used to allocate rates or council entitlements. Because the address is the one the ATO held at the time, a person who moved mid-year is counted wholly in one council area.
rationale: The ABS standard defines local government areas as a non-ABS structure approximated from mesh blocks and states the statistical-use limitation.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory. ABS approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the boundaries are mesh block approximations of gazetted council areas rather than the legal boundaries.

value_domain: ASGS Local Government Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the taxpayer's address falls in, at the 2024 boundaries. Unlike the SA codes beside it this is an administrative boundary rather than a statistical one: it is drawn by state legislation and changes when councils amalgamate or split, so it is the right column for anything involving council rates, local government policy or a comparison with council-published data.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Local Government Areas
value_definition: A five-digit ABS-assigned code for the LGA, whose leading digit is the state. The ABS approximates LGA boundaries from mesh blocks, so the coded area is a close fit to the gazetted boundary rather than the boundary itself.
limitation: LGAs vary enormously in size and population, from a few hundred people to more than a million, so a per-LGA average is not comparable across them the way an SA3 average is. Amalgamations break the series: an LGA that merged has no continuous history, and the 2024 vintage cannot be joined to an earlier one by code.
rationale: The field is an LGA code at the 2024 vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes how it approximates LGA boundaries from mesh blocks and that LGAs are a non-ABS structure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2024 Local Government Area code.' with no value domain, and nothing said the boundary is administrative rather than statistical.

value_domain: Deduction for the long-life small business pool (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The write-off claimed on long-lived business assets that were pooled under the simplified small business depreciation rules. The pool held the slow-depreciating end of the asset base: "a long-life small business pool for depreciating assets with an effective life of 25 years or more", and the ATO's formula is "Long-life small business pool deduction = opening pool balance ($) X 5%", with half that rate in an asset's first year. Assets carried over from a general or long-life pool under the earlier simplified tax system kept the same treatment.
description_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010, item 5 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A dollar amount, 5% of the opening pool balance plus 2.5% of assets first used during the year. It is one pooled figure, not an asset-by-asset calculation.
limitation: The individual assets behind the figure cannot be recovered, and disposals reduce the pool rather than showing up as a separate loss or gain. The pool is no longer available and the ATO now refers to it as formerly available, so a long run of this column stops without the underlying assets disappearing.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions publish the long-life pool definition, the 5% rate and the half rate in the first year, and the same pool and rate applied to sole traders through the business and professional items schedule.
evidence_quote: Long-life small business pool deduction = opening pool balance ($) X 5%
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what the long-life pool held, at what rate it was written off, or that it has since closed.

value_domain: Lodgment channel for the return
value_source: ATO, How to lodge your tax return
variable_description: How the return reached the ATO: prepared by the taxpayer online, lodged through an agent, or sent in on paper. The ATO's own channels are myTax for self-preparers, a registered tax agent - "they are the only people that can charge a fee" - and the paper return lodged by mail, for which the ATO says most refunds issue within 50 business days. The channel matters for reading the rest of the row, because agent-lodged returns follow a later due date and pre-filled online returns carry fewer keying errors.
description_source: ATO, How to lodge your tax return
value_definition: A code for the lodgment channel. The ATO's public channels are self-prepared online, registered tax agent and paper, with older years including the retired e-tax software; the stored code list is not published.
limitation: It records the path the form took, not who did the work, so a taxpayer who pays an accountant to prepare a return they then lodge themselves is counted as a self-preparer. It also cannot date the lodgment, so it does not distinguish an on-time return from a late one.
rationale: The ATO page enumerates the lodgment channels available to individuals and what each involves, which is the domain this column codes. The mapping from the ATO's channel names to the stored codes is not published and is not asserted.
evidence_quote: Use a registered tax agent to prepare and lodge your tax return, they are the only people that can charge a fee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which lodgment channels exist or why the channel changes how the return should be read.

value_domain: Low and middle income tax offset applied against tax (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Low and middle income earner tax offsets
variable_description: How much of the low and middle income tax offset was actually used to reduce the person's tax, as against how much they were entitled to. The offset was never claimed on the return: "You don't need to do anything to claim this tax offset, except lodge your tax return for the relevant year. We work out the offset after you lodge." It ran for four years only, and "The 2021-22 income year was the last year for the LMITO - it isn't available for 2023 onwards."
description_source: ATO, Low and middle income earner tax offsets
value_definition: A dollar amount, the part of the entitlement absorbed by tax payable. Entitlement ranged from $255 to $1,080 for 2018-19 to 2020-21 and from $675 to $1,500 for 2021-22.
limitation: Because it is the used amount, it understates entitlement for anyone whose tax payable was smaller than their offset, and it falls to zero for a person with no tax to pay however low their income. The offset was also non-refundable and unused amounts were never paid out, so the column cannot be read as a transfer received.
rationale: The ATO page states that the offset was calculated after lodgment, that it only reduces tax payable to zero, and the years it operated, which is what separates a used amount from an entitlement.
evidence_quote: The 2021–22 income year was the last year for the LMITO – it isn't available for 2023 onwards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the offset was calculated by the ATO, ran only from 2018-19 to 2021-22, and could not be refunded.

value_domain: Low income tax offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Low income tax offset
variable_description: The low income tax offset worked out for the taxpayer from their taxable income, which reduces the tax they pay but is never paid as cash. Nothing is claimed for it: "We will work out your offset and reduce your tax payable by this amount", and it appears on the notice of assessment under non-refundable offsets. The current scale gives $700 up to a taxable income of $37,500 and tapers to nothing at $66,667; earlier years had different amounts and a separate low income offset for seniors.
description_source: ATO, Low income tax offset
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by the ATO from taxable income alone. The taper is a two-stage formula, so the amount is a deterministic function of taxable income within a year.
limitation: Its value cannot be compared across years without the year's scale, because the maximum and the cut-out have both moved, and for a time it interacted with the separate middle income offset. Being non-refundable, a positive amount here does not mean the person received money; it means tax that would otherwise have been payable was not.
rationale: The ATO page publishes the offset's income scale, states that the ATO calculates it after lodgment, and states that it cannot be refunded.
evidence_quote: We will work out your offset and reduce your tax payable by this amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is derived from taxable income by the ATO and cannot be refunded.

value_domain: Lump sum payment in arrears tax offset available (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
variable_description: The lump sum payment in arrears offset the ATO worked out that the taxpayer was entitled to, before any of it was applied. The offset exists because back pay is taxed in the year it lands: "Lump sum payments in arrears (LSPIA) are assessable in the income year you receive the payment", which can push someone into a higher bracket for income they earned years earlier. The ATO calculates the entitlement from the year-by-year breakdown the payer supplies.
description_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
value_definition: A dollar amount produced by comparing tax on the arrears in the year received against tax had it been taxed in the years it accrued. It arises only where the arrears are at least 10% of threshold test income.
limitation: An available amount is an entitlement, not a benefit received, so it overstates what the person gained wherever their tax payable was smaller. It also does not identify what the back payment was for, so an underpayment settlement, a delayed pension and a reinstatement after suspension all look the same here.
rationale: The ATO page defines the offset, the assessability rule that creates the need for it, the 10% threshold test and the fact that the ATO works the amounts out from the return.
evidence_quote: Lump sum payments in arrears (LSPIA) are assessable in the income year you receive the payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said why the offset exists or that the available amount is an entitlement rather than a benefit.

value_domain: Lump sum payment in arrears tax offset applied against tax (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
variable_description: How much of the lump sum payment in arrears offset was actually absorbed by the person's tax for the year. It is the applied twin of the available column on the same row, and the difference between them is entitlement that went unused because there was not enough tax to offset. The ATO does not publish the working: "As the calculations are complex and relate to each individuals' personal circumstances, there currently is no online calculator or detail we provide to explain the outcome."
description_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
value_definition: A dollar amount, at most equal to the available offset on the same row and at most the tax otherwise payable.
limitation: A zero here is ambiguous: it can mean no arrears were received, or that an entitlement existed but no tax was payable to apply it against. Because the ATO publishes no breakdown of the calculation, the used amount cannot be reproduced from the other columns on the return.
rationale: The ATO page establishes that the offset is calculated by the ATO from information in the return and that no explanation of the outcome is published, which is what separates an applied amount from an entitlement.
evidence_quote: As the calculations are complex and relate to each individuals' personal circumstances, there currently is no online calculator or detail we provide to explain the outcome.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is the part of the offset absorbed by tax payable rather than the entitlement.

value_domain: Lump sum payment in arrears tax offset entitlement, later table (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
variable_description: The entitlement to the lump sum payment in arrears offset, sitting beside the column that records how much of it was used. Qualifying is a threshold test rather than a claim: "The eligible LSPIA amount must be 10% or more of your threshold test income in the income year you receive it" once earlier-year accruals and leave paid on termination are taken out. From 1 July 2024 the same arrears can also carry a Medicare levy exemption and a surcharge offset, which are separate amounts again.
description_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
value_definition: A dollar amount of entitlement for the income year, sitting on the same row as the used amount so that the two can be differenced.
limitation: It repeats a quantity the registry also holds under an older name in an earlier table, so summing the two across years counts one entitlement twice. It also covers the income tax offset only, not the Medicare levy exemption or the surcharge offset that the same arrears may attract.
rationale: The ATO page defines the offset and its 10% threshold test and lists the separate Medicare concessions that accompany it. That this column and the earlier available column are the same quantity under two names is inferred from the custodian's identical wording for both.
evidence_quote: The eligible LSPIA amount must be 10% or more of your threshold test income in the income year you receive it
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is the entitlement paired with the used column, or that it overlaps an identically described column in an earlier table.

value_domain: Lump sum A on the payment summary (dollars)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out on leaving a job, reported by the employer outside gross payments because it is taxed on its own basis. The ATO defines lump sum A as unused long service leave "that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993", unused holiday pay accrued before 18 August 1993, and any post-1993 unused leave paid with a genuine redundancy, early retirement or invalidity payment. Ordinary unused leave outside those cases is inside gross payments instead, not here.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A dollar amount the payer shows in the lump sum A field for the income year, never inside gross payments. It carries a type code of R or T on the same statement.
limitation: It is a third-party report, so an employer's misclassification lands here uncorrected, and it is not a measure of leave taken or accrued. The accrual dates mean two people with identical payouts can report very different amounts here purely because of when their leave built up.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instructions define each lump sum type for the payer, which is where these amounts originate before they reach the return.
evidence_quote: unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993

value_domain: ATO lump sum A type code

The ATO instruction is direct: "Write the number of days you were covered for a full exemption at question M1 - label V." Three categories qualify, covering defence and veteran medical entitlement, foreign residency and people not entitled to Medicare benefits, and the half-exemption days claimed under the same item sit in a separate column.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
value_definition: A whole number of days from 0 to 366, capped so that overlapping qualifying periods are counted once and any overlap between full and half periods is treated as full.
limitation: It records what the taxpayer claimed, not what was allowed, since the ATO says it works out the entitlement afterwards. It also does not say which of the three exemption categories applied, so defence personnel, foreign residents and people without Medicare entitlement are indistinguishable here.
rationale: M1 label V is a single defined box and the ATO instructions state the counting rule, the 366-day cap and the overlap treatment.
evidence_quote: The maximum total number of days you can claim is 366. If you have overlapping qualifying periods, count the days in those overlapping periods only once.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the 0 to 366 range nor the claim-not-assessment status was stated.

value_domain: Medicare levy exemption claim type code (M1 CLAIM TYPE box)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: A one-letter code printed beside the full-exemption days box to flag a particular kind of claim. For 2023-24 the ATO gives a single instruction for it: "If you were a temporary resident for Medicare purposes and have a Medicare Entitlement Statement from Services Australia covering a period in 2023-24 (see Category 3), then print C in the CLAIM TYPE box." Everyone else leaves it blank, so the column is mostly empty by design and appears only from the 2009-10 table onward.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
value_definition: A single character drawn from a very short list, sitting beside the day counts at M1 rather than carrying an amount of its own.
limitation: A blank does not mean no exemption was claimed, because most claimants are told to leave the box empty, so the code cannot be used to identify who was exempt. It also does not distinguish the medical, foreign resident and no-Medicare-entitlement categories from one another.
rationale: The M1 instructions describe the CLAIM TYPE box that sits with label V and give the one code currently in use, which is the box the custodian's label names.
evidence_quote: If you don't fall within this category, leave the CLAIM TYPE box blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Medicare levy full exemption - claim type' with the generic sentence twice and no values, so a reader had no way to know the box is deliberately blank for most claimants.

value_domain: Count of days, 0 to 366, at M1 label W
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: The number of days for which a person claimed to owe only half the Medicare levy, typically because a dependant was not covered by their own exemption. The ATO instruction is: "Write the number of days you were covered for a half exemption at question M1 - label W." A half exemption normally arises through a family agreement with a spouse over shared dependants, so this column often depends on the other partner's circumstances rather than the taxpayer's own.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
value_definition: A whole number of days from 0 to 366, counted so that any day that also qualifies for a full exemption is recorded as full rather than half.
limitation: Full and half days cannot simply be added to get a total exempt period, since the levy relief differs by a factor of two, and the overlap rule pushes shared days into the full column. Like the full-exemption count, this is a claim rather than the ATO's assessed entitlement.
rationale: M1 label W is a defined box, and the ATO instructions describe both the count and the family-agreement circumstances that produce a half rather than a full exemption.
evidence_quote: If a full exemption period overlaps a part exemption period, count the overlapping days as a full exemption period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label and gave the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain what half exemption means or why the days cannot be added to the full-exemption days.

value_domain: Dollar amount of spouse's taxable income reported for the Medicare levy tests
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals 2001 (NAT 2541), Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The spouse's taxable income as reported by the taxpayer, held only in the 1999-2000 to 2005-06 income and loss tables. The spouse details pages of the returns of that era collect "Spouse's 2000-01 taxable income" and require it only in defined cases, one being that the person completed the Medicare levy reduction item. The figure is therefore third-hand, written by one partner about the other, and it feeds the family-income test that reduces or removes the levy.
description_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals 2001 (NAT 2541), Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar figure of the spouse's taxable income for the same income year, reported on the taxpayer's return rather than taken from the spouse's own assessment.
limitation: A blank does not mean the person had no spouse or that the spouse had no income, only that no item on the return triggered the requirement to report it. Because one partner writes down the other's figure, it can disagree with the spouse's own lodged taxable income.
rationale: The ATO return form of the period defines the spouse income box and lists the items, including the Medicare levy question, that make it compulsory; no live ATO page covers the retired layout.
evidence_quote: You only need to complete spouse's 2000-01 taxable income if: - you had a spouse on 30 June 2001 AND you completed item M1
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's title-case wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say whose income this is, who reported it, or when reporting was required.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessed Medicare levy
value_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Reference material, Calculating net tax
variable_description: The total Medicare levy the ATO assessed on the person for the year, after any reduction or exemption. It is one of the terms the ATO adds when it works out an individual's net tax: "Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax - Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge - Remaining foreign income tax offset". The column appears only from the 2020-21 tables, and it is a calculated result, not anything the taxpayer wrote on the return.
description_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Reference material, Calculating net tax
value_definition: A dollar amount computed by the ATO from taxable income at the year's levy rate, then adjusted for the low-income reduction and for any full or half exemption days claimed at M1.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as an exemption, because a low income, a family-income reduction or no taxable income all produce the same result, and the M1 day counts are needed to tell them apart. The surcharge is a separate liability and is not included here.
rationale: The ATO's taxation statistics reference material sets out where the Medicare levy sits in the individual net tax calculation, which identifies this column as the assessed levy rather than a return label.
evidence_quote: Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax - Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge - Remaining foreign income tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Total Medicare levy liability' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish an assessed amount from a claimed one or place it in the net tax calculation.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessed Medicare levy surcharge
value_source: ATO, Paying the Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: The extra levy the ATO charged a person for going without private patient hospital cover while earning above the surcharge threshold.
