The ATO explains what it bites on: "The MLS rate of 1%, 1.25% or 1.5% is levied on: your taxable income, total reportable fringe benefits, and any amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid." It is calculated by the ATO, prorated by the days the person reported as not liable at M2 label A, and it sits on top of the ordinary Medicare levy.
description_source: ATO, Paying the Medicare levy surcharge
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to the applicable surcharge rate applied to the surcharge base, scaled to the part of the year for which the person was liable.
limitation: A zero does not identify people with hospital cover, since income below the threshold, an exemption or no taxable income all give zero, and cover has to be read from the private health insurance columns instead. The rate depends on combined family income, so the amount reflects a spouse's circumstances as well as the taxpayer's.
rationale: The ATO surcharge page states the rates and the base the surcharge is levied on, which defines the quantity the custodian's label names.
evidence_quote: The MLS rate of 1%, 1.25% or 1.5% is levied on: your taxable income, total reportable fringe benefits, and any amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Medicare levy surcharge' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the surcharge applies to or that a zero is uninformative about hospital cover.

value_domain: Count of days, 0 to 366, at M2 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: The number of days a person declared they were not liable for the Medicare levy surcharge. The ATO instruction is: "Write at question M2 - label A the number of days for which you don't have to pay MLS", and a person with no liability for the whole year writes 366. The question is compulsory for every taxpayer, so the column is populated even for people far below the surcharge threshold.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
value_definition: A whole number of days from 0 to 366, entered by the taxpayer, that scales the surcharge the ATO then calculates.
limitation: A full-year value cannot be read as holding private hospital cover, because everyone under the income threshold also writes the full year, and the two reasons are not distinguished. It records a taxpayer's own conclusion about liability, which the ATO may override on assessment.
rationale: M2 label A is a single compulsory box and the ATO instructions state exactly what number goes in it and the values for the two extreme cases.
evidence_quote: If you don't have to pay MLS for any days during the period 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024, write 366 at question M2 - label A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label with the generic sentence twice, so it never noted the compulsory nature of the question or that a full-year value confounds cover with low income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the base the surcharge rate was applied to
value_source: ATO, Paying the Medicare levy surcharge, and Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
variable_description: The amount of a person's income that the surcharge rate was actually charged on, held only in the 2022-23 and 2023-24 tables. The ATO describes that base as "your taxable income, total reportable fringe benefits, and any amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid", which is narrower than income for surcharge purposes. Income for surcharge purposes decides whether the surcharge applies and at which rate, and it also folds in net investment losses, reportable super contributions and a spouse's income.
description_source: ATO, Paying the Medicare levy surcharge, and Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to taxable income plus reportable fringe benefits plus any family trust distribution tax amount, before the 1%, 1.25% or 1.5% rate is applied.
limitation: It is not the income test that decides liability, so using it as a threshold measure will misclassify people whose investment losses or super contributions push their surcharge income higher. It is an individual base even though the rate that hits it was set by combined family income.
rationale: The ATO surcharge pages separate the base the rate is levied on from income for MLS purposes, which is the distinction the custodian's label turns on.
evidence_quote: We use a special definition of income (called income for MLS purposes) to work out if you have to pay the MLS and the rate you will pay. This income is different from your taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Amount subjected to medicare levy surcharge' with the generic sentence twice, leaving the reader to assume it was the surcharge income test, which it is not.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the Medicare levy surcharge lump sum in arrears tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: Relief the ATO grants where a surcharge liability arose only because a back-payment covering earlier years landed in this year's income. The ATO sets out the spouse case at M2: "If you are liable for MLS only because your spouse has shown a lump sum payment in arrears at question 20 ... or question 24 ... you may be entitled to a tax offset up to the amount of MLS you have to pay. We will calculate the tax offset for you." The column runs from the 2015-16 tables onward and is worked out by the ATO, not claimed at a label.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
value_definition: A dollar offset capped at the surcharge otherwise payable, granted where arrears income rather than ordinary income took the household over the surcharge threshold.
limitation: It cannot be used to find everyone who received arrears, because it appears only where the arrears actually created a surcharge liability and the taxpayer supplied the supporting schedule. It offsets the surcharge alone and does not undo the extra ordinary tax or Medicare levy the arrears caused.
rationale: The M2 instructions describe the offset, its cap and the fact that the ATO calculates it, which matches the custodian's label naming a surcharge lump sum in arrears offset.
evidence_quote: you may be entitled to a tax offset up to the amount of MLS you have to pay. We will calculate the tax offset for you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's run-on title with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said that this is ATO-calculated relief capped at the surcharge payable.

value_domain: ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 4 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The SA4 covering the business address a sole trader gave for their main business, on ASGS 2016 boundaries. It runs from the 2010-11 to the 2019-20 tables. The address comes from the Business and professional items schedule, where the taxpayer writes the street address of the main business, so it locates the enterprise rather than the person. The ABS says SA4 "boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities".
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
value_definition: An SA4 identifier from the ASGS main structure, the largest sub-state region in that structure, geocoded from a single reported business address.
limitation: It shows only the main business where a person ran several, and for a mobile or home-based trade the registered address can be an accountant's or a home office far from where work was done. The taxpayer's own residential geography is in different columns and the two should not be conflated.
rationale: The ABS publishes the classification and defines what an SA4 represents; the address it is coded from is the business address item on the ATO schedule that accompanies the return.
evidence_quote: SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Business address of main business - SA4' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say whose address this is or which ASGS edition applies.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 4 code, 2021 edition
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The main business SA4 as recoded to the ASGS 2021 boundaries, present only in the 2020-21 context table. It replaces the 2016-edition column of the same content at the point where the ABS moved to Edition 3, so a business that did not move can still change code between the two columns. The ABS counts "108 SA4s covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps", including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes such as no usual address.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
value_definition: An SA4 identifier under ASGS Edition 3 boundaries, geocoded from the business address reported on the Business and professional items schedule.
limitation: Because only one table carries it, this column supports no trend on its own and joining it to the 2016-edition column will attribute boundary changes to business relocation. The special purpose codes mean a valid value can represent no locatable address at all.
rationale: The ABS defines the SA4 unit and the Edition 3 counts; the 2021 suffix matches the ASGS edition adopted for the year this single table covers.
evidence_quote: There are 108 SA4s covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the lower-case custodian label with the generic sentence twice, so the boundary change against the earlier SA4 column went unrecorded.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 4 code, 2021-22 table
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The main business SA4 in the 2021-22 context table, where the column suffix follows the financial year rather than any ASGS edition. No edition of the standard is numbered 2122, so the boundary vintage cannot be read off the name and has to be taken from the year's ABS release, Edition 3. The ABS designs SA4s "with an emphasis on stability over time to support the time series of statistical releases such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication".
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
value_definition: An SA4 identifier from the ASGS main structure, geocoded from the reported business address of the taxpayer's main business for 2021-22.
limitation: The suffix in the column name is a year label, not a classification version, so treating it as an ASGS edition will produce a nonexistent vintage. Only one table carries the column, so it cannot be differenced against a neighbouring year without first confirming the boundaries match.
rationale: The ABS defines the SA4 unit and its design intent; the naming pattern across the ATO context tables shows the suffix here tracks the financial year rather than the standard.
evidence_quote: They are designed with an emphasis on stability over time to support the time series of statistical releases such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's upper-case fragment with the generic sentence twice, so the misleading year suffix was not flagged at all.

value_domain: ATO business industry code (five digits, derived from ANZSIC)
value_source: ATO, Business industry code tool
variable_description: The industry of the taxpayer's main business or professional activity, as coded on the return. The ATO says: "A business industry code (BIC) is a five-digit code you include on relevant tax returns and schedules that describes your main business activity" and that "BICs are derived from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) codes and have been simplified for tax return reporting purposes". The paper schedule asks at P2 only for a written description of the main business or professional activity and carries no code box, so the five-digit code reaches the record through electronic lodgment or through ATO coding of that description.
description_source: ATO, Business industry code tool
value_definition: A five-digit code from the ATO's simplified derivative of ANZSIC, describing one activity only.
limitation: A BIC does not map one to one onto an ANZSIC class, so joining it to ABS industry statistics requires a concordance rather than a direct match. Someone with more than one business is told to code the activity with the highest gross income, and the code changes only when a new one is entered, so it can sit stale for years after the work changed.
rationale: The ATO's own tool page defines the code, its length and its relationship to ANZSIC, which is precisely what the custodian's label describes.
evidence_quote: BICs are derived from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) codes and have been simplified for tax return reporting purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that a BIC is a simplified derivative of ANZSIC rather than an ANZSIC code.

value_domain: Marital status code held against the tax return record
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: A coded marital status carried against the 2009-10 return record, and against no other year. The individual return does not ask for marital status directly; it asks whether the person had a spouse and for how long, and for the spouse's date of birth and sex, and those fields sit beside this one in the same table. The code is therefore either drawn from ATO client registration or derived from the spouse questions, and its code list is not published.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A short code standing for a marital status category, with no published value list and no matching label on the return.
limitation: Because it exists in one table only, it cannot support any change over time, and it cannot be checked against the spouse questions without knowing which code means what. Tax-record marital status also lags real relationship changes, since it only moves when a person tells the ATO.
rationale: No ATO publication defines a marital status code on the individual return; the reading rests on the spouse details section, which is the only place the return touches relationship status, and on the columns beside it in the same table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Marital Status' and printed the generic sentence twice; it now records that the return has no such question and that the code list is unpublished.

value_domain: Dollar amount of mature age worker tax offset applied
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2008 (NAT 2679), item T12
variable_description: The mature age worker tax offset actually applied against a person's tax, held only for the 2006-07 to 2008-09 tables. There was no claim box for it: the taxpayer supplied their net income from working and, as the 2008 supplementary return says, "we use this amount to work out your mature age worker tax offset entitlement". The offset was targeted at workers aged 55 and over and was later abolished, which is why no later table carries the column.
description_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2008 (NAT 2679), item T12
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-refundable offset computed by the ATO from the taxpayer's net income from working and their age.
limitation: Because the offset is non-refundable, the amount used is capped by the tax otherwise payable and so understates entitlement for people with little tax to pay. Its absence in later tables reflects the offset ending, not a change in who was working past 55.
rationale: The ATO's own supplementary return for 2008 states that the offset is worked out by the ATO from the net income from working figure, which fixes what a 'used' amount means; no live ATO page remains for the retired offset.
evidence_quote: We use this amount to work out your mature age worker tax offset entitlement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Mature age worker tax offset' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the offset was ATO-calculated, non-refundable, or limited to three tables.

value_domain: Dollar amount of business motor vehicle expenses, P8 label N
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: What a sole trader claimed for running vehicles in the business, as the combined primary production and non-primary production total. The ATO instructs: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production motor vehicle expenses and enter the total at N item P8 on your schedule", and rules several costs out of the box: "Do not include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid." Ride-sourcing costs belong here, and the method used to work the claim out is coded in the companion column MTR_VHCL_BUS_EXPNSS_TYP_CD.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar business expense total covering running costs for cars and other vehicles, excluding depreciation, lease charges and interest, which sit at separate P8 labels.
limitation: It is not the cost of owning the vehicles, since the capital and financing components are deliberately excluded, so it understates the true motoring cost of a business. It is a business expense on the schedule and is not the employee work-related car expense claim made at D1.
rationale: P8 label N is a single defined total and the ATO schedule instructions state both what is added into it and what is kept out.
evidence_quote: Do not include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Motor vehicle expenses - total' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the total excludes depreciation, lease and interest costs.

value_domain: Motor vehicle expense method code (P8 Type box beside label N)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: A one-letter code saying how the business motor vehicle claim beside it was worked out. The ATO lists "S if you used the 'cents per kilometre' method" and "B if you used the 'logbook' method", with N printed instead where the amount relates to a motorcycle, a taxi taken on hire, a vehicle carrying a tonne or nine passengers, or other non-car motoring costs. The column starts at the 2010-11 tables, and earlier years offered further calculation methods that were later withdrawn.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A single character sitting in the Type box beside P8 label N, identifying the substantiation method rather than carrying an amount.
limitation: Where a person used more than one method or ran several vehicles, the ATO tells them to print only the code for the largest claim, so the code cannot be used to split the dollar total by method. The code says nothing about how many kilometres were driven or how many vehicles were involved.
rationale: The ATO schedule instructions define the Type box beside label N, list the codes and state the tie-break rule when more than one applies.
evidence_quote: If you have more than one code, print the code that applies to the largest claim.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Motor vehicle expenses - total - type' with no values and the generic sentence twice, so the code meanings and the largest-claim rule were absent.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net financial investment loss, IT5 label X
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question IT5 Net financial investment loss
variable_description: How far a person's deductions on shares and managed investments ran ahead of the income those investments produced. The ATO puts it plainly: "The loss you show at this question is the amount your deductions from your financial investments exceed your income from those investments." It is an income test figure, not a deduction, and it is added back into adjusted taxable income for family payments, the surcharge and several offsets. Rental losses are excluded and belong at IT6.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question IT5 Net financial investment loss
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount reported as a positive number, covering dividends, managed investment scheme distributions, franking credits and related deductions, including a partnership share of the same.
limitation: The label is censored at zero, so a person with net investment income records nothing and the column cannot be turned into a distribution of investment returns. Everyday transaction account interest is excluded by instruction, so it is not a complete picture of a household's financial income either.
rationale: IT5 is a defined income test label and the ATO instructions state the calculation, the inclusions and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: The loss you show at this question is the amount your deductions from your financial investments exceed your income from those investments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net financial investment loss' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is reported only when negative or that it feeds income tests.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 20 label U
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: Foreign employment income that arrived with an Australian payment summary or income statement, net of the work deductions claimed against it. The ATO builds it from the documents: add the gross payments and lump sum A and E amounts from each PAYG payment summary - foreign employment and each income statement, then "take the total deductible expenses from Step 2 away from the total gross payments from Step 1 and write the answer at question 20 - label U". Foreign employment income with no such document goes to label T instead, and exempt foreign employment income to label N.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, which can be a loss, covering only foreign employment income substantiated by an Australian payment summary or income statement.
limitation: It is not total foreign earnings, because the same person's undocumented foreign employment income and exempt foreign employment income sit in two other labels on the same row. Being net of deductions already claimed at D1 to D5, it also cannot be read as gross foreign salary.
rationale: Item 20 label U is a defined box and the ATO instructions give the exact three-step build and the neighbouring labels that carry the rest of foreign employment income.
evidence_quote: Take the total deductible expenses from Step 2 away from the total gross payments from Step 1 and write the answer at question 20 - label U.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's run-on wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish payment-summary foreign employment income from the other two foreign employment labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 20 label R
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: Rent from property outside Australia, after deductible expenses but before interest and borrowing costs. The ATO tells taxpayers to gross up for foreign tax already taken out, then subtract expenses "excluding any debt deductions" and transfer the result to label R, printing L if it is a loss. Interest on a foreign rental property is claimed at D15 instead, so an owner with a large mortgage can show positive rent here while running a loss overall.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
value_definition: A whole-dollar net figure, positive or a flagged loss, covering all foreign rental properties combined and including foreign tax added back.
limitation: It does not measure foreign property investment returns, because financing costs are deliberately pushed to another question and any capital gain on sale goes to the capital gains item. It also gives no count of properties and no country, so a portfolio in several jurisdictions looks like a single number.
rationale: Item 20 label R is a defined box and the ATO instructions set out the gross-up, the exclusion of debt deductions and the loss treatment.
evidence_quote: Debt deductions, such as interest and borrowing costs, are not deductible for the purposes of this calculation unless they are related to income earned through a permanent establishment in an overseas country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that interest is excluded and sits at a different question.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net income from working, supplementary section
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2008 (NAT 2679), item T12
variable_description: The part of a person's income from working that came through the supplementary section, reported so the ATO could size the mature age worker tax offset. The 2008 supplementary return carries it at item T12 label M with two instructions attached: "We use this amount to work out your mature age worker tax offset entitlement" and "Do not include it in your total supplement tax offsets below". Despite the word offset in the custodian's label, this is an income figure, not relief, and it exists only in the 2006-07 to 2008-09 tables.
description_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2008 (NAT 2679), item T12
value_definition: A whole-dollar income amount covering business, partnership and other work-related income declared in the supplementary section, entered by the taxpayer.
limitation: It is only the supplementary-section component, so salary and wages from the main return have to be added before it means anything as total income from working. It is an input to a calculation and cannot be added to the tax offset columns beside it without double counting.
rationale: The ATO's own supplementary return for 2008 names the item, its label letter and its purpose, and warns against treating it as an offset; no live ATO page covers the retired item.
evidence_quote: Do not include it in your total supplement tax offsets below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, which itself calls the figure a tax offset, alongside the generic sentence twice, so the mislabelling went uncorrected.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld, foreign resident withholding, item 15
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
variable_description: Tax withheld from business payments to a foreign resident, claimed as a credit at question 15. The ATO builds it from the payment documents: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule 2024 shown in the Tax withheld boxes where you have printed F in the Type box", and those amounts must line up with the gross payments at P8 label B. The column starts at the 2006-07 tables, after foreign resident withholding began, and the credit is shown with cents.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
value_definition: A dollar-and-cents withholding credit reported by the taxpayer from payer-issued documents, matched to a specific gross payments label on the business schedule.
limitation: It is a credit and not income, so it cannot be added to the business income columns, and its size depends on the withholding rate for the payment type rather than on profit. Credits for foreign resident capital gains withholding are excluded by instruction and appear at the capital gains question instead.
rationale: The item 15 instructions define each of the four business withholding boxes by the Type letter on the payment summary schedule, which is how this column is distinguished from its three siblings.
evidence_quote: Don't include credits for amounts withheld as a result of the foreign resident capital gains withholding rules at question 15 Net small business income - label E.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's run-on label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing separated this withholding box from the voluntary agreement, no-ABN and labour hire boxes on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label Y, primary production
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The final primary production business result for a sole trader, after prior-year deferred non-commercial losses have been brought in. The ATO says of this line: "This amount takes into account non-commercial losses deferred from a prior year", and it is worked out by taking the deferred primary production losses at label D away from the current year figure at label B. This is the number that leaves the schedule: it is transferred to label B at question 15 of the supplementary return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar net result for primary production activities, positive or flagged as a loss, after deferred non-commercial losses from earlier years.
limitation: It is not this year's farming result, since a prior-year deferred loss can turn a profitable year into a reported loss, and the current-year figure is a separate column. Primary production covers plant and animal cultivation, fishing, pearling and forestry, so it is broader than farming alone.
rationale: P8 label Y is a defined line on the schedule and the ATO instructions state both the calculation and how it differs from the current-year line above it.
evidence_quote: This amount takes into account non-commercial losses deferred from a prior year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net income or loss from business - primary production' with the generic sentence twice, giving no way to tell it apart from the three other primary production business columns in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15 label C, non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The non-primary production business result as it appears on the tax return itself, rather than on the schedule behind it. The ATO closes the schedule with an instruction that ties the two together: "Transfer the amounts at Y and Z to B and C (respectively) item 15 on your tax return (supplementary section)." It is present in the 2009-10 table, where the schedule-level column for the same concept is missing, so it is the safer choice for a series that has to span that year.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar net result for all non-farming business activities of a sole trader, after prior-year deferred non-commercial losses.
limitation: It should equal the schedule column for the same concept, so counting both as separate income would double a person's business income. Its identification as the return-level rather than schedule-level field is inferred from the column set in each table, not from custodian metadata.
rationale: The ATO instructions establish that the schedule figures are transferred to item 15 labels B and C, which gives the return-level pair a defined meaning; which of the paired columns is which is read from the tables that carry only this pair.
evidence_quote: Step 4 Transfer the amounts at Y and Z to B and C (respectively) item 15 on your tax return (supplementary section).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's unpunctuated wording with the generic sentence twice, so it was indistinguishable from the hyphenated non-primary production column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15 label B, primary production
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
variable_description: The primary production business result carried onto the return at question 15, transferred from the schedule that sits behind it. The ATO says: "Transfer your net income or loss from a primary production business shown at P8 Business income and expenses - label Y in the Business and professional items schedule 2024 to question 15 - label B in your supplementary tax return", and a loss is signalled by printing L in the box rather than by a minus sign. It defines a primary producer as someone cultivating plants or animals, fishing or pearling, or farming or felling trees.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
value_definition: A whole-dollar net result for primary production activities as reported on the return, with losses carried by an adjacent flag rather than by the sign of the number.
limitation: A loss stored without its flag reads as income of the same size, which will invert the sign of any farm income measure built from it. It duplicates the schedule-level primary production column in the same table, so the two must not be summed.
rationale: The item 15 instructions define the return-level label and its source on the schedule; which member of the paired columns carries the return-level figure is inferred from the tables that hold only this pair.
evidence_quote: If you made a loss, print L in the LOSS box at question 15 - label B.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's unpunctuated wording with the generic sentence twice, so it could not be told apart from the hyphenated primary production column in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label B, primary production, current year
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: This year's primary production trading result, before any losses deferred from earlier years are brought back in. The ATO is explicit that the deferral is kept out of it: the amount "should not include any non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior year (which are shown at D or E)". That makes it the cleanest available measure of how a farm, fishing or forestry business actually performed in the reference year, and it feeds the after-deferral figure at label Y.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar net trading result for the year for primary production activities, being gross business income less business deductions and reconciliation adjustments.
limitation: It is not the amount that reaches taxable income, because the deferred loss step happens after it, so a person can show income here and a loss on the return. Where several primary production activities are run together, they are added into one figure and cannot be separated.
rationale: The ATO schedule instructions define the current-year line, state that deferred losses are excluded from it, and place it above the after-deferral line in the same block.
evidence_quote: The amount you show should not include any non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior year (which are shown at D or E, see Deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior year).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain that 'this year' means before the deferred loss adjustment.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Totals column, current year net business result
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The whole-business trading result for the year, being the primary production and non-primary production figures added together before deferred losses. The ATO builds it in one step: "Add B and C and enter the total in the adjacent Totals column", with L printed beside it if the business overall made a loss. It is the row total of the two current-year columns in the same table and adds no information beyond them, but it is the field that carries the loss flag for the business as a whole.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar sum of the primary production and non-primary production current-year results, before prior-year deferred non-commercial losses.
limitation: Adding it to its own two components will double count the same business result, since it is their total and not an extra source of income. It also masks the case where a profitable farm activity is offsetting a loss-making non-farm activity in the same person's affairs.
rationale: The ATO schedule instructions describe the Totals column of the current-year line and how it is formed from the two component labels.
evidence_quote: Step 3 Add B and C and enter the total in the adjacent Totals column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net income or loss from business this year - totals' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that the column is the sum of two others on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net non-primary production business income, pre-2006 returns
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2001 (NAT 2679), item 14
variable_description: The net result of a sole trader's non-farming business, as reported on the returns of the 1999-2000 to 2005-06 years. The supplementary return of that period carried it at item 14 as "Non-primary production - transferred from Z on your 2001 business and professional items schedule", so it already reflects any deferred non-commercial losses applied on the schedule. Its primary production counterpart and the gross business income totals sit in separate columns of the same table.
description_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2001 (NAT 2679), item 14
value_definition: A whole-dollar net figure for all non-primary production business activities of the individual, after business deductions and after prior-year deferred non-commercial losses.
limitation: It is a net result, so a large business with thin margins and a small one can produce the same number, and the gross income behind it has to be taken from the total business income columns. The later tables use differently named columns for the same concept, so a series spanning 2005-06 needs the two to be mapped by hand.
rationale: The ATO return form of the period shows the non-primary production business line and its source on the schedule; the identification rests on that form and on the sibling columns in the same table.
evidence_quote: Non-primary production - transferred from Z on your 2001 business and professional items schedule
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's title-case wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not connect the field to the return item or say it was already net of deferred losses.

value_domain: Dollar amount of primary production partnership distribution
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A person's share of a primary production partnership, held for the 1999-2000 to 2005-06 tables. On the return this is the distribution from partnerships box on the primary production side of the partnerships and trusts item, reported at label N, and it excludes the trust distributions and the landcare and other deductions that appear beneath it. The derived line those deductions produce, the net primary production amount, sits in the neighbouring DSTBN_PP_NET_AMT column.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar share of partnership income or loss from primary production activities, as distributed to the partner and reported on the individual's own return.
limitation: It is only the partnership channel, so a farmer operating as a sole trader shows nothing here and their result appears in the business income columns instead. Being a distributed share, it says nothing about the size or profitability of the partnership itself.
rationale: The partnerships and trusts item separates primary production partnership distributions from trust distributions and from the deductions that follow, which is the structure the custodian's label and the neighbouring columns reproduce.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's title-case wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the partnership share from the net primary production line beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net tax
value_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Reference material, Calculating net tax
variable_description: The tax a person owed for the year before refundable credits are applied, and the measure the ATO uses to call a taxpayer taxable or non-taxable. The ATO defines it: "Net tax is essentially the amount of tax owed for the income year, before applying refundable credits. It may not be the amount of tax payable or refundable on a notice of assessment." For individuals it is tax on taxable income plus extra income tax, less non-refundable offsets, plus the Medicare levy and surcharge, less any remaining foreign income tax offset. The column runs across every year of the withholding and debt tables except 2009-10.
description_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Reference material, Calculating net tax
value_definition: A whole-dollar calculated amount built from the individual formula published by the ATO, floored at zero for the purpose of classifying taxable and non-taxable entities.
limitation: It is not what the person paid or got back, because PAYG withholding, franking credits and other refundable credits have not been taken off, so a refund and a bill can sit behind the same net tax figure. Its inclusion of the Medicare levy and surcharge means it is not a clean measure of income tax alone.
rationale: The ATO's taxation statistics reference material gives the definition and the exact individual formula for net tax, which is what the custodian's one-word label names.
evidence_quote: Net tax is essentially the amount of tax owed for the income year, before applying refundable credits. It may not be the amount of tax payable or refundable on a notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Net tax' and printed the generic sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know it excludes refundable credits and includes the Medicare levy.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 20 label D
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: Foreign pensions and annuities that the recipient partly paid for themselves, reported net of expenses at item 20 label D. An undeducted purchase price is the part of the pension bought with contributions that were never deducted, and the ATO handles it as a separate deduction rather than a reduction here: "If your foreign pension or annuity has a deductible amount of a UPP, you claim a deduction for this amount at question D11." Foreign tax withheld overseas has to be added back before the figure is reported.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, grossed up for foreign tax, covering only those foreign pensions and annuities that carry an undeducted purchase price.
limitation: It is not the taxable amount, because the deductible part of the purchase price is subtracted at a different question, so this label overstates what is actually taxed. The instructions bar a loss larger than the pension itself, which compresses the distribution at the bottom.
rationale: Item 20 label D is a defined box and the ATO instructions state how pensions are sorted by UPP status and where the deductible amount is claimed.
evidence_quote: Don't include as a loss any amount by which the UPP exceeds the amount of your foreign pension or annuity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviated wording with the generic sentence twice, so it never explained what an undeducted purchase price is or that the deduction is taken elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 20 label L
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: Foreign pensions and annuities with no undeducted purchase price, which are assessable in full and reported at item 20 label L. The ATO makes the split the first step of the calculation: "Sort your foreign pensions and annuities into those with an undeducted purchase price (UPP) and those without a UPP." The companion label D holds the pensions the recipient part-funded, so the sorting step at the start of the calculation decides which of the two labels a given pension reaches.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, grossed up for any foreign tax withheld and reduced by deductible expenses other than interest and borrowing costs.
limitation: It cannot be compared directly with the UPP column as though the two were alternative measures of the same pension, since only the UPP side attracts a further deduction at D11. The label gives no country and no pension type, so a state age pension and a private annuity look identical.
rationale: Item 20 label L is a defined box and the ATO instructions describe the sorting step that separates it from label D and the expenses that are netted off.
evidence_quote: Sort your foreign pensions and annuities into those with an undeducted purchase price (UPP) and those without a UPP.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviated wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say why the with and without UPP labels are kept apart.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Totals column, net business result after deferred losses
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The final whole-business result for a sole trader, being the farm and non-farm figures added after prior-year deferred non-commercial losses. The ATO closes the block with: "Step 3 Add up the amounts at Y and Z. Enter the answer at Net income or loss from business in the Totals column. If the total is negative, print L in the box at the right of the amount." This is the bottom line of the business schedule, one step further on than the current-year total in the same table.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar sum of the after-deferral primary production and non-primary production results, with a loss carried by an adjacent flag.
limitation: It is a row total, so adding it to its two components counts the same business result twice, and its difference from the current-year total is the deferred loss adjustment rather than any trading activity. A negative stored without its loss flag will read as positive business income.
rationale: The ATO schedule instructions define the Totals column of the after-deferral line and the loss flag that accompanies it.
evidence_quote: Step 3 Add up the amounts at Y and Z. Enter the answer at Net income or loss from business in the Totals column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net income or loss from business - totals' with the generic sentence twice, so it was indistinguishable from the current-year total in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, item 15
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
variable_description: Tax a payer withheld from business payments because the person did not quote an Australian business number. The ATO identifies it by the code on the payment document: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule 2024 shown in the Tax withheld boxes where you have printed N in the Type box", and it must reconcile with the gross payments at P8 labels C and D. Withholding at the no-ABN rate is punitive, so the credit is large relative to the payment.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
value_definition: A dollar-and-cents withholding credit, reported with cents, drawn from payer-issued payment summaries and tied to a nominated pair of gross payment labels.
limitation: It marks the payer's treatment of the transaction, not the taxpayer's ABN status, since a person with a valid ABN who failed to quote it on one job appears here as well. It is a credit and cannot be added to any business income column.
rationale: The item 15 instructions define each business withholding box by its Type letter and its matching gross payments labels, which separates this column from the other three withholding columns on the same row.
evidence_quote: Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule 2024 shown in the Tax withheld boxes where you have printed N in the Type box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's run-on label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which payment summary code produces it or that the rate is punitive.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld under a voluntary agreement, item 15
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
variable_description: Tax withheld from a contractor's business income under a voluntary PAYG agreement between the contractor and the payer. The ATO identifies it by code: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule 2024 shown in the Tax withheld boxes where you have printed V in the Type box", and it must correspond with the gross payments at P8 labels E and F. Unlike the other three withholding boxes at question 15, this one exists only because both parties chose it, so it flags a deliberate arrangement rather than a default rule.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding credit, shown without cents, drawn from payment summaries carrying the voluntary agreement type code.
limitation: Its absence does not mean a person had no contracting income, only that no voluntary agreement was in place, so it cannot be used to count independent contractors. Like the other withholding boxes it is a credit and carries no information about the profitability of the work.
rationale: The item 15 instructions define this box by its Type letter and its matching gross payments labels, which is what tells it apart from the no-ABN, foreign resident and labour hire boxes.
evidence_quote: These amounts must correspond with the Gross payments shown at P8 Business income and expenses - labels E and F in the Business and professional items schedule 2024.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's compressed label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain that a voluntary agreement is elective and how the box is identified.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label C, non-primary production, current year
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: This year's trading result for a sole trader's non-farming activities, struck before prior-year deferred non-commercial losses are brought back. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "transfer the amount at row p on worksheet 6 to C item P8" and to print L beside it if the result is a loss. Because it stops short of the deferral step, it is the column to use when the question is whether a small business traded profitably in the reference year.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar net trading result for the year across all non-primary production business activities, after expenses and reconciliation adjustments.
limitation: A loss here is not necessarily deductible against other income, because the non-commercial loss rules can defer it, so this column overstates the tax relief a struggling business obtained. Several distinct businesses run by one person are added together and cannot be separated from this column alone.
rationale: P8 label C is a defined line on the schedule and the ATO instructions state how it is built and that it precedes the deferred loss adjustment.
evidence_quote: Step 2 Transfer the amount at row p on worksheet 6 to C item P8. Do not show cents. If the amount is a loss, print L in the box at the right of this amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's compressed label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not separate the current-year result from the after-deferral result in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from labour hire or specified payments, item 15
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
variable_description: Tax withheld from a person working through a labour hire firm, or from one of a short list of payments named in tax law. The ATO identifies it by code: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule 2024 shown in the Tax withheld boxes where you have printed S in the Type box", and it must correspond with the gross payments at P8 labels N and O. The specified payments are narrow, covering tutorial services under the Indigenous Student Success Programme, translating and interpreting for the national service, and performing artists in promotional activity.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 15 Net income or loss from business
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding credit, shown without cents, covering labour hire arrangements and the statutory list of specified payments together.
limitation: It does not isolate labour hire work, because the same box absorbs three unrelated specified payment types, so it cannot be used to size the labour hire workforce. As a withholding credit it says nothing about how much was earned or what the person was paid per engagement.
rationale: The item 15 instructions define this box by its Type letter and matching gross payments labels, and list the specified payments the box also covers.
evidence_quote: Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule 2024 shown in the Tax withheld boxes where you have printed S in the Type box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's compressed label with the generic sentence twice, so the mixing of labour hire and unrelated specified payments in one box was not recorded.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label Z, non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The final non-farming business result for a sole trader, after prior-year deferred non-commercial losses have been applied. The ATO gives the arithmetic: take the deferred non-primary production losses at label E away from the current-year figure at label C, "enter the answer at Z Net income or loss from business item P8", and print L if it is negative. This is the figure that leaves the schedule for label C at question 15 of the supplementary return.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions, P8 Business income and expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar net result for all non-primary production business activities, positive or flagged as a loss, after deferred non-commercial losses from earlier years.
limitation: It cannot be read as this year's trading performance, since a deferred loss from an earlier year can turn a profitable year negative, and the untouched trading figure is a separate column. A person who prints L here must also complete the loss activity items, so a loss carries a reporting obligation that a small profit does not.
rationale: P8 label Z is a defined line and the ATO schedule instructions state the calculation and its relationship to the current-year line above it.
evidence_quote: If you have net income from non-primary production business this year at C, take away from it the amount of your deferred non-commercial non-primary production business losses from a prior year shown at E.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net income or loss from business - non-primary production' with the generic sentence twice, giving no way to distinguish it from the other three non-primary production business columns in the table.

value_domain: Dollar amount of reportable fringe benefits, IT1 label W
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts
variable_description: Fringe benefits received from ordinary employers, meaning those that do pay fringe benefits tax. The ATO builds it from the documents: add the reportable fringe benefits amounts from "payment summaries with No selected at Is the employer exempt from FBT under section 57A of the FBTAA 1986" and from "income statements at Reportable fringe benefits - non-exempt amount". Benefits from exempt employers, mainly public hospitals and charities, go to label N instead, and the split first appeared on the 2016-17 return.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of grossed-up reportable fringe benefits amounts from non-exempt employers, counting only individual benefits at or above the year's reporting threshold of $3,773.
limitation: The amount is a grossed-up value used for income testing, so it is well above what the benefit cost the employer or was worth to the employee. Benefits below the threshold are excluded entirely, which means a zero does not establish that no benefits were received, and the column appears in the 2015-16 table a year before the return carried this label.
rationale: IT1 label W is a defined box and the ATO instructions state which payment summary answer feeds it and the threshold below which amounts are left out.
evidence_quote: This question is about reportable fringe benefits amounts that you received. Do not show any benefit less than $3,773.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long section 57A wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain grossing up, the reporting threshold, or when the exempt and non-exempt split began.

value_domain: Reportable fringe benefits total, employer not exempt under section 57A (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Reportable fringe benefits for employees
variable_description: Reportable fringe benefits on the 2023-24 return, for a payee whose employer is NOT exempt from fringe benefits tax under section 57A. It is the same concept as the 2022-23 column but spelled differently in the data item list, EXMPTN here against EXPTN there, so the series has to be joined by hand. The amount is grossed up and is not taxable income, though it counts toward the income tests behind the Medicare levy surcharge, family assistance and child support.
description_source: ATO, Reportable fringe benefits for employees
value_definition: A grossed-up dollar amount for the fringe benefits tax year, which runs to 31 March rather than 30 June. Employers report it only once the benefits exceed the reporting threshold.
limitation: The one-letter difference from the 2022-23 column name is a spelling variant in the source metadata rather than a change of meaning, and treating the two as different variables breaks a series that is continuous. The amount is grossed up, so it overstates the cash value of the benefit.
rationale: The ATO publishes what a reportable fringe benefits amount is and how the section 57A exemption splits it. That the two column names denote one concept is read from their identical custodian description and their appearance on consecutive years of the same table family.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description shared word for word with the 2022-23 column, and no value domain, so nothing recorded that the two names are the same variable in different years.

value_domain: Reportable fringe benefits total, employer not exempt under section 57A (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Reportable fringe benefits for employees
variable_description: Reportable fringe benefits on the 2022-23 return, for a payee whose employer is NOT exempt from fringe benefits tax under section 57A. The amount is grossed up, so it is larger than the benefit's cash value, and it is not taxable income: it does not enter the tax calculation but it does count toward the income tests behind the Medicare levy surcharge, family assistance and child support. The section 57A split matters because exempt employers - public hospitals, charities, ambulance services - have their own column, and only the non-exempt amount is treated this way in some of those tests.
description_source: ATO, Reportable fringe benefits for employees
value_definition: A grossed-up dollar amount for the fringe benefits tax year, which runs to 31 March rather than 30 June. Employers report it only once the benefits exceed the reporting threshold, so a zero means either no benefits or benefits below it.
limitation: The name differs by one letter from the 2023-24 column, NNELGBTXEXMPTN_FBT_TTLRPRTBAMT, which is the same concept in the following year; a name-based join across the two years silently drops both. The amount is grossed up, so reading it as the value of the benefit received overstates it by roughly the gross-up factor, and the threshold means small benefits are invisible rather than zero.
rationale: The ATO publishes what a reportable fringe benefits amount is, that it is grossed up, that it is not taxable income and that it counts toward income tests. The section 57A distinction is the ATO's own, and the column's sibling on the 2023-24 table carries the exempt-employer half.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description shared word for word with the 2023-24 column, and no value domain, so the two years looked like the same variable and neither said what year it belonged to.

value_domain: Dollar amount of non-refundable tax offsets applied at assessment
value_source: ATO, About tax offsets
variable_description: How much of a person's non-refundable tax offset entitlement the ATO actually applied against their tax for the year. It is an assessment outcome, not a label the taxpayer filled in, and it is capped by the tax they owed: the ATO says "Most offsets aren't refundable, which means they can't reduce your tax below zero." The neighbouring 'available' offset columns carry entitlement, so the two together show how much of an entitlement was wasted.
description_source: ATO, About tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount computed at assessment, summing the non-refundable offsets that were used across every offset type claimed on the return. It is bounded below by zero and above by tax payable before offsets.
limitation: It cannot measure entitlement or eligibility. A zero here is as likely to mean the person had no tax to reduce as it is to mean they claimed nothing, so an offset take-up rate built from this column will understate claims among low-income filers.
rationale: The label names the used, rather than available, total of non-refundable offsets, and the ATO's own explanation of tax offsets sets out exactly why a used amount differs from an entitlement.
evidence_quote: Most offsets aren't refundable, which means they can't reduce your tax below zero.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Non refundable offsets used' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the amount is capped by tax payable rather than by entitlement.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Spouse details label S
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts and Spouse details
variable_description: The reportable fringe benefits the taxpayer's spouse received from employers that are not exempt from fringe benefits tax under section 57A. The lodger copies the figure their spouse reports at IT1 label W into the spouse details section, and the ATO treats the two as one quantity: "We don't adjust the amounts at question IT1 - label W, and question Spouse details - married or de facto - label S, when we calculate the following offsets." The exempt-employer half of the spouse's benefits sits in the neighbouring column.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts and Spouse details
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up taxable value of fringe benefits, originally reported by the spouse's employer on an income statement or payment summary, with benefits below the reporting threshold (currently $3,773) excluded.
limitation: It is one side of a split the return did not always have, so it cannot be joined to the single spouse fringe benefits total that earlier years carried without breaking the series. It is also third-hand: the lodger is describing someone else's income, and the instructions permit a reasonable estimate.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the section 57A non-exempt half of the spouse's reportable fringe benefits, and the ATO instruction for IT1 defines that half and states that the spouse details label carries the same amount.
evidence_quote: We don't adjust the amounts at question IT1 - label W, and question Spouse details - married or de facto - label S, when we calculate the following offsets
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long custodian label and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said where the figure comes from, that a spouse's employer reports it, or that it is only half of the spouse's reportable benefits.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Deductions the taxpayer claims against non-primary production distributions from partnerships and trusts. The ATO instruction is to "Write at question 13 - label Y the total of other deductions (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) you can claim in relation to your share of both: non-primary production income or loss from a partnership; non-primary production income of a trust". It is subtracted, with the landcare deduction at label J, when the net non-primary production amount is worked out.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: Whole dollars, self-assessed, covering residual deductions against flow-through income: it excludes the landcare expenditure claimed at label J and the primary production equivalent claimed at label X.
limitation: It does not separate a current-year expense from a business loss deferred out of an earlier year, and the only thing that distinguishes them is the Type code beside it, which reports all, part or none rather than an amount.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the non-primary production other deductions against distributions, which is the ATO's own description of item 13 label Y, and the instruction defines what may and may not go there.
evidence_quote: Write at question 13 - label Y the total of other deductions (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) you can claim in relation to your share of both:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so it never identified the label or said that deferred prior-year losses are folded into the same number.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label C
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Franked distributions a beneficiary received from trusts, shown apart from the rest of their trust income. The ATO says: "If your statement of distribution or advice shows your share of franked distributions from trusts separately, write this amount at label C, together with any share of franking credits referrable to those franked distributions." A partner in a partnership never uses this label, because the same instruction sends partnership franked distributions to label O.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: Whole dollars, grossed up to include the attached franking credits, and confined to non-primary production trust income.
limitation: It captures only the trust channel, so it understates a person's franked income from flow-through entities whenever a partnership is in the chain. The credits themselves are claimed again at label Q, so adding this column to label Q counts the gross-up twice.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own name for item 13 label C, and the instruction states what goes in the label, what it must include and which taxpayers must use a different label instead.
evidence_quote: If your statement of distribution or advice shows your share of franked distributions from trusts separately, write this amount at label C, together with any share of franking credits referrable to those franked distributions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never said the amount includes franking credits or that partnership distributions are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 16 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
variable_description: Losses from non-primary production business activities that the taxpayer was not allowed to use this year and had to defer. The ATO is explicit that the number does no work in the current year: "You can't use the amount at question 16 to reduce your 2024-25 taxable income." It is a subtotal, formed by adding the non-primary production part of the partnership losses at label F to the non-primary production part of the sole trader losses at label G.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
value_definition: Whole dollars of net loss deferred under the non-commercial business loss rules, split from the primary production deferral at label I.
limitation: It cannot tell you whether the loss came from a partnership or from a sole trader activity, because the split by legal form lives in labels F and G. Nor is it a loss written off: the amount stays available against the same or a similar activity in a later year, and bankruptcy is the main way it disappears.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the non-primary production deferred loss total, which the ATO instruction defines as label J and builds from labels F and G.
evidence_quote: Add up any amounts of non-primary production deferred losses at question 16 - labels F and G. Write the total of non-primary production deferred losses at question 16 - label J.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that the amount is quarantined from taxable income or that it is a subtotal of two other labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A partner's share of landcare operations spending, claimed against non-primary production distributions at item 13 label J. The deduction is pushed out to the partners rather than taken by the entity: "If a partnership incurs eligible expenditure on landcare operations, the partnership can't claim the expenditure. Costs the partnership incurs are allocated to each partner who can then claim the deduction." The primary production version of the same claim sits at label I and is wider, taking in water facilities, fencing and fodder storage assets.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the taxpayer's allocated share of eligible landcare expenditure that is deductible in the year of the return.
limitation: It is a partner's claim only. A trust beneficiary can never appear here, because the instruction reserves the deduction to the trustee, so a zero says nothing about whether the underlying entity spent money on landcare.
rationale: The custodian's wording names non-primary production landcare operations expenses, which the ATO instruction places at item 13 label J and defines by who may claim it.
evidence_quote: Write your share of the total of any such expenditure that relates to non-primary production income or loss from partnerships that you can deduct in 2024-25 at question 13 - label J in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that only partners can use the label or how it differs from the primary production landcare column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at L1 label R
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
variable_description: The stock of non-primary production tax losses from earlier years that the taxpayer brought into this return. The worksheet reaches it by taking losses from earlier years and reducing them by net exempt income: "Non-primary production losses available for use in 2024-25. Subtract row f from row c." How much of that stock was actually deducted is the claimed column at label Z, not this one.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
value_definition: Whole dollars of prior-year losses available for use, already net of exempt income and split from the primary production stock at label Q.
limitation: It is the opening balance, not the closing one. The instructions tell the taxpayer to keep their own record of what carries forward to the next year, so the amount still unused at year end cannot be read off the return and has to be reconstructed from this column and the claimed column.
rationale: The custodian's wording names non-primary production losses carried forward at L1, and the instruction gives the worksheet row that feeds label R and the deduction for net exempt income.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount at row i to question L1 - label R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished the available stock from the amount claimed, which is the confusion this pair of columns invites.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at L1 label Z
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
variable_description: How much of the taxpayer's earlier-year non-primary production losses was actually deducted against this year's income. The amount is mechanical rather than chosen: the instruction says the steps "will help you work out what to write at question L1 - labels F and Z, if the amount at Subtotal isn't a loss", and primary production losses at label F are applied before any non-primary production loss reaches label Z. The stock the claim draws on is the carried-forward column at label R.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
value_definition: Whole dollars, bounded above by the losses available at label R and by the income left after the primary production claim at label F.
limitation: A zero does not mean the person had no losses. It usually means there was no income left to absorb them, so this column measures the interaction of losses with income rather than the existence of losses, which only label R can show.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the non-primary production losses claimed this year, and the L1 instruction sets out the ordering rule that determines the amount at label Z.
evidence_quote: The following steps will help you work out what to write at question L1 - labels F and Z, if the amount at Subtotal isn't a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the claim is forced by a worksheet or that it is capped by the primary production claim on the same row.

value_domain: Type code beside item 13 label Y (D, P or blank)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A one-letter code saying how much of the deduction at item 13 label Y is a business loss deferred out of an earlier year. The ATO sets only two codes: "Print D if the entire amount at label Y is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year" and "Print P if only part of the amount at label Y is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year", with the box left blank otherwise. It qualifies the non-primary production deduction column beside it and nothing else.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A single character: D where the whole label Y amount is a deferred loss, P where only part of it is, and blank where none of it is.
