limitation: P gives no fraction, so the deferred component cannot be recovered from the code and the amount together. The matching code for primary production sits in the Type box at label X and is a separate column, so this one says nothing about farm activities.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a type code for other deductions against non-primary production distributions, and the instruction publishes the two-value code list for the Type box at label Y.
evidence_quote: Print D if the entire amount at label Y is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, even though the ATO publishes a two-value code list for this exact box.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at IT6 Net rental property loss
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT6 Net rental property loss
variable_description: A person's total loss from renting out property, collected for the income tests rather than for working out taxable income. The ATO defines it plainly: "Net property loss is the amount of net loss from any rental property you own", and says "We'll calculate the amount of your net rental property loss for you using the information you provide in your tax return." It pulls together net rent, net foreign rent, partnership rental distributions and rental business income, less low-value pool and other rental deductions.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT6 Net rental property loss
value_definition: A whole-dollar loss amount, written as zero whenever the rental position is a profit, and covering Australian and foreign rent together.
limitation: It is censored at zero, so it cannot measure rental profit, the number of properties or the scale of a portfolio, and a zero cannot be read as 'no rental property'. Capital gains and losses on rental properties are excluded, so it is not a measure of how a property investment performed.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own name for the income test item, and the instruction defines the quantity and lists the components its worksheet adds and subtracts.
evidence_quote: Net property loss is the amount of net loss from any rental property you own.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Net rental property loss' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the value is censored at zero or that it is an income test measure rather than a deduction.

value_domain: ATO salary and wage occupation code
value_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
variable_description: The coded occupation the taxpayer gave for the salary and wage job that earned them the most during the year. The coverage rule is narrow: "the occupation description and codes apply to salary and wage income only and not to other types of income such as pensions and business or investment income". Where nothing fits, the ATO directs the filer to "use the 'Occupation not listed' code 999000", so that value is a residual rather than an occupation.
description_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
value_definition: A numeric code drawn from the ATO's published salary and wage occupation list, six digits in the current edition and grouped by the leading digits, with 999000 reserved for occupations not on the list.
limitation: It is not a labour force classification and not a person's main activity. A wage earner who also runs a business is coded on the wage job alone, a person with no salary or wages has no code at all, and the code is entered by the filer or their agent rather than derived from an employer record.
rationale: The custodian's wording names an occupation group code on the individual return, and the ATO publishes the code list, the label it is written at and the rule for choosing between multiple jobs.
evidence_quote: the occupation description and codes apply to salary and wage income only and not to other types of income such as pensions and business or investment income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt custodian wording 'Ocupation group code' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which job is coded, that the list is the ATO's own, or that 999000 means not listed.

value_domain: ato_salary_wage_occupation_4digit
value_source: ATO 'Salary and wage occupation codes' NAT 1932-6.2006 (for 2005-06 and subsequent year tax returns), numeric listing. The publication states its codes are the same as NAT 1932-6.2003 and subsequent versions.
variable_description: The four digit code for the occupation that earned the taxpayer the most salary and wage income in the year. The ATO's code list states the rule: "You must provide an accurate description of a taxpayer's main salary and wage occupation at item 1 of the tax return, and insert the appropriate 4-digit code from the list at X item 1." This is the older ATO list rather than ANZSCO, and it is unchanged from the 2002-03 publication onwards, so codes compare across the years the column covers. IDV_OCPTN_CD carries the same item in the later context tables.
description_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes (NAT 1932-6.2006), for 2005-06 and subsequent year tax returns
value_definition: Four digit numeric codes grouped into broad occupation categories, running from 0910 army officer through to the nine hundreds for labourers, with 0990 reserved for an occupation not listed.
limitation: Only salary and wage work is coded, so a sole trader, a retiree or an investor has no meaningful value here. The codes also do not map one to one onto ANZSCO or ASCO, so they cannot be joined to Census or Labour Force occupation data without a concordance.
rationale: OCPTN4_CD is the 'old' occupation code held for 2006-07 to 2008-09, and the ATO's occupation code at label X of item 1 was a 4-digit ASCO-based code in exactly those years before the 6-digit ANZSCO-based list took over.
evidence_quote: insert the appropriate 4-digit code from the list at X item 1
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination missed that the ATO publishes the 4-digit list; the bundled ato-occupation-codes.tsv is the later 6-digit list, not this one.

value_domain: Dollar cost reported at P18 label J
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P17 to P20 Depreciating assets
variable_description: The cost of tangible depreciating assets the business began claiming decline in value on for the first time this year. The ATO says: "At P18 Other depreciating assets first deducted you need to include the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time." Assets costing under $1,000 that went into a low-value pool are counted here too, and the cost is not scaled back for private use.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P17 to P20 Depreciating assets
value_definition: Whole dollars of asset cost, summed across all of the person's businesses, and covering everything except the intangible assets that are reported at P17.
limitation: It is not depreciation and not investment in the year. An asset bought in an earlier year but first deducted now lands here, and an asset the business bought and immediately wrote off under a small business concession may be reported elsewhere, so this column will not reconcile to capital spending.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own name for P18, and the instruction defines what the label counts, how pooled assets are treated and that cost is not reduced for non-taxable use.
evidence_quote: At P18 Other depreciating assets first deducted you need to include the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the figure is a cost rather than a deduction or how it differs from the intangible column.

value_domain: Dollar termination value reported at P20 label K
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P17 to P20 Depreciating assets
variable_description: What the business received for tangible depreciating assets it stopped holding or using during the year. The ATO defines the amount as "the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using", including the market value of non-cash benefits, and substitutes market value where the parties do not deal at arm's length. Assets sold, lost or destroyed are all treated the same way, and the intangible equivalent is reported separately at P19.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P17 to P20 Depreciating assets
value_definition: Whole dollars, summed across the person's businesses, and including assets that had been allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: It is gross proceeds, not a gain or a loss on disposal: working out the balancing adjustment needs the asset's adjustable value, which the schedule never collects. It also gives no count of assets, so a single large disposal and many small ones look identical.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the termination value of other depreciating assets, which is the ATO's own name for P20, and the instruction defines termination value and the non-arm's length rule.
evidence_quote: Generally, the termination value is the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what termination value means or that it is not a measure of profit on disposal.

value_domain: Dollar amount of baby bonus claimed as a refundable tax offset
value_source: ATO Legal database, Explanatory Memorandum, Taxation Laws Amendment (Baby Bonus) Act 2002
variable_description: A parent's claim for the first-child baby bonus in a year after the year they first claimed it. This was a tax measure rather than a welfare payment: "The Baby Bonus is available as a refundable tax offset" and "Taxpayers will be able to make a claim for the Baby Bonus as part of their annual income tax return process." The explanatory memorandum sets the size and duration of the entitlement: "The repayment of tax will occur over a maximum period of 5 years with a maximum entitlement of $2,500 per year", with a $500 minimum for people on $25,000 or less.
description_source: ATO Legal database, Explanatory Memorandum, Taxation Laws Amendment (Baby Bonus) Act 2002
value_definition: Whole dollars, refundable, generally derived from the claimant's gross tax paid in a base year spread over five years and capped at $2,500 a year.
limitation: It is not the maternity payment that later took the same popular name, so it cannot be used as a measure of birth-related assistance across the 2000s. The entitlement could also be transferred to a spouse, so the person carrying the amount is not necessarily the parent who gave birth.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a baby bonus claim in a year of the individual return when the first-child refundable tax offset was in force, and the explanatory memorandum gives the offset's nature, ceiling, floor and five-year run.
evidence_quote: The Baby Bonus is available as a refundable tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Baby bonus claim' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said which baby bonus this is or that it was a refundable offset claimed through the return.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Expenses label K
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Expenses
variable_description: The value of trading stock the business held at the start of the income year, across primary and non-primary production together. The figure is tied to the year before rather than independently measured: "The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous year." Stock of a business that started up during the year is deliberately left out and shows up in purchases instead.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Expenses
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the sum of the primary production and non-primary production opening stock columns of the P8 expenses section.
limitation: It is not an independent inventory count, and where the change in stock over the year is $5,000 or less the taxpayer may repeat the opening value as closing stock, so a zero change between the two columns can mean a genuine reconciliation or an election not to count.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the opening stock total, which the ATO instruction places at P8 Expenses label K and defines by reference to last year's closing stock.
evidence_quote: The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Opening stock - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the value is constrained to equal last year's closing stock or that new businesses are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar compulsory study and training loan repayment raised on an overseas resident
value_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
variable_description: The compulsory Trade Support Loan repayment worked out for a person who was living overseas, based on their worldwide income rather than their Australian income. Leaving the country does not suspend the debt: "You must repay your HELP (previously known as HECS), AASL (previously known as TSL) and VSL if you live overseas and are not an Australian resident for tax purposes." The Trade Support Loan has since been renamed the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan, so the column and the current ATO wording use different names for the same debt.
description_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
value_definition: A whole-dollar obligation raised at assessment, calculated from repayment income plus non-resident foreign sourced income against the published minimum repayment thresholds.
limitation: It only exists where the person reported worldwide income, so a zero mixes a genuine below-threshold year with a year of non-reporting. It is an amount raised, not an amount collected, and voluntary payments made from overseas do not reduce it.
rationale: The custodian's wording names an overseas Trade Support Loan compulsory repayment, and the ATO's overseas repayment guidance sets out the obligation, the income base and the compulsory-versus-levy split.
evidence_quote: You must repay your HELP (previously known as HECS), AASL (previously known as TSL) and VSL if you live overseas and are not an Australian resident for tax purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Overseas TSL compulsory repayment due' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount rests on self-reported worldwide income or that the loan has been renamed.

value_domain: Dollar HELP repayment obligation raised on an overseas resident
value_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
variable_description: The Higher Education Loan Program repayment obligation raised on a person who lived overseas and reported their worldwide income. The obligation is not always the same instrument: "Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up", so this column and the overseas levy column beside it describe two routes to the same debt. The Trade Support Loan and VET Student Loan columns on the same row carry the equivalent amounts for those loan types.
description_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
value_definition: Whole dollars raised against a HELP account at assessment, worked out from repayment income plus non-resident foreign sourced income converted to Australian dollars.
limitation: It says nothing about the loan balance behind it, which keeps being indexed whether or not a repayment is raised. A person with a HELP debt who never lodged a worldwide income report simply has no row, so absence is not evidence of no debt.
rationale: The custodian's wording names an overseas HELP repayment, and the ATO's overseas repayment guidance defines the income base and distinguishes a compulsory repayment from an overseas levy.
evidence_quote: Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Overseas HELP repayment' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished it from the levy and Trade Support Loan columns beside it.

value_domain: Dollar VET Student Loan overseas repayment obligation
value_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
variable_description: The VET Student Loan repayment obligation raised on a person living overseas, charged as an overseas levy where the income behind it was foreign sourced. The ATO explains the split: "Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up." A levy is worked out on net non-resident foreign sourced income after a standard deduction under the simple self-assessment method, which is why it can differ from an ordinary compulsory repayment on the same income.
description_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
value_definition: Whole dollars raised against a VET Student Loan account, derived from worldwide income converted to Australian dollars under one of the three published income assessment methods.
limitation: The column cannot show which assessment method produced the figure, and the three methods give different answers on the same underlying income. It also covers only the VET loan, so a person with several study debts has their obligation spread across the neighbouring loan columns.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a VET Support Loan overseas compulsory repayable amount, and the ATO's overseas repayment guidance defines the overseas levy, the income base and the assessment methods.
evidence_quote: Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what an overseas levy is or why it sits apart from a compulsory repayment.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessable Australian pension and annuity income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: The assessable amount of Australian pensions and annuities other than government pensions and allowances, which are reported at their own item. The ATO describes the private side of this income as follows: "Australian annuities (or non-super annuities) are a series of regular payments you receive from a life insurance company or friendly society in return for a lump sum payment." The amount is net of the deductible part of any undeducted purchase price, so it is smaller than the gross pension shown on the payer's payment summary.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_definition: Whole dollars of assessable pension or annuity income, taken from a payment summary issued by a super fund, retirement savings account provider or life office, and reduced by the deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price.
limitation: It is not a measure of retirement income across time. From 1 July 2007 superannuation income streams from a taxed source stopped being assessable for people aged 60 and over, so the same person with the same pension can drop out of this column entirely without any change in what they receive.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other Australian pensions or annuities on an early individual return, and the current instruction for the successor item defines the income, its source documents and the undeducted purchase price adjustment.
evidence_quote: Australian annuities (or non-super annuities) are a series of regular payments you receive from a life insurance company or friendly society in return for a lump sum payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other Australian pensions or annuities' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said what the amount excludes or that the 2007 superannuation changes break the series.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Income label J
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Income
variable_description: Business income from non-primary production activities that none of the named payment labels picked up, which for most sole traders is the bulk of their turnover. It is defined by exclusion: "Your 'other business income' excludes amounts shown at labels C, D, B, E, F, N, O, G and H in your schedule." What is left includes gross sales of trading stock, gross earnings from services, recouped expenses, bad debts recovered, profit on sale of depreciating assets, royalties, insurance recoveries, subsidies and foreign exchange gains.

The ATO describes the two routes: the rebate can be claimed "through your private health insurance provider (where it will be applied to reduce your private health insurance premiums)" or "when you lodge your tax return - as a refundable tax offset". Because it is refundable, the amount is paid out even where the person owes no tax.
description_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
value_definition: Whole dollars of refundable offset for premiums paid on an eligible policy during the year, covering only the part of the entitlement not already delivered as a premium reduction.
limitation: It measures a claiming channel, not a benefit. Most policyholders take the rebate as reduced premiums and never appear in this column, so it cannot be used to count people with private cover or to size the rebate they received.
rationale: The custodian's wording describes the refundable offset for rebate not previously taken as a premium reduction, and the ATO page defines the two claiming routes and the refundable character of the tax return route.
evidence_quote: when you lodge your tax return - as a refundable tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long custodian label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the column captures only one of the two ways of getting the rebate.

value_domain: Count of dependent children recorded for private health insurance purposes
value_source: ATO, Income thresholds and rates for the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: How many dependent children the taxpayer reported in the private health insurance part of the return. The count does two jobs in the current system: it decides whether the single or family thresholds apply, since a single person with dependent children "is considered a family and will be income tested using the family income thresholds", and it lifts the family threshold, which "is increased by $1,500 for every Medicare levy surcharge dependent child after the first child". It is a count of children, not of people covered by a policy.
description_source: ATO, Income thresholds and rates for the private health insurance rebate
value_definition: A small non-negative integer, self-reported, counting dependent children as defined for the Medicare levy surcharge rather than for family assistance.
limitation: It cannot be read as the number of children on the health policy, which the ATO treats as a different concept, and in the earliest years of the column the rebate itself was not income tested, so the count then bore on surcharge thresholds rather than on the size of any rebate.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a private health insurance dependant children count, and the ATO's threshold page explains what a dependent child count does in the private health insurance rules; the page does not document the field on the 1999-2000 return itself.
evidence_quote: If you have 2 or more children, the family income threshold is increased by $1,500 for every Medicare levy surcharge dependent child after the first child.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the count is used for or how it differs from the people covered by a policy.

value_domain: Dollar private health insurance rebate calculated at assessment
value_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: The rebate the ATO worked out for the person when it assessed the return, rather than an amount they claimed. The ATO explains: "If you haven't received your full private health insurance rebate entitlement, we calculate the rebate amount you are entitled to, which becomes payable to you as a refundable tax offset when we assess your tax return." The calculation runs against the income thresholds and against the person's share of the policy, so two adults on one policy can be assessed differently.
description_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
value_definition: Whole dollars of refundable offset determined at assessment from the person's income for surcharge purposes, their share of the premiums and the tax claim code they selected.
limitation: It only records rebate flowing to the taxpayer. Where too much was taken as a premium reduction the correction goes the other way and appears as an excess private health insurance liability, so this column alone cannot give the net position between a household and the rebate.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a calculated private health insurance rebate, and the ATO page states that the ATO calculates the entitlement at assessment and how the income test and policy share enter it.
evidence_quote: If you haven't received your full private health insurance rebate entitlement, we calculate the rebate amount you are entitled to, which becomes payable to you as a refundable tax offset when we assess your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Private health insurance rebate' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is calculated by the ATO or that an over-claim is recorded as a liability elsewhere.

value_domain: Date a payment covered by the payment summary was made
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Rules of reporting through STP
variable_description: The date attached to the payment behind the summary row, as distinct from the reporting period that the start and end date columns carry. Payroll reporting defines the date from the payer's side: "The pay day is either the payment date stipulated in the electronic transaction to your financial institution or, if you did not specify a date for payment, the date you intend to make the payment into your employee's bank account." It is most meaningful on rows for a single dated payment, such as a termination or lump sum, where a period would say little.
description_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Rules of reporting through STP
value_definition: A calendar date reported by the payer, falling in or near the financial year of the summary, and paired on the same row with the payment summary type that says what kind of payment it was.
limitation: The registry metadata does not say which payment summary types populate it, so a blank cannot be told apart from a type that never carries a payment date. It is also the payer's intended pay day rather than the day money reached the payee's account, so it can precede receipt.
rationale: The column sits in a payment summary table alongside the period dates and the payment summary type, and the payroll reporting rules define the payment date a payer supplies; no fetchable page documents this PLIDA field directly.
evidence_quote: The pay day is either the payment date stipulated in the electronic transaction to your financial institution or, if you did not specify a date for payment, the date you intend to make the payment into your employee's bank account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Payment date' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished it from the period start and end dates on the same row.

value_domain: PAYG payment summary type
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary forms and guidelines
variable_description: Which PAYG payment summary form this row came off, which decides what the amounts on it mean. The ATO issues a different form for each kind of payment: individual non-business for employees, company directors and office holders; business and personal services income for contractors; employment termination payment; superannuation lump sum and superannuation income stream; and foreign employment. Reading gross amounts across rows without this column adds together quantities that are not comparable.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary forms and guidelines
limitation: The ATO publishes the forms but not the codes PLIDA uses for them, so the mapping between the values here and the form names is not confirmed. Someone who received more than one kind of payment from one payer has a separate row for each.
rationale: The field is named as a PAYG payment summary type on the payment summary tables, and the ATO publishes the set of forms it corresponds to. The codes themselves are not published.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Payg payment summary type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset calculated for a government pension or allowance recipient
value_source: ATO, Beneficiary tax offset
variable_description: The offset the ATO worked out for someone receiving a government pension or allowance, so that the payment itself does not generate tax. Nothing is claimed on the form: "We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return." Where a person qualifies under more than one of these concessions only one is granted, because "If you are eligible for both offsets, you will receive the one with the highest amount."
description_source: ATO, Beneficiary tax offset
value_definition: Whole dollars, calculated from the taxable government payments received and the person's other income, and applied as a non-refundable offset in the assessment.
limitation: It cannot identify the payment behind it, since the pension and the allowance concessions resolve to a single amount and only the larger one survives. Being non-refundable it is also zero for a recipient with no other income, which is the majority of full-rate recipients.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a calculated rebate for pensioners and government allowance recipients, and the ATO page for that offset states that it is calculated automatically and that only the larger of the competing offsets is given.
evidence_quote: We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pensioner rebate amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is ATO-calculated or that it collapses two competing concessions into one figure.

value_domain: Tax offset code letter recording the claimant's circumstances
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: A code letter recording the living and partnership circumstances that set the rate of the pensioner tax offset. The surviving version of this box, on the seniors and pensioners offset, uses five letters for circumstances such as "You're single, separated or widowed" and living apart because one partner is in a nursing home, with the letter chosen at the taxpayer's circumstances at any time in the year. On the earlier return the pensioner offset stood apart from the senior Australians offset and carried its own code list.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
value_definition: A single letter identifying the claimant's circumstances for offset rate purposes, drawn from the code list printed in the instructions for the year of the return.
limitation: The code list for the earlier pensioner offset is not published on the current page, so a letter in this column must not be read against the modern list. It describes household circumstances for offset purposes only, and does not establish who a person lived with.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a pensioner tax offset code, and the current instruction documents the equivalent code box on the successor offset; the earlier code list itself was not found on a fetchable page.
evidence_quote: No, print your code letter from Step 1 in the TAX OFFSET CODE box at question T1 - label N.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pensioner tax offset code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the code describes or warned that the list has been rewritten since.

value_domain: Veteran code letter accompanying the pensioner tax offset claim
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: A code saying whether the claimant, their spouse or both are a veteran, war widow or war widower, which matters because veterans reach the offset at a younger age. The ATO publishes three values: "V - you're a veteran, war widow or war widower", "W - your spouse is a veteran, war widow or war widower" and "X - both V and W apply to you and your spouse". It qualifies the pensioner offset claim on the same row rather than standing on its own.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
value_definition: A single letter, present only where the claimant or their spouse has veteran, war widow or war widower status, and blank otherwise.
limitation: It cannot count veterans in the tax population, because it is recorded only where the person claimed the offset and met its other conditions. It also does not say which department pays the pension, so it is not a substitute for a veterans' affairs record.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a pensioner veteran code, and the ATO instruction for the surviving offset publishes the veteran code box and its three values.
evidence_quote: V - you're a veteran, war widow or war widower
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pensioner veteran code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the ATO publishes the three code values, and it never said the code is conditional on an offset claim.

value_domain: Dollar averaging adjustment for a primary producer
value_source: ATO, Income averaging for primary producers
variable_description: The result of evening out a primary producer's income across years, which is a tax offset in a good year and extra tax in a bad one. The ATO gives the formula: "The averaging adjustment is the averaging component (step 2) multiplied by the gross averaging amount (step 3) divided by the basic taxable income", and notes that "The amount of your averaging tax offset or extra income tax is calculated automatically." The first adjustment a farmer ever receives is always favourable: it "is always a tax offset (or nil)".
description_source: ATO, Income averaging for primary producers
value_definition: Whole dollars produced at assessment, being the difference between tax at basic rates and tax at the comparison rate applied to the averaging component of basic taxable income.
limitation: The sign is what matters and the label does not carry it: the same column holds an offset in one year and complementary tax, which is a liability, in another. It also cannot be read as a measure of farm income volatility, because averaging draws on up to five years of income including non-farm income.
rationale: The custodian's wording names complementary tax and the averaging tax offset together, and the ATO's income averaging page defines the adjustment, its two directions and how it is calculated.
evidence_quote: The amount of your averaging tax offset or extra income tax is calculated automatically. Your notice of assessment will show you the averaging details.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Complementary tax / averaging tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that one column carries both a benefit and a liability.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 16 label I
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
variable_description: Losses from farm and other primary production activities that the non-commercial loss rules would not let the taxpayer use this year. The instruction builds the label from the two business forms: "Add up any amounts of primary production deferred losses at question 16 - labels F and G. Write the total of primary production deferred losses at question 16 - label I." The loss is parked rather than lost, and comes back against the same or a similar activity in a later year.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
value_definition: Whole dollars of deferred primary production loss, sitting beside the non-primary production deferral at label J and outside taxable income for the year.
limitation: A large amount here does not mean a failing farm: the deferral rules bite hardest on people whose other income is high, so the column partly measures the taxpayer's non-farm income rather than the farm's performance. It also cannot separate partnership from sole trader losses.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the primary production deferred losses total, which the ATO instruction defines as item 16 label I built from labels F and G.
evidence_quote: Add up any amounts of primary production deferred losses at question 16 - labels F and G. Write the total of primary production deferred losses at question 16 - label I.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is quarantined for the year or that it aggregates two business forms.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label I
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A partner's share of farm conservation and water spending, claimed against primary production distributions. The label is wider than its non-primary production twin, covering "eligible expenditure on landcare operations, water facilities, fencing assets or fodder storage assets", and the partnership cannot claim any of it: the costs are allocated out to the partners. Where a trust rather than a partnership spent the money, only the trustee can deduct it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the partner's allocated share of eligible primary production conservation and water expenditure deductible in the year.
limitation: The four kinds of asset it covers cannot be told apart within the label, so it will not support a statement about drought infrastructure or fencing on its own. A beneficiary of a trust that spent the money records nothing, so the column understates the expenditure sitting behind farm structures.
rationale: The custodian's wording names landcare operations and the water facility deduction for primary production, which the ATO instruction places at item 13 label I and defines by the allocation rule.
evidence_quote: Write your share of the total of any such expenditure that relates to primary production income or loss from partnerships that you can deduct this year at question 13 - label I in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which assets the label covers or that trust beneficiaries are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at L1 label F
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
variable_description: How much of the taxpayer's earlier-year primary production losses was deducted against this year's income. Farm losses are used before other losses: the worksheet transfers the primary production stock at label Q into label F when income allows, and only what is left over reaches the non-primary production claim. The instruction then says that subtracting "the amount at label F from the amount at label Q" gives the primary production losses carried forward to next year.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
value_definition: Whole dollars, capped by the primary production losses available at label Q and by the income remaining before losses are applied.
limitation: It cannot be read as a choice or as a sign of farm distress. The worksheet forces the order and the amount, so a farmer with large losses and no income shows zero here while the losses remain intact in the carried-forward column.
rationale: The custodian's wording names primary production losses claimed this income year, and the L1 instruction sets out how label F is filled from label Q and what the remainder becomes.
evidence_quote: Subtract the amount at label F from the amount at label Q. The answer is the amount of primary production losses you carry forward to 2025-26.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said farm losses are applied first or that a zero can coexist with a large loss balance.

value_domain: Dollar amount of carried-forward primary production tax losses (question L1, label Q)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
variable_description: The stock of unused farming and fishing losses the taxpayer brought into the year from earlier years, written at question L1 label Q. The ATO sets the amount as the balance after exempt income is absorbed: "The amount of tax losses from earlier income years that you write at question L1 – labels Q and R is the amount of tax losses you carry forward from 2023–24 less the amount of your net exempt income for 2024–25". Losses have to be split by activity, because primary production losses and non-primary production losses at label R are carried and applied separately.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, self-assessed from the taxpayer's own loss records rather than from any third-party report. It is a stock brought forward, so the same underlying loss can appear year after year until it is used up.
limitation: It is the loss available, not the loss used: the amount actually deducted this year sits at label F, and a large figure here can coexist with no deduction at all if there is no income to absorb it. Because the balance is the taxpayer's own running record, an error carries forward across years unchanged.
rationale: The DIL label names primary production losses of earlier income years carried forward, which is question L1 label Q on the individual return. The 2025 instructions define how the figure is worked out and why it is split from the non-primary production balance; the 2011 edition uses the same labels, so the reading holds across the years the column covers.
evidence_quote: The amount of tax losses from earlier income years that you write at question L1 – labels Q and R is the amount of tax losses you carry forward from 2023–24 less the amount of your net exempt income for 2024–25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said this is a stock of losses available rather than a deduction claimed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other deductions against primary production distributions (item 13, label X)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Deductions the taxpayer claims against their farming or fishing distributions from partnerships and trusts, at question 13 label X. The ATO asks for "the total of any other deductions (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) you can claim" in relation to that share of primary production income. It is a residual: landcare and water facility expenditure has its own label I, and the non-primary production equivalent is label Y.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction total for one taxpayer, self-assessed. It is subtracted, along with label I, from the primary production distributions at labels N and L to give the net primary production amount on the same row.
limitation: It cannot tell you what the deductions were for, because a deferred loss released from an earlier year and an ordinary current-year expense both land in the one box; the type code beside it only says whether deferred losses are part or all of the figure. It is also a deduction against a distribution, not an expense of the partnership, so it says nothing about the partnership's own costs.
rationale: The DIL label names other deductions relating to a primary production distribution, which is question 13 label X. The 2025 instructions state what goes in the box, what is excluded to label I, and how the amount feeds the net primary production calculation.
evidence_quote: Write at question 13 – label X the total of any other deductions (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) you can claim in relation to your share of either:
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's compressed wording, 'Other deductions relating to distribution primary deduction', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell which question it belonged to.

value_domain: Deferred non-commercial loss type code at item 13, label X (D, P or blank)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A one-letter code saying how much of the primary production deduction beside it is a business loss released from an earlier year. The ATO sets three states: "Print D if the entire amount at label X is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year", print P if only part of it is, and "Leave the Type box blank if the amount at label X doesn't include any deferred non-commercial business losses from a prior income year". It qualifies PP_OTHR_DDCTNS_DSTBN_AMT on the same row and has no meaning without it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A single character: D for all, P for part, blank for none. The type box sits beside label X and there is a separate one for the non-primary production label Y.
limitation: A P tells you that some of the deduction is a released loss but never how much, so the deferred and current-year components cannot be separated. A blank is ambiguous in practice: it is the correct entry when no deferred loss is claimed, but it is also what an unanswered box looks like.
rationale: The DIL label names the type of other deductions relating to a primary production distribution, which is the Type box at question 13 label X. The 2025 instructions publish the full code list and the rule for leaving it blank.
evidence_quote: Print D if the entire amount at label X is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both the definition and the limitation, which was wrong twice over: the codes are published, and the field is a qualifier on a neighbouring amount.

value_domain: Taxable primary production income calculated for averaging (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Tax averaging (primary producers)
variable_description: The farming and fishing profit the ATO works out for the income averaging calculation, not a figure the taxpayer writes on the return. The ATO defines it plainly: "A primary producer has a taxable primary production income when their assessable primary production income exceeds their deductions", and "When your income is less than your deductions, the taxable primary production income is treated as being nil". It drives the averaging component that decides whether the taxpayer gets an averaging tax offset or pays extra tax.
description_source: ATO, Tax averaging (primary producers)
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount computed by the ATO from the return, floored at zero. It combines primary production income from a sole trader business with primary production distributions from partnerships and trusts, less the deductions attributable to them.
limitation: Because it is floored at zero, a bad season looks identical to a break-even one, so it cannot be used to measure farm losses or the variability that averaging exists to smooth. It is also not a return label, so it can shift when an assessment is amended even though nothing the taxpayer wrote changed.
rationale: The DIL label names a calculated taxable primary production income amount, and the ATO's tax averaging guidance is the only place that quantity is defined; it also states the nil rule and the part the figure plays in the averaging component.
evidence_quote: A primary producer has a taxable primary production income when their assessable primary production income exceeds their deductions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Taxable pp income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing explained that this is an ATO calculation for averaging rather than a self-reported income label.

value_domain: Dollar amount of business purchases and other costs (schedule label P8 L)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: What a sole trader spent on trading stock and the direct inputs to what they sold, at schedule label P8 L. The ATO defines it as expenditure that "represent the direct cost of materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business", including inwards freight and stock bought when starting or buying a business. The figure on this row is the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns, which the schedule collects separately.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting figure taken from the taxpayer's books, excluding GST for a registered business. It is a cost of sales input rather than a deduction, and it is combined with opening and closing stock to arrive at cost of sales.
limitation: It is not the amount deducted for stock: a business that bought heavily and held the goods at year end shows a large figure here that is offset by closing stock, so reading it as an expense overstates the deduction. It also merges the farming and non-farming columns, so the split the schedule collects is lost on this row.
rationale: The DIL label names purchases and other costs as a total, which is label L of P8 Expenses on the business and professional items schedule. The 2025 instructions define the label and state that the total is the sum of the two columns.
evidence_quote: Purchases and other costs represent the direct cost of materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is a cost of sales input on the sole trader schedule.

value_domain: Dollar amount deducted for a project pool (question D13)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question D13 Deduction for project pool
variable_description: This year's write-off of capital set-up costs for a project, claimed at question D13. The ATO allows it for "Certain capital expenditure you incur after 30 June 2001, which directly connects with a project that you carry on (or propose to carry on) for a taxable purpose", which the taxpayer allocates to a pool and writes off over the project life. Feasibility studies, site preparation and community infrastructure are typical inclusions, and the deduction normally runs from the year the project starts to operate, with a separate claim available in the year a project is abandoned, sold or otherwise disposed of.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question D13 Deduction for project pool
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for one income year, worked out as the pool value at a rate of 150 or 200 per cent divided by the taxpayer's own estimate of project life in years. Capital expenditure connected with a project carried on in a business is excluded from this question.
limitation: It cannot be read as the size of the project, because the annual write-off depends on an estimated project life the taxpayer chooses, and a pool with no finite life gives no deduction at all. A zero is therefore consistent with a live project pool, and a spike usually means the project was abandoned or sold, when the whole closing pool value falls in at once.
rationale: The DIL label names the deduction for project pool, which is question D13 on the supplementary return. The instructions define what a project amount is, when the deduction starts, the two rates and the disposal rule that produces large single-year values.
evidence_quote: Certain capital expenditure you incur after 30 June 2001, which directly connects with a project that you carry on (or propose to carry on) for a taxable purpose, you can allocate to a project pool and write-off over the 'project life'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Deduction for project pool', with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never said what a project pool is or why the amount is spread over years.

value_domain: Count of primary school students claimed for the education tax refund (item T6, label W)
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals instructions 2011, question T6 Education tax refund
variable_description: How many primary-school children the taxpayer claimed the education tax refund for, at item T6 label W. The instruction is direct: "Add up the number of primary school students you are claiming ETR for and write the answer at W item T6". Eligibility ran through family tax benefit Part A, so the count picks up children in families receiving or blocked from receiving FTB Part A rather than all school-age children, and the secondary-school count sits in a separate box at label X.
description_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals instructions 2011, question T6 Education tax refund
value_definition: A small whole number of children. The refund was half of eligible education expenses up to a per-student limit, which the 2010-11 worksheet sets at $397 for a student who attended only primary school and $794 for one who attended secondary school.
limitation: It counts claims, not children: a separated couple could each claim a share for the same child, and a parent with eligible children who claimed nothing shows a blank, so the column cannot be used as a child count for the family. The refund was short-lived and this column is present only for 2008-09 and 2009-10 in this asset, so it cannot support a series.
rationale: The DIL label names the education tax refund count of primary school students, and the 2011 instructions give the exact label and the counting instruction, and the same page gives the per-student limits and the halving step that produces the refund.
evidence_quote: Add up the number of primary school students you are claiming ETR for and write the answer at W item T6 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviation, 'Education tax refund- no. of primary school students', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing explained the FTB eligibility gate or that the item existed for only a few years.

value_domain: Dollar amount of rebatable private health premiums, statement row 1 (label J)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The first row of premiums the taxpayer copied from their private health insurance statement into the return, at label J. The ATO instruction is a transcription step: "Transfer the whole dollar amount at label J on your PHI statement to label J Your premiums eligible for Australian Government rebate in your tax return". Because the rebate percentage resets on 1 April, one policy normally produces two rows, so this first row usually covers only the part of the year before 1 April.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
value_definition: A whole-dollar premium amount for one row of one policy, as certified by the insurer. It is premiums that attract the Australian Government rebate, and the rebate actually received for the same row sits at label K.
limitation: On its own it is a part-year figure, so treating it as the household's annual premium understates spending whenever the statement has more than one row. The number is also the taxpayer's share of the policy, not the policy premium, so a family policy is split across the returns of the people claiming it.
rationale: The DIL label names the taxpayer's premiums eligible for the Australian Government rebate, numbered 1, which is the first row at the Private health insurance policy details section. The instructions state the transfer rule and why the statement carries a row for each side of 1 April.
evidence_quote: Transfer the whole dollar amount at label J on your PHI statement to label J Your premiums eligible for Australian Government rebate in your tax return.

value_domain: Dollar amount of rebatable private health premiums, statement row 2 (label J)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details

The ATO explains the split: "In most cases, there will be 2 rows of information on your PHI statement. One row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive before 1 April, and the other row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive on or after 1 April". Adding this to row 1 therefore gives one member's rebatable premiums for the whole year in the ordinary single-policy case.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
value_definition: A whole-dollar premium amount for the second row of the taxpayer's statement, usually the 1 April to 30 June part of the same membership. The insurer certifies it and the taxpayer copies it across without recalculation.
limitation: Row 2 is not always the second half of row 1's policy: someone who changed insurer or held two memberships will have row 2 belonging to a different policy, and the membership number columns are what tell them apart. A blank row 2 does not mean six months without cover, only that the statement carried a single row.
rationale: The DIL label names the taxpayer's premiums eligible for the Australian Government rebate, numbered 2, which is the second row of the Private health insurance policy details section. The 2025 instructions state that a statement normally carries two rows split at 1 April and that rows must not be combined.
evidence_quote: In most cases, there will be 2 rows of information on your PHI statement. One row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive before 1 April, and the other row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive on or after 1 April.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording with a trailing digit and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know that rows 1 and 2 usually split one policy year at 1 April.

value_domain: Dollar amount of rebatable private health premiums, statement row 3 (label J)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details

The ATO tells claimants to "Transfer all rows of information separately to your tax return, as they appear on your PHI statement. Don't combine the rows of information", and to repeat the steps "for each row of information on your statement for each policy". A non-blank row 3 is therefore a marker of switching insurer, adding a policy or claiming a spouse's share.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
value_definition: A whole-dollar premium amount for the third row on the return, tied to the health insurer identifier, membership number and tax claim code in the same row group.
limitation: It is close to useless as a level: most returns leave it blank, so the mean across taxpayers measures how rare multiple policies are rather than what anyone pays. It also cannot be read in isolation, since the same membership number may already appear at rows 1 and 2.
rationale: The DIL label names the taxpayer's premiums eligible for the Australian Government rebate, numbered 3, which is the third row of the Private health insurance policy details section. The 2025 instructions state that each policy and each row is entered separately and never combined.

value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details

The column is present in this asset from the 2012-13 tables, the point at which the rebate became income tested and a four-row statement stopped being unusual.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
value_definition: A whole-dollar premium amount for the fourth row group on the return, with its own health insurer identifier, membership number, rebate received and tax claim code.

The column is also absent before the 2012-13 tables, so a series across the income testing change is not continuous.
rationale: The DIL label names the taxpayer's premiums eligible for the Australian Government rebate, numbered 4, which is the last row group the return provides. The 2025 instructions state the four-row limit and the overflow schedule, and the registry shows the column starting with the 2012-13 tables.
evidence_quote: If you have more than 4 rows of information on your statement, you'll need to provide a Schedule of additional information .

value_domain: Dollar amount of provisional tax credited on assessment
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), Pay as you go instalments (replacing provisional tax)
variable_description: Credit for provisional tax the taxpayer had already paid under the system that PAYG instalments replaced. TaxPack 2000 records both the change and the credit: "On 1 July 2000 the pay as you go (PAYG) instalments system replaced the provisional tax system. Any provisional tax you paid during 1999–2000 will be credited against the tax payable on your 1999–2000 notice of assessment". The taxpayer did not write it on the return; TaxPack took the figure "from your assessment notice" when estimating the refund.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), Pay as you go instalments (replacing provisional tax)
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit for tax already paid, applied against the year's liability at assessment. Provisional tax was charged to people with business and investment income, so the credit only ever existed for that group.
limitation: It measures tax prepaid under a system that ended, not income or liability, so it cannot be used as an income marker. The column stays in the schema through the 2005-06 tables even though provisional tax stopped after 1999-2000, so anything non-zero in the later years reflects amended or late assessments of earlier years rather than current provisional tax.
rationale: The DIL label names a provisional tax credit, and TaxPack 2000 is the ATO instruction covering the last year the system operated: it states the replacement date, the credit mechanism and that the amount came from the notice of assessment rather than the return.
evidence_quote: On 1 July 2000 the pay as you go (PAYG) instalments system replaced the provisional tax system. Any provisional tax you paid during 1999–2000 will be credited against the tax payable on your 1999–2000 notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Provisional Tax Credit' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, leaving a reader without the one fact that matters, that the system was abolished from 1 July 2000.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed personal services income (question 9, label O)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 9 Attributed personal services income
variable_description: Income earned through a company, partnership or trust for the person's own work, pushed back onto them at question 9. The ATO sets out the mechanism: "Personal services income (PSI) is income that is mainly a reward for your personal efforts or skills. It is generally paid either to you or to a personal services entity (a company, partnership or trust)", and where the entity neither runs a personal services business nor pays it out promptly as salary, the income is attributed to the individual. Sole traders never use this label; their PSI goes to question 14 instead.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 9 Attributed personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar income amount, net of certain deductions the entity incurred in producing it, taken from a PAYG payment summary showing personal services attributed income or from the person's own attribution calculation.
limitation: It captures only the interposed-entity case, so it is not a measure of contracting income: the same person as a sole trader would show nothing here. A nil figure also does not mean the entity earned nothing, since income paid out promptly as salary is taxed as wages and appears at question 1 instead.
rationale: The DIL label names attributed personal services income, which is question 9 on the individual return. The instructions define the attribution rule, name the payment summary that reports it and state the boundary with the sole trader question.
evidence_quote: Personal services income (PSI) is income that is mainly a reward for your personal efforts or skills. It is generally paid either to you or to a personal services entity (a company, partnership or trust).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Attributed personal services income', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the sole trader PSI labels elsewhere in the same asset.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from attributed personal services income (question 9)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 9 Attributed personal services income
variable_description: Tax the interposed entity already withheld and remitted on the personal services income attributed to this person. The instruction pairs it with the income box: "Write the total amount of tax withheld from the PSI attributed to you under Tax withheld at the left of question 9 – label O". It is a credit against the person's assessment, not a deduction, and it belongs to the amount at PRSNL_SRVCS_ATRBD_INCM_AMT on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 9 Attributed personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding credit reported by the personal services entity on a PAYG payment summary, so it is third-party reported rather than estimated by the taxpayer.
limitation: It is not a tax liability and not a tax rate: an entity that withheld nothing leaves this blank while the attributed income still has to be declared, so a zero here beside a positive income figure is normal rather than an error. It also cannot be read as the tax finally paid on that income, which is settled on assessment.
rationale: The DIL label names tax withheld on attributed personal services income, which is the Tax withheld box beside question 9 label O. The instructions state exactly what to write there and where the amount comes from.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of tax withheld from the PSI attributed to you under Tax withheld at the left of question 9 – label O .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say that the amount is a third-party reported credit tied to the attributed income column.

value_domain: Date of becoming or ceasing to be an Australian resident (question A2)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A2 Part-year tax-free threshold
variable_description: The day the taxpayer says they became, or stopped being, an Australian resident for tax purposes. The instruction is a single step: "Write the date you became, or stop being, an Australian resident for tax purposes in the Date box at question A2". The ATO uses it with the months count at label N to work out a reduced tax-free threshold for the year.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A2 Part-year tax-free threshold
value_definition: A calendar date within the income year, self-assessed by the taxpayer against the residency tests. It is present only where question A2 applies, that is, where residency started or ended part way through the year.
limitation: One date field carries two opposite events, so on its own it cannot say whether the person arrived or left; the months figure at label N and the residency status elsewhere in the return are needed to tell. It is also a tax residency date, not a migration or travel date, and this asset holds the column only in the 2009-10 table, so it supports no series.
rationale: The DIL label names the part-year tax-free threshold date, which is the Date box at question A2. The instructions give the exact entry rule and the purpose the date serves, and the registry shows the column in a single year's table.
evidence_quote: Write the date you became, or stop being, an Australian resident for tax purposes in the Date box at question A2 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the same box records both arrival and departure.

value_domain: Count of months of Australian tax residency, 1 to 12 (question A2, label N)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A2 Part-year tax-free threshold
variable_description: The number of months of the income year the taxpayer was an Australian resident for tax purposes, at question A2 label N. The counting rule rounds up: "Write the number of months that you were an Australian resident for tax purposes in 2024–25, counting the month during which you became, or stop being, a resident for tax purposes". The ATO uses the count to scale the tax-free threshold, so it is an entitlement input rather than a demographic measure.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A2 Part-year tax-free threshold
value_definition: A whole number of months, in practice 1 to 12, stored as a code. The ATO's own worked case is a person who became a resident in November and writes 8, or who stopped being a resident in September and writes 3.
limitation: It overstates residency by up to a month, because the part-month in which residency changed is counted whole, so it cannot be used to date arrivals or departures. A blank is ambiguous rather than zero: full-year residents and people who were never resident both leave the question alone.
rationale: The DIL label names the months eligible for the part-year tax-free threshold, which is question A2 label N. The instructions state the counting rule and give the ATO's own examples of the values it produces.
evidence_quote: Write the number of months that you were an Australian resident for tax purposes in 2024–25, counting the month during which you became, or stop being, a resident for tax purposes at question A2 – label N .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the count rounds part-months up or that a blank does not mean zero.

value_domain: Dollar amount of partnership share of net small business income (item 13, label D)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partner's share of a small business partnership's net income, after attributable deductions, used only to work out the small business income tax offset. The ATO is explicit that it is not income: "You don’t include amounts you show at this question in your income. We only use the amounts for the purpose of working out your small business income tax offset". The column appears in this asset from the 2015-16 tables, matching the start of the offset.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts

The floor at zero also hides losses: a partner whose share was reduced below zero writes nothing, so a blank covers both no small business partnership and a bad year.
rationale: The DIL label names a partnership share of net small business income, which is question 13 label D. The 2025 instructions state the purpose, the zero floor and the deduction steps, and the registry shows the column starting with the 2015-16 tables.
evidence_quote: You don’t include amounts you show at this question in your income. We only use the amounts for the purpose of working out your small business income tax offset.

value_domain: Dollar amount of non-primary production partnership distribution (item 13, label O)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partner's share of a partnership's non-farming income or loss, with foreign income stripped out, at question 13 label O. The ATO defines the boundary: "Write the total of your share of non-primary production partnership income or loss (excluding any attributed foreign income or other foreign source income) at question 13 – label O", and adds that a franked distribution belongs here grossed up: "The amount you include at label O should include the amount of any attached franking credits". Foreign amounts go to the foreign income questions instead, which is why the label carries the qualifier.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar share of the partnership's net income worked out for tax purposes, which can be negative and is then flagged with an L in the loss box. It is grossed up by franking credits attached to any franked distributions.
limitation: It is not cash the partner received: partnership income is taxed on the share of net income whether or not it was drawn. The foreign exclusion and the franking gross-up both make it a poor proxy for a partnership's total distribution, and a magnitude without the loss flag cannot be told apart from a positive share.
rationale: The DIL label names a non-primary production partnership distribution less foreign income, which is question 13 label O. The 2025 instructions state the exclusion, the treatment of franked distributions and the loss flag.
evidence_quote: Write the total of your share of non-primary production partnership income or loss (excluding any attributed foreign income or other foreign source income) at question 13 – label O .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the foreign income exclusion or the franking gross-up.

value_domain: Dollar amount of primary production partnership distribution (item 13, label N)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts

The instruction is direct: "Write the total of your share of primary production partnership income or loss at question 13 – label N Distribution from partnerships". The activity split matters because primary production amounts feed the income averaging calculation, and the trust equivalent sits separately at label L.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A whole-dollar share of the partnership's net income for tax purposes, positive or negative, with a loss marked by printing L in the box at the right of label N.
limitation: It is a share of taxable net income, not drawings, so it cannot be read as farm household cash. It also covers partnerships only: a farmer operating as a sole trader shows nothing here, and one who also has a farm trust interest has that amount in a different column, so the label alone understates farm income.
rationale: The DIL label names a primary production partnership distribution, which is question 13 label N. The 2025 instructions give the entry rule, the loss flag and the separation from trust distributions and from the non-primary production label.
evidence_quote: Write the total of your share of primary production partnership income or loss at question 13 – label N Distribution from partnerships .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that partnership and trust farm income sit in different columns.

value_domain: Yes or no answer to the 80% one source question (schedule label P1 Q)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether 80 per cent or more of the sole trader's personal services income came from a single client and its associates, answered at schedule label P1 Q. The answer decides who may self-assess: "If you don’t satisfy the results test and 80% or more of your PSI in 2024–25 comes from one client and its associates (that is, from one source), you can't self-assess whether you satisfy the other personal services business tests".
