A labour-hire firm counts as the one source even where the work came through several jobs.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A yes or no indicator, printed as an X in one of two boxes. It is only reached by a sole trader who has PSI and does not satisfy the results test, so it is blank for most lodgers.
limitation: It is a threshold answer, not a concentration measure: a contractor with 81 per cent from one client and one with 100 per cent are recorded identically, and neither the client count nor the share is captured anywhere. A Yes also does not mean the PSI rules applied, since a determination from the Commissioner overrides the test.
rationale: The DIL label names the 80 per cent one source question, which is schedule label P1 Q. The instructions state the question, its consequence for self-assessment and the labour-hire rule that shapes the answer.
evidence_quote: If you don’t satisfy the results test and 80% or more of your PSI in 2024–25 comes from one client and its associates (that is, from one source), you can't self-assess whether you satisfy the other personal services business tests.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's run-on wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing explained what turns on the answer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of PSI paid without an ABN quoted (schedule label P1 N)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Personal services income the sole trader was paid without having quoted an ABN to the payer, at schedule label P1 N. The ATO defines it as "your total PSI from which an amount is withheld because you didn't quote your ABN, including the amounts of tax withheld", so it is a gross figure. The payer must withhold at the top rate in that case, which is why the matching withholding column is usually large relative to the payment.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross payment total, built by adding the gross payment amounts on the payment summary schedule that carry an N in the type box. GST is excluded where the taxpayer is registered.
limitation: It marks a paperwork failure rather than a kind of work, so it cannot be read as a category of contracting: the same job done after quoting an ABN appears in a different column. It is gross of the tax withheld, so adding it to the withholding column on the same row double counts.
rationale: The DIL label names PSI where an ABN was not quoted, which is schedule label P1 N. The instructions define the amount, state that it includes tax withheld and give the payment summary type code it is built from.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label N is your total PSI from which an amount is withheld because you didn't quote your ABN, including the amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's shorthand, 'Psi - where abn not quoted', with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the amount is gross of withholding.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from no-ABN PSI (item 14, label H)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 14 Personal services income
variable_description: Tax the payer withheld because the sole trader did not quote an ABN, claimed as a credit at question 14 label H. The instruction ties it to the payment summary schedule: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule at the Tax withheld boxes with an N in the TYPE box", and those amounts must relate to the income shown at schedule label P1 N. The instructions set no rate here; they only tie the credit to the gross payment reported at schedule label P1 N.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 14 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding credit, third-party reported by the payer on a payment summary and transcribed by the taxpayer. It belongs to PSI_ABN_NOT_QTD_AMT on the same row.
limitation: It is a credit against the assessment, not the tax finally borne, so the ratio to the gross payment says nothing about the taxpayer's tax rate. It also cannot stand in for the income: a payer who failed to withhold leaves this blank while the gross payment still has to be declared.
rationale: The DIL label names personal services income tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, which is question 14 label H. The 2025 instructions give the exact build rule and the link back to the income label on the schedule.
evidence_quote: Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule at the Tax withheld boxes with an N in the TYPE box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not identify the income column the credit belongs to.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on holding a personal services business determination (schedule label P1 C)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer held a ruling from the Commissioner that they were running a personal services business, at schedule label P1 C. The question asks about a determination in force for the whole of the period PSI was earned. The ATO describes it as "a notice from the Commissioner stating that you're conducting a personal services business", and says that with one "the PSI rules don't apply to your PSI", which makes it the only route out of the rules that does not depend on passing one of the four tests.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A yes or no indicator printed as an X. The question asks specifically about a determination in force for the whole of the period PSI was earned, so partial-year cover is answered No.
limitation: It records that a determination existed, not what it covered or why it was granted, and a No is not evidence that the PSI rules applied, since the results test or one of the other tests can achieve the same outcome. The column is present in this asset only from the 2010-11 tables, so earlier years cannot be compared on it.
rationale: The DIL label names the personal services business determination question, which is schedule label P1 C. The instructions state what the determination is, its effect on the PSI rules and the whole-period condition, and the registry shows the column beginning with the 2010-11 tables.
evidence_quote: This is a notice from the Commissioner stating that you're conducting a personal services business. If you have a personal services business determination from the Commissioner, the PSI rules don't apply to your PSI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's misspelt wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said what a determination does or that the column starts late.

value_domain: Indicator that the business premises test is satisfied (schedule label P1 F1)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the sole trader self-assessed that they kept separate business premises, at schedule label P1 F1. It is one of the three tests that can take a contractor out of the PSI rules. The ATO requires premises that are mainly used for the work, exclusively the taxpayer's, and physically separate from both their home and their clients' premises; the question is reached only where "You satisfy the business premises test if you can answer yes to all the following questions". A home office fails it by design.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A one-way indicator: an X is printed only when the test is satisfied, so the field is marked or empty rather than yes or no. It is only reachable for a taxpayer who failed the results test and gets less than 80 per cent of their PSI from each source.
limitation: An empty field carries two meanings and cannot separate them: the taxpayer failed the premises test, or never reached the question because the results test or the 80 per cent rule stopped them earlier. The test is also self-assessed against a written condition, so it records a claim rather than a verified fact about premises.
rationale: The DIL label names the business premises test, which is schedule label P1 F1. The instructions set out the four conditions, the marking convention and the path that decides whether the question is reached at all.
evidence_quote: You satisfy the business premises test if you can answer yes to all the following questions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording, 'Satisfied psi business premises test', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that a blank is not a No.

value_domain: Indicator that the employment test is satisfied (schedule label P1 E1)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the sole trader self-assessed that other people did enough of the work, at schedule label P1 E1. The ATO sets two ways to pass: an apprentice for at least half the year, or "employees, or do you engage subcontractors or entities, who performed at least 20% (by market value) of your principal work". Support work such as secretarial duties does not count, and neither do associated companies, partnerships or trusts.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A one-way indicator, marked with an X only when the test is satisfied. Like the other two self-assessed tests, it is reached only after the results test is failed and the 80 per cent rule is passed.
limitation: It is not a measure of employment: passing needs only a fifth of the principal work by market value, and a contractor with several employees who never reached the question shows nothing. Because the marking is one-way, an empty field mixes failure with never having been asked.
rationale: The DIL label names the personal services employment test, which is schedule label P1 E1. The instructions give both limbs of the test, the 20 per cent market value threshold and the exclusion of support work.
evidence_quote: Did you have employees, or do you engage subcontractors or entities, who performed at least 20% (by market value) of your principal work?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Satisfied psi employment test', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said how low the threshold is.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on receiving personal services income as a sole trader (schedule item P1)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: The gateway question on the schedule: did the taxpayer receive any personal services income as a sole trader. The ATO narrows it deliberately: "P1 Personal services income (PSI) concerns PSI you earn as a sole trader only. Answer No to the question below if you gain all your PSI as an employee or through a company, partnership or trust". A Yes opens the four business tests and the income and deduction labels that follow; a No sends the lodger straight past them.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A yes or no indicator printed as an X in one of two boxes on the business and professional items schedule. PSI itself is income "mainly a reward for an individual's personal efforts or skills", measured contract by contract against a 50 per cent test.
limitation: It does not identify contractors: employees and people working through their own company answer No by instruction, so the flag misses the interposed-entity cases that show up at question 9 instead. A Yes also says nothing about whether the PSI rules ended up applying, which the tests and the determination question decide.
rationale: The DIL label names the question on whether any personal services income was received, which is the opening question at schedule item P1. The instructions define PSI, the 50 per cent contract test and the sole trader restriction that governs the answer.
evidence_quote: P1 Personal services income (PSI) concerns PSI you earn as a sole trader only. Answer No to the question below if you gain all your PSI as an employee or through a company, partnership or trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's run-on wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the question excludes employees and interposed entities.

value_domain: Dollar amount of labour hire and specified payment PSI (schedule label P1 O)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Personal services income the sole trader earned through a labour-hire arrangement or from a short list of specified payments, at schedule label P1 O. The ATO defines it as "the total income you receive from labour hire or other specified payments, including amounts of tax withheld". Specified payments are narrow: tutorial services for the Indigenous Student Success Programme, translating and interpreting for the Translating and Interpreting Service National, and performing artists in promotional activity.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross total, built from the payment summary schedule rows carrying an S in the type box. It is gross of withholding and excludes GST for a registered taxpayer.
limitation: It is not a count of labour-hire work: someone engaged by a labour-hire firm as an employee is told to report the pay as wages at question 1, so the column captures only the contractor version of the same arrangement. Labour hire and the three specified payment types are also merged, so a policy interest in one of them cannot be isolated.
rationale: The DIL label names PSI from labour hire or other specified payments, which is schedule label P1 O. The instructions define the label, list the specified payments and state the exclusion of labour-hire employees.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label O is the total income you receive from labour hire or other specified payments, including amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's shorthand and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said which payments qualify or that employees of labour-hire firms are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from labour hire PSI (item 14, label J)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 14 Personal services income
variable_description: Tax withheld from labour-hire and specified payment personal services income, claimed as a credit at question 14 label J. The build rule is mechanical: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule at the Tax withheld boxes with an S in the TYPE box", and those amounts must relate to the income at schedule label P1 O. The rate the labour-hire payer withheld at is set outside these instructions, so the credit cannot be turned back into a rate from the return alone.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 14 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding credit reported by the payer on a PAYG payment summary and transcribed to the return. It pairs with PSI_LBR_HIR_PMTS_AMT on the same row.
limitation: It cannot be used to infer a withholding rate for the person, because the gross income it relates to is on the schedule rather than in this table's own income columns for every year, and several payers are added together first. It is a credit at assessment, not tax finally paid.
rationale: The DIL label names personal services income tax withheld for labour hire or other specified payments, which is question 14 label J. The 2025 instructions give the type code and the link to the income label.
evidence_quote: Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule at the Tax withheld boxes with an S in the TYPE box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing tied the credit to the labour hire income label it belongs to.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net personal services income or loss (schedule label P1 A)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: What the sole trader's personal services work left them with after deductions, and the only PSI figure that reaches taxable income. The ATO builds it by subtraction: the four income labels for voluntary agreement, no-ABN, labour hire and other PSI, less the deductions for payments to associates and other deductions, with the result written at label A and transferred to question 14 label A. A negative result is not written with a minus sign; the lodger prints "L in the Loss box at the right of" the label instead.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount that can be positive or negative. It is fully determined by the other PSI columns on the same row, so it is a derived subtotal rather than new information.
limitation: The sign lives in a separate loss flag, so a stored magnitude cannot be told apart from a profit of the same size, and losses will look like income if the flag is dropped. It also covers only contractors caught by the PSI rules: one who satisfies the results test reports the same work as ordinary business income, so this column is not all self-employed personal services earnings.
rationale: The DIL label names net PSI, which is schedule label P1 A. The instructions give the arithmetic that produces it, the transfer to question 14 and the loss box convention.
evidence_quote: Step 3: Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1. Write your answer at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label A .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's shorthand, 'Psi - net psi', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said the value is derived from its neighbours or that losses carry a separate flag.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other personal services income (schedule label P1 J)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Personal services income with no withholding attached to it, at schedule label P1 J. The instruction is short because the label is a residual: "Work out the total amount of other PSI and write this amount at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label J". It is what is left after the voluntary agreement, no-ABN and labour hire categories, so in practice it is fees billed directly to clients who withheld nothing.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar income total worked out by the taxpayer rather than transcribed from a payment summary, excluding GST for a registered taxpayer.
limitation: It is the one PSI income label with no third-party report behind it, so it rests entirely on the taxpayer's own records and is the weakest of the four for accuracy. Being a residual, its meaning also shifts with the others: income that would have sat here appears in a neighbouring column as soon as a payer starts withholding.
rationale: The DIL label names other PSI, which is schedule label P1 J. The instructions place it after the three withholding categories and state that the taxpayer works the amount out rather than taking it from a payment summary.
evidence_quote: Work out the total amount of other PSI and write this amount at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label J .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's shorthand, 'Psi - other', with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the label is a residual with no payment summary behind it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other deductions against PSI (schedule label P1 L)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Everything the sole trader deducted against their personal services income apart from payments to associates for principal work, at schedule label P1 L. The ATO asks for "the total amount of all other expenses (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) that you can deduct from your PSI", and adds "Don't include amounts already recorded at" label K. The PSI rules bar the big household items, so home rent, mortgage interest, rates and land tax cannot be in it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction total, self-assessed, excluding input tax credit amounts for a GST-registered taxpayer. With label K it is subtracted from the four PSI income labels to give net PSI.
limitation: It is not total PSI deductions, because payments to associates for principal work sit in a separate box, so adding it to the income labels overstates the deduction unless label K is included too. The figure is also suppressed by the deduction restrictions the PSI rules impose, so it cannot be compared with the expenses of an unrestricted business.
rationale: The DIL label names the total amount of other deductions against PSI, which is schedule label P1 L. The instructions state what belongs there, what must not be double counted from label K and which expenses the rules disallow.
evidence_quote: Add up the total amount of all other expenses (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) that you can deduct from your PSI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a second deduction label sits beside it.

value_domain: Indicator that the unrelated clients test is satisfied (schedule label P1 D1)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the sole trader self-assessed that they served two or more unrelated clients won by advertising to the public, at schedule label P1 D1. The ATO asks two questions together: "Do you receive PSI from 2 or more clients who aren't associated with each other or with you?" and whether those clients came "as a direct result of making offers to the public". Clients obtained by registering with a labour-hire firm or placement agency do not count, which is what separates this test from simply having several payers.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A one-way indicator, marked with an X only when the test is satisfied. It is the first of the three self-assessed tests on the schedule and is reached only after the results test is failed and the 80 per cent rule is passed.
limitation: It is not a client count and not a measure of market breadth, since two clients are enough and the number is never recorded. Because the agency exclusion is judged by the taxpayer, an unmarked field can mean the test failed, the question was never reached, or the lodger read the advertising condition strictly.
rationale: The DIL label names the unrelated clients test, which is schedule label P1 D1. The instructions state both conditions and the labour-hire exclusion that gives the test its content.
evidence_quote: Do you receive PSI from 2 or more clients who aren't associated with each other or with you?
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording, 'Satisfied psi unrelated clients test', with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained the advertising and agency conditions.

value_domain: Dollar amount of PSI under a PAYG voluntary agreement (schedule label P1 M)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Personal services income paid under a voluntary agreement for the payer to withhold tax, at schedule label P1 M. The ATO defines it as "the total income you receive that is subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement, including amounts of tax withheld". A voluntary agreement is a written arrangement between a contractor with an ABN and a payer, so a figure here marks a settled ongoing relationship rather than an incidental job.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross total, built by adding the gross payment amounts on the payment summary schedule that carry a V in the type box.
limitation: It measures an administrative election, not a type of work: the identical contract without an agreement in place appears in the other PSI label instead, so trends in this column can be about paperwork rather than about the labour market. It is gross of the withholding claimed on the same row.
rationale: The DIL label names PSI under a voluntary agreement, which is schedule label P1 M. The instructions define the amount, state that it includes tax withheld and give the type code the total is built from.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label M is the total income you receive that is subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement, including amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's shorthand, 'Psi - voluntary agreement', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said what a voluntary agreement is or that the amount is gross.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld under a PAYG voluntary agreement (item 14, label G)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 14 Personal services income
variable_description: Tax withheld by a payer under a voluntary agreement, claimed as a credit at question 14 label G. The instruction is a transcription from the payment summary schedule: "Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule at the Tax withheld boxes with a V in the TYPE box", and the amounts must relate to the income at schedule label P1 M. The instructions give only how to total the amounts withheld, not the rate the payer applied under the agreement.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 14 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding credit reported by the payer and transcribed to the return, paired with PSI_VLNTRY_AGREMT_AMT on the same row.
limitation: It is a prepayment credit, so it says nothing about the tax finally assessed on the income, and it will not match a marginal rate. A blank does not mean the agreement lapsed, only that no tax was withheld under it in the year.
rationale: The DIL label names personal services income tax withheld under a voluntary agreement, which is question 14 label G. The 2025 instructions give the type code and tie the credit to the matching income label.
evidence_quote: Add up all the amounts on your Individual PAYG payment summary schedule at the Tax withheld boxes with a V in the TYPE box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing linked the credit to the voluntary agreement income column.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on full-year private patient hospital cover (question M2, label E)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer and everyone they were responsible for held appropriate hospital cover for the whole year, answered at question M2 label E. The ATO frames it as a household, full-year test: "If you and all your dependants (including your spouse) have an appropriate level of private patient hospital cover for the whole of 2024–25, print X in the Yes box". Appropriate means hospital cover from a registered insurer with an excess of $750 or less for a single policy and $1,500 or less for any other.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
value_definition: A yes or no indicator printed as an X. Extras or general cover does not qualify, and the answer governs whether the Medicare levy surcharge questions and the exempt days count at label A have to be completed.
limitation: A No cannot be read as uninsured: it is also the answer for someone with cover for eleven months, with an excess above the limit, or with extras only, and it turns No if any dependant or a spouse lacked cover even when the taxpayer was covered all year. It describes a tax test on a household, so it is a poor substitute for an individual's insurance status.
rationale: The DIL label names the Medicare levy surcharge private patient hospital cover question, which is question M2 label E. The 2025 instructions give the entry rule, the household scope and the definition of appropriate cover with the excess limits.
evidence_quote: If you and all your dependants (including your spouse) have an appropriate level of private patient hospital cover for the whole of 2024–25, print X in the Yes box at the right of question M2 – label E .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the answer covers dependants and the whole year at once.

value_domain: Dollar amount of private health insurance tax offset claimed in the return
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals instructions 2011, question T5 Private health insurance
variable_description: The private health insurance rebate claimed back through the tax return rather than taken off the premium during the year. The two routes were mutually exclusive: "You cannot claim this tax offset for premiums paid if you have already claimed a private health insurance rebate for them, either as reductions in your premiums through the health insurer or as cash or cheque rebates from Medicare". The claim ran off the insurer's statement rather than off the premiums paid: "If the amounts at G on your statements are $0, you have already received your full entitlement and you do not need to complete this item".
description_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals instructions 2011, question T5 Private health insurance
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax offset, worked out from the insurer's annual statement as the rebatable share of premiums paid less any reduction already received. This asset holds the column only for the 2006-07 and 2007-08 tables.
limitation: It is not a measure of private health cover or of premiums, because most people took the rebate as a premium reduction and appear here as blank, so the column selects a minority who chose the claim-back route. The figure is the residual entitlement certified by the insurer, less any cash or cheque rebate from Medicare, so it is not a fixed fraction of the premiums paid.
rationale: The DIL label names the private health insurance tax offset, and the 2011 instructions for the same item explain the offset, its interaction with the premium reduction route and the age-based rate steps. The item number moved between years, so the citation is to the mechanism rather than to a 2006-07 label position.
evidence_quote: You cannot claim this tax offset for premiums paid if you have already claimed a private health insurance rebate for them, either as reductions in your premiums through the health insurer or as cash or cheque rebates from Medicare.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said the column captures only claimants who did not take the rebate at the till.

value_domain: Dollar amount credited for PAYG income tax instalments
value_source: ATO, Starting PAYG instalments
variable_description: Credit for the quarterly prepayments of tax the person made during the year on business and investment income. The ATO describes the settling up plainly: "When you lodge your tax return, the PAYG instalments you have paid during the year are offset against your tax, leaving you with little or no tax to pay". Entry to the system is largely automatic: an individual enters on all three of instalment income of $4,000 or more on the latest return, tax payable of $1,000 or more on the latest notice of assessment, and notional tax of $500 or more, so the credit marks people with substantial income outside wages.
description_source: ATO, Starting PAYG instalments
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit applied at assessment, sourced from the ATO's own instalment records rather than written on the return by the taxpayer.
limitation: It is a prepayment of tax, not income and not a liability, so it cannot be added to withholding credits as though it measured earnings. A blank does not mean no business or investment income, only that the person was below the entry thresholds or had exited the system, and a large credit can reflect an instalment rate set from a previous year rather than this year's income.
rationale: The DIL label names a credit for PAYG income tax instalments, and the ATO's instalment guidance states that instalments paid are offset against tax when the return is lodged, and publishes the entry thresholds that decide who has a credit at all.
evidence_quote: When you lodge your tax return, the PAYG instalments you have paid during the year are offset against your tax, leaving you with little or no tax to pay.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Credit for PAYG income tax instalments', with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said who is in the instalment system or that the figure is a prepayment.

value_domain: Dollar total of rebates and credits allowed on assessment, 2010-11 to 2014-15
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The assessment's combined total of tax offsets and credits for the year, under the older column name used in the 2010-11 to 2014-15 tables. The notice of assessment is the statement that carries the same quantities, showing the tax owed on taxable income and the "credit you have for tax already paid during the income year". The word rebate is an older name for what the return now calls a tax offset, which is why the column label reads oddly against the modern form.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A whole-dollar total computed at assessment rather than written on the return. It draws together the offsets claimed on the return and the credits for tax already paid, such as amounts withheld and PAYG instalments.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed: an offset that only reduces tax to zero and a refundable credit that produces a cash refund are added into the one figure, so it cannot be used to measure either. The column also stops after the 2014-15 tables, and RBTS_AND_CRS_TOTL_AMT carries the same custodian wording for the earlier and later years, so a continuous series needs both and still has no value for 2009-10.
rationale: No ATO page documents this field name, which is an internal calculated column rather than a return label. The notice of assessment page establishes that the assessment carries a total of tax already paid alongside the tax owed, and the registry establishes the exact years the column exists, which is the fact that distinguishes it from its twin.
evidence_quote: Your NOA will show the amount of: tax you owe on your taxable income
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's wording, 'Total rebates and credits calculated amount', and the generic no-value-list sentence, giving no way to tell this column from the identically labelled one in the same table family.

value_domain: Dollar total of rebates and credits allowed on assessment
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The assessment's combined total of tax offsets and credits, under the column name used for 1999-2000 to 2008-09 and again from 2015-16 onwards. It is the same quantity the notice of assessment reports when it sets the tax owed against the "credit you have for tax already paid during the income year". Its twin, RALLCALC, fills the 2010-11 to 2014-15 tables, so the two names between them cover every year in this asset except 2009-10.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A whole-dollar total computed at assessment. It combines the tax offsets allowed against the year's tax with the credits for tax already collected, including amounts withheld by payers and instalments paid.
limitation: A change in this column between years can come from a rule change to an offset, from more tax being withheld, or from an amended assessment, and nothing in the column separates those causes. Because the wording is identical to RALLCALC, joining the two into one series is an inference from the years each covers rather than a documented continuation.
rationale: No ATO page documents this field name, which is a calculated assessment column rather than a return label. The notice of assessment page establishes what the assessment totals, and the registry gives the years each of the two identically labelled columns covers.
evidence_quote: Your NOA will show the amount of: tax you owe on your taxable income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave a reader no way to know that a second column with the same label covers the missing years.

value_domain: Row identifier within the salary and wage table
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: A row key on the salary and wage table, which holds one row for each payer that paid a person in the year. The row it identifies also carries the payer's hashed ABN, an income type code, the gross payment and the tax withheld, so the identifier is what keeps a person's several jobs apart when the table is joined to the spine by SYNTHETIC_AEUID. It is administrative bookkeeping rather than a fact about the taxpayer.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: An opaque record number scoped to this table and this extract. The registry holds it for a single table and year, so no cross-year convention can be assumed.
limitation: It is not a person key, not a payer key and not stable across extracts, so counting distinct values counts rows rather than people or employers. Two rows for the same person and payer can exist where the payer reported more than once, so the identifier cannot be used to count jobs either.
rationale: No ATO or ABS page documents this field. The reading comes from the columns that sit beside it in the same table, which identify the payer, the income type, the gross payment and the tax withheld, and from the ABS description of PLIDA as a person-linked asset built on such records.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Record id' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said what a row of the table represents or warned against treating the number as a key.

value_domain: abs_address_repair_result
values: ["Repaired: the reported address was changed by the address repair step","Not repaired: repair was attempted and the address was not changed","No repair required: the address needed no repair"]
value_source: ABS Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, 'Geocoding unit record data using address and location', section 'Address repair'
variable_description: What the address cleaning step did to the taxpayer's reported address before it was geocoded. Repair is a documented stage of the ABS process: "Prior to address coding it may be advisable to examine the address records and repair the content of these records to facilitate the automatic address coding processes." The typical repairs are formatting fixes, adding a state derived from the postcode and stripping stray characters, rather than substituting a different address. Together with GEOCODE_INDEX it describes how the SA1 and mesh block codes on the row were produced.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, SSF Guidance Material - Geocoding Unit Record Data Using Address and Location, section 'Address repair'
value_definition: A small set of outcome values separating an address the repair step changed, one it examined and left unchanged, and one that needed no repair. The ABS does not publish the codes themselves.
limitation: A repaired address is not a wrong address and an untouched one is not a right one. The column records whether the text was edited, not whether the geocode that followed was correct, so it cannot stand in for a match quality flag.
rationale: 'Address repair' is a named, published step in the ABS address geocoding process, so the field records the outcome of that step; the ABS does not publish the outcome codes, so the three-way domain above is a coarse guess of the right shape.
evidence_quote: Prior to address coding it may be advisable to examine the address records and repair
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination gave no domain; the ABS documents the process step, which supports a coarse outcome domain.

value_domain: Grossed-up dollar amount of reportable fringe benefits (question IT1)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts
variable_description: The total value of non-cash benefits an employer provided, reported at question IT1 and used in income tests rather than taxed. The ATO defines them as "fringe benefit amounts that you receive from your employer and have the taxable value of those benefits on your income statement or payment summary", and sets a floor that moves each year, $3,773 for 2024-25. The figure is grossed up to the pre-tax salary the employee would have needed to buy the benefit themselves, so it is larger than the benefit's cash value.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up total across all employers, transcribed from income statements and payment summaries, so it is third-party reported. The return splits it between label N, for employers exempt from FBT under section 57A, and label W for the rest; this asset carries the two components as separate columns from the 2015-16 tables.
limitation: It cannot be added to salary as though it were pay, because the gross-up inflates it to a pre-tax equivalent that the employee never received in cash. It is also measured over the fringe benefits tax year of 1 April to 31 March, not the income year, and benefits with a total taxable value of $2,000 or less are not reported, so small benefits are invisible.
rationale: The DIL label names the total reportable fringe benefits amount, which is question IT1. The 2025 instructions give the definition and the annual floor, and the ATO's employee guidance states the $2,000 threshold, the FBT year and the gross-up.
evidence_quote: Reportable fringe benefits are fringe benefit amounts that you receive from your employer and have the taxable value of those benefits on your income statement or payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the number is grossed up and measured over a different twelve months.

value_domain: Dollar amount of business rent expense (schedule label P8 K)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Rent a sole trader paid as a tenant for business premises, at schedule label P8 K. The ATO defines it as "expenditure you incur as a tenant for rental of land and buildings used for producing assessable income. Include the cost of leasing real estate". Despite the similar name it has nothing to do with rental income: leases of vehicles and plant belong in the lease expenses label instead.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense, the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns the schedule collects separately.
limitation: A zero does not mean the business had no premises, since an owner-occupier pays no rent and a sole trader working from home under the PSI rules cannot claim home rent at all. Because it is the accounting figure, any private-use or capital portion is still in it and is dealt with at the expense reconciliation adjustment rather than here.
rationale: The DIL label names total rent expenses, which is label K of P8 Expenses on the business and professional items schedule. The instructions define the label, exclude vehicle and plant leases and state that the total is the sum of the two columns.
evidence_quote: This is expenditure you incur as a tenant for rental of land and buildings used for producing assessable income. Include the cost of leasing real estate.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, tagged as housing, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so a reader could easily have read a business expense as a household rent payment.

value_domain: Dollar amount of rental capital works deduction (question 21, label F)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
variable_description: The slow write-off of the building itself claimed against rental income, at question 21 label F. The ATO allows "a deduction for the construction costs of your property over a 25-year or 40-year period", at "the rate of 2.5% or 4% (adjusted for part-year claims) depending on the date the capital works began". Residential construction qualifies only if it began after 17 July 1985, so the age of the building, not the value of it, decides whether there is anything in this column.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the taxpayer's share of the property, self-assessed, usually from a quantity surveyor's schedule. In this asset the column runs from the 2006-07 tables onwards.
limitation: It is not a repair or a cash cost: the money was spent when the building went up, often by someone else, and claiming it reduces the CGT cost base, so a large deduction now means a larger capital gain later. A zero is common for older houses that never qualified and cannot be read as the owner spending nothing on the property.
rationale: The DIL label names rent capital works deductions, which is question 21 label F. The 2025 instructions state the entry rule, the rates, the qualifying construction dates and the treatment of structural improvements; the registry gives the years the column exists.
evidence_quote: Write your share of the capital works deductions that you can claim as a deduction at question 21 – label F .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Rent capital works deductions', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said that eligibility turns on construction dates or that the claim feeds back into CGT.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross rent (question 21, label P)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
variable_description: The rent an individual landlord received before any expenses, at question 21 label P. The ATO counts it broadly: "Rental income is the full amount of money you earn when you rent out your property (including renting out a room through the sharing economy)", with retained bond money, insurance payouts for lost rent and cancellation fees all included. The taxpayer writes only "your share of the total amount of gross rent", so a jointly owned property is split across the co-owners' returns.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross receipt for the taxpayer's ownership share, before the interest, capital works and other deduction columns on the same row are subtracted.
limitation: It is not the property's rent and cannot be used to value a dwelling's rental yield, because co-owners each report a fraction and the property is not identified. Rent from overseas property is reported elsewhere and board from a family member is not rental income at all, so the column understates what a household receives for accommodation.
rationale: The DIL label names gross rent, which is question 21 label P. The 2025 instructions define rental income, list what must be included and state the co-ownership share rule that shapes the values.
evidence_quote: Rental income is the full amount of money you earn when you rent out your property (including renting out a room through the sharing economy).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's shorthand, 'Rent gross rent', with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the figure is an ownership share rather than the property's rent.

value_domain: Dollar amount of rental interest deduction (question 21, label Q)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
variable_description: Interest on borrowings claimed against rental income, at question 21 label Q, and normally the largest single rental deduction. The taxpayer writes "your share of the interest expenses that you can claim as a deduction", which is the deductible part only: "If you have redrawn funds or increased your rental property loan for personal use, you can claim interest only on the part of the loan related to the rental property". Read against gross rent on the same row, it is what makes a property negatively geared.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the taxpayer's ownership share, self-assessed by apportioning loan interest to the rental use. In this asset the column runs from the 2006-07 tables onwards.
limitation: It gives neither the loan balance nor the interest rate, and mixing the two is a common error: a rise in this column can be a rate rise, more borrowing, or a larger ownership share. It is also the amount claimed, so a redraw used privately reduces it without any change in what the landlord actually pays the bank.
rationale: The DIL label names rent interest deductions, which is question 21 label Q. The 2025 instructions state the entry rule and the apportionment condition on redrawn or increased loans; the registry gives the years the column exists.
evidence_quote: Write your share of the interest expenses that you can claim as a deduction at question 21 – label Q .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Rent interest deductions', and the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing warned that the figure is an apportioned claim rather than interest paid.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net rent or rental loss (question 21)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
variable_description: What the landlord's rental activity contributed to taxable income once the three deduction columns are taken off, at the Net rent box of question 21. The arithmetic is fixed: "Add up the amounts at question 21 – labels Q , F and U . Subtract the total from the amount at question 21 – label P . This is your net rent". A negative result, the usual sign of negative gearing, is not written with a minus: "If your expenses are greater than your gross rent, you have made a rental loss. Print L in the Loss box at Net rent".
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar derived amount, fully determined by gross rent and the three rental deduction columns on the same row, with the sign carried in a separate loss flag.
limitation: The sign is the trap: a stored magnitude without the loss flag makes a heavily geared landlord look like a profitable one, and aggregating without it will overstate rental income. It also omits low-value pool deductions, which are rental costs claimed at question D6, so it is not the full rental result even before tax.
rationale: The DIL label names net rent, which is the Net rent box at question 21. The 2025 instructions give the exact calculation, the loss flag convention and the exclusion of the low-value pool deduction.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at question 21 – labels Q , F and U . Subtract the total from the amount at question 21 – label P . This is your net rent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's shorthand, 'Rent net rent', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing warned that losses are flagged rather than signed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other rental deductions (question 21, label U)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
variable_description: Every rental expense other than interest and capital works, collapsed into one box at question 21 label U. The instruction names the single carve-out: write "your share of the other rental expenses that you can claim as a deduction (except any low-value pool deduction)". Rates, insurance, agent commission, repairs, and decline in value of assets all sit inside it, which is why it is the second largest rental column after interest.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 21 Rent
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual deduction for the taxpayer's ownership share, self-assessed. Its one documented exclusion is the low-value pool deduction, which is claimed at question D6 instead.
limitation: Nothing inside it can be separated, so it cannot answer whether a landlord spent on repairs, management or insurance. Its composition also shifts over time as the deduction rules change, for example deductions for the cost of holding vacant land stopped from 1 July 2019 and travel to a residential rental property is no longer deductible for most landlords, so a fall in the column can be a rule change rather than lower spending.
rationale: The DIL label names other rental deductions, which is question 21 label U. The 2025 instructions give the entry rule with its low-value pool exclusion, and the same page records the vacant land and travel restrictions that changed what belongs in the residual.
evidence_quote: Write your share of the other rental expenses that you can claim as a deduction (except any low-value pool deduction) at question 21 – label U .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Rent other rental deductions', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the residual contains or that its content changes between years.

value_domain: Dollar amount of business repairs and maintenance (schedule label P8 O)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: What a sole trader's accounts show for keeping premises and equipment in working order, at schedule label P8 O. The ATO defines it as "expenditure shown in your accounts for repairs and maintenance of premises, plant, machinery, implements, utensils, rolling stock or articles associated with the production of income", and adds that any capital or private portion in that figure has to be added back at the expense reconciliation adjustment. The value on this row is the sum of the primary production and non-primary production columns.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense taken from the taxpayer's books, not a tax-adjusted deduction. Improvements and capital replacements can be inside it and are corrected elsewhere on the schedule.
limitation: It is a book figure, so it overstates the deduction whenever capital or private amounts are reversed at the reconciliation label, and the two cannot be netted from this column alone. It also cannot separate repairs to buildings from repairs to plant, so it says nothing about what kind of assets the business runs.
rationale: The DIL label names repairs and maintenance as a total, which is label O of P8 Expenses on the business and professional items schedule. The instructions define the label, state the reconciliation requirement and confirm the total is the sum of the two columns.
evidence_quote: This is expenditure shown in your accounts for repairs and maintenance of premises, plant, machinery, implements, utensils, rolling stock or articles associated with the production of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing distinguished the accounting figure from the amount finally deducted.

value_domain: Dollar amount of reportable employer superannuation contributions on a payment summary
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT2 Reportable employer superannuation contributions
variable_description: Extra superannuation one employer put in beyond what the law requires, as that employer reported it on this payment summary. The ATO defines the class: "Reportable employer superannuation (super) contributions are additional to the compulsory contributions your employer must make. An example of a reportable employer super contribution is a contribution made on your behalf under a salary sacrifice arrangement". This row is per payer, so the question IT2 figure on the return is the sum across an employee's payment summaries.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT2 Reportable employer superannuation contributions
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount reported by the employer alongside the gross payment, tax withheld and reportable fringe benefits on the same payment summary record.
limitation: It is not total employer superannuation, because compulsory contributions are excluded by definition, so it cannot be used to measure superannuation coverage or the guarantee. A zero means no salary sacrifice or negotiated extra with that employer, and says nothing about the person's total contributions, which may come from another job or from personal contributions.
rationale: The DIL label names reportable employer superannuation contributions, and the payment summary table it sits in carries the payer-level fields the return aggregates. The IT2 instructions define what is reportable and confirm that the return figure is built by adding the payment summary amounts.
evidence_quote: Reportable employer superannuation (super) contributions are additional to the compulsory contributions your employer must make. An example of a reportable employer super contribution is a contribution made on your behalf under a salary sacrifice arrangement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said the amount excludes compulsory contributions or that the row is one employer's report.

value_domain: Grossed-up dollar amount of reportable fringe benefits on a payment summary
value_source: ATO, Reportable fringe benefits for employees
variable_description: The value of non-cash benefits one employer provided, as reported by that employer on this payment summary. The ATO explains the inflation built into the number: "Your RFBA is 'grossed-up' to reflect the pre-tax income you would have had to earn, at the highest marginal tax rate (plus the Medicare levy), to buy the benefits yourself". Reporting is triggered only where benefits exceed a total taxable value of $2,000 in the fringe benefits tax year of 1 April to 31 March.
description_source: ATO, Reportable fringe benefits for employees
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up amount from a single payer's payment summary, sitting beside the gross payment, tax withheld and reportable employer superannuation contributions for that payer.
limitation: It is not taxed and not received in cash, so adding it to the gross payment on the same row invents income the person never got. Its reference period is the FBT year, which is three months out of step with the income year the rest of the row covers, and benefits below the $2,000 threshold never appear at all.
rationale: The DIL label names a reportable fringe benefits amount on a payment summary record. The ATO's employee guidance defines the amount, states the gross-up basis, the $2,000 threshold and the FBT year, and confirms the employer is the reporter.
evidence_quote: Your RFBA is 'grossed-up' to reflect the pre-tax income you would have had to earn, at the highest marginal tax rate (plus the Medicare levy), to buy the benefits yourself.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing warned about the gross-up or the mismatch between the FBT year and the income year.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item IT2 label T
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT2 Reportable employer superannuation contributions
variable_description: Employer super contributions the taxpayer influenced, most often salary sacrifice, totalled across every employer for the year. The ATO says these "are additional to the compulsory contributions your employer must make", so ordinary super guarantee amounts are excluded. The taxpayer copies the figure from income statements and payment summaries, which makes it employer reported rather than self-assessed, and it is an income test input rather than assessable income.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT2 Reportable employer superannuation contributions
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, summed over all income statements and payment summaries for the year. Zero is written when there are no reportable contributions, so a blank and a nil are meant to differ.
limitation: It is not the person's total super contribution. Super guarantee, personal deductible contributions claimed at D12 and any contribution the employee could not influence are all outside it, so this column understates flows into a fund and cannot be used to reconstruct a contribution history.
rationale: The label is item IT2 of the individual return. The ATO instruction for that item defines the amount, names its source documents and states its relation to compulsory contributions.
evidence_quote: Reportable employer superannuation (super) contributions are additional to the compulsory contributions your employer must make.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Reportable employer superannuation contributions' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that compulsory super is excluded or that the figure is an income test input.

value_domain: Dollar amount of trade support loan debt due for repayment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
variable_description: Trade support loan debt the assessment worked out as repayable for the income year, for an apprentice who drew loan instalments during training. The ATO describes the scheme, since renamed, as one where "eligible Australian apprentices are offered loans over a 4-year period". The amount is calculated by the ATO from repayment income rather than entered by the taxpayer, and it only appears from 2020-21 in this asset.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of compulsory repayment raised on the notice of assessment for the trade support loan component. It is one loan type among several that share a single set of repayment thresholds.
limitation: It is not the outstanding trade support loan balance, and it is not a payment. A person with a trade support loan below the repayment threshold shows nothing here, so a zero is compatible with a substantial debt that is simply not yet repayable.
rationale: The DIL label names the trade support loan repayable debt. The ATO page defines the loan programme and confirms it was renamed the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan, which explains why the label stops using the old name.
evidence_quote: Generally, under the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan (AASL) - previously known as Trade Support Loan (TSL) - program, eligible Australian apprentices are offered loans over a 4-year period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Trade Support Loan Repayable Debt' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say whether the number was a balance or a repayment, nor that the scheme was renamed.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at P1 label P of the business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether a sole trader claims to pass the results test, the first of the four personal services business tests. Passing it lifts the deduction restrictions the personal services income rules otherwise impose. The ATO sets the bar at three conditions over most of the income: "you satisfy the results test for 2024-25 if, in respect of at least 75% of your PSI, you can answer yes to all of the following 3 questions". The answer is self-assessed on the business and professional items schedule, alongside PSI_BUS_DTMNTN_IND, PSI_80_PCT_ONE_SRC_IND and the three other test flags on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A yes or no indicator, printed as an X in one of two boxes at P1 label P. It is only completed by a taxpayer who answers yes to receiving personal services income.
limitation: A yes here is the taxpayer's own assertion, never an ATO determination, and the ATO can and does dispute it on review. A no does not mean the PSI rules applied either, because the person may hold a personal services business determination or pass one of the other three tests recorded in the neighbouring flags.
rationale: The DIL label asks the results test question at P1 of the business and professional items schedule. The ATO instruction for that label states the 75 per cent threshold and the three conditions the taxpayer must meet.
evidence_quote: If you earn PSI, you satisfy the results test for 2024-25 if, in respect of at least 75% of your PSI, you can answer yes to all of the following 3 questions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the garbled custodian wording 'Psi did you satisfy the results test' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said the answer is self-assessed or what the test requires.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 1 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1
variable_description: The smallest ABS statistical area the lodger's address falls in, attached to the return by the ABS rather than reported by the taxpayer. SA1s are small: "SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people." It sits with SA2 and LGA in the context table, so the three describe one address at three scales.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1
value_definition: An ASGS statistical area code. The edition varies by table: the custodian's own label says the 2011 boundaries while the table named itr_geo2021_1516 carries the 2021 boundaries for the same reference year.
limitation: It is the address the ATO held when the return was processed, not a residence at 30 June, and a person who moved mid-year is placed at one point only. Boundaries are also not stable across editions, so an SA1 series spanning the 2011, 2016 and 2021 standards is not a series for one place.
rationale: The ABS defines the SA1 as the smallest ASGS unit and gives its design population, which is the fact that decides whether the column is usable for small-area work.
evidence_quote: SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Statistical Area Level 1 (SA1) 2011' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, which stated an edition the table name contradicts and said nothing about what an SA1 is.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 1
variable_description: The finest ASGS area the taxpayer's address geocodes to on the return, at the 2021 boundaries. SA1s hold a few hundred people each, so this is the level at which a tax record says something about a neighbourhood rather than a suburb, and it is what SA2, SA3, SA4 and the state code on the same row roll up from. Because it is derived from the address, it inherits whatever the address is: a postal address or an agent's office puts the taxpayer in the wrong SA1 entirely.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 1
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. There are 61,845 SA1s, of which 34 are special purpose codes for migratory, offshore and no-usual-address records.
limitation: SA1 counts are small enough that a cell can identify people, which is why tax analysis at this level is normally aggregated before release. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions, so an SA1 series across the change needs a correspondence rather than a join.
rationale: The field is an SA1 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA1 definition, its design population and its special purpose codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code.' with no value domain, so nothing said how fine the area is or that it is derived from an address that may not be a residence.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: The suburb-scale statistical area for the lodger's address, one level above the SA1 on the same row. The ABS designs SA2s to be meaningful places rather than convenient blocks: their "purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically", with populations "between 3,000 and 25,000". Most published small-area tax statistics are built at this level, so it is the practical unit for joining PIT to ABS estimates.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2
value_definition: An ASGS statistical area code aggregating whole SA1s. As with SA1, the boundary edition differs between the geo2021 tables and the yearly context tables.
limitation: It cannot separate people within a suburb, and it carries no information on where income was earned, only where the lodger's recorded address was. Non-spatial codes such as No Usual Address are valid SA2 values, so an unmatched or itinerant lodger appears as a real area code rather than as missing.
rationale: The ABS page defines the SA2 as the community-scale ASGS unit and gives its population range, which is what tells a reader whether the column supports the analysis they have in mind.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s) are medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s). Their purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label 'SA2' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page said nothing at all about the geography or its edition.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 2
variable_description: The taxpayer's SA2 at the 2021 boundaries, which is the ASGS level most tax analysis is published at. SA2s are built to represent communities that interact socially and economically, so they answer questions about a suburb or town where the SA1 below them is too small to release and the SA3 above them is too coarse to recognise. It is derived from the same geocoded address as the other geography columns on the row.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 2
value_definition: A nine-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. There are 2,473 SA2s, of which 19 are special purpose codes, with populations generally between 3,000 and 25,000.
limitation: An SA2 is a statistical area, not a suburb: its boundaries follow population rather than local names, so an SA2 and the suburb it is named after are not the same place. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions, so a series across the change needs a correspondence.
rationale: The field is an SA2 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA2 definition, its design population and its special purpose codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code.' with no value domain.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 3 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 3
variable_description: The taxpayer's SA3 at the 2021 boundaries, a regional grouping of SA2s. SA3s are designed around labour markets and regional service catchments, which makes this the natural level for questions about where people work and what a regional economy looks like, rather than where a particular street is. It is derived from the same geocoded address as the finer geography on the row.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 3
value_definition: A five-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. SA3s generally hold between 30,000 and 130,000 people.
limitation: An SA3 aggregates communities that differ from one another, so a median or a rate at this level hides variation the SA2 column would show. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions.
rationale: The field is an SA3 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA3 definition and its design population.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 3 code.' with no value domain.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 4
variable_description: The taxpayer's SA4 at the 2021 boundaries, the largest sub-state ASGS area. SA4s are built to be big enough for the Labour Force Survey to publish at, which is why labour market comparisons are made here and why an SA4 is the level at which a tax measure can be set beside an unemployment rate. It is derived from the same geocoded address as the finer geography on the row.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 4
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. There are 108 SA4s, of which 19 are special purpose codes, generally holding 100,000 to 500,000 people.
limitation: An SA4 covers a whole city sector or a large slice of a state, so it cannot answer anything local; the SA2 column is the one for that. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions.
rationale: The field is an SA4 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA4 definition, its design population and that it is the level the Labour Force Survey publishes at.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code.' with no value domain.

value_domain: Seniors and pensioners tax offset code letter at item T1 label N
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: A single letter at item T1 saying which living arrangement the taxpayer claims for the seniors and pensioners tax offset, because the offset amount depends on it. The code table runs from A, for a person who is "single, separated or widowed", through B and C for couples living apart through illness or a nursing home, to D and E for couples living together, split by whether the spouse is also eligible. The code is claimed by the taxpayer; the offset itself is worked out by the ATO from it and from rebate income.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
value_definition: One letter from A to E, entered in the tax offset code box. It is present only where the taxpayer claims the offset, so it is missing for the great majority of lodgers.
limitation: The code records a claimed circumstance, not a granted entitlement, so a filled code does not mean any offset was allowed; eligibility still turns on rebate income and can fail. It also cannot be read as a marital status variable, because the A to E distinctions are drawn for offset purposes and collapse separated, single and widowed people into one letter.
rationale: The DIL label names the seniors and pensioners tax offset code. The ATO instruction for item T1 publishes the full code letter table and the rule for choosing between letters when more than one applies.
evidence_quote: print your code letter from Step 1 in the TAX OFFSET CODE box at question T1 - label N
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Seniors and pensioners tax offset code' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it gave neither the code letters nor the fact that the letters describe living arrangements.
