value_domain: Dollar amount of bonus deduction claimed under the small business energy incentive
value_source: ATO, Small business energy incentive
variable_description: The extra 20 per cent deduction a sole trader claimed for energy efficient assets and improvements, on top of the ordinary deduction for the same spending. The ATO describes it as "a bonus 20% tax deduction for the cost of eligible assets and improvements that support more efficient use of energy", capped by "Up to $100,000 of total expenditure ... with the maximum bonus tax deduction being $20,000". The incentive ran for one year only, so this column exists for 2023-24 and no other.
description_source: ATO, Small business energy incentive
value_definition: A whole-dollar bonus deduction, self-assessed, bounded above by $20,000 for the year. It is additional to the deduction already claimed for the same asset elsewhere on the return.
limitation: It is not the amount spent on energy efficiency; it is one fifth of the eligible portion of that spending, so multiplying by five recovers eligible expenditure only where the taxpayer was under the cap. A zero in any other year is not a fall in energy spending, because the column has no other year.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business energy incentive, and the ATO page for that measure gives the bonus rate, the expenditure and deduction caps and the single bonus period the label covers.
evidence_quote: Businesses with an aggregated annual turnover of less than $50 million will have access to a bonus 20% tax deduction for the cost of eligible assets and improvements that support more efficient use of energy.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Small business energy incentive' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said the amount was a bonus rather than the expenditure, or that it applies to a single year.

value_domain: Dollar amount of small business income tax offset available
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: The small business income tax offset the ATO worked out as available to the taxpayer before it was applied against tax payable. The ATO calls it the "unincorporated small business tax discount" and says it "can reduce the tax you pay by up to $1,000 each year". The amount is calculated by the ATO from the net small business income figures on the return, not entered by the lodger, and the rate rose over time from 5 per cent in 2015-16 to 16 per cent from 2021-22.
description_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset amount, capped at $1,000 for the year, derived by the ATO. It first appears for 2015-16, the year the offset began.
limitation: Available is not the same as delivered. The offset is non-refundable, so a lodger with little or no tax payable can show an available amount and receive nothing, which is what SB_TO_USED_AMT on the same row records. The cap also means the column is a poor proxy for business size once income is high enough to bind it.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business income tax offset available. The ATO page for that offset gives the cap, the year by year rates and the fact that the ATO calculates it from the return.
evidence_quote: The small business income tax offset (also known as the unincorporated small business tax discount) can reduce the tax you pay by up to $1,000 each year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Small business income tax offset available' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish an entitlement from an amount actually used.

value_domain: Dollar amount of small business income tax offset applied against tax payable
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: How much of the small business income tax offset actually reduced this taxpayer's assessment, which is the available amount limited by the tax they owed. The ATO works it out as a share of liability: "The offset is worked out on the proportion of tax payable on your business income." The used amount is the one that costs revenue and reaches the taxpayer, so it is the right column for measuring benefit received.
description_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, never greater than the available amount on the same row and never greater than basic income tax liability. It is derived by the ATO during assessment.
limitation: A zero here does not mean the taxpayer was ineligible; it usually means there was no tax left to offset, so using this column to count beneficiaries drops the low-income small business owners the measure was aimed at. It also cannot be added to other offsets to get a refund, because this one is non-refundable.
rationale: The DIL label names the amount of the small business tax offset used. The ATO page explains that the offset is a proportion of tax payable, which is what makes used differ from available.
evidence_quote: The offset is worked out on the proportion of tax payable on your business income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Small business tax offset amount used' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader had no way to tell it apart from the available amount alongside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15 label A, net small business income
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 15 Net income or loss from business
variable_description: The taxpayer's own small business income after the deductions attributable to it, reported at item 15 label A. The ATO uses it to work out the small business income tax offset and defines it as "your assessable income from carrying on your business less your deductions to the extent that they're attributable to that assessable income". A net loss does not carry through, because it is treated as zero and no offset follows. Shares of small business income from partnerships and trusts are reported separately at item 13 labels D and E, not here.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 15 Net income or loss from business
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, self-assessed, never negative because losses are recorded as zero. Present only from 2015-16, and only for lodgers who are small business entities.
limitation: The floor at zero destroys information: a business that lost $80,000 and one that broke even both show zero, so this column cannot measure business losses. It also excludes personal services income shown at item 14 and salary or director's fees, so it is narrower than any general measure of self-employment income.
rationale: The DIL label names net small business income, which is item 15 label A. The ATO instruction for that item defines the amount and separates it from the partnership and trust shares reported at question 13.
evidence_quote: To answer Part D, you need to work out your net small business income, which is your assessable income from carrying on your business less your deductions to the extent that they're attributable to that assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net small business income' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the amount is floored at zero or what it excludes.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total net small business income used in the offset calculation
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: The taxpayer's small business income from all sources combined, which is the base the ATO divides by taxable income to work out the offset. It brings together the sole trader amount at item 15 label A with the shares of partnership and trust small business income at item 13 labels D and E. The ATO states the mechanism plainly: "The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income."
description_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar derived total, assembled by the ATO from several return labels rather than entered at any single one. Like its components it treats a loss as zero.
limitation: It is a wider figure than SBI_NET_AMT on the same row, so treating the two as alternative measures of the same thing double counts or undercounts depending on which is used. Because each component is floored at zero, a person with a large sole trader loss and a modest trust share shows the trust share alone rather than a net position.
rationale: The DIL label names total small business income. The ATO page describes total net small business income as the aggregate of sole trader and partnership or trust shares used in the offset formula.
evidence_quote: The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total small business income' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say that the total includes partnership and trust shares that the net figure beside it excludes.

value_domain: Count of eligible secondary school children claimed for the education tax refund
value_source: ATO, Education tax refund - what you need to know, How much you can claim
variable_description: How many secondary school children the taxpayer claimed the education tax refund for, which set the ceiling on their claim. The limit was per child and higher for secondary than primary; for 1 July 2010 to 30 June 2011 the ATO set it at "$1,588 for each eligible child in secondary school - that is, a refund of $794." The limits were set year by year, and in this asset the count exists for 2008-09 and 2009-10 only, before the refund was abolished.
description_source: ATO, Education tax refund - what you need to know, How much you can claim
value_definition: A small non-negative integer, self-assessed on the return. Its sibling column counts primary school children on the same basis.
limitation: It counts children a claim was made for, not children in the household or even children in secondary school, so it misses families who were not receiving family tax benefit part A and those who lodged no claim. The column stops after 2009-10, so its absence in later years is the end of the measure rather than a change in school enrolment.
rationale: The DIL label names the education tax refund count of secondary school students. The ATO guidance for the refund states the per child secondary school limit, for the period ending 30 June 2011, that the count was used to apply.
evidence_quote: $1,588 for each eligible child in secondary school - that is, a refund of $794.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Education tax refund- no. of secondary school students' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the measure was abolished or that the count is a claim rather than a headcount.

value_domain: Dollar amount of section 40-880 deduction at P8 reconciliation items
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Reconciliation items
variable_description: Business capital costs the taxpayer wrote off under section 40-880, the provision that catches start-up and wind-up expenditure no other deduction reaches. The ATO gives two routes: an immediate deduction for eligible start-up costs, and otherwise a spread, since the section "allows you to deduct in equal proportions over a 5-year period certain capital expenditure you incur if the expenditure isn't already taken into account or not denied a deduction by another provision". The figure is the primary production and non-primary production columns added together.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Reconciliation items
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, self-assessed, that is the sum of the two production columns on the schedule. For the five-year route it is one fifth of the underlying spend in each of five years.
limitation: It cannot tell you when the money was spent. A small business claiming immediately and a larger one claiming a fifth of a five-year write-off appear identically here, so the column is not a measure of current-year capital outlay. Deductions deferred under the non-commercial loss rules also do not appear in the year the expense was incurred.
rationale: The DIL label names the total section 40-880 deduction, which is a reconciliation item on the individual's business and professional items schedule. The ATO instruction sets out both the immediate and the five-year treatments.
evidence_quote: Section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997 also allows you to deduct in equal proportions over a 5-year period certain capital expenditure you incur if the expenditure isn't already taken into account or not denied a deduction by another provision.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Section 40-880 deduction - total' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing explained what the provision covers or that the amount can be a fifth of the spend.

value_domain: Dollar amount of credit for trustee tax under subsection 98A(2)
value_source: ATO, Tax on trust distributions to non-resident beneficiaries
variable_description: A credit a non-resident beneficiary claims for tax the trustee already paid on their share of a trust's net income. The ATO explains the sequence: tax assessed to the trustee "is generally not a final tax", and "when the non-resident beneficiary prepares their Australian tax return, they can claim a credit for the tax paid by the trustee (under subsection 98A(2))". Its presence is a strong marker that the lodger was a foreign resident with trust income, which is worth reading against CLNT_RSDNT_IND in the same context table.
description_source: ATO, Tax on trust distributions to non-resident beneficiaries
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit against tax payable, not a deduction from income despite the DIL label, and reported only by beneficiaries assessed under section 98A.
limitation: It is not a measure of trust income received; a large credit can sit against a modest distribution taxed at the non-resident trustee rate. It also does not identify the trust, so it cannot be joined to a trust return, and it says nothing about credits claimed under the neighbouring section 98B route for chains of trusts.
rationale: The DIL label names the section 98A amount. The ATO page on trust distributions to non-resident beneficiaries states exactly what subsection 98A(2) allows and who can claim it.
evidence_quote: When the non-resident beneficiary prepares their Australian tax return, they can claim a credit for the tax paid by the trustee (under subsection 98A(2)).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Section 98a amount' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it named a subsection without saying that the amount is a credit for tax a trustee already paid.

value_domain: Sex recorded on the ATO client record for the lodger
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office data
variable_description: The lodger's sex as the ATO holds it on its client record, carried onto the return rather than answered on the form. It comes from what was supplied at tax file number registration and later updates, so it is an administrative attribute of a tax record and not a question the taxpayer answers each year. IDV_SPSS_SEX_CD in the same context table records the spouse's, and the two are collected the same way.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office data
value_definition: A short sex code with no published category list. Whether it carries anything beyond male and female, and how an unstated value is represented, cannot be read from the metadata.
limitation: It is not collected to an ABS statistical standard, so it should not be pooled with Census or vital statistics sex without first checking that the categories agree. Where it disagrees with a linked Census or birth record, the tax record is the weaker source, and a change between years reflects a register update rather than a measured event.
rationale: No ATO publication gives the client record's sex categories. The ABS PLIDA page establishes that the personal income tax module is supplied from ATO administrative records, which supports the claim that the value comes from the client record rather than the return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the single word 'Sex' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it said neither where the value comes from nor that no code list is published.

value_domain: Flag marking inclusion in an ATO 16 per cent sample file of individual returns
value_source: ATO, Taxation statistics, Individuals sample files
variable_description: A flag marking whether this return was drawn into a 16 per cent sample file of individual tax returns. The ATO publishes sample files of individual return information for modelling and research, noting that "For income years 2003-04 to 2010-11, the files contain a 1% sample of records. From 2011-12 onwards, the files contain a 2% sample of records", so the 16 per cent frame named here is a larger internal sample rather than one of the published files. It first appears for 2018-19 and sits with SA1, SA2 and LGA in the context table.
description_source: ATO, Taxation statistics, Individuals sample files
value_definition: A record-level indicator, present from 2018-19 onwards. The sampling frame, the stratification and whether the flag is stable for a person across years are all unpublished.
limitation: It is not a survey weight and carries no expansion factor, so selecting on it produces a sample that cannot be grossed to the lodger population without design information the asset does not carry. Because the frame is undocumented, a comparison of flagged and unflagged records could reflect the sample design rather than any real difference.
rationale: The ATO's sample file page documents the published individual sample files and their sampling fractions, which establishes the practice of drawing sample files from individual returns but does not describe a 16 per cent file. No fetchable ATO or ABS page defines this flag.
evidence_quote: For income years 2003-04 to 2010-11, the files contain a 1% sample of records. From 2011-12 onwards, the files contain a 2% sample of records.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried '16% sample file indicator' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it repeated the label without saying that the sample design behind the flag is not published.

value_domain: Dollar balance of student financial supplement scheme debt
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
variable_description: The accumulated student financial supplement scheme debt still outstanding for this taxpayer at assessment. The scheme is closed to new borrowing, so the population can only shrink: it "was a voluntary loan scheme to help tertiary students cover their expenses while they studied" and "closed on 31 December 2003. However, all existing SFSS loans continue to be collected through the tax system." The balance is held by the ATO, not reported by the lodger.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
value_definition: A whole-dollar accumulated balance, indexed annually and reduced by compulsory and voluntary repayments. It is one of several loan types that share a single repayment threshold.
limitation: It is not evidence of current or recent study, and after 2003 it cannot be, so treating it as an education indicator dates the person to a cohort that borrowed twenty years earlier. It is also only one loan type: a person with a large HELP debt and no SFSS shows zero here.
rationale: The DIL label names the student financial supplement scheme accumulated debt. The ATO page defines the scheme, states that it is closed and confirms that existing balances are still collected through the tax system.
evidence_quote: This scheme closed on 31 December 2003. However, all existing SFSS loans continue to be collected through the tax system.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Supplementary loan accum amount' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not even expand the abbreviation, let alone say the scheme has been closed since 2003.

value_domain: Dollar amount of compulsory SFSS repayment raised on assessment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Compulsory repayments
variable_description: The compulsory student financial supplement scheme repayment the ATO raised for the year, taken out of the assessment rather than paid separately. The ATO does the calculation without any entry on the return: "If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment." It exists only above the repayment threshold, so most people with a balance in a given year show nothing.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Compulsory repayments
value_definition: A whole-dollar compulsory repayment for the income year, worked out from repayment income against published thresholds. It reduces the balance carried in SFSS_CLCTBL_DEBT_OUTSTG_AMT on the same row.
limitation: It is not the amount the person paid off in the year, because voluntary repayments and employer withholding are not in it, and indexation can raise the balance by more than the repayment reduces it. A zero can mean no debt, income below the threshold, or a Medicare levy reduction that removes the obligation, and the column cannot separate the three.
rationale: The DIL label names the SFSS assessment debt. The ATO page on compulsory repayments states that the ATO calculates the repayment from repayment income and puts it on the notice of assessment, and that no loan information is entered on the return.
evidence_quote: If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Supplementary loan assessment debt' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish a yearly repayment from an outstanding balance.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 13 label B, share of NRAS tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of the national rental affordability scheme tax offset, passed through from a partnership or trust that held NRAS rental property. It is reported alongside the partnership and trust income it belongs to: the ATO directs a lodger with "national rental affordability scheme (NRAS) rent" to "write your share of the NRAS tax offset at question 13 - label B (show cents)". The offset is refundable, unlike most of the offsets recorded elsewhere in this table.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A dollars and cents amount, reported to the cent rather than rounded, and claimed only by investors holding NRAS property through a partnership or trust.
limitation: It is a share of an offset, not a share of rent, so it measures the subsidy rather than the investment; the underlying dwelling count and rent are not here. NRAS entitlements held directly rather than through a partnership or trust are claimed elsewhere on the return, so this column undercounts scheme participation.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of the NRAS tax offset, which is item 13 label B. The ATO instruction for item 13 names the label and states the condition under which a share is reported there.
evidence_quote: national rental affordability scheme (NRAS) rent, then write your share of the NRAS tax offset at question 13 - label B (show cents)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Share of national rental affordability scheme tax offset' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the amount arrives through a partnership or trust or that the offset is refundable.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 13 label M, credit for TFN amounts withheld from closely held trust payments
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A credit for tax a closely held trust withheld from a beneficiary's payment because the beneficiary's tax file number was not held. The ATO puts it at its own label: for "payments from a closely held trust from which TFN amounts are withheld", write "the total of your credits for those amounts withheld at question 13 - label M (show cents)". It is distinct from label R on the same row, which carries TFN credits from interest, dividends and unit trust distributions.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: A dollars and cents credit against tax payable, reported to the cent. It is present only where a trustee actually withheld under the closely held trust reporting rules.
limitation: It marks an administrative failure rather than an income source, so its presence says that a tax file number was missing at the time of payment, not that the beneficiary was untraced or non-compliant afterwards. The credit also does not reveal the gross distribution, which is reported separately at the trust income labels.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of the credit for TFN amounts withheld from closely held trust payments. The ATO instruction for item 13 assigns exactly that credit to label M and separates it from the label R credits.
evidence_quote: payments from a closely held trust from which TFN amounts are withheld, then write the total of your credits for those amounts withheld at question 13 - label M (show cents)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the run-together custodian wording with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never separated this credit from the other TFN withholding credit on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P15 label G, total salary and wage expenses
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P15 Total salary and wage expenses
variable_description: The wage bill of the taxpayer's own unincorporated business, added up across every business they carry on. The ATO defines it as "salary, wages and other labour costs actually paid or payable to persons employed in your business (excluding those forming part of capital expenditure or paid for private or domestic assistance)", including holiday pay, overtime, bonuses and retiring allowances, and excluding contract, agency, consultant and superannuation payments. It is the closest thing in the individual return to a measure of a sole trader's employment.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P15 Total salary and wage expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar total across all of the lodger's businesses, self-assessed. It is a memorandum figure: the same wages are already inside the expense components at P8, and SLRY_AND_WG_EXPNSS_TOTL_CD says which one.
limitation: It is not a head count and not a payroll for a single business, so it cannot be turned into employee numbers or compared with an employer's Single Touch Payroll reporting for one entity. Amounts paid to contractors and to the proprietor are outside it, so a business that runs on subcontractors shows a small figure with a large workforce.
rationale: The DIL label names the total salary and wage expenses amount, which is P15 label G of the individual's business and professional items schedule. The ATO instruction for that item lists exactly what is inside and outside the figure.
evidence_quote: Salary, wages and other labour costs actually paid or payable to persons employed in your business (excluding those forming part of capital expenditure or paid for private or domestic assistance) are usually deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total salary and wage expenses - amount' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the amount is a memorandum total already counted inside the P8 expense labels.

value_domain: Expense component code letter in the type box at P15 label G
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P15 Total salary and wage expenses
variable_description: A letter saying which expense line at P8 the wage bill was reported inside, so the same wages are not counted twice. The ATO's four letters are "C - all included in the expense component Cost of sales", "A - all included in the expense component All other expenses", "B - included in the expense component of both Cost of sales and All other expenses" and "O - included in expense components other than Cost of sales and All other expenses". It qualifies the dollar amount in SLRY_AND_WG_EXPNSS_TOTL_AMT rather than adding to it.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P15 Total salary and wage expenses
value_definition: One letter from C, A, B or O, printed in the type box beside the wage total. It is only present where a wage amount is reported.
limitation: The letter describes the taxpayer's own bookkeeping, not the nature of the work, so it says nothing about the kind of labour employed and should never be read as an industry or occupation code. Code O in particular is a residual that could mean almost any other expense line.
rationale: The DIL label names the type of the total salary and wage expenses. The ATO instruction for P15 publishes the four code letters and the purpose of choosing between them.
evidence_quote: C - all included in the expense component Cost of sales
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total salary and wage expenses - type' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so the code letters and their purpose were both absent.

value_domain: Date of a single Australian superannuation lump sum payment at item 8
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
variable_description: The day a super lump sum was paid, copied from the payment summary onto item 8 of the return. The ATO asks for it only where a single lump sum is reported: "Write the date of payment and your payer's ABN, in the left column at question 8." Where two or more lump sums were received the taxpayer completes a separate schedule instead and the instruction says "Don't write any date of payment or payer's ABN in your tax return", so the date goes missing precisely for the people with the most payments.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
value_definition: A calendar date taken from the PAYG payment summary for a superannuation lump sum. In this asset it appears for 2009-10 only.
limitation: A missing date is not evidence of no lump sum: it is the expected result when a person received more than one, which the M code in SLS_PMT_TYP_CD marks. The date also belongs to the payment, not to retirement or to a condition of release, so it cannot be read as a retirement date.
rationale: The DIL label names the date of payment for Australian superannuation lump sum payments. The ATO instruction for item 8 says when the date is written on the return and when it is deliberately left off.
evidence_quote: Don't write any date of payment or payer's ABN in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Australian superannuation lump sum payments -Date of payment' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not warn that the date is absent by design for multiple payments.

value_domain: Type box code letter at item 8 for a superannuation lump sum
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
variable_description: A letter at item 8 marking a super lump sum as a death benefit, or marking that a lump sum schedule was attached because there was more than one payment. The ATO gives two uses of the box: "If you receive a lump sum death benefit payment, print N in the TYPE box at question 8. Otherwise, leave the TYPE box blank", and for two or more lump sums "Print M in the TYPE box." The box is therefore blank for the ordinary single lump sum, which is the most common case.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
value_definition: A single letter, blank for a single ordinary lump sum, N for a death benefit and M where a superannuation lump sum schedule has been attached. Older return editions may use further letters not published on the current page.
limitation: The code mixes two unrelated facts, the nature of the payment and the number of payments, so an M row does not say whether any of the payments was a death benefit. A blank is meaningful rather than missing, which means treating blanks as unknown will wrongly discard the standard case.
rationale: The DIL label names the type of Australian superannuation lump sum payments, which is the type box at item 8. The ATO instruction for that item states both code letters and when the box stays blank.
evidence_quote: If you receive a lump sum death benefit payment, print N in the TYPE box at question 8. Otherwise, leave the TYPE box blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Type of australian superannuation lump sum payments' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so neither the codes nor the meaning of a blank was recorded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from superannuation lump sums at item 8
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
variable_description: Tax the super fund withheld before paying a lump sum, totalled across every lump sum the person received in the year. The taxpayer copies it from the payment summary rather than calculating it: "Write the total amount of tax withheld, from your payment summary, under Tax withheld at question 8." It is a credit against the assessment, so it sits with the other withholding columns in the whld_debt table rather than with the income components at labels P and Q.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit for the year, summed over payment summaries where more than one lump sum was received. Reported by the fund on the payment summary, so third-party sourced.
limitation: It is not the tax paid on the lump sum. The final liability is settled in the assessment and can be more or less than the amount withheld, so this column overstates or understates the tax cost of the payment depending on the person's other income. Nil withholding is common for people over 60, and does not mean no lump sum was received.
rationale: The DIL label names the tax withheld on Australian superannuation lump sum payments, which is the tax withheld column at item 8. The ATO instruction states that the amount is copied from the payment summary and totalled where there are several.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of tax withheld, from your payment summary, under Tax withheld at question 8.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Tax withheld on australian superannuation lump sum payments' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish withholding from final tax.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 8 label Q, taxed element of a superannuation lump sum
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
variable_description: The part of a super lump sum that came from contributions and earnings already taxed in the fund, reported at label Q. The ATO tells the taxpayer to write "the taxed element amount at label Q", and the label is only used where the amount is assessable, because a taxed element paid on or after age 60 is tax free and "you don't include them in your assessable income". The untaxed element goes to label P on the same row, and the two together are the assessable part of the payment.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable component taken from the superannuation lump sum payment summary, totalled where a lump sum schedule was completed.
limitation: It is not the size of the lump sum. The tax-free component never appears anywhere on the return, and for most people over 60 the taxed element is excluded as well, so a large withdrawal by a retiree typically shows nothing here at all. Using this column as a drawdown measure will find mainly under-60 and death benefit payments.
rationale: The DIL label names the taxed element of Australian superannuation lump sum payments, which is item 8 label Q. The ATO instruction for that item assigns the label and lists the amounts that are excluded from it.
evidence_quote: Taxed element of a super lump sum payment you receive on or after your 60th birthday (these amounts are tax free and you don't include them in your assessable income) unless it is a death benefit super lump sum payment you receive as a non-dependant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Australian superannuation lump sum payments taxed element' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say that most retiree withdrawals never reach the label.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 8 label P, untaxed element of a superannuation lump sum
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
variable_description: The part of a super lump sum that had not been taxed in the fund, reported at label P and assessable at any age. The ATO directs the taxpayer to write "the untaxed element amount at label P", separately from the taxed element at label Q. Untaxed elements come mainly from unfunded public sector schemes and from certain death benefits, so this column identifies a particular kind of fund rather than a particular size of withdrawal.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable component from the superannuation lump sum payment summary, totalled where a lump sum schedule was completed. It is taxed differently from the taxed element at label Q on the same row.
limitation: A zero here is the normal case rather than an absence of super, because most private funds pay no untaxed element; reading a zero as no lump sum will misclassify almost every ordinary retiree. The column also cannot be added to label Q to get the payment, since the tax-free component is on neither.
rationale: The DIL label names the untaxed element of Australian superannuation lump sum payments, which is item 8 label P. The ATO instruction assigns the amount to that label and separates it from the taxed element.
evidence_quote: the untaxed element amount at label P
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Australian superannuation lump sum payments untaxed element' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it gave no sense of which funds produce an untaxed element.

value_domain: Veteran code letter at item T1 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: A letter at item T1 saying whether the taxpayer, their spouse or both are a veteran, war widow or war widower. It matters because a veteran can reach the seniors and pensioners tax offset at a lower age than a Centrelink pensioner. The ATO's letters are "V - you're a veteran, war widow or war widower", "W - your spouse is a veteran, war widow or war widower" and "X - both V and W apply to you and your spouse". It sits beside SATO_CD, which records the living arrangement rather than the veteran status.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
value_definition: One letter from V, W or X, entered in the veteran code box. Left blank where neither member of the couple is a veteran, war widow or war widower.
limitation: It identifies only people claiming the seniors and pensioners offset, so it is not a veteran indicator for the lodger population and misses every veteran who is ineligible or does not claim. The letters also do not distinguish a veteran from a war widow or widower, which are different entitlements under different tests.
rationale: The DIL label names the seniors and pensioners veteran code. The ATO instruction for item T1 publishes the three code letters and the veteran pension age test that makes the code matter.
evidence_quote: V - you're a veteran, war widow or war widower
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Seniors and pensioners veteran code' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not give the letters or warn that the code only exists inside an offset claim.

value_domain: Dollar amount of seniors and pensioners tax offset applied against tax payable
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: How much seniors and pensioners tax offset actually reduced this person's tax, after the ATO worked the entitlement out from the T1 codes and rebate income. The maximum entitlement depends on the couple's arrangement: for a couple who "live apart due to illness, the maximum tax offset is $2,040 each" and for a couple who "live together, the maximum tax offset is $1,602 each". The offset is non-refundable, so the used amount stops at the tax the person owed.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount derived by the ATO during assessment, bounded above by both the calculated entitlement and basic tax payable. Present only for lodgers who claimed at item T1.
limitation: A zero does not mean ineligibility; a retiree with income below the tax-free threshold shows zero used because there was no tax to reduce, which is the outcome the offset is designed to accommodate. Any unused portion transferred to or from a spouse is settled by the ATO elsewhere, so this column does not close the couple's arithmetic on its own.
rationale: The DIL label names the SAPTO used amount. The ATO instruction for item T1 states the maximum offset amounts, that the ATO calculates the offset from the information provided, and that unused entitlement can transfer between spouses.
evidence_quote: live apart due to illness, the maximum tax offset is $2,040 each
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Seniors and pensioners tax offset (sapto used)' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say that the offset is non-refundable or that the ATO rather than the taxpayer sets the amount.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total supplement deductions carried to label D of the main return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement deductions
variable_description: The supplementary section's deduction total as it lands on the front return, where it joins the D1 to D10 claims to give total deductions. The ATO closes the supplement with a transfer step: "Transfer the amount you wrote at Total supplement deductions in your supplementary tax return to label D in your tax return." It runs from 2006-07, three years earlier than the companion column that holds the supplement's own total, so it is the longer series of the two.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement deductions
value_definition: A whole-dollar total carried from the supplementary return to label D of the main return. Zero or blank where the taxpayer made no D11 to D15 claim.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's total deductions; the work-related and other main-return claims at D1 to D10 are outside it, so using this column as a deductions measure captures only the supplement. The composition also changes over the series as questions D11 to D15 were renumbered and redefined, so a level comparison across two decades is not comparing the same claims.
rationale: The DIL label names the total supplement deductions transferred. The ATO instruction for that section states the transfer to label D that distinguishes this column from the supplement's own total.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount you wrote at Total supplement deductions in your supplementary tax return to label D in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total supplement deductions' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, identical to its companion column, so the two could not be told apart.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total supplement deductions on the supplementary return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement deductions
variable_description: The sum of the deductions the taxpayer claimed in the supplementary section, before it is carried to the front return. The ATO defines it by addition: "Add up all the deduction amounts in the right-hand column of questions D11 to D15 in your supplementary tax return." Those five questions cover foreign pension undeducted purchase price, personal super contributions, project pool, forestry managed investment schemes and other deductions not claimable elsewhere.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement deductions
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the D11 to D15 amounts. It begins in this asset at 2009-10, later than the transferred total on the same row.
limitation: It is a subtotal, not a category: two lodgers with the same figure may have claimed entirely different things, since a personal super contribution and a forestry scheme payment both land here. The column also does not indicate whether the deduction was allowed, only that it was claimed.
rationale: The DIL label names the total supplement deductions. The ATO instruction states which questions are added to form it, which is the fact the label alone does not carry.
evidence_quote: Add up all the deduction amounts in the right-hand column of questions D11 to D15 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total supplement deductions' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, the same text as its companion column, so nothing said which of the two was the supplement's own total.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total supplement income or loss, signed
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss
variable_description: Everything the taxpayer declared on the supplementary income pages, netted to one figure that is carried to label I on the front return. The ATO builds it from the whole supplement: "Add up all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24", then subtracts the losses at questions 13, 17, 20 and 21. Partnership and trust income, capital gains, rent, foreign income and other income are all inside it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed total. A negative result is recorded by printing L in the loss box rather than by a minus sign, so the sign may be carried in a separate indicator in the extract.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed: a $50,000 capital gain offset by a $50,000 rental loss gives the same zero as a lodger with no supplementary income at all. Business income at item 15 and personal services income at item 14 sit in the same supplement but are not part of this total, so it is not all non-salary income either.
rationale: The DIL label names the total supplement income or loss. The ATO instruction lists exactly which questions are added and which are subtracted, and states how a loss is marked.
evidence_quote: Add up all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total supplement income or loss' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say which questions the total covers or how a loss is signed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total supplement tax offsets
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement tax offsets
variable_description: The offsets claimed on the supplementary return added together and carried to label T on the front return. The ATO defines the sum: "Add up all the tax offset amounts in the right-hand column of questions T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8 and T9 in your supplementary tax return." Those questions cover spouse super contributions, zone and overseas forces, invalid carer, landcare, early stage venture capital, early stage investor and other refundable offsets.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the T3 to T9 claims. The offsets combined here are a mixture of refundable and non-refundable entitlements.
limitation: It is a claimed total, not an amount allowed, and because refundable and non-refundable offsets are added together the figure cannot be converted into a tax reduction without knowing which questions produced it. The main return offsets at T1 and T2 are outside it, so it is not the taxpayer's total offsets.
rationale: The DIL label names the total supplement tax offsets. The ATO instruction names the seven questions summed into it and the label it is transferred to.
evidence_quote: Add up all the tax offset amounts in the right-hand column of questions T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8 and T9 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total tax supplement offsets' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which offsets are inside it or that refundable and non-refundable claims are mixed.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 14 label A, net personal services income
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P1 Personal services income
variable_description: A sole trader's personal services income after the deductions the personal services income rules still allow, reported at item 14 label A. The ATO builds it by subtraction: "Add up the amounts shown at P1 Personal services income (PSI) - labels M, N, O and J", then the deductions at labels K and L, then "Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1." The four income labels split PSI by withholding type: voluntary agreement, no ABN quoted, labour hire or specified payments, and other.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P1 Personal services income
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount that can be negative, in which case L is printed in the loss box. Completed only where the taxpayer receives PSI and is not conducting a personal services business.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's contracting income. A sole trader who passes the results test or holds a personal services business determination reports the same work at item 15 instead, so this column selects the failing cases rather than the industry. Deductions denied by the PSI rules, such as home occupancy costs, are excluded, so the net figure is higher than an accounting profit.
rationale: The DIL label names net PSI, which is P1 label A carried to item 14 label A. The ATO instruction gives the arithmetic and the four income labels it draws on.
evidence_quote: Step 3: Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1. Write your answer at P1 Personal services income (PSI) - label A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviation 'Net PSI' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never expanded the term or said which sole traders complete the label.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 24 label S, tax withheld from an assessable FHSS released amount
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 24 Other income
variable_description: Tax the ATO withheld when it released first home super saver savings from the taxpayer's super fund. The instruction puts it at its own label: "If you receive assessable FHSS released amounts, write the amount of tax withheld from these payments at question 24 - label S." The released amount itself goes to label R on the same row, so a filled value here identifies a person who withdrew super to buy a first home in that year.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 24 Other income
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit against tax payable, reported from the payment summary that accompanies the release. It appears only from 2019-20 onwards in this asset.
limitation: It is not the amount released, and it is not a measure of home purchase either, since a release can be requested and the purchase not proceed. The withheld amount is provisional: the final tax on the released amount is worked out in the assessment at the person's marginal rate less a 30 per cent tax offset, so the credit does not equal the tax cost.
rationale: The DIL label names other income tax withheld on the assessable FHSS released amount. The ATO instruction for item 24 assigns the withheld amount to label S and the released amount to label R.
evidence_quote: If you receive assessable FHSS released amounts, write the amount of tax withheld from these payments at question 24 - label S.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other income tax withheld assessable fhss released amount' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not expand FHSS or separate the withholding from the released amount.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label G, superannuation expenses
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses P8
variable_description: Super contributions the taxpayer's unincorporated business made for its employees, claimed as a business expense at P8. The ATO draws a firm line around the proprietor: "Show super expenses for the income year. Don't include any amount that is a contribution for yourself. The deduction for your own super contributions must be claimed at question D12 in your supplementary tax return." The figure is the primary production and non-primary production columns added together.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses P8
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, self-assessed, summing the two production columns. Only contributions to complying funds and retirement savings accounts belong in it.
limitation: It is not the business's super guarantee liability. Contributions made to settle a super guarantee charge are not deductible and so are absent, meaning a business that underpaid and then made good shows less here than one that paid on time. The proprietor's own contributions are also outside it, so it understates super flowing from the enterprise.
rationale: The DIL label names total superannuation expenses, which is the P8 expenses label on the individual's business and professional items schedule. The ATO instruction states what is included, what is excluded and where the proprietor's own contribution goes instead.
evidence_quote: Show super expenses for the income year. Don't include any amount that is a contribution for yourself.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Superannuation expenses - total' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the proprietor's own contributions are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item T3 label A, spouse super contributions tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T3 Super contributions on behalf of your spouse
variable_description: The tax offset claimed for contributing to a low-income spouse's superannuation, worked out from the contributions paid and the spouse's income. The ATO caps and rates it: "You're eligible for a tax offset of up to $540", calculated as "18% of the lesser of" $3,000, reduced above a $37,000 spouse income threshold, and "the total of your contributions for your spouse for the year". It is the offset amount, whereas SPNTNCNTRBTNSPDONBHLFOFSPS_AMT on the same row is the contribution that generated it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T3 Super contributions on behalf of your spouse
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset amount, self-calculated by the taxpayer from the ATO worksheets and capped at $540 for the year. Blank where no eligible spouse contribution was made.
limitation: It records a claim, not a payment into a fund, and the cap means it stops rising once contributions reach $3,000, so it cannot rank couples by how much they contributed. Eligibility also depends on the spouse's income and total super balance rather than the taxpayer's, so its absence is often a fact about the spouse.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse super contributions tax offset available, which is item T3 label A. The ATO instruction for T3 gives the cap, the rate and the income taper used to work the amount out.
evidence_quote: You're eligible for a tax offset of up to $540 in 2024-25
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Superannuation contributions on behalf of your spouse tax offset - available' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not give the cap, the rate or the spouse income test.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item T2 label S, Australian superannuation income stream tax offset available
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T2 Australian superannuation income stream
variable_description: The superannuation income stream tax offset the taxpayer claimed at item T2, mostly for pension payments received before age 60. For a taxed element the amount is reported by the fund: "Your PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream shows the tax offset amount available to you on your taxed element." For an untaxed element from a capped defined benefit stream the taxpayer works it out instead, at 10 per cent of the amount within the defined benefit income cap.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T2 Australian superannuation income stream
value_definition: A whole-dollar claimed offset amount. Its two components are sourced differently: the taxed element figure comes from the payment summary, the untaxed element figure from an ATO worksheet or tool.
limitation: It is an entitlement claimed, not tax saved, so it overstates benefit for anyone whose tax payable is below the claim. It is also not a measure of pension income: a taxed element received on or after age 60 carries no offset at all, so most retirees drawing a super pension show nothing here.
rationale: The DIL label names the Australian superannuation income stream tax offset available, which is item T2. The ATO instruction states where the taxed element amount comes from and how the untaxed element amount is calculated.
evidence_quote: Your PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream shows the tax offset amount available to you on your taxed element.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Australian superannuation income stream tax offset - available' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say that the fund reports part of it and the taxpayer calculates the rest.

value_domain: Dollar amount of Australian superannuation income stream tax offset applied against tax payable
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T2 Australian superannuation income stream
variable_description: How much of the superannuation income stream tax offset actually reduced this person's tax, which is the claim at item T2 limited by the tax they owed. The claim itself is bounded before it gets here, because "There is a limit on the amount of tax offset you can claim on your untaxed element", set by the defined benefit income cap. Read against SPNTNANNTY_PNSN_OFST_AVLBL_AMT on the same row, the gap between available and used is entitlement the taxpayer could not use.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T2 Australian superannuation income stream
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount derived by the ATO at assessment, never greater than the available amount on the same row and never greater than tax payable.
limitation: A zero used amount with a positive available amount is a common and meaningful outcome rather than an error, so dropping zeros discards exactly the low-income pensioners the offset targets. The column also does not identify whether the unused part came from the taxed or the untaxed element, which are capped differently.
rationale: The DIL label names the Australian superannuation income stream tax offset used. The ATO instruction for item T2 establishes the claimable amount and the cap on the untaxed element, and the offset is non-refundable, so the used amount is bounded by tax payable.
evidence_quote: There is a limit on the amount of tax offset you can claim on your untaxed element.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Australian superannuation income stream tax offset - used' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it was indistinguishable from the available amount beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item T3, contributions paid on behalf of a spouse
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T3 Super contributions on behalf of your spouse
variable_description: Money the taxpayer put into their spouse's superannuation during the year, reported so the ATO can check the spouse contributions tax offset. The instruction is direct: "Write the total of your contributions at question T3 - label Contributions paid in your supplementary tax return." It is the input to the offset, while SPNTN_PDONBHLF_SPSTAX_OFST_AMT on the same row is the offset itself, and the contribution is not deductible to the person making it.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T3 Super contributions on behalf of your spouse
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution total for the year, self-assessed. Where the taxpayer had more than one spouse in the year the steps are repeated for each, so the label can aggregate across spouses.
limitation: It only captures contributions made in support of an offset claim, so contributions to a spouse who earns too much for the offset are unlikely to appear at all. Contributions made to satisfy a family law super split are specifically outside the offset and so outside this figure, which means the column is not a record of all spouse-directed contributions.
rationale: The DIL label names the contributions paid at the spouse super contributions question. The ATO instruction for T3 states the label and the eligibility conditions that decide whether a contribution is reported there.
evidence_quote: Write the total of your contributions at question T3 - label Contributions paid in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Superannuation contributions on behalf of your spouse - contributions paid' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish the contribution from the offset it supports.

value_domain: Dollar amount at spouse details label P, spouse's Australian Government pensions and allowances
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The taxable government pension or allowance the taxpayer's spouse received, reported by the taxpayer in the spouse details section. The ATO defines it by reference to the spouse's own return: "At label P, write the amount your spouse shows at question 6 Australian Government pensions and allowances in their tax return that they receive in 2024-25 (not including exempt pension income)." Exempt pension income goes to label Q instead, which is SPS_EXMT_PNSN_INCM_AMT on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount about the spouse, entered on this lodger's return. Zero must be written where the spouse received nothing, so a blank and a nil are meant to differ.
limitation: It is a second-hand report and may be an estimate, since the ATO tells lodgers who cannot obtain the figure to "make a reasonable estimate" and undertakes not to penalise a good-faith error. It is therefore weaker evidence about the spouse than the spouse's own return, and the two can disagree for the same couple and year.
rationale: The DIL label names the amount of Australian Government pensions and allowances the spouse received. The ATO spouse details instruction assigns it to label P and states the exclusion that separates it from label Q.
evidence_quote: At label P, write the amount your spouse shows at question 6 Australian Government pensions and allowances in their tax return that they receive in 2024-25 (not including exempt pension income).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long wording with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the value is reported by the partner and may be an estimate.

value_domain: Calendar month of the spouse's date of birth
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The month of the spouse's birthday, taken from the date of birth the lodger enters in the spouse details section. The ATO asks for the full date: "Write your spouse's date of birth at label K." This column is the month component of that date in the returns from 2021-22 onwards, and it replaces SPS_DOB_MONTH, which carries the same fact for years up to 2020-21.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A month number from 1 to 12, derived from the date of birth entered at label K. Present only where the lodger had a spouse at some time during the year.
limitation: It cannot give an age on its own; the year is in SPS_BRTH_DT_YEAR and only the two together support an age calculation. Because it is the lodger's report of someone else's birthday rather than a register value, it can disagree with the spouse's own record and it is missing entirely for lodgers with no spouse.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse birth month. The ATO spouse details instruction establishes that the lodger enters the spouse's date of birth at label K, which is the source of the month component.
evidence_quote: Write your spouse's date of birth at label K.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shouted custodian wording 'SPOUSE BIRTH MONTH' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say where the value comes from or which years it covers.

value_domain: Calendar year of the spouse's date of birth
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The year the taxpayer's spouse was born, from the date of birth entered in the spouse details section. The lodger supplies the full date, since the ATO says "Write your spouse's date of birth at label K", and the extract keeps the year and month in separate columns. This column covers 2021-22 onwards and is the successor to SPS_DOB_YEAR.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A four-digit year derived from the date of birth entered at label K. Present only for lodgers who had a spouse during the year.
limitation: It supports an approximate age at best, since without the month a spouse's age at 30 June is uncertain by a year. The custodian's own label for this column is misspelt, which is a warning that these spouse date fields have had little scrutiny and should be checked against SPS_DOB_YEAR at the changeover.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse birth year. The ATO spouse details instruction establishes the label K date of birth from which the year is taken.
evidence_quote: Write your spouse's date of birth at label K.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt custodian wording 'SPOUSE BRITH YEAR' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing corrected the label or explained the field.

value_domain: Dollar amount at spouse details label O, spouse's taxable income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The spouse's taxable income for the year, reported by the lodger rather than by the spouse. The ATO uses it for the private health insurance rebate, the seniors and pensioners offset, the Medicare levy reduction and the Medicare levy surcharge. The instruction is specific about which figure to use: "At label O, write your spouse's 2024-25 taxable income (excluding any assessable first home super saver released amount) ... If this amount is zero or a loss, write 0 (zero)."
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar taxable income figure for the spouse, floored at zero. Where the couple was together for only part of the year the details relate to the last spouse in the income year.
limitation: A loss is written as zero, so this column cannot show a spouse with negative taxable income and understates dispersion at the bottom of the couple income distribution. It is also the lodger's report and may be an estimate, so it is not interchangeable with the taxable income on the spouse's own return.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse's taxable income. The ATO spouse details instruction assigns it to label O, states the FHSS exclusion and gives the zero-flooring rule.
evidence_quote: At label O, write your spouse's 2024-25 taxable income (excluding any assessable first home super saver released amount).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried "Your spouse's taxable income" with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say that losses are recorded as zero or that the figure may be an estimate.

value_domain: Dollar amount at spouse details label E, child support the spouse paid
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: Child support the taxpayer's spouse provided to someone else during the year, reported in the spouse details section. The ATO collects it to work out family-tested entitlements, and defines it as "the total amount of any payments or benefits that your spouse must provide to another person to maintain their natural or adopted child". Support the spouse provides to the lodger is excluded unless the couple live apart permanently, and the child support the lodger pays is reported separately in the income tests section of their own return.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the year covering payments and benefits in kind, not only cash transfers. Zero must be written where the spouse paid nothing.
limitation: It is a liability met, not a liability assessed, so it does not show arrears or the Services Australia assessment behind them; a spouse who paid nothing of a large obligation shows zero. Voluntary support with no legal obligation is outside the definition, so the column understates transfers to children in other households.
rationale: The DIL label names child support the spouse paid. The ATO spouse details instruction assigns it to label E and defines what counts and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: At label E, write the total amount of child support your spouse provides to another person, that is, the total amount of any payments or benefits that your spouse must provide to another person to maintain their natural or adopted child.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Child support your spouse paid' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the amount covers benefits as well as cash or that it is reported by the partner.

value_domain: Yes or no answer in the spouse details section on spouse death during the year
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer's spouse died during the income year, asked only so the Medicare levy surcharge can be worked out correctly. The ATO ties the question to a narrow case and a stated purpose: "If your spouse dies during 2024-25 and you don't have another spouse on or before 30 June 2025, print X in the Yes box to the right of Did your spouse die during the year? We use this information to calculate your Medicare levy surcharge." It is answered by the surviving partner on their own return.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A yes or no indicator, present only where the lodger completed the spouse details section. Available from 2012-13 onwards in this asset.
limitation: It is not a death register and should never be used as one. A widowed person who repartnered before 30 June is instructed not to tick yes, and a person who does not lodge, or who omits the spouse details, records nothing at all, so the column undercounts spousal deaths by an unknown margin.
rationale: The DIL label asks whether the spouse died during the year. The ATO spouse details instruction states the exact condition for answering yes and the single purpose the answer serves.
evidence_quote: If your spouse dies during 2024-25 and you don't have another spouse on or before 30 June 2025, print X in the Yes box to the right of Did your spouse die during the year?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the answer is conditional on not repartnering or that it exists for the Medicare levy surcharge.

value_domain: Calendar month of the spouse's date of birth, earlier return editions
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The month of the spouse's birthday for return years up to 2020-21, before the field was renamed. It comes from the date of birth the lodger writes in the spouse details section, where the ATO says "Write your spouse's date of birth at label K." SPS_BRTH_DT_MONTH carries the same fact from 2021-22, so a continuous series has to be built by joining the two columns at the changeover.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A month number from 1 to 12, taken from the label K date of birth. Present in this asset for 2009-10 and again for 2019-20 to 2020-21.
limitation: The custodian's description for the 2009-10 table calls this field the birth year, which is wrong for a month column, so the label cannot be trusted to identify the component and the values should be checked before use.
