The coverage is also broken rather than continuous, so an unbroken spouse birth month series does not exist in this column alone.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse's month of birth. The ATO spouse details instruction establishes the label K date of birth that both this column and its successor are derived from.
evidence_quote: Write your spouse's date of birth at label K.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the mistaken custodian wording 'Your spouse date of birth - birth year' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it neither corrected the label nor flagged the break in coverage.

value_domain: Calendar year of the spouse's date of birth, earlier return editions
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The spouse's year of birth as recorded for 2019-20 and 2020-21, from the date of birth in the spouse details section. The ATO collects the full date at one label, since "Write your spouse's date of birth at label K", and the extract splits it. SPS_BRTH_DT_YEAR carries the same fact from 2021-22 onwards.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A four-digit year taken from the label K date of birth. Present in this asset for 2019-20 and 2020-21 only.
limitation: The two-year window is too short to follow a couple over time, so any longitudinal use has to bridge to SPS_BRTH_DT_YEAR and accept that the two columns were populated by different extract runs. A birth year on its own also cannot place the spouse either side of an age threshold such as pension age.
rationale: The DIL label names the spouse's year of birth. The ATO spouse details instruction establishes the label K date of birth from which the year component comes.
evidence_quote: Write your spouse's date of birth at label K.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Spouse year of birth' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not record the narrow coverage or the successor column.

value_domain: Dollar amount at spouse details label U, spouse's distribution carrying family trust distribution tax
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: A trust distribution the spouse received on which family trust distribution tax had already been paid. It is collected so the couple's income can be restored for the Medicare levy surcharge, because a distribution that has already borne family trust distribution tax is left out of assessable income. The ATO routes the figure from the spouse's own return, telling the lodger "At label U, write the amount your spouse shows at question A5 - label X in their supplementary tax return."
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount net of expenses that would have been deductible against the distribution. Zero must be written where the spouse received no such distribution.
limitation: It is a rare field and its absence is not informative, since it is only completed where a trust distributed outside its family group and the trustee paid the tax. It also cannot be added to the spouse's taxable income at label O without care, because the two are defined to be mutually exclusive.
rationale: The DIL label names distributions to the spouse on which family trust distribution tax has been paid. The spouse details instruction assigns it to label U and takes the figure from question A5 of the spouse's own supplementary return.
evidence_quote: At label U, write the amount your spouse shows at question A5 - label X in their supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long wording with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say the amount is excluded from assessable income and reported only for the surcharge.

value_domain: Dollar amount at spouse details label Q, spouse's exempt pension income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: Tax-exempt pension income the spouse received, listed separately because it is outside their taxable income but still counts for income tests. The ATO names the payments exactly: disability support pension, youth disability supplement, carer payment, and invalidity and partner service pensions under the Veterans' Entitlements Act. It is kept apart from the other tax-free payments on the same page, since "Don't include at label Q any of the exempt payments from label B", and apart from label P, which carries the spouse's taxable government pensions and allowances.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount limited to the five payment types the instruction lists. Zero must be written where the spouse received none of them.
limitation: It is not all of the spouse's tax-free income: the military compensation and veterans' payments at label B are explicitly kept out of it, so adding label Q alone to taxable income understates the couple's resources. Because the lodger reports it, a spouse who does not disclose a disability support pension leaves a zero that looks like an absence of payment.
rationale: The DIL label names the amount of exempt pension income the spouse received. The ATO spouse details instruction assigns it to label Q and enumerates the payments that belong there and the ones that do not.
evidence_quote: Don't include at label Q any of the exempt payments from label B.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long wording with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not list which payments count or how the field differs from labels P and B.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's income for surcharge purposes
value_source: ATO, Income thresholds and rates for the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: The spouse's income measured the way the private health insurance rebate tests it, which is wider than taxable income. The ATO calculates it rather than the taxpayer reporting it: "When you lodge your tax return, we calculate your income for surcharge purposes and determine your rebate entitlement." Where the couple is tested on family income the ATO adds this column to the taxpayer's own figure, SRCHRG_PURPSS_INCM_AMT on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Income thresholds and rates for the private health insurance rebate
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount for the spouse alone, comprising their taxable income plus reportable fringe benefits, total net investment losses and reportable super contributions, with exempt foreign employment income and section 98 trust income brought in.
limitation: It does not show whether a rebate was received or a surcharge paid: private patient hospital cover, the number of dependent children and the couple's status on 30 June all move the threshold and none of them are in this column. It is also not the spouse's taxable income, which is carried separately as SPS_CRNT_FY_TI_AMT.
rationale: The variable names the spouse's income for surcharge purposes for the private health insurance rebate, and the ATO rebate page defines that measure, says who calculates it and explains when the spouse's figure is combined with the taxpayer's.
evidence_quote: When you lodge your tax return, we calculate your income for surcharge purposes and determine your rebate entitlement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Spouse income for surcharge purposes for phir', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this measure is wider than taxable income or that it is combined with the taxpayer's own.

value_domain: Dollar amount, dependent spouse tax offset applied in the assessment
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, item T1 Spouse (without dependent child or student), child-housekeeper or housekeeper
variable_description: How much of the dependent spouse tax offset was absorbed in the assessment, not how much was claimed. The offset was for maintaining a spouse with little income of their own and it withdrew as that income rose; because it is not refundable, the used amount stops at the tax otherwise payable. The claim type code on the same row, SPS_OR_HSKPR_TAX_OFST_CLM_CD, says which of the spouse, child-housekeeper or housekeeper claims produced it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, item T1 Spouse (without dependent child or student), child-housekeeper or housekeeper
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount worked out by the ATO at assessment, bounded above by the offset entitlement and by tax payable.
limitation: A zero does not mean there was no dependent spouse: it also arises when an entitlement existed but no tax was left for it to reduce, and when the spouse's income exceeded the cut-out. The used amount is therefore not the entitlement, and it cannot be compared with the available amounts recorded in later years without allowing for that difference.
rationale: The ATO instructions for item T1 set out the dependent spouse offset, its income test and its interaction with the child-housekeeper and housekeeper claims, which is the offset this 1999-2000 to 2000-01 column records. The instructions are for 2012, so the eligibility detail they carry is later than the column's years.
evidence_quote: You cannot claim this tax offset if: your spouse was born on or after 1 July 1971, your adjusted taxable income (ATI) for 2011-12 was more than $150,000, or you had a spouse for the whole year and their ATI for 2011-12 was $9,702 or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Spouse tax offset used' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished an offset applied in the assessment from an offset claimed.

value_domain: Dollar amount, item T1 tax offset worked out on the return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, item T1 Spouse (without dependent child or student), child-housekeeper or housekeeper
variable_description: The item T1 offset amount a taxpayer worked out on the return worksheets, before any of it was applied against tax. The one label pooled three different claims, and the ATO defines the second of them as someone who "kept house for you full time and also cared for your dependent child, student (under 21 years old), invalid relative or invalid spouse". The amount is reduced for a part-year claim and for shared care of a child.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, item T1 Spouse (without dependent child or student), child-housekeeper or housekeeper
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax offset amount calculated on the item T1 worksheets, apportioned for days of the year and for a family tax benefit shared-care percentage.
limitation: Being an amount available, it overstates the benefit received wherever tax payable was smaller, and the used amount is a separate column. It also cannot be split between the three claims it pools, so without the claim type code on the same row a dependent spouse and a housekeeper look identical.
rationale: The ATO instructions for item T1 give the definitions, the eligibility tests and the worksheets that produce this amount, and show that the one label covers spouse, child-housekeeper and housekeeper claims.
evidence_quote: A housekeeper is someone who kept house for you full time and also cared for your dependent child, student (under 21 years old), invalid relative or invalid spouse.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long custodian label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that three claims share the label or that this is a pre-application amount.

value_domain: ATO item T1 claim type code (S, W, H, C)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, item T1 Spouse (without dependent child or student), child-housekeeper or housekeeper
variable_description: Which of the three item T1 claims produced the offset, entered as a code letter in the claim type box. For a dependent spouse the ATO says "Print S in the CLAIM TYPE box at the right of P item T1"; for a child-housekeeper or housekeeper claim the letter is W where there was no dependent child or student and H where there was, and C marks a claim that changed type part way through the year. It qualifies the offset amount on the same row rather than adding anything to it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, item T1 Spouse (without dependent child or student), child-housekeeper or housekeeper
value_definition: A single letter. S is the dependent spouse claim, W and H separate the child-housekeeper and housekeeper claims by whether a dependent child or student was present, and C is a combined claim across parts of the year.
limitation: The letter cannot tell a child-housekeeper from a housekeeper, because both use W and H and only the worksheet the taxpayer chose separates them. It also says nothing about whether the offset survived the assessment, which the used amount answers.
rationale: The 2012 item T1 instructions name each code letter and the circumstance that produces it, which is the code list this column holds.
evidence_quote: Print S in the CLAIM TYPE box at the right of P item T1 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a coded column shipped with neither its codes nor a statement of what the code distinguishes.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's reportable superannuation contributions
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The spouse's reportable superannuation contributions, written into the spouse details section of the taxpayer's return. The ATO defines them as the sum of two things: "Reportable super contributions are the sum of reportable employer super contributions and deductible personal super contributions", taken from the spouse's own IT2 and D12 entries. They are collected because the income tests add them back to the spouse's taxable income.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount covering employer contributions above the compulsory rate, chiefly salary sacrifice, plus personal contributions the spouse claims as a deduction.
limitation: This is one person's statement about another's superannuation, and the ATO allows a "reasonable estimate" where the figure cannot be obtained, so it is weaker evidence than the spouse's own return. It is also not total contributions, since compulsory super guarantee amounts never enter it.
rationale: The spouse details instructions define reportable super contributions for this label and name the two questions the taxpayer adds together to get it.
evidence_quote: Reportable super contributions are the sum of reportable employer super contributions and deductible personal super contributions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording, 'Amount of your spouse's reportable superannuation contributions', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said what counts as reportable or that super guarantee amounts are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's section 98 trust income outside taxable income
value_source: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
variable_description: Trust income taxed in the trustee's hands because the spouse was under a legal disability, and therefore missing from the spouse's own taxable income. The ATO counts it in the couple's income test as "their share of the net income of a trust on which the trustee must pay tax (under section 98 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936) and which hasn't been included in their taxable income". The return names the disabilities: bankruptcy, being declared legally incapable because of a mental condition, and being under 18 at 30 June.
description_source: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount that sits outside the spouse's taxable income and is added to it for the income tests, taken from the trust's distribution statement.
limitation: It identifies neither the trust nor the disability, so it cannot be used to find minors with trust distributions in any reliable way. The instructions also require a zero to be written where there is no such income, which makes a genuine nil and an unanswered label look the same.
rationale: The Medicare levy surcharge page defines the spouse income component this label collects, and the spouse details instructions describe the same amount and list the disabilities that put trust income in the trustee's hands.
evidence_quote: If you have a spouse, their share of the net income of a trust on which the trustee must pay tax (under section 98 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 ) and which hasn't been included in their taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Your spouse's share of trust income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which is misleading: the column is only the part taxed to the trustee and left out of the spouse's taxable income, not their trust income generally.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse super contributions tax offset applied in the assessment
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T3 Super contributions on behalf of your spouse
variable_description: How much of the spouse super contributions tax offset was absorbed in the assessment, not the contributions that earned it. The offset is capped at $540 and the ATO works it out as "18% of the lesser of" $3,000, reduced by every dollar the spouse's income exceeds the lower threshold, and the contributions actually paid. The contributions themselves sit on the same row as SPNTNCNTRBTNSPDONBHLFOFSPS_AMT.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T3 Super contributions on behalf of your spouse
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, non-refundable and therefore bounded by both the $540 maximum and the tax otherwise payable.
limitation: It cannot measure contributions made for a low-income spouse: the calculation ignores contributions above $3,000 and cuts out entirely once the spouse's income reaches the upper threshold, so generous contributions and contributions for a working spouse both leave nothing here. The income thresholds have also been raised since the offset began, so a long series is not on one basis.
rationale: The question T3 instructions give the offset's formula, its maximum and its income test, which is what this used amount is derived from, and distinguish the offset from the contributions paid label.
evidence_quote: We calculate the tax offset as 18% of the lesser of: $3,000, reducing this amount by $1 for every $1 that the total of your spouse's assessable income, total reportable fringe benefits amounts and reportable employer super contributions for the year is more than $37,000
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never separated the offset used from the contributions paid or gave the cap that bounds it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's tax-free government pensions
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: Tax-free government pensions the spouse received, listed in the spouse details section because the income tests count them. The instructions name a closed set: special rate disability pension and compensation under the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004, income support supplement, and "a pension for defence, peacekeeping or war-caused death or incapacity or any other pension granted under Part II or Part IV of the Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986". Exempt pension income such as the disability support pension belongs in a different box on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual total of veterans' and military compensation payments that carry no income tax.
limitation: It is not all of the spouse's untaxed income: the disability support pension, carer payment and invalidity service pension are reported at the exempt pension income box instead, so treating this column as the couple's non-taxable support understates it. The list of qualifying payments is set by the instructions and has changed, so coverage is not fixed across years.
rationale: The spouse details instructions enumerate exactly which tax-free government pensions belong at this label and which belong at the neighbouring exempt pension income label.
evidence_quote: a pension for defence, peacekeeping or war-caused death or incapacity or any other pension granted under Part II or Part IV of the Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Your spouse's amount of any tax free government pensions paid' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell it from the exempt pension income column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's total reportable fringe benefits
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The reportable fringe benefits shown on the spouse's income statements, copied into the taxpayer's return. The instruction is to "write the amount your spouse shows at question IT1 - label N in their tax return" and the matching amount at label W, so the figure originates with the spouse's employer rather than with either partner. From the 2016-17 return IT1 is split between exempt employers and other employers, and the spouse section carries both parts.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up annual amount that an employer must report once a person's benefits pass the reporting threshold.
limitation: The amount is grossed up, so it is not the cash value of the benefits and cannot be added to wages as if it were salary. Where the year's return kept exempt and non-exempt employers apart, a single total here loses the distinction that some income tests depend on.
rationale: The spouse details instructions say where the amount comes from and which questions in the spouse's own return supply it, and the 2025 return shows the two-label split of IT1.
evidence_quote: At label R , write the amount your spouse shows at question IT1 - label N in their tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Your spouse's total reportable fringe benefits amounts' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is grossed up or that it comes from the employer.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's total net investment loss
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The spouse's net investment loss, collected so that a loss cannot reduce the income the couple is tested on. The instruction is arithmetic: "Your spouse's total net investment loss is the sum of any net financial investment loss and any net rental property loss", taken from their IT5 and IT6 entries. A negatively geared rental property and a geared share portfolio both end up in this one number.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount written as a positive number although it represents a loss: the excess of deductions over income, measured separately for financial investments and for rental property and then added.
limitation: It cannot say which of the two losses it is, and it does not scale with the investment behind it, since a large loss can come from a small holding in a high interest year. Because the income tests add it back, a large value raises the couple's tested income rather than lowering it, which is the opposite of its effect on taxable income.
rationale: The spouse details instructions define the label as the sum of the two loss questions in the spouse's own return.
evidence_quote: Your spouse's total net investment loss is the sum of any net financial investment loss and any net rental property loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Your spouse's total net investment loss' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never named the two components or explained that the loss is added back.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's target foreign income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT4 Target foreign income
variable_description: Foreign income the spouse received that never reaches an Australian tax return. The ATO defines target foreign income as income from sources outside Australia, or "a periodical payment by way of gifts or allowances from a source outside Australia", that is neither in taxable income nor a fringe benefit, and it must be converted to Australian dollars before it is written down. Exempt foreign employment income the spouse shows at item 20 is included in it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT4 Target foreign income
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount in Australian dollars, gross, covering money and periodic benefits from outside Australia that sit outside the Australian tax base.
limitation: It is self-reported about a third party with no statement behind it, which makes it the weakest income figure on the row. It also excludes foreign income that is taxable here, since that is already inside the spouse's taxable income, so it is not a measure of the couple's foreign income overall.
rationale: The IT4 instructions define target foreign income and list what belongs in it, and the spouse details instructions apply the same definition to the spouse's label.
evidence_quote: a periodical payment by way of gifts or allowances from a source outside Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Your spouse's target foreign income' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is by definition outside taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount, spouse's taxed element of a super lump sum taxed at zero
value_source: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
variable_description: The taxed element of a superannuation lump sum the spouse received on which the tax rate was zero, collected so it can be taken back out of the couple's income test. The ATO allowed a taxpayer to "reduce your income for MLS purposes by any taxed element of the super lump sum, other than a death benefit, that does not exceed your (or your spouse's) low rate cap" where the person was aged from preservation age to under 60. The concession applies to "2023-24 and prior income years", so the label belongs to the older returns.
description_source: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount, effective only up to the low rate cap and only for a spouse between preservation age and 60.
limitation: It is not the size of the lump sum: only the taxed element within the low rate cap belongs here, so a large withdrawal can show a small figure and a withdrawal at 60 or over shows nothing at all. It also moves the income test downwards, unlike every other spouse income column on the row, so adding it to them is wrong.
rationale: The Medicare levy surcharge page defines the reduction this label supports, names the age and cap conditions, and dates its end, which explains why the column exists only in the earlier return years.
evidence_quote: For 2023-24 and prior income years, if you meet both of the following conditions, you can reduce your income for MLS purposes by any taxed element of the super lump sum, other than a death benefit, that does not exceed your (or your spouse's) low rate cap
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Your spouse's taxed element of a superannuation lump sum' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is subtracted from tested income or that the concession has ended.

value_domain: Dollar amount, income for surcharge purposes
value_source: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
variable_description: The taxpayer's own income measured for the Medicare levy surcharge and the private health insurance rebate, which is deliberately wider than taxable income. The ATO builds it up: "Your income for MLS purposes is the sum of the following items for you (and your spouse, if you have one)" - taxable income, reportable fringe benefits, total net investment losses and reportable super contributions, with exempt foreign employment income added where taxable income is $1 or more. It is worked out at assessment, so no one writes it on the return.
description_source: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount for the individual that adds back salary sacrifice, grossed-up fringe benefits and negative gearing losses that taxable income removes.
limitation: It is an individual figure while the surcharge and rebate are tested on family income, so on its own it cannot place a couple against a threshold and the spouse column on the same row has to be added. It also says nothing about whether the surcharge was payable, because private patient hospital cover exempts the taxpayer at any income.
rationale: The Medicare levy surcharge page defines income for surcharge purposes item by item, which is the measure this column holds, and states that the spouse's figure is combined with it.
evidence_quote: Your income for MLS purposes is the sum of the following items for you (and your spouse, if you have one)
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Income for surcharge purposes' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never listed the components or said the figure is calculated rather than reported.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Student Start-up Loan compulsory repayment raised
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - compulsory repayments
variable_description: The Student Start-up Loan repayment the ATO raised on this year's assessment. Nothing is claimed by the taxpayer: "If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment." The scheme began on 1 January 2016, so the column has nothing in it for earlier income years.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - compulsory repayments
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one income year, worked out from repayment income against that year's thresholds and rates and added to the assessment.
limitation: It is the amount raised, not the amount paid, and it excludes both voluntary repayments and the extra amounts an employer withheld through PAYG during the year. A zero means repayment income sat below the threshold, not that the loan was cleared.
rationale: The ATO compulsory repayments page states who calculates the repayment, what it is based on and where it appears, and the types of loans page dates the start of the Student Start-up Loan scheme.
evidence_quote: If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is ATO-calculated or that it is a raised liability rather than a payment.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Student Start-up Loan balance outstanding
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - types of loans
variable_description: The Student Start-up Loan balance still owing at the assessment, a stock rather than the year's flow. The ATO describes the loan as "a voluntary loan available to eligible students in higher education" who receive Youth Allowance, Austudy or the ABSTUDY Living Allowance, with Services Australia making the payments. The ABSTUDY version of the loan is carried in its own columns on the same row, so the two must be added to get a student's total start-up borrowing.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - types of loans
value_definition: A whole-dollar accumulated balance at the time of assessment, indexed each year and reduced by compulsory and voluntary repayments.
limitation: Because it is a balance at one moment, differencing it across years does not give repayments: indexation moves it too. It also covers this loan only, so someone with a HELP debt as well looks far less indebted here than they are.
rationale: The types of loans page defines the Student Start-up Loan, who receives it and who administers it, and the compulsory repayments page explains how the balance is reduced through the tax system.
evidence_quote: This is a voluntary loan available to eligible students in higher education
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'AUSTUDY Student Start-Up Loan Outstanding Repayable Debt', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish a balance from a repayment or note the separate ABSTUDY loan.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Student Start-up Loan debt treated as repayable at assessment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - compulsory repayments
variable_description: The part of the Student Start-up Loan account treated as repayable when the year's compulsory repayment was worked out. It sits between the outstanding balance and the repayment raised, and the three loan columns on the row are nested rather than additive. HELP, VET Student Loans, trade support loans and the ABSTUDY start-up loan each repeat the same three-column pattern, which is what identifies this one as the middle step.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - compulsory repayments
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount attached to one assessment, smaller than or equal to the accumulated balance on the same row.
limitation: Do not add it to the outstanding balance or to the compulsory repayment beside it, because the three overlap. The ATO does not publish a definition of a repayable debt distinct from the outstanding balance, so the boundary between the two columns cannot be checked against guidance and the reading here is inferred from the sibling loan columns.
rationale: The compulsory repayments page establishes the mechanism that produces the three loan columns, but it does not name a repayable debt separately from an outstanding balance, so the distinction between this column and its neighbour rests on the column pattern rather than on published wording.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'AUSTUDY Student Start-Up Loan Repayable Debt' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave a reader no way to see that the column overlaps the two loan columns beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total expenses on an early individual return
value_source: ATO, Forms and instructions
variable_description: A total expenses figure carried on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06 under an acronym the data item list does not expand. It sits among the business expense totals in the same table - total expenses, all other expenses, motor vehicle expenses - which points to the business and professional items section of the return rather than to work related deductions. Read it against EXPNSS_TOTL_AMT on the same row, which is the plain total expenses label, before assuming what it covers.
description_source: ATO, Forms and instructions
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual expense total attached to an individual's return, on the same footing as the other expense totals in that table.
limitation: The column cannot be treated as the business total expenses without confirmation, because STAC is not expanded anywhere in the metadata and the ATO does not publish the acronym, so its relationship to EXPNSS_TOTL_AMT is unresolved. It also stops after 2005-06, so any series that uses it ends there rather than continuing at zero.
rationale: The column sits among the business expense totals in the same table, which places it in the business and professional items family, but no published ATO source expands STAC, so the identification stops at the neighbourhood.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'STAC Total Expenses Amount' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left an unexpanded acronym on the page with nothing said about where it sits or how far it can be trusted.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 state and territory code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, States and Territories
variable_description: The state or territory the taxpayer's address falls in, at the 2021 boundaries. It is the coarsest of the geography columns on the row and the one that survives every boundary revision, which makes it the safe level for a long series where the SA codes below it change between editions. It is also the leading digit of every other ASGS code on the row, so a disagreement between them is a data problem rather than a real difference.
description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, States and Territories
value_definition: A single digit, 1 to 8 for the states and territories in ABS order and 9 for other territories, with a further code for migratory, offshore and no-usual-address records.
limitation: State of address is not state of economic activity: someone living near a border, or working in one state and living in another, is counted where they live. The code says nothing about metropolitan against regional, which the SA4 or the remoteness columns carry.
rationale: The field is a state code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the state and territory codes and their order.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 state or territory code.' with no value domain.

value_domain: Dollar amount, Student Financial Supplement Scheme balance outstanding
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - types of loans
variable_description: The Student Financial Supplement Scheme debt still owing at assessment, from a scheme that has been closed for two decades. The ATO says the SFSS "was a voluntary loan scheme to help tertiary students cover their expenses while they studied", that it "closed on 31 December 2003", and that "all existing SFSS loans continue to be collected through the tax system". A balance here therefore marks someone who borrowed before 2004.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans - types of loans
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance owing at assessment on a scheme closed to new borrowing, so it moves only with indexation and with repayments and never with fresh lending.
limitation: The column dates a person's study rather than measuring current borrowing, and it cannot be pooled with HELP as one student debt: the scheme had its own repayment thresholds for most of its life and it is repaid after other study loans. A zero also cannot separate someone who never borrowed from someone who has paid the loan off.
rationale: The types of loans page defines the SFSS, dates its closure and states that outstanding loans are still collected through the tax system, which is exactly what a positive balance in a 2020-21 return means.
evidence_quote: This scheme closed on 31 December 2003. However, all existing SFSS loans continue to be collected through the tax system.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Student Financial Supplement Scheme Outstanding Repayable Debt' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing on the page said the scheme had closed or what a balance implies about when the person studied.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary
variable_description: The state or territory of the address the ATO held for the taxpayer for that income year, coded to the ABS geographic standard. The geography table it sits in carries SA1, SA2 and LGA for the same address, all on the 2021 edition of the standard even though the return year is 2015-16, so the columns are comparable across return years by design. It is where the taxpayer was, not where the income was earned or the employer sat.
description_source: ABS, Census geography glossary
value_definition: A state and territory identifier from the ABS standard: the six states, the two internal territories, and a further category covering the external territories.
limitation: An address on a return is not a residence for the whole year, and the ATO holds one address rather than a history, so a person who moved is placed where they finished rather than where they lived while earning. Coding an old return to current boundaries also means the geography is consistent across years while the underlying address is not.
rationale: The ABS glossary defines the state and territory level of the geographic standard the geography table codes to, and the neighbouring SA1, SA2 and LGA columns fix that this is address geography rather than an ATO region.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'State and territory' with an inferred value domain and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said whose address it is or that the 2015-16 return is coded to 2021 boundaries.

value_domain: Dollar amount, aggregated turnover of the taxpayer and connected entities
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
variable_description: The aggregated turnover of the taxpayer's business, the test that decides whether it counts as a small business entity. The ATO defines it as "your annual turnover for the income year plus the annual turnover of any entity connected or affiliated with you at any time during the income year less income derived from dealings between you and any entity connected or affiliated with you". The variable name preserves the older Simplified Tax System wording, STS group turnover, which the small business entity rules later replaced.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual turnover figure, excluding GST charged on transactions and ordinary income from retail fuel sales, covering the taxpayer plus every connected or affiliated entity.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's own business income, because turnover of connected entities is inside it, so it can be far larger than anything else on the row. It is also a self-assessed threshold test rather than an accounting figure, so a taxpayer with no threshold to test may leave it blank instead of writing a real turnover.
rationale: The entrepreneurs tax offset instructions define aggregated turnover, annual turnover and the small business entity test, which is the quantity this label records in the years the offset ran.
evidence_quote: Broadly, your aggregated turnover for the income year is: your annual turnover for the income year plus the annual turnover of any entity connected or affiliated with you at any time during the income year less income derived from dealings between you and any entity connected or affiliated with you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Small business entity aggregated turnover' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that other entities' turnover is included or that the column carries the older STS name.

value_domain: Dollar amount, net small business income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
variable_description: Net small business income, the base the entrepreneurs tax offset was worked out on. The ATO puts it plainly: "Your net small business income is your small business entity turnover less the deductions that directly relate to that turnover." Prior year tax losses, personal superannuation contributions, gifts, the cost of managing tax affairs and deferred non-commercial losses are named as amounts that cannot reduce it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual net figure - turnover less directly related deductions - taken at the taxpayer's share where the business is carried on through a partnership or trust.
limitation: It is not net business income as reported elsewhere on the return, because the deductions allowed against it are narrower, so it will usually be the larger of the two. The offset it supported was later repealed, so a zero in the years after that means the question was no longer asked rather than that the business made nothing.
rationale: The entrepreneurs tax offset instructions define net small business income and list the deductions that are excluded from it, which is the calculation this label holds.
evidence_quote: Your net small business income is your small business entity turnover less the deductions that directly relate to that turnover.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net small business entity income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know the deductions allowed against it are narrower than for business income generally.

value_domain: ato_itr_loss_code
values: ["L: the amount is a loss","(blank): the amount is not a loss"]
value_source: ATO TaxPack 2010 (NAT 0976-6.2010) - the tax return's standard convention for a net income amount that can be negative
variable_description: The loss marker on the taxpayer's net simplified tax system income, saying whether the amount beside it is negative. The individual return carries no minus sign, so any amount that can be negative is written as a positive figure with a separate box filled in when it is a loss. The simplified tax system ran from 2001-02 to 2008-09 for small businesses that elected into it, which is why the column appears only in the earlier return context tables. It qualifies the net income amount on the same row and holds no value of its own.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2010 (NAT 0976-6.2010), the individual tax return's loss box convention
value_definition: A single letter box that is either L, marking the amount as a loss, or empty, marking it as not a loss.
limitation: A blank is ambiguous. It is left empty both by a taxpayer with a positive amount and by one who was never in the simplified tax system, so the column cannot on its own identify who elected into that system.
rationale: A '- code' suffix on a net income amount on the individual return is normally the adjacent LOSS box, in which the taxpayer prints L when the amount is negative.
evidence_quote: If it is a loss, print L in the LOSS box
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination gave no domain; the loss-code shape is defensible from the tax return's standard convention.

value_domain: Dollar amount, small business general pool depreciation deduction
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: The depreciation a small business claimed on its general pool for the year, at label B of the simplified depreciation item. The ATO instruction is to "Show the total amount you claimed at Depreciation expenses relating to the general small business pool", so the label carries the year's deduction and not the closing pool balance. Assets above the write-off threshold go into the pool and are deducted at a set rate rather than in full.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction that is already inside the business depreciation expense on the same return, not an addition to it.
limitation: It cannot be read as capital spending, because a pool deduction is a percentage of a running balance and so reflects assets bought in earlier years as much as this year's. For 2020-21 to 2022-23 the pool balance itself was written off under temporary full expensing, which inflates the amount without any change in investment.
rationale: The temporary full expensing label guide names this label and says what belongs in it, and it places the label at P10B alongside the deduction for certain assets at P10A.
evidence_quote: Show the total amount you claimed at Depreciation expenses relating to the general small business pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is a deduction rather than a balance, nor that it sits inside the depreciation expense.

value_domain: Dollar amount, small business immediate write-off deduction for low cost assets
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: The immediate write-off a small business claimed for assets costing less than the year's threshold, at label A of the simplified depreciation item. This is the instant asset write-off: the whole cost comes off in the year the asset is first used rather than being pooled and depreciated. For the 2021, 2022 and 2023 income years the ATO told small businesses using simplified depreciation that they "cannot claim instant asset write-off" and to "insert 0 at this label", because temporary full expensing replaced it.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for assets below the year's cost threshold, already counted in the business depreciation expense on the same return.
limitation: The cost threshold behind the label has moved repeatedly, so the number of assets behind a given amount is not comparable across years. The instructed zeros for 2020-21 to 2022-23 also mean an empty claim in those years says nothing at all about asset purchases.
rationale: The temporary full expensing label guide names this label, says what it holds, and records the years in which small businesses were instructed to report zero, which is the trap in any series built from it.
evidence_quote: For the 2021, 2022 and 2023 income years, small businesses using the simplified depreciation rules cannot claim instant asset write-off. You therefore need to insert 0 at this label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Small business entity simplified depreciation - deduction for certain assets' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which assets qualify or that the label was forced to zero for three years.

value_domain: ATO salary and wage occupation grouping
value_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
variable_description: A grouping of the occupation the taxpayer nominated as the source of most of their salary and wages. The return itself carries a six-digit code: the ATO says to "insert the appropriate 6-digit code from the list at question 1 - label X", chosen for the activity that produces the greatest amount of salary and wage income. This column holds a coarser grouping of that code, and the full code appears in later return years as IDV_OCPTN_CD.
description_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
value_definition: A short code standing for a group of the ATO's six-digit occupation codes, which follow the structure of the occupation classification.
limitation: The ATO publishes the six-digit code list but no sub occupation grouping, so the grouping cannot be mapped to the classification with certainty and should not be treated as an ANZSCO major or sub-major group without checking. The occupation covers salary and wage income only, so a person whose main income is business or pension income is coded from a job that may be minor or absent.
rationale: The occupation codes guide establishes what the underlying return code is and how the taxpayer chooses it, but it publishes no grouped version, so the identification of this column as a rollup of that code is inference from the name and from the full code held elsewhere in the asset.
evidence_quote: You must provide an accurate description of the main salary and wage occupation at question 1 of the individual tax return and insert the appropriate 6-digit code from the list at question 1 - label X.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Sub occupation group code' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a coded occupation column carried neither its parent classification nor a warning that the grouping is undocumented.

value_domain: Dollar amount, annuity and superannuation pension income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
variable_description: Annuity and superannuation pension income declared at item 7 of the 2006-07 return. The ATO separates the two sources: annuities are "a series of regular payments you receive from a life insurance company or friendly society in return for a lump sum payment", while super income streams are payments from super funds, retirement savings account providers and life companies. From 1 July 2007 most benefits paid to people aged 60 and over stopped being assessable, so the same item covers a much smaller population afterwards.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross annual amount taken from the payer's PAYG payment summaries, before the undeducted purchase price of an annuity is deducted.
limitation: It is not retirement income: a tax-free superannuation pension paid to someone 60 or over never appears here from 2007-08, so the column follows the taxable part of the market rather than the whole of it. Superannuation lump sums are also excluded, since they are declared at the next item.
rationale: The item 7 instructions define what annuity and superannuation income stream income is and which payment summaries carry it, which is the label this 2006-07 column records; the instructions are for 2025, so the tax treatment they describe is later than the column's year.
evidence_quote: Australian annuities (or non-super annuities) are a series of regular payments you receive from a life insurance company or friendly society in return for a lump sum payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Super annuity and pension' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not distinguish annuities from superannuation income streams or flag the 2007 change in what is assessable.

value_domain: ato_itr_r4_claim_type
values: ["S: claiming the superannuation contributions rebate only","A: claiming the annuity or pension rebate only","C: claiming both"]
value_source: ATO TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976-6.2000), question R4 'Superannuation contributions, annuity and pension', CLAIM TYPE box, page 83
variable_description: Which of the two rebates bundled at the superannuation, annuity and pension item the taxpayer was claiming. TaxPack 2000 sets it out: "If you are claiming the superannuation contributions rebate only, print the letter S in the CLAIM TYPE box at the right of S item R4. If you are claiming the annuity or pension rebate only, print A. If you are claiming both, print C." One dollar amount sits at that item, so without this letter two very different rebates cannot be told apart. The table calls it an action code; the return calls it a claim type.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976-6.2000), question R4 Superannuation contributions, annuity and pension
value_definition: A single letter: S for the superannuation contributions rebate alone, A for the annuity or pension rebate alone, and C where both were claimed.
limitation: It does not split the money. Where the letter is C the row carries one combined figure, so the superannuation contributions rebate cannot be separated from the annuity and pension rebate for those taxpayers.
rationale: In this table 'action code' is the ATO's name for a tax return code-letter box (the same variable is called 'action code' in 1999-2000 and 'claim type' in later years), and R4 is the only super-contribution item with a code box in the years the field covers.
evidence_quote: print the letter S in the CLAIM TYPE box ... print A ... print C
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination assumed a private codeframe; the claim type letters are published, though the identification of the field with item R4 is inference rather than proof.

value_domain: Dollar amount, superannuation contributions on an early individual return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question D12 Personal superannuation contributions
variable_description: A superannuation contributions figure recorded against the 1999-2000 and 2000-01 returns, paired with a super contribution action code in the context table for the same year. It is not the deduction for personal contributions, which the deductions table of the same year carries separately as personal superannuation contributions, so it records contributions captured for some other purpose - most plausibly a contributions rebate or surcharge decision. The modern equivalent of the deductible amount is question D12.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question D12 Personal superannuation contributions
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual contributions figure attached to an individual's return for one income year.
limitation: The column cannot be assumed to be either contributions the taxpayer deducted or contributions an employer made: the data item list does not name the label and the paired action code has no published code list, so it should be treated as unresolved rather than used as a contributions measure. It is also confined to the earliest return years, so it cannot anchor a series.
rationale: The D12 instructions establish what a personal superannuation contributions deduction is, which rules that reading out for this column because the same year already carries that deduction under another name; nothing published identifies the label behind this one.
evidence_quote: You may be able to claim a deduction for personal super contributions you make to your super fund or RSA provider from your after-tax income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Super Contribution Amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited a reader to treat it as the personal contributions deduction that sits elsewhere in the same year's tables.

value_domain: Dollar amount, gross salary and wages from one payer
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 1 Salary or wages
variable_description: Gross salary and wages that one payer reported for the taxpayer, before tax and before any deduction. The wages table holds one row per payer, with that payer's hashed ABN beside it, which mirrors how item 1 is completed: for each income statement the taxpayer writes the payer's ABN, the tax withheld and "the gross payment amounts under Income". Allowances are not in it, because they belong at item 2.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 1 Salary or wages
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross annual amount per payer, covering salary, wages, commissions, bonuses, casual and part-time earnings, parental leave pay and payments for lost wages under an income protection or workers compensation policy.
limitation: It is not total employment income: allowances, employment termination payments, lump sums and salary sacrificed amounts sit in other items or never appear at all, so adding this column across payers understates what employers paid. It also carries no hours, so it cannot be turned into a wage rate.
rationale: The item 1 instructions define what salary or wages income covers, what is excluded to item 2, and that the gross amount is reported per payer, which is the shape of this table.
evidence_quote: For each income statement and payment summary, write at question 1 : the payer's ABN or WPN, the 'Total Australian tax withheld' amounts under Tax withheld , the gross payment amounts under Income .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-word description, 'Income', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so a per-employer gross wage column said nothing about whose income it is or what it leaves out.

value_domain: Dollar amount, tax withheld by one payer from salary and wages
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The tax one payer withheld from the taxpayer's salary and wages over the year. It sits beside that payer's gross payment in the same row of the wages table, so the pair gives a withholding rate per job rather than per person. The figure is the employer's own calculation under PAYG - the instruction to the payer is to "Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars" - and it is a credit in the assessment rather than tax finally borne.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual amount withheld by one payer and reported by that payer on the income statement or payment summary.
limitation: It is not the tax paid on that job's income, because the liability is worked out across all income at assessment and much of a large withholding can come back as a refund. Extra amounts withheld to cover a study loan are inside it, which makes the implied rate higher than the tax scale alone would give.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define the total tax withheld field that this per-payer column reproduces, and establish that the payer, not the taxpayer, produces it.
evidence_quote: Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Tax withheld' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is per payer, employer-calculated, and a credit rather than a liability.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total tax withheld from salary and wages
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 1 Salary or wages
variable_description: Total tax withheld from salary and wages across every payer, as carried into the assessment. Where SW_TW_AMT is one payer's withholding in the wages table, this is the single figure the return works with, and it sits with the other withholding columns - allowances, government payments, termination payments, superannuation lump sums - that add up to total tax withheld. Item 1 is the source, and the taxpayer with more than five payers is instructed to combine them.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 1 Salary or wages
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual total summed across income statements and payment summaries, covering salary and wage income only.
limitation: It is a credit, not a liability: it says what employers remitted during the year, so a large figure can end in a refund and a small one in a bill. It also excludes withholding on every other income type, each of which has its own column, so it is not the total tax withheld shown on the assessment.
rationale: The item 1 instructions establish that tax withheld is reported per payer and totalled for the return, which is the difference between this column and the per-payer column in the wages table.
evidence_quote: If you have more than 5 income statements and payment summaries, go to Step 3 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax withheld from salary and wages' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never separated the return-level total from the per-payer amounts held elsewhere in the asset.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The taxpayer a return row belongs to, and the key that turns a year's separate ITR tables into one person's tax affairs. Every table for a return year carries it - context, income and loss, deductions and offsets, withholding and debt, geography, wages by payer - so a person's income, claims and assessment are assembled by joining on this column and the income year. ABS keeps the identifying information away from the data through the person linkage spine, so the value itself carries no meaning.
description_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque integer that is stable within the asset and meaningless outside it; in fplida it is generated rather than a real key.
limitation: One value is one tax entity, not one household: a couple appear as two unlinked keys, and the spouse income columns are the only bridge between them. A person who did not lodge in a year has no row at all rather than a row of zeros, so an absence is not a nil income.
rationale: The ABS spine page explains how a person is given a linkage key separated from their data, which is what this column is; the joining role across the ITR tables is read off the registry itself.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which tables it joins or that a couple cannot be assembled from it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, item D10 deduction for managing tax affairs
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
variable_description: The whole item D10 deduction for managing tax affairs, covering all three of its parts. The ATO tells the taxpayer to "Separate the costs of managing your tax affairs into the following 3 components: interest charged by the ATO, litigation costs, other expenses incurred in managing your tax affairs", written at labels N, L and M. Tax agent fees are the bulk of it for most people, and they are deductible in the year the fee is incurred.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual deduction equal to the sum of the interest, litigation and other-expenses components carried on the same row.
limitation: It cannot be read as the price of a tax agent, because ATO interest charges and legal costs sit inside it, and because the fee falls in the year it is incurred rather than the year the return it relates to covers, so it lags the work. A claim here also does not prove an agent was used, which the lodgment source column answers.
rationale: The D10 instructions define what the deduction covers, what is excluded, and the three components that make up the total, which is the composition of this column.
evidence_quote: Separate the costs of managing your tax affairs into the following 3 components: interest charged by the ATO, litigation costs, other expenses incurred in managing your tax affairs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Cost of managing tax affairs' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the total has three parts or that ATO interest is one of them.

value_domain: Dollar amount, item D10 other expenses component
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
variable_description: The other expenses part of the cost of managing tax affairs, which is where tax agent fees, tax reference material, tax software and travel to a tax adviser go. The ATO splits the item three ways - "interest charged by the ATO at label N", "litigation costs at label L", "other expenses incurred in managing your tax affairs at label M" - and this column is the third of them. It is a component, not the item total.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual deduction for one of the three D10 components, excluding ATO interest charges and litigation costs.
limitation: Do not add it to the D10 total on the same row, because it is already inside that total. In return years where the three-way split was not collected, the component and the total carry the same amount, so a change across years can be a change in how the label was captured rather than in what people spent.
rationale: The D10 instructions name the three labels and say which costs belong at each, which identifies this column as the label M component rather than the item total.
evidence_quote: other expenses incurred in managing your tax affairs at label M
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the full custodian label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a component column looked like a standalone deduction and could be double counted against the total.

value_domain: Dollar amount, tax-free government pensions or benefits
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT3 Tax-free government pensions or benefits
variable_description: Tax-free government pensions and benefits the taxpayer received, declared at item IT3 so they count in adjusted taxable income. The ATO gives the reason for collecting untaxed money: "Your ATI is an income test we use to work out your eligibility for certain tax offsets and the amount of those offsets." Government payments that are taxable belong at items 5 and 6 instead, and superannuation income streams at item 7.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT3 Tax-free government pensions or benefits
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual total, written at label U, of government payments that carry no income tax.
limitation: It changes offsets and family assistance tests but never tax payable, so it is not part of taxable income and cannot be added to it to build a total income measure. Which payments qualify is set by the special circumstances guidance and has changed over time, so the column's coverage is not constant across years.
rationale: The IT3 instructions state why the amount is collected, where it belongs and which government payments go elsewhere, which is what separates this column from items 5 and 6.
evidence_quote: Your ATI is an income test we use to work out your eligibility for certain tax offsets and the amount of those offsets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax-free government pensions' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain that the amount feeds an income test and never affects tax payable.

value_domain: Dollar amount, tax-free component on a payment summary
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
variable_description: The tax-free component of the payment reported on this payment summary, money that never enters assessable income. The ATO is direct about it: "Tax-free component of any super lump sum, including any super co-contribution or low-income super tax offset payment from us. These amounts are tax free and you don't include them in your assessable income." The taxable component of the same payment sits beside it as TOTL_TXBL_AMT, and the payment summary type column says which kind of payment the pair belongs to.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 8 Australian superannuation lump sum payments
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount on one payment summary: the part of a superannuation benefit or termination payment made up of after-tax contributions and pre-1983 service.
limitation: Because it never reaches assessable income, a person's tax return understates what they actually received by this amount, so income built from returns alone misses it. It cannot be added to gross payments on the same row either, since a payment summary carries employment income or a benefit component, not both.
rationale: The item 8 instructions define the tax-free component of a superannuation lump sum and state that it is left out of assessable income, which is the number this payment summary column holds and the reason it does not appear on the return.
evidence_quote: Tax-free component of any super lump sum, including any super co-contribution or low-income super tax offset payment from us. These amounts are tax free and you don't include them in your assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax-free component' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is outside assessable income or that the taxable component sits beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total supplement tax offsets
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement tax offsets
variable_description: The offsets claimed in the supplementary section of the return, added into one line. The instruction is arithmetic: "Add up all the tax offset amounts in the right-hand column of questions T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8 and T9 in your supplementary tax return", and then transfer the result to label T of the main return. Which questions are inside it has changed as offsets were added and repealed, so the contents are not the same set from year to year.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual total of the supplementary offsets as claimed, before any of them is applied against tax.
limitation: It is a claim rather than a benefit: most of the offsets in it are non-refundable, so the amount actually absorbed can be smaller and is held in separate used columns. Because the supplementary questions were renumbered and offsets such as the entrepreneurs, mature age worker and zone offsets came and went, a series of this column tracks changes to the form as much as to taxpayers.
rationale: The total supplement tax offsets instructions name the questions that are added together and where the total is transferred, which fixes both the composition of this column and its relationship to the main return total.
evidence_quote: Add up all the tax offset amounts in the right-hand column of questions T3 , T4 , T5 , T6 , T7 , T8 and T9 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total supplement tax offsets' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never listed what is inside the total or warned that the set changes between years.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total tax offsets
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax offsets
variable_description: Every tax offset on the return added together, the figure that takes gross tax down to net tax. The ATO's step is short and revealing: "Add up all the tax offset amounts you claimed at questions T2 and T in your tax return. (We work out the amounts at question T1 automatically.)" The parenthesis matters, because the seniors and pensioners offset and other calculated offsets are added by the ATO rather than written by the taxpayer.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual total written at label U, combining the main return offsets with the supplement total carried on the same row.
limitation: The total does not say which offsets it contains, and refundable and non-refundable offsets behave differently inside it: a refundable offset can produce a refund while the rest stop at zero tax. It is also not the amount that changed the assessment, because offsets in excess of tax payable are simply lost.
rationale: The total tax offsets instructions say what is added, what the ATO adds itself, and where the result goes, which is the composition of this column.
evidence_quote: Add up all the tax offset amounts you claimed at questions T2 and T in your tax return. (We work out the amounts at question T1 automatically.)
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total tax offsets' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that some offsets are ATO-calculated or that the total can exceed the benefit received.

value_domain: Dollar amount, ATO estimate of tax attributable to the net capital gain
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
variable_description: An ATO estimate of the tax attributable to the net capital gain inside taxable income, not an amount anyone reports. It sits among the calculated assessment fields - gross tax, tax on taxable income, Medicare levy, net tax - rather than among the return labels, and the gain it refers to is the item 18 net capital gain, which is total current year gains after capital losses and the CGT discount. Treat it as a derived split of the year's tax rather than a liability in its own right.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount produced at assessment from the net capital gain and the taxpayer's rates for the year.
limitation: The ATO does not publish how the estimate is worked out, so it cannot be reconciled with the notice of assessment or added to any other tax column on the row. A zero can mean there was no capital gain or simply that no estimate was produced for the record, and the two cannot be told apart.
rationale: The item 18 instructions define the net capital gain the estimate is built on, but no published ATO source describes an estimated tax on capital gain field, so the reading of this column rests on its position among the calculated assessment columns.
evidence_quote: You must apply your current year capital losses from step 5 against (that is, deducted from) any capital gains you made during the year to determine your net capital gain or net capital loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Estimated tax on capital gain' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing marked it as a derived estimate rather than an assessed amount.

value_domain: Dollar amount, tax on taxable income before offsets and levies
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: Tax on taxable income before offsets, levies and credits: the raw rate scale applied to the year's taxable income. The notice of assessment begins from the same figure, showing "tax you owe on your taxable income" and then the "credit you have for tax already paid during the income year". Gross tax, net tax and the balance of the assessment sit beside it on the row, and each one subtracts something further.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount from applying the year's rate scale to taxable income, before tax offsets, the Medicare levy and any withholding credit.
limitation: It is not what the taxpayer paid or owed.
