Offsets, the Medicare levy and surcharge, study loan repayments and withheld tax all sit outside it, so a person with a large figure here can still get a refund, and a person who paid no tax at all can carry a positive amount because the low income offset comes off later.
rationale: The notice of assessment page names the components of an assessment in order, which places this column at the start of the calculation rather than at its end.
evidence_quote: Your notice of assessment (NOA) is the statement we issue that explains how your tax assessment is calculated. Your NOA will show the amount of: tax you owe on your taxable income
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax on taxable income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invites a reader to treat a pre-offset figure as tax paid.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total tax withheld on a payment summary
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The total tax the payer withheld from the payments covered by this payment summary. It is the payer's own figure, sent to both the ATO and the payee, and the instruction is to "Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars" for the period the summary covers. Gross payments on the same row are what it was withheld from, and the payment summary type column says what kind of payment it was.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payment summary and one reporting period, covering all withholding on that summary, including amounts withheld from lump sum payments.
limitation: It is per summary rather than per person or per year: someone with several jobs has several rows, and a summary can cover only part of a year. It is also money remitted during the year rather than tax assessed, so it does not measure the tax the person finally bore.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define the total tax withheld field, its units and its period, which is exactly this column on the payment summary table.
evidence_quote: You must include all amounts you withheld from lump sum payments in the total tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax withheld amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount belongs to one summary and one period rather than to a person's year.

value_domain: ato_taxable_status
values: ["Taxable","Non Taxable"]
value_source: ATO Taxation statistics 2023-24, Individuals Table 3 ('Selected items, by sex, taxable status, age range and taxable income range, 2010-11 to 2023-24 income years'), column 'Taxable status'
variable_description: Whether the return produced a net tax liability after all offsets, or none at all. This is the ATO's own two-way split of individual returns, the classification it uses to report taxable and non-taxable individuals in Taxation statistics. A return can show substantial taxable income and still be non-taxable, because offsets such as the low income tax offset and the seniors and pensioners tax offset can reduce net tax to zero. The column runs in the context tables from 2010-11 onwards, the same span as the published series.
description_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Individuals Table 3, column 'Taxable status'
value_definition: Two values, Taxable and Non Taxable, attached to the return rather than to the person.
limitation: Non-taxable does not mean no income and does not mean no tax was paid during the year. Someone whose withheld tax is refunded in full on assessment is non-taxable here, and the Medicare levy is charged separately, so the column measures neither low income nor a zero total payment to the ATO.
rationale: The ATO publishes taxable status as a two-value classification of individual income tax returns over exactly the years this PLIDA field covers (2010-11 onwards).
evidence_quote: Taxable status: Taxable; Non Taxable
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination assumed a private codeframe; the ATO publishes this classification in its own taxation statistics.

value_domain: Age in completed years
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
variable_description: The taxpayer's age for the reference year, one of three age columns in the same table. AGE_FY_START is described as age at the start of the reference period and AGE_RANGE is a banded version, which leaves this column as the second point-in-time measure, most plausibly age at the end of the income year. Age is not asked on the return: the ATO holds a date of birth from registration and derives an age from it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
value_definition: A whole number of completed years for one income year.
limitation: The reference date is not published, so this column cannot be assumed to agree with AGE_FY_START on the same row, and for anyone with a birthday inside the income year the two differ by a year. Age also comes from registration data rather than the return, so it is missing or stale wherever the ATO's record of date of birth is.
rationale: The instructions for completing individual information establish that the return carries date of birth rather than age, which makes any age column derived; the choice between reference dates is inference from the sibling age columns in the same table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's typo, 'TAXPER AGE', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so a reader could not tell it from the age at the start of the year in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount, temporary budget repair levy payable
value_source: ATO, Tax rates - Australian resident
variable_description: The temporary budget repair levy payable for the year, an extra impost on high incomes that ran for three years only. The ATO records that the levy "is payable at a rate of 2% for taxable incomes over $180,000" and that it "ceased applying from 1 July 2017", so it can only be positive for 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17. It is separate from the Medicare levy and the Medicare levy surcharge, which have their own columns on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Tax rates - Australian resident
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount equal to 2 per cent of the part of taxable income above $180,000 in the years the levy applied.
limitation: A zero means different things in different years: income at or below the threshold while the levy ran, and no levy at all outside those years, so the column cannot be used to compare high-income tax burdens across the period. Dividing it by taxable income also gives an average rate on the whole income rather than the 2 per cent that applied at the margin.
rationale: The ATO rates page states the levy's rate, its threshold and the date it ceased, which is all that is needed to read the column and to date its non-zero years.
evidence_quote: The above rates don't include the Temporary Budget Repair Levy ; this levy is payable at a rate of 2% for taxable incomes over $180,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total temporary budget repair levy payable' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it gave neither the rate and threshold nor the years in which the column can be non-zero.

value_domain: Dollar amount, temporary full expensing deduction
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: The deduction claimed under temporary full expensing for the year, at label F of item P11. The instruction is to "Show the total amount of the deductions you are claiming under temporary full expensing", and the amount is already inside the business depreciation expense rather than added to it. The measure let an eligible business write off the whole business portion of an asset in the year it was first used, and it applied for the 2020-21 to 2022-23 income years only.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A whole-dollar annual deduction covering eligible new assets, second-hand assets for smaller businesses, and improvements to existing assets.
limitation: It is a deduction rather than investment: only the business portion of a cost appears, so a car used half privately shows half its price, and improvements are mixed in with purchases. Outside 2020-21 to 2022-23 the column is empty because the measure did not exist, which breaks any series that treats a blank as no capital spending.
rationale: The label guide names item P11 label F, says what belongs in it, and its notes tie the measure to the 2020-21 to 2022-23 income years, which bounds the years the column can be used.
evidence_quote: Show the total amount of the deductions you are claiming under temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Temporary full expensing - Temporary full expensing deductions' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the deduction sits inside depreciation expenses or that it exists for three years only.

value_domain: Count of assets claimed under temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: How many assets the temporary full expensing claim covered, a count rather than a dollar amount. The ATO instruction at label G of item P11 is to "Show the total number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing", which lets the deduction on the same row be read as an average cost per asset. Counts of this kind are rare on the individual return, which makes the pair unusually informative about business investment.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A whole number of assets for one income year and one taxpayer, counted from the claim rather than from an asset register.
limitation: The count includes improvements to existing assets as well as purchases, and an asset used partly privately counts once whatever the business share, so it is not a count of things bought. On its own it says nothing about scale either, because a single asset can be worth more than fifty.
rationale: The label guide names the label and states what is counted at it, which distinguishes this column from the opt-out count on the same row.
evidence_quote: Show the total number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a count column shipped with no statement of what is counted or how it relates to the deduction beside it.

value_domain: Temporary full expensing opt-out code (A, B)
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer chose to opt out of temporary full expensing, and whether for some assets or for all of them. The ATO sets two values at label C of item P11: "A if you are opting out for some of your assets" and "B if you are opting out for all of your assets". Opting out was open only to businesses not using the simplified depreciation rules, and the choice cannot be changed once the return is lodged.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A single letter: A for a partial opt-out and B for a complete one, left blank where no choice was made.
limitation: A blank is not a decision to use the measure: a small business using simplified depreciation was instructed to leave the label empty, and a business with no eligible assets leaves it empty too. The code also does not say which assets were opted out or what was deducted for them instead under the general depreciation rules.
rationale: The label guide gives both code values and their meanings, and states which entities were told to leave the label blank, which is what makes a blank ambiguous.
evidence_quote: Write: * A if you are opting out for some of your assets * B if you are opting out for all of your assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question wording as its description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a two-value coded column shipped with neither code nor an explanation of the blanks.

value_domain: Count of assets opted out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: How many assets the taxpayer opted out of temporary full expensing for, at label D of item P11. The instruction is to "Show the number of assets for which you made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing", so it counts choices rather than the business's assets. It belongs with the opt-out code and the opted-out value on the same row, which together describe one decision.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A whole number of assets for one income year, counted from the opt-out choice made in the return.
limitation: It does not say how large the opted-out assets were, since one expensive asset and ten cheap ones give the same number, and the value column on the same row is needed for that. It also cannot be netted against the count of assets claimed, because an asset falls into one count or the other by choice rather than by eligibility.
rationale: The label guide names the label and states what is counted at it, and the opting out page establishes that the choice is made asset by asset and is irrevocable.
evidence_quote: Show the number of assets for which you made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished this count from the count of assets claimed on the same return.

value_domain: Dollar amount, value of assets opted out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: The value of the assets the taxpayer opted out of temporary full expensing for, measured by the deduction forgone. The ATO defines it at label E of item P11: "The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out." It is therefore a deduction not taken, not a purchase price.
description_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount equal to the temporary full expensing deduction the taxpayer chose not to claim for those assets in that year.
limitation: It is neither capital expenditure nor a deduction: the assets were still written off, only under the general depreciation rules, so the amount overlaps with depreciation claimed in this and later years. Nothing on the row records how much of it came back as ordinary depreciation in the same year.
rationale: The label guide defines the value at this label in terms of the deduction that would otherwise have been claimed, which is the only reading that separates it from asset cost.
evidence_quote: Show the value of the assets for which you made the choice to opt out of temporary full expensing. The value is the amount you would have otherwise claimed for these assets under temporary full expensing if you had not made the choice to opt out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary full expensing - Value of assets you are opting out for' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited a reader to treat a forgone deduction as the cost of the assets.

value_domain: Dollar amount, TFN amounts withheld from employee share scheme discounts
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes
variable_description: Tax an employer withheld from an employee share scheme discount because the employee did not quote a tax file number. The instruction is to "Add up all the TFN amounts withheld from discounts from your Employee share scheme statements" and write the total at label C of item 12. The discount itself is reported at the other item 12 labels, split by whether the scheme is taxed upfront or deferred.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 12 Employee share schemes
value_definition: An annual amount taken from the employee share scheme statements the employer issues, credited against the assessment like any other withholding.
limitation: It is not tax on share scheme income in general: withholding happens only where a TFN or ABN was not quoted, so most employees who receive a discount show zero here while still being taxed on it. A non-zero value marks a records failure rather than a large benefit.
rationale: The item 12 instructions define TFN amounts withheld on share scheme statements and name the label they are written at, which is this column.
evidence_quote: Add up all the TFN amounts withheld from discounts from your Employee share scheme statements . Write the total TFN amounts withheld from discounts at label C .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Employee share schemes tfn amounts withheld from discounts' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount only arises when a TFN was not quoted.

value_domain: Dollar amount, TFN amounts withheld from gross interest
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 10 Gross interest
variable_description: Tax a bank withheld from interest because the account holder did not give a tax file number. The ATO says what to look for on a statement: "TFN amounts are amounts of tax withheld by financial institutions because you didn't give them your TFN or ABN. TFN amounts show on your statement or document as 'Commonwealth tax' or 'TFN withholding tax'." The interest it was taken from is reported gross at label L on the same return.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 10 Gross interest
value_definition: An annual amount reported including cents at label M, summed across accounts and excluding amounts the ATO has already refunded.
limitation: It cannot be used to measure interest income, because withholding happens at a penalty rate and only on accounts where no TFN was quoted. A child's account or a dormant account is the usual source, so a value here signals an unquoted TFN rather than wealth.
rationale: The item 10 instructions define TFN amounts, say where they appear on a bank statement and name the label they are written at, which is this column.
evidence_quote: TFN amounts are amounts of tax withheld by financial institutions because you didn't give them your TFN or ABN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax file number amounts withheld from gross interest' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not explain why the amount exists or that it is reported with cents.

value_domain: Dollar amount, share of credit for TFN amounts withheld inside a partnership or trust
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of credits for tax file number amounts withheld from a partnership's or trust's interest, dividends and unit trust distributions. The withholding happened to the entity, not to the person: the instruction is to write "the total of your share of credits for TFN amounts withheld at question 13 - label R (show cents)". Credit for amounts a closely held trust withheld is a separate label on the same question.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_definition: An annual amount including cents, the taxpayer's proportionate share of amounts withheld from investment income earned inside a partnership or trust.
limitation: It is a credit share, not income: the distributions behind it are reported at other item 13 labels, so it cannot be used to size a person's trust or partnership income. It also pools interest, dividends and unit trust distributions into one figure, so the source of the withheld amount cannot be recovered.
rationale: The item 13 instructions name the label, say what the share covers and separate it from credits for amounts withheld by a closely held trust.
evidence_quote: interest, dividends and unit trust distributions from which TFN amounts are withheld, then write the total of your share of credits for TFN amounts withheld at question 13 - label R (show cents)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long custodian label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the withholding occurred inside the entity or how the column relates to the distribution labels.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, item 19 transfer to a non-resident trust
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
variable_description: A yes or no box at item 19 recording whether the taxpayer transferred property or services to a non-resident trust. The ATO asks it directly - "Do you, at any time, directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of money, property or services to a non-resident trust?" - and the answer goes at label W, with any attributed foreign income from transferor trusts written at label B. The data item list labels this column 'FIF indicator', which belongs to the foreign investment fund questions that shared item 19 before those rules were repealed, so the column name and the custodian's description disagree.
description_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
value_definition: A flag with a yes state, a no state and an unanswered state; the amount attributed under the transferor trust rules is held in a separate column.
limitation: A yes says a transfer happened at some time, not that income was attributed or that any tax followed, and the question reaches back over the taxpayer's whole history rather than the income year. The mismatch with the custodian's 'FIF indicator' wording also means the year's form has to be checked before the column is used, because item 19 carried both questions in the earlier years.
rationale: The item 19 instructions give the transferor trust question, its label and the separate label for attributed income, which matches the variable name; the custodian's description names the other question that shared the item, which is the conflict a reader needs flagged.
evidence_quote: Do you, at any time, directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of money, property or services to a non-resident trust?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'FIF indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, which left the page asserting a foreign investment fund flag for a column named after transfers to a non-resident trust.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at label B, item 19 Foreign entities
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 19 Foreign entities, part B
variable_description: Attributed income from a non-resident trust to which the taxpayer transferred property, money or services, reported at label B of item 19 Foreign entities. The ATO says "The transferor trust measures may apply if, at any time, you directly or indirectly transferred or caused the transfer of property (including money) or services to a non-resident trust", and the taxpayer works out the attributable amount themselves using the Foreign income return form guide. The controlled foreign company amount sits at label K on the same item, so K and B split attributed foreign income by the structure that produced it. Because attribution does not require a distribution, a figure here can appear in a year when the taxpayer received nothing.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 19 Foreign entities, part B
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of attributed foreign income, self-assessed by the taxpayer from the trust's attributable income, with cents dropped. It is gross of nothing on the return itself; any foreign income tax offset is claimed separately at item 20.
limitation: It does not measure money received. Attribution taxes the taxpayer on a share of an offshore trust's income whether or not it was paid out, so this column cannot be read as an overseas cash flow. A zero is also not evidence of no offshore trust: the measures only bite where the taxpayer was the transferor, and a beneficiary with no transfer reports nothing here.
rationale: The DIL label names transferor trust income under foreign entities, which is exactly part B of item 19 on the individual return, and the ATO instruction for that year defines when the measures apply and which label carries the amount.
evidence_quote: The transferor trust measures may apply if, at any time, you directly or indirectly transferred or caused the transfer of property (including money) or services to a non-resident trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Foreign entities transferor trust income', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said that this is attributed income rather than a distribution.

value_domain: Dollar amount at TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS on the individual return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Taxable income or loss
variable_description: The taxpayer's taxable income for the year, or their loss, after tax losses of earlier years are deducted. The ATO builds it in two steps: "Transfer the amount you have shown at SUBTOTAL on page 4 of your tax return to $ TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS", unless earlier-year losses are being deducted, in which case those amounts are taken away from the subtotal first. It is the base for the tax scale, the Medicare levy and most income tests, and it is the figure the ATO assesses. A negative value is a tax loss and carries an L indicator on the paper form.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Taxable income or loss
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount: total income or loss, less total deductions, less any prior-year tax losses claimed at item L1. It runs across every year of the individual return in this asset, 1999-2000 to 2023-24.
limitation: It is not income received. Taxable income is net of deductions the taxpayer chose to claim, so two people with identical earnings differ here by their claiming behaviour, and negative gearing or a business loss can drive it below zero for a high earner. It also excludes reportable fringe benefits, reportable employer super contributions and exempt pensions, which is why the income tests carry their own columns.
rationale: The DIL label is the return's own bottom-line total, and the ATO instruction for the year states which lines feed it and how earlier-year losses are applied.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount you have shown at SUBTOTAL on page 4 of your tax return to $ TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Taxable income or loss' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the figure is net of or that it can be negative.

value_domain: Dollar amount at TOTAL TAX INSTALMENTS DEDUCTED on pre-2006 individual returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
variable_description: Total tax the taxpayer's payers deducted from their income during the year and which is credited against the assessment. On the returns of this era the label reads TOTAL TAX INSTALMENTS DEDUCTED, and TaxPack tells the taxpayer to build it from the deduction column of each income item: "For items 1 to 7 add up all the amounts in the tax instalments deducted column." It is the ancestor of the modern TOTAL TAX WITHHELD line, and it is reported in dollars and cents rather than whole dollars. The column runs 1999-2000 to 2005-06 only, and disappears once the ATO's schema moved to withheld-amount fields.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
value_definition: A dollar-and-cents credit amount, summed by the taxpayer from group certificates and payment summaries across salary and wages, allowances, lump sums, eligible termination payments, government payments and pensions.
limitation: It is a credit claimed, not tax finally borne. The assessment can reduce or refund it, so it says nothing about the taxpayer's tax liability on its own. It is also not comparable to the later withholding columns without care: the pre-2000 tax instalment deduction system and PAYG withholding cover different payment types, and the change happened partway through the column's own life.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 reproduces the individual return for the first year this column covers and names TOTAL TAX INSTALMENTS DEDUCTED as one of the totals the taxpayer must write, with the instruction for building it.
evidence_quote: For items 1 to 7 add up all the amounts in the tax instalments deducted column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Total Tax Instalment Deduction Amount', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving the abbreviation TID unexplained and the pre-PAYG vintage invisible.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax instalment deductions refunded, pre-2006 individual returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
variable_description: The part of a taxpayer's tax instalment deductions that was refunded rather than credited in the assessment, on returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. It sits directly beside TID_AMT, which is the total instalment credit claimed, so the pair separates the credit from the money returned to the taxpayer on account of that credit. TaxPack for this era names the credit total but does not print a matching refund label, which points to the field being an ATO processing amount rather than something the taxpayer wrote on the form. Treat it as an accounting movement on the income tax account for the year.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
value_definition: A dollar-and-cents amount attached to the instalment credit for the same income year, present only in the pre-2006 deductions and offsets tables.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's tax refund. A refund of income tax after assessment is a different quantity and is carried by the assessment balance columns, so summing this field across taxpayers does not give total refunds paid. Because no published label matches it, its exact trigger is unconfirmed, and a zero cannot be read as evidence that nothing was refunded.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 fixes the meaning of the neighbouring instalment deduction total and shows no refund label on the return of the period, which supports the reading that this is an administrative companion field rather than a taxpayer entry. No ATO document naming this field could be found.
evidence_quote: For items 1 to 7 add up all the amounts in the tax instalments deducted column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Tax Instalment Deduction Refunded Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that the field is not a taxpayer refund.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the dependant (invalid and carer) tax offset applied in the assessment
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2015, question T6 Invalid and invalid carer
variable_description: The part of the dependant (invalid and carer) tax offset that was actually used to reduce tax payable, not the amount the taxpayer was entitled to claim. The offset is tightly gated: the ATO requires that the invalid received "a disability support pension under the Social Security Act 1991", a special needs disability support pension, or an invalidity service pension under the Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986. The available amount is carried in a separate column, so the difference between the two shows where a taxpayer's tax liability was too small to absorb the offset. The single dependant (invalid and carer) offset replaced a family of older dependant offsets in 2012-13, and this column runs from 2014-15 to 2023-24.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2015, question T6 Invalid and invalid carer
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-refundable offset amount worked out in the assessment, capped by the taxpayer's tax on taxable income and reduced by the dependant's adjusted taxable income above the threshold.
limitation: A zero here does not mean no caring relationship, and it does not even mean no entitlement: a taxpayer with little or no tax payable has nothing for the offset to reduce, so the used amount falls to zero while the available amount stands. The column is also a poor proxy for disability in the household, because it only counts invalids on the three named pensions and only where the taxpayer maintained them.
rationale: The DIL label names the used component of the dependant (invalid and carer) offset, and the ATO instruction for the item sets out the pension conditions that decide who can claim it at all.
evidence_quote: The invalid must have received one of the following: a disability support pension under the Social Security Act 1991, a special needs disability support pension under the Social Security Act 1991, an invalidity service pension under the Veterans' Entitlement Act 1986.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Dependant (invalid and carer) tax offset - used', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished used from available.

value_domain: Dollar amount in the Total allowances field of a PAYG payment summary
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: payment details
variable_description: Total allowances the employer paid the payee to cover work-related costs, reported by the employer and kept apart from gross payments. The ATO says "Allowances are payments you made to cover your payee's work-related expenses. For example, tool allowances and motor vehicle allowances", and is explicit that "You must show the total amount of all allowances you paid in the Total allowances field. Do not include these amounts in gross payments." Living-away-from-home allowance is excluded because it is not assessable to the payee. The figure is third-party reported, so it is independent of anything the payee later claims as a deduction.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: payment details
value_definition: A dollar total for the payment period on the row, covering every allowance the payer paid that payee, with individual allowance types named separately on the form and collapsed to VARIOUS where there were more than two.
limitation: It is not extra pay on top of the gross figure that a reader can simply add: an allowance is separate from gross payments here but is still assessable to the payee, and some award transport and cents-per-kilometre payments are reported differently again. The column also cannot tell you what the allowance was for once more than two were paid, since the types collapse to a single label, and by 2023-24 most of these rows originate from Single Touch Payroll reporting rather than a paper payment summary.
rationale: The variable sits in a payment summary table beside gross payments, lump sums A to E, tax-free and taxable components, and the ATO's own instruction for that form defines the Total allowances field and its relationship to gross payments.
evidence_quote: You must show the total amount of all allowances you paid in the Total allowances field. Do not include these amounts in gross payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total allowances' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is excluded from gross payments or that it is reported by the employer.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label B, item 12 Employee share schemes
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 12 Employee share schemes, steps 5 and 6
variable_description: The employee share scheme discount that is assessable this year, written at label B of item 12 after the up-to-$1,000 reduction is applied. The ATO defines the underlying quantity plainly: "The discount is the difference between the market value of the ESS interests and the amount you or one of your associates paid to acquire them." Label B is a net total of the four component labels on the same item - taxed-upfront eligible for reduction, taxed-upfront not eligible, deferral schemes and pre-1 July 2009 interests at cessation time - so those columns explain B rather than adding to it. The reduction only applies where the taxpayer's income test total is $180,000 or less.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 12 Employee share schemes, steps 5 and 6
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable amount: the sum of the discount labels D, E, F and G at item 12, less $1,000 where the taxpayer satisfies the income test and label D exceeds $1,000.
limitation: It is not the value of shares received and not a realised gain. A discount is taxed when the interest is acquired or when the deferred taxing point arrives, which can be years before the taxpayer sells anything and can fall in a year when the shares later lose value. Adding this column to the four component columns double counts, because B is their total.
rationale: The DIL label names the total assessable employee share scheme discount, which is label B of item 12, and the ATO instruction gives both the definition of the discount and the arithmetic that produces B.
evidence_quote: The discount is the difference between the market value of the ESS interests and the amount you or one of your associates paid to acquire them.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Employee share schemes total assessable discount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the figure is net of the $1,000 reduction or that it totals the neighbouring labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax credits claimed in the assessment, 2006-07 to 2008-09
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: Total credits for tax already paid that the taxpayer claimed on the return, held for the three income years 2006-07 to 2008-09 only. The ATO describes the assessment as showing "credit you have for tax already paid during the income year" alongside the tax owed on taxable income, and this column is that credit side as claimed rather than as allowed. Credits of this kind include amounts withheld from wages, franking credits, tax file number amounts withheld and credits distributed through partnerships and trusts. Its short life reflects a change in the ATO's own extract structure rather than any change in the return.
description_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
value_definition: A dollar amount aggregating the credit labels on the return for the year, distinct from the tax offsets aggregate carried in the deductions and offsets table for the same three years.
limitation: It cannot be treated as tax paid by the taxpayer. Franking credits are company tax already paid on the taxpayer's behalf, and a credit claimed can be reduced on assessment, so the column mixes withheld tax with imputed tax and states the claim rather than the outcome. Because it exists for only three years, any series built from it breaks at both ends.
rationale: The ATO's notice of assessment page defines the credit side of an individual assessment, which is the quantity this aggregate carries. No ATO document names this specific extract field, so the mapping to particular return labels is inferred from the column's position among the 2006-07 to 2008-09 income and loss fields.
evidence_quote: Your NOA will show the amount of: tax you owe on your taxable income, credit you have for tax already paid during the income year, tax you need to pay or your refund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total credits claimed' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell credits from offsets or know the column lasts three years.

value_domain: Dollar amount at SUBTOTAL on the individual return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Subtotal
variable_description: Total income or loss less total deductions, the line the return prints as SUBTOTAL. The ATO's rule is arithmetic: "take away the amount at TOTAL DEDUCTIONS from the amount at TOTAL INCOME OR LOSS; write the result at SUBTOTAL", and where total income is itself a loss the deductions are added to it instead. It is taxable income before any tax losses of earlier years are deducted at item L1, so it sits one step above TI_OR_LSS_AMT on the same row. Comparing the two isolates how much of a year's taxable income was absorbed by carried-forward losses.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Subtotal
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount, the difference between the return's total income or loss and its total deductions, with a loss indicator on the paper form where it falls below zero.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's assessed taxable income, and using it as such overstates the base for anyone deducting earlier-year losses. It also cannot be compared with total income to measure deduction intensity in a loss year, because the sign convention changes: where total income is negative, deductions are added rather than subtracted.
rationale: The DIL wording, total income or loss less total deductions, is the definition of the SUBTOTAL line, and the ATO instruction for that line states the calculation in both the income and the loss case.
evidence_quote: take away the amount at TOTAL DEDUCTIONS from the amount at TOTAL INCOME OR LOSS; write the result at SUBTOTAL
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Total income or loss less total deductions', and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said this is the SUBTOTAL line sitting above taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax offsets claimed, 2006-07 to 2008-09
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Total tax offsets
variable_description: Total tax offsets the taxpayer claimed, before the ATO worked out how much of them could be used, held for 2006-07 to 2008-09 only. The claimed total is built the way the ATO describes the return's own offsets line, by adding "all the tax offset amounts you claimed" at the individual offset items, with the seniors and pensioner offsets calculated by the ATO rather than written by the taxpayer. It pairs with the used and available offset columns elsewhere in the deductions and offsets table for the same years. Its three-year span reflects the ATO extract structure of that period.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Total tax offsets
value_definition: A dollar aggregate of the non-refundable offset amounts claimed at the tax offset items on the front and supplementary sections of the return for the year.
limitation: A claimed offset is not a tax reduction. Non-refundable offsets are capped by tax payable, so a taxpayer with a large claim and a small liability shows a big number here and gets little benefit, and the used-amount columns rather than this one measure the effect on tax. The column also does not separate refundable from non-refundable offsets.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the total tax offsets line and how a taxpayer builds it, which fixes the family of amounts this aggregate covers. The instruction cited is for 2010-11 while the column covers 2006-07 to 2008-09; no ATO page for the earlier years is published, and no document names this extract field, so the mapping is inferred.
evidence_quote: Add up all the tax offset amounts you claimed at items T1 , T4 , T5 , T6 and T on your tax return. (We work out the amounts at items T2 and T3 automatically.)
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total offsets claimed' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to tell it from the used and available offset columns beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label Y, item 24 Other income (category 1)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019, question 24 Other income
variable_description: Category 1 other income at label Y of item 24, a named list of one-off assessable amounts rather than a residual. The ATO's category 1 list covers "Lump sum payments in arrears except lump sum payments in arrears relating to superannuation income streams", BSWAT lump sums in arrears, foreign exchange gains, lottery and game-show benefits, reimbursements of tax-related or election expenses, assessable balancing adjustments, gains on traditional securities and work-in-progress amounts. This column carries the category 1 total from 2018-19 onwards; the earlier column TOTL_OTHR_INCM_CTGRY_1_AMT carries the same label up to 2017-18. Category 1 exists as a separate label because several of its items attract a lump sum in arrears tax offset.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019, question 24 Other income
value_definition: A whole-dollar total, self-assessed, summing every category 1 amount the taxpayer received. Tax withheld from lump sums in arrears is reported separately at label E of the same item.
limitation: It is a bucket, not a measure of any one thing. A back payment of wages, a game-show prize and a depreciation balancing adjustment all land in the same figure, so it cannot be used to count arrears payments or windfalls without the type description that only exists as free text on the form. It also breaks in series against the 2006-07 to 2017-18 column, since the ATO renumbered the item 24 categories when the FHSS category was added.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the first year of this column lists exactly what category 1 covers and states that the category 1 total goes to label Y of item 24.
evidence_quote: Add up all your category 1 income. Write the total at Y item 24 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other income category 1' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which told a reader nothing about what a category 1 amount is.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label X, item 24 Other income (category 2, ATO interest)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019, question 24 Other income, category 2
variable_description: ATO interest the taxpayer must bring back to income at item 24, reported at label X as category 2. The ATO defines the category in one line, "Remissions of the ATO interest charge that you can claim or have claimed as a deduction". The amount arises when the ATO forgives interest the taxpayer had already deducted at item D10, so it is a reversal of an earlier deduction rather than money received. The ATO-interest category first appears in the instructions for the 2017-18 return, while this column starts in 2015-16, so the first two years are likely to be empty.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019, question 24 Other income, category 2
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of remitted general interest charge, shortfall interest charge and similar amounts that were, or will be, claimed as a deduction.
limitation: It is not interest the taxpayer earned or paid. A figure here means a charge was remitted, so it is a marker of a debt that was forgiven rather than of investment income, and reading it as an interest receipt inverts its meaning. A zero is also uninformative in 2015-16 and 2016-17, where the separate ATO-interest label was not yet in use on the paper return.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines category 2 of item 24 as ATO interest remissions and names label X, matching the custodian's own wording for this column. The instruction is dated 2018-19 while the column begins in 2015-16; the 2015-16 and 2016-17 instructions for the same item list only two categories and carry no ATO-interest label, which is the basis for the coverage note.
evidence_quote: Types of income: Category 2 (ATO interest) Remissions of the ATO interest charge that you can claim or have claimed as a deduction
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Other income - category 2 (ato interest) - total', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could easily read it as interest income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label R, item 24 Other income (category 3)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019 and 2018, question 24 Other income
variable_description: Assessable First Home Super Saver amounts released to the taxpayer, reported as category 3 other income at label R of item 24 from 2018-19. The ATO's category 3 list for that year is one item, "Assessable FHSS released amounts", and the tax withheld from the release goes to label S on the same item. The number therefore identifies people who withdrew voluntary super contributions to buy a first home, the first releases being possible from 1 July 2018. In 2017-18 the same category number carried the item's residual income instead, and in 2015-16 and 2016-17 the ATO ran item 24 with only two categories, so the column changes meaning partway through.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019 and 2018, question 24 Other income
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable amount from 2018-19 onwards, being the released FHSS contributions and associated earnings that are included in assessable income and then reduced by a tax offset.
limitation: The column is not a consistent series. In 2017-18 the ATO's category 3 was the residual bucket, "Any income not described in category 1 or 2", and from 2018-19 it is the FHSS release, while in 2015-16 and 2016-17 the item had no category 3 at all, so a taxpayer-level trend across those boundaries compares different quantities. It also does not measure home purchases: a release can be made and the purchase not proceed.
rationale: The 2018-19 instruction defines category 3 as assessable FHSS released amounts at label R, and the 2017-18 instruction defines category 3 as the residual, which together explain the break in the column's meaning. The 2015-16 and 2016-17 instructions show only two categories, so what the column holds for those two years is inferred rather than published.
evidence_quote: Types of income: Category 3 (FHSS) Assessable FHSS released amounts
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Total other income category 3 amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that the category number was reused for a different amount in 2018-19.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label V, item 24 Other income (category 4, residual)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019, question 24 Other income, category 4
variable_description: Residual other income at label V of item 24 from 2018-19, defined by the ATO as "Any income not described in category 1, 2 or 3". It is the item's catch-all, and the ATO notes that "Category 4 income shown at this item and certain amounts of income from some other items are used to work out whether you have to pay PAYG instalments and, if so, your instalment rate", which gives the label an administrative consequence the other categories do not have. Taxable professional income written at label Z is added into this total unless it was already reported at items 1, 2, 13, 14 or 15. Before 2018-19 the residual sat at the same label V but under a different category number.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2019, question 24 Other income, category 4
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed total covering royalties, taxable scholarships, jury fees, income protection payments, other Centrelink taxable payments and anything else assessable with no item of its own.
limitation: It is the least interpretable income column on the return, because it is defined by exclusion: the same figure can be a scholarship for one taxpayer and an insurance payout for another, and the type description exists only as free text on the form. It also cannot be compared straight against the pre-2018-19 residual column, which carried a different category number and, until 2017-18, also absorbed the ATO interest and FHSS amounts that later moved out.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the first year of this column defines category 4 as the residual, names label V, and states its role in setting PAYG instalments.
evidence_quote: Category 4 income shown at this item and certain amounts of income from some other items are used to work out whether you have to pay PAYG instalments and, if so, your instalment rate.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other income category 4' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the label is a residual or that it drives PAYG instalments.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item D15 Other deductions
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D15 Other deductions
variable_description: Deductions claimed at item D15 for expenses that have no other place on the return, held only for the 2009-10 income year in this asset. The ATO's list for the item includes "election expenses for local, territory, state or federal candidates", income protection, sickness and accident insurance premiums, foreign exchange losses, section 40-880 business capital expenditure not fully claimed, United Medical Protection support payments and expenses incurred in actively seeking paid work while on Newstart or Youth Allowance. Election expenses sit at label E and everything else at label J, so the item is really two claims under one heading. Every other year of the asset carries item D15 under OTHR_DDCTNS_TOTL_AMT, so this column is a one-year renaming rather than a separate field.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D15 Other deductions
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction total for the year, combining the election-expense label and the other-expenses label at item D15.
limitation: One year of data cannot support a trend, and the single-year presence is the main trap: a reader joining this column across the ATO's yearly tables will find it empty for every year but 2009-10, when the deduction itself continued to be claimed under a differently named column. The figure is also a claim rather than an allowed amount, and it does not say which of the item's very mixed expense types produced it.
rationale: The ATO instruction for question D15 lists the expenses the item covers and the two labels that carry them. The instruction cited is for 2010-11 and the column covers 2009-10, one year earlier; the item's content is unchanged between those years.
evidence_quote: You may claim at this item: election expenses for local, territory, state or federal candidates, income protection, sickness and accident insurance premiums, foreign exchange losses
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other deductions' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named item D15 nor flagged that the column exists for one year.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label Y, item 24 Other income (category 1, pre-2018-19 form)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 24 Other income
variable_description: Category 1 other income at label Y of item 24, on the form the ATO ran with just two income categories until 2016-17; this column covers 2006-07 to 2017-18. On this form category 1 is a closed list of one-off amounts: lump sum payments in arrears other than super income stream arrears, jury attendance fees, foreign exchange gains, investment lottery and game-show benefits, reimbursements of tax-related or election expenses, assessable balancing adjustments, traditional securities gains and work-in-progress amounts. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "Add up all your category 1 income and write the total at Y item 24". From 2018-19 the same label is carried by TOTL_OI_CTGRY_1_AMT after the ATO renumbered the categories.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 24 Other income
value_definition: A whole-dollar total, self-assessed, of every category 1 amount received in the year. Tax withheld from any lump sum in arrears within it is reported separately at label E of item 24.
limitation: It cannot separate the kinds of income inside it, so a jury fee and a several-year salary back payment are indistinguishable in the number. Nor can the column be read continuously past 2017-18: the ATO stopped populating it when the item gained the ATO interest and FHSS categories, and a naive join makes the drop look like behaviour rather than a schema change.
rationale: The ATO instruction for a year in the middle of the column's life lists the category 1 income types and names label Y, and the two-category structure it describes held until 2016-17, one year short of the column's 2006-07 to 2017-18 span.
evidence_quote: Add up all your category 1 income and write the total at Y item 24 on page 15 of your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other income category 1' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which is also indistinguishable from the later category 1 column.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label V, item 24 Other income (category 2, pre-2018-19 form)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 24 Other income
variable_description: Category 2 other income at label V of item 24, the item's residual income; the ATO ran item 24 with just two categories until 2016-17, and this column covers 2006-07 to 2017-18. The ATO defines it by exclusion, "Any income not described in category 1", and notes that "Category 2 income shown at this item and certain amounts of income from some other items are used in working out whether you have to pay PAYG instalments and, if so, your instalment rate." It absorbs royalties, taxable scholarships, bonuses from friendly society income bonds, income protection payments and other taxable Centrelink amounts not shown at items 5 or 6. Taxable professional income at label Z is added into this total unless already declared at another item.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 24 Other income
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed residual total for the year, defined as everything assessable at item 24 that does not fall in category 1.
limitation: Its content is not fixed even within its own span: in 2017-18 the ATO gave ATO interest its own category and renumbered the residual to category 3, so the residual at label V quietly narrows in the last year of the series. The column also does not reveal what the income was, since the type description sits in a free-text box on the form and collapses to a schedule reference when more than one type is present.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines category 2 as the residual, names label V and states its role in the PAYG instalment calculation, which is the fact that makes this label different from the other item 24 columns.
evidence_quote: Category 2 income shown at this item and certain amounts of income from some other items are used in working out whether you have to pay PAYG instalments and, if so, your instalment rate.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other income category 2' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the ATO-interest column that carries the same category number in later years.

value_domain: Dollar amount at TOTAL REBATES/TAX OFFSETS on pre-2006 individual returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
variable_description: Total rebates and tax offsets the taxpayer claimed, the line the returns of this era print as TOTAL REBATES/TAX OFFSETS. TaxPack's checklist for the year asks the taxpayer to have "written totals at TOTAL TAX INSTALMENTS DEDUCTED, TOTAL INCOME OR LOSS, TOTAL DEDUCTIONS, SUBTOTAL, TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS and TOTAL REBATES/TAX OFFSETS", which is where this column comes from. Rebate is the older word for what the law now calls a tax offset, and the return of this period used both, which is why the column carries the older name. It runs 1999-2000 to 2005-06 and is replaced from 2006-07 by the total tax offsets columns.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the rebates and offsets claimed at the rebate items of the return, including the beneficiary, pensioner, spouse, dependant and zone rebates of that period.
limitation: A rebate claimed is not tax saved. Most of these rebates were non-refundable and capped by tax payable, so a taxpayer with little liability shows a claim here and no benefit. The column is also not continuous with the later offsets columns, because several of the era's rebates, including the pensioner and low income aged person rebates, were later restructured or abolished.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 covers the first year of this column and names TOTAL REBATES/TAX OFFSETS as a return total the taxpayer must write, which fixes the label the column carries.
evidence_quote: written totals at TOTAL TAX INSTALMENTS DEDUCTED, TOTAL INCOME OR LOSS, TOTAL DEDUCTIONS, SUBTOTAL, TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS and TOTAL REBATES/TAX OFFSETS
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Total Rebates Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never explained that rebate is the period's term for a tax offset.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label U, TOTAL TAX OFFSETS on the individual return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Total tax offsets
variable_description: Total non-refundable tax offsets on the front section of the return, at label U, held for 2006-07 to 2008-09. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to add up the offsets claimed at the individual T items and to "Write the total amount at U TOTAL TAX OFFSETS on page 5 of your tax return", while noting that some offsets, including the seniors and pensioner offsets, are worked out by the ATO rather than by the taxpayer. Offsets claimed in the supplementary section are totalled separately and brought across, so this line is not the taxpayer's whole offset position on its own. TAX_OFSTS_TOTL_AMT carries the same line for the whole 2006-07 to 2023-24 span, so for these three years the two columns sit side by side.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, Total tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the non-refundable offsets claimed at the front-section tax offset items, part self-assessed by the taxpayer and part calculated by the ATO.
limitation: It is a total of claims, not of benefits: non-refundable offsets can only reduce tax to zero, so this figure overstates what a low-liability taxpayer actually received. Because the column is limited to 2006-07 to 2008-09, an apparent series break at either end reflects the ATO extract structure and not a change in the offsets themselves.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the TOTAL TAX OFFSETS line, names label U and says which offsets the ATO calculates. The instruction is for 2010-11 while the column covers 2006-07 to 2008-09; the line and its label are unchanged across those years, but no ATO page for the earlier years is published.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount at U TOTAL TAX OFFSETS on page 5 of your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total tax offsets' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the offsets are non-refundable or that supplementary offsets are totalled elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount in the Taxable component field of a lump sum payment summary
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - superannuation lump sum, How to complete the form
variable_description: The taxable component of a lump sum payment summary, reported by the paying fund or employer. The ATO defines it exactly: "The taxable component is the total of the payment, less the tax-free component. This amount is assessable income." For a super lump sum the taxable component splits into a taxed element and an untaxed element, and the ATO tells payers "Do not show taxed element amounts paid to people when they have turned 60. Show the untaxed element in all cases". The tax-free component sits in its own column on the same row, and the payment summary type column says which form the row came from.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - superannuation lump sum, How to complete the form
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, third-party reported, being the payment less its tax-free component. Cents are dropped, so a payment of $122.76 is reported as $122.
limitation: It is not the size of the lump sum. Adding it to the tax-free component recovers the payment only where the payee was under 60, because a taxed element paid after age 60 is left off the form entirely, so a large withdrawal by an older member can show a small taxable component or none. It also says nothing about the tax paid, which is carried by the withheld column.
rationale: The payment summary table carries a tax-free component beside this taxable component, together with lump sum A, B, D and E fields and a payment summary type, which identifies it as a lump sum payment summary field. The ATO's instruction for the superannuation lump sum form defines the taxable component and the age-60 reporting rule.
evidence_quote: The taxable component is the total of the payment, less the tax-free component. This amount is assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Taxable component' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the component is taxable relative to or that amounts drop out at age 60.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label H, item D12 Personal superannuation contributions
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2018, question D12 Personal superannuation contributions
variable_description: Personal super contributions the taxpayer claimed as a deduction at label H of item D12, not contributions the employer made. The eligible population widened sharply in 2017-18: the ATO says "Previously, only those who earned less than 10% of their total income as an employee were eligible to claim this deduction" and that "This 10% rule has been removed which means most Australians under 75 years old can claim an income tax deduction for after-tax personal super contributions". A deduction is only allowed where the taxpayer gave their fund a valid notice of intent and the fund acknowledged it. The column runs the full span of the asset, 1999-2000 to 2023-24, which makes the 2017-18 rule change the single most important thing about it.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2018, question D12 Personal superannuation contributions
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction for after-tax contributions the taxpayer made to a complying fund or retirement savings account in the year, limited by age rules and by the amount notified to the fund.
limitation: It measures a deduction claimed, not contributions made. A taxpayer who contributed but did not lodge a notice of intent, or who left the contribution to attract the government co-contribution instead, shows zero here while having contributed. The pre-2017-18 and post-2017-18 figures are also not comparable, because the removal of the maximum earnings condition changed who could claim rather than who could contribute.
rationale: The ATO instruction names label H of item D12 as the deduction for personal super contributions and states the maximum earnings condition and its removal, which is the discontinuity a user of a 27-year series needs to know about.
evidence_quote: Previously, only those who earned less than 10% of their total income as an employee were eligible to claim this deduction.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Personal superannuation contributions' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could mistake it for a contributions total and would not know the eligibility rule changed in 2017-18.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label F, item P14 Trade creditors
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P13 and P14 Trade debtors and creditors
variable_description: What the sole trader's business owed its suppliers at the end of the year, reported at label F of item P14 on the business and professional items schedule. The ATO defines it as "the total amount owed by the business at the end of the year for goods and services received", that is, current trade and other creditors. Where the taxpayer runs more than one business the schedule requires a single combined figure. It is a balance sheet position at one instant, not a flow, which sets it apart from every expense column on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P13 and P14 Trade debtors and creditors
value_definition: A whole-dollar closing balance of current trade and other creditors, self-assessed, summed across all of the taxpayer's businesses.
limitation: It is not a debt total for the person. Only trade payables of the business are in scope, so business loans, tax debts and personal borrowings are absent, and a leveraged sole trader can report zero. Because the figure is a point-in-time balance, comparing it with the year's purchases or expenses to infer payment terms will mislead for any seasonal business.
rationale: The DIL label is item P14 on the individual business and professional items schedule, and the ATO's instruction for that item gives the definition and the label letter.
evidence_quote: This is the total amount owed by the business at the end of the year for goods and services received during 2021-22 (that is, current trade and other creditors).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Trade creditors' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said this is a closing balance limited to trade payables.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label E, item P13 Trade debtors
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P13 and P14 Trade debtors and creditors
variable_description: What customers owed the sole trader's business at the end of the year, reported at label E of item P13 on the business and professional items schedule. The ATO defines it as "the total amount owing to the business at the end of the year for goods and services provided", that is, current trade and other debtors. It is the mirror of the trade creditors label on the same schedule, and like it, a taxpayer with several businesses adds them together into one figure. Reported gross, with no allowance for doubtful debts deducted at this label.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P13 and P14 Trade debtors and creditors
value_definition: A whole-dollar closing balance of current trade and other debtors, self-assessed, summed across all of the taxpayer's businesses.
limitation: It cannot be used to measure recoverable income. Bad debts are written off through a separate deduction label rather than netted here, so the balance includes amounts the business will never collect, and a business on a cash basis for accounting purposes may still report a debtor position that never becomes income. A zero simply means no receivables at 30 June, which is common for cash-settled trades.
rationale: The DIL label is item P13 on the individual business and professional items schedule, and the ATO's instruction for that item gives the definition and the label letter.
evidence_quote: This is the total amount owing to the business at the end of the year for goods and services provided during 2021-22 (that is, current trade and other debtors).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Trade debtors' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is a year-end balance nor how it relates to bad debts.

value_domain: Trading stock election flag at label P, item P21
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P21 Trading stock election
variable_description: A flag that the taxpayer valued closing trading stock below every standard method and therefore had to notify the Commissioner, at label P of item P21. The ATO's rule is narrow: "If you have valued trading stock on hand at the end of 2021-22 at an amount that is less than the lowest amount available using one of the valuation methods at Closing stock , you must notify the Commissioner." Where the notification is required the taxpayer enters Y, and otherwise the label is left blank. It sits in the context table beside the closing stock action code and the closing stock total, which are the amounts the election bears on.
description_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, P21 Trading stock election
value_definition: A one-character flag, Y where the taxpayer made a trading stock election and blank otherwise, so the field is effectively present-or-absent rather than yes-or-no.
limitation: It does not say what the stock was written down to, or why. Obsolescence, damage and special circumstances all produce the same Y, and the amount of the write-down has to be read from the closing stock columns. A blank is also ambiguous in a way a No is not, because it covers both a taxpayer who made no election and a taxpayer with no trading stock at all.
rationale: The DIL label is item P21 on the individual business and professional items schedule, and the ATO's instruction for that item states the notification test and how the label is completed.
evidence_quote: If you have valued trading stock on hand at the end of 2021-22 at an amount that is less than the lowest amount available using one of the valuation methods at Closing stock , you must notify the Commissioner.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Trading stock election' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the flag is set by a below-market valuation nor that blank is the usual value.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label V, item IT4 Target foreign income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question IT4 Target foreign income
variable_description: Overseas income that never reaches taxable income, declared at label V of item IT4 so that the income tests can pick it up. The ATO defines target foreign income as "any income earned, derived or received from sources outside Australia", plus periodical gifts or allowances from an overseas source, "provided that the amount has not been included in your taxable income, or received in the form of a fringe benefit". Its examples are regular money from relatives living overseas, exempt income from foreign business interests, and foreign income received while a temporary resident. Exempt foreign employment income shown at item 20 forms part of it, so the two columns overlap by design.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question IT4 Target foreign income
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed amount converted to Australian dollars, covering foreign-sourced income and periodical gifts that are outside taxable income for the year.
limitation: It is not a measure of foreign income. Anything taxed here in Australia is deliberately excluded, so a taxpayer with large but assessable overseas earnings reports nothing at this label, and the column understates offshore income by exactly the part the tax system already sees. Underreporting also has no direct tax cost to the taxpayer, since the amount only affects income-tested entitlements.
rationale: The DIL label is item IT4 of the income tests section, and the ATO instruction for that item gives the definition of target foreign income, the label letter and the overlap with exempt foreign employment income.
evidence_quote: Target foreign income is: any income earned, derived or received from sources outside Australia, a periodical payment by way of gifts or allowances from a source outside Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Target foreign income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is defined by its absence from taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount, share of trust net small business income at item 13
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2016, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part E
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of a trust's net small business income, used only to work out the small business income tax offset. The ATO is explicit that the amount does not add to income: "Amounts you show at this item are not included in your income, they are only used for the purpose of working out your small business income tax offset." The share is taken from the trustee's statement of distribution and is then reduced by any deductions attributable to it and by deductible farm management deposits. A partnership share is reported separately, so the two together make up the offset base. The column starts in 2015-16 with the offset itself.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2016, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part E
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, self-assessed from the trust's advice, being the share of net small business income less attributable deductions. A trust that made an overall loss gives a share of zero.
limitation: Adding it to the taxpayer's income columns double counts, because the same trust distribution is already inside the share of trust net income at item 13. The column also does not identify the offset received: the small business income tax offset is a percentage of tax on this base and is capped, so a large share here can produce a small offset.
rationale: The DIL label names the trust share of net small business income, which is part E of item 13 from 2015-16, and the ATO instruction states what the amount is for and that it is not included in income.
evidence_quote: Amounts you show at this item are not included in your income, they are only used for the purpose of working out your small business income tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Trust share of net small business income', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would naturally have added it to income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label U, item 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part B
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of a trust's non-primary production net income or loss, at label U of item 13, with capital gains and foreign income stripped out. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "Write at U the total of your share of non-primary production trust net income or loss" and then to exclude net capital gains, attributed foreign income and other foreign source income, which are reported at items 18, 19 and 20 instead. The share of any credits distributed with that income is included in the amount at U and then also shown at the credit labels of the same item.
