Where the trust made an overall tax loss the loss stays in the trust and the taxpayer has no share.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part B
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount, self-assessed from the trustee's statement of distribution, being the beneficiary's share of the trust's net income for tax purposes other than primary production, capital gains and foreign income.
limitation: It is not money received. A present entitlement at 30 June is enough to require the share to be declared even if the trust pays nothing until the following year, so the column measures entitlement rather than cash. It is also not the whole trust story for a taxpayer, because the capital gains and foreign components of the same distribution sit at other items entirely.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the return's own wording for label U at item 13, and the ATO instruction states which components are excluded and where they go instead.
evidence_quote: Write at U the total of your share of non-primary production trust net income or loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said where the excluded components are reported or that entitlement rather than payment triggers it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label L, item 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part B
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of a trust's primary production net income or loss, at label L of item 13. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "Write the total of your share of primary production trust net income or loss at L item 13 on your tax return", and explains that the trustee's statement separates primary from non-primary production because "This information is needed for averaging purposes". The split matters for the taxpayer because primary production income feeds the income averaging calculation and the farm management deposit rules. The corresponding partnership share is at label N on the same item.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part B
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount, self-assessed from the trustee's statement of distribution, being the beneficiary's share of the trust's primary production net income for tax purposes, with a loss indicator on the paper form.
limitation: It does not identify farmers. A discretionary trust can distribute primary production income to a beneficiary with no involvement in the farm, so the column marks an entitlement to farm income rather than an occupation. It also cannot be added to the non-primary production share to get total trust income without checking the capital gains and foreign income items, which carry the rest of the same distribution.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the return's own wording for label L at item 13, and the ATO instruction gives the label and the reason the primary production split exists.
evidence_quote: Your statement of distribution or advice from the trust should show separately your share of primary production and non-primary production income ... This information is needed for averaging purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Distribution from trusts primary production', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said why the primary production split is on the form.

value_domain: Dollar amount of outstanding Trade Support Loan debt at assessment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
variable_description: The Trade Support Loan debt still outstanding after this year's compulsory repayment, for apprentices who borrowed under the scheme. The ATO describes the programme as one where "eligible Australian apprentices are offered loans over a 4-year period" and notes that "A 20% discount will be granted where an Australian Apprentice successfully completes their apprenticeship", so the balance can fall through completion as well as through repayment. The scheme has since been renamed the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan. On the same row the repayable debt and the compulsory repayment due columns give the amounts the assessment acted on, while this column gives what remains.
description_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Types of loans
value_definition: A whole-dollar accumulated debt balance carried by the ATO for the taxpayer, indexed annually and reduced by compulsory repayments raised through the assessment and by voluntary repayments.
limitation: It is not the amount borrowed. Indexation raises the balance and the completion discount cuts it, so the figure diverges from cumulative loan payments in both directions and cannot be used to estimate what an apprentice drew down. A zero also does not distinguish an apprentice who never borrowed from one who has repaid in full.
rationale: The ATO's page on loan types defines the Trade Support Loan scheme, its four-year structure and the completion discount, which are the mechanics behind the balance. The page describes the scheme rather than this specific assessment field, so the reading of outstanding against repayable is taken from the neighbouring columns in the withholding and debt table.
evidence_quote: Generally, under the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan (AASL) - previously known as Trade Support Loan (TSL) - program, eligible Australian apprentices are offered loans over a 4-year period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Trade Support Loan Outstanding Repayable Debt', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained TSL or how the balance moves.

value_domain: Dollar and cents credit at label P, item 13 Partnerships and trusts
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part E
variable_description: The taxpayer's share of a credit for tax withheld from partnership or trust income because no Australian business number was quoted, at label P of item 13. The ATO's condition is that the distribution shown at labels N, L, O or U includes or is attributable to "income from which an amount of tax was withheld because an Australian business number was not quoted; write your share of the distributed credit at P item 13 (show cents)". Withholding where no ABN is quoted is at the top marginal rate, so the credit is large relative to the income behind it. It is one of seven credit and tax offset labels at item 13 in that year, each carrying a different kind of distributed credit.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 13 Partnerships and trusts, part E
value_definition: A dollar-and-cents credit amount, self-assessed from the partnership or trust statement, being the taxpayer's proportionate share of tax withheld from the entity's income under the no-ABN withholding rules.
limitation: It says nothing about the taxpayer's own ABN status. The failure to quote was the entity's or its customer's, not the individual's, so this column cannot be used to identify unregistered contractors. Nor does it stand alone as a withholding measure: the taxpayer's directly earned no-ABN withholding is reported at a different label in the business items.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of credit for tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, and the ATO instruction for part E of item 13 gives the condition, the label letter and the cents requirement.
evidence_quote: income from which an amount of tax was withheld because an Australian business number was not quoted; write your share of the distributed credit at P item 13 (show cents)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said whose failure to quote produced the withholding or that the field carries cents.

value_domain: Dollar and cents tax withheld at item 7, Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: Tax the fund or annuity provider withheld from the taxpayer's superannuation income stream and annuity payments, totalled at item 7. The ATO's step is a simple aggregation: "Add up the tax withheld amounts on your payment summaries for your superannuation income streams and annuities. Write the total in the left column under Tax withheld at item 7 on your tax return." It is third-party reported and pre-filled from payment summaries, so it is one of the more reliable numbers on the return. The income it relates to sits in the taxed element, untaxed element and lump sum in arrears columns of the same item.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
value_definition: A dollar-and-cents credit amount for the year, summed across every superannuation income stream and annuity payment summary the taxpayer received.
limitation: It is not a tax rate on pension income. A person over 60 drawing a taxed-element pension has nothing withheld even though they receive a large income stream, so a zero here is common among retirees and does not mean the income stream was small. The withheld amount also cannot be attributed to a particular fund, because the item carries one total.
rationale: The DIL label names tax withheld on Australian annuities and superannuation income streams, which is the tax withheld column of item 7, and the ATO instruction gives the aggregation step and the source documents.
evidence_quote: Add up the tax withheld amounts on your payment summaries for your superannuation income streams and annuities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is third-party reported or why it is so often zero.

value_domain: Date the ATO finished processing the return
value_source: ATO, Status of your tax return
variable_description: The day the ATO finished processing the return, which is when the assessment issues rather than when the taxpayer lodged. The ATO's own status wording for that point is "We've completed processing your tax return and your notice of assessment has issued". Processing usually takes about two weeks for an electronically lodged return, and longer where the return is under review, amended, or lodged with several years at once. It sits in the context table beside the lodgment source and the amendment code, which say how the return arrived and whether the row is an original or a later version of the assessment.
description_source: ATO, Status of your tax return
value_definition: A calendar date on the ATO's income tax account for the taxpayer and income year, falling after lodgment and on or about the notice of assessment date.
limitation: It is not a lodgment date and should never be used as one. The gap between lodging and processing varies from days to months with review activity and lodgment method, so ordering taxpayers by this date ranks them partly by how much scrutiny they attracted. Where a row is an amendment it records the processing of that amendment, not of the original return, so a late date can belong to an early lodger.
rationale: The ATO's status page defines what completed processing means and gives the usual timeframes, which fixes the event the date records. No ATO or ABS document names this extract field, so the mapping of the column to the assessment-issue event is inferred from the field name and its neighbours in the context table.
evidence_quote: Issued - Dollar amount/ Nil: We've completed processing your tax return and your notice of assessment has issued.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Processed date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited exactly the mistake of reading it as the lodgment date.

value_domain: Dollar amount of taxable income calculated in the assessment, pre-2006 returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
variable_description: Taxable income as calculated for the assessment on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. TaxPack for the period lists the totals the taxpayer must write, among them "TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS", and this column is the version the ATO carried into the assessment after processing. It sits on the same row as TI_OR_LSS_AMT, which is the taxpayer's own figure, so the pair shows where the ATO's calculation departed from the return as lodged. This column ends in 2005-06, while TI_OR_LSS_AMT runs on to 2023-24, so the two sit side by side only in the early years.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of taxable income for the income year as computed in the assessment, after total deductions and any earlier-year tax losses.
limitation: It is not necessarily the same number as the taxpayer wrote, and that is the point of having both columns: a difference marks an ATO adjustment rather than a data error, so treating the two as duplicates hides the adjustments. It also cannot be compared straight with the taxable income column for later years, because the calculated and declared distinction disappears from the schema after 2005-06.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 fixes what taxable income means on the returns of this period and names the return line the column corresponds to. Whether the calculated column reflects assessment adjustments or is simply a derived copy is inferred from its coexistence with the declared column, not from a published statement.
evidence_quote: TAXABLE INCOME OR LOSS
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Taxable Income Calculated Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained what calculated adds over the declared column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label Z, item 24 Other income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 24 Other income, step 3
variable_description: Taxable professional income of a special professional, written at label Z of item 24 so the ATO can average it. The ATO's instruction is direct: "If you are a special professional, write the taxable professional income you received at Z item 24 . Do not show cents. We take this amount into account for income averaging." A special professional is an author of a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work, an inventor, a performing artist, a production associate or an active sportsperson. The amount may already be reported at items 1, 2, 13, 14 or 15, and the return warns that showing it at Z does not tax it twice.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question 24 Other income, step 3
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed amount identifying the professional-income part of the taxpayer's assessable income, used to set the averaging concession rather than to add income.
limitation: Adding it to income totals double counts, because the same earnings are already reported at the salary, business, partnership or personal services items. It is also a marker of a claim rather than of an occupation: an eligible professional who does not seek averaging leaves it blank, so the column undercounts artists and sportspeople.
rationale: The DIL label names taxable professional income under other income, which is label Z of item 24, and the ATO instruction states its purpose in the averaging calculation and its overlap with other items.
evidence_quote: If you are a special professional, write the taxable professional income you received at Z item 24 . Do not show cents. We take this amount into account for income averaging.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Other income taxable professional income', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the amount is a duplicate of income reported elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount of salary and wages carried into the assessment, pre-2006 returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000, item 1
variable_description: The salary and wages figure taken into the assessment on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. On the returns of this period item 1 gives five employer rows, each with a tax instalments deducted column and an income column at labels C to G, and the taxpayer totals them; a separate salary or wages column, GRS_PMT_TOTL_CALCD_AMT, sits beside it. Allowances, tips and directors' fees are a separate item, so neither column includes them. This column ends in 2005-06, while the salary or wages column resumes in 2009-10, so only the early years carry both.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), tax return for individuals 1999-2000, item 1
value_definition: A whole-dollar salary and wages amount for the income year, held alongside the declared salary or wages total in the same table.
limitation: Whether it is gross salary or a figure net of work-related deductions is not stated in any published ATO document, so it cannot be used interchangeably with the later gross payment columns without checking against the salary or wages column on the same row. Either way it excludes allowances, tips, directors' fees and lump sum payments, which have their own items, so it understates employment income.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 and the accompanying return form for the first year of the column show how salary and wages were reported in the period, including the five employer rows and the separate allowances item. No ATO document names this field or says what makes it taxable as distinct from the salary or wages column beside it, so the reading is inferred.
evidence_quote: 1 Salary or wages ... Name of employer | Tax instalments deducted-show cents | Income-do not show cents
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Taxable Salary and Wages Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that a separate salary or wages column sits beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label J, item A1 Under 18
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question A1 Under 18
variable_description: The excepted net income of a taxpayer who was under 18 at 30 June, at label J of item A1, being the part of a minor's income that is taxed at ordinary rates. The ATO tells the minor to add up employment income, Centrelink and veterans' payments, compensation, superannuation and pension fund benefits, income from a deceased estate, income from their own business or an active partnership, and income from property transferred on a death or family breakdown, then to "Take away the total of those deductions from the total income you worked out at step 2". Everything else a minor receives, chiefly investment and trust income, is taxed at penalty rates. Where the minor is an excepted person the label carries zero and the type code carries A.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question A1 Under 18
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, self-assessed, being excepted income less the deductions attributable to it. It is written as zero, not left blank, when the minor has no excepted income.
limitation: A zero is ambiguous in a way the amount alone cannot resolve. It appears both for a minor whose whole income is at penalty rates and for an excepted person whose entire income is taxed normally, and only the type code on the same row separates the two. The column also tells you nothing about the size of the minor's other income, which is the part the penalty rates are aimed at.
rationale: The DIL label names under 18 income, which is item A1 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction sets out the income types that qualify, the deduction step and the zero-and-code-A treatment.
evidence_quote: Write the amount from step 3 at J item A1 . This amount is taxed at normal rates. If you do not have any of the income listed at step 2 or the amount from step 3 is nil, write 0 at J item A1 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Under 18 income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would take it for a minor's total income rather than the excepted part.

value_domain: Type code at item A1 Under 18 (A or M)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question A1 Under 18, steps 1 and 5
variable_description: A one-letter code saying why a minor's income escapes the penalty rates that otherwise apply to unearned income. Code A marks an excepted person, for whom "all your income will be taxed at normal rates": someone working full time or intending to, a disability support or rehabilitation pensioner, a person who is permanently blind or has a lasting disability, a double orphan, or a minor unable to work full time because of a permanent disability and with little family support. Code M marks a minor who is not excepted and whose excepted income amount is written at label J instead. The code is what makes the amount column readable, since both cases can show zero.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question A1 Under 18, steps 1 and 5
value_definition: A single character, A or M, printed in the TYPE box beside label J at item A1, present only where the taxpayer was under 18 at the end of the income year.
limitation: It is not a disability or employment indicator. Code A collects six quite different circumstances into one letter, so a full-time working teenager and a minor on a disability support pension are indistinguishable, and code M covers everyone else including minors with substantial earned income. A missing code means the taxpayer was 18 or older, not that the question was skipped.
rationale: The DIL label names the under 18 income type, and the ATO instruction for item A1 lists the excepted categories, gives code A for them and code M otherwise, and ties both to label J.
evidence_quote: If you were in any of the above categories on 30 June 2011, all your income will be taxed at normal rates. Write 0 at J item A1 . Then print the code letter A in the TYPE box at the right of J .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Under 18 income type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the two codes and their meanings were nowhere on the page.

value_domain: not specified
variable_description: A code box on the 1999-2000 return relating to unemployment and sickness benefits, whose meaning the ATO has not published. It appears in one return context table only, beside AGE_PNSN_ACTN_CD and SUPER_CONTRB_ACTN_CD, which are both code letter boxes on rebate items. Sickness allowance and Newstart allowance were declared at question 5 of TaxPack 2000, an item with no code box of its own, and the beneficiary rebate on those payments was worked out by the ATO rather than claimed by the taxpayer. No documented letter list therefore exists for this column.

value_definition: No code list is published for this column. Its neighbours are single letter code boxes, so a short alphabetic value is likely, but neither the letters nor their meanings can be sourced.

rationale: 'Unemployment and sickness benefits' is a legacy ATO item name; in 1999-2000, the only year the field exists, the corresponding return item (item 5, government allowances including sickness allowance) has no code box and the beneficiary rebate is calculated by the ATO, so no domain can be defended.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label A, item 5 Australian Government allowances and payments, pre-2006 returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), question 5
variable_description: Taxable Australian Government allowances the taxpayer received, reported at label A of item 5 on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. TaxPack's list for the item runs to Newstart allowance, youth allowance, sickness allowance, special benefit, partner allowance, widow allowance, austudy payment, mature age allowance, additional parenting payment (partnered), exceptional circumstances relief payment, ABSTUDY living allowance and other taxable Commonwealth education or training payments. Age and service pensions are a different item, so this column is the allowance side of the payment system rather than the pension side. The beneficiary rebate worksheet in the same publication points back to it as "Total amount of allowance or payment you received-from A item 5 on your tax return". The column's name survives from the older unemployment and sickness benefit terminology.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), question 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of taxable allowance income for the year, taken from Centrelink group certificates or payment summaries and totalled by the taxpayer at one label.
limitation: Exempt payments are missing entirely, so the column is not a measure of income support received: a taxpayer whose payment was exempt, or who did not have to lodge, shows nothing. It also cannot separate the payment types inside it, so unemployment, study and caring payments are one figure, and the amount is annual so it says nothing about how many fortnights were paid.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 covers the first year of this column and sets out exactly which Commonwealth allowances go at question 5, and the beneficiary rebate worksheet in the same publication refers to "the total amount of allowance or payment you received-from A item 5 on your tax return", which fixes the label.
evidence_quote: Total amount of allowance or payment you received-from A item 5 on your tax return
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Unemployment Sickness Benefit Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the label covers the whole family of Commonwealth allowances.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the beneficiary rebate worked out in the assessment, pre-2006 returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), Beneficiary rebate worksheet
variable_description: The beneficiary rebate the ATO worked out on the taxpayer's Australian Government allowances, held on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. TaxPack sets out the calculation from the allowance amount at label A of item 5, taking the tax-free threshold off it and applying 20 per cent, with an extra 14 per cent above a higher threshold, and is explicit that the taxpayer does not enter it: "Do not write your rebate anywhere on your tax return." The rebate exists so that a person living on allowance income pays no tax on it. It is therefore a derived amount on the same row as the allowance that generated it.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), Beneficiary rebate worksheet
value_definition: A dollar amount computed by the ATO as a function of the allowance amount at item 5 and the taxpayer's tax-free threshold, not a taxpayer entry.
limitation: It is not evidence of anything the taxpayer claimed, so it should not be read as take-up of a concession. As a non-refundable rebate it is also capped by tax payable, which means a taxpayer on allowances alone can show a rebate that exceeds the tax it could ever offset. Movements in this column track the allowance amount and the threshold rules rather than any change in behaviour.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 prints the beneficiary rebate worksheet, its dependence on the item 5 amount, and the instruction that the taxpayer does not write it on the return, which identifies this column as an ATO-calculated companion to the allowance column.
evidence_quote: Do not write your rebate anywhere on your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Unemployment Sickness Benefit Rebate Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no sign that the figure is calculated by the ATO rather than claimed.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item A4 Working holiday maker net income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2018, question A4 Working holiday maker net income
variable_description: Income earned on a 417 or 462 working holiday visa less the deductions relating to it, the slice of a taxpayer's income taxed at the working holiday maker rate. The ATO defines it as "the income you earned or derived while you were on a 417 or 462 working holiday visa, less deductions relating to earning that income", and notes that "The first $37,000 of your working holiday maker net income is taxed at 15%. All other income is taxed according to your residency status." Employers flag the income with payment type H on the payment summary, which is how a taxpayer identifies it. The rate applied only from 1 January 2017, so the column's first year, 2015-16, precedes the measure and 2016-17 covers 1 January to 30 June 2017 alone.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2018, question A4 Working holiday maker net income
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, self-assessed, floored at zero: gross working holiday maker income from all sources less the related deductions at items D1 to D10.
limitation: It does not identify everyone who held a working holiday visa. Only income earned while on the visa counts, so a person who transitioned to another visa mid-year reports part of their earnings here and part in the ordinary items, and someone on the visa who did not work reports nothing. Because the column is net of deductions it also cannot be used as a wages measure.
rationale: The DIL label names working holiday maker net income, which is item A4 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction gives the definition, the calculation and the rate that attaches to it.
evidence_quote: Your working holiday maker net income is the income you earned or derived while you were on a 417 or 462 working holiday visa, less deductions relating to earning that income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Working holiday maker net income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is net of deductions or that the measure only starts partway through 2016-17.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label A, item D1 Work related car expenses
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses
variable_description: The deduction claimed at label A of item D1 for using the taxpayer's own car for work. The claim is a modelled figure rather than an expense record, because the ATO lets the taxpayer choose the calculation: "If you have more than one car and you are claiming expenses under different methods, add the amounts you work out under each method and write the total at item D1 on your tax return." The claim type column on the same row says which method produced the largest amount and was therefore coded. The methods were cut from four to two in 2015-16, when only the cents per kilometre and logbook methods survived, which puts a structural break in the middle of the series.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction for the income year, totalled across cars and across calculation methods where more than one was used.
limitation: It is not the cost of running a car for work. Under the cents per kilometre and 12 per cent of original value methods the claim is a formula output that needs no receipts, so identical work travel can produce very different claims, and the 2015-16 change in available methods shifts the distribution independently of behaviour. It is also a claim, not an allowed amount, and includes claims later denied on review.
rationale: The DIL label is item D1 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction sets out the four calculation methods, the total at label A and the rule for combining methods.
evidence_quote: If you have more than one car and you are claiming expenses under different methods, add the amounts you work out under each method and write the total at item D1 on your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related car expenses' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is method-dependent or that the methods changed in 2015-16.

value_domain: Claim type code at item D1 (S, T, O or B)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses, methods 1 to 4
variable_description: The method the taxpayer used to work out the item D1 car deduction, printed in the CLAIM TYPE box beside label A. Four codes were available on returns of this period: S for cents per kilometre, T for 12 per cent of original value, O for one-third of actual expenses and B for the logbook method. Where more than one car and method are involved the ATO says to "Print the code letter for the method that gave you the largest amount in the CLAIM TYPE box", so the code describes the dominant method, not every method used. From 2015-16 only the cents per kilometre and logbook methods remain, so T and O disappear from later years.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses, methods 1 to 4
value_definition: A single character in the claim type box at item D1, present only where a car expense deduction was claimed.
limitation: It does not partition the dollar amount beside it. A taxpayer using two methods across two cars reports one code and one combined total, so the code cannot be used to split the claim by method. The available code set also shrinks in 2015-16, which means a fall in the share coded T or O between 2014-15 and 2015-16 records the abolition of those methods and not a change in taxpayer choice.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item D1 sets out each of the four methods and the code letter to print for it, and states the rule that decides which code applies when methods are mixed.
evidence_quote: Print the code letter for the method that gave you the largest amount in the CLAIM TYPE box beside the amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related car expenses - claim type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the four codes were undocumented.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label C, item D3 Work related clothing expenses
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3 Work-related clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning expenses
variable_description: The deduction claimed at label C of item D3 for work clothing and its laundry and dry-cleaning. Only four kinds of clothing qualify, named by the claim type column on the same row, and conventional clothing is excluded no matter how strictly an employer requires it. Substantiation is light at the bottom of the range: the ATO allows a taxpayer who launders at home to "use a reasonable basis to calculate the amount, such as $1 per load for work-related clothing, or 50 cents per load if other laundry items were included", and written evidence for laundry is needed only where the laundry claim is above $150 and the total work expense claim is above $300. Protective footwear and clothing come here, while other protective items such as hard hats and sunscreen are claimed at item D5.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3 Work-related clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction combining the cost of eligible work clothing with laundry and dry-cleaning costs for the year.
limitation: It is not a record of spending. The laundry component is routinely estimated at a per-load rate, with no receipts required while the laundry claim stays under $150, so a large part of the mass of small claims is formula-driven, and the column cannot separate the clothing purchase from the washing. It also does not identify uniformed occupations, because occupation-specific and protective clothing sit in the same total as uniforms.
rationale: The DIL label is item D3 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction gives the label letter, the substantiation thresholds and the reasonable-basis laundry rate.
evidence_quote: If you did washing, drying or ironing yourself, you can use a reasonable basis to calculate the amount, such as $1 per load for work-related clothing, or 50 cents per load if other laundry items were included.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related clothing expenses' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the laundry part is commonly an estimate.

value_domain: Claim type code at item D3 (C, N, S or P)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3, step 3
variable_description: The main kind of clothing behind the item D3 claim, printed as a single letter in the CLAIM TYPE box. The ATO's four codes are C for a compulsory work uniform, N for a non-compulsory work uniform, S for occupation-specific clothing and P for protective clothing. The taxpayer is asked to "Select the code letter that describes the main type of clothing you are claiming for", so the code is a dominant category rather than an exhaustive one. The distinction has consequences: a non-compulsory uniform is only deductible where the design is registered, while occupation-specific and protective clothing are deductible on their own terms.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3, step 3
value_definition: A single character in the claim type box at item D3, present only where a clothing deduction was claimed.
limitation: It cannot be used to split the deduction. A nurse claiming both a uniform and protective footwear reports one code and one amount, so the code understates the mix of clothing behind the claim. Nor is it an occupational classifier: the same code covers very different jobs, and the occupation code elsewhere on the return is the field for that question.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item D3 lists the four code letters with their clothing categories and states that the taxpayer picks the main type.
evidence_quote: Select the code letter that describes the main type of clothing you are claiming for: C compulsory work uniform, N non-compulsory work uniform, S occupation-specific clothing, P protective clothing
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related clothing expenses - claim type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the four codes were undocumented.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total work-related deductions, pre-2006 returns
value_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), deduction items D1 to D5
variable_description: A total of the work-related deduction items on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. The returns of this period carry the five work expense items separately, at labels A for car expenses, B for travel, C for clothing and laundry, D for self-education and E for other work expenses, with no printed total, so this column is an aggregate the ATO derived rather than a form label. A separate declared total sits beside it in the same table, which suggests the pair distinguishes an assessed total from the taxpayer's own. The five component columns for these years remain available, so the total can be checked against them.
description_source: ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), deduction items D1 to D5
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering the work-related deduction items D1 to D5 of the individual return for the income year.
limitation: Its relationship to the declared total on the same row is unstated, so it should not be assumed to equal the sum of the five component columns without testing. The $300 substantiation threshold of the period is also invisible here: a taxpayer claiming just under $300 without written evidence and one with full records produce indistinguishable figures.
rationale: TaxPack 2000 and the return form for the first year of the column show the five separate work expense labels and the absence of a total on the form, which is what makes this an ATO-derived aggregate. No ATO document names the field or says how it differs from the declared total beside it.
evidence_quote: D1 Work related car expenses A ... D2 Work related travel expenses B ... D5 Other work related expenses E
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Work Related Deduction Amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention the declared total sitting beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label E, item D5 Other work related expenses
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D5 Other work-related expenses
variable_description: The deduction claimed at item D5 for work expenses with no item of their own. The ATO's list runs to union fees and professional association subscriptions, overtime meal expenses paid under a genuine allowance, seminars, courses and conferences, reference books and trade journals, tools, equipment and professional libraries, and "items that protect you from the risk of injury or illness posed by your work or your work environment, such as hard hats, safety glasses and sunscreens (but not protective clothing and footwear, which you claim at item D3 )". Home office and computer running costs are also claimed here, which is why the item grew sharply in the working-from-home years. It is the largest and most heterogeneous of the five work expense labels.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D5 Other work-related expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction totalling every work expense that does not belong at items D1 to D4, including apportioned home office and equipment costs.
limitation: Its composition is unknowable from the number. Union fees, a laptop's decline in value and a home office rate claim are one figure, so a rise in the column can reflect a change in the ATO's shortcut working-from-home rates rather than any change in spending. Immediate deduction applies only to items costing $300 or less, so equipment above that appears here as a decline in value spread over years, not as the purchase price.
rationale: The DIL label is item D5 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction lists the expense types the item covers and the boundary with item D3 for protective items.
evidence_quote: items that protect you from the risk of injury or illness posed by your work or your work environment, such as hard hats, safety glasses and sunscreens (but not protective clothing and footwear, which you claim at item D3 )
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other work related expenses' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the mixture inside the label was invisible.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label D, item D4 Work related self-education expenses
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D4 Work-related self-education expenses
variable_description: The deduction claimed at label D of item D4 for study connected to the taxpayer's current work. The claim is not a simple sum of course costs, because the ATO reduces certain categories: "in working out what you can claim, certain costs are reduced by $250", and other expenses in the calculation can absorb that reduction before it bites. The claim type column on the same row records the connection between the study and the work, which is the test for deductibility. Study undertaken to get a new job rather than to support the present one is not deductible at all, so the column is narrower than education spending.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D4 Work-related self-education expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction for the year, being eligible self-education costs after the $250 reduction is applied under the worksheet in the instructions.
limitation: It is not a measure of education expenditure. Course fees paid through a HELP loan are excluded, study aimed at a career change is excluded, and the $250 reduction removes the smallest claims entirely, so a large share of study spending never reaches this label. The claim also cannot be linked to a course or a provider from this column alone.
rationale: The DIL label is item D4 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction gives the label letter and the $250 reduction that shapes the amount.
evidence_quote: To complete this item, you must add up your self-education expenses under the following categories because, in working out what you can claim, certain costs are reduced by $250.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related self education expenses' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the $250 reduction and the current-work test were nowhere on the page.

value_domain: Claim type code at item D4 (K, I, O or X)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D4, steps 4 and 5
variable_description: The reason the study at item D4 counts as work-related, printed as one letter in the CLAIM TYPE box. The ATO's codes are K where "the study maintained or improved a skill or specific knowledge required for those work activities", I where the study "was leading to, or was likely to lead to, increased income from those work activities", O for another direct connection between the self-education and the taxpayer's work as an employee, and X where the expense was incurred on a course for which the taxpayer received Austudy, ABSTUDY or Youth Allowance. Code X therefore identifies a different population from the other three: students on income support rather than employees upgrading skills.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D4, steps 4 and 5
value_definition: A single character in the claim type box at item D4, present only where a self-education deduction was claimed.
limitation: The code records the basis the taxpayer asserted, not one the ATO tested, so the K, I and O split reflects how the claim was framed rather than a verified fact about the study. It is also not a field of study or qualification indicator, and it cannot be used to count students, since only those claiming a deduction appear at all.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item D4 lists the four code letters with the deductibility basis each represents and states that the letter is printed in the claim type box.
evidence_quote: K At the time you incurred the expense the study maintained or improved a skill or specific knowledge required for those work activities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related self education expenses - claim type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the four codes were undocumented.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label B, item D2 Work related travel expenses
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D2 Work-related travel expenses
variable_description: The deduction claimed at label B of item D2 for work travel other than car expenses. The ATO's instruction is a plain aggregation, "Add up all your deductible travel expenses", and the amount covers fares, accommodation, meals and incidentals on work trips, along with travel in a vehicle that is not a car. Where the taxpayer received a travel or overtime meal allowance within the ATO's reasonable amounts, the expense can be claimed without written evidence, which is set each year by a taxation determination. Car expenses have their own item, so this label and item D1 partition work travel between them.
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D2 Work-related travel expenses
value_definition: A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction totalling deductible travel costs for the income year, excluding anything claimable as a car expense at item D1.
limitation: It is not a travel volume measure. The reasonable amounts concession lets a taxpayer claim up to a published daily rate against an allowance without receipts, so the figure tracks award allowances as much as spending, and travel reimbursed by an employer is not claimable and so never appears. It also cannot be separated into domestic and overseas travel.
rationale: The DIL label is item D2 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction gives the label letter, the aggregation step and the reasonable-amount determination that governs substantiation.
evidence_quote: Step 1 Add up all your deductible travel expenses. Step 2 Write the total amount at B item D2 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Work related travel expenses' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never separated this label from car expenses or mentioned the reasonable-amounts concession.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item T12 Net income from working, supplementary section
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question T12 Net income from working - supplementary section
variable_description: Net income from working reported at item T12 so the ATO could work out the mature age worker tax offset, held for the 2009-10 income year only. However, we need you to work out your net income from working for items you completed on pages 13-16". Income from working means income mainly rewarding personal effort or skills less related deductions, business income less related deductions, reportable fringe benefits, reportable employer superannuation contributions and the net movement in farm management deposits. Only taxpayers aged 55 or over at 30 June had to complete it.

value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering only the working income declared in the supplementary section of the return, worked out by the taxpayer using the item's worksheets.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's total income from working, only the supplementary-section part, so using it as an earnings measure omits salary, wages and other front-section income entirely. It is also confined to taxpayers 55 and over who had supplementary income, and the mature age worker tax offset was phased out and then abolished, so the column has no successor.
rationale: The DIL label is item T12 of the individual return, and the ATO instruction states the offset it feeds, the age condition and that the item covers only the supplementary section.
evidence_quote: We will work out your net income from working from any items you completed on pages 1-12 of your tax return. However, we need you to work out your net income from working for items you completed on pages 13-16 of your tax return (supplementary section).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Net income from working - supplementary section', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is partial by design.

value_domain: yes_no_indicator
values: ["Y: employed by a not-for-profit organisation in the main job","N: not employed by a not-for-profit organisation in the main job"]
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer's main job was with a not-for-profit employer. The distinction matters for tax because some not-for-profits, among them public benevolent institutions and health promotion charities, are exempt from fringe benefits tax up to a capped amount, so their employees' reportable fringe benefits are treated differently at the income tests items. It sits beside XMEMPTYPEGOV, which handles the government side of the same question, in the context tables from 2010-11 onwards. The ATO does not publish how the flag was derived.
description_source: ATO, Not-for-profit organisations
value_definition: A two state flag marking whether the main job employer was a not-for-profit organisation. The stored codes are not published, so a yes and no pair is inferred from the custodian's description.
limitation: Not-for-profit is not the same as exempt from fringe benefits tax. Most not-for-profit employers are taxed on fringe benefits like anyone else, so this flag cannot be used to find employees entitled to the capped exemption.
rationale: The description 'Employed in nfp in main job' states a condition that is either met or not, so the field is a yes/no indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination gave no domain; a yes/no shape is plainly defensible from the description.

value_domain: yes_no_indicator
values: ["Y: a PAYG withholding variation applied for certain offsets or HELP debts","N: no PAYG withholding variation applied"]
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer had a pay as you go withholding variation in place for certain offsets or a study and training loan debt. A variation changes how much tax the employer takes out during the year, so a taxpayer with one reaches assessment with a smaller refund or balance owing than their income and deductions alone would suggest. It is the third of the derived main-job columns added to the return context tables from 2010-11. The ATO does not publish the codes it carries.
description_source: ATO, PAYG withholding variation application
value_definition: A two state flag marking whether a withholding variation applied. The stored values are not published, so a yes and no pair is inferred from the custodian's description.
limitation: It carries neither a rate nor dates. The column cannot say how much withholding was varied, which of the two grounds applied, or how much of the year the variation covered, so it explains the direction of a refund but not its size.
rationale: The description names a condition (a PAYG withholding variation was in place) that is either true or not, so the field is a yes/no indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination gave no domain; a yes/no shape is defensible from the description.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax offset applied in the assessment
value_source: ATO, About tax offsets
variable_description: The part of the zone or overseas forces tax offset that actually reduced the taxpayer's tax bill, which can be less than the amount claimed. The offset is not refundable, so the ATO warns that "If you don't have any tax to pay, you don't receive any offset. Most offsets aren't refundable, which means they can't reduce your tax below zero." Read it against the available amount on the same row: the gap between the two is offset entitlement that was wasted because tax payable ran out.
description_source: ATO, About tax offsets
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount from the assessment, bounded above by the offset available on the same row and by the tax payable before refundable offsets are applied. It is worked out by the ATO rather than written on the return.
limitation: It is a poor measure of who lives remotely or who served overseas. A person who lived in Zone A all year shows nothing here whenever their taxable income was too low to generate tax, so a zero mixes 'not eligible' with 'eligible but no tax to reduce'. It also does not say whether the zone offset or the overseas forces offset produced it.
rationale: The ATO page explains how an offset is applied against tax payable and that most offsets are not refundable, which is exactly the difference between the available and used columns of the return data.
evidence_quote: If you don't have any tax to pay, you don't receive any offset. Most offsets aren't refundable, which means they can't reduce your tax below zero.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the amount consumed in the assessment rather than the amount the taxpayer claimed.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the zone or overseas forces tax offset label
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2015, question T4 Zone or overseas forces
variable_description: The zone or overseas forces tax offset the taxpayer worked out and claimed for the year, before the assessment tests it against tax payable. The ATO builds it from two parts: "The fixed amount is a prescribed amount available to all people in the zone or overseas area eligible for the tax offset", plus a base amount for dependants. Anyone paid a remote area allowance has already netted it off, because "If you received a remote area allowance from Centrelink or the Department of Veterans' Affairs you must reduce the amount of your zone tax offset by the amount you received for this allowance."
description_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2015, question T4 Zone or overseas forces
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount written at the zone or overseas forces offset label on the supplementary return, shown as item T4 on the 2015 return; the item number differs in other years. It is the sum of a fixed amount set by zone and a dependant base amount, less any remote area allowance received.
limitation: It is the taxpayer's own claim, not a verified fact about where they lived, and it turns on a 183-day test, so a person who spent five months in a zone claims nothing. The amount also does not identify the zone: Zone A, Zone B, a special area and overseas service all resolve to a single dollar figure, and a person entitled to both offsets may claim only the higher one.
rationale: The ATO question instructions define the offset the label carries, its fixed and base components, and the remote area allowance reduction that is already inside the reported figure.
evidence_quote: If you received a remote area allowance from Centrelink or the Department of Veterans' Affairs you must reduce the amount of your zone tax offset by the amount you received for this allowance.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what the claimed amount is built from or that it is a self-assessed claim rather than the offset that was allowed.

value_domain: Australian Business Number (hashed and truncated)
value_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
variable_description: The employer who reported the payment summary, as a key rather than as a number. Two rows for one payee in one year mean two payers, or one payer reporting under two ABNs, which is the usual shape for someone who changed jobs mid-year. The identifier is the only thing on the row that distinguishes employers, since nothing else describes the payer, and it is the same value for the same employer across the ATO products and DEX.
description_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
value_definition: A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as "a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register", structured as "a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded, cannot be checked against the public register, and is useful only for matching one record to another.
limitation: The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a workplace or a job. A large employer commonly holds several ABNs across its subsidiaries, so one job can look like several employers and a transfer within a group can look like a change of employer. An entity that restructures takes a new ABN, which breaks a continuous employment relationship in two. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed employer ABN on the payment summary tables. The Australian Business Register publishes the ABN's format, issuer and check-digit rule.
evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Hashed employer ABN' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation.

value_domain: Age in completed years at the start of the financial year
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years on 1 July, the first day of the financial year the payment summary reports. It is derived by the ABS from date of birth rather than reported by the employer, and the 2020-21 table names the same column age at the start of the reference period. Because it is fixed at 1 July, a person is one year younger here than they are for most of the payments on the row.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A whole number of years with no fractional part, constant for a person within a year table and rising by one between consecutive year tables.
limitation: It is not age at the payment, at the job start or at the extract, so it cannot be used to place someone either side of a birthday-linked threshold such as the preservation age or the seniors offset age. A payment summary covering only part of the year still carries the 1 July age, so short spells are aged as though they began in July.
rationale: The ABS assembles PLIDA from linked administrative records and derives demographic columns such as age; no ATO payment summary label carries an age, so the column can only be a derived one, and its name and the sibling wording in the 2020-21 table fix the reference date.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the age is fixed at the start of the year rather than measured when the payments were made.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 30 June 2022
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the close of the 2021-22 financial year, the companion to the age recorded at the start of that year. Where the two differ by one, the person had a birthday during 2021-22; where they agree, the birthday falls outside the file's window. Like its partner it is derived from date of birth by the ABS rather than reported by the employer.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 30 June 2022, equal to the start-of-year age or one greater.
limitation: It is not age at the last payment: the summary period often ends before 30 June, so a person who left a job in September is still aged here at the following June. Nor does it establish residence or presence in Australia at that date, since the row records a payment, not a person's location.
rationale: The column name carries the financial year and the endpoint, and it sits beside the start-of-year age in the same 2021-22 table, which is what makes the pair readable as a birthday indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The entry had no custodian description at all and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing distinguished it from the age at the start of the same year.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 1 July 2021
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the start of the 2021-22 financial year, in the file extracted 16 months after that year closed. It is a derived demographic column, not a label on the payment summary, and it is paired with the age at the end of the same year so a birthday inside the year can be seen. A person shown as 64 here may have spent most of the year at 65.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 1 July 2021, one value per person per row, with no code list.
limitation: The pair of start and end ages narrows a birthday to a year, not to a date, so it cannot be used to work out how much of the year's pay fell either side of an age threshold. The column exists only in the 2021-22 tables, so an age series across years has to be rebuilt from differently named columns.
rationale: The column name carries both the financial year and the endpoint, and the table is the 2021-22 payment summary file; the ABS derives this kind of demographic column when it assembles PLIDA rather than taking it from the form.
supersedes_rationale: The entry had no custodian description at all and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which year the age was measured in or which end of it.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 30 June 2023
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the close of the 2022-23 financial year, labelled age end of 2223 by the custodian. Subtracting the start-of-year age gives a one or a zero, which is the only birthday signal in the table. The topic tagging calls it income, which is wrong: nothing about the payments on the row enters this column.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 30 June 2023, either equal to the 1 July 2022 age on the same row or one greater, and repeated across the 6-month and 12-month extracts.
limitation: An age at the end of a financial year says nothing about whether the person was still employed then, because the payment summary period may have closed months earlier. Reading it as age at last payment therefore ages short spells upward, and the error grows the earlier in the year the job ended.
rationale: The custodian's label names the year and the endpoint, and the column pairs with the start-of-year age in the same 2022-23 table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the later of the two ages on the row and that it carries no income content despite the income tag.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 1 July 2022
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the start of the 2022-23 financial year, in the file extracted 12 months after that year closed. The custodian labels it age start of 2223, and it repeats for 2022-23 the paired age design used in the 2021-22 tables. It is derived from date of birth, so it is present even for rows where the employer reported little else.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 1 July 2022. It is carried on both the 6-month and the 12-month extracts of 2022-23, so the same person's age appears twice if the two are stacked.
limitation: A twelve-month extract catches only the payment summaries lodged by then, so the population this age describes is not the same as the population in a longer extract of the same year, and age distributions from the two are not directly comparable. The column also cannot be joined to the 2021-22 age columns by name.
rationale: The custodian's label names the year and the endpoint, and the column sits in the 12-month extract of the 2022-23 payment summary file.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which day of the 2022-23 year the age refers to or that it is derived rather than reported.

value_domain: Payment summary amendment indicator
value_source: ATO, Correct a mistake, PAYG withholding payment summaries
variable_description: Says whether this payment summary is an original report or an amended one replacing a report already sent for the same payee and year. The ATO sets the values in the annual report file: "In the Amendment indicator field in your annual report file, type: 'A' for Amended payee records 'O' for original records not previously sent to us." Employers amend when they find a wrong tax file number, dollar amount, payment type or code, so a marked row usually means a corrected dollar figure.
description_source: ATO, Correct a mistake, PAYG withholding payment summaries
value_definition: A single-character code carried on every payment summary record, A for an amended payee record and O for an original one not previously reported.
limitation: It does not say what changed or which earlier row it supersedes, and the amended summary repeats the payee and payer details rather than reversing the earlier amounts. Both rows can therefore sit in the same file, so totalling gross payments by person and year without filtering on this code double counts the amended employment.
rationale: The ATO page on correcting payment summaries names the amendment indicator field, gives its two values and lists the mistakes that trigger an amended record, which is the field this column carries.
evidence_quote: In the Amendment indicator field in your annual report file, type: 'A' for Amended payee records 'O' for original records not previously sent to us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what the code distinguishes or that unfiltered totals double count amended rows.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address the ATO held for the payee when the payment summary was reported. The MB, LGA, SA1, SA2, SA3, SA4 and STE columns on the same row are that one address geocoded to progressively coarser ASGS areas, so this identifier is the finest thing they all derive from: it separates two payees in the same mesh block, which the geography codes cannot. It is also the key that matches the row to the same address in Core Locations and in the other ATO products.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. An administrative address is only as current as the payee's last dealing with the ATO, so it can lag a move by a year or more. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed, truncated ARID. ABS publishes what the Address Register and its identifier are, and the payment summary table carries MB, LGA, SA1 to SA4 and STE alongside the identifier, which are the ASGS codings of the address it stands for.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'not specified' as its domain and repeated 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both its value definition and its limitation, which told a reader nothing about what the column holds.

value_domain: Confidentialised business identifier for the payer
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The employer or payer that issued the payment summary, as a confidentialised business identifier assigned by the ABS. In the later extracts it takes the place of the hashed and truncated ABN that the earlier payment summary tables carry, so a payer series that spans the change has to bridge the two columns. It is what makes an employee's job history readable: rows sharing a person and a payer are one employment relationship.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: An opaque identifier, stable within the asset, standing for a business rather than for an ABN. It is generated in fplida rather than derived from any real business.
limitation: A business identifier is not a workplace or a job. A large employer with many sites shows as one value, a person with two summaries from the same payer in a year is not two jobs, and a business that restructures can change identifier without any change to the employment.
rationale: The same column name in the registry's business and income products carries the custodian's fuller wording, an ABS derived confidentialised business identifier that took over from the hashed ABN, and in the payment summary tables it appears exactly where the hashed ABN drops out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the column identifies the paying employer or that it stands in for the hashed ABN used in the earlier tables.

value_domain: abs_address_coding_index_identifier
value_source: ABS Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, 'Geocoding unit record data using address and location'
variable_description: Which address coding index was used to geocode the payee's address on this payment summary. The custodian labels it a geocode index, and it names the index the reported address was matched against in a process the ABS says should return "a location coordinate, preferably obtained from G-NAF, and an ASGS region code". ARID_HASH_TRUNC on the same row is the address, MB, SA1, SA2, SA3, SA4, LGA and STE are what the match produced, and REPAIR_RESULT records what the cleaning step did to the address text first.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, SSF Guidance Material - Geocoding Unit Record Data Using Address and Location
value_definition: A short identifier for one version of the coding index the ABS applied. No list of index identifiers is published, so the domain is open and has to be read from the data.
limitation: The address on a payment summary is the one the payer held for the payee, often a payroll record that was never updated. This column says nothing about how stale that address was, so it cannot flag rows whose geography belongs to a residence the person had already left.
rationale: Described as 'Geocode index' and sitting beside REPAIR_RESULT and the ASGS geography columns in the same table, so it identifies the address coding index used; no list of index identifiers is published.
evidence_quote: the geocoding system should use a G-NAF based coding index
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination gave no concept; the concept is now identified even though the domain remains unenumerable.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the exempt foreign employment income label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Foreign employment income the employer paid that is exempt from Australian tax, reported apart from gross payments. The ATO states plainly that "Income from foreign employment is exempt from tax if your payee meets certain conditions", and no tax is withheld from it. Where it is all a payer paid there is no form at all: "If the only income you have paid is exempt foreign employment income, you do not need to provide a payment summary."
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of employment income exempted under the foreign service rules, reported separately from the gross payments on the same summary.
limitation: Exempt does not mean irrelevant. The amount is used to work out the rate applied to the payee's other income, so treating it as untaxed and setting it aside understates the effective rate on the rest. Coverage is also incomplete by design, because a payer whose only payments to a person were exempt foreign employment income need issue no summary at all, so those workers leave no row.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the payment summary names the label, states the exemption condition and gives the case in which no summary is issued at all.
evidence_quote: If the only income you have paid is exempt foreign employment income, you do not need to provide a payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is exempt income reported outside gross payments, or that some exempt income never reaches the file.

value_domain: ATO extract reference date
value_source: ABS administrative income sources
variable_description: When the ATO took the extract this row came from, not anything about the taxpayer. Tax records keep changing after the income year closes, as returns are lodged late, amended and audited, so the same income year extracted at two dates is two different datasets. The suffix on the table name is that lag: ato_pay_sum_2223_12m is the 2022-23 year as it stood twelve months after the year ended. This column is what tells you which vintage you are reading, and comparing across years means comparing like lags rather than like income years.
description_source: ABS administrative income sources
limitation: The column describes the extract, not the person, so it is never an analysis variable. An early extract understates a year's income because late lodgers are missing, and the shortfall is not spread evenly: it falls on people with complex affairs and on those who lodge through an agent. Mixing lags across years builds a trend out of coverage rather than out of income.
rationale: The field is named as an extract reference on the ATO tables, and every product carrying it has a table-name suffix giving a lag in months from the end of the income year. ABS documents the administrative income sources as point-in-time extracts of tax records, but does not publish a definition of this column, so the reading is inferred from the naming and the table structure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'ATO data extract time' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left a reader with no reason to care about the column.

value_domain: Australian financial year of the extract (1 July to 30 June)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The financial year that the payment summary file itself covers, constant within a table and set by which year's annual reports the ATO extracted. It is the outer frame for the row, while the income year column repeats the year written on the form and the period dates say how much of that year the payments span. Its value earns its keep once several year tables are stacked, because it is what the stacked rows are ordered by.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: A financial year label rather than a date. It appears only in the 2020-21 and later extracts, where several tables can share a year and differ only in how long after 30 June the file was cut.
