value_definition: A dollar market value of the assets held on trust, not of the money borrowed: the outstanding borrowing under these arrangements is reported separately in the liabilities item.
limitation: The abbreviated column name reads like an overseas direct investment, but the label it carries is the borrowing arrangement one, so treating it as the fund's overseas shareholding double counts against OS_SHRS_AMT and misstates gearing. Borrowing arrangement labels were also added to the return well after the earliest years in this file, so early years are empty by design rather than because no fund was geared.
rationale: The assets section defines label J5 in the limited recourse borrowing arrangement block, states that the amounts are asset values rather than borrowings, and keeps them out of the ordinary overseas share label.
evidence_quote: The amounts you write at labels J1 to J6 are the values of the assets held on trust under limited recourse borrowing arrangements and not the amounts borrowed or the amount of outstanding borrowings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt label 'Limited recourse borring arrangements - Overseas shares' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not flag that the column name and the label describe different things.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 11 label E, Australian franking credits from a New Zealand company, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
variable_description: Australian franking credits attached to dividends from a New Zealand company that has joined the Australian imputation system. The ATO notes that "Dividends paid by New Zealand resident companies don't normally carry Australian franking credits" and that such a company "can choose to join the Australian imputation system and distribute Australian franking credits with its dividends". The dividend itself is reported as gross foreign income, so this column is only the credit.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
value_definition: A dollar amount of imputation credits, not reduced by any loss or outgoing, and reduced by any supplementary dividend the fund received in connection with the franked dividend.
limitation: It is not a measure of New Zealand investment income and it is not New Zealand imputation credits, which cannot be claimed in Australia at all. Very few funds report anything here, so a zero says nothing about whether the fund held New Zealand shares.
rationale: The income section defines the label, explains the trans-Tasman imputation arrangement it depends on, and separates the credit from the dividend and from New Zealand imputation credits.
evidence_quote: However, a New Zealand company can choose to join the Australian imputation system and distribute Australian franking credits with its dividends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Australian franking credits from a New Zealand company' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave a reader no way to see why such a column exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15b label J2, limited recourse borrowing arrangements - Australian non-residential real property, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
variable_description: Commercial or industrial property in Australia that the fund holds through a geared structure, valued at 30 June. The ATO defines the label as the fund's beneficial interest in "non-residential real property" that is "held in a trust as security for a borrowing under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement". The classic case is business real property bought with borrowed money and leased back to the members' own business, which is permitted where residential property leased to a member is not.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
value_definition: A dollar market value of the property held on trust at 30 June, reported instead of, not as well as, the ungeared non-residential property label elsewhere in the same item.
limitation: The value is the asset, not the debt, so it cannot show gearing on its own; the outstanding borrowing sits at the liabilities label and the two have to be read together. The column is also silent on the tenant, so a property leased to a related business looks identical to one leased at arm's length.
rationale: The assets section defines label J2 and states that non-residential property held under a borrowing arrangement is excluded from the ordinary non-residential property label.
evidence_quote: Write at label J2 the value (on 30 June 2025) of the SMSF's beneficial interest in non-residential real property
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt label 'Limited recourse borring arrangements - Australian non-residential real property' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say that the amount is the asset rather than the borrowing.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15d label U, total Australian and overseas assets, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
variable_description: The fund's whole balance sheet in one number: every asset it held at 30 June, in Australia and overseas. It is the denominator for the in-house asset test and the usual measure of fund size. The return requires it to balance: "The SMSF's total assets must equal its total liabilities, that is, the amount at label U Total Australian and overseas assets must equal the amount at label Z Total liabilities".
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
value_definition: A dollar amount at 30 June, the sum of the Australian asset labels, the crypto asset label and the overseas direct investment labels on the same row.
limitation: It is not the fund's net wealth. Members' entitlements are counted as liabilities on this form, so total assets equalling total liabilities is a bookkeeping identity rather than a sign the fund is fully geared. As a subtotal of the asset labels beside it, adding it to them double counts.
rationale: The assets section states the balancing requirement between total assets and total liabilities and sets out the asset labels that feed the total.
evidence_quote: The SMSF's total assets must equal its total liabilities, that is, the amount at label U Total Australian and overseas assets must equal the amount at label Z Total liabilities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'TOTAL AUSTRALIAN AND OVERSEAS ASSETS' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned that assets equal liabilities by construction here.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15b label J1, limited recourse borrowing arrangements - Australian residential real property, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
variable_description: Australian housing the fund bought with borrowed money, valued at 30 June, which is the single most watched holding in the sector. The ATO's example makes the reporting explicit: a residential property worth $300,000 held under an arrangement with $100,000 still owing is reported as "$300,000 at label J1 Australian residential real property" and "$100,000 at label V1 Borrowings for limited recourse borrowing arrangements". Residential property the fund owns outright is reported at a different label in the same item.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
value_definition: A dollar market value of the fund's beneficial interest in the property held on trust as security, at 30 June, gross of the borrowing against it.
limitation: Taking the column as the fund's residential exposure understates it, because ungeared housing sits elsewhere in the item, and taking it as debt overstates it, because the borrowing is a separate label. A count of properties is also not implied: the arrangement's property count label is what says how many titles are behind the value.
rationale: The assets section defines label J1, gives a worked example separating the property value from the outstanding borrowing, and keeps ungeared residential property at its own label.
evidence_quote: $300,000 at label J1 Australian residential real property
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt label 'Limited recourse borring arrangements - Australian residential real property' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never separated the property value from the loan.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator at item 8 label A of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10
variable_description: Whether the trustees say the fund met the residency test that keeps it taxed at the concessional rate. The consequence is severe: "If the SMSF doesn't meet the definition of Australian super fund at all times during the income year, the SMSF isn't a complying SMSF and it won't receive the concessional rate of tax". The question is most often at issue where trustees move overseas, which is why the fund's residency and its members' whereabouts are connected.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10
value_definition: A single indicator with two states, reported once for the fund for the income year in the status block at item 8, alongside the fund benefit structure code and the government contribution question.
limitation: It is the trustees' own answer to a legal test, not an ATO determination, so a yes is a claim rather than a finding of residency. The test is also whole-of-year, so the indicator cannot show a period during the year when the fund would have failed it.
rationale: Section A of the instructions puts this question at item 8 label A and states the tax consequence of failing the Australian superannuation fund definition at any time in the year.
evidence_quote: If the SMSF doesn't meet the definition of Australian super fund at all times during the income year, the SMSF isn't a complying SMSF and it won't receive the concessional rate of tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Australian superannuation fund' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what turns on the answer.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 15b label J4, limited recourse borrowing arrangements - Australian shares, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
variable_description: Australian shares the fund holds through a geared structure, typically instalment warrants, valued at 30 June. The ATO defines it as the fund's beneficial interest in "public shares, unlisted shares, equities and similar financial contracts that are held in a trust as security for a borrowing under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement". Shares the fund owns outright are reported at the listed and unlisted share labels instead, so this column is the geared slice of the equity portfolio.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16
value_definition: A dollar market value of the shares held on trust at 30 June, gross of the borrowing, which is reported separately in the liabilities item.
limitation: It is not the fund's Australian share holding despite the column name, and adding it to the listed and unlisted share columns is the right move only if you want total exposure rather than direct holdings. Derivatives are excluded by instruction and reported at other assets, so a geared derivative position is not visible here.
rationale: The assets section defines label J4 inside the borrowing arrangement block, lists what it includes and excludes, and keeps ordinary shareholdings at their own labels.
evidence_quote: Write at label J4 the value (on 30 June 2025) of the SMSF's beneficial interest in public shares, unlisted shares, equities and similar financial contracts that are held in a trust as security for a borrowing under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt label 'Limited recourse borring arrangements - Australian shares' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not separate geared from directly held shares.

value_domain: Business identifier carried on the SMSF member contributions record
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: A business identifier held against the member record, with no definition published beyond the words 'Business Number'. The column sits on the member contributions statement table, and the one business identifier the ATO asks for in that part of the return is the employer's: "Write at label A1 the ABN of the employer who made contributions to the member's account". The fund's own ABN is asked for elsewhere, in Section A, so the employer reading is the more likely of the two but is not established.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: An identifier value with no published format in the data item list. An ABN would be an 11-digit number, but PLIDA does not release business identifiers in clear, so the shape in the delivered data has to be checked before use.
limitation: The custodian publishes only the words 'Business Number' and no definition, so whether the value is a contributing employer's ABN, the fund's own ABN or an internal reference is not established here. It should not be joined to BLADE or to any ABN-keyed file on the assumption that it is a clear-text ABN, and SF_SID on the same row is the fund key the data actually supports joining on.
rationale: The neighbouring columns on the member statement are all fund-level or member-level fields and the fund is identified by its ABN on the annual return, which makes the fund's ABN the most likely reading; the ATO page supports what an ABN is but not the mapping itself.
evidence_quote: Write at label A1 the ABN of the employer who made contributions to the member's account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Business Number' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which read as though the meaning were settled when it is not.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 11 label A, net capital gain, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
variable_description: The capital gain that actually reaches the fund's assessable income, after losses and the discount have been applied. The ATO defines it as the total capital gain for the year less "any 2024-25 capital losses", "any prior year net capital losses" and "any other relevant CGT discount or concession". Where the fund had gains above $10,000 a full capital gains tax schedule is attached, so the CGT dataset holds the working behind this single number.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
value_definition: A dollar amount net of current and prior year capital losses and of the one-third discount available to complying funds on assets held at least twelve months, and inclusive of the capital gains component of trust and partnership distributions.
limitation: It cannot be turned back into disposal proceeds or a gross gain, since losses and the discount are already inside it. It is also not the fund's whole capital gain: gains on segregated current pension assets are disregarded entirely and non-arm's-length capital gains are reported at the non-arm's-length income labels instead.
rationale: The income section defines the label, its deductions in order, the treatment of pension and non-arm's-length gains, and the threshold at which the capital gains tax schedule must be attached.
evidence_quote: The SMSF's net capital gain is the total capital gain for 2024-25 less: any 2024-25 capital losses; any prior year net capital losses; any other relevant CGT discount or concession.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Net capital gain' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what had already been netted out of the figure.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator at item 11 label G of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
variable_description: Whether anything happened during the year that engaged the capital gains rules, which is a wider question than whether the fund sold something. The ATO says answer yes if the fund "had a CGT event occur during the income year", "received a share of net income from a trust that includes a capital gain", or had a harvest or interest sale under a forestry managed investment scheme. It is the gate for the net capital gain amount and for attaching a capital gains tax schedule.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
value_definition: A single indicator with two states for the fund for the income year, reported ahead of the exemption or rollover question and the net capital gain amount on the same row.
limitation: A yes does not imply a gain or any tax: a loss, a rollover, a disregarded gain on a segregated pension asset, or a trust distribution carrying a gain all produce the same answer. A no is also not a statement that the fund's assets were unchanged, only that no CGT event was identified.
rationale: The income section lists the three circumstances that require a yes at this label and places it at the head of the capital gains block that follows.
evidence_quote: Answer Yes if the SMSF: had a CGT event occur during the income year
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question 'Did you have a capital gains tax (CGT) event during the year?' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no sense of how wide the question is.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label D, CGT small business 15-year exemption amount, member section of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: Sale proceeds a member put into the fund after selling a business asset held fifteen years or more, kept outside their non-concessional cap. The ATO defines the label as "the total value of personal contributions made by the member in 2024-25 that the member elected to exclude from their non-concessional contributions with a CGT small business 15-year exemption amount". A value here marks a business exit rather than ordinary saving, so it identifies the retiring small business owner in the member file.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member for the year, counted against the lifetime CGT cap, which was $1,650,000 in 2024-25 and is indexed annually.
limitation: It is a contribution, not a capital gain, so it cannot measure what the business sold for and it does not identify the asset or the business. Contributions above the cap fall back to the ordinary personal contributions label, so a member at their limit shows a smaller number here than the sale would suggest.
rationale: The member information section defines the label, the election it depends on, and the CGT cap that limits what can be reported at it.
evidence_quote: Write at label D the total value of personal contributions made by the member in 2024-25 that the member elected to exclude from their non-concessional contributions with a CGT small business 15-year exemption amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'CGT small business 15 year exemption amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said the amount is a contribution rather than a gain.

value_domain: Dollar amount at label C, CGT small business retirement exemption, member section of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: Business sale proceeds a member contributed under the retirement exemption, outside their non-concessional cap but inside a lifetime limit of its own. The ATO caps it hard: "a member can't elect to apply a CGT small business retirement exemption to more than $500,000 during their lifetime". Unlike the fifteen-year exemption beside it, this concession does not require a long holding period, so it reaches business owners exiting earlier.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member for the year, subject both to the $500,000 lifetime retirement exemption limit and to the indexed CGT cap that it shares with the 15-year exemption label.
limitation: One year's figure cannot show how much of the $500,000 lifetime limit is left, because the limit runs across a member's whole life and across funds. Amounts in excess of either limit are reported as ordinary personal contributions instead, so the column undercounts the money that came from a business sale.
rationale: The member information section defines the label, the election behind it and both the lifetime limit and the CGT cap that constrain it.
evidence_quote: The CGT small business retirement exemption lifetime limit - a member can't elect to apply a CGT small business retirement exemption to more than $500,000 during their lifetime.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'CGT small business retirement exemption' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the 15-year exemption column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 11 label T, assessable income due to changed tax status of fund, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
variable_description: A one-off amount brought to tax because the fund changed status, either losing complying status or becoming an Australian fund. The ATO writes at this label the amount included "because it changed from either: complying to non-complying at the beginning of 2024-25; a foreign fund to an Australian super fund at the beginning of 2024-25". For a fund that became non-complying the amount is close to its entire asset value, worked out as asset value less non-concessional contributions, and it is taxed at 45 per cent.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
value_definition: A dollar amount for the fund for the year, not reduced by any loss or outgoing, and not exempt under the exempt current pension income rules.
limitation: It is a penalty inclusion, not income the fund earned, so leaving it in an income series makes the fund look enormously profitable in the year it failed. The single column also mixes two opposite events, a compliance failure and an inbound residency change, which cannot be told apart without the status indicators elsewhere on the return.
rationale: The income section defines the label, gives the two triggering events, sets out formula A for the non-complying case and states the 45 per cent rate that applies to it.
evidence_quote: Write at label T the amount that is to be included in the SMSF's assessable income because it changed from either: complying to non-complying at the beginning of 2024-25; a foreign fund to an Australian super fund at the beginning of 2024-25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Assessable income due to changed tax status of fund' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount is roughly the fund's asset value rather than earnings.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 14 label V, net capital losses carried forward to later income years, of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section E: Losses - item 14
variable_description: The stock of capital losses the fund still has available to set against future capital gains. The ATO defines it as "the total of any unapplied net capital losses from collectables and unapplied net capital losses from all other CGT assets and events", and capital losses can be carried forward indefinitely until a gain absorbs them. Where this and the fund's tax losses together exceed $100,000, a separate losses schedule is attached to the return.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section E: Losses - item 14
value_definition: A dollar amount at the end of the income year, accumulated across years rather than earned in one, and reported separately from tax losses at the label beside it.
limitation: It is a closing balance, not the year's loss, so a change between years mixes new losses with losses used up against gains and cannot be read as this year's investment result. It also merges collectables losses with all other losses even though collectables losses can only ever be applied against collectables gains, so the usable amount is smaller than the total for a fund holding art or wine.
rationale: The losses section defines label V, its two components, its separation from tax losses at label U, and the threshold for lodging a losses schedule.
evidence_quote: Write at label V the total of any unapplied net capital losses from collectables and unapplied net capital losses from all other CGT assets and events.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Net capital losses carried forward to later income years' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is an accumulated stock or that collectables losses are ring-fenced inside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at member label M, any other contributions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label M
variable_description: Contributions received for this member that fit no other contribution label, mostly the government super co-contribution and low income super amount. The ATO tells trustees to include at label M "super co-contributions and low income super amounts paid to the SMSF for the benefit of the member by us", along with any foreign fund transfer the member chose to have taxed inside the fund. It is the last of the thirteen contribution labels that add to label N Total contributions on the same member row, so it works as a residual rather than as a named category.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label M
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member for one income year, gross and not reduced by contributions tax or expenses. It sits between the named contribution labels A to L and the label N total on the same row.
limitation: It cannot separate a government co-contribution from a low income super amount or from an elected foreign transfer, so it is not a clean measure of government contributions. A zero also does not mean the member received no co-contribution, because the ATO can pay it after 30 June and it then lands in a later year's return.
rationale: The member section of the SMSF annual return is what the smsf_mcs tables carry, and the ATO instructions for label M name exactly what belongs in this residual and what does not.
evidence_quote: super co-contributions and low income super amounts paid to the SMSF for the benefit of the member by us
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is a residual contribution label dominated by government payments.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label R3, no-TFN-quoted contributions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label R3
variable_description: Assessable contributions the fund received for members who had not quoted a tax file number, which carry extra tax on top of the ordinary rate. The ATO narrows it: report the contributions only where "a member's account was opened on or after 1 July 2007" or that member's assessable contributions for the year came to more than $1,000. Label R3 is mandatory and the ATO tells trustees to write a zero at it where the question does not apply, so the column is populated on almost every return whether or not the fund had such contributions.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label R3
value_definition: A dollar amount of contributions rather than of tax; the extra tax charged on it, 32 per cent for a complying fund, is reported separately at Section D label J. The amount is gross and is not reduced by any loss or outgoing.
limitation: A value here is a reporting fact about a missing tax file number, not about the generosity of an employer, and the fund-level return does not say which member it was for. Because the label is mandatory, a zero cannot be read as a considered answer.
rationale: The DIL label matches Section B label R3 exactly, and the ATO instructions give both the threshold rules and the mandatory-zero behaviour that decide how the column reads.
evidence_quote: a member's account was opened on or after 1 July 2007
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'No-TFN quoted contributions' and used the generic sentence twice, so it never said that the amount is contributions rather than tax, or that a zero is compulsory.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at member label N, total contributions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label N
variable_description: Everything contributed for one member during the year, which the ATO defines as "the total of all the contributions for this member that you wrote at labels A to M". Those labels run from employer and personal contributions through the CGT small business exemptions, a personal injury election, spouse and child contributions, downsizer proceeds, foreign fund amounts and reserve transfers to the residual label M. Money that arrived by other routes is outside it: rollovers in, allocated earnings and benefit payments each have their own label further down the member row.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label N
value_definition: A dollar total for one member for one income year, gross of the contributions tax the fund pays, equal to the sum of the thirteen contribution labels on the same row.
limitation: It mixes concessional and non-concessional contributions, so it cannot be compared with either contributions cap. It is also not the change in the member's balance over the year, because earnings, rollovers, lump sums and pension payments sit outside it.
rationale: The ATO instructions for label N enumerate the labels the total is built from, which is what a reader needs to know before using the column as a contributions measure.
evidence_quote: the total of all the contributions for this member that you wrote at labels A to M
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total contributions' and gave the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving the reader unable to tell which components are inside the total.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label H3, credit for tax withheld where ABN or TFN not quoted
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H3
variable_description: Tax that a payer withheld from money paid to the fund because the fund itself did not quote an ABN or tax file number, claimed back as a credit. The ATO asks for "the total tax withheld from payments to the SMSF because the SMSF had not quoted its ABN or TFN", and the payer must give the fund a payment summary showing the amount. This is about the fund's own registration details, not a member's: contributions for a member who has not quoted a tax file number are reported at Section B label R3 instead.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H3
value_definition: A dollar amount of tax already withheld, reported to the fund by a third party on a payment summary, and one of the five credits that add to label H Eligible credits.
limitation: It cannot tell you how large the underlying payment was, only the tax taken out of it, and the gross payment is reported somewhere in Section B with no link back to this credit. A fund claiming it must also lodge a non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule, which PLIDA does not carry.
rationale: The custodian's label is the ATO's own label H3 wording, and the instructions distinguish it from the member-level no-TFN case that the name invites a reader to confuse it with.
evidence_quote: Write at label H3 the total tax withheld from payments to the SMSF because the SMSF had not quoted its ABN or TFN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label verbatim and the generic sentence twice, so it did not say whose ABN or TFN was missing, which is the only thing that makes the column readable.

value_domain: Dollar amount of interest reported at Section D item 13 label H1, credit for interest on early payments
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2019 instructions, Section D item 13, H1 to H eligible credit questions
variable_description: Interest the ATO owed the fund for paying a tax liability more than 14 days before it fell due, claimed as a credit. The 2018-19 instructions ask for "the calculated interest amount of 50 cents or more for early payments" and tell trustees not to write the early payment itself at this label. The label has since gone from the return: the 2025 eligible credit questions run H2, H3, H5, H6 and H8 with no H1, so a series built on this column ends part way through the PLIDA years.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2019 instructions, Section D item 13, H1 to H eligible credit questions
value_definition: A dollar amount of interest calculated under the early payment rules, not a payment or a tax, and reported only where the calculated interest reaches 50 cents.
limitation: It does not measure how much the fund prepaid or how early. It also excludes liabilities that were satisfied by crediting PAYG instalments, withholding credits or a running balance surplus, which the ATO says do not attract early payment interest at all.
rationale: The 2019 edition of the instructions still carries label H1 with its own heading, and the 2025 edition lists the eligible credits without it, which together date the column's disappearance.
evidence_quote: Write at H1 the calculated interest amount of 50 cents or more for early payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and gave the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is interest rather than the prepayment, nor that the label stops appearing on later returns.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label H2, credit for tax withheld under foreign resident withholding
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H2
variable_description: Tax withheld in Australia under the foreign resident withholding rules from payments made to the fund, claimed back as a credit. The ATO allows the credit only where the amount was both "withheld in Australia" and "remitted to us", and it includes the fund's share of such credits passed through a partnership or a trust. Withholding on a property sale is excluded and goes to label H8 instead.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H2
value_definition: A dollar amount of Australian withholding tax, reported to the fund by the payer on a payment summary, and one of the components of label H Eligible credits.
limitation: The label name misleads: this is withholding under the foreign resident rules on Australian-source payments, not tax the fund paid overseas. Foreign tax paid abroad is relieved through the foreign income tax offset at label C1 and never appears here.
rationale: The custodian's label is the ATO's label H2 wording, and the instructions set the two conditions and the boundary against the capital gains withholding credit.
evidence_quote: The SMSF is entitled to a credit at label H2 only if the amount was both: withheld in Australia remitted to us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Credit for tax withheld - foreign resident withholding' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish Australian withholding from foreign tax paid.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label H6, credit for interest on the no-TFN tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H6
variable_description: Interest the ATO pays a fund on the no-TFN tax offset it is claiming this year, credited in the tax calculation. Entitlement is tied to the offset: "If the SMSF hasn't claimed a no-TFN tax offset at label E2, it can't claim a credit at label H6", and only calculated interest of 50 cents or more is written. The interest is payable only where an employer failed its duty under section 299C of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 to pass the member's tax file number on to the fund.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H6
value_definition: A dollar amount of interest at the base rate set by section 8AAD of the Taxation Administration Act 1953, worked out by the fund and included in the label H Eligible credits total.
limitation: It is not the offset and cannot be added to it as a measure of tax recovered; the offset sits at label E2 on the same return. The trigger is an employer failure, so a value says nothing about the member or the fund.
rationale: The DIL label matches label H6, and the ATO instructions give the dependency on label E2 and the statutory reason interest arises at all.
evidence_quote: If the SMSF hasn't claimed a no-TFN tax offset at label E2, it can't claim a credit at label H6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and printed the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the credit exists only alongside the offset at label E2.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label E2, no-TFN tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E2
variable_description: A refundable offset that gives back the extra no-TFN contributions tax the fund paid in an earlier year, once the member finally supplies a tax file number. The claim is narrow: the fund must have paid the additional tax "in any of the 3 previous income years" for a member who quoted their tax file number for the first time in the current year. The ATO adds that because SMSF members are usually the trustees, "it is rare for an SMSF to pay no-TFN contributions tax, and therefore rare for SMSFs to be entitled to a no-TFN tax offset".
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E2
value_definition: A dollar amount of refundable tax offset, equal to the additional no-TFN contributions tax being recovered, and reported in the same refundable group as franking credits.
limitation: The year on the row is the year of recovery, not the year of the contributions, which can be up to three years earlier. It also cannot be used to count members without tax file numbers, because only members who supplied one during the year generate an entry.
rationale: The ATO's label E2 instructions give the three-year window, the first-time-quoting condition and an explicit statement of how rare the offset is for this fund type.
evidence_quote: Because SMSF members are generally either trustees of the SMSF, or directors of a corporate trustee, it is rare for an SMSF to pay no-TFN contributions tax, and therefore rare for SMSFs to be entitled to a no-TFN tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'No-TFN tax offset' and the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount relates to tax paid in an earlier year.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label E1, complying fund's franking credits tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E1
variable_description: The franking credits a complying fund claims as a refundable offset, which is why many SMSFs finish the year receiving a refund rather than paying tax. The ATO includes credits attached to dividends "including where they are exempt current pension income", and credits attached to franked distributions from New Zealand franking companies. Only a complying fund uses this label; a non-complying fund puts the same credits at label C2, where the unused part is lost rather than refunded.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E1
value_definition: A dollar amount of imputation credit treated as a refundable tax offset under section 67-25 of the ITAA 1997, drawn from the franking credits already declared as income in Section B, including those at labels L and E.
limitation: It is an offset claim, not dividend income, so it cannot stand in for the fund's shareholdings or their yield. Neither is it the refund: the refund is what remains after gross tax and the other offsets have been worked through.
rationale: The ATO's label E1 instructions state what the offset covers, the requirement to also report the credits as income, and the complying against non-complying split that decides refundability.
evidence_quote: Include at label E1 Australian franking credits that are attached to: dividends and non-share dividends including where they are exempt current pension income
supersedes_rationale: The entry reused the label wording and the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain that this is the refundable route only complying funds take.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label E3, National Rental Affordability Scheme tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E3
variable_description: A refundable offset for a fund holding an approved National Rental Affordability Scheme dwelling, set entirely by the certificate it was issued. The ATO says the offset is "only available when the Secretary of the Department of Social Services has issued a certificate under the NRAS", and that "the amount of the tax offset is the amount in the NRAS certificate". The certificate claimed on the 2024-25 return must cover the scheme year 1 May 2024 to 30 April 2025.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E3
value_definition: A dollar amount of refundable offset taken from a government certificate rather than calculated by the fund, reported in the refundable group with franking credits and the exploration credit offset.
limitation: The scheme year runs to 30 April, so the offset on a return does not match the income year the rest of the row describes. The column also does not identify the dwelling, which appears only as part of the fund's residential real property total in Section H.
rationale: The ATO's label E3 instructions fix both the amount and the qualifying period to the DSS certificate, which is what makes the column readable as an incentive rather than a calculation.
evidence_quote: The amount of the tax offset is the amount in the NRAS certificate.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label and the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is set by an external certificate covering a period that is not the income year.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section A item 10 label A, exempt current pension income amount
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 10 label A
variable_description: The fund's income that is exempt from tax because it supports retirement phase pensions, declared up front in Section A. The ATO requires the two exempt pension income entries on the return to agree: the amount at item 10 label A "must be the same as the amount that you write at label Y Exempt current pension income for item 11 in Section B". Only funds that answered yes to paying retirement phase income stream benefits during the year complete it at all.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 10 label A
value_definition: A dollar amount of exempt income worked out under the segregated assets method, the proportionate method or both, and not reduced by the expenses of earning it.
limitation: It is fund income treated as exempt, not the pensions paid to members, which appear on the member rows as income stream payments. Reading it as a share of the fund's income needs gross income at Section B label W as the denominator, since the column carries no percentage.
rationale: The Section A instructions define item 10 label A and tie it to the Section B figure, which is what separates this column from its twin in the income statement.
evidence_quote: If you complete Section B, the amount that you write at label A for item 10 in Section A must be the same as the amount that you write at label Y Exempt current pension income for item 11 in Section B.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and gave the generic sentence twice, and it did not explain how this column relates to the identically named amount in Section B.

value_domain: Exempt current pension income method indicator, Section A item 10 labels B and C
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 10 labels B and C
variable_description: Which method the fund used to work out its exempt pension income: segregated assets, proportionate, or both within the one year. The return puts this as two tick boxes rather than a single choice, and the ATO tells trustees to "Print X in the appropriate box or boxes (labels B or C or both labels B and C)". A fund using the proportionate method also answers a further question at label D on whether it obtained an actuarial certificate.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 10 labels B and C
value_definition: A code standing for a pair of tick boxes, so the domain has to allow segregated only, proportionate only and both, and is blank for a fund that paid no retirement phase pensions.
limitation: The method says nothing about how much income was exempt, and it does not identify which assets were segregated. A both-methods value is not a contradiction or an error: it is normal for a fund that starts or stops a pension part way through the year.
rationale: The Section A instructions show the question is answered with one or two ticks, which explains why a single code has to carry a combination.
evidence_quote: Print X in the appropriate box or boxes (labels B or C or both labels B and C) to indicate which method or methods you use to calculate the SMSF's ECPI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text as the description with the generic sentence twice, so it did not name the two methods or explain that both can be selected.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label Y, exempt current pension income
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label Y
variable_description: The exempt pension income figure as it appears inside the income statement, where it is subtracted from gross income to reach assessable income. The instructions make the arithmetic explicit: total assessable income at label V is gross income at label W less this amount. The ATO also warns against netting costs off it, since "Expenses incurred in gaining or producing exempt income aren't generally deductible" and belong in the non-deductible column of Section C.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label Y
value_definition: A dollar amount of exempt income, equal by instruction to the Section A item 10 figure on the same return, and entering the income statement as a subtraction rather than an addition.
limitation: It duplicates the Section A column, so adding the two double counts the fund's exempt income. Where they disagree the difference is a lodgment error rather than two different quantities.
rationale: The Section B instructions place label Y in the income calculation and repeat the requirement that it equal the Section A amount, which is what tells a reader the two columns are one number.
evidence_quote: Work out the SMSF's total assessable income or loss for 2024-25: subtract Y Exempt current pension income from W Gross income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and used the generic sentence twice, so a reader could not tell it from the Section A column of nearly the same name.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 15c label N, crypto asset investment
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2019 instructions, What's new in 2018-19
variable_description: The value of the fund's crypto holdings at 30 June, carved out into an asset label of its own. The label was added for 2018-19, when the ATO said crypto-currency "needs to be reported separately in the crypto-currency label within Section H Assets and liabilities". By the 2025 return the wording had shifted to crypto asset, and the cash and term deposits label explicitly pushes crypto here rather than allowing it to sit with cash.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2019 instructions, What's new in 2018-19
value_definition: A dollar value at a single date, 30 June, self-assessed by the trustee, covering crypto held as an investment of the fund.
limitation: The column is empty for every year before 2018-19, so a jump in the series is the label appearing rather than funds buying in. It is a closing value, not a purchase, a disposal or a gain, and crypto held on trust under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement is reported among the LRBA labels instead.
rationale: The 2018-19 what's new page dates the label's introduction, and the 2025 Section H instructions confirm where crypto sits relative to the cash label.
evidence_quote: If your SMSF holds investment in crypto-currency, this information needs to be reported separately in the crypto-currency label within Section H Assets and liabilities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other investments - Crypto-Currency' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the label starts in 2018-19 and is empty in the earlier tables.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 15b label E, cash and term deposits
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label E
variable_description: The fund's cash and term deposits at 30 June, valued in Australian dollars and held with Australian institutions. The ATO reads the label widely, giving "money market funds and cash management trusts" as examples, so it is broader than a bank balance. It excludes crypto assets, which go to the separate crypto label, and any deposit held on trust under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label E
value_definition: A dollar value at one date, 30 June, self-assessed by the trustee as part of the asset side of the fund's balance sheet, and one of the labels adding to total Australian and overseas assets.
limitation: A closing balance says nothing about the cash that moved through the fund during the year, so it cannot support a liquidity or turnover measure. Cash held outside Australia is reported among the overseas asset labels, so this is not the fund's total cash.
rationale: The Section H instructions for label E give the valuation date, the currency and the inclusions, and set the boundary against the crypto label on the same item.
evidence_quote: Write at label E the value (on 30 June 2025) in Australian currency of all cash accounts and term deposits held by the SMSF with Australian financial institutions (or other similar organisations).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Cash and term deposits' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is a 30 June point value or that managed cash trusts are inside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C item 12 label M1, tax losses deducted
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label M1
variable_description: Losses from earlier years that the fund is using this year, capped so that they cannot create a fresh loss. The ATO allows the claim "only to the extent that its total assessable income exceeds total deductions (other than tax losses)", and requires the losses to be applied against net exempt income first where the fund pays pensions. Capital losses are not part of it: they run through the net capital gain label and the Section E carry forward.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label M1
value_definition: A dollar deduction, self-assessed, drawn from a stock of carried forward losses that the fund reports separately at Section E label U.
limitation: It measures losses used, not losses held, so a fund with a large accumulated stock shows zero in a year with little income. Losses tied to non-arm's length income are excluded and can only reduce that income, so the column understates the fund's total loss position.
rationale: The label M1 instructions state the cap, the interaction with exempt income and the exclusion of capital losses, which are the three things that decide how the number reads.
evidence_quote: The SMSF can claim tax losses only to the extent that its total assessable income exceeds total deductions (other than tax losses).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Tax losses deducted' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not separate losses used in the year from losses carried forward.

value_domain: Single-letter other amounts category code beside Section C item 12 label L1
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, table 7
variable_description: A single letter naming the largest item inside the fund's other deductible expenses, taken from the ATO's table of other amounts categories. The published codes are A for balancing adjustment amounts, B for a contribution that is a fringe benefit, C for exclusion of personal contributions, E for environmental protection activities, F for forex losses, I for a listed investment company capital gain deduction, N for a deduction relating to foreign non-assessable non-exempt income, R for a return of contributions by a non-complying fund, T for taxation of financial arrangements amounts and O for anything else. The rule is to "print the code from Table 7 that best describes the largest amount" written at the label.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, table 7
value_definition: One letter from the closed Table 7 list, mandatory whenever an amount appears at label L1 and blank otherwise.
limitation: It describes only the biggest component, so a row coded F can hold forex losses that are a minority of the amount and several other items besides. The non-deductible column carries its own code, and the two are chosen independently and need not agree.
rationale: Table 7 in the Section C instructions is the code list this column is drawn from, and the surrounding text states the largest-amount selection rule.
evidence_quote: Print the code from Table 7 that best describes the largest amount you include at each of labels L1 and L2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Other deductions code' with the generic sentence twice, so the reader had no list of codes and no rule for how one is chosen.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C item 12 label N, total deductions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label N
variable_description: The fund's deductible expenses for the year added up, which the ATO reaches by the instruction "Add all the deductions from labels A1 to M1". That sweep takes in interest, capital works, decline in value, member insurance premiums, the auditor fee, investment and administration expenses, forestry payments, other amounts and prior year tax losses. Taxable income on the next line is total assessable income less this figure.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label N
value_definition: A dollar total covering the deductible column only. The non-deductible column totals separately at label Y, and the two add to label Z, total SMSF expenses.
limitation: It is not what the fund spent. Costs attributable to exempt pension income are not deductible and sit outside it, so a fund fully in retirement phase can run real expenses and still report a small total here.
rationale: The Section C instructions name the labels the total sweeps up and set it against the parallel non-deductible total, which is the distinction the column depends on.
evidence_quote: Add all the deductions from labels A1 to M1.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'TOTAL DEDUCTIONS' with the generic sentence twice, and never warned that the fund's non-deductible expenses are outside it.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 15b label F, debt securities
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label F
variable_description: The value at 30 June of bonds, notes and similar Australian debt instruments the fund holds directly. The ATO describes debt securities as instruments that "represent borrowings that must be repaid by the issuer", and folds in hybrid securities that combine bonds or notes with swaps, forwards, futures or options. Only securities traded or available in Australia belong here; overseas debt is reported among other overseas assets.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label F
value_definition: A dollar value at 30 June, self-assessed, covering Australian debt and hybrid securities the fund holds in its own right.
limitation: It does not separate a plain bond from a hybrid carrying equity risk, so it is a weak proxy for the fund's credit exposure. Debt securities held on trust under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement are excluded and appear in the LRBA other label.
rationale: The Section H instructions define debt securities for this label and set out both the Australian boundary and the LRBA carve-out.
evidence_quote: are typically financial securities which establish ownership and represent borrowings that must be repaid by the issuer
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Debt securities' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said hybrids are inside the label or that overseas debt is not.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label J, unfranked dividend amount
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label J
variable_description: Unfranked dividends, including unfranked non-share dividends, paid directly to the fund. The ATO says the amount "shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income", so it is a gross figure. Dividends that reached the fund inside a trust or partnership distribution are excluded and reported at the trust and partnership labels, which makes this a measure of direct shareholdings only.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label J
value_definition: A dollar amount of assessable dividend income, gross, covering unfranked dividends and unfranked non-share dividends received directly.
limitation: It is not the fund's dividend income: franked dividends, New Zealand company dividends and dividends inside trust or partnership distributions all sit at other labels, and non-arm's length private company dividends are carved out again. A zero is common for a fund holding blue chip Australian shares, which pay franked dividends.
rationale: The label J instructions state the gross basis and list every category of dividend that is directed elsewhere, which defines what the column can and cannot count.
evidence_quote: Write at label J the total amount of unfranked dividends, and unfranked non-share dividends, that were paid to the SMSF.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Unfranked dividend amount' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the label is direct holdings only and gross of expenses.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C item 12 label E1, deductible decline in value of depreciating assets
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label E1
variable_description: The deductible share of the year's decline in value of the fund's depreciating assets, most often fittings inside a property it rents out. The ATO puts at label E1 the deductible amount, "for example, the decline in value of a depreciating asset that the SMSF uses for the purposes of gaining or producing assessable income", and sends the part attributable to exempt pension income to the paired non-deductible label. Second-hand depreciating assets in existing residential property have been largely excluded since 1 July 2017.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label E1
value_definition: A dollar deduction for one income year under the capital allowance rules, self-assessed, rather than the cost or the written down value of the asset.
limitation: It cannot be read as the fund's capital spending, and it names no asset. Where the fund pays pensions the same asset's write-down is split across the deductible and non-deductible columns, so this one alone understates the decline.
rationale: The Section C instructions define the deductible half of the decline in value pair and give the exempt income split that determines what lands in this column.
evidence_quote: Write at label E1 the deductible amount for the decline in value of the SMSF's depreciating assets, for example, the decline in value of a depreciating asset that the SMSF uses for the purposes of gaining or producing assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the write-down is split between a deductible and a non-deductible column.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 15b label J, limited recourse borrowing arrangement assets
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, labels J1 to J6 and J
variable_description: The value at 30 June of assets held on trust as security for the fund's limited recourse borrowing arrangements. The ATO is emphatic about which side of the arrangement this is: the labels carry "the values of the assets held on trust under limited recourse borrowing arrangements and not the amounts borrowed", with the loan reported as a liability further down. The total covers assets held "including instalment warrants", which is the wording the abbreviated column name preserves from an earlier edition of this label.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, labels J1 to J6 and J
value_definition: A dollar value at 30 June, being the sum of the arrangement sub-labels for Australian residential and non-residential property, overseas property, Australian and overseas shares, and other assets.
limitation: It is the geared asset, so it overstates the fund's own stake by the size of the loan sitting in the liabilities item. As a single total it cannot say whether a fund is geared into property or shares without the sub-labels, and the abbreviated name still points at derivatives, which the current form reports among other assets instead.
rationale: The custodian's description for this column is the current label J wording, and the Section H instructions confirm both what the total holds and that instalment warrants sit inside it, which reconciles the label with the older abbreviation.
evidence_quote: The amounts you write at labels J1 to J6 are the values of the assets held on trust under limited recourse borrowing arrangements and not the amounts borrowed or the amount of outstanding borrowings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Limited recourse borrowing arrangements' with the generic sentence twice, leaving the mismatch against the derivatives-and-warrants column name unexplained and the asset against loan distinction unstated.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C item 12 label G1, death benefit increase
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2019 instructions, Section C item 12, G1 Death benefit increase
variable_description: A deduction for topping up a lump sum death benefit so that it is not reduced by the tax once paid on the underlying contributions. The ATO says a death benefit increase "is also known as an 'anti detriment payment'", and confines it to a member who died before 1 July 2017 with the benefit paid by 30 June 2019: "This deduction is not available for later financial years." The deduction is the tax saving amount divided by the low tax component rate of 15 per cent, so it is far larger than the top-up itself.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2019 instructions, Section C item 12, G1 Death benefit increase
value_definition: A dollar deduction, self-assessed and grossed up from the tax saving amount actually added to the benefit, claimed in the year the lump sum was paid.
limitation: The column closes after 2018-19, so a zero in later tables is the law ending rather than funds declining to claim. The figure is also not money the beneficiary received: at a 15 per cent divisor it is close to seven times the top-up.
rationale: The 2019 edition carries a dedicated page for label G1 that both defines the deduction and states the date it stops being available, which is what a reader needs to interpret a run of zeros.
evidence_quote: This deduction is not available for later financial years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Death benefit increase' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not identify the anti-detriment deduction or note that the label is closed from 2019-20.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C item 12 label F1, deductible insurance premiums for members
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label F1
variable_description: The deductible share of insurance premiums the fund paid to cover its members. The ATO scopes label F1 as premiums "to provide benefits upon the death, existence of a terminal medical condition, or temporary or permanent disability of a member". The custodian's wording is the label's older name; by the 2018-19 return the same label reads Insurance premiums - members, and premiums for other events such as funeral cover are non-deductible and go to the paired column.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label F1
value_definition: A dollar deduction, self-assessed, which a complying fund may instead work out under the section 295-470 formula rather than claiming the premium it actually paid.
limitation: It is not the fund's insurance bill. Only part of a bundled policy or an own-occupation total and permanent disability premium is deductible, and the remainder appears in the non-deductible column, so this column alone understates the cover bought.
rationale: The current instructions define label F1 in terms of the same events the older label name lists, which anchors the custodian's wording to a live label, and they set out the deductible against non-deductible split.
evidence_quote: Write at label F1 the amount that is deductible for insurance premiums to provide benefits upon the death, existence of a terminal medical condition, or temporary or permanent disability of a member
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the retired label name with the generic sentence twice, so a reader could not match it to the insurance premiums label on later returns.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label L, dividend franking credit
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label L
variable_description: Franking credits attached to dividends paid directly to the fund, counted first as income and then claimed back as an offset. The ATO restricts the label to credits "for which the SMSF is entitled to a franking credits tax offset", and requires the same figure to be repeated at Section D label E1 for a complying fund. Credits inside trust or partnership distributions, and Australian credits from New Zealand franking companies, are excluded and reported at their own labels.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label L
value_definition: A dollar amount of imputation credit reported as assessable income, gross, sitting beside the franked dividend it attaches to on the same return.
limitation: It is not tax the fund paid, and adding it to franked dividends gives a grossed up figure rather than cash received. Credits the fund is not entitled to use are reported nowhere on the return, so the column understates the credits attached to the shares it holds.
rationale: The label L instructions set the entitlement condition and the requirement to carry the same amount into the offset section, which explains why the figure appears twice on one return.
evidence_quote: for which the SMSF is entitled to a franking credits tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the credit is income here and an offset in Section D.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label H, eligible credits
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H
variable_description: The fund's withholding and interest credits added together near the end of the tax calculation. The ATO builds it from labels H2, H3, H5, H6 and H8, covering foreign resident withholding, ABN or TFN not quoted, closely held trust amounts, interest on the no-TFN offset and foreign resident capital gains withholding. Where the total beats the tax and the levy, "the SMSF may be entitled to a refund of the excess".
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H
value_definition: A dollar subtotal, being the sum of the credit sub-labels on the same return, all of them amounts already withheld from the fund or owed to it by the ATO.
limitation: Adding it to its own components double counts. It also leaves out the two credits that matter most to a typical SMSF: franking credits, which enter as a refundable offset, and PAYG instalments raised, which sit at a separate label further down.
rationale: The eligible credit instructions enumerate the labels the total is made from and describe its role in producing a refund, which is what distinguishes it from the individual credits.
evidence_quote: If the amount of eligible credits exceeds the tax payable and the levy amount then the SMSF may be entitled to a refund of the excess.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Eligible credits' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the column is a subtotal of five other columns on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at member label A, employer contributions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label A
variable_description: Contributions an employer made for this member during the year, taken widely. The ATO includes contributions made "under a salary sacrifice arrangement or to meet the employer's obligations under the super guarantee, awards, agreements or other obligations", together with super guarantee charge shortfall amounts and transfers out of the ATO's super holding accounts special account. Contributions the member made themselves belong at the personal contributions label even where they have claimed a deduction for them.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label A
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member for one income year, gross of the contributions tax the fund pays, recorded when the fund received the money rather than when it allocated it.
limitation: It cannot be read as the member's wage or their super guarantee entitlement, because salary sacrifice and voluntary employer amounts are mixed into the same figure. For a defined benefit interest the number is a notional taxed contribution, a formula output rather than cash received.
rationale: The member section instructions define what an employer contribution covers for this label, and separate it from the member's own contributions, which is the distinction the column turns on.
evidence_quote: contributions made by an employer for an employee (including contributions made under a salary sacrifice arrangement or to meet the employer's obligations under the super guarantee, awards, agreements or other obligations)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Employer contributions' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say salary sacrifice is inside the figure and personal deductible contributions are not.

value_domain: Signed dollar amount reported at member label O, allocated earnings or losses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label O
variable_description: Earnings allocated to this member's account for the year, less the expenses, taxes and losses charged against it. The ATO writes the label as a catch-all: it holds "any transactions affecting the member's closing balance that you haven't included at another question in Section F or Section G", including investment earnings, allocated costs, insurance proceeds for death or disability cover, and reserve allocations not reported at the two transfer-from-reserve labels. A negative amount is flagged with a loss box rather than a minus sign.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label O
value_definition: A signed dollar amount for one member for one income year, net of the tax and expenses allocated to that account.
limitation: It is not an investment return, and it cannot be turned into one without an account balance to divide by, since the tax and expense drag inside it cannot be separated. Anything the trustee could not place elsewhere lands here, so it is not a clean earnings series.
rationale: The label O instructions define it explicitly as the residual for the member row, which is the fact that decides whether it can be used as an earnings measure.
evidence_quote: Include at label O any transactions affecting the member's closing balance that you haven't included at another question in Section F or Section G.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Allocated earnings or losses' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is net of tax and expenses or that it is a residual.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label D3, early stage investor tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D3
variable_description: An offset for the fund investing in an early stage innovation company during the year, subject to a group-wide ceiling.
