The ATO caps it: "The maximum offset (including current year and carried forward prior year amounts) that the fund, and its affiliates combined, can claim in 2024-25 is $200,000." Where the sophisticated investor test is failed for even one investment, the fund cannot claim at all if it paid more than $50,000 for eligible shares, and entitlement can also arrive through a partnership or trust that invested.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D3
value_definition: A dollar offset, non-refundable but able to be carried forward, worked out from what the fund paid for eligible shares in the year rather than from the value of the holding.
limitation: It measures a tax entitlement, not the size of the investment, and it is reduced by claims made by the fund's affiliates, so it understates a related group's early stage exposure. The shares themselves sit inside the unlisted shares asset label with no link back to this column.
rationale: The label D3 instructions give the ceiling, the sophisticated investor rule and the partnership and trust route, which are the constraints that shape the distribution of this column.
evidence_quote: The maximum offset (including current year and carried forward prior year amounts) that the fund, and its affiliates combined, can claim in 2024-25 is $200,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the offset is capped across affiliates or that it derives from what was paid for the shares.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label D4, early stage investor tax offset carried forward
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D4
variable_description: Unused early stage investor offset brought into this year from an earlier one, kept apart from the current year claim. It also eats into the ceiling for the current year: step 5 of the label D3 calculation is to "Subtract from $200,000 the amount (if any) reported at label D4 Early stage investor tax offset carried forward from previous year". Whether an amount can be carried forward at all is decided by Division 65 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D4
value_definition: A dollar offset brought forward, non-refundable, reported alongside the current year claim within the non-refundable carry forward group.
limitation: It does not date the investment that generated it, which may be several years old, and it is not simply the unused remainder of an earlier claim once the carry forward adjustments are applied. A zero can mean the earlier offset was fully used, that none was ever claimed, or that the carry forward failed the Division 65 tests.
rationale: The label D4 instructions and the step 5 calculation at label D3 together fix what the column is and how it interacts with the current year claim on the same row.
evidence_quote: Step 5: Subtract from $200,000 the amount (if any) reported at label D4 Early stage investor tax offset carried forward from previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the carried forward amount from the current year offset in the neighbouring column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label D1, early stage venture capital limited partnership tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D1
variable_description: An offset for what the fund contributed to an early stage venture capital limited partnership during the year. For a limited partner the ATO sets the offset at "10% of the lesser of" the fund's contributions to the partnership in the year and its share of the partnership's eligible venture capital investments, and the partnership "must have become unconditionally registered on or after 7 December 2015". A fund can also become entitled through a partnership or trust, which has to notify it in writing.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D1
value_definition: A dollar offset, non-refundable with a carry forward, calculated from contributions made in the year rather than from the value of the underlying venture investments.
limitation: At 10 per cent of contributions the offset is roughly a tenth of the money committed, so it cannot stand in for the investment, which is not reported on this row at all. The registration date rule means an older partnership generates nothing here however much the fund puts in.
rationale: The label D1 instructions give the 10 per cent formula, the lesser-of test and the registration date, which are what determine when this column can be non-zero.
evidence_quote: The ESVCLP must have become unconditionally registered on or after 7 December 2015.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is a tenth of contributions or that the partnership registration date gates it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label D2, ESVCLP tax offset carried forward
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D2
variable_description: Unused venture capital partnership offset brought forward from an earlier year, after the exempt income reduction has been applied. The ATO cuts the carried forward amount "by 30 cents for every dollar of net exempt income, provided the SMSF had taxable income for that year", and asks for the reduced figure: write "the amount of unused ESVCLP tax offset carried forward from the previous year, less any reductions, if applicable". It sits beside the current year contribution offset in the same non-refundable carry forward group.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label D2
value_definition: A dollar offset brought forward and already reduced for net exempt income, non-refundable, reported separately from the current year claim.
limitation: Because of the exempt income reduction it will not reconcile against the earlier return's unused amount, so it cannot be used to audit a fund's offset history. It also cannot be attributed to a particular partnership.
rationale: The label D2 instructions state both the reduction rule and the requirement to report the reduced figure, which is the fact that stops the column being read as a simple carry forward.
evidence_quote: The unused ESVCLP tax offset carried forward from a previous year is reduced by 30 cents for every dollar of net exempt income, provided the SMSF had taxable income for that year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that the carried forward amount is adjusted before it is written.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label E4, exploration credit tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E4
variable_description: A refundable offset for exploration credits a minerals exploration company distributed to the fund. The ATO makes it mechanical: "The amount of the tax offset is the total value of exploration credits the SMSF received in the income year", available where the fund was an Australian resident for the whole year, with special rules where the credits come through a partnership or trust. It is refundable, so a fund with no tax to pay still gets the cash.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label E4
value_definition: A dollar refundable offset equal to credits issued to the fund by the company, set outside the fund rather than calculated by the trustee.
limitation: It does not measure the fund's stake in the company, because a credit depends on that company's exploration spend and how it chose to allocate credits. It also does not distinguish credits issued under the Exploration Development Incentive from those under the later Junior Minerals Exploration Incentive.
rationale: The label E4 instructions define the amount as the credits received and name the residence condition, which is what a reader needs before treating the column as an investment signal.
evidence_quote: The amount of the tax offset is the total value of exploration credits the SMSF received in the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Exploration credit tax offset' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is set by the issuing company rather than by the fund.

value_domain: Financial year of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO forms and instructions index, plus the fplida table registry for the SMSF year coverage
variable_description: The income year of the SMSF annual return the row comes from, running 1 July to 30 June. PLIDA splits the product into a fund level table and a member level table for each year from 2007-08 to 2022-23, so the column is constant inside a table and earns its keep only once the years are stacked. Because one return carries both parts, a fund's row and its members' rows for a year share this value and join on the fund identifier.
description_source: ATO forms and instructions index, plus the fplida table registry for the SMSF year coverage
value_definition: A financial year label, one value per table, derived by the custodian from the income year written on the return.
limitation: It is the year the return covers, not the year it was lodged, and SMSF returns are often lodged many months after the year ends. It also does not bound a fund's life: a registered fund can lodge for a year in which it did nothing, and a fund that closes still lodges for the year it wound up.
rationale: The ATO publishes one set of annual return instructions per income year, which fixes what a year value on this form means; the mapping to one table per year is read from the registry's own table list. No single ATO page defines this custodian-derived column, so the general forms and instructions index is cited.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Financial year (derived from income year)' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the column is constant within a table or how the fund and member tables line up on it.

value_domain: SMSF benefit structure code reported at Section A item 8 label B
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 8 label B and table 1
variable_description: A one letter code for how the fund pays benefits: accumulation, defined benefit, or a hybrid of the two. The ATO's table 1 gives code A for an accumulation fund, code D for a defined benefit fund that was already paying a defined benefit pension before 12 May 2004, and code E for a hybrid with both kinds of member. It notes that "Most SMSFs will use code A", and that a fund keeps code A even when one of its accounts is supporting a pension.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 8 label B and table 1
value_definition: A single letter from a closed list of three, self-assessed at item 8 label B and reported once per fund per year.
limitation: It does not tell you whether the fund pays a pension, which is asked separately at item 10, so code A funds include many in retirement phase. The defined benefit code is closed by its pre-2004 test, so a fund established later cannot carry it however its deed is written.
rationale: Table 1 of the Section A instructions is the published code list for this label and gives the definition attached to each letter.
evidence_quote: Print at label B the code from Table 1 that best describes the benefit structure of the SMSF. Most SMSFs will use code A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Fund benefit structure' with the generic sentence twice and no code list, so a reader could not tell what values to expect or what they mean.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at Section H item 15f label A, LRBA borrowings from a licensed financial institution
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, item 15f label A
variable_description: Whether the fund's limited recourse borrowing came from a bank or similar lender rather than from a related party. The ATO says a licensed financial institution "includes a bank or authorised deposit-taking institution", listing Australian and foreign banks, credit unions, building societies and finance companies. The answer is No if any part of any of the fund's arrangements was borrowed from a related party or an unlicensed lender, which makes it a strict test rather than a majority one.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, item 15f label A
value_definition: A yes or no tick box, answered only by funds that report limited recourse borrowing assets, and left blank where all the arrangement labels are zero.
limitation: One box covers the whole fund, so a No cannot say how many arrangements were related party loans or how large they were. A blank is ambiguous between a fund with no such borrowing and one that skipped a question the ATO asks it not to answer.
rationale: The item 15f instructions define the lender test, list the qualifying institutions and give the rule for funds with more than one arrangement, which is what makes a No interpretable.
evidence_quote: Also answer No if the fund holds more than one LRBA, and the money to acquire at least one (or part) of an asset has been borrowed from a source other than a licensed financial institution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say a single related party loan turns the whole answer to No.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 16 label V3, other borrowings
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label V3
variable_description: Borrowings still outstanding at 30 June that are neither limited recourse arrangements nor permissible temporary borrowings. The ATO asks for "the value (on 30 June 2025) of all other borrowing amounts", including accrued interest, as the third of three borrowing labels that add to the fund's total borrowings. Most funds leave it blank, since "SMSFs are prohibited from borrowing to invest except in certain limited circumstances".
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label V3
value_definition: A dollar liability at 30 June, including accrued interest, self-assessed by the trustee and reported alongside the limited recourse and temporary borrowing labels.
limitation: It does not say who lent the money or on what terms, and the licensed lender and personal guarantee questions cover only limited recourse arrangements, so a borrowing reported here has no counterparty information anywhere on the return.
rationale: The item 16 instructions define label V3 as the residual borrowing category and state the general prohibition that makes a non-zero value notable.
evidence_quote: Write at label V3 the value (on 30 June 2025) of all other borrowing amounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other borrowings' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not place the label against the two named borrowing categories beside it.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at member label Y, outstanding limited recourse borrowing arrangement amount
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label Y
variable_description: The share of the fund's outstanding limited recourse loan attributed to this member, added into their total superannuation balance. It is reported only where the arrangement began or was refinanced on or after 1 July 2018, and then only where the lender is an associate of the fund or the member has met a condition of release with a nil cashing restriction. The ATO caps the column against the fund level figure: the total across members "shouldn't be greater than the amount you report at Section H" for limited recourse borrowings.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G member and supplementary member information, label Y
value_definition: A dollar amount at 30 June for one member, being their attributable share of an outstanding loan rather than the whole loan or the geared asset.
limitation: A blank does not mean the fund has no borrowing: most geared funds report nothing here because their arrangement predates 1 July 2018 or their lender is a bank. It is also not a debt of the member, only an adjustment used in the balance test.
rationale: The member section instructions set out the 1 July 2018 start, the two qualifying conditions and the cap against the fund level borrowing label, all of which decide when the column can be non-zero.
evidence_quote: Label Y represents the member's outstanding limited recourse borrowing arrangement (LRBA) amount at 30 June (if applicable).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the column is empty before 2018-19 or that it only captures associate lenders and members past a condition of release.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 16 label V2, permissible temporary borrowings
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label V2
variable_description: Short term borrowings the law lets the fund make, still outstanding at 30 June. The ATO ties them to subsections 67(2), (2A) and (3) of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993, allowing "borrowing money for a maximum of 90 days to meet benefit payments due and required to be made to members" or up to 7 days to settle a securities transaction. In each case the borrowing must not exceed 10 per cent of the value of the fund's total assets.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label V2
value_definition: A dollar liability at 30 June, including accrued interest, and one of the three borrowing labels that add to the fund's total borrowings.
limitation: A single 30 June snapshot misses borrowing that was taken and repaid during the year, which is exactly what these 7 and 90 day provisions are for, so the column badly understates how often they are used.
rationale: The item 16 instructions name the statutory provisions, the day limits and the 10 per cent asset cap, which together explain why the reported balances are small and rare.
evidence_quote: borrowing money for a maximum of 90 days to meet benefit payments due and required to be made to members, by law or by the governing rules
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Permissible temporary borrowings' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say what makes a borrowing permissible or that the figure is a year end snapshot.

value_domain: Dollar value at 30 June reported at Section H item 16 label V1, borrowings for limited recourse borrowing arrangements
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label V1
variable_description: What the fund still owed at 30 June under all its limited recourse borrowing arrangements, which is the measure of how geared it is. The ATO separates it from the asset side: write at label V1 "the value of outstanding borrowings held under all limited recourse borrowing arrangements at 30 June 2025", while the assets held on trust are reported in the asset item. A fund reporting a figure here must also complete the arrangement asset total and both LRBA questions at item 15f.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, label V1
value_definition: A dollar liability at 30 June, including accrued interest, covering every limited recourse arrangement the fund has open.
limitation: One number for all arrangements cannot separate a bank loan from a related party loan, or one property from several, and the member level attribution column captures only a narrow subset of these loans. It is also not the fund's total debt, since temporary and other borrowings sit at their own labels.
rationale: The item 16 instructions define label V1 as the outstanding borrowing, distinguish it from the asset labels and list the companion labels a fund must complete, which is how the gearing picture is assembled.
evidence_quote: Write at label V1 the value of outstanding borrowings held under all limited recourse borrowing arrangements at 30 June 2025.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the loan from the geared assets reported in the same section.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at Section A item 10 label E, other assessable income
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 10 label E
variable_description: A routing question that decides whether the fund fills in the income section at all. The ATO treats a No as the statement that "The SMSF didn't receive any no-TFN-quoted contributions or have other assessable income for the income year", and sends the trustee straight past Section B to the deductions section; a Yes sends them into item 11.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 10 label E
value_definition: A yes or no tick box at Section A item 10 label E, answered once per fund per year, and reached only after the exempt pension income questions above it.
limitation: A No does not mean the fund had no money coming in, since exempt current pension income is not assessable and a fund fully in retirement phase can earn substantially and still answer No. It therefore cannot be used as an activity or dormancy test.
rationale: The Section A instructions state what each answer asserts and where it sends the trustee, which is what makes the indicator readable as a routing switch rather than an income measure.
evidence_quote: No - The SMSF didn't receive any no-TFN-quoted contributions or have other assessable income for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that exempt pension income falls outside what the question asks about.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at Section H item 15f label B, personal guarantees or other security for an LRBA
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, item 15f label B
variable_description: Whether a member or a related party personally guaranteed, or gave other security for, the fund's limited recourse borrowing. The ATO asks for a Yes where any single arrangement was supported that way: answer Yes if "the fund holds more than one LRBA, and a member or related party has used a personal guarantee or other security for at least one of the LRBAs". Despite the amount suffix on the column name, the form carries a tick box rather than a dollar figure.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H assets and liabilities items 15 and 16, item 15f label B
value_definition: A yes or no tick box, completed only where the fund reports limited recourse borrowing assets, and left unmarked where those labels are zero or blank.
limitation: It cannot size the guarantee or say whose it was, and it does not separate a personal guarantee from other security such as a mortgage over a member's own property. The column name promises an amount the form never collects.
rationale: The item 15f instructions give the question and the any-one-arrangement rule, and show the answer is a tick box, which corrects what the column name implies.
evidence_quote: the fund holds more than one LRBA, and a member or related party has used a personal guarantee or other security for at least one of the LRBAs
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that the amount-suffixed column is an indicator.

value_domain: Date the fund was wound up, reported at Section A item 9 as DDMMYYYY
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 9
variable_description: The day the fund stopped holding assets, supplied only where the trustees answered that the fund was wound up during the year. The ATO requires the date to fall inside the income year and to be "the date on which the fund no longer held any assets", not the date the decision was taken or the last return lodged. A fund reporting one must also complete the supervisory levy adjustment for wound up funds in Section D.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A SMSF information items 1 to 10, item 9
value_definition: A calendar date written DDMMYYYY, self-reported, and present only on the final return a fund lodges.
limitation: It marks when the assets ran out, not when the fund stopped operating or when its registration was cancelled, and it is blank for a fund that simply stopped lodging. It also says nothing about where the money went: benefit payments and rollovers out are on the member rows.
rationale: The item 9 instructions fix both the definition of the date and the range it must sit in, which is what lets it be used as an exit marker.
evidence_quote: That date must be a date from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 and be the date on which the fund no longer held any assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label and format with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the date means the fund had no assets left, nor that it appears only on a final return.

value_domain: Whole hours reported in Section J, time taken to prepare the annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections J and K other information and declarations
variable_description: The hours the trustees and their agent say they spent preparing this return, collected to gauge compliance cost. The ATO states plainly that "Your response to this question is voluntary", and asks for time rounded up to the nearest hour covering reading the instructions, collecting information, doing the calculations and completing the form. The count is supposed to include the trustee, the tax agent and anyone else who helped.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections J and K other information and declarations
value_definition: A whole number of hours, self-reported and optional, despite the amount suffix on the column name.
limitation: Being voluntary and unverified it cannot support a population estimate of compliance cost, and a blank means no answer rather than no time. It also excludes the annual audit that every SMSF must obtain, so it is not the full burden of the fund's yearly obligations.
rationale: The Section J instructions state the voluntary basis, the rounding rule and the activities to include, which are what determine whether the column can be analysed at all.
evidence_quote: We want to reduce the cost of complying with the SMSF's taxation and regulatory obligations. Your response to this question is voluntary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the answer is optional or that the unit is whole hours.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label H8, credit for foreign resident capital gains withholding
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H8
variable_description: Tax a purchaser withheld from the fund on a property sale and paid to the ATO, credited back in the fund's tax calculation. The ATO restricts the claim to what was actually remitted: "You should only claim at label H8 a credit equal to the amount of foreign resident capital gains withholding paid by a purchaser to the ATO on your behalf", with the ATO having confirmed the amount. Ordinary foreign resident withholding is a different credit and goes to label H2.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label H8
value_definition: A dollar amount of withholding tax remitted by a third party, including the fund's share of such credits arriving through a trust distribution, and part of the eligible credits total.
limitation: It is not evidence that the fund is a foreign resident, since the regime withholds from a vendor who has not established otherwise. It also gives neither the sale price nor the gain: the withholding is a slice of the purchase price and the capital gain is reported in the income section.
rationale: The label H8 instructions define what may be claimed, require ATO confirmation of the amount and separate it from the neighbouring foreign resident withholding credit.
evidence_quote: You should only claim at label H8 a credit equal to the amount of foreign resident capital gains withholding paid by a purchaser to the ATO on your behalf.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label with the generic sentence twice, so it did not separate capital gains withholding from ordinary foreign resident withholding.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label D1, gross foreign income
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label D1
variable_description: All the assessable income the fund earned from foreign sources, before any expense or foreign tax is taken off. The ATO says the amount "shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing related to the income" and that it includes the foreign tax paid on it. Foreign dividends, foreign interest, foreign income inside trust and partnership distributions and controlled foreign company attributable income all land here, while foreign capital gains and foreign exchange gains are reported elsewhere.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label D1
value_definition: A dollar amount of gross assessable foreign income, self-assessed, with an ATO concession letting a fund report a net after-tax figure where it cannot obtain the gross amount from a trust distribution.
limitation: That concession makes rows inconsistent: some are pre-tax and some post-tax, and nothing on the return flags which. It is also a poor proxy for offshore exposure, because income from an Australian managed fund that invests abroad is not foreign source income for this label.
rationale: The label D1 instructions set the gross basis, list the inclusions and exclusions and state the net-amount concession, which is the flaw a reader most needs to know about.
evidence_quote: The amount at label D1 shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing related to the income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross foreign income' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount includes foreign tax paid or that a net figure is sometimes permitted.

value_domain: Signed dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label D, net foreign income
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label D
variable_description: Foreign income after the losses and costs of earning it, which is the figure that flows into the fund's gross income. The ATO derives it from the gross label by subtracting foreign source losses for the year other than capital losses, and "deductible expenses to the extent to which they were incurred in producing that foreign income". Debt deductions are not netted off unless they belong to an overseas permanent establishment, and a negative result is marked with a loss box.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label D
value_definition: A signed dollar amount, self-assessed, and mandatory whenever a value appears at the gross foreign income label on the same return.
limitation: It is not gross foreign income less foreign tax: the tax stays inside the gross figure and is relieved separately through the foreign income tax offset. The expenses netted off here are also missing from the deductions section, so total deductions understate the fund's costs by this amount.
rationale: The label D instructions give the subtraction, name what may and may not be taken off, and tie the label to the gross figure beside it.
evidence_quote: deductible expenses to the extent to which they were incurred in producing that foreign income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net foreign income' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say what is netted off or that the netted expenses never reach Section C.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D item 13 label C1, foreign income tax offset
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label C1
variable_description: Relief for foreign tax the fund already paid on income Australia taxes again, capped by a statutory limit. The ATO restricts the offset to the lesser of the foreign income tax paid and the fund's own limit, which is "$1,000 or the amount calculated under paragraph 770-75(2)(b) of the ITAA 1997, whichever is greater". It sits in the non-refundable, non-carry-forward group, so anything above the fund's gross tax is lost rather than banked.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D income tax calculation statement item 13, label C1
value_definition: A dollar offset, self-assessed, reported alongside rebates and tax offsets in the first offset group of the tax calculation.
limitation: It is not the foreign tax the fund paid, because the limit can bite, and a fund with substantial exempt pension income can pay foreign tax and claim little or none of it. The column also cannot be attributed to a country or an investment.
rationale: The label C1 instructions state the lesser-of rule and the statutory limit, and the surrounding text places the offset in the group whose excess is lost.
evidence_quote: the SMSF's foreign income tax offset limit (which is $1,000 or the amount calculated under paragraph 770-75(2)(b) of the ITAA 1997, whichever is greater)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Foreign income tax offset' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is capped or that any excess cannot be carried forward.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B item 11 label K, franked dividend amount
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label K
variable_description: Franked dividends, including franked non-share dividends, paid directly to the fund and reported without the credits attached to them. The ATO says the amount "shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income", and directs the franking credits to their own label. Franked dividends received through a trust or partnership, from a New Zealand franking company, or as non-arm's length income are all reported at other labels.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B income item 11, label K
value_definition: A dollar amount of assessable dividend income, gross, covering direct holdings only and excluding the imputation credits carried with the dividend.
limitation: Adding it to the franking credit label gives a grossed up dividend, which is neither cash received nor taxable income on its own, so the two columns should not be summed casually. It also cannot stand for Australian share income, since most funds hold shares through managed investments whose distributions are reported as trust income.
rationale: The label K instructions set the gross basis, exclude the credits and list the routes that send franked dividends to other labels, which bounds what the column counts.
evidence_quote: Write at label K the total amount of franked dividends, and franked non-share dividends, that were paid to the SMSF.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Franked dividend amount' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the credits are excluded or that indirect dividends are elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C item 12 label U1, deductible forestry managed investment scheme expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label U1
variable_description: The deductible part of payments the fund made into a forestry managed investment scheme during the year. The ATO asks for "the total amount of deductible payments made under an FMIS", and pushes out payments that relate to foreign income, non-arm's length income or exempt pension income, which go to the paired non-deductible label. Where the fund pays pensions the payment is apportioned before it is written here.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C deductions and non-deductible expenses item 12, label U1
value_definition: A dollar deduction, self-assessed, for payments made under the scheme in the income year rather than the value of the forestry interest the fund holds.
limitation: It records money paid out, not the scheme's performance, and it names no scheme. Income from the scheme appears at its own income label, and a later harvest or sale is a capital gains event rather than a reversal of this deduction.
rationale: The label U1 instructions define the deductible half of the forestry pair and set out the exclusions that decide how much of a payment reaches this column.
evidence_quote: Write at label U1 the total amount of deductible payments made under an FMIS.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Forestry managed investment scheme deduction' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is a payment or that it is split against a non-deductible column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label X, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label X
variable_description: What the fund earned from forestry managed investment schemes, before any of the costs of earning it. The ATO instruction is "Write at label X the SMSF's income from all FMISs", and adds that "The amount at label X shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income." Capital gains on a forestry interest are excluded here and go to label A instead, so a fund that sold its interest can show nothing at X in the year it made the most money from the scheme.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label X
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, gross of expenses, covering the fund's share of income from every forestry scheme it held. Payments the fund makes to the scheme are reported separately in Section C at labels U1 and U2.
limitation: It does not tell you whether the fund made or lost money on forestry, because the matching outgoings sit in another section and capital gains are pushed to the net capital gain label. The forestry scheme rules in Division 394 also began part way through the period this asset covers, so a zero in an early year can mean the label was not yet in use rather than that the fund held nothing.
rationale: The variable name expands to forestry managed investment scheme income, which is a named label of Section B of the SMSF annual return, and the ATO publishes what belongs at that label and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: Write at label X the SMSF's income from all FMISs. The amount at label X shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording 'Forestry managed investment scheme income' as its own description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so it never said the amount was gross or that capital gains are excluded.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, Section A item 8 label C, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10, item 8 label C
variable_description: Whether the fund's trust deed lets it accept government super co-contributions and low income super amounts for its members. The ATO asks "Does the fund trust deed allow the SMSF to accept the government's super co-contribution and low income super amount for all eligible members?" and the trustee marks yes or no. It is a statement about the deed, not a record that any co-contribution was received; the money itself, when it arrives, is reported for each member at Section F label M.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10, item 8 label C
value_definition: A two-state indicator taken from a tick box. The question widened over time: the low income super amount was added to a box that had asked only about the government super co-contribution, so the wording is not identical across years.
limitation: A yes does not mean the fund received anything, and a no does not mean a member was ineligible - it means the deed as written would not let the fund take the payment. The answer also carries an administrative condition rather than a member outcome, since a fund answering yes must supply an electronic service address.
rationale: The custodian's description repeats the wording of the Section A item 8 question, and the ATO instruction for that label states the question and the yes or no rule.
evidence_quote: Does the fund trust deed allow the SMSF to accept the government's super co-contribution and low income super amount for all eligible members?
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the question text with no answer domain and the same generic sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that this describes the deed rather than a payment.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label I, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label I
variable_description: Everything the fund was distributed by partnerships in the year, reported as one figure rather than split by the type of income inside it. The ATO says "Write at label I the total of all gross distributions from partnerships received in 2024-25" and "If the total amount is a loss, print L in the LOSS box." Interest, rent and franking credits that came through a partnership belong here rather than at their own labels, while capital gains, foreign income and non-arm's length amounts are stripped out to labels A, D1 and U3.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label I
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount that can be negative, with the sign carried by a separate loss flag rather than by the number. It is a mixed bundle: any franking credit the fund can use as an offset is included in the amount as well as claimed in Section D.
limitation: It cannot be read as investment income of a particular kind, because the composition of a partnership distribution is not reported. Nor can it be compared straight against label C or label B, since amounts that would sit there are diverted here whenever they arrive through a partnership.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label I heading, and the ATO instruction lists exactly what is included in and excluded from that label.
evidence_quote: Write at label I the total of all gross distributions from partnerships received in 2024-25. If the total amount is a loss, print L in the LOSS box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the figure mixes income types or that it can be a loss.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label W, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label W
variable_description: The fund's total income for the year before any pension exemption is taken out. The ATO builds it by adding the income labels: "Add the amounts from Section B, item 11 - labels A to U, including D and R", and warns against double counting the component labels D1, R1, R2, R3, R6, U1, U2 and U3 that make up those totals. Subtracting exempt current pension income at label Y from this figure gives total assessable income at label V.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label W
value_definition: A whole-dollar subtotal that can be a loss, in which case a loss flag is set. It counts contributions, investment income, non-arm's length income and assessable transfers together.
limitation: It is not the fund's taxable income and not the amount that is taxed: a fund paying pensions can show a large gross income here and almost no assessable income. The gross income and exempt current pension income labels were also added part way through the period this asset covers, so an early year can be empty rather than zero and should be checked before a series is built.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label W heading, the ATO gives its arithmetic, and the 2008 and 2012 return forms show when the label was introduced.
evidence_quote: Add the amounts from Section B, item 11 - labels A to U, including D and R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the word 'Gross income' with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing distinguished it from total assessable income at label V or explained why early years are empty.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label C, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label C
variable_description: Interest the fund earned from Australian sources, counted before any cost of earning it. The ATO says "Write at label C the total interest income that the SMSF earned in 2024-25" and that the amount "shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income." Bank and term deposit interest belongs here, as does interest the ATO itself pays the fund, but interest received through a partnership or trust is reported at labels I or M instead.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label C
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, gross, restricted to Australian-source interest. Foreign interest is carried at label D1 gross foreign income and non-arm's length interest at label U3.
limitation: It understates the fund's interest earnings whenever the fund invests through a managed vehicle, because interest inside a partnership or trust distribution is never unbundled to this label. It is also self-assessed by the trustee, not matched to a payer report, so the Australian and foreign split reflects the trustee's classification.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label C heading, and the ATO lists what is included at and excluded from that label.
evidence_quote: Write at label C the total interest income that the SMSF earned in 2024-25. The amount at label C shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Gross interest' and printed the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is Australian-source only or that interest arriving through a trust is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label H, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label H
variable_description: Payments to the fund from which the payer withheld tax because the fund had not given its ABN. The ATO requires the pre-withholding figure: "The amount that you write at label H must be the gross value, that is, it must include both the amounts paid to the SMSF and the amounts that payers withheld." The withheld tax is claimed back on the same return in Section D at label H3, so a non-zero value here should have a credit beside it.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label H
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount, supported by a PAYG payment summary from each payer and by an attached non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule.
limitation: It is not a measure of income type - the payments could be anything - and it is not the tax withheld, which is a different column. A zero is the normal case for a functioning fund and says nothing about the fund's income; it usually just means the fund quoted its ABN.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label H heading, and the ATO instruction states the gross-up rule and the matching credit label.
evidence_quote: The amount that you write at label H must be the gross value, that is, it must include both the amounts paid to the SMSF and the amounts that payers withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label and printed the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure includes the withheld tax or where the offsetting credit is reported.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label B, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label B
variable_description: Rent and other leasing or hiring income the fund earned, taken before expenses. The ATO says "Write at label B the total income that the SMSF earned from renting, leasing and hiring of land, buildings and other assets", and the amount "shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income." Rent from a property the fund leases to a related party at other than market terms is excluded and shown at label U3 instead, so this label is meant to hold arm's length rent only.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label B
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount covering land, buildings and any other leased or hired asset. Foreign rent goes to label D1, and rent inside a partnership or trust distribution goes to labels I or M.
limitation: It cannot be netted against property costs to get a rental result, because interest, capital works and depreciation on the same property sit in Section C and are not tied to the property. It also cannot be split by property or by residential against commercial, which the Section H asset labels do separately and at a different date.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label B heading, and the ATO instruction defines the coverage and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: Write at label B the total income that the SMSF earned from renting, leasing and hiring of land, buildings and other assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label wording and the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is gross or that non-arm's length rent is reported elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D label B, SMSF annual return calculation statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label B
variable_description: The fund's tax bill before any offset or credit is applied. On the current calculation statement the ATO says "Write at label B the total of label T1 and label J", so it is tax on taxable income plus the extra tax on contributions made for members whose tax file number the fund does not hold. The rate mix inside it is not one number: a complying fund pays 15 per cent on ordinary income and 45 per cent on non-arm's length income, and a non-complying fund pays 45 per cent throughout.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label B
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, the top line of the calculation statement. It is gross of foreign income tax offsets, franking credit offsets, rebates and PAYG instalments.
limitation: Dividing it by taxable income does not give the fund's tax rate, because the amount blends rates and includes tax on no-TFN contributions that are not part of the low tax component. It is also not what the fund paid: offsets and credits sit below it, and the tax payable line can be zero while this figure is large.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the calculation statement label B heading, and the ATO instruction gives the arithmetic and the rates that feed it.
evidence_quote: Write at label B the total of label T1 and label J.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Gross tax' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never distinguished the figure from tax payable or explained the blended rates.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label M, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label M
variable_description: The fund's share of the net income of other trusts, including unit trusts and managed funds. The ATO says "Write at label M the total share of net income that the SMSF received or was entitled to receive from other trusts" and that "The amount at label M can't be a loss." Entitlement counts even when the cash has not been paid, and any franking credit the fund can use as an offset is included in the amount here as well as claimed in Section D.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label M
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount that is bounded below by zero and reported with a trust type code in the box beside it. Capital gains, foreign income and non-arm's length trust income are carved out to labels A, D1 and U2.
limitation: Because the label cannot be negative, a trust loss disappears rather than showing as a negative distribution, and a zero cannot be read as no trust investment. The figure is also a share of net income rather than cash received, so it will not reconcile with the fund's bank statements.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label M heading, and the ATO instruction states the entitlement basis, the no-loss rule and the code requirement.
evidence_quote: Write at label M the total share of net income that the SMSF received or was entitled to receive from other trusts. The amount at label M can't be a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label name and the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is entitlement based, cannot be a loss, or carries a trust type code.

value_domain: Trust type code letter, Section B label M code box, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, Table 3 trust type codes
variable_description: A single letter saying what kind of trust the fund's trust distribution came from. The ATO directs the trustee to "Print the letter from Table 3 that best describes the type of trust from which you received the income you wrote at label M", with letters for deceased estates, testamentary, fixed, hybrid, discretionary, cash management unit, fixed unit and listed or unlisted public unit trusts. Where income came from more than one kind of trust, only the type paying the largest amount is coded.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, Table 3 trust type codes
value_definition: One letter drawn from a closed list published in the instructions, attached to the dollar amount at label M and mandatory whenever that label is used.
limitation: It describes a single trust type for a row that can bundle several trusts, so a fund holding both a listed unit trust and a family trust shows only the larger one. It also says nothing about how much came from each type, and the letters have been added to over time, so a code list from one year does not necessarily cover another.
rationale: The custodian's description names the code box beside label M, and the ATO publishes the letters, the rule for choosing between them and the definitions behind each.
evidence_quote: Print the letter from Table 3 that best describes the type of trust from which you received the income you wrote at label M. If this income is from more than one type of trust, print the letter that describes the type of trust from which you received the greatest amount of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Gross trust distributions code' with the generic sentence twice and no letters, so a reader could not tell that a closed and documented code list exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D label G, SMSF annual return calculation statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label G
variable_description: An interest charge the fund owes on income it received from a non-resident trust. The ATO explains that "An interest charge is imposed on certain distributions from non-resident trusts under Section 102AAM of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936", and the trustee works out the charge and writes it in. It sits outside the tax calculation itself, added after tax payable when the amount due for the year is struck.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label G
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, self-calculated by the trustee rather than raised by an assessment, and reported only when a charge arises.
limitation: It is an interest charge, not tax, so adding it to tax payable overstates the fund's income tax. A non-zero value marks a foreign trust distribution but does not size it. The charge has also not carried the same label letter in every version of the calculation statement, so match it on the printed name rather than on its position.
rationale: The custodian's description names the section 102AAM interest charge, which is a labelled line of the SMSF calculation statement in both the 2008 and current instructions.
evidence_quote: An interest charge is imposed on certain distributions from non-resident trusts under Section 102AAM of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936.
supersedes_rationale: The entry named the section of the Act and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said this is interest rather than tax or where it sits in the calculation.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label S, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label S and Table 5
variable_description: Assessable income that does not fit any other income label, reported as one figure with a code for its largest part. The ATO says "Write at label S any assessable income of the SMSF that doesn't fall into any other category in Section B", and the code letters cover balancing adjustments, listed investment company capital gain amounts, forex gains, income from premiums paid for death or disability benefits, financial arrangement gains and payments subject to foreign resident withholding. Because the categories are unrelated, the dollar figure only means something once the code beside it is read.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label S and Table 5
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount paired with a one-letter code from a published list, with code O reserved for anything the other letters do not describe.
limitation: The label mixes categories that have nothing in common, so a time series of it measures no single economic quantity. The code names only the largest component, so a row coded F for forex can still be mostly something else.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label S heading, and the ATO publishes both the residual rule and the code table that qualifies the amount.
evidence_quote: Write at label S any assessable income of the SMSF that doesn't fall into any other category in Section B.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other income' with the generic sentence twice, which told a reader nothing about the code box that gives the amount its meaning.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, Section A item 10, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10, item 10
variable_description: Whether the fund paid a pension to any of its members during the year, which is the gateway to the pension tax exemption. The ATO asks "Did the fund pay retirement phase superannuation income stream benefits to one or more members during 2024-25?" and a yes opens the exempt current pension income amount at the same item. A yes therefore marks a fund in or partly in the pension phase, which changes how much of its investment income is taxed.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10, item 10
value_definition: A two-state indicator from a tick box, answered for the fund and not for a member. It gates the exempt current pension income amount reported beside it and repeated at Section B label Y.
limitation: It does not say how many members were paid, how much, or whether the pension ran for the whole year, and the member-level income stream payment amounts are held on separate rows. The question was also narrowed to retirement phase income streams, so a yes in an early year and a yes now are not exactly the same statement.
rationale: The custodian's description repeats the Section A item 10 question, and the ATO instruction states the question and what a yes answer requires.
evidence_quote: This question asks - Did the fund pay retirement phase superannuation income stream benefits to one or more members during 2024-25?
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the question with no answer domain and the same generic sentence twice, so it did not connect the flag to the pension exemption it controls.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section F or G label R2, SMSF annual return member statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label R2
variable_description: The pension the fund paid this member during the year. The ATO says "Write at label R2 the total amount of super income stream benefits paid to the member in 2024-25", and a code beside it names the benefit type. Money the member took as a lump sum, including a full or partial commutation of a pension, is not counted here - it goes to label R1 - so a member drawing down heavily can show a small figure at this label.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label R2
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount on the member's own statement, paired with a benefit type code. It is the payment made, not the minimum required to be drawn and not the member's entitlement.
limitation: It cannot be used as pension income received by the person, because a member with accounts in more than one fund shows only this fund's payments, and a commutation is reported as a lump sum instead. The 2017 rule change that stopped members electing to treat a pension payment as a lump sum also shifts the split between this label and the lump sum label across years.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the member statement label R2 heading, and the ATO instruction defines the amount, the code and the commutation exclusion.
evidence_quote: Write at label R2 the total amount of super income stream benefits paid to the member in 2024-25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Income stream payment' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is per member, per fund, or that commutations are excluded.

value_domain: Income stream benefit type code letter, Section F or G label R2 code box
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G, Table 12 income stream benefit type codes
variable_description: A letter saying what kind of pension the member was paid, separating an ordinary pension from a transition to retirement one or a death benefit. The ATO says "Use Table 12 to work out which code applies to the amount you wrote at label R2", with letters distinguishing members aged 60 and over, members under 60, transition to retirement, and death benefits to a dependant. Where several kinds were paid, the trustee codes only the income stream with the largest total.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G, Table 12 income stream benefit type codes
value_definition: One letter from a published list, attached to the income stream payment amount and required whenever that amount is present.
limitation: It is a single label for a whole year of payments, so a member who turned 60 mid-year or converted a transition to retirement pension is described by one letter only. Because the letter follows the largest payment, it can also hide a smaller stream of a different type entirely.
rationale: The custodian's description names the code beside label R2, and the ATO publishes the letters and the rule for choosing among them.
evidence_quote: Use Table 12 to work out which code applies to the amount you wrote at label R2. Print the code in the Code box to the right of label R2. If more than one benefit type applies, use the code that describes the income stream with the largest total payment amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Income stream payment - code' with the generic sentence twice and no letters, so it did not show that the codes carry the age and death benefit distinction.

value_domain: Financial year (1 July to 30 June) the return relates to
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, How to get the SMSF annual return 2025
variable_description: The Australian financial year the return covers, running from 1 July to 30 June. It is the only field that dates a row: the income and deduction labels are annual totals for this year, while the asset and liability labels are balances at its 30 June, and the member statements combine both. A fund must lodge for a year if it was an SMSF at 30 June or was wound up during the year, so a fund can appear for part of a year and then stop.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, How to get the SMSF annual return 2025
value_definition: A year identifier rather than a date, present on both the annual return table and the member statement table so that the two can be joined for the same fund and year.
limitation: It is not a lodgement or processing date, so it says nothing about when the ATO received or amended the return, and an amended return replaces the earlier figures for the same year rather than adding a row. A fund that changed its balancing period or was wound up mid-year still reports under one income year, so the year cannot be read as twelve months of activity.
rationale: The ATO page for the annual return states the reporting period the form covers and who must lodge for a year, which is what this field identifies.
evidence_quote: Your super fund must lodge a Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 if it was either: a SMSF on 30 June 2025, a SMSF that was wound up during 2024-25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Income year' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it did not say that the same year label carries flow measures and point-in-time balances.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, Section A item 9, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10, item 9
variable_description: Whether this is the fund's final return because it was wound up during the year. A yes has consequences elsewhere on the same return: the ATO says the wind-up date "must be a date from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 and be the date on which the fund no longer held any assets", the total member closing account balances label is left blank, and total liabilities are reported as zero. It is the field that closes a fund's history rather than one that describes its finances.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section A: SMSF information - items 1 to 10, item 9
value_definition: A two-state indicator from a tick box, accompanied on the form by the wind-up date and by a separate question on whether all lodgement and payment obligations were met.
limitation: It does not mark the year the fund stopped operating in any economic sense - a fund can pay out every member and still lodge as a live fund until the wind-up is completed. Reading a no as a fund that continued is also unsafe, since a fund that simply failed to lodge leaves no row at all.
rationale: The custodian's description repeats the Section A item 9 question, and the ATO instruction sets the date rule and the flow-on effects on the assets and liabilities labels.
evidence_quote: That date must be a date from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 and be the date on which the fund no longer held any assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the question with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that a yes empties the closing balance and liability labels on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar asset value reported at Section H label C, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label C
variable_description: The value of life insurance policies the fund holds as an investment, counted among its Australian managed investments. The ATO says "Write at label C the value (on 30 June 2025) of life insurance policies owned by the SMSF that were issued by an organisation registered under the Life Insurance Act 1995." This is an asset the fund owns, not the cover it buys for members: premiums for death and disability cover are an expense in Section C, and the two have no arithmetic relationship.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label C
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance sheet value at 30 June, taken from the fund's own statement of financial position. Policies held on trust under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement are excluded and shown among the borrowing labels instead.
limitation: A zero here does not mean members are uninsured, because ordinary member cover is a policy the fund pays for rather than an investment it owns. The value is also the trustee's own, since SMSF assets are self-valued at market value rather than independently priced.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label C heading, and the ATO instruction defines the asset class and the exclusion.
evidence_quote: Write at label C the value (on 30 June 2025) of life insurance policies owned by the SMSF that were issued by an organisation registered under the Life Insurance Act 1995.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Insurance policy' with the generic sentence twice, so a reader could easily have taken it for member insurance cover rather than an owned asset.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label F2, SMSF annual return non-deductible expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label F2
variable_description: The part of the fund's member insurance premiums that it cannot deduct. Non-deductible premiums, in the ATO's words, include "any insurance premiums paid by a non-complying SMSF" and "payments for insurance that covers events other than death, the existence of a terminal medical condition, or temporary or permanent disability". The deductible part of the same premiums sits at label F1 on the same row, so the two together are what the fund spent on cover.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label F2
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense amount in the non-deductible column of Section C, feeding total non-deductible expenses rather than total deductions.
limitation: It is not the fund's insurance bill and not a measure of cover, because it is only the disallowed slice, and its size is driven as much by the deduction rules as by the premium. The label wording also changed: the custodian calls it death or disability premiums while the current return calls it insurance premiums, and the separate non-deductible column was added part way through the period this asset covers, so an early year can be empty rather than zero.
rationale: The custodian's description names the non-deductible side of the death or disability premium item, which is label F2 of Section C, and the ATO lists what falls into it.
evidence_quote: Non-deductible insurance premiums include: any insurance premiums paid by a non-complying SMSF, payments for insurance that covers events other than death, the existence of a terminal medical condition, or temporary or permanent disability (for example, funeral insurance).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is only the disallowed part or that the column did not exist in the early years.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label A1, SMSF annual return deductions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label A1
variable_description: Deductible interest on money the fund borrowed from an Australian source, which is what the custodian's own description says this column holds. The ATO says "Write at label A1 the amount of deductible interest expenses incurred on borrowings from sources within Australia", deductible to the extent the borrowing was used to buy income-producing assets, finance operations or meet current expenses. The non-deductible part of the same interest is at label A2, and interest on overseas borrowings is a separate pair of labels.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label A1
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, limited to interest and reported by the source of the borrowing rather than by what the money bought. Interest attributable to foreign or non-arm's length income is excluded from the deductible label.
limitation: The abbreviated variable name and the custodian's description disagree: the name reads as an overseas total while the description says within Australia, and the same reversal runs through every interest expense column in this table. Do not decide the domicile of the borrowing from the name alone - check the label letter on the return before building an Australian against overseas split.
rationale: The custodian's description names the within Australia interest expense item, which is label A1 of Section C, and the ATO instruction defines what is deductible there.
evidence_quote: Write at label A1 the amount of deductible interest expenses incurred on borrowings from sources within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the description 'Interest expenses within Australia' with the generic sentence twice, and never flagged that the variable name points the other way.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label B1, SMSF annual return deductions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label B1
variable_description: Deductible interest on money the fund borrowed from an overseas source, which is what the custodian's own description says this column holds. The ATO says "Write at label B1 the amount of deductible interest expenses incurred on borrowings from overseas sources", on the same use test that applies to Australian borrowings. A fund reporting an amount here may also have withholding obligations on the interest it pays to non-residents, which are settled outside this return.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label B1
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, classified by where the lender is rather than where the asset is. The non-deductible part of the same interest goes to label B2.
limitation: The abbreviated variable name and the custodian's description disagree: the name reads as within Australia while the description says overseas, and the reversal is systematic across the interest expense columns here. A borrowing from a foreign lender used to buy an Australian asset still sits at this label, so it is not a proxy for offshore investment.
