rationale: The custodian's description names the overseas interest expense item, which is label B1 of Section C, and the ATO instruction defines what is deductible there.
evidence_quote: Write at label B1 the amount of deductible interest expenses incurred on borrowings from overseas sources.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the description 'Interest expenses overseas' with the generic sentence twice, and did not warn that the variable name reads as the opposite.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label I1, SMSF annual return deductions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label I1
variable_description: What the fund spent running its investments, to the extent it can deduct it. The ATO gives adviser retainers, brokerage, bank fees, rental property expenses and the cost of advice to change the investment mix as examples, and it says "The exact nature of the investment related expenses is critical in determining deductibility." Fund administration and the audit fee are deliberately kept out of this label and reported at labels J1 and H1, so the three do not overlap.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label I1
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction of a revenue nature. Capital costs of acquiring an investment are not here, and the non-deductible part of the same expenses sits at label I2.
limitation: It is not the total cost of investing: fees netted off inside a managed fund or a pooled superannuation trust never reach the fund's own accounts, so a fund invested through managed products can report almost nothing here. The deductible and non-deductible split also depends on how much pension income the fund has, not on how it invests.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section C investment expenses item, and the ATO instruction lists the examples and the boundary against the administration and audit labels.
evidence_quote: Show at I the amount of expenses of a revenue nature incurred in deriving investment income, unless the expense is more appropriately shown at another label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Investment expenses' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not mark the boundary against administration and audit costs.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section F or G label P, SMSF annual return member statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label P
variable_description: Money moved into this member's account from elsewhere in the Australian super system, as distinct from a contribution. The ATO says "Write at label P the total amount of rollovers and transfers received for the member in 2024-25 from within the Australian superannuation system", and includes amounts split from a spouse's account, amounts transferred under a family law order, a reversionary entitlement after a spouse's death, and unclaimed super paid out by the ATO. Transfers from a foreign fund are excluded and reported at the contribution labels instead.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label P
value_definition: A whole-dollar member-level amount, supported by a rollover benefits statement from the transferring fund. The custodian's wording, inward amounts less any rolled in contributions, reflects that contributions inside the transfer are not counted again here.
limitation: It is not new saving - the money already existed in the system - so adding it to contributions double counts a person's balance growth. It also cannot be read as consolidation into an SMSF alone, because family law splits, death benefits and ATO-held money all land at the same label.
rationale: The custodian's description names the inward amounts item of the member statement, which is label P, and the ATO instruction lists what is and is not included.
evidence_quote: Write at label P the total amount of rollovers and transfers received for the member in 2024-25 from within the Australian superannuation system.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish a rollover from a contribution or list what else lands at this label.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label R6, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label R6
variable_description: Assessable contributions the fund has handed to a life insurance company or pooled superannuation trust to be taxed there instead. The ATO describes it as "the total amount that would otherwise have been included in the complying SMSF's assessable income" that the trustee "has agreed to transfer to a life insurance company or PST (the transferee) under an agreement with that transferee entity". It is subtracted, not added, when total assessable contributions are struck at label R.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label R6
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount reported inside the assessable contributions block, reducing the total at label R by the amount transferred under section 295-260 of the ITAA 1997.
limitation: Despite sitting among income labels, a larger figure lowers the fund's assessable income rather than raising it, so summing the contribution labels without subtracting it overstates income. The transfer also does not carry the tax on no-TFN contributions, which stays with the fund, so it is not a clean shift of the whole liability.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label R6 heading, and the ATO instruction states what is transferred and how the total at label R is worked out.
evidence_quote: Write at label R6 the total amount that would otherwise have been included in the complying SMSF's assessable income for 2024-25 that the trustee of the SMSF (the transferor) has agreed to transfer to a life insurance company or PST (the transferee) under an agreement with that transferee entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice and gave no hint that the amount is subtracted from assessable contributions.

value_domain: Dollar total reported at Section H label Z, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label Z
variable_description: The whole right-hand side of the fund's balance sheet at 30 June, which is dominated by what it owes its own members. Borrowings, total member closing account balances, reserve accounts and other liabilities are added to get it, and the ATO requires that "Label Z Total liabilities must equal label U Total Australian and overseas assets". Because member balances are counted as a liability, this total is normally about the same size as the fund's assets rather than a measure of debt.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label Z
value_definition: A whole-dollar total at 30 June, made up of labels V to Y, and written as zero if the sum would be negative or if the fund was wound up during the year.
limitation: Reading it as fund borrowing is wrong by an order of magnitude, since the borrowings component is usually a small part of it and most funds have none. The identity with total assets is also an instruction rather than an audited fact, so a row where the two differ points to a reporting error rather than to real leverage.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label Z heading, and the ATO instruction gives the components and the balancing rule.
evidence_quote: Label Z Total liabilities must equal label U Total Australian and overseas assets in item 15d.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'TOTAL LIABILITIES' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain that member balances sit inside the total.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section H label V, SMSF annual return liabilities
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label V
variable_description: What the fund still owed on money it had borrowed, measured at 30 June and including accrued interest. The ATO asks for "the total value of each type of outstanding borrowing by the SMSF (including accrued interest)" across three component labels, then "Write at label V the total of labels V1, V2 and V3." Most of it is limited recourse borrowing used to buy property, since SMSFs are barred from borrowing except in narrow cases, and the other two components are permissible temporary borrowings of 7 to 90 days and everything else.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label V
value_definition: A whole-dollar closing balance of outstanding debt, not a flow of new borrowing during the year, and separate from the value of the assets bought with it.
limitation: It cannot be read as gearing on its own, because the geared asset is reported at its own labels and the fund's other assets are unencumbered. The component split into limited recourse, temporary and other borrowings was added later than the total, so a series of the components starts well after the series of label V.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H borrowings label, and both the 2008 and current ATO instructions define what the amount covers.
evidence_quote: Show at V the total amount of borrowings by the SMSF, including accrued interest, at 30 June 2008.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Borrowings' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is a closing balance including accrued interest.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section H label Y, SMSF annual return liabilities
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label Y
variable_description: Everything the fund owed at 30 June that is not a borrowing, a member balance or a reserve. The ATO defines it by exclusion, as "the total value (on 30 June 2025) of liabilities that you couldn't include in labels" V Borrowings, W Total member closing account balances and X Reserve accounts. In practice it collects accrued tax, unpaid fees and benefits owed but not yet paid, so it is a small residual rather than a category.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label Y
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual balance at 30 June, defined only by what the three named liability labels do not take.
limitation: It cannot be interpreted as a kind of liability, because its content depends on what the trustee could not fit elsewhere and no code identifies it. A fund that treats an amount as a reserve and one that treats the same amount as other liabilities both balance, so the split between labels X and Y is a bookkeeping choice.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H other liabilities label, and the ATO instruction defines it as the residual of the other three.
evidence_quote: Write at label Y the total value (on 30 June 2025) of liabilities that you couldn't include in labels: V Borrowings, W Total member closing account balances, X Reserve accounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other liabilities' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the label is defined by exclusion from the other three.

value_domain: Dollar asset value reported at Section H label H, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label H
variable_description: The value of listed Australian shares the fund held directly at 30 June. The ATO says "Write at label H the value (on 30 June 2025) of public shares and equities held by the SMSF that are traded on Australian stock exchanges", and directs listed trust units to label A, debt securities to label F and shares held under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement to a separate label. This is the fund's direct equity holding, which is the label most often used to size SMSF exposure to the Australian share market.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label H
value_definition: A whole-dollar market value at 30 June from the fund's own statement of financial position, restricted to Australian-listed shares and similar contracts held directly.
limitation: It understates the fund's share exposure, because shares held through a managed fund, an exchange traded fund taxed as a trust, or a limited recourse borrowing arrangement are reported at other labels. Being a 30 June snapshot valued by the trustee, it also cannot show trading through the year or guarantee a market price.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label H heading, and the ATO instruction defines the class and its exclusions.
evidence_quote: Write at label H the value (on 30 June 2025) of public shares and equities held by the SMSF that are traded on Australian stock exchanges.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Listed shares' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that indirect share holdings sit at other labels.

value_domain: Dollar asset value reported at Section H label A, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label A
variable_description: The value of units in listed trusts the fund held at 30 June, the first of the four Australian managed investment labels. The ATO says "Write at label A the value (on 30 June 2025) of listed trust units owned by the SMSF", and it defines the category: "A listed trust is a trust which has its units traded on an Australian stock exchange, and the unit values are reported as shares.". Listed property trusts and most exchange traded funds sit here rather than with listed shares, which is why the two labels have to be read together.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label A
value_definition: A whole-dollar market value at 30 June, covering trust units that can be bought through a stockbroker. Unlisted trusts are at label B and other managed vehicles at label D.
limitation: A reader comparing funds on share exposure will misclassify anything held as a listed trust unit, since it looks like a share on a broker statement but is reported here. The value is also a trustee valuation at one date and cannot show what was held during the year.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label A heading, and both the current and 2008 ATO instructions define what a listed trust is for this label.
evidence_quote: Write at label A the value (on 30 June 2025) of listed trust units owned by the SMSF.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Listed trusts' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the label from listed shares or explain what counts as a listed trust.

value_domain: Dollar asset value reported at Section H label G, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label G
variable_description: Loans the fund has made to others and still holds at 30 June, an asset rather than a debt. The ATO is explicit about the direction: it asks "Did the SMSF have any Australian loans (where the SMSF is the lender)?" and takes the total value of loans where the fund is the lender and the loan was entered into or finalised in Australia. Money the fund has borrowed is a liability at label V, so the two must not be confused.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label G
value_definition: A whole-dollar carrying value at 30 June of amounts lent out, on the fund's own valuation. Overseas lending falls outside the label and is reported among overseas assets.
limitation: It cannot be used to identify lending to related parties, which is captured separately by the in-house asset question, and it says nothing about whether the loan is performing. A large balance may be a legitimate investment or a compliance problem, and this column cannot tell the two apart.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label G heading, and the ATO instruction states that the fund is the lender and sets the Australian condition.
evidence_quote: Write at label G the total value (on 30 June 2025) of loans where both: the SMSF is the lender, the SMSF entered into or finalised the loan in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Loans' with the generic sentence twice, leaving it ambiguous whether the fund is the lender or the borrower.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section F or G label R1, SMSF annual return member statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label R1
variable_description: Lump sums the fund paid for this member during the year. The ATO says "Write at label R1 the total amount of super lump sum benefits paid for the member in 2024-25", with a code beside it for the benefit type. Commutations count here rather than as pension payments: "A payment made as a result of a full commutation of an income stream is a super lump sum and must be reported at label R1", and since 1 July 2017 a partial commutation is treated the same way.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label R1
value_definition: A whole-dollar member-level amount, paired with a benefit type code, and separate from rollovers out of the fund, which go to label Q.
limitation: It is not a withdrawal by the member in every case, because a death benefit paid to a dependant or a release authority payment to the ATO also lands here, and the code is needed to tell them apart. The 2017 change to commutations breaks comparability with earlier years, since payments that once appeared as income stream benefits now appear as lump sums.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the member statement label R1 heading, and the ATO instruction defines the amount, the code and the commutation treatment.
evidence_quote: Write at label R1 the total amount of super lump sum benefits paid for the member in 2024-25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Lump sum payment' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that death benefits and commutations are counted here.

value_domain: Lump sum benefit type code letter, Section F or G label R1 code box
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G, Table 11 lump sum benefit type codes
variable_description: A letter saying why a lump sum was paid, which is the only field separating a retirement withdrawal from a death benefit or an early release. The ATO says "Use Table 11 to work out which code applies to the amount you wrote at label R1", with letters for a member aged 60 or over, a member under 60, a death benefit to a dependant, a death benefit to a non-dependant, a terminal medical condition, other types such as permanent incapacity or severe financial hardship, and a release authority payment. Where more than one type was paid, the letter follows the largest payment.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G, Table 11 lump sum benefit type codes
value_definition: One letter from a published list, attached to the lump sum amount and required whenever that amount is present.
limitation: It codes a whole year of lump sums with one letter, so a member who took a retirement lump sum and a hardship payment shows only the larger. The letter also carries no dollar split, so it cannot be used to value death benefits separately from ordinary withdrawals on the same row.
rationale: The custodian's description names the code beside label R1, and the ATO publishes the letters and the rule for choosing between them.
evidence_quote: Use Table 11 to work out which code applies to the amount you wrote at label R1. Print the code in the Code box to the right of label R1. If more than one benefit type applies, use the code that describes the largest payment amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Lump sum payment - code' with the generic sentence twice and no letters, so it did not show that the code carries the death benefit and early release distinction.

value_domain: Dollar total reported at Section H label W, SMSF annual return liabilities
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label W
variable_description: The total of every member's closing account balance at 30 June, reported as a liability of the fund. The ATO ties it to the member statements: "The amount at label W must equal the total of all the label S Closing account balance amounts in Sections F and G." It is the closest thing the return has to the size of the fund from the members' point of view, and for a fund with no borrowings it is close to total assets.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label W
value_definition: A whole-dollar total at 30 June, and the reconciling link between the fund-level balance sheet and the member-level statements on the other table.
limitation: It is left blank rather than set to zero when the fund was wound up during the year, so a missing value in a fund's last year is a rule and not a gap. Because trustees value the fund's assets themselves, a large one-year movement can be a revaluation rather than contributions or earnings.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label W heading, and the ATO instruction states the equality with the member statements and the wind-up rule.
evidence_quote: The amount at label W must equal the total of all the label S Closing account balance amounts in Sections F and G.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Total member closing account balances' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain the link to the member rows or the wind-up blank.

value_domain: Code identifying the member record on the SMSF annual return member statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: A code attached to a member's row on the fund's member statement, most likely identifying the record rather than any amount on it. The only coded field the ATO attaches to a member record is the account status letter used in Section G, where O means "The member's account was open on 30 June 2025, and the SMSF will accept payments from us" and C means the account was closed. Section F holds members who were still in the fund at 30 June and Section G those who left, died, or could not be fitted into Section F for lack of space, so a record code may also carry that split.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A short code on the member row. The ATO's own coded member-record field is the account status letter, O or C, which is completed only for members reported in Section G.
limitation: The custodian's wording does not name a label, so this column cannot be pinned to a printed field with confidence, and it should not be used as an account status flag without checking the values against a real extract. Reading a missing code as a live account would also be wrong, since the account status box is left empty for every member reported in Section F.
rationale: The member statement is the only part of the SMSF return that carries a per-member code, and the ATO publishes that code and the Section F against Section G split; but no published label is named 'member record', so the mapping is inferred.
evidence_quote: For members reported in Section G, you also: write the date of death, if the member died during 2024-25, print the account status code (from Table 10: Account status codes) in the Account status code box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Member record' with the generic sentence twice; this at least names the coded member fields the ATO does publish and is honest that the mapping is not settled.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label J1, SMSF annual return deductions
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label J1
variable_description: What it cost to run the fund as an entity, to the extent the cost is deductible. The ATO says "Write at label J1 the amount of deductible management and administration expenses" and counts tax agent fees, the SMSF supervisory levy, the general interest charge and the shortfall interest charge among them, while sending investment management expenses to labels I1 or I2 and auditor fees to labels H1 or H2. Setup costs, deed amendments and late lodgement penalties are not deductible and go to the non-deductible column instead.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label J1
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction of a revenue nature for administering the fund, sitting alongside a non-deductible counterpart at label J2.
limitation: It is not the full cost of running the fund, because the audit fee, investment costs and anything non-deductible are recorded at other labels, so a cost-per-fund measure built on this column alone is too low. It also cannot be compared cleanly across time, since the deductible share depends on how much of the fund's income is exempt pension income.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section C management and administration expenses item, and the ATO instruction lists its contents and the boundary against the audit fee.
evidence_quote: Show at J the amount of expenses of a revenue nature incurred in the management and administration of superannuation entities, unless the expense is more appropriately shown at another label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Management and administration expenses' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that audit and investment costs are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar asset value reported at Section H label D, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label D
variable_description: Money the fund has placed with Australian managed vehicles that is not a listed trust, unlisted trust or insurance policy. The ATO says the label "includes investments with all external investment managers and pooled superannuation trusts (PSTs) located or registered in Australia", and adds that "A managed fund that is registered in Australia is an Australian managed investment even if it invests in overseas assets." That last rule matters: an Australian managed fund holding global shares is counted here, not among the fund's overseas assets.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16, label D
value_definition: A whole-dollar market value at 30 June, the residual of the four Australian managed investment labels, classified by where the manager is registered rather than by what it holds.
limitation: It cannot be used to measure the fund's home bias, because a globally invested Australian managed fund is indistinguishable from a domestic one at this label. The residual definition also means its content shifts when a trustee reclassifies a holding between it and the listed or unlisted trust labels.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section H label D heading, and the ATO instruction defines the residual and the registration test.
evidence_quote: A managed fund that is registered in Australia is an Australian managed investment even if it invests in overseas assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other managed investments' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that overseas exposure held through an Australian manager falls here.

value_domain: Month and year of birth, truncated from the reported date of birth
value_source: ATO, Superannuation member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section C: Member details, question 28
variable_description: The month a member was born, cut down from the full date of birth the fund reports for that member. The ATO asks the provider to "Provide the member's day, month and year of birth, if known" and allows partial dates: "Write '0' in any part of the date of birth that is unknown", giving an example of 00/02/1975 for a member known to be born in February 1975. The month is what survives into this asset, so age can be worked out to about a month against any event date on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Superannuation member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section C: Member details, question 28
value_definition: A truncated date carrying month, and in practice the year, rather than a full calendar date. The underlying reported value is a self-reported member detail held by the fund, not a verified registry record.
limitation: Because the source permits zero-filled parts of the date, a month can itself be unknown and recorded as zero, which is not the same as missing. Age derived from it is age of the member as recorded by this fund, so a person with accounts in several funds can carry inconsistent birth details across rows.
rationale: The date of birth on a super member record is defined by the ATO's member reporting instructions, including the rule for unknown parts of the date, which explains why a month can be present without a day.
evidence_quote: Write '0' in any part of the date of birth that is unknown. For example, where you know the member was born in February 1975 but you do not know on what day, record their date of birth as 00/02/1975.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Month of birth' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain that the source date can be partly unknown or that it is fund-reported.

value_domain: Month and year of death, truncated from the reported date of death
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: The month a member died, as reported by the fund on the member's own statement. It is only ever completed in the supplementary member section: the ATO says that for members reported in Section G you "write the date of death, if the member died during 2024-25". A deceased member is reported there rather than in the ordinary member section, so this field and the section a row came from move together.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A truncated date carrying month and year, present only on rows for members who died in the reporting year and reported by the trustee rather than by a registry.
limitation: It records the year the fund reported a death, so a death late in a year that the trustee reports in the following return is dated to that later return rather than corrected in place. It is also not a death registration: for population work the death registry is the authority, and this field only tells you the fund knew.
rationale: The custodian's description names the date of death on the member statement, and the ATO instruction states which members carry it and when it is written.
evidence_quote: For members reported in Section G, you also: write the date of death, if the member died during 2024-25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Month of death' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the field is confined to the supplementary member section or that it is trustee reported.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D label T5, SMSF annual return calculation statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label T5
variable_description: The tax the fund is left owing for the year once every offset has been applied. It is the last line of the calculation statement: where refundable tax offsets are "less than the tax at label T3, the shortfall becomes the SMSF's tax payable amount at label T5 Tax payable", and where they exceed it the fund writes zero and takes the excess as a refund. A complying fund with large franking credits can show zero here while still reporting substantial gross tax.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label T5
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount bounded below by zero, struck after non-refundable and refundable offsets but before PAYG instalment credits, eligible credits and the supervisory levy.
limitation: A zero does not mean no tax, because franking credits can wipe out the liability and even generate a refund, so this column understates the tax borne on the fund's income. The calculation statement has also been renumbered between versions of the return, so match this field on its printed name, Tax payable, rather than on where it sits in the statement.
rationale: The custodian's description sits among the calculation statement items, and the ATO defines the tax payable line those items lead to; the reading of 'Net tax' as that line is inferred from the surrounding columns rather than from a printed label of that name.
evidence_quote: is less than the tax at label T3, the shortfall becomes the SMSF's tax payable amount at label T5 Tax payable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net tax' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say what has been subtracted, that it cannot be negative, or that the statement was redesigned.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D label T2, SMSF annual return calculation statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label T2
variable_description: Tax still owing after the first tier of offsets, the ones that cannot be refunded or carried forward. The ATO says "Subtract the amount at label C Non-refundable non-carry forward tax offsets from label B Gross tax", write the result if it is positive and zero otherwise, and warns that "If the non-refundable non-carry forward tax offsets are greater than the gross tax, the excess can't be carried forward and is lost." It is a working line, not a liability: two further tiers of offsets are applied below it.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label T2
value_definition: A whole-dollar intermediate figure bounded below by zero, sitting between gross tax and tax payable in the calculation statement.
limitation: Because it is floored at zero, the difference between gross tax and this line understates offsets whenever offsets exceed tax, and the lost excess is not recorded anywhere on the return. The subtotal lines in the calculation statement have also been renumbered between versions of the return, so check the label letter for the year in hand before joining a series across years.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the SUBTOTAL 1 line of the current calculation statement, and the ATO instruction gives its arithmetic and the treatment of excess offsets.
evidence_quote: Subtract the amount at label C Non-refundable non-carry forward tax offsets from label B Gross tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'SUBTOTAL 1' with the generic sentence twice, which named a position on the form without saying what had been subtracted.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label U1, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label U1
variable_description: Dividends from a private company that the trustee has judged not to be at arm's length, net of the expenses of earning them. The ATO builds the label from the dividends paid to the fund, plus any franking credits the fund can claim as an offset, less deductible expenses attributable to them, and directs that "Include non-share dividends that are non-arm's length income at label U1." Anything reported here is taxed at 45 per cent even in a complying fund, so the label carries a large tax consequence for a small number of funds.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label U1
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount, one of the three non-arm's length income labels that add to the total at label U. Expenses deducted against it are not shown again in Section C.
limitation: It rests on the trustee's own judgement about whether a dealing was at arm's length, so a zero can mean the income was arm's length or that the trustee did not treat it as caught. Because it is net of attributable expenses, it is not comparable with the gross dividend labels J, K and L on the same return.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label U1 heading, and the ATO instruction states the composition and the tax rate that follows.
evidence_quote: Include non-share dividends that are non-arm's length income at label U1.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that the amount is net, self-assessed, or taxed at the top rate.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section B label U2, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label U2
variable_description: Trust income the fund received that is not at arm's length, net of the expenses of earning it. The ATO takes "any non-arm's length income which the complying SMSF received in 2024-25 as a share of net income from a trust" and subtracts deductible expenses attributable to it. A distribution is caught automatically where the fund has no fixed entitlement to the trust's income, which is why an SMSF holding units in a discretionary trust reports here rather than at label M.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label U2
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount that can include capital gains and franked dividends received through the trust, and that feeds the non-arm's length total at label U taxed at 45 per cent.
limitation: The amount is a residual of the trustee's classification, so movement between this label and label M can reflect a change of view rather than a change in the investment. A net figure also cannot be compared against label M, which is gross of the expenses of earning it.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label U2 heading, and the ATO instruction gives the composition and the fixed entitlement test that routes income here.
evidence_quote: Write at label U2 the total of: any non-arm's length income which the complying SMSF received in 2024-25 as a share of net income from a trust, subtract deductible expenses attributable to the amount at label U2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain what makes a trust distribution non-arm's length or that the amount is net.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section F or G label T, SMSF annual return member statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label T
variable_description: Contributions made for this member while the fund was non-complying, reported once in the first year the fund becomes complying again. The ATO asks it only of a fund whose status changed, and takes contributions that "were made on or after 10 May 2006, and when the SMSF was non-complying" and that "haven't previously been reported at this question in an earlier year". The point is to bring historic contributions into the member's non-concessional contribution history rather than to record money received this year.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information, label T
value_definition: A whole-dollar member-level catch-up amount, counted in total contributions at label N but deliberately excluded from the member's opening account balance.
limitation: It is not a flow for the reporting year, so treating it as contributions received in that year overstates the year and understates the earlier ones it belongs to. It is also rare and almost always zero, since it only arises when a fund moves from non-complying to complying.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the member statement label T heading, and the ATO instruction defines the gate, the period covered and the once-only rule.
evidence_quote: Write at label T the total amount of contributions received for the member where those contributions: were made on or after 10 May 2006, and when the SMSF was non-complying, and haven't previously been reported at this question in an earlier year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount relates to earlier years rather than the reporting year.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label D2, SMSF annual return non-deductible expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label D2
variable_description: The share of the fund's capital works write-off that it cannot deduct, usually because the building supports pension income. The ATO says "Write at label D2 the amount of capital works expenditure that isn't deductible. For example, if the SMSF uses the capital works area for the purposes of gaining or producing exempt income, such as exempt current pension income." Capital works covers construction, extensions, alterations and structural improvements, and the deductible share of the same calculation sits at label D1.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label D2
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount in the non-deductible column, part of an annual write-off on building expenditure rather than a cash cost paid in the year.
limitation: It measures the pension share of a building deduction, not spending on buildings, so it rises when a fund moves into pension phase even though the property has not changed. The separate non-deductible column was also added part way through the period this asset covers, so an early year can be empty rather than zero.
rationale: The custodian's description names the non-deductible side of the capital works item, which is label D2 of Section C, and the ATO instruction says what falls into it.
evidence_quote: Write at label D2 the amount of capital works expenditure that isn't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is driven by exempt pension income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label E2, SMSF annual return non-deductible expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label E2
variable_description: The part of the year's depreciation on the fund's assets that it cannot deduct. The ATO says "Write at label E2 the amount for the decline in value of the SMSF's depreciating assets that isn't deductible. This includes an amount for the decline in value of a depreciating asset to the extent the asset is used for the purposes of gaining or producing exempt income, such as exempt current pension income." The deductible part of the same decline is at label E1, and the two together are the fund's full depreciation for the year.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label E2
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-cash amount, being the exempt-income share of the decline in value of fittings, plant and similar assets held by the fund.
limitation: It is not a purchase or a payment, so it cannot be used to track fund investment in assets, and it says nothing about the assets' value, which is reported separately in Section H. Its size follows the fund's exempt income proportion, so two funds with identical assets can report very different amounts.
rationale: The custodian's description names the non-deductible side of the decline in value item, which is label E2 of Section C, and the ATO instruction defines it.
evidence_quote: Write at label E2 the amount for the decline in value of the SMSF's depreciating assets that isn't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish a non-cash write-down from spending or explain the exempt income link.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label B2, SMSF annual return non-deductible expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label B2
variable_description: Interest on overseas borrowings that the fund cannot deduct, which is what the custodian's own description says this column holds. The ATO says "Write at label B2 the amount of interest expenses that the SMSF incurred on borrowings from overseas sources that isn't deductible. This includes an amount of interest expense to the extent the expense is incurred for the purposes of gaining or producing exempt income." The deductible half of the same interest is at label B1 on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label B2
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount in the non-deductible column of Section C, classified by where the lender is rather than by what the borrowing bought.
limitation: The abbreviated variable name reads as within Australia while the custodian's description says overseas, the same reversal that runs through the other interest expense columns here, so the name must not be used to build the Australian against overseas split. The amount also reflects the fund's exempt income share rather than the cost of borrowing offshore.
rationale: The custodian's description names the non-deductible side of the overseas interest item, which is label B2 of Section C, and the ATO instruction defines it.
evidence_quote: Write at label B2 the amount of interest expenses that the SMSF incurred on borrowings from overseas sources that isn't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic sentence twice and gave no warning that the variable name points the other way.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label H2, SMSF annual return non-deductible expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label H2
variable_description: The part of the fund's audit fee it cannot deduct, which is the share attributable to exempt pension income. The ATO says "Write at label H2 the amount for auditor fees that isn't deductible. This includes auditor fees to the extent the fees are incurred for the purposes of gaining or producing exempt income, such as exempt current pension income", and requires a zero rather than a blank if there were none. Every SMSF must be audited each year, so the fee exists even when this column is zero.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label H2
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount in the non-deductible column, paired with the deductible audit fee at label H1; the two together are what the auditor charged.
limitation: It is not the cost of the audit and cannot be used to price auditing, since a fund entirely in accumulation phase reports nothing here while still paying a fee. The custodian calls it the approved auditor fee while the current return calls it the SMSF auditor fee, and the separate non-deductible column was added part way through the period this asset covers, so an early year can carry no value.
rationale: The custodian's description names the non-deductible side of the auditor fee item, which is label H2 of Section C, and the ATO instruction defines it.
evidence_quote: Write at label H2 the amount for auditor fees that isn't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is only the disallowed share of the fee.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section C label U2, SMSF annual return non-deductible expenses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label U2
variable_description: Payments to a forestry managed investment scheme that the fund cannot deduct. The ATO says "Write at label U2 the total amount of payments made under an FMIS that aren't deductible", and gives two reasons why a payment fails: it is one of the excluded payments set out in the appendix on forestry managed investment schemes, or the income from the scheme is exempt income of the fund. The deductible payments are at label U1, and the income side of the same scheme is at Section B label X.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12, label U2
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount in the non-deductible column, covering payments to a forestry scheme rather than a valuation of the forestry interest.
limitation: It cannot be read as the fund's cost of forestry investing, because excluded payments and the pension share are mixed in the one figure and the deductible payments are recorded elsewhere. There is also a four-year holding rule for initial participants, so a disposal can turn earlier deductions around in ways this column does not show.
rationale: The custodian's description names the non-deductible side of the forestry managed investment scheme item, which is label U2 of Section C, and the ATO sets out both the excluded payments and the exempt income rule.
evidence_quote: Write at label U2 the total amount of payments made under an FMIS that aren't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say why a forestry payment is disallowed or where the deductible payments sit.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Section D label J, SMSF annual return calculation statement
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label J
variable_description: The penalty tax the fund pays on contributions made for a member whose tax file number it does not hold. It is the top-up that lifts those contributions to the top rate: "All SMSFs, complying and non-complying, have an overall tax rate of 47% on no-TFN-quoted contributions", made up of 15 per cent at label T1 plus 32 per cent here for a complying fund, or 45 plus 2 per cent for a non-complying one. It is added to tax on taxable income to give gross tax.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13, label J
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount worked out as a fixed percentage of the no-TFN-quoted contributions reported at Section B label R3, and mandatory, with a blank read as zero.
limitation: It measures a reporting failure rather than an economic quantity, and a fund can recover it later through a no-TFN tax offset, which appears at a different label and in a different year. The pension exemption does not reduce it, so it can be payable by a fund with no other tax.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the calculation statement label J heading, and the ATO instruction gives the rates and the link to the contributions label that drives it.
evidence_quote: All SMSFs, complying and non-complying, have an overall tax rate of 47% on no-TFN-quoted contributions: complying SMSFs pay 15% (at label T1) and 32% (at label J), a total of 47%.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label name with the generic sentence twice, so it did not give the rate, the base, or the offset that can reverse it.

value_domain: Dollar total reported at Section B label U, SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label U
variable_description: All of the fund's non-arm's length income for the year, added up and taxed at the top rate. The ATO forms it by adding the private company dividend, trust distribution and other non-arm's length labels, and says that "a tax rate of 45% is applied to the income you write at label U" when tax on taxable income is worked out. Each component is already net of the deductions attributable to it, so the total is not comparable with the gross income labels that sit above it.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return instructions 2025, Section B: Income - item 11, label U
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of labels U1, U2 and U3, excluded from the pension exemption that shelters the fund's other income.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as clean dealings, because whether a dealing was at arm's length is the trustee's own call and nothing on the face of the return tests it. The label also no longer captures every non-arm's length outcome: income arising from a non-arm's length general expense is dealt with inside the tax calculation instead, which the ATO notes means the label may not match the form's own 45 per cent descriptor.
rationale: The custodian's description matches the Section B label U heading, and the ATO instruction gives the arithmetic, the tax rate and the treatment of losses.
evidence_quote: When you work out Section D, item 13 - label T1 Tax on taxable income, a tax rate of 45% is applied to the income you write at label U.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net non-arm's length income' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say that losses are hidden or that the top rate follows from this label.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label U3
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
variable_description: Non-arm's length income the fund earned that was neither a private company dividend nor a trust distribution, net of the expenses attributed to it. The ATO directs the trustee to "Write at label U3 any non-arm's length income which the complying SMSF has for 2024-25 and that wasn't included at labels U1 or U2" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section B). It sits beside the private company dividend and trust distribution labels, and their total at label U is taxed at 45% rather than 15%.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income - item 11
value_definition: Whole dollars with no cents, already reduced by the deductible expenses attributable to that income. It is one of the three components of net non-arm's length income at label U.
limitation: Only a complying fund separates this income out; a non-complying fund reports the same amounts among the ordinary income labels, so a zero does not mean the fund dealt at arm's length. Since the non-arm's length expense changes, income arising from a general expense under the twice-the-difference approach is deliberately kept out of this label and handled in the tax calculation, so the column understates what is taxed at the top rate.
rationale: The label is a defined step of the SMSF annual return, and the ATO instructions for Section B set out what belongs at U3, what is excluded to U1 and U2, and how the total is taxed. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Write at label U3 any non-arm's length income which the complying SMSF has for 2024-25 and that wasn't included at labels U1 or U2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label J, member sections
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: Money transferred in from a foreign superannuation fund that is not taxed in the Australian fund. The ATO says to "Write at label J the total amount transferred from a foreign super fund or scheme for the member in 2024-25 except any part of the transfer that is assessable income of the fund" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G). The taxable part, being the growth not vested in the member at transfer, goes to label I, and any earnings the member elects to have taxed in the fund go to label M.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: Gross dollars of the non-assessable portion of a foreign transfer received for the member during the income year.
limitation: Untaxed does not mean unconstrained: the amount counts against the member's non-concessional contributions cap in the year it arrives, which is where excess contributions problems on overseas transfers arise. The full size of a transfer cannot be read from this column alone, because it is split across three labels according to tax treatment.
rationale: The member sections instructions define labels I, J and M for a foreign transfer and work an example that splits one transfer across all three. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Write at label J the total amount transferred from a foreign super fund or scheme for the member in 2024-25 except any part of the transfer that is assessable income of the fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label L, member sections
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: An amount moved out of the fund's own reserves into the member's account that is not taxed as a contribution to the fund. The ATO says to "Write at label L the non-assessable amount allocated from the SMSF's reserves to the member's account (other than amounts included at label O Allocated earnings or losses)" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G), and adds that "The amount written at label L is included in the member's non-concessional contributions".
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: Gross dollars allocated from a reserve during the income year that are not assessable to the fund, counted in the member's non-concessional contributions.
limitation: Non-assessable to the fund does not mean free of consequence for the member, since the allocation still uses up non-concessional cap space. Most reserve allocations never reach this label: fair and reasonable allocations under 5% and allocations to pay a current pension liability are reported as allocated earnings instead, so the column understates movement out of reserves.
rationale: The member sections instructions define label L, state its effect on the member's cap and list the allocations that are directed to the allocated earnings label instead. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Write at label L the non-assessable amount allocated from the SMSF's reserves to the member's account (other than amounts included at label O Allocated earnings or losses).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label A2
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
variable_description: Interest the fund incurred on borrowed money that it cannot deduct, usually the share relating to exempt pension income. The custodian's wording places it at label A2, where the ATO says to "Write at label A2 the amount of interest expenses that the SMSF incurred on borrowings from Australian sources that isn't deductible" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section C). The variable name says overseas while the custodian's description says within Australia, and the sibling column NN_DDCTB_EXPN_INTS_WTH_AUS_AMT carries the mirror image of the same conflict.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
value_definition: Whole dollars, the non-deductible portion only; the deductible portion of the same borrowing sits at label A1 and the pair together is the fund's interest cost on that source of funds.
limitation: The name and the label description point at opposite sides of the Australia against overseas split, so this column alone cannot tell you where the money was borrowed; the two interest columns have to be read together against the fund's totals. The deductible and non-deductible split is also the trustee's own apportionment rather than an ATO determination.
rationale: The Section C instructions define both non-deductible interest labels, which lets the custodian's description be placed at label A2 and exposes the disagreement with the variable name. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Write at label A2 the amount of interest expenses that the SMSF incurred on borrowings from Australian sources that isn't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and it never flagged that the variable name and the custodian's description disagree about Australian against overseas borrowing.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label I2
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
variable_description: Investment management costs the fund cannot deduct, in practice the share of them that relates to exempt current pension income. The ATO says to "Write at label I2 the amount of investment expenses that aren't deductible" and that this "includes an amount of investment expense to the extent the expense is incurred for the purposes of gaining or producing exempt income, such as ECPI" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section C). The deductible share of the same costs is at label I1 on the same row.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
value_definition: Whole dollars covering revenue-nature costs of managing or maintaining investments, such as adviser retainers, brokerage and portfolio servicing fees.
limitation: The split between the deductible and non-deductible halves is the trustee's own apportionment, usually driven by an actuarial pension percentage, so the figure is a self-assessed allocation and not an audited fact. A fund with no pension member normally reports nothing here even though it clearly incurs investment costs.
rationale: The Section C instructions define both investment expense labels and give worked examples showing how a pension-paying fund splits one fee between them. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Write at label I2 the amount of investment expenses that aren't deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label J2
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
variable_description: Fund running costs that cannot be deducted, such as set-up fees, trust deed changes and late lodgment penalties. The ATO lists "fees for setting up the SMSF", "legal fees incurred to amend a trust deed to include a new member" and "late lodgment penalties" among them (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section C). Auditor fees and investment management costs are kept out and reported at labels H2 and I2.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
value_definition: Whole dollars of revenue-nature administration and management costs that the fund cannot claim, including the exempt-income share of otherwise deductible administration.
limitation: It is not the cost of running the fund: the deductible half at label J1 usually holds most of the spending, since tax agent fees, the supervisory levy and interest charges are all deductible and never appear here. A large value is more often a set-up or penalty event than a high administration burden.
rationale: The Section C instructions define label J2, name the expenses that belong to it and say which costs must be reported at other labels instead. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Non-deductible management and administration expenses include: fees for setting up the SMSF, legal fees incurred to amend a trust deed to include a new member, late lodgment penalties.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label L2
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
variable_description: Expenses that fit no other Section C label and cannot be deducted, the largest of which is normally the fund's own income tax. The ATO says to "include income tax paid by the SMSF at label L2 as it isn't deductible at all" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section C). A one-letter code in the box beside it names the biggest component, and the deductible counterpart is at label L1.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
value_definition: Whole dollars of residual non-deductible expenditure, paired on the same row with the category code at NON_DDCTBL_EXPNS_OTHR_CD.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed. Income tax paid, forex losses, balancing adjustment losses and a return of contributions by a non-complying fund all land in one number, and only the largest of them is named by the code. Because income tax is usually the biggest item, movements in this column tend to track last year's tax bill rather than this year's spending.
rationale: The Section C instructions define the other amounts labels, publish the category table and state expressly that income tax paid belongs at label L2. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: For example, include income tax paid by the SMSF at label L2 as it isn't deductible at all.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: ATO other amounts category code (Table 7, SMSF annual return)
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
variable_description: A single letter naming the largest kind of expense inside the non-deductible other amounts figure at label L2. The ATO says to "Print the code from Table 7 that best describes the largest amount you include at each of labels L1 and L2" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section C). The letters are A balancing adjustment, B a contribution that is a fringe benefit, C exclusion of personal contributions, E environmental protection activities, F forex losses, I a listed investment company capital gain deduction, N a deduction for foreign non-assessable non-exempt income, R a return of contributions by a non-complying fund, T taxation of financial arrangements amounts, and O other.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
value_definition: One upper case letter from a closed list of ten, attached to the dollar amount at label L2 on the same row.
limitation: It describes the largest component only, so a fund with several kinds of other expense reveals just one of them, and code O says nothing beyond none of the above. The same code table serves the deductible label L1, so a code taken out of context does not say which of the two columns it qualifies.
rationale: The Section C instructions publish the code table and the rule for choosing a code, which is what turns this column from an unexplained letter into a readable category. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Print the code from Table 7 that best describes the largest amount you include at each of labels L1 and L2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label Y
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
variable_description: Everything the fund spent during the year that it cannot claim as a deduction, added across the non-deductible column. The ATO instruction is to "Add all the non-deductible expenses from labels A2 to L2" and "Write the total at label Y" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section C). Added to total deductions at label N it gives total SMSF expenses at label Z.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section C: Deductions and non-deductible expenses - item 12
value_definition: Whole dollars, the arithmetic sum of the eleven non-deductible expense labels on the same return.
limitation: It is a subtotal of columns that also appear separately on the same row, so adding it to its components double counts. It is also a poor measure of waste: most of it is the pension-exempt share of ordinary running costs plus the fund's own income tax, not spending that went astray.
rationale: The Section C instructions define label Y as the sum of labels A2 to L2 and place it in the chain that produces total SMSF expenses. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Add all the non-deductible expenses from labels A2 to L2. Write the total at label Y.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label D
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13
variable_description: Tax offsets that can cut the fund's tax to zero and be kept for later if unused, all of them early stage investment incentives. The ATO explains that "If the total of the non-refundable carry forward tax offsets at label D is greater than the remaining tax at label T2, the excess may be carried forward to a future income year" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section D). It totals the early stage venture capital limited partnership and early stage investor offsets, current year and carried forward.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label T3

variable_description: The fund's tax after the non-refundable offsets have been applied, and before franking credits and the other refundable ones. Zero has two meanings here, a fund with no taxable income and a fund whose offsets wiped out its tax, and this column cannot tell them apart without the gross tax and offset columns beside it.
rationale: The Section D instructions name label T3 as subtotal 2 and define it as the tax remaining after the carry forward offsets are applied. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label T5
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13

The ATO instruction is to "Subtract the amount at label E Refundable tax offsets from label T3 Subtotal" and "Write the result at label T5" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section D). The variable name is misleading: the sibling column NEW_SBTOTL_AMT holds subtotal 1, while this one holds the tax.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13

The supervisory levy, the section 102AAM interest charge, eligible credits and PAYG instalments already raised are all applied afterwards to give the amount due or refundable. Because zero is both common and mandatory, a zero cannot be distinguished from a question that did not apply.
rationale: The Section D instructions define label T5 by the subtraction that produces it, mark it mandatory and set out the further steps that lead to the amount due or refundable. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Subtract the amount at label E Refundable tax offsets from label T3 Subtotal. Write the result at label T5.

value_domain: Scrambled identifier for a self-managed superannuation fund
value_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The self-managed fund itself, carried as a scrambled code so a fund's return can be joined to its members' statements. It is the key that ties the fund-level annual return table to the member-level table, in the same way that the member contributions data uses provider and supplier scrambled identifiers for the entities that lodge. The Productivity Commission describes the general method, whereby the ABS replaces a source identifier with a synthetic one so that tables can be connected without re-identifying the entity.
description_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque code with no meaning in its digits, one value per fund, repeated on every row belonging to that fund within the SMSF tables.
limitation: It identifies a fund, not a person: a couple's fund is a single value covering two members, so counting distinct values counts funds and not people. Nothing published states that the value survives from one data extract to the next, so a fund cannot safely be followed across vintages on this column without checking that first.
rationale: No ATO or ABS page defines this column by name. The reading is assembled from the PLIDA identifier method the Productivity Commission documents, from the naming pattern of the scrambled identifiers in the sibling member contributions tables, and from the fact that the column appears on both the fund and member tables of this module.
evidence_quote: The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Fund scrambled identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the key is the join between the fund return and the member statements, nor that it is not a person.
