value_domain: Count of properties reported at SMSF annual return label J7
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities - items 15 and 16

The ATO says to "Write at label S1 the closing account balance of accounts that are in the accumulation phase" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G), and requires that the three closing balance labels add to the member's closing account balance at label S.

value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: What the member would actually receive from their accumulation accounts if they cashed out, which can be less than the account balance. The ATO defines it: "The accumulation phase value is the total amount of the superannuation benefits that would become payable if the member voluntarily caused the interest to cease" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G), and adds that it "is often less than the value at label S1 Accumulation phase account balance as the costs to cease the interest are subtracted from the account balance".

value_definition: Whole dollars at 30 June, required where the gap between it and the accumulation phase account balance is not limited to administration and exit fees and realisation costs, and used in place of that balance in the total superannuation balance whenever a figure above nil is supplied.
limitation: It is usually blank, and blank means the same as the account balance rather than unknown or zero. Treating an empty value as zero destroys the member's total superannuation balance. The reporting rule is also conditional and self-assessed, so its presence tells you about the fund's reporting choices as much as about the member's benefits.
rationale: The member sections instructions define the accumulation phase value, explain why it usually falls short of the account balance and state the conditions under which it must be reported. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.

value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13

rationale: The Section D instructions state the levy amount, forbid the trustee from changing it, and explain the year it covers. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Label L shows the amount of supervisory levy due for 2025-26 ($259). Don't change the amount printed on the annual return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label N
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13
variable_description: An extra levy a newly registered fund pays with its first return, covering the year it has just finished. The ATO explains that "The amount at label N is the SMSF supervisory levy for 2024-25. SMSFs that are lodging their first annual return haven't paid this amount previously" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section D). It is added to the amount due, so a first return carries a double levy.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13
value_definition: Either blank or the full year levy for the income year being reported, $259 on the 2025 return, and never any other value.
limitation: It flags a fund's first return, but not reliably: the ATO also requires the matching first return answer in Section A, and a trustee who leaves this label blank produces a first return that looks like any other. Unlike the wind-up adjustment, it increases what the fund owes rather than reducing it, so the two adjustment columns must not be treated as a pair of offsets.
rationale: The Section D instructions define label N, publish the table of levy amounts by fund circumstance, and state which return it applies to. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: The amount at label N is the SMSF supervisory levy for 2024-25. SMSFs that are lodging their first annual return haven't paid this amount previously.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label M
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13
variable_description: A credit that cancels the levy for a fund that wound up during the year, so it does not pay for a year in which it will not exist. The ATO says "An SMSF which was wound up during 2024-25 doesn't pay the SMSF supervisory levy for 2025-26. Writing $259 at label M reduces the levy payable by $259" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Section D). It is subtracted in working out the amount due or refundable.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement - item 13
value_definition: Either blank or the full year levy, $259 on the 2025 return, and never a part year amount.
limitation: It is not a complete register of wind-ups. The ATO's own table leaves this label blank for a fund that was both newly registered and wound up in the same year, so counting wind-ups on this column misses first-year funds that closed. It also gives no wind-up date; that comes from the wind-up date and indicator columns in Section A.
rationale: The Section D instructions define label M, publish the table of levy amounts by fund circumstance, including the newly registered and wound up case, and explain how the credit is applied. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: An SMSF which was wound up during 2024-25 doesn't pay the SMSF supervisory levy for 2025-26. Writing $259 at label M reduces the levy payable by $259.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at SMSF annual return label F, member sections
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: Money put into the member's account by their spouse, or by a parent or relative for a member under 18. The ATO defines the label as covering "contributions made by the member's spouse" and "contributions made by parents, relatives or others on behalf of a member who is under 18 years old" (ATO, SMSF annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G). Contributions from a former or separated spouse are excluded and reported as other third party contributions.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: Gross dollars received for the member during the income year from a spouse or, for a child member, from a family contributor.
limitation: The two kinds are not separated, so a spouse contribution and a grandparent's gift to a teenage member are the same number and cannot be told apart. Contributions splitting transfers are excluded to the inward rollover label, so this is not a measure of money moving between partners.
rationale: The member sections instructions define label F, name both kinds of contributor it covers and list the cases that must go to other labels. The page was read live in a browser, since ato.gov.au refuses automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: contributions made by parents, relatives or others on behalf of a member who is under 18 years old.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's own label text as its description and printed the same no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which form label the number comes from or how to read it.

value_domain: PLIDA synthetic person identifier (Agency Entity Unique ID)
value_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The individual member a superannuation statement belongs to, carried as a meaningless code in place of a name or tax file number. The Productivity Commission describes how it is built: "The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it". It is the only person-level key on the row, so grouping by it turns member statements into one person's superannuation history, while SF_SID beside it identifies the fund.
description_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque code standing in for the person's identifier in the source data, repeated across the datasets from the same source, with no age, sex, location or account information in the value and nothing to decode or order.
limitation: It is not a common key across agencies: the Productivity Commission notes that "Synthetic AEUIDs are unique to an entity within a data source and are not repeated across sources", so a value matching one in Census or Centrelink data is a coincidence and any cross-module join has to go through the spine concordance tables. One person can also appear on several rows in a year through membership of more than one fund, so counting rows counts memberships rather than people.
rationale: The Productivity Commission's PLIDA guide documents the identifier the ABS places on every module, including the tax and superannuation data, and states both how it links within a source and why it does not link across sources.
evidence_quote: The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset' with a domain inferred from the variable name, so it never said what the key joins, what it cannot join, or how it relates to the fund identifier beside it.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at Section A item 9 of the SMSF annual return
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A: SMSF information (items 1 to 10)
variable_description: The trustees' own yes or no answer on whether the fund has met all its tax lodgement and payment obligations. The question hangs off item 9, which asks whether the fund was wound up during the income year, and the instruction is to "Print X in the appropriate box, either No or Yes at item 9". For a fund being wound up the ATO is asking whether the trustees have paid all outstanding debts, paid out or transferred all member benefits, and lodged all previous years' annual returns.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section A: SMSF information (items 1 to 10)
value_definition: A two-state indicator, yes or no, with a blank where the trustees left the box empty. It carries no amount, no date and no detail of which obligation was outstanding.
limitation: It cannot establish that the obligations were met. The box records what the trustees asserted on the day they lodged, and a later ATO review can contradict it. Because the question sits inside the wind-up item, a blank is far more often a fund that kept operating than a fund in default, so counting blanks as non-compliance is wrong.
rationale: The custodian's label is the exact wording of a question in Section A of the SMSF annual return, and the ATO instruction page for that section says where the answer goes and what the trustees are being asked to confirm.
evidence_quote: Have all tax lodgment and payment obligations been met? Print X in the appropriate box, either No or Yes at item 9.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return's question as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said who answers, when the question is asked, or that the answer is a trustee assertion.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section E label U, tax losses carried forward
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section E: Losses (item 14)
variable_description: The stock of tax losses the fund still has available to deduct in later years. The ATO says to "Write at label U the total tax losses of the SMSF that are to be carried forward to later income years", made up of this year's tax loss plus prior year losses "to the extent that they haven't previously been utilised". Net capital losses are excluded and go at label V, and losses tied to non-arm's length income are excluded altogether.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section E: Losses (item 14)
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance with no cents, and a stock rather than a flow: the current year loss added to the unused remainder of earlier losses. Net exempt income for the year is netted off before the current year loss is worked out.
limitation: It is not this year's loss. A fund with a profitable year can still carry a large balance from years past, and a fund with a bad year can show nil because net exempt income absorbed the loss. It also understates unrecouped losses, since losses attached to non-arm's length income are kept only in the fund's own records.
rationale: The label text matches Section E label U of the SMSF annual return exactly, and the ATO instruction page defines what the balance comprises, what it excludes, and how net exempt income changes it.
evidence_quote: Write at label U the total tax losses of the SMSF that are to be carried forward to later income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reused the form label as its description and repeated the generic sentence about no published value list twice, so it never said the figure is a cumulative balance rather than the year's loss.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section D label T1, tax on taxable income
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
variable_description: Tax worked out on the fund's taxable income alone, before any other charge, offset or credit. The rate depends on the fund's status and on how the income arose: "All assessable income for a non-complying SMSF is taxed at 45%", while a complying fund pays 15% on its arm's length income and 45% on the non-arm's length component. The next label adds tax on no-TFN-quoted contributions, and the two together make gross tax at label B.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax amount computed from label A. For a complying fund it is 15% of taxable income less the non-arm's length component, plus 45% of that component; for a non-complying fund it is 45% of the whole.
limitation: It is not the fund's tax bill and not a tax rate numerator you can trust on its own. Franking and other credits, tax offsets, the supervisory levy and PAYG instalments all sit between this figure and the amount finally due, and dividing it by taxable income only recovers 15% for funds with no non-arm's length income.
rationale: The label matches Section D label T1, and the ATO instruction page sets out the rates, the arm's length split and the worked example that shows T1 feeding into gross tax at label B.
evidence_quote: All assessable income for a non-complying SMSF is taxed at 45%, whether arm's length income, non-arm's length income or arising from a change in the SMSF's tax status.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Tax on taxable income' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not say which rate applies or how far this figure sits from the amount payable.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section D label A, taxable income used for the tax calculation
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
variable_description: The taxable income the fund's tax is actually calculated on, which is set to zero whenever the fund made a loss. The ATO instruction is explicit about the censoring: transfer the Section C figure to label A if it is income, but "Yes - Write 0 (zero) at label A" if it is a loss. This is the Section D copy of the figure, not the signed Section C figure that the loss version of this column carries.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, never negative, that equals the Section C taxable income or loss when that figure is positive and zero otherwise. It is one of the five mandatory labels, so a blank is treated as zero.
limitation: A zero does not mean the fund broke even. It means the fund made a loss whose size shows up only at Section C or in the carried-forward losses at Section E, so an average built on this column censors every loss-making fund at zero and overstates the typical fund's position.
rationale: The instruction page distinguishes label A in Section D from label O in Section C by name and by the zero rule, which is exactly the distinction between this column and the taxable income or loss column beside it.
evidence_quote: Is the amount at label O Taxable income or a loss? No - Transfer the amount from Section C, item 12 - label O Taxable income or loss to label A. Yes - Write 0 (zero) at label A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Taxable income' and nothing more, which left it indistinguishable from the taxable income or loss column on the same table and hid the fact that losses are recorded here as zero.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section C label O, taxable income or loss (signed)
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
variable_description: The fund's assessable income less its deductions, signed, so a loss-making fund shows a negative figure. It is the Section C label O total that the calculation statement starts from: "You wrote the SMSF's taxable income, or its loss, at Section C, item 12 - label O Taxable income or loss." Exempt current pension income has already been taken out before this line.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount that may be positive or negative, being total assessable income, including assessable contributions and net non-arm's length income, less allowable deductions.
limitation: It is a tax figure, not a measure of what the fund earned. A fund paying pensions can hold large investments and report a small taxable income because exempt current pension income was removed first. Read against the Section D taxable income on the same row, the difference is the size of the loss, not an error.
rationale: The instruction page names label O in Section C as the signed taxable income or loss and shows how it feeds label A, which is what separates this column from the taxable income column beside it.
evidence_quote: You wrote the SMSF's taxable income, or its loss, at Section C, item 12 - label O Taxable income or loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form's upper-case label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure can be negative or how it relates to the taxable income column on the same table.

value_domain: Signed dollar amount at Section D, amount due or refundable
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
variable_description: The bottom line of the fund's tax calculation, with the sign carrying the direction of the payment. The ATO says the label "can be zero, positive or negative", that "a positive amount is what you must pay to us" and that "a negative amount is the refund you will receive". It is built by adding tax payable, the section 102AAM interest charge, the supervisory levy and the new-fund levy adjustment, then subtracting eligible credits, tax offset refunds, PAYG instalments raised and the wound-up levy adjustment.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section D: Income tax calculation statement (item 13)
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount covering income tax and the SMSF supervisory levy together, net of credits and instalments already raised for the year.
limitation: It is not tax on income, and it is not cash moved. The supervisory levy is inside it, so a fund with no taxable income still shows an amount due; and interim or voluntary payments the fund has already made are deliberately left out of the calculation, so the figure differs from what the trustees actually remitted. A negative value is a refund, so summing the column without keeping the sign turns refunds into liabilities.
rationale: The instruction page gives the arithmetic of the label and states the sign convention, which is the fact a user needs before treating the column as a tax liability.
evidence_quote: Label S Amount due or refundable can be zero, positive or negative: a positive amount is what you must pay to us, a negative amount is the refund you will receive.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form's upper-case label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that negative values are refunds or that the supervisory levy is bundled into the total.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section I, total assessable TOFA gains
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section I: Taxation of financial arrangements (item 17)
variable_description: Gains the fund brought to account on financial arrangements under the taxation of financial arrangements rules. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label H the SMSF's total assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements", and only a small group of funds ever reaches the label: the rules apply where "the value of the SMSF's assets is $100 million or more" or where the fund elected in. Losses under the same rules are reported separately at the next label rather than netted here.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section I: Taxation of financial arrangements (item 17)
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross gain figure for the income year, worked out under the accruals, realisation, fair value, retranslation, hedging or financial-reports methods that the TOFA rules allow.
limitation: A blank almost always means the rules did not apply, not that the fund had no gains on financial instruments, because the $100 million asset test excludes nearly every SMSF. The label is a disclosure of gains already brought into the income items, so adding it to assessable income counts the same money twice.
rationale: The instruction page for Section I gives the label wording and states the threshold and election that decide whether any fund reports here, which is what makes the column interpretable.
evidence_quote: The TOFA rules apply to an SMSF only where: the value of the SMSF's assets is $100 million or more; the SMSF has elected to have the TOFA rules apply to it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total TOFA gains' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so a reader could not tell that the column is near-empty by design or what a TOFA gain is.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section I, total deductible TOFA losses
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section I: Taxation of financial arrangements (item 17)
variable_description: Losses on financial arrangements that the fund can deduct under the taxation of financial arrangements rules. The instruction is to "Write at label I the SMSF's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements", and the question is asked only of funds inside the rules, which take in assets of $100 million or more or an election. The gain side of the same calculation sits at the previous label and is not offset against this one.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section I: Taxation of financial arrangements (item 17)
value_definition: A whole-dollar figure of deductible losses for the income year, reported as a positive number rather than as a negative gain.
limitation: It is a deductible amount, not an economic loss, so a fund holding a hedge that fell in value reports here only if the TOFA method it uses recognises the fall this year. Subtracting it from the TOFA gain column does not give a net position that appears anywhere on the return, because both feed the income and deduction items separately.
rationale: The instruction page carries the label wording for the loss side and the same threshold test that governs the gain side.
evidence_quote: Yes - Write at label I the SMSF's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Total TOFA losses' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it was indistinguishable from the TOFA gains column apart from the word 'losses'.

value_domain: Dollar amount at Section B label F, assessable transfers from foreign super funds
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income (item 11)
variable_description: Only the part of money moved into the fund from a foreign super fund that counts as the fund's own assessable income. It covers the amount the former member of the foreign fund "has made a written choice to have included in the SMSF's assessable income", plus any amount transferred above what was vested in the member. The ATO adds that the figure "shouldn't be reduced by any loss or outgoing incurred in gaining or producing the income".
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income (item 11)
value_definition: A gross whole-dollar income amount for the year, summed over all qualifying transfers the fund received, and not sheltered by the exempt current pension income rules.
limitation: It is not the size of the transfer. In the ATO's own example a $100,000 transfer produces $10,000 at this label because that is all the member elected to have taxed in the fund, and the remaining $90,000 appears nowhere on the return. Using the column to measure retirement savings moved into Australia will understate it heavily.
rationale: The Section B instruction page names the label, states the two components of the amount and works an example that shows how far the reported figure sits below the money transferred.
evidence_quote: SMSF F reports $10,000 at label F Transfers from foreign funds and writes 1 (one) in the Number box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it read as the value of foreign transfers when it is only the assessable slice of them.

value_domain: Count in the Number box beside Section B label F
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income (item 11)
variable_description: How many qualifying transfers from foreign super funds the fund received during the year, counted beside the dollar amount. The instruction is to "Write in the Number box the number of transfers received from foreign super funds or schemes during 2024-25 that meet the criteria above", where the criteria are the same written choice and excess-over-vested tests that govern the amount. It counts transfers, not members and not foreign funds.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section B: Income (item 11)
value_definition: A small whole number for the income year, usually zero or one, restricted to transfers that produced an assessable amount at the paired dollar label.
limitation: It undercounts inbound foreign transfers, because a transfer with no assessable component is not counted here at all even though the money arrived. It also does not identify the member, so it cannot be used to attribute a transfer to a person without going to the member sections of the return.
rationale: The instruction page defines the Number box explicitly and ties its counting rule to the same criteria as the dollar label, which is what distinguishes this column from the amount beside it.
evidence_quote: Write in the Number box the number of transfers received from foreign super funds or schemes during 2024-25 that meet the criteria above.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Number of transfers from foreign funds' with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say that transfers without an assessable component are not counted.

value_domain: Count of transition to retirement income stream accounts held by a member
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: How many transition to retirement accounts this member still holds in accumulation phase in this fund. The ATO instruction is to "Write the total number of accounts that are transition to retirement income stream products that the member has in accumulation phase", and it adds that "The TRIS is in accumulation phase unless you have reached age 65 or have met another nil cashing restriction condition of release". The account balances that go with it are reported at the accumulation and retirement phase labels on the same member record.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A whole number of accounts for one member in one fund at the end of the income year, not a number of members and not a count of income streams being paid.
limitation: A drop to zero is ambiguous between the member closing the account and the member turning 65 or meeting another condition of release, which moves the same account out of the count and into retirement phase. It is also fund specific, so a member drawing a transition to retirement pension from an APRA fund shows nothing here.
rationale: The member information part of the instructions gives the counting rule for the TRIS count and states the condition that moves an account out of the count, which is the interpretive trap in the column.
evidence_quote: Write the total number of accounts that are transition to retirement income stream products that the member has in accumulation phase.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'TRIS count' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving the abbreviation unexpanded and the phase rule unstated.

value_domain: Dollar asset value at Section H item 15, unlisted shares
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities (items 15 and 16)
variable_description: What the fund's holdings in unlisted companies were worth at 30 June, as the trustees valued them. The ATO instruction is to "Write at label I the value (on 30 June 2025) of shares, equities and similar financial contracts held by the SMSF that aren't listed on Australian stock exchanges". Unlisted trust interests belong at the unlisted trusts label instead, and unlisted shares held under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement go to the Australian shares label in the borrowing item.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities (items 15 and 16)
value_definition: A whole-dollar stock value at a single date, covering shares, equities and similar financial contracts in entities that are not on an Australian exchange.
limitation: It is not the fund's whole exposure to private companies, because holdings inside a limited recourse borrowing arrangement are reported at a different label and are invisible here. There is no market price to check the number against, so the column reflects the trustees' valuation practice as much as the assets, and a related-party shareholding looks the same as an arm's length one.
rationale: The Section H instruction page names the label, gives the valuation date and lists what has to be reported elsewhere, which sets the boundary of the column.
evidence_quote: Write at label I the value (on 30 June 2025) of shares, equities and similar financial contracts held by the SMSF that aren't listed on Australian stock exchanges.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Unlisted shares' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no valuation date and no warning about the borrowing-arrangement carve-out.

value_domain: Dollar asset value at Section H item 15a, unlisted trusts
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities (items 15 and 16)
variable_description: What the fund's units in Australian trusts that are not traded on an exchange were worth at 30 June. The ATO defines the category plainly - "Unlisted trusts are trusts that aren't traded or purchased through an Australian stock exchange" - and asks for "the value (on 30 June 2025) of unlisted trust interests held by the SMSF that were registered or located in Australia". Units in listed trusts go at the label above, and units held under a limited recourse borrowing arrangement go to the other-assets label in the borrowing item.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Section H: Assets and liabilities (items 15 and 16)
value_definition: A whole-dollar stock value at a single date, limited to trusts registered or located in Australia, and covering unit holdings rather than shares.
limitation: A large balance says nothing about whether the trust is a related party; non-arm's length distributions from it have to be read at the net non-arm's length trust distributions label in Section B. Overseas managed investments are excluded by the Australian-registration test, so the column is not the fund's total managed-fund exposure.
rationale: The Section H instruction page defines an unlisted trust in the ATO's own words and gives the valuation date and the exclusions for this label.
evidence_quote: Unlisted trusts are trusts that aren't traded or purchased through an Australian stock exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Unlisted trusts' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not define the category or say that only Australian trusts are counted.

value_domain: Year of birth (four digits)
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: The year part of the member's date of birth as the fund's trustees reported it. The member sections of the annual return require the trustees to write the member's "family name, first given name, other given names, tax file number (TFN)" and "date of birth", and the PLIDA table keeps the year and the month in separate columns with the day removed. It is the birth date attached to a superannuation account, not one drawn from a births register.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year. The day of birth is not carried, and the month sits in the companion month-of-birth column on the same member record.
limitation: It cannot give exact age at a contribution, a benefit payment or a condition of release, which matters because most superannuation age tests fall on a birthday. It is also self-reported by the trustees, so the same person's year can differ between funds or between years of the return, and it should not be used to correct or override the spine's demographic data.
rationale: The instructions establish that date of birth is collected from the trustees in the member information part of the return; the truncation to year and month is visible in the PLIDA table structure rather than in the ATO source.
evidence_quote: Write the member's: family name, first given name, other given names, tax file number (TFN), date of birth.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Year of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say who supplies the date or that the day has been removed.

value_domain: Year of death (four digits), reported for members who died in the income year
value_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
variable_description: The year a member died, present only where the death fell inside the year the return covers. The instruction applies to the supplementary member section, which is used for people who were members during the year but not at 30 June: for those members the trustees also "write the date of death, if the member died during 2024-25". The month sits in a companion column and the day is not carried.
description_source: ATO, Self-managed superannuation fund annual return 2025 instructions, Sections F and G: Member and supplementary member information
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year on a member record, populated only for a death reported in that return, and blank for every other member.
limitation: It is not a death indicator for fund membership. A member who died in an earlier year carries no year here, so counting non-blank values counts deaths reported in a given return rather than deaths of SMSF members over time. The Deaths registrations data in PLIDA remains the authority on the fact and date of death.
rationale: The instructions tie the date of death to the supplementary member section and to deaths within the income year, which sets the population the column can describe; the truncation to year and month is a PLIDA treatment rather than an ATO one.
evidence_quote: For members reported in Section G, you also: write the date of death, if the member died during 2024-25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Year of death' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that only deaths inside the reported year appear.

value_domain: Year-to-date dollar amount of allowances reported in an STP pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Allowances
variable_description: The allowances an employer paid this person, reported apart from ordinary pay. Allowances cover work-related costs or conditions, and the ATO separates them from money paid back against receipts: "Reimbursements should not be reported through STP." The basis of the column moves at the phase change, because "In Phase 1 reporting, some allowances are reported separately, and some are reported as part of Gross. This has changed for STP Phase 2."
description_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Allowances
value_definition: A dollar amount reported in a pay event for one payee under one payer, cumulative for the financial year to the date of the event rather than the value of that single pay.
limitation: It is not the cost of the person's work-related expenses. Overtime meal and travel allowances up to the ATO reasonable amount need not be reported at all, so the smaller allowances are missing; living away from home allowance fringe benefits are excluded; and the set of allowances inside the total widens once an employer moves to Phase 2.
rationale: The allowances page in the STP guidelines defines what an employer must and must not report as an allowance, and states the Phase 1 to Phase 2 change that breaks the series.
evidence_quote: In Phase 1 reporting, some allowances are reported separately, and some are reported as part of Gross. This has changed for STP Phase 2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name 'Allowance Income Total Amount - Event payment' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what counts as an allowance or that the definition changed mid-series.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum A payment on termination
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out on termination that falls into the lump sum A category, which is taxed at a concessional flat rate rather than as ordinary pay. The ATO limits it to "unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993", holiday pay and other leave-related payments that accrued before 18 August 1993, and post-1993 leave paid in connection with a genuine redundancy, an early retirement scheme or the invalidity segment of a termination payment. The type code column beside it says which of those two situations applies.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer, reported apart from gross pay and cumulative to the date of the pay event within the financial year.
limitation: It is not all unused leave paid on termination. Leave that accrued after 17 August 1993 and was paid on an ordinary resignation goes into gross pay instead, so the column captures old accruals and redundancy-linked leave only, and a nil value in a genuine termination is normal rather than a gap.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define the four lump sum types in the ATO's own words, and the STP pay event carries the same lump sum categories as the payment summary it replaced.
evidence_quote: unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which accrual periods fall into lump sum A or why the rest of unused leave is missing.

value_domain: Lump sum A type code, R or T
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: A one-letter code saying why the lump sum A on the same row was paid, which sets the rate of withholding on it. The ATO gives two valid values: "R - if the payment was made for a genuine redundancy, invalidity or under an early retirement scheme" and "T - if the payment was made for any other reason." The code is only completed where there is a lump sum A amount: "If there is no amount included at Lump sum A, do not complete the 'Type' box."
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A single character from a closed pair, R or T, attached to the lump sum A amount on the same record and blank when that amount is absent.
limitation: A code of T does not mean the person resigned. It is the residual for every reason other than redundancy, invalidity and early retirement, so dismissal, the end of a fixed term and a voluntary quit all sit inside it. The code also describes the lump sum only, not the termination, so it cannot be read as a reason-for-leaving field for the job.
rationale: The payment summary instructions publish both codes with their meanings and the rule for when the box is left blank, which is exactly the domain of this column.
evidence_quote: R - if the payment was made for a genuine redundancy, invalidity or under an early retirement scheme. T - if the payment was made for any other reason.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the field name 'Annual Long Service Leave Unused Lump Sum A Code' and the generic no-value-list sentence, so the two-value domain was never stated.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum B payment on termination
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused long service leave paid out on termination that accrued in the oldest tax era. The ATO defines lump sum B as "Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978", which is why it is reported apart from both gross pay and lump sum A. Anything accrued after that date is reported at lump sum A or inside gross pay depending on when it accrued and why it was paid.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer, covering long service leave entitlements earned before 16 August 1978 and reported outside gross pay.
limitation: It is a vanishing category rather than a live measure: only a person with continuous service since the 1970s can have any, so an overwhelmingly nil column is the expected result and a non-nil value marks extreme tenure rather than a large payout. It does not indicate how much long service leave the person actually took or accrued in total.
rationale: The payment summary instructions give the accrual cut-off that defines lump sum B and separate it from the other three lump sum types.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished lump sum B from lump sum A.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum D payment, tax-free redundancy component
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The part of a redundancy payout that is not taxed at all, reported apart from every other amount on the row. The ATO defines lump sum D as "The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment", which is capped by a base amount and a per-year-of-service amount that both change each year. It is the only lump sum type the STP guidelines leave out of the employer's gross total.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer that is non-assessable, non-exempt income, so no withholding attaches to it and it is not part of the person's taxable income.
limitation: The column name refers to unused leave, but a lump sum D is not a leave payment: it is the tax-free slice of a redundancy or early retirement payout. Because the tax-free cap rises each year, an amount here is bounded by the year's cap rather than by the size of the settlement, so it understates redundancy generosity for long-serving and highly paid workers.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define lump sum D directly, and the STP guidelines' employer-totals table confirms it is the one lump sum type excluded from the gross total.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the leave-flavoured payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, which actively misled: nothing said lump sum D is a redundancy component and not leave.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum E payment, back pay for an earlier year
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Back pay for work done more than a year earlier, kept apart so the payee can claim the lump sum E tax offset. The ATO defines it as "Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments". Back pay that accrued within the last twelve months is not reported here; it goes to whichever payment type it would have been paid as at the time.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer, covering arrears that relate to an earlier income year rather than to the current pay period.
limitation: The category narrows across the phase change: under Phase 2 a return to work payment is reported as lump sum W instead, and back pay below the lump sum E threshold is reported as the payment type it matches, so a fall in this column after an employer transitions is a reporting rule and not a fall in arrears paid. It also says nothing about which year the arrears relate to.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define lump sum E, and the STP Phase 2 quick reference guide shows return to work payments moving to lump sum W and small back payments moving to the matching payment type.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the twelve-month rule nor warned about the Phase 2 change.

value_domain: Year and month of the payee's date of birth, ABS derived
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The payee's date of birth reduced by the ABS to a month and a year. The ABS treats month and year of birth as a jobholder characteristic on STP data, drawn from the ATO Client Register and otherwise derived from the payroll record, and it holds the value still once set: "the month and year of birth variable is held constant", while age "continues to be updated at the start of a jobholder's birth month each year". Age at a pay event has to be worked out against the pay dates on the same row.
description_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
value_definition: A year and month pair with no day component, constant for a payee across their pay events, and derived by the ABS rather than reported as such by the employer.
limitation: It cannot place a person either side of an age threshold that falls on a birthday, which is the point at which superannuation, minimum wage and tax settings change. Because the value is held constant once assigned, a later correction to the underlying record does not necessarily flow through, so the column should be checked against the spine rather than treated as the authority.
rationale: The ABS methodology names a month and year of birth variable on STP-based payroll data, says where the characteristic comes from and states that it is held constant, but it documents the payroll jobs product rather than this PLIDA column, so the mapping is inferred.
evidence_quote: While the month and year of birth variable is held constant, the jobholder's age (as derived from month and year of birth) continues to be updated at the start of a jobholder's birth month each year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Month and year of payee's DOB' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said who derives the value or that the day is not carried.

value_domain: ABS confidentialised identifier for the employing business
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The employer on a pay event, held as an ABS-issued confidentialised business identifier rather than an ABN. The ABS explains the underlying pipeline: it "receives selected employer and employee level data from the ATO STP system, which are combined with employer and jobholder characteristics from the ABS Business Register and ATO Client Register", and the business identifier is what carries industry and size onto a payroll record. On a contractor row the contractor's own business identifier sits in a separate column.
description_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
value_definition: An opaque identifier for a business unit, stable across pay events within an extract, and the key that joins a pay event to business characteristics rather than a readable ABN.
limitation: It is not a workplace and not an enterprise group. A single identifier can cover a national employer with branches in every state, so it cannot locate where the work was done, and business restructures create new identifiers that break an employer series without any change in the underlying operation.
rationale: The ABS methodology documents the STP-to-ABS pipeline and the use of the Business Register to attach employer characteristics, but the construction of the confidentialised identifier itself is not published, so the reading is inferred.
evidence_quote: The ABS receives selected employer and employee level data from the ATO STP system, which are combined with employer and jobholder characteristics from the ABS Business Register and ATO Client Register.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'ABS Derived confidentialised business identifier' and the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said what the identifier is for or what it cannot distinguish.

value_domain: ATO PAYG withholding branch number for the employer
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section C: Payer details
variable_description: The withholding branch the employer reported the pay under, which splits one ABN into separate tax registrations. The ATO explains the arrangement in the payer details of its payment summaries: "If a business has one ABN but multiple branches, each branch may have an individual branch number." It is a tax administration division chosen by the business, so it exists only where the business registered branches with the ATO.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section C: Payer details
value_definition: A short numeric code attached to the payer on a pay event, present only for businesses that hold more than one PAYG withholding registration under one ABN, and blank otherwise.
limitation: A branch is not a site, a state or a division of operations, so it cannot stand in for workplace geography. Most employers have no branch at all, and a business that reorganises its registrations can renumber branches, which splits or merges an employer series built on ABN plus branch without anything changing on the ground.
rationale: The ATO's payer details instruction defines the branch number in the same terms the custodian's label uses, and the same identifier is carried on the STP pay event.
evidence_quote: If a business has one ABN but multiple branches, each branch may have an individual branch number.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label about sub-dividing activities and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not warn that a branch is a tax registration and not a location.

value_domain: ABS confidentialised identifier for the contractor's own business
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
variable_description: The business identifier of the person being paid, present where the payee is a contractor rather than an employee. The ATO sets out when the payer has to supply it: "When you report a payment and withholding for a contractor under the voluntary agreement (VOL) income type, you must provide the contractor's ABN. The contractor's TFN is not required." Where a payee is both a contractor and an employee under the same payroll identifier in a year, the payer reports both the ABN and the TFN.
description_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
value_definition: An opaque business identifier for the payee's own enterprise, populated only on contractor arrangements, and confidentialised by the ABS in the same way as the employer identifier.
limitation: A value here identifies the payee's business, not the payer's, so joining it to business characteristics describes the contractor rather than the hirer. It is also not a general contractor flag: labour hire and other specified payments identify the payee by tax file number instead, so those rows carry nothing here even though the payee is a contractor.
rationale: The guidelines state which income type requires the contractor's ABN and how a mixed contractor-and-employee case is reported, which is what fixes the meaning of the column and its blanks.
evidence_quote: When you report a payment and withholding for a contractor under the voluntary agreement (VOL) income type, you must provide the contractor's ABN. The contractor's TFN is not required.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Contractor Client Identifier - ABS Derived confidentialised business identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said which side of the payment the identifier belongs to.

value_domain: Derived end date of the pay period covered by an STP pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Definition of terms
variable_description: The last day of the period the pay event covers, worked out rather than reported by the employer. The event itself is anchored to the payment: a pay event is "the file generated by an STP-enabled software or solution" that "must be lodged to us on, or before, the payment date when an employer makes a payment to an employee or payee". The derived end date lets a payment be placed against the weeks worked instead of the day the money moved, which is what the payment date column gives.
description_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Definition of terms
value_definition: A calendar date marking the close of the pay period. It pairs with the derived start date on the same row, and the two together bound the period the reported amounts relate to.
limitation: It is not an employment date. A pay period ending does not mean the job ended, which is what the payer-payee cessation date records, and because the date is derived it can be modelled from a pay cycle where the payroll file carried no period. Overlapping and out-of-sequence periods occur when an employer corrects earlier reporting.
rationale: The ATO defines the pay event and its relationship to the payment date, but the derivation of the pay period bounds is an ABS treatment that is not documented on a fetchable page, so the reading rests on the field name and the neighbouring date columns.
evidence_quote: Pay event - the file generated by an STP-enabled software or solution. This file must be lodged to us on, or before, the payment date when an employer makes a payment to an employee or payee that is subject to withholding.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Derived end date for a pay event' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not distinguish the pay period from the payment date or from the end of the job.

value_domain: Derived start date of the pay period covered by an STP pay event
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The first day of the period the pay event covers, worked out rather than reported by the employer. Pay cycles differ between employers: the ABS notes that STP "transactions reported each week are generally for payments of wages and salaries for a defined pay cycle period" and that submissions "vary from employer to employer based on pay cycle frequency". The start date is what makes a weekly, fortnightly and monthly payer comparable on a time basis.
description_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
value_definition: A calendar date marking the opening of the pay period, paired with the derived end date on the same row, and expressed in the same daily resolution as the payment date.
limitation: It is not the date the job started, which the payer-payee commencement date carries and which can be decades earlier. A long gap between this date and the previous event's end date can be a change of pay cycle, a correction or a period of unpaid leave, and the column cannot tell those apart.
rationale: The ABS methodology describes the pay cycle periods STP transactions carry and the calendarisation that uses the start and end date of the payment period, but the derived start date itself is an ABS construction that is not published field by field.
evidence_quote: Transactions reported each week are generally for payments of wages and salaries for a defined pay cycle period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Derived start date for a pay event' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not separate the pay period from the start of employment.

value_domain: True or false flag marking a record with a holding identifier
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
variable_description: A true or false marker showing that the payee identifier on the row is a stand-in rather than a real one. Payroll reporting produces these cases by design: "You must provide either a TFN or Australian business number (ABN) for each payee included in your STP report. If you have not been provided with the employee's TFN you must use the TFN exemption codes." A row flagged true still carries pay amounts, but the person behind it cannot be linked to the spine with confidence.
description_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
value_definition: A two-state flag, true or false, applied at the record level and independent of the amounts reported on the same row.
limitation: It does not say why the identifier is a stand-in, so a new starter whose tax file number declaration has not yet come through, a payee who declined to quote one and a payroll error all look the same. Dropping flagged rows removes real wages from an employer's total, and keeping them risks attaching one person's pay to another, so the choice has to be made deliberately rather than by default.
rationale: The ATO documents the exemption codes that stand in for a missing tax file number, which is the situation this flag most plausibly marks, but no published page defines the PLIDA flag itself.
evidence_quote: If you have not been provided with the employee's TFN you must use the TFN exemption codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Dummy flag. Value of True or False' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it stated the shape of the field and nothing about what it marks.

value_domain: Identifier for one payee and payer pairing, that is, one payroll job
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The job, in the sense the ABS uses for payroll statistics: one person paid by one employer. The ABS definition is direct - "A payroll job is a relationship between an employee and their employer where the employee is paid through STP-enabled payroll or accounting software" - and this key is what makes that relationship countable across pay events. The sequence key on the same row goes finer, adding the payroll identifier, branch number and business management software identifier.
description_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
value_definition: An encrypted identifier that is constant for a payee and payer combination and repeats across every pay event for that relationship in the extract.
limitation: Counting keys counts relationships, not people and not job starts. One person holding two jobs generates two keys, a person rehired by the same employer can keep the same key across a break, and a person who moves to a related entity with a different business identifier gets a new key even though the work did not change.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines a payroll job in exactly the payee-and-payer terms the custodian uses for this key, and that definition governs how the column behaves in counts.
evidence_quote: A payroll job is a relationship between an employee and their employer where the employee is paid through STP-enabled payroll or accounting software.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Key unique to a payee-payer combination' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never connected the key to the payroll job concept or warned how it behaves in counts.

value_domain: Date an employment termination payment was made
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The day the employer actually paid the termination payment. The ATO instruction is the plainest possible: "Show the date you made the payment to the payee." It is the date the money moved, which is what determines the income year the payment is taxed in and which cap applies to it.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A calendar date on an employment termination payment record, one per payment type reported, since a separate record is required for each code.
limitation: It is not the date employment ended. A termination payment can follow the last day of work by weeks or months, and can be paid in instalments that fall in different financial years, which is why the codes for a payment continuing an earlier year's entitlement exist. The end of the job sits in the payer-payee cessation date on the pay event table.
rationale: The ATO's payment details instruction defines the date field on the termination payment record, and the same field is carried through STP reporting of termination payments.
evidence_quote: Show the date you made the payment to the payee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Date Employment Termination Payment was paid' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not warn that this is a payment date rather than a termination date.

value_domain: Employment termination payment code, life benefit or death benefit
values: ["R: Genuine redundancy or early retirement scheme payments - a life benefit paid only for reasons of genuine redundancy to employees under their pension age or earlier age of mandatory retirement, invalidity, an ATO approved early retirement scheme, or compensation for personal injury, unfair dismissal, harassment or discrimination","O: Other reasons - a life benefit paid for reasons other than for ETP type R","S: Split ETP type R - multiple payment of life benefit ETP type R for the same termination of employment, where the later payment is paid in a later financial year than the original payment","P: Split ETP type O - multiple payment of life benefit ETP type O for the same termination of employment, where the later payment is paid in a later financial year than the original payment","D: Dependant - a death benefit payment directly to a dependant of the deceased employee","N: Non-dependant - a death benefit payment directly to a non-dependant of the deceased employee","B: Split ETP type N - a multiple payment for a death benefit ETP type N for the same deceased person, where the later payment is paid in a later financial year than the original payment","T: Trustee of deceased estate - a death benefit payment directly to a trustee of the deceased estate"]
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, When an employee transfers or leaves, ETP types you can report
variable_description: A one-letter code putting the termination payment into a tax category, which decides the cap and the rate applied to it. The first split is who the payment is for: "A life benefit ETP is a lump sum payment made to a living employee in consequence of their employment being terminated", and codes for a death benefit are used "If you are paying the ETP to a person because of another person's death". A second split marks payments continuing an entitlement partly paid in an earlier income year for the same termination.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Employment termination payment (ETP) codes
value_definition: One of eight letters, one per record, since a payer reporting more than one type has to report each separately. Two splits set them. R and O are life benefit codes, paid to a living former employee: R covers genuine redundancy, an approved early retirement scheme, invalidity and compensation for personal injury, unfair dismissal, harassment or discrimination, and O covers every other life benefit. D, N and T are death benefit codes, paid because the employee died, and name the recipient: a dependant, a non-dependant, or the trustee of the deceased estate. S, P and B mark a payment continuing an entitlement part-paid in an earlier income year for the same termination, and follow R, O and N respectively. There is no split code for a payment to a dependant or to a trustee, so a later instalment to either keeps its original code.
limitation: The code does not say why the job ended. It classifies the payment for tax, so the choice between the two life benefit codes turns on which cap applies rather than on redundancy against resignation, and a person made redundant can appear under either depending on what the payment consists of. Codes marking a continuing entitlement also describe the payment's history, not the current year's separation.
rationale: The Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines state the size of the domain outright and enumerate all eight codes in one list, with the life benefit, death benefit and split branches named. Schedule 11 and the payment summary instructions carry the same eight letters, so the domain does not depend on which reporting channel the row came through.
evidence_quote: There are 8 ETP types you can report.
supersedes_rationale: The entry named the two branches but carried no codes, because the custodian's description points at a value domain "included below the DIL" and no such appendix exists in the 19 March 2026 workbook the package ships from. The codes are published by the ATO instead, so the entry now carries all eight rather than repeating the pointer.

value_domain: Dollar amount, tax-free component of an employment termination payment
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The part of a termination payment that is not taxed, which is narrow and historical in origin. The ATO says "The tax-free component consists of the: pre-July 1983 segment" and the "invalidity segment", so it reflects very long service or a payment made because the person could no longer work. It is also optional on the form: "You do not have to complete this field."
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount that is non-assessable, non-exempt income, so no withholding attaches to it and it stays outside the payer's gross total.
limitation: A blank is not evidence that the whole payment was taxable, because the payer is not required to complete the field, so the split between the two components on a row can be incomplete. It is also not the same concept as the tax-free redundancy lump sum on the pay event table, which is reported under a lump sum type rather than as part of a termination payment.
rationale: The payment details instruction defines the two segments that make up the tax-free component and states that completing the field is optional, which governs how a blank should be read.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component consists of the: pre-July 1983 segment, invalidity segment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about non-assessable non-exempt income with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say what the component consists of or that the field is optional.

value_domain: Dollar amount of PAYG withholding on an employment termination payment
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Tax the employer held back from the termination payment and sent to the ATO. The instruction is to "Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars", covering the whole payment reported on that record. Withholding on a termination payment follows its own tax table, so the rate is not the person's marginal rate and not the rate applied to their ordinary pay.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding amount attached to one termination payment record, and part of the payer's PAYG withholding total rather than its gross payment total.
limitation: Withholding is not tax paid. The caps that govern how much of a termination payment is concessionally taxed are applied by the ATO across the person's year, so an assessment can refund or add to this amount, and the ratio of this column to the taxable component is not an effective tax rate.
rationale: The payment details instruction defines the withholding field on the termination payment record, and the STP guidelines put the same amount into the payer's withholding total rather than the gross total.
evidence_quote: Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about tax withheld under the Pay As You Go arrangement with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not separate withholding from final tax.

value_domain: Dollar amount, taxable component of an employment termination payment
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The assessable part of a termination payment. The ATO defines it as a residual: "Include the total of the payment, less the tax-free component." A death benefit paid to a dependant is reported differently, because for those payments the payer must "only include the amount over the ETP cap in the taxable component". A payee with more than one type of termination payment has more than one record, since each code is reported separately.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable amount for one payment and one code, included in the payer's gross total and paired with the tax-free component on the same record.
limitation: It understates the payment for a death benefit to a dependant, where everything under the cap is reported as nothing at all, so summing the column across payees is not the value of termination payments made. Nor is it the whole payout on separation: unused leave paid at the same time is reported on the pay event table under the lump sum types, not here.
rationale: The payment details instruction defines the taxable component as the payment less the tax-free component and states the different treatment of a dependant's death benefit, which is where the column stops being additive.
evidence_quote: For death benefit ETP's paid to a dependant of the deceased, only include the amount over the ETP cap in the taxable component.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's note about a repeating array of amounts with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say how the component is worked out or where it is deliberately understated.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross foreign employment income in a pay event
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - foreign employment, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Pay an Australian tax resident earned working overseas, where that income is assessable in Australia. The ATO says "The gross payments amount is the assessable foreign employment income" and adds that on this reporting stream "allowances must be included in Gross payments", unlike the domestic gross column, where allowances sit separately. Foreign service that qualifies as exempt is reported elsewhere and is not part of this amount.
description_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - foreign employment, Section B: Payment details
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for one payee, payer and income type, cumulative for the financial year at the time of the pay event.
limitation: It is not all money earned abroad. Exempt foreign earnings are excluded, and payments made by a foreign employer with no Australian payroll never enter STP at all, so the column measures foreign work paid through an Australian payroll. Because allowances are folded in here but not in domestic gross, the two gross columns are not on the same basis.
rationale: The foreign employment payment summary defines the gross figure as assessable foreign employment income and states the allowance treatment, and the STP income types page confirms the foreign employment income type carries the same concept.
evidence_quote: The gross payments amount is the assessable foreign employment income. For this payment summary it also includes total allowances.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is assessable income only or that allowances are inside it.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross income for work in the Joint Petroleum Development Area
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types; type letter from ATO, PAYG payment summary - foreign employment, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Gross pay for work done in the Timor Sea joint petroleum area, which was taxed under its own treaty arrangements. The foreign employment payment summary marks it with a distinct type - "J - income earned for work conducted in the Joint Petroleum Development Area (JPDA)" - and the ATO now treats the category as closed: "You can only use this income type to make amendments to your STP reporting for the 2019-20 or earlier financial years, because the tax arrangements relating to the JPDA changed in 2019."
description_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types; type letter from ATO, PAYG payment summary - foreign employment, Section B: Payment details
