The ABS states that "For Census dates, ERP is derived from usual resident Census counts, estimated net Census undercount, and the estimated resident population temporarily overseas on Census night", so the status turns on usual residence and not on being in the country. The 2011 Census is also the base the population estimates for the 2006 to 2011 quarters were later rebased on, which makes this column the anchor for the first five years of the quarterly series in this table.
description_source: ABS, Historical population methodology, 2021
value_definition: A status at one instant rather than a count: in the estimated resident population on Census night, or not. The classification is the same in-scope test the quarterly ERP_STATUS columns use, evaluated at the Census date instead of at a quarter end.
limitation: It does not say where the person was living. The column carries scope and not geography, so someone in scope on 9 August 2011 could have been anywhere in Australia or briefly overseas; STATE on the traveller rows is the only state signal and it belongs to a movement, not to Census night.
rationale: The ABS historical population methodology gives the 2011 Census date and the components the estimated resident population is built from at a Census date, which is the status this column carries for each person.
evidence_quote: For Census dates, ERP is derived from usual resident Census counts, estimated net Census undercount, and the estimated resident population temporarily overseas on Census night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry offered only 'Erp status on census night 2011' with the same generic sentence standing in for both the value definition and the limitation, and nothing linking the column to the Census it is named after or to the rebasing that Census drove.

value_domain: Estimated resident population status on Census night
value_source: ABS, Methodology used in rebased population estimates, June 2021
variable_description: Whether the person was in the estimated resident population on Census night 2016, 9 August 2016. Scope and physical presence part company here, because "The Census count by place of usual residence excludes people in Australia on Census night who were visiting Australia for less than one year", while Australian residents abroad that night stay in the population. Of the four Census columns this is the last taken under ordinary travel conditions, which makes it the natural comparison point for the 2021 column rather than the other way round.
description_source: ABS, Methodology used in rebased population estimates, June 2021
value_definition: A status at one instant rather than a count: in the estimated resident population on Census night, or not. The classification is the same in-scope test the quarterly ERP_STATUS columns use, evaluated at the Census date instead of at a quarter end.
limitation: An out-of-scope value does not mean the person was absent from the country. A visitor standing in Australia on 9 August 2016 on a short stay sits outside the estimated resident population despite being present, so this column and 'in Australia that night' are different facts and cannot be substituted for one another.
rationale: The ABS rebasing methodology states which people the Census usual residence count excludes and which are added back to the estimated resident population, which is precisely the scope test this column applies at the 2016 Census date.
evidence_quote: The Census count by place of usual residence excludes people in Australia on Census night who were visiting Australia for less than one year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian wording 'Erp status on census night 2016' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave a reader no way to see that presence in the country and inclusion in the population are different things.

value_domain: Estimated resident population status on Census night
value_source: ABS, Methodology used in rebased population estimates, June 2021
variable_description: Whether the person was in the estimated resident population on Census night 2021, 10 August 2021. Australians who were abroad that night can still be in scope, since "Residents temporarily overseas (RTOs) are Australian residents who were temporarily overseas on Census Night and who should be added to the ERP". This is the most recent of the four Census columns and the 2021 Census is the base the 2016 to 2021 quarterly estimates were rebased on, so it anchors the later part of the ERP_STATUS run.
description_source: ABS, Methodology used in rebased population estimates, June 2021
value_definition: A status at one instant rather than a count: in the estimated resident population on Census night, or not. The classification is the same in-scope test the quarterly ERP_STATUS columns use, evaluated at the Census date instead of at a quarter end.
limitation: It cannot be read as an ordinary year. International travel was heavily restricted around 10 August 2021, so a traveller out of scope on that date is far more likely to have been kept outside the country than in earlier Census years, and comparing this column with the 2016 one measures the border settings as much as it measures the person.
rationale: The ABS rebasing methodology for the June 2021 base states how residents temporarily overseas on Census night are treated, which is the rule that decides a traveller's ERP status at the 2021 Census date.
evidence_quote: Residents temporarily overseas (RTOs) are Australian residents who were temporarily overseas on Census Night and who should be added to the ERP.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Erp status on census night 2021' with no domain named and the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing warned a reader that 2021 sits inside a closed border and does not compare with 2016.

value_domain: SACC country code for country of birth (four digits)
value_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
variable_description: The traveller's birthplace, held as a four-digit country code rather than a name. The ABS "endorses the use of this classification when collecting, aggregating and disseminating data relating to characteristics such as birthplace and country of residence", and the code on this row is the country level of that classification. IMPUTED_COUNTRY_OF_BIRTH beside it marks the rows where the birthplace was filled in rather than captured at the border, which matters because the ABS imputes missing traveller characteristics rather than leaving them blank.
description_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
value_definition: A four-digit code from the Standard Australian Classification of Countries. "Countries have four-digit codes where the first two digits represent the parent minor group code and the final two digits represent the sequence of countries within a minor group", so the code aggregates to minor group and major group without a lookup table.
limitation: Birthplace is not nationality and not ancestry. A person born in one country to parents from another is coded to the place of birth alone, and COUNTRY_OF_CITIZENSHIP on the same row can disagree with it entirely. The classification also carries its own treatment of countries whose borders have changed, so a birthplace series is not a fixed geography across the 2006 to 2023 span of this file.
rationale: The custodian's own wording names the SACC, and the ABS classification page gives both the endorsement for birthplace coding and the four-digit country code structure that the column's values take.
evidence_quote: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) endorses the use of this classification when collecting, aggregating and disseminating data relating to characteristics such as birthplace and country of residence.
supersedes_rationale: The entry inferred 'SACC country code' from the variable name and warned that the mapping was unconfirmed, with the same generic sentence standing as the value definition, so it neither cited the classification nor mentioned the imputation flag sitting next to it.

value_domain: SACC country code for country of citizenship (four digits)
value_source: ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia methodology, May 2026; ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
variable_description: The citizenship shown on the travel document the person used at their reference movement, coded to the same four-digit country classification as COUNTRY_OF_BIRTH. Citizenship is one of the few characteristics known for every crossing: the ABS notes that "While the total number of travellers and their citizenship is known", other characteristics of short-term arrivals rest on a sample. It is also what drives the fallback codes in VISA_SUBCLASS, where a traveller with no valid subclass is coded 000 if Australian, 444 if a New Zealand citizen and 001 otherwise.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia methodology, May 2026; ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release
value_definition: A four-digit country code from the Standard Australian Classification of Countries, the same classification used for country of birth. IMPUTED_COUNTRY_OF_CITIZENSHIP on the same row marks the records where the value was filled in rather than read from the document.
limitation: It records one citizenship, not all of them. A dual national is carried under the passport they travelled on, so the same person can appear with different citizenships in different quarters, and a naturalisation after the reference movement never updates the value. Citizenship also carries no residency information: an Australian citizen living permanently abroad sits outside the estimated resident population.
rationale: The ABS methodology for the border collection states that citizenship is known for all travellers while other characteristics are sampled, which is the fact that decides how far this column can be pushed, and the SACC supplies the code structure.
evidence_quote: While the total number of travellers and their citizenship is known, statistics for other characteristics of short-term arrivals (such as their state/territory of stay/residence) are based on a sample.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only 'Country of citizenship' with no domain named and the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader could not tell that the values are SACC codes or that the citizenship is the one on the passport presented at a single crossing.

value_domain: Crew movement exclusion flag
value_source: ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia methodology, May 2026
variable_description: Marks travellers who made a crew movement in the 16 months after the reference quarter, so the ABS can lift their records out of published migration estimates. Overseas arrivals and departures statistics "exclude the movements of operational air and sea crew, of transit passengers who pass through Australia but are not cleared for entry", and this flag is how that exclusion is carried at the person level in the linked file. Because it is set from travel that happened after the quarter being described, it uses the same 16-month follow-up window as the 12/16 month rule.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia methodology, May 2026
value_definition: A binary indicator applied by the ABS during processing, not a characteristic the traveller supplied. It is derived from the person's later movement records rather than from the reference movement on the row it sits on.
limitation: A set flag does not make the person a crew member by occupation and does not say they were working on the reference movement. Any crew crossing inside the follow-up window trips it, so an airline employee who also flew as a passenger is caught. Since the flagged records are dropped from published output, keeping them in a linked analysis produces a migration total that will not reconcile with published net overseas migration.
rationale: The ABS methodology states the crew exclusion that this flag implements, and the custodian's own wording states the 16-month window over which it is set and that flagged records are removed from preliminary and final estimates.
evidence_quote: The statistics exclude the movements of operational air and sea crew, of transit passengers who pass through Australia but are not cleared for entry.
supersedes_rationale: The entry named no value domain and printed 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page gave a long custodian sentence with nothing said about what the flag does to a user's own estimates.

value_domain: Date of the border crossing used to measure duration
value_source: ABS, Improvements to the estimation of net overseas migration; ABS, Measuring Net Overseas Migration in Australia
variable_description: The date of the border crossing from which this traveller's duration in or out of Australia is measured. The ABS explains that "Records of each traveller's overseas arrivals and departures are used to measure his/her cumulative duration in (or out of) Australia over the subsequent 16 months following an initial arrival or departure", and this column holds the date that window runs from. It is also the day the population count moves, because the ABS article Measuring Net Overseas Migration in Australia states that a person considered to have migrated "is added to, or removed from, the Australian population from the date they arrived or departed".
description_source: ABS, Improvements to the estimation of net overseas migration; ABS, Measuring Net Overseas Migration in Australia
value_definition: A calendar date. The domain is open: any date on which the traveller crossed Australia's international border, rather than a period label like the quarter carried in REFERENCE_PERIOD.
limitation: It is not the date the person became a migrant. Whether the crossing counts as migration is only settled after 16 months of subsequent travel, so the date says when someone crossed the border, not when the 12/16 month test was passed. It also carries no direction of its own, so NOM_DIRECTION has to be read alongside it to know whether the crossing was into Australia or out of it.
rationale: The ABS research paper on net overseas migration estimation describes the duration measurement that starts from a traveller's arrival or departure, which is the role this date plays, and the companion article states that the population is adjusted from that same date.
evidence_quote: Records of each traveller's overseas arrivals and departures are used to measure his/her cumulative duration in (or out of) Australia over the subsequent 16 months following an initial arrival or departure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry inferred 'Calendar date' from the variable name and said only that the shape looked right, so it explained neither which movement the date belongs to nor why that date is the point at which a migrant enters or leaves the population count.

value_domain: Annual estimated resident population flag
value_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
variable_description: An estimated resident population flag held on an annual footing, rather than at a quarter boundary like the pair beside it. INITIAL_ERP_FLAG gives the person's status at the start of the reference quarter and FINAL_ERP_FLAG gives it at the end, so this column is the yearly counterpart used when quarters are rolled up. The status behind all three is the same: the official population measure counts people by usual residence, keeping usual residents who are overseas briefly and excluding visitors who are here briefly, with the 12/16 month rule drawing the line for every year of this file from September quarter 2006 on.
description_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
value_definition: A flag rather than a count, giving estimated resident population status over an annual reference window. The classification is the same in-scope test the quarterly flags use, applied across a year instead of a quarter.
limitation: The column cannot date a change. Someone who entered the population part-way through the year reads the same as someone in scope for the whole of it, so the quarterly flags and the ERP_STATUS columns in the derived table are needed to place the change in time. Adding the flag across people also does not give net overseas migration, because migration is the flow between two population stocks and this is a status.
rationale: The ABS glossary settles what estimated resident population status means and how the 12/16 month rule decides it. The annual rather than quarterly framing is read from the custodian's wording and from the two quarterly flags on the same row, not from a published data item list, so the status stays guessed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Annual erp flag' with no value domain and the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, leaving a reader unable to tell it apart from the two quarterly ERP flags sitting next to it.

value_domain: Estimated resident population status at quarter end
value_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
variable_description: The person's estimated resident population status as at 31 March 2006, the last day of the March quarter of 2006. Scope follows usual residence rather than presence: the ABS defines the measure as one that "includes usual residents who are overseas for less than 12 months over a 16 month period". That 16-month framing post-dates this column, because "The rule of 12 months out of 16 has applied since September quarter 2006", so the March and June quarters of 2006 rest on the earlier continuous 12-month test. This is the first of the 74 quarterly columns and it closes before the August 2006 Census that the surrounding intercensal estimates were rebased on.
description_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
value_definition: One status per person per quarter: whether the ABS counted them in the estimated resident population when that quarter closed. The classification is the ABS scope test, but at this quarter end that test was the continuous 12-month rule rather than the 12/16 month rule the ABS adopted from September quarter 2006. The table carries 74 such columns, 2006Q1 to 2024Q2, one for each quarter.
limitation: An out-of-scope value does not mean the person left. Someone who had not yet made a first crossing reads exactly like someone who emigrated, so the column cannot separate 'not arrived yet' from 'departed' without inspecting the columns on either side of it. This column also sits on the far side of a break in series: the residency test changed from September quarter 2006, so it is not directly comparable with the columns after 2006Q2.
rationale: The methodology's glossary gives both the population concept and the residency test behind it, and dates the 12/16 month rule to September quarter 2006, which places this column before the rule change rather than under it.
evidence_quote: It includes usual residents who are overseas for less than 12 months over a 16 month period.
supersedes_rationale: Before this, the 2006Q1 column carried a description that repeated its own name, an unnamed value domain, and one boilerplate sentence doing duty as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what estimated resident population status means.

value_domain: Estimated resident population status at quarter end
value_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
variable_description: A single status for the June quarter of 2006, recording whether the person was a usual resident of Australia on 30 June 2006. Standing in the country is not enough on its own, since the population measure "excludes overseas visitors who are in Australia for less than 12 months over a 16 month period". That wording describes the test from September quarter 2006 onward, and the ABS states that "The rule of 12 months out of 16 has applied since September quarter 2006", so this is the last column before the change and still rests on the earlier continuous 12-month test. It is also the column that lines up with the published 30 June 2006 estimated resident population, the date the ABS states its annual estimate against.
description_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
value_definition: One status per person per quarter: whether the ABS counted them in the estimated resident population when that quarter closed. The classification is the ABS scope test, applied here under the continuous 12-month rule that preceded the 12/16 month rule adopted from September quarter 2006. The table carries 74 such columns, 2006Q1 to 2024Q2, one for each quarter.
limitation: The status is the ABS's determination, not the traveller's own report and not Home Affairs' view of their visa. A person can hold a valid temporary visa and still sit outside the estimated resident population, so this column cannot stand in for lawful status or for the visa held. It is also the last column measured under the old residency test, so a change between it and 2006Q3 can reflect the rule change rather than the person.
rationale: An end-of-quarter estimated resident population status is the ABS scope test applied at a date. The population methodology publishes that test and dates the 12/16 month rule to September quarter 2006, which places the 2006Q2 column under the earlier continuous 12-month test.
evidence_quote: It excludes overseas visitors who are in Australia for less than 12 months over a 16 month period.
supersedes_rationale: The page for 2006Q2 said 'Erp status at end of 2006q2' and nothing else, with the definition and the limitation identical, so a reader could not tell whether the column described presence in the country or membership of the population.

value_domain: Estimated resident population status at quarter end
value_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
variable_description: Residency status in the estimated resident population at the close of the September quarter of 2006, on 30 September 2006. This is the first quarter the 12/16 month rule reached, since "The rule of 12 months out of 16 has applied since September quarter 2006", under which "incoming overseas travellers (who are not currently counted in the population) must be resident in Australia for a total period of 12 months or more, during the 16 month follow-up period to then be added to the estimated resident population". Census night for the 2006 Census, 8 August 2006, falls inside this quarter, so this column and CENSUS_2006 describe the same person only weeks apart and should agree unless their residency changed between the two dates. Because the file is one row per person and one column per quarter, a spell of residency shows up as a run of columns, and this is the 3rd of the 74 quarters on offer.
description_source: ABS, National, state and territory population methodology, December 2025 (glossary: estimated resident population; 12/16 month rule)
value_definition: One status per person per quarter: whether the ABS counted them in the estimated resident population when that quarter closed. The classification is the ABS scope test, settled by the 12/16 month rule applied to the person's border crossings over the 16 months that follow. The table carries 74 such columns, 2006Q1 to 2024Q2, one for each quarter.
limitation: A change between this column and the one before it dates a change in residency to a quarter, not to a day. The crossing behind it can fall anywhere in the three months, so quarter-to-quarter differences will not support a duration or survival analysis measured in days.
rationale: The ABS population methodology defines the estimated resident population and the 12/16 month rule that decides who is inside it, which is exactly what a status at the end of the September quarter of 2006 records.
evidence_quote: incoming overseas travellers (who are not currently counted in the population) must be resident in Australia for a total period of 12 months or more, during the 16 month follow-up period to then be added to the estimated resident population
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian wording 'Erp status at end of 2006q3', named no value domain, and printed the same generic sentence about no published value list as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Estimated resident population status at quarter end

The value is fixed by applying the 12/16 month rule to the sixteen months after the quarter, so it is an ABS determination made well after the traveller crossed the border.

value_domain: ERP status at the start of the reference quarter
value_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year, 'The 12/16 month rule'
variable_description: Whether the traveller was already counted in Australia's estimated resident population when the quarter this file covers began. It is the baseline the quarter's movements act on, and the ABS uses the same idea in its own modelling: "The characteristics used to match similar travellers for preliminary modelling are: age, country of citizenship, direction of first and last movement in the reference quarter, initial ERP status, time spent out of Australia, and visa group." (Overseas Migration methodology). A person who starts inside the population can only leave it, and a person who starts outside can only enter it, so this column decides which half of net overseas migration the row can contribute to.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year, 'The 12/16 month rule'
value_definition: A status flag on the quarterly traveller record, one value per person per reference quarter, measured at the first day of the quarter rather than derived from the quarter's own movements. It appears in all 32 traveller files alongside FINAL_ERP_FLAG.
limitation: Consecutive files are not independent readings. A person's starting status should agree with the previous quarter's closing status, so stacking the files and treating each row as a fresh observation double counts the same residence spell; and the flag on its own identifies no migration, since most travellers begin and end the quarter on the same side.
rationale: The methodology names initial ERP status as one of the characteristics the ABS matches travellers on when it models preliminary estimates, which fixes both what the column measures and when it is measured.
evidence_quote: The characteristics used to match similar travellers for preliminary modelling are: age, country of citizenship, direction of first and last movement in the reference quarter, initial ERP status, time spent out of Australia, and visa group.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Erp status at start of quarter' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, so a reader could not tell that it is a baseline rather than an outcome, nor that it pairs with the end-of-quarter flag.

value_domain: Net overseas migration direction of travel
value_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year, glossary
variable_description: Which way the person travelled in the quarter this file covers, and so which side of net overseas migration the row can fall on. The ABS defines the departure side as "Outgoing international travellers who leave Australia for 12 months or more over a 16-month period, who are currently counted within the population, and are then subtracted from the population." (Overseas Migration methodology), and the arrival side as its mirror. Direction is taken from the movement records rather than from anything the traveller declared about their plans.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year, glossary
value_definition: A short direction code on the quarterly traveller record, one value per person per reference quarter. Where a person made several crossings in the quarter the ABS works with the direction of the first and the last movement, so this column summarises a movement history rather than a single border crossing.
limitation: Direction is not migration. Most people who cross the border in a quarter are on a short trip and never change the population count, so counting arrivals in this column counts travellers, not immigrants; only the change between INITIAL_ERP_FLAG and FINAL_ERP_FLAG says who moved.
rationale: The methodology's glossary defines migrant arrivals and departures in terms of direction plus duration, and its preliminary modelling section shows the ABS working with the direction of the first and last movement in the reference quarter.
evidence_quote: Outgoing international travellers who leave Australia for 12 months or more over a 16-month period, who are currently counted within the population, and are then subtracted from the population.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the data item wording 'Direction of travel of a person in the reference quarter' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving the impression that a direction on its own identifies a migration event.

description_source: ABS, Population physically present in Australia (article)
value_definition: A numeric weight for one person in one month, held in a wide table with one column per month. This column is the September quarter 2023 month end.
limitation: A month-end weight is not a duration. Adding this person's September 2023 weight to their other monthly weights gives neither months lived in Australia nor a count of people, because each of the 240 columns is a separate point-in-time estimate. rationale: The ABS article on the physically present population defines the estimate this weight works towards and states that its components are determined at the end of a reference quarter under the 12/16 month rule. The classification behind it is the ABS physically present population, which the ABS calculates as the estimated resident population plus visitors temporarily in Australia less residents temporarily overseas, each component determined at the end of a reference quarter under the 12/16 month rule. This column is the June quarter 2025 month end.
limitation: A month-end weight is not a duration. Adding this person's June 2025 weight to their other monthly weights gives neither months lived in Australia nor a count of people, because each of the 240 columns is a separate point-in-time estimate. To describe the June quarter 2025, take this quarter-end column rather than a sum of its three months.
rationale: The ABS article on the physically present population defines the estimate this weight works towards and states that its components are determined at the end of a reference quarter under the 12/16 month rule. The article does not name the PLIDA column, so the mapping from column to estimate is read off the table's shape and its PP_STATUS sibling. The 240-column span, this column's place in the June quarter 2025 and the ERP_STATUS coverage to the June quarter 2024 come from the package registry rather than from the article.
evidence_quote: Physically present population estimates (PPPE) are calculated as ERP plus total Visitors Temporarily in Australia (VTA) less total Residents Temporarily Overseas (RTO).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Physically present weight at end of 2025m6', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what the weight weights or that the column is one month of a wide panel.

value_domain: Physically present population weight for the month
value_source: ABS, Population physically present in Australia (article)
variable_description: The weight this person carries in the estimate of Australia's physically present population at the end of July 2025, the first month of the September quarter 2025. It is an estimation weight rather than a headcount: PP_STATUS_2025M7 in madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current says whether the person was in the country at that month end, and this column says how much that presence contributes to the total. The table runs one row per person and 240 monthly columns, PP_WT_2006M1 through PP_WT_2025M12, so a person's series reads across the row rather than down the file, and this is column 235. The ABS compiles the physically present population by reference quarter, so July sits inside the September quarter 2025 with no published quarterly figure of its own, and PP_WT_2025M9 is the column that falls on one. ERP_STATUS in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current stops at the June quarter 2024, so there is no usual-residence status to set beside July 2025. The ABS puts the seasonal swing in this series down to more residents being overseas in the June and December quarters, which is not the September quarter, so a level shift out of July 2025 is more likely to be real than seasonal.

value_domain: Overseas migration reference quarter
value_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation, NOM Traveller data (Department of Home Affairs)
variable_description: The reference quarter a traveller's record belongs to, which is what separates the four quarters pooled inside each annual travellers table. ABS receives the Home Affairs movement records "via monthly extracts with the data being compiled on a quarterly basis", and net overseas migration is estimated one reference quarter at a time, so a person appears once for each quarter in which they moved. The column runs through the annual files from 2006 to 2019 and the four 2020 quarterly files, then disappears from the March quarter 2021 onward because the table name carries the quarter instead.
description_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation, NOM Traveller data (Department of Home Affairs)
value_definition: A quarter identifier combining year and quarter number. The classification is the ABS overseas migration reference quarter, the period over which movement records are compiled and net overseas migration is estimated.
limitation: It is not the date the person crossed the border. DURATION_MOVEMENT_DATE holds the movement date, and a traveller with several crossings in one quarter is reduced to a single reference movement, so this column cannot be used to place someone in Australia for the whole quarter or to count border crossings.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page for the NOM Traveller data states that the movement records are compiled quarterly, and the overseas migration methodology lists reference quarter/year as a data item available from the December quarter 2003, which is what this column carries.
evidence_quote: Movement records are supplied via monthly extracts with the data being compiled on a quarterly basis.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Time period in which the information was recorded' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said the period is a quarter or that the column vanishes after 2020.

value_domain: Sex of the traveller
value_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2024-25 financial year
variable_description: The traveller's sex as it reached the ABS on the Home Affairs movement record, not as it would be reported to a survey. ABS lists sex among the characteristics net overseas migration is compiled by, so this is one of the few demographic splits available for every quarter back to 2006. IMPUTED_SEX on the same row flags whether the value was supplied or assigned during ABS processing, and the pair has to be read together before sex is used as a covariate.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2024-25 financial year
value_definition: A short coded set of ABS sex categories, with provision for a not stated category. The value is fixed at the traveller's reference movement for the quarter rather than maintained as a current attribute of the person.
limitation: It is not a gender measure and it is not refreshed. A person tracked over twenty years keeps whatever the border record carried at each reference movement, so a value that changes between two quarters can be an imputation artefact flagged by IMPUTED_SEX rather than anything about the person.
rationale: The ABS overseas migration methodology lists the data items available for net overseas migration, sex among them, and describes the border collection those items come from, which is what places this column in the movement record rather than in a survey response.
evidence_quote: Overseas arrivals and departures (OAD) refer to the recorded arrival or departure of persons through Australian air or sea ports (excluding operational air and ships' crew).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Sex of traveller' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the value comes from a border record or that a companion imputation flag exists.

value_domain: State or territory of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2024-25 financial year
variable_description: The state or territory the traveller counted as home at their reference movement, in the annual files from 2006 to 2019 and the four 2020 quarterly files. For overseas movements ABS defines this as "the state or territory regarded by the traveller as the one in which they live or have lived". ORIGINAL_STATE on the same row holds the value before ABS editing and ORIG_STATE_IMP_FLAG and IMPUTED_STATE say how the edited value was arrived at, so STATE is the cleaned column and the others are its audit trail. From the March quarter 2021 the same concept is carried by STATE1.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2024-25 financial year
value_definition: One code per state and territory, following the ABS state and territory categories, with categories for other territories and for not stated. For arrivals the value originates on the incoming passenger card, and from July 2017 a small proportion of Australian residents' values are taken from Medicare enrolment data instead.
limitation: It is not where the person ended up living. The value is what the traveller reported at a border crossing, and the ABS attaches the matching warning to the companion intended-residence item, that it "does not necessarily relate to the state or territory in which the traveller will eventually establish a permanent residence", so a settlement measure needs a residential source rather than this column. One value per reference movement also hides any move made inside the quarter.
rationale: The overseas migration methodology glossary defines state or territory of usual residence specifically for overseas movements and the data sources section names the passenger card and, from July 2017, Medicare enrolment as the two sources of the value.
evidence_quote: In the case of overseas movements, state or territory of usual residence refers to the state or territory regarded by the traveller as the one in which they live or have lived.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'State of residence' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no way to tell it apart from ORIGINAL_STATE sitting on the same row.

value_domain: State or territory of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2024-25 financial year
variable_description: The traveller's state or territory of residence in the quarterly files from the March quarter 2021 onward, where the column name carries a 1 suffix. It runs to the June quarter 2024 and is the same concept as STATE in the earlier files, which ABS defines for overseas movements as "the state or territory regarded by the traveller as the one in which they live or have lived". The imputation flag is renamed to match, IMPUTED_STATE1 rather than IMPUTED_STATE, while ORIGINAL_STATE keeps its name across the whole series. Pooling 2006 to 2024 therefore means coalescing STATE and STATE1, or the recent quarters go missing without warning.
description_source: ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2024-25 financial year
value_definition: One code per state and territory, following the ABS state and territory categories, with categories for other territories and for not stated. The value is derived from the incoming passenger card, and since the outgoing card was removed in July 2017 a small proportion of Australian residents' values come from Medicare enrolment data.
limitation: The rename is not a change of meaning, so a break in a state series at the March quarter 2021 is a coding mistake rather than a migration event. The column also will not line up with a Census or estimated resident population state of usual residence, because it is recorded at a border crossing and, for departing residents, partly sourced from Medicare enrolment rather than from the traveller.
rationale: The overseas migration methodology defines state or territory of usual residence for overseas movements and names the passenger card and Medicare enrolment as its sources; the registry itself shows the column and its imputation flag renamed at the March quarter 2021 while ORIGINAL_STATE is unchanged.
evidence_quote: From July 2017, due to the removal of the outgoing passenger card, the ABS has also used Medicare enrolment data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the same custodian wording as STATE, 'State of residence', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained why two differently named columns hold one concept.

value_domain: PLIDA person spine identifier (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person key that ties a traveller record to the same individual everywhere else in PLIDA. It is the only column present in all thirty-five tables of this dataset, so it is the join between the quarterly and annual movement records and the three wide derived tables that hold quarterly ERP status, monthly physically present status and monthly physically present weights. The word synthetic describes the identifier, not the person: it is a de-identified stand-in for the spine identity, supplied so that records can be linked without names or dates of birth.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
value_definition: An opaque person-level identifier with no internal structure and no meaning outside the asset. It is stable across the tables of the asset for one person, which is what makes a longitudinal traveller history possible.
limitation: It counts people, not crossings, and it is not a family or household key. A traveller who could not be linked to the spine is absent from the key rather than flagged, so a count of distinct identifiers understates travellers, and nothing in this column says which of a person's movements in a quarter was the reference one.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA pages describe the asset as a set of de-identified datasets linked through a person spine, which is the role this column plays, and the registry shows it as the one column common to every table in the traveller dataset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the column is the join across the movement tables and the wide derived tables.

value_domain: Primary or secondary visa applicant
value_source: ABS, Temporary visa holders in Australia methodology, 2021, Glossary
variable_description: Whether the traveller was the person the visa was assessed on or a family member included on the same application. ABS defines a primary applicant as "the person whose skills or proposed activities in Australia are assessed by Home Affairs as part of their visa application" and a secondary applicant as "a person whose visa was granted on the basis of being the family member (e.g., spouse, dependent child) of a person who qualified for a visa". Because secondary applicants sit in the same visa stream as their primary applicant, this column is the only thing separating a skilled migrant from the partner who arrived on the skilled stream alongside them.
description_source: ABS, Temporary visa holders in Australia methodology, 2021, Glossary
value_definition: A short coded set separating primary from secondary applicants, with a category for travellers the concept does not apply to, such as Australian and New Zealand citizens moving without a visa grant. The classification is the applicant role recorded by Home Affairs on the visa application.
limitation: It does not cover the whole series and it does not identify the sponsor. ABS lists visa applicant type as available only from the September quarter 2011, so a blank in an earlier annual file means the item was not collected rather than that the person was neither kind of applicant, and a secondary applicant cannot be joined from here to the primary applicant they came with.
rationale: The ABS temporary visa holders methodology glossary gives the department's own definitions of primary and secondary applicant, and the overseas migration methodology lists visa applicant type as a net overseas migration data item with its availability date.
evidence_quote: Generally, the person whose skills or proposed activities in Australia are assessed by Home Affairs as part of their visa application.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's typo, 'Primary or seconary visa applicant', and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing on what either role means or when the item starts.

value_domain: four-character visa stream code, 0000 when unavailable (inferred)
rationale: Only the format and the fallback are supportable. The PLIDA description fixes the field at four characters with '0000' where no valid stream is present, and that is the single value whose meaning is published. The package's bundled codeframe inst/extdata/codeframes/visa_subclass.tsv carries a 'stream' column, but it is empty for all 82 subclass rows, so it supplies nothing. I found no Home Affairs numeric stream codeframe: streams are published only as named categories in statistical outputs (programme-level Skill, Family and Special Eligibility streams; subclass-level streams such as Short-term, Medium-term and Labour Agreement), never with the four-character codes used in the movements data. Attempts to reach a Home Affairs code list through immi.homeaffairs.gov.au and the Home Affairs visa statistics pages returned 404 or 403.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination stands on substance; the only change is that the documented four-character shape with '0000' as the published fallback can carry a low-confidence inferred domain instead of typed missing.

value_domain: Home Affairs visa subclass code
value_source: Department of Home Affairs, visa list
variable_description: Which visa the traveller held on the movement record for the reference quarter. A subclass is Home Affairs' three-digit identifier for a specific visa product - 500 for a student visa, 482 for a skilled temporary worker, 189 for skilled independent - so it is the finest available statement of what somebody was entitled to do in Australia. Three of the values are not visas at all: the DIL records that Australian citizens are given 000, New Zealand citizens 444, and any other traveller with no valid subclass 001.
description_source: Department of Home Affairs, visa list
limitation: 000 and 001 are dump codes rather than visas, so filtering on a subclass silently drops citizens and anyone whose record failed to resolve. The subclass is taken from the reference movement, so it describes the visa held at that crossing and not the one held later; a person who changed status after arriving still carries their arrival subclass. Home Affairs publishes the subclasses but not the PLIDA code list, so the mapping between these values and the published subclasses is not confirmed.
rationale: The DIL states the derivation and names the three dump codes explicitly. Home Affairs publishes the visa subclasses themselves, but no published crosswalk to the values used here was found.
evidence_quote: australian citizens are allocated to the visa category 000 (dump code). new zealand citizens are to be allocated to the special visa category of 444.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's derivation text as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what a subclass is or warning that two of the values are not visas.

value_domain: Education provider ABN (hashed and truncated)
value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
variable_description: The Australian Business Number of the education provider named on the applicant's first-highest Confirmation of Enrolment, hashed and truncated. "An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public." (business.gov.au), so this column identifies the legal entity behind the college or university rather than the campus or the course. It appears on the 2000 to 2021 visa application extract and carries the ABN_HASH_TRUNC name that business-side datasets such as BUSOWN, JK and PIT_PS also use, which makes it the block's most likely bridge to a business record; the ABS does not publish whether those hashes agree, so treat such a join as unproven. The three CoE blocks on a row are ranked by course level, not by date, so this is the applicant's first highest course rather than their first course in time. Because it is the top of the ranking, this block is filled whenever the applicant holds any CoE, so it is the one of the three to use for a single-provider measure.
description_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
value_definition: An eleven-digit Australian Business Number put through a hash and then truncated, so the stored value is a fixed-width opaque string. The classification is the Australian Business Register's ABN, which identifies a business entity.
limitation: An ABN is a coarser unit than a provider. One entity can hold several CRICOS provider codes and many campuses, so grouping students by the first-ranked CoE's owner merges distinct colleges under one business, and the hashed form cannot be turned back into an ABN to look the entity up on the Australian Business Register. The block is filled for primary applicants only, so an empty value on a student visa row can mean the person is a partner or child included on someone else's application rather than that no enrolment existed.
rationale: business.gov.au states what an ABN is and what it identifies, which is what fixes the unit of this column as the provider's legal entity rather than the course or campus that COE1_PRVDR_CD and COE1_COURSE_CD carry. The shared ABN_HASH_TRUNC column name in the business-side datasets comes from the package registry; nothing in either source says the hashes are comparable.
evidence_quote: An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's lower-cased wording about a provider abn and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what an ABN identifies or how it differs from the provider code beside it.

value_domain: CRICOS registered course code
value_source: Department of Education, PRISMS frequently asked questions
variable_description: The course code recorded on the applicant's first-highest Confirmation of Enrolment. "The CoE confirms the student's eligibility to enrol in a course with the registered provider and contains information about the provider, course and duration of study in which the student has enrolled." (Department of Education), and the code identifies which of that provider's registered courses the student was accepted into. The three CoE blocks on a row are ranked by course level, not by date, so this is the applicant's first highest course rather than their first course in time. On a packaged offer this is the destination qualification, the highest level the applicant was accepted into.
description_source: Department of Education, PRISMS frequently asked questions
value_definition: A course identifier drawn from the provider's registered course listing on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students. The domain is open and provider-specific, with one value per Confirmation of Enrolment.
limitation: A course code is only unique within its provider, so two applicants sharing a value are not on the same course unless COE1_PRVDR_CD also matches. It records an accepted enrolment rather than study: PRISMS is loaded when an enrolment is offered, before a visa is granted, so a code here does not mean the course was started, let alone finished.
rationale: The Department of Education explains what a Confirmation of Enrolment contains, naming the provider, course and duration, which is exactly the set of columns the COE1 block holds.
evidence_quote: The CoE confirms the student's eligibility to enrol in a course with the registered provider and contains information about the provider, course and duration of study in which the student has enrolled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's line about a course code from the CoE with the first highest course level and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained what a CoE is or that the ranking is by level rather than by date.

value_domain: Course level description (AQF-aligned sector)
value_source: Department of Education, Explanatory notes for data relating to international students studying in Australia
variable_description: The level of the course on the applicant's first-highest Confirmation of Enrolment, held as descriptive text rather than a code. This is the field the ranking itself is built on, and it is the same idea the Department of Education uses to sort international enrolments: "Enrolments are allocated to sectors based on their course level within the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF).". Its five sectors are higher education, vocational education and training, schools, English language intensive courses for overseas students and non-award, so a packaged offer of an English course followed by a degree puts the degree here, in COE1, and the English course lower down.
description_source: Department of Education, Explanatory notes for data relating to international students studying in Australia
value_definition: A short descriptive string naming a course level. Levels are aligned to the Australian Qualifications Framework and roll up to five sectors, with courses outside the framework treated as non-award and English language courses treated as ELICOS whatever their level.
limitation: A level is not an outcome and not a duration. "Data is initially uploaded into PRISMS by education providers when an enrolment is offered to a prospective student before a visa is granted.", so the first-ranked level can belong to a student who never arrived, and nothing in the column says how long that course ran or whether the qualification was awarded. The block is filled for primary applicants only, so an empty value on a student visa row can mean the person is a partner or child included on someone else's application rather than that no enrolment existed.
rationale: The Department of Education's explanatory notes set out how course level maps to a sector under the Australian Qualifications Framework and list the five sectors PRISMS covers, which is the classification the text in this column comes from.
evidence_quote: Enrolments are allocated to sectors based on their course level within the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line about a course level from the CoE with the first highest course level and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never named the classification or explained the ranking.

value_domain: Education provider ABN (hashed text)
value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
variable_description: The education provider's Australian Business Number for the applicant's first-highest Confirmation of Enrolment, stored as hashed text. It sits on the 2000 to 2023 visa application extract, and the custodian's entire description for it is the parenthetical note that the variable has been hashed, so the meaning comes from the name: "An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public." (business.gov.au). Three vintages of the same fact sit in this dataset under three names, this one plus COE1_ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the 2000 to 2021 extract and COE1_PRVDR_ABN_TX_HASH_TRUNC on the extracts that run to 2025. Because the ranking is by level, a change in this column between two applications can mean a new provider or the same provider at a higher-level course.
description_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
value_definition: An eleven-digit Australian Business Number carried as a text field and hashed, so the stored value is an opaque string of fixed length. The underlying classification is the Australian Business Register's ABN.
limitation: Values are not comparable across the three extracts. A hash produced for one extract is not guaranteed to equal the hash of the same ABN in another, so joining this column to COE1_ABN_HASH_TRUNC or COE1_PRVDR_ABN_TX_HASH_TRUNC is not a supported operation, and a provider that changes its ABN after a restructure looks like a different provider on either side of the change.
rationale: business.gov.au defines the ABN and what it identifies, which is the only way to attach a meaning to a column whose custodian description says nothing but that the field was hashed.
evidence_quote: An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's bare note that the variable has been hashed as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page said nothing at all about what the field holds.

value_domain: Education provider ABN (hashed and truncated text)
value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
variable_description: The education provider's Australian Business Number for the applicant's first-highest Confirmation of Enrolment, hashed and truncated. The column sits on the visa application extracts that run to 2025. "An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public." (business.gov.au), and truncating the hash trades a small chance of collision for a shorter key. The custodian's note that the value is for primary applicants only and comes from ICSE or IRIS names the departmental systems the value was drawn from, which is why it is missing on rows for family members. It is the provider identifier to use when the question is which business the applicant's top-level enrolment sat with.
description_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
value_definition: An eleven-digit Australian Business Number hashed and then cut to a fixed number of characters, giving an opaque short key. The underlying classification is the Australian Business Register's ABN.

value_domain: State or territory of the education provider on the third Confirmation of Enrolment
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation; ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory where the education provider on the student's third-ranked Confirmation of Enrolment is registered. The visa application file holds three enrolment slots ranked by course level, so COE1_* is the highest course level, COE2_* the second and this the third. ABS describes the Home Affairs feed this comes from as carrying "data on educational studies for student visas", which is exactly this block of columns. It is recorded for primary applicants only, so a dependant travelling on a student visa has nothing here.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation; ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Australia and State/Territory
value_definition: A short code for one Australian state or territory attached to the provider named on the third Confirmation of Enrolment. The ABS standard for the same concept uses one-digit codes 1 to 8 for the states and territories with 9 for Other Territories; whether Home Affairs codes to that order is not stated in the item list, so the mapping has to be read off the data.
limitation: An empty value usually means the applicant had no third enrolment rather than that the provider's state is missing, so treating blanks as missing data will overstate non-response badly. The code also locates the provider's registration, not the student: someone studying at an interstate campus of a nationally registered provider counts to the provider's jurisdiction, and someone who never commenced the course still carries the code.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms that the Home Affairs visa feed carries educational study detail for student visas, which is what the COE block is, and the ABS geography standard supplies the state and territory concept behind the code.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's wording about the third highest course level, with the generic sentence about no published value list printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what a Confirmation of Enrolment is, why there are three of them, or that a blank means no third enrolment.

value_domain: IELTS proficiency band label
value_source: IELTS, IELTS scoring in detail
variable_description: The word label for the applicant's IELTS result, such as competent or good, rather than the number. IELTS reports on a nine-band scale with a label for each band: Band 9 is "Expert" and Band 0 is "Did not attempt the test". IELTS_OVRL on the same row carries the score the label came from, so the two are one result expressed twice. It is populated only for applicants who sat IELTS.
description_source: IELTS, IELTS scoring in detail
value_definition: A word label drawn from the IELTS nine-band descriptor set, one label per band from Band 1 to Band 9 plus a state for a test not attempted. It reports a sat test result, not a self-assessment of English.
limitation: A blank does not mean poor English. Applicants who took PTE Academic, TOEFL, Cambridge or OET, applicants exempt from the English requirement, and applicants on visas that never required a test are all blank, so restricting to non-blank rows selects a particular slice of the skilled and student programmes rather than the good English speakers.
rationale: IELTS publishes the band scale and the descriptor label attached to each band, which is what this column carries.
evidence_quote: Did not attempt the test
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's four-word description, 'English capability (IELTS) proficiency', with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell it was a band label rather than a score, nor why it was missing for most people.

value_domain: IELTS overall band score
value_source: IELTS, IELTS scoring in detail
variable_description: The applicant's overall IELTS band score, the single number formed from the four skill bands. IELTS reports in half-band steps on a nine-band scale, so the value sits on 0, 0.5, 1.0 and so on rather than varying continuously. English requirements and points for skilled visas were set against this number, which makes it the field to use when reconstructing whether an applicant cleared a threshold. IELTS_ENGLISH_PROF is the word label for the same result.
description_source: IELTS, IELTS scoring in detail
value_definition: A number from 0 to 9 in half-band steps, formed by averaging the listening, reading, writing and speaking bands and rounding to a half or whole band. The four component bands are not carried separately in this table, so the composition of the score is lost.
limitation: It is not comparable with a score from another English test, and it carries no test date, so a score attached to a 2015 application may come from a test sat years earlier and a person who applies twice can show two different numbers with no way to order them. It also measures English at test time, not English after settlement.
rationale: IELTS publishes the band scale, the half-band reporting and the way the overall score is formed from the four sections, which is the shape of this column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'English capability (IELTS) score' and the generic sentence about no finite value list twice over, so it never said the score runs 0 to 9 in half bands, that it is an average of four sections, or that no test date comes with it.

value_domain: Labour agreement nomination indicator
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: A flag marking a skilled visa nomination made under a labour agreement rather than under the standard employer nomination rules. A labour agreement is a negotiated arrangement between the Commonwealth and an employer, industry or region that permits sponsorship in occupations or on terms the ordinary programme does not allow, so the flag separates a concessional pathway from the mainstream one. ABS describes this collection as holding "working arrangements for skilled migration visas", and this is one of those working arrangements.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
value_definition: A two-state flag attached to the nomination, set where the nominated position sits under a labour agreement and otherwise not set. It describes the nomination, not the person nominated.
limitation: It does not name the agreement or the concession used, so a designated area migration agreement, a company-specific agreement and an industry agreement are indistinguishable. It also cannot tell you a visa followed, because a nominated position can lapse or be withdrawn with the flag still set.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms this Home Affairs feed carries the working arrangements attached to skilled migration visas, which is the block of nomination and sponsorship columns this flag belongs to.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's sentence about identifying visas under a labour agreement, with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never explained what a labour agreement is or that the flag attaches to a nomination rather than to a grant.

value_domain: Latest-grant-on-day flag
value_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: Marks which of several visas granted to one person on one day is the last. More than one grant can be recorded against a person on a single date - a bridging visa and the substantive visa it bridges to, a primary grant and a correction, a visa granted and then replaced the same day - and counting all of them counts one migration event several times. The flag is what makes a grant countable: filtering to it gives one row per person per grant date.
description_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation
limitation: The flag resolves same-day duplicates only. It says nothing about which grant mattered, and the last one recorded is not always the one the person travelled on. The domain is inferred from the DIL's own parenthetical rather than a published list.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as a flag for the latest visa granted to an individual on a given date of grant, and states the coding in its own text. No separate published definition was found.
evidence_quote: Flag to indicate the latest visa granted to an individual on the given date of grant
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why a reader should filter on it.

value_domain: Nomination approval date
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the department approved the employer's nomination of a position, which is a separate decision from granting the visa. An employer-sponsored skilled visa runs in stages: a sponsor is approved, a position is nominated (NM_LODGED_DT), the nomination is approved, and only then is a visa granted. This column dates the third stage, and the gap between it and the lodgement date is nomination processing time.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
value_definition: A calendar date with an open domain, running over the collection's coverage from 2000 onward. It is populated only for applications that went through an employer or government nomination, which is a minority of the file.
limitation: A blank carries three different meanings that the column cannot separate: the visa needed no nomination, the nomination was refused or withdrawn, or it was still undecided at the extract. Any nomination approval rate built from this field will therefore be wrong. It is also not the day the person started work.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page establishes that this Home Affairs feed carries the working arrangements attached to skilled migration visas, which is the nomination sequence this date sits inside.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Approval date of the nominated application' with the generic sentence about no finite value list repeated as definition and limitation, so it never placed the date in the sponsor-nominate-grant sequence or warned what a blank means.

value_domain: Nomination case identifier
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The identifier for the employer's nomination, shared by everyone on it, so a primary applicant and their family all carry the same value. It is the key that ties a family's visa applications to one nominated position, and the key that lets several nominations by the same sponsor be counted. VA_CASE_ID is the parallel identifier for the visa application itself, and SP_CLIENT_ID identifies the sponsor behind the nomination.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no meaning in its digits. It identifies a nomination event, not a person, not an employer and not a job.
limitation: Counting distinct values does not count jobs or workers. The same position renominated when a visa expires gets a fresh identifier, an employer with several vacancies in one occupation lodges several nominations, and a nomination that was never used still has an identifier, so the count is of administrative events only.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms this collection carries the skilled visa working arrangements, and the identifier's behaviour across primary and secondary applicants is stated in the custodian's own item list.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's note that secondary applicants share the primary's identifier, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what a nomination is or why counting the identifier is not counting jobs.

value_domain: State or territory of the nominated position
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory of the nominated position on an employer-sponsored skilled visa. A secondary applicant inherits the primary applicant's nomination, so a partner and children on the same case all carry the primary's work location. It is the closest thing the visa file has to an intended place of work, and it is fixed at nomination rather than observed after arrival. ABS says of the same geographic concept that "In general, the total area of each State and Territory, including their offshore islands, is used for statistical purposes as a separate geographic area in the ASGS."
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory
value_definition: A single code for one Australian state or territory. The ABS standard for the concept uses one-digit codes 1 through 8 with 9 for Other Territories; the item list does not say whether Home Affairs follows that order, so the codes must be checked against known cases.
limitation: It is not where the person lived or worked. Nothing in the visa stops a holder moving interstate after arrival, a state-nominated regional visa records the nominating jurisdiction rather than the workplace, and the field is blank for every visa granted without a nomination, which is most of the file.
rationale: The ABS geography standard defines the state and territory concept and publishes the one-digit code set that any Australian jurisdiction code of this shape is measured against.
evidence_quote: In general, the total area of each State and Territory, including their offshore islands, is used for statistical purposes as a separate geographic area in the ASGS.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about the nominated position location with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never gave a candidate code set and never warned that the location is an intention rather than an observed workplace.

value_domain: Nomination lodgement date
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the employer lodged the nomination of a position for a skilled visa. The custodian's own text for this column is a mistake: it repeats the NM_CASE_ID description about secondary applicants and does not describe a date at all, so the column name and the date_time tag are the evidence for what it holds. Read against NM_APPRVL_DT it gives nomination processing time, and against VA_LODGED_DT it says whether the employer or the applicant moved first.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
value_definition: A calendar date marking the start of the nomination stage, so on a well-formed row it is the earliest of the nomination dates and sits at or before NM_APPRVL_DT. It exists only where the visa pathway required an employer or government nomination, and unlike the approval date it is present for nominations that were refused or withdrawn as well as approved ones.
limitation: The identification of this column rests on its name rather than on documentation, so check it against NM_APPRVL_DT before use: a lodgement date sitting after its own approval date would show the mapping is wrong. Beyond that, a lodged nomination is not labour demand met, because a nomination later withdrawn looks identical here to one that produced a worker.
rationale: No fetchable page documents this column, and the custodian's own description for it is a copy of another variable's text, so the reading rests on the column name and its neighbours rather than on a source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the custodian's broken sentence, 'The date on which the nomination identifier is the same as the primary applicants', with the generic no-value-list line as definition and limitation, so the page asserted something that is not a description of a date and gave no warning that the metadata is wrong.

value_domain: Nominated occupation code (ASCO or ANZSCO)
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, ANZSCO classification structure, 2022
variable_description: The occupation code for the position an employer nominated, recorded in whichever occupation classification was current at the time. ASCO described the Australian labour market to 2005 and ANZSCO from 2006, so a nomination from 2003 and one from 2015 carry codes from different classifications in the same column. NM_OCPTN_TYPE_CD says which edition applies and NM_OCPTN_FULL_DS gives the words. ABS states that "Occupations are subdivisions of the unit groups and are denoted by 6-digit codes (the relevant unit group code plus an additional two digits)."
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, ANZSCO classification structure, 2022
value_definition: A numeric occupation code. ANZSCO occupations are six digits sitting under a four-digit unit group, a three-digit minor group, a two-digit sub-major group and a one-digit major group; ASCO is structured differently, so code length alone does not identify the edition.
limitation: Pooling the column across years silently mixes two classifications, and the same number can name different occupations in each, so a long time series of nominated occupations built without conversion is wrong rather than noisy. The code also describes the position the employer nominated, not the work the person did after arrival.
rationale: The ABS classification structure page gives the exact code geometry for ANZSCO occupations, which is the classification most of this column uses, and the ABS occupation classification history establishes the ASCO to ANZSCO boundary.
evidence_quote: Occupations are subdivisions of the unit groups and are denoted by 6-digit codes (the relevant unit group code plus an additional two digits).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's sentence naming ASCO or ANZSCO, with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never gave the code geometry nor warned that pooling across editions breaks the series.

value_domain: Nominated occupation title
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Previous occupation classifications
variable_description: The occupation title of the nominated position, written out rather than coded.
